roles.title: Terrazzo Workers and Finishers
roles.description: Apply a mixture of cement, sand, pigment, or marble chips to floors, stairways, and cabinet fixtures to fashion durable and decorative surfaces.

tasks.label: Measure designated amounts of ingredients for terrazzo or grout, according to standard formulas and specifications, using graduated containers and scales, and load ingredients into portable mixer.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Active construction site (building shell): worker proportions sand, portland cement, water (sometimes latex admixture) by bag count, shovel and graduated bucket for terrazzo underbed/sand-cushion mortar, and dumps them into a 3-6 cu ft portable drum or mortar mixer, batch after batch, on an uneven dusty floor shared with other trades.

Active construction site: batching epoxy terrazzo topping - weighing/measuring two-part resin (Part A and B) to the manufacturer's exact ratio on a scale, adding pigment and pre-blended marble/glass chips at the spec ratio, and loading them into a portable mortar mixer under pot-life time pressure.

Job site or renovation: small grout / patch batch - measuring cement, matching pigment, fine sand and water in a graduated pail to a standard formula (and to match the existing floor color) and loading a bucket/paddle mixer to fill voids after grinding.

Precast terrazzo fabrication shop: batching topping and backing mixes (cement or resin, marble chips, pigment, water) on floor scales and in graduated containers into a shop mixer for casting treads, bases and sills; fixed layout, standard equipment, controlled access.

Restoration/repair inside an occupied institutional building (school corridor, airport concourse, hospital lobby) during off-hours: small measured batches of grout or patching mix prepared in a protected work zone with a portable scale and pail mixer.

sources.title: Huntsman launches Granumat 4.0 pigment dosing system for faster colored concrete - Concrete Decor
sources.claim: Granumat pigment metering machines automatically weigh pigment to the color recipe and convey the weighed amount from bulk storage straight into a concrete mixer - an automated batching operation for the pigment ingredient in a purpose-built plant installation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pigment dosing for colored concrete. It is the same operation the terrazzo finisher performs for the pigment ingredient - weigh a designated amount to a recipe and load it into the mixer - at tighter tolerance than hand batching.

sources.system: Wurschum COM 70 / Mini-Com fully automatic color metering system at High Concrete Group
sources.title: High precision color dosing system for High Concrete - Concrete Plant Precast Technology (BFT International)
sources.claim: A US precast concrete producer runs a fully automatic color metering system in its production plant, handling batch sizes up to about 60 lbs with tight metering tolerance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: ingredient/pigment dosing in a precast plant making architectural concrete (same product family as precast terrazzo); the weighing-to-formula and mixer-charging steps are identical to the terrazzo batching step.

sources.system: Automatic concrete batching plant equipment (overhead bins, load-cell weigh hoppers, water meters) per MnDOT Concrete Manual 5-694.411
sources.developer: Minnesota Department of Transportation (specification of standard plant equipment)
sources.title: CONCRETE MANUAL 5-694.400 BATCHING AND MIXING (MnDOT)
sources.claim: Automatic batching equipment used in US concrete production weighs each material to its designated mass in sequence from a single start command and discharges it into the mixer, under specified weighing tolerances and delivery interlocks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: batching cement, aggregate and water for concrete. Same ingredients (cement, sand/chips, water, admixture) and same act (weigh to a formula, charge a mixer) at equal or better accuracy than a worker using buckets and a scale.

sources.title: AI in Concrete Batching - Command Cloud Batch AI Feed From: Command Alkon | For Construction Pros
sources.claim: Commercial batch-plant automation batches concrete to mix designs across ready-mix plants without constant operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: recipe-driven batching of cementitious materials; shows the measure-and-charge loop runs unattended at production quality, which is the whole of the terrazzo batching step once ingredients are presented in silos and hoppers.

sources.system: A-Lab autonomous laboratory (robotic powder dosing and mixing station)
sources.developer: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory / UC Berkeley (Ceder group)
sources.title: Meet the autonomous lab of the future | EurekAlert!
sources.claim: In the A-Lab, a robotic-arm station autonomously weighs dry powder precursors to recipe, mixes them and transfers the mixture onward, choosing among roughly 200 stored ingredients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: gravimetric dosing of dry powders to a formula and loading them into a mixing vessel by robot arm - the same act as measuring cement and pigment into a mixer, at smaller scale, inside a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Graco meter, mix and dispense systems (EFR, PR-X, PR70, HFR)
sources.title: Meter, Mix & Dispense Equipment for Sealant & Adhesives | Graco
sources.claim: Graco meter-mix-dispense proportioners automatically meter two-component epoxies and other reactive materials at a programmed ratio in plant manufacturing settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-ratio proportioning of two-component epoxy - exactly the resin/hardener measuring step of epoxy terrazzo batching, at equal or better ratio accuracy, in a fixed plant installation.

sources.system: Magma portable mixing unit (with Vulcan printer and BuildOS)
sources.title: 3D Printed Houses in Texas and Later the Moon | NextBigFuture.com
sources.claim: ICON's Magma portable mixing unit on 3D-printed housing job sites automatically mixes the cementitious material with additives and water for site conditions and feeds the printer; it starts from a single pre-blended proprietary dry mix rather than batching separate site-supplied ingredients to a formula.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-site automated dosing and mixing of a cementitious material - the closest job-site analogue, but it proportions only water and additives into a pre-blended dry mix, so it does not cover formula batching of cement, sand, pigment and chips.

tasks.label: Grind surfaces with a power grinder, or polish surfaces with polishing or surfacing machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New cast-in-place or epoxy terrazzo installation in a commercial building under construction (school, airport terminal, hospital, retail): initial/rough grinding of the large open field of the floor with a heavy planetary grinder, several passes with coarse diamonds/stones, wet or dry with slurry or dust extraction, working around columns, staged materials and other trades.

Same jobs, later stage: after grouting and cure, honing and final polishing passes over the large open field with progressively finer diamonds/pads to the specified aggregate exposure and gloss, checking uniformity before sealing.

Edge, corner and around-obstacle grinding and polishing on the same jobs with hand-held edger/small grinders: along walls and cove bases, in doorways and closets, under casework toe kicks, around columns, drains, thresholds and floor boxes, blending edge work into the machine-ground field.

Grinding and polishing cast-in-place terrazzo stairs, landings, treads, risers and nosings, and vertical surfaces such as curbs, cove base and cabinet-fixture faces, in place with small hand-held grinders and polishers, often on ladders/kneeling and in confined stairwells.

Restoration/refinishing of existing terrazzo in an occupied institutional facility (school corridor, hospital lobby, courthouse, museum): area cleared and cordoned for night or weekend work, honing out scratches and stains and re-polishing the open field of the floor to a uniform finish before reopening.

Shop/precast work: grinding and polishing precast terrazzo units (window sills, bases, cabinet-fixture tops, flat panels) at a fabrication shop bench or machine before delivery, to a specified flat, filled and polished face.

sources.title: Professional Demolition International – Husqvarna Construction's first self-operating floor grinder
sources.claim: Husqvarna Autogrinder 8 D is a self-operating planetary floor grinder (based on the PG 8 DR) that performs grinding or polishing of concrete floor fields on job sites after the operator sets the working area; LiDAR scans the room and tracks machine position.
sources.transferJustification: Terrazzo finishers grind and polish cementitious/epoxy terrazzo with the same class of planetary diamond grinder used for concrete grinding and polishing; the machine, abrasives and multi-pass progression are the same.

sources.title: Manpower meets machine power: Will Husqvarna Autogrinder™ transform the surface preparation industry?
sources.claim: Husqvarna states the Autogrinder self-navigates while grinding and polishing, freeing the operator for other floor finishing tasks; it was unveiled at Bauma 2025 after field tests, with sales starting in Europe at end of 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Same planetary grinding/polishing process and tooling used by terrazzo finishers on cementitious and epoxy terrazzo floors.

sources.title: Professional Demolition International – Husqvarna Construction's first self-operating floor grinder
sources.claim: Edge grinding remains manual work while the Autogrinder runs the open field; the operator must change tools between grinding and polishing passes and stay onsite, and finish quality still depends on operator skill.

sources.system: BMR Floor Grinding Robot (850 M series)
sources.title: Floor Grinding Robot | Automatic Concrete Grinder | Epoxy Floor Polishing Machine - BMR
sources.claim: BrightMaster (Bright Dream Robotics) sells a Floor Grinding Robot that autonomously navigates and grinds floors, explicitly including epoxy terrazzo, inorganic terrazzo and terrazzo floors, in underground garages, factory workshops, laboratories and sports venues, with automatic dust collection and obstacle stop.

sources.system: XINGYI AT8 autonomous floor grinder (ATLAS FSG)
sources.developer: Fujian Xingyi Intelligent Equipment Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Xingyi in AI+Construction Pilot Program | AI Floor Robots
sources.claim: Fujian Xingyi's AT8 autonomous floor grinding robot (ATLAS FSG system, laser + visual navigation, self-navigation, full-coverage path planning, adjustable pressure) was selected for Wenzhou's 2026 'AI + Construction' pilot and demonstrated in live tests; the product line covers floor preparation through fine polishing of concrete, stone and terrazzo floors.

sources.title: True Autonomy: Introducing autonomy in concrete floor polishing (LightWare LiDAR)
sources.claim: True Autonomy's ACP-100 is a retrofittable autonomous robot that navigates and operates a concrete floor polishing machine through the methodical progressively-finer-diamond passes of a polishing job, while contractors do the harder hand grinding and caulking in parallel.
sources.transferJustification: Multi-pass diamond polishing of a cementitious floor field is the same operation terrazzo finishers perform with polishing/surfacing machines; abrasives, machine class and acceptance criteria (uniform gloss over the field) match.

sources.system: Pedrini GALAXY B220GX automatic slab polishing line
sources.title: Italian Graniti: new polishing line and multiwire machine by Pedrini to increase production capacity
sources.claim: Automatic-cycle slab polishing lines are standard production equipment in stone/agglomerate plants: Pedrini's GALAXY B220GX slab polisher runs an automatic cycle and was installed at Italian Graniti to polish marble and granite slabs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory calibrating/polishing of stone and cement-marble agglomerate (terrazzo) slabs. Same abrasive progression and finish specification as shop grinding/polishing of flat precast terrazzo units, with the workpiece conveyed and fixtured under the heads.

tasks.label: Cut metal division strips and press them into the terrazzo base for joints or changes of color to form designs or patterns or to help prevent cracks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial construction (school, hospital, airport, retail): after the underbed or slab is prepared, the worker snaps chalk lines from shop drawings for a large open field area, cuts zinc or brass L-strips to length with snips/shears, and presses them into the plastic sand-cement underbed or beds them in epoxy adhesive on the cured slab, keeping long runs straight, level with the finish elevation, and aligned over slab control joints. Dusty, congested active jobsite with other trades working around him.

Same jobsites, perimeter and obstruction work: fitting short strip pieces around columns, door openings, floor boxes, drains, thresholds and wall junctions; cutting angles and coped ends by eye to as-built dimensions that differ from the drawings, splicing strips, and pressing each piece into the base flush with adjacent runs.

Custom decorative work: logos, lettering, medallions, curved and freeform multi-color patterns transferred from shop drawings or stencils; strips bent to radius by hand or with a bender on site, mitred or soldered at intersections, intricate closed shapes set and pressed into the base to tight tolerance so each color pour is contained.

Stairs, cove base, landings and cabinet/counter tops poured in place: setting divider and nosing strips on treads and risers, at stringers and at base-to-floor junctions; short pieces, awkward body positions, vertical and sloped surfaces, work at the head of a stair or in a tight toilet room.

Precast terrazzo fabrication shop: cutting and setting divider strips into forms/molds for precast treads, panels, sills and window stools before the terrazzo mix is placed; fixed benches, standard mold sizes, controlled indoor conditions.

Renovation/repair in an existing or partially occupied building: chopping out damaged terrazzo and corroded strips, cutting replacement strips to match existing profiles and alignments, and pressing them into patch material so the repair ties into the surrounding existing floor.

sources.date: 2022 (installed at Glass Madrid Berlanas; product line current)
sources.title: Spacer application for laminated glass - LiSEC.com (VSA-A)
sources.claim: Fully automatic machine that applies a thin spacer strip from a roll along a programmed path onto a fixtured flat glass panel, positioning it precisely and pressing it into an adhesive (butyl) bond, including corners and cut-off; in commercial production use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying an insulating-glass spacer strip. It is the same class of action as pressing a division strip into a terrazzo base - a long thin strip is fed, positioned to a programmed line on a flat fixtured substrate, pressed into an adhesive bond and terminated at length, at millimetre accuracy. Strip stock, flat substrate and required precision are comparable; only the bedding medium differs.

sources.title: Individual machines - LiSEC.com
sources.claim: The same production line includes a robot system that automatically mounts rigid (aluminium/steel) spacer frames onto glass sheets, i.e. robotic placement of a preformed metal frame onto a fixtured panel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mounting a preformed rigid metal frame onto a fixtured flat panel - the placement half of setting a preformed division-strip pattern into a terrazzo base; comparable thin metal profiles, comparable positional tolerance, workpiece presented by the machine.

sources.system: Weckenmann shuttering robot (3rd generation), e.g. at Keegan Precast
sources.title: Highly dynamic shuttering robot of the third generation - BFT International (Concrete Plant + Precast Technology)
sources.claim: Fully automated shuttering robots in precast concrete plants take steel shuttering profiles from magazines and place them onto flat casting pallets in the positions required by the element geometry, driven by production data from the plant master computer; installed and running in production plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic shuttering of precast casting beds. Placing steel profiles on a flat casting bed to the lines of a digital design, so the profiles divide and contain the concrete pour, is functionally the same operation as setting division strips that divide and contain terrazzo pours; same thin steel profiles, same flat fixtured substrate, same layout-from-drawing precision.

sources.system: House of Design Automated Floor Truss System
sources.title: Automated Floor Truss Systems - House of Design Robotics
sources.claim: Robotic cell that picks metal connector plates, positions them to the design geometry on the member and presses/embeds them into the workpiece, building floor trusses from digital design files in a purpose-built production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic nail-plate embedding. It demonstrates the 'press a metal element into the workpiece at a design-specified location' step with a fixtured workpiece and design-file-driven positioning, the core motion of pressing a division strip into a terrazzo base.

sources.title: FieldPrint Platform | Dusty Robotics
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile robots are in routine commercial use on building floors at active jobsites, but the deployed capability is printing BIM layout lines on the slab for human trades, not cutting or installing material.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only to characterise what on-site autonomous floor robots actually do (layout marking); it does not substantiate cutting or embedding division strips, so it supports no positive judgment at E2 or E3.

tasks.label: Blend marble chip mixtures, place into panels, and push a roller over the surface to embed the chips.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial construction (school, hospital, airport, retail): crew mixes cementitious or epoxy terrazzo matrix with marble/glass chip blends in a portable mixer, wheels or pumps it onto an underbed, places it into panels bounded by brass/zinc divider strips, screeds to strip height, broadcasts extra chips, and pushes a heavy roller over the surface to embed chips and squeeze out excess matrix, then trowels to finish. Large open floor areas, unfinished building, other trades working nearby, temporary lighting and power.

Same construction jobsites, but stairs, landings, cove/wall base, curbs, and small irregular areas: mix placed and packed by hand into narrow or vertical panels, small hand rollers or hand tampers used to embed chips, abrasive nosing strips and divider strips already set; tight access, changing geometry.

Precast terrazzo fabrication shop: worker batches the chip/cement or epoxy mix, fills wood or steel molds for panels, treads, risers, sills, bases and countertops laid out on shop tables, screeds and vibrates/rolls to embed the chips, then the piece cures for grinding and polishing. Fixed indoor facility, standard equipment, controlled access.

Restoration/patch work in an existing occupied institutional building (school corridor, courthouse, hospital): damaged panel or saw-cut area is chipped out and cleaned, a small batch of matching chip mix is blended, packed into the bounded panel area, and rolled/tamped to embed chips flush with adjacent terrazzo; color and aggregate must match the surrounding floor; work occurs off-hours around furniture and occupants.

Small residential or custom-feature work: a homeowner's bathroom/kitchen floor, entry, shower pan, or a custom terrazzo countertop/vanity; small hand-blended batches placed into small panels or molds and rolled/tamped to embed chips; cluttered, non-standard site with limited access and no institutional control.

sources.system: Qunfeng QPV600K Terrazzo Tile Production Line
sources.title: Terrazzo Tile Production Line QPV600K – Advanced System for Mass Tile Manufacturing
sources.claim: A commercially sold terrazzo tile production line performs the whole work content of the task under machine control in a purpose-built plant: it automatically blends the marble/stone chip and cement mixture, fills the mould (the panel), and compacts/presses it to embed the chips, in a 45-55 s cycle under Siemens PLC control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory casting of terrazzo panels/curb units. Transfer: identical materials (marble/stone chips in cement matrix), identical operations (blend the chip mixture, place it into a bounded panel, compact it so the chips are embedded and the matrix closed), and the output is green terrazzo that is subsequently ground and polished exactly as poured-in-place terrazzo is. It substantiates completion only when the panel is presented to the machine as a fixtured mould on a line (E1).

sources.system: Terrazzo tile making machine (hydraulic press line)
sources.title: Terrazzo Tile Making Machine - Zhengzhou City Golden Mountain Machinery Company
sources.claim: Terrazzo tile making machines mix marble/stone/glass chips with cement to a uniform mixture and then ... that mixture into the hydraulic press mould to form terrazzo tiles of different thicknesses, sizes and patterns.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated terrazzo tile forming. Transfer: it covers the blending of the marble-chip mixture and its placement into a bounded panel plus the compaction step that the hand roller performs in situ; same aggregate sizes and cement matrix, same required result (chips embedded, surface dense enough to grind).

sources.system: Hongfa automatic hydraulic press terrazzo tile production line
sources.title: Hongfa automatic hydraulic press terrazzo tile cement floor tiles concrete mosaic tiles making machines
sources.claim: A second established block/tile machinery maker describes the same fully automatic terrazzo/cement tile line workflow: elevating raw material, mixing, fixed-quantity filling of the mould, pressure forming, mould unloading and stacking, with polishing downstream.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated terrazzo tile manufacture. Transfer: confirms that blending the chip mixture, dosing it into a panel mould and compacting it to embed the chips is a routine, multi-vendor, machine-controlled operation when the panel is brought to the machine.

sources.system: Vollert SMART CAST concrete spreader and SMART COMPACT compaction station
sources.date: 2026-01 (page assets), product line in commercial use for years
sources.title: Concrete spreader and compaction - Vollert Precast Solutions
sources.claim: Precast concrete plants use automated concrete spreaders that dose fresh mix into shutterings/moulds on stationary or pallet-circulation lines, followed by automated vibratory compaction stations, i.e. mould filling and compaction of shaped units is machine-controlled in a purpose-built plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated filling and compaction of precast concrete moulds. Transfer: precast terrazzo treads, bases and sills are cast the same way — a cementitious chip-loaded mix dosed into a shaped mould and vibrated/compacted instead of rolled; comparable material rheology, tolerances and finish requirements, but only inside a purpose-built casting line.

tasks.label: Modify mixing, grouting, grinding, or cleaning procedures, according to type of installation or material used.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial poured-in-place epoxy terrazzo in a building under construction (airport concourse, school, hospital, retail): worker changes the resin/hardener and aggregate loading for ambient temperature, humidity and chip type, then alters the grind sequence (initial cut depth, diamond grit progression, machine weight/speed) for the hardness of the marble, granite, glass or mother-of-pearl chips, applies a matching grout coat into pinholes, re-grinds, and cleans. Dusty active site shared with other trades, layout differs job to job.

On-site detail and vertical work in the same buildings: stair treads and risers, cove base, curbs, wainscot, thresholds, cabinet/fixture tops. Worker stiffens the mix for vertical and small pours, hand-grouts, and switches to hand/edge grinders and different grit sequences in corners, on nosings and around drains and dividers.

Restoration/refinishing of an existing terrazzo floor in an operating institution (school corridor, courthouse lobby, hospital wing): worker identifies whether the matrix is cement or epoxy and how worn/cracked it is, adjusts the chemical cleaning/stripping method, chooses the grit progression and patch/grout mix to match the old chips, fills cracks, polishes and seals, working in a barricaded zone in an occupied, institution-controlled building.

Precast terrazzo shop fabrication of stair treads, bases, sills, window stools and panels: worker batches cement or epoxy matrix mixes adjusted for chip size/type and product, casts and cures units, machine-grinds coarse then fine with material-appropriate abrasives, grouts voids, and cleans units before shipping. Fixed indoor shop with standard machines.

Residential terrazzo install or refinish in a private home (common in Florida): worker adapts cleaning/stripping to old sealers, carpet adhesive or paint, adapts grinding to a thin or cracked slab and to unknown chip material, patches and re-polishes room by room around furniture, doorways and fixtures.

sources.system: LT Automation robotic terrazzo stair grinding cell (Leth Beton)
sources.title: Robot grinding terrazzo stairs | LT Automation
sources.claim: A robot cell at precast producer Leth Beton autonomously coarse- and fine-grinds cast terrazzo stair elements, using a sensor system that reads elements of varying size so that no per-part programming is needed; it runs daily on up to two shifts.
sources.transferJustification: Same trade operation on the same material: machine grinding of cast terrazzo elements (stairs) in a precast shop, i.e. the grinding branch of this task, with the process automatically adapted to differing element sizes.

sources.system: GrayMatter Robotics GMR-AI robotic finishing cells
sources.title: GrayMatter Robotics opens physical AI innovation center - The Robot Report
sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics' GMR-AI finishing cells autonomously scan an unseen part, generate their own force-controlled process program in under a minute, and sand, grind, polish and buff parts across different materials and geometries; more than 25 such cells run production work at its headquarters and at customer plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic abrasive surface finishing of fixtured workpieces. It transfers to the grinding branch of this task only inside a purpose-built cell, because the robot adjusts abrasive process parameters to the material and geometry of the part presented to it.

sources.system: Hydronix microwave moisture sensors with automated batch-plant control
sources.developer: Hydronix / concrete batch plant control vendors
sources.title: Moisture measurement – an essential for automating concrete production - Concrete Plant Precast Technology
sources.claim: Modern precast/ready-mix batch plants use microwave moisture sensors on aggregate bins and in mixers so the plant control system automatically changes aggregate dosing and mix water in each batch according to the condition of the raw materials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated batching of cementitious mixes. Same materials (cement, sand/aggregate, water) and the same kind of adjustment — changing the mixing recipe according to the material actually being used — but only inside a fixed plant.

sources.system: Breton agglomerate stone plant (Santa Margherita) with Levibreton KCP/KFG polishing lines
sources.title: Agglomerate stone producer adds new plant | Stone World
sources.claim: In an automated Breton agglomerate (marble/quartz chip plus resin) slab plant, the mixing process itself is switched according to the product being made, and the cast slabs then run automatically through calibrating and multi-head polishing lines and finishing/packing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory production of chip-and-binder (terrazzo-type) slabs. It covers the mixing and grinding/polishing branches of this task with the procedure varied by product/material, but only on a fixtured conveyor line.

sources.system: Bright Dream Robotics floor grinding robot (as reviewed)
sources.title: Application and Development of Autonomous Robots in Concrete Construction: Challenges and Opportunities
sources.claim: Concrete/epoxy floor grinding robots used in underground garages and indoor workshops still require a person to control the machine during the grinding work, and cover open floor areas rather than edges, grouting or mix adjustment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: powered grinding of hard floor surfaces on site. Cited to show the closest field system is operator-attended and limited to open-area grinding, so it cannot substantiate whole-task completion in situ.

sources.title: Automated Floor grinding & dust collection robot
sources.claim: A commercially offered floor grinding robot for hardener, epoxy and stone/terrazzo floors in garages, workshops and sports venues performs grinding and dust collection but is paired one-to-one with a worker.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine grinding of terrazzo/epoxy floors in facilities. Cited as the closest in-situ product; because a worker accompanies each robot and no grouting or material-based procedure change is shown, it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Spread, level, or smooth concrete or terrazzo mixtures to form bases or finished surfaces, using rakes, shovels, hand or power trowels, hand or power screeds, or floats.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Epoxy (thin-set) terrazzo topping poured over a prepared slab in a commercial building under construction (school, airport, hospital, retail): resin/chip mix is dumped, spread with squeegee and trowel to about 3/8 in. between brass/zinc divider strips, and hand-troweled flat before it sets, working around columns, doorways and wall lines.

Cementitious terrazzo topping (sand-cushion or bonded system) over an underbed: mix spread and screeded flush to divider strips, extra marble chips seeded, then rolled/tamped and troweled smooth, in an interior space of a building under construction.

Placing the base: concrete slab or sand-cement underbed over the open field of a large floor area - raking/shoveling the mix out, screeding to grade with a power or hand screed, then floating and power-troweling the field before set.

Detail and edge work: stair treads, risers and landings, cove base, curbs, thresholds, cabinet/counter tops, borders around columns and doorways, plus the perimeter strip of every pour - small quantities hand-placed and hand-troweled to feathered, shaped edges.

Patch, repair and retrofit in an existing occupied institutional building (school, hospital, airport) during off-hours: damaged terrazzo or concrete cut out, a matching mix hand-placed into small irregular areas and troweled flush with the surrounding floor.

sources.title: Concrete Finishing Robot - BrightMaster Robotics
sources.claim: BrightMaster (Bright Dream) Robotics sells a Concrete Finishing Robot that runs in a fully automatic mode ... SLAM navigation to compact, slurry-lift, finish and polish cast-in-place concrete floors in basements, plazas, factories, airports and malls.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the 'smooth concrete ... using power trowels' element of the task on the same material (fresh cast-in-place concrete floors), though on plain concrete rather than terrazzo topping.

sources.title: Floor Screeding Robot - BrightMaster Robotics
sources.claim: BrightMaster Robotics sells a Floor Screeding Robot for dry-mixed mortar screeding of residential, public-building and metro-station floors, operated as a one-touch fully automatic cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Spreading and screeding a dry-mix sand-cement mortar bed is the same operation as placing and leveling the mortar underbed/base for terrazzo.

sources.title: About BMR - BrightMaster Robotics
sources.claim: The developer of these concrete floor robots reports large-scale field delivery and use of its construction robot line.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployment maturity of the same product family (concrete leveling, screeding and finishing robots) rather than a separate task.

sources.system: Ground leveling robot (地面整平机器人)
sources.title: 工地迎来"机器人"工友——博智林建筑机器人应用调研纪实 (Sina Finance)
sources.claim: On-site reporting from a Chinese residential construction project describes the ground-leveling robot as planning its own path under a navigation system and performing fully automatic leveling of freshly poured concrete floors to millimetre accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Same operation as the task's leveling element: automatically screeding/leveling freshly placed concrete on a building floor.

sources.title: Surface technology - Vollert Precast Solutions
sources.claim: Precast concrete plants use an automated trowelling machine station that travels over the fixtured casting pallet and smooths the exposed concrete surface of the element.
sources.transferJustification: Machine performs the 'smooth concrete mixture to form a finished surface' step with rotating trowel vanes, on a mould fixtured on a plant pallet - the E1 form of the same work.

sources.system: Weckenmann carousel (pallet circulation) casting line at Molin Concrete
sources.title: Carousel Course - Concrete Products
sources.claim: A US precast plant (Molin Concrete, Ramsey MN) runs a Weckenmann carousel line where an automatic concrete spreader pours the panels and an overhead troweling station applies the final finishes, with almost no manual handling.
sources.transferJustification: The spreader-plus-troweling-station sequence places, levels and finishes a concrete mixture into a fixtured mould, i.e. the same spread/level/smooth work brought to a purpose-built machine line.

sources.system: Hongfa HFT300 terrazzo tile making machine
sources.title: Hongfa automatic hydraulic press terrazzo tile cement floor tiles making machines
sources.claim: Fully automatic PLC-controlled terrazzo tile plants mix the cement/marble-chip terrazzo mixture, meter it into the mould through a dosing feeder and press it to form the finished terrazzo surface.
sources.transferJustification: Handles the identical material (cement plus marble-chip terrazzo mix) and forms the finished terrazzo surface, but with the work brought to the machine in a fixtured mould instead of placed in situ.

tasks.label: Grind curved surfaces or areas inaccessible to surfacing machine, such as stairways or cabinet tops, with portable hand grinder.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New-construction jobsite (school, airport, hospital, retail shell): after the walk-behind surfacing machine passes over a poured-in-place terrazzo floor, the finisher hand-grinds the perimeter strip along walls, inside corners, door jambs, around columns and embedded floor items with a portable wet edge grinder, stepping through grits and matching the machine-ground finish; dusty/slurry conditions, other trades working nearby.

Terrazzo stairway in a building under construction: grinding treads, nosings, risers, landings and stair cove base with a portable hand grinder, working on and around the flight, matching the finish of the adjacent floor, often on scaffolded or unfinished stair enclosures.

Curved and vertical features on the jobsite: integral cove base, curved walls, radiused corners, columns, curbs, planters and seat walls hand-ground with a portable grinder to a uniform exposure of the marble chips.

Cabinet tops, vanity tops, window sills, thresholds and bench tops finished in place: hand-grinding the top surface, bullnosed or eased edges and backsplash junctions of terrazzo cast on or set onto casework, in a partly finished room.

Precast terrazzo fabrication shop: units (stair treads, wall base, vanity/counter tops, sills) demolded on benches and hand-ground/polished with a portable grinder on curved edges, returns and corners the shop's slab machines cannot reach, before shipment.

Restoration/refinishing in an occupied institutional building (school corridor and stairs, airport concourse, courthouse) during off-hours: hand-grinding worn stair treads, cove base and floor edges of an existing installed terrazzo surface to blend with machine-restored areas, working around furniture, railings and building services.

sources.system: ABB robot + FerRobotics Active Angular Kit AAK 617 Concrete (accell integration) at STS Fertigteile

sources.claim: At STS Fertigteile's precast concrete plant, an ABB robot fitted with FerRobotics' AAK 617 Concrete angle-grinder end effector scans and grinds precast concrete stairs, balconies and other parts fully automatically after they are set on a traversing table; the cell replaces the previous manual grinding by trained specialists.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic angle-grinding of cast cementitious surfaces (fair-faced precast concrete stairs/balconies) to a specified surface class. Terrazzo hand-grinding uses the same tool class (portable angle grinder with abrasive/diamond media) on the same material family (cement matrix with aggregate), with force-controlled contact needed to reach a uniform finish.

sources.title: Automated scanning grinding precast concrete Active Angular Kit end effector AAK 601 Concrete - FerRobotics
sources.claim: The same FerRobotics/ABB concrete-grinding cell reaches right up to edges and into corners of the fixtured precast part while holding constant contact force.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grinding the edge and corner zones of a cementitious workpiece — the exact geometry a terrazzo finisher must hand-grind because the surfacing machine cannot reach it.

sources.title: Grinding and sanding go autonomous | The Fabricator
sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics supplies autonomous robotic sanding, grinding and polishing cells that plan their own toolpaths for varied fixtured parts in fabrication shops, automating surface finishing that remains manual in most shops.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous force-controlled abrasive finishing of fixtured workpieces of varying geometry in a purpose-built cell; establishes that hand-grinder-class finishing is achievable at production quality when the work is presented to the machine, though on metal rather than cementitious substrate.

sources.title: Autonomous Concrete Floor Polishing & LightWare's SF40/C LiDAR | Unmanned Systems Technology
sources.claim: Autonomous jobsite concrete polishing robots operate the large walk-behind/ride-on floor machine on open floor area, while the difficult hand grinding at edges and details is still left to human contractors.
sources.transferJustification: Same trade context (in-situ concrete/terrazzo floor grinding): the most advanced fielded jobsite grinding robot covers only open floor area and explicitly leaves hand grinding of edges and details to workers, indicating the in-situ (E2/E3) version of this task is not covered.

tasks.label: Wash polished terrazzo surface, using cleaner and water, and apply sealer and curing agent according to manufacturer's specifications, using brush or sprayer.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large open field areas of newly polished terrazzo in a commercial building under construction (school, airport concourse, hospital, retail): after final grinding/polish the crew machine-washes hundreds to thousands of square feet with cleaner and water, vacuums the slurry/rinse, lets it dry, then applies sealer and curing agent with applicator or sprayer. Active jobsite: other trades present, debris, temporary lighting, adjacent finishes to protect.

Detail work on the same jobs: stair treads and risers, landings, cove/base, curbs, thresholds, restroom floors, cabinet fixtures and precast-in-place trim. Hand-washing with cleaner and sponge/mop, then brush or small-sprayer application of sealer into corners, vertical cove and tight geometry without runs onto walls.

Restoration/resealing of an existing terrazzo floor in an occupied institution (school corridor, hospital lobby, airport concourse) worked after hours: furniture cleared, floor scrub-washed with cleaner and water, rinsed and dried, then sealer applied wall-to-wall on a mostly open, standard-layout floor and buffed.

Residential or small cluttered commercial terrazzo (mid-century house floors, small shop or lobby with fixtures): small rooms, doorways, furniture and cabinetry in place, varied layout site to site; wash with cleaner and water and hand-apply sealer.

Precast terrazzo units (stair treads, window sills, wall/base panels, shop-cast items) washed and sealed/cured in the fabrication shop before shipping, with units handled on benches or a conveyor line.

sources.title: Worlds leading autonomous floor scrubbing robot (Meet Neo 2W)
sources.claim: Avidbots Neo is a commercially sold fully autonomous scrubbing robot that washes hard floors, explicitly including terrazzo, with brushes, water and detergent.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the wash step of this task (cleaner plus water on polished terrazzo); it does not cover sealer application.

sources.title: Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport to Deploy Floor Cleaning Robot

sources.title: Avidbots Designs Fully Autonomous Cleaning Robots for Airports and Hospitals
sources.claim: Autonomous scrubbing robots are in routine service across structured human work facilities worldwide.

sources.claim: Terrazzo tiles and slabs are ground, wet-polished and finished continuously under PLC control on automatic production lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated wet processing (water flush during grind/polish) of terrazzo units on a conveyor line, covering the wash portion of the shop instance in a purpose-built setting.

tasks.label: Position and secure moisture membrane and wire mesh in preparation for pouring base materials for terrazzo installation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New construction of a large open institutional floor (school corridor bank, airport concourse, hospital lobby): worker rolls polyethylene/isolation moisture membrane sheets over the cured concrete slab, laps and tapes seams, then unrolls 2"x2" galvanized welded wire mesh over the sand/membrane bed, cuts rolls to length, laps and wire-ties or clips laps, and keeps the mesh flat and centered. Active construction site with other trades, staged materials, dust, temporary lighting.

Rooms, corridors and areas full of interruptions: membrane and mesh must be cut and fitted around columns, door thresholds, floor drains, pipe sleeves, embedded conduits and irregular perimeters; sheets trimmed at walls, mesh clipped back from divider strips and expansion joints. Kneeling, confined work in partially built-out spaces.

Stairs, landings, cove bases and other non-flat geometry: membrane turned up walls, mesh/lath cut and bent over treads, risers and nosings and fastened to the substrate so the base mix can be packed over it. Requires shaping fine mesh to 3-D surfaces and securing it against movement.

Renovation/retrofit in an existing building (school over summer break, retail remodel, hospital wing phase): old flooring demolished, substrate patched and swept, then membrane and mesh laid in a space with existing walls, doorways, fixtures and tight access, often on night or phased schedules with unpredictable substrate conditions.

Shop fabrication of precast terrazzo units (panels, treads, bases, sink surrounds) at a fabrication facility: bond-breaker/backing sheet and reinforcing wire mesh positioned and secured inside forms on casting tables before the base mix is poured; repeatable mold layouts, fixed workstations, controlled indoor conditions.

sources.title: New generation of rebar-tying robot TyBot 3.0 hits the market | Equipment World
sources.claim: TyBot 3.0 is an autonomous gantry robot used on bridge decks that travels the deck and ties rebar intersections without pre-programming; it works on horizontal reinforcing steel installations that already have screed rails, and has been used on 65+ US projects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: securing horizontal reinforcement before a concrete pour on an open construction site. It shows field autonomy for tying only; it does not unroll or position sheet membrane or welded wire mesh, and it requires screed rails spanning the deck, so it cannot complete this task's instances in the field.

sources.title: RBR50 Spotlight: Advanced Construction Robotics' IronBOT makes rebar installation faster, safer - The Robot Report
sources.claim: IronBOT lifts, carries and places ... bundles up to 5,000 lb on bridge decks, paired with TyBOT for a carry-place-tie sequence; autonomy of the placement step is not clearly documented in independent reporting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing reinforcement on a deck before a pour. Objects are heavy rebar bundles handled by a deck-spanning gantry, not rolled membrane or light welded wire fabric, and autonomy is not established, so it cannot support a positive field judgment.

sources.system: MSM-M mesh welding machine (with DRA-M straightening/cutting machine)
sources.title: Mbk mesh welding machine for precast slabs, double and solid walls - Concrete Plant Precast Technology (BFT International)
sources.claim: The mbk MSM-M mesh welding machine automatically produces welded reinforcing steel mesh from CAD data (including meshes with recesses for openings) and, via a mesh conveyor and traverse, deposits the mesh on the shuttering pallets of a precast circulation plant according to master-computer specifications, ready for concreting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: positioning welded wire mesh reinforcement on a casting bed immediately before cementitious material is poured. Same object class (welded steel mesh sheets up to 3.5 x 8 m), tighter positional tolerance than terrazzo underbed mesh, in a purpose-built machine line.

sources.system: Fully automatic gypsum board production line (forming station with paper correcting and glue devices)
sources.title: Hot Air Gypsum Board Production Line - Shandong Yurui Machinery Group Co., Ltd
sources.claim: Fully automatic gypsum board production lines continuously position a lower paper facing web on the forming belt, feed and glue the upper web through a correcting/glue station, and deposit the cementitious slurry onto the positioned sheet, with edges folded and bonded automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: positioning and securing a continuous sheet (facing web) on a bed and lapping/bonding it immediately before a cementitious mix is poured over it. Same functional step as laying and sealing a moisture membrane, executed by purpose-built machinery at production tolerances.

sources.system: Grenzebach plasterboard production line (paper handling, mixing and forming, forming belt)
sources.title: Production lines for plasterboard | Grenzebach
sources.claim: Grenzebach supplies and has commissioned complete plasterboard production lines (e.g., two lines for XINFA with 120 million m2/year total output) whose plant components include paper handling, forming belt, and mixing/forming stations, i.e. automated sheet handling integrated with slurry deposition.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: continuous automated positioning of facing sheet material on a forming line before cementitious slurry is cast onto it; corroborates that purpose-built lines handle roll-goods placement and pouring together at commercial scale.

sources.title: RBR50 Spotlight: Renovate Robotics puts Rufus to work on roofs - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Rufus is a prototype roofing robot that attaches to a roof and travels in a ... pattern placing and securing asphalt shingles; it remains a prototype in development with a distributor partnership, and independent reporting does not establish unattended autonomous completion of whole roofs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing and fastening overlapping sheet-goods over a large flat surface in an unstructured site. It is the closest field analog found, but it handles rigid shingles from a magazine, is a prototype, and autonomy is unclear, so it cannot support an E3 judgment for membrane and mesh.

tasks.label: Fill slight grinding depressions with matching grout material and hand-trowel for a smooth, uniform surface.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-field grout coat on a large newly ground poured-in-place terrazzo floor in a commercial building under construction (airport concourse, school, hospital lobby): mix pigmented cement or epoxy grout to match the mix, spread it over hundreds to thousands of square feet with squeegee/float, work it into pinholes and slight grinding depressions, trowel off excess for a uniform surface before the re-grind.

Perimeter and detail areas of the same new-construction floor: grouting and hand-troweling along walls and cove bases, around columns, doorways, floor drains, divider strips and embedded inserts, in corridors and small rooms, on knees with hawk and small trowel while other trades work nearby.

Stairs, landings, integral cove base, nosings, curved/vertical terrazzo elements: filling grinding depressions on treads, risers and vertical faces with matching grout and hand-troweling in constrained, non-planar geometry on the jobsite.

Restoration/regrout of an existing terrazzo floor inside an occupied institution (school corridor, courthouse lobby, hospital wing) after grinding: filling pits and depressions with color-matched grout, hand-troweling smooth, working around furniture and barricades on a night/weekend schedule.

Precast/fabrication shop work: grouting and hand-troweling ground precast terrazzo panels, stair treads, window sills and cabinet-fixture tops on benches or carts before shipment, then re-grinding and polishing.

sources.title: Gravity B480 – Cartesian robot for the resin automatic application
sources.claim: Pedrini's Gravity B480 is a commercial three-axis Cartesian robot in stone resining lines that senses each slab's size and shape, computes a tool path, and automatically spreads two-component epoxy filler over the slab surface using a rotating head with inclined spatulas or an idler roller.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: filling the surface voids/fissures of stone and engineered-stone slabs with a viscous filler spread by spatulas. It transfers to filling slight grinding depressions in terrazzo with matching grout: the same class of substrate (cement/resin-bound stone composite), the same viscous paste worked flush across the surface with trowel-like spatulas, and the same acceptance criterion (voids filled, no excess left) — performed on fixtured slabs in a purpose-built line.

sources.title: How does marble resining work? Technologies and solutions
sources.claim: Pedrini Resinline plants run the resining sequence — load, dry/preheat, uniform epoxy application over the slab surface, catalysis/hardening, unload — as an automated line at 6 to 60 cycles per hour, healing and filling the treated stone.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (factory void-filling of stone slabs); it establishes that the fill step is executed as an automated production cycle rather than a one-off demo, which is what the E1 counterfactual (work brought to the machine) requires.

sources.system: MosCut automatic stone slab polishing line
sources.title: Automatic Stone Slab Polishing Line For Marble Granite Quartz
sources.claim: Automatic multi-head slab polishing lines follow the factory pore-filling step and level the cement/resin filler flush with the stone, producing the uniform finished surface.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine leveling of a filler applied to fill surface voids in stone. It supplies the second half of the terrazzo grouting task — troweling/levelling the grout flush so the surface reads smooth and uniform — in the same fixtured, conveyor-fed setting.

sources.system: DINOSAW TBMJ-1200/DBMJ-2000 multi-head automatic polishing machine
sources.title: Multi-head Automatic Marble & Granite Polishing Machine
sources.claim: Fully automated multi-head slab polishing machines with PLC control and laser scanning of the slab profile are sold for production lines that process terrazzo and engineered-stone slabs, not only natural stone.
sources.transferJustification: Confirms that the fixtured, automated fill-and-polish line handles terrazzo/agglomerate slabs specifically, so the transfer from stone-slab resining to precast terrazzo grouting is not a leap across materials.

sources.title: More Contractors See Benefits of Drywall Finishing Robot (ENR, reposted by Canvas)
sources.claim: Canvas's drywall finishing robot works semi-autonomously on real construction sites applying finishing compound and sanding to a Level 5 uniform finish, but workers handle the complex geometries and come behind it for final touch-ups; it works walls and ceilings, not floor grouting.
sources.transferJustification: Closest in-situ analog (apply a filler compound to a surface and smooth it to a uniform finish on a jobsite). It does not substantiate the terrazzo instances: it operates on vertical gypsum board, leaves complex geometries and final touch-ups to workers, and no floor-grouting version exists.

sources.title: True Autonomy: Introducing autonomy in concrete floor polishing
sources.claim: True Autonomy's ACP-100 retrofits a concrete floor polishing machine for autonomous navigation and operation on flooring jobs, while the hand grinding, caulking and edge work is still done by people in parallel.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the boundary of in-situ floor automation: open-field grinding/polishing is automated, but material-application and hand finishing on the floor remain human. Supports the negative E2/E3 judgments rather than any positive one.

tasks.label: Clean installation site, mixing and storage areas, tools, machines, and equipment, and store materials and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Final floor clean-down of a freshly poured/ground terrazzo area inside a building under construction: after the grinder passes, the finisher vacuums/wet-vacuums and rinses and squeegees the large open slab area so the surface is left clean for the next step. Mostly open, cleared floor; layout differs building to building.

Debris cleanup of the installation site: sweeping up chips, broken divider strip, sacks and packaging, scraping splattered mortar off adjacent walls, bases and door frames, pulling up masking/protection sheeting, bagging waste and carting it out to the dumpster.

Washing out the mixing area at the end of a pour: hosing and scraping the mortar mixer drum, buckets, hoppers, trowels, floats and hoses before the cementitious material sets, and dumping the wash water/slurry into the containment or washout bin on the jobsite.

Servicing machines after the shift: emptying the dust extractor bag and the grinder's slurry/water tank, changing worn abrasive/polishing discs and stones, wiping down and hosing off the grinder body, coiling cords and checking water lines.

Moving and storing materials and equipment: stacking bags of cement/marble chips and pails of epoxy and chips on pallets or in the site storage room, and loading grinders, vacuums, hoses and hand tools into the truck or gang box at end of shift.

Cleanup in the company shop or precast terrazzo fabrication plant/yard: sweeping and scrubbing the shop floor, cleaning molds and the mixing station, and putting raw materials back on the storage racks. Fixed layout, controlled by the employer.

sources.title: Premier Tech AR-200 Series Robotic Bag Palletizer
sources.claim: Premier Tech supplies standard robotic bag palletizing cells (AR-200 series) built around FANUC robots for stacking bagged product; such cells are used in dry-mix cement/concrete product plants.

sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch robot is in commercial service with DHL autonomously unloading cases from trailers and containers in warehouses, identifying boxes without pre-programming and handling mixed stacks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous handling and stowing of heavy uniform cases inside a structured facility. Shows the current E2 ceiling — uniform boxes presented in a trailer — not mixed tools, hoses and machines.

sources.title: Sandpaper changing station - FerRobotics
sources.claim: FerRobotics supplies an automated abrasive changing station that removes a used sanding/grinding disc and fits a new one from a magazine, enabling 24/7 robotic grinding cells without operator intervention.

sources.title: AI Robots Enter Construction Sites to Haul Materials, Build - Seoul Economic Daily

tasks.label: Sprinkle colored marble or stone chips, powdered steel, or coloring powder over surface to produce prescribed finish.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large open floor area (school corridor, airport concourse, lobby) in a building under construction: after the cementitious terrazzo topping is placed and screeded, the finisher broadcasts marble/stone chips by hand or shovel over the wet topping, judging coverage by eye, adding chips to bare spots, then rolling/troweling them in before set. Dust, other trades, changing light, panels bounded by divider strips.

Detail and small-field work on site: seeding chips into stair treads and risers, landings, cove base, curbs, thresholds, base of cabinet fixtures and countertops, and small fields of different chip colors between divider strips; worker kneels or reaches, sprinkles by hand from a bucket, feathers to strip edges, and matches the prescribed chip blend for each field.

Dry-shake application on a freshly floated concrete slab in a warehouse/industrial building under construction: broadcasting metallic (powdered steel) hardener or colored shake in two passes at a prescribed lb/ft2 rate, timed to the slab's set, working off the wet surface or a wheeled spreader, then floating/troweling the powder into the surface.

Precast/fabrication shop of a terrazzo contractor: sprinkling chips or coloring powder onto terrazzo mixes in molds for treads, base, sills, tiles and panels laid out on casting benches or the shop floor; controlled indoor conditions, standard molds, repeated batches.

Restoration/patch work in an occupied building (hospital lobby, school, courthouse): after grinding out a damaged spot or filling a crack, sprinkling matching marble chips and coloring powder into the fresh patch material to blend with the surrounding historic floor, working around barricades and passing occupants.

tasks.label: Wet surface to prepare for bonding, fill holes and cracks with grout or slurry, and smooth with a trowel.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial construction (school, hospital, airport, retail): preparing a large open concrete substrate before the terrazzo underbed/topping - hosing/wetting the slab to a damp bonding condition, filling bugholes, spalls and shrinkage cracks with cement slurry or patching mortar, and troweling the patches flush; slab is dusty, cluttered with other trades' materials, and the defect pattern varies from bay to bay.

Grout coat after the first grind on a large poured-in-place cementitious terrazzo floor: washing/wetting the ground surface, spreading matching pigmented cement grout slurry over the whole area, working it into pinholes and voids and squeegeeing/troweling it smooth, in an active building under construction.

Flat but small/awkward pieces of the same work - stair treads, landings, flat cove-base strips, thresholds: wetting, packing holes and cracks with slurry, troweling smooth, largely kneeling hand work.

Three-dimensional detail work - risers, nosings, inside/outside corners, curbs, edges at columns, drains and door bucks: forcing slurry into voids and cracks and hand-troweling smooth in confined, non-planar geometry.

Renovation/repair in an existing building (school, hospital, store) partly in use: patching cracks, holes and delaminated spots in existing terrazzo or its substrate with grout/slurry and feathering smooth with a trowel before regrinding and re-grouting; damage location and extent taken as found, working around furniture and occupants.

Shop fabrication of precast terrazzo (stair treads, base, sills, panels): filling casting voids and pinholes in cured pieces with matching cement or epoxy slurry and troweling smooth on a bench or line before grinding and polishing.

Objects, material rheology and flatness standard are comparable, and the line is a purpose-built setting with the slab conveyed and fixtured.

tasks.label: Mix cement, sand, and water to produce concrete, grout, or slurry, using hoe, trowel, tamper, scraper, or concrete-mixing machine.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial building under construction (school, terminal, hospital): the finisher batches sand-cement underbed/screed mortar in a portable drum or mortar mixer staged near the pour, dumping bagged cement and sand, hosing in water, judging consistency by eye/hoe, and dumping into wheelbarrows or buggies for the placing crew. Dust, cords and hoses, other trades working around the mixer.

Same job site: mixing the cementitious terrazzo topping matrix - portland cement, pigment, water and marble chips to a color-matched recipe - batch after batch in a mixer, and delivering uniform, color-consistent batches to panels bounded by divider strips.

Grouting and patching batches: after grinding, mixing small quantities of neat cement/pigment grout slurry or patching mortar in a 5-gallon bucket or wheelbarrow with a hoe, trowel or paddle mixer, inside a partly finished interior with limited water access, and re-tempering to a workable consistency.

Small residential or restoration jobs (private home, small remodel, stair/cove repair): hand-mixing a few gallons of cement slurry, grout or patch material in a bucket or on a mortar board in a driveway or occupied room, hauling water, and cleaning tools.

Precast terrazzo/fabrication shop: batching cement, sand or chips, pigment and water in shop mixers to standard recipes for casting stair treads, bases and panels into molds; fixed layout, stored materials, company-controlled premises.

sources.title: Robots Building Neighborhoods: Inside the Technology Transforming Construction at Wolf Ranch in Texas

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated on-site production of a portland-cement mortar for 3D printing. It substantiates machine mixing of cementitious material with water to a controlled consistency, on a construction site taken as found, which is the output the terrazzo finisher's mixing produces; the material class (portland-cement mortar) and the consistency judgment are comparable.

sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the Wolf Ranch item: it documents automatic proportioning of water/additives into a cementitious mix in the field rather than in a plant.

sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the on-site automated mixing hardware is in sustained commercial deployment, not a one-off demonstration.

tasks.label: Chip, scrape, or grind high spots, ridges, or rough projections to finish concrete, using pneumatic chisel, hand chisel, or other hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial construction site: after the slab has cured, the finisher chips and scrapes concrete splatter, form ridges, fins and rough projections off the slab surface and off adjacent surfaces (curbs, walls, embeds, divider strips) with hand chisel, scraper and chipping hammer, so the terrazzo underbed can be placed. Dust, debris, other trades working nearby.

New-construction jobsite, room- or bay-sized floor area: knocking down localized high spots and ridges across an open cured concrete substrate with a pneumatic chipping hammer and hand-held grinder until the substrate is within flatness tolerance for the topping. Open, largely cleared floor.

Tight and detail areas on the same jobsites: chipping and grinding projections and ridges at slab edges, inside corners, stair treads and risers, door thresholds, column bases and around pipe penetrations, where machines cannot reach; hand and pneumatic chisel, small angle grinder, kneeling/awkward postures.

Renovation in an occupied institutional or industrial facility (school gym, lab, hospital wing, retail store, plant): re-grinding an existing cured concrete floor area to remove high spots and old ridges before a patch or new topping, worked off-hours in a cleared, institution-controlled room.

Same occupied-facility renovation, detail portion: localized chipping and grinding of individual high spots, old adhesive ridges and projections around thresholds, stair nosings, wall bases and floor fixtures, done by hand around furniture, partitions and building services.

Precast/terrazzo fabrication shop: chipping and grinding fins, rough projections and high spots off cast terrazzo and concrete units (stair treads, bases, wall panels, sills) at a bench or on a stand before they are polished and shipped.

tasks.label: Mold expansion joints and edges, using edging tools, jointers, or straightedges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial interior (school, hospital, airport under construction): after the cement/sand underbed or slab is placed, the finisher strikes it off with a straightedge and tools the perimeter arrises with an edger along walls, columns, doorways and floor drains, working to the concrete's set window on an active site with other trades, debris and changing layout.

Large open floor areas in new construction: forming expansion/control joints at prescribed spacing in the fresh cementitious bed with a hand or walking jointer/groover run against a straightedge, aligning the grooves with substrate joints and with the lines of the terrazzo divider strips.

In-place details: stair treads, risers and landings, cove base, curbs, thresholds and cabinet fixtures/window sills, where edges and joints must be molded on inclined, vertical and small-radius work in confined stairwells and rooms.

Precast terrazzo shop/plant: casting units (treads, risers, base, sills, panels) in molds, striking off with a straightedge, and forming/finishing the edges, nosings and joint profiles of each unit on a fixed production layout indoors.

Repair, patching and restoration in an occupied facility (school corridor, airport concourse, hospital lobby): re-forming the edges around a patch in the existing terrazzo and re-cutting/reworking failed expansion joints in a floor already in service, around furniture and public traffic.

tasks.label: Move terrazzo installation materials, tools, machines, or work devices to work areas, manually or using wheelbarrow.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bulk material haul on an active jobsite: pallets/bundles of cement, sand and marble chips (50–100 lb bags), pails of epoxy resin and hardener, boxes of divider strips arrive by truck at a curb or laydown area; the finisher unloads them and moves them by hand truck, pallet jack or wheelbarrow across an unfinished slab, up ramps or via the construction hoist/elevator, to the floor and room where terrazzo will be placed.

Repeated wheelbarrow runs of freshly mixed material (sand-cement underbed, cement terrazzo topping, or epoxy resin blended with chips) from the mixing station to the pour area, dumping each load at the placement point on a time-critical cycle before the mix stiffens, on a floor with hoses, screeds and strips already set.

Moving heavy equipment into the work area: planetary grinders/polishers (200–1,000 lb), mortar mixers, dust vacuums, generators, hose reels and water tanks — unloaded from truck by ramp or liftgate, wheeled through doorways and around obstructions, taken up or down stairs or into hoists/elevators, and set in position in the room.

Frequent short trips within and around the work zone: buckets of water and grout, trowels and hand tools, hoses and power cords, edging and divider strips, sacks of chips, kneeling boards, plastic sheeting and tarps — staged around a partially finished floor and returned to the van at tear-down.

Renovation or repair job in an occupied institutional/commercial building (school, hospital, airport, mall) with protected corridors and elevators: materials and tools are carried from a parked van through finished corridors and elevators to a small work area, keeping paths clean and protected.

Terrazzo material moving is the same fetch-and-deliver operation with comparable loads (palletized bags, pails, crated machines) and no precision placement requirement, so performance carries over within a structured facility.
