sources.system: Tecwill flying bucket concrete delivery system
sources.title: Concrete mixing plants for precast factories | Tecwill
sources.claim: Tecwill's fully automatic rail-guided flying-bucket system carries fresh concrete from the batching/mixing plant to multiple casting points in a precast factory and discharges it there without an operator driving it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving a batch of freshly mixed cementitious material from the mixer discharge to the placement point and dumping it. This is the wheelbarrow run itself, performed in a purpose-built rail-and-fixture setting (E1), with the same material and same start/end points.

sources.title: Shimizu Begins Collaborating People and Autonomous Robots at Construction Site, Toranomon-Azabudai Project
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Carrier autonomously picks up palletized materials on a building construction site, rides freight elevators by itself, avoids people and obstacles, and transports pallets to designated locations on the working floor; five units were fielded on the Toranomon-Azabudai high-rise project.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: horizontal and vertical transport of palletized building materials on an active construction site. It is the closest E3 analogue to hauling terrazzo materials, but is limited to palletized unit loads on prepared routes on a mega-project, not truck unloading, loose bags, buckets, hoses or machines placed at the point of use.

sources.system: FANUC LR Mate machine tending cell
sources.title: Machine Tending Robots | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC machine-tending robots commercially load and unload parts between fixtured positions and machine tools in fenced industrial cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repetitive pick-and-place transfer of objects presented in known, fixtured positions to defined destinations. At E1 the terrazzo instance reduces to exactly this — items presented in fixed positions and moved to a fixed drop point.

sources.title: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid passes 100,000-tote milestone in live GXO implementation
sources.claim: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid has moved more than 100,000 ... a GXO Logistics warehouse, picking totes on and off ... conveyors and stacking containers at floor locations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting and carrying rigid containers between floor locations, conveyors and robots inside a warehouse. Shows container-scale (up to ~16 kg) loose-load handling in a structured human facility, but not assorted loose tools, hoses or bagged goods.

tasks.label: Clean chipped area, using wire brush, and feel and observe surface to determine if it is rough or uneven.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial/institutional construction: after the poured-in-place terrazzo topping is rough-ground, the finisher works across the floor locating pits, voids and chipped spots, scrubs each one out with a hand wire brush to remove dust and loose particles, then runs a bare hand over it and eyes it to decide whether it is still rough or uneven before grout is applied. Active jobsite with dust, slurry, other trades and site-specific layout.

Same new-construction jobs but on stairs, stair nosings, cove base, curbs, thresholds and terrazzo cabinet/fixture edges: tight, vertical and angled geometry reached by kneeling or crouching; chipped edges and corners cleaned with a small hand wire brush and judged by fingertip feel for roughness and lippage before patching.

Repair/restoration of damaged terrazzo in an existing occupied building (school corridor, hospital lobby, airport, courthouse): the spalled area is chipped out, wire-brushed clean of dust and loose aggregate, and felt and observed to confirm the cavity is sound and not rough or uneven before matching patch material goes in. Barricaded work zone inside a facility with fixed layout but surrounding furniture, fixtures and traffic.

Precast terrazzo fabrication shop: cast units (stair treads, wall base, sills, cabinet tops) stripped from molds onto benches or carts; the finisher wire-brushes chipped corners, bug holes and void areas, then feels and inspects the surface to decide whether it is rough or uneven and needs more grouting or grinding before shipment.

Small private job: chipped terrazzo floor or stair in a private home or small storefront; the worker cleans the chipped area with a wire brush amid furniture, unknown substrate condition and poor lighting, with no controlled work zone, then feels and looks to judge roughness before patching.

sources.system: 3M Finesse-it Robotic Paint Repair System (FANUC M-710iC/70 robots, Inovision SMARTInspect)
sources.developer: 3M / Inovision / FANUC America, deployed by General Motors
sources.title: General Motors and 3M Partner on New Robotic Paint System | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: 3M's Finesse-it robotic paint repair ..., installed on GM's moving assembly line at Spring Hill, TN, autonomously finds and classifies surface imperfections with a vision system and then sands and polishes each localized defect using FANUC robots carrying abrasive end effectors, adjusting trajectories in real time on contact.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: localized surface-defect repair. It couples autonomous detection of small (>0.2 mm) surface imperfections with abrasive work confined to the defect area and verification of the result - the same find, abrade and judge loop the terrazzo finisher performs on a chipped spot, though on paint rather than cementitious matrix.

sources.title: Scan&Sand in high-quality, complex, skilled sanding and finishing operations (Zivid application story)
sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics' Scan&Sand cells autonomously scan an arbitrary part with a robot-mounted 3D camera, plan their own toolpaths without CAD models, and sand contoured surfaces to roughly millimetre or sub-millimetre tolerances; sold commercially and installed at manufacturers such as BetterWay Products.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: skilled abrasive surface finishing of a fixtured workpiece. It shows a cell can perceive an as-found surface, target abrasive action to it and hold fine surface tolerances, which is the perception-plus-abrasion core of cleaning and checking a chipped terrazzo area presented on a fixture.

sources.system: MESH Automation robotic deflashing and deburring cells (wire-brush spindles with force control)
sources.title: Robotic Deflashing and Deburring | Robotic Machining | MESH Automation, Inc.
sources.claim: Commercial robotic finishing integrators build production cells in which robots hold wire brushes and buffing pads on spindles with automatic tool changing and apply uniform controlled force to deflash and deburr cast metal and plastic parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic wire-brushing of hard workpieces to remove flash and adhering debris. Same tool and same abrasive cleaning action as the terrazzo finisher applies to a chipped area, executed under force control on a fixtured part.

sources.title: R-Series Automated Inspection | 3D Scanners for Quality Control
sources.claim: Robot-mounted optical CMM scanners are commercially installed for automated at-line inspection of part surfaces on production floors, supplying the surface-deviation data a cell needs to accept or reject a finish.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated surface and geometry inspection of a fixtured workpiece. It substantiates the 'observe the surface to determine if it is rough or uneven' half of the task inside a cell, replacing the finisher's eye-and-hand check with scanned deviation data.

sources.system: Vollert automatic pallet cleaner (rotary brushes and steel scraper unit)
sources.title: The Oschatz concrete plant relies on robot technology | Vollert
sources.claim: Precast concrete circulation plants include automatic pallet cleaners that drive rotating roller brushes and a ... across the surface to strip adhering hardened concrete residue, with the cleaning cycle triggered automatically as the pallet enters the zone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine brush-cleaning of hardened cementitious residue in a purpose-built line. It shows brush cleaning of concrete-type material is routinely automated where the work is conveyed to the machine, supporting the cleaning step at E1.

sources.system: Okibo EG7 / EG7+ autonomous plastering, sanding and painting robot
sources.title: Okibo launches autonomous, AI-guided painting and drywall finishing EG7+ robot - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7/EG7+ is a fully autonomous construction-site finishing robot that navigates interior jobsites using AI-guided 3D scanning and performs plastering, sanding and painting of walls up to 24 feet; its work is broad gypsum and plaster wall planes, not localized chip-outs in cured terrazzo floors or stairs.
sources.transferJustification: Closest jobsite analogue (autonomous abrasive surface finishing in an unstructured construction setting), but it treats large flat gypsum/plaster planes with a sanding head; no evidence it locates centimetre-scale chip-outs in cured terrazzo, brushes them clean, or renders a rough/uneven verdict, so it does not substantiate this task at E3 or E2.

sources.system: ACP-100 autonomous concrete polishing robot (LightWare SF40/C lidar)
sources.title: True Autonomy: Introducing autonomy in concrete floor polishing | LightWare LiDAR
sources.claim: The autonomous concrete floor polishing robot ACP-100 self-navigates a floor polishing job with lidar while the more difficult hand grinding, ... work is still done in parallel by human contractors.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest in-situ floor-surfacing robot. It automates bulk area polishing only, and the vendor itself assigns detail hand grinding and cleaning to people - evidence that in-situ chipped-area cleaning and judging is not automated at E2 or E3.

tasks.label: Repair concrete by cutting out damaged areas, drilling holes for reinforcing rods, and positioning reinforcing rods, using power saw and drill.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Prepping a spalled/cracked area of an interior concrete floor slab in a commercial building under construction or renovation (school, hospital, airport, courthouse) before a terrazzo topping: sound out the unsound area, saw-cut a clean perimeter with a handheld cut-off or walk-behind saw, chip and remove the damaged concrete, drill dowel holes into the sound slab edges with a rotary hammer, epoxy and set short rebar dowels. Active site with other trades, debris, cords, dust control.

Repairing damaged concrete stairs before terrazzo: cutting out crumbled tread nosings, riser faces and landing edges in a confined stairwell, drilling horizontal/angled holes into risers and stringers, positioning reinforcing pins/dowels. Awkward postures, varied stair geometry, work above and below the worker.

Localized patch in an occupied institutional building (hospital corridor, school lobby, mall concourse) with the work area barricaded by the facility: small saw-cut square, break out the deteriorated concrete, drill a few dowel holes, set pins, keep dust and noise controlled and the floor safe for occupants each shift.

Cutting out and repairing damaged substrate at edges and around obstructions - curbs, cabinet and casework bases, thresholds, floor drains, column bases, pipe penetrations - where the saw cut must be made to an irregular line by hand, holes drilled close to embedded items, and rods positioned to tie the patch to existing work.

Larger deteriorated area on an exterior or heavy-duty slab (plaza deck, exterior stair landing, parking or mechanical-room slab): saw-cut and remove a sizeable damaged section down to or past existing reinforcement, drill into surrounding sound concrete, position reinforcing rods/dowel mats before repair concrete is placed. Outdoor weather, larger equipment.

sources.system: Schindler RISE (ABB IRB 2600-based robotic installation system)
sources.title: Autonomous drilling robot debut | News center | ABB
sources.claim: Schindler's RISE robot (built on an ABB IRB 2600 industrial arm) autonomously drills holes in concrete elevator-shaft walls and installs anchor bolts to a pre-uploaded digital layout, working unattended in the shaft.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: post-installed anchor setting in structural concrete. It is the same physical operation as this task's second and third steps - percussion-drilling holes of controlled depth in concrete and seating a steel rod/bolt in the hole to a load-bearing standard.

sources.title: Schindler expands RISE robot fleet as automated elevator installation demand grows
sources.claim: Schindler reports the shaft robot operates autonomously from a digital work plan, drilling precise holes and installing anchor bolts at programmed positions, and is expanding its global installed fleet.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (drill-and-set anchors in structural concrete), showing sustained production-quality output on real projects rather than a one-off demo.

sources.developer: DEWALT (Stanley Black & Decker) with August Robotics
sources.title: DEWALT Unveils the World's First Downward Drilling, Fleet-Capable Robot to Accelerate Data Center Construction
sources.claim: The DEWALT / August Robotics 'DALE' autonomous robot navigates a concrete floor slab and drills downward anchor holes from an uploaded CAD layout with dust extraction; over 90,000 holes across ten data-center projects at 99.97% location/depth accuracy, commercially released in 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drilling anchor holes downward into concrete floor slabs. Same substrate, comparable hole diameters and depths, and the same positional accuracy requirement as drilling dowel holes for reinforcing rods in a floor repair.

sources.title: Hydrodemolition Equipment | Conjet
sources.claim: Conjet ACR hydrodemolition robots selectively remove deteriorated concrete from structures (bridge and parking decks, dams) to a set boundary, width and depth; the operator programs parameters and positions the machine, after which it removes the damaged concrete autonomously under supervision from a distance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: selective machine removal of damaged concrete for repair. It delivers the same output as saw-cutting and chipping out a damaged area - a bounded, sound, clean repair cavity with reinforcement exposed - by machine rather than by hand tool.

sources.title: The AQUA CUTTER family - Aquajet
sources.claim: Aquajet Aqua Cutter hydrodemolition robots are programmed machines used for concrete removal in renovation and bridge/road repair, cleaning and descaling exposed rebar in the process.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine removal of damaged concrete in repair work, including around and behind existing reinforcing steel - the removal half of this task, at comparable scale and boundary precision.

sources.title: Hilti Jaibot BIM-enabled Construction Jobsite Robot | For Construction Pros
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a commercially sold semi-autonomous mobile drilling robot that drills dust-controlled holes in concrete ceilings and walls on live construction sites from BIM coordinates, with the operator positioning it and the machine executing the drilling automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: layout-driven drilling of holes in structural concrete on a jobsite. Demonstrates machine drilling in concrete to programmed positions and depths (the drilling step of this task), though the operator repositions the base between zones.

sources.system: Robotic rebar insertion and grouting system for 3D-printed concrete
sources.developer: Academic research group (published via ScienceDirect / Additive Manufacturing)
sources.title: Robotic rebar insertion and grouting for reinforcement of 3D printed concrete: Technique development and bond behavior characterization
sources.claim: A laboratory robotic system (mobile base, 6-axis arm, force/torque sensor and gripper) picks and inserts steel reinforcing bars into concrete using self-calibrating surface detection and force-controlled insertion, with grouting and bond characterization.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic placement of steel reinforcing bars into concrete with force feedback and grouting - the 'positioning reinforcing rods' step, with the same objects and comparable insertion tolerances, shown in a fixtured cell.

tasks.label: Precast terrazzo blocks in wooden forms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Precast terrazzo shop, production run of standard rectilinear units (straight cove base, stair treads/risers, window sills, thresholds) in reusable wooden forms: set and oil forms on casting tables, place reinforcement/anchors, batch and place single-color cement/marble-chip mix, vibrate and screed, cure, strip forms, then grind, patch and polish to accepted finish.

Precast shop, custom/architectural one-off pieces (curved bases, benches, vanity tops, logo or multi-color inlay panels): wooden forms built from shop drawings for the specific piece, zinc/brass divider strips laid to a pattern, two or more colored mixes hand-placed field by field, consolidated, cured, stripped, ground, grouted and polished.

Shop/plant production of repetitive terrazzo tile, slab and wall-panel stock in gang forms: identical cavities filled with the same chip mix, machine-consolidated, cured on racks, demolded and run through grinding/polishing to a standard finish.

Shop casting of match/repair or replacement pieces from field measurements: a bespoke wooden form built to an existing profile, chip blend and pigment matched by eye to the installed work, one or a few units cast, cured, stripped and finished to blend with the original.

Jobsite casting in wooden forms at an active construction site: forms built and braced on site for thresholds, curbs, stair nosings or short base runs, mix hauled and placed by hand amid other trades, dust, weather and changing access; units stripped and ground on site.

sources.system: Shuttering / deshuttering robots in pallet-circulation precast plants (state-of-practice survey)
sources.developer: Reichenbach & Kromoser (survey of Progress/Weckenmann-class plant equipment), Journal of Building Engineering
sources.title: State of Practice of Automation in Precast Concrete Production
sources.claim: Automated precast concrete plants use shuttering robots that select and position formwork shutters on the mould surface from CAD data, and deshuttering robots that scan the mould and remove the shutters automatically, after which mould and shuttering are automatically cleaned.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: forming and casting precast concrete elements. Terrazzo precast is cement plus marble chips cast in a form of the same size class and dimensional tolerance, so form setting, casting and stripping transfer directly; only the aggregate blend differs.

sources.system: Form Master shuttering and deshuttering robot
sources.title: Swabian company of long-standing tradition gears up for the future (BFT International 04/2017)
sources.claim: A named shuttering and deshuttering robot (Form Master, Progress Maschinen & Automation) was supplied and put into service in a working precast plant's carousel line at Gebr. Kaltenbach, Dornstetten.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated formwork setting and stripping for precast concrete units. The wooden form of a terrazzo shop plays the same role as the shutter set here — defining a cavity of set dimensions — so form set-up and stripping carry over.

sources.system: UniControl / UniCAM automated pallet-circulation precast plants
sources.title: Software and automation for precast concrete plants
sources.claim: Commercial precast plant automation covers the whole casting cycle — mould cleaning, shuttering, reinforcement, concreting, compaction, hardening (curing), smoothing and lifting — with these stations able to run fully automatically using shuttering robots and concrete spreaders.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated production of precast concrete elements from empty mould to demoulded unit. The step sequence is the same one a terrazzo precaster performs (oil form, place mix, vibrate, cure, strip); the material is a cementitious aggregate mix in both cases.

sources.system: Weckenmann/Vollert pallet circulation plant (installed plant inventory)
sources.title: Double wall production Archives - Precastplants.com
sources.claim: A real, installed pallet-circulation plant (Weckenmann/Vollert equipment) is documented with a fully automatic shuttering robot with ..., automatic concrete spreader, cleaning and release-oil station, vibration station and automatic curing chamber storage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated mould preparation, filling and compaction of cementitious mixes in a precast plant — the same physical operations (release agent, filling, vibration, curing) required to cast a terrazzo unit in a form.

sources.system: HFT300 automatic terrazzo tile making machine / production line
sources.title: Hongfa automatic hydraulic press terrazzo tile cement floor tiles making machines
sources.claim: Automatic hydraulic-press terrazzo tile production lines cast cement/marble-chip terrazzo tiles in interchangeable moulds under PLC control, producing double-layer tiles (colored terrazzo face over a concrete backing) at several pieces per minute.

sources.system: SIMEC calibrating/polishing lines and BORDI T804/T604 edge-polishing machines
sources.title: SIMEC - CALIBRATING / POLISHING
sources.claim: Completely automatic calibrating, polishing and edge-polishing machines are sold for agglomerated marble (terrazzo) slabs and step/tread profiles, giving the ground and polished finish required of a demolded precast terrazzo unit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine grinding and polishing of agglomerated marble (cement/resin plus marble chips) — physically the same material and finish operation as grinding and polishing a demolded precast terrazzo unit.

sources.title: This Robot Could Build Zaha Hadid Architects' Next Project
sources.claim: Robotic hot-wire cutting cells produce complex, doubly curved moulds for concrete casting, showing that bespoke mould fabrication can be automated in a factory cell (in expanded polystyrene rather than wood).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fabrication of one-off concrete moulds. It bears on the custom-piece instance, but it produces foam moulds only and does not cover divider-strip layout or multi-color terrazzo placement.

tasks.label: Wet concrete surface and rub with stone to smooth surface and obtain specified finish.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: After forms are stripped on a commercial jobsite, the finisher wets cast-in-place concrete walls, columns, beams, exposed foundations and curbs with a brush/hose and rubs them with a carborundum rubbing stone (sometimes with a slurry of cement paste) to knock down fins and form marks and produce a uniform rubbed finish; work is overhead/at height on ladders or scaffold, amid other trades, layout differing site to site.

Following machine grinding of a cast-in-place terrazzo or concrete floor in a building interior under construction, the worker wets and hand-stones the perimeter strip, corners, borders, divider-strip lines, and areas around columns, drains and door jambs that the walk-behind grinder cannot reach, kneeling and working small irregular areas to match the field finish.

Wetting and rubbing terrazzo or concrete stair treads, risers, nosings, landings and cove base in a jobsite stairwell with hand stones and small edge tools until the specified smooth finish is obtained; confined, sloped, stepped geometry with limited light and access.

Wet field honing of a newly cast terrazzo or concrete floor area in a large open interior (school corridor, lobby, warehouse, garage deck) under construction: repeated passes of a stone/abrasive-equipped grinder over the open slab, progressively finer grits, slurry or dust handled, to reach the specified surface.

Shop/bench work in a precast terrazzo, cast-stone or fabrication plant: wetting and rubbing/honing precast units — treads, sills, window stools, curbs, cabinet-fixture tops and small panels — on stands or a bench to the specified finish before shipment or installation.

sources.system: ABB robot + FerRobotics Active Angular Kit AAK 617 Concrete (accell integration) at STS Fertigteile
sources.title: Automated scanning grinding precast concrete Active Angular Kit end effector AAK 601 Concrete - FerRobotics
sources.claim: At precast maker STS Fertigteile, an ABB robot with a FerRobotics force-controlled angle-grinder end effector scans and grinds hardened precast concrete parts aceclad stairs, balconies and panels loaded on a traversing table, producing specified grinding patterns/anti-slip classes fully automatically in daily production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic abrasive grinding of hardened concrete surfaces (fair-faced precast panels, stairs) to a specified surface class. It is the same physical operation as the terrazzo finisher's stone rubbing — abrading a cementitious surface with a bonded abrasive under controlled contact force until a specified smooth/anti-slip finish is reached — on the same material and geometries (flat faces, stair treads, edges); only the dust-control method differs (suction hood instead of water).

sources.title: Automated scanning grinding precast concrete Active Angular Kit end effector AAK 601 Concrete - FerRobotics
sources.claim: The same installation performs the scanning-and-grinding sequence fully automatically and reaches edges and corners of the concrete part with constant contact force.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above; this item specifically substantiates that the robotic cell can finish edges and corners of a fixtured concrete workpiece, which is the part of stone-rubbing that mobile floor robots leave to hand labor.

sources.developer: Shenzhen Legend Robot Technology Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Automated Floor grinding & dust collection robot (Floor Grinding Robot)
sources.claim: A commercially sold mobile floor grinding robot performs autonomous path-planned grinding and dust collection over concrete/hardener/epoxy floors in garages, factory workshops and other project interiors, with one operator supervising rather than driving the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine honing/grinding of a cementitious floor slab to a specified surface. It matches the field portion of this task — repeated abrasive passes over an open floor to obtain a uniform specified finish — on the same material, at the same scale, in the same jobsite interiors.

sources.system: Automatic Floor Grinding Robot (High Precision Flooring R&D team)
sources.developer: Hong Kong Center of Construction Robotics (exhibited via CIC CITAC)
sources.title: CITAC - Automatic Floor Grinding Robot
sources.claim: An automatic floor grinding robot exhibited by Hong Kong's construction industry technology centre plans its own path in the work area and adjusts the grinding disc to hold the finished floor's elevation and flatness without human intervention during operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous abrasive grinding of a concrete floor to a controlled finished surface; the output criterion (flatness/finish of the ground floor) is the same criterion the finisher's stone rubbing must meet on floor areas.

sources.system: Floor grinding robot / basement glazing robot (Bright Dream Robotics, Guangdong Bojiatuo)
sources.developer: Bright Dream Robotics / Guangdong Bojiatuo Construction Technology
sources.title: Application and Development of Autonomous Robots in Concrete Construction: Challenges and Opportunities (Encyclopedia mirror)
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed review of concrete-construction robots describes a deployed floor grinding robot (Guangdong Bojiatuo / Bright Dream Robotics) that carries a water tank and removes floating slurry from hardened concrete floors in underground garages and indoor workshops, and notes that a companion floor-finishing robot following a pre-programmed path cannot work at wall edges, which must be done manually.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wet mechanical grinding of hardened concrete floor surfaces on Chinese jobsites; it substantiates both machine capability on open floor areas (water-fed grinding of slurry from the slab) and the documented limitation at wall edges that keeps perimeter stone work manual.

sources.developer: True Autonomy LLC (with LightWare SF40/C LiDAR)
sources.title: True Autonomy: Introducing autonomy in concrete floor polishing (LightWare LiDAR)
sources.claim: A US retrofit kit makes existing concrete floor polishing machines navigate and polish a building's floor autonomously, while contractors continue to perform the hand grinding and detail work in parallel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous multi-pass abrasive polishing of a concrete floor with progressively finer abrasives, i.e. the machine-borne version of this task's floor work; it also documents that the hand-grinding portion remains human.

sources.system: Floor grinding robot (Chinese construction robot line resold by ProBuild Robotics)
sources.developer: ProBuild Robotics (supplier of Chinese construction robots)
sources.title: Automated Concrete Floor Leveling Robots for High-Precision Construction – ProBuild Robotics
sources.claim: A construction-robot supplier's floor grinding robot is offered for fully automatic grinding of stone and terrazzo floors as well as cured, epoxy and corundum floors in garages, factories and outdoor floors, using a high-power grinding head with automatic navigation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic abrasive grinding of terrazzo and stone floors — the identical material and finish objective as the terrazzo finisher's floor grinding/stoning, establishing that the mobile floor robots are marketed and configured for terrazzo, not only industrial slabs.

tasks.label: Build wooden molds, clamping molds around areas to be repaired, or setting up frames to the proper depth and alignment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New cast-in-place terrazzo job on an active commercial construction site (school, airport, hospital under construction): worker measures the area, cuts dimensional lumber and plywood, and builds wooden forms/molds for curbs, stair treads and risers, cove bases and pour edges, nailing and bracing them to fit as-built conditions.

Setting up screed frames, edge/depth gauges and divider-strip alignment over a prepared slab in a building under construction: frames set to the finished-floor depth, checked with laser/string line and shimmed to grade over an uneven substrate, then anchored before the terrazzo mix is placed.

Patch repair in an existing occupied institutional building (school corridor, hospital lobby, airport concourse): worker saw-cuts out the damaged terrazzo, then builds and clamps a small wooden mold/dam around the irregular repair area, sealing edges against the existing floor so the patch mix can be poured, working around furniture, foot traffic and occupied-space restrictions.

Precast terrazzo fabrication shop: worker builds and sets up molds on casting tables/beds for precast items (stair treads, bases, sills, cabinet-fixture and vanity tops), assembling plywood/steel side rails and inserts, clamping them and checking depth and alignment before casting.

Small in-situ custom forming: clamping and fitting wooden molds against existing walls, columns, cabinet fixtures and stair nosings for cove bases and irregular terrazzo details, on remodel or occupied-site work with varied, found geometry.

sources.system: Elematic Shuttering Robot E9 / automatic shuttering station
sources.title: Robot for automatic shuttering in precast wall production | Elematic
sources.claim: Elematic's Shuttering Robot E9 is a commercial precast-plant robot that automatically places and sets formwork side profiles (shutters) on casting tables from CAD/production data, operating inside a fenced robot cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling/positioning mold side forms on a casting bed for cementitious casting. It transfers to 'setting up frames to the proper depth and alignment' and to precast mold setup because the objects (form rails defining pour depth and outline), the mm-level alignment tolerance, and the cast material class are the same as terrazzo formwork.

sources.title: Shuttering Robots for Precast Concrete Plants | Sommer precast technology
sources.claim: Sommer's multi-function shuttering robot handles formwork tasks in precast concrete plants, including placing shuttering profiles, aligning them and activating their magnets, working from element data on the casting pallet.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic placement and alignment of mold side forms on a casting pallet. Same operation as a terrazzo worker setting frames to depth and alignment before a pour — the robot positions the frame elements to defined coordinates and fixes them.

sources.title: Highly dynamic shuttering robot of the third generation - Concrete Plant Precast Technology (BFT International)
sources.claim: Weckenmann's third-generation shuttering robot was installed and put into production at a precast concrete manufacturer's plant, forming molds automatically for wall and slab elements.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated mold/formwork build-up on casting beds in a precast plant. Shows the shuttering-robot capability is a fielded production deployment, not a lab demo, supporting E1 for frame/mold setup on a fixtured casting surface.

sources.system: WEINMANN FRAMETEQ framing station (with FEEDBOT robot)
sources.title: WEINMANN FRAMETEQ Framing Stations - Stiles Machinery
sources.claim: WEINMANN's FRAMETEQ framing stations are commercial machines that automatically position, index, cut and nail dimensional lumber studs and plates into accurately dimensioned wooden frames in offsite production plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic cutting and nailing of dimensional lumber into a dimensionally specified frame. Building a wooden mold/form is the same material (lumber and sheet goods), the same operations (cut to length, position, nail), and comparable tolerances, so capability carries over when the work is presented at the machine.

sources.system: House of Design robotic roof/floor truss assembly systems
sources.title: Video Showcase: Robots at the truss plant | HBS Dealer
sources.claim: House of Design's fully automated robotic truss systems, which robotically pick, position and assemble nail-plated wooden truss members, are installed and operating in Builders FirstSource component plants in the US.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly of wooden structural frames from lumber on a fixtured table. Comparable objects (sawn lumber members), comparable placement precision, and fastening in a fenced plant cell — the same competence needed to build a wooden mold at a machine.

sources.system: Odico robotic hot-wire cutting / Factory On The Fly
sources.title: Odico's Factory on the Fly is a pop-up robotic manufacturing unit for construction sites | Dezeen
sources.claim: Odico used robotic wire-cutting cells to manufacture formwork moulds for cast concrete, including load-bearing concrete structures of a completed building, and packaged the cell as a container-based on-site unit driven from a digital model.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic fabrication of moulds for casting cementitious material to specified geometry. Transfers to 'build molds' for terrazzo casting: same purpose (define the cast shape and depth), comparable dimensional tolerance, but only inside a robot cell, not fitted in situ.

tasks.label: Spread roofing paper on surface of foundation and spread concrete onto roofing paper with trowel to form terrazzo base.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial/institutional building (school, hospital, airport, retail), large open floor 2,000–20,000 sq ft on a concrete foundation slab: unroll and lap roofing felt/isolation sheet over the slab, set wire mesh, then place, spread, screed and rough-trowel a 1.25–3 in sand-cement underbed to grade and flatness for the terrazzo topping. Active construction site with other trades, debris, temporary lighting and power.

New construction interior rooms and corridors of 300–2,000 sq ft: cut and fit roofing paper around doorways, columns, floor drains, pipe penetrations and wall edges; barrow or pump mortar in and screed the base to screed strips, thresholds and divider strip elevations.

Renovation or tenant fit-out inside an existing building after demolition (school wing, hospital area, store): out-of-level and patched existing slab, isolation sheet over cracks, limited access through elevators/doors, night or weekend phasing, dust and occupancy constraints.

Small and irregular areas: stair landings, thresholds, vestibules, closets, curbs and cove edges, and pockets around cabinet fixtures and columns; paper cut to fit and mortar base placed and hand-troweled in confined, obstructed spaces.
Exterior or partially exposed slabs (plaza, entry vestibule, terrace) with slopes to drains, edge conditions and weather exposure; membrane laid over the foundation and base mortar screeded to pitch.

Shop/precast work at a terrazzo contractor's fabrication shop: casting terrazzo base slabs, treads and panels on casting beds with a separating paper/release sheet over the bed, mortar base spread and screeded before the topping is placed.

sources.system: Knauf plasterboard production line (continuous board forming line)
sources.title: Knauf Plasterboard Production | Knauf
sources.claim: Plasterboard is produced on continuous automated plant lines in which a paper liner is unrolled onto the forming conveyor and a cementitious (gypsum) slurry is spread over it in a uniform stream to controlled thickness — machine execution of 'lay paper on a surface, spread cementitious mix onto the paper'.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: board forming in a plasterboard plant. It transfers to the terrazzo-base step because the objects are the same class (a rolled paper sheet laid over a flat support, and a wet cementitious mix spread over it), the operation is the same (deposit and level a layer of controlled thickness on the paper), and the required precision (millimetre thickness uniformity) is comparable; it is done in a purpose-built machine environment (E1).

sources.system: Vollert pallet circulation system (shuttering robot, concrete spreader, compaction station)
sources.title: Pallet circulation system - Vollert Precast Solutions
sources.claim: Precast concrete pallet-circulation plants place and compact concrete layers of specified thickness onto fixtured casting pallets using CAD/CAM-controlled shuttering robots and fully automated concrete spreaders with vibratory compaction stations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: casting flat precast floor/wall elements. The 'spread concrete to form a base' step transfers directly — the same material (fresh concrete/mortar) is distributed and levelled to a set thickness over a flat fixtured surface, at flatness tolerances at least as tight as a terrazzo underbed, in a purpose-built line.

sources.system: Hongfa HFT300 terrazzo tile making machine
sources.title: Terrazzo tile making machinery produced by Hongfa machinery factory
sources.claim: Automatic hydraulic terrazzo tile presses form a terrazzo unit consisting of a marble-chip/cement face layer over a concrete base layer in a fixtured mould under PLC control, i.e. machine formation of the terrazzo base itself.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precast terrazzo tile/curb production. It substantiates machine formation of a cement terrazzo base course under a terrazzo topping in a fixtured mould — the same material and layer function as the site-poured base, with the work brought to the machine (E1).

sources.title: Four Wheel Concrete Laser Screeding Robot for Sale
sources.claim: Commercially sold concrete laser screed 'robots' used on building floors are operated by remote control rather than autonomously; the manufacturer's specification lists the control mode as remote control with a 200 m control range.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as context for the on-site variant: the closest commercial machine for spreading and levelling a cementitious floor layer on a jobsite is human-teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive E2/E3 judgment for this task.

sources.system: Smooth G1 concrete troweling and leveling robot
sources.title: iF Design - Basement Concrete Troweling and Leveling Robot
sources.claim: A commercial construction floor robot exists that levels and trowels concrete with automatic navigation and laser levelling in basement slab construction, but it finishes concrete already placed on the slab; it does not lay an isolation sheet or place a mortar underbed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: concrete floor finishing on jobsites. It covers only the finishing of an already-placed slab, not the membrane laying and underbed placement that this task requires, so it bounds rather than establishes on-site capability.

tasks.label: Produce rough concrete surface, using broom.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interior commercial building under construction (school, airport, hospital, retail): after the concrete underbed/subfloor for a terrazzo installation is placed and screeded, the finisher drags a stiff broom across the still-plastic surface to leave an even scratch/rough texture so the sand-cement or epoxy terrazzo topping will bond. Large open floor areas, other trades working nearby, debris and temporary lighting, timing dictated by the concrete's set.

Exterior flatwork tied to the terrazzo scope — entry slabs, ramps, walkways, exterior landings and thresholds. Broom is pulled across fresh concrete for slip resistance, working from edges and joints outward, in sun, wind or heat that shortens the finishing window; grade and site conditions vary.

Small and awkward areas: stair treads and landings, cove/base areas, around columns, floor drains, door openings, closets and cabinet bases. Hand brooming while kneeling or reaching, matching texture direction to adjacent work and avoiding marring edges and formed corners.

Repair/renovation inside an occupied facility (hospital wing, school corridor, terminal) where a slab section is patched or a new underbed placed off-hours: broom the fresh patch to a rough bond surface, matching surrounding texture, within a barricaded work zone controlled by the building owner.

Shop/precast work: casting precast terrazzo units, concrete bases, treads or curbs in the fabricator's shop and brooming the fresh bond face (or exposed face) to the required roughness before the topping is applied or before shipment. Fixed layout, molds on casting tables, controlled conditions.

sources.system: Vollert roughening device (spiked-roller/roughening unit on precast pallet circulation line)
sources.title: New Caledonia focuses on precast construction – Vollert
sources.claim: Vollert supplies an automated roughening device integrated into precast concrete pallet-circulation lines that roughens the fresh top surface of floor slabs and double walls so that the later cast-in-place concrete bonds — the same purpose as brooming a terrazzo underbed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical roughening of a fresh concrete surface for bond. It is the same operation and purpose as brooming a terrazzo underbed — a brush/spiked tool drawn across plastic concrete to leave an even rough profile — performed on the same material to a specified texture.

sources.system: Vollert Smart Cast concrete distributor with built-in roughening device
sources.title: Manufacturers of precast concrete elements increase product quality and system productivity through modernization investments
sources.claim: A built-in roughening device on an upgraded, automatically controlled casting line produces an even roughening profile on fresh precast ceiling/floor slabs at production rates of up to four elements per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: producing a rough (scratch) texture on fresh concrete for bonding a later topping — the identical output the broom produces on a terrazzo underbed, here delivered at production quality and rate.

sources.system: Vollert Smart Cast automatic concrete distributor (MÜVA Beton plant)
sources.title: Concrete Plant Precast Technology — Modernization improves product quality and increases plant productivity
sources.claim: Trade-press account of the same plant confirms the casting station carrying the roughening device is a CAD/CAM-controlled automatic distributor rather than a manually driven spreader, establishing machine control of the roughening pass.

sources.system: Smoothing-and-roughening robot with integrated intelligent end-effector
sources.developer: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology (Gang, Duan, Wang, Nan, Song)
sources.title: A Robotic Solution for Precision Smoothing and Roughening of Precast Concrete Surfaces: Design and Experimental Validation (Sensors 24(11):3336)
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed robot system with a multi-DOF brushing/smoothing end-effector autonomously smooths and then roughens (brushes) precast concrete component surfaces on an assembly line, planning paths around embedded obstacles, validated on a physical prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic brushing (roughening) of precast concrete surfaces. Same medium (fresh concrete), same tool action (brush drawn across the surface) and same accepted output (specified rough texture) as broom-finishing an underbed; the paper reports texture variety and obstacle avoidance on fixtured components.

sources.system: Somero Broom + Cure Machine (S-15R/S-22EZ hybrid frame)
sources.title: Broom + Cure Machine - Somero
sources.claim: The only widely marketed brooming machine for on-site slabs applies the broom, float and cure by machine but is a ride-on unit driven by an operator, not an autonomous robot.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as a negative: it is the closest on-site brooming machine, but it is operator-driven, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment at E2 or E3.

sources.title: Autonomous Concrete Floor Polishing & LightWare's SF40/C LiDAR
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile floor robot navigates and operates a concrete polishing machine on building floors, but it works on cured concrete (grinding/polishing), not on plastic concrete within a finishing window, and does not produce a broom texture.
sources.transferJustification: Considered as a related task (mobile robotic floor surface treatment) but judged NOT to transfer: polishing hardened slabs has no set-timing window, no risk of marring plastic concrete, and yields a smooth, not broomed, texture, so it does not substantiate E2/E3 brooming.

tasks.label: Remove frames when the foundation is dry.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large cast-in-place floor in a commercial building under construction (lobby, school corridor, airport concourse): once the sand-cement underbed/foundation has set, the finisher strips the perimeter wood or metal edge forms, screed rails and blockouts — backing out screws, pulling nails, prying boards free without spalling the green edge — then stacks and cleans the forms and sweeps debris. Dust, cords, other trades working nearby, layout differs per job.

Phased/large-area pours: removal of interior bulkhead and pour-strip forms between adjacent panels of underbed before the next pour, plus temporary keyway strips. Flat slab work, forms are straight boards or steel angle fixed to the deck; the joint edge must be left clean and square for the abutting pour.

Stairways, landings and treads: stripping riser boards, nosing forms, stringer boards and side forms from cast terrazzo steps. Awkward three-dimensional geometry, elevated and confined work positions, forms wedged/braced and nailed, high risk of chipping arrises.

Small features and trim: cove/wall base, curbs, thresholds, planters, and cabinet-fixture or vanity bases. Small braced or clamped forms cast against walls and casework, removed with pry bar, hammer and screw gun in tight spaces alongside finished surfaces that must not be marred.

Renovation/repair or small patch pour in an existing occupied institutional building (school, hospital, transit station), often night or weekend work: strip the temporary edge frames from the patch once set, remove protection/dams and dust barriers, clean the joint to the existing terrazzo, and leave the area usable by morning.

sources.system: Elematic Shuttering Robot E9 (EDGE wall line)
sources.title: Robot for automatic shuttering in precast wall production | Elematic
sources.claim: Elematic's Shuttering Robot E9 is a commercial gantry robot in fenced precast wall plants whose listed functions include demolding of all shutters (including ... the magnets that hold them), driven by element CAD data and the production plan.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: de-shuttering a hardened precast concrete element. Same act as the terrazzo task — removing the frames that retained a cement mix once the foundation has set — on comparable cementitious workpieces with edge-damage-sensitive arrises, but with the element fixtured on a steel pallet and the forms presented as machine-handled magnetic side rails.

sources.date: product page retrieved 2026-07; product in market for years
sources.title: Shuttering Robots for Precast Concrete Plants – Multi-Function-Shuttering-Robot
sources.claim: Sommer's Multi-Function-Shuttering-Robot performs all demoulding and shuttering functions of ... precast pallet circulation plant; it scans the pallet, computes each shuttering's position, grips them and transfers them to cleaning/storage, replacing heavy manual form stripping.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing the side forms from a cured concrete element on a circulating pallet. It is the same removal-of-frames-after-set operation, performed autonomously with perception rather than to a fixed script, in a purpose-built plant.

sources.title: Formwork stripping robot enhances productivity | CPi worldwide
sources.claim: Trade-journal technical article by plant automation supplier Unitechnik describes formwork-stripping robots in precast plants that, using a scanner and software, clear the formwork left on the pallet after the hardened elements have been lifted off.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated stripping of formwork from cured concrete elements. Establishes that scanner-guided robotic form removal after the concrete has set is an established, in-service plant function, not a one-off demo.

sources.system: Progress Form Master (shuttering, deshuttering and storage robot)
sources.title: Schwörer Bausysteme relies on modernization in the precast plant - Concrete Plant Precast Technology
sources.claim: Progress Group's Form Master shuttering/deshuttering/storage robot was installed and put into service in 2021 at Schwörer Bausysteme's precast plant, automating the shuttering and de-shuttering of magnets and mounting parts on a pallet carousel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: de-shuttering hardened precast elements in a production plant. Shows a named system in real daily production (not a demo) performing the removal of frames after the cast has set.

sources.developer: reported plant installation (BFT International case report)
sources.title: Geared up for the future with new pallet carrousel technology - Concrete Plant Precast Technology
sources.claim: A pallet carrousel plant reported by the trade journal runs shuttering and de-shuttering as a fully automated operation, with a warehouse robot retrieving shutters from storage and feeding the shuttering robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: de-shuttering of cured elements in production. Confirms end-to-end automation of the form-removal cycle (strip, transport, clean, store) rather than only the gripping sub-step.

tasks.label: Signal truck driver to position truck to facilitate pouring concrete and move chute to direct concrete on forms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Exterior at-grade slab/underbed pour at a commercial jobsite: worker hand-signals the ready-mix driver to back the truck to the form edge over rutted, muddy ground with other trades, vehicles and parked material around; adds/extends steel chute sections, swings and walks the chute along the forms as concrete discharges, and signals the driver to slow, stop or reposition.

Interior floor/underbed pour in a building shell under construction: truck stays at a door or opening; worker signals the driver into position, then directs the chute into wheelbarrows, buggies or through the opening onto forms inside, working around columns, rebar, debris and limited headroom, repositioning the truck several times per load.

Small residential or light-commercial job (driveway, patio, stoop, stair and landing forms, curbs): tight lot access, homeowner property, worker guides the driver into a narrow approach and directs the chute precisely into narrow, shallow forms, frequently repositioning truck and chute for small placements.

Elevated deck or pump/conveyor placement: worker signals the pump or conveyor-truck operator and the ready-mix driver, and guides the hose or chute end over congested rebar and edge forms at height, coordinating flow rate with the placing crew.

Shop or yard casting of precast terrazzo/concrete components (stair treads, bases, curbs, wall base): mixer truck or shop mixer discharges onto level, institution-controlled shop floor; worker signals the driver into a marked bay and directs the chute into fixed forms laid out on the casting slab.

sources.system: Ebawe concrete spreader / concrete distributor (Progress Group, ebos control)
sources.title: Concrete Spreader | Ebawe - Progress Group
sources.claim: Ebawe (Progress Group) concrete spreaders are commercial machines used in precast carousel plants that take concrete from a mixer or bucket conveyor and discharge it into shuttered pallets/moulds evenly to the element contours and ..., under automatic control fed by the ebos control system; a segment-gate version pours into battery (deep, narrow) moulds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: filling forms with fresh concrete from a delivery vessel. The terrazzo worker's job here is to bring the concrete stream to the right place over the forms and control how much lands where; the spreader performs exactly that placement function (same material, same forms/shuttering, tighter volume control) once the forms are presented to the machine, which is the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: Fully automatic concrete spreader in Ebawe carousel plant (Hungary)
sources.developer: Ebawe Anlagentechnik / Progress Group (plant operator: ASA Építőipari)
sources.title: Biggest automated precast plant in Hungary starts production - Concrete Plant Precast Technology (BFT International)
sources.claim: A large automated precast plant in Hungary operating since 2022 uses a fully automatic concrete spreader that pours concrete into the shuttered, reinforced pallets as part of an automated carousel line driven by CAD/PXML data.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (placing fresh concrete into forms), evidenced as an in-production deployment rather than a product claim: the machine, not a worker, positions the discharge over the forms and meters the concrete into them.

sources.system: Automatic concrete distribution systems for precast production
sources.developer: Various precast equipment suppliers (industry overview, TDM Extruder)
sources.title: Automatic concrete distribution system for precast concrete production
sources.claim: Automatic concrete distribution systems that deposit concrete mix accurately and uniformly into moulds are in routine use across many precast concrete production plants, reducing errors from improper pouring or moving of concrete.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: directing the concrete stream into forms/moulds. It substantiates that automatic placement of concrete into forms is a mature, widely deployed capability in purpose-built plant settings, not a one-off demonstration.

roles.title: Construction Laborers
roles.description: Perform tasks involving physical labor at construction sites. May operate hand and power tools of all types: air hammers, earth tampers, cement mixers, small mechanical hoists, surveying and measuring equipment, and a variety of other equipment and instruments. May clean and prepare sites, dig trenches, set braces to support the sides of excavations, erect scaffolding, and clean up rubble, debris, and other waste materials. May assist other craft workers.

tasks.label: Tend pumps, compressors, or generators to provide power for tools, machinery, or equipment or to heat or move materials, such as asphalt.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Towable/portable generator or light plant on an active jobsite: laborer checks oil and fuel, starts the unit, runs cords and spider boxes to power saws, lights and small tools, watches load and fuel through the shift, tops it off from a can or fuel truck, shuts it down and secures it. Mud, dust, changing site layout, other trades working nearby.

Towable diesel air compressor supplying pneumatic tools (breakers, rock drills, chipping hammers, nailers) on a street or building site: position the rig, couple air hoses with whip checks to tools and manifolds, start the engine, set and watch pressure, drain moisture, add fuel and oil, respond when a hose blows or a tool starves, shut down at day's end.

Dewatering pump keeping a trench, excavation or foundation dry: drop in a submersible or set a trash pump, run suction hose with strainer and lay discharge hose to a discharge point, prime and start, watch for loss of prime, clear mud, rags and gravel from the intake, reposition hoses as the dig advances, refuel the engine, keep it running through the pour or pipe-laying.

Heating or moving materials: tending a tar kettle, crack-seal melter or asphalt hot box (light and adjust the burner, watch temperature, feed material, tend the wand/hose, clean out), or tending a grout/mortar/concrete pump and its lines during a pour, on a roadway or site.

Tending pumps or compressors for construction/renovation work inside a facility whose owner controls access and keeps standard equipment - a plant shutdown, water/wastewater plant, tunnel, or parking structure: fixed or skid-mounted units, permanent power and piping, fixed layout, work under a permit system.

sources.title: Robotic refuelling for mines - Robofuel | Scott
sources.claim: Robofuel is a commercially deployed robotic refuelling station that uses vision sensing to locate a machine's fuel receiver and autonomously couple the nozzle and fill the tank, at purpose-built (relocatable) fuel bays serving mining equipment including autonomous haul fleets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic refuelling of diesel machines. Refuelling and fuel-level servicing is the hands-on core of tending engine-driven generators, compressors and pumps; the objects (diesel fill points, nozzles, hoses) and precision are the same, and the work is done at a purpose-built station the machine is brought to.

sources.title: SCOTT making ROBOFUEL refuelling system progress with AHS mining truck fleets - International Mining
sources.claim: Trade press describes ROBOFUEL as an automation and control solution using vision and sensing to refuel mine trucks autonomously, in use at several sites including with an autonomous Komatsu 930E ....
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the Robofuel product page: it substantiates that autonomous machine refuelling is fielded at real sites, not merely demonstrated.

sources.title: Automated Frac Fueling Services | Atlas Oil
sources.claim: The Fuel Automation Station is a fielded automated fuelling skid that, using guided-wave radar level sensing, keeps a bank of up to 28 diesel pumping units fuelled simultaneously with automatic overfill/spill fail-safes and remote SCADA control, so workers no longer walk the pad to fuel running equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: keeping banks of running diesel pumps and gensets supplied with fuel and monitored. That is the fuel-tending component of this task, executed by machine with pre-plumbed hoses at a purpose-built fuelling installation.

sources.title: Intelligent Clog-Free Wastewater Pumping: Flygt Concertor | Xylem US
sources.claim: Flygt Concertor is a commercially sold intelligent pumping system for fixed pump installations whose integrated intelligence detects clogging and runs automatic pump-cleaning cycles, plus self-adjusting performance, removing routine unplanned attendance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: keeping a solids-handling pump running without an attendant. Clearing clogs and restoring flow is the main hands-on element of tending a dewatering pump; the machine performs it itself, but only in a fixed, plumbed installation.

sources.system: Godwin Dri-Prime with PrimeGuard 2 / Field Smart Technology
sources.title: Xylem's Godwin Field Smart Technology (FST) | For Construction Pros
sources.claim: Godwin Dri-Prime dewatering pumps with PrimeGuard 2 / Field Smart Technology self-prime and can be programmed to start and stop automatically from level inputs with no operator intervention, with remote monitoring used by contractors to reduce or eliminate on-site pump attendance.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the priming, start/stop and monitoring portion of pump tending; it does not cover set-up, hose handling, refuelling or clearing a fouled strainer, which still require a laborer on an as-found site.

sources.title: Asphalt Automation Software | Ammann
sources.claim: Ammann's as1 plant control runs a hot-mix asphalt plant with fully automated mix production, automatic burner control and integrated heated bitumen storage tanks - heating and moving asphalt under machine control in a purpose-built process plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tending burners, heated tanks and transfer pumps that heat and move asphalt. The material, temperatures and pumping duty match a kettle or hot box, but are handled by fixed purpose-built plant equipment rather than a portable unit.

sources.title: A Retrospective on Uses of Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot
sources.claim: Across Boston Dynamics' Spot fleet, robots autonomously navigated missions and inspected over 130,000 industrial assets ... and construction sites, while arm-based manipulation (picking objects, opening doors) was performed with operators driving the robot manually.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the state of mobile robots on real construction sites and in plants: autonomous work is sensing and data collection, while physical servicing with an arm remains teleoperated, so full tending of a portable pump, compressor or generator is not substantiated at E2 or E3.

sources.title: Equinor's autonomous robotics: inspection 'dogs' and record-holding subsea drones | Offshore Technology
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal quadruped was deployed in November 2024 ... running autonomous inspection missions of process equipment, and ANYmal X is in commercial use for inspection at Petronas oil and gas facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous rounds reading gauges and checking pumps and compressors in a structured facility. It substantiates only the watch-and-monitor element of tending; these robots do not fuel, start, or hook up equipment, so they cannot complete the instance at E2.

tasks.label: Lubricate, clean, or repair machinery, equipment, or tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-shift cleaning of hand tools and small equipment at an active jobsite: scraping and hosing wet or partly hardened concrete, mortar and mud off mixer drums, wheelbarrows, buckets, screeds, trowels and shovels, wiping and oiling them, and returning them to the gang box. Items sit where the work stopped, in varying shape and soil level.

Interval greasing/lubrication round on machinery at the jobsite: grease gun on zerk fittings of excavator/loader/compactor pins, bushings and swing bearings, greasing a hydraulic breaker every couple of hours, oiling saw chains, drill shanks and hammer bits. Machine positions, weather and access vary.

Minor field repair and servicing to keep tools running: swapping worn saw blades, bits and chains, replacing frayed cords, air hoses and fittings, clearing a jammed plate compactor or a clogged concrete pump line/hose, changing filters, and figuring out why a tool will not start.

Washing down heavy equipment and vehicles at a designated washout pad or the contractor's yard: pressure-washing mud and concrete off machines, undercarriages, mixer chutes and pump hoppers before transport or return to the rental yard.

Bench servicing in the contractor's shop or tool crib: cleaning returned power tools and equipment, blowing out dust, degreasing, lubricating and re-oiling, topping off fluids and checking or sharpening blades before the tools go back out.

sources.title: Fives' Smart Automation Solutions Division | RoboWash Robotic Industrial Parts Washer
sources.claim: Commercial robotic industrial parts washer: a 6-axis robot manipulates the workpiece through pre-wash, high-pressure wash and dry inside an enclosed purpose-built cell, fully automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated washing of soiled metal workpieces. Transfers to cleaning tools/equipment when items are fixtured and presented to the machine, as the E1 counterfactual assumes: comparable object size and weight, comparable high-pressure water/detergent removal of oil, chips and residue.

sources.title: Robotic solutions for washing-cleaning parts | Staubli United States
sources.claim: Sealed industrial robots handle both the high-pressure water jet and the workpiece in automated washing/cleaning cells, tolerating acidic and alkaline solutions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic wet cleaning of dirty parts in a purpose-built cell; the same manipulator-plus-jet arrangement is what cleaning caked tools in a fixtured cell would require.

sources.title: Sioux engineers automated mixer truck washing station - Concrete Products
sources.claim: Automated wash station cleans concrete off a mixer truck's drum, chutes and charge hopper; sensors trigger the cycle as the truck enters and a PLC runs rotary high-pressure arms and spray bars with no worker leaving the cab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing fresh concrete off concrete-handling equipment. Same material and cleaning method as a laborer hosing out a mixer or pump hopper, performed by machine in a purpose-built station.

sources.title: Heavy Vehicle Washing Systems - Reduce Vehicle Equipment Downtime | InterClean
sources.claim: Fully automatic robotic wash systems clean oversized vehicles and mining/oil equipment in a drive-in bay, recognizing the vehicle and washing designated areas with no personnel in the bay.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated pressure washing of heavy off-road machinery. Same objects (mud/concrete-covered heavy equipment) and same accepted output (clean machine) as the laborer's wash-down, achieved in a purpose-built bay.

sources.system: Autolube / centralized automatic lubrication systems (Lincoln Industrial, Graco)
sources.date: 2007-08-20 article; technology in continuous commercial use since
sources.title: Reduce Downtime with Autolube Systems | For Construction Pros
sources.claim: Centralized automatic lubrication systems installed on construction machines meter grease to every lube point while the machine works, replacing the manual point-by-point grease-gun round.
sources.transferJustification: Same task rather than a related one: scheduled greasing of construction machinery lube points, performed by a machine-controlled pump and metering valves mounted on the machine instead of a laborer with a grease gun.

sources.system: Automatic lubrication system for Caterpillar 320-class excavator
sources.title: What's the Return on Investment (ROI) of an Automatic Lubrication System? - GreasePoint
sources.claim: Automatic lubrication systems are a routinely priced option for ordinary construction excavators, indicating current commercial deployment on jobsite machines.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: replaces the laborer's daily grease-gun round on jobsite excavators; cited to establish current commercial availability on ordinary construction machines.

sources.date: 2026-04 product page; in mine use since ~2020
sources.title: Robotic refuelling for mines - Robofuel | Scott
sources.claim: Autonomous refuelling robot uses vision sensing to locate a haul truck's fuel receiver and couple the nozzle with no personnel present; in use at mine sites and offered for replenishing drills and excavators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fluid servicing of heavy off-road equipment brought to a service point. Shows vision-guided coupling to a service port on a dirty machine, the nearest demonstrated analogue to robotic fluid/lube service of construction machinery.

sources.title: Automation Drives Grease-dispensing Machine | Machinery Lubrication
sources.claim: Industrial robot cell applies lubricating grease to specified contact surfaces of an assembly as part of an automated production machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of grease/oil to defined points on a fixtured item, which is what 'lubricate the tool' reduces to once the tool is presented to a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Automatic Machines for Precast Panels | Bianchi Casseforme
sources.claim: Automatic brushing machine cleans concrete residue off precast plant casting tables and pallets between shifts, automating the whole clean-and-prepare cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized removal of concrete residue from steel forming equipment. Comparable soil (green/cured concrete) and acceptance standard (clean, ready-to-use surface) to cleaning forms and concrete tools, on a purpose-built line.

tasks.label: Signal equipment operators to facilitate alignment, movement, or adjustment of machinery, equipment, or materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Acting as signal person for a mobile or tower crane lift on a commercial building site: giving standard ASME B30.5 hand signals (hoist, lower, swing, boom up/down, stop) or radio calls to guide a load of steel, trusses, precast panels, or a material bundle from pick point to set point, including blind lifts where the operator cannot see the landing zone.

Spotting and backing a dump truck, ready-mix truck, or delivery trailer into position on an active site or shoulder of a roadway: watching clearances and other workers, hand-signaling the driver rearward, and signaling the stop point and discharge timing for gravel, asphalt, or concrete.

Guiding an excavator, backhoe, or loader operator during trenching, grading, or pipe/utility work: signaling bucket depth and lateral position, warning of marked or exposed utilities and trench-box clearance, and calling stops when the bucket approaches a worker or a buried line.

Directing an operator for fine alignment of a placed item or material flow: positioning a concrete bucket or pump boom over a form, seating a beam, panel, box culvert, or manhole section onto its bearing, or aligning forms and shoring, with incremental inch-level correction signals until the piece is seated.

Signaling equipment maneuvering in congested or hazardous conditions: night or roadway work zones with live traffic, tight urban streets, work near overhead power lines or existing structures, in noise, dust, or poor light, often coordinating multiple pieces of equipment and pedestrians simultaneously.

tasks.label: Measure, mark, or record openings or distances to layout areas where construction work will be performed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interior floor layout on a concrete slab or metal deck in a commercial building under construction: laborer pulls dimensions from drawings/control points, snaps chalk lines and marks wall runs, door and window openings, and penetrations across a floor plate so framers and MEP trades know where to build.

Outdoor site layout on rough-graded ground: measuring off control points and marking building corners, footing/pier and pile locations, trench and utility runs, and grade/offset points with spray paint, lath, flags or stakes over open terrain, in weather and around moving equipment.

Workface measuring and marking at the point of installation: measuring an existing rough opening, gap or piece of material with a tape, marking cut lines on lumber, drywall, pipe or form panels, and marking spacing/anchor points on walls, columns and formwork, often in cluttered space or from a ladder.

Overhead and vertical layout transfer: shooting or plumbing points from the floor up to the deck/ceiling and onto walls to mark hanger, sleeve, and anchor locations for pipe, duct and supports, working overhead at 9-16 ft.

Measuring and recording: taking as-built dimensions of openings, rooms and distances and recording them in a field log, tablet app or on a drawing for quantity takeoff, fabrication, or verification against the model.

tasks.label: Clean or prepare construction sites to eliminate possible hazards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interior housekeeping on an active building project: at breaks and end of shift, gather scrap lumber, drywall offcuts, cardboard/packaging, banding, buckets and stray fasteners from congested work floors; coil and hang extension cords, hoses and welding leads out of walkways; clear egress paths and stairs; broom-sweep and carry debris to a chute, cart or dumpster. Layout and clutter change daily and other trades are working nearby.

Installing and maintaining physical safeguards: building and setting wood or steel guardrail at leading edges and stair/floor openings, cutting and screwing down hole covers and marking them, capping protruding rebar, pulling or bending protruding nails, erecting barricades, warning tape and signage around wet concrete, overhead work or excavations, and securing loose materials against wind.

Outdoor earthwork housekeeping with equipment: backfilling and closing open excavations and trenches, knocking down spoil piles, regrading rutted haul roads and laydown yards, filling holes and removing rock/stumps so the site is safe to walk and drive on.

Keeping paved and travel surfaces clean: sweeping tracked mud, gravel, sand and dust off site roads, ramps, parking decks and adjacent public streets; wetting down for dust control; shovelling snow/ice or squeegeeing standing water off walkways and slabs.

Roadway/utility work-zone setup and takedown: placing and retrieving cones, barrels, delineators and portable signs along a lane closure, and sweeping loose gravel, millings and debris out of travel lanes before opening the road back to traffic.

Final clean of a substantially finished building before inspection/turnover: removing remaining debris and protective coverings from finished floors, sweeping/vacuuming and scrubbing corridors, lobbies, units and underground parking areas so the space is clear of trip and slip hazards.

Backfilling trenches and small excavations by shovel and compacting the fill in lifts with a pneumatic rammer (jumping jack) or plate compactor: shading and haunching around pipe and conduit, backfill against foundation walls and around poles, in narrow trenches or trench boxes where equipment cannot reach.

Digging a trench or drainage ditch in open ground where equipment has room to work: utility corridor, solar field, road shoulder or open pad, cut to line, depth and grade per spec with spoil placed alongside; laborer digs and cleans the line by hand or alongside a machine.

Digging small trenches or ditches in confined, cluttered or landscaped ground: residential back yards, between buildings, around trees, fences, sprinkler lines and existing hardscape, using hand tools or a mini machine with hand finishing.

Spreading, leveling and compacting fill or aggregate over larger open areas — building pads, road subgrade, embankment lifts — moving material with shovel and rake behind machines and compacting in lifts with plate compactor or roller to grade and density spec.
