tasks.label: Load, unload, or identify building materials, machinery, or tools, distributing them to the appropriate locations, according to project plans or specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: A truck delivers palletized/unitized materials (pallets of drywall, cubes of block, banded bundles, boxed fasteners) to an active jobsite; the laborer helps unload with pallet jack/forklift/boom truck, checks items against the packing slip, and stages them at the laydown area designated on the site plan. Ground is graded dirt or partly paved; weather and traffic vary.

A mixed, non-palletized load arrives (loose dimensional lumber, pipe and conduit, ladders, buckets, boxes of fittings, hand and power tools) on a flatbed or pickup; the laborer hand-unloads item by item, identifies each against the order/spec, and sorts it into piles by trade and location.

Inside a multi-storey building under construction, the laborer moves palletized and carted material (board, cartons, duct, fixtures) from the ground-floor drop point onto the construction hoist/freight elevator and out to the designated staging point on each working floor, following the floor plan and the day's material schedule.

Hand distribution to the work face: carrying boxes of fittings, buckets of compound, bundles of studs and tool kits to specific rooms and crews, up stairs and through partially framed, debris-strewn spaces; breaking down pallets and spreading material at layout positions per plan.

At the contractor's yard, shop, or a supply house, the laborer picks tools and materials against the job list/plans, loads them onto the company truck or trailer, straps/secures the load, and unloads it at the end of the day back into racks and the tool crib. Fenced, graded, institution-controlled premises with standard racking and forklifts.

Receiving hoisted loads on a structure: rigging and hooking bundles of material for a crane or telehandler, signaling, landing them at the planned position on the deck or ground, unhooking, and distributing the pallets/bundles around the floor per the placement plan.

Residential remodel or small site: unload a pickup or trailer at the curb/driveway, carry material (cabinets, tile boxes, sheet goods, tool bags) up porch steps and through doorways into an occupied home, and set it in the designated room without damaging finishes.

tasks.label: Position, join, align, or seal structural components, such as concrete wall sections or pipes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground utility pipe installation in an open trench: laborer works in a shored, often muddy trench, receives 8-48 in. RCP/PVC/DI pipe lowered by excavator or crane, sets it to laser/GPS grade on bedding, lubricates and aligns bell-and-spigot with gasket, pulls/pushes the joint home, then seals joints and manhole connections with butyl/mortar/boots.

Setting precast concrete structures on site: manholes, catch basins, box culverts, headwalls, barrier and retaining-wall units. Crane or excavator lifts the unit; laborers guide it with tag lines onto a prepared base, align to layout marks, shim/level, apply butyl rope or mortar, and grout/point the joints.

Erecting building wall sections: tilt-up or precast concrete panels and prefabricated wall assemblies lifted by crane; laborers guide, set on shims/dowels, plumb and align with braces and turnbuckles, hold while embed connections are bolted or welded, then dry-pack, grout and caulk the panel joints.

Laying block/segmental units by hand: CMU or segmental retaining-wall and landscape blocks positioned course by course on a footing or leveling pad, aligned to line and level, bedded in mortar or construction adhesive, with caps and joints sealed.

Joint sealing and grouting work on site: caulking vertical and horizontal joints between concrete panels, sealing pipe penetrations and sleeves, installing backer rod and expansion-joint material, grouting base plates and structure collars, in varying weather and at height on lifts or scaffolds.

Assembling and joining above-ground pipe and conduit: PVC/HDPE/steel pipe sections and fittings joined at grade or inside a building shell before or during installation, solvent-welded, fused, threaded or coupled, aligned and supported to line and grade with hangers, blocks or clamps.

tasks.label: Perform site activities required of green certified construction practices, such as implementing waste management procedures, identifying materials for reuse, or installing erosion or sedimentation control mechanisms.

Cluttered, changing, dusty jobsite shared with other trades.

Working the site's recycling / laydown staging area: breaking down cardboard and pallets, separating scrap metal, clean wood, gypsum and concrete into their bins, culling still-usable offcuts, pallets and salvaged fixtures into a reuse stack, and loading/consolidating bins for haul-off with weights recorded.

Installing perimeter erosion and sedimentation controls at a newly cleared site: cutting a trench and driving stakes for silt fence, stretching and backfilling the geotextile along contours, staking straw wattles across a slope, placing catch-basin inlet protection, and spreading the gravel stabilized construction entrance. Uneven graded soil, mud, slopes, weather.

Post-rain SWPPP/BMP inspection and maintenance: repairing torn or undermined silt fence, shoveling out accumulated sediment, re-staking displaced wattles, shoveling and sweeping tracked-out mud from the adjacent public street, and covering soil stockpiles with plastic sheeting weighted down.

Deconstruction/salvage for reuse in an existing structure being renovated or taken down: judging which doors, casework, fixtures, brick and dimensional lumber are salvageable, carefully removing them intact with pry bars and hand tools, de-nailing, and stacking/palletizing them for reuse or donation.

sources.title: C&D Waste | Sorting Bulky Waste | ZenRobotics
sources.claim: ZenRobotics (Terex) Heavy Picker is a commercially sold AI robotic sorter that autonomously separates bulky construction & demolition waste into recyclable fractions (metals, wood by grade, inert mixed waste, rigid plastics) inside materials recovery facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Same work product as the laborer's waste-management step: mixed jobsite C&D debris separated into clean recycling streams; objects (wood, drywall, metal, plastics, rubble) are the same materials the laborer handles.

sources.system: ZenRobotics Heavy Picker (12 arms) at Remeo MRF
sources.title: Remeo | Case Study | ZenRobotics
sources.claim: Deployed installation: Remeo's materials recovery facility in the Helsinki region runs twelve ZenRobotics Heavy Pickers sorting 120,000 tonnes/year of construction waste, achieving a 71.8% recycling rate in its first months of operation.
sources.transferJustification: Demonstrates sustained, production-scale autonomous separation of construction waste into recovered streams — the accepted output of the laborer's on-site waste-segregation and diversion work — in a purpose-built conveyor-fed robotic line.

sources.title: ZenRobotics Launch Fourth Generation of Waste Sorting Robots
sources.claim: ZenRobotics 4.0 generation robots come pretrained to recognize over 500 waste categories and prioritize the most valuable resource when picking, supporting reliable material identification (including grade/reuse-relevant distinctions).
sources.transferJustification: Speaks to the identification/judgment component of 'identifying materials for reuse' and keeping recycling streams uncontaminated, on the same C&D material classes the laborer sorts.

sources.title: These Robots Will Pick Through and Clean Up Construction Debris - Engineering.com
sources.claim: AMP Robotics and Ryoshin built robotic cells (AI-Benkei, AI-Musashi) using AMP's AI vision to identify, sort and pick construction and demolition debris, with AI-Benkei handling debris up to 40 kg at up to 25 tonnes/hour in a single-robot cell.
sources.transferJustification: Second independent system doing the same C&D debris identification and separation the laborer performs, again in a conveyor-fed robotic cell rather than on the jobsite.

tasks.label: Control traffic passing near, in, or around work zones.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rural/suburban two-lane road, short-term lane closure: laborer flags alternating one-way traffic with a STOP/SLOW paddle, coordinates by radio with a flagger at the far end, judges gaps and queue length, releases platoons, waves construction equipment and dump trucks across the live lane, lets emergency vehicles and residents through, and reacts to non-compliant drivers. Public traffic, variable weather and light.

Highway or arterial lane closure setup/takedown: laborer rides or walks the taper placing and later retrieving cones, drums, advance-warning signs and an arrow board per the traffic-control plan, then shifts devices as the work area moves along the closure. Live adjacent lanes, often at night.

Urban street/intersection work zone: laborer controls a mix of cars, buses, delivery trucks, cyclists and pedestrians around a lane or sidewalk closure, gestures and speaks to drivers, redirects pedestrians into a temporary walkway, holds traffic for driveways, and coordinates with a police detail. Dense, negotiated, ad-hoc interactions.

Construction site access control: laborer stands at the site entrance holding traffic on the adjacent street while dump, concrete and lowboy trucks enter and exit, spots backing trucks into the gate, keeps pedestrians clear of the crossing, and releases the street queue between truck movements.

Mobile/moving operation on a low-volume rural highway (line striping, sweeping, crack sealing, shoulder patching): traffic control is provided by pacing a shadow/attenuator vehicle with arrow board behind the moving crew, keeping the correct buffer and warning and merging approaching traffic.

sources.system: Kratos ATMA / Autonomous Impact Protection Vehicle (with Royal Truck & Equipment)
sources.developer: Kratos Defense; Royal Truck & Equipment; Colorado DOT
sources.title: Colorado Expands Autonomous Highway Safety Trucks
sources.claim: Kratos' Autonomous Truck-Mounted Attenuator (ATMA) crash trucks operate driverless behind striping and maintenance crews on Colorado highways; CDOT runs three and Kratos has fielded 15 across several states.
sources.transferJustification: The shadow/attenuator vehicle IS the traffic-control element of a mobile work zone (buffer plus arrow-board warning/merging); the ATMA performs that positioning role driverless on the same public highways, so it substitutes for the person providing mobile-operation traffic control.

sources.title: Autonomous Vehicles — Colorado Department of Transportation
sources.claim: CDOT describes the autonomous impact protection vehicle as a leader/follower system in which the unmanned vehicle reproduces the leader's maneuvers, used in striping operations.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: establishes the autonomy mechanism and official use of the driverless follower for work-zone protection during mobile operations.

sources.title: Automated Flagger Assistance Devices — General (MUTCD 2023 §6L.02)
sources.claim: Automated Flagger Assistance Devices — the machine substitute for a flagger on US roads — are remotely operated by human flaggers, not autonomous.

sources.title: Falcon 100 Automated Cone Laying Machine (ACLM) | Highway Care
sources.claim: The Falcon 100 Automated Cone Laying ..., approved by National Highways for UK roads, drops and collects motorway cones but is operated by a person in the truck cab.

sources.system: Automated road gate complex, DCT Gdańsk SA (OCR/LPR portals with barrier lanes)
sources.title: Automation of the Road Gate Operations Process at the Container Terminal—A Case Study of DCT Gdańsk SA
sources.claim: Automated container-terminal road gates admit and hold trucks with cameras and barriers so that no personnel work in the gate lanes during normal operation (DCT Gdańsk case study).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stopping, checking and releasing a stream of road trucks at a facility control point — the same hold/release function a flagger performs at a site entrance — done by machine-actuated barriers in purpose-built single-file lanes.

sources.title: Container Gate Operations Infrastructure | ConPDS Autogate
sources.claim: Commercial autogate systems read arriving vehicles automatically and raise the physical barrier without any staff involvement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-actuated admission/holding of road vehicles at a fixed control point, i.e. the stop-and-release core of flagging, achieved when the approach is engineered into single-file gated lanes.

sources.system: Automatic grade-crossing gate with flashing-light signal (train-detection circuits)
sources.developer: US railroads / FHWA-ITE Railroad-Highway Grade Crossing Handbook
sources.title: FHWA - Railroad-Highway Grade Crossing Handbook - 4 Identification of Alternatives
sources.claim: Automatic railroad grade-crossing gates physically bar public road traffic when a train is detected and release it afterwards, with no human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously stopping and releasing public road traffic at a hazard. It works only where the roadway has been rebuilt around the device (fixed installation, detection circuits) and performs only stop-all/release, not alternating-flow flagging.

sources.system: FANUC R-2000iC/165F and M-410iC palletizing cells
sources.title: Robotic Palletizing Systems | FANUC America
sources.claim: Industrial pick-and-place/palletizing robots deployed in fenced cells autonomously handle 25 kg-class objects with 3D vision at production rates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeatedly grasping and placing 10-25 kg objects (traffic cones and drums are in this class) at programmed positions from a presented supply inside a fenced cell — the E1 form of deploying and retrieving channelizing devices.

sources.developer: Texas A&M Unmanned Systems Lab (Hartzer, Saripalli)
sources.title: AutoCone: An OmniDirectional Robot for Lane-Level Cone Placement
sources.claim: AutoCone demonstrated self-driving cone robots that position themselves for lane-level traffic delineation using RTK GPS, as a research prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the device-placement half of work-zone traffic control; a prototype only, so it supports feasibility of machine cone positioning in a controlled setting, not live-highway worker-quality deployment.

tasks.label: Install sewer, water, or storm drain pipes, using pipe-laying machinery or laser guidance equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Municipal open-cut sewer or storm main in a city street: laborers work inside a shored trench/trench box 8-16 ft deep, receive 12-48 in. RCP or PVC pipe lowered by excavator, set and home gasketed bell-and-spigot joints, check line and grade with a pipe laser or GPS rod, place and tamp stone bedding and haunching, while dodging live utilities, groundwater, and adjacent traffic.

Subdivision / commercial site underground utilities in open ground: install PVC or ductile-iron water main and storm drain runs, set fittings, valves, hydrants, and tie pipe into catch basins and manholes; grade set by laser or machine-control excavator, joints assembled and restrained by hand, trench backfilled and compacted.

Small-diameter service work: water services and sewer laterals from main to building, often in shallow or hand-dug trenches, tight yards, or around existing utilities; cut-in tees or saddles on live mains, glue/fuse or gasket short pipe lengths, set cleanouts, verify slope with laser or level.

Large-diameter storm drain / culvert in a highway or heavy-civil corridor: heavy RCP or corrugated metal pipe handled with excavator, vacuum lifter, or pipe hooks, joints pulled home with come-alongs or excavator, laser/GPS grade control, mud mats and dewatering, work under traffic control.

Trenchless installation support: pipe jacking/microtunneling from shafts with laser guidance, HDD pullback of fused HDPE, or pipe bursting; laborers rig and load pipe segments in the shaft or on the surface, grout/lubricate, monitor line and grade, and complete manhole and end connections.

sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofit makes standard excavators dig trenches fully autonomously to about 0.1 ft accuracy on utility-solar jobsites; the product automates trench excavation only — the cable/pipe placement and jointing remain crew work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: trench excavation to grade, the precursor step to pipe laying. It shows autonomous earthmoving on open jobsites but provides no capability to lower, align, gasket-home, bed, or grade-check pipe, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Leads Major Autonomous Excavation Push | Equipment World
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics runs supervised-autonomy excavators on active US construction sites, moving bulk earth; full autonomy was still a stated goal for 2026 and the scope is earthmoving, not utility pipe installation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mass excavation on construction sites. Demonstrates autonomous heavy-equipment digging in unstructured settings, but no pipe handling, jointing, or grade-critical invert placement, so it does not carry over to installing sewer/water pipe.

sources.system: Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System (RRES/RRES prototype)
sources.title: ULC Technologies Improves Roadwork Excavation With All-Electric Autonomous Excavation Robot - The Robot Report
sources.claim: ULC Technologies' Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System autonomously core-cuts road, vacuum-excavates a keyhole to expose buried utility assets and backfills, in UK street field trials; work on the pipe itself (e.g., fitting installation) is tool-assisted and the system remains a prototype rather than a pipe-installation machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic excavation and backfill over buried utility mains in public streets. It is the closest robotic system to trench utility work, but it exposes existing gas assets through a small keyhole; it does not lay new pipe runs to line and grade or make bell-and-spigot joints, and it is a prototype.

sources.system: Microtunnel boring machines (e.g., Herrenknecht AVN with MT jacking frame and control container)
sources.title: Tunnelling into trenchless: microtunnelling and pipe jacking explained - The Australian Pipeliner
sources.claim: Microtunneling/pipe jacking does install sewer pipe with laser guidance and jacking machinery, but the machines are run continuously by an operator from a surface control container, and crews rig each pipe segment in the shaft.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (installing sewer pipe with laser guidance), but the installation is continuously remote-operated with crew pipe handling, so it cannot support a positive autonomy judgment.

tasks.label: Operate or maintain air monitoring or other sampling devices in confined or hazardous environments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Permit-required confined space on a jobsite (street manhole, utility vault, wet well, tank, deep excavation): bump-test the 4-gas monitor, attach a sample pump and tubing, lower the probe and test O2/LEL/CO/H2S at top, middle and bottom, record readings on the entry permit, then keep the pumped monitor sampling continuously while entrants work and respond to alarms.

Continuous atmospheric monitoring while work proceeds in an enclosed or underground work area (tunnel heading, sewer/utility vault, shored trench near gas mains, enclosed demolition area): carry or hang the monitor, watch readings against ventilation, evacuate on alarm, and log the shift's readings.

Media-based exposure sampling on an abatement/renovation job: pre-calibrate personal sampling pumps with a rotameter, clip pumps to workers' belts with cassettes/sorbent tubes in the breathing zone for silica, lead or asbestos, run the shift, post-calibrate, seal samples and complete chain-of-custody for the lab.

Direct-reading area/perimeter monitoring at a remediation or demolition site: place and start real-time dust (PM), VOC/PID and LEL area monitors around the exclusion zone and downwind, check and download readings through the day, relocate units as the work face moves.

Keeping the monitoring fleet serviceable at the contractor's tool room or site trailer: daily bump tests with calibration gas, periodic span calibrations, battery charging, pump flow checks, filter/sensor checks, and downloading datalogs into the compliance record.

sources.system: Spot with Teledyne FLIR MUVE C360 gas sensor (MFE Inspection Solutions integration)
sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / Teledyne FLIR / MFE Inspection Solutions
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped, carrying a Teledyne FLIR MUVE C360 multi-gas monitor and Enhanced Autonomy Payload, ran autonomous inspection rounds across a 40-acre midstream gas plant, detecting a combustible-gas plume from a pinhole leak and auto-shutting down at an LEL threshold.

sources.system: ANYmal with modular gas detection payload
sources.title: ANYbotics Launches New Gas Leak & Presence Detection Solution for its ANYmal Inspection Robot
sources.claim: ANYbotics launched a gas leak and presence detection ... the ANYmal inspection robot, with swappable gas detectors (oxygen, hydrocarbons, ammonia and others) that the robot calibrates on site and uses to monitor concentrations continuously during autonomous missions in petrochemical plants.

sources.system: Spot with Blackline Safety connected gas detector
sources.developer: MFE Inspection Solutions / Blackline Safety / Boston Dynamics
sources.title: MFE Launches Robotic Gas Detection for Boston Dynamics' Spot - DRONELIFE
sources.claim: MFE Inspection Solutions released a commercial robotic gas detection product pairing Blackline Safety's connected gas detector with Spot, with automated return-to-home when LEL thresholds are crossed; the vendor cites a prior mission in which Spot found combustible gas autonomously.

sources.system: Vertex Edge / Vertex M multi-point toxic gas monitoring system
sources.title: Vertex™ Edge System Overview (Quick Reference Guide)
sources.claim: The Honeywell Vertex Edge is a fixed, machine-controlled sample-draw system that pulls air through tubing from up to 72 remote points (up to ~400 ft away), mechanically advances Chemcassette collection media, analyses it and raises alarms and records unattended; it is standard equipment in semiconductor fabs monitoring gas cabinets, valve boxes and ducts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fixed multi-point sample-draw gas monitoring. It performs exactly what the laborer's pumped monitor does in a confined space — drawing an air sample through tubing from an enclosed hazardous point, analysing the same gas families at ppm/LEL sensitivity, alarming and logging — but under machine control once the sample lines are installed, i.e. with the space plumbed to the machine as a purpose-built setting would present it.

sources.system: Radius BZ1 pumped area gas monitor with LENS Wireless
sources.title: Radius® BZ1 Area Gas Monitor | Reliable Gas Detection by Industrial Scientific
sources.claim: The Industrial Scientific Radius BZ1 area gas monitor with a pumped SafeCore module draws air through tubing from inside a confined space and monitors it continuously and unattended, streaming readings and alarms over LENS wireless to remote personnel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended pumped area monitoring of a confined space. Once the sampling line is fixed in the space, the machine performs the sampling, evaluation, alarming and record transmission that the worker performs with a hand-held pumped monitor, on the same gases and thresholds.

sources.title: DSX Docking Station | Automated Gas Monitor Maintenance & Calibration | Industrial Scientific
sources.claim: Industrial Scientific's DSX docking station automatically performs the routine maintenance of portable gas monitors — charging, bump testing with calibration gas, span calibration, firmware updates and storage of the compliance records — once an instrument is seated in the dock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated bump test/calibration/record-keeping of the same portable 4-gas monitors the laborer maintains. The machine performs the maintenance operations and generates the compliance record; the only human step is presenting the instrument in the dock fixture, which is part of an E1 environment.

tasks.label: Smooth or finish freshly poured cement or concrete, using floats, trowels, screeds, or powered cement finishing tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential / light-commercial flatwork: driveway, sidewalk, patio, garage or basement slab poured from a truck chute or buggy. Laborer strikes off with a 2x4 or roller screed, bull-floats, edges, cuts control joints, hand-trowels tight spots and applies a broom finish, working to the weather and the set of the mix; access is tight and the perimeter is formed lumber against a house, fence or existing walk.

Large interior slab-on-grade in a warehouse, big-box store or industrial building under construction: laser-screed placement over vapor barrier and mesh, bull-floating, ride-on and walk-behind power trowels for the field, hand floats and edgers along walls, columns, dock pits and penetrations, all to specified FF/FL flatness within one pour window.

Elevated structural deck or podium slab in a multi-story building: concrete pumped onto metal deck or formed deck, screeded to laser-set wet screeds, bull-floated and power-floated/trowelled around columns, embeds, edge forms and rebar dowels, often outdoors with wind and on a congested, changing floor plate.

Street and site concrete: curb and gutter, valley gutters, ADA ramps, sidewalk panels and driveway aprons. Laborer hand-finishes behind a slipform machine or forms and finishes entirely by hand — floating, edging the curb face and gutter line, tooling joints, brooming, and matching existing adjacent concrete beside live traffic.

Small pours, patches and detail work: equipment pads, stair treads and landings, footing tops, sacking/rubbing formed walls, filling and finishing around penetrations, columns and posts, and patching defects in freshly stripped or previously placed concrete; irregular shapes, vertical and sloped surfaces, hand tools only.

sources.system: Vollert VARIO SMOOTH trowelling machine (precast pallet-circulation surface technology)
sources.title: Surface technology - Vollert Precast Solutions
sources.claim: Vollert's VARIO SMOOTH trowelling machine is a commercial precast-plant machine that travels over the casting pallet and power-trowels the exposed fresh concrete surface of the element to a smooth finish.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical act as the task: power-trowelling fresh/green concrete to a smooth finish, with the same material, the same rotating-blade tooling and comparable surface tolerance; only the setting differs (element fixtured on a steel pallet rather than a site slab).

sources.system: Unitechnik UniControl / UniCAM automated pallet-circulation precast plants
sources.title: Software and automation for precast concrete plants — Unitechnik
sources.claim: Automated precast concrete plants are pallet-circulation lines in which the smoothing (trowelling) work station, alongside concreting and compacting, can be run fully automatically under the plant control system.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the concrete-surface smoothing station in a purpose-built plant runs under machine control without an operator, i.e. the E1 counterfactual (work brought to the machine, fixtured on a pallet) is realised in commercial practice.

sources.system: Ground levelling robot (地面整平机器人), used with the floor smoothing robot and basement troweling robot
sources.developer: Guangdong Bright Dream Robotics (Country Garden subsidiary), China
sources.title: 工地迎来“机器人”工友——博智林建筑机器人应用调研纪实 (Sina Finance / 中国企业家)
sources.claim: Bright Dream Robotics' ground levelling robot works on freshly poured reinforced-concrete floors on Country Garden high-rise construction sites, setting its own path from its navigation system and performing fully automatic levelling to about ±5 mm flatness.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the screeding/levelling portion of this task (the task names screeds) on freshly poured concrete at a real building site, but not the float, edge, joint and trowel finishing of the whole pour.

sources.developer: Taisei Corporation with Nikken Lease Kogyo / University of Tsukuba (Japan)
sources.title: 半自律で施工可能に、大成建設の床仕上げロボットが進化 — BUILT (ITmedia)
sources.claim: Taisei's T-iROBO Slab Finisher, a concrete floor finishing robot rented and sold in Japan and used on building sites since 2016, was given a semi-autonomous control system so it runs automatically over an operator-taught area; operators still remotely change trowel speed and blade angle as the concrete sets, and the robot is used together with skilled floor finishers.
sources.transferJustification: Directly this task (troweling freshly placed floor concrete) on Japanese construction sites, but the machine covers the open field only and is operated in cooperation with human floor finishers, so it does not evidence whole-pour completion.

sources.system: Bright Dream Robotics concrete construction robot fleet (distribution, levelling, smoothing, troweling robots)
sources.title: 博智林建筑机器人多机协同体系渐显，建标准与向外落地加速 — 21经济网
sources.claim: On a Shenzhen project billed as the city's first comprehensive construction-robot project, base-slab pouring was done with humans and robots working together, reaching ±5 mm flatness at initial set with a 95% level pass rate and saving about 20% of labour — i.e. the crew was reduced, not replaced.
sources.transferJustification: Same task on a real site; shows the state of the art is human-robot collaboration on the open field, supporting the negative judgments at E2/E3 rather than a positive one.

tasks.label: Erect or dismantle scaffolding, shoring, braces, traffic barricades, ramps, or other temporary structures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Erecting frame or system scaffold (e.g., PERI UP, Layher, tube-and-clamp) on a building exterior or industrial plant: leveling base plates/mudsills on uneven ground, hoisting and pinning frames lift by lift, installing braces, decks, toeboards and guardrails, tying to the structure, working at height in wind and weather among other trades.

Dismantling scaffold after the work is finished: breaking ties, removing planks and guardrails, unpinning and passing components down by hand or gin wheel/hoist, sorting damaged parts, stacking and loading the truck, cleaning the area.

Setting up and taking down roadway traffic control: advance warning signs, cones/drums, a taper, barricades, arrow boards and sometimes temporary barrier, on a public street or highway with live traffic, per an approved traffic control plan; devices later retrieved.

Installing shoring in an excavation: lowering and setting trench boxes with an excavator's help, placing hydraulic/aluminum shores or plate bracing against trench walls, adjusting spreaders as the trench advances, then removing them during backfill, in muddy, confined, variable soil conditions.

Other temporary structures on site: rolling scaffold towers and baker's scaffolds indoors, temporary ramps and walkways, guardrails and covers at floor/roof openings, wall and formwork bracing, jobsite barricades and pedestrian fencing, assembled from mixed stock to fit whatever the site presents.

sources.developer: PERI with University of Southern Denmark (LSP), KU Leuven, RWTH Aachen, UC Leuven Limburg, Jožef Stefan Institute
sources.title: The future of scaffolding is here – SDU
sources.claim: Genio, a mobile dual-arm robot from PERI with SDU and European university partners, autonomously performs the lifting, positioning and connecting of PERI UP scaffold components from a scaffolder-defined digital plan, with an integrated transport system feeding it material.

sources.title: Researchers develop new robot: The future of scaffolding is here (SDU press release)
sources.claim: Genio remains a prototype whose testing to date has been confined to closed, controlled environments; it was first shown publicly at bauma in April 2025, with real construction-site testing planned over following years.

sources.title: KEWAZO - BuiltWorlds
sources.claim: The only scaffolding robot in routine site/plant deployment, Kewazo's LIFTBOT, is a remote-controlled hoist that transports scaffold components up and down the scaffold; human scaffolders still erect and dismantle the structure.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (scaffold erection/dismantling): shows the deployed state of the art is machine material transport under remote control, not robotic assembly.

sources.title: Falcon 100 Automated Cone Laying Machine (ACLM) – Highway Care
sources.claim: The Falcon 100 ACLM is a commercially deployed machine that automatically lifts, places and retrieves traffic cones on live roads, keeping operatives off the carriageway.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (erecting traffic barricades/channelizing devices); recorded as unclear autonomy because the machine is driven and commanded by an on-board operator.

sources.title: Highway Care adds Falcon 75 ACLM to its specialised product range for local road projects - LCRIG
sources.claim: Falcon cone-laying operations are commanded by an operator from the vehicle cab via a touch-screen, who sets cone spacing and taper patterns; the vehicle itself is human-driven.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (placing traffic control devices); establishes that a human operator continuously drives and commands the machine, so it is not autonomous operation.

sources.developer: Highway Care (with Highways England, Kier, Balfour Beatty Vinci JV)
sources.title: FALCON Automated Cone Laying Machine completes on-road trials – Highways Magazine
sources.claim: The Falcon ACLM completed on-road trials in live traffic on the UK strategic road network with a single on-board operator per shift and was endorsed for deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (setting out cones for lane closures); shows real-road deployment but with a human operator present throughout.

tasks.label: Provide assistance to craft workers, such as carpenters, plasterers, or masons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Tending a masonry crew on a commercial or residential building site: mixing mortar in a paddle mixer, keeping mud boards and brick/block stocked within the masons' reach on scaffold, cutting block on a wet saw to called-out dimensions, moving planks and rebuilding scaffold levels as the wall rises, outdoors in whatever weather.

Assisting carpenters framing walls or setting concrete formwork: carrying and passing studs, plates, plywood and form panels from the stack to the work face, holding members plumb while the carpenter nails, fetching hardware and fasteners, bracing, pulling and stacking stripped forms, sweeping cutoffs from the work area.

Assisting a concrete placement/finishing crew on a slab or footing pour: dragging and repositioning the pump hose, spreading and raking concrete, helping pull the screed, handing floats/edgers/trowels to finishers, wetting and covering the slab, cleaning tools and forms after the pour.

Assisting interior finishing trades (drywall hangers, tapers, plasterers, painters) in a building under fit-out: mixing joint compound or plaster to consistency, stocking sheets and buckets room to room up stairs and through partly framed openings, lifting and holding board while it is fastened, masking and protecting floors, continuous cleanup behind the crew.

General gopher/support runs across an active site: responding to ad hoc verbal requests from tradespeople, retrieving specific tools, fasteners, blades or short material from the gang box, laydown yard or truck, hauling them up floors and ladders to the crew's work position, and returning tools and scrap.

Heavy/civil work assisting rebar and pipe crews on a bridge deck, roadway or utility job: distributing and positioning rebar bundles and individual bars on the deck grid, tying, handing tools and holding grade for the craft workers, outdoors alongside live equipment.

sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor robotic systems automate handling, cutting and fastening of full-size sheet goods onto prefabricated wall panels, floor cassettes ... in fixtured factory lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sheathing/panel assembly. The physical content of a laborer's assistance to carpenters and board hangers is moving, positioning and holding dimensional lumber and 4x8 sheet goods while they are fastened; these fixtured lines do exactly that with the same objects at equal or better precision.

sources.title: How FrameTec plans to cut build-cycle times and reduce waste
sources.claim: A production plant in Arizona runs Randek-built robotic lines that cut, frame, sheath, glue, route, ... building components with a small human crew supervising.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated wall-panel framing. It substantiates that in a purpose-built cell machines perform the lumber fetching, positioning and holding that a laborer performs for a carpenter, with workers present in the same facility.

sources.system: House of Design / Alpine robotic truss assembly systems (ABB IRB 4600)
sources.developer: House of Design Robotics with Alpine (ITW)
sources.title: Video Showcase: Robots at the truss plant
sources.claim: Robotic truss lines built by House of Design with ABB robots pick and position lumber and assemble roof and floor trusses in component plants, taking the lifting and placing off the human assemblers; Builders FirstSource has bought multiple systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic truss fabrication. Lifting and positioning framing lumber into a press is the same object class and precision as a laborer holding and feeding stock for a carpenter, performed in a fixtured cell with personnel on the line.

sources.title: Software: Lay It Again, SAM – Masonry Magazine
sources.claim: The SAM100 masonry robot picks brick off a conveyor, applies mortar and places each unit on the wall to a laser string line while working on a scaffold, with the brick supply loaded onto its conveyor by a human tender.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic brick placement. Given a fixtured brick supply and pumped mortar, the machine performs the handling, mortaring and precise presentation of masonry units that constitutes tending a mason; same units, same reach, greater placement precision.

sources.title: Robotic Masonry Is Helping to Fill the Skilled Labor Gap - Construction Executive
sources.claim: Even the commercially deployed masonry robot still depends on a human mason tender to load it with brick and mortar and on masons to operate it and finish corners and joints.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about the mason-tending role: it documents that on real jobsites the tending function remains human even where masonry laying itself is automated.

sources.title: Hadrian X bricklaying robot builds first homes in demo program - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The Hadrian X mobile blocklaying machine works outdoors on uncontrolled sites building block walls from a 3D CAD model, and has built its first houses in the US demonstration program.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor autonomous block placement. It shows heavy masonry units can be handled autonomously on an open site, but the machine is loaded and set up by a human crew and does not supply or tend a working mason.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Okibo's autonomous AI-guided plastering, drywall-finishing and painting robots operate on active US and European construction sites, having covered more ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous interior finishing on jobsites. It establishes that jobsite autonomy exists for the finisher's own spraying/sanding work, but the machine is fed and tended by people; it does not perform the laborer's stocking, mixing, board-holding and cleanup role.

sources.title: Equipment Management: The Right Tool for the Job Might Be a Robot | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: The Canvas drywall-finishing machine used on jobsites is operated by a worker rather than running unattended.
sources.transferJustification: Negative evidence on jobsite interior finishing support: the leading commercial drywall machine still requires a human operator, so it cannot stand in for a laborer assisting a finishing crew.

sources.title: IronBOT Rebar Placing Robot | Advanced Construction Robotics
sources.claim: IronBOT lifts, carries and places ... bundles of up to 5,000 lb on bridge decks for the placing crew, automating the physical handling while a Robot Supervisor oversees it and singulates bars.
sources.transferJustification: This is the laborer's supply role for a rebar crew: carrying heavy bundles to the work face and placing them where the craft workers need them, on an open bridge deck alongside the crew.

sources.title: Road building robotics firm releases third-gen rebar-tying machine - Construction Briefing
sources.claim: TyBOT, an autonomous rebar-tying robot, has been used on more than 65 field deployments on US highway and bridge projects and is sold as an accepted tool of the ... for rodbuster crews.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous rebar tying on the same bridge decks where IronBOT places bar; it shows self-locating autonomous operation among a working crew in an outdoor construction setting.

sources.title: Digit's Next Steps | Agility
sources.claim: Digit humanoids work full time in a GXO warehouse, autonomously unloading totes from mobile robots at a station and loading them onto a conveyor, passing 100,000 totes moved in commercial operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repetitive material transfer. It substantiates autonomous move-and-hand-off of standardized load units when the material is presented at an engineered station, the E1 form of keeping a work face supplied.

sources.title: Featured in ENR: LIFTBOT transforming site logistics - KEWAZO LIFTBOT case study with Chevron
sources.claim: Kewazo's LIFTBOT robotic hoist that carries scaffolding and materials up structures on jobsites, including the US Capitol facade project, is remote-controlled.
sources.transferJustification: Negative evidence for jobsite material supply: the leading site-logistics machine runs on a rail on the scaffold, is remote-controlled, and is loaded and unloaded by workers.

tasks.label: Spray materials, such as water, sand, steam, vinyl, paint, or stucco, through hoses to clean, coat, or seal surfaces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-work cleanup power washing on a job site: laborer drags a pressure-washer hose and wand to blast concrete flatwork, masonry, siding, forms, scaffolding and equipment clean of mud, mortar smears and overspray, working around debris, cords, stored material and other trades.

Spraying water through a hose or truck-mounted spray bar for dust control and moisture: wetting subgrade before compaction, fogging/curing fresh concrete, knocking down saw-cutting or demolition dust, and washing mud off haul-road/street approaches and truck tires.

Spray-applying interior coatings inside a building under construction: joint compound/texture on hung drywall, primer and paint on walls and ceilings, or spray-applied fireproofing on structural steel, working off the floor or a lift amid studs, ducts and other trades.

Spraying exterior cementitious material through a hose from ground or scaffold: stucco/plaster scratch and brown coats over lath on a building facade, or shotcrete/gunite on a wall, slope or pool shell, including tending the pump/hopper and nozzle work at height.

Abrasive or high-pressure water blasting through a hose to strip paint, rust, curing compound or laitance from steel members, concrete walls, tanks or masonry, typically inside containment with respirator and blast hood on a renovation or infrastructure site.

Spraying sealers and protective liquids on flatwork: curing compound on fresh slabs, penetrating concrete sealer, waterproofing/damp-proofing on foundation walls, or sealcoat on asphalt drives and lots, applied with a pump sprayer and hose to a uniform, holiday-free film.

sources.system: Okibo EG7 / EP-1000 plastering and painting robot
sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Okibo's autonomous plastering/painting robots spray plaster and paint on walls and ceilings inside buildings under construction, and are reported to be working on major construction sites in Europe and the US.

sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction’s Dirty Work Is Going Robotic - Architect Magazine
sources.claim: Canvas robots spray joint compound onto hung drywall on active jobsites and then sand it to a level 5 finish, working alongside human crews; the operator positions the machine and the robot executes the spraying pass.

sources.title: Discover the Robot for Painters ! PACO - Les Companions
sources.claim: PACO is a commercial mobile painting robot with an automated airless spray system that paints interior walls and ceilings on new-build and renovation sites after the operator programs the job.

sources.title: Development and Application of a Fire Resistive Covering Spraying Robot to Building Construction Site - IAARC/ISARC
sources.claim: A fire-resistive covering spraying robot that moves autonomously on a pre-built map and sprays rock-wool fireproofing onto steel beams was developed and applied at a building construction site.

sources.title: Lucid Bots Announces Lavo AI: The First Fully Autonomous Pressure Washing Robot (PRWeb)
sources.claim: Lavo AI is a ground-based pressure washing robot that maps and navigates facility exteriors and washes paved surfaces at up to 6,000 sq ft/hour without manual operation; pilots began winter 2025 with general availability in 2026.

sources.title: Lucid Bots raises Series B funding as operator network hits $75M in revenue - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Lavo AI is offered as a shipping product to Lucid Bots' network of professional exterior-cleaning operators for washing sidewalks, driveways and parking lots.

sources.title: Toilet-cleaning robot makes us feel better about all this AI business - New Atlas
sources.claim: Somatic's cleaning robot works unattended in commercial office buildings, riding elevators between floors and cleaning restrooms on a service contract.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: janitorial surface cleaning. It is the same physical act as the rated task — spraying liquid under pressure through a nozzle to clean hard surfaces — performed autonomously in an occupied building.

sources.title: SOMATIC - bathroom cleaning robots for office buildings
sources.claim: The Somatic robot cleans by spraying a chemical solution, then rinsing with a jet of fresh water, then vacuuming dry — i.e., pressurized spray cleaning of hard surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: restroom sanitizing. Same action class as the rated task (spray water/solution through a hose to clean surfaces) at comparable precision, performed autonomously indoors.

sources.system: Autonomous Caterpillar water trucks at Gudai-Darri
sources.title: Rio Tinto to deploy world’s first fully autonomous water trucks at Gudai-Darri
sources.claim: Fully autonomous water trucks whose main job is dust suppression have been put into service on mine haul roads alongside autonomous haul trucks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dust suppression by water spraying. Same purpose and material (water sprayed onto ground surfaces to control dust and moisten fill) as the laborer's hose work, executed autonomously outdoors on working haul roads.

sources.title: Videos - ASI Robots
sources.claim: ASI sells a commercial autonomy kit that drives water trucks on repeatable routes with automated spray control for dust suppression, replacing the human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dust suppression water spraying on working sites; identical output (wetted surfaces) to the laborer's hose/water-truck work.

sources.system: Sandy and Rosie autonomous grit-blasting robots (SABRE ALPHA-1 lineage)
sources.developer: UTS Centre for Autonomous Systems / Roads and Maritime Services NSW

sources.claim: Two autonomous grit-blasting robots developed at UTS scanned and blasted old paint and corrosion from the steel structure of the Sydney Harbour Bridge as part of the bridge's maintenance program.

sources.system: Empire pre-engineered robotic blast cells and blast rooms
sources.title: Robotic Abrasive Blast Systems - Empire Abrasive Equipment
sources.claim: Robotic abrasive blast cells and blast rooms, in which a manipulator blasts fixtured workpieces inside purpose-built enclosures, have been commercially integrated for decades.

sources.system: ABB painting robots (IRB 5500 family, Compact Interior Paint Station)
sources.title: Paint solutions for Automotive | ABB
sources.claim: Industrial paint robots with atomizers spray liquid coatings onto vehicle bodies presented by a conveyor inside fenced paint booths, meeting production film-thickness and appearance specifications.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic spray coating. Same act as the rated task (pumping coating through hoses and spraying it to a controlled film on a surface) with the work fixtured and conveyed to the machine, i.e., the E1 counterfactual.

sources.title: Normet SmartSpray | Advancing Automated Concrete Spraying
sources.claim: Automated concrete (shotcrete) spraying on tunnel surfaces remains operator-directed: the boom follows operator-set lines or pre-defined areas while the operator keeps position and distance to the surface.

tasks.label: Raze buildings or salvage useful materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interior soft-strip / gut demolition of a building under renovation: laborer pries off drywall, ceilings, trim, cabinets, flooring and non-load-bearing partitions with sledge, pry bar, sawzall and rotary hammer, works around live utilities and unknown conditions behind finishes, and hauls debris out through stairs/chutes to a dumpster.

Razing a small structure (house, garage, small commercial building) alongside an excavator/skid steer: laborer torch- or shear-cuts rebar and steel, knocks down remaining walls with hand tools, hoses debris for dust control, spots the machine operator, and pulls hazardous or non-conforming items out of the pile.

Breaking out and removing concrete and masonry — slabs, sidewalks, footings, foundation walls, chimneys, stair landings — with pneumatic/electric breakers, saws and pry bars, then busting the rubble small enough to muck out by wheelbarrow or bucket.

Selective salvage/deconstruction in place: carefully removing reusable or scrappable items — doors, windows, cabinets, fixtures, HVAC units, copper piping and wiring, dimensional lumber, brick, structural steel — without destroying them, then de-nailing/cleaning and stacking or bundling them for reuse or scrap sale.

Separating mixed demolition debris on site into salvage/recycling streams: pulling ferrous and non-ferrous metal, clean wood, cardboard, gypsum and inert rubble out of the mixed pile and placing each into the correct bin, container or scrap pile.

sources.title: Why Brokk – Original demolition power
sources.claim: The dominant class of commercial 'demolition robots' (Brokk, and equivalents from Husqvarna/Darda) are remote-controlled machines driven continuously by a human operator, not autonomous systems; they are the standard tool for interior, selective and concrete demolition.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task: machine-assisted razing of structures and concrete breaking. Cited to establish that in-situ demolition machinery is teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: C&D Waste | Sorting Bulky Waste | ZenRobotics
sources.claim: Robotic sorting arms autonomously identify and pick multiple recyclable fractions (metals, wood by grade, inert mixed waste, rigid plastics) out of bulky construction and demolition waste on a conveyor-fed sorting line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: recovery of useful/saleable material from demolition debris. Same objects (scrap metal, wood, brick/inert rubble, plastics) and same accept/reject decision as a laborer separating salvage on site, but with the debris presented on a conveyor.

sources.system: ZenRobotics Heavy Picker installation at Eberhard's automated recycling plant
sources.title: Eberhard | Case Study | ZenRobotics
sources.claim: A production C&D recycling plant runs ZenRobotics heavy-duty sorting robots around the clock, picking up to 12,000 items per ... of up to 30 kg and separating minerals from impurities in mixed demolition waste at 200 tons per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: separating salvageable/recyclable fractions from demolition debris, demonstrating sustained worker-replacing throughput and reliability in a purpose-built, conveyor-fed cell.

sources.system: ZenRobotics ZRR2 AI sorting robot at Zanker Recycling
sources.developer: ZenRobotics / Plexus Recycling Technologies / Zanker Recycling (San Jose, CA)
sources.date: 2020-06 (article); install announced for the prior period
sources.title: AI-powered robotic waste sorting system installed at Zanker Recycling facility
sources.claim: AI robotic sorting of construction and demolition material is also installed in the US, at a C&D materials processing operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: US commercial recovery of useful materials from C&D debris on a conveyor line, confirming the sorting capability is deployed in the US market, not only in Europe.

sources.system: Bedrock Robotics autonomy kit on excavators
sources.title: Bedrock Robotics begins supervised autonomous excavation on live construction sites as it moves toward commercialization
sources.claim: The most advanced in-situ construction autonomy reaching live jobsites is earthmoving/mass excavation under human supervision — not razing structures or salvaging materials from them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous heavy-equipment work on an unstructured construction site. Cited to bound the state of the art — the demonstrated envelope is bulk earthmoving, with no demonstrated structure teardown, hand-tool demolition or material salvage.

sources.developer: RWTH Aachen-led EU consortium (Robotnik, Eurecat, indurad)
sources.title: Bots2ReC - Analysis of Key Findings for the Application Development of Semi-Autonomous Asbestos Removal
sources.claim: The closest research system to robotic interior strip-out — removal of asbestos-containing plaster, tiles and tile adhesive in apartment buildings — was only semi-autonomous and remained an EU research prototype rather than a fielded system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic stripping of interior building surfaces. Cited as the state of the art for interior strip-out; it is semi-autonomous, surface-removal-only, and a prototype, so it does not substantiate completing a soft-strip instance.

tasks.label: Mop, brush, or spread paints, cleaning solutions, or other compounds over surfaces to clean them or to provide protection.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interior finish work on an active commercial building site: rolling, brushing or spraying primer, paint or joint/plaster compound over drywall walls and ceilings in framed-out rooms and corridors, working around other trades, cords and stacked material, cutting in at edges and corners.

Outdoor/slab work: spreading curing compound, densifier or concrete/asphalt sealer over freshly placed or cured slabs, sidewalks, driveways and garage decks with a spray wand, roller or squeegee, in variable weather, over uneven and freshly finished surfaces.

Waterproofing and protective mastics: mopping or brushing damp-proofing, tar, bituminous or elastomeric coatings onto foundation walls, footings, planter and deck areas, roof flashing and joints, often in trenches, at heights, or in tight geometry with detail work at penetrations.

Spreading form-release oil/bond breaker on formwork panels and plywood before pours, or spreading bonding agents, adhesives, epoxy primers on surfaces before concrete or covering material is applied, at the jobsite lay-down area or in place.

Cleaning work: mopping/washing floors and slabs with cleaning solutions, degreasing or acid-etching concrete before coating, hosing and wiping down walls, glazing and fixtures during rough and final clean-up of a nearly complete building.

sources.system: Okibo EG7+ painting and drywall finishing robot
sources.title: Okibo launches autonomous, AI-guided painting and drywall finishing EG7+ robot - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7/EG7+ is a commercially launched, fully autonomous AI-guided painting and drywall-finishing robot that scans and executes without site preparation, external markers or BIM, covering ~1,000 sq ft/hour.

sources.title: Construction robotics company Okibo helping build Netflix House project - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Okibo robots were used by specialty contractor Performance Contracting Inc. to paint, sand and finish drywall on the Netflix House construction project in King of Prussia, ..., with the contractor reporting quality standards consistently met.

sources.system: Okibo autonomous plastering and painting robot
sources.title: Video | Robot decorator makes its debut - Construction Management
sources.claim: Okibo's plastering/painting robot is built to move itself over the rough, cluttered terrain of a normal construction site, mapping the space by 3D scanning without prior information.

sources.title: Canvas, World's First Robotic Drywall Finishing Company, Launches the 1200CX - Business Wire
sources.claim: Canvas's drywall finishing robots spray-apply joint compound over walls on large commercial jobsites (SFO Harvey Milk Terminal 1, UCSF, Chase Center towers), delivering Level 4/5 finishes; workers set up and supervise the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family as spreading compounds over surfaces: the machine meters and spreads a viscous compound over large wall areas on an active jobsite. Cited only as supporting context because operator involvement is not clearly bounded.

sources.title: GNSS-guided Turf Tank employed to paint stadium lines - GPS World
sources.claim: Turf Tank is an autonomous ... robot that sprays paint onto outdoor ground surfaces unattended; over 550 units are deployed across US schools, universities, parks departments and stadiums.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor paint application onto ground surfaces. It shows self-navigating, unattended coverage-path spraying of coating material outdoors on institution-controlled grounds, the same act and material class as spreading sealer/curing compound, though it lays lines rather than full-area film.

sources.system: Floor paint coating robot (ProBuild Robotics construction robot line)
sources.title: Intelligent Spraying Painting Robots for Commercial and Residential Construction – ProBuild Robotics
sources.claim: A commercially offered floor paint coating robot performs fully automatic scraping/coating of epoxy floor paint over concrete floors in underground parking lots, laboratories and dust-free workshops, with automatic navigation, feeding and mixing.

sources.title: Precast wall production | PRO Double Wall | Elematic
sources.claim: In precast concrete plants, mould tables are driven automatically through a cleaning and oiling machine that cleans the surface and applies release agent before shuttering robots place the forms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated spreading of release oil and cleaning fluid over a large flat forming surface with the work conveyed to the machine — the same act as oiling formwork or coating a panel, performed unattended in a purpose-built line.

sources.system: Avidbots Neo / Neo 2 autonomous floor scrubber
sources.title: Avidbots Designs Fully Autonomous Cleaning Robots for Airports and Hospitals - Onshape case study
sources.claim: Avidbots Neo is a fully ... that dispenses cleaning solution and scrubs floors in large commercial facilities such as airports, malls, hospitals, factories and schools; over 1,000 units deployed.
