sources.claim: BrainOS-powered Tennant T7AMR robotic scrubbers are deployed by a building-services contractor to autonomously wet-clean 58,000 sq ft daily on a polytechnic campus.

sources.title: Skyline Robotics deploys Ozmo window cleaning robot in New York City - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Skyline Robotics' Ozmo robotic arm autonomously washes exterior glass on a 45-story Manhattan office tower, supervised by a human operator on the roof rather than driven continuously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: spreading cleaning solution over building surfaces to clean them. Comparable fluid application, surface-following precision and supervised autonomy, performed on a building controlled by its management.

tasks.label: Position or dismantle forms for pouring concrete, using saws, hammers, nails, or bolts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/light-commercial footing and foundation-wall forms: on an excavated dirt pad at a house or small building site, cut 2x lumber and plywood with a circular saw, set boards to the layout string, drive and nail stakes, plumb and brace, install spreaders/ties; mud, weather, uneven grade.

Flatwork edge forms: sidewalks, curbs, driveways, patios and slabs-on-grade in streets, yards or parking lots - set and stake wood or steel edge forms to line and grade (including curves), cut and nail, check with string line and level, form isolation joints around utilities.

Modular handset/gang panel wall forms (aluminum or steel) for foundation and retaining walls: carry and align panels on a footing, drive pins and wedges, install snap ties, walers, corner locks and kickers, bolt braces - heavy panels, tight tolerances, crane or hand set.

Stripping/dismantling forms after cure: pry panels and lumber off green concrete, break snap ties, pull and denail boards, knock out stakes and bracing, scrape/clean and oil panels, stack and load for reuse or haul debris - done in place at the pour location.

Commercial elevated formwork: shoring towers/props, stringers and joists, plywood decking and edge forms for suspended slabs, plus bolted column and beam forms - assisting form carpenters at height inside a partially built structure, around rebar, MEP sleeves and other trades.

sources.system: Elematic Shuttering Robot E9 (automatic shuttering station)
sources.title: Robot for automatic shuttering in precast wall production | Elematic
sources.claim: Elematic's E9 shuttering robot is a commercial, CAD/production-plan-driven gantry robot in a fenced station of a precast wall plant that places magnetic side forms on the casting table and later demolds all shutters, including opening the magnets, plus oiling and cleaning them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: positioning and stripping the side forms (shutters) that contain a concrete pour - the same function as positioning/dismantling forms on site, with comparable objects (steel/aluminium form profiles several metres long) and dimensional accuracy, but performed in a fenced, fixtured plant station rather than on a jobsite.

sources.system: Vollert Smart Set shuttering/demolding robot line
sources.title: The Oschatz concrete plant banks on robot technology - Concrete Plant Precast Technology (BFT)
sources.claim: A Vollert Smart Set robot line installed at the Betonwerk Oschatz precast plant positions shuttering profiles of many different lengths on circulating pallets and performs demolding fully automatically under CAD/CAM control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: setting and stripping the forms that shape a concrete pour; it is the plant-floor equivalent of positioning form boards to layout and later stripping them, with transfer limited to the fixtured pallet-circulation environment.

sources.title: Formwork stripping robot enhances productivity | CPi worldwide
sources.claim: Unitechnik-automated formwork robots in precast plants set formwork down, position it precisely and fix it to the pallet with integrated magnets, and the same gantry robot, using a scanner and software, clears the formwork off the pallet after the elements are lifted.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dismantling forms after a pour - the robot removes and clears the side forms from the casting bed autonomously, the plant analogue of stripping panels and stacking them for reuse.

sources.title: Shuttering Robots for Precast Concrete Plants | Sommer Precast Technology
sources.claim: Sommer's Multi-Function-Shuttering-Robot scans the pallet, picks shuttering profiles from magazines, places longitudinal and cross shutterings, aligns them with automatic gap optimisation, activates the magnets, and later opens the magnetic fixing system and feeds dirty shutterings to the cleaning machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: positioning forms for a concrete pour and removing them afterwards at the same alignment tolerances; the environment is a purpose-built plant station with profile magazines and a pallet conveyor.

sources.system: WEINMANN FEEDBOT W-500 robot with WALLTEQ M-500 multifunction bridge
sources.title: Robot FEEDBOT W-500 | HOMAG
sources.claim: Weinmann/Homag timber-construction cells autonomously cut and fasten lumber and sheathing: the FEEDBOT W-500 robot places and fixes sheathing panels on the frame, and the WALLTEQ multifunction bridge performs sawing, drilling, stapling and nailing with an automatic tool changer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling nailed timber-and-plywood panels - the same materials, saw cuts and nail/staple fastening used to build wooden concrete forms - inside a fixtured production cell, which is what an E1 version of on-site form carpentry looks like.

sources.system: dataform.work AI-enabled formwork design and CNC fabrication service
sources.title: PERI UK launches AI-enabled custom formwork fabrication service powered by dataform.work
sources.claim: PERI UK offers a service that automates design and CNC fabrication of ..., already used on HS2 footbridge foundations; the cutting of form components is done by machine in a shop, while erection on site remains manual.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the sawing/cutting half of formwork work. It shows machine cutting of form components to project geometry is routine in a shop, while positioning and stripping on site is still done by workers.

sources.developer: ETH Zurich (NCCR Digital Fabrication) with Empa NEST
sources.title: DFAB HOUSE - dfabhouse.ch
sources.claim: The most advanced on-site concrete-forming robot, ETH Zurich's In situ Fabricator with Mesh Mould, was a one-off research demonstration at the NEST/DFAB HOUSE building that fabricated a steel mesh serving as formwork and reinforcement; it does not position or strip conventional forms.
sources.transferJustification: Closest on-site robotic evidence for concrete forming; cited to show on-site robotic work is limited to a single research building and to a formwork-free process, so it cannot substantiate conventional form setting or stripping at E2/E3.

tasks.label: Grind, scrape, sand, or polish surfaces, such as concrete, marble, terrazzo, or wood flooring, using abrasive tools or machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-field grinding/polishing of a large concrete slab in a commercial or industrial building under construction (warehouse, garage, factory shell): walk-behind or ride-on planetary grinder, multiple passes with progressively finer diamond tooling, wet/dry with dust extraction, working around columns and stacked materials.

Edge, corner, stair, doorway and around-obstacle work with handheld angle grinders, edgers and hand scrapers: perimeter strip against walls, stair nosings, closets, curbs, chipping and scraping stubborn residue, kneeling/stooped in tight spots.

Open-floor-area surface preparation in renovation: grinding/scraping off old mastic, carpet adhesive, thinset, paint or failed coatings and knocking down high spots with a walk-behind scraper or grinder before new flooring or coating.

Grinding hard concrete vertical and overhead surfaces: removing form fins, snap-tie protrusions and offsets from walls and columns, smoothing patched areas, with a handheld cup-wheel grinder on ladders or lifts.

Sanding a wood floor in a residence during renovation: drum or belt sander over the field, edger at the perimeter, buffer/screen between grits, hand sanding at corners and thresholds, then vacuuming for finish.

Honing and polishing a marble or terrazzo floor in an institutional lobby or corridor: weighted planetary machine with a diamond grit sequence, wet slurry, edges by hand, in a facility with controlled access.

sources.developer: Shenzhen Legend Robot Technology Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Automated Floor grinding & dust collection robot
sources.claim: Legend Robot's commercial Floor Grinding Robot performs autonomous, path-planned floor grinding with dust collection in underground parking garages, factory ... and sports venues, with one supervising operator; it detects columns and obstacles and claims >95% coverage (edges/perimeter remain manual).

sources.title: True Autonomy: Introducing autonomy in concrete floor polishing
sources.claim: True Autonomy's ACP-100 retrofits a commercial concrete polishing machine with LiDAR-based autonomous navigation so it covers a warehouse floor in a planned path; the company notes human crews still do the hand grinding and edge work in parallel.

sources.system: Floor grinding robot / basement glazing robot
sources.title: Autonomous Robots in Concrete Construction (Encyclopedia entry of Drones 2022, 6(12), 424)
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed review of concrete construction robots describes a deployed floor grinding robot used on epoxy/hardened floors of underground garages and workshops, and notes that a companion floor-finishing robot follows a pre-planned path but cannot work the wall edges, which must be done manually.

sources.system: DEWALT/August Robotics autonomous concrete floor drilling robot (DALE, Lionel platform)
sources.developer: DEWALT (Stanley Black & Decker) and August Robotics
sources.title: 9 weeks to 9 days: How autonomous drilling is transforming data center construction
sources.claim: DEWALT and August Robotics field autonomous mobile robots that drill thousands of anchor holes into the concrete slabs of data centers and warehouses under construction, navigating around obstructions on as-found jobsite floors; 12 robots had drilled 108,000 holes in an early-access program.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: powered contact tooling applied to building concrete floors by an autonomous mobile base on active construction sites. It substantiates that floor-processing AMRs navigate cluttered, as-found jobsite slabs at production quality, which is the environmental (not abrasive) part of large-area floor grinding.

sources.system: Canvas drywall finishing robot (1200CX, UR10e arm)
sources.title: Drywall finishing robots accelerate construction schedules (Universal Robots case story)
sources.claim: Canvas's worker-operated robot autonomously sprays and sands drywall joint compound to Level 4/5 finishes on active US construction sites, scanning each site itself without prior plans; workers handle intricate areas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine sanding of a building surface to a specified finish on an unstructured jobsite. Transfer is limited to soft joint compound on flat walls; it does not substantiate abrasive removal on cured concrete, marble or wood.

sources.title: Okibo launches autonomous, AI-guided painting and drywall finishing EG7+ robot
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7+ autonomously sands and paints walls up to 24 ft on construction sites and was used by a US contractor before its December 2025 US launch, with customers reporting large productivity gains on Level 4/5 sanding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous abrasive sanding of vertical building surfaces on construction sites. Comparable in navigation and finish inspection, but the substrate is plaster/joint compound rather than cured concrete, so it does not carry over to concrete grinding.

sources.system: Vention Rapid Series Sanding robotic cell (with 3M abrasives)
sources.title: Robotic Sanding | Vention
sources.claim: Vention's turnkey Rapid Series Sanding cell autonomously sands wood panels and cabinet doors placed on a fixture table, running operator-created recipes; woodworking customers report measured productivity gains in production use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: abrasive sanding of wood surfaces to a finish-ready quality with the workpiece fixtured and presented to the machine — the E1 form of sanding wood flooring stock, comparable material, abrasive sequence and required smoothness.

sources.title: 6 Axis Robot Arm for Stone Polishing | DINOSAW Robotic Grinder
sources.claim: DINOSAW supplies a commercial 6-axis robot arm that grinds and polishes granite, marble and other stone surfaces and edges in fabrication shops under programmed control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diamond abrasive grinding and polishing of marble/granite to a finished surface. Same materials and abrasive sequence as marble/terrazzo floor polishing and comparable hardness to concrete, with the workpiece brought to the machine (E1 presentation).

sources.system: 3M/ATI robotic sanding kit; PushCorp force-compliance sanding tools
sources.title: Robotic sanding from 3M and ATI Industrial Automation
sources.claim: 3M and ATI Industrial Automation sell a turnkey robotic sanding package (compliant orbital sander plus selected abrasives) for industrial robots, and force-compliance suppliers such as PushCorp provide devices that hold constant pressure on contoured or uneven surfaces for robotic sanding and edge finishing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: force-controlled robotic abrasive finishing of edges, corners and contoured features on fixtured workpieces inside fenced cells — the E1 counterfactual for the handheld edge/corner grinding a laborer does on site.

tasks.label: Place, consolidate, or protect case-in-place concrete or masonry structures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Slab-on-grade or interior floor slab pour at a commercial/industrial jobsite: laborers guide the pump hose or truck chute over rebar mats, chairs and embeds, pull and spread concrete with come-alongs and shovels, wet-screed or run a vibratory screed to grade, then bull-float; work moves with the truck sequence in whatever weather the day brings.

Formed structural concrete — spread footings, foundation and retaining walls, columns, grade beams, and elevated metal-deck/PT slabs: place concrete in lifts through a pump hose or bucket into congested rebar and formwork, consolidate with immersion vibrators, tap forms, watch for blowouts and cold joints, and screed the top of the pour, often working from scaffold or deck edges at height.

Small residential/site flatwork: driveway, sidewalk, curb, stoop, equipment or A/C pad. Concrete comes down the ready-mix chute onto grade between form boards; the laborer spreads it by hand, strikes off with a screed board, jitterbugs/vibrates edges, and sprays curing compound or covers it before leaving.

Protecting freshly placed concrete and masonry: spraying curing compound, laying plastic sheeting or wet burlap, spreading and weighting insulating blankets in cold weather, building wind/rain protection and heated enclosures, keeping slabs wet in hot weather, and tarping open masonry walls at the end of the day.

Masonry support work for block/brick crews: mixing and hauling mortar and grout, filling and consolidating grout in CMU cores and bond beams by bucket or grout pump with a pencil vibrator, cleaning cells and excess mortar, bracing and covering the wall.

Heavy-civil mass cementitious placement: roller-compacted concrete / cemented-fill lifts on dam, spillway or large embankment work, where material is dumped by truck, spread in lifts by dozer, and consolidated by vibratory roller with laborers directing placement and edge work.

sources.system: Vollert SMART CAST concrete spreader (MyHome Group precast plant, Jingzhou)
sources.title: MyHome Group produces semi-finished precast concrete elements for the Chinese construction boom in Jingzhou
sources.claim: Fully automatic, machine-controlled concrete spreaders dose and place fresh concrete into fixtured moulds on a precast plant's circulating pallet line, i.e. concrete placement performed entirely by machine in a purpose-built setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory casting of concrete elements. Transfer: the same physical acts — metering fresh concrete into a form to a set depth over reinforcement — are performed by machine, with the form fixtured on a pallet instead of built in the ground.

sources.system: Vollert VArio COMPACT vibrating station and VArio STORE curing chamber
sources.title: MyHome Group produces semi-finished precast concrete elements for the Chinese construction boom in Jingzhou
sources.claim: On the same automated line, consolidation is done by a vibrating station and protection/curing by an insulated, heated curing chamber served by an automated storage machine, with no human handling of the fresh concrete.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory consolidation and curing of cast concrete. Transfer: vibration to expel voids and controlled curing are the same 'consolidate' and 'protect' operations the laborer performs with an immersion vibrator, blankets and curing compound.

sources.system: Ground leveling robot (Guangdong Bojiatuo) reviewed in Drones 2022
sources.developer: Guangdong Bojiatuo Construction Technology / review by Zhao et al., Jilin University
sources.title: Autonomous Robots in Concrete Construction (Encyclopedia entry of Drones 2022, 6, 424)
sources.claim: Commercially available ground-leveling robots plan their own path by GNSS and autonomously level/consolidate freshly poured concrete floors, including residential slab-on-grade, but they act only after the concrete has been placed by others.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: screeding/leveling fresh concrete. It covers only the consolidate-and-strike-off step of the instance; the placement of the concrete itself is not performed by this machine.

sources.system: Cantilever concrete placing boom / boom pump
sources.developer: Reviewed by Zhao et al. (Drones 2022), covering Putzmeister/Liebherr-class equipment
sources.title: Autonomous Robots in Concrete Construction (Encyclopedia entry of Drones 2022, 6, 424)
sources.claim: Concrete placing booms — the machines that actually deliver and distribute fresh concrete on jobsites — are remote-controlled by a human operator rather than autonomous.

sources.system: A4CSEL (Quad Accel) automated construction system, Naruse Dam
sources.title: A⁴CSEL for DAM | Technology & Services | KAJIMA CORPORATION
sources.claim: Kajima's A4CSEL system runs fleets of automated dump trucks, bulldozers and vibratory rollers that place and compact cemented sand-and-gravel lifts around the clock at an active dam construction site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing and roller-compacting cemented fill lifts. Transfer: this is the same place-and-consolidate operation for mass cementitious material on heavy-civil work, performed autonomously in the open at a real construction site.

sources.system: ICON Vulcan printer (Wolf Ranch, Georgetown, Texas)
sources.title: Icon's 3D-printed village in Texas, US, nearing completion - Construction Briefing
sources.claim: Gantry 3D printers extrude cementitious wall material in place on residential lots at production scale, showing on-site machine placement of concrete-like material — but by a printing method that involves no formwork, no rebar-congested lifts and no vibration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-site placement of cementitious material to form walls. It substitutes for, rather than performs, the instance's formwork placement and vibratory consolidation, so it is not treated as completing those instances.

sources.title: Hadrian X bricklaying robot builds first homes in demo program - The Robot Report
sources.claim: An autonomous bricklaying robot has built complete block structures on site, including five homes in a US demonstration program, showing machine construction of masonry walls in the open.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: erecting masonry walls on site. It lays adhesive-bonded blocks; it does not mix or haul mortar, fill and vibrate grout in CMU cores, or protect green masonry, which is the laborer work in this instance.

sources.title: Robots in the Mix - Autonomous Remote Tech in Concrete Equipment | For Construction Pros
sources.claim: Laser-guided boom screeds used to strike off and consolidate slab pours are operated by a person with a remote control, with the site set up around the machine's operator.

tasks.label: Mix ingredients to create compounds for covering or cleaning surfaces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Active jobsite, outdoors: laborer mixes bagged mortar/concrete (60-80 lb bags), sand and water in a portable drum mixer or mortar tub for a mason crew or a small pour; hauls and slits bags, runs a hose, judges slump/consistency with a trowel, re-tempers, and delivers batches to the work.

Interior of a building under construction or renovation: laborer whips thinset, tile grout, or drywall joint compound in a 5-gallon bucket with a drill-mounted paddle mixer, follows bag water ratios, lets it slake, and re-tempers to the finisher's preferred consistency.

Plaster/stucco or spray-applied render: laborer sets up and feeds a mixer or continuous mixing pump (bag hopper or site silo), sets water dosing, and keeps a continuous supply of correctly mixed material going to the plastering pump/spray gun.

Surface cleaning/prep chemicals: laborer dilutes concentrates (masonry acid wash, efflorescence cleaner, degreaser, TSP) with water in buckets or a pressure-washer tank per label ratios, in PPE, at a site or in a facility being renovated.

Two-part materials: laborer proportions and mixes epoxy floor coatings, resin patching compounds or sealers by weight/volume within pot life, typically with a drill mixer, and hands the batch off for immediate application.

sources.title: Vulcan | ICON
sources.claim: ICON's Magma is an automated on-site material system that mixes the cementitious Lavacrete blend with additives and water automatically, adjusting for site weather, and supplies ready-to-print material to the Vulcan printer; material is supplied to Magma from its own reservoirs/silos rather than fetched by the machine.

sources.system: ICON Vulcan / Magma at Wolf Ranch
sources.title: World's largest 3D-printed neighborhood nears completion in Texas
sources.claim: The ICON Vulcan/Magma system has been used in real production homebuilding, printing 100 houses in the Wolf Ranch community in Georgetown, Texas, establishing that the automated mixing/delivery rig runs at real residential construction sites.

sources.system: PFT G 4 / G 4 XL mixing pump
sources.title: Knauf PFT - Mixing pump G 4 XL
sources.claim: The Knauf PFT G 4 mixing pump continuously and fully automatically mixes machine-compatible dry mortars (gypsum, lime, cement) with dosed water and pumps the finished material; it is fed by workers with bagged material or automatically from a silo/container.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class: producing plaster/mortar/render by combining dry powder ingredients and water to a working consistency; the machine performs the mixing itself once material is presented.

sources.system: m-tec mixing pumps (duo-mix / EMP class continuous mixers)
sources.title: M-TEC Mixing pumps
sources.claim: Continuous mixing pumps (m-tec type) are machines that mix dry mortar products with water automatically and continuously; they must be fed either by hand with sacked material or automatically from a silo, i.e. the ingredients are presented to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task: combining bagged/silo dry compound with water to produce plaster, render or tile-adhesive-type compounds at working consistency.

sources.title: Concrete pipe: automated and software controlled batching plant
sources.claim: Software-controlled batching plants weigh aggregates, cement and water to a stored mix design, sense aggregate moisture and automatically correct the batch water, producing concrete/mortar of specified consistency without a human judging the mix.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: proportioning cementitious ingredients and water to produce a compound at a target consistency; the plant substitutes for the laborer's water judgement using moisture probes.

sources.title: Operation ProMix 3KS Plural Component Proportioner 313885F
sources.claim: Graco electronic plural-component proportioners automatically meter and blend two- and three-component epoxy, polyurethane and catalysed coatings at a set ratio from bulk supply, delivering mixed material ready for application.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: proportioning and mixing multi-part resin/epoxy coating compounds to specification within pot life, with the components supplied to the machine from drums.

sources.system: One Solution closed-loop chemical dilution system
sources.title: One Solution - Chemical Dilution System
sources.claim: Closed-loop chemical dilution/proportioning dispensers meter concentrated cleaning chemical into water and fill the container presented at the unit, producing correctly diluted cleaning solutions without the worker judging the ratio.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: combining a concentrate with water at a specified ratio to create a compound used for cleaning surfaces; the dispensing machine performs the metering and mixing once a container is placed at it.

sources.title: Automated Dilution Ratios
sources.claim: Automated dilution equipment is standard in facility cleaning so that staff no longer estimate concentrate-to-water ratios; portable and fixed proportioning units produce measured cleaning solutions.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: creating a cleaning compound by diluting a concentrate to a specified ratio; the machine performs the proportioning and mixing.

tasks.label: Mix, pour, or spread concrete, using portable cement mixers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/small commercial site: laborer loads bagged mix, sand/gravel and water into a portable drum mixer, wheelbarrows batches to hand-dug or augered holes, pours around fence/deck/sign posts or small footings, rods/tamps to consolidate, crowns and slopes the top. Uneven ground, weather, other trades working nearby.

Small flatwork pour: sidewalk panel, stoop, patio, curb section or equipment pad. Mixer batches are placed into wood/steel forms set on grade, spread with shovel and rake, screeded to the forms, bull-floated, edged and jointed, then broomed. Access is by wheelbarrow over uneven ground; the crew works to the concrete's set time.

Interior of a building under construction: portable mixer or mixing paddle/drill used to batch mortar, grout, patching compound or self-leveling underlayment; material is carried in buckets, poured and spread/screeded over a floor area or pumped/troweled into block cores, walls and openings. Debris, partitions, stairs and other trades present.

Larger slab, footing or deck pour where most concrete arrives by truck or pump: laborer moves and spreads concrete with shovels, rakes and come-alongs, runs the vibrator, helps screed, and mixes small portable-mixer batches for blockouts, curbs, or topping off where the truck cannot reach.

Repair and patch work: mixing small batches of concrete/mortar in a portable mixer or tub to fill a spalled curb, broken sidewalk corner, pothole, pipe penetration or damaged step; placing into an irregular prepared cavity, striking off and matching the surrounding finish, often in a roadway or around an existing structure.

sources.title: Caster E9 - Elematic precast technology
sources.claim: Elematic's Caster E9 is an automatically operated casting machine that pours wet concrete into molds/side forms on a long casting bed in a precast plant, dosing to measured thickness under machine control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine placement of fresh concrete into forms. It is the same material and the same act (pouring a measured volume of wet concrete into a bounded form and levelling it) that the laborer performs by hand, done in a purpose-built plant.

sources.title: Caster E9 - Elematic precast technology
sources.claim: The same Elematic casting machine automatically consolidates the placed concrete with vibrators that raise and lower themselves over side forms, and includes a device that works the slab surface after casting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: consolidating/vibrating fresh concrete, the same rodding-and-vibrating step the laborer performs after pouring.

sources.system: Elematic Batching and Mixing Plant E9
sources.title: Batching and Mixing Plant E9 - Elematic precast technology
sources.claim: Precast batching and mixing plants mix the concrete under automatic weigh-batching and plant control as part of an automated concrete delivery system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: proportioning and mixing cement, aggregate, admixture and water. This is the mixing step of the task, performed by machine weigh-batchers and a twin-shaft mixer instead of a portable drum mixer.

sources.system: Elematic Shuttle E9 concrete distribution system
sources.title: Concrete transportation for walls | Elematic precast technology
sources.claim: Concrete is moved from the mixing plant to the casting machine fully automatically on rails in precast plants, closing the loop from mixing to placement without a human carrier.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transporting mixed concrete from the mixer to the point of placement — the wheelbarrow/bucket step of the laborer's task, automated in a plant.

sources.system: Vollert VArio SMOOTH trowelling machine and puller
sources.title: Surface technology - Vollert Precast Solutions
sources.claim: Automated precast lines finish the surface of the placed concrete by machine: a puller strikes off the surface right after concreting and a trowelling machine travels over the pallet and smooths the element.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: screeding/floating/troweling freshly placed concrete to an accepted surface — the finishing half of 'spread concrete', performed by line machines on fixtured elements.

sources.system: ICON Vulcan construction system with Magma portable mixing unit
sources.title: Texas' First 3D-Printed Homes at Wolf Ranch, TX
sources.claim: On an outdoor residential construction site (100 homes at Wolf Ranch, Georgetown TX), ICON's Magma portable cement mixing unit mixes the cementitious material automatically on site and feeds the Vulcan gantry printer, which places it under software control; the placed geometry is limited to extruded printed walls.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-site automated mixing and placement of a cement material. It shows unstructured-site mixing is automatable, but the placement is restricted to printed wall beads on a prepared slab — it cannot pour into post holes or forms, consolidate, screed or float flatwork, so it does not carry over to these instances.

sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction's Dirty Work Is Going Robotic - Architect Magazine
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile robot applies plaster/render and finishes interior surfaces on ordinary interior construction sites without site preparation, navigating by onboard 3D scanning; material is loaded into its hopper rather than batched by the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: spreading a cementitious coating on an unstructured interior construction site. It shows autonomous spreading is possible there, but it does not batch or mix material and does not place or screed concrete, so it cannot complete the mix-and-place instances.

sources.system: GNSS-guided concrete ground leveling robot (Bright Dream Robotics class)
sources.developer: Bright Dream Robotics (Country Garden) / reviewed in MDPI
sources.title: Application and Development of Autonomous Robots in Concrete Construction: Challenges and Opportunities
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed review of concrete-construction robots describes a GNSS-guided ground leveling robot that plans its own path and levels placed concrete autonomously; the machine covers only the leveling step and is a research/limited-deployment system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: spreading/levelling concrete already placed on a slab. It substantiates only the levelling sub-step on large open floors; it does not mix, transport or place concrete, nor work around forms, posts and small pours.

tasks.label: Operate jackhammers or drills to break up concrete or pavement.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Street/roadway work zone: laborer saw-cuts and then breaks out asphalt or concrete pavement with a pneumatic/hydraulic breaker (60-90 lb jackhammer or excavator-mounted hammer) to open a utility cut, patch, or valve box, under traffic control, over live buried utilities, then breaks the slab into haulable pieces.

Exterior flatwork demolition on residential/commercial/municipal property: breaking up sidewalk panels, curb and gutter, driveways, patios and steps with a handheld breaker, working around fences, trees, landscaping, adjacent slabs to be preserved, and pedestrians.

Interior/structural demolition inside an occupied or gutted building: jackhammering a slab-on-grade to open a plumbing trench, chipping out concrete around embeds, breaking walls/curbs/housekeeping pads in confined space, with dust control, tight access, and hand-carried debris.

Excavation and foundation work on an active construction site: breaking concrete obstructions, old footings, encased ducts, or rock ledge in the bottom of a trench or pit, often standing in the excavation next to shoring and exposed utilities.

Drilling hole patterns in concrete or pavement with rotary hammers/rock drills: dowel and anchor holes, holes for expansive agents or stitch-drilling to split a slab, holes for rebar dowels in a pavement patch, laid out to a plan and drilled to specified depth.

Bridge deck, parking deck, or structural concrete repair: removing deteriorated concrete from a marked area down to sound concrete and around/behind reinforcing steel without damaging the rebar, on a closed-off deck work zone.

sources.system: Normet Xrock Autobreaker (breaker boom + autonomous module)
sources.title: Normet Xrock Launches the World's First Fully Autonomous Rock-Breaking System, Xrock Autobreaker
sources.claim: Normet Xrock Autobreaker is a commercially available autonomous rock-breaking module for fixed breaker-boom installations that identifies, targets and breaks oversize material presented at a crusher grizzly with a hydraulic hammer, with no person in the breaking area.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hydraulic-hammer breaking of oversize rock/lumps presented to a fixed breaker station. Same tool class (hydraulic impact hammer) and same physical action as breaking concrete; concrete lumps and rock are comparable targets for a boom breaker, and the material is brought to the machine, matching an E1 presentation.

sources.system: Autonomous rock-breaking system with real-time 3D visual perception (Lampinen et al., Tampere University)
sources.title: Enhancing 3D Rock Localization in Mining Environments Using Bird's-Eye View Images from the Time-of-Flight Blaze 101 Camera
sources.claim: A research breaker boom fitted with a stereo-vision perception system broke rocks autonomously on a grizzly, detecting and localizing irregular targets in real time and driving an industrial hydraulic manipulator to strike them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous impact-hammer breaking of hard material presented to a fixed manipulator. Peer-reviewed confirmation that perception-driven, unscripted hammer breaking of presented lumps works, transferring to concrete pieces fixtured/presented in a purpose-built breaker cell.

sources.title: Hydrodemolition Equipment | Conjet
sources.claim: Conjet ACR hydrodemolition robots remove concrete to a programmed depth and shape: the operator positions the machine and enters parameters, after which the robot performs the concrete removal autonomously while the operator supervises from 5-10 m away.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic concrete removal by high-pressure water instead of a jackhammer. Same accepted output (deteriorated concrete broken out to sound concrete/specified depth on a deck or structure), same worksite; Conjet markets it explicitly as an alternative to mechanical jackhammering.

sources.title: Maximize Hydrodemolition Productivity For Bridge Repair Applications With These 3 Attachments
sources.claim: Hydrodemolition robots are standard equipment for road and bridge repair concrete removal in the US, used by contractors on DOT bridge deck rehabilitation to strip deteriorated concrete from decks, parapets, abutments and piers.
sources.transferJustification: Supporting deployment evidence that robotic concrete removal is accepted at worker quality on real US bridge/road repair work zones; autonomy for the removal cycle is established separately by the Conjet item.

sources.title: Jaibot Drilling Robot - Hilti USA
sources.claim: The Hilti Jaibot is a commercially sold semi-autonomous mobile drilling robot that locates itself on a jobsite from a total station and BIM data and then drills all overhead holes in concrete within its range autonomously, with dust removal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: rotary-hammer drilling of hole patterns in structural concrete on an active construction site. Same material, same tool class and hole tolerances as laborers' dowel/anchor/stitch drilling; only the drilling direction differs.

sources.system: DALE downward drilling robot (DEWALT + August Robotics AMR)
sources.title: 9 weeks to 9 days: How autonomous drilling is transforming data center construction - The Robot Report
sources.claim: DEWALT and August Robotics launched DALE, an autonomous mobile drilling robot that reads the drilling plan and drills thousands of anchor holes into concrete jobsite floors; it ran a year-long pilot and became commercially available on 9 July 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drilling plan-specified hole patterns downward into a concrete slab on an active construction site, the same action and accuracy class as a laborer drilling dowel/anchor/stitch holes in slabs and pavement.

sources.title: Brokk Reveals New Robots, Equipment for All-Electric Demolition | Equipment World
sources.claim: The demolition machines actually used to break concrete on jobsites and in interior demolition are remote-controlled by an operator, not autonomous.

sources.title: Roadwork Robot Autonomously Digs Out, Repairs, Buried Utility Lines | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: ULC Technologies' RRES prototype cut and removed a road-surface core and vacuum-excavated a keyhole to a buried utility largely hands-off, taking about 45 minutes to cut and remove a core, with operators still needed to change end-effectors; live field trials followed on SGN's UK gas network.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic opening of a road surface for a utility excavation. Shows the closest available autonomous street-pavement work, but by chainsaw coring of a small keyhole rather than breaking out a pavement section.

tasks.label: Apply caulking compounds by hand or caulking guns to protect against entry of water or air.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interior finish caulking on an active jobsite: sealing gaps around door and window casings, trim, base, and drywall-to-frame joints before paint. Worker moves room to room, works off ladders or stilts, cuts nozzle tips, guns a bead into varied gap widths and tools it smooth; other trades, dust and clutter present.

Exterior building-envelope joint sealing: caulking vertical/horizontal joints between precast or metal panels, brick-to-window and curtain-wall perimeters. Includes cleaning/priming the joint, installing backer rod, masking, gunning the sealant and tooling it, working from swing stage, scaffold or boom lift in outdoor weather.

Wet-area and fixture caulking during finish-out: tubs, showers, sinks, countertops, tile-to-fixture and corner joints. Confined bathroom/kitchen spaces, awkward reaches, silicone bead must be uniform and tooled to a visually clean, watertight finish.

Horizontal joint sealing at grade on site: control and expansion joints in slabs, sidewalks, curbs, parking decks and pavement. Clean/blow out the joint, insert backer rod, gun self-leveling sealant along long runs, outdoors with traffic or equipment nearby.

Weatherproofing penetrations, flashings and rough openings during envelope work: sealing pipe and conduit penetrations, sill pans, sheathing seams and air-barrier laps, roof flashing edges, sole plates. Irregular geometries, overhead and kneeling positions, sealant often combined with tape or flashing membrane.

Shop/prefab setting: applying sealant beads inside a panel plant, precast yard, modular or bath-pod factory - e.g. bedding a window unit into a wall panel or sealing a panel perimeter on a bench or moving line, under cover with staged materials.

sources.system: FANUC LR Mate 200iD / CRX dispensing-sealing robots (with Graco PCF metering)
sources.title: Dispensing and Sealing Robots and Cobots | FANUC America
sources.claim: Commercially deployed FANUC industrial robots and cobots dispense silicone, urethane and seam sealer beads onto fixtured parts in production cells, with laser checks and part/nest detection ensuring accurate bead placement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial sealant/adhesive bead dispensing. It is the same physical act as caulking - extruding a viscous silicone or urethane sealant from a gun along a joint at a controlled bead size - on comparable joint geometries, but with the workpiece fixtured in a cell.

sources.system: Encore Automation robotic sealing systems (interior seam sealing, underbody sealer)
sources.title: Robotic Sealing Applications | Encore Automation
sources.claim: Production robotic seam-sealing systems apply sealant beads over joints specifically to achieve water resistance, in automotive body plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic seam sealing. The purpose matches the caulking task - a gunned sealant bead over a joint to block water entry - and the beads are applied to seams of comparable width and length inside a fenced line cell.

sources.system: KUKA automated sealing and damping system
sources.title: Kuka showcases new fully automated sealing and damping system at Audi
sources.claim: A fully automated robotic sealing and damping (adhesive/sealant application) system was engineered and commissioned for series body-in-white production at Audi.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: body-in-white sealing. Same action of laying continuous sealant beads along seams to seal against water and air, performed unattended in a purpose-built robotic line.

sources.developer: Robotiz3d / University of Liverpool / Hertfordshire County Council
sources.title: Hertfordshire County Council: AI road maintenance robot | Local Government Association
sources.claim: A mobile robot autonomously detected road cracks and filled them with sealing material to stop water ingress in the first public-road trial, but the pilot repaired only a small number of cracks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pavement crack sealing - dispensing sealant into a crack/joint to keep water out. Closest analogue to horizontal joint caulking in an unstructured outdoor setting, but the source records a prototype pilot that fixed only a small number of cracks.

sources.system: Robotic Maintenance Vehicle (FANUC-powered road sealing system)
sources.title: Dispensing and Sealing Robots and Cobots | FANUC America
sources.claim: A truck-mounted FANUC robot scans and fills road cracks with sealant, operated from the truck cab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pavement crack sealing. Shows sealant-gun automation moved out of the plant, but the description places an operator in the cab ... the degree of autonomy is not established, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: A fully autonomous, AI-guided mobile robot performs plastering, drywall finishing and painting alongside workers on active construction sites, with over a million square feet covered in Europe and a US launch in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous application of a wet compound to walls on an unstructured jobsite. It shows site-navigating coating robots exist, but it sprays and screeds broad flat surfaces rather than gunning and tooling a sealant bead into a joint, so it does not substantiate caulking at E3.

sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction's Dirty Work Is Going Robotic - Architect Magazine
sources.claim: Drywall finishing robots working on commercial construction sites apply joint compound over seams but are described as semi-autonomous, working alongside human crews.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying compound along drywall seams on an active site. The nearest jobsite analogue for filling a linear joint, but it is operator-assisted and coats flat seams rather than sealing perimeter joints against water and air, so it cannot support a positive E3 judgment.

tasks.label: Tend machines that pump concrete, grout, cement, sand, plaster, or stucco through spray guns for application to ceilings or walls.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Exterior stucco/render work on a house or low-rise commercial building: laborer sets up and tends the mixer-pump rig, dumps bags of stucco mix and sand, keeps water and pressure right, drags and clears the hose, and runs the spray gun to lay scratch and brown coats on lath-covered walls from the ground and from scaffold; unclogs the line and washes out the pump at the end.

Interior spray of plaster, veneer coat, joint compound or wall/ceiling texture inside a building under construction: laborer feeds and tends the texture/plaster pump, keeps the hopper full, sprays walls and ceilings room by room, masks and protects openings, and cleans the gun and hoses.

Shotcrete/gunite outdoors on a pool shell, retaining wall, basement wall or slope: laborer tends the gunite rig (feeds dry mix or charges the wet-mix pump, sets air and water), handles and repositions the heavy hose behind the nozzleman or runs the nozzle, blows out clogs, and cleans the machine.

Shotcrete lining in a tunnel, shaft, culvert or bridge repair: laborer tends the pump/sprayer and accelerator dosing, keeps concrete supplied to the machine, manages hoses in a confined wet heading, and cleans equipment; nozzle work by boom manipulator or hand-held lance.

Spray-applied cementitious fireproofing (SFRM) on structural steel beams, columns and metal deck in a steel-frame building under construction: laborer mixes and tends the pump, keeps the mixer fed with bagged material and water, moves hoses up floors, sprays overhead beams and deck from a lift or scaffold, and cleans out the rig.

instances.label: Highway/street hot-mix paving: keeping the paver hopper supplied on a live job site. Aggregate spreading (chip seal, stone spreader, shoulder widener, base material): the spreader hopper is filled by dump trucks on the roadway or lot, usually hitched to or pushed by the spreader and dumping while moving; dusty, uneven surfaces, open road conditions.

Loading small machines and packaged materials in the field: charging a crack-seal melter kettle with boxed sealant blocks, shoveling or bucket-loading cold patch into a small paver or hopper, dumping bags of sand/additive into a sealcoat mixer, filling striping paint tanks.

tasks.label: Control paving machines to push dump trucks and to maintain a constant flow of asphalt or other material into hoppers or screeds.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mainline highway/interstate hot-mix asphalt overlay or new lane construction in a closed work zone: the operator advances the paver at a steady speed, keeps the push rollers in contact with end-dump/belly-dump trucks that back in and discharge into the hopper, manages hopper wings, conveyor and auger feed to hold a constant head of material at the screed, and paces truck exchanges so the mat is never starved or stopped.

High-specification, high-production paving (interstate mainline, airport runway/taxiway rebuild, multi-layer full-width work) where a material transfer vehicle or a second paver in echelon sits between trucks and the paver: operator maintains continuous, non-segregating flow into the hopper/screed, coordinates with the MTV operator, and keeps head of material constant across a very wide screed under strict smoothness/density specs, often at night.

Municipal street or county road mill-and-overlay: paver works half-width under live traffic or night closures, feeding from tandem dump trucks in short passes, past curbs, manholes, driveways, intersections and utility structures, with frequent stops, starts and truck exchanges in a confined lane.

Small commercial and residential work with an 8-10 ft class paver: parking lots, driveways, apartment complexes, trench and patch overlays. Irregular lot geometry with islands, curbs and light poles, very frequent truck exchanges in tight quarters, short runs, and a hand crew raking and shoveling right at the machine while the operator meters material into hopper and augers.

Chip seal / aggregate surfacing: self-propelled chip spreader hitched to and pushing a haul truck along a rural road, operator matching spread rate and speed to the distributor truck and maintaining continuous aggregate flow from the truck bed into the spreader hopper.

Concrete paving: slipform paver on a roadway or airfield slab fed by ready-mix trucks discharging in front of the machine (or by a placer/spreader), operator maintaining a constant head of concrete ahead of the pan/screed and pacing truck discharge to keep the machine moving without a cold joint.

tasks.label: Observe distribution of paving material to adjust machine settings or material flow, and indicate low spots for workers to add material.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mainline highway/interstate asphalt overlay or new lift: operator rides the screed of a full-width paver in a coned-off work zone, watching the head of material in front of the screed and the mat behind it, adjusting feed-sensor/auger and conveyor settings, screed angle of attack, crown and tow points to hold thickness and slope, and pointing out low or torn spots for rakers.

Parking lots, aprons, driveways and paths with a small/compact paver: short irregular passes, hand-fed corners and edges, tie-ins to existing pavement; operator judges mat thickness and material spread largely by eye, adjusts auger/conveyor feed and screed settings, and directs laborers to add or rake material in deficient spots.

Concrete paving: slipform paver or placer/spreader laying slab, curb-and-gutter or barrier; operator watches the head of concrete in front ... mold/spreader and the surface leaving the machine, adjusts spreader augers, paver speed and grade/steer settings, and calls for more concrete or hand placement where the surface comes up short.

Chip seal / surface treatment / aggregate and base spreading on rural roads and shoulders: operator watches aggregate coverage or spread thickness behind the chip spreader or stone spreader, adjusts gate openings and application rate, and flags bare or thin areas for hand spreading and re-rolling.

Airport runway/taxiway or large industrial paving under night closure: wide, echelon-paved uniform mats to tight smoothness/thickness tolerance, usually with 3D or stringless screed control; operator monitors material head and mat surface, adjusts settings, and marks deficient areas for the hand crew.

Hot-mix asphalt haul: operator drives a dump truck to the asphalt plant, loads under the silo, drives loaded over public roads to the paving operation, backs up to the paver or material transfer vehicle in the moving work zone, dumps into the hopper, and returns to the plant.

Aggregate, base rock, sand or emulsion haul: truck loaded at a quarry, stockpile or yard, hauled over public and site haul roads to the job, and dumped at a stockpile, into a spreader/chip box, or in a windrow for the grader/spreader.

Pickup or flatbed run: driving a company pickup/one-ton flatbed loaded with cold patch, sealer, tack, signs, plate compactors and hand tools from the yard to a municipal, commercial or residential job and back, parking within the work zone or at the curb.

tasks.label: Inspect, clean, maintain, and repair equipment, using mechanics' hand tools, or report malfunctions to supervisors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-shift cleaning of the asphalt-contact surfaces of a paver or material transfer vehicle at the paving site: scraping and wiping hardened mix off the hopper wings, conveyor tunnels and flight bars, augers, screed plates, endgates and push rollers while components are still warm, then spraying release agent over those surfaces so the machine is ready for the next shift.

General washdown of equipment exteriors at the yard or jobsite: hosing/pressure-washing dust, mud and tack splatter off the tractor body, undercarriage, tracks or tires, roller drums and drum scrapers; done daily as a rinse and at least twice a month as a full wash-down of the machine.

Pre-shift (and post-shift) walkaround inspection of the paver, roller or tamper with defect reporting: checking engine oil/hydraulic/coolant levels, looking for leaks, cracked hoses, damaged or worn tracks, tires, screed plates and belts, checking lights and safety devices, recording findings on an inspection sheet and reporting problems to the foreman or shop.

Daily lubrication and fluid service in the field: greasing auger and conveyor fittings mid-shift and end-of-shift while the machine is hot, topping off hydraulic and engine oil and coolant, adding fuel and DEF from the service truck, filling the roller's water tank, and cleaning or replacing clogged water spray nozzles and filters.

Mid-shift troubleshooting and minor repair with mechanics' hand tools at the paving site: unclogging a spray bar, replacing a broken bolt, screed plate section or auger segment, swapping a burst hydraulic hose, adjusting conveyor/drag chain tension, reseating a grade sensor or ski — or, when beyond the operator, diagnosing the fault and reporting it to the supervisor or field mechanic to get the machine running again.

Scheduled preventive maintenance and larger repairs at the contractor's shop or equipment yard: engine oil and filter changes, hydraulic filter service, full greasing, belt and drive-chain replacement, replacing worn screed plates and wear parts, torquing fasteners, working with or alongside the shop mechanic on a parked machine.

instances.label: Mainline highway/interstate asphalt paving or resurfacing inside a closed work zone: operator runs a highway-class paver over long pulls (often echelon or full-width), holding thickness, cross-slope and mat texture, controlling the material head, stopping and restarting for truck exchanges, with rollers following behind.

Concrete pavement work: running a slipform paver on mainline pavement, ramps, or an airport taxiway — placing and consolidating PCC to line and grade with dowel baskets/tie bars, screeding and finishing behind the machine.
Steel reinforcement work on paving/bridge-deck placements: setting and tying rebar mats, dowels and tie bars over the prepared bed or deck ahead of the concrete pour.

tasks.label: Light burners or start heating units of machines, and regulate screed temperatures and asphalt flow rates.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mainline highway/interstate paving or mill-and-fill with a full-size highway-class paver: at shift start the operator energizes electric screed heaters or lights propane/diesel screed burners and brings the screed to working temperature, then through the shift holds screed temperature and continuously regulates conveyor/auger (head-of-material) flow as trucks or an MTV feed the hopper. Day or night, live traffic alongside, milled surface, variable width.

Municipal/residential street resurfacing with a mid-size paver: screed heat-up at the yard or on site, then frequent stops for driveways, utility castings, tapers and width changes, requiring repeated re-balancing of flow gates, conveyor and auger speeds to keep a consistent head of material and avoid screed cool-down during waits.

Commercial parking lot, driveway or shoulder work with a commercial-class paver (8-10 ft class), usually propane-burner or electric screed heat lit by the operator; small tonnages, tight maneuvering, short pulls, frequent restarts, hand-work crews at the endgates.

Airport runway, taxiway or large industrial pad paving under a night closure to tight smoothness/temperature specification, often echelon paving with two pavers and MTVs; screed preheat before the closure window and tight control of screed temperature and material flow to avoid segregation and cold joints.

Small-scale repair and maintenance work: lighting burners / starting heating units on an asphalt distributor tank, joint heater, infrared patcher or small paving box, bringing the material or plate to working temperature and holding it while applying material to a patch or seal.

Late-season, cold, windy or thin-lift paving where mix arrives near the lower temperature limit: the operator runs screed heat harder, keeps a full head of material and adjusts flow to avoid tearing and rapid mat cool-down.

tasks.label: Control traffic.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine flagging of alternating one-lane, two-way traffic through a stationary lane closure on a rural or suburban two-lane road being resurfaced: steady, moderate traffic, coordination with the flagger at the far end or with a pilot car, holding and releasing platoons for minutes at a time.

Flagging under interactive conditions on a street or arterial paving job: repeatedly stopping the public to let loaded haul trucks, the paver, and rollers cross into and out of the closed lane, admitting residents and side-street/driveway traffic, waving through emergency vehicles, dealing with drivers who ignore the paddle, and hand-signalling individual motorists.

Establishing and removing the temporary traffic control zone on a street or highway: setting out and later picking up advance warning signs, cones, drums, and barricades along a taper and buffer, on the live roadway with traffic passing, and repositioning devices as the paving train advances.

Traffic control for a moving/slow-rolling operation on a higher-speed highway (chip seal, crack seal, striping, patching): driving/positioning the shadow vehicle with truck-mounted attenuator and arrow board at the correct buffer behind the work convoy, keeping the rolling closure intact as the operation advances.

Paving a commercial parking lot, driveway, or apron: coning off the fresh mat, redirecting customer vehicles and delivery trucks around the work, and waving pedestrians away from hot asphalt in a layout that differs at every site.

Paving on access-controlled premises (airport taxiway/apron, military base, industrial plant, campus): controlling authorized vehicle movement through gates and single-lane sections around the closed area under an escort/permit protocol, with no general public present.

instances.label: Mainline street/highway paving: operator hand-shovels hot mix (~300F) from the paver hopper/auger area or truck tailgate to feed the ends of the screed and fill low spots and joints in the fresh mat, in a live work zone with traffic control, moving trucks and rollers.

Handwork around obstructions and tie-ins: shovelling hot mix around manhole frames, valve boxes, catch basins, curb-and-gutter lines, driveway aprons and cold joints the paver cannot reach, placing small measured amounts that a raker then lutes to grade.

Small commercial/residential jobs (parking lots, driveways, alleys): shovelling mix out of the truck bed or from dumped piles onto hand-laid areas, edges and around islands and light bases, on varied, sloping, obstacle-strewn surfaces.
Pothole, utility-cut and pavement patch repair: shovelling hot or cold mix from a patch truck body into a prepared, cleaned hole in a street, crowning the material, then tamping or rolling it.

Cleanup: shovelling spilled, cold or leftover blacktop off the roadway, gutter and around the paver/rollers, and out of the hopper or truck bed, back into the truck or a low area at the end of a run or shift.

It shares the material (hot mix), the required output (mix placed to specified depth in a defined area) and the tolerance of hand-shovelled mix, so it substantiates the shovelling step when the material and the work are presented to the machine, though not the free-form handwork a paver cannot reach.

tasks.label: Operate tamping machines or manually roll surfaces to compact earth fills, foundation forms, and finished road materials, according to grade specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mainline highway/expressway resurfacing or widening: operator runs a double-drum vibratory or pneumatic roller in the breakdown/intermediate/finish sequence directly behind the paver in a closed-lane work zone, matching paver speed, staying on rolling pattern and mat temperature window, and hitting density/smoothness acceptance specs over long uniform lane-width runs.

Earthwork lift compaction: ride-on smooth-drum or padfoot vibratory soil compactor making planned passes over subgrade, embankment fill, or aggregate base for a roadway, building pad, or subdivision, over open ground with changing terrain and moisture, working to grade stakes/3D model and pass-count or density spec.

Urban street, arterial, parking lot, driveway and small commercial asphalt rolling: small tandem roller in tight geometry with curbs, gutters, islands, manhole and valve castings, driveway tie-ins, joints against existing pavement, adjacent live traffic and parked cars, and crew members working the edges by hand.

Confined and small-area compaction: walk-behind roller, vibratory plate, or jumping-jack rammer used to compact trench backfill over pipe, utility cut patches, backfill against foundation forms and abutments, curb and sidewalk subbase, and around structures where a ride-on machine cannot reach.

Large open compaction on major restricted-access earthwork: airport runway/taxiway subgrade and base, dam or levee embankment lifts, landfill cells, large industrial pads — big machines, long uniform passes, high-volume placement, tight lift-thickness and pass-count control.

tasks.label: Operate oil distributors, loaders, chip spreaders, dump trucks, and snow plows.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hauling with a dump truck on a paving job: loading hot-mix asphalt or aggregate at the plant, driving public roads to the job, backing into the paver hopper or MTV and dumping, or end-dumping millings/base rock in a live work zone with crew, traffic control and flaggers present.

Operating an oil (asphalt) distributor truck: heating and circulating emulsion, setting spray-bar height/nozzle angle, calibrating and applying a metered tack, prime or chip-seal binder shot over a street, highway lane, ramp or parking lot ahead of the paver or chip spreader, hand-wanding edges and joints.

Running a self-propelled chip spreader in a chip-seal train on a rural or county road: taking aggregate from haul trucks backing into the hopper, spreading cover stone at the specified rate immediately behind the distributor, holding line and speed ahead of the rollers, with traffic and crew nearby.

Operating a front-end loader in an asphalt plant yard, aggregate stockpile area or municipal yard: loading haul trucks, feeding cold-feed bins/hoppers, blending and rehandling RAP and aggregate piles, loading salt/sand in winter.

Operating a loader or skid steer on the active paving site: moving base material, cleaning up and loading millings and debris into trucks, feeding shouldering/patch work, maneuvering among the crew, parked equipment and passing traffic.

Winter snow plowing: driving a plow-equipped dump truck on public streets/highways clearing lanes and spreading salt/sand during storms, or plowing large lots and airfield pavements, in low visibility with parked cars, pedestrians and other vehicles present.

sources.title: Scaling a Proven Autonomy System to Support New Industries
sources.claim: Caterpillar's MineStar Command for hauling runs a fleet of autonomous Cat 777 off-highway trucks at Luck Stone's Bull Run quarry, hauling load-to-dump cycles at productivity matching staffed trucks.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class as dump-truck hauling on a paving job: loading at a stockpile/face, hauling a defined route, and reversing to dump at a designated point; same vehicle class (off-highway rigid dump truck) and same bulk material.

tasks.label: Place strips of material, such as cork, asphalt, or steel into joints, or place rolls of expansion-joint material on machines that automatically insert material.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mainline concrete paving (highway lane, airport taxiway): placing steel dowel bars / tie bars or pre-assembled dowel baskets at transverse and longitudinal joints as the slipform paver advances, to DOT alignment and depth tolerances, in the open, in traffic-adjacent work zones.

Placing preformed expansion-joint filler strips (asphalt-impregnated fiber, cork, sponge rubber board) along forms, curb lines and slab edges before concrete placement on a street, parking lot or apron job: measuring, cutting board to length, seating it flush and staking it upright on uneven subgrade.

Placing asphalt joint material along an asphalt paving longitudinal/transverse construction joint: unrolling and pressing self-adhesive joint tape or laying hot-poured joint adhesive strip on the vertical cold-joint face ahead of the paver, on a hot, dusty, open roadway.

Loading and threading rolls/reels of expansion-joint or joint-sealing material onto the machine that automatically inserts or feeds it (paver-mounted joint inserter, tape applicator wheel, sealing-strip dispenser): lifting the roll onto the spindle, feeding the leading end, splicing to the running material and clearing jams.

Fitting strip material into joints at irregular, congested locations: around manholes, drainage structures, light bases, ramp tie-ins, sidewalk/curb returns and hand-work patch repairs, where the strip must be cut, notched and hand-fitted to shapes that differ at every location.

sources.date: product in field since 1990s; page retrieved 2026-07
sources.title: GOMACO, Manufacturer of Concrete Slipform Paving Equipment: IDBI Dowel Bar Inserter
sources.claim: GOMACO's IDBI is a commercially deployed paver attachment that automatically inserts steel dowel bars into transverse joints of a concrete slab during paving on highway and airport jobsites, with a computer control system managing joint spacing, insertion timing and depth.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: this is the placement of steel into pavement joints, performed by machine on the paving train instead of by hand-set dowel baskets; accuracy is held to DOT bar-location and rideability specifications.

sources.title: Step By Step - Independent IDBI Attachment
sources.claim: The IDBI's bar handling is machine-fed: a bar loading trolley automatically distributes a dowel bar into each insertion tray across the paving width before the forks insert them, so the placement cycle does not require a worker to hand-place each bar.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that material feeding as well as insertion is automated, so the steel-into-joint instance is completed with only periodic bar restocking rather than continuous manual feeding.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing a continuous compliant sealing strip along a defined seam/groove of a workpiece. sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading a heavy roll of web material onto a machine that automatically feeds/inserts it, including orientation, threading and splicing — the same operation as placing a roll of expansion-joint material on an automatic inserting machine, done in a purpose-built machine environment.

tasks.label: Drive and operate curbing machines to extrude concrete or asphalt curbing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Slipform curb-and-gutter along new streets in a residential or commercial subdivision: operator sets the mould, aligns to stringline or a 3D model, drives the machine hundreds to thousands of feet on prepared subgrade, judges mix slump as ready-mix trucks and a loader keep the hopper fed, handles radii at intersections and driveways, and watches for slumping or blowouts.

Curb, islands and radii in a parking lot or commercial site with a compact curb machine: short runs, tight radii, work threaded around existing pavement, light poles, stored materials, other trades and sometimes moving vehicles.
Curb, gutter, median or barrier along a live roadway under lane closures and traffic control, often at night, to DOT line-and-grade tolerance with inspection.
Extruded hot-mix asphalt curbing around a parking lot perimeter or drainage berm with a small asphalt curbing machine, following the existing pavement edge.

Short runs, repairs and tie-ins: replacing damaged curb sections, curb ramps, driveway transitions and matching into existing inlets and pavement, with heavy hand-forming and finishing around the machine work.

sources.system: Wirtgen AutoPilot 2.0 on SP 15i/SP 25i slipform pavers (curbs, barriers, traffic islands)

sources.claim: State of the art for on-site slipform curb machines is 3D stringless machine guidance: GNSS automatically controls steering and cross-slope, but a trained operator must still run the machine and a ground crew works around it.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task (extruding concrete curb with a slipform curbing machine); it shows automation of steering and grade only, with an operator required, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment on a jobsite.
