tasks.label: Operate machines that clean or cut expansion joints in concrete or asphalt and that rout out cracks in pavement.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Highway/state-route crack sealing prep: operator runs a self-propelled random-crack router (or walk-behind router/saw) along transverse and longitudinal cracks in an asphalt or concrete lane inside a lane-closure work zone, following the crack's irregular path, holding reservoir width/depth, working around patches, manholes, rumble strips, and passing traffic, then blows the routed crack clean with air/heat lance before the seal crew follows.

Sawing contraction/expansion joints in freshly placed concrete paving (mainline pavement, ramps, intersections, bridge approach slabs): operator runs an early-entry or wet joint saw along stringlines/chalk marks within the green-concrete timing window, matching depth (T/4) and alignment, on a live paving project with changing weather and concrete set times.

Rehabilitation of existing joints on roads and bridge decks: operator re-saws/refaces the joint reservoir, removes old sealant with a plow/router, and cleans the joint with a saw-clean pass, air-blast, or sandblast head before resealing, in a work zone on in-service pavement of varying condition.

Airport airside pavement work during a night closure: operator saws and cleans runway/taxiway joints or routs cracks on PCC pavement to airfield spec, working under escort inside the secured airfield with hard time limits to reopen the surface before the morning bank.

Small commercial/municipal jobs: routing cracks and saw-cutting joints in parking lots, city streets, driveways, and industrial aprons, with tight quarters, curbs, islands, parked cars, utility covers, and irregular crack patterns; frequent machine repositioning and hand-guided passes.

sources.title: Precast concrete saw E9 | Elematic
sources.claim: Elematic's Saw E9 is a commercially sold machine that automatically saw-cuts hardened precast concrete slabs (hollow core, massive slabs, piles, T-beams) up to 500 mm ... at any angle on a precast plant production line, with slab data imported to the on-board control system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated diamond-blade cutting of concrete slabs at planned positions. It is the same physical operation as cutting a joint in concrete pavement (same material, same blade technology, comparable straightness/depth tolerance); it substantiates only the purpose-built case, where the slab is presented to the machine on a casting bed.

sources.title: Automatic hollow core machine Modifier E9 - Elematic precast technology
sources.claim: Elematic's Modifier E9 automatically cuts openings and recesses into fresh (green) concrete slabs on a hollow-core production line, running from production plans transferred wirelessly and locating the slab with a laser positioning system; it is in operation at plants such as Contiga in Norway.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled cutting into fresh concrete at plan-specified locations. Cutting a joint in green concrete is the same operation (same material state, same timing window, plan-defined geometry), demonstrated only where the slab is presented to the machine in a purpose-built line.

sources.system: Kane Robotics GRIT with AI vision system
sources.title: GRIT Vision System applies AI to Kane Robotics' cobot weld grinding - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Kane Robotics' GRIT vision system lets its collaborative grinding robot automatically find and follow weld seams and grind them, an irregular linear feature located by vision rather than by fixed program, in a manufacturing cell; deployed at a customer fabricator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided material removal along an irregular line whose path is not known in advance. Routing a crack is the same control problem (detect the line on the workpiece, drive a cutting tool along it at set depth); the demonstration is in a fixtured shop cell, so it supports only the purpose-built tier.

sources.system: Automated Crack Sealing Machine (ACSM) / Operator Controlled Crack Sealing Machine
sources.developer: AHMCT Center, UC Davis with Caltrans
sources.title: ROBOTIC MACHINE FOR HIGHWAY CRACK SEALING - TRID
sources.claim: The AHMCT/Caltrans Automated Crack Sealing Machine mapped random pavement cracks by machine vision, prepared the pavement surface and sealed cracks from a single truck on highway pavement, with a human operator acting as driver and decision-maker; it remained a research prototype and was not commercialized.
sources.transferJustification: Same work family (crack preparation and sealing on highway pavement), but the operator drives and supervises continuously and the machine never went beyond field prototype, so it cannot support a positive judgment on its own.

sources.developer: Robotiz3d / University of Liverpool with Hertfordshire County Council
sources.title: Hertfordshire County Council: AI road maintenance robot | Local Government Association
sources.claim: Robotiz3d's ARRES PREVENT prototype autonomously detects cracks on public roads and deposits sealant into them; it completed its first live road test in Potters Bar, Hertfordshire in 2024 and remained in trials ahead of production. It does not rout, saw, or clean joints.
sources.transferJustification: Closest in-setting system (public roadway crack work), but it performs sealant deposition, not the routing, saw-cutting, or joint-cleaning that this task consists of, and it is a pilot prototype, so it does not substantiate completion of these instances.

sources.developer: DEWALT (Stanley Black & Decker) with August Robotics
sources.title: 9 weeks to 9 days: How autonomous drilling is transforming data center construction - The Robot Report
sources.claim: DEWALT and August Robotics launched DALE commercially in July 2026: an autonomous mobile robot that reads hole positions from building CAD plans and drills into concrete jobsite floors to about 1/8 in. accuracy, operating in fleets on data-center construction floors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous plan-driven diamond-tool work on an as-built concrete floor. It shows navigation and layout-following on real floors, but drilling discrete anchor holes indoors is not continuous joint sawing or crack routing on pavement (no blade steering, depth-of-cut control, slurry, or work-zone traffic), so it does not substantiate these instances.

sources.title: Video | Roadworks robot on trial - Construction Management
sources.claim: ULC Technologies' Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System uses a robotic arm with a concrete-cutting chainsaw to cut shapes into a road surface, sensing material hardness and adjusting cutting speed; it was in supervised field trials with gas utility SGN on UK streets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic cutting of in-situ road pavement. Autonomy level in the trials is not established (operator-supervised keyhole excavation), and the throughput and output differ from production joint sawing/crack routing, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Cut or break up pavement and drive guardrail posts, using machines equipped with interchangeable hammers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-depth breakout of deteriorated concrete or asphalt on a street/highway rehab or utility cut: operator runs an excavator, backhoe or skid steer with a hydraulic hammer inside a coned work zone with live traffic, breaking rebar-reinforced slab of varying thickness into loadable pieces to the marked limits without damaging subbase, buried utilities or adjacent sound pavement.

Sawcutting the perimeter of a patch, utility trench or joint on a street or lot (walk-behind saw, wheel-saw or saw attachment) to a clean vertical edge at specified depth following layout marks, then breaking out the material inside the cut with a hammer attachment.

Driving guardrail posts along a highway shoulder, ramp or bridge approach with a truck- or skid-steer-mounted hydraulic hammer post driver: positioning each W-section or wood post at staked spacing and line, driving to specified height and plumb, coping with rock, soft shoulder, slopes and existing hardware, alongside traffic under a lane closure.

Breaking out a large area of old concrete slab on a closed site (parking lot, industrial yard, airport apron/taxiway section) before repaving: repetitive hammering across a wide open area with dowels and mesh, no traffic, spoil pushed up for loading.

Close-quarters, precise breaking around structures: manholes, catch basins, curb and gutter, bridge deck joints, shallow utilities or existing pavement to be saved; frequent machine repositioning in tight urban space with hand-crew nearby.

sources.system: Normet Xrock Autobreaker (breaker boom with hydraulic hammer)
sources.title: Normet Xrock Launches the World's First Autonomous Rock-Breaking System, Xrock Autobreaker
sources.claim: Normet Xrock's Autobreaker module makes a hydraulic breaker boom fully autonomous: camera vision and sensor fusion build a point cloud, the system identifies oversize material, plans strike positions and executes breaking sequences with no person at the grizzly; commercially available since Dec 2025, with optional automatic tool changing between breakers, grapples and magnets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous secondary breaking of oversize rock/lumps with a hydraulic hammer at a fixed grizzly station. Transfer to 'break up pavement' under the E1 counterfactual: same tool class (hydraulic breaker on a boom, with interchangeable tools), same material class (hard brittle rock/concrete), same coarse precision requirement (fracture the piece to size), and the work is delivered to a machine-built station exactly as a purpose-built pavement-breaking cell would present slabs.

sources.system: Built Robotics RPD 35 / RPS 25 autonomous piling system
sources.title: The World's First Autonomous Piling System for Utility-Scale Solar — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 is described by the developer as a fully autonomous robotic pile ... surveying, pile distribution, hammer driving and data collection in one machine, driving steel W-sections from W6x7 to W8x28 to tolerances of ~30 mm z-height on grades up to 10%.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous driving of steel posts/piles into ground at surveyed positions on an open earth site. Transfer to 'drive guardrail posts': guardrail posts are W6x8.5/W6x9 steel sections inside the RPD's stated W6x7–W8x28 range, driven by hammer to a staked line and target height/plumb; the machine already handles post pick-up, positioning and driving to tighter tolerance than guardrail work requires, in the same class of unstructured outdoor site.

sources.system: Built Robotics autonomous pile driver (RPD 35) and pile stabilizer (RPS 25)
sources.title: Autonomous construction bots are building the solar infrastructure behind Meta's massive Hyperion data center
sources.claim: Built Robotics machines are in commercial field use: over 40 deployments, sensors/GPS/software let stock machines operate autonomously within defined work ..., and about 10 robots on one Louisiana solar site handle over half the pile-driving scope, driving nearly 1,000 steel piles per day.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the RPD 35 product evidence: hammer-driving steel W-section posts into unimproved ground at surveyed locations, here shown as sustained real-site production (including muddy, uneven terrain), which is the core act of driving guardrail posts.

sources.title: Blattner and Built Robotics Announce Contract to Improve Safety in Solar Construction
sources.claim: Blattner (Quanta Services) contracted in September 2025 to deploy dozens of Built ...' autonomous machines on US solar projects for pile driving, surveying, material handling, ....
sources.transferJustification: Establishes commercial-scale, multi-site field deployment of the autonomous hammer pile-driving system cited for the guardrail-post instance.

sources.system: Park Industries VOYAGER XP CNC Saw
sources.title: How to Cut Granite Countertops & Slabs for Stone Fabricators
sources.claim: Park Industries' VOYAGER XP CNC saw cuts granite and other hard slabs under full program automation on a fixtured machine table, running straight, miter and profile cuts in automatic mode.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated diamond-blade sawing of hard mineral slabs to programmed lines and depths. Transfer to 'cut pavement' under the E1 counterfactual, where the slab is brought to the machine and fixtured: same cutting medium (diamond blade in stone/concrete), same or tighter edge precision than a pavement sawcut, machine-controlled feed with no operator manipulation.

sources.title: Top 10: Construction Robotics
sources.claim: Compact demolition machines that break concrete on job sites (Brokk, Husqvarna DXR) remain remote-controlled rather than autonomous, indicating no autonomous in-situ concrete/pavement breaking capability in unstructured field settings.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (breaking concrete with a hydraulic hammer) but operator-controlled, so it cannot support a positive judgment; it is cited to show why field pavement breaking is not substantiated above E1.

tasks.label: Install dies, cutters, and extensions to screeds onto machines, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Asphalt paving crew: before/during a shift on an open road or parking-lot jobsite, the operator bolts heavy steel bolt-on extensions (2-4 ft sections, often 100+ lb each) onto the hydraulically extendable screed of a paver, aligning them flush to the main screed, torquing bolts with wrenches/impact gun, and hooking up screed-heat cables and hydraulic/electrical lines. Outdoors, uneven ground, dust, sometimes at night.

Screed wear parts and attachments: replacing or installing screed plates, strike-off/cut-off shoes, cutting edges, end gates and endgate skis on the paver screed at the jobsite or on the trailer, using hand tools, prying/hammering stuck bolts, sometimes with the screed jacked up or blocked.

Slipform curb-and-gutter/barrier machine: mounting or swapping the extrusion mold (die) on the machine's mold mount, adding bolt-on mold extensions, blockouts and outflow plates, then bolting, squaring and adjusting the mold. Heavy steel parts hoisted by loader or by hand, done at the jobsite or contractor yard.

Cold planer / trimmer / stabilizer: replacing carbide cutting bits (picks) and quick-change toolholder tops on the drum, and installing cutting edges on moldboards or trimmer heads, using hammer, extractor tool and wrenches, drum rotated by hand or hydraulically, at the jobsite between passes or at shift end.

Contractor equipment yard or maintenance shop before mobilization: pre-assembling and bolting screed extensions, dies/molds and cutter sets onto the machine in a covered bay with overhead hoist, air tools and parts bins available; institution controls access and the bay is kept to a working standard.

sources.developer: Zeman Bauelemente / Lincoln Electric, distributed by Peddinghaus
sources.title: Robotic Welding for Structural Steel Fabrication | PeddiAssembler | Peddinghaus
sources.claim: The Zeman/Lincoln Electric steel beam assembler (sold by Peddinghaus as PeddiAssembler) is a commercial robotic cell in which robot arms pick heavy steel attachments from a magazine, position them precisely on a beam and join them automatically; it handles parts up to 440 lb on profiles up to 11,000 lb.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fetching a heavy steel attachment, aligning it to a large steel structure held in a fixture, and joining it. This matches installing a bolt-on screed extension, mold section or endgate onto a fixtured screed/mold body in comparable mass, size and placement precision; the fastening step (bolting rather than welding) is covered by evidence 1.

sources.system: MIRAI-guided UR cobots with automatic torque wrench
sources.developer: Micropsi Industries with a leading US automotive OEM
sources.title: Leading US automotive OEM — Automated bolt torquing
sources.claim: A North American automotive OEM has deployed seven Universal Robots cobots with MIRAI vision and an automatic torque wrench that autonomously locate and tighten bolts on seat assemblies despite position, part and lighting variance, at near-100% success on four production lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving and torquing threaded fasteners on a workpiece presented with real-world positional variance. Installing screed extensions, dies and cutting edges is fundamentally bolt-up work with hand/power tools; this shows robotic torque-controlled fastening at production quality when the workpiece is presented to the machine.

sources.system: LVD ToolCell press brake with integrated automatic tool changer
sources.title: ToolCell: smart automation of tool changes | LVD
sources.claim: LVD ToolCell press brakes are commercial machines whose integrated automatic tool changer installs punches and dies into the machine from an on-board tool warehouse without an operator handling the tooling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mounting dies onto a machine. Same object class (steel dies), same operation (select, transport, seat and clamp a die in the machine's mounting), performed automatically when the tooling is stored and presented in known positions, i.e., the E1 counterfactual for die installation on a curb machine.

sources.system: Fastems Tool Automation / Gantry Tool Storage (GTS)
sources.date: 2020-2026 (product in commercial use; page updated Jan 2026)
sources.title: Tool automation maximizes spindle utilization | Fastems
sources.claim: Fastems Gantry Tool Storage is a commercial system in which gantry robots hold thousands of cutting tools centrally and load them into machining-centre tool magazines just-in-time under software control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing cutters onto a machine. A robot selects a cutting tool from storage and seats it in the machine's tool holder positions automatically, which is the same operation as loading cutter sets into a machine when tools and machine are presented in fixed, known positions.

sources.title: Hydraulic Stamping Solutions, Press Machine Components | Pascal
sources.claim: Quick die change systems for stamping presses use automated hydraulic/pneumatic die clamps, lifters and shuttle carts with sensor interlocks to move heavy dies into the press and clamp them, cutting manual changeover work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: seating and clamping a heavy die in a machine. Supporting context for die installation at E1 only; die staging can still involve a forklift, so autonomy is unclear and it is not relied on for a positive judgment.

sources.developer: university/industry research team (published in Automation in Construction)
sources.title: Robotic replacement for disc cutters in tunnel boring machines - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Robotic replacement of disc cutters on a real tunnel boring machine — the closest field analogue of changing cutting tools on a large construction machine in situ — remains a teleoperated/semi-autonomous prototype tested in the lab and applied to one TBM.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing and installing heavy cutting tools on a machine in the field. Cited as negative context: even this closest field analogue is teleoperated, supporting the judgment that no cited system performs this work autonomously at E2 or E3.

tasks.label: Set up forms and lay out guidelines for curbs, according to written specifications, using string, spray paint, and concrete or water mixes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Street reconstruction: straight curb-and-gutter runs. Worker reads plan/offset stakes, snaps or paints an alignment line on the trimmed subgrade, pulls a string line, then sets, aligns, stakes and braces steel or wood curb forms to line and grade in an open, traffic-controlled work zone.

Subdivision or parking-lot perimeter curb on a graded base: mostly straight and gently curved runs; layout with string and spray paint from grade stakes, forms set on soil/aggregate, staked, braced, and joints buttered with concrete/water mix before the pour.

Radius and special work: parking-lot islands, cul-de-sac returns, ADA curb ramps, driveway aprons. Hand-bent flexible forms, custom geometry cut and fitted on site, tie-ins matched to existing pavement and drainage grades.

Repair/replacement of short curb sections after utility cuts or damage: tight quarters between existing pavement and structures, forms cut to fit and held with stakes, braces, and mud/concrete mix, grades matched to abutting existing curb.

Layout-only ahead of a slipform curb machine or form crew: marking the curb alignment, offsets and station points with spray paint on base or existing pavement from plan coordinates (stringless/GPS job, no forms set).
Setting a physical stringline for a slipform curb machine: driving grade stakes at intervals, hanging and tensioning guide wire to plan line and elevation, checking with level/laser along the run.

sources.title: Shuttering Robot | Progress Maschinen & Automation
sources.claim: Progress Maschinen & Automation's Form Master shuttering/deshuttering robot autonomously selects magnetic formwork profiles from storage and positions them on the casting bed to CAD geometry in a precast concrete plant, then removes and re-stores them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing concrete formwork to written (CAD) specification. Same class of objects (steel formwork profiles that shape a poured concrete element), tighter precision than curb forms require, performed in a purpose-built cell where the work (the casting bed) is brought to the machine — the E1 counterfactual of curb form setting.

sources.title: Plotter/shuttering robot | Vollert Anlagenbau GmbH
sources.claim: Vollert's plotter/shuttering robot pair marks the formwork layout lines on the casting pallet in paint and then places the shutters automatically per CAD data in precast plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying out guidelines in paint according to written specification, then setting forms on those lines. This is the same two-step operation the curb task describes, executed automatically in a purpose-built (E1) production cell.

sources.system: Form Master (installed at Schwörer Bausysteme precast plant)
sources.title: Schwörer Bausysteme relies on modernization in the precast plant - Concrete Plant Precast Technology (BFT International)
sources.claim: A Form Master shuttering robot was installed and put into production at Schwörer Bausysteme's precast plant, showing shuttering robots are deployed in working plants, not just demonstrated.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes real plant deployment of the formwork-placement robot cited for the E1 counterfactual of setting curb forms to specification.

sources.system: Shuttering robots in precast carousel plants (industry survey)
sources.title: State of Practice of Automation in Precast Concrete Production
sources.claim: Survey of precast production practice confirms shuttering robots in carousel plants place formwork elements using position data transmitted from CAD by the plant control system.
sources.transferJustification: Independent confirmation that automated form placement from written/digital specifications is standard practice in purpose-built concrete plants, supporting the E1 judgment for curb form setup.

sources.date: 2022-11 (trade press); product in commercial use through 2025
sources.title: Video: Civ Robotics' robots can perform autonomous surveying | Equipment World
sources.claim: Civ Robotics' CivDot is an autonomous four-wheel-drive layout robot used on outdoor civil construction sites (roads, pipelines, foundations) that navigates to plan coordinates and spray-paints them on the ground with roughly 1-2 cm accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Same task element: laying out guidelines on the ground in spray paint from written plan coordinates, on unstructured outdoor construction sites (E3). It does not set forms, so it supports only the layout-only instance.

sources.title: Civ Robotics FAQ | Answering Your Questions on Construction Layout Robots
sources.claim: Civ Robotics states CivDot Mini automates roadway layout and parking-lot line marking in spray paint at sub-inch accuracy, up to 17 miles of ... lines per day.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers laying out curb alignment guidelines in spray paint on roadway and parking-lot surfaces to plan geometry; does not address form setting.

sources.title: HP announces autonomous construction layout printing robot | The Robot Report
sources.claim: HP SitePrint is an autonomous layout robot that prints lines, arcs, ... and text from digital plans directly onto construction surfaces including concrete, tarmac and pavement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transferring written layout specifications to marked guidelines on a job-site surface. Corroborates that autonomous plan-to-ground marking works on as-found construction surfaces, though it does not set physical forms.

roles.title: Pile Driver Operators
roles.description: Operate pile drivers mounted on skids, barges, crawler treads, or locomotive cranes to drive pilings for retaining walls, bulkheads, and foundations of structures such as buildings, bridges, and piers.

tasks.label: Move hand and foot levers of hoisting equipment to position piling leads, hoist piling into leads, and position hammers over pilings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bridge/highway heavy-civil foundation piling: crawler crane with fixed or swinging leads on a rough, muddy job site; operator hoists 40-100 ft steel pipe, H, or precast concrete piles off a delivery stack, threads them into the leads with a signal person and rigging crew, seats the diesel/hydraulic impact hammer over the pile head, and drives plumb or on batter to surveyed locations near live traffic.

Marine/waterfront work: barge- or amphibious-platform-mounted crane with leads or spuds driving timber, concrete or steel piles for piers, docks, bulkheads and fender systems; operator positions leads over water while the barge moves with tide, wind and wake, hoists piles from a supply barge, and holds the hammer plumb over each pile.

Building/commercial deep-foundation piling on a congested urban site: crane with leads driving H-piles or pipe piles for a structure's foundation, working around excavation edges, adjacent utilities, existing walls and other trades; piles pitched into leads by the rigging crew, spliced and welded mid-drive, hammer repositioned pile to pile.

Sheet-pile walls, cofferdams and excavation shoring: crane- or excavator-mounted vibratory hammer; operator positions leads/mast, hoists each sheet or pair, threads the interlock into the previously driven sheet through a template, and drives to grade on roadway, levee or riverbank sites.

Utility-scale solar farm or battery-storage field piling: open graded site spanning hundreds of acres, thousands of identical W6/W8 steel H-piles about 10-20 ft long on a surveyed grid; masted rig with vibratory hammer, operator picks each pile from a stack, sets it in the mast/chute, and drives it to tight plumb and reveal tolerances; wet, uneven or rocky ground.

sources.system: Built Robotics RPD 35 / RPS 25 autonomous piling system
sources.title: Blattner Picks Autonomous Pile Drivers From Built Robotics for Solar Projects — Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Built Robotics' autonomous pile-driving excavators (RPD 35 with RPS 25 stabilizer) pick up steel piles carried onboard, position them and drive them for solar array foundations on US utility-scale solar construction sites; EPC contractor Blattner (Quanta) adopted them nationwide.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: the robot pair replaces the operator's hoisting of the pile into the mast/lead and positioning of the vibratory hammer over the pile head.

sources.title: Solar Piling — The World's First Autonomous Piling System for Utility-Scale Solar, Built Robotics
sources.claim: Vendor technical description: the RPD 35 is a ... combining surveying, pile distribution, driving and data collection; the paired RPS 25 stabilizer holds piles to tracker tolerances. Capability is bounded: piles up to 19 ft, W6x7-W8x28, 40,000 lb impulse vibratory hammer, 10% max grade.
sources.transferJustification: Specifications bound where the system can substitute: short, light H-piles driven by a vibratory hammer, not the 40-100 ft crane-lead piles of heavy-civil and marine pile driving.

sources.system: Built Robotics autonomous pile driver fleet (RPD 35 / RPS 25)
sources.title: Autonomous construction bots are building the solar infrastructure behind Meta's massive Hyperion data center (Business Insider via AOL)
sources.claim: As of July 2026 about 10 Built Robotics machines were autonomously driving roughly 1,000 steel piles per day at a swampy, mile-long Louisiana utility-scale solar site (40+ deployments nationwide); no human handles the beams and supervisors monitor the fleet from a trailer, resupplying piles and fuel.
sources.transferJustification: Direct evidence of the task at production rate in an as-found outdoor construction environment (knee-deep mud, uneven terrain), with humans only resupplying and supervising.

sources.system: GIKEN GYRO PILER F401-G1200 with iNAVILINK / G-Lab Vision
sources.title: Next-generation Press-in Piling Using Digital Transformation. On-site Verification of Autonomous Operation and Remote Support — GIKEN LTD.
sources.claim: GIKEN's iNAVILINK autonomous press-in trial on a Kochi seawall raised automation of the press-in process only to roughly 65%; pitching each pile into the piler still requires a service crane and site workers, and the remote-support variant used a human operator through a digital twin.
sources.transferJustification: Closest system to sheet/tubular pile lead work, but it automates only part of the cycle and leaves pile pitching — the hoisting-into-leads step at the core of this task — to a human-operated service crane, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion.

tasks.label: Move levers and turn valves to activate power hammers, or to raise and lower drophammers that drive piles to required depths.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Utility-scale solar/renewable field piling: on a graded open site, driving hundreds of 12-16 ft steel H-piles per day on a surveyed grid with a vibratory or impact hammer to specified embedment/reveal height, flagging refusals for pre-drilling, holding plumbness and z-height within tracker tolerances.

Building/structure foundation piling on land: crawler-crane or rig-mounted diesel/hydraulic impact hammer driving 40-100 ft steel H-piles, pipe piles or precast concrete piles in leads on a congested active jobsite; operator works levers and valves to hoist and set each pile, control hammer stroke and energy, splice, and drive to specified tip elevation or blow-count refusal while an inspector logs blows.

Bridge and highway foundation piling (abutments, bents, trestles): driving battered and plumb piles through variable soils to a state-DOT driving criterion, with template alignment, dynamic (PDA) monitoring, and stop-driving decisions made in real time from blow count and hammer stroke.

Sheet piling for retaining walls, cofferdams and bulkheads: threading interlocking sheets into the previously driven sheet through a template and driving with a vibratory hammer (finishing with an impact hammer where needed) to required depth while holding line, plumb and interlock, often in tight urban or waterfront settings.

Marine barge-based piling for piers, docks, wharves and bulkheads: crane and hammer working from a floating barge in current, wind and tide, setting timber, pipe or concrete piles in a floating template and driving to depth over water, with a rigging crew and boat traffic around.

sources.system: Built Robotics RPD 35 / autonomous solar piling robots (with RPS 25 stabilizer)
sources.title: Blattner Picks Autonomous Pile Drivers From Built Robotics for Solar Projects | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Built Robotics' autonomous pile-driving excavators (RPD system) pick up and drive steel solar foundation piles unaided on utility-scale solar construction sites in the US; EPC contractor Blattner adopted them nationwide after four projects.

sources.title: The World's First Autonomous Piling System for Utility-Scale Solar — Built Robotics
sources.claim: The RPD 35 combines surveying, pile distribution, pile driving ... autonomous machine, drives with a 40,000 lb impulse-force hammer, detects refusal automatically and continues the sequence; operators monitor from a distance.

sources.system: GIKEN iNAVILINK / GYRO PILER F401-G1200 (Silent Piler press-in)
sources.title: Next-generation Press-in Piling Using Digital Transformation. On-site Verification of Autonomous Operation and Remote Support | GIKEN LTD.
sources.claim: Giken's iNAVILINK field verification on a Kochi seawall project installed 13 tubular piles under 'autonomous operation', but automation of the press-in process reached only about 65%, an operator remained in the loop, and the technology was still pre-commercial.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hydraulic press-in installation of tubular/sheet piles yields the same output (piles installed to planned depth and position) as hammer driving, so it is the closest evidence for automating sheet-pile and foundation-pile installation; it shows only partial automation with an operator retained.

sources.system: IQIP C-36 Control System for Hydrohammer
sources.title: Smarter pile driving, C-36 Control - IQIP
sources.claim: State-of-the-art hydraulic impact hammer control for large piles automates blow rate and blow energy but keeps a human operator driving the hammer by remote control; no autonomous set-and-drive-to-criterion capability is claimed.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (activating and regulating a power hammer to drive piles) on large piles; shows that automation available for heavy hammers is operator-in-the-loop remote control, not autonomous driving to a required depth.

sources.developer: Harvard SEAS / Wyss Institute (Werfel et al., ICRA 2019)
sources.title: Autonomous Sheet Pile Driving Robots for Soil Stabilization (IEEE ICRA 2019)
sources.claim: Romu is an autonomous research robot that drives interlocking sheet piles with an on-board vibratory hammer, but it is a small laboratory/field-test platform driving miniature sheets, not construction-scale sheet piling.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (vibratory driving of interlocking sheet piles) but at research scale; cited to show the only autonomous sheet-pile driving demonstrated is far below worker-quality construction sheet piling.

tasks.label: Drive pilings to provide support for buildings or other structures, using heavy equipment with a pile driver head.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Building foundation piling on an urban/commercial construction site: operating a crawler crane or leader rig with fixed leads and a diesel/hydraulic impact hammer to drive 40-100 ft steel H-piles or pipe piles, with crew rigging and pitching each pile, splicing/welding sections, driving to refusal against blow-count/bearing criteria, adjusting for obstructions and congested site conditions.

Bridge and highway structure foundation piling on land: driving precast prestressed concrete piles or heavy steel piles at abutments, bents and retaining structures, using templates and pile cushions, monitoring set/dynamic testing (PDA), coordinating with inspectors and cutting off to grade.

Sheet pile walls, bulkheads and excavation shoring/cofferdams: threading interlocks and driving steel sheets (or soldier piles) with a crane- or excavator-mounted vibratory hammer against a template, correcting plumb and creep, working around utilities and adjacent structures.

Marine/waterfront pile driving from a barge-mounted rig: driving timber, concrete or steel piles for piers, docks, dolphins and bulkheads with swinging leads, contending with tide, current, barge motion, water depth and batter piles.

High-volume repetitive small H-pile driving on a large open, graded site (utility-scale solar arrays and similar racking foundations): thousands of 10-19 ft W6-W8 steel piles set to surveyed coordinates and driven with a vibratory hammer to tight plumb/height tolerances, sometimes with pre-drilling.

Small light-structure and tight-access piling: timber or small steel piles and mini-piles for residential foundations, small commercial buildings, boat docks and underpinning, driven with a compact excavator-mounted vibratory hammer or small rig on cramped, obstructed lots.

sources.system: Built Robotics RPD 35 + RPS 25 autonomous piling system
sources.title: Blattner Picks Autonomous Pile Drivers From Built Robotics for Solar Projects — Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 / RPS 25 pair of autonomous excavator-based pile drivers install steel solar foundation piles unaided on US utility-scale solar construction sites; EPC contractor Blattner signed a nationwide deal after using them on multiple projects, citing maintained or improved quality.

sources.developer: Built Robotics (hosted by Fortescue / ARENA Pilbara Solar Innovation Hub)
sources.title: Milestone 1 Report — Fortescue Solar Innovation Hub (ARENA)
sources.claim: In a hosted trial at Fortescue's Cloudbreak Solar Farm the RPD35/RPS25 autonomously retrieved piles from onboard baskets, positioned and drove them to required depth and alignment, evaluated against placement accuracy, productivity, quality and reliability criteria in dusty, hot field conditions.

sources.title: Built Robotics – Australian Robotic Piling Deployment for Large Scale Solar – Lesson Learnt Report 1 (ARENA)
sources.claim: An ARENA-funded pilot deployment of Built Robotics' autonomous piling system at the Goorambat East Solar Farm completed installation of 1,723 piles between February and April 2025.

sources.title: Robots that Build the World — Built Robotics
sources.claim: The autonomous piling system's working envelope is limited to short, light solar H-piles driven with a vibratory hammer — far smaller than the heavy foundation, bridge, sheet and marine piles driven with crane leads and impact hammers.

sources.system: SILENT PILER / GYRO PILER F401-G1200 with iNAVILINK autonomous operation
sources.title: Next-generation Press-in Piling Using Digital Transformation. On-site Verification of Autonomous Operation and Remote Support — GIKEN LTD.
sources.claim: Giken's iNAVILINK on-site verification at a Kochi seawall project pressed in 1,000 mm diameter, 10.5 m steel tubular piles under autonomous operation to planned location and depth meeting government quality standards, but raised the automation rate only to about 65%, with the crew reduced by one person rather than eliminated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: press-in installation of tubular/sheet piles for seawall and retaining-wall foundations. It is the closest heavy-pile automation found, but the machine automates only part of the cycle and retains a manned crew, so it does not substantiate whole-instance completion.

sources.system: Junttan PM5 pile driving rig (Evolution Series)
sources.title: NEWS RELEASE: Junttan Unveils the New PM5 Evolution Series Pile Driving Rig
sources.claim: The newest generation of dedicated heavy pile-driving rigs remains manned: Junttan's 2026 PM5 offers remote-controlled setup and operator-assist features, not autonomous pile installation.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (driving foundation piles with a leader rig); cited to show that commercially available heavy piling rigs provide operator assistance and remote setup only, with no autonomous drive cycle.

sources.title: Laying the ground for robotic strategies in environmental protection — Wyss Institute
sources.claim: Romu, a research robot, autonomously drives interlocking steel sheet piles into ... using an onboard vibratory hammer, demonstrated in the lab and on a beach; it is a small research prototype, not construction-scale sheet piling equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous driving of small interlocking sheet piles for erosion barriers. Scale (short light sheets, natural terrain, research prototype) is far below construction sheet-pile walls, so it does not carry over to worker-quality shoring or bulkhead work.

tasks.label: Conduct pre-operational checks on equipment to ensure proper functioning.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-of-shift walk-around of a crawler-crane pile rig on an active land jobsite: check engine oil, hydraulic, coolant and fuel levels; look for leaks and damaged/chafed hoses; inspect tracks, boom and lead structure for cracks, loose bolts and bent members; inspect running wire rope, sheaves, hook and rigging for broken wires/wear; check grease points and top up; record deficiencies on the shift inspection form and decide go/no-go.

Pre-start check of the driving system itself on the jobsite: diesel, hydraulic impact or vibratory hammer with power pack/compressor — check hammer lube oil and fuel, hydraulic hoses and quick couplers, cushion block/pile cap and wear plates, clamp jaws, bolt torque and keeper pins, then test-fire/idle the hammer to confirm blow rate, clamp force and no leaks before the first pile.

In-cab functional check before operating: start engine, watch gauges and warning lamps, cycle hoist, swing, boom and lead-adjust controls, verify drum brakes, clutches, load moment indicator and anti-two-block/limit devices, horn, backup alarm, mirrors/cameras, fire extinguisher and radio; listen and feel for abnormal response and stop for anything out of spec.

Marine spread pre-op check on a barge-mounted pile driver: crane/rig checks plus spuds and spud winches, deck winches and mooring lines, generator, air compressor and hose runs to the hammer, fuel and spill kit, all performed on a moving deck in wind, spray and variable light at a waterfront/marine construction site.

Pre-mobilization or post-service check in the contractor's equipment yard/shop: rig components and hammer on stands or laid out, systems checked and functions verified with shop support and lighting before the spread ships to the job; controlled premises, standard layout, mechanics on hand.

sources.title: Inspection and maintenance robots: drones, quadrupeds, crawlers, and subsea systems transform infrastructure safety

tasks.label: Clean, lubricate, and refill equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Land jobsite, start or end of shift: operator greases the pile-driving rig — crawler crane swing bearing, boom and lead pins, sheaves, hammer slides and guides — 20-60 zerk fittings, several reached by climbing the leads or catwalks; muddy, weather-exposed, machine shut down.

Land jobsite: refuelling the rig and the auxiliary power pack, generator or air compressor from a fuel truck or an on-site tank — dragging the hose across the site, opening the fill cap on the upper deck, pumping several hundred gallons of diesel, topping DEF.

Checking and topping off fluids on the rig: engine oil, hydraulic tank, coolant, winch gear oil, hammer lube-oil reservoir, and refilling the auto-lube grease reservoir; reading dipsticks and sight glasses and adding the correct fluid from pails or a service truck.

Cleaning the machine: pressure-washing or scraping mud, grease and grout off tracks, leads, deck and hammer; clearing spoil and debris, cleaning cab glass, blowing out radiator screens and air filters, at the jobsite or in the contractor's equipment yard.

Marine spread: servicing a barge-mounted rig — refuelling the hammer power pack and generator from deck totes or a fuel barge, greasing leads and crane, topping hydraulic oil and washing salt and river mud off, on a moving deck with ladder/catwalk access over water.

sources.claim: Scott Automation's Robofuel is a commercial robotic refuelling system that uses vision sensing to locate a mining truck's fuel tank and couple the nozzle without personnel present, installed at mine refuelling stations placed on-circuit or in-pit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: refuelling heavy off-road diesel equipment. A 300-t haul truck's deck-level fuel receiver is comparable in scale, access and precision to the fuel fill on a pile rig or hammer power pack, so 'refill equipment' with diesel transfers directly.

sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above: robotic diesel refuelling of large mobile plant, showing sustained production use rather than a demonstration.

tasks.label: Learn and follow safety regulations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-shift safety routine on a jobsite: don PPE (hard hat, hi-vis, boots, eye/hearing protection) and perform the required walk-around/pre-start inspection of a dozer, excavator, loader or grader — fluid levels and leaks, tires/tracks, guards, ROPS and seatbelt, lights, mirrors, backup alarm, control function test — record the check and tag out any machine found unsafe.

Following operating safety rules while doing production work on an active mixed-trade construction site: seatbelt buckled, keeping the machine back from trench edges and unstable slopes, clearances from overhead power lines and marked utilities, watching for ground workers entering the swing/blind zone, obeying spotter and hand signals, respecting load and grade limits, stopping when someone or something intrudes.

Following the standing safety rules on a large single-purpose production site (quarry or mine haul road, big earthmoving spread, utility-scale solar field): exclusion zones, haul-road right-of-way and speed rules, radio protocol, separation from light vehicles and pedestrians, repetitive cycles over a surveyed, prepared work area.

Roadway/utility work in and around live traffic: setting up and maintaining the work zone — cones, barrels, barricades, signs, positioning the protective/attenuator vehicle — coordinating with flaggers and spotters, and reacting when the public, a utility strike, or another hazard intrudes (stop work, clear the area, report).

End-of-shift and servicing safety: park on level ground, lower blade/bucket to the ground, engage brakes and locks, chock, shut down, three-point contact on mount/dismount, lockout/tagout and pressure relief before greasing or servicing, safe fueling and spill control at the machine or in the yard.

Learning the rules: new-hire site orientation, weekly toolbox talks, reviewing and signing the JHA/AHA for the day's activity, OSHA 10/30 and competent-person or equipment certification classes, absorbing changed regulations and site-specific rules and applying them afterward.

tasks.label: Take actions to avoid potential hazards or obstructions, such as utility lines, other equipment, other workers, or falling objects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Excavator/backhoe/loader operator digging in a developed area (street, campus, subdivision) where gas, electric, fiber and water lines are marked by locates but positions are approximate: the operator digs cautiously toward the tolerance zone, reads spoil for warning tape, tracer wire and disturbed soil, stops for hand-digging/potholing, and works around exposed lines without striking them.

Machine working shoulder-to-shoulder with a ground crew: loader backfilling around pipe layers, excavator holding/placing pipe or box while laborers work at the bucket, grading around form carpenters, taking hand signals from a spotter, swinging and tracking with people inside the machine's radius while still producing work.

Open-area earthmoving on a large site (mass grading, site prep, solar/wind field, landfill): the machine works its own area while other machines, pickup trucks, surveyors and crew members are present but usually at a distance; operator watches, slows, yields and stops when someone or something enters the work radius.

Hauling and equipment-traffic interaction on shared site and haul roads, including quarries, pits and large mass-excavation jobs: dump trucks, scrapers and loaders cycling in dust and blind spots, backing to loading and dump points, yielding at intersections, keeping off soft edges and berms.

Highway or urban work zone with live public traffic: machine works within feet of a moving traffic stream, flaggers, cones and pedestrians; operator watches for errant vehicles, keeps the boom/bucket/counterweight out of the open lane, and coordinates with the flagger before swinging or backing.

Work exposed to overhead and falling hazards: keeping boom, bed or mast clear of energized overhead lines and structures, operating under a highwall, near unstable trench walls or a partially demolished structure, repositioning to avoid falling material or spoil sloughing.

tasks.label: Start engines, move throttles, switches, or levers, or depress pedals to operate machines, such as bulldozers, trench excavators, road graders, or backhoes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-site bulk work with an excavator: mass excavation and loading haul trucks, digging ponds/pads, and running long utility or solar cable trenches on a cleared site-development or energy project. Repetitive cycles, open ground, staked/modelled grades, few adjacent obstacles.

Dozer work on an active earthmoving job: stripping topsoil, pushing and spreading fill in lifts, slot dozing/ripping, building stockpiles and haul roads, pushing waste at a landfill face. Rough tolerances, dust, varying traction, other trucks and machines moving nearby.

Backhoe/excavator in congested conditions: utility trench in a city street or around existing buried lines, footings tight to a standing structure, laborers in and around the trench giving hand signals, traffic and pedestrians past cones, careful bucket work near live services.

Motor grader (or dozer/box blade) finish work: trimming subgrade and base course to line and grade tolerance for a roadway, slab or parking lot, cutting ditches and slopes, blending into existing pavement and structures, feathering material with repeated passes.

Loader/hauler/dozer at a controlled industrial site: aggregate quarry, sand-and-gravel pit, asphalt or ready-mix plant yard or materials yard. Repetitive load-haul-dump and stockpile feeding on maintained roads, restricted access, company traffic rules.

tasks.label: Coordinate machine actions with other activities, positioning or moving loads in response to hand or audio signals from crew members.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Utility/trenching crew: excavator or backhoe operator lowers pipe sections, trench boxes, manholes or valves into an open trench while a ground man in or beside the trench gives hand signals and radio calls; muddy uneven ground, load swinging over workers, joints homed to within an inch.

Building/site construction: loader, telehandler or excavator moves palletized block, forms, steel or pipe from a laydown area and sets it where a crew member points or hand-signals; congested site with other trades, parked equipment and shifting stockpile locations.

Precision heavy placement: machine rigged as a lifting device sets precast panels, box culverts, beams or trench plates while a rigger/signal person gives continuous corrections and laborers hand-guide the load into its seat; inch-level tolerance with people beside and under the load.

Roadway/paving/grading: operator coordinates machine moves and material placement with a foreman, flagger or paving crew (backing trucks to the paver, spreading and shaping to hand signals, working around laborers and live traffic) in a highway work zone.

Quarry, aggregate plant or material yard: wheel loader operator loads haul trucks and works stockpiles, responding to truck drivers' and plant personnel's horn, hand and radio signals; fixed plant layout on institution-controlled premises.

Quarry/mine or mass-earthmoving job: haul unit operator (off-highway truck, articulated dump truck, scraper) spots at the loading tool where the loader/excavator operator signals, waits for the load, then hauls and dumps at a point designated by a spotter or grade foreman.

sources.claim: H&P's FlexRobotics rig floor automates handling of heavy tubulars from tailing to racking with three six-axis manipulators, executing sequences commanded by the driller while crews stay out of the red zone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling and stabbing of heavy pipe. Same object class (large-diameter pipe), tighter alignment tolerance, machine acts on the driller's command in a purpose-built robotic zone - the E1 counterfactual of setting pipe on a crew's direction.

sources.title: Reliable, Safe Deployment of Autonomous Robots — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' autonomous excavators operate only inside a zone from which workers are barred by virtual and physical barriers, so the machine does not take direction from crew members standing in its work area.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant negative evidence: the leading autonomous earthmoving system works by excluding the crew, the opposite of positioning loads in response to signals from crew working alongside the machine.

sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Announces Supervised Autonomy Testing on Active Construction Sites in Move Towards Commercialization
sources.claim: The largest autonomous excavation programme on live US construction sites was still running under supervised autonomy in late 2025, with fully operator-less deployments only targeted for 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Bounds the state of the art for autonomous heavy equipment on unstructured construction sites (E3): supervised mass excavation, not crew-signalled load placement.

sources.title: IronBOT Rebar Placing Robot | Advanced Construction Robotics
sources.claim: IronBOT, the closest fielded machine that lifts, carries and places heavy loads (5,000-lb rebar bundles) on active bridge-deck jobsites, rides screed rails under a Robot Supervisor who walks alongside with a remote control and feeds the load.
sources.transferJustification: Closest E3 analogue of crew-coordinated load placement on a construction site; it still requires a supervisor with a remote control at the machine, so it does not establish unattended crew-signalled load handling.

tasks.label: Align machines, cutterheads, or depth gauge makers with reference stakes and guidelines or ground or position equipment, following hand signals of other workers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dozer or motor grader operator on an open site-grading or roadway job aligns the blade to grade stakes, hubs, stringlines or a 3D design surface, holding cut/fill and slope from rough cut to finish grade; changing terrain, weather, other crew and haul traffic nearby.

Excavator operator lines the machine up on a staked or painted trench/footing line and works to the marked depth and grade (utility trench, cable trench in a solar field, footing), with a grade checker or laser/GPS reference and spoil piled to one side.

Cold planer (milling machine) or slipform/asphalt paver operator sets and holds cutterhead/screed depth and lateral alignment to a stringline, curb, ski or grade references in an active roadway work zone under traffic control.

Backing or spotting a haul truck, articulated truck, loader or dozer into a designated point (under a loading tool, at a dump/fill point, at a paver hopper) on an active construction site, guided by a ground worker's hand signals.

Fine positioning of a machine or its attachment in close quarters under a worker's live hand signals: lowering pipe, box or precast into a trench, easing a bucket around an exposed utility, spotting the machine on mats near structures and workers on foot.

Quarry, aggregate pit or large mine operation: spotting haul trucks at the shovel/loader and at dump points and pushing to marked references, within an institution-controlled pit with maintained haul roads and controlled access.

sources.system: Trimble Earthworks Grade Control Platform (dozers, motor graders, excavators)

tasks.label: Locate underground services, such as pipes or wires, prior to beginning work.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Paved urban/suburban street or parking lot: before trenching for a main repair, service tap or road cut, the operator/crew verifies the 811 paint marks over the dig footprint — sweeping the area with an EM locator wand and/or GPR cart, tracing gas, water, electric and telecom lines, and painting/flagging them on the pavement. Work zone coned off under traffic management, traffic and pedestrians nearby.

Raw dirt/greenfield site development (subdivision pad, commercial lot, solar farm, pipeline or highway right-of-way): before grading or trenching, the operator walks the alignment with an EM locator, checks plans and prior markings, and sets pin flags/lath on soil, gravel, grass and rutted ground with uneven terrain, spoil piles and vegetation.

Verification potholing / soft dig: after marks are placed, physically exposing the line to confirm depth and position before machine excavation — hand digging, careful bucket work, or vacuum/air excavation through pavement or soil, then confirming and recording the utility's position. Usually a street, shoulder or active dig site.

Excavation inside an institution-controlled facility (industrial plant, refinery, airport airside, university or hospital campus, water treatment works, port or utility yard): scanning and marking buried services on paved drives and aprons before digging, with escorted access and facility as-built drawings.

Residential lot or backyard / tight congested private property: locating unrecorded sewer laterals, water services, irrigation, septic and buried electric drops before digging footings, pools or trenches — lawns, fences, gates, slopes, landscaping and driveways, with poor or absent records.

sources.title: AUSMOS | GPR Mapping Robot for Underground Damage Prevention | ULC Technologies
sources.claim: AUSMOS (Automated Utility Service Mark-Out System) is a robotic GPR+EM platform that, after an operator walks it onto site and defines the scan area, autonomously navigates and scans the ground, processes the data on-site, and produces same-day mark-out of buried utilities; offered by ULC Technologies as a robotic GPR mapping service.

sources.title: AUSMOS | GPR Mapping Robot for Underground Damage Prevention | ULC Technologies (Specifications)
sources.claim: AUSMOS's published operating envelope restricts it to urban/suburban paved roads and walkways, i.e. it is not specified for unpaved, vegetated or rutted ground typical of raw construction sites and residential yards.

sources.developer: ULC Technologies, LLC with SGN and Transport for London
sources.title: Robotic Mapping and Mark Out: Clapham Hill – ULC Technologies
sources.claim: In a field pilot at Clapham Hill, London, AUSMOS scanned two adjacent sites in a live public street with traffic flowing under traffic-management, and carried the job through to on-site interpretation and painted mark-out of buried assets; two ULC operatives interpreted the processed data via the robot's UI and the robot placed the paint marks, which matched utility drawings and an exposed pit.

sources.title: AUSMOS GPR Mapping and Mark Out Robot Pilot: Epsom, UK – ULC Technologies
sources.claim: In the Epsom (greater London) pilot, AUSMOS autonomously scanned a 3 m x 5 m congested urban area and the robot marked the ground; the crew of two had only limited GPR experience and needed no off-site subject-matter expert, and the marks corresponded to the utility owner's records and an exposed 24-inch gas main.

sources.system: AUSMOS with Sensors & Software NOGGIN GPR
sources.title: Enabling Innovation: The Development of a Utility-Locating Robot, AUSMOS GPR Survey
sources.claim: Independent sensor-vendor account confirms AUSMOS uses a NOGGIN GPR antenna plus an EM sensor and autonomously collects far denser data (10 cm line spacing) than human pushcart operators, with centimetre-level localization including GPS-denied urban areas, enabling on-site mark-out of utilities.

sources.title: The Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System (RRES): From Innovation Funding to Field Trials – ULC Technologies
sources.claim: During a two-week field trial at SGN's gas holder site in ..., UK, the Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System (RRES) scanned the ground, identified crossing buried pipes, then robotically cut a keyhole and vacuum-excavated down to expose the pipe — i.e. it performed the locate-and-pothole verification sequence on a utility-controlled paved site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic keyhole excavation; it carries over because the sensing step (GPR/EM detection of buried pipes) and the exposure step (soft-touch vacuum excavation over the asset) are exactly the detect-and-pothole actions this task requires, on the same objects (gas mains, cables) and at the same precision.

sources.title: Robotic Roadworks & Excavation System – ULC Technologies
sources.claim: RRES combines GPR and electromagnetic sensing with AI to detect buried infrastructure before cutting the road surface, then uses supersonic-air/vacuum soft-touch excavation over the asset; ULC describes the system as conducting end-to-end autonomous excavation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic road excavation; its mandatory first stage is locating buried services in the excavation path with GPR/EM before any cutting, which is the task being rated.

sources.title: Roadwork Robot Autonomously Digs Out, Repairs, Buried Utility Lines | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Trade press reported an early RRES demonstration of autonomously digging out buried utility lines that was staged inside a tent — i.e. a purpose-built, enclosed setting prepared for the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic excavation over buried utilities; cited only to establish that the locate-and-expose sequence has been executed in a fully prepared, enclosed setting (E1-type environment).

tasks.label: Signal operators to guide movement of tractor-drawn machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mass-grading site: worker stands clear of a dozer pushing/pulling a scraper or pan and gives standard hand signals (advance, swing, raise/lower blade, stop) to guide the machine's travel path and cut depth across the fill area, in dust and engine noise.

Spotting a tractor-drawn machine working in tight quarters near buried utilities, footings, curbs, or an adjacent structure: the signaler watches the swing radius and clearances the operator cannot see and signals slow/stop/back to keep the towed unit off the obstruction.

Guiding a tractor backing a lowboy or equipment trailer into a laydown yard, ramp, or unloading position on the jobsite: repeated back-up signals, distance-to-stop indications, and a final stop signal.

Roadway work zone with live traffic: signaling the operator of a tractor-towed roller, water pull, or grader train when it is clear to move, when to hold for passing traffic or workers on foot, and where to align the pass.

Hook-up and positioning: signaling an operator to inch a tractor rearward into alignment with an implement hitch, towed compactor, or trailer kingpin, calling out fine left/right/stop corrections until the pin can be dropped.

tasks.label: Repair and maintain equipment, making emergency adjustments or assisting with major repairs as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily pre-/post-shift service of the assigned machine (dozer, excavator, loader, grader) on an active construction site: walk-around looking for leaks, cracks, loose pins and damaged hoses; greasing pins and bushings with a grease gun; checking and topping engine oil, coolant, hydraulic oil and DEF; draining the water separator; blowing out or swapping a clogged air filter; cleaning tracks, steps and glass. Machine parked on rough graded ground in dust, mud, heat or cold.

Emergency adjustment or minor repair during the shift, in place on the site: replacing a burst hydraulic hose or weeping fitting, cleaning a plugged radiator/cooler, re-tensioning or reseating a thrown track, changing a fuel filter and bleeding the system, jumping or swapping a battery, replacing a broken work light or mirror, re-torquing loose bolts — done with hand tools from the service truck, under time pressure, often in bad weather.

Scheduled service in the contractor's equipment yard or shop: oil-and-filter change, hydraulic/fuel filter replacement, full grease service, coolant and DEF fill, replacing bolt-on wear parts such as dozer cutting edges or bucket teeth, minor weld repairs — machine parked on a level pad or shop floor with shop tools, air lines and a hoist available.

Assisting a field mechanic with a major repair on the jobsite: positioning the machine and blocking it, rigging and lifting heavy components (final drive, track group, hydraulic cylinder, blade) with another machine or a chain hoist, breaking loose seized/rusted fasteners, torch cutting, cleaning components, refilling fluids and test-operating the machine afterward.

Wear-tooling and attachment changes needed to keep the machine working: swapping a bucket for a ripper, hammer or thumb, driving out pins to replace worn bucket teeth or a dozer cutting edge, adjusting grader moldboard/scarifier and blade wear strips — done in a site staging area with hammer, pry bar, impact wrench and pins.

sources.title: Robotic refueling technology market maturing, expanding | Plant Engineering
sources.claim: SCOTT Automation's Robofuel is an industrial robot arm with custom end effector and sensing that autonomously refuels large mining haul trucks at fixed and in-pit fuelling stations; it is in use at mine sites including autonomous Komatsu fleets in the Pilbara. It performs only diesel transfer — lubricants and coolants are described as future applications.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fluid servicing of heavy earthmoving equipment. It shows a robot can locate a large machine and connect a nozzle to one standard port at a purpose-built station, which is the closest automated analogue to the fluid-replenishment part of operator servicing; it does not cover greasing many fittings, inspection, filter changes or any repair.

sources.system: Pit Viper with Automatic Bit Changer (ABC)
sources.title: Epiroc's ground-breaking drill rig Pit Viper celebrates 25 years including a decade with autonomous operations
sources.claim: Epiroc's Automatic Bit Changer, an option on autonomous Pit Viper blasthole drills operating unmanned in open-pit mines, changes a worn rotary tricone bit (a wear part on the machine's tooling) by machine, without a person handling the drill string.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: replacing a worn wear part on heavy equipment. It is a purpose-built, single-part mechanism dedicated to one threaded tool on one machine, with replacement bits presented in an onboard carousel; it does not generalise to unbolting rusted cutting edges, hammering out tooth pins, or any diagnostic or repair work.

sources.title: RoboTire installs another system with Discount Tire - The Robot Report
sources.claim: RoboTire's four-arm robotic system, installed and operating in Discount Tire and other retail service bays, removes lug nuts and removes/installs wheel-and-tire assemblies on passenger cars using 3D vision, with a technician supervising.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vehicle maintenance requiring fastener removal and heavy part handling inside a structured service facility. It shows vision-guided unbolting/rebolting of a standardised, clean, uniform interface on light vehicles; construction-equipment service involves varied machines, seized and mud-caked fasteners, fluids, filters and diagnosis, none of which it addresses.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics' robot dog patrols 1.5 million-square-foot factory
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot runs autonomous inspection rounds in industrial facilities, using thermal and acoustic sensors to detect developing equipment faults for maintenance planning; it collects data and does not perform repairs, adjustments or fluid service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: condition monitoring of machinery. It substantiates only the perception half of maintenance (finding a problem) inside institution-controlled facilities; it has no capability to grease, top fluids, replace parts or make adjustments.

sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Automated Tire's SmartBay, a 2026 autonomous tire-changing cell for a service shop, still requires a human operator to remove the used tire, position the new one and connect the air line — indicating that even in a purpose-built bay, robotic vehicle servicing is not yet an end-to-end substitute for the technician.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic servicing of vehicles in a dedicated bay; cited to show the current boundary of the art, where humans still perform the handling steps around the robot.

tasks.label: Load and move dirt, rocks, equipment, or other materials, using trucks, crawler tractors, power cranes, shovels, graders, or related equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mass excavation on a large open construction site (site prep for a data center, manufacturing plant, solar farm or subdivision): operator runs a 20-80 ton excavator or front-end loader, digging dirt and rock and loading a stream of haul trucks in repetitive cycles for weeks, with spotters, foremen and other machines moving nearby.

Hauling material across the jobsite: operator runs an articulated dump truck or off-road rock truck, spotting under the excavator, tramming loaded over temporary site haul roads that shift as the job progresses, dumping at fill or spoil areas, and returning, in mud, dust and mixed traffic.

Quarry, aggregate pit, sand plant or landfill on fenced industrial premises: loader or shovel loads haul trucks at the face or stockpile and trucks cycle to the crusher or tip point over maintained haul roads, under site rules controlling who and what enters.

Highway, street or utility work: loading spoil into tandem trucks and moving aggregate, bedding stone, pipe and asphalt along a linear work zone next to live traffic, with flaggers, barrels, buried utilities and a pipe/paving crew working within feet of the machine.

Handling equipment and non-bulk materials: using a crane, excavator with thumb or telehandler to pick and set pipe, precast structures, trench boxes, mats, plates and pallets rigged by a ground crew, and loading machines onto lowboy trailers for transport.

Crawler tractor (dozer) work: pushing, spreading and stockpiling dirt and rock — cutting down piles, spreading truck-dumped fill in lifts, building ramps and pushing material to a loading point on an active earthwork site.

sources.title: Bedrock Robotics announces autonomous excavation milestone - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics' retrofit autonomy kit ran autonomous excavators in production mass excavation on an active 130-acre construction site with Sundt Construction, loading human-driven articulated rock trucks; over 65,000 cubic yards moved under supervised autonomy (no continuous teleoperation).

tasks.label: Drive and maneuver equipment equipped with blades in successive passes over working areas to remove topsoil, vegetation, or rocks or to distribute and level earth or terrain.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Site-development or road project: dozer makes successive passes to strip topsoil and push out vegetation, roots, stumps and loose rock, windrowing or stockpiling the spoil. Ground is as-found, obstacles are unknown until hit, strip limits are staked.

Mass grading on an open earthwork site: dozer (or scraper/dozer pair) spreads dumped fill in lifts and levels it toward a design surface in successive passes, working to GPS machine-control grade over an area cleared of other trades.

Motor grader fine-grades subgrade or aggregate base for a road, shoulder or parking lot to tight tolerance with crown and cross-slope, in a live corridor with stakes, hand crews, hauling traffic and phased lane closures.

Institution-controlled production yard: dozer pushes and levels material at a quarry/plant stockpile, a landfill working face, or a mine spoil/dump area, repeating the same push pattern shift after shift under site traffic rules.

Congested or hazardous blade work: grading around exposed utilities, backfilling and dressing trench spoil, tight pads between structures, ditch and slope trimming next to traffic, with laborers, pipe crews and inspectors working alongside the machine.

sources.system: A4CSEL (automated bulldozers, vibratory rollers, dump trucks)
sources.title: A⁴CSEL for DAM | Technology & Services | KAJIMA CORPORATION
sources.claim: Kajima's A4CSEL system runs autonomous bulldozers that spread and level CSG embankment material in successive lifts at the Naruse Dam construction site, with more than ten automated machines working around the clock since 2020, monitored by three remote 'IT pilots' 400 km away.

tasks.label: Operate tractors or bulldozers to perform such tasks as clearing land, mixing sludge, trimming backfills, or building roadways or parking lots.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Site development on an open greenfield parcel (commercial pad, subdivision, solar/wind project): dozer strips topsoil, pushes and spreads fill in lifts, and rough-grades a building pad to a GPS design model, working with scrapers/haul trucks over acres of open ground.

Roadway or parking lot construction: dozer spreads and cuts subgrade and base material to design grade in an active corridor, working alongside haul trucks, graders, rollers, flaggers and traffic control, with grade checked to paving tolerance before the next trade follows.

Trimming backfills and finish grading in tight quarters: dozer/tractor pushes and trims backfill along foundations, retaining walls, utility trenches and curb lines, repositioning constantly, taking hand signals from pipe or concrete crews, and avoiding buried and above-ground obstructions.

Land clearing on raw ground: dozer pushes over brush and trees, grubs stumps and roots, windrows and piles debris, and works across uneven terrain with unknown obstacles (rocks, old foundations, soft spots).

Bulk dozing at an institution-controlled industrial site: stockpile push and slot dozing at a mine or quarry, dump/leach-pad construction, landfill working-face push and cover spreading, and reclamation grading, with restricted access and a defined traffic plan.

Tractor work at a wastewater or compost facility: mixing and turning sludge/biosolids in drying beds or windrows with a tractor and implement, making repeated passes over a bounded, flat, facility-controlled area.

tasks.label: Connect hydraulic hoses, belts, mechanical linkages, or power takeoff shafts to tractors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Active job site: operator hooks a hydraulic attachment (auger, breaker, mulcher, grapple, broom) to a skid steer/compact track loader, backhoe or excavator - wipes dirt from quick-couplers, relieves residual pressure, pushes the couplers together until they latch, routes and secures the hoses, then tests function. Couplers are muddy, hose ends vary by attachment brand, ground is uneven, weather is whatever it is.

Contractor yard or staging area: mounting a PTO-driven implement (mower, chipper, pump, post driver) on a utility/agricultural tractor - sliding the splined driveline yoke onto the tractor PTO stub and seating the spring-loaded locking collar, hooking the driveline shield's safety chain to the frame, then connecting two hydraulic hoses and the 7-pin electrical lead.

Job site: connecting mechanical linkages - dropping three-point hitch lower arms onto implement pins and inserting lynch/klik pins, fitting the top link and adjusting the turnbuckle, dropping a drawbar or pintle pin for a towed compactor/water trailer, hooking safety chains, with the implement sitting where it was parked on uneven, soft ground so parts must be nudged into alignment.

Shop or maintenance bay: installing or replacing belts during scheduled service on a tractor/loader engine - releasing the tensioner or loosening an alternator bracket, routing the serpentine or V-belt around several pulleys in a cramped engine bay, setting tension and checking alignment.

Field work under degraded conditions: couplers that will not mate because of trapped pressure, dirt or a damaged/mismatched fitting - fetching an adapter, wrenching threaded JIC/ORFS fittings, swapping a burst hose, bleeding air, then checking for leaks; done in mud, cold or tight quarters beside the machine.
