sources.claim: flextos SUPERCUT CNC is a commercially sold CNC milling/sawing table built specifically for drywall trades: gypsum- and cement-based boards are held on the table and the programmed machine performs the milling, sawing and cut-out shapes (circles, rectangles, arches) automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shop CNC cutting of board materials. It is the same operation as the worker's bench cut — a flat gypsum, cement or fiber panel held on a table and cut to a programmed outline for openings — at equal or better precision, so it transfers to socket, pipe and fixture cut-outs including lay-in ceiling tiles.

sources.title: More Contractors See Benefits of Drywall Finishing Robot | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: The most capable drywall robot actually deployed on US construction sites, Canvas, performs finishing only — spraying compound, taping and sanding — and does not measure or cut openings in panels.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the state of the art for autonomous drywall work in the unstructured jobsite environment (E3); it establishes what jobsite systems do (finishing), supporting the negative judgment that no cited system cuts openings on site.

sources.title: Robots under Autonomous Control at Robot Lab | Shimizu Corporation
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy uses two 6-axis arms to lift a ceiling board into position and screw it to the grid after sensing the frame, but the demonstrated capability is board installation, not measuring or cutting openings; it was shown under autonomous control in the company's robot laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic ceiling-board handling on building sites. Cited only to show the frontier of ceiling robotics — placement and fastening — which does not include measuring and cutting fixture openings, supporting the negative E3/E2 judgments.

tasks.label: Cut metal or wood framing and trim to size, using cutting tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial interior build-out: cutting light-gauge steel studs and track to length for partitions, soffits and bulkheads. Worker measures in the field, marks, and cuts with aviation snips, a portable metal chop saw or shear at a temporary cut station amid stacked material, other trades and dust.

Suspended acoustical ceiling work: cutting main tees, cross tees and perimeter wall angle to length (including mitered corners) with aviation snips or a grid shear, working off a ladder or lift in a room whose dimensions rarely match module sizes, with cuts fitted around columns, ducts and light fixtures.

Cutting wood framing members for backing and support: furring strips, blocking, nailers and wood lath cut to length with a circular saw or miter saw on the jobsite, sized from field measurements to fit between existing studs, joists and obstructions.

Cutting metal trim and beads to size: corner bead, J-bead, L-bead, reveal and expansion trim cut to length with snips, bead cutters or a chop saw, including miters at outside corners and returns, at a jobsite cut area.

Residential remodel or repair inside an occupied home: cutting a handful of framing pieces and wood trim to fit out-of-square, non-standard existing conditions, in a cramped room with furniture, using a cordless circular saw or handsaw on sawhorses.

Contractor prefabrication shop or yard: cutting studs, track, grid components and trim to size in batches from a cut list for prefabricated wall or ceiling assemblies, at fixed benches and saw stations under shop supervision.

sources.system: FRAMECAD light gauge steel (LGS) roll-forming machine / FRAMECAD System
sources.title: LGS Machine: Light Gauge Steel Roll-Formers Cut Costs & Build Faster
sources.claim: FRAMECAD light-gauge steel roll-forming lines take steel coil and automatically shape, punch and cut framing members (studs, track) to length per digital design, producing members ready for assembly; commercially deployed in framing factories worldwide.

sources.title: 5 Ways Robotic Automation Is Enhancing Cold-Formed Steel Construction
sources.claim: Industry association material contrasts manual on-site stud cutting with BIM-driven automated roll forming that produces studs and tracks cut precisely ... specification, confirming cut-to-size metal framing is an established automated factory process, not an on-site robotic one.

sources.system: Randek ZeroLabor robotic framing (Robotic Stud Feeder / Nogging Machine)
sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor robotic framing line automatically cuts and places wood studs and noggings to the correct length inside a wall-panel production line; a commercially sold system installed in prefab housing factories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting wood framing members to length in a panel plant. Same materials (dimensional wood studs and blocking) and same accepted output (members cut to specified length within framing tolerance) as the installer's furring/blocking cuts.

sources.title: TigerSaw 1000 - TigerStop automated table saw
sources.claim: TigerSaw 1000 is a commercially sold, fully automatic push-feeding optimizing saw station that crosscuts wood and plastic stock to programmed lengths from a downloaded cut list at +/-0.012 in accuracy; TigerStop's SawGear software handles crown molding, trim and baseboard cut lists.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting wood trim and framing stock to size at a shop saw station. Identical objects (linear wood trim and framing stock) and tighter precision than jobsite hand cutting; the machine feeds and cuts autonomously from a cut list.

sources.system: Dallan D5 T-bar roll forming systems
sources.title: T-bar ceiling T-grid - Roll forming machines | Dallan
sources.claim: Dallan D5 roll-forming plants are a named commercial product line for manufacturing suspended-ceiling T-bars (cross tees and main runners), the same cold-formed profiles a ceiling installer cuts to length on site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: producing ceiling grid tees and wall angle at specified lengths. Same cold-formed steel profiles as the on-site cut, and the line's cut-off sets the member length, which is the same accepted output as cutting grid to size.

sources.developer: Roll forming machine industry (rollformingmachine.us technical article)
sources.title: Rollforming Lines | Roll Forming Machines | USA
sources.claim: Roll-forming lines end with a flying cutoff press that cuts the formed profile to length automatically and accurately to the design specification, the standard mechanism by which metal framing, trim and bead profiles are cut to size in a plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting cold-formed metal trim and bead stock to length. Same materials (galvanized steel profiles such as corner bead and wall angle) and same accepted output (profile cut to a specified length).

sources.title: Autonomous Drywall Finishing Robotic System - CPWR Construction Solutions
sources.claim: The drywall jobsite robot that is actually deployed (Canvas) performs mudding, taping and sanding of installed board; no deployed jobsite robot cuts framing or trim to size in situ.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the jobsite (E3) state of the art: the one deployed drywall jobsite robot finishes board and does not cut framing or trim to size.

tasks.label: Cut fixture or border tiles to size, using keyhole saws, and insert them into surrounding frameworks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial construction (office, school, retail build-out): after full 2x2/2x4 lay-in tiles are set, the installer measures each out-of-square perimeter opening, scribes and cuts border tiles with a knife/keyhole saw, cuts tiles to receive recessed lights, sprinkler heads, diffusers and speakers, then tilts each piece up through the grid and drops it onto the tee flanges. Work from stilts or a lift, amid other trades, dust and debris.

Occupied institutional facility (hospital wing, school, office, retail store) renovation or repair: replacement or re-fit of tiles in an existing grid around light fixtures, sprinklers and diffusers; field-cut border tiles at new partitions; off-hours work with dust barriers, furniture and equipment present.

Gypsum-board ceiling work in new construction: cutting openings in ceiling board with a keyhole saw for can lights, HVAC registers and sprinkler penetrations, cutting fill/border pieces to size, and fitting them into the surrounding drywall-grid or furring framework overhead.

Residential and small light-commercial jobs (basement drop ceiling, small tenant suite, remodel): irregular room shapes, out-of-square walls, ducts and pipes intruding into the plenum; tiles cut to odd border widths and notched around obstructions, then inserted into the grid.

Specialty or decorative ceilings: metal pan, wood-slat, tegular/reveal-edge or acoustic-cloud systems, curved or angled borders, high atrium work from a boom lift; custom scribing of border panels and field-cut fixture penetrations in finished-face material where damage is not acceptable.

sources.system: 天井ボード取付ロボット (ceiling board mounting robot, Kajima × tmsuk)
sources.title: 天井ボード取付ロボットと移動式天台を開発～システム天井施工における省人化と仮設材の大幅削減を実現～ | プレスリリース | 鹿島建設
sources.claim: Kajima's ceiling-board mounting robot, co-developed with tmsuk, was introduced on an office building under construction; after a worker specifies the work area on a tablet, the robot measures its position relative to the ceiling substructure and automatically moves, adjusts and fixes boards into the grid substructure (~1 min per board, 40-board stocker), while skilled workers handle boards in narrow/edge areas the robot cannot reach. No cutting of boards is performed by the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inserting standard (uncut) system-ceiling boards into the grid framework. It substantiates robotic insertion into a ceiling framework on a real site, but the press release states craftsmen still install the boards in narrow/edge zones, i.e. the cut-to-fit border and fixture tiles that this task covers.

sources.system: システム天井施工ロボット (system ceiling construction workroid)
sources.title: ロボット同士が指示し合い天井を施工する「システム天井施工ロボット」を実現場に適用、鹿島とテムザックが開発
sources.claim: Kajima and tmsuk applied a 'system ceiling construction robot' at an actual construction site; the machines communicate position information to each other and transport and install hanging bolts, T-bars and ceiling boards. They do not cut border or fixture tiles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling the suspended-ceiling grid and setting full boards. Shows on-site robotic handling of ceiling components but no measuring/cutting of border or fixture tiles, so it does not carry over to the cut-to-fit step.

sources.title: Robots under Autonomous Control at Robot Lab | Shimizu Corporation
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy uses sensors to recognize the position of ceiling grid framing, inserts suspension bolts, lifts a ceiling board into position with one arm and screws it with the other, under autonomous control; the family of robots was taken to a high-rise building site in Osaka.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing and fastening full ceiling boards into overhead framing. Comparable objects and overhead framework insertion, but the robot works with pre-sized boards and does no keyhole-saw cutting for borders or fixtures.

sources.title: Shimizu Deploys Robot for Installing Raised Floor Named “Robo-Buddy Floor” | Shimizu Corporation
sources.claim: Shimizu deployed Robo-Buddy Floor at the SHIN-OSAKA DOI BLDG No5 project, where it locates panel positions with an arm-mounted camera, lifts a panel from a carrying robot and attaches it ... adjustable pedestals, working alongside craftsmen.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precise placement of rigid modular panels into a supporting framework (pedestal grid) at a building site; supports panel insertion capability but involves no cutting of panels to fit borders or fixtures.

sources.developer: Randek AB (deployed at FrameTec, Camp Verde, Arizona)
sources.title: This Plant Runs Itself - Offsite Builder Magazine
sources.claim: In FrameTec's panel plant, two Randek robots apply sheathing board to framed wall panels, fasten it, and ...; Randek's ZeroLabor robotic cells cut, frame, sheath, glue and route with only monitoring and material-loading labor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fixing a board panel into a surrounding framework and cutting fixture/rough openings in it. Same class of sheet material and millimetre-level fit, and the whole sequence (place into framework + cut openings) is done by one automated cell with the frame fixtured on a table — i.e. an E1 purpose-built presentation of the work.

sources.title: WEINMANN WALLTEQ Multi-Function Bridges - Stiles Machinery
sources.claim: WEINMANN WALLTEQ CNC multifunction bridges, used on prefabricated wall-element lines, fasten planking to the element and provide routing and drilling to cut rough openings such as windows, doors and power outlets in the sheathing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-cutting fixture-sized openings (outlets, windows) in board fixed to a framework, in a fixtured factory cell — the cutting-and-fitting operation of this task with comparable board material and tolerances.

sources.title: KOBOTS - Apps on Google Play / Kobots I Products
sources.claim: KOBOTS sells a mobile cutting robot for construction boards in several sizes (up to 1200 x 2500 mm); the operator enters measurements in a phone app and the machine automatically cuts the boards on site, dust-free.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting plasterboard/ceiling boards to specified size. The board is clamped in the machine's own purpose-built frame (an E1-style presentation of the work) and the measurements are supplied by a human; the machine does not insert the piece into the ceiling framework.

tasks.label: Coordinate work with drywall finishers who cover the seams between drywall panels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Trim rough edges from wallboard to maintain even joints, using knives.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New residential construction, walls: after screwing 4x8 or 4x12 sheets to wood studs, the hanger runs a utility knife along the perimeter and inside corners to cut off board that overhangs framing, door bucks and window returns, so the next sheet butts tight and the joint is even. Dusty, unfinished framing; boards deliberately cut oversize; the worker judges by eye and feel where the edge is proud.

On-site cut station (stack of board on the floor or a pair of horses, residential or commercial): sheets are scored, snapped and back-cut to size, then the ragged snapped edge and torn face paper are trimmed and the cut edge back-beveled with a knife before the piece is lifted into place.

Commercial interior fit-out (offices, healthcare, schools; metal stud partitions): after hanging, trimming ragged edges around electrical box cutouts, sprinkler and duct penetrations, window/door openings and control joints, and shaving over-tight board edges so sheets seat flush and joints line up.

Ceiling work: overhead from stilts, a baker scaffold or a lift, trimming board edges at the wall/ceiling junction, at soffits and around light fixtures and diffusers, cutting off overhang and cleaning crushed edges so perimeter joints are even.

Remodel/repair in an occupied home or occupied building: cutting back the ragged, broken or water-damaged edges of existing wallboard around a patch or new opening to a straight, sound edge over backing, in tight, furnished spaces with existing finishes to protect.

Offsite prefab/modular plant: boards applied to wall or ceiling panels at a production station; the worker trims the board flush to the panel frame and cleans up edges and openings before the panel moves down the line. Fixed layout, standard panel sizes, plant-controlled conditions.

sources.date: 2025-01 (page); product line in commercial production for years
sources.title: WEINMANN multifunction bridges | HOMAG
sources.claim: WEINMANN (HOMAG) multifunction bridges perform all panel-sheathing operations on framed wall, ceiling, roof and gable elements fully automatically under CNC control: fastening the board to the frame, formatting (trimming the panel outline flush) and cutting every opening.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: CNC formatting/trimming of wallboard on a fixtured panel table. It yields the same accepted output as knife trimming - board edges cut flush to the frame so adjoining boards meet in an even joint - on the same material and to tighter tolerance; only the cutting implement (router/saw vs utility knife) differs.

sources.title: WEINMANN Multifunction Bridge WALLTEQ M-300
sources.claim: The WALLTEQ M-300 multifunction bridge trims, saws, staples, marks and nails sheathing, with a sawing unit described as suited to plasterboard processing and a high-performance trimmer that cuts openings such as socket holes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine sawing/trimming of plasterboard to final size and cutting of socket-box openings. Same material and same required outcome as knife cut-to-size and edge trimming at a cut station, at equal or better edge quality.

sources.title: High flexibility and quality with the WEINMANN compact line | HOMAG
sources.claim: A deployed WALLTEQ M-380 compact line at Holzbau Henz (Trierweiler, Germany), with BUILDTEQ assembly tables and vacuum lifters, processes gypsum plasterboard as a standard material and produces roof, ceiling and special elements as well as walls.
sources.transferJustification: Confirms the automatic trimming/formatting evidence applies to gypsum wallboard (not only wood sheathing) and to ceiling elements, i.e. the materials and element types the human task covers.

sources.system: WEINMANN production line (multifunction bridge + FRAMETEQ F-500)
sources.title: The Next Step Into Automated Off-Site Construction in the US | HOMAG
sources.claim: A US prefabrication plant (JL Schwieters Construction, Hugo, Minnesota) runs a WEINMANN production line in which wall elements are processed on ..., which nails the sheathing and trims the openings such as windows and ....
sources.transferJustification: Shows the fasten-then-trim workflow running in routine US production, i.e. the trimmed output is accepted by builders, establishing worker-quality completion at E1 rather than a one-off demonstration.

sources.title: Development of a humanoid robot prototype, HRP-5P, capable of heavy labor
sources.claim: AIST's HRP-5P humanoid autonomously handled and installed gypsum board at a mock-up residential construction site; it lifts and fastens boards, with no reported trimming of board edges with a cutting tool, and the setting was a laboratory simulation rather than a live site.
sources.transferJustification: Closest jobsite-oriented drywall manipulation result; cited to bound the unstructured-site (E3) judgment - board handling and screwing was shown in a mock-up, knife trimming of rough edges was not.

sources.title: Okibo, Global Leader in Construction Painting and Drywall Finishing Robotics, Launches US Headquarters
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7 autonomous robots work on active construction sites in Europe and the US, but their scope is drywall finishing (plastering, skim coating, painting), not cutting or trimming wallboard edges.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the E3 judgment: the drywall robots actually deployed on unstructured jobsites apply and sand compound; none cuts or trims wallboard edges.

tasks.label: Install horizontal and vertical metal or wooden studs to frames so that wallboard can be attached to interior walls.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial interior build-out (office, school, medical, retail shell under construction): lay out and shoot floor/deck track, cut and set light-gauge steel studs at 16"/24" o.c., add horizontal bridging/blocking and door king studs, plumb and screw off, so wallboard can be hung. Open shell, other trades working, dust, temporary lighting, as-built deck variation.

Residential and light-commercial wood stud partition framing in new construction (apartments, single-family, small tenant spaces): nail vertical studs and horizontal blocking to top and bottom plates, set the wall in place, plumb and brace it for wallboard.

Renovation of a gutted or newly demised space inside an existing building: new straight full-height partitions framed to dimensioned drawings, floor and ceiling reasonably regular, access through corridors and elevators.

Retrofit framing and furring against as-found existing conditions: hat channel/wood furring shimmed to out-of-plumb masonry or concrete, patch framing at demolished openings, framing scribed around existing pipes, conduit, and beams in an occupied or partly occupied building.

Complex in-place assemblies: soffits and bulkheads around ducts, chases around columns and risers, elevator/stair shaft-wall framing, curved radius walls with bent track, and tall walls framed from scissor lifts or scaffold, all fitted to as-built conditions.

Off-site panel/prefab shop: worker frames wall panels on assembly tables or jigs from a cut list or BIM output — placing studs and noggings into top and bottom plates and fastening them — before sheathing or wallboard is applied.

sources.title: WEINMANN Framing Station FRAMETEQ F-700
sources.claim: WEINMANN (HOMAG) FRAMETEQ F-700 framing station is a commercially sold machine that produces timber wall frame works fully automatically, placing studs (including angled studs for gable and spandrel elements) and fastening them to the plates/belts.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, wooden-stud variant: vertical and horizontal members are positioned to layout and fastened into a frame that receives sheathing/wallboard; the difference from the field job is only that the work is brought to the machine.

sources.system: WEINMANN FRAMETEQ framing stations (North American distribution)
sources.developer: HOMAG / WEINMANN, distributed by Stiles Machinery
sources.title: WEINMANN FRAMETEQ Framing Stations - Stiles Machinery
sources.claim: The FRAMETEQ framing stations sold in North America perform automated stud positioning, indexing, nailing and cutting, with automatic material feeding available.
sources.transferJustification: Same task in a factory cell: studs are positioned at layout spacing and nailed to the plates of the frame, which is the framing step that precedes wallboard attachment.

sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor robotic framing system automatically cuts and places vertical studs and horizontal noggings into wall frames in offsite wall-element factories.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the task's "horizontal and vertical" members: noggings are the horizontal blocking and studs the verticals, assembled into the frame that later receives wallboard.

sources.title: Randek - Manufacturing Today
sources.claim: Randek's robotic framing cells have been installed in real production plants, including two ZeroLabor units in North America.

sources.system: House of Design Robotics Panel Framing (ABB robot cells)
sources.title: Panel Framing - House of Design Robotics
sources.claim: House of Design Robotics sells ABB-robot cells installed in operating factories that frame wall panels by automatically inserting and fastening top and bottom plates and ....
sources.transferJustification: Same task in a robotic cell: studs/span members are inserted between plates and fastened to form the frame that wallboard is attached to.

sources.title: HOMAG Product Finder: Frame work station FRAMETEQ F-300 / Robot FEEDBOT F-500
sources.claim: The WEINMANN FEEDBOT F-500 robot automatically inserts studs and belts into the frame work on timber framing lines.
sources.transferJustification: Material handling plus placement of studs into the frame is the core motion of the task; the robot performs it inside the framing cell.

sources.system: Robotic CFS panel framing cells (BIM-driven robotic arms; e.g., OFFSITEK's Charlotte, NC panel factory)
sources.developer: CFS panel fabricators / Steel Framing Industry Association members (article by SFIA in STRUCTURE Magazine)
sources.title: Robots in Cold-Formed Steel Projects — STRUCTURE Magazine
sources.claim: In cold-formed (light-gauge) steel panel plants, robotic arms guided by BIM-derived paths weld and screw studs to tracks and place sheathing; named CFS panel manufacturers such as OFFSITEK run robotic assembly in their factories.
sources.transferJustification: This is the metal-stud form of the task (studs screwed to track), performed in factory cells; it corroborates that the timber-line capability carries to steel studs and track.

sources.system: Robo-Buddy (with Robo-Carrier, Robo-Welder), Shimz Smart Site
sources.title: Shimizu Corporation introduces robots for civil construction
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy works on real high-rise construction sites, autonomously navigating by BIM/SLAM and using two arms to insert ceiling suspension ... ceiling base material and fasten ceiling boards — the closest deployed in-place framing-type robot, and it addresses ceilings, not wall stud partitions.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the nearest in-place (site) analogue — overhead ceiling base-material assembly — to show that no deployed site robot frames vertical stud partitions to as-built walls; it does not substantiate the wall-framing task.

tasks.label: Fasten metal or rockboard lath to the structural framework of walls, ceilings, or partitions of buildings, using nails, screws, staples, or wire-ties.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Exterior stucco lathing: self-furring diamond-mesh metal lath stapled/nailed over WRB and sheathing on wood- or steel-framed walls of a house or apartment building, worked from ladders/scaffold outdoors, cutting and lapping around windows, corners and penetrations, in variable weather.

Interior commercial plaster lathing: expanded metal lath screwed/wire-tied to steel studs, columns, arches and soffits during fit-out of an occupied-to-be building, with corner beads, curved and cut-to-fit pieces, other trades working nearby.

Overhead ceiling lathing: 3.4 lb rib or diamond lath wire-tied or screwed to suspended furring channels/cross-furring for a plaster ceiling or exterior soffit, worked overhead from stilts or a lift in a building under construction.
Rock (gypsum) plaster-base board panels screwed to ceiling furring/joists in the interior fit-out of a new large commercial building, flat open floor plate, boards delivered in stacks.

Rock (gypsum) lath and small lath patches nailed to wood studs and joists in an occupied remodel or historic-plaster repair: irregular framing, cramped rooms, furniture and existing finishes to protect.
Fireproofing / enclosure lathing: metal lath wrapped and wire-tied around steel columns and beams, shaft and chase enclosures, tight and awkward spaces above ceilings.
Off-site panel shop: metal or gypsum lath fastened to framed wall panels lying flat on assembly tables/jigs in a panelization plant, repeated panel types from shop drawings.

sources.title: Multifunction bridge WALLTEQ M-300
sources.claim: WEINMANN WALLTEQ M-300 CNC multifunction bridge automatically staples, nails, marks and trims sheathing/planking (including plasterboard) onto fixtured timber-frame wall elements in prefabrication plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastening sheet planking (OSB, gypsum/plasterboard) to a stud framework with staples or nails at CAD-defined spacing. Same fastening operation, same substrate (framing members), same accuracy requirement (fastener must land in the member) as fastening lath; the sliding shoe presses flexible sheet material during fastening.

sources.system: WEINMANN WALLTEQ M-500 / M-300 insuFill multifunction bridge
sources.title: Multifunction Bridge WALLTEQ M-300 insuFill /M-500
sources.claim: The WALLTEQ M-500 class of multifunction bridge performs fastening fully automatically under CNC control on wall, roof and floor elements presented on the line.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above: automatic, unattended fastening of sheet layers onto framed elements held on a fixtured table, which is the E1 form of fastening lath to a framework.

sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor robotic cell automates sheathing of prefabricated wall panels, ..., including straightening studs before nailing so nails land on the stud.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a robot cell picking, positioning and nailing sheet material onto a framed panel held in a jig. Object handling, fastener placement accuracy on framing members and the fixtured environment match the E1 form of fastening lath to framing.

sources.title: A Production System for a New Era – The Shimizu Smart Site autonomous robots can transform a job site!
sources.claim: Shimizu's dual-arm Robo-Buddy senses the ceiling frame grid, holds a ceiling board up with one arm and screws it to the base material with the other, operating autonomously after tablet instruction on building sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: screwing rigid gypsum ceiling boards to a metal ceiling furring framework overhead — the same operation as fastening rock (gypsum) plaster-base panels to ceiling framing, with comparable panel size, fastener spacing and overhead access.

sources.title: 清水建設が天井施工ロボットをついに実用化、30年越しで開発成功 | 日経Robotics
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy Ceiling was applied on an actual Japanese construction site in March 2023, installing about 100 ceiling boards with a 100% success rate, described as finally reaching practical use.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as evidence 3 (screwing gypsum ceiling boards to ceiling framing); this item establishes on-site reliability at a real construction site rather than a laboratory.

sources.title: Shimizu Deploys Robot for Installing Raised Floor Named “Robo-Buddy Floor”
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy platform deployed on an active Shin-Osaka high-rise matched craftsmen in speed and accuracy when installing raised-floor panels, with roughly 70% labor saving.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the same dual-arm Robo-Buddy platform placing and fixing building panels on an active construction site; establishes that this platform reaches craftsman-level speed/accuracy in real site conditions, supporting the ceiling-board judgment.

sources.claim: At the karaksa hotel Shin-Osaka high-rise site, the interior multi-skill robot Robo-Buddy recognized the work location with sensors and autonomously inserted ceiling hanger bolts, positioned boards and drove screws alongside human workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous overhead board fastening to suspended ceiling framing on a real high-rise construction site; shows the environment of the deployment (an active jobsite, not a lab).

tasks.label: Install blanket insulation between studs and tack plastic moisture barriers over insulation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New single-family house under construction (mixed/warm climate): installer friction-fits unfaced or kraft-faced fiberglass/mineral-wool batts into 16 in. o.c. wood stud exterior wall cavities, cutting batts around outlet boxes, wires and pipes; no separate poly sheet because the kraft facing is the retarder. Dusty, unconditioned, cluttered site with other trades working.

Cold-climate new residential or light-commercial work: batts installed in stud cavities, then a continuous 6-mil polyethylene moisture barrier is rolled out over walls (and ceilings), stapled to studs/plates, lapped, cut around boxes and windows, and taped before drywall. Full-height sheets handled from ladders/stilts at a jobsite.

Commercial or multifamily interior fit-out: unfaced acoustic/sound batts friction-fit or wire-tied into light-gauge steel stud partitions and above suspended ceilings for STC ratings; no vapor barrier. Shell is enclosed but the floor is an active construction zone with scaffolds, ducts and conduit crossing cavities.

Overhead work on a jobsite: batts installed between ceiling joists, rafters, or in sloped-ceiling and garage-ceiling cavities, wire-supported or stapled, worked from ladders/lifts in tight, hot ceiling or attic spaces; no separate plastic sheet on this scope.

Retrofit/remodel of an occupied or partly finished building: insulating basement stud walls, crawl-space walls, knee walls or gutted rooms where framing is irregular, cavities are non-standard widths and are crossed by existing wiring, plumbing and ductwork; batts cut to fit and poly moisture barrier stapled over basement/crawl-space walls.

Offsite panelized/modular plant: framed wall or roof cassettes arrive flat and clamped on a production table and the worker fits batts into each cavity to a fixed cut list before sheathing is applied; controlled indoor plant, standard panel geometry.
