sources.claim: Peer-reviewed robotic method that autonomously inserts batt thermal insulation into light-frame wood wall panels with a 6-DOF arm and custom end effector, tested on mineral wool and fiberglass across frame sizes with 92.5% success, in a prefabrication (fixtured panel) setting.

sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: Commercial robotic cell that fully automates fitting insulation material into prefabricated wall, floor and roof elements on an offsite production line.

sources.title: Prefab Building Processes: Robots ensure a warm Home (LIGNA)
sources.claim: Trade coverage confirming Randek's robotic insulation of wall and ... runs fully automatically.

sources.system: Randek AutoWall line with ZeroLabor R2 robotic insulation
sources.title: Randek - References - Arcabo (ZeroLabor)
sources.claim: Customer reference showing a delivered robotic wall production line that includes robotized insulation for exterior and interior wall elements at a house manufacturer's plant.

sources.title: Tilbury Douglas deploys first humanoid robot on live construction site - Tech Digest
sources.claim: The first humanoid robot deployed by a Tier One contractor on a live construction site performs autonomous site navigation and 360-degree imagery capture, not material installation such as insulating or membrane tacking.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only to characterise the state of on-site (E3) construction robotics: the most advanced live-site humanoid deployment does data capture, so no on-site system substantiates batt installation or membrane tacking.

tasks.label: Assemble or install metal framing or decorative trim for windows, doorways, or vents.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial interior build-out (offices, schools, healthcare): lay out and assemble light-gauge steel framing for door openings and interior borrowed-lite window openings in metal-stud partitions - cut track and studs to field-measured lengths, build jamb/king studs, headers and sills, screw them to floor and deck track amid other trades, stacked material and changing conditions on an active jobsite.

Metal framing for vents in commercial work: framing openings and backing in drywall ceilings and walls for HVAC diffusers, grilles and access panels, and building metal-stud soffits, bulkheads and chases that enclose ductwork - overhead, field-fit around installed duct, from stilts, ladders or scissor lifts.

Residential new-build and remodel: cut and install metal or vinyl corner bead, J-bead/L-bead and casing trim around window openings, window returns, door openings and wall/ceiling vent openings after board hang - measure, cut and miter each piece, fasten by nail/screw/staple, clinch tool or spray adhesive, in as-found and sometimes occupied houses.

Commercial interiors after hang: install bead and trim accessories around door and borrowed-lite openings, window returns, archways, diffusers and access panels - L-bead/J-bead terminations at frames, corner bead on returns, plus decorative trim such as reveal moldings and expansion joints at openings.

Set knock-down or welded hollow-metal door frames into stud-wall rough openings: position, plumb and square the frame, shim, screw or strap anchors to jamb studs, brace and check for door swing before board is hung.

Offsite panel plant work: assemble metal-framed wall panels containing door and window openings on framing tables from pre-cut, pre-punched roll-formed studs and track, to shop drawings, inside a controlled manufacturing facility.

sources.title: Randek ZeroLabor Robotic System (product brochure)
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor Robotic Sub-Assembly system is a commercially launched robotic cell that automatically fabricates door and window rough-opening frames and multi-stud assemblies for wall panels in a factory line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly of timber rough-opening frames. Transfer to metal framing of window/door openings is close in geometry (rectangular frame of studs, header, sill fastened to plates/track) and precision (mm-level panel tolerances); cold-formed steel studs are lighter and dimensionally stable, which industry sources describe as more amenable to robotic assembly than lumber. Fastening differs (screwing vs nailing), a standard end-effector change.

sources.title: Randek builds on heritage of offsite automation | Built Offsite
sources.claim: Trade coverage of the same Randek system confirms it automates fabrication of door and window ... previously done manually in panel plants.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: opening-frame sub-assembly in a fixtured factory station corresponds to the 'assemble metal framing for windows/doorways' half of the task when the work is brought to the machine.

sources.date: product page retrieved 2026-07 (product line marketed for several years)
sources.title: WEINMANN Framing Station FRAMETEQ F-700
sources.claim: WEINMANN's FRAMETEQ F-700 framing station places studs with a gripper and fastens them, producing complete wall frameworks fully automatically in a purpose-built line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated framing of wall elements including openings in a fixtured framing station. Comparable members, fastening pattern and tolerances to metal stud framing of door/window openings; the same vendor supplies framing tables for steel-frame construction.

sources.system: WEINMANN steel-frame construction line (NC insert tables)
sources.title: Steel Frame Constructions | HOMAG
sources.claim: The same machine family is offered for cold-formed steel-frame construction, with NC-controlled insert tables that fasten steel frameworks automatically and automated sheathing attachment.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the fixtured framing-station approach is productized for metal stud panels; an operator still inserts members, so this is supporting context rather than a decisive autonomous system.

sources.system: Robotic arms in cold-formed steel (CFS) panel fabrication
sources.developer: CFS offsite manufacturers (e.g., OFFSITEK), reported by STRUCTURE magazine
sources.title: Robots in Cold-Formed Steel Projects | STRUCTURE magazine
sources.claim: Cold-formed steel panel factories use robotic arms to screw studs to tracks and place sheathing, with screw locations and spacing driven by the digital model.

sources.title: Robotic Light-Gauge Truss Welding Cell | Midwest Engineered Systems
sources.claim: A production robotic cell welds light-gauge galvanized steel members into large structural frames for a steel manufacturer, with parts presented in a fenced or light-curtained loading zone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic joining of light-gauge steel framing members into frames within a fixtured cell. Same material class and member sizes as metal stud/track opening framing; shows presented, fixtured CFS members can be joined to spec by a robot.

sources.title: OFFSITEK partners with Charlotte-area municipalities to deliver affordable housing using robots and steel | PR Newswire
sources.claim: An offsite builder operates a factory in Charlotte, NC where robots are used to produce cold-formed steel wall, floor and roof panels for houses.
sources.transferJustification: Supporting context that robotic CFS panel production, including panels with door and window openings, runs commercially in a purpose-built plant; press-release level detail, so autonomy is recorded as unclear.

sources.title: Autonomous Drywall Finishing Robotic System | CPWR Construction Solutions
sources.claim: The drywall robot actually deployed on US commercial jobsites is limited to finishing operations - spraying compound, taping and sanding - and does not install bead, trim or framing.
sources.transferJustification: Closest jobsite-deployed system in this trade; cited to bound capability - it finishes already-beaded walls, so it does not substantiate installing metal framing, bead or trim at openings.

tasks.label: Scribe and cut edges of tile to fit walls where wall molding is not specified.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial office/retail tenant fit-out: installer works from a lift or stilts at the perimeter of a 2x2 or 2x4 lay-in mineral-fiber suspended ceiling where no wall angle/molding is specified. Each border tile is measured against the as-built gypsum wall, scribed with pencil/straightedge, cut face-up with a utility knife (slight back-bevel) and dropped in. Active construction site: dust, staged material, other trades, walls out of square.

Renovation/alteration in an occupied institution (school, hospital, hotel, older retail): border tiles scribed to wavy plaster or masonry walls, around columns, pilasters, pipes and existing trim. Worker uses dividers/compass or a scrap-tile template to transfer the irregular contour, then cuts and test-fits, often at night with limited access.

Tegular/kerfed-and-rabbeted or concealed-grid tile: the perimeter cut must reproduce the reveal - the cut edge is rabbeted, kerfed or field-routed so the exposed edge matches the factory edge and sits at the correct plane against the wall. Cut with knife plus a tegular-edge cutting tool or router, then fitted.

Architectural/specialty ceilings (wood or metal pan, linear plank, felt/PET or fiberglass acoustic panels, clouds, direct-glued tile) where the scribed edge stays visible: tighter tolerance, harder or finish-face material, cut with fine saws/routers and dressed, then fitted to the wall.

Small residential or light-commercial job: basement or remodel drop ceiling in a private home, low headroom, irregular masonry/foundation walls, ductwork and beams; border tiles scribed and knife-cut on a makeshift bench.

sources.system: Zund G3 XL-3200 flatbed digital cutter (in production at Impact Acoustic)
sources.title: The impact of digital cutting - Zund
sources.claim: Impact Acoustic runs three Zund G3 XL-3200 flatbed CNC cutters in its Lucerne plant (plus an identical machine in the Philippines) cutting acoustic wall and ceiling panel material to custom CAD-defined shapes - projects running to 30,000 individual, each-one-different parts - at the precision and edge quality the maker's own standard requires.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting acoustic ceiling/wall panel blanks to arbitrary CAD outlines. Same material class (acoustic panel board), same operation (profile-cutting a panel edge), tighter tolerance than a hand-scribed ceiling tile; transfers once the wall profile is supplied as geometry.

sources.system: Zund G3 digital cutter with V-Cutting Tool
sources.date: retrieved 2026-07 (product line commercially sold since the 2010s)
sources.title: G3 digital cutter | Flatbed CNC Cutter | Zund
sources.claim: Zund's G3 flatbed CNC cutter line offers a V-cutting tool with nine cutting angles marketed for three-dimensional designs in fiberboard and acoustic panels - i.e. machining bevelled/rabbeted profiles into panel edges, not only through-cuts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: profiled (angled/rabbeted) edge cutting in acoustic panel stock, which is what re-forming a tegular reveal on a field-cut border tile requires.

sources.system: Proliner digital templating + CNC saw/router fabrication line (CNC Stonecrafters)
sources.title: Fabrication - CNC STONECRAFTERS
sources.claim: In countertop fabrication a Proliner digital templating system captures as-built cabinet and wall shapes, CAD converts the points, and CNC machines cut the slab so the piece has a scribed fit with no gap at the wall - the same scribe-to-an-irregular-wall outcome, produced by machine in a shop.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scribing a panel edge to an as-built, out-of-square wall and cutting it to fit. Harder material and tighter tolerance than mineral-fiber ceiling tile; shows the profile-capture-to-machine-cut chain yields an accepted scribed fit.

sources.system: WEINMANN WALLTEQ M-300 / M-500 multifunction bridge
sources.developer: Homag/Weinmann (distributed in the US by Stiles Machinery)
sources.date: brochure dated 2024-08 (posted 2025-01); product line in commercial use for years
sources.title: WEINMANN WALLTEQ multifunction bridges (brochure)
sources.claim: WEINMANN WALLTEQ multifunction bridges are CNC-controlled gantries used in prefabrication plants to saw, trim/rout, drill and fasten sheathing - including plasterboard - on fixtured wall, ceiling and roof elements driven by digital element data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine sawing/trimming of gypsum board and other sheathing to programmed outlines on fixtured building elements - the same board-cutting operation on a coarser material than ceiling tile.

sources.title: [Press Announcement] Construction Robot Laboratory Tours (April 23) - FPCJ
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy, a two-armed robot on an AGV, localizes from laser sensors and BIM and installs ceiling boards and floorboards - the closest on-site ceiling automation - but it places standard boards and is not reported to scribe or cut border tiles to as-built walls.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the on-site frontier: autonomous ceiling-board handling exists on jobsites, but no cited system measures an as-built wall and cuts a border tile to fit in situ.

sources.system: Okibo EG7 / EG7+; Canvas drywall finishing robot
sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction's Dirty Work Is Going Robotic - Architect Magazine
sources.claim: Autonomous interior-finishing robots working on US and European jobsites (Okibo EG7/EG7+, Canvas) perform plastering, painting and drywall mudding/sanding only; none of the cited jobsite systems scribes or cuts ceiling tile to fit walls.

tasks.label: Hang dry lines to wall moldings to guide positioning of main runners.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial office tenant buildout: after wall molding (wall angle) is set at the benchmark height around an open floor, the installer stretches taut dry lines (mason's line) from wall molding to wall molding across 30-60 ft spans at main-runner spacing and elevation, ties/clamps them off, checks level and squareness, and leaves them up to guide main runner hanging. Active jobsite with other trades, debris, lifts and ladders.

Occupied institutional renovation (school, hospital wing, office remodel): room-by-room dry lines run under and around existing ductwork, sprinkler drops, conduit and soffits; irregular wall conditions, partial demolition, dust protection, often night/weekend shifts with tight access.

Large open-span space (big-box retail, gym, warehouse office, terminal area): very long dry lines (60 ft+) requiring intermediate support or laser cross-check to control sag, run from scissor lifts over uneven or obstructed floors, in high bays with variable lighting.

Small rooms, corridors, closets and residential basement drop ceilings: short, frequent dry lines in confined, irregular geometry with pipes, beams and out-of-square walls; usually one worker on a ladder, minimal staging, frequent repositioning.

Shop/prefabrication facility: ceiling grid for modular units or prefabricated ceiling assemblies laid out on a fixed line, with dry lines strung across fixtured wall angles on a repeatable jig under controlled indoor conditions.

sources.system: System Ceiling Construction Robot (tmsuk / Kajima swarm robots)
sources.developer: tmsuk Co., Ltd. with Kajima Corporation
sources.title: Release | World's First AI-Powered Swarm Robots for Suspended Ceiling Construction
sources.claim: tmsuk and Kajima built a swarm of small robots that install hanging bolts, assemble T-bar grid and place ceiling boards for suspended ceilings, tested on active office construction sites in Japan; the robots position grid members from digital position data exchanged between robots rather than by hanging physical dry lines, and humans still perform edge work.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task: assembling suspended-ceiling T-bar main runners on jobsites. It does NOT substantiate this task: the robots derive runner position from BIM/robot-to-robot data and never string, tension or tie a dry line to wall molding, so no dry-line output is produced for a human crew, and the system remains a prototype with humans doing perimeter work.

sources.title: Hilti Unveils BIM-Enabled Construction Jobsite Robot
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot performs semi-autonomous overhead drilling on commercial construction sites: an operator drives it into position and it then drills the programmed holes automatically from BIM data set out with a total station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: BIM-guided overhead ceiling work (drilling anchor holes for hangers) in the same rough-in phase and same jobsites. It does not transfer to this task: Jaibot only drills fixed points overhead with a rigid tool; it has no capability to grasp, span, tension or tie a flexible line between wall moldings.

sources.title: FieldPrinter autonomous robot automates jobsite layout - Construction Briefing
sources.claim: Dusty Robotics' FieldPrinter is a commercially deployed autonomous mobile robot that prints BIM layout lines directly on jobsite floors, paired with a robotic total station, at accuracy of about 1/16 inch, replacing manual string-line-and-chalk floor layout.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: jobsite layout that substitutes for string lines. It does not substantiate this task: FieldPrinter prints two-dimensional marks on the floor deck and cannot work overhead, cannot set elevation references, and cannot attach or tension a physical dry line to wall molding at ceiling height.

sources.title: HP Revolutionizes Construction Layout Process With New SitePrint Robotic Solution
sources.claim: HP SitePrint is a commercially released autonomous layout printing robot used on construction sites to mark plans on floors, again a floor-marking device rather than an overhead line-stringing device.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated construction layout replacing manual chalk/string layout. It does not transfer: the machine is a floor-driving printer with no manipulator, no ability to reach wall molding at ceiling height, and no ability to handle a flexible line.

tasks.label: Apply or mount acoustical tile or blocks, strips, or sheets of shock-absorbing materials to ceilings or walls of buildings to reduce reflection of sound or to decorate rooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial construction / tenant fit-out, large open area (office floor plate, school, retail): lay 2x2 or 2x4 mineral-fiber acoustical tiles into an already-hung T-bar grid across the space, including straight border cuts at walls and cutouts around light fixtures, diffusers and sprinkler heads; dusty, cluttered active site, work from stilts or a rolling scaffold.

New construction / fit-out of cut-up spaces: corridors, small offices, restrooms, patient rooms, classrooms with soffits. High ratio of cut and notched tiles, many penetrations and irregular room shapes, tight access around ducts, conduit and door frames; frequent coordination with other trades.

Renovation or replacement in an existing, largely occupied facility (school, hospital, office): remove stained/damaged acoustical tiles and install replacements, or re-tile a space after MEP work; furniture and equipment in place, often night/weekend work, tiles must match existing pattern and be handled without soiling.

Wall-applied acoustical or decorative panels: fabric-wrapped fiberglass panels, wood-slat panels, mineral-wool boards or foam strips glued, Z-clipped or screwed to walls (and some ceilings) in auditoriums, conference rooms, restaurants, studios, gyms; layout lines, level/plumb alignment and tight visible reveals matter.

Suspended acoustical clouds, baffles and high-ceiling work: hanging cloud rafts or vertical baffles from structure in atria, lobbies, gyms and arenas, or mounting acoustic panels high on walls from a scissor/boom lift; variable heights, obstructions and structural attachment points.

sources.system: Shimizu ceiling board construction robot (Robo-Buddy Ceiling / Robo-BC) with assist robot
sources.title: Development of Autonomous Robots for Construction (ISARC 2024)
sources.claim: Shimizu's autonomous ceiling board construction robot (two industrial arms on an AMR, with a materials assist robot) measures the ceiling foundation, lifts ~14 kg plasterboards, presses them tight against installed boards and screws them, and was applied at a real construction site in Japan where it installed 74 boards (123 m2); human workers still perform board cutting/processing and precision perimeter tasks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mounting plasterboard sheets overhead onto a ceiling grid/foundation. Objects (large flat boards, heavier than acoustical tile), overhead placement precision (gap-free positioning against adjacent boards) and the environment (interior fit-out of an active building site) match acoustical ceiling panel mounting; it does not cover cut/perimeter tiles.

sources.system: AI swarm robots for suspended ceiling construction (Hanging Bolt, T-Bar Assembly, Ceiling Board Installation robots)
sources.developer: tmsuk Co., Ltd. with Kajima Corporation
sources.title: Release | World's First AI-Powered Swarm Robots for Suspended Ceiling Construction | tmsuk co., ltd.
sources.claim: tmsuk and Kajima developed a swarm of compact edge-AI robots that automate suspended ceiling construction in office buildings — installing hanging bolts, assembling the T-bar grid, and a Ceiling Board Installation Robot that places ceiling panels onto the ...; the prototype has been tested on multiple active office ..., with humans still doing edge work.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task (placing panels into a suspended ceiling grid), but it is a prototype field trial and the release notes humans still perform edge work and parts of the process, so whole-instance completion including border/cut tiles is not substantiated.

sources.title: WEINMANN multifunction bridges | HOMAG
sources.claim: WEINMANN multifunction bridges are commercially sold CNC gantries used in prefabricated building element factories that carry out all planking of framed elements fully automatically — fastening boards, formatting them and cutting all openings — for wall, ceiling, roof and gable elements.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mounting boards/sheets onto a fixtured wall or ceiling element in a factory, including automatic cutting of openings — the same operation as applying acoustical sheet material to a ceiling or wall element, with comparable board sizes and millimetre placement precision.

sources.developer: HOMAG Group / WEINMANN (brochure distributed by Stiles Machinery)
sources.title: WEINMANN WALLTEQ multifunction bridges brochure
sources.claim: The WALLTEQ bridge brochure lists the board materials the machines process, including gypsum plasterboard and soft wood fibre board, and shows a processing example of gypsum plasterboard.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the fixtured factory machines handle the class of sheet goods used for acoustical/insulating board (soft wood fibre, gypsum board), supporting transfer to mounting acoustical sheets on ceiling or wall elements.

sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor is a commercially offered robotic sheathing cell (two to five robots) that automates sheeting of prefabricated wall panels, floor ... with multiple layers of material, including robotic gluing, a robotic saw tool and router tool changing, and sorts OSB and plasterboard waste separately.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robots pick, glue and fasten board sheets onto fixtured wall/floor/roof elements in a purpose-built cell — the same handling, adhesive application and fastening required to mount acoustical boards or decorative acoustic sheets onto a wall or ceiling element presented to the machine.

sources.system: Cloud-based hierarchical imitation learning ceiling-tile installation robot (KUKA KR120, simulation/lab)
sources.title: Cloud-Based Hierarchical Imitation Learning for Scalable Transfer of Construction Skills from Human Workers to Assisting Robots
sources.claim: University of Michigan researchers studying robotic ceiling tile installation report that ceiling tiles are larger than the grid slots and must be maneuvered through them, a manipulation ordinary motion planners cannot handle; their evaluation used VR demonstrations and a simulated KUKA KR120, not a field installation.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (lay-in acoustical ceiling tile), cited as context showing the in-situ lay-in maneuver remains a research problem demonstrated only in simulation; it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Remove existing plaster, drywall, or paneling, using crowbars and hammers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential remodel: gut existing gypsum board from walls (and sometimes ceiling) of a room in an occupied or vacant house or apartment. Worker scores/cuts, pries sheets and chunks off wood studs with a flat bar and hammer, works around outlets, switches, plumbing stacks and ductwork, pulls remaining screws/nails, avoids damaging framing and adjacent finished rooms, controls dust, and piles debris for haul-out.

Commercial tenant strip-out: remove gypsum partitions, wood/laminate paneling and suspended ceiling tile and grid in an office, retail or medical space undergoing renovation, often at night in an otherwise occupied building. Overhead MEP (conduit, sprinkler, ductwork) must be left intact, adjacent finishes protected, and demolition kept within marked scope lines.

Old plaster-and-lath removal in a pre-1950s home or building: break dense keyed plaster off wood or metal lath with hammer and crowbar, pull lath from studs, work overhead on ceilings from ladders or scaffold, handle very heavy dusty debris, and work around possible lead paint or asbestos content and hidden knob-and-tube wiring.

Water- or fire-damage remediation: cut and pry out wet, moldy or charred drywall (often the lower 2-4 ft of walls, or a whole ceiling) in a basement, bathroom or kitchen, working around cabinets, fixtures, baseboard and insulation, saving undamaged material where possible, in a contaminated and sometimes structurally compromised space.

Small selective removal for repair: open a damaged or leaking section of wall or ceiling, cut back squarely to the nearest framing members with utility knife/saw, pry the piece free without cracking surrounding board or nicking wires and pipes, so a patch or new opening can be framed in.

sources.date: 2025-08 (page modified); product line in commercial use for decades
sources.title: Why Brokk — Brokk Global
sources.claim: Brokk, the leading maker of machines used for interior demolition (breaking walls, floors, stair removal), builds remote-controlled demolition robots: an operator drives the machine continuously by radio remote; the machines are not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the demolition class of machine used for interior strip-out of walls and slabs; it establishes that the deployed machines for this work are continuously operator-driven, not autonomous.

sources.system: Bots2ReC mobile robotic units (mobile platform + arm with abrasive tool)
sources.developer: RWTH Aachen University (IGMR) with Robotnik, indurad and EU H2020 consortium
sources.title: Bots2ReC: introducing mobile robotic units on construction sites for asbestos rehabilitation (Construction Robotics)
sources.claim: The EU Bots2ReC project built mobile manipulators that strip asbestos-containing plaster, tiles and tile adhesive from walls of apartment buildings using an abrasive grinding tool; an operator selects wall areas on a virtual site model and the removal is then executed autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic removal of wall surface material (plaster/tile) inside dwellings under renovation. It is the closest demonstrated system to plaster removal, but it grinds coatings off masonry rather than prying plaster, lath, board or paneling off framing.

sources.title: Bots2ReC, robotic extraction of asbestos fibres from buildings — Robotnik
sources.claim: Bots2ReC's own reported outcome: the system reached about 90% geometric accessibility of dwelling wall surfaces and was never benchmarked against manual removal; the project ended in November 2019 as a prototype, with the removal system not commercialized.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above; cited to show worker-equivalent completion (full wall coverage, comparable speed and reliability) was not established even for plaster-coating removal.

sources.system: Conjet ACR hydrodemolition robots (e.g., Robot 327, 557 MPA XL)
sources.title: Hydrodemolition Equipment | Conjet
sources.claim: Commercially deployed automated surface-removal robots exist for concrete hydrodemolition, but they execute a removal pattern that a human operator sets up beforehand, and they work on infrastructure such as bridges, parking decks, dams and tunnels rather than interior wall coverings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled selective removal of building material from a surface. Transfer fails: the process is water-jetting of concrete on infrastructure with a pre-set pattern, not prying gypsum board, lath or paneling off framing indoors, and the motion is operator-programmed rather than perceived from the as-found wall.

sources.system: Okibo EG7+ autonomous drywall finishing and painting robot
sources.title: Okibo launches autonomous, AI-guided painting and drywall finishing EG7+ robot — Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Autonomous jobsite robots for drywall work exist, but they perform additive surface work (joint compound finishing, sanding, painting) on newly hung board, not removal or demolition of existing wall coverings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic work on drywall surfaces at real construction sites. It does not transfer to this task: finishing applies material to a flat known plane, whereas removal requires forceful prying/impact against unknown fastening, hidden utilities and unpredictable fracture, plus debris handling.

tasks.label: Suspend angle iron grids or channel irons from ceilings, using wire.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial construction, large open floor plates (office floors, school classrooms/corridors, big-box retail): installer shoots or drills hanger points into concrete deck or bar joists on a regular ~4 ft grid, hangs 12-gauge wire, twists three tight turns, then hangs and levels main runners/carrying channels to a laser line over hundreds of square feet with a clear floor and lift access.

New construction in congested or irregular areas: corridors, lobbies, toilet rooms, mechanical zones. Hanger wires must be placed around ducts, sprinkler mains, cable tray and structural members, with splayed or spliced wires, varying drop lengths, soffits, height changes and seismic bracing; frequent field decisions about where a hanger can land.

Renovation and tenant fit-out in existing buildings (hospital wings, schools on breaks, occupied offices, retail remodels): found deck conditions, existing hangers and abandoned MEP overhead, tie-ins to existing grid heights, dust or infection barriers, night and weekend shifts, partial-area work with furniture or equipment nearby.

Furring/lath work for gypsum-board ceilings and bulkheads: 1-1/2 in cold-rolled carrying channels hung with tie wire (saddle ties) and hat channel/furring wired or clipped across them, including curved soffits, drop headers and framed openings, cut and fitted in the field.

Small jobs: residential basements, small clinics, single offices or shops. One or two rooms of drop-ceiling grid hung with wire from wood joists or low concrete decks, tight clearances, many cut-in perimeter pieces, work often around stored contents.

sources.system: System ceiling installation robot (hanger-bolt robot, three T-bar robots, board robot)
sources.title: テムザックと鹿島建設、エッジAI搭載の"群れ"で働く「システム天井施工ロボット」共同開発 - ドローンジャーナル
sources.claim: Tmsuk and Kajima's prototype 'system ceiling installation robot' swarm includes a hanger-bolt robot that carries hanger bolts, recognizes beams, equipment and cables already overhead, judges whether a bolt can be attached there, and automatically detects and accurately inserts the bolt - i.e. it creates the overhead suspension points for a ceiling grid.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hanging a Japanese system-ceiling grid. The work product (a metal grid suspended from the structural deck, positioned to mm accuracy, built overhead by floor-standing mobile robots inside a building under construction) matches the US task; the fastening detail differs (threaded hanger bolt into a cast-in insert plus metal clips rather than twisted 12-gauge wire).

sources.system: System ceiling installation robot (T-bar installation robots)
sources.title: エッジAI搭載の「群れ」で働く「システム天井施工ロボット」共同開発。テムザックと鹿島 | デジコン
sources.claim: The same swarm's three T-bar robots transport long T-bars, fix them to the hanger bolts with hardware, splice long T-bars end to end and then add medium and short T-bars until a complete lattice ceiling framework exists; each robot carries edge AI and adjusts its own task, and the set has already run trial installations at Kajima construction sites in Japan.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling and suspending a T-bar ceiling grid. Comparable objects (long light-gauge metal grid members lifted overhead and locked to suspension points), comparable precision (the shared carriage robot performs mm-level positioning), and the same environment (interior floor of a building under construction).

sources.system: 天井ボード取付ロボット (ceiling board attachment robot) with 移動式天台 (mobile work platform)
sources.title: 天井ボード取付ロボットと移動式天台を開発～システム天井施工における省人化と仮設材の大幅削減を実現～ | プレスリリース | 鹿島建設
sources.claim: As of June 2026 Kajima's production use of ceiling robots on a live office-building site covers only board attachment: the ceiling board robot works automatically from a tablet instruction, while the ceiling substrate/grid framing is still installed by skilled workers riding a powered mobile work platform.
sources.transferJustification: Same trade and setting: system-ceiling installation on an office-building site. It shows that the grid/substrate step of this very task is still performed by human technicians in production work, even where ceiling-board robots are deployed.

sources.title: Hilti unveils BIM-enabled construction robot for mobile ceiling work | Construction Dive
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a commercially available semi-autonomous mobile robot that locates itself from BIM data and drills and marks overhead anchor holes in concrete and metal-deck ceilings on live construction sites; anchors, hangers and grid members are still installed by workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: overhead anchor-hole drilling to layout for MEP hangers, the first step in hanging a suspended grid. It shows autonomous overhead drilling on real jobsites but stops short of setting anchors, tying wire or hanging any grid member.

sources.title: Rebar tying robot completes 11,000 ties in one day on Florida bridge - Construction Management
sources.claim: TyBot is a commercially deployed autonomous robot that locates reinforcing steel intersections without BIM input and forms twisted wire ties on them at over 1,000 ties per hour on bridge decks, running on screed rails.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine formation of twisted wire ties on found steel members. It supports feasibility of the wire-twisting element of this task, but the geometry is downward onto a deck from a rail-mounted gantry, not overhead threading of hanger wire through anchors and grid legs.

tasks.label: Seal joints between ceiling tiles and walls.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial building construction (office, school, retail): after setting a suspended acoustical grid and tiles, run a continuous bead of acoustical sealant along the perimeter joint where edge tiles and wall angle meet the walls; overhead work from stilts, ladder or scissor lift on an active jobsite with other trades, dust, cut edge tiles and out-of-plumb walls.

New healthcare, laboratory, cleanroom or food-processing facility fit-out: seal ceiling panel perimeters to walls with a continuous silicone/gasket-grade bead so the ceiling plane is airtight and washable; bead must be void-free, tooled and pass inspection; overhead work in a partially finished high-spec space.

Interior renovation / tenant improvement in an existing (gutted, unoccupied) building: new grid and tile installed against existing walls, soffits, columns and ductwork, then perimeter joints caulked in place; layout differs room to room and existing surfaces are irregular.

Occupied-facility repair and maintenance: re-caulk failed, cracked or stained ceiling-to-wall joints after a leak or after replacing a few tiles in a hospital, school or office; after-hours work around furniture, equipment and occupants, with masking and clean-up.

Residential or small-suite retrofit drop ceiling (basement remodel, small office): install tile in a low, cluttered existing space with pipes and ducts, then caulk/seal the perimeter joint at the walls, often on a step ladder in tight quarters.

sources.system: Six-axis robotic dispensing systems (industrial arms with dispense valves)
sources.title: Dispensing With Six-Axis Robots | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Six-axis industrial dispensing robots routinely lay a continuous, even bead of viscous adhesive/sealant along a defined joint on a fixtured workpiece, holding nozzle angle and standoff constant - the same motion a caulker makes by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic bead dispensing of adhesive/gasket material along part seams. Transfer: sealing a ceiling-panel-to-wall joint is the same operation - a continuous viscous bead laid along a linear joint at millimetre tolerance - when the assembly is fixtured and presented to the machine, which is the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: ABB dispensing / seam-sealing robot cells (IRB robots with Integrated Dispensing Function Package)
sources.title: Body-in-White | ABB
sources.claim: Production seam-sealing cells apply precise sealant beads to panel joints on car bodies as a standard, deployed automotive process.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic seam sealing of sheet-metal joints in fenced cells. Transfer: the physical act - controlled-flow sealant bead along a joint between two fixtured surfaces to an inspected water-tight/cosmetic standard - matches sealing a ceiling-tile-to-wall joint once the assembly is fixtured.

sources.title: Robotic Sealing Applications | Encore Automation
sources.claim: Turnkey robotic interior seam-sealing systems are supplied and run in production plants, delivering uniform sealed seams accepted as production quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated seam sealing on assembly lines. Transfer: demonstrates repeatable, worker-quality sealant bead application on fixtured assemblies, the capability required at E1 for sealing a panel-to-wall perimeter joint.

sources.system: LiSEC VL-1N automatic insulating-glass sealing system
sources.title: Fully automatic sealing system for insulating glass - LiSEC.com
sources.claim: Fully automatic factory sealing lines fill the continuous perimeter joint of a fixtured building-component panel assembly (insulating glass unit) with two-component sealant to a process-reliable standard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated perimeter-joint sealing of a building component in a factory. Transfer: same geometry (continuous bead run around the perimeter joint between two fixtured planar elements) and same acceptance criterion (void-free, air/water-tight bead), supporting the E1 counterfactual for ceiling-to-wall joint sealing.

sources.system: Robot learning system for mastic deposition (manipulator with M18 caulk gun)
sources.title: Robot Learning from Teleoperated Demonstrations: A Pilot Study Towards Automating Mastic Deposition in Construction Sites
sources.claim: Automating caulk/mastic deposition on construction joints is still a research pilot: the robot is taught from teleoperated human demonstrations and evaluated in the lab, not deployed on jobsites.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related task (field caulking of building joints). It shows the field version of this task is at teleoperated pilot stage, so no cited system substantiates completion at E2 or E3.

sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction's Dirty Work Is Going Robotic - Architect Magazine
sources.claim: Autonomous interior-finishing robots do work on real construction sites, but their demonstrated jobs are spraying plaster/paint and finishing drywall surfaces, not gun-applied bead sealing at suspended-ceiling perimeters.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous surface finishing of walls and ceilings on jobsites. It does not transfer here: spraying and blading broad gypsum surfaces is not laying and tooling a caulk bead along the edge of a suspended acoustical ceiling, so it cannot support an E3/E2 judgment.

tasks.label: Inspect furrings, mechanical mountings, or masonry surfaces for plumbness and level, using spirit or water levels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial interior fit-out: across an office/school/hospital floor plate under construction, the installer checks metal-stud partition framing, track, and hat/Z-furring over concrete or CMU for plumb and level with a 4-6 ft spirit level (sometimes a laser), flagging members needing shimming or resetting before board is hung; open floor, other trades working, debris and stacked material.

Residential and multifamily new construction: in units, corridors and garages, the installer checks wood or light-gauge framing and furring strips for plumb and ceiling joists/furring for level before hanging board, spotting bowed, twisted or proud members; rooms are small and cluttered with stacked board, subfloors uneven, access by stairs.

Suspended acoustical ceiling work: checking wall angle, main runners and cross tees for level across rooms and corridors with a water level, laser or spirit level, and confirming hanger wires/mountings are set to the datum; work performed from ladders, stilts or scissor lifts in commercial buildings under construction or in off-hours occupied space.

Renovation and remodel: furring applied to old masonry, brick or concrete in basements, historic buildings and occupied spaces; the installer checks the wall for plumb and flatness, finds bulges and hollows, and determines shim thicknesses; irregular surfaces, low headroom, poor light, clutter and no consistent layout.

Localized checks of individual mechanical mountings and backing: verifying a shaft-wall attachment clip, ceiling hanger insert, bracket, or Z-furring clip is plumb/level right before fastening, usually while standing on a ladder or lift and needing an immediate yes/no answer.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot + Trimble X7 / FieldLink
sources.title: Trimble releases autonomous robotic scanning solution - AEC Magazine
sources.claim: Trimble and Boston Dynamics ship a commercial turnkey system in which Spot autonomously walks recorded waypoint routes on construction sites and captures Trimble X7 laser scans of as-built conditions, on a scheduled basis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: as-built dimensional capture of interior surfaces. Millimetre-class scans of walls/ceilings from a self-levelling scanner yield the same plumb/level determination a spirit level gives, on the same construction-site surfaces (studs, furring, masonry).

sources.title: Automated Construction Site Documentation | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot runs repeat autonomous documentation missions on construction sites; scans captured with the X7 payload are overlaid on the BIM model and assessed for deviations.
sources.transferJustification: Deviation assessment against the model is exactly the accept/reject output of a plumb-and-level check on framing, furring and masonry surfaces.

sources.title: AI Startup Using Robots and Lidar to Boost Productivity on Construction Sites - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Doxel's lidar-equipped autonomous robots scan active construction sites daily and the system automatically evaluates whether installed work is correct and in the right place; used on projects including a medical office building and Kaiser Permanente work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated quality/position verification of installed elements on site. The same lidar-plus-model pipeline produces the out-of-tolerance findings that a level check produces for framing and furring.

sources.developer: Wu et al., published in Buildings (MDPI)
sources.title: On-Site Measuring Robot Technology for Post-Construction Quality Assessment of Building Projects
sources.claim: A fully automated on-site measuring robot with autonomous lidar navigation measures wall evenness, wall alignment (verticality), floor heights and corner angles from its own point clouds, and was applied on two real building projects with validated accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Wall alignment/verticality and evenness assessment is the same measurement as checking masonry surfaces and furring for plumbness and level; performed in building interiors during/after construction.

sources.title: QuicaBot: Quality Inspection and Assessment Robot | IEEE Xplore
sources.claim: QuicaBot autonomously scans a whole room with cameras and laser scanners and grades evenness, alignment and inclination of walls against the CONQUAS quality standard, in completed building interiors with prepared floors.
sources.transferJustification: Alignment/inclination assessment of interior walls is the plumbness check; evenness is the flatness check performed on masonry before furring.

sources.system: Spot with Autowalk missions / BLK ARC scanning payload
sources.title: A Retrospective on Uses of Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot fleets run thousands of recorded autonomous data-collection missions inside factories, power plants and construction sites, including automated laser-scanning reality capture with the Leica BLK ARC payload.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes routine autonomous inspection/measurement rounds inside institution-controlled facilities (E2), the setting a relocated furring/mounting check would occupy.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics’ robot dog patrols 1.5 million-square-foot factory
sources.claim: ST Engineering MRAS deployed Spot to autonomously inspect equipment and capture high-resolution 3D scans throughout a 1.5-million-square-foot aerospace manufacturing plant.
sources.transferJustification: Shows autonomous 3D geometric capture of built structures inside a structured human work facility, supporting E2 for a geometry-inspection task.

sources.date: 2024-10 (product listing); product line in series production use
sources.title: 3D scanning with ATOS | flexible, reliable | ZEISS
sources.claim: ZEISS ATOS ScanBox is a commercially sold enclosed robotic optical 3D measuring cell that automatically digitizes fixtured parts up to about 6000 x 1250 mm and reports GD&T deviations such as flatness without operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated dimensional/flatness inspection of large fixtured panels in a fenced cell. If a furring or panel assembly were presented fixtured to the machine, the same cell would return the flatness/squareness verdict the level check provides.

tasks.label: Install metal lath where plaster applications will be exposed to weather or water, or for curved or irregular surfaces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New single-family or low-rise multifamily house: lather hangs self-furred expanded metal lath (27"x96" sheets) over building paper/WRB on wood-framed exterior walls from scaffold or ladders, snips sheets to fit, laps sides 1/2" and ends 1", ties laps with wire, staples/nails into studs at ~7" o.c., cuts and wraps lath around window and door openings, installs casing beads, corner aid and weep screed, outdoors with weather and site debris underfoot.

Commercial exterior stucco/plaster: lath over sheathed steel-stud or CMU walls of a hotel, school or retail building, worked from swing stage, scaffold or boom lift at height, including soffits and overhead work, screw or power-actuated fastening to metal framing, control and expansion joints, inspected to ASTM C1063.

Curved or irregular interior features: lath bent and cut around arches, radius walls, round columns, barrel vaults, coves and domes, wire-tied to metal framing/hangers or existing substrate and shaped to templates so the plasterer can screed a true curve; unfinished building interior with other trades present.

Wet-area interior: metal lath fastened over waterproofing/felt in tub surrounds, shower walls and floors, tiled commercial kitchen or pool-area walls; small, confined, obstructed spaces with plumbing penetrations; lath cut around valves and drains and fastened without puncturing the pan.

Repair, remodel and restoration: cut out failed stucco or historic plaster in an occupied home or building, tie new lath into existing lath at ragged patch edges, match irregular contours and ornamental profiles, tight or elevated access with dust control around occupants and furnishings.

Shop/prefabrication: lath applied to prefabricated stucco or plaster wall panels lying on tables in a panel plant, with sheets cut, lapped and stapled to a fixtured framed-and-sheathed panel before the panel ships to site.

sources.title: Development of a humanoid robot prototype, HRP-5P, capable of heavy labor
sources.claim: AIST's HRP-5P humanoid autonomously picked up and screwed a gypsum board to a stud wall in a mock-up residential room; it is a laboratory prototype, slow and single-board, and no version has been shown handling flexible expanded metal lath, laps, ties, snip cutting or lath accessories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = rigid wallboard hanging. Transfer to metal lath fails: lath is a limp expanded-metal sheet that must be applied cups-up, lapped and wire-tied, snip-cut around openings and fastened into framing through a WRB; the demo covers none of these and is a single lab board, not accepted-quality production output.

sources.title: WEINMANN at the Dach+Holz | HOMAG
sources.claim: WEINMANN WALLTEQ multifunction bridges automatically staple/nail and rout rigid sheathing (OSB, gypsum) onto fixtured timber wall frames in panel plants; retrieved material describes board sheathing only, with no application of expanded metal or wire lath.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated fastening of sheet material to a fixtured panel in a purpose-built cell (the E1 counterfactual for the shop instance). Transfer fails on the object: the gantry handles rigid boards and cuts them with a router, whereas lath is limp expanded metal requiring stretching, 1/2" side laps, wire ties and snip cutting; no source shows lath run on this equipment.

sources.title: Construction robotics: Okibo brings painting robot to America
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7/EG7+ robots autonomously spray, sand and finish drywall and paint on active US commercial construction sites, showing that the most mature site robots in this trade perform surface coating, not fastening of lath or other plaster backing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = interior plaster/drywall finishing on real sites. It substantiates autonomous navigation and surface work in construction interiors but not lath installation, which requires sheet handling, cutting, lapping and fastening into concealed framing.

sources.title: New generation of rebar-tying robot TyBot 3.0 hits the market | Equipment World
sources.claim: TyBot autonomously ties intersections of horizontal rebar mats from a rail-mounted gantry on bridge decks and has run on dozens of US projects; it works only on flat, pre-placed horizontal reinforcement and does not place, cut, lap or fasten sheet reinforcement to walls.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous tying of steel reinforcement on a construction site. Transfer fails: TyBot requires a flat horizontal mat already placed beneath a gantry on screed rails, while lathing requires lifting, cutting and fastening sheets to vertical, overhead and curved surfaces.

sources.title: Mining: Underground & Open Pit - Geobrugg
sources.claim: Geobrugg's MESHA handler unrolls chain-link ground-support mesh onto tunnel walls and backs from a drill jumbo or bolter; it is machine-mounted mechanization run by the jumbo crew and installs rock-support mesh, not plaster lath with code lap and fastener patterns.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = mechanized placement of steel mesh against a surface. Transfer fails on autonomy (operated from the jumbo carrier) and on requirements: no ASTM C1063 lap/fastener pattern, no snip cutting, no accessories, and no vertical framed-wall or curved-feature work.

tasks.label: Nail channels or wood furring strips to surfaces to provide mounting for tile.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/institutional interior fit-out: fastening metal hat/furring channel or wood furring strips to concrete or CMU walls and columns (powder-actuated pins, concrete screws, or nails) to create a base plane for acoustical tile or board; layout snapped from lines, shims where masonry is out of plumb, work from stilts or a lift in an active construction/renovation zone.

Overhead ceiling furring in commercial/institutional buildings: nailing/screwing cross-furring channels or wood strips to wood or steel joists, or fastening them to a concrete deck, to receive acoustical tile or wallboard; work done overhead amid ducts, sprinkler lines and conduit, leveled to a laser plane across the room.

Residential or light-commercial remodel: nailing 1x3 wood furring strips across an existing ceiling (old joists, sagging plaster) or over a basement masonry wall so ceiling tile can be stapled up; as-found framing is out of level, strips must be shimmed, and the room is cluttered and occupied.

Small, irregular cut-and-fit furring: soffits, bulkheads, columns, perimeter borders and returns; short strips scribed and fitted around ducts, pipes, beams and existing fixtures, cut on site and fastened piece by piece.

Off-site prefabrication shop or panel plant: attaching furring strips/battens (or channel) to wall, ceiling or roof elements laid on production tables/jigs so tile or board can later be mounted; CAD-driven layout, standard lumber, controlled indoor plant.

sources.system: WEINMANN WALLTEQ M-380 / M-500 multifunction bridge with LatTec
sources.title: Roof and ceiling production line — HOMAG
sources.claim: HOMAG/WEINMANN's WALLTEQ multifunction bridge with the LatTec option automatically positions and fastens battens (furring strips) onto a beam or rafter framework held on a production table in a timber-element plant — the same operation as nailing furring strips to provide a mounting base for tile.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic fastening of roof/ceiling battens to a framework. Battens are furring strips and form the mounting base onto which tile is fastened; objects (1x lumber strips), fastening (nail/staple/screw units), spacing accuracy and substrate (wood framework) match the rated task. Transfer holds only where the element is fixtured on the machine's table.

sources.system: WEINMANN multifunction bridge with integrated batten support (LIGNUM TECH plant)
sources.title: LIGNUM TECH entrusts WEINMANN | HOMAG
sources.claim: A production customer (LIGNUM TECH) runs a WEINMANN line whose multifunction bridge places roof battens on elements fully automatically, showing the batten-fastening capability is in real factory production, not just a spec sheet.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (automatic batten/furring placement and fastening on a framed element), evidenced in an operating prefabrication plant rather than in a brochure.

sources.system: WEINMANN wall panel line at Bensonwood
sources.title: From Lumber to Bundle: The Prefabrication of a Bensonwood Panel
sources.claim: US timber prefabricator Bensonwood runs a WEINMANN line that automatically aligns framing members and nails them together from machine files, showing autonomous CNC nailing of lumber to a fixtured panel in a North American plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-driven nailing of dimensional lumber members at CAD-specified positions on a fixtured panel. Same fastener type, materials and comparable placement tolerance as nailing furring strips; shows the capability is in commercial production in the US.

sources.title: Hilti Releases All New Features for the Hilti Jaibot — Hilti Corporation
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot performs semi-autonomous overhead anchor-hole drilling from BIM data on real construction sites worldwide, but its on-site capability stops at drilling and marking holes; it does not lift, align or fasten channels or furring strips.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: overhead anchor-hole drilling for ceiling installations on live jobsites. It covers only a sub-step of channel/furring installation (hole preparation) and cannot handle strip material, leveling or fastening, so it cannot substantiate whole-task completion at E3 or E2.

sources.title: Robots under Autonomous Control at Robot Lab | Shimizu Corporation
sources.claim: Shimizu's two-armed Robo-Buddy autonomously lifts ceiling boards and screws them to already-installed ceiling base material at building sites, i.e. it fastens finish boards to a pre-existing frame rather than installing the furring channels themselves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous overhead screw-fastening of ceiling material inside a building under construction. It presupposes the ceiling grid/base material (what the rated task installs) is already in place, and the ceiling variant remained trial-stage, so it does not substantiate on-site furring/channel installation.

sources.title: humanoid construction robot HRP-5P is capable of installing walls and handling screwdrivers
sources.claim: AIST's HRP-5P humanoid autonomously picked up a plasterboard and screwed it to a stud/furring wall frame in a simulated construction mock-up, demonstrating autonomous power-tool fastening of building material — but only in a purpose-built laboratory setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous handling and screw-fastening of sheet material to a furring/stud frame. Comparable tools and substrate, but performed on a prepared mock-up wall in a lab, so it supports only a purpose-built (E1) setting.

sources.title: Introducing Rufus, the Automated Roofing Robot from Renovate Robotics | Roofing Contractor
sources.claim: Renovate Robotics' Rufus is a cable-driven robot that installs asphalt ..., the closest fielded example of autonomous nailing of course-laid material in an unstructured setting; it rides on an upward-facing roof deck and is specialized to shingles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous nailing of material to a wood deck outdoors. Transfer to the rated task fails on environment and pose: Rufus is supported on top of a sloped deck, whereas furring is fastened overhead to ceilings or vertically to walls, requiring leveling and shimming of rigid strips against gravity in interiors it cannot enter.

tasks.label: Mount tile, using adhesives, or by nailing, screwing, stapling, or wire-tying lath directly to structural frameworks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/institutional room being finished or remodeled: acoustical tile or board direct-mounted to wood furring strips or joists with mastic adhesive and staples/screws; whole room including layout, perimeter tiles cut to fit, and cuts around lights, diffusers and sprinkler heads; work off stilts or a baker scaffold in a partially finished room with stored materials and other trades present.

New commercial construction, large open floor plate: full-size (4x8-type) gypsum/mineral ceiling boards screwed to steel furring channels across the open field of the ceiling, no cutouts in the field, clear level slab, materials palletized nearby.

Same new-construction ceilings, non-field work: boards cut and fitted at walls, columns, bulkheads, soffit edges and around MEP penetrations, then screwed to the framing; requires measuring, scribing and notching each piece.

Acoustic wall tiles/panels adhered with mastic to interior walls of gyms, band rooms, classrooms, studios or restaurants; layout lines snapped, pattern maintained, panels trimmed at corners, outlets and door casings; walls out of plumb in places.

Expanded metal or wire lath fastened to steel studs or wood framing over flat wall and ceiling areas as a plaster/stucco base: sheets lapped and cupped correctly, screwed/stapled/nailed at code spacing and wire-tied at laps between framing members.

Lath or tile on complex geometry: soffits, arched openings, round columns, curved or stepped ceilings, and lath wrapped and wire-tied for fireproofing or ornamental plaster; sheets cut, bent and tied to irregular framing overhead.

sources.system: Robo-Buddy Ceiling (ceiling board construction robot) + ceiling assist robot
sources.title: 建築工事向け作業ロボットの開発 (Development of Autonomous Robots for Construction Works), Shimizu Technical Research Report No.101
sources.claim: Shimizu's autonomous twin-arm ceiling robot lifts gypsum boards and screws them to ceiling furring; in a field application at a Japanese construction site it installed 74 boards (~123 m2), but the scope excluded the areas around walls and columns and the robot only handles uncut 910x1820 mm boards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastening gypsum ceiling board to steel/wood furring with screws. The report defines this work as fixing board material to steel or wooden substrate with screws, staples or adhesive - the same fastening modes, overhead position, board weights (11-14 kg) and framing as mounting tile/lath to structural frameworks.

sources.title: 清水建設が天井施工ロボットをついに実用化、30年越しで開発成功 | 日経Robotics
sources.claim: Trade press reports that Shimizu put the ceiling-board robot into practical use and applied it at a domestic construction site in March 2023, installing about 100 boards with a 100% success rate; one arm grips the board while the other drives screws into the ceiling substrate.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above: screwing boards directly to ceiling framing on a live construction site.

sources.title: Shimizu Deploys Robot for Installing Raised Floor Named “Robo-Buddy Floor”
sources.claim: Shimizu's twin-arm Robo-Buddy Floor was deployed on an operating high-rise construction site, autonomously bonding pedestals with adhesive and laying access-floor panels to within 1 mm, but it covered only the inner field area while human workers handled the outer area requiring detail and cut-size panels.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mounting rigid panels with a bonding agent onto a structural base at a construction site. It shows on-site panel-mounting robots today complete uniform field areas but leave perimeter, cut and detail pieces to trades workers.

sources.system: SCADAware wall sheathing cell (Kawasaki BX250L robots, Güdel TMF-3 rails)
sources.developer: SCADAware / Kawasaki Robotics for Rehkemper & Son
sources.title: Assembling Walls for Prefabricated Homes | Industrial Robots by Kawasaki
sources.claim: In a US prefabrication plant, four Kawasaki BX250L robots on Güdel rails autonomously pick 4x8 ft sheathing panels with vacuum heads, place them on frames held and straightened by a motorized fixture table, nail them to the studs, and rout out window and door openings, running in production with reported 25% throughput gains.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: nailing sheet material directly to a structural stud framework, including cutting openings. Objects (4x8 rigid boards), fastening mode (nails/staples), tolerance (fastener must hit the stud) and the framework are the same as mounting board/tile and rockboard or wood lath to framing; here the frame is fixtured and presented to the machine.

sources.system: WEINMANN WALLTEQ M-500 / M-300 multifunction bridge
sources.title: Multifunction Bridge WALLTEQ M-500 | HOMAG
sources.claim: WEINMANN's WALLTEQ multifunction bridges are commercial CNC gantries used in prefab plants that automatically fasten sheathing to wall, roof and ceiling frames by screwing, stapling and nailing, apply PU glue, trim openings, and in the LatTec option automatically position and attach battens (wood lath) to a beam or rafter framework.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatically gluing, stapling, nailing or screwing boards and battens to a timber framework in a fixtured factory cell - the same fastening modes and substrate as mounting tile with adhesive or fastening wood/rockboard lath to framing.

sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor is a commercially sold robotic cell for offsite panel plants that automates sheathing of wall, floor and roof elements with multiple layers, handling OSB and plasterboard, with robotic gluing, sawing and separated sheet handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotically gluing and fastening plasterboard/OSB sheets onto framed elements in a purpose-built cell; comparable board sizes, adhesive application and frame substrate to mounting tile or board to a structural framework.

roles.title: Tapers
roles.description: Seal joints between plasterboard or other wallboard to prepare wall surface for painting or papering.

tasks.label: Press paper tape over joints to embed tape into sealing compound and to seal joints.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New single-family / townhouse construction: taper embeds paper tape into freshly applied joint compound on flat butt and tapered wall seams and ceiling seams throughout a house under construction — uneven subfloors, framing debris, stilts or benches, varying room geometry, other trades working nearby.

Commercial/institutional build-out (office, school, hospital, data center): taper runs tape into compound over long flat joints on high walls and ceilings, often from a lift or scaffold, on partitions with fire-rated assemblies; Level 4/5 finish expected, joints must be centered, bubble-free and wiped clean.

Inside corners, angles, and around openings/soffits in any project type: pre-creased paper tape folded and pressed into corner beads of compound at wall-ceiling and wall-wall intersections, around door/window returns and bulkheads, where a knife must seat both legs without wrinkling or starving the tape.

Repair, remodel and punch-list work in occupied homes and businesses: taping patches, short seams and cracks in furnished rooms with existing finishes, requiring masking, working around fixtures and matching adjacent surfaces.

Factory/prefab setting: taping joints of gypsum board on wall panels or in volumetric modular units inside a manufacturing plant, with fixed workstations, standard panel sizes and controlled conditions.

sources.system: Canvas drywall finishing robot (Canvas Construction / JLG)
sources.title: More Contractors See Benefits of Drywall Finishing Robot | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: The Canvas drywall finishing robot, the leading commercially deployed drywall automation system in the US, performs joint-compound spraying and sanding only; human workers still do the taping (tape embedding) and complex geometries.
sources.transferJustification: Same trade and same joints as this task (drywall joint finishing); the cited system's scope explicitly excludes the tape-embedding step that this task consists of.

sources.title: How a Drywall Robot Is Reshaping Interior Construction | Built (Bluebeam)
sources.claim: In current Canvas jobsite workflow (2025), human crews tape the seams first and only then does the robot work the wall; the machine's autonomous portion begins after taping.
sources.transferJustification: Directly adjacent step in the same trade on the same joints; the source shows tape embedding is performed by humans as a precondition for the robot's work.

sources.title: Canvas, World's First Robotic Drywall Finishing Company, Launches the 1200CX (Business Wire)
sources.claim: Canvas's latest commercial machine is marketed as spray-applying joint compound and sanding; taping is not among the machine's functions.
sources.transferJustification: Same trade and joints; the product description covers compound application and sanding but not embedding paper tape.

sources.title: Okibo launches autonomous, AI-guided painting and drywall finishing EG7+ robot - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Okibo's autonomous construction robots perform plastering, painting and drywall surface finishing/sanding on active construction sites; no tape-embedding capability is described.
sources.transferJustification: Closest autonomous system in the same trade and environment (interior wall finishing on construction sites); its demonstrated scope is spray plaster/paint and sanding, not pressing paper tape into compound.

Overhead and hard-to-reach work on new construction: ceilings, soffits, stairwells and high walls, done from stilts, baker scaffold or a lift; taper feels/spots proud fasteners overhead and drives them below the surface before compound is applied.

Remodel, repair and punch-list work in existing occupied homes or buildings: popped nails/screws in already-finished or previously patched walls and ceilings; taper refastens the board to the stud, drives the popped fastener below the surface with hammer or screw gun, then patches. Furniture, finished floors, occupants present; wall cannot be moved.

Offsite modular/panelized plant: drywall is hung on wall panels or module interiors inside the factory; the finisher checks the boarded panels for proud fasteners and sets them below the surface before taping and coating on the plant's finishing line.

instances.label: Residential new-build or remodel jobsite, unfinished interior: taper opens 4.5-gal boxes/pails of ready-mixed all-purpose or topping compound stored wherever they were dropped, dumps into a clean pail, adds water a cup at a time and works it with a 1/2-in. drill and paddle mixer until it is the right consistency for taping or for a spray rig, then carries it to the work area. Dust, cords, scaffolding, no fixed layout.

Setting-type ('hot mud') powder mixed from a bag on a residential or light-commercial jobsite: measured water into a clean 5-gal pail or mud pan, powder added, mixed by paddle or by hand knife to a lump-free consistency, batch sized to the working time before it kicks; pail and paddle must be washed between batches.

Large commercial jobsite (high-rise floor, hospital shell, school): high-volume batching at an informal mud station near the material drop, thinning many boxes of compound and mixing powder blends to feed taping tools, pumps and texture rigs over a shift; other trades working around, temporary power and a hose bib for water.

Small patch or punch-list repair in an occupied home or office: a pint or two of compound mixed by hand in a mud pan with a taping knife (or a small batch of powder mixed in a cup), with dust/spill control around finished surfaces and furnishings.

tasks.label: Check adhesives to ensure that they will work and will remain durable.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential or light-commercial jobsite, start of a taping day: worker opens 5-gallon pails of pre-mixed all-purpose/lightweight joint compound, looks and probes for skinning, mold, lumps, freeze-thaw damage or over-age product, checks lot/date, thins with water and paddle-mixes, and judges by feel and trowel pull whether the mud is workable and will bond and stay bonded.

Commercial interior build-out: worker checks bagged setting-type (hot mud) or powder taping compound for moisture caking, confirms the grade/set time suits temperature, humidity and schedule, mixes a small test batch, and verifies working time, stiffness and bite on the board before committing it to the wall.

Verifying bond after application: worker inspects bedded tape, glued-on corner bead, laminated second-layer board or previously coated joints for blisters, loose tape edges, hollow spots or debonded compound - by eye, touch, tapping and knife probe - and decides whether the adhesive held or the joint must be cut out and redone.

Adhesive products other than mud: cartridge or pail construction/laminating adhesive checked before use - not gelled, skinned or past date, extrudes a proper bead, sets up on a test scrap - plus a check that the substrate (dust, moisture, temperature) will let the bond last.

Prefabricated wall-panel plant or finishing shop: the same compound and adhesive checks performed indoors at fixed stations under a plant QC procedure, with batch records, consistent product and controlled temperature and humidity.

Timing depends on set, and the pattern must be consistent across a whole room and match adjoining rooms.

Remodel, repair and punch-list work in occupied or already-finished buildings: after patching, apply texture to the patched area with aerosol/hopper, trowel, brush or sponge and blend it to match the existing surrounding pattern, then spot-prime. Specialty hand-applied decorative finishes in custom homes and upscale interiors: skip-trowel, Santa Fe, Venetian/plaster-look and hand-troweled knockdown applied with trowel, brush or roller to a sample the designer approved, including feature walls, curved soffits, arches and vaulted ceilings.
