sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7 is a battery-powered, fully autonomous painting and drywall-finishing robot that needs no site preparation, markings or BIM, fits through standard doorways, and is marketed for residential, multifamily and office interiors; its robots have finished over a million square feet on European construction sites.

sources.system: Okibo EG7+ with BLASTER spray gun
sources.title: Okibo Unleashes BLASTER Technology: A Breakthrough in Autonomous High-Speed Coating for the Construction Industry | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: Okibo's BLASTER dual-nozzle airless spray head for the autonomous EG7/EG7+ is commercially available for painting and priming walls up to 24 ft on large jobsites, and a BLASTER-equipped EG7+ was deployed on a commercial construction project in Jacksonville, FL.

sources.system: Okibo EG7/EG7+ fleet at Performance Contracting Inc.
sources.title: Okibo and PCI Scale Construction Tech with New Robot Fleet | Walls & Ceilings
sources.claim: Performance Contracting Inc., one of the largest US specialty (drywall/finishes) contractors, expanded its fleet of Okibo finishing robots after an initial deployment, using them on large commercial projects including data centers, indicating output accepted in place of crew work.

sources.developer: Guangdong Bright Dream Robotics Co., Ltd.
sources.title: CITAC - Indoor Spraying Robot (Construction Industry Council, Hong Kong)
sources.claim: Bright Dream Robotics' Indoor Spraying Robot autonomously navigates and sprays primer and topcoat on interior walls, ceilings and bay windows in houses, apartments, hotels and offices; listed project references include Hong Kong public housing and transitional housing developments in 2023.

sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction's Dirty Work Is Going Robotic - Architect Magazine
sources.claim: The Okibo EG7 is described by trade press as fully autonomous and able to paint, apply plaster and finish drywall on interior construction sites, moving through standard doorways using AI-guided 3D scanning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of plaster/skim coating to interior walls and ceilings. Applying a texturizing compound before final finishing uses the same materials, the same spray/manipulator tooling and the same surfaces in the same interior jobsite setting.

sources.system: Canvas autonomous drywall finishing robotic system
sources.title: Solution | Autonomous Drywall Finishing Robotic System | CPWR Construction Solutions
sources.claim: CPWR (construction safety research center) characterizes the Canvas system as an autonomous drywall finishing robot that performs mudding and sanding automatically after scanning and 3D-mapping the work surfaces, confirming the application step is machine-executed rather than hand-guided.

roles.title: Electricians
roles.description: Install, maintain, and repair electrical wiring, equipment, and fixtures. Ensure that work is in accordance with relevant codes. May install or service street lights, intercom systems, or electrical control systems.

tasks.label: Prepare sketches or follow blueprints to determine the location of wiring or equipment and to ensure conformance to building and safety codes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Place conduit, pipes, or tubing, inside designated partitions, walls, or other concealed areas, and pull insulated wires or cables through the conduit to complete circuits between boxes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/institutional new-construction rough-in on an active jobsite: measuring, cutting, bending and strapping EMT between outlet/junction boxes inside metal-stud partitions and above hard ceilings, then fishing/pulling THHN conductors with fish tape or a tugger to complete circuits; congested, changing site with other trades present.

Residential new construction (single-family/multifamily) rough-in: drilling stud and plate penetrations, running smurf tube/EMT or conduit sleeves inside stud bays and up walls to device boxes, stapling and pulling insulated conductors/cables between boxes; unfinished framed rooms, ladders, tight bays, variable framing.

Retrofit/remodel in existing finished buildings (homes, small offices, tenant fit-outs): fishing conduit or tubing and pulling wire through closed walls, ceilings, attics and crawlspaces with limited access holes, unknown obstructions and existing wiring, working around occupants and furnishings.

Industrial/plant work in an operating facility: running rigid/IMC conduit concealed in block walls, chases, floor slabs and underground ducts between pull boxes in mechanical rooms and process areas, then pulling heavy feeders with a cable tugger and lube; institution-controlled premises with standard equipment and permits.

Electrical contractor prefab shop: building conduit racks, wall-panel rough-in assemblies and box-and-whip assemblies on benches/jigs, installing conduit into stud panels and pulling wire between boxes before shipping to the site; indoor shop with standard layout and equipment.

Site/underground work: placing PVC conduit and ductbank in trenches, under slabs and through building penetrations into concealed chases, then pulling feeders and control cables between handholes, pull boxes and panels; open, weather-exposed, muddy site conditions.

sources.title: Robots Revolutionize Construction: A New Era of Building Efficiency and Safety
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot, the leading MEP-trade construction robot deployed on active jobsites, performs only hole marking and ceiling drilling for anchors preparatory to electrical/mechanical installation; it does not place conduit or pull conductors, and it is navigated by a worker via remote control.
sources.transferJustification: Adjacent task (drilling anchor holes for MEP installation on the same jobsites). Cited to show the state of the art for electrical-trade jobsite robots stops at hole drilling and does not extend to conduit placement or wire pulling.

sources.title: Jaibot - Hilti Corporation (media release)
sources.claim: Jaibot's mobility is remote-controlled by a worker; only the drilling within reach is automatic, so the system is not an autonomous installer.
sources.transferJustification: Same adjacent task as above; cited to establish the autonomy status of the most widely deployed electrical-trade construction robot.

sources.title: Modular Robotic Stations for Control Cabinet Manufacturing | WAGO
sources.claim: Commercially available wiring robots route and connect insulated wires only inside fixtured control cabinets in a factory cell, and only for a portion of the wiring work; they do not install raceway or pull conductors through conduit in building partitions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routing and terminating insulated conductors between electrical devices. Transfer is limited because the work is a flat, fixtured backplane in a purpose-built cell with no conduit, no concealed partitions, and no pull between remote boxes; it also covers only part of the wiring labor.

sources.system: Rittal automated control cabinet wiring cobot (with Fraunhofer IPA)
sources.title: Automated Control Cabinet Wiring Solution for Scalable Renewable Energy Systems (SpringerLink)
sources.claim: Research/industrial cabinet-wiring cobots can grasp a pre-assembled wire, terminate both ends and route it inside an enclosure, demonstrating wire handling only in a fixtured factory cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routing insulated conductors between terminals. Objects (single flexible wires) and precision are comparable to terminations, but the environment is an open fixtured backplane; no conduit is placed and no conductor is pulled through an enclosed raceway.

sources.title: Multifunction Bridge – Homag Wallteq M-340
sources.claim: The most automated prefab wall-panel machinery (CNC multifunction bridges) drills stud holes for electrical wires and cuts outlet openings, but stops before electrical rough-in: no conduit is placed in the panel and no wire is pulled.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing framed wall panels (fixtured on a table, a purpose-built E1 setting) for wiring. It bounds what factory automation does — hole drilling and cutouts — showing conduit placement and wire pulling in panels remain manual.

sources.developer: university research prototype reported by Offsite Builder
sources.title: Semi-Automated Wall Panel Framer - Offsite Builder Magazine
sources.claim: A prototype semi-automated wall-panel framing machine likewise reaches only sheathing, openings, and drilling holes for ...; electrical rough-in is not performed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fabrication of framed wall panels in a fixtured factory line. Cited to show that even prototype panel automation does not place conduit inside the partition or pull conductors between boxes.

sources.system: Single-arm wire routing and clipping (UC Berkeley / FANUC research)
sources.title: The Twist: How Single-Arm Robots Tame Deformable Wires | Deep Paper
sources.claim: Robotic manipulation of insulated wire remains at the level of laboratory demonstrations of routing and clipping single wires on fixtured boards, far short of pulling multi-conductor pulls through installed conduit runs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: manipulating deformable insulated wire into fixed routing features. Shown only on a fixtured bench with single wires; it does not establish conduit installation or pulling conductors through raceway between boxes.

tasks.label: Work from ladders, scaffolds, or roofs to install, maintain, or repair electrical wiring, equipment, or fixtures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service call: electrician sets a step or extension ladder in an occupied home and replaces or installs a ceiling luminaire, ceiling fan, smoke/CO detector, or repairs a failed overhead box — de-energizes circuit, removes old device, supports fixture one-handed, splices solid conductors of unknown vintage with wire nuts, remounts canopy, tests. Furniture, flooring, pets, and homeowner present.

Operating commercial/institutional facility (warehouse, big-box store, office, plant): from a scissor lift or rolling scaffold, replace or install high-bay/troffer luminaires, LED retrofits, whips and occupancy sensors, or troubleshoot a dead overhead circuit at 15-30 ft, working around racking, ductwork and staff during off-hours.

New construction or major renovation, interior overhead rough-in from lifts and scaffolds: hang strut and threaded rod, run EMT and cable tray, set boxes, pull and terminate branch wiring, mount fixtures per plan in a congested, changing, multi-trade site with debris and partial structure.

Rooftop work: run conduit on strut across a flat or sloped roof, set disconnects and flex whips for rooftop HVAC units and exhaust fans, wire PV array conductors and combiners, coordinate penetrations and seals — weather, ballast, curbs, edge exposure, layout differs per building.

Exterior ladder/bucket work on an existing building: replace weatherhead/service mast conductors, mount and wire wall packs, soffit lighting, sign circuits and photocells, or repair parking-lot pole fixtures — uneven ground, weather, existing corroded hardware, public traffic nearby.

sources.title: Jaibot Drilling Robot - Hilti USA
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a commercially sold, BIM-driven mobile robot that autonomously marks and drills overhead anchor holes for mechanical, electrical ... installations on active construction sites; it performs only the drilling/marking sub-step and does not handle conduit, conductors, terminations or fixtures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: overhead anchor-hole drilling for electrical hangers at height. It shows the drilling sub-step of at-height electrical installation is automated on real sites, but the robot never installs wiring, equipment or fixtures, so it cannot complete any instance of this task.

sources.title: A Production System for a New Era: The Shimizu Smart Site autonomous robots can transform a job site!
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy autonomously performs overhead installation work at high-rise construction sites — locating work points from BIM and sensors, inserting ceiling hanger bolts, holding boards and driving screws — but it is a ceiling/floor board installer with no electrical wiring or termination capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous overhead fastening at height inside a building under construction. Comparable elevation and fastening precision, but the objects are ceiling boards, not conductors or fixtures, and no electrical connection or energized-circuit work is performed.

sources.system: Raise Robotics platform (with Universal Robots cobot)
sources.title: Raise Robotics deploys UR cobots with Harmon for high rise fastener installation
sources.claim: Raise Robotics' autonomous mobile robot platform, deployed commercially with glazing contractor Harmon, performs slab-edge layout, hammer drilling and facade bracket/fastener installation at height on mid- and high-rise construction sites, accumulating thousands of autonomous hours; the work is mechanical anchoring, not electrical.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous at-height fastener/bracket installation on building edges. Demonstrates that drilling and anchoring at elevation can be autonomous on real sites, but there is no conductor handling, splicing, or fixture energizing, so an electrician's at-height instance is not completed.

sources.system: 10 kV live-working robots (State Grid / Shandong Luneng / NARI 'Dawn' generations)
sources.developer: State Grid China research institutes, Soochow University review
sources.title: Research on Live Working Robots for 10 KV Distribution Networks Adopting Four-Dimensional Safety Guarantee Framework
sources.claim: A July 2026 peer-reviewed review of 10 kV distribution live-working robots states that existing generations of overhead-line work robots rely on remote master-slave teleoperation rather than full autonomy, with most work still at the laboratory stage and manual maintenance dominating.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: connecting and repairing overhead energized conductors from an elevated insulated platform — the closest robotic analogue to exterior at-height wiring work. Because it is teleoperated, it cannot support a positive judgment for any instance.

sources.system: Automated control cabinet wiring robot cell (research prototype)
sources.title: Automated Control Cabinet Wiring Solution for Scalable Renewable Energy Systems
sources.claim: Research on automated control-cabinet wiring — the most fixtured, purpose-built version of electrical wiring work — reports that no industry-proven purchasable system covers the full process of wire supply, insertion and routing, indicating that even in a purpose-built cell, making up electrical connections is not a solved, commercially available capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic installation and termination of building-type conductors on fixtured equipment. This is the E1 counterfactual of electrical wiring work; the source shows the capability is still pre-commercial, so instances cannot be judged complete even at E1.

sources.title: Autonomous Robots Install Solar Panels 3 Times Faster
sources.claim: Rosendin demonstrated an autonomous three-robot system that transports and places PV modules onto pre-installed racking at a utility-scale solar farm in Texas; the environment is a flat, surveyed, purpose-laid ground-mount field, and the system places modules rather than performing conduit, disconnect or termination work at height.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic installation of electrical equipment by an electrical contractor. Transfer fails for this task because the work is at ground level on regular pre-laid racking, with no ladder/roof access, no conduit runs and no conductor terminations.

sources.system: Trinabot rooftop PV installation robot; Solar D rooftop robot
sources.title: Robots Make Solar Installation Faster and Easier - Solar Washington
sources.claim: Rooftop solar placement robots (Trinabot in China, Solar D in Thailand) automate transporting, aligning and laying panels on roofs, but human operators must still finalize the installation; none is documented performing rooftop conduit, disconnect or conductor termination work in the US.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic work on building roofs installing electrical equipment. Transfer fails because the robots only place modules and humans complete the installation, including the electrical connections that define this task.

tasks.label: Use a variety of tools or equipment, such as power construction equipment, measuring devices, power tools, and testing equipment, such as oscilloscopes, ammeters, or test lamps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential rough-in and remodel tool work in an occupied house or a house under construction: measuring and marking, boring stud/joist holes with a right-angle drill and auger bits, cutting box and fixture openings in sheathing or finished drywall with a hole saw/oscillating tool, driving fasteners, working around existing framing, insulation and homeowner belongings.

Commercial/industrial raceway work on a jobsite: measuring runs, cutting and reaming EMT/rigid conduit with a band saw or threader, bending offsets and 90s with hand/hydraulic/electric benders, hammer-drilling supports, and mounting strut and conduit overhead from a lift or ladder amid other trades.

Layout and anchor-hole drilling on an active commercial construction site: transferring drawing/BIM points to the deck or slab with a laser or total station, marking hanger and penetration locations, then drilling hundreds of overhead or floor anchor holes in concrete with a rotary hammer and vacuum dust control.

Test-and-measurement work in an operating facility (plant, hospital, campus, data center): using a multimeter, clamp ammeter, test lamp, phase rotation meter, insulation tester, oscilloscope or power-quality analyzer and an IR camera on switchgear, motor control centers, drives and control circuits to verify, commission, or diagnose faults, often with the equipment energized and under an energized-work permit.

Service call at a home or small business: using a test lamp, multimeter and receptacle tester to trace a dead circuit, tripping breaker, or failed device; probing terminals in loadcenters and junction boxes, then using hand and power tools to correct the fault.

Prefab shop or electrical room: machining enclosures and back-panels (drilling, tapping, cutting knockouts), cutting/stripping/ferruling and landing conductors, torqueing lugs and terminal screws to spec with a calibrated torque tool, and performing continuity/insulation-resistance checks before energizing.

sources.title: Jaibot - Hilti Corporation (media release)
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a commercially sold, semi-autonomous mobile robot deployed on real construction sites that drills anchor holes for mechanical, ... installation from BIM data and marks hole positions, with dust removal built in.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: use of a power tool (rotary hammer) with layout measurement to produce anchor holes for electrical supports, in the electrician's own jobsite environment.

sources.title: Introducing the Hilti Jaibot, Your New Robotic Partner
sources.claim: Jaibot's operating mode is operator setup then unattended drilling and marking of a batch of holes within reach, with the operator only repositioning the base between stations.

sources.system: DEWALT / August Robotics downward drilling robot
sources.developer: DEWALT (Stanley Black & Decker) with August Robotics
sources.title: DEWALT Unveils the World's First Downward Drilling, Fleet-Capable Robot to Accelerate Data Center Construction
sources.claim: DEWALT and August Robotics' autonomous, fleet-capable concrete drilling robot has drilled over 90,000 holes at 99.97% location/depth accuracy across ten phases of data center construction, including holes for the supports of overhead electrical systems.
sources.transferJustification: Same tool work as the electrician's anchor drilling: a machine-held rotary hammer producing dimensioned anchor holes in concrete on an active construction site.

sources.title: Robotic Concrete Marking Case Study | REA JET
sources.claim: Rugged Robotics fields an autonomous layout vehicle that prints coordinated BIM layout directly on unfinished construction floors, replacing manual tape-measure and chalk layout, and is scaling commercially on large projects.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the measuring-device half of jobsite layout: transferring drawing coordinates to the deck, the same output an electrician produces with a total station, laser and tape.

sources.title: WEINMANN WALLTEQ Multi-Function Bridges - Stiles Machinery
sources.claim: WEINMANN/HOMAG WALLTEQ multifunction bridges on prefabricated wall-panel lines perform automatic routing and drilling of openings for power outlets, plus sawing, trimming and fastening, on panels fixtured on the machine table.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is CNC panel processing in house-panel factories; it performs exactly the drilling/cutting tool operations of residential electrical rough-in (bores and outlet openings in wood framing and sheathing) on fixtured workpieces.

sources.title: Rittal's New Perforex MT 2201 Automated Milling Terminal Provides Accelerated Throughput Times for Enclosure Modifications
sources.claim: Rittal's Perforex MT machining terminal performs fully automated drilling, thread-tapping and milling of electrical enclosures and back panels in a single cycle, a job electricians and panel shops otherwise do with hand power tools.

sources.date: 2014-09-15 (launch; still in Rittal Kiesling product portfolio)
sources.title: Rittal Kiesling Product portfolio
sources.claim: The Kiesling (Rittal) Averex robotic wiring centre fully automatically wires control-panel mounting plates: cutting wire to length, stripping, crimping ferrules, routing through cable duct and connecting to components such as terminal ... breakers.

sources.title: 3 Ways Automating Your Wire Processing Can Increase Productivity | Rittal
sources.claim: Rittal's Wire Terminal WT C produces prepared, cut, stripped, ferruled and labelled panel wires at over 200 wires per hour with no manual intervention.

sources.system: Komax Zeta 633/656 (and Zeta 650) harness/panel wiring machines
sources.title: Control Panel Manufacturing Gets Automated | Cable Assembly Supplier
sources.claim: Komax Zeta wire-processing systems automatically cut, strip and crimp conductors and insert them into spring-loaded terminal blocks, verifying each landed connection with an automatic pull test.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is automated panel/harness wiring; it performs the electrician's strip-crimp-land-and-verify tool sequence, including a mechanical verification equivalent to a torque/pull check, on fixtured work.

sources.system: SPEA / Takaya APT flying probe testers
sources.title: Takaya Flying Probe Test System - Texmac Inc. / SPEA Flying Probe Test
sources.claim: SPEA and Takaya flying-probe testers are commercial machines that autonomously drive probes onto conductors of a fixtured assembly and measure electrical characteristics to detect shorts, opens and out-of-tolerance components.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is automated in-circuit electrical test: machine-held probes make contact measurements (continuity, resistance, component value) and localize the fault — the same measure-and-diagnose function an electrician performs with a meter, but on fixtured work.

sources.title: How Spot Helps the ENR Sector | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs autonomous inspection rounds in utility and industrial facilities, capturing thermal images of electrical connection points, motors and pumps and reading analog gauges; Consumers Energy uses it in production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous infrared/gauge inspection rounds in an operating facility — the non-contact survey portion of an electrician's test-equipment work, but it makes no contact measurements with meters or scopes.

tasks.label: Assemble, install, test, or maintain electrical or electronic wiring, equipment, appliances, apparatus, or fixtures, using hand tools or power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rough-in and trim-out of a single-family house or apartment unit under construction/remodel: drilling studs and joists, mounting device and fixture boxes, pulling and stapling NM cable, setting the panel, then terminating receptacles, switches and fixtures and testing circuits. Cluttered active jobsite, other trades present, layout differs house to house.

Service/repair call in an occupied home or small business: diagnose a dead circuit or failed device, replace receptacles, switches, breakers, ceiling fans and light fixtures, hook up an appliance or EV charger, working in attics, crawlspaces, closets and finished walls with customer furniture present, then test and verify.

Commercial/institutional building under construction or fit-out: bending and mounting EMT/rigid conduit and cable tray, pulling feeders, installing panelboards, transformers, disconnects, lay-in troffers and lighting controls from lifts and ladders, terminating and megger/continuity testing. Multi-story, congested overhead, layout unique per job.

Maintenance and equipment installation inside an operating industrial plant, hospital, warehouse or data center: replacing motor starters and VFDs, landing control wiring in an MCC, troubleshooting a stopped machine circuit, installing branch circuits and receptacles to equipment, testing and returning to service, often under energized or partially shut-down conditions.

Shop/bench prefabrication and assembly at the contractor's prefab shop or a panel shop: cutting, stripping, crimping and labeling conductors, building fixture whips and MC cable assemblies, assembling and wiring control panels and DIN-rail terminal strips to a drawing, then continuity/pull-out testing before shipment to the job.

Outdoor site electrical on public or semi-public ground: installing or servicing parking-lot and street lighting poles, pulling conductors in underground raceway, splicing in pole hand holes, mounting photocells and pedestal EV chargers, working from a bucket truck in traffic and weather.

sources.title: Fully automatic machine Zeta 620: Huge opportunity for smaller control cabinet builders | Komax
sources.claim: Komax Zeta series machines fully automatically produce finished, ferruled and labeled wires for control-cabinet construction inside an enclosed purpose-built machine, automatically producing entire parts lists and depositing the cables sorted and labeled.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cable-lead assembly. Transfers to the shop-prefabrication instance because the objects (stranded building/control conductors, ferrules, labels) and the operations (measure, cut, strip, crimp, mark, test) are exactly the bench work electricians do in a prefab shop.

sources.title: Modular Robotic Stations for Control Cabinet Manufacturing | WAGO
sources.claim: WAGO's Cabinet Wiring Robot / Wiring Bot automatically prepares conductors (cut to length, stripped, crimped, printed, pull-out tested) and wires them onto terminal rails, delivering pre-wired DIN rails as semi-finished assemblies in control-cabinet manufacturing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated control-cabinet wiring. Transfers to shop assembly of electrical panels and terminal strips — same components (DIN-rail terminal blocks, ferruled conductors), same termination precision, same fixtured bench presentation.

sources.title: Q5D Introduces the CY1000 Wiring Harness Automation Cell | New Equipment Digest
sources.claim: Q5D's CY1000 robotic cell automatically routes, places and terminates conductors and components onto fixtured parts to produce finished wired assemblies, replacing manual harness build-up.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic wire routing and termination on a fixtured workpiece. Supports the E1 counterfactual for bench assembly of wired electrical assemblies, but only for parts presented in a fixture inside the cell.

sources.title: Automated Architecture uses robotic micro-factories to build homes | Building Design + Construction
sources.claim: In deployed robotic housing micro-factories, robots assemble the timber wall, floor and roof panels, but the electrical, mechanical and plumbing systems are still installed by human trades.
sources.transferJustification: Bears on the E1 counterfactual for residential rough-in: even where house construction has been brought into a purpose-built robotic factory, no cited system performs the electrical installation — it remains manual.

sources.title: Hilti Unveils BIM-Enabled Jobsite Robot | Construction Equipment
sources.claim: The only commercially available construction robot marketed for electrical installation work performs a single sub-step — semi-autonomous drilling of BIM-located overhead anchor holes — and does not install boxes, raceway, conductors, devices or fixtures.

sources.title: Meta Tests Robot Technicians: Inside Its Push to Automate Data Center Work | TechRepublic
sources.claim: Robotic handling of cabling inside a tightly controlled institutional facility (a hyperscale data center) is still at the testing stage; the machines actually operating at multiple sites move racks and track inventory rather than install or terminate wiring.

tasks.label: Connect wires to circuit breakers, transformers, or other components.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential new construction, remodel, or service call: in a house under framing or an occupied home, terminating 14–10 AWG branch-circuit conductors onto breaker screw lugs in a load center, onto device and fixture terminals, and onto small control transformers (doorbell/thermostat). Cramped, dusty, ladder and kneeling work; layout differs house to house.

Commercial/institutional new construction or tenant fit-out: in an electrical room or above ceilings of a building under construction, landing dozens of 12–8 AWG branch-circuit conductors on breakers in panelboards, plus terminations at lighting relay panels, contactors, disconnects and control devices. Other trades present, temporary lighting, unfinished site.

Industrial/facility maintenance and installation: inside an operating plant, hospital or campus, terminating control and small power conductors (18–10 AWG) on terminal blocks, motor starters, VFDs, PLC I/O cards and control transformers within cabinets and MCC buckets, under lockout/tagout, on premises the institution controls.

Heavy power terminations: landing large conductors (2/0 AWG–500 kcmil) or bus onto main breakers, service disconnects, dry-type or pad-mounted transformers, switchgear and generators — cable cut and stripped, lugs crimped or set-screwed and torqued to spec — in electrical rooms, outdoor pads and vaults.

Shop prefabrication: in the contractor's prefab shop or a panel shop, wiring control panels, gear assemblies and pre-built branch assemblies on a bench from schematics — connecting prepared wires to breakers, relays, terminal blocks and transformers on a mounting plate.

sources.system: Averex robotic wiring centre (Kiesling Maschinentechnik / Rittal)
sources.title: Averex wiring centre from Kiesling | Rittal - The System.
sources.claim: Averex, a portal-robot wiring centre from Kiesling (Friedhelm Loh/Rittal group), automatically cuts, strips, crimps and routes wires and attaches them to components including terminal blocks, contactors and motor ... on an enclosure mounting plate loaded into the machine; declared production-ready after field tests, ~40 s per connection vs ~180 s manual.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: connecting conductors to circuit breakers and other components. Objects (insulated copper conductors with ferrules, screw and spring-clamp terminals on breakers/contactors) and precision match an electrician's panel terminations; the setting is a purpose-built machine cell.

sources.system: Averex; Wirebot (Polygon Technologies); Rittal cobot wiring solution
sources.title: Automated Control Cabinet Wiring Solution for Scalable Renewable Energy Systems (Springer, GCSM 2025)
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed 2025 open-access review of automated control-cabinet wiring: Averex wires both spring-loaded and screw connections; Polygon Technologies' Wirebot uses an articulated robot with vision and tactile sensing to plug prepared wires into spring-loaded and screw-type terminals (~1 min/wire) while a portal robot routes them; Rittal showed a cobot wiring solution at SPS 2023. The authors note no turnkey, industry-proven system yet covers the whole wiring chain for varying cabinet sizes.
sources.transferJustification: Same task performed in a fixtured cell: inserting and securing prepared conductors into screw and spring terminals of breakers, relays and terminal blocks, which is the core act of connecting wires to circuit breakers and other components.

sources.system: WIRES robotized switchgear cabling system (University of Bologna et al.)
sources.developer: University of Bologna / EU ECHORD++ WIRES experiment
sources.title: Automatized Switchgear Wiring: An Outline of the WIRES Experiment Results
sources.claim: The EU WIRES experiment developed a sensorized dual-purpose end effector with an electric screwdriver and tactile sensing that autonomously grasps a wire, inserts it into switchgear screw/clip connection points and tightens it, reporting about 95% success on the wire insertion and connection ....
sources.transferJustification: Switchgear cabling is the same physical act as an electrician terminating conductors on breakers/terminal blocks — screw terminals tightened with a driver — demonstrated on real switchgear components in a robot cell.

sources.system: WAGO Wiring Bot / WAGO Cabinet Wiring Robot
sources.title: Modular Robotic Stations for Control Cabinet Manufacturing | WAGO
sources.claim: WAGO markets modular robotic stations for control cabinet manufacturing: the Wiring Bot pre-wires DIN rails (one-sided pre-wired rails as semi-finished ...) and a fully automated conductor preparation ... cuts, strips, crimps and prints up to 16 conductors, supporting cross-sections of only 0.5–2.5 mm² (about 20–14 AWG).
sources.transferJustification: Same task at small gauges: machine-connecting prepared conductors into terminal blocks on rails inside a purpose-built station; the stated 0.5–2.5 mm² limit also bounds what such systems can do for heavy feeder terminations.

sources.title: Polygon Technologies reduces onsite commissioning time by 70 percent - Tecnomatix (Siemens)
sources.claim: Polygon Technologies' Wirebot is a commercially offered robotic system that automates wire assembly and routing for electrical control cabinets, validated through Siemens Process Simulate virtual commissioning with reported 70% reduction in onsite commissioning time and 60% less rework.
sources.transferJustification: Wirebot's application is wiring electrical control panels — connecting conductors to terminals of breakers, relays and terminal blocks — the same physical task, performed inside a fenced robotic cell.

instances.label: Journeyman electrician on a residential or light-commercial jobsite directs an apprentice or helper: assigns the day's work, explains where to run cable and set boxes, answers questions, inspects the apprentice's work and tells them what to correct.

Lead electrician or foreman gives a hands-on demonstration to a helper — walking through how to bend a conduit offset, terminate a panel, or land conductors — narrating each step while the trainee watches and then repeats the work under observation.

Crew foreman on a commercial construction site runs a start-of-shift briefing/toolbox talk: reads the day's scope from prints, assigns crew members to areas, and reviews code and lockout-tagout/safety requirements for the task.

Maintenance electrician in an industrial plant instructs junior technicians or operators: reviews one-line diagrams and ladder logic prints, explains the troubleshooting sequence for a failed motor circuit, and coaches them through the procedure.

Formal instruction at a contractor shop or union apprenticeship training center: an experienced electrician teaches a class on wiring methods and NEC requirements using mockup boards, whiteboard explanation, and supervised practice.

tasks.label: Test electrical systems or continuity of circuits in electrical wiring, equipment, or fixtures, using testing devices, such as ohmmeters, voltmeters, or oscilloscopes, to ensure compatibility and safety of system.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential new construction/remodel: before and after energizing, the electrician rings out branch circuits in a house (panel, device boxes, attic/crawlspace runs), checking continuity of conductors and grounds, correct polarity, and absence of unintended shorts, using a multimeter, continuity tester and receptacle tester; ladders, dust, incomplete finishes.

Residential/light-commercial service call in an occupied building: diagnose a dead or intermittent circuit, tripping breaker or flickering lights with voltmeter, ohmmeter and clamp meter; the electrician chooses test points ad hoc on undocumented wiring, isolates the fault, then verifies the repair.

Commercial/institutional jobsite: pre-energization testing of a new distribution system - insulation-resistance (megger) tests on feeders, continuity of conduit-run circuits and equipment grounds, phase rotation and voltage checks at panels and switchgear; active construction site with other trades, lifts, temporary lighting.

Maintenance electrician in an operating plant, hospital or campus: routine testing of installed equipment - continuity of control circuits at terminal blocks, motor winding resistance and insulation resistance, voltage and current checks, scope traces on a drive output - inside electrical rooms and machine rooms of a facility kept to a working standard.

Shop/prefab bench work: point-to-point continuity and hipot/insulation testing of assembled control panels, cable assemblies, or luminaires on a bench in the contractor's prefabrication shop before shipment to the jobsite, following a wiring schedule and recording pass/fail.

Outdoor/utility field work: fault-finding on street-lighting circuits, site feeders and service entrances - locating an open or a ground fault in installed underground cable with insulation testers and meters, in traffic, weather and after-dark conditions.

tasks.label: Diagnose malfunctioning systems, apparatus, or components, using test equipment and hand tools to locate the cause of a breakdown and correct the problem.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service call in an occupied private home: homeowner reports dead receptacles, a repeatedly tripping breaker, or flickering lights. Electrician interviews the occupant, opens the panel, uses a multimeter/non-contact tester/circuit tracer, pulls devices out of boxes, finds a loose backstab, failed GFCI, or damaged cable in a wall/attic/crawlspace, and repairs it, working around furniture, pets, and unknown legacy wiring.

Commercial building maintenance (office, retail, school, hospital): lighting circuit or receptacle branch is dead, LED drivers/ballasts or an occupancy-sensor/contactor/lighting-relay circuit misbehaves. Electrician works from a lift or ladder above ceiling grid, meters at panelboards and junction boxes in occupied space, isolates the fault, replaces the failed device or repairs the connection, and verifies operation.

Industrial plant downtime call: a machine, conveyor, or pump won't run. Electrician troubleshoots the MCC/control panel — checks fuses, overloads, contactors, VFD fault codes, 24 VDC control circuits, limit switches and sensors — with meter and clamp-on ammeter and prints, under lockout/tagout and time pressure, then replaces the failed component and retests under load.

Troubleshooting during construction or renovation: at rough-in or trim, a circuit fails testing — open neutral, reversed polarity, drywall screw through a cable, shared neutral tripping an AFCI, or a miswired 3-way. Electrician traces the run through partially finished walls and ceilings on an active jobsite with other trades, opens boxes, finds and corrects the wiring error.

Exterior/site electrical faults: street or parking-lot lighting out, photocell/contactor failure in a pole base, faulted underground feeder or service entrance, damaged outdoor disconnect or pump-panel circuit. Electrician works outdoors at grade or from a bucket truck, in weather, using megger/fault-location gear, and repairs or replaces the faulted component.

sources.system: Spot with arm (Boston Dynamics) at Ontario Power Generation

sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot with an arm autonomously trips and racks out a 600 V circuit breaker in an Ontario Power Generation switchgear room using a custom end effector, with a human giving high-level commands from a safe distance. sources.transferJustification: Related task: operating switchgear in an electrical facility. It does not transfer to diagnosis-and-repair: the breaker position is known and pre-taught, the tool is a purpose-built racking effector, and no test instrument is used or fault located.

Its output is inspection data; it does not probe circuits with test equipment or perform repairs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: condition monitoring of electrical apparatus in an institution-controlled facility. It substantiates autonomous navigation and sensing in E2 electrical settings only; it cannot locate a wiring fault with meters or correct it, so it cannot complete this task's instances.

Transfer fails because it only diagnoses PCB nets against a known netlist and never corrects the fault, whereas this task requires locating the cause and repairing it.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fault-driven component replacement inside an institution-controlled facility. Transfer fails: the object is a uniform hot-swap drive in a standardized rack slot, the fault is reported by software, and no test instrument, hand tool, live conductor or wiring repair is involved.

tasks.label: Inspect electrical systems, equipment, or components to identify hazards, defects, or the need for adjustment or repair, and to ensure compliance with codes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service call in an occupied home or apartment: remove the panel dead front, check breakers, terminations, grounding/bonding, trace circuits, test receptacles/GFCIs/AFCIs with meter and plug tester, check fixtures, attic/crawl-space runs and older wiring, and report hazards, defects and code violations. Clutter, furniture, pets, ladders, tight access, no site control.

Service and maintenance inspection in a commercial or institutional building (office, retail, school, hospital, restaurant): open panelboards and disconnects, verify breaker sizing and labeling, inspect terminations, receptacles, occupancy and emergency lighting, exit signs and life-safety circuits, take voltage/current readings, and write up defects and code deficiencies for repair.

Routine condition-monitoring round of electrical equipment in an industrial plant, utility substation or data center: walk a fixed route past switchgear, MCCs, transformers, motors, cable trays and distribution panels; look and listen for damage or abnormal operation, take infrared thermography and gauge readings, and log/flag hotspots and anomalies for follow-up repair.

Job-site inspection of new construction or renovation electrical work before cover-up/energization: verify box placement and fill, cable supports and protection plates, conduit runs and supports, grounding/bonding, conductor sizing and terminations, panel schedules; correct deficiencies and self-check against NEC ahead of the AHJ inspection. Active site, changing layout, other trades present.

Outdoor electrical assets on streets, parking lots and campuses: inspect street and area lighting (luminaires, photocells, pole-base fuses and handhole wiring), service entrances, pad-mounted and pole-mounted equipment for damage, corrosion, water ingress and hazards, working from a truck, ladder or bucket in traffic and weather.

Shop/bench inspection and testing of electrical components and assemblies brought in: control panels, motors, contactors, cord sets and portable tools, luminaires and devices; visual check plus continuity, insulation-resistance and functional testing to determine defects and whether the item is serviceable.

tasks.label: Install ground leads and connect power cables to equipment, such as motors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Industrial/manufacturing plant maintenance: connect a replacement 3-phase motor (roughly 5-100 hp) on the plant floor - route the flex whip into the motor peg box, strip conductors, crimp/bolt them to the motor leads, tape or insulate, land the equipment grounding conductor on the frame ground lug, torque to spec, verify rotation. Cramped access, adjacent running equipment, sometimes on a ladder or lift.

New commercial construction jobsite: hook up mechanical equipment (rooftop HVAC units, exhaust fans, booster pumps) - mount/land the disconnect, terminate MC cable or whip conductors at the unit's terminal block or lugs, install and bond the equipment grounding conductor. Unfinished building, other trades working, debris, weather exposure on roofs.

Residential and light-commercial service work: connect small motor-driven equipment - AC condenser/heat pump, well or sump pump, garbage disposal, attic or bath fan, ceiling fan motor - small conductors under screw terminals or wire connectors, plus the green ground screw/pigtail. Occupied homes, tight crawl spaces, attics, varied existing wiring.

Plant/building electrical room: land large feeder conductors and grounding/bonding conductors at motor control centers, VFDs, starters and disconnects serving large motors - compression lugs on 4/0 to 500 kcmil cable, torqued bolted connections, bonding jumpers to the ground bus, sometimes medium-voltage terminations with stress cones.

Prefabrication or panel shop: an electrician builds motor control panels and equipment skids on a bench - cutting, stripping, ferruling and landing power conductors on breakers, contactors and terminal blocks, and bonding the green protective-earth conductors to the ground bar, per a wiring diagram.

Outdoor/site electrical: connect power cables and install ground leads on outdoor equipment - lift-station and irrigation pumps, street-light pole bases, generator/transformer pads - including grounding electrode conductors to driven rods, exothermic welds or ground clamps, in trenches, handholes and pole bases, in weather.

tasks.label: Repair or replace wiring, equipment, or fixtures, using hand tools or power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service call in an occupied home: replace a failed device or fixture — ceiling light or fan, dimmer/switch, receptacle, range/dryer outlet, doorbell transformer. Electrician kills the circuit, works off a ladder at an existing box, removes the old unit, re-terminates conductors with wire nuts/screw terminals, mounts and tests the new one. Layout, box condition, wire type (including old cloth/aluminum) vary house to house.

Commercial or institutional building (office, school, retail, hospital): replace failed lighting fixtures, LED drivers/ballasts, lamps, breakers, receptacles, occupancy sensors or disconnects. Work is done on a ladder or lift, in a suspended ceiling grid, in occupied space, on standardized building equipment maintained by a facilities department.

Industrial/manufacturing plant maintenance: after lockout/tagout, repair or replace motor leads, contactors, relays, VFD or control-panel components, limit switches, and damaged conductors/conduit on machinery — often removing a panel or the equipment to the maintenance shop bench, re-landing wires on terminal blocks to torque spec, and testing.

Troubleshooting-driven wiring repair: an intermittent or dead circuit, tripping breaker, or rodent/water/nail-damaged cable. Electrician localizes the fault with a meter/tracer, opens ceiling, wall or conduit to reach it, cuts out the damaged run, splices or pulls replacement conductors, restores the opening and verifies. Fault location and access differ every time.

Exterior/site work: repair or replace parking-lot and street lighting heads, photocells, pole wiring and in-ground splices, sign circuits, EV chargers, and weather- or vehicle-damaged service equipment. Bucket truck or lift, outdoors on a roadway or lot, in variable weather and traffic.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: wiring a control cabinet in a panel shop. It uses the same objects and precision as replacing wiring/components in electrical equipment — insulated conductors, ferrules/crimps, screw and clamp terminals to torque — with the mounting plate fixtured and presented to the machine, i.e. the E1 counterfactual for panel and equipment rewiring.

tasks.label: Construct or fabricate parts, using hand tools, according to specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: On an active commercial/industrial construction site, the electrician fabricates a conduit run to a specification (spool sheet or field measurements): cuts EMT/IMC/rigid to length with a hacksaw or bandsaw, reams, and bends 90s, offsets, saddles and kicks with a hand or hydraulic bender, checking angles and take-up so the finished piece matches the run.

At the jobsite or a site trailer, the electrician fabricates supports and brackets from strut channel, all-thread, angle iron or flat bar per a detail drawing: measures and cuts to length with a bandsaw/chop saw, drills and deburrs holes, files edges, and bolts the pieces into a trapeze, stand-off or equipment bracket.

In a contractor panel shop or plant maintenance shop, the electrician fabricates enclosure and backplate parts to a schematic: lays out and cuts device cutouts and knockouts in the enclosure (hole saw, punch, nibbler, file), drills and taps mounting holes, and cuts DIN rail and wire duct to exact lengths.

In an electrical prefabrication shop, the worker produces repeated standardized assemblies to a written spec: cut-to-length MC/AC fixture whips with connectors and terminations, device-box assemblies with plaster rings, straps and pigtails, and pre-cut conduit/strut rack kits, in batches with labeling.

In an occupied building (hospital wing, plant floor, finished home), the electrician makes a one-off part fitted to as-found conditions: measures the existing opening or obstruction, cuts and files a cover plate, spacer, filler or modified bracket, test-fits it in place and trims repeatedly until it seats correctly.

tasks.label: Fasten small metal or plastic boxes to walls to house electrical switches or outlets.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential new-construction rough-in: on an open wood-stud jobsite (single-family or low-rise multifamily), the electrician nails or screws dozens of plastic nail-on device boxes to stud faces at layout heights (~15" for receptacles, ~48" for switches), setting each box to the correct setback so it will finish flush with future drywall; framing is warped and irregular, other trades are working nearby.

Commercial new construction / tenant build-out rough-in: metal 4" square or gangable steel boxes with brackets or bar hangers screwed to light-gauge metal studs in new drywall partitions (offices, schools, retail shells), often multi-gang, coordinated with conduit stub-ups and ladders/lifts, on an active construction floor.

Remodel / service work in an existing occupied building: locate a stud-free cavity in finished drywall or plaster, cut the opening, fish wire, and secure an 'old-work' remodel box with wing clamps or side ears; furniture, occupants and unknown wall contents are present.

Surface-mounted boxes in an operating industrial or institutional facility: drill anchors into CMU, concrete or steel and bolt a metal FS/4-square box to the wall for a switch or receptacle, aligned to existing conduit runs, working around live equipment and production areas.

Offsite prefabrication: installing device boxes into wall panels or volumetric modules on a panel/module production line (or into an electrical contractor's shop-built wall assemblies), with panels lying flat on fixtured tables and box locations taken from the digital model.

sources.title: Robot FEEDBOT F-500 | HOMAG
sources.claim: WEINMANN (HOMAG) FEEDBOT F-500 is a commercial six-axis robot in timber-frame wall production lines that autonomously picks and inserts studs and top/bottom plates into a fixtured wall frame at high precision from digital data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic component placement onto a fixtured wall frame in a panel line. Transfer: a device box is a far smaller, lighter part than a stud, placed onto the same fixtured frame at a model-defined coordinate; the required placement precision (a few mm on a stud face) is within the demonstrated repeatability.

sources.system: Kawasaki BX250L robot cell (SCADAware integration) at Rehkemper & Son
sources.title: Assembling Walls for Prefabricated Homes | Industrial Robots by Kawasaki
sources.claim: Four Kawasaki BX250L robots on Guedel rails at prefab home builder Rehkemper & Son place OSB sheathing on framed walls held on a large motorized table and drive nails into hidden studs at positions computed from the wall's digital design.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: model-driven robotic fastening onto a fixtured wood-frame wall. Transfer: fastening a nail-on device box to a stud is the same pick-place-and-drive-fastener operation on the same workpiece and table, with comparable (or looser) tolerance than hitting a hidden 1.5" stud with nails.

sources.transferJustification: Same task, factory setting: shows box installation is not yet automated in practice even on the leading robotic wall line, while the same line already does robotic pick-place-fasten and precision routing of box openings on fixtured panels.

sources.title: Hilti unveils new robot-powered drilling capabilities | Design World
sources.claim: The state of the art for jobsite MEP robots is BIM-driven hole drilling: Hilti's Jaibot is positioned by an operator with a ... and then drills marked holes in concrete ceilings and walls; it does not set anchors or mount boxes.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only as a limit: the leading jobsite electrical/MEP robot performs drilling under operator positioning, so no cited system mounts device boxes to in-situ walls at E3 or E2.

tasks.label: Perform physically demanding tasks, such as digging trenches to lay conduit or moving or lifting heavy objects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-ground trenching for underground conduit/duct bank on a commercial, utility-solar, or site-development job: staked route across open dirt, machine-dug trench 18-48 in. deep to line and grade, spoil placed beside the trench for later conduit laying and backfill. Weather and terrain as found; a crew works nearby.

Congested hand excavation: digging a service-lateral or lighting trench in a residential yard or tight urban strip - shovel and pick work around foundations, sidewalks, roots, sprinklers and live buried utilities, hand-potholing to locate existing lines, then backfilling, tamping and restoring the surface.

Receiving and staging heavy material at an active jobsite: offloading pallets of fittings, bundles of 10-ft conduit, 300-800 lb wire spools and boxed gear from a delivery truck, and hauling them across mud/gravel to the laydown area or building floor with a forklift, cart or by hand.

Manhandling heavy irregular items to the point of installation inside a building under construction: carrying/hoisting a 200-400 lb panelboard, transformer, or large fixture up stairs, on a lift, or through framed walls and ceiling spaces, then holding and positioning it for mounting.

Moving and setting heavy gear inside an existing operating facility (plant, hospital, data center): rolling a switchgear section on pipe rollers into a tight electrical room, lifting motors or UPS batteries with a hoist or pallet jack, repositioning equipment in occupied mechanical spaces.

sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution - Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofit turns a standard excavator into a fully autonomous trenching machine for DC/AC cable trenches on utility solar construction sites, digging to 0.1 ft accuracy with clean spoil placement.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: digging trenches in which electrical conduit/cable is laid, on outdoor construction sites.

sources.title: Built Robotics raises $64 million for robotic excavator Exosystem | Equipment World
sources.claim: Excavators fitted with Built Robotics' Exosystem were deployed doing trenching work on a 1.1-GW solar farm, i.e. in real production, not only in demonstrations.

sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Moves Earth with Autonomous Excavators | Engineering News-Record

sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics ran supervised-autonomy excavators on active US construction sites, moving 65,000+ cubic yards of earth on a 130-acre site in standard contractor workflows.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk earthmoving/excavation with the same machines and site conditions as trenching for conduit; shows autonomous earth excavation at contractor production rates on unstructured sites.

sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch is commercially deployed at DHL unloading heavy cases from trailers and containers autonomously, handling mixed stacking and fallen boxes.

sources.title: FANUC M-2000iA/2300 Robot - Ultra Heavy Payload Robot | FANUC America
sources.claim: Ultra-heavy-payload industrial robots such as the FANUC M-2000iA/2300 lift and precisely position loads up to 2.3 t (entire car bodies, bulky castings) onto fixtures in fenced production cells, replacing cranes and manual lifting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heavy-part pick-and-place in a fenced cell. Weights (up to 2.3 t) far exceed the panelboards, transformers and reels electricians move, and placement accuracy exceeds mounting tolerances, so capability transfers when the load is presented and the destination fixtured.

sources.developer: AIT Austrian Institute of Technology (EU AWARD project)
sources.title: [2503.14331] ADAPT: An Autonomous Forklift for Construction Site Operation
sources.claim: The ADAPT autonomous off-road forklift transported pallets on unstructured outdoor construction terrain in extensive field trials, reaching near human-operator performance across weather conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pallet transport on a construction site - the same haul-and-stage work, but a research prototype at near-human (not accepted worker) reliability.

tasks.label: Provide assistance during emergencies by operating floodlights or generators, placing flares, or driving needed vehicles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Storm or outage callout: electrician drives a service truck to a customer site, street-light circuit or damaged service, then positions a portable/towable generator, grounds it, runs and connects feeder cables to a panel or spider box, fuels and starts it to restore temporary power. Outdoors, wet, dark, debris, bystanders.

Night emergency repair scene: unload, position and level portable floodlights or a light-tower, aim them at the work area, connect them to a generator or truck power, and re-aim as the crew moves. Uneven ground, traffic, weather.
Hazard-scene protection: place flares, cones, triangles and warning signage around a downed conductor, an open vault, or the work vehicle on a public street or shoulder, with live traffic passing.

Driving needed vehicles during the emergency: shuttling crew and equipment, repositioning the bucket truck or a generator trailer at the scene, moving vehicles clear of hazards, driving on public roads and rough site ground under storm or incident conditions.

Emergency support inside an institutional facility (hospital, plant, campus, data center) during a power failure: start and monitor the standby generator, connect a portable unit or temporary feeders, string temporary lighting in corridors and equipment rooms while staff and responders move through.

sources.title: Rocsys launches integrated platform to enable hands-free charging for autonomous mobility - Charged EVs
sources.claim: Rocsys' automatic connection device autonomously locates the charge port and inserts/removes a high-power charging cable at depots and ports, i.e. vision-guided autonomous mating of a heavy power connector at a fixed station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: plugging a heavy charging cable into a receptacle. It transfers to the electrical hookup part of 'operating a generator/floodlight' at E1 — same class of object (a bulky power connector), coarse-to-moderate precision, and a station built around the machine.

sources.system: Universal Robots UR10e machine-tending cells (e.g. Raymath)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: fixtured pick-and-place plus machine control actuation. It transfers to placing a cone/lamp presented in a fixture and pressing a start switch at E1 — comparable object weight, coarse placement tolerance, and a fenced cell built around the machine.

sources.claim: Caterpillar's autonomous haulage system runs hundreds of driverless haul trucks at customer mine sites worldwide, moving billions of tonnes without operators in the cab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving heavy work vehicles over site roads. It transfers to 'driving needed vehicles' at E2 — full-size trucks, mixed traffic of site machines and light vehicles, on premises an operator controls and maintains.

sources.claim: Outrider operates driverless yard trucks that move trailers around distribution yards and use a robotic manipulator to hitch and connect trailer air and electrical lines.

sources.claim: Waymo runs driverless paid robotaxi service at large scale on public streets and freeways in several US metros.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: point-to-point driving on public roads. Cited to bound the driving instance: it is limited to mapped geofences and light passenger vehicles, so it does not cover driving loaded work trucks into storm-damaged or incident scenes.

sources.title: ANYmal Monitors High-Voltage Transmission at RTE - ANYbotics
sources.claim: Autonomous legged robots are deployed in power plants and high-voltage substations, but their function there is scheduled inspection and data collection, not operating equipment.

roles.description: Install glass in windows, skylights, store fronts, and display cases, or on surfaces, such as building fronts, interior walls, ceilings, and tabletops.

tasks.label: Read and interpret blueprints or specifications to determine size, shape, color, type, or thickness of glass, location of framing, installation procedures, or staging or scaffolding materials required.
