tasks.label: Determine plumb of walls or ceilings, using plumb lines and levels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial new construction at grade: before setting storefront, window wall or entrance framing, the glazier checks plumb of the rough opening jambs, masonry/steel returns and the set mullions with a 4–6 ft spirit level, laser plumb and plumb bob, on an active jobsite with dust, debris, other trades and a layout that changes daily.

High-rise curtain wall: glazier/erector verifies plumb of slab-edge anchors, starter mullions and installed unitized panels, working mostly from the interior of the glazing floor at the slab edge (some checks from a swing stage or boom lift), on an active high-rise construction site.

Interior glass in occupied, finished commercial or institutional buildings: office glass partitions, mall storefronts, hospital vestibules, mirrors and display cases — glazier checks plumb of the existing walls, columns and door jambs before laying out and mounting glass, with the premises controlled and kept to a working standard.

Residential window, patio-door or entry-door replacement in an occupied house: glazier checks plumb of the existing opening, jamb and adjacent wall with a level and plumb line to decide shimming, working in furnished rooms of varying layout.

Residential/hospitality bathroom work: shower and tub enclosures, framed/frameless doors and mirrors — glazier levels and plumbs the tiled walls and curb inside a small confined bathroom to determine taper before cutting and shimming the frame.
Glass shop / fabrication floor: display case, glass wall assembly, mock-up or frame stood up on a bench or rack and checked for plumb and square before delivery, in the company's own controlled shop.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot + Trimble X7 scanner / FieldLink
sources.title: Trimble Releases Turnkey Autonomous Robotic Scanning Solution
sources.claim: Trimble and Boston Dynamics sell a turnkey product in which Spot carries a Trimble X7 3D laser scanner ... runs autonomous waypoint scanning missions on construction sites, with self-docking and automated data flow to the office.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous as-built laser scanning of walls and openings on a jobsite. It transfers because determining plumb is a geometric measurement of the same wall surfaces the scanner captures at 2 mm-class accuracy, in the same unstructured jobsite environment where the glazier works.

sources.title: Advancing Robotics in Construction with Spot | Turner Construction Company
sources.claim: A general contractor deployed Spot on its construction projects for routine autonomous site walks and laser scanning, and uses the resulting scan data for rapid QA/QC checks and as-built model updates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic jobsite QA/QC scanning. Plumb determination of walls and openings is one of the dimensional QA checks performed from exactly this scan data, on the same active construction sites.

sources.title: 3D Laser Scanning Solutions & Autonomous Reality Capture | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics markets Spot for autonomous reality-capture laser scanning missions in worksites, factories and new construction, producing accurate 3D representations of the facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine autonomous laser scanning inside operating facilities and factories. The captured point cloud is the input from which wall plumbness is computed, so the capability transfers to determining plumb in structured human work facilities.

sources.system: Laser-scanning verticality-check method for installed wall panels
sources.developer: University of Cambridge researchers (ISPRS Annals / ASCE JCEM)
sources.title: A TIME EFFICIENT QUALITY CHECK METHOD BASED ON LASER SCANNING FOR INSTALLATION OF PREFABRICATED WALL PANELS
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed work shows laser-scanning point clouds can replace manual, contact-type verticality (plumb) checks of installed wall panels on site, applying the same acceptance criteria far faster than the manual level-based method.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-site verticality (plumb) checking of installed wall panels from scan data. It validates that a scan-derived plumb determination meets the same criteria as the worker's spirit-level check; the scanner here is tripod-mounted, so it supports only the analysis step, not autonomy.

sources.title: Trimble RealWorks User Guide
sources.claim: Trimble RealWorks includes a Wall Verticality Inspection tool that inspects the plumbness and flatness of ... from point-cloud data against a fitted vertical reference plane.
sources.transferJustification: Software component of the scan-to-plumb pipeline: it converts the robot-captured point cloud into the plumbness output the glazier needs. It is not itself a robot and does not support autonomy.

sources.title: Verity verifies as-built point cloud data meets design specs
sources.claim: ClearEdge3D Verity automatically compares captured point clouds against design models and reports out-of-tolerance deviations with heat maps, giving 100% verification of installed work.
sources.transferJustification: Automated analysis step that turns robot-captured scans into tolerance/deviation results (including verticality of installed elements) without a human interpreting the cloud point by point.

sources.title: Top 10: AI Tools in Construction | Construction Digital
sources.claim: Doxel operates autonomous LiDAR-equipped rovers and drones that scan live construction sites and automatically compare the data with the BIM model to flag deviations of installed work; deployed on data-centre and healthcare projects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic dimensional QA of installed elements on active sites. Deviation of a wall from its modelled vertical plane is precisely the plumb determination the glazier makes, measured on the same objects in the same setting.

sources.system: Quadruped scanning robots (Spot) for autonomous site capture
sources.title: How autonomous construction scanning creates a repeatable site record
sources.claim: Independent trade reporting on autonomous construction scanning states that Spot walks defined routes across active sites — over stairs, ramps and uneven slabs — capturing laser-scan and 360 data used to compare as-built conditions with BIM.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile scanning of cluttered, as-found interiors. Establishes that the capture platform copes with the clutter, stairs and varying layouts of unstructured interiors, the environmental condition at issue for homes and jobsites.

sources.title: BIMBot for Autonomous Laser Scanning in Built Environments (Robotics, MDPI)
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed robotics literature confirms a commercial autonomous scanning integration in which FARO's Trek payload lets Boston Dynamics' Spot repeat a taught route and scan a site autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Independent academic confirmation that robotic autonomous scanning of built environments is a fielded capability; the paper also notes limits (taught routes, low scanner height, cluttered spaces), which bear on confined-space instances.

sources.title: Portable coordinate measuring machine - 360° SIMS - HEXAGON MANUFACTURING INTELLIGENCE
sources.claim: Hexagon's 360° SIMS supplies fully automated robotic dimensional measurement cells for production plants, where robot-mounted white-light sensors measure fixtured assemblies against CAD and report geometric deviations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated geometric inspection (flatness, perpendicularity, position) of a fixtured workpiece in a fenced cell. Under the E1 counterfactual, a wall panel or enclosure frame presented in a fixture is the same class of measurement at equal or better precision.

sources.system: OKIBO wall and ceiling finishing robot
sources.title: OKIBO Robotics: What Does This Company Do? | CEMEX Ventures
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile construction robot built for jobsite conditions scans walls and ceilings floor-to-ceiling at 2-3 mm accuracy and moves autonomously while it renders/plasters them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous on-site 3D measurement of walls and ceilings prior to finishing them to plane. Measuring a wall's deviation from vertical is the same measurement at the accuracy the robot already achieves, in the same unstructured setting.

tasks.label: Install pre-assembled metal or wood frameworks for windows or doors to be fitted with glass panels, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential window units: setting pre-assembled wood, vinyl-clad or aluminum window frames into rough openings of a single-family house (new build or replacement), from a ladder/scaffold or interior floor — shim, plumb and level, nail flange or screw the jamb, insulate and flash, ready for glazing/sash. Openings vary in size, squareness and wall build-up house to house.

Entry, patio and service door frames in houses and light-commercial buildings: setting a pre-hung wood or metal door framework into an opening, shimming to plumb, anchoring through jambs, checking reveal and swing, sealing — later fitted with glass lites.

Commercial aluminum storefront framing at a retail/office build-out: laying out and erecting sub-sill, jambs, header and intermediate mullions of a pre-assembled/knock-down metal framework in a masonry or steel opening, anchoring with fasteners, shimming and sealing so glass can be set. Active construction/renovation site with other trades, dust and variable openings.

Interior fit-out: installing metal or wood frames for interior glass partitions, borrowed lights and glass office doors inside a building being fitted out — align to floor layout lines, plumb, fasten to floor and ceiling track/soffit framing, then glaze.

Curtain wall / window wall framing on a multi-story building: hoisting and installing pre-assembled metal framing units or mullion grids at slab edges and openings, working at height from a swing stage, mast climber or interior slab edge, anchoring to embeds/brackets and sequencing with the hoist crew.

sources.system: Bluewrist EzRG robot-guidance system with LMI Gocator 3D sensors on a six-axis windshield-insertion robot
sources.developer: Bluewrist Inc. / LMI Technologies (integrated at automotive OEM lines, e.g. Wuhan TopEagle)
sources.title: Sensors Make Robots Smarter When Inserting Vehicle Windshields — ASSEMBLY Magazine
sources.claim: Vision-guided six-axis robots on automotive final-assembly lines autonomously pick a large glazed unit, locate the body aperture and insert the glass to ±0.2 mm; the same system is used for installing hoods, trunk lids and doors (pre-assembled metal frameworks that carry glass).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic glazing/closure fitment in automotive assembly. It is the E1 form of 'set a pre-assembled framework or panel into a prepared opening': comparable object size and fragility (large glazed unit handled by a vacuum end-effector), far tighter precision than the ~1/16-in. tolerance glaziers work to, adhesive/sealant applied by the same cell, and the work presented fixtured on a line — the counterfactual E1 presentation of a window/door framework and its opening.

sources.system: Kawasaki BX250L robots on Güdel TrackMotion rails with SCADAware wall-panel line (Rehkemper prefab plant)
sources.title: Assembling Walls for Prefabricated Homes | Industrial Robots by Kawasaki Robotics
sources.claim: Four Kawasaki BX250L robots on rails at a prefabricated-home wall line autonomously pick and place sheathing onto fixtured wood wall frames, nail it to the studs from the digital design, and rout out the window and door openings; the table squares and straightens the frame to within 1/16 in. of the digital design.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sheathing and nailing of prefabricated wall panels. It supplies the fastening half of frame installation — placing a large building component on a fixtured wood frame and driving fasteners at model-defined points to 1/16-in. accuracy in a purpose-built cell with the workpiece squared and held, which is the E1 presentation of a window/door framework in a rough opening.

sources.system: Blueprint Robotics wall-panel line (pneumatic window/door setting gantry), Baltimore
sources.title: Will Robots Install the Windows in Your Next House? | Glass.com
sources.claim: In a US modular-home factory, a gantry sets the actual door and window units into the pre-framed, pre-cut openings of wall panels and secures them, with factory carpenters completing the fastening and flashing.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (setting a pre-assembled window/door framework into an opening) but performed in a fixtured factory line; the gantry's autonomy is not established and human carpenters finish the fastening and flashing, so it is corroborating context for the E1 setting rather than decisive evidence.

sources.system: Raise Robotics mobile platform with two Universal Robots UR20 arms (deployed with Harmon Inc.)
sources.title: Raise Robotics deploys UR cobots with Harmon for high rise fastener installation — The Robot Report
sources.claim: A mobile two-arm robot is deployed by a glazing contractor on live high-rise construction sites to lay out, drill and torque the brackets/fasteners that curtain wall panels hang from — the on-site frontier for facade work is anchor and bracket installation, not setting the framework itself.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: facade bracket/fastener installation at slab edges. It shows what on-site glazing robotics actually completes today (drilling and torquing anchors to layout); it does not include lifting, plumbing, shimming or anchoring a pre-assembled window or curtain-wall framework, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion of this task in a building.

tasks.label: Fabricate or install metal sashes or moldings for glass installation, using aluminum or steel framing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop fabrication in a glazing contractor's metal shop: aluminum storefront/curtain-wall extrusions are pulled from racks, cut to length, drilled/punched for screw splines and shear blocks, notched and routed for door hardware, gasket applied, then bundled by opening for shipment to the job.

New commercial storefront/window-wall on an active construction or remodel site: set and shim the sub-sill, screw-spline the jambs, headers and intermediate mullions together, plumb and level the assembly in the rough opening, anchor to concrete or steel, and seal before glazing.

High-rise curtain wall: lay out and install slab-edge embeds/anchor brackets, then erect stick-system aluminum mullions or hang unitized aluminum frames from the brackets at height, aligning to survey lines in wind and weather.

Retrofit/replacement in an occupied home, storefront or school: remove the existing metal sash or frame from an out-of-plumb existing opening, fit and shim the new aluminum frame, anchor and seal it, and restore adjacent finishes.

Interior metal moldings and trim: mirror J-channels and clips on finished walls, head/floor tracks and vertical channels for glass office partitions, display-case framing, and framed shower/tub enclosures fitted to existing tile and finishes.

sources.system: RhinoFab 900 Automated Extrusion Fabrication Center (Rhino Machine / Glaziers Center)
sources.title: RHINOFAB 900 | Automated Extrusion Fabrication Center
sources.claim: The RhinoFab 900 automated extrusion fabrication center, sold to glazing contractors, takes the layout digitally from drawn elevations and automatically loads, cuts, drills, countersinks and routs storefront and curtain-wall aluminum extrusions, with automatic infeed of 10+ stock lengths and automatic sorting on the outfeed.

sources.system: LiSEC RHF-A25/25 frame setting robot (fully automated frame assembly)
sources.title: Last step frame application: Fully automated IG production

sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling a metal frame to glass. It shows commercial robots gripping, squaring and placing metal window-frame members to tight tolerance on glass in a fixtured, fenced cell — the same class of objects and precision as fabricating/glazing a metal sash.

sources.system: Raise Robotics façade fastener/bracket robot (2x Universal Robots UR20 on mobile base)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: anchor/bracket installation for glass façades on jobsites. Establishes the scope of demonstrated field automation (fastening only) and therefore the limits of E3 capability for erecting metal framing.

tasks.label: Operate cranes or hoists with suction cups to lift large, heavy pieces of glass.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial exterior glazing on an active construction site: rigging a 200-500 kg insulated curtain-wall or storefront lite to a crane or mobile vacuum lifter, hoisting it to the opening, and setting it into the frame amid scaffolding, wind, uneven ground and other trades.

Interior commercial fit-out/renovation: using a hoist or tracked glazing lifter with suction cups to move and set large glass partitions, storefront lites or oversized mirrors inside a building under construction, through door openings, over finished floors and around obstructions.

Glass shop, warehouse or truck yard: using an overhead bridge crane, gantry or powered vacuum lifter with suction cups to pull jumbo lites from A-frame racks, feed cutting/fabrication tables, restack, and load/unload delivery racks.

Residential and light-commercial replacement: setting a large picture window, patio door or oversized shower/mirror glass at a home using a small crane truck, spider crane or glazing robot, with tight access, landscaping and varying openings.
Overhead work: craning glass to a roof or atrium and setting skylight, canopy or sloped-glazing units into framing, often with a boom crane and remote-controlled vacuum lifting frame at height.

sources.system: LiSEC RHV-A robot handling system (ABB/KUKA/Fanuc robot with vacuum suction clamp)
sources.date: 2026-07 (product page; technology in commercial use since ~2019)
sources.title: Vertical loading & unloading of glass planes - LiSEC RHV-A
sources.claim: LiSEC's RHV-A robot handling system uses a vacuum suction clamp on an industrial robot to load/unload glass sheets between glass racks/blocks and insulating-glass lines fully automatically, handling panes up to 480 kg.
sources.transferJustification: Same core act as the task: gripping large heavy architectural glass with vacuum cups and lifting it from/to racks. The lifting device is a fixed robot in a fenced plant cell rather than a crane, but the objects (up to 480 kg lites) and the pick-and-set precision match.

sources.system: HEGLA PBK automatic gantry loading system
sources.date: 2026-07 (product page; product line long in commercial use)
sources.title: Gantry loading system | Mechanical engineering - HEGLA GmbH & Co. KG
sources.claim: HEGLA's PBK gantry loading system is a crane-rail-mounted gantry with a self-activating suction-cup frame that automatically pulls jumbo raw glass sheets from A/L racks and compact storage and feeds cutting lines.
sources.transferJustification: This is the crane/hoist-with-suction-cups act itself, automated: a gantry running on crane rails with a suction-cup frame lifts jumbo (large, heavy) glass off storage racks and deposits it without an operator driving the lift.

sources.system: TECAUMA robotic glazing cell on assembled window (robot with vacuum gripper + 3D vision)
sources.date: 2026-07 (product page; cells sold to window manufacturers)
sources.title: Robotic Glazing cell on assembled window | Tecauma
sources.claim: TECAUMA's robotic glazing cell takes glass lites from trolleys or racks with a vacuum gripper and, guided by 3D vision, sets each pane automatically into an assembled window or sash; glazing weight up to 150 kg, frames up to 3000 x 2500 mm.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory glazing rather than field glazing. It covers the same end-to-end act - vacuum-lift a glass lite off a rack and seat it in its frame to tolerance - establishing the lift-and-set can be done autonomously when the frame is fixtured and presented.

sources.title: Anatomy of a Glazing Robot | Hird
sources.claim: Field 'glazing robots' used by glaziers (Winlet class machines) are operator-driven vacuum lifters: the machine is steered and its boom and vacuum actuated by a person via joysticks or a wired remote pad; no autonomous site glazing is offered.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task, on site: documents that the state of practice for jobsite glass lifting with suction cups is continuous human control, so it cannot support a positive E2/E3 judgment.

sources.system: Curtain wall installation robotic arm (research prototype)
sources.title: Dynamic Parameter Identification of a Curtain Wall Installation Robotic Arm
sources.claim: A 2025 research prototype robotic arm for glass curtain-wall installation is limited to 40 kg panels up to 1 m x 1 m and is remotely operated, indicating on-site curtain-wall glass placement is not autonomous at building-glass scale.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task in the site environment; shows the best current site-oriented glass-handling arm is teleoperated and far below the panel weights glaziers crane into place.

tasks.label: Set glass doors into frames and bolt metal hinges, handles, locks, or other hardware to attach doors to frames and walls.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial storefront entrance: glazier sets a heavy aluminum-framed or all-glass (herculite) swing door into storefront framing at an active new-build or renovation jobsite, fits top/bottom patch fittings and pivots, bolts closer, push/pull handles and locks, then adjusts swing, gaps and latch engagement. Dust, uneven floors, other trades present.

Interior commercial fit-out: frameless tempered glass office/partition door hung on patch hinges or pivots in a glass wall system; handle, lock and floor closer bolted through pre-drilled glass and into finished floor/header, in a tenant space under construction with variable framing tolerances.

Residential shower/tub enclosure: glazier carries a tempered glass door into an occupied home bathroom, anchors hinge plates into tile/stud wall, hangs the glass panel on the hinges, fits the handle, seals and adjusts so the door closes plumb without leaking. Tight space, out-of-square walls, homeowner property to protect.

Service call in an occupied facility: re-hang a sagging or damaged glass entry door and replace hardware (pivot, floor closer, lock cylinder, handle) at a retail store, restaurant or office lobby during or just after business hours, working around the public and existing finished construction.

Display and cooler doors: set glass doors into display cases, showcases or walk-in cooler/freezer openings in a supermarket, retail store or museum, bolting hinges, handles and locks to case frames and walls.

sources.system: Risong Technology flexible intelligent door/hood/lid assembly line (Changan Mazda)
sources.title: Flexible Intelligent Door Assembly Line of Changan Mazda Automobile Co., Ltd. — IFR case study
sources.claim: Risong Technology's flexible intelligent door/hood/lid assembly line at Changan Mazda automatically hangs all four vehicle doors onto the body: robots grab doors from the overhead conveyor, use laser/binocular vision guidance and gap measurement to align them to the frame, and torque the hinge bolts under monitoring, in mass production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive door hanging. Same physical operation as the glazier task performed in a fixtured cell — a heavy glazed door leaf is aligned to a frame within millimetre tolerances by vision, hinge hardware is bolted with torque control, and fit is verified by gap measurement before acceptance.

sources.system: TECAUMA robotic glazing cell on assembled window (Fanuc robot, 3D vision)

sources.claim: TECAUMA's robotic glazing cell uses a Fanuc arm with a vacuum gripper and 3D vision to unstack glass panes from trolleys and set each pane automatically into the sash of an assembled window in a factory cell, compensating for mating clearance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory glazing of window/door sashes. Same objects (large glass lites) and same operation (seating glass into a frame to a fit tolerance) with the frame fixtured — exactly how the glazier instance would arrive in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Stürtz SHA Sash Hardware Assembly system

sources.transferJustification: Related task: fitting locks, handles and hinge hardware to fenestration units in a factory. Same hardware classes and fasteners as the glazier's bolt-on hinges, handles and locks, performed on a fixtured frame with drilling and screwdriving under machine control.

sources.system: Winlet glazing robots / SmartLift / MAVLift vacuum glass lifters
sources.title: Winlet Glazing Robots for Glass & Windows | GMV
sources.claim: The 'glazing robots' actually used on glazing jobsites (Winlet, SmartLift, MAVLift) are self-propelled vacuum lifters driven by an operator via cable or radio remote control; they carry and position the glass but every motion is commanded by a human.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the glazier task's on-site lifting step; cited to show that the only jobsite 'glazing robots' in commercial use are continuously human-operated, so they cannot support an autonomous judgment at E2/E3.

sources.system: Raise Robotics facade bracket/fastener installation robot
sources.developer: Raise Robotics (with Universal Robots, Harmon, TSI Corp.)
sources.title: TSI Corp. Partners with Robotics Firm to Install Curtainwall Brackets — USGlass
sources.claim: The most advanced field-deployed facade robot, Raise Robotics' UR-cobot platform, installs curtainwall anchor brackets and fasteners on high-rise slab edges semi-autonomously with a worker managing it at each installation location; it does not hang doors or fit door hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Adjacent glazing-trade jobsite task (bracket/fastener installation for curtain wall). Cited as the ceiling of current jobsite capability: fastener placement at a human-positioned station, far short of setting a door leaf into a frame and hanging its hardware.

tasks.label: Cut, fit, install, repair, or replace glass or glass substitutes, such as plastic or aluminum, in building interiors or exteriors or in furniture or other products.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial exterior glazing on an active construction site: setting unitized curtain wall panels or storefront lites into aluminum framing on a new mid- or high-rise, working from swing stages, lifts or a crane with vacuum lifters, shimming, anchoring, gasketing and wet-sealing to line and level amid other trades, weather and changing site layout.

Residential glass replacement at a private home: measure the opening, remove failed/broken IG unit, sash or pane, order or cut replacement glass, set it in the frame with tape/sealant, refit glazing beads or putty, clean up, in an occupied house with furniture, landscaping and ladder access.

Interior glass work in homes and commercial buildings: mirrors on walls, frameless shower enclosures in tiled alcoves, glass office partitions, shelving, tabletops and display-case glass — measuring out-of-square openings, drilling/anchoring hardware, setting fragile lites by hand in finished spaces.

Shop/plant work at the glazier's own facility: cutting float glass, laminated glass, acrylic or polycarbonate to size on a cutting table, seaming edges, and fitting the cut lite into a sash, frame, IG unit, screen or furniture piece before delivery.

Emergency repair/replacement in an occupied institutional or retail building: broken storefront lite or school/office window — clearing shards and old glazing compound from the frame, temporary board-up, then cutting and fitting a replacement pane and sealing, with the public or occupants nearby.

sources.system: TECAUMA robotic glazing cell on opening sash
sources.title: Robotic glazing cell on opening sash | Tecauma
sources.claim: TECAUMA sells a robotic glazing cell in which a 6-axis robot with a vacuum gripper automatically de-stacks glass from trolleys/racks and sets each lite into the matching window sash that has been clamped on the conveyor — i.e., automated fitting of glass into a frame inside a fenced industrial cell.

sources.system: TECAUMA robotic glazing cell on assembled window
sources.title: Robotic window glazing cell by TECAUMA - DirectIndustry
sources.claim: A variant TECAUMA cell adds 3D vision to locate an already-assembled window and automatically place the glass into it, with a stated cycle of 45–60 seconds per frame.

sources.claim: LiSEC supplies robot handling stations that load and unload flat glass and finished insulating-glass units to and from processing lines fully automatically in glass fabrication plants.

sources.claim: Erdman Automation's automated glazers apply the bedding sealant bead to sash/frame rabbets automatically at production speed, and its robotic arms handle large IG units on the glass line at a US window plant (Viwinco).

sources.claim: The EU Hephaestus cable-driven parallel robot autonomously installed curtain wall modules and brackets on two close-to-real demonstration buildings, with measured installation accuracy of 4–23 mm and about half an hour per module; it remained a project prototype rather than a commercial product.

sources.system: Hyundai E&C curtain wall installation robot
sources.title: AI Robots Enter Construction Sites to Haul Materials, Build - Seoul Economic Daily
sources.claim: Hyundai E&C reports using a curtain wall installation robot at its high-rise sites to place glass panels on exterior walls, but the reporting gives no evidence of autonomous operation (the same articles describe it alongside operator-directed lifting and transport machines), so it is treated as operator-controlled.

sources.title: Shimizu Deploys Robot for Installing Raised Floor Named "Robo-Buddy Floor"
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy Floor autonomously installed raised-floor panels on an active high-rise construction site, matching craftsmen in speed and placing panels within 1 mm — showing autonomous panel placement, but on rigid access-floor panels dropped onto pedestals, not fragile glass lites set into gasketed/sealed frames.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous placement of building panels on a live construction site. Transfer to glazing is not accepted here — floor panels are rigid, self-locating on pedestals and tolerant of handling, whereas glass lites are fragile, must be bedded on tape/sealant and captured by gaskets or beads, which no cited site robot does.

sources.title: A Guide to Robotic Unitized Curtain Wall Installation - Raise Robotics
sources.claim: Raise Robotics' facade robot works on active high-rise sites doing curtain wall layout marking autonomously to 1/16-inch precision, but its demonstrated on-site scope is layout/anchor preparation, not setting or glazing the glass panels.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic curtain wall layout on an active jobsite. Cited only to show what is actually autonomous in the field today (marking, not glazing); it does not substantiate autonomous glass installation at E3.

tasks.label: Drive trucks to installation sites and unload mirrors, glass equipment, or tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service call: glazier drives a pickup or van with an exterior glass rack over public streets to a private house, parks in a driveway or at the curb, and unloads a few window lites (2x3 ft to 4x6 ft), a mirror, a toolbox, caulk gun, ladder and sawhorses, carrying glass by hand with suction cups across lawn, steps and gravel to the work opening.

Commercial storefront/office replacement: box truck with a glass rack driven downtown, parked curbside with cones in traffic, unloading large lites (roughly 6x10 ft, 200-400 lb) using the rack's hoist or two-worker manual suction cups onto a glass cart, then wheeling glass and tools over the sidewalk and through the lobby door.

New-construction / curtain-wall job: flatbed or trailer of crated glass and glazing hardware driven onto an active construction site with mud, ruts and other trades present; crates and A-frames offloaded with a telehandler, forklift or crane and staged per site logistics on uneven ground.

Institutional interior job (hospital, school, office tower): drive to the facility, back into a loading dock, unload mirrors, interior glass, glazing tools and sealant onto carts, and move them through corridors and elevators to the work area.

Emergency call-out / board-up: drive at night or in bad weather to a storm- or break-in-damaged storefront or home, park on a debris-strewn street, unload plywood sheets, temporary glass, hand tools and a generator, often with limited lighting and no site preparation.

sources.system: LiSEC robot handling (RHV-A) glass loading/unloading robot
sources.title: Robotics in the glass industry | LiSEC | glassonweb.com
sources.claim: Commercial industrial robots with vacuum grippers load and unload flat glass panes between glass racks (A-frames) and vertical production lines fully automatically in glass fabrication plants, handling panes up to 480 kg.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unloading glass panes from transport/storage racks in a fixtured plant cell. It involves the same objects (large fragile glass lites, hundreds of kg) and the same handling means (vacuum suction) as unloading a glazier's truck rack, but with the rack presented in a known position, i.e. an E1 presentation of the work.

sources.system: BBKS glass loading and unloading robot

sources.transferJustification: Related task: de-stacking glass sheets from racks. Same fragile large-format workpieces and vacuum handling as unloading glass from a truck rack, performed in a purpose-built line where the rack position is known.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: unloading a loaded vehicle body of mixed cases (tools, boxed hardware, sealant) at a dock. Objects and reach are comparable to unloading a glazier's boxed tools and supplies, but it happens at a fixed dock inside a warehouse, not at a job site.

sources.title: How Fox Robotics went from scrappy startup to making self-driving forklifts for Walmart
sources.claim: Fox Robotics' FoxBot autonomous forklifts unload trailers at Walmart distribution centers, picking and moving pallets in and out of trailers without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: forklift offloading of palletized/crated freight from a trailer, analogous to offloading crated glass. It is demonstrated only at prepared warehouse docks with flat floors and known trailer positions, not on job sites.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: the driving leg of the instance. It shows autonomous highway hub-to-hub driving exists, but it is fixed-lane freight between terminals with human cargo handling, so it does not cover curbside parking at arbitrary job sites or any unloading.

sources.title: Glazing contractors overcome skills shortages with Winlets | Hird
sources.claim: Glazing 'robots' actually used on job sites to move and place glass (e.g. Winlet 575, lifting 575 kg) are vacuum lifters driven continuously by an operator with a wired remote control.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant machine class for moving glass at installation sites; recorded to show the on-site glass-handling machines are operator-driven, so they cannot support a positive autonomous judgment at E3.

tasks.label: Load and arrange glass or mirrors onto delivery trucks, using suction cups or cranes to lift glass.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Glass shop / fabrication shop loading dock or yard: the glazier pulls finished cut lites and insulating glass units of mixed sizes from interior harp/A-racks, carries them with hand suction cups (often two-person), sets them on the exterior A-frame racks of a flatbed glass truck with rubber/wood separators, sequences them by delivery stop, and straps the load down.

Fabrication plant or warehouse: oversized, heavy architectural lites (spandrel, laminated, jumbo IGUs) or crated units are loaded onto interior truck racks / shipping stillages using an overhead crane, boom truck, or powered vacuum lifter, with the glazier guiding placement and blocking the units.

Mirrors, shower enclosures, tabletops and small custom-shape pieces are padded, separated with cardboard/foam and blankets, and arranged into the interior padded racks of a van or box truck; many small pieces of varying shape and ... per load.

Job-site pickup/return: at a house, storefront, or high-rise site, the glazier loads removed sashes and old glass, broken/scrap glass, and unused leftover stock back onto the truck's racks over uneven ground, curbs and tight access.

Distribution yard/warehouse: bulk stock sheets and uncut lites are pulled from storage A/L racks and loaded onto a flatbed or side-loader glass truck using forklift-mounted or gantry vacuum lifting equipment, then secured for over-the-road transport.

tasks.label: Measure mirrors and dimensions of areas to be covered to determine work procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential in-home field measure: glazier visits an occupied house for a shower enclosure, wall mirror, tabletop or broken-pane replacement. Measures the tiled alcove width at three heights and height at both jambs, checks plumb/level/square of finished walls and curb slope with a level, gauges existing glass thickness, notes obstructions (faucets, tile lip, outlets, trim), then sets cut sizes with deductions and decides hardware and install sequence. Tolerance about 1/16 in; cluttered, furnished, unstandardized rooms.

Occupied commercial/institutional building interior: measuring for glass office partitions, gym/lobby mirrors, interior storefront glass or a broken tempered lite. Works inside a facility controlled by an owner or property manager, measures daylight opening and frame glazing-channel depth, verifies squareness and existing frame condition, and determines glass type, sizes and installation method around business hours.

Active construction or renovation jobsite: field-measuring rough openings, installed storefront/curtain-wall frames and skylight curbs against shop drawings before glass is ordered; verifying anchor and slab-edge conditions and out-of-plumb frames, then recording panel sizes and the glazing procedure. Dust, debris, temporary lighting, other trades present.

Glass shop / fabrication: measuring mirror and glass stock and finished panels on the shop cutting table — marking cut sizes from the order, checking a cut panel's length, width, squareness, cut-outs and hole positions against the cut list before edging and delivery.

Exterior ground-level measure from a sidewalk, parking lot or short ladder: storefront entrances, low-rise window openings and facade panels for replacement — recording opening sizes, frame pocket depth and access constraints (traffic, pedestrians, weather) to plan the installation.

It performs the measuring step of this task — acquiring millimetre-class dimensions of openings, frames and wall areas that the glazier records with tape and laser — over the same building geometry, and the point cloud is tied to a project coordinate system so dimensions can be extracted.

sources.system: Leica BLK ARC on Boston Dynamics Spot
sources.developer: Leica Geosystems (Hexagon) / Boston Dynamics, user: Turner Construction
sources.title: Automation in Construction - BLK Autonomy | Leica Geosystems
sources.claim: Turner Construction bought a Leica BLK ARC for Spot and uses it routinely and autonomously on jobsites to capture as-built conditions, which its VDC teams check against the coordinated BIM model.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous as-built verification on active jobsites. It measures installed frames, openings and surfaces against design dimensions — the same dimensional check a glazier makes before ordering glass — in the same unstructured construction environment.

sources.title: Turner Launches Pilot Program to Field Test an Advanced Mobility Robot: Spot
sources.claim: Turner deployed Spot on the 550 Washington Street project in New York City to automate site laser scanning and progress ... and to update as-built BIM models.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: jobsite laser scanning for QA/QC and as-built models, which is the dimension-capture element of a glazier's field measure, performed in the same active construction environment.

sources.system: Leica BLK ARC on Spot (facility reality capture)
sources.title: How autonomous technology is transforming reality capture | Hexagon
sources.claim: A BLK ARC mounted on Spot navigates an electrical substation that remains operational and scans the entire site within hours, producing dense static and dynamic point clouds — autonomous dimensional capture inside a working, institution-controlled facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous reality capture in an operating facility. It shows the same measuring capability being executed in occupied, institution-controlled premises (indoor and outdoor), the environment class of a glazier's commercial field measure.

sources.title: Spot - The Agile Mobile Robot | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot is a mature commercial platform with over 1,500 robots in ... running autonomous inspection missions in factories, foundries and other ....
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the carrier used for autonomous scanning is routinely deployed and navigates structured human work facilities without continuous teleoperation.

sources.title: Automatic dimension control with our LineScanner - Glass-iq.com
sources.claim: The LineScanner performs automatic inline dimensional control of flat glass panels on the production line, checking external and internal contours, edge cut-outs and drill hole positions and diameters against tolerances.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated measurement of flat glass and mirror panels. Identical objects and tighter tolerances than a glazier's shop measure of a mirror or cut lite, with the outcome (accept, re-cut, or route the piece onward) driving the downstream work procedure — but it requires the glass fed on a fixtured conveyor line.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Okibo's fully autonomous, AI-guided plastering/drywall-finishing robot uses onboard 3D scanning (2-3 mm accuracy) to model interior walls and ceilings and plan its coverage, and is active on major construction sites having covered over 1 million sq ft in Europe before its 2025 US launch.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the robot autonomously 3D-scans the wall and ceiling areas to be covered and derives its own work plan from those measurements — structurally the same 'measure the area to be covered to determine work procedures' step, in interior construction sites, though at coating tolerance rather than glass-cut tolerance.

sources.title: Automated Layout for Mechanical | Dusty Robotics
sources.claim: Dusty Robotics' FieldPrinter autonomously performs measure-and-mark layout on jobsite floors directly from the coordinated BIM model at 1/16-inch accuracy, and is used in production by contractors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic dimensional measure-and-mark on active construction floors at the same 1/16-inch tolerance a glazier works to, showing that mobile robots hold trade-grade dimensional accuracy in unstructured jobsite conditions.

tasks.label: Cut and attach mounting strips, metal or wood moldings, rubber gaskets, or metal clips to surfaces in preparation for mirror installation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential mirror install prep in a private home (bathroom vanity, closet door, home gym): snap a level line on drywall/tile, cut aluminum J-channel or mounting strips to length with a hacksaw, drill and set anchors, screw bottom channel and top mirror clips, sometimes cut and nail wood molding. Finished-surface cosmetic quality, varied wall construction, tight rooms, existing fixtures.

Commercial mirror wall prep on an active interior jobsite (gym/dance studio, school restroom, retail): long runs of J-channel and continuous mounting strips cut to length and fastened into studs/blocking, top clips laid out to a datum line, work amid other trades, debris, and changing conditions.

Retrofit/replacement in an occupied, institution-controlled facility (hotel, hospital, school, office, store) during off-hours: strip old clips/moldings, patch and re-anchor new metal clips or wood/metal moldings on finished walls, cut trim to fit existing openings.

Shop prep at the glass/mirror fabrication shop: cut wood or metal moldings and mounting strips to size, fasten Z-clips/French cleats/backing strips to mirror backs or frames, apply mounting tape/mastic strips, before delivery to the site.

Mirrored panels in casework, display cases, and millwork: cut and fit rubber gaskets, setting blocks and glazing beads/metal clips into the case opening or frame so the mirror can be glazed in, done in the shop or at a fixture-install site.

sources.system: WEINMANN WALLTEQ M-300 / M-500 multifunction bridge
sources.title: Multifunction Bridge WALLTEQ M-300 insuFill /M-500
sources.claim: WEINMANN/HOMAG WALLTEQ multifunction bridges automatically saw, trim, mark, screw, clip, staple and nail strips and sheathing onto fixtured wall elements in a panel factory gantry cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting and fastening battens, strips and trim onto a fixtured wall element. Same operations as cutting mounting strips/moldings to length and screwing/nailing them to a surface, at millimetre placement accuracy, when the surface is brought to the machine.

sources.title: System solution for sealing with high process reliability
sources.claim: Sonderhoff FIPFG dosing cells use 6-axis robots to precisely apply a formed-in-place elastomeric gasket along the contour of a fixtured component before the mating cover/panel is assembled.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying a resilient gasket to a surface in preparation for a panel/cover being set. Comparable to laying rubber gasket material on a frame or opening before a mirror or glass light is glazed in; contour-following precision is comparable.

sources.system: Automotive trim panel clip insertion systems (e.g., VIM clip inserter spindles on UR/industrial robots)
sources.developer: assembly-equipment suppliers integrated with Universal Robots and industrial robot OEMs
sources.title: Automotive Trim Panel Clip Insertion Gear | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Automated clip-insertion end effectors on industrial and collaborative robots feed and install metal or ... into parts at defined positions with verification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastening metal clips onto a fixtured surface at programmed locations, which is the clip-attachment half of this task when the surface is presented to the machine.

sources.title: Automotive Windshield Glass Assembly - Arnold Machine
sources.claim: Robotic glass assembly cells locate and install brackets on glass and apply primer and urethane beads before the glass is set, using 3D vision to find the exact bracket location.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: attaching brackets/clips and adhesive-gasket material to a glass light in preparation for its installation. Same class of objects (glass, metal brackets, sealant) and tighter precision than mirror clip work.

sources.title: Glass Sealing Extruders and Robots - Forel
sources.claim: Insulating-glass production lines use automatic sealing robots that extrude and precisely apply the sealant/gasket material along glass unit edges.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying gasket/sealant strip material to glass units in a purpose-built line, comparable to bedding rubber gaskets on frames or glass edges before a mirror/glass unit is fixed.

sources.system: RoboTape / SD-610 robot-mounted tape applicators for 3M double-sided tape
sources.title: A Tight Bond: Automated Industrial Tape Dispensing Systems | Machine Design
sources.claim: Robot- and cobot-mounted applicators automatically apply double-sided mounting tape strips to parts in production cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting and applying adhesive mounting strips/tape to a surface, which is one of the listed mounting methods in this task, when the surface is fixtured in a cell.

sources.title: Automated Crosscut Saw System for Metals | Woodworking Network
sources.claim: Fully automated cross-cut saw systems cut metal and wood molding stock to programmed lengths with an automatic pusher and length optimization.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting aluminum J-channel/metal moldings and wood moldings to length, the 'cut' half of this task, performed automatically when stock is fed to the machine.

sources.system: Raise Robotics platform (Universal Robots arms on mobile base)
sources.developer: Raise Robotics (with Harmon Inc., TSI Corp.)
sources.title: Raise Robotics deploys UR cobots with Harmon for high rise fastener installation - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Raise Robotics' mobile robot with cobot arms performs layout, drilling and installation of fasteners and brackets for glass facade panels on active high-rise construction sites, supervised by one worker per location.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: anchoring metal brackets/clips to building structure in preparation for glass panel installation. It shows on-site anchoring of pre-made brackets into concrete slab edges, but not cutting strips/moldings to length or fastening finish trim on interior drywall/tile walls.

tasks.label: Pack spaces between moldings and glass with glazing compounds and trim excess material with glazing knives.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial storefront / curtain-wall wet glazing on an active jobsite: after the lite is set in the aluminum frame and the removable stop (molding) is installed, the glazier guns glazing sealant/compound into the space between glass and stop, tools it flush, and knifes off excess from glass and metal. Work at grade or from ladders/lifts, weather and dust exposure, frames of varying size and orientation.

Residential service call at a private home: replace a broken pane in a wood or metal sash, bed the glass, pack glazing compound between the glass and the wood molding/rabbet or metal stop, strike the bevel and trim excess with a glazing knife, clean the glass. Ladder work, occupied dwelling, one-off sash sizes, old paint and putty conditions.

Bench glazing in the glass company's own shop: sashes, doors, transoms and frames brought in are clamped on a bench, glass is bedded, compound is packed between glass and the stops/moldings, and excess is knifed off before the unit is shipped back out. Mixed sizes, one-off jobs, shop-controlled lighting and layout.

Interior finish glazing in a finished/occupied institutional or commercial building: display cases, interior partitions, borrowed lights, cooler/freezer doors and mirrors - sealing the joint between glass and retaining moldings with compound and cleaning excess with a knife. Building operated and kept to a standard by its owner; furniture and occupants present.

Historic/restoration or irregular glazing: linseed-oil knife-grade putty on old wood sash, arched, curved or leaded panes, matching the existing beveled putty line and back-puttying, often on site in variable weather with deteriorated substrates.

sources.system: Forel SR NL Automatic Sealing Robot for Insulating Glass
sources.title: AUTOMATIC SEALING ROBOT FOR INSULATING GLASS - NO LIMITS - Forel
sources.claim: Forel's SR NL automatic sealing robot fills the perimeter cavity of insulating glass units with sealant on a factory line, using a depth-reading sensor and variable-depth nozzle so the compound is packed to the correct depth and finished flush with the glass edges, on units up to 9 m.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: secondary sealing of IG units. The machine packs a viscous sealing compound into a narrow channel bounded by glass and a spacer, senses the actual cavity depth, and strikes the material level with the glass edges - the same operation (fill the space at the glass edge, leave no excess on the glass) a glazier performs between molding and glass with a knife, on comparable materials and millimetre tolerances.

sources.system: LiSEC VL-1N fully automatic sealing system
sources.title: Fully automatic sealing system for insulating glass - LiSEC.com
sources.claim: LiSEC's VL-1N is a fully automatic sealing system for insulating glass that measures the frame inset during sealing, applies the sealing compound with a rotating application head, and performs corner correction on the finished bead.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: filling and finishing the compound-filled edge channel of a glass unit. Sensing the inset of the frame and correcting material at the corners is the machine equivalent of packing compound tight against the molding and dressing the joint, corners included, with a glazing knife.

sources.title: Sealing robots Archivi - Marval
sources.claim: Marval's ROBO SEAL automatic robotic sealing machine applies the final perimeter seal to assembled insulating glass panels in production, including corner sealing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: perimeter compound packing of glass units in a fixtured factory station; a second independent vendor supplying the same glass-edge compound-filling-and-finishing operation as production equipment.

sources.system: LiSEC automated IG line (BSV frame bender, LBH butyl applicator, VFL sealing robot) at Ardic Cam
sources.title: Precision at Scale: Ardic Cam's Supersized Lami IG Units Enabled by LiSEC | glassonweb.com
sources.claim: A commercial glass fabricator (Ardic Cam) runs a fully automated LiSEC insulating glass line in its plant that includes a butyl applicator and a sealing robot, evidencing real production deployment rather than a demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory application of glazing/sealing compound to glass units. Establishes that the sealing robots cited above run in ordinary glass plants, not only at trade fairs.

sources.system: Erdman 3000/5000 Series Automated Glazer (back bedder) with Glass Lay-in and Bead Roll / Wood Bead Nailer
sources.title: Automated Glazers - Erdman Automation
sources.claim: Erdman Automation supplies automated glazers/back bedders for window and door factories that automatically apply a metered, consistent bead of glazing sealant into the sash rabbet, alongside glass lay-in, bead roll and wood bead (molding) nailing stations on the same line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory glazing of sashes. The joint filled is exactly the glass-to-sash/molding joint of this task; volumetric metering places the compound where the glazier would pack it and leaves no excess to knife off, and the same line installs the retaining moldings.

sources.system: Broetje Automation robotic sealing / fillet sealing systems
sources.title: Sealing - Broetje Automation
sources.claim: Broetje Automation supplies robotic sealing systems for aircraft structure, including fillet sealing on straight and curved parts, with the bead applied and shaped by industrial robots or cobots under continuous process monitoring; the technology is described as industrially mature.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic fillet sealing of aerospace joints. It shows robots laying and shaping a sealant fillet into a bounded joint on curved, complex geometry to an inspected finish - the shaping/dressing step analogous to striking and trimming glazing compound.

tasks.label: Assemble, erect, or dismantle scaffolds, rigging, or hoisting equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interior/renovation work: erect a rolling tower or sectional frame scaffold (frames, cross-braces, planks, outriggers, guardrails, casters/screw jacks) inside a building under construction or being remodeled, on uneven or obstructed floors, to reach interior glass, mirrors and storefront transoms; reposition it repeatedly, then dismantle and haul it out.

Exterior low-rise storefront/window job: set mudsills and screw jacks on uneven ground or a sidewalk, erect a frame/system scaffold or ladder-jack/pump-jack staging against the building, level and plumb it, plank it, add guardrails and ties, then dismantle and load onto the truck after glazing.

Rig a large glass unit for a lift on a jobsite: select and attach a vacuum lifting frame or glass clamps/slings/shackles and a spreader bar to a heavy IGU or curtain-wall panel, connect it to a crane, boom lift or glazing hoist hook, attach tag lines, verify the load, then release and de-rig after the panel is set.

Set up hoisting equipment on site: mount and reeve a chain hoist/come-along, gin pole, davit or parapet-mounted glazing hoist; or deploy a tracked glazing machine (Smartlift/Winlet type) with outriggers, boom and cup head, connect power/vacuum and function-check it; break it all down afterward.

Mid-rise curtain-wall job: rig suspended access — outrigger beams, counterweights, tiebacks, wire ropes and traction hoists for a two-point swing stage on the roof/parapet — function-test it, and dismantle it at completion.

Glass shop/warehouse: assemble or adjust the overhead hoist/jib crane rigging with a vacuum lifter and set up A-frame racks to move lites from storage to the cutting/fabrication table; break the rigging down and re-hang a different lifter when panel size changes.

sources.title: Vertical loading & unloading of glass planes - LiSEC.com
sources.claim: LiSEC RHV-A is a commercial robot cell (ABB, KUKA or Fanuc arm) whose vacuum suction clamp automatically activates the required suction cups from part data and lifts glass sheets up to 480 kg out of racks onto/off a production line, fully automatically inside a fenced glass-plant cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: attaching a vacuum lifting device to a large glass unit and hoisting/releasing it. That is the rigging-a-glass-panel instance with the work presented in racks in a purpose-built cell — comparable objects (heavy architectural lites up to 480 kg), comparable load-security and placement precision, machine-controlled engagement and release of the lifting attachment.

sources.system: CMS automatic robotic cells for glass loading and unloading
sources.title: Automatic Robotic Cells for Glass Loading and Unloading | CMS
sources.claim: CMS automatic robotic cells load and unload glass sheets with NC control of each individual suction cup, explicitly to remove operator intervention, in factory glass-handling cells.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the LiSEC item — machine-controlled attachment of a vacuum lifting head to glass and hoisting it — corroborating that glass rigging and hoisting is automated in purpose-built cells, and only there.

sources.title: KEWAZO raises funding to accelerate LIFTBOT deployment in heavy industry - The Robot Report
sources.claim: KEWAZO's LIFTBOT, the only fielded scaffolding robot, is a rail-mounted lifting robot deployed at 20+ industrial sites that moves scaffold tubes and boards vertically; the scaffold itself is still assembled by the crew and the robot's rail is installed by workers as the scaffold grows.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related to scaffold erection: the leading scaffolding robot automates only vertical material transport, not the assembly, levelling, bracing or dismantling of the scaffold.

sources.title: KEWAZO at AFPM NSC26 in San Antonio, May 2026
sources.claim: KEWAZO's own account of a 30 m chimney scaffold built with LIFTBOT still describes a crew on the structure doing the building, with the robot removing manual carrying of tubes and boards.
sources.transferJustification: Direct evidence on the scaffold erection/dismantling instances: even the best-automated scaffold builds retain human scaffolders assembling the structure.

sources.title: Glazing Robots | GGR Group
sources.claim: The on-site 'glazing robots' sold to glaziers are operator-driven vacuum lifting machines that a person sets up and controls; they are lift assists, not autonomous systems.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the hoisting-equipment instance: the lifting machines glaziers deploy on site are manually or remotely controlled, so their existence does not substantiate autonomous set-up, rigging or breakdown of hoisting equipment.

sources.title: Robots could climb and assemble structures, make construction sites safer | Cornell Chronicle
sources.claim: A Cornell lab prototype autonomously climbed, assembled and disassembled a truss structure, but only with purpose-designed truss members, gears and joints, as a small research demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Closest research analogue to scaffold erection, but it needs a bespoke truss system rather than standard scaffold frames and wedge-lock/coupler connections, is a small lab prototype, and produces no planked, guardrailed, load-rated work platform, so it does not transfer at worker quality even in a purpose-built setting.

tasks.label: Cut and remove broken glass prior to installing replacement glass.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied private home: broken single pane or failed/cracked IGU in a wood, vinyl or aluminum sash (window, patio door, side-light). Glazier masks/protects the room, pries out glazing stops or chisels/heat-guns out hardened putty and glazier points, scores and snaps remaining shards free of the rabbet, extracts jagged pieces by hand, vacuums the channel clean and bags the cullet before reglazing. Variable frame types, paint layers, furniture and pets nearby, sometimes weather-exposed.

Commercial storefront after a break-in, vehicle strike or vandalism: 1/4" plate or tempered lite shattered in an aluminum storefront frame. Glazier works from the public sidewalk/parking lot, breaks out and cuts free glass still hanging in the frame, strips vinyl glazing gasket or tape and setting blocks, rakes tempered pebbles out of the glazing pocket, sweeps and disposes of shards, often after an emergency board-up, amid pedestrians and traffic.

Interior glass inside an institutional or commercial building (office partition, school or hospital door lite, retail display case, mirror, shower enclosure): remove trim/stops or clips, cut and lift out cracked or shattered glass, protect finished floors and merchandise, vacuum shards from the frame and floor, dispose safely, while the facility stays occupied.

Curtain wall, skylight or upper-floor unit on an occupied or under-construction building: work from a swing stage, boom lift or roof; cut structural silicone/sealant, remove pressure plates and gaskets, break out or vacuum-lift the damaged lite, clear all shards from the glazing pocket with containment so glass does not fall to the street below.

Bench work in the glass shop: a sash, transom, door panel, table top or cabinet frame brought in on a truck; on a bench (sometimes in a simple jig) the glazier removes beads or putty, cuts and breaks out the remaining broken glass, cleans the rabbet of old bedding compound and points, and drops cullet into a bin before the new lite is set.

sources.system: 2ndLife robot window-restoration cell (LPS Ruhr-Universität Bochum + Kilivations)
sources.developer: Chair of Production Systems (LPS), Ruhr University Bochum, with Kilivations GmbH & Co. KG
sources.title: Robotics: Automated restoration of windows from old buildings - INDUSTRIAL Production
sources.claim: The 2ndLife research project (Ruhr University Bochum Chair of Production Systems with Kilivations) is developing an enclosed robot cell in which a clamped old wooden window sash is imaged by a robot-mounted 2D camera, contours are found by edge detection, and an industrial robot with a circular saw cuts an offset path so the (intact) glazing can subsequently be removed non-destructively; the cell runs under negative pressure with H-class extraction for asbestos-bearing putty.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated de-glazing of window sashes before new insulating glass is fitted. It is the closest published system to 'cut and remove glass prior to installing replacement glass', but it is a funded R&D project still under development, it handles intact heritage panes (cutting the wooden sash, not shards), the sash must be clamped manually outside the cell, and the actual lifting-out of the glazing is described only as a 'subsequent' step, so it does not substantiate completion of the whole task at worker quality.

sources.system: Kilivations Bearbeitungszelle für Fenster und Türen (processing cell for window and door sashes)
sources.title: Bearbeitungszelle für Fenster und Türen - Kilivations
sources.claim: Kilivations advertises a concept robot cell for restoring old windows and doors in which a ceiling-mounted robot with tool changer would locate pane and frame with a light field and camera, then mill/cut out window putty, take out glass panes, blast and sand frames and remove hardware; the published images are CAD mock-ups.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing putty and glass from a sash before new glass is installed. It is presented as a concept ('Wanna Do') illustrated with CAD renderings, with no evidence of a built, autonomously running installation, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: LiSEC ARS-TBXY / ARS-TBX float glass breakout system and glass waste disposal line
sources.title: Automatic Glass Breaking Line for Float Glass - LiSEC.com
sources.claim: LiSEC supplies commercially deployed float-glass cutting and breakout lines that automatically break trim cuts, remnants and X/Y sub-plates after scoring and convey the resulting waste glass to cullet crushers and collection stations inside a fenced, purpose-built production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cutting of glass and removal/disposal of the resulting scrap glass in a purpose-built line. Transfer fails for this task: the line handles clean, intact, flat stock delivered flat on conveyors with known geometry, whereas the glazier task requires extracting irregular shards bedded in putty, tape or silicone from a damaged frame and cleaning the rabbet — different objects, different fixturing, and no cited demonstration of it.

sources.system: GGR Oscar glazing robots / Winlet glazing robots
sources.title: Glazing Robots | GGR Group
sources.claim: Commercial 'glazing robots' used by glaziers for removing and replacing damaged glass panels on buildings (GGR Oscar range, Winlet) are operator-driven vacuum-lift manipulators: the operator drives the unit and rotates/positions the head manually; they carry no capability to cut out or clear broken glass.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-site handling of glass panels during replacement work. These machines are human-operated lifting aids, not autonomous systems, so under the autonomy rule they cannot support a positive judgment for removing broken glass.

tasks.label: Secure mirrors in position, using mastic cement, putty, bolts, or screws.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential bathroom/vanity or bedroom mirror: in an occupied or newly built house, glazier carries a 3x4 to 4x6 ft mirror in, buttons mastic cement onto the back, presses and levels it on drywall or tile over the vanity, sets bottom J-channel and top clips with screws into studs/anchors, and tapes it until the adhesive cures. Tight room, plumbing fixtures in the way, walls out of plumb.

Commercial interior fit-out: full-height mirror wall in a gym, dance studio, or locker room during construction. Multiple 4x8 ft or larger panes lifted by two workers, mastic applied in beads/buttons, bottom J-channel shimmed level, panes butted and aligned, top clips screwed to blocking. Dust, other trades working nearby, uneven substrate.

Service/replacement call in an occupied institutional or commercial building: replacing a broken or corroded mirror in a school, hospital, hotel, or office restroom, an elevator cab, or a retail fitting room. Old mirror removed, wall cleaned, new mirror set with mastic and/or clips, bolts or screws into existing anchors, work done around occupants and finished surfaces.

Shop fabrication at the glazier's glass shop: mirrors bonded and fastened into products before delivery — mirrored closet/bifold doors, framed and cabinet mirrors, mirror-backed display cases, furniture and tabletop mirrors. Mirror laid on a bench or table, mastic/adhesive applied to a backer or frame, mirror set, clips or screws driven.

Custom/decorative on-site mirror work: mirrored panels on restaurant or retail columns, ceilings and soffits, antique or heavy beveled mirrors, angled or shaped panels on out-of-plumb walls; combination of mastic cement, hidden brackets, and through-bolted rosettes, with careful fitting and one-off layout.

sources.system: Arnold Machine windshield glass assembly cell (FANUC robots) at Carlex
sources.title: Automotive Windshield Glass Assembly - Arnold Machine
sources.claim: A production automation cell at automotive glass maker Carlex uses robots to pick formed glass from racks, apply primer, dispense urethane adhesive, and place hardware onto the glass under 3D vision guidance, with parts held in fixtures; the cell handles glass edge/curvature variation without breaking it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: adhesive bonding of hardware to a glass lite in a fixtured cell. It involves the same physical operations as securing a mirror with mastic — gentle handling of a large fragile pane, dispensing an adhesive bead, vision-guided positioning, and holding until set — at equal or tighter precision.

sources.system: GEBE2 robotic gluing/bonding cells (mirror assembly stations; ELT M1 mirror segment gluing for Safran Reosc/ESO)
sources.title: Robotic gluing, sealing & bonding for industry - Glue robot system | GEBE2
sources.claim: GEBE2 builds and delivers robotic gluing cells that dispense glue, primer or mastic beads with measured bead geometry, including cells with fixed and mobile mirror assembly stations for automotive mirrors and a cell that robotically glues fittings to the 39 m ELT primary-mirror segments, using positioning tooling and clamps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic mastic/adhesive bonding of components to mirrors in fixtured cells. Same material (mastic/adhesive), same workpiece class (mirrors), and the cell also manipulates and assembles the part onto the structure, i.e. the placement step of securing a mirror.

sources.system: LiSEC RHV-A robot glass handling (vacuum suction clamp)
sources.title: Vertical loading & unloading of glass planes - LiSEC.com
sources.claim: LiSEC supplies robot handling systems with vacuum suction clamps that load and unload individual large glass sheets fully automatically between glass racks and processing lines in flat-glass factories, adapting the gripper to different product and stack sizes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated pick, transport and accurate placement of large mirror-sized glass sheets without breakage — the handling half of securing a mirror — demonstrated at production reliability in a purpose-built glass plant.

sources.system: Southwestern PTS Automated Smart Screwdriving Solution (FANUC CRX + ESTIC tools)
sources.title: Automated Smart Screwdriving Solution - FANUC CRX robot
sources.claim: Commercially integrated robotic screwdriving cells pair FANUC CRX cobots with transducerized fastening tools and automatic screw feeding to drive and torque screws to specification with traceability in fixtured assembly stations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic screw driving with controlled torque, covering the 'bolts or screws' fastening step of mirror securing (clips, J-channel, rosettes) when the work is presented fixtured in a cell.

sources.system: Raise Robotics mobile manipulator (two UR20 arms) with Harmon Inc.
sources.developer: Raise Robotics / Universal Robots / Harmon Inc.
sources.title: Raise Robotics deploys UR cobots with Harmon for high rise fastener installation - The Robot Report
sources.claim: On real high-rise construction sites, the most advanced glazing-contractor robot deployed does layout, hammer drilling and bracket/fastener installation at the slab edge with one operator per location; it does not handle, bond, or set the glass panels themselves, which remain a crane-and-crew operation.
sources.transferJustification: Boundary evidence for the same trade in unstructured/field settings: it substantiates only anchor drilling and bracket torquing, not picking a mirror, buttering it with mastic, and setting it to a wall, so it cannot substantiate the whole task at E2 or E3.

sources.title: Japanese researchers create humanoid bot that installs drywall independently | Construction Dive
sources.claim: The closest demonstration of a robot autonomously lifting a wall panel and screwing it to framing is AIST's HRP-5P humanoid, shown in a laboratory mock-up in 2018; it works slowly and has not been shown installing panels or mirrors on real job sites at production quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hoisting a large panel and fastening it with screws in a human-scale space. Cited as a laboratory demo only — the panel is rigid gypsum, no adhesive bonding of fragile glass, and speed/reliability are far below worker quality, so it does not support E2/E3.

tasks.label: Measure and mark outlines or patterns on glass to indicate cutting lines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Glass shop / fabrication bay of a glazing contractor: glazier takes a stock sheet or remnant of annealed float glass to the cutting bench, measures with rule/square/measuring bar, and marks straight score lines for rectangular replacement lites, IG blanks, or shower-door blanks; tolerance roughly 1/16 in.

instances.label: Glass shop / fabrication shop: glazier pulls a stock lite of clear annealed float (e.g. 6 mm, 96"x130") off an A-frame or harp rack, walks or lifts it onto the felt-covered cutting table, squares it against the table stop, lays out the cut lines and runs an oil-fed cutter (or brushes light cutting oil along the marked line) before scoring. Shop floor is shared with other workers, forklifts and lifters.

Small-piece bench work in the shop: mirror, tabletop, display-case, storm-window or small replacement panes. Glazier rests the small lite on the rack edge or against the bench, dips the steel-wheel or carbide cutter in oil (or uses an oil-reservoir cutter), and oils the short cut line before hand-scoring against a straightedge or pattern.

Specialty stock in the shop: laminated safety glass, low-E coated, patterned or heavy (10-19 mm) glass. Glass is set on the cutting table, cut lines oiled on both faces for laminate (or the wheel re-oiled for thick glass), coating side identified and the sheet positioned so both scores register.

Field/job-site preparation: glazier trims a lite to fit at a house, storefront or construction site. Glass is rested on the van's exterior rack edge, a portable A-frame or a padded folding table; dust, wind and uneven ground; the cutter is dipped in oil or oil wiped along the line before the field cut.

Large architectural lite in the shop: jumbo or oversize insulating/monolithic stock moved from a harp rack with a vacuum lifter or overhead crane, laid flat on a tilting cutting table, aligned to the zero corner, and the cutting head/lines oiled before scoring; two-person handling and precise placement to avoid edge damage.
