tasks.label: Measure, cut, fit, and press anti-glare adhesive film to glass or spray glass with tinting solution to prevent light glare.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retrofit solar/anti-glare film on vision glass in an occupied commercial office building: technician surveys and measures each lite, cuts film oversize from a roll on a portable table, cleans the glass, wets it with slip solution, positions the film, squeegees out water and bubbles, and razor-trims to the gasket line, working around desks, blinds and occupants from a ladder or small platform.

Residential job: anti-glare/solar film on a home's windows, sliders and skylights, including some arched or odd-shaped lites, dual-pane units and glass over furniture; measuring and cutting done on-site (often on a garage floor or driveway table), wet application and trimming in dusty, uncontrolled conditions with pets, drapes and homeowner present.

Institutional/retail interior: large storefront lites, school or hospital glazing and interior partitions get anti-glare or glare-plus-safety film; big single sheets handled by two workers, applied wet in place from ladders or lifts inside a facility kept to a working standard.

Shop/warehouse pre-application: glass lites are laid on a bench or cutting table in the glazier's shop, film is measured and cut to the lite, applied and squeegeed, then the filmed lite is glazed later on site.

Exterior application on an existing building: solar/anti-glare film applied to the outside face of upper-floor glazing from a boom lift, swing stage or ladder, with wind, sun and dust affecting wet application and trimming.

Spray-applied tinting/coating solution instead of film: masking the surrounds and spraying a tint or glare-reducing coating onto glass panels (typically shop-sprayed panels or small in-place lites), then inspecting for even coverage and runs.

sources.system: OPTI-STREAM PRO film applicator (Ashton Industrial / Universal Laminators)
sources.title: New range of protective film applicators | Ashton Industrial | glassonweb.com
sources.claim: Ashton Industrial's OPTI-STREAM PRO is a commercial in-line machine that applies adhesive film simultaneously to both faces of mixed-size insulating glass units on a conveyor and automatically trims the excess film; the range covers single/double-sided application with automatic trim options, and stated applications include mirror anti-shatter backing films.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine application of adhesive polyester film to architectural flat glass/IGUs. Same workpiece (flat glass lites), same operation sequence (present glass, lay adhesive film, press/roll it down, trim to the glass edge) as pressing anti-glare film to glass; the machine also handles permanent functional films (mirror anti-shatter backing).

sources.system: WALCO VX / VX2 glass and window laminators
sources.title: Glass & window laminating machines manufactured in Europe and the USA | WALCO
sources.claim: WALCO's vertical and horizontal glass laminators automatically apply film to IGUs, flat glass and mirrors, with the VX2 automatically calculating the film area to match the glass product and cutting technology keeping edges film-free; output is stated to be bubble-free and wrinkle-free, and horizontal machines are used for permanent mirror safety-backing film.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated measuring, cutting and pressing of adhesive film onto architectural glass in a production line. It covers the same sub-actions as the glazier task (measure the lite, size/cut the film, press it bubble- and wrinkle-free, keep edges clean) on the same objects, differing only in the film's optical function.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine lamination of adhesive window film (including permanent explosion-proof/safety film, the same polyester+PSA construction as solar/anti-glare film) onto flat glass, with automatic cut-off — the mechanical equivalent of measuring, cutting and pressing anti-glare film onto glass.

sources.claim: The most capable in-situ building-glass robot deployed on real facades, Skyline Robotics' Ozmo, performs window cleaning from a suspended platform on New York skyscrapers; no comparable field system performs measuring, cutting or wet application of window film on installed glazing.

tasks.label: Assemble and cement sections of stained glass together.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Stained-glass shop/studio bench: build a new leaded panel from dozens of hand-cut, irregular art-glass pieces — lay pieces to the cartoon, cut and fit lead came around each piece, hold with horseshoe nails, flux and solder every joint on both faces, then force glazing cement/putty under the came flanges, dust with whiting, brush and clean both sides.

Shop bench, copper-foil (Tiffany) method: foil-wrap the edges of many small irregular glass pieces (suncatcher, lamp panel, small window), assemble on a jig, flux, tack, tin and run bead solder on both sides, add zinc/brass edging and hanging rings, then wash, patina and polish.

Shop restoration/re-lead of a historic church or house window: dismantle the deteriorated panel, clean and edge-repair fragile original glass, reassemble the pieces into new lead came following the rubbing/template, solder all joints, cement and whiting both faces, and attach tie wires and reinforcing saddle bars.

Shop production run of repetitive small leaded units (door lites, cabinet-door inserts, transoms) built on a fixed jig from machine-cut glass shapes and came: assemble, solder joints, cement/seal the panel and prepare it for capture between tempered lites.

On-site work at a church or historic building, from scaffolding or ladders: cut out and replace cracked pieces in an installed panel, re-solder failed came joints, and re-cement/putty loosened sections in place, then clean the glass in situ.

sources.system: Artaic Arty / Artemis mosaic assembly robot
sources.title: When Art Marries Robotics to Create Mosaics - Artaic
sources.claim: Artaic's factory robots ('Arty'/'Artemis') autonomously pick and place uniform, machine-made mosaic tiles fed from color hoppers into square-foot mosaic sections in a Boston production facility; the sections are faced with polymer film for later installation. The system handles regular tiles from feeders, not irregular hand-cut art glass, and performs no came fitting, soldering or putty cementing.
sources.transferJustification: Closest cited analog: robotic assembly of many small glass/ceramic pieces into a decorative panel. Transfer to this task fails — Artaic works with uniform tiles fed right-side-up from hoppers and adheres a facing sheet, whereas the glazier task requires fitting irregular hand-cut glass into lead came channels, soldering every joint on both faces, and forcing cement under the came flanges.

sources.system: Beyond Transparency robotic polychromatic glass printing (UR arm + multi-channel granular dispenser)
sources.title: Beyond Transparency: Robotically Enhanced Glass Architecture - dbt
sources.claim: ETH Zurich's Digital Building Technologies group used a UR robot arm with a multi-channel granular-glass dispenser to 'print' polychromatic patterns onto float glass, which is then kiln-fused into a single colored glass element — a research alternative to stained glass that involves no assembly of cut sections and no cementing.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the nearest robotic work on colored architectural glass. It substitutes a printing/fusing process for the craft entirely and never assembles or cements sections of stained glass, so it cannot complete this task's instances.

sources.title: Robotic window glazing cell by TECAUMA - DirectIndustry
sources.claim: TECAUMA supplies a commercial robotic window-glazing cell in which a robot unstacks glass panes from managed trolleys and glazes opening frames at 45-60 second cycle times inside a fenced factory line — demonstrating autonomous industrial handling and setting of rectangular glass into frames, but not stained-glass panel assembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is factory glazing of window sashes (handling glass, sealing it into a frame). It does not transfer: the robot handles single rectangular panes into machined frames, with no fitting of many irregular pieces, no lead came, no soldering, and no putty cementing of a stained-glass panel.

In the shop: an etched/frosted design produced chemically - etching cream or acid applied through a resist stencil on a mirror or flat lite (house numbers, decorative bands, restaurant logo), rinsed, neutralized and inspected.

On site at a customer's commercial premises: applying a frosted/etched or painted design (logo, privacy band, manifestation dots) to glass already installed in a storefront door, office partition or display case, working around occupants and finished floors.

tasks.label: Measure and cut insulation for covering surfaces, using tape measures, handsaws, power saws, knives, or scissors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential new construction, wood-framed walls: worker measures each stud bay with a tape, cuts fiberglass/mineral wool batts to length on a scrap board or table with a utility knife, and splits/notches pieces around outlet boxes, wiring, plumbing and irregular bays. Bays vary in width, framing is out of square, the site is dusty and cluttered.

Retrofit of an existing home's attic, knee wall, or crawlspace: worker measures irregular joist/rafter bays, cuts rolls or batts to fit around ducts, wiring, chimneys, blocking and low-clearance obstacles, often kneeling on joists with poor light and limited headroom.

Rigid board insulation (XPS, polyiso, EPS, wood fiber) for basement walls, rim joists, foundations or exterior sheathing: worker measures the surface, marks and cuts boards to size and around penetrations with a handsaw, circular saw or knife, cutting on horses or on the ground outdoors.

Commercial/institutional building under construction: cutting mineral wool, safing, or rigid board insulation for large wall assemblies, ceilings, and soffits, fitting around ductwork, hangers, and penetrations, often measuring from a lift or scaffold in an active multi-trade site.

Offsite prefabrication/panel shop or SIP plant: cutting batts or foam/board insulation to shop-drawing dimensions at a bench, table saw or cutting table for wall, floor and roof panels; dimensions come from panel drawings rather than field measurement.

tasks.label: Fit, wrap, staple, or glue insulating materials to structures or surfaces, using hand tools or wires.

instances.label: New single-family/townhome construction on a jobsite: installing faced fiberglass batts in exterior and interior wood stud wall cavities, cutting batts to length, splitting and fitting around wiring, boxes, plumbing and blocking, and stapling flanges to studs with a hand stapler; ladders, dust, variable framing quality, other trades present.

sources.transferJustification: Closest fielded in-situ insulation robot for existing homes; cited to show the only deployed retrofit system is teleoperated.

tasks.label: Distribute insulating materials evenly into small spaces within floors, ceilings, or walls, using blowers and hose attachments, or cement mortars.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retrofit attic in an occupied single-family home: worker drags a 3-inch hose through a small hatch, crawls over joists around ducts, wiring, recessed cans and knee walls, and blows loose-fill cellulose or fiberglass to an even depth against depth rulers, keeping baffles and eave vents clear.

New tract-home or multifamily construction site: after drywall, blow loose-fill fiberglass/cellulose into the attic/ceiling cavity from the hatch or from inside the attic to the specified R-value and even depth, working amid other trades, debris and temporary lighting.

New construction, open framed walls on site: blown-in-blanket (BIBS) or dense-pack fiberglass blown behind stapled netting into stud cavities, including narrow bays and cavities crowded with wiring, boxes and blocking, filled to uniform density without voids or bulges.

Retrofit dense-pack of closed wall cavities in an existing house: locate studs/firestops, drill access holes through siding or plaster, feed a fill tube into each cavity, dense-pack to specified density by feel and machine pressure, then plug and patch the holes.

Existing building crawl space, floor joist cavities and small spaces around pipes, ducts and penetrations: blow insulation into floor/ceiling cavities in a low, dirt-floored crawl space, and pack small openings with insulating cement mortar or similar fill.

Off-site panel/modular plant: wall, floor and roof cassettes clad on one side are moved onto work tables on a production line and loose-fill insulation is blown into each cavity to a controlled density before the second face is closed.

sources.system: WEINMANN WALLTEQ M-380 blowTEC + ISOCELL blowing plate
sources.title: Insulating has never been so easy | HOMAG
sources.claim: WEINMANN WALLTEQ M-380 blowTEC multifunction bridge with an integrated ISOCELL blowing plate blows loose-fill insulation (cellulose, wood and mineral fiber) fully automatically into the cavities of timber wall/ceiling elements fixtured on production tables, including small cavities and gable shapes, with compaction controlled by a weighing unit; in permanent production use at Fluck Holzbau.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: distributing blown insulating material evenly into the small cavities of wall, floor and ceiling assemblies through a blowing head/hose, with fill density controlled and visually verified.

sources.title: ISOblow Elements | ISOCELL
sources.claim: ISOCELL's ISOblow ELEMENTS blow-in plate is a commercial product for precise blow-in insulation of timber construction elements ..., usable with all standard blow-in insulation materials and integrable into fully automated production lines.

sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor Robotic Insulation system is a commercially offered, fully automated robotic cell that installs insulation into prefabricated wall, floor and roof cassettes on factory production lines; Randek AutoWall lines are configured with blow-in insulation for closed panels.
sources.transferJustification: Same task performed on fixtured elements: filling wall, floor and roof cavities with insulation to a consistent standard in a factory cell.

sources.title: The Little Bot That Can | SprayFoam Magazine News
sources.claim: Q-Bot's Spraybot, the only fielded robot that insulates cavities of existing homes (spraying foam onto the underside of suspended timber ... from the crawl space), is driven and directed by a human operator throughout spraying, i.e. teleoperated rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Closest in-situ analogue (applying insulation inside an existing building's floor void); cited to establish that the only existing-building system is operator-driven, so E3 is unsupported.

sources.title: ORNL demonstrates affordable, energy efficient, low-carbon building technologies on National Mall during HUD Innovation Housing Showcase
sources.claim: ORNL and collaborators built an autonomous spray foam robot that installs insulation foam in walls, shown in live demonstrations at the 2024 HUD Innovation Housing Showcase; it is a research demonstration rather than a deployed on-site product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled distribution of insulating material into wall cavities; supports that cavity filling is automatable when the wall is presented to the machine, but only at demonstration maturity.

sources.system: GLITPP robotic batt insulation insertion method
sources.title: A robotic method for installing batt thermal insulation into prefabricated light-frame wood wall panel | Construction Robotics
sources.claim: A 6-DOF robot arm with a custom end-effector inserted batt thermal insulation (mineral wool and fiberglass) into light-frame wood wall panel cavities of various frame sizes with a 92.5% success rate and tight fits without gaps, in a prefabrication panel setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: filling the same stud-cavity 'small spaces' with insulation, using batts rather than blown fiber; shows fixtured wall cavities can be filled to standard by machine in a panel line.

tasks.label: Move controls, buttons, or levers to start blowers and regulate flow of materials through nozzles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Attic loose-fill retrofit in an occupied single-family home: blowing machine in the truck at the curb, hose run up through a hatch; one worker in the hot, joist-and-truss-filled attic works the nozzle to depth markers while the machine-side worker starts the blower, sets air and material gates, feeds bales, and clears clogs.

New residential construction: blown fiberglass/cellulose into netted or membrane-covered stud bays (BIBS/dense-pack) and open-blow over the ceiling after drywall; machine parked outside, hose fed into the framed shell; flow and air pressure regulated to hit specified density without voids or bulges.

Spray polyurethane foam work: setting rig temperatures and pressures, purging and triggering the gun, spraying open stud bays, roof-deck undersides, rim joists and crawlspace floors in homes and light commercial buildings, adjusting flow for pass thickness and yield.

Retrofit dense-pack of existing closed wall and sloped-ceiling cavities through drilled holes (siding or interior plaster removed at holes): feeling for blockages through the fill tube, throttling material and air to reach dense-pack density without blowing out lath or plaster.

Commercial/industrial spray-applied work in a building under construction: spray-applied fiber insulation or fire-resistive material onto steel decks, beams and masonry walls in a warehouse, school or office shell, working off lifts with the pump/hopper on the slab and the operator regulating material and air at the nozzle.

sources.system: WEINMANN WALLTEQ M-380 blowTEC (with ISOCELL blowing plate)
sources.title: Insulating has never been so easy | HOMAG
sources.claim: WEINMANN's WALLTEQ M-380 blowTEC multifunction bridge, installed at Fluck Holzbau's prefab plant, blows loose insulation fully automatically into the cavities of fixtured timber wall/roof/ceiling elements, with compaction density controlled automatically by a weighing unit.

sources.title: Multifunction Bridge WALLTEQ M-300/M-500 insuFill
sources.claim: WEINMANN sells the WALLTEQ M-300/M-500 insuFill multifunction bridge as a standard product for fully automatic blow-in insulation of timber construction elements, including logging of blow-in quantity.

sources.title: YOUR SOLUTION for timber framing at the DACH+HOLZ 2018 | HOMAG
sources.claim: WEINMANN offers several machine configurations for fully automated blowing-in of loose insulation material into timber frame elements, from the WMS 150 blowTEC multifunction bridge to a dedicated blow-in bridge.

sources.title: Here's A Robot That Solves For Prefab Wall Panel Spray Foam Insulation
sources.claim: Spray-R offers a robotic cell that applies closed-cell spray polyurethane foam to prefabricated wall panels in offsite panel facilities; the robot sprays while the human operator supervises from outside the enclosure, and each panel is photo-documented before and after.

sources.system: ORNL Robotically and Autonomously Installed Wall Interior Spray Foam
sources.title: Robotically and Autonomously Installed Wall Interior Spray Foam | ORNL
sources.claim: ORNL's autonomous spray foam robot scans a wall, locates the stud cavities, plans a spray path and sprays the foam automatically while managing thickness.

sources.title: ORNL demonstrates affordable, energy efficient, low-carbon building technologies on National Mall during HUD Innovation Housing Showcase
sources.claim: ORNL publicly demonstrated its autonomous spray foam robot installing insulation foam in walls at the HUD Innovative Housing Showcase on the National Mall.

sources.system: Obayashi fireproof coating spray robot (2nd generation)
sources.title: Obayashi Develops a New Fireproof Coating Spray Robot for Wider Use on Construction Sites
sources.claim: Obayashi's second-generation fireproof coating spray robot moves autonomously around an active construction site and sprays semi-dry rockwool onto steel beams; first-generation units have run on multiple mid- to high-rise office building sites since 2019, covering roughly the same daily area as a skilled sprayer at standard-compliant thickness and density.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: spray-applied fire-resistive rockwool coating. It uses the same equipment class as spray-applied insulation (hopper/pump, hose, nozzle with machine-regulated material and air flow) and is judged on the same acceptance criteria (specified coating thickness and density over structural surfaces), performed overhead on an active jobsite.

sources.title: Meet Canvas, the Drywall Finishing Robot Offering Level 5 Quality
sources.claim: Canvas's drywall finishing robot, deployed on US commercial construction sites, is positioned by an operator, scans the workspace, then sprays joint compound onto walls and ceilings and sands it to Level 4/5 finish.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic nozzle application of a wet building material to interior walls and ceilings on active construction sites, with machine-regulated flow and thickness control — the closest commercially deployed analogue to in-situ spray-applied insulation coverage, though it works on finished flat board rather than open cavities.

sources.title: The Little Bot That Can | SprayFoam News
sources.claim: Q-Bot's underfloor insulation robot has sprayed foam insulation beneath suspended timber floors in over 3,000 UK homes, but the operator drives the robot through the void and defines each spray pattern, so the mobility is remotely controlled rather than autonomous.

tasks.label: Fill blower hoppers with insulating materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential retrofit attic top-up: blowing machine sits in a trailer or truck bed parked in a driveway or at the curb; the loader repeatedly hauls 25–35 lb poly bags of cellulose or loose-fill fiberglass off a stacked load, slits them with a knife, dumps the compressed blocks into the machine hopper, clears the agitator, and keeps the hopper fed at the rate the hose operator demands, in dust, heat, wind or cold.

New residential construction: machine or truck rig staged on a muddy driveway, garage slab or in the street at a framed house; pallets of loose-fill fiberglass or BIBS/dense-pack material shrink-wrapped on site; loader breaks down the pallet, cuts and empties bags into the hopper continuously while a partner blows attics or netted wall cavities, with trades, cords and debris around.

Commercial/institutional job (school, warehouse, hospital wing, multifamily) under construction or renovation: high-output rig at a loading dock or interior staging area, large bag counts, bags moved by hand cart from a pallet drop, hopper kept fed for hours; layout and access change day to day.

Contractor shop/yard or supply-house warehouse: loading and priming truck-mounted or portable blowing machines before dispatch, emptying bags into hoppers to purge/test a machine, or transferring bagged material into a rig's hopper on a controlled, paved, employer-managed premises.

Factory-based insulating (modular/manufactured home plant, panel or truss plant): a stationary or line-side blowing machine whose hopper is kept charged with bagged loose-fill by a worker inside a plant with a fixed layout, forklift-delivered pallets and standard housekeeping.

sources.system: LaborSave automatic bag slitting and emptying machine
sources.date: 2025-01 (page updated; product on market since 2004, installations since 2006)
sources.title: Laborsave - Products | The world's leading automated bag emptying robot
sources.claim: LaborSave (Ayal Robotics) is a commercially deployed automated bag-emptying robot: a full pallet of sacks is loaded by forklift or conveyor, mechanical claspers lift the top layer over cutting blades, the cut sacks are shaken over a feed hopper to discharge their contents, and empty sacks are ejected — i.e. it autonomously keeps a hopper filled from palletized bags inside a fenced industrial station.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class as filling a blower hopper: pick 25 kg bags off a stacked pallet, slit them, and empty the contents into a hopper at a sustained rate, discarding the empty bag. Objects (paper/poly sacks), weights and the receiving hopper are comparable; only the bulk material differs.

sources.title: SackBot® 100 Series – robotic depalletising with bag cutting and emptying
sources.claim: Palamatic Process SackBot 100 is a commercial robotic depalletising-and-bag-emptying cell built on a FANUC R-2000iC/125L arm with 3D vision: it detects the top layer of bags on a pallet, picks a bag with a vacuum gripper, transfers it to a fixed blade that opens it, and gravity-discharges the product into a buffer hopper with no human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same physical operation as filling a blower hopper — depalletize bag, cut open, empty into hopper — performed autonomously with 3D vision in a fenced cell; the transfer is in the bulk material, not the manipulation.

sources.title: Automatic Bag Opener - Bag Emptying
sources.claim: Premier Tech (PT Chronos) sells automatic bag openers that slit incoming bags and tumble them in a trommel so the material falls into the feed hopper below, with the emptied bags sent to a waste bag compactor — an off-the-shelf machine for continuously charging a hopper from bagged material.
sources.transferJustification: Same end state as the task (hopper charged from bags, empties disposed of); establishes that hopper charging from bagged product is standard automated practice in purpose-built lines.

sources.title: Blendomat - BO-A - Bale Opener for Gentle Fibre Handling | A.T.E India
sources.claim: Trützschler BLENDOMAT automatic bale openers pluck fibre from rows of compressed fibre bales with opening rolls and feed the tufts into the downstream blowroom line, a long-established automated installation in spinning mills.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatically breaking out compressed fibrous material and feeding it into a process intake. It shows the compressible, fibrous nature of cellulose/fiberglass loose-fill is handled routinely by purpose-built machinery, supporting transfer of the bag-emptying cells to insulation material.

tasks.label: Cover, seal, or finish insulated surfaces or access holes with plastic covers, canvas strips, sealants, tape, cement or asphalt mastic.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retrofit attic in an occupied single-family home: after blowing/laying insulation, seal top plates, wire and pipe penetrations, and can-light boxes with caulk or canned foam; tape seams of baffles and the kraft/poly vapor retarder; install and weatherstrip an insulated cover over the attic access hatch. Low headroom, walking on joists, poor light, stored belongings, dust.

New residential construction, framed and unfinished: tape and seal joints and edges of rigid foam board and poly vapor retarder, seal air-barrier laps, run beads of sealant at plates, rim, and penetrations, and seal around window and door openings. Other trades working nearby, cluttered floor, ladders, varying weather.

Commercial/institutional mechanical insulation: over duct and pipe insulation, paste canvas lagging with lagging adhesive, seal butt joints and laps with mastic and foil/vapor tape, apply insulating cement at elbows and fittings, and patch/seal insulation at hangers and access openings. Mechanical rooms, above ceilings, from ladders and scissor lifts.

Crawlspace or basement encapsulation in an existing home: lay plastic sheeting vapor barrier over dirt floor, cut and seal it around piers and ducts, tape seams and terminations, mastic/tape the rim-joist insulation and seal penetrations. Tight, damp, uneven ground, obstructions.

Large open commercial, warehouse, or metal building shell: seal and tape the seams and laps of vapor-barrier facing on banded blanket/roll insulation at walls and roof deck, seal laps at purlins with tape or sealant, and finish edges at penetrations. Work from lifts at height in a building under construction.

Prefab/modular or SIP panel plant: on a production line, apply sealant beads and seam tape to insulated panel joints and cover panel faces with facing/film before the panel moves down the line. Indoor plant floor, standard stations, panels on tables or conveyors.

sources.system: FANUC dispensing/sealing robots (e.g., automotive seam sealer application)
sources.date: 2026-06 (page), technology in production use for decades
sources.title: Dispensing and Sealing Robots and Cobots | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC industrial robots and cobots are commercially deployed to dispense sealants, adhesives and gasketing materials along programmed paths on fixtured workpieces in production cells, with vision used to inspect the seam as sealant is applied.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic seam sealing/adhesive dispensing. The insulation task's sealing element is laying a controlled bead of sealant or mastic along a joint or penetration; the materials (mastics, sealants, adhesives) and the bead placement precision are comparable, and the robot performs it on presented, fixtured work — exactly the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: FANUC robotic body/floor plug insertion system at GM
sources.title: Case Studies | FANUC America (GM automated floor plug insertion system)
sources.claim: General Motors automated the insertion of plastic body plugs into holes in vehicle bodies using FANUC robots, with a validated system delivering accurate, error-free installation on the production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic insertion of plastic plugs/covers into holes. This is the same physical act as 'cover ... access holes with plastic covers' — picking a compliant plastic cover and seating it into an opening — performed at production quality on fixtured work.

sources.title: RoboTape™ System for 3M™ Tape | 3M
sources.claim: 3M and Innovative Automation sell a pre-configured robotic tape application ... that applies adhesive tape along curved and straight paths with controlled pressure and clean cuts in manufacturing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic adhesive-tape application. Taping seams of foam board, facings and vapor barriers is the same operation — unrolling adhesive tape along a joint, pressing it down and cutting it — and the robotic cell performs it repeatably on presented work.

sources.title: Where to Find Automatic Spiral Wrap Taping Machines – CAM Innovation
sources.claim: Automatic spiral wrap taping machines are commercially available industrial equipment that apply tape in a spiral ... workpieces such as tubing and coils, replacing manual taping.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine wrapping of tape/strip material around cylindrical workpieces. Covering pipe insulation with canvas strips or tape lagging is the same wrapping motion on a fixtured cylindrical piece; combined with robotic mastic dispensing it covers the jacketing/sealing sequence when the pipe is brought to the machine.

sources.title: Meccanica Ronzani | Apply Protection Film | Laminating Machines
sources.claim: Commercial laminating machines automatically apply self-adhesive protective film to the surfaces of flat panels and sheets, with automatic film cutting and roller conveyors for loading and unloading.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine application of sheet/film coverings to surfaces. Covering an insulated surface with plastic sheeting or facing film is the same act of unrolling, positioning and adhering a limp sheet, done at production quality when the workpiece is presented flat and fixtured.

sources.title: Solution | Autonomous Drywall Finishing Robotic System | CPWR Construction Solutions
sources.claim: Canvas drywall finishing robots work on real commercial construction interiors, automatically applying joint compound and sanding large wall and ceiling surfaces after 3D-scanning them, but they are set up and driven into position by a human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-site robotic application of finishing compound to flat wall/ceiling surfaces. It shows what construction-site robots do today — broad flat-surface coating — not the detail sealing, taping, canvas lagging and hole-covering this task requires; sources also describe it as user-operated, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: OKIBO - Smart Robots For Construction Sites
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7 is a battery-powered robot that autonomously navigates interior construction sites using AI-guided 3D scanning and applies plaster and paint to walls alongside human workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous on-site application of a cementitious coating to wall surfaces. It establishes that autonomous coating of large flat surfaces is possible on E3 sites, but its demonstrated envelope is spray plaster/paint on open walls, not taping seams, caulking penetrations, canvas lagging fittings, or fitting access-hole covers.

sources.title: Robotics Underfloor Foam Insulation Technology - Q-Bot
sources.claim: Q-Bot's underfloor insulation robot enters crawl spaces of occupied homes and sprays polyurethane foam onto the underside of floors, but it is driven by a technician using a gamepad and video feed from a tethered control unit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ robotic application of sealing/insulating material in residential crawl spaces (E3). It is the closest deployed system to this task's home-retrofit instances, but the application is operator-driven, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: PARIS (Precise Air-sealing Robot for Inaccessible Spaces)
sources.title: Robotics for HVAC applications: A critical review and future perspectives - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: PARIS is a research tracked robot that performs semi-autonomous air sealing in attic spaces, planning a spray-gun trajectory to leak areas, but it still requires a human operator to navigate it to the specific area.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: sealing air leaks in residential attics. It is a research prototype requiring operator navigation, so it shows the in-situ E3 version of this work is not yet done autonomously at worker quality.

tasks.label: Read blueprints, and select appropriate insulation, based on space characteristics and the heat retaining or excluding characteristics of the material.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Remove old insulation, such as asbestos, following safety procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential attic tear-out: worker crawls over joists in a low-clearance, hot attic of an occupied single-family home, drags a large-diameter vacuum hose to suck out old blown-in cellulose/fiberglass (often rodent- or smoke-contaminated), hand-pulls and bags settled batts, HEPA-vacuums decking and framing, in Tyvek and respirator, protecting finished ceilings and living space below.

Crawl space / underfloor removal: worker enters a 24-36 inch dirt crawl space under a house, pulls down sagging, wet or mold-damaged fiberglass batts and old vapor barrier from between floor joists, cuts away support wire, bags material and hauls it out through a small access hatch.

Wall-cavity removal during a residential remodel: worker opens or drills sidewalls, vacuums out old loose-fill or dense-pack insulation from stud bays, pulls degraded batts from opened walls around wiring and plumbing, cleans cavities for re-insulation, works around finished surfaces and other trades.

Commercial/institutional gut renovation: on an active renovation site (school, office, warehouse), worker strips old batt, board or blanket insulation from walls, ceiling plenums and deck undersides from ladders and scissor lifts, amid partially demolished layout, debris, and other trades working nearby.

Removal inside an operating institutional facility during scheduled maintenance (e.g., school on summer break, hospital wing): fixed layout, controlled access, escorted work; worker removes deteriorated ceiling/wall insulation above a hard-lid or in a mechanical space, cleans up and leaves the area turnkey.

Regulated asbestos/vermiculite abatement: worker builds poly containment with negative-air machines and decon chamber, wets and removes asbestos-containing insulation (vermiculite attic fill, ACM board/wrap, asbestos-contaminated wall/ceiling material), double-bags and labels waste, performs final cleaning, awaits clearance air sampling.

sources.system: Bots2ReC mobile robotic units (RWTH Aachen, Robotnik, Eurecat et al.)
sources.title: Bots2ReC: introducing mobile robotic units on construction sites for asbestos rehabilitation (Construction Robotics, Springer)
sources.claim: Bots2ReC (EU project, 2016-2019) built mobile manipulator prototypes for asbestos removal in apartment buildings; the concept has an operator assign removal areas on a virtual site model that the robot then executes, i.e. supervised semi-autonomy in tele-operated and partially autonomous modes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: abrasive removal of asbestos-containing plaster/tile adhesive from dwelling walls. It is the closest robotic analogue to removing old asbestos-containing wall/ceiling material, so its limitations bound what is available for this task.

sources.title: Bots2ReC, robotic extraction of asbestos fibres from buildings — Robotnik
sources.claim: Final Bots2ReC results (project ended 2019) report only that the robot could reach about 90% of wall surfaces in a general dwelling, with no comparison to manual work yet performed; no commercial asbestos-removal robot resulted.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic removal of asbestos-contaminated wall surface material in residential buildings; the reported accessibility and unproven productivity show the state of the art falls short of worker-quality completion of insulation/asbestos removal.

sources.system: Brokk tele-operated demolition manipulator with suspended abrasive tool
sources.title: Bots2ReC: introducing mobile robotic units on construction sites for asbestos rehabilitation (Construction Robotics, Springer)
sources.claim: The most capable machines actually used for asbestos surface decontamination in buildings are tele-operated demolition manipulators fitted with abrasive tools; they are driven continuously by an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized stripping of asbestos-containing coatings/materials from building surfaces. It is the commercially available machine class closest to this task, and it is continuously tele-operated, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Robots to clean and air seal attics – Signetron
sources.claim: A prize-stage attic robot pair (tracked vacuum robot plus hexapod air-sealing robot) was developed for cleaning and air sealing attics under the US DOE E-ROBOT competition; it remains a competition prototype with no evidence of autonomous, worker-quality attic insulation removal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic vacuuming/cleaning of residential attic cavities, the same setting and material handling as attic insulation removal; its prototype status bounds capability for this task.

sources.title: Robotics for HVAC applications: A critical review and future perspectives (ScienceDirect)
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed review of robotics for HVAC/building retrofit work finds attic robots such as PARIS perform only semi-autonomous air sealing and still require a human operator to navigate them to the work area.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic work inside residential attics (navigating joists, applying tools). It establishes that even navigation in attics is operator-dependent, so autonomous removal of attic insulation is not substantiated.

sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute / US DOE
sources.title: A Robotic Pipe-Asbestos Insulation Removal System — Robotics Institute, Carnegie Mellon University
sources.claim: The most developed robotic insulation-removal machine, the BOA pipe crawler, was a 1990s DOE-funded prototype that remotely stripped and bagged asbestos lagging from industrial pipes; it was never a building floor/ceiling/wall system and operated remotely.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic removal and bagging of asbestos insulation, but on fixtured cylindrical pipe runs in industrial plants rather than building floors, ceilings and walls; it shows removal robotics exist only as prototypes on highly regular geometry.

tasks.label: Prepare surfaces for insulation application by brushing or spreading on adhesives, cement, or asphalt, or by attaching metal pins to surfaces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential new construction: worker applies construction adhesive/mastic in beads or dabs to framing members, rim joists, sheathing, or poured/CMU foundation walls inside stud and joist cavities so rigid foam board or batt will bond; cluttered active house site, kneeling, ladders, uneven subfloor.

Retrofit in an existing/occupied building: brushing or spreading adhesive, mastic or asphaltic coating on as-found surfaces in an attic, crawlspace, or basement - dusty, obstructed, low headroom, wiring and ducts in the way - before insulation is placed.

Commercial/institutional building under construction: attaching metal stick pins, weld pins, or adhesive-backed insulation hangers (usually overhead or on vertical faces, from lift or ladder) to metal deck, steel studs, CMU, or plenum/duct surfaces so board or blanket insulation can be impaled and capped.

Commercial/industrial jobsite: spraying or troweling adhesive or cementitious/asphaltic coating over large, open, accessible wall, ceiling-deck, or structural-steel areas to prepare them for insulation board or blanket; repetitive, room- or bay-scale, robot-accessible floor.

Prefab/panel plant or fabrication shop: adhesive applied to panels, boards, or metal components at a bench or on a production line, or pins welded to fabricated metal parts, before insulation is laid in; fixed layout, institution-controlled premises.

sources.title: Obayashi Develops a New Fireproof Coating Spray Robot for Wider Use on Construction Sites
sources.claim: Obayashi's second-generation fireproof coating spray robot autonomously moves around an active construction site and sprays semi-dry rockwool coating onto steel frames, at roughly a skilled sprayer's daily area and meeting construction quality standards; introduced at Tokyo sites in Nov 2023.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: spray application of a rockwool/cement fireproof covering onto building steel. It transfers to spreading cement or adhesive coatings over large building surfaces to prepare them for insulation: same viscous sprayed material class, same bay-scale wall/ceiling/steel surfaces, same active-jobsite conditions, and lower precision demand than a finish coat.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7/EG7+ mobile manipulator autonomously scans interiors and applies and finishes plaster/joint compound and paint on walls and ceilings on active commercial and residential construction sites, with no site prep, markers, or BIM.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous application and smoothing of joint compound/plaster over as-found interior walls and ceilings. Transfers to brushing or spreading adhesive or cement over the same open surfaces before insulation board is applied - same surfaces, same viscous material handling, coarser tolerance.

sources.date: n.d., retrieved 2026-07 (product family shown at LIGNA 2025)
sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor robotic gluing cell, part of commercial wall/floor/roof panel production lines, reads CAD data and applies adhesive automatically across panel assemblies ahead of sheathing.
sources.transferJustification: Same task at E1: spreading adhesive on building wall/floor/roof assemblies to bond the next layer, with the workpiece fixtured and presented by the line rather than found in place.

sources.title: Randek - Wall, Floor and Roof Production Lines
sources.claim: Randek's EasyFloor line for floor and roof cassettes uses an automated multi-function bridge that performs gluing and fastening on the fixtured element.
sources.transferJustification: Corroborates E1 adhesive application on floor/roof cassettes of the same kind an insulation worker would prepare, with the work brought to the machine.

sources.title: BizLink Factory Automation & Machinery | Robotic Stud Welding Solutions
sources.claim: Automated stud welding systems are routinely used to apply insulation anchors and similar fasteners to HVAC and construction sheet-metal components in robotic cells.
sources.transferJustification: Same task at E1: attaching metal insulation pins/anchors to a metal surface, with the workpiece fixtured in a robotic cell instead of hung overhead on a jobsite.

sources.system: HBS CNC / robot stud welding systems
sources.title: Automation | HBS
sources.claim: HBS, an established stud-welding equipment maker, supplies CNC and robot stud welding systems integrated ..., with automatic stud feeding at up to 20 studs per minute.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that pin/stud attachment to metal surfaces is a mature, fully automated fixtured-cell process (E1), matching the 'attaching metal pins to surfaces' half of the task.

roles.title: Insulation Workers, Mechanical
aliases: AC Insulation Installer (Air Conditioning Insulation Installer)
roles.description: Apply insulating materials to pipes or ductwork, or other mechanical systems in order to help control and maintain temperature.

tasks.label: Measure and cut insulation for covering surfaces, using tape measures, handsaws, knives, and scissors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial/institutional construction: in an unfinished mechanical room or overhead ceiling space, the worker measures pipe runs with a tape, then cuts pre-formed fiberglass pipe covering to length and cuts/miters fitting and elbow segments with a knife and handsaw at a makeshift jobsite cutting station, working around other trades, dust, and changing site conditions.

Duct insulation on a jobsite: worker measures rectangular/round duct sections, then cuts fiberglass duct wrap, liner board, or flexible blanket from rolls to size with knives and scissors on the floor or a sawhorse bench, allowing for overlaps, hangers, and access doors.

Industrial plant, refinery, or power plant new-build and turnaround work: measuring around vessels, valves, flanges and large-bore pipe, then sawing rigid calcium silicate, mineral wool, or cellular glass sections and cutting jacketing to fit, often outdoors, at height on scaffolding, near hot or live equipment.

Service/retrofit work in existing occupied buildings (hospitals, schools, offices): measuring and cutting patch pieces and replacement pipe covering to fit as-found conditions in congested ceiling plenums, crawl spaces, and tight equipment rooms, trimming iteratively around hangers, supports, and existing obstructions.

Contractor or supplier fabrication/prefab shop: working from a field cut list or BIM model, the worker lays out and cuts pipe covering, fitting covers, valve/flange pads, and duct wrap patterns to specified dimensions on a shop bench using tape measure, band/table saws and knives, for delivery to the jobsite.

sources.system: Lockformer Vulcan 1600 Fiberglass and Insulation Foam Waterjet Cutting System
sources.title: Lockformer Vulcan 1600 Fiberglass and Insulation Foam Waterjet Cutting System | Mestek Machinery
sources.claim: A commercial CNC waterjet cutting system sold to mechanical contractors automates cutting and fabrication of insulation, cutting up to 4" fiberglass or 2" foam into precise shapes such as square-to-rounds, radius elbows and transitions at +/- 1/32" positional accuracy, in a fab-shop machine station where sheet stock is loaded onto the table.

sources.system: Vulcan CAD | CAM | MEP Software for Lockformer Vulcan cutting systems
sources.title: Lockformer® Cutting Systems Vulcan® CAD | CAM | MEP Software | Mestek Machinery
sources.claim: The CAD/CAM software driving the Lockformer Vulcan cutting tables holds a library of thousands of duct and fitting shapes and automatically segments and nests the cut patterns, so the layout/marking-out step that a worker does with a tape measure and square is generated by the machine's software from entered dimensions.

sources.system: KMT Waterjet HVAC insulation cutting systems (incl. OEM Mestek/Lockformer tables)
sources.title: Waterjet Cutting in the HVAC Industry | KMT Waterjet
sources.claim: Waterjet cutting tables are used in HVAC fabrication to cut duct liner and insulation into precise shapes (square-to-rounds, elbow cuts) from fiberglass and foam, with material sheet-fed or coil-fed onto the machine table.

sources.system: CNC Robotics KUKA robotic routing cell at Carbolite Gero (ALPHACAM/RoboDK programmed)
sources.title: CNC robot driven by ALPHACAM cuts high temperature furnace insulation boards | Hexagon
sources.claim: An industrial furnace manufacturer replaced a flatbed router with an enclosed robotic cell using a KUKA arm with a routing spindle, programmed offline from CAM, to cut its rigid high-temperature insulation board to the shapes needed for each unit, running up to eight times faster than before.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting rigid insulation board to shape for covering furnace surfaces. Same materials (rigid board insulation), same required precision (fit-up of covering pieces), and it substantiates that a robot arm, not only a gantry, executes the cut-to-shape work in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Pacor waterjet / CNC autocutter / die cutting insulation fabrication
sources.title: Waterjet Cutting, Die Cutting Services – Pacor, Inc.
sources.claim: A US insulation fabricator supplies insulation pre-cut to customer specification using waterjet, CNC autocutter, die-cut and sheeter machines, generating the cutting programs from customer prints/CAD or by designing the panels from a sample part, covering fiberglass, foam and aerogel for applications up to power plant turbines.

sources.system: MegaPlot XTR Master abrasive fastwire rockwool contour cutting machine
sources.title: Rockwool cutting machine - stone wool, mineral wools | MegaPlot
sources.claim: A commercial CNC abrasive-fastwire contour cutting machine cuts mineral wools (stone wool, glass wool, rockwool), PIR/ISO foams and polystyrene fully automatically, and is marketed as suited to producing pipe and chimney insulation shapes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: contour-cutting rigid mineral wool/foam stock into pipe and vessel insulation shapes. Same materials and geometries as field-cut industrial insulation sections, showing the cutting itself is machine-executable when stock is presented on the machine table.

tasks.label: Apply, remove, and repair insulation on industrial equipment, pipes, ductwork, or other mechanical systems such as heat exchangers, tanks, and vessels, to help control noise and maintain temperatures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Insulating hydronic and steam piping in a commercial/institutional building's mechanical room and ceiling plenums: measuring, cutting and fitting fiberglass or elastomeric sections around straight runs, elbows, tees, valves and hangers, sealing vapor-barrier laps, and installing PVC/ASJ fitting covers, working from ladders and lifts alongside other trades.

Applying and re-applying insulation to process piping in an operating industrial plant (refinery, chemical, power, pharma): mineral wool or calcium silicate half-sections on racked and elevated lines, wire/banding, aluminum or stainless jacketing with screws and sealant, from scaffolding and outdoors in weather, under permit.

Insulating large field-erected equipment — storage tanks, pressure vessels, heat exchangers, boilers and breeching: cutting and fitting blocks/blankets to curved and irregular surfaces, welding/attaching pins and clips, banding, and installing metal lagging; occasionally spray-applied foam on tank exteriors.

Insulating HVAC ductwork in a building under construction: wrapping rectangular supply/return duct with faced fiberglass blanket, stapling and taping seams, applying duct board or board-and-mastic on plenums and risers, in a partially built, cluttered site with changing layout.

Removing and stripping existing insulation for replacement or access: cutting off damaged, wet, oil-soaked or asbestos-containing pipe covering and jacketing, bagging debris, working in containments or confined spaces during maintenance outages.

Repairing localized damage during maintenance or turnaround: patching torn jacketing, re-sealing joints and terminations, replacing short sections of covering around valves, flanges and instrument penetrations on live or recently shut-down systems.

sources.title: randek.com ROBOTIC INSULATION (product flyer)
sources.claim: Randek sells a fully automatic robotic insulation cell that cuts and fits insulation into prefabricated building elements inside a factory production line, replacing manual insulation fitting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fitting mineral-wool insulation into framed wall/floor/roof elements in a factory jig. Transfer is partial — same class of material and the same cut-to-size-and-place action, performed autonomously on a fixtured workpiece — but the workpieces are flat framed panels, not pipe, duct or vessels, and the cell does no jacketing, banding or sealing. It supports only fixtured, purpose-built (E1) application of insulation.

sources.title: Huashida PERT Pre-insulation pipe production line is an energy-saving equipment
sources.claim: Continuous factory production lines apply polyurethane foam thermal insulation and an outer polyethylene jacket to pipe conveyed through the line, producing finished pre-insulated pipe.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory pre-insulation of piping. Same object (pipe) and same accepted output (a bonded thermal insulation layer plus protective jacket), produced under machine control with the pipe fixtured and conveyed — exactly the E1 counterfactual of bringing pipe to the machine. It does not cover fittings, valves, hangers or any in-situ installation.

sources.title: Products — Permapipe
sources.claim: Perma-Pipe manufactures pre-insulated piping systems in which insulation is applied by direct foam injection with automated process steps in the plant.
sources.transferJustification: Corroborates that machine-applied foam insulation on pipe is a standard commercial factory process, but the degree of automation of the insulating step is not established here, so it is not relied on for a positive judgment.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized spray-foam application. The device is a guided cart for large flat surfaces; its control mode (operator-set passes) is not established as autonomous, and it performs no cutting, fitting, banding or jacketing, so it cannot substantiate completion of mechanical insulation instances.

tasks.label: Select appropriate insulation, such as fiberglass, Styrofoam, or cork, based on the heat retaining or excluding characteristics of the material.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Fit insulation around obstructions, and shape insulating materials and protective coverings as required.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial new construction (hospital, school, office tower under build-out): insulating overhead chilled-water, steam and domestic piping in mechanical rooms and above ceilings. Worker works from ladders/scissor lifts in congested racks, mitering fiberglass sectional pipe covering to fit elbows, tees, unions, hangers and pipe-shoe supports, cutting relief for valve stems, and snapping on PVC fitting covers sealed with tape and mastic.

Industrial plant maintenance or turnaround (refinery, chemical plant, power station): insulating valves, flanges, pumps, expansion joints and irregular elbows on hot process piping from scaffold, cutting calcium silicate or mineral wool to fit around bolt bosses, trunnions and instrument taps, then field-fabricating and fitting aluminum/stainless jacketing, bands and removable blankets, outdoors and in weather.

Retrofit / repair work in an occupied institutional or commercial building: insulating or re-insulating duct and pipe runs inside ceiling plenums, pipe chases and mechanical mezzanines, fitting insulation around existing hangers, sprinkler drops, conduit and structural steel encountered as found, with limited access and short work windows.

Contractor fabrication shop: pre-cutting and shaping insulation pieces and protective coverings from a job cut list — nesting and cutting fiberglass/foam board segments for square-to-rounds, radius elbows, transitions and valve boxes, and cutting duct liner and jacketing blanks before shipping them to the jobsite.

Residential and light-commercial mechanical work: insulating water heaters, boiler and hydronic lines, refrigerant line sets and small ducts in basements, crawl spaces and attics, fitting elastomeric or fiberglass covering around joists, valves, pumps, tees and existing utilities in cramped, dusty, as-found spaces.

tasks.label: Determine the amounts and types of insulation needed, and methods of installation, based on factors such as location, surface shape, and equipment use.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mechanical room / boiler room in a commercial building: worker walks the job with the drawings or spec book, reads pipe sizes, service temperatures and equipment types (chilled water, steam, hot water, condensate), and decides insulation type (fiberglass, mineral wool, cellular glass, elastomeric), thickness per the energy code/spec, jacketing (ASJ, PVC, aluminum), and installation method (snap-on sections with staples/mastic vs. wrap), then tallies linear feet, fitting counts and material quantities.

Field takeoff/estimate for a bid or change order: worker or lead reviews mechanical plans and a site walk, counts pipe runs, valves, flanges, elbows, tanks and duct area, and determines quantities and types of insulation and accessories to order, producing a material list and installation approach for the crew.

Irregular or non-standard surfaces and equipment: large tanks, vessels, heat exchangers, pumps, valve bodies, breechings and ductwork with transitions, where the worker judges whether to use fabricated segments, removable insulation blankets/jackets, blanket wrap with lagging, or field-cut pieces, and estimates material based on surface geometry.

Retrofit / repair in an occupied facility (hospital, school, plant) or a residential/light-commercial crawlspace or attic mechanical run: worker inspects existing damaged, wet or asbestos-suspect insulation, determines what can be patched vs. replaced, selects compatible material and vapor barrier, and decides how to install around existing hangers, supports and tight clearances.

Outdoor or harsh-service applications: exterior piping, rooftop duct, cryogenic or high-temperature process lines, where the worker determines material suited to weather, UV, personnel protection or condensation control, plus metal jacketing, banding, and sealing methods, and computes quantities for the run.

tasks.label: Cover, seal, or finish insulated surfaces or access holes with plastic covers, canvas strips, sealants, tape, cement, or asphalt mastic.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial/institutional construction: after fiberglass insulation is installed on long straight chilled-water, steam or condensate runs in a mechanical room or above ceilings, the worker cuts and wraps PVC or aluminum jacketing over it, closes the longitudinal lap with solvent adhesive or tape, and seals butt joints and end laps; work from ladders and scissor lifts amid other trades, varying pipe heights and obstructions.

Fittings and irregular items on the same jobs: fitting two-piece molded PVC or metal covers over elbows, tees, valves, flanges and hangers; cutting and pasting canvas strips over fittings with lagging adhesive; troweling insulating cement; taping and sealing access holes and terminations. Each fitting is a one-off field fit-up requiring cutting, mitering and hand smoothing.

Industrial plant (refinery, chemical, power, food/pharma): outdoor pipe racks, vessels and large-bore lines; installing and closing metal jacketing over insulation and weatherproofing seams, laps, end caps and penetrations with caulk, sealant and asphalt mastic; performed from scaffolds and lifts, in weather, often during turnarounds in congested piping.

Service/retrofit inside an occupied institution-controlled facility (hospital, school, campus central plant): patching damaged jacketing, re-covering and re-sealing seams and access holes cut for valve, trap or gauge service on installed pipe and ductwork; tight mechanical rooms and overhead work around live systems and occupants.

Contractor's fabrication shop: pre-insulated pipe spool pieces, duct sections and fabricated covers finished on benches — jacket rolled and cut to size, wrapped over the insulation and seams sealed with adhesive and tape, canvas applied with lagging adhesive, mastic coated, then staged for delivery to the job.

sources.title: Coating equipment | Allseas
sources.claim: Allseas' sheet wrapper is an automated machine in a pipeline field-joint coating station that wraps a polyolefin sheet top layer over the coated joint and seals it, with operators not interfacing with the machine; launched 2023 and used on Allseas pipelay spreads.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pipeline field-joint jacketing. It is the same physical act as this task's core — covering a pipe surface with a plastic cover/sheet and sealing the overlap — on comparable cylindrical objects at comparable or tighter precision, with the pipe presented to the machine in a purpose-built station.

sources.system: Allseas FBE / injection-moulded polypropylene field joint coating machines
sources.title: Coating equipment | Allseas
sources.claim: Allseas' field-joint coating machines apply coatings, including over thermal insulation thicknesses, fully automatically on pipes up to 48 inches, and its injection-moulded polypropylene process automatically fills and seals the joint cavity.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying weatherproof/protective coating over pipeline thermal insulation. Comparable to sealing and finishing insulated pipe surfaces with mastic-type coatings; same object class (insulated pipe) with the work brought to a fixed coating station.

sources.system: FANUC dispensing and sealing robots (e.g., LR Mate 200iD, CRX-20iA/L)
sources.title: Dispensing and Sealing Robots and Cobots | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC sells and integrates industrial robots and cobots that autonomously dispense sealants, adhesives and gasketing materials along programmed bead paths on fixtured parts in industrial cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive seam sealing and adhesive dispensing. It is the same act as sealing jacketing seams and laps with sealant/adhesive, on fixtured workpieces at bead precision far tighter than insulation finishing requires.

sources.system: Automated tape laying (ATL) / automated fiber placement (AFP) machines
sources.title: Fiber placement and tape laying | CompositesWorld
sources.claim: Automated tape laying / fiber placement machines place tape onto mandrels under numerical control, dispensing, clamping and cutting the tape automatically — routine commercial practice in aerospace composite production cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine application of tape onto a rotating cylindrical mandrel. Transfers to taping and strip-wrapping a fixtured insulated pipe section in a purpose-built cell: same motion class, same flexible strip material handling, far higher precision than jacket taping needs.

sources.system: Wire-hoisted gas riser jacket assembly robot (CityU HK)

sources.claim: A wire-hoisted maintenance robot assembled paired protective jackets onto live gas riser pipes on high-rise buildings with polyurethane foam sealing, reported >96% success, but it is a published research prototype whose degree of operator control ('remote handling') is not established.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing a rigid protective jacket over a pipe in the field. Closest published analogue to fitting covers, but autonomy is unclear and it is a research demo on straight riser pipe only, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.claim: Q-Bot's insulation robot, the closest field-deployed insulation robot, sprays polyurethane foam under suspended floors in occupied homes but is moved and directed by a contractor rather than operating autonomously, and performs no covering, jacketing or seam-sealing finish work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of insulation material in unstructured residential voids. Cited as the state of field insulation robotics; it is operator-moved and does not cover, jacket or seal insulated surfaces, so it does not substantiate this task in E2/E3.

sources.title: Canvas, world's first robotic drywall finishing company, unveils 1200CX compact offering - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Canvas' drywall finishing robot works on active commercial construction sites spray-applying and sanding joint compound on flat walls and ceilings, operated and positioned by a worker; it addresses flat gypsum surfaces only, not pipe or duct jacketing, covers or fittings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic surface finishing with a troweled/sprayed compound on a construction site. Shows the only fielded finishing robot class works on large planar drywall, not on pipe jacketing, canvas lagging or fitting covers, so it does not carry over to E3 for this task.

tasks.label: Install sheet metal around insulated pipes with screws to protect the insulation from weather conditions or physical damage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outdoor industrial plant work (refinery, chemical plant, power plant): worker measures, cuts and rolls 0.016–0.024 in aluminum or stainless jacketing, wraps it over pipe insulation on horizontal and vertical runs in congested pipe racks, orients the longitudinal lap to shed water, staggers circumferential laps, and secures with self-tapping screws (plus bands/S-clips), working from scaffold, lift or ladder in weather.

Commercial/institutional building work (new construction or fit-out): jacketing insulated chilled-water, steam and condensate lines and risers in mechanical rooms, on rooftops, and above ceilings; overhead and tight-clearance work around hangers, other trades and unfinished space; pieces cut on site and screwed at the laps.

Fittings and irregular geometry: fabricating and installing metal covers over elbows (gore/two-piece), tees, reducers, valves, flanges, pump bodies and vessel heads; layout, cutting, beading and forming to fit each specific fitting, then fastening with screws so the assembly sheds water and clears bolting.

Repair/retrofit in an operating, occupied facility (hospital, campus plant, refinery turnaround): removing damaged or corroded jacketing, refitting new sheet metal over existing insulation on live lines, in crawlspaces, tunnels and congested equipment rooms, with permits and around operating equipment.

Shop or module-yard pre-jacketing: insulated pipe spools set on stands or rollers at a fabrication bench, jacket sheets cut and rolled on shop equipment, then wrapped and screwed on before the spool ships to site.

sources.title: A Production System for a New Era — The Shimizu Smart Site autonomous robots can transform a job site! | Shimizu Corporation
sources.claim: Shimizu's two-armed Robo-Buddy autonomously locates ceiling framing with imaging/laser sensors, holds flat ceiling boards up and screws them to the base material; used on Shimizu Smart Site building projects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: overhead screw-fastening of rigid flat panels on a building site. It does NOT transfer to this task: metal jacketing requires cutting and forming thin sheet to a specific pipe/insulation OD, wrapping it around a cylinder, orienting and overlapping longitudinal and circumferential laps for water shedding, and driving self-tapping screws through a curved double thickness in congested pipe racks — none of which Robo-Buddy performs.

sources.developer: academic research group (Automation in Construction paper)
sources.title: Maintenance robot for remote assembly of protective jackets on live gas risers - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A research wire-hoisted robot assembles protective jackets with PU foam on live gas risers on building exteriors; a prototype reported in Automation in Construction.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task found: mechanically fitting protective jackets around vertical pipes. Transfer fails because the jackets are pre-formed PU/plastic assemblies bonded with foam rather than site-cut sheet metal fastened with screws, autonomy is not established, and the work is a single-paper prototype rather than a system completing jacketing runs at worker quality.

sources.title: Robotics improve insulated pipe cutbacks | Offshore Magazine
sources.claim: Bredero Shaw commercialized robotic equipment for preparing insulation cutbacks on coated/insulated line pipe inside pipe-coating plants — i.e., machine removal of insulation at pipe ends, not installation of metal jacketing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine work on insulated pipe in a purpose-built coating plant. It removes coating/insulation from pipe ends and does not wrap or fasten protective sheet-metal jacketing, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task at any tier.

sources.title: A robotic method for installing batt thermal insulation into prefabricated light-frame wood wall panel | Construction Robotics
sources.claim: A robotic method for placing batt thermal insulation into prefabricated light-frame wall panels reached 92.5% success in testing — insulation-adjacent robotics remains at the research/factory-panel stage and does not address metal jacketing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling and placement of insulation material in a factory fixture. It places compressible batts into flat rectangular stud bays; it does not cut, form, wrap or screw-fasten sheet-metal jacketing on cylindrical insulated pipe, so it does not transfer.

sources.system: manual metal jacketing/cladding installation (no robotic system)

sources.transferJustification: Not a robotic system; cited only to characterize the acceptance standard (staggered laps, fastener spacing, site-fabricated clips) that any machine would have to meet, supporting the negative judgments.

tasks.label: Read blueprints and specifications to determine job requirements.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Prepare surfaces for insulation application by brushing or spreading on adhesives, cement, or asphalt, or by attaching metal pins to surfaces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial building mechanical room, ceiling plenum or pipe chase: worker brushes/rolls lagging adhesive, sealant or vapor-barrier mastic onto pipe insulation seams, fitting covers and jacketing in situ, working off ladders or lifts around installed hangers, valves and conduit.

Industrial plant, refinery or power plant: worker trowels or brushes insulating cement, weather-barrier mastic or asphalt cutback onto vessels, tanks, breechings and large-bore pipe, often from scaffold, in a congested unit undergoing outage/turnaround work.

Field attachment of metal pins: weld-pin gun or adhesive-backed stick pins fastened to installed ductwork, plenums, tank shells and vessel heads at the job site, laid out by hand so pins hold duct wrap or board insulation.

Sheet-metal / insulation prefabrication shop: adhesive spread on duct sections and fabricated pieces and weld pins attached to sheet metal before the piece ships to the job, done at the bench or on the shop's coil line.

Residential and light-commercial crawlspace, attic or mechanical closet: adhesive and mastic brushed onto small ducts, plenums and domestic hot-water piping, in tight, dirty, unlit spaces of varying construction.
