sources.system: MESH custom robotic stud welding cell (HBS automatic stud guns, servo fixturing)
sources.title: Robotic Stud Welding Cell | Case Study | MESH Automation, Inc.
sources.claim: A fixtured industrial robot cell welds capacitive-discharge and collar studs into sheet-metal enclosures autonomously, holding stud placement to 0.008 in with 91% OEE and automatic changeover between parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: arc/CD stud welding to steel sheet. Insulation weld pins are attached by the same resistance/CD stud-welding process onto the same class of gauge steel surfaces, with looser placement tolerance than the 0.008 in demonstrated, so performance carries over when the panel is fixtured.

sources.system: INROPA STEEL PAINTER robotic paint system
sources.title: Steel Painter | Robotic Painting by Innovation Tech, LLC
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic coating cell sprays high-mix structural steel beams and columns conveyed past the robots, generating a tailored program for each unique part from a 3D scan aligned to CAD, with minimal touch-up.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying a liquid coating over the whole surface of a varied, large steel workpiece brought to the machine on a conveyor. Brushing/spreading adhesive, mastic or cutback onto duct, pipe and vessel surfaces is the same class of viscous-material surface coverage at similar or looser precision, so it carries over when the piece is presented fixtured.

sources.title: 10Q Paint Robot | Technology Catalogue
sources.claim: The leading field robot for coating large storage tanks in service is a ground-operated crawler described by its makers as semi-automated, with workers running it from a control module — no autonomous in-situ coating of plant vessels is substantiated.
sources.transferJustification: Boundary evidence for the in-situ (E2/E3) case: operator-driven, semi-automated, and applied to bare tank steel rather than insulated surfaces, so it cannot support a positive judgment for field mastic/adhesive work.

sources.title: Development and Application of a Fire Resistive Covering Spraying Robot to Building Construction Site (ISARC 2020)
sources.claim: A research spray robot applied fire-resistive covering to steel beams at a building construction site, navigating autonomously from a pre-built map but relying on spray parameters recorded in advance for each beam size.
sources.transferJustification: Boundary evidence for E3: sprays coating onto exposed structural beams using pre-registered per-beam work data; it does not address pipe/fitting geometry, brushed adhesive at jacket seams, or pin attachment, so it does not substantiate this task in situ.

roles.title: Painters, Construction and Maintenance
aliases: Industrial Coating and Lining Application Specialist
roles.description: Paint walls, equipment, buildings, bridges, and other structural surfaces, using brushes, rollers, and spray guns. May remove old paint to prepare surface prior to painting. May mix colors or oils to obtain desired color or consistency.

tasks.label: Cover surfaces with dropcloths or masking tape and paper to protect surfaces during painting.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied private residence, interior repaint: painter spreads canvas/plastic drop cloths over floors, carpets and furniture, moves and covers belongings, masks baseboards, door and window casings, outlet and switch plates, cabinet hardware and light fixtures with tape and paper; clutter, pets and occupants present, layout differs house to house.

New-construction or gut-renovation interior (residential or commercial) before spray or roll application: rolling paper/plastic over finished floors, poly sheeting over window and door openings, taping off window frames, trim, sprinklers, HVAC diffusers and already-finished surfaces; active construction site with other trades, changing conditions and debris.

Exterior repaint of a house or small commercial building: draping drop cloths and plastic over shrubs, walkways, decks, HVAC units and vehicles, masking windows, glass doors, light fixtures, meters and hardware with tape and film, working off ladders/scaffolds around uneven terrain and weather.

Maintenance painting inside an occupied institutional or commercial facility (school, hospital, hotel, office): drop cloths in corridors and rooms, masking baseboards, door frames, handrails, signage, fire devices and casework, protecting furniture and equipment while the facility stays in use.

Industrial plant or shop finishing: masking fabricated parts, machinery, pipe, structural steel or equipment before spray coating - taping and papering off threads, machined faces, nameplates, gauges, glass and adjacent components, often with the workpiece staged on a rack, cart or turntable in a paint shop or booth.

sources.system: MTU / Robooptic Systems SpeedMask automated masking machine
sources.developer: MTU Aero Engines with Robooptic Systems (Dymax SpeedMask material)
sources.title: Fully automated masking process for MTU manufacturing - MTU AEROREPORT
sources.claim: MTU Aero Engines runs a fully automated robotic masking cell (built with Robooptic Systems, using Dymax SpeedMask elastomer) that vision-identifies a fixtured engine component on a rotary table, dispenses masking material precisely along edges, into holes and over broad areas to protect surfaces during thermal spray coating, then UV-cures and optically inspects it.
sources.transferJustification: Same task purpose (covering/protecting surfaces so coating does not reach them) executed on a fixtured workpiece; masking material is dispensed rather than taped, and the precision required exceeds ordinary painter's masking.

sources.system: Active Taping Kit (ATK) on six-axis robot

sources.claim: Aerobotix and FerRobotics sell an Active Taping Kit end-of-arm tool that lets a six-axis industrial robot apply masking tape automatically to aircraft assemblies and other ..., using force-compliant control to follow varying shapes and lay straight tape lines for paint masking.

sources.system: Automatic robot taping system with compliant force control
sources.developer: Malmgren et al., International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
sources.title: Automatic robot taping system with compliant force control
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed automatic robot taping system applies masking tape to protect surfaces before spray painting/plasma spraying: a 3D scanner reconstructs the workpiece held on a rotating platform, path planning covers the surface, and a compliant taping end-effector tapes flat, cylindrical, freeform and grooved surfaces with uniform overlap and little wrinkling.

sources.title: Robotic Tape Application | FANUC Authorized System Integrator
sources.claim: FANUC-based robotic tape application cells are offered and used in automotive paint shops specifically to apply protective masking tape to parts before painting.

sources.title: Okibo launches autonomous, AI-guided painting and drywall finishing EG7+ robot - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: The most capable in-situ construction painting robot marketed in the US, Okibo's EG7/EG7+, autonomously navigates job sites and performs plastering, sanding and spray/roller painting, but its described capabilities cover coating application and finishing only - no drop-cloth laying, masking or surface protection.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the closest in-situ system: it operates in the painter's own environment but performs coating, not the covering/masking task, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

tasks.label: Apply paint, stain, varnish, enamel, or other finishes to equipment, buildings, bridges, or other structures, using brushes, spray guns, or rollers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New-construction or gut-renovation interiors of commercial, institutional or multifamily buildings: large open floors, corridors and high walls (up to ~20-24 ft) of bare taped drywall; prime and finish coats applied by airless spray and back-roll; active jobsite shared with other trades, floors protected, no furnishings.

Repaint of finished, occupied interiors (private homes, offices, schools, hospitals in use): furniture and equipment shifted and masked, spot patch/prime, brush-and-roll walls and ceilings, extensive cutting in at trim, ceilings, outlets and fixtures, daily clean-up so the space can be used.

Finish coatings on interior woodwork and metalwork: doors and jambs, casings and baseboard, handrails, cabinets and shelving; enamel, stain or varnish applied by brush or fine-finish spray, multiple coats with sanding between, sharp lines against adjacent surfaces.

Exterior repaint of a house or small commercial building: wash/scrape, spot prime, spray-and-backbrush lap siding or stucco, brush trim, fascia, window sashes and doors; ladders and planks, uneven ground, landscaping and weather constraints.

Field coating of large industrial/commercial structures: warehouse and plant facades, storage tanks, steel framing, water towers and bridges; airless spray of primers and protective coatings from boom lifts, swing stages or rigging, to specified dry-film thickness, with overspray containment.

Painting equipment, machinery and fabricated metal items in maintenance shops or plants: pumps, guards, frames, railings and small structural pieces degreased, primed and top-coated by spray or brush, often in or near a shop paint area.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7 painting and drywall-finishing robots operate autonomously on active construction sites, having applied coatings/finishes over more than one million square ... before the 2025 US launch.

sources.claim: The commercially launched EG7+ reaches 24 ft for painting and finishing of high walls and needs no site preparation or external references to operate.

sources.claim: The PACO robot autonomously spray-paints large interior surfaces on French new-build and renovation jobsites and is offered commercially (roughly EUR 2,000 per site day).

sources.system: iGiotto robotic spray coating line (with cVision)

sources.claim: Industrial anthropomorphic spray-coating cells apply water- and solvent-borne finishes to doors, window frames and other large complex-shaped workpieces carried through the booth on overhead conveyors, with 3D vision generating the spray trajectory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory spray-finishing of building components. It is the same physical act the painter performs - applying paint, stain, varnish or enamel to building surfaces and joinery at accepted finish quality - performed with the workpiece fixtured and presented on a conveyor, i.e. the E1 presentation of painting work.

sources.claim: Apellix's spray-painting drone, bought and used by state DOTs and commercial coating firms for elevated structures, is described as a semi-autonomous piloted aerial system that manages standoff distance, perpendicularity and travel speed.

tasks.label: Fill cracks, holes, or joints with caulk, putty, plaster, or other fillers, using caulking guns or putty knives.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Repaint prep inside an occupied/furnished home: painter walks the room and spot-fills nail holes, hairline cracks, dents and gouges in drywall or plaster walls, ceilings and trim with spackle/patching compound using a putty knife, then sands flush; works around furniture, fixtures, flooring and occupants.

New-construction or gut-renovation interior, empty rooms on an active jobsite: filling drywall joints, seams, corner beads, fastener heads and surface cracks across whole walls and ceilings with joint compound/plaster to a paint-ready Level 4/5 finish, including sanding.

Finish-carpentry paint prep on new residential/commercial work: running caulk beads with a caulking gun along trim-to-wall joints, baseboards, door and window casings and crown, tooling the bead smooth, and puttying nail holes in wood trim and doors before painting.

Exterior prep on houses and low-rise commercial buildings: caulking joints around windows, doors, siding laps, corner boards and fascia, and filling cracks/holes in wood, stucco or masonry, working from ladders, scaffolds or lifts in outdoor weather.

Maintenance painting in an operating institutional or commercial facility (school, hospital, office, hotel): filling anchor holes, cracks and damaged patches in corridor and room walls with spackle/plaster, caulking around door frames, while the facility stays in use.

Industrial/structural coating prep: filling weld seams, pits, crevices and joints on steel structures, tanks, or bridge members with caulk/sealant or filler before priming and coating, often within containment or at height.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7 is a fully autonomous, AI-guided painting ... that navigates and works on active construction sites without site prep or external references, and has covered more than one million ... of real projects.
sources.transferJustification: Drywall finishing is filling wall joints and seams with joint compound/plaster to a paint-ready surface — the same material class, tolerance and accepted output as the painter's joint- and crack-filling work, performed in the same building-under-construction setting.

sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction's Dirty Work Is Going Robotic - Architect Magazine
sources.claim: Independent trade press describes the Okibo EG7 as fully autonomous and as applying plaster and finishing drywall on interior construction sites, moving through standard doorways using AI 3D scanning.
sources.transferJustification: Applying plaster/skim coat and drywall finish over wall surfaces fills joints, seams and surface cracks — the same filling output the painter produces before painting.

sources.title: How a Drywall Robot Is Reshaping Interior Construction | Built (Bluebeam)
sources.claim: The Canvas drywall finishing robot maps the wall with onboard sensors, sprays joint compound over panel seams in one pass and later re-maps and sands the seams flush to Level 4/5, and has been used on commercial jobsites including SFO Harvey Milk Terminal 1 and UCSF.
sources.transferJustification: Filling drywall joints with compound to a paint-ready finish is the same operation as the painter's 'fill joints with plaster' work; the robot is operator-set-up but executes sensing and application itself.

sources.system: Con-Vey + Argos Solutions automated panel repair (patch) line
sources.developer: Con-Vey / Argos Solutions / PRE-TEC (installed at Timber Products, Grants Pass)
sources.title: Robots Introduced to Grants Pass - Timber Products
sources.claim: A production plywood plant runs an automated patch line in which panels are conveyed and scanned, defects are classified, and robotic putty heads fill the defects to produce an even, paint-ready surface; the line has been operating continuously since mid-2024.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-vision-guided filling of holes, knots and surface defects with putty on wood panels. Same filler material and same accepted output (flush, smooth, finish-ready surface) as the painter filling holes with putty — demonstrated only with the workpiece conveyed and fixtured in a purpose-built line.

sources.title: Dürr sells 2,000th sealing robot: New robot model optimizes sealing application in tight spaces
sources.claim: Fully automatic robots apply high-viscosity PVC sealant beads to seams and joints on car bodies — coarse and fine seam sealing plus cosmetic seals on doors and lids — with Dürr alone having sold 2,000 sealing robots into production lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dispensing a controlled sealant bead along a joint/seam of a fixtured workpiece, including cosmetic (appearance-grade) seams. Same tool action as caulking-gun bead application on trim or steel seams, but demonstrated only on parts presented by conveyor in a fenced cell.

sources.title: Fully automatic sealing system for insulating glass - LiSEC.com
sources.claim: Fully automatic machines seal the perimeter joint of insulating glass window units with two-component sealant as units are conveyed through the sealing station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: filling the perimeter joint of a window unit with sealant to a uniform, tooled profile — the same joint-filling output as caulking a window perimeter, achieved with the unit conveyed and clamped in a purpose-built machine.

tasks.label: Smooth surfaces, using sandpaper, scrapers, brushes, steel wool, or sanding machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interior repaint prep in occupied, furnished spaces (private homes, apartments, and occupied institutional premises such as school or hospital wings): sanding spackle patches and skim repairs, feathering edges, scraping flaking paint and drips, scuff-sanding walls, trim, doors and sashes, working around furniture, occupants and dust-control masking.

Large-area wall and ceiling smoothing on active job sites (new commercial, institutional and multifamily construction, gut renovation): sanding joint compound, skim coats and primer across open, cleared floors to a level 4/5 finish before topcoats, with dust extraction.

On-site detail smoothing of installed woodwork and irregular surfaces: sanding doors, jambs, casings, base, stair parts, handrails and metal railings in place; steel-wooling and scuff-sanding between coats; scraping runs, sags and hardware edges.

Exterior repaint prep on existing buildings: hand and power scraping of peeling paint from wood siding, fascia, soffits, window trim and porch rails, followed by sanding and feathering, worked from ladders, scaffold or lifts under weather exposure.

Industrial and structural steel/equipment prep in the field: scraping, wire-brushing, grinding and power-tool cleaning of rust and failed coating on bridges, tanks, towers, stacks and plant equipment, often at height inside containment, to SSPC cleanliness standards.

Shop and spray-booth prep of components: sanding fabricated metal parts, doors, cabinet parts and millwork placed on racks, benches or horses in a contractor's or manufacturer's finishing shop, including scuff-sanding between coats before spraying.

sources.claim: The Canvas drywall finishing robot scans and 3D-maps wall areas and then automatically performs mudding and sanding, presented as an engineering control against silica dust and fall exposure on construction sites.

sources.claim: Canvas robots use an automated sanding head with integrated vacuum to smooth sprayed joint compound to a level 5 finish on job-site walls and ceilings, working alongside human crews.

sources.title: Drywall finishing robot saves time, prevents injuries — Construction Dive
sources.claim: Canvas drywall spraying-and-sanding machines have been used in production by major commercial contractors on large projects such as the Harvey Milk Terminal at ....

tasks.label: Erect scaffolding or swing gates, or set up ladders, to work above ground level.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential repaint: painter carries and sets up extension ladders, stepladders and ladder-jack planks at a single-family home — footing on lawn, gravel or deck, adjusting for slope, avoiding shrubs/gutters/wires, moving the ladder every few feet as work progresses; also stepladders indoors on carpet and stairs.

Commercial/institutional interior painting: setting up stepladders, A-frames and rolling 'baker' scaffold towers (with outriggers, planks, guardrails, locked casters) inside an occupied or fitted-out school, hospital, office lobby or hotel corridor to reach walls and ceilings 10-20 ft up.

Commercial exterior / new construction: erecting sectional frame or system scaffold bays along a building facade — mudsills and base plates, leveling screw jacks, stacking frames, cross braces, planks, guardrails, ladder access and wall ties — on varied ground beside an active jobsite.

Industrial plant, refinery, tank farm or shipyard maintenance painting: building tube-and-clamp or system scaffold around vessels, piping and steel, fitting the structure to congested one-off geometry, tagging and inspecting it, inside a facility that controls access and enforces permits.

High-rise or bridge work: rigging two-point suspended scaffolds (swing stages) — setting outrigger beams and counterweights or parapet clamps on a roof, reeving wire ropes through traction hoists, assembling the stage and tie-backs — or hanging pick staging under a bridge/steel structure.

sources.title: KEWAZO LIFTBOT - Edison Awards
sources.claim: The only fielded scaffolding robot, KEWAZO's LIFTBOT, is a rail-mounted lifting robot that moves scaffold components vertically up the scaffold; the scaffold itself is still erected by human scaffolders, and the robot must be mounted on scaffold the crew has already begun to build.
sources.transferJustification: Closest system to the task: it works on scaffold erection jobs at industrial plants and commercial sites, but it only performs material transport, not the erection of frames, braces, planks, ties or ladders, so it does not complete the task.

sources.title: Meet the robot that transports scaffolding
sources.claim: Kewazo's scaffolding robot is described as carrying scaffold pieces to human erectors, confirming that assembly of the structure remains manual.
sources.transferJustification: Same job site and materials as the task (scaffold components on erection jobs); cited to show that even the leading scaffolding robot's scope stops at transport, so no transfer to erecting the structure exists.

sources.title: Watch Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid work at a 'construction site' - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most advanced humanoid demonstration involving scaffolding and construction lumber is a staged Boston Dynamics Atlas video in which the robot places a single plank and delivers a tool bag on a mock scaffold set; it does not assemble any access structure and the behaviors are choreographed on a prepared set.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling plank-like construction elements around scaffolding. It is cited as the ceiling of demonstrated humanoid capability; it is a scripted/unclear-autonomy demo of one plank placement, so it cannot substantiate erecting a load-bearing scaffold or setting ladders.

sources.title: Okibo launches EG7+ autonomous robot for painting and finishing - Engineering.com
sources.claim: Commercially deployed painting robots reach elevated work by extending their own mast rather than by erecting scaffolding or ladders for a human, so no fielded system produces the erected access structure that is this task's output.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: painting above ground level in the same occupation. It shows automation bypasses the access-erection task by self-elevating; it does not erect scaffolding or ladders, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

tasks.label: Wash and treat surfaces with oil, turpentine, mildew remover, or other preparations, and sand rough spots to ensure that finishes will adhere properly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Repaint prep inside an occupied, furnished home: wash grease off kitchen walls and mildew off bathroom walls with cleaners, spot-treat stains, feather-sand patched spackle, scuff-sand glossy trim, doors and cabinets, wipe dust — working around furniture, floors and fixtures.

Prep of cleared, unfurnished interiors on new-construction or gut-renovation jobsites (commercial, institutional, multifamily): sand drywall joints, ridges and rough spots across walls and ceilings to a paint-ready level 4/5 finish and remove sanding dust before priming.

Exterior repaint prep on a house or small commercial building: pressure/soft wash siding, apply mildew remover or bleach solution, rinse, then scrape and sand peeling paint on wood siding, fascia, window trim and porch rails from ladders or a lift.

Maintenance repaint prep inside an occupied institutional or commercial building (school corridor, hospital wing, hotel, office): wash scuffed and grimy wall surfaces with detergent/TSP, treat stains, sand patched holes, scuffs, door frames and trim while occupants and furnishings remain.

Industrial/marine coating prep inside a controlled facility (shipyard dry dock, plant, fabrication shop, tank farm): degrease and wash down steel structures, hulls, tanks and equipment, then blast or power-sand rust and loose coating to a coating-ready profile.

Field structural steel prep: bridge members, water towers and exposed steel taken as found — wash down dirt and salts, treat rust, and blast or sand rough/corroded spots inside containment before recoating.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7 autonomous, AI-guided drywall finishing/painting robots sand and finish interior walls and are working on commercial construction sites; the company opened a U.S. HQ and launched the robot in the U.S. market.
sources.transferJustification: Machine sanding of drywall walls/ceilings to a paint-ready level 4/5 finish is the in-situ equivalent of 'sand rough spots to ensure that finishes will adhere properly' on new-construction interiors.

sources.title: Okibo launches autonomous, AI-guided painting and drywall finishing EG7+ robot - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: The EG7+ performs sanding, painting and level ... on high walls up to 24 feet and was launched nationally in the U.S. after a demonstration hosted by general contractor Hensel Phelps.
sources.transferJustification: Sanding walls to a paint-ready finish is the surface-preparation step this task describes for new-construction interiors.

sources.title: Meet Canvas, the Drywall Finishing Robot Offering Level 5 Quality — Construction Junkie
sources.claim: The Canvas robot, set up on a jobsite by a human operator who positions it and sets parameters, sprays drywall compound on walls and ... performs dust-free sanding to level 4/5 finish quality.
sources.transferJustification: Dust-free machine sanding of finished drywall to a paint-ready surface matches the sanding/dust-removal preparation a painter performs before priming.

sources.title: Construction robotics startup Canvas launches drywall finishing robot - Robotics & Automation News
sources.claim: Canvas machines are operated independently by trained contractor crews at partners including Webcor, DPR Construction and Swinerton, i.e. commercial jobsite deployment rather than a lab demo.

sources.title: Skyline Robotics deploys Ozmo window cleaning robot in New York City - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Skyline Robotics' Ozmo autonomously cleans the glass facade of a 45-story Manhattan office tower from a suspended platform, supervised by a rooftop operator.

sources.title: NOSCO Shipyard takes delivery of hydroblasting robots - Smart Maritime Network
sources.claim: NOSCO shipyard took delivery of HighMate-series hydroblasting robots for ship hull surface preparation ..., replacing manual blasting with ultra-high-pressure water jetting; degree of autonomy is asserted by the vendor only.

tasks.label: Apply primers or sealers to prepare new surfaces, such as bare wood or metal, for finish coats.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Active commercial/institutional construction site: spray a prime coat (PVA/latex primer or sealer) over large areas of newly hung and taped gypsum board walls and ceilings, including high walls in lobbies and corridors, before finish coats; floors bare, other trades present, work sequenced to a schedule.

New residential or multifamily construction: spray prime new drywall throughout unit rooms, closets, baths, hallways and stairwells (back-rolling where specified) ahead of the finish coats; smaller rooms, tighter access, fixtures and openings to work around.

Bare wood millwork on site: prime/seal doors, jambs, casing, base, shelving, stair parts, plus exterior fascia, soffits and bare wood siding and trim, using brush, roller and small sprayer, often from ladders or staging and subject to weather.

Field priming of bare metal in buildings and on job sites: hollow metal door frames and doors, handrails and ornamental iron, exposed structural steel, pipe, conduit and ductwork; brush/roller/small spray application of a rust-inhibitive primer after solvent or mechanical prep.

Industrial steel prime coat inside a controlled facility: newly blasted tanks, vessels, ship blocks/sections, bridge girders and structural steel in a shipyard, fabrication yard or terminal; heavy-duty zinc or epoxy primer sprayed to a specified dry film thickness with inspection.
Plant paint shop/booth: prime newly fabricated metal parts, machinery and equipment components brought to the shop by a maintenance or industrial painter, spraying primer to spec before topcoats.

sources.system: Okibo EG7+ with BLASTER spray gun
sources.title: Okibo Unleashes BLASTER Technology: A Breakthrough in Autonomous High-Speed Coating for the Construction Industry
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7/EG7+ autonomous construction robot, fitted with the BLASTER dual-nozzle airless spray gun, is marketed and used for painting and priming, and a BLASTER-equipped EG7+ was deployed on a commercial construction project in Jacksonville, FL.

sources.title: Okibo launches autonomous, AI-guided painting and drywall finishing EG7+ robot - Robotics 24/7

sources.title: Okibo, Global Leader in Construction Painting and Drywall Finishing Robotics, Launches US Headquarters
sources.claim: Okibo's autonomous painting/drywall finishing robots are in use on American construction sites and have covered more than a million square ... work in Europe.

sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction's Dirty Work Is Going Robotic - Architect Magazine
sources.claim: The Okibo EG7 is a compact cordless robot that navigates interior construction sites by AI 3D scanning and passes through standard-size doorways, and it applies paint, plaster and drywall finish.
sources.transferJustification: Same coating operation as priming (spray application of a wall coating to gypsum board); Okibo states primer among supported materials, so wall/ceiling prime coats in residential-scale rooms are within the demonstrated envelope.

sources.title: Solutions - GrayMatter Robotics
sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics' SCAN&SPRAY autonomously sprays primers and paint on a wide mix of parts in robotic finishing cells, scanning each part and generating toolpaths without programming or complex fixturing.
sources.transferJustification: Same operation as the painter's: spraying a rust-inhibitive primer to a uniform film thickness on bare metal parts; differs only in that the work is brought into the robot's cell rather than primed in place.

sources.title: US' largest shipbuilder teams with GrayMatter Robotics on physical AI | Manufacturing Dive

sources.transferJustification: Identical material and coating step to the painter's priming of bare wood trim, doors and siding stock, with the workpiece presented on a conveyor instead of installed on the building.

sources.title: Meet the industry's first automated paint robot: 10Q | Qlayers
sources.claim: Qlayers' 10Q coating robot, used on storage tank exteriors including a 40,000+ sq ft US tank project, is a semi-automatic crawler run remotely by an operator from ground level rather than an autonomous system.

sources.claim: PaintJet's lift-mounted Bravo end effector paints warehouse and commercial building exteriors, but ground crews drive both the lift and the spray head by remote control.

tasks.label: Remove old finishes by stripping, sanding, wire brushing, burning, or using water or abrasive blasting.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interior repaint prep in an occupied private home: scraping loose/peeling paint on walls and ceilings, sanding glossy enamel on trim, doors and casings, feathering patched areas, occasional heat-gun or chemical stripping of built-up paint on woodwork; furniture and occupants present, dust control required, pre-1978 lead-safe practices where applicable.

Exterior repaint prep on a house or small building: hand-scraping and power-sanding failing paint from wood siding, trim, soffits, porch rails and window sash, worked from ladders/scaffold; weather-dependent, uneven substrates, RRP lead-safe containment on older homes.

Maintenance repaint prep inside an institutional/commercial building (school, hospital, office, hotel, apartment common areas): sanding and scraping old coatings from corridor walls, doors and frames, stairwell metal handrails and railings; facility occupied or partially closed off, fixed layout, building staff control access.

Industrial coating removal on steel inside a facility or shipyard: dry/wet abrasive blasting or UHP water-jetting of tank interiors and exteriors, vessels, structural steel, hull plating in drydock, to SSPC/NACE cleanliness standards, inside containment and with blast suits/confined-space permits.

Field removal of old (often lead) paint from a bridge, water tower or exposed outdoor steel structure: grit blasting or power-tool cleaning of girders, gusset plates and lattice members inside a rigged containment enclosure, at height or in confined interior chambers, with negative-air and waste capture.

Shop/booth stripping of removable items brought to the contractor's shop or a blast facility: doors, shutters, railings, grilles, machinery components, vehicle or railcar bodies stripped by blast cabinet/blast room, chemical dip or machine sanding before refinishing.

sources.claim: The UTS/RMS steel bridge maintenance robots autonomously explore an unknown environment, build a 3D map, plan blasting paths and collision-free motion, and conduct grit-blasting; two deployable systems have been used at Sydney Harbour Bridge maintenance sites ....

sources.transferJustification: Related task: stripping an existing coating system from a large structure by a non-contact method, replacing manual plastic-media blasting and chemical stripping crews; same output (bare, refinish-ready substrate) inside an institution-controlled maintenance facility.

sources.system: Blastman B20C / B20S blast cleaning robots

sources.system: rpGatta Robotic Grit Blast Booth and Robotic Chemical Paint Removal System (Fanuc P350iA/45)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: booth-based robotic removal of old paint from components brought to the cell; some of the same integrator's booths are joystick-operated, so autonomy is not established and this item is treated as supporting context only.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7 is a fully autonomous AI-guided plastering, drywall-finishing and painting robot that maps sites by 3D scanning and works on active construction sites; its hopper swaps for a dust collector for ....
sources.transferJustification: Nearest in-building system: it sands the plaster it has just applied on flat walls, not old failing finishes on walls, trim, doors and rails, so it bounds rather than establishes in-situ interior capability.

tasks.label: Remove fixtures such as pictures, door knobs, lamps, or electric switch covers prior to painting.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied private home, interior repaint: painter walks each room and removes switch and outlet cover plates (often painted over, single small screw), picture hangers and wall art, curtain rods, register grilles, and sometimes door knobs and strike plates; furniture in the way, varied wall heights, screws stored per room for reinstallation.

Institutional/commercial interior repaint (office suite, school corridor, hospital wing, apartment turnover) under facility control: remove switch and data plates, wall signage, thermostats, coat hooks, door hardware and closers on many identical door/wall assemblies, working around scheduled access.

New construction or gut-renovation interior before spray/roll finish: strip or hold back hardware such as door knobs, hinges, cabinet pulls, plate covers and temporary fixtures on an active site with debris, other trades, incomplete lighting and changing layouts.

Exterior repaint of a house or small commercial building: remove shutters, house numbers, mailboxes, downspout straps, exterior sconces/porch light covers and hose-bib escutcheons, often from a ladder or lift, with weathered, painted-over or rusted fasteners.

Shop/bench work in the contractor's paint shop or a controlled staging area: doors, cabinet doors and millwork brought in and laid on horses or a bench, where knobs, pulls, hinges and hardware are unscrewed and bagged before spraying.

sources.system: UR10e-based automated e-waste unscrewing system (Díaz et al.)
sources.developer: Universidad / research group publishing in Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing (Elsevier)
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A vision- and force-guided robot cell autonomously locates screw heads, aligns a mechatronic screwdriver and unfastens screws on electronic products presented in the cell, with 91–100% success depending on screw type.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly of screwed covers on products presented in a cell. Removing an electrical switch cover plate, a door knob or a shutter is the same physical act — vision-locate a small screw, drive it out, retain the fastener — on comparable millimetre-scale fasteners and light plastic/metal covers, so performance transfers when the workpiece is presented to the machine.

sources.system: Fraunhofer IFF automated electronics disassembly demonstrator ('disassembly twin')
sources.developer: Fraunhofer Institute for Factory Operation and Automation IFF
sources.title: Robots to the rescue: Automated disassembly for e-waste recycling
sources.claim: A disassembly robot demonstrator performs a chained sequence of disassembly skills — screwing, lifting, extracting, localizing, repositioning, releasing, moving ..., cutting wires — fully autonomously on devices in a work cell, including lifting a motherboard out of a computer housing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: full autonomous disassembly of a fixtured product. It covers the whole sequence a fixture removal needs — undo the fastener, lift the cover/part clear, set it aside — not just the unscrewing sub-step, on objects of similar size and fragility to cover plates and knobs.

sources.title: ABB Robotics and US start-up Molg tackle data center e-waste with robotic microfactories
sources.claim: A commercial robotic micro-factory built on ABB arms autonomously assembles and disassembles complex electronic products such as laptops, servers and industrial electronics for component recovery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial autonomous disassembly of screwed/clipped assemblies in a purpose-built cell, showing the unscrew-and-remove-hardware capability exists beyond the lab, at throughput and reliability accepted by paying customers, when work is fed to the machine.

sources.developer: Academic group publishing in MDPI Automation
sources.title: Digital Twin with Model Predictive Control for Screw Unfastening by Robots
sources.claim: Robotic screw unfastening has been extended to degraded fasteners: a digital twin with model-predictive control adapts unscrewing to real-time force/torque data for screws affected by rust or thread damage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unfastening degraded screws. Exterior painting prep involves weathered, rusted or painted-over fasteners on shutters and hardware; this shows force-feedback unscrewing handles the degraded-fastener case when the part is presented to the robot.

sources.title: Meet Daisy and Taz: Apple’s iPhone-Disassembling Robots | Supply Chain Digital
sources.claim: Apple operates a deployed, purpose-built robotic disassembly line that takes in used iPhones and removes fasteners/components on a conveyor-fed cell in Austin.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production-scale removal of fasteners and covers from workpieces fed to a fenced machine line, establishing that fixture/fastener removal is routinely done at worker-equivalent reliability when the environment is built around the robot.

tasks.label: Use special finishing techniques such as sponging, ragging, layering, or faux finishing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied private home: painter applies a sponged, ragged or color-washed multi-tone glaze to an accent wall, powder room or dining room. Furniture masked, trim cut in by hand, glaze kept wet-edge, look matched to a sample board approved by the homeowner.

High-end residence, on site: faux wood graining of entry doors or paneling, marbleizing of a fireplace surround or column, hand-glazed/distressed cabinetry. Small, three-dimensional, in-place elements; multiple translucent layers, veining and figure worked freehand.

Hospitality/retail/commercial interior in a managed building (hotel lobby, restaurant, bank branch): Venetian/polished plaster, metallic layered glaze or strie on a feature wall, worked off scaffolding, scheduled around other trades and building operations.

New construction or gut renovation, unoccupied: layered decorative and textured finishes applied over large wall areas in model homes, amenity spaces or lobbies before turnover; site dusty, cluttered with materials, layout changing daily.

Contractor's shop or spray area: decorative finish applied to removable components (cabinet doors, shutters, columns, panels, trim) laid out on horses or hung on racks, then delivered and installed on site.

Maintenance/repair call: patching and blending into an existing aged faux finish or decorative glaze (damaged hotel corridor wall, historic residence), matching color, sheen and pattern of surrounding work so the repair is invisible.

sources.title: Okibo launches EG7+ autonomous robot for painting and finishing - Engineering.com
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7+ is an autonomous, AI-guided robot deployed on US construction sites for sanding, painting and Level ...; its capability set is flat coating and drywall finishing, not decorative or faux techniques.
sources.transferJustification: Same trade and same on-site environment (interior walls under construction); establishes what on-site autonomous painting robots actually deliver - uniform coats and Level 4 finish - and therefore bounds decorative-finish capability at E2/E3.

sources.title: Solution | Autonomous Drywall Finishing Robotic System - CPWR Construction Solutions
sources.claim: Canvas robots autonomously spray and sand drywall compound to Level 4/5 finishes on commercial construction sites; the automated repertoire is uniform compound application and sanding, with no decorative multi-tone or glaze work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (drywall finishing) in the same buildings and on the same surfaces a decorative painter works; shows the state of on-site autonomous surface finishing is flat, uniform coating, supporting negative judgments at E2/E3.

sources.title: Spray with a Cefla iBotic - MPS Machines
sources.claim: Cefla's iBotic is a commercially sold Cartesian spraying robot used in industrial finishing lines to coat fixtured, conveyor-presented workpieces (panels and complex 3D parts) at high finish quality, including multi-coat systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (industrial spray finishing of wood components) with the same coatings, base/glaze/topcoat layering and the same acceptance criterion of finish appearance, but only when the workpiece is fixtured and conveyed through a booth - i.e., E1 conditions.

sources.title: Digital printing lines - Barberan
sources.claim: Barberan's single-pass digital printing lines industrially reproduce the appearance of wood, stone and marble on panels and mouldings fed through the line, producing faux-material decorative surfaces at commercial quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (industrial decorative surfacing) delivers the same accepted output as faux finishing - a surface that imitates wood/marble/stone - on components of the same kind (doors, panels, mouldings), but requires the workpiece to be presented to a conveyorized line (E1).

sources.system: Barberan digital texture printing (Hot Coating / digital finishes)
sources.title: Barberán presents new machinery for a wide range of digital finishes
sources.claim: Barberan machinery shown in 2023 produces boards carrying wood, stone and marble textures with realistic 3D texture effects, i.e. faux-material finishes with relief, not just flat print.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the Barberan line item: the deliverable of faux finishing (marble/stone/wood look with tactile texture) is produced by machine on fixtured panels in a purpose-built line.

sources.system: Automated hydrographic (water transfer printing) dipping lines
sources.title: Water-Transfer Printing Process (Hydrographic Printing) — Step-by-Step Guide & Applications
sources.claim: Water transfer printing (hydrographics) lines decorate three-dimensional parts with wood grain, marble and similar patterns, and automated lines use a servo arm or multi-axis robot to perform the dipping motion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (industrial faux-wood/marble decoration of 3D parts such as trim and mouldings) yields the same accepted output as hand wood-graining or marbleizing of similar components, but only with parts racked and presented to a purpose-built dipping line.

sources.title: The e-David project – Rediscovering Art and Artisanship Through Robotic Painting
sources.claim: The e-David robotic painting system applies brushstrokes to a canvas and closes the loop with visual feedback, autonomously deciding subsequent strokes to converge on a target appearance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (layered brush application of paint judged by resulting appearance) on a rigidly fixtured flat surface in a lab cell; supports feasibility of appearance-driven layered paint application only under E1 conditions, not on-site.

tasks.label: Waterproof buildings, using waterproofers or caulking.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New-work interior caulking before painting in houses, apartments and light-commercial interiors: running and tooling beads of acrylic/siliconized caulk at door and window casings, baseboards, crown, wall-to-ceiling and inside-corner gaps, plus filling nail holes; done by hand with a caulk gun in rooms of varied layout with furniture or other trades present.

Exterior caulking on houses and low-rise commercial buildings before or during repainting: sealing joints around window and door frames, siding-to-trim laps, fascia joints, pipe and fixture penetrations and small masonry cracks, working from ladders or the ground in outdoor weather.

Applying water-repellent sealer or elastomeric waterproof coating to exterior masonry, stucco or concrete walls: masking windows and landscaping, spraying and back-rolling to specified coverage in two coats, cutting in at edges and penetrations on a building exterior.

Below-grade and wet-area waterproofing on construction sites: brushing, spraying or trowelling damp-proofing or fluid-applied membrane onto foundation/basement walls, planter and plaza decks, including patching tie holes, forming cove fillets and detailing penetrations to a required mil thickness.

Scheduled maintenance re-caulking at an institutional or commercial facility (school, hospital, office, plant): cutting out and removing failed sealant from expansion joints, masonry control joints and window perimeters, cleaning and priming the joint, installing backer rod, then gunning and tooling new sealant.

Weather-sealing large panelized facades on new commercial construction: gunning and tooling silicone beads in vertical and horizontal joints between precast or curtain-wall panels, worked from a swing stage or boom lift at height.

sources.system: Dürr sealing robots (EcoGun2 / EcoJet applicators, Ecopaint sealing line)
sources.date: 2024-02 (product page; technology in series production for years)
sources.title: Sealing Process – Efficiency in application - Dürr
sources.claim: Dürr's robotic sealing systems apply PVC sealant beads over overlapping panels and joints of car bodies in paint shops specifically to keep water out; fully automatic robotic sealing is standard production practice.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive seam sealing. The physical act matches caulking a building joint — dispensing a controlled, millimetre-accurate bead of elastomeric sealant along a joint to make it watertight and shaping it — performed on workpieces held in fixtures and presented by conveyor, i.e. exactly the E1 counterfactual of a caulking job.

sources.title: Dürr sells 2,000th sealing robot: New robot model optimizes sealing application in tight spaces
sources.claim: Robotic sealing of body joints is a mature, widely sold commercial technology: Dürr had sold its 2,000th sealing robot by 2016, used for coarse and fine seam sealing as well as underbody and sill coating.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive seam sealing/underbody coating. Establishes that unattended, programmed bead application to joints at production quality is routine in fixtured cells, which is what a caulking instance reduces to when the work is brought to the machine.

sources.system: LiSEC VL-1N fully automatic sealing system
sources.title: Fully automatic sealing system for insulating glass - LiSEC.com
sources.claim: LiSEC's VL-1N is a fully automatic machine that applies the two-component perimeter weather seal around insulating glass units on a factory sealing line, measuring the unit and performing corner correction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: perimeter sealing of glazing units. It is caulking of a building component — extruding a sealant bead into the perimeter joint of a window unit to keep water out — done fully automatically with the workpiece presented on a conveyor, matching the E1 counterfactual for window-perimeter caulking.

sources.title: Automatic sealing – Glaston
sources.claim: Glaston markets an automatic sealing robot for the sealing of double and triple insulating ..., with mixing and dosing of approved two-component sealants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory sealant application to glazing units. Same materials (two-component silicone/polysulfide) and same act (bead extrusion into a joint to form a weather seal) as building caulking, executed automatically on fixtured units.

sources.system: Dürr Ecopaint painting robots (EcoRP family; EcoJetSE wide-slot nozzle)
sources.title: Dürr launches new automotive painting robots with optimized arm geometry
sources.claim: Dürr's Ecopaint robots spray liquid coatings onto fixtured workpieces in enclosed booths at controlled film build; nearly 20,000 have been shipped since 1998, and the same applicator family lays thick underbody protection and PVC coatings over large areas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic spray coating in a booth. Spraying a waterproofing sealer or elastomeric membrane onto a presented wall panel is the same operation — uniform atomised application of a liquid coating at specified wet-film thickness onto a fixtured surface — including thick, high-viscosity protective coatings.

sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction's Dirty Work Is Going Robotic - Architect Magazine
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7 is a fully autonomous mobile robot that plasters, paints and finishes drywall on interior construction sites using AI-guided 3D scanning — the closest on-site autonomous coating system, but it applies plaster and paint, not waterproofing systems or caulk.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous interior plastering/painting on construction sites. Cited to bound the on-site state of the art: it covers broad flat wall surfaces, but no source shows it running or tooling sealant beads, detailing penetrations, or applying waterproofing systems, so it does not substantiate these instances at E3.

sources.developer: academic study published in Scientific Reports
sources.title: Control technology research of building wall spraying robot | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: A 2025 study of exterior building-wall spraying robots reports that such a robot must be brought to the construction site two to three months in advance and debugged repeatedly before practical use, indicating on-site facade coating robots are not drop-in capable.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: exterior wall spray coating. Cited only as a negative bound on E3 exterior waterproof-coating application.

tasks.label: Select and purchase tools or finishes for surfaces to be covered, considering durability, ease of handling, methods of application, and customers' wishes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Mix and match colors of paint, stain, or varnish with oil or thinning and drying additives to obtain desired colors and consistencies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/light-commercial repaint job in an occupied house or apartment: painter opens several gallons of the same latex color, boxes them into a 5-gallon pail on a drop cloth, adds water or a conditioner/extender for spray or brush consistency, and stirs with a drill-mounted paddle before loading the sprayer or cut-in pot.

Industrial/protective coating work on a bridge, tank or steel structure: two-component epoxy or polyurethane proportioned at the specified A:B ratio and reduced with the manufacturer's thinner for the day's temperature, then supplied on-ratio to the spray gun for a large sprayed volume.

Same industrial job, small hand-mixed batches: painter kits a partial unit of 2K epoxy/urethane in a pot for brush-and-roll stripe coats and touch-up, adjusts thinner by feel/viscosity cup, and works within pot life.

On-site color match/touch-up: painter must match an existing wall, trim or equipment color, tints a quart or gallon with universal colorants (or field-adjusts a store mix), brushes out a test patch, and re-adjusts by eye until it blends.

Wood finishing work: blending stain colors and thinning varnish, lacquer or conversion coatings with the correct reducer/retarder and drier additive to spray viscosity, done at a bench in the contractor's shop or a shop-like staging area on the project.

Batch mixing to a written formula at a fixed mixing station (body-shop/fab-shop paint kitchen or contractor shop): weighing toners, additives and thinner on a scale per the formula card and homogenizing the batch before it goes to the booth.

sources.system: PPG MOONWALK automated paint mixing system
sources.title: PPG Delivers 1,000th PPG MOONWALK Automotive Refinish Mixing System
sources.claim: PPG MOONWALK is a commercially deployed automated refinish paint mixing system: the technician loads tinter, additive and thinner bottles ... a dispensing rack and the machine verifies barcodes and dispenses each component's exact amount to formula.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive refinish paint mixing. Same objects (paint cans, toners, thinner and additives), same output (a batch mixed to a color formula and to spray consistency), and tighter color tolerance than architectural/maintenance painting requires.

sources.title: PPG MOONWALK paint mixing system now has customers in all 50 U.S. states
sources.claim: MoonWalk is in routine production use in body-shop mixing rooms across the US, indicating deployed rather than demonstration status.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive refinish mixing room work; same physical operation of dosing tinters/additives into a container to a formula.

sources.title: PPG launches automated stirring tech to improve paint mix consistency
sources.claim: PPG sells an automated stirring unit that homogenizes the dispensed mix to a ready-to-spray state, covering the stirring/consistency step that follows automated dosing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical homogenization of a mixed paint batch; identical to the drill-paddle/shaker step painters perform on architectural paint.

sources.title: Sher-Color - Sherwin-Williams
sources.claim: A computerized color-matching and tint-dispensing system reads a customer's sample, derives a formula, and dispenses the tints to reproduce the color.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: matching an existing color sample and dispensing the matching tint formula, which is the color-match half of the painter's mixing task, on the same paint bases.

sources.system: Chemspeed FORMAX paints and coatings / FLEX platforms
sources.title: Solutions for Paints, Coatings & Adhesives R&D | Chemspeed
sources.claim: Chemspeed FORMAX is a commercial robotic platform that formulates paints and coatings, controlling stirring and viscosity, with automated workflows that run without manual intervention.

sources.title: NOVAFLOW Advanced Gravimetric & Weigh-Based Ink and Paint Dispensing Systems
sources.claim: COROB NOVAFLOW gravimetric systems blend paint and ink batches by weight on demand, at the point of use as well as in the factory, across batch sizes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: weigh-based blending of paint components (bases, colorants, solvents) to a recipe - the same operation as boxing and adjusting a batch of paint to formula and consistency.

sources.title: XM Plural Component Sprayers | Graco
sources.claim: The XM sprayer's dosing technology maintains and displays the mix ratio automatically and logs spraying data, i.e., the ratio/consistency control is machine-controlled rather than operator-judged.

tasks.label: Polish final coats to specified finishes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Private residence (new build or remodel): rub out and polish cured clear/high-gloss lacquer or varnish on installed interior woodwork — doors, cabinetry faces, handrails, trim — by wet-sanding nibs, then compounding and buffing with an orbital polisher to the specified sheen, working in place amid furnishings, adjacent finished walls and variable lighting.

Occupied or institution-controlled commercial building (hotel lobby, office, hospital, school): polish final coats on installed millwork, entry doors, panelling and coated handrails/fixtures during fit-out or maintenance — sanding out defects and buffing to the specified gloss, with building staff controlling access and conditions.

Decorative wall finishes: burnish/polish Venetian or polished plaster, high-gloss glaze or metallic wall coating to the specified sheen, using trowel burnishing, wax and pad polishing on a vertical in-situ wall in a high-end home or upscale interior; sheen judged by eye against a sample board.

Maintenance shop or industrial plant: buff and polish the final topcoat on equipment housings, machinery, tanks, architectural metal panels or coated fixtures held on stands or benches, using compounds and a rotary/orbital polisher to a specified gloss and uniformity.

Spot polish-out of defects in a freshly cured topcoat (dust nibs, orange peel, runs, overspray) on a shop- or field-coated surface — vehicle body, cabinet, panel or equipment — locating each defect, denibbing with fine abrasive and polishing back to the surrounding finish without burn-through.

sources.title: 3M and GM Partner on First-Ever Robotic Paint Repair System on Moving Assembly Line
sources.claim: 3M's Finesse-it Robotic Paint Repair ... deployed at GM's Spring Hill plant, where a vision system locates topcoat imperfections and robots sand and polish them out on a moving assembly line — i.e., polishing a final coat back to the specified finish.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: sanding and polishing a cured topcoat to an accepted appearance standard, using the same class of abrasives and polishing compounds a painter uses to rub out a finish; performed in a purpose-built robotic line.

sources.title: 3M Finesse-It Robotic Paint Repair System Fixes Paint Defects on Assembly Lines - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The same system autonomously identifies paint defects with its vision system and uses abrasives to sand and polish the imperfections, replacing manual search-and-repair by a person on the automotive line.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (defect denibbing and polish-out of a cured topcoat); establishes that defect location and polish-out is machine-decided rather than hand-guided.

sources.system: Gottschild HBS 1600/1800/2200/2600 polishing and sanding machines
sources.title: Polishing Buffing Sanding Machines for high gloss Furniture Components | Gottschild GmbH
sources.claim: Gottschild HBS machines are fully automatic sanding and polishing systems that polish lacquered high-gloss furniture fronts and wall panels (and Corian, glass, metals) to a mirror finish, with automatic part size and height detection.
sources.transferJustification: Same task on the same materials a painter polishes (cured lacquer on wood-composite doors, fronts and wall panels), but with the workpiece presented to the machine rather than installed in the building.

sources.title: Panels Polishing Machine | Cefla Finishing
sources.claim: Cefla's Smartgloss is a production polishing machine for lacquered panels (white, black or pastel), used in wood/furniture finishing lines to bring a cured lacquer coat to high gloss.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (polishing a cured lacquer topcoat to a specified gloss) on flat panels/doors of the kind a painter finishes, in a conveyor-fed finishing line.

sources.title: Acme Robotic Metal Finishing Solutions / Robotic Polishing Machine
sources.claim: Acme Manufacturing builds robotic polishing and buffing cells used by high-volume producers in which custom surface finishes and scratch patterns are produced and repeated consistently on complex part geometries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic buffing/polishing of metal parts and coated hardware to a specified finish with force-controlled abrasive heads — the same buffing motion, compounds and finish-uniformity acceptance criteria used when a painter polishes coated metalwork or equipment.

tasks.label: Cut stencils and brush or spray lettering or decorations on surfaces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Parking-lot pavement work at a commercial/institutional property: laying out and spraying stencilled handicap symbols, directional arrows, 'FIRE LANE'/'NO PARKING' legends and stall numbers on asphalt or concrete, working around parked cars in daylight, using traffic paint and reusable stencils.

Inside a warehouse, distribution center or plant: brushing/spraying safety and wayfinding markings on the concrete floor — aisle labels, bay and rack numbers, hazard symbols, 'KEEP CLEAR' text — with taped or cut stencils during a production-off shift.

Stencilled identification lettering and numbers on equipment and fixed assets at an industrial or institutional site: pipe and tank service labels, door/room numbers, dumpster and utility-box markings, curb address numbers — small character sets on flat, curved and vertical surfaces, often from ladders.

Occupied private home: cutting a mylar/cardboard stencil or laying out a freehand design, then brushing/spraying a decorative border, accent motif, child's-room mural or house-number graphic on an interior wall, working around furniture, trim, corners and older uneven plaster/drywall.

Commercial building interior or exterior wall: hand-lettered or stencilled signage, a company logo, wayfinding text or a decorative feature wall in a retail store, restaurant, office, school or gym, on prepared flat drywall, block, stucco or brick within reach of a ladder or low lift.

Public roadway under traffic control: stencilling pavement legends such as 'STOP', 'ONLY', 'BUS ONLY', school-zone text, bike symbols and turn arrows on live city streets with a cone taper and flaggers.

sources.developer: RoadPrintz Inc. (Case Western Reserve University spin-off)
sources.title: Revolutionizing road safety: RoadPrintz puts groundbreaking robotic pavement-marking system to use across Cleveland
sources.claim: RoadPrintz's truck-mounted robotic arm applies pavement markings — turn arrows, bike symbols, 'bus only' legends, school-zone markings, crosswalks — with computer-controlled vector strokes instead of hand stencils, and has painted handicap spots and parking lines at two Cleveland MetroParks lots plus legends on Cleveland streets.

sources.title: RoadPrintz Enhances Road Safety and Efficiency with Automated Street Marking System
sources.claim: RoadPrintz's commercial product Electra applies traffic markings, legends and symbols traditionally hand-stencilled, using an industrial robotic arm and software that maps placement onto the pavement while operators remain in the cab.

sources.title: TinyLineMarker Sport | Precision Robotics for Sports Fields
sources.claim: TinyMobileRobots' TinyLineMarker Sport is a GPS-guided robot that paints automatically from tablet-loaded templates, adds custom logos, emblems and lettering, and works on asphalt as well as turf.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous paint application of lettering, numbers and logos onto ground surfaces from a digital template. Same medium (line-marking/traffic paint), same character-and-symbol geometry and comparable placement precision as pavement stencil work; the manufacturer states asphalt and parking-lot use.

sources.title: Turf Tank launches new line-marking robot for sports fields
sources.claim: Turf Tank Two, an autonomous GPS line-marking robot in wide use at US schools and clubs, paints fields autonomously after a few setup points and includes text and logo functionality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous spraying of lettering, numbers and logo artwork onto a ground surface at an institution-controlled facility; the painting, layout and paint media are the same as stencilled pavement/floor lettering.

sources.title: HP SitePrint Autonomous Robotic Layout Solution Leverages HP's Multi Jet Fusion 3D Printing...
sources.claim: HP SitePrint is a commercially available autonomous robot that prints lines, points, arcs and text directly onto building slabs, navigating by robotic total station with obstacle avoidance, using inks offered in permanent or semi-permanent durability for indoor and outdoor surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of text and symbols onto interior concrete floors. Same surfaces and character sizes as stencilled floor labels/bay numbers; positioning is by total station so it works indoors, and permanent inks are offered.

sources.title: wallPen [EN] – Frequently Asked Questions
sources.claim: The wallPen is a commercial direct-to-wall printer that moves itself along vertical surfaces on a ... wheeled platform under laser-sensor control, compensating for uneven floors and up to 10 cm of wall irregularity, printing UV-cured images on plaster, wallpaper, latex paint, brick, wood, metal and tile.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine application of decorations, murals and lettering directly onto finished wall surfaces, replacing cut stencils and brush/spray artwork; the manufacturer notes prints need no foils or stencils and adhere to the same substrates painters decorate.

sources.title: The WallPen: An Unhoused Plotter That Can Print Murals on Anything - Core77
sources.claim: Independent trade coverage confirms the WallPen as a working direct-to-wall digital printer producing murals on many building substrates, suitable for indoor or outdoor use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying decorative artwork and typography onto walls by machine rather than by cut stencil and brush; output is the same visual deliverable on the same wall substrates.

sources.system: Autonomous field/traffic marking robots with RoboTRAFFIC RTS paint
sources.developer: US Specialty Coatings (USSC Products), with robot OEMs
sources.title: Robot Traffic Paint Concrete & Asphalt | RoboTRAFFIC RTS by USSC
sources.claim: A US traffic-paint supplier that also deals autonomous marking robots reports that warehouses, distribution centers, parking facilities and manufacturing plants are using the same marking robots with ready-to-spray traffic paint on concrete and asphalt.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic spraying of durable traffic paint markings on indoor concrete and parking-lot asphalt; establishes that the same marking robots that paint text and logos are operated inside institution-controlled facilities and parking lots.

sources.title: Overspray-free painting: high-tech paint application | Automotive Manufacturing Solutions
sources.claim: Dürr's EcoPaintJet Pro paint robot applies decorative design elements such as contrasting stripes and custom graphics with sharp edges onto complex vehicle surfaces fully automatically inside a production paint booth, with no masking or stencils.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic spray application of sharp-edged decorative graphics onto a fixtured workpiece in a fenced booth — the same act as spraying stencilled decorations/lettering, at equal or better edge precision, when the item is brought to the machine.

sources.developer: Baroudi et al., King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals
sources.title: Development of an Autonomous Robot for Precision Floor Marking (Robotics, MDPI)
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed prototype mobile robot autonomously draws letters, signage and decorative patterns on indoor floors while avoiding obstacles, without external localization infrastructure, with millimetre-level repeatability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous marking of letters, signage and decorative patterns on indoor floors — the same deliverable as stencilled floor lettering, though with a plotting pen rather than traffic paint.

roles.title: Paperhangers
roles.description: Cover interior walls or ceilings of rooms with decorative wallpaper or fabric, or attach advertising posters on surfaces such as walls and billboards. May remove old materials or prepare surfaces to be papered.

tasks.label: Place strips or sections of paper on surfaces, aligning section edges and patterns.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied existing private home: hang patterned wallpaper with a straight or drop repeat in a dining room, bedroom or powder room; furniture moved and covered, strips cut and scribed to baseboards, crown molding, door casings, windows and outlets, with pattern matched at every seam and inside/outside corners.

Existing home, room emptied and walls prepped: plain, textured, grasscloth or random-match covering hung on straight, flat, unobstructed wall runs (e.g., a single accent wall), ceiling-to-baseboard, standard 8–9 ft height.

New residential construction or gut renovation: uniform, largely non-repeating wallcovering applied over bare, freshly prepped drywall in an empty unit on a builder-controlled site, before trim and fixtures are installed.

Commercial fit-out in an institution-controlled building (hotel guestroom, office suite, clinic exam room): random-match Type II vinyl wallcovering on long, flat, unobstructed wall runs in empty rooms, standard layouts and heights, work scheduled by the facility.

Commercial job with sequenced digital murals or patterned wallcovering, and corridors/lobbies dense with door frames, sconces, columns, soffits and ceilings; panels must be hung in numbered sequence and matched across walls while the building is partly occupied.

Bill posting: pasting paper poster sections onto an outdoor billboard face or an exterior/interior wall, aligning the section edges and image across sheets, working from a catwalk or ladder in outdoor weather.

sources.system: 墙纸铺贴机器人 (Wallpaper laying robot)

sources.claim: An English distributor page for the same robot describes automatic navigation, automatic paving and automatic edge cutting, with multi-sensor fusion and laser calibration for laying accuracy and about 3x human productivity.

tasks.label: Smooth strips or sections of paper with brushes or rollers to remove wrinkles and bubbles and to smooth joints.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Repapering a standard room in an occupied or renovated private house/apartment: worker hangs pasted or prepasted strips on flat wall runs and immediately works them down with a smoothing brush/plastic smoother from center outward, expelling air and wrinkles, then rolls butt seams; furniture pushed to room center, older uneven plaster/drywall, outlets, baseboards and door casings to work around.

Commercial fit-out or refurbishment inside a facility (hotel guest rooms and corridors, offices, healthcare, restaurants): heavy 54" vinyl wallcovering or commercial paper on freshly prepared drywall, long straight floor-to-ceiling runs, smoothed with broad knife/smoother and seam-rolled; premises controlled by the owner/GC, work scheduled around occupancy.

Overhead and awkward-access work: papering ceilings, soffits, dormers, and tall stairwell walls from ladders, planks or scaffolds; strips must be supported and brushed out flat while gravity pulls them, joints smoothed with the worker in an unstable posture.

Delicate/specialty coverings on feature walls in high-end homes and hospitality: pattern-matched murals in numbered panels, grasscloth, silk, foils and hand-printed papers that mark, burnish or stretch; strips smoothed with a soft brush only, seams butted and eased into alignment without a roller.

New-construction or model-unit work: empty, cleared, standardized rooms with freshly prepared flat drywall; repetitive full-height strips laid one after another on long straight walls, smoothed down and seams closed with roller/brush in production fashion.

Poster/bill work: pasting paper poster sections onto a billboard face outdoors from a catwalk or ladder, or onto interior poster boards/panels; overlapping sections are brushed out to remove wrinkles and blisters and to blend the joints, often in wind and changing light.

sources.system: "墙纸铺贴机器人" (wallpaper laying robot), Guangdong Bozhilin / Bright Dream Robotics
sources.developer: Guangdong Bozhilin Robot Co., Ltd. (Bright Dream Robotics, Country Garden)
sources.title: 碧桂园集团：探索技术创新 推进智能建造 (People's Daily report, via Sina Finance)
sources.claim: Bright Dream Robotics' (Bozhilin) wallpaper-laying robot worked autonomously on a real residential project, following operator-issued instructions and a pre-planned work path to lay wallpaper during the interior decoration phase, alongside other finishing robots under a multi-machine scheduling system.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: the robot lays wallpaper strips onto interior walls, which necessarily includes pressing/rolling each strip down; the smoothing pass is the robot's laying action itself.

sources.system: Wallpaper laying robot (ProBuild Robotics construction robot line)
sources.developer: ProBuild Robotics (distributor of Chinese construction robots)
sources.title: Wallpaper laying robot – ProBuild Robotics
sources.claim: A commercially offered wallpaper-laying robot integrates wallpaper conveying, gluing, ... and laying with automatic navigation and paving, and uses constant-force paving to press strips down without bubbles or hollows, for interior decoration projects in residences, apartments and office buildings.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the rated task: constant-force paving is the machine equivalent of brushing/rolling a strip down to expel air, and the spec claims verticality and splicing (joint) accuracy.
