sources.claim: Fully automatic panel laminating lines feed rigid wall/ceiling boards on conveyors, apply adhesive, unwind the covering material and press it onto the board pneumatically/with multi-stage rollers, then cut it, producing bubble-free decorative surfaces without manual smoothing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bonding a decorative sheet covering to a wall/ceiling board. With the workpiece fixtured and conveyed to the machine (the E1 counterfactual), roller/pneumatic pressing performs exactly the wrinkle- and bubble-removal that hand brushing performs on a hung strip.

sources.system: Full Automatic PVC Laminating Machine for gypsum plasterboard / ceiling board (panel wrapping line)
sources.title: Full Automatic PVC Laminating Machine for Gypsum Plasterboard Ceiling Board
sources.claim: Panel wrapping/laminating production lines apply paper (as well as vinyl and metal foil) to wall and ceiling panels used in interior decoration, with roller pressing on a continuous automatic line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying paper covering to interior wall/ceiling panels. Confirms the medium (paper, not only plastic film) is handled bubble-free by machine when the substrate is presented to the line.

tasks.label: Staple or tack advertising posters onto fences, walls, billboards, or poles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wild posting / street bill posting: a crew works a route of city blocks, stapling stacks of paper posters onto plywood construction hoardings, scaffold barricades and boarded storefronts along public sidewalks; surfaces vary in height, texture and condition, pedestrians and traffic pass by, weather and torn existing posters must be dealt with, work done from the ground or a step ladder.

Billboard/poster panel posting: an outdoor-advertising bill poster climbs a ladder or catwalk on a roadside 30-sheet poster panel or wall-mounted board, hangs and aligns paper sections with paste and tacks/staples along edges and battens, at height in wind and sun; access and ground conditions differ at every structure.

Poles, posts and fences: tacking or stapling event, political or promotional placards onto wooden utility poles, sign posts, chain-link and wooden fences and kiosks around neighborhoods and roadsides; each object is a different diameter and material, in an as-found public setting.

Posters inside a controlled facility: posting advertising posters and cardboard placards on interior walls, corkboards, columns and standard frames in retail stores, malls, transit stations, campuses, arenas and trade-show halls; fixed layout, premises controlled by the operator, standard mounting points.
Shop prefabrication: in a sign/print shop, mounting and stapling posters onto rigid backer boards, stretcher frames, A-frames or panel faces on a bench before they are taken out and hung.

sources.title: MHP Ultra | fully automatic | MH+P Technology GmbH | canvas production
sources.claim: The MHP ULTRA is a commercial, fully automatic machine that stretches a printed canvas sheet over a wooden/MDF frame and staples it on all four sides at production speed, with an optional loading module ... operator-free running.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stapling a large limp printed sheet onto a rigid wooden backing. The objects (printed sheet, wood substrate), the tool (staple gun) and the tensioning/edge-placement precision match stapling a poster onto a board, but only with the workpiece fixtured and fed as a purpose-built cell would present it (E1).

sources.system: Certis modular self-loading staple guns for robot applications
sources.title: Self-loading modular devices - Easy to assemble modular staplers for automation projects
sources.claim: Industrial staple guns are built specifically for mounting on robot arms, with automatic self-refilling stations and electronic monitoring of each staple, and are used in panel, furniture, fencing and prefab production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic stapling of sheet material to timber substrates (fencing, panels, prefab elements) in fenced production cells; the fastening action, fastener and materials are those of tacking a poster to a board or fence panel.

sources.title: Automation - Robotic Nail Gun, Staple Gun, Screw Gun Systems
sources.claim: Integrators supply robotic nailing, stapling and screw-driving cells and retrofit collated fastening tools onto existing production lines for timber-frame, house and pallet manufacture.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated driving of staples/nails into timber workpieces in purpose-built cells; establishes that the fastening step of poster tacking is routinely automated when the work is fixtured and presented.

sources.title: Robotic Label Applicator | Signode
sources.claim: A vision-guided robot arm picks a freshly printed label and applies it to a determined position on a product in an industrial cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking a printed flexible sheet and applying it at a specified position on a surface; covers the pick-place-and-align half of poster hanging, demonstrated only inside a fenced industrial cell.

sources.title: Okibo, Provider in Drywall Finishing Robotics, Launches U.S. Headquarters | Walls & Ceilings
sources.claim: Autonomous construction robots work on interior walls of real jobsites (spraying plaster, sanding, painting) without site preparation, but the demonstrated field capability is surface coating, not handling large limp sheets or driving fasteners into varied vertical surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous work on vertical wall surfaces in unstructured sites; cited to bound the E3 judgment — it sprays and sands rather than aligning and stapling posters, so it does not substantiate completion of this task at E3.

tasks.label: Measure surfaces or review work orders to estimate the quantities of materials needed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied, furnished private home: paperhanger walks the client's rooms (living room, dining room, bedroom, stairwell or an accent wall), measures wall widths and ceiling heights with tape/laser, deducts doors, windows and built-ins, notes pattern repeat and drop match, and computes rolls plus primer/adhesive. Furniture, art, drapes and pets are present; walls are out of plumb and layouts vary house to house.

Residential or commercial interior at the construction/renovation stage: empty rooms at drywall-finish stage on a contractor's jobsite, with dust, ladders, other trades and partially finished surfaces. Worker measures wall and ceiling surfaces room by room and estimates wallcovering quantities for the scope.

Finished, operating commercial facility (hotel guest rooms and corridors, office suite, clinic, restaurant) managed by an institution: measure a typical repeated room, verify a few others, multiply across the count of rooms, and compute vinyl wallcovering yardage, borders and adhesive for the job.

Desk/shop review: no on-site measuring. Worker reviews a work order, finish schedule, or contractor drawings that already carry dimensions, and calculates quantities (single-roll/bolt counts, yardage, waste allowance, pattern repeat, dye-lot ordering) for the order.

Outdoor advertising work: measure a billboard face, transit panel, or exterior wall for poster sheets or vinyl banner, at roadside or on a building exterior, with weather, traffic and access constraints; determine the number of poster sheets/panel size needed.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7 finishing robot is a fully autonomous, AI-guided drywall-finishing and painting robot commercially active on major construction sites, having covered over 1 million sq ft in Europe before its 2025 US launch.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous wall/ceiling finishing. To plan its coating passes the robot must itself measure the wall and ceiling surfaces it faces (same objects and same interior settings a paperhanger measures); a materials quantity follows arithmetically from the measured area and the product's coverage/roll dimensions.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The same robot builds its own dimensioned 3D model of the walls and ceilings on arrival, with no site preparation, markers, measurement tools or BIM input required.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-site 3D scanning for autonomous plastering/painting. Zero-prep in-situ surface measurement of interior walls is the measuring half of this task, performed in the same unstructured interior construction settings and at the millimetre-scale precision wallcovering takeoff needs.

sources.system: Spot + Leica BLK ARC (Orbit mission control)
sources.title: Maintain Accurate Digital Twins with Autonomous Reality Capture | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot carries the Leica BLK ARC laser-scanning module and runs repeatable autonomous scanning missions that document site conditions in plants, warehouses ..., producing point clouds used for BIM/digital twins.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous as-built reality capture inside operating buildings. The deliverable is a dimensionally accurate model of interior wall surfaces, from which wall areas and finish-material quantities are computed — the same measurement product a paperhanger produces with a tape measure.

sources.system: Trimble X7 + FieldLink on Boston Dynamics Spot
sources.title: Trimble Releases Turnkey Autonomous Robotic Scanning Solution for Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot | For Construction Pros
sources.claim: Trimble's turnkey X7 laser scanner integration with Spot enables autonomous scanning operation on construction sites, with scans registered to the project coordinate system and composited into point clouds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: jobsite laser scanning for progress/quantity verification. It establishes that a robot can autonomously traverse an unstructured interior jobsite and capture survey-accurate surface geometry — the measuring step this task requires before quantities are computed.

sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / Trimble, operated by Mace
sources.title: How one construction contractor is using Spot the Robot Dog | Equipment World
sources.claim: Contractor Mace deployed a Spot unit ('Setanta') that autonomously roamed a building under construction and laser-scanned it three or more times a week, with the scans processed in Trimble software into reports compared against the BIM model.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous as-built scanning and automated comparison of measured geometry against the model. This is the same measure-then-compute-quantities pipeline, on real building interiors, at production reliability in a contractor's workflow.

sources.title: AI Startup Using Robots and Lidar to Boost Productivity on Construction Sites - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Doxel's autonomous lidar-equipped robots scan construction sites daily, and its software automatically tracks what has been installed against the plan, turning robot-captured geometry into quantity/progress measures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic quantity/progress takeoff. It shows the full chain — robot measures the space, software derives installed quantities against the plan — which is the same chain needed to convert measured wall surfaces (or drawing dimensions) into material quantities.

sources.title: Skydio 3D Scan | Autonomous Drone Flights for 3D Mapping | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio 3D Scan lets Skydio drones autonomously plan and execute the full data-capture flight around a structure, yielding inspection-grade 3D models and maps that teams measure from.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous exterior structure scanning for inspection. Measuring the face of an outdoor billboard or exterior wall to size poster sheets is the same act — autonomous capture of a flat exterior surface's dimensions — on comparable outdoor structures.

tasks.label: Check finished wallcoverings for proper alignment, pattern matching, and neatness of seams.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential job: after hanging patterned wallpaper in a living room, bedroom or dining room of an occupied or newly built home, the paperhanger walks the walls, views seams in raking daylight and lamp light, checks pattern match at butt seams, corners, ceiling line and baseboard, runs a hand or seam roller over each seam to feel for lifted edges, and flags bubbles, gaps, overlaps and paste squeeze-out before the room is accepted by the homeowner.

Commercial/hospitality/healthcare job: vinyl or Type II wallcovering in hotel guestrooms and corridors, offices, or clinic walls; repeat-unit walkthrough with a superintendent or designer, checking butt seams for gaps/overlap, pattern drop repeat across the run, alignment around door frames and corner guards, and seam adhesion; results recorded on a punch list.

High or awkward areas on the same jobs: ceilings, stairwell walls, above cabinets, soffits, and cutouts around outlets, switches and trim; the check is made both close-up from a ladder or plank scaffold and from the floor at a distance, in poor or uneven light.

Specialty/high-end materials: sequenced scenic murals, grasscloth, silk or fabric, hand-printed and metallic papers; the check covers panel sequence and registration across joins, acceptable seam visibility and colour/batch shading variation between adjacent strips, judged against a designer's or client's expectations.

Large-format graphics and posters: retail wall graphics, event murals, and billboard poster panels applied outdoors or in public retail space; the check covers panel-to-panel overlap alignment, image continuity across joins, trapped bubbles, and lifted edges, often in wind, sun or traffic conditions.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated appearance inspection of a large finished decorative surface. tasks.label: Trim excess material at ceilings or baseboards, using knives.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied private residence (bedroom, dining room, powder room): after hanging pasted wallpaper, the paperhanger creases the strip into the ceiling and baseboard junctions with a broad/smoothing knife and slices the excess off with a fresh razor blade, working off a stepladder over moved furniture and drop cloths; the ceiling line is often out of level and the cut must not score the painted ceiling or nick the wood base.

New-construction or gut-renovation single-family/multifamily unit, unoccupied, under general-contractor control: vinyl or paper wallcovering trimmed at the ceiling line and at the floor/base line, sometimes before base trim is set; dusty active jobsite, other trades present, variable lighting and wall conditions.

Hotel guestroom or hospitality renovation program: dozens of near-identical rooms, Type II vinyl wallcovering, trimmed at ceiling/crown and above the base and around door casings; owner controls access, layout repeats room to room, rooms taken out of service on a schedule.

Occupied commercial/institutional interior (corporate office, clinic corridor, school, retail store): commercial wallcovering trimmed at the ceiling grid/soffit line and at rubber or wood base, usually after hours, with existing finishes, furniture and equipment that must not be damaged.

Specialty/difficult work: grasscloth, silk or fabric wallcovering, murals and borders in historic homes or high-end residences; wavy plaster, sloped/vaulted or coffered ceilings, curved walls and ornate moldings, where excess must be cut to an irregular line in delicate material that tears or marks easily.

tasks.label: Mix paste, using paste powder and water, and brush paste onto surfaces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied private home, one room or feature wall: worker mixes a bucket of paste powder with water to the specified consistency, then rolls/brushes paste onto the wall one strip-width at a time (paste-the-wall) or onto strips on a folding table set up among furniture; must cover to ceiling line, baseboards, corners and around outlets, with paper hung within the paste's open time.

Vacant new-build or gut-renovation interior (contractor-controlled, empty rooms, dusty floors, other trades present): mix paste with a drill mixer or bagged mix, apply paste over large plain wall/ceiling areas for lining paper or whole-room papering, then edges and corners by brush.

Commercial fit-out inside an operating institution (hotel corridor, office suite, clinic, retail): heavy vinyl or fabric wallcovering; prepare clay or vinyl-over-vinyl adhesive, run goods through a hand-fed pasting machine in a staged room or roll paste on the wall, brush paste at seams, edges and cut-outs, working around occupants and finished floors.

Detail and small-area pasting: borders, patch repairs, re-pasting lifted seams and corners, ceilings, soffits, pieces around windows, switches and pipework; small quantities of paste mixed in a pail and applied with a brush or small roller, often at height on a ladder.

Outdoor bill posting: mix wheat/poster paste with water, brush paste onto poster sections and onto the billboard face or kiosk panel from a catwalk, ladder or truck, in wind, sun or cold, at a roadside or street location.

tasks.label: Apply adhesives to the backs of paper strips, using brushes, or dunk strips of prepasted wallcovering in water, wiping off any excess adhesive.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential home: hanging standard unpasted paper or non-woven wallpaper in a bedroom or dining room. The worker sets a pasting table amid furniture, lays each cut strip face down, rolls or brushes paste evenly over the back to the edges, wipes stray paste off the face and table, and books the strip.

Residential home: prepasted wallcovering. The worker loosely rolls each cut strip, submerges it in a water tray for about 15 seconds, draws it out slowly under the tray rod to activate the paste and wipe off excess water and adhesive, then books it.

Commercial job (hotel corridor, office, hospital, retail): heavy Type II vinyl or wide commercial wallcovering at high strip volume. Rolls are run through a pasting machine or paste is rolled on at a staging table set up in a corridor or empty room; excess is wiped and strips are booked or hung immediately.

Upscale residence or hospitality space: textured specialty goods (grasscloth, string cloth, suede, burlap, heavy embossed vinyl). Paste is applied uniformly to the back by roller or machine, taking care that no paste reaches the textured face.

Delicate goods: silk, foil/mylar, hand-printed or antique-reproduction murals. Paste must be brushed on by hand with controlled moisture (or applied to the wall instead), with no staining, creasing or stretching of the fragile face.

Bill posting / poster work: printed poster sections for a billboard face, construction hoarding or interior poster panel. Wheat paste is brushed from a bucket onto the backs of the sheets and/or the surface, outdoors on a catwalk or at street level, in wind and variable weather.

tasks.label: Apply thinned glue to waterproof porous surfaces, using brushes, rollers, or pasting machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied, furnished residential room (living/dining/bedroom) being redecorated: walls patched and sanded, furniture pushed to center and covered, finished floors, baseboard/casing and outlets in place; worker rolls thinned glue/wallcovering size over plaster or drywall and cuts in at trim, corners and ceiling line with a brush without dripping on trim or floors.

Bare, empty room in a new-build or gut-renovated home: unfurnished drywall or plaster walls and ceiling, no finish flooring or fixtures yet; sizing/thinned glue rolled or sprayed over the full wall and ceiling field before hanging.

Commercial fit-out on an active construction site (hotel guestrooms and corridors, offices, healthcare, restaurants): large repetitive areas of new drywall sized/primed with roller or pasting-machine-fed adhesive before vinyl wallcovering; other trades working nearby, materials and debris on the deck.

Refresh of an in-service commercial facility after hours (hotel corridor or lobby, retail store, office suite): carpet and furnishings, sconces, door frames and signage in place; old covering stripped, walls washed, then thinned glue applied by roller and brush with full masking and floor protection.

Tight and awkward detail areas within a job: closet interiors, stairwell walls and soffits, arched or curved surfaces, behind radiators and pipes, small powder rooms, around cabinetry and switch boxes — brush-applied thinned glue in confined, irregular spaces.

Outdoor billposting/poster work: applying thinned paste with a brush or roller to a porous billboard face, plywood hoarding or masonry wall from a catwalk, ladder or lift, in wind, sun and street conditions before the poster sheets are hung.

tasks.label: Fill holes, cracks, and other surface imperfections preparatory to covering surfaces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied, furnished private home: before hanging paper in a dining room, bedroom or feature wall, the worker spot-fills scattered nail and picture-hanger holes, small hairline cracks and dents in existing painted or previously papered drywall with spackle/joint compound, feathers with a knife, sands and dusts. Furniture is pushed to the room's center under drop cloths; floors and trim must not be soiled.

Vacant or under-renovation home (older house, whole rooms): after stripping old wallpaper the worker faces torn drywall face paper, glue residue, plaster settlement cracks, gouges and fist-size holes; cracks are raked out and taped, holes backed and patched in multiple coats, then walls skimmed and sanded room by room.

Commercial new-build or fit-out interior (hotel guest rooms and corridors, offices, healthcare, retail): large open gypsum-board wall areas to be covered with vinyl wallcovering; the worker fills seams, fastener dimples, dings and scrapes left by other trades, skims to a Level 4/5 standard and sands the surface smooth over hundreds of square feet.

Tall and overhead surfaces in commercial spaces: lobby and atrium walls above 10 ft, corridor soffits and ceilings prepared before wallcovering or mural application, worked from lifts or scaffold; large uninterrupted planes, filling and sanding of seams, dings and rough spots.

Intricate or obstructed areas on any job: filling and sanding around door and window casings, chair rails and wainscot, electrical outlets and switch boxes, inside closets and stairwells, on curved or paneled feature walls and in inside/outside corners, where knife work must feather to trim edges without damaging finished millwork.

Outdoor advertising and display work: preparing a billboard or sign face or a semi-exterior display panel before posting — filling panel joints, gouges, delaminated spots and fastener holes on plywood/metal faces and smoothing them, exposed to weather and traffic.

tasks.label: Mark vertical guidelines on walls to align strips, using plumb bobs and chalk lines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied private residence: paperhanger papers a bedroom, dining room or accent wall. After prepping, he finds a starting point near a corner, drops a plumb bob or holds a level/laser, and snaps or pencils a vertical guideline, then repeats a line every strip width around the room, working around out-of-plumb corners, furniture pushed to the center, baseboards, switch plates and window/door casings.

Residential difficult geometry: two-story stairwell walls, sloped dormer or knee walls, small powder rooms crowded with fixtures, or ceilings. Guidelines must be marked from ladders, planks or scaffold, at heights of 12-20 ft, on surfaces that are rarely square or plumb, with tight access.

Finished, institution-controlled commercial interior (hotel guest rooms and corridors, offices, clinic exam rooms, restaurant): repetitive rooms of standard 8-10 ft height and known layout, controlled access and lighting, vinyl wallcovering. Worker marks a plumb start line in each room and successive lines at strip width, often with a laser level plus pencil marks.

Active construction or renovation jobsite (multifamily building, tenant fit-out, model home): freshly primed drywall, other trades working nearby, dust, temporary lighting, unfinished floors. Worker lays out plumb guidelines on many walls per day, coordinating starting points with the wallcovering pattern and room features.

Outdoor advertising / large-format posters: marking vertical alignment guidelines on a billboard face, wall mural surface, or transit/mall poster panel so multi-section paper posters align, worked from a catwalk, lift or ladder, in wind and variable weather.

sources.system: WEINMANN WALLTEQ M-500 multifunction bridge (marking ballpoint pen / marking inkjet printer units)
sources.date: 2024-08 (brochure); product line in commercial use for years
sources.title: WEINMANN WALLTEQ multifunction bridges (product brochure, EN 2024-08)
sources.claim: The WEINMANN WALLTEQ multifunction bridge is a CNC gantry that runs over a wall element clamped on the work table in a prefabricated wall-panel line and performs marking with a ballpoint-pen unit or inkjet marking printer (as well as sawing, drilling, labeling) on materials including gypsum plasterboard, i.e. it draws accurately positioned guide lines on a wall surface presented to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: CNC layout marking of wall elements in prefab panel factories. Transfer holds because the object is the same (a flat wall surface, including gypsum board), the output is the same kind of straight, precisely located guide line drawn in pen/ink to align subsequent material, and CNC gantry placement tolerance is far tighter than the few-millimetre accuracy of a snapped chalk line; it occurs exactly in the E1 configuration where the wall is fixtured and presented to the machine.

sources.title: HP SitePrint - Robotic Layout Solution | HP Official Site
sources.claim: HP SitePrint is a deployed autonomous layout robot that prints lines, points, curves and text from BIM/CAD onto construction surfaces at about +/-2 mm layout accuracy, used on real projects (medical center interior wall layout, Vancouver airport, residential buildings) - but it is a wheeled robot that marks floors/slabs, not vertical wall surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated construction layout marking. It shows machine line-marking at better-than-chalk-line accuracy is deployed, but only on horizontal floors; it cannot mark plumb guidelines on a standing wall, so it supports no positive judgment for this task in situ.

sources.title: Jaibot - Hilti Corporation (media release)
sources.claim: The Hilti Jaibot, the main in-situ marking robot deployed in buildings, drills and marks drill points from BIM data on ceilings (and, since 2022, concrete walls), but it is navigated between work positions by a worker with a remote control and its marking output is trade-coded hole points, not continuous plumb guidelines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: BIM-driven marking/drilling of points on building surfaces in situ. Cited to show the limits of in-situ marking robots (operator-steered, point marking, overhead/concrete), which is why no positive E2/E3 judgment is made.

sources.title: Canvas | Drywall Finishing Robot
sources.claim: Canvas's drywall finishing machine works on in-place interior walls and ceilings on commercial construction sites using a Universal Robots arm on a mobile lift, delivering Level 4/5 finishes - showing robotic work on standing walls exists, but its output is a sprayed and sanded surface, not layout lines, and it is operator-set-up/semi-autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic surface work on in-place vertical walls. Cited for the negative: the deployed wall-working robots perform coating/sanding at coverage tolerances and do not produce plumb layout lines, so they do not substantiate completion of this marking task in situ.

tasks.label: Remove old paper, using water, steam machines, or solvents and scrapers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied single-family home: strip dated wallpaper from a bedroom, living room or hallway. Worker masks floors/trim, moves furniture, scores the paper, applies hot steam or solvent, waits for penetration, scrapes sheets and backing off drywall or plaster around outlets, switches, baseboards and inside corners without gouging the substrate, then washes off paste residue and bags wet debris.

Private-home bathroom or kitchen: strip vinyl or foil wallpaper in a tight wet room, working around vanity, toilet, tub surround, tile edges, mirrors, cabinets and appliances; multiple painted-over layers common, limited working space, ladder work over fixtures.

Hotel guest rooms or senior-living/healthcare rooms during a phased renovation: repeated identical rooms in a facility the owner controls, commercial vinyl wallcovering pulled from the face and the paper backing steamed/soaked off gypsum board, corridors and rooms turned over on a schedule with dust and noise controls.

Commercial office, retail or institutional space under renovation: long straight runs of Type II vinyl wallcovering removed from partition walls and columns on an unoccupied floor, scaffolds or lifts for high walls, adhesive residue washed to leave a paintable/repaperable surface.

Older or historic residence: several layers of paper (some over horsehair plaster or over unprimed drywall), removed slowly with solvent gels and hand scrapers to avoid destroying fragile plaster, ornamental trim, or the drywall face paper; frequent judgment calls about when to stop and skim-coat instead.

Outdoor advertising: stripping accumulated old paper posters from a billboard face or poster panel before the new sheets are pasted, done from a catwalk or ladder in wind and weather with wet paper peeled and collected.

sources.title: Okibo launches autonomous, AI-guided painting and drywall finishing EG7+ robot - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7/EG7+ is a fully autonomous, AI-guided mobile robot that sands, paints and performs level 4 drywall finishing on construction sites; it was used on a real project in August 2025 and nationally launched in December 2025. It performs additive/abrasive wall finishing, not removal of adhered wallpaper.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest deployed wall-surface robot (interior finishing). Transfer to wallpaper removal does NOT hold: the robot sprays compound and sands flat new gypsum surfaces; it has no steam/solvent application, no dwell-and-peel manipulation of wetted sheet material, no paste-residue washdown, and no capability to work in furnished occupied rooms around trim and fixtures.

sources.title: Drywall Finishing Robots Accelerate Construction Schedules - Tech Briefs
sources.claim: Canvas's drywall finishing robot, built on a Universal Robots arm and piloted by a trained worker, sprays and sands drywall to Level 4/5 finishes on commercial construction sites; it addresses surface finishing rather than removal of existing wallcoverings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drywall surface finishing on jobsites. It does not transfer to stripping old paper: the machine is worker-piloted, works on bare new board in empty rooms, and performs no wetting, scraping, peeling, or residue removal on a finished, papered wall.

sources.title: SwRI's Laser Coating Removal Robot wins R&D 100 Award
sources.claim: Robotic laser coating removal systems strip paint and coatings from aircraft inside purpose-built depaint facilities using computer-vision-controlled scanning lasers; this is the closest automated 'remove an old covering' capability, and it exists only for metal/composite aircraft skins in dedicated hangars.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated removal of an old surface covering. Transfer to wallpaper stripping fails: the substrate (aircraft aluminum/composite in a controlled depaint hangar) tolerates laser ablation, whereas paper-faced gypsum and plaster do not; no demonstration exists of paper plus paste being removed from building walls by this or any similar system.

tasks.label: Remove paint, varnish, dirt, and grease from surfaces, using paint remover and water soda solutions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied private home: before hanging paper in a living room or bedroom, wash walls with detergent/soda solution, cut back or strip peeling gloss enamel and old paint edges with chemical remover, rinse and let dry; furniture pushed to center, floors covered, homeowner and pets present, layout and wall condition differ house to house.

Woodwork and trim adjacent to papered areas (door frames, baseboards, chair rails, paneling, doors) in homes and small offices: apply chemical paint/varnish remover, scrape and neutralize/wash, feather edges to a sound surface for papering or repainting; intricate profiles, in-place work.

Commercial/institutional interior kept by an owner-operator (hotel guest rooms and corridors, offices, healthcare, retail): wash and degrease walls, de-gloss or strip old coatings and remove adhesive/dirt residue over large repeatable wall areas before vinyl or fabric wallcovering; standard layouts, controlled access, scheduled work windows.

Heavy-soil areas — kitchen and bath walls/ceilings, restaurant and breakroom walls: remove cooking grease films and nicotine/soot with soda or TSP solution, multiple washes and rinses around cabinets, fixtures, outlets and tile, verifying the surface will take adhesive.

Outdoor advertising surfaces: clean dirt, road film and grease from billboard/bulletin faces, transit shelter and wall poster panels before posting; work from catwalk, ladder or lift on a company-owned standardized structure, weather-exposed.

sources.title: Robot Laser Cleaning Machine | Laserax
sources.claim: Commercial robotic laser cleaning cells strip paint, coatings and oils from workpieces presented to a fixed robot arm in an enclosed industrial cell.
sources.transferJustification: Same operation as the task (removing paint/coatings and oil-grease films from a surface to leave a sound, adhesion-ready substrate), performed on workpieces brought to and fixtured in a purpose-built cell — the E1 form of the task.

sources.system: Dynabrade Automated Cabinet Door Sanding Cell (FerRobotics Active Contact Flange)
sources.title: Dynabrade Automated Cabinet Door Sanding Cell - FerRobotics
sources.claim: A commercial robotic cell sands complete wooden doors, including corners, edges, rails and panels, holding each door in a vacuum fixture with force-controlled abrasive tooling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: abrasive removal of finish/coating from profiled wooden doors and trim held in a fixture. Same objects (doors, rails, profiled woodwork) and same required outcome (finish removed, surface ready to recoat/paper) as the trim-stripping variant of this task, in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Advanced Robotic Laser Coating Removal System (ARLCRS)
sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon NREC with Concurrent Technologies Corporation
sources.title: Laser Coating Removal for Aircraft - NREC
sources.claim: Teams of autonomous mobile robots carrying laser strippers removed paint and coatings from whole aircraft at a US Air Force depot, with operators virtually masking sensitive areas rather than driving the tool.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine removal of aged multi-layer paint from a large fixed workpiece positioned in a dedicated coating-removal facility, substituting for manual chemical/mechanical stripping — the same purpose as this task's stripping step, at the scale of a wall-sized surface.

sources.developer: US Air Force / AFRL Materials and Manufacturing Directorate
sources.title: Robotic Paint Removal System - Mobility Engineering Technology
sources.claim: The Air Force adopted a robotic laser coating removal system that moves a laser-equipped robotic arm over an F-16 mapped to that aircraft, vaporizing paint layer by layer in place of manual/chemical stripping.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production paint stripping of large painted surfaces by a programmed robot in a dedicated facility; demonstrates worker-quality coating removal without damaging the substrate, the core of this task when the work is brought to the machine.

sources.system: Cuda and Alkota automatic aqueous parts washers
sources.title: Parts Washers - Action Cleaning Systems
sources.claim: Automatic aqueous washers strip grease, oil and grime from parts loaded into the machine using hot detergent solution jets, replacing manual scrubbing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated hot detergent (alkaline/soda-type) washing to remove grease and dirt from surfaces loaded into a machine — the degreasing half of this task performed in a purpose-built enclosure.

sources.title: Skyline Robotics deploys Ozmo window cleaning robot in New York City - The Robot Report
sources.claim: A robot-armed window-cleaning system autonomously washes the exterior glass of a 45-storey Manhattan office tower, supervised by one operator on the roof rather than teleoperated stroke by stroke.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing dirt and road/atmospheric film from large flat vertical exterior surfaces at height on an institution-owned, standardized structure using water and detergent — comparable surface, comparable soil, comparable access to cleaning a billboard face before posting.

sources.title: Okibo launches autonomous, AI-guided painting and drywall finishing EG7+ robot - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: The most capable autonomous interior wall robot in commercial use sands and paints drywall on construction sites; it performs no chemical stripping, washing or degreasing and does not work on trim.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the in-situ state of the art: autonomous wall work in buildings today is limited to sanding fresh joint compound and spraying paint, not removing aged paint, varnish, dirt or grease with strippers and soda solutions.

emergingTasks.label: Hang and secure vinyl tarps to billboards.
emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

roles.title: Pipelayers
roles.description: Lay pipe for storm or sanitation sewers, drains, and water mains. Perform any combination of the following tasks: grade trenches or culverts, position pipe, or seal joints.

tasks.label: Grade or level trench bases, using tamping machines or hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Gravity sanitary or storm sewer main in an open street/urban trench inside a trench box: after the excavator rough-cuts, the pipelayer spreads #57 stone or sand bedding, fine-grades it to the laser line and grade (roughly ±1/4 in over the run), knocks down high spots with a shovel/rake, hand-digs bell holes and tamps bedding lifts with a jumping jack or plate compactor. Wet or variable soils, traffic control, adjacent live utilities.

New subdivision or greenfield development mains (storm/sanitary): GPS/laser-guided excavator cuts to grade, pipelayer trims the trench base, places and levels imported bedding and compacts it with a plate compactor before each pipe stick is set. Open ground, varied soils, changing weather, machines and crew working nearby.

Water main, force main or culvert trench in rural roadway or open ground where the pipe beds on the shaped native trench bottom: level the trench base to design depth (no strict slope tolerance), remove rock/high spots, tamp soft spots. Loose grade tolerance (~±0.1 ft), no imported bedding layer required.

Deep trench (8–16 ft) with shoring/trench box: bedding stone placed in lifts and leveled, compacted with a remote-controlled trench roller or excavator-mounted hydraulic plate operated from outside the trench, with laser/grade rod checks by a worker who enters the shored trench to trim the base.

Small-diameter service laterals, yard drains and tie-ins in tight residential settings: hand-dug or mini-excavator slot trench 8–18 in wide, base graded with shovel and grade rod, bed tamped with a hand tamper or small rammer, working around fences, landscaping and existing utilities.

Process/utility pipe trench inside an institution-controlled facility (industrial plant yard, water treatment plant, airport airside, hospital or campus grounds): fixed layout, controlled access, standard equipment; pipelayer levels the trench base and compacts bedding with a plate compactor to spec.

sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem converts standard excavators into fully autonomous trenching ... that dig to a programmed depth and leave a finished, smooth trench floor with stated digging accuracy of 0.1 ft; the company explicitly leaves backfill and compaction to human crews.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous utility-trench excavation. The machine produces the trench base itself — cutting native soil to a design elevation and leaving a smooth floor for buried infrastructure — which is the same physical output as grading/leveling a trench base at loose (±0.1 ft) tolerance. It does not place, screed or tamp imported bedding.

sources.title: Building the Future of Construction — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built's autonomous trenching robots have excavated over ... real energy construction projects in the US and Australia, i.e. open greenfield jobsites, and contractors such as Bechtel have used them for trenching on Texas solar projects.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: field deployment establishes that the autonomous trench cut to design depth is accepted work on unstructured greenfield construction sites, though the deployments are cable trenches rather than pipe with imported bedding.

sources.system: A4CSEL (automated bulldozers, vibratory rollers, dump trucks)
sources.title: A⁴CSEL for DAM | Technology & Services | KAJIMA CORPORATION
sources.claim: Kajima's A4CSEL system runs automated bulldozers (spreading and leveling placed material in layers) and automated vibratory rollers (compacting each layer to spec) together, day and night, in a work area no person may enter, on real dam and erosion-control construction sites since FY2020, supervised remotely by 'IT pilots'.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous layered placement, leveling and compaction of granular fill to a design elevation. Comparable material (sand/gravel fill), comparable objective (level a base and tamp it to spec), and it is done in a machine-only exclusion zone — the E1 mark — though on an open embankment rather than in a narrow trench.

sources.date: 2026-02 (product page); track record at JRA Ritto Training Center
sources.title: Roller Autonomous System -GeoControl Roller- | DeepX
sources.claim: DeepX's GeoControl Roller is a commercially offered retrofit that makes a vibratory roller compact a designated area autonomously with centimeter-level accuracy after an operator specifies area and pass count; the vendor states it is best suited to closed, stable sites and that use on dynamic construction sites is currently limited to automated-construction demonstration sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous compaction of a prepared base to a target elevation. Same tool class as the pipelayer's tamping machine and cm-level precision, but demonstrated on open surfaces at closed/controlled sites, not inside a pipe trench.

sources.system: Trimble Earthworks Grade Control Platform for Autonomous Compactors on Dynapac CA 5000
sources.title: Trimble completes field test of an autonomous compactor | Equipment World
sources.claim: A Dynapac CA 5000 soil ... running Trimble Earthworks for Autonomous Compactors completed 37 hours of real, fully autonomous compaction work on the live Site C dam jobsite alongside operator-run machines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soil compaction on a live earthworks site. Establishes autonomous operation of a compaction machine at worker-accepted quality on real fill, but at embankment scale on open lifts, not in a trench bottom.

sources.title: ROBOTTER® – New sewerage construction technology that requires no workers inside the trench and no trench panels
sources.claim: ROBOTERR is a sewer-construction robot that performs the in-trench work a pipelayer does — levelling the sand bed to ±1 cm respecting design slope and elevation — so no worker enters the trench, but the machine is remote-controlled by an operator rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task (levelling the bedding in a sewer trench), but under continuous remote control, so per the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment; it is cited to show the in-trench fine-grading step has no autonomous implementation.

sources.title: Roadwork Robot Autonomously Digs Out, Repairs, Buried Utility Lines | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: ULC Technologies' Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System excavates over buried utilities in public roadways and compacts the backfill layer by layer with a compactor attachment, but human operators still shovel material back into the hole during the reinstatement step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic excavation and backfill compaction in a public street. Shows a field robot handling soil and a compactor tool in a roadway, but the trial mixes human shovel work with machine compaction and autonomy of the compaction step is not established, so it cannot support a positive field-tier judgment.

tasks.label: Dig trenches to desired or required depths, by hand or using trenching tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-corridor mainline trench: new subdivision street before paving, rural road shoulder, pipeline right-of-way, or cleared site-utility corridor. Excavator digs a 4-10 ft deep trench along a staked/GPS-designed line to required depth and grade, spoil windrowed alongside; trench is opened ahead of the pipe crew, few or no crossing utilities.

Trench in an existing street or congested ROW: saw-cut pavement, traffic control, multiple marked and unmarked crossing utilities (gas, water, telecom, laterals), narrow working width, shoring boxes set as the trench advances; excavator digs short segments to depth while the crew locates and works alongside.
Hand trimming the trench bottom to grade after machine excavation: shoveling out over-dig and loose spoil, cutting the bottom to laser/GPS invert grade for bedding, in a 3-6 ft wide trench.

Hand digging by shovel around obstacles: bell holes at pipe joints, hand-exposing (potholing) marked utility crossings and live services, digging out around existing manholes, valves and fittings, and squaring the trench where a machine cannot safely work.

Residential/commercial service line trench: water or sewer lateral through a yard, driveway or behind a building, using a mini-excavator, walk-behind trencher or hand tools; fences, landscaping, sidewalks, tight access, shallow depth, private property taken as found.

Difficult ground: trenching in rock requiring a hydraulic hammer, high groundwater needing dewatering/well points, unstable or caving soils, or a deep excavation for a manhole/structure where the hole must be benched or boxed.

sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofit converts a standard mid-size excavator into a fully autonomous trenching machine that digs to design depth with stated 1/10 ft accuracy and produces smooth trench floors and clean walls.
sources.transferJustification: Trenching for buried solar DC/AC cable and for pipe is the same physical act — cutting a trench to a designed depth and grade with an excavator bucket in soil — at comparable depths, widths and grade tolerances to sewer/water trench subgrade.

sources.title: Exosystem | Robots in Construction
sources.claim: The Exosystem follows pre-loaded GPS ... and executes the dig-and-grade cycle autonomously with one remote 'Robotic Equipment Operator' supervising several machines; four confirmed customer deployments including pipeline trenching and solar trenching, ~191 linear ft/hr, 93% uptime.
sources.transferJustification: Listed deployments include 'Pipeline trenching (Australia)' — trenches dug for pipe, the pipelayer's own product — so the transfer from cable trenching to pipe trenching is direct.

sources.system: Built Robotics AI Guidance System on 30-36 t excavators (MPC Kinetic fleet)
sources.title: Australian-first autonomous excavators — The Australian Mining Review
sources.claim: Autonomous excavators running Built Robotics' AI guidance have been in production work digging pipeline trenches across Queensland's Surat Basin for contractor MPC Kinetic, following a fully autonomous 30-t excavator trial in late 2019.
sources.transferJustification: This is trench digging for pipe in a greenfield right-of-way — the same output a pipelayer's trench must provide (line, depth, grade) before pipe is lowered in.

sources.system: Built Robotics autonomous excavators (Bechtel solar projects)
sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Moves Earth with Autonomous Excavators | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Trade press reports Bechtel has used Built Robotics autonomous excavators for trenching on utility-scale solar projects in Texas, alongside other autonomous earthmoving equipment on live construction sites.
sources.transferJustification: Independent trade-press confirmation that the autonomous trenching product is used in production on outdoor construction sites, not only in vendor demonstrations.

sources.title: Kawasaki Develops "Autonomous Excavation System for Excavators", Achieved "Autonomous Operation" for Trench Excavation
sources.claim: Kawasaki demonstrated an autonomous excavation system that plans digging from 3D design data and LiDAR terrain sensing and autonomously excavated a 2 m wide, 0.6 m deep, 10 m long trench, and also autonomously leveled the trench floor and performed compaction.
sources.transferJustification: Trench excavation plus autonomous leveling of the trench floor is the machine analogue of trimming a trench bottom to grade, the finishing step pipelayers otherwise do with a shovel.

sources.title: Bedrock Robotics announces autonomous excavation milestone - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics' retrofit autonomy ran excavators on a 130-acre heavy-civil site preparation project with Sundt Construction, removing 65,000 cubic yards, using LiDAR and GPS; the company describes these as supervised-autonomy site tests with fully autonomous customer deployments targeted in 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Mass excavation to design surfaces on an open construction site shows general autonomous earthmoving competence, but it is bulk cut-and-fill rather than trenching to a pipe invert, so it only corroborates the trenching evidence.

sources.title: Power industry first sees robotic excavator | Engineer Live
sources.claim: ULC Technologies' Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System scans for buried assets with GPR, cuts the road surface and performs vacuum excavation over gas mains; it was field-trialed on SGN's network in Epsom, Surrey, but remains a trial/prototype rather than a deployed product.
sources.transferJustification: Closest system to hand-exposing a buried utility in a live street, but it performs small keyhole excavations over gas mains, not a pipelayer's continuous trench, and autonomy/quality in trials is not established.

tasks.label: Cut pipes to required lengths.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Gravity sewer / water main job: cut PVC (SDR-35, C900) pipe to a length measured off the last laid joint, using a handheld cut-off saw or chop saw at the edge of an open trench; muddy, uneven ground, pipe on skids or in the ditch, cut must be square and often chamfered before belling.

Storm drain / culvert job: cut HDPE (solid-wall or dual-wall corrugated) or corrugated metal pipe to length in the field with a hand saw, chainsaw or cut-off saw, typically at a valley cut, headwall or a mitered end section.

Water main job: cut ductile iron pipe to a field-measured length with an abrasive (K12) rotary saw or belly saw, then bevel/grind the spigot end so it will enter the gasketed bell; heavy pipe blocked up beside or inside the trench.

Tie-in / repair: cut an existing, already-installed or in-service main (DI, PVC, AC, clay) in place in the trench to remove a damaged section or make room for a cut-in tee or closure sleeve; confined trench, water present, pipe not removable to a bench.

Cut reinforced concrete or vitrified clay pipe to length at the site with a diamond cut-off saw, chain saw with diamond chain, or snap cutter — e.g., shortening an RCP section at a structure or manhole.

Batch cut-to-length at the laydown yard or shop trailer: several pieces (risers, stubs, casing pieces, hydrant leads) cut from stock pipe to a cut list before being hauled to the trench, working off pipe racks or dunnage.

sources.system: Behringer automatic bandsaw sawing line with robot (plastic pipe)
sources.title: Automatic bandsaw line with robot - Behringer GmbH
sources.claim: Behringer supplies a commercial automatic bandsaw line for plastic pipe in which pipe is loaded onto a transfer roller conveyor, cut-off lengths are entered on a touch control, and the line then feeds, saws, deburrs the end face, sorts and stacks the parts with a robot — i.e. autonomous cut-to-length of plastic pipe inside a purpose-built machine cell.

sources.system: HGG SPC 1200 RB pipe cutting / 3-D profiling machine
sources.title: HGG's SPC 1200 RB pipe cutting/3-D profiling machine offers automated pipe handling
sources.claim: HGG's SPC 1200 RB CNC pipe cutting/profiling machine cuts pipe from 3 to 48 .... diameter and 20-40 ft long to programmed geometry, with automated roller-bed infeed/outfeed conveyors and a floating chuck for accuracy, removing the need to crane individual pipes in and out.

sources.title: Automatic Mitre Bandsaw HBE610-1256GA - Behringer GmbH
sources.claim: Behringer's automatic mitre bandsaws are built for automatic sawing of pipes and profiles in steel and cast materials, with servo saw feed and programmable automatic cutting cycles — the standard purpose-built way heavy metal pipe (including cast/ductile iron) is cut to length in a fixtured cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic cut-to-length sawing of steel and cast-iron pipe stock in a fabrication cell. Same objects (large-diameter metal pipe), same required output (square cut at a specified length), so it carries over to cutting ductile iron water-main pipe when the pipe is presented to the machine.

sources.title: TPC Planetary Cutter for Extrusion Cutting | Conair
sources.claim: Conair's TPC planetary cutter is a commercial automatic machine that cuts extruded plastic tube/pipe to length on a traveling table with a servo clamping system, producing clean square cuts without distortion.

sources.system: BOBO spiral corrugated culvert pipe machine (BTF series)
sources.title: Spiral Corrugated Culvert Pipe Machine – BOBO MACHINE
sources.claim: Spiral corrugated metal culvert pipe forming lines cut the finished pipe to the programmed length automatically on the line with a plasma torch, eliminating offline sawing and inaccurate manual cuts.

sources.system: Elematic Saw E9 precast concrete saw
sources.title: Precast concrete saw E9 | Elematic
sources.claim: The Elematic Saw E9 automatically cuts hardened, steel-prestressed precast concrete elements (hollow-core slabs, piles, T-beams up to 500 mm ...) to the lengths called for by the production plan, on the casting bed in a precast plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic diamond-blade cut-to-length of steel-reinforced concrete elements in a fixtured plant setting. Same material class (reinforced concrete with embedded steel), same tolerance class (cut to a called-out length), so it carries over to shortening reinforced concrete pipe presented on a fixture.

sources.title: Roadwork Robot Autonomously Digs Out, Repairs, Buried Utility Lines | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: ULC Technologies' RRES is an autonomous field robot ... locates buried utilities, cuts a road core and vacuum-excavates over gas mains in public roadways, then backfills and reinstates — the closest demonstrated autonomous cutting work in an unstructured street environment, but it cuts pavement, not pipe to length.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only as a negative bound: it is the most advanced autonomous field system found for buried-utility work, and it cuts road surface and excavates rather than cutting pipe to a required length, so it does not substantiate E3 pipe cutting.

sources.system: Dual-manipulator mobile platform for pipe cutting (nuclear decommissioning)
sources.title: Towards a Cooperative Robotic System for Autonomous Pipe Cutting in Nuclear Decommissioning | IEEE Xplore
sources.claim: Autonomous pipe cutting by a mobile manipulator remains a research problem: the Lancaster/nuclear decommissioning dual-arm system that identifies, grasps and cuts pipes is described as semi-autonomous assisted teleoperation, not autonomous operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting pipe with a mobile manipulator outside a purpose-built cell. It is cited as negative evidence — the system is teleoperated/assisted and laboratory-stage, so it cannot support an E2 or E3 judgment.

tasks.label: Install or use instruments such as lasers, grade rods, or transit levels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Gravity sewer/storm drain in an open street trench: pipelayer mounts a pipe laser in the manhole invert or in the launching pipe on its bracket, dials in the design slope, aims the beam at the target in the first pipe length, then checks the target in each successive pipe as it is laid and adjusts bedding/laser as needed. Muddy, wet invert, traffic and spoil piles alongside.

Grade rod / laser receiver on a grade pole used in and around the trench: worker holds the rod on trench bottom, bedding, pipe invert, or manhole rim while readings are taken or the receiver beeps on grade, calls out cut/fill, and shovels or adds stone to bring the point to grade. Confined trench, unstable footing, arbitrary points on demand.

Tripod instrument setup at the job: pipelayer sets a rotary laser level, builder's level, or transit on a tripod near the trench, levels it, sets it on the benchmark or offset hub, checks calibration, and shoots elevations for the crew; the instrument is moved and re-set as the line advances down the block.

GNSS rover / robotic total station along the route on open ground beside the trench: locating and marking line and offsets for the pipe run, checking manhole and inlet locations and rim/invert elevations against the plan, and recording as-built points.

Grade checking during excavation on a greenfield or wide-corridor job: working with the excavator operator, checking trench depth with a laser receiver on a grade pole or machine-control display as digging proceeds so the bottom reaches design grade before bedding and pipe.

tasks.label: Cover pipes with earth or other materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Municipal open-cut trench in a paved street: after a sanitary/storm sewer or water main is laid, place select embedment (sand or crushed stone) around the pipe haunches and 12 in. over the crown — worker in a shored trench with shovel/rake plus careful bucket work — then backfill spoil or imported aggregate in 8–12 in. lifts, compacting each lift with jumping jack, plate or hoe-pack to a density spec, working around existing utility crossings under traffic control.

Residential/small-commercial service lines and laterals: shallow, narrow trenches through yards, driveways and parkways; mini excavator and hand shovel return sand/spoil around the water or sewer service, hand tamping in lifts near existing gas, electric and irrigation lines, landscaping and fences, finished back to grade for restoration.

Greenfield subdivision or site-development work: long runs of storm sewer and water main across open, unpaved ground with ample working room; excavator shades the pipe with select material then returns spoil/aggregate in lifts over the pipe, compacted with a hoe-pack, wheel or roller to the project's density spec.

Rural/open-country drains and culverts: field tile, farm drainage line, roadside culvert or cross-country utility pipe; spoil is crowned back over the pipe with a dozer, loader or excavator in open terrain, with light or no compaction requirement and essentially no in-trench hand work.

Confined and congested backfill: filling around manholes, vaults, tie-ins and pipe crossings on tight urban blocks — hand backfill and tamping in the narrow annulus inside a trench box, or placement of flowable fill/CLSM from a ready-mix chute, with live utilities and structures immediately adjacent.

sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem performs fully autonomous trenching on utility solar construction sites, but the company's own product page states that backfill and compaction are still done by human crews whose workflow the robot's spoil piles support.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous utility trenching on the same kind of buried-pipe/cable jobsite. It is cited as calibration — the leading commercial trenching autonomy explicitly leaves covering (backfill) and compaction of the trench to human crews.

sources.system: Develon Real-X (DX225LC-7X) with Gravis Robotics autonomy
sources.developer: Develon / HD XiteSolution with Gravis Robotics

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous trench excavation and earthworks on a real site with the same machines and soils a pipelayer's cover work uses; establishes that operator-less bucket earthmoving to a 3D model is deployed, though covering a laid pipe is not shown.

sources.system: Gravis Rack / Gravis autonomy platform on 36-ton excavators
sources.title: Gravis Robotics expands into US with AI-powered autonomous construction equipment
sources.claim: Gravis-powered excavators are deployed on a 60-mile oil and gas pipeline project with Techint in Argentina, with multiple 36-ton machines autonomously digging six-foot trenches in compacted, heterogeneous soil and shallow bedrock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pipeline-trench excavation in open right-of-way. Same machine, same material and terrain as bulk covering of a pipe in open country; supports machine-only earthmoving along a pipe alignment, but not embedment placement around the pipe or compaction to density spec.

sources.system: Bedrock Operator (retrofit autonomy kit on 20–80 ton excavators)
sources.title: Bedrock Robotics begins supervised autonomous excavation on live construction sites as it moves toward commercialization
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics ran supervised-autonomy mass excavation on a live 130-acre construction site with Sundt Construction, moving more than 65,000 cubic ... with autonomous excavators using the same workflow as manual ....

sources.system: A4CSEL automated construction system (automated bulldozers, vibratory rollers, backhoes, dump trucks)
sources.date: 2024–2026 (Naruse Dam application from FY2020; land development FY2024)
sources.title: A⁴CSEL for Earthworks | A⁴CSEL | Technology & Services | KAJIMA CORPORATION
sources.claim: Kajima's A4CSEL system automates the full embankment cycle — automated backhoe loading, automated articulated dump haulage, automated bulldozer leveling and automated vibratory-roller compaction of fill lifts — with more than ten automated machines running day and night at Naruse Dam and first application to a land-development site.
