This is the same physical operation as covering a pipe once material is presented in engineered lifts, so it supports machine-only covering where the work is laid out for the machines; it does not show embedment placed around a pipe in a narrow trench.

sources.title: A⁴CSEL for DAM | A⁴CSEL | Technology & Services | KAJIMA CORPORATION
sources.claim: Kajima has repeatedly applied A4CSEL to automate vibratory ... on real dam construction sites, including the CSG embankment at Naruse Dam.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous spreading and compaction of earth/CSG fill layers at a working construction site, i.e. the covering-and-compacting half of the pipelayer's task performed by machine without an operator.

tasks.label: Connect pipe pieces and seal joints, using welding equipment, cement, or glue.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Gravity sewer or storm drain: joining gasketed bell-and-spigot PVC, HDPE or reinforced concrete pipe in an open, often muddy and shored trench — clean the bell, position/lubricate the gasket, align on grade, and push the spigot home to the witness mark using an excavator bucket, come-along or bar, then check the joint before bedding.

Water main: assembling push-on gasketed joints on ductile iron or PVC C900 pipe in a street trench — lubricating gaskets, aligning heavy pipe hung from an excavator, seating the joint, and deflecting/restraining as needed for pressure service.

HDPE force main, water or gas pipe joined by butt fusion at grade beside the trench (pipe loaded into a tracked fusion machine, faced, heated and fused, cooled under pressure) or by electrofusion couplings on tie-ins and fittings.

Small-diameter solvent-cement work: service laterals, house connections, drain and conduit runs — cutting and deburring PVC/ABS, priming, applying cement, and making up fittings by hand in a tight trench, at the bench, or in a vault, often in cold or wet conditions.

Field welding of steel pipe joints (welded steel water transmission main, casing pipe, force main, or pipeline tie-in): fit-up and line-up clamp, root/hot/fill/cap passes at grade or in a trench bell hole, followed by coating of the joint.

Connections to structures and appurtenances: sealing pipe into precast manholes, catch basins and box culverts with flexible boots, clamping bands, butyl mastic, external joint wrap and grout; making up bolted mechanical-joint or flanged fittings, valves and restraints to torque.

sources.system: McElroy TracStar iSeries with FusionGuide Control System (Level 3 Automatic Fusion)
sources.title: McElroy TracStar® Fusion Machines
sources.claim: McElroy TracStar iSeries jobsite butt-fusion machines offer a FusionGuide Level 3 mode in which the whole fusion cycle — carriage/alignment control, facing, drag management, heat soak, fusion pressure and cooling — is run automatically by software once pipe is clamped in the machine's fixtures.

sources.system: CRC Evans Internal Welding Machine (IWM), used with P-series external automatic welders
sources.date: 2023-06 (product page), technology in field use for decades
sources.title: Internal Welding Machine (IWM) - CRC Evans
sources.claim: The CRC Evans Internal Welding Machine is a combination internal line-up clamp and multi-head root-pass welding system that aligns the two pipe ends and deposits the root weld in a fully automatic cycle, used on onshore pipeline right-of-way and on lay barges.

sources.system: KRANENDONK Robotic Pipe Shop (ZEROGAP beveling, robotic fit-up and welding)
sources.title: Robotic Pipe Shop - KRANENDONK
sources.claim: Kranendonk's Robotic Pipe Shop is an installed, integrated robotic line that takes pipe spool fabrication from cutting and beveling through fit-up and welding of the joints without manual input, implemented with fabricator JGC Corporation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shop fabrication of pipe spools. It is the same operation as the field task — aligning two pipe ends to fit-up tolerance and welding the girth joint on comparable steel pipe — performed in a purpose-built robotic cell, so it substantiates the E1 counterfactual only.

sources.system: PEMA robotic welding stations with PEMA FMS / WeldControl
sources.title: PEMA robotic welding stations
sources.claim: Pemamek's PEMA robotic welding stations for heavy fabrication (including pipe, nozzle and vessel girth seams) are run by an FMS that controls material flow and automatic work ... as an unmanned, software-controlled production solution with adaptive seam compensation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic girth welding of pipe/vessel components in fixtured stations; same weld geometry and steel pipe sizes as field girth welds, establishing that the joint can be completed when the work is presented fixtured.

sources.title: Weld Faster, Weld Better — Novarc SWR Brochure (ABICOR BINZEL)
sources.claim: Novarc's Spool Welding Robot is a commercially deployed collaborative pipe-welding robot in fabrication shops, but it is characterized as semi-autonomous: it maintains torch stand-off and assists seam tracking while an operator stands beside it, loads and tacks parts and makes changes on the fly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shop pipe welding. Cited to show that even the most advanced fab-shop pipe welding robots keep an operator in the loop, which is why no positive judgment above E1 rests on it.

sources.title: ROBOTTER® - New sewerage construction technology that requires no workers inside the trench
sources.claim: ROBOTTER is a trench pipe-laying machine that levels bedding and mounts PVC, PE, PP, GRP and ceramic pipes in the trench so workers need not enter it, but it is driven by an operator using radio remote control from the surface.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task (placing and joining pipe in a trench); cited as the closest field system, and it is teleoperated, so it cannot support any positive E3 judgment.

sources.system: Robotic gluing / adhesive dispensing cells integrated by Olympus Technologies
sources.title: Robotic Gluing & Adhesive Dispensing: Automation Guide
sources.claim: Industrial robot and cobot cells are commercially integrated to apply glues, sealants and other liquid or semi-liquid materials to components and sub-assemblies with high precision and repeatability in manufacturing settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: programmed application of adhesive/sealant to a fixtured part before assembly. Applying solvent cement to a PVC socket or lubricant to a gasketed bell is the same bead-on-fixtured-part operation, at similar or looser precision, in a purpose-built cell.

tasks.label: Install or repair sanitary or stormwater sewer structures or pipe systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New gravity sanitary sewer main in an open-cut trench on a subdivision/roadway job: crew grades and beds the trench bottom, lowers 8-24 in. PVC/RCP sections with an excavator, homes gasketed bell-and-spigot joints, checks line and grade to laser/GPS, then backfills and compacts - inside a trench box, with groundwater, mud, spoil piles and crossing utilities.

Storm sewer system on a site-development or roadway job: setting catch basins/curb inlets, RCP storm pipe and culverts, headwalls and outfall structures; heavy precast pieces rigged from an excavator or crane, joints mortared/gasketed, connections cut into structures, in open weather-exposed ground.

Setting a precast manhole in the street or an easement: excavating and preparing the base, rigging and stacking base/riser/cone sections, cutting or booting pipe penetrations, grouting and sealing joints, adjusting grade rings and casting to finished pavement grade under traffic control.

Point repair of an existing sanitary or storm line: locating and hand-excavating around the failed section in a street or backyard easement amid live utilities, cutting out cracked/offset pipe, installing a repair section with shielded couplings or a saddle, sealing, and restoring bedding and surface - often with flow bypassed and shoring/confined-space rules in play.

Sewer service lateral/connection work: tapping or coring the main, installing a wye/saddle or inserta-tee, running lateral pipe and cleanout to a building at grade in a residential street, yard or driveway with tight clearances and unknown existing pipe materials.

Trenchless repair/rehabilitation of an existing sewer segment accessed from manholes: cleaning and CCTV, installing and curing a CIPP liner or a mechanical sleeve/point repair, reinstating laterals with a cutter, chemical-grouting leaking joints, plus flow bypass and manhole/street work-zone setup.

sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution - Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofit lets a standard excavator dig trenches autonomously on utility and solar construction sites, but the product covers excavation only - pipe placement, jointing and sealing remain crew work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: trench excavation, the preparatory step for pipelaying. Cited only to bound the state of the art - the autonomy covers digging soil, not lowering pipe, homing gasketed joints, setting precast structures or sealing, so it cannot complete this task's instances.

sources.title: Kawasaki Develops "Autonomous Excavation System for Excavators", Achieved "Autonomous Operation" for Trench Excavation at Construction and Civil Engineering Sites
sources.claim: Kawasaki demonstrated autonomous trench excavation with a standard excavator at construction and civil engineering sites; the demonstrated autonomy is earthmoving, not pipe installation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: trenching. Cited to show field autonomy in this trade extends to soil excavation only; positioning and joining pipe or structures is not demonstrated.

sources.title: High-Traction Sewer Robot with Compact DC Motors
sources.claim: Commercial in-pipe sewer rehabilitation robots carrying milling, cutting and repair tooling are steered by an operator using a cable remote control ... video monitor - teleoperated, not autonomous.

sources.title: CIPP Sewer Repair And Lateral Reinstatement: A Complete Guide
sources.claim: In CIPP sewer rehabilitation, lateral reinstatement is done with a robotic cutter that a human operator locates and positions from the surface; liner installation and curing are crew work.

sources.title: SOLO Pipeline Inspection Robot CCTV | RedZone Robotics
sources.claim: The one class of genuinely autonomous unmanned robots working inside municipal sewers performs inspection only - traversing a pipe segment with onboard sensors - with no repair or installation function.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-pipe sewer inspection. Cited to bound autonomy inside sewers - the autonomous capability is locomotion and imaging, not cutting, lining, grouting or pipe replacement, so it does not transfer to installation or repair.

sources.title: Humanoid robots in the construction industry: A future vision
sources.claim: Industry review as of late 2025 finds construction automation still concentrated in off-site precast/prefab manufacturing, with on-site automation rare because each project is unique ... changing.
sources.transferJustification: General background on the absence of autonomous on-site pipe installation systems; supports negative judgments only.

tasks.label: Check slopes for conformance to requirements, using levels or lasers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Gravity sewer/storm main installation: pipelayer sets a self-leveling pipe laser in a manhole or the first pipe, dials in the design grade, and checks the beam against the target in the bore of each newly laid pipe, calling for bedding adjustment until on grade; muddy, wet, shored trench 6-15 ft deep with an excavator working overhead.

Rotating/grade laser on a tripod at the surface with a laser receiver on a grade rod: worker checks bedding and pipe invert elevations at intervals down the open trench (and at manhole inverts), reads cut/fill against the flowline sheet, and signals the operator; dust, traffic control, spoil piles.

Checking the excavated trench bottom / subgrade slope before bedding is placed, with a laser receiver on a rod or a GNSS rover, verifying the cut falls continuously at design grade over the run and calling for additional cut or fill.

Short residential or commercial service lateral / area drain: checking fall (e.g., 1/4 in. per ft) on a shallow, tight, hand-dug or mini-ex trench in a yard or behind a curb using a hand level, smart level, or string line and a tape.

Final pre-backfill conformance/as-built check of the completed run for the inspector: shooting invert elevations at each manhole and at stations along the line with laser or level and rod, recording readings for acceptance.

sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' autonomous trenching excavators dig utility trenches to design depth/grade using RTK GNSS and IMUs, hitting depths within 1/10 of a ... and producing as-built data automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous trench excavation to design grade. The machine continuously measures the excavated invert against the design surface with RTK GNSS and reports as-builts, which is the same grade-conformance determination the pipelayer makes with a laser and rod on the trench bottom, on the same open-jobsite trenches and at the same tolerance class (~0.1 ft before bedding).

sources.title: Building the Future of Construction — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' trenching robots have accumulated large-scale field deployment digging trench on energy/utility projects in the US and Australia.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above; establishes that the autonomous grade-holding trenching is real field deployment on unstructured open jobsites, not a lab demo.

sources.title: Built Robotics releases 1st fully autonomous construction machinery in US | Construction Dive
sources.claim: Built Robotics' autonomy kit was released commercially in the US for excavators to dig trenches and grade fully autonomously between GPS points, supervised remotely rather than driven.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous trenching/grading to a design surface; confirms the autonomy status (no operator in cab, remote supervision only) underlying the grade-conformance judgment.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot + Trimble X7 / FieldLink
sources.title: Trimble Releases Turnkey Autonomous Robotic Scanning Solution for Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot | For Construction Pros
sources.claim: Trimble and Boston Dynamics ship a turnkey autonomous scanning workflow in which Spot walks a predefined waypoint path and collects Trimble X7 laser scans without an operator at the instrument.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous survey-grade capture of installed work. The robot performs the measurement step (positioning a survey instrument and capturing geometry of installed elements) that the pipelayer performs with a level/laser and rod.

sources.title: Trimble X7 3D Laser Scanner | SEP Geospatial
sources.claim: The Trimble X7 scanner used on the autonomous Spot workflow measures at roughly 2 mm accuracy and self-levels to survey grade, precision comparable to or better than a laser level and grade rod for slope checks.

sources.system: Hexagon PRESTO robotic inspection cell (AS1 laser scanner)
sources.title: PRESTO Quality Stations | Hexagon
sources.claim: Hexagon's PRESTO robotic inspection cell automatically scans a fixtured part with a robot-mounted laser scanner and evaluates it against the loaded CAD/PMI definition, with automatic robot path generation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated dimensional conformance inspection of a fixtured workpiece against a CAD tolerance. Checking whether a presented pipe or run falls at the specified slope is the same geometric pass/fail measurement, at far tighter precision, inside a fenced purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Robot Surveyors Bring Autonomous Precision to Construction Layouts | Thomasnet
sources.claim: CivDot is an autonomous ground robot that navigates open construction sites by RTK GNSS and marks survey points at roughly centimetre/sub-inch accuracy, thousands of points per day.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous survey-grade positioning/layout on unstructured outdoor earthwork sites; supports the claim that GNSS-based grade/position work can be executed autonomously in the same open-jobsite conditions where trench grade is checked.

tasks.label: Align and position pipes to prepare them for welding or sealing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Municipal water main or sanitary sewer main in an open street trench: pipelayer works in/around a 6-12 ft trench, receives an 8-24 in. ductile-iron or PVC gasketed section lowered by excavator, swings and stabs the spigot into the bell of the previously laid pipe, sets it to line and grade against a laser/grade rod, and homes the joint with a bar or come-along before sealing. Mud, water, traffic, shoring boxes, buried utilities.

Storm drain or culvert run on a site-development/roadway job: 18-60 in. reinforced concrete or corrugated metal sections slung from an excavator, lubricated gaskets, aligned to the bell of the last piece on a bedded trench bottom and pulled home with cables/come-alongs; heavy sections, uneven bedding, weather.

Steel transmission line (gas, water, force main) on a right-of-way: joints strung on skids, sideboom lowers the joint, crew sets end gap and hi-lo with internal or external line-up clamps and holds alignment for the welders; long open-country or urban corridor, varying terrain.

Small-diameter service lines, sewer laterals and yard drains: 4-8 in. PVC/HDPE or clay pipe positioned by hand in narrow, shallow, often hand-dug excavations next to houses, driveways and existing utilities; tight space, awkward postures, obstacles.

Yard/shop prefabrication and staging before installation: in the contractor's pipe yard or fab area, sections are set on stands/rollers, ends aligned and clamped for butt-fusion, double-jointing or tack welding of spools and fittings before being carried to the trench.

sources.system: KRANENDONK Robotic Pipe Shop (Apollo Pipe Spool Milling Station + Aurora Spool Welding Station)
sources.title: Pipe Spool Automation - KRANENDONK
sources.claim: KRANENDONK's Robotic Pipe Shop is a commercially sold, fully automated pipe-spool line combining a milling station and the Aurora spool welding station, covering cutting, beveling, fit-up (aligning pipe to fittings for welding) and welding with minimal operator input inside robot cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is pipe-spool fit-up: bringing a pipe end and a mating pipe/fitting into weld-ready alignment (root gap and hi-lo) before welding, i.e. the same align-and-position-for-welding act the pipelayer performs, on comparable steel pipe, but with the work delivered to a fixtured robot cell.

sources.system: KRANENDONK Robotic Pipe Shop at JGC
sources.title: KRANENDONK strengthens collaboration with JGC through advanced Robotic Pipe Shop installation
sources.claim: The fully automated Robotic Pipe Shop has been implemented with an industrial customer (JGC Corporation) for pipe spool fabrication, evidencing deployment rather than concept.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the Robotic Pipe Shop item: automated fit-up aligns pipe and fittings for welding; this source establishes the automated line is installed and producing spools for a real fabricator.

sources.system: Canrig Red Zone Robotics (RZR) rig floor module / SmartROS

sources.claim: Nabors' Canrig RZR robotics module autonomously handles drill pipe and casing on a rig floor, positioning and aligning tubulars to make up connections and trip pipe with no crew on the floor; deployed on a working land rig drilling horizontal wells for ExxonMobil.

sources.claim: Nabors' fully automated R801 rig replaced the catwalk with a robotic pipe handler that moves and aligns drill pipe and tubulars up ... 13.375 in. diameter, drilling, tripping and casing roughly 2 million ft across nine wells.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the RZR item: automated positioning and coaxial alignment of large-diameter steel pipe joints for end-to-end joining, at production rates, in a purpose-built machine zone.

sources.title: Drill Floor Robot - Nabors
sources.claim: Canrig's electric Drill Floor Robot is a commercial machine with 1,500 kg capacity that automates pipe and tool handling on the rig floor using automated grippers, spinners and clamping tools.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is robotic handling and stabbing of heavy pipe on a drill floor; it establishes payload and gripping capability for pipe of the weight class pipelayers handle when the work is presented in a machine-structured zone.

sources.system: Novarc Spool Welding Robot (SWR) with NovEye Autonomy
sources.title: Novarc's Spool Welding Robot | SWR | Pipe Welding Robot
sources.claim: In pipe fabrication shops, robotic pipe welding systems still depend on humans to fit up and tack the joint to a tight root-gap tolerance before the robot welds, indicating the alignment step itself is not automated in ordinary shop (non-cell) settings.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the judgment, not to support it: the widely deployed shop welding cobot presumes human fit-up, so robotic alignment of pipe in an ordinary human work facility is not substantiated.

sources.title: Exosystem Kit Converts Excavator into a Robot
sources.claim: Field construction autonomy is limited to earthmoving: Built Robotics' Exosystem autonomously digs utility trenches within a geofenced area on jobsites, with no cited capability to place or align pipe in the trench.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the judgment: the leading field trenching system automates excavation only; pipe placement and joint alignment in the trench remain manual, so no E3 capability is substantiated.

tasks.label: Lay out pipe routes, following written instructions or blueprints and coordinating layouts with supervisors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New subdivision or commercial pad: mainline sanitary/storm run through a graded, unpaved street corridor. Worker reads plan-and-profile sheets, marks trench centerline and offsets, manhole/catch-basin and station points with paint, lath and hubs on open graded dirt, then reviews the marked route with the foreman before excavation.

Existing urban street: water-main or sewer replacement/extension under traffic control. Worker lays out the route among existing utility locate paint, ties to existing manholes, valves, curb and property lines, marks sawcut lines and structure locations, and adjusts the route in the field with the superintendent when the plan conflicts with what is found.

Open trench, line and grade: transferring plan invert elevations into the trench — setting a pipe laser in the manhole or first pipe, or string line/batter boards — checking grade with a rod at each joint as pipe is laid, adjusting bedding, and confirming cuts against the cut sheet with the foreman.

Long rural or cross-country run (force main, water transmission line, field drainage) across fields and rights-of-way: staking and painting the alignment over long distances with GPS, marking bends, valves, and depth-change stations on rough open ground.

Owner-controlled institutional or industrial premises (wastewater plant, airport, campus, plant yard): laying out yard piping or drain runs on paved yard, prepared subgrade or slab from coordinated drawings, coordinating the layout with plant staff and the supervisor.

Small residential or service-lateral job: laying out a sewer/water service or yard drain from a plot plan, sketch or written instruction, measured with a tape off building corners, property irons and the existing main, marked with paint and flags in a tight yard with landscaping and fences.

sources.title: Automated Layout Startup Civ Robotics Secures $7.5M Series A Funding Round | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: CivDot is an autonomous four-wheeled outdoor layout robot that drives to surveyed coordinates and spray-paints layout points at 8 mm accuracy, up to 3,000 points/day, on uneven ground and in inclement weather.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is construction stakeout/layout marking: driving to design coordinates and marking them on the ground. Pipe-route layout produces the same deliverable (paint/stakes at plan coordinates for the trench line and structures) at the same cm-level tolerance on the same outdoor jobsites.

sources.title: Automated Layout Startup Civ Robotics Secures $7.5M Series A Funding Round | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: The layout robot marks points autonomously in large outdoor sites with ..., indicating supervised autonomy rather than continuous teleoperation.
sources.transferJustification: Same layout/stakeout deliverable as pipe-route layout; establishes that the marking runs are executed autonomously, not by step-by-step remote control.

sources.claim: CivDot robots are in commercial field use by major contractors on rugged outdoor construction sites in the US.

sources.claim: CivDot marks coordinates with spray paint that crews follow with stakes, and it also records ground elevation at each point (cut/fill); reported uses include heavy civil work such as pipelines, foundations and roads.

sources.title: TinySurveyor Terra – TinyMobileRobots
sources.claim: TinySurveyor Terra marks out construction and infrastructure layouts across varied outdoor surfaces including gravel, dirt and grass.

sources.claim: Automated layout with FieldPrinter is deployed at large commercial scale across many controlled building sites, including data centers, healthcare and manufacturing facilities.

sources.title: HP SitePrint FAQ | HP Official Site

sources.transferJustification: Related task is trade layout printing from CAD, including plumbing; transfers to pipe-route layout on controlled premises because the deliverable (route lines, points and text annotations on the working surface) and tolerance are the same.

tasks.label: Tap and drill holes into pipes to introduce auxiliary lines or devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dry tap on a newly installed water main in an open trench before the line is placed in service: crew drills (and threads, for a direct tap) a 3/4"–1" hole in ductile iron or C900 PVC, through a service saddle or directly, to receive a corporation stop for a service line. Muddy trench, pipe already bedded, hole located to suit the service.

Wet/hot tap into an existing pressurized main at a tie-in or new service connection: bolt on tapping sleeve or saddle plus valve, mount the tapping machine, drill and cut threads through the wall while the main stays under pressure, retract cutter, close valve and install the corporation stop. Live buried main, water and traffic present.

Drilling/coring a branch opening into an existing in-service sewer or storm main (or manhole barrel) in a deep trench for a lateral connection — hole saw or core drill, then saddle/Inserta-tee installed. Confined, wet, flowing line, variable pipe material (VCP, concrete, PVC).

Drilling and tapping holes in new pipe sections and fittings staged at grade at the jobsite (on blocks or a pipe rack) before they are lowered in: taps for air-release valves, blow-offs, pressure/test gauges, sampling ports, sensor bosses. Clean, unpressurized pipe handled as a discrete workpiece.

Prefabrication at the contractor's shop or municipal yard: drilling and tapping holes in pipe spools, fittings, and saddles on a bench or rack so auxiliary lines and devices can be attached later. Indoor/roofed facility with fixed layout and standard equipment.

sources.title: SPC 1500 - 4000 PT Pipe Profiler - HGG Group
sources.claim: Commercial CNC pipe profilers clamp and rotate pipe up to very large diameters and cut branch/nozzle holes in the pipe wall under machine control inside a purpose-built cutting cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: CNC cutting of branch/nozzle holes in fixtured pipe. It transfers to making the opening a pipelayer cuts for a saddle, service clamp or Inserta-tee: same object (round pipe wall, comparable diameters), same required output (a correctly sized, correctly located opening), performed with the pipe presented fixtured as an E1 setting would present it.

sources.system: DOBEMY DBM-430D(R1) Auto CNC Round Tube Drilling and Tapping Machine
sources.title: DBM-430D(R1) Auto CNC Round Tube Drilling Machine - DOBEMY CNC Machine
sources.claim: Commercially sold 4-axis CNC tube machines clamp round pipe and both drill and cut threads (M2–M16) in the wall automatically from a stored program.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: CNC drilling and thread-tapping of fixtured round tube/pipe, including PVC and PP pipe. The pipelayer's direct tap is the same operation — a drilled hole plus a cut thread in a pipe wall to receive a threaded corporation stop or device — at comparable hole sizes (3/4"–1" ≈ M20–M25).

sources.title: Robotic Cutting, Deburring, Polishing, Buffing & More | FANUC America
sources.claim: Industrial robot cells perform drilling and thread tapping on parts as an automated machining process, a standard commercial application.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic drilling and tapping of fixtured workpieces. Transfers to tapping a pipe wall because the operation, tooling and thread precision are the same; only the workpiece changes, and the pipe is presented fixtured in the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: Robotic deflashing/drilling/tapping cell with FANUC M10iA
sources.title: Robotic Deflashing, Drilling, Tapping Cell Case Study
sources.claim: A deployed production cell drills and taps parts after a fixture holds the workpiece and a light curtain separates people from the robot — the standard purpose-built robotic work environment for this operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: an installed drilling-and-tapping robot cell in a US plant. It documents that hole-making plus thread-cutting to production quality is routinely done by robots when the workpiece is fixtured and fenced — the E1 presentation assumed for the pipe instances.

sources.title: Roadwork Robot Autonomously Digs Out, Repairs Buried Utility Lines | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: The most advanced field robot for work on buried utility pipes autonomously excavates a keyhole and can fit a thermoplastic fitting to a gas pipe, but it was a prototype demonstrated on mock/test pavement and does not drill and thread service taps.

Cited to show the state of field capability — cleaning, clamping, cutting and fitting a gas pipe as a prototype on test pavement — which does not extend to drilling and threading taps in a trench at worker quality.

sources.developer: various (IMS Robotics, Prokasro, Picote and others)
sources.title: Technological Advancements Help Lateral Cutters Keep Pace with Evolving Rehab Processes | Trenchless Technology
sources.claim: Robots that cut openings into pipe from the inside (lateral reinstatement cutters used after CIPP lining) are remote-controlled by an operator watching a camera, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting branch openings in installed sewer pipe. Cited as a negative bound — the only fielded machines that open holes in in-service mains are continuously teleoperated, so they cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Direct Tapping Machine | Reed Manufacturing
sources.claim: Field tapping of water mains under pressure is performed with hand-set, human-operated tapping machines covering 4"–48" cast/ductile iron and C900 PVC, including installing the corporation stop.
sources.transferJustification: Not a robotic system; cited only to characterize what the instance requires (drill, thread, install stop under pressure) and to show that the fielded tooling for live mains is manually set up and controlled.

tasks.label: Operate mechanized equipment, such as pickup trucks, rollers, tandem dump trucks, front-end loaders, or backhoes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Running a rubber-tire backhoe or hydraulic excavator to open and later backfill a sanitary-sewer or water-main trench in a built-up street or subdivision: live gas/electric/telecom crossings, spoil piled between parked cars, traffic control around the hole, laborers working in and beside the trench, grade checked continuously.

Trenching with an excavator/backhoe in an open corridor: greenfield subdivision before paving, rural water/force-main run, or an energy or industrial site with long, uniform, obstruction-free trench runs cut to a set width, depth and grade.

Operating a front-end loader or skid steer/compact track loader around the active job: pulling bedding stone and backfill from stockpiles, dropping it at the trench, moving spoil, carrying pipe, fittings, trench box and pallets to the crew, all while people and other machines work in the same area.

Operating a ride-on vibratory roller/compactor (plus walk-behind compactors in the trench) to compact bedding and backfill lifts over the completed pipe run and to compact subgrade and stone base for the street or shoulder restoration, working within traffic-controlled lanes.

Driving a tandem dump truck: loading spoil at the trench, hauling it over public streets to a spoil site or landfill, dumping, then returning from a quarry with bedding stone or select backfill and spotting the load along the trench line.

Driving the crew pickup (often towing a trailer with a plate compactor, pump, or saw) between the shop yard, supply house and the jobsite over public roads, then positioning it on unpaved staging ground at the site during the day.

tasks.label: Train or supervise others in laying pipe.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Experienced pipelayer/crew leader verbally instructs and coaches a new laborer at the edge of an open street trench during a sewer main installation — explaining bedding depth, grade checks with a laser or grade rod, and correct bell-and-spigot orientation, then watching and correcting the trainee's work.

Crew leader oversees a two- to four-person pipe crew for a shift on a water main or storm drain job: assigning who works in the trench versus at the excavator, calling out signals to the operator, monitoring line and grade against plans, checking joint deflection and thrust blocking, and telling workers to redo or adjust work that is out of tolerance.

Foreman delivers a pre-shift toolbox talk / job briefing to the crew: sequence of the day's pipe installation, trench box and shoring rules, confined-space and utility-locate cautions, and traffic control assignments; answers questions and confirms understanding.

Hands-on demonstration of a specific technique to an apprentice — lubricating and homing a gasketed joint, cutting and beveling pipe, setting a laser in the trench, or mortaring a manhole connection — performing it once while narrating, then having the apprentice repeat it under observation.

Administrative and evaluative supervision away from the trench: signing off on apprentice competency checklists and OSHA/utility-district training records, reviewing plans and inspection findings with the crew in the truck or job trailer, and counseling a worker on repeated errors or safety violations.

tasks.label: Locate existing pipes needing repair or replacement, using magnetic or radio indicators.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Paved street or alley, traffic-managed work zone: before excavating on a main break or a tie-in, the pipelayer sweeps the planned dig footprint (a few square meters) with a pipe locator/magnetic locator to find the existing water main, sewer or service, and paints the pipe's line and depth on the asphalt.

Long-run route trace along a street or right-of-way for a replacement project: clamp a transmitter to a hydrant, valve, or tracer wire (or induce a signal), then walk the receiver hundreds of feet, peaking the signal and marking the route every few feet, plus depth readings at intervals.

Unpaved verge, utility easement, gravel shoulder or residential lawn: sweep with a magnetic locator/EM wand for buried ferrous appurtenances (valve boxes, curb stops, cleanout lids, buried cast-iron pipe) under sod, gravel or landscaping; set flags and paint marks on grass/dirt.

Non-metallic (PVC, clay, AC) sewer lateral or main: push a sonde or camera in from a cleanout or manhole, track the sonde from the surface across a yard, driveway or street, and mark the route and depth so the crew can dig on the defect.

Active excavation/construction site: rutted, muddy ground with spoil piles, open trench, plates and running equipment; re-locate and verify existing crossings as the trench advances, sweeping over broken ground and marking on dirt or stakes.

Institutional or industrial premises (wastewater treatment plant, campus, port, industrial yard): locate buried process, water or sewer lines on paved, controlled grounds using as-builts plus an EM locator, sometimes scanning inside buildings; mark on pavement.

sources.title: AUSMOS GPR Mapping Robot – ULC Technologies
sources.claim: AUSMOS, a wheeled robot carrying a 250 MHz GPR antenna and a 3-axis EM sensor, is driven onto site by an operator, then autonomously scans a programmed area, processes the data on-site and performs the mark-out; its stated operating environment is urban/suburban paved roads and walkways.

sources.title: ULC Technologies Announces Robotic System for Underground Utility Damage Prevention
sources.claim: ULC announced AUSMOS as a semi-autonomous robotic platform that ... marks out buried utilities using GPR and electromagnetic sensors, developed with UK gas network SGN and Transport for London, with pilot projects completed in Epsom and Clapham Hill and pilots running in the US and UK.

sources.title: Robotic Mapping and Mark Out: Clapham Hill – ULC Technologies
sources.claim: On two adjacent sites on a live London street (Clapham Hill), with traffic flowing and under normal traffic-management, AUSMOS carried an operation through from autonomous scanning to interpretation and ground mark-out, covering about 25 square meters in a few hours in a GPS-degraded urban setting.

sources.title: AUSMOS GPR Mapping and Mark Out Robot Pilot: Epsom, UK – ULC Technologies
sources.claim: In the Epsom pilot on a public road, after autonomous scanning the robot itself applied the ground marks; the system located a foul sewer at 0.75 m, a gas main at 0.75 m and two telecom ducts at 0.625 m, with marks agreeing with utility drawings and an existing trench.

sources.title: Enabling Innovation: The Development of a Utility-Locating Robot, AUSMOS
sources.claim: The AUSMOS EM sensor works the same way as the pipelayer's radio/magnetic locator: it detects power cables passively and detects any metal utility carrying a signal induced by a nearby transmitter, alongside the GPR antenna.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (locating buried pipes with radio/magnetic indicators); the quote establishes the robot uses the transmitter-induced EM signal method that the task names.

sources.title: AUSMOS | Robotic GPR Mapping Services | ULC Technologies
sources.claim: ULC sells robotic utility locating as a service using AUSMOS, and states the robot holds navigation and localization accuracy in congested areas and inside buildings ... — i.e. on controlled institutional premises as well as streets.

sources.title: 5 Examples of Robotic Infrastructure Automation – ULC Technologies
sources.claim: As of January 2025 ULC describes AUSMOS as autonomously detecting and marking out buried assets with same-day interpretation and mark-outs, confirming the capability is current rather than a one-off 2023 pilot.

sources.title: Robotic Utility Mapper Reduces Costs, Improves Safety During Infrastructure Planning and Maintenance
sources.claim: RUMI, a four-wheeled ground robot with GPR, GPS, stereo camera and LiDAR built under FHWA SBIR funding, autonomously scans a region for underground utility ... while its operator stays clear of traffic; it reached Phase IIB prototype and for-hire scanning services.

sources.title: Robotic Roadworks & Excavation System – ULC Technologies
sources.claim: ULC/SGN's Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System scans the road with GPR and electromagnetic sensors to identify buried assets in ... before and during robotic excavation, and has undergone live field trials on UK streets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (pre-excavation asset location on live streets) using the same GPR+EM sensing on the same surfaces; supports that robotic locating is performed in public-street work zones.

roles.title: Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters
aliases: Dry Docks Utility Systems Repair Operator
roles.description: Assemble, install, alter, and repair pipelines or pipe systems that carry water, steam, air, or other liquids or gases. May install heating and cooling equipment and mechanical control systems. Includes sprinkler fitters.

tasks.label: Shut off steam, water, or other gases or liquids from pipe sections, using valve keys or wrenches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service call: plumber isolates a fixture or the whole house before a repair — closes an angle stop under a sink/toilet, a hose-bibb, or the main ball/gate valve in a basement, crawlspace, or utility closet; valves are often corroded or stuck and need a wrench, then a faucet is opened to bleed the line and confirm flow has stopped.

Outdoor/buried shutoff at a home or small business: plumber locates the curb stop or meter valve box in a lawn or parkway (lid may be silted over), clears the box, drops a long curb key or valve key onto the square operating nut roughly 3-5 ft below grade, and turns it blind to closed, then verifies at a fixture; or shuts the gas cock at an outdoor meter with a wrench.

Commercial/institutional building (hospital, school, office, hotel): plumber isolates a branch or riser in a mechanical room, riser closet, or above a ceiling — OS&Y gate, butterfly, or ball valves, sometimes reached from a ladder or lift — tags the valve, closes it, and drains/bleeds the section to confirm isolation.

Construction or renovation jobsite: plumber shuts off temporary or partially installed piping before cutting in or testing — valves in unfinished walls, on temporary risers, or in trenches; layout differs by site, access is cluttered with materials and other trades.

Industrial/process facility or powerhouse: steamfitter isolates steam, condensate, or process piping — large handwheel gate valves, valve wrenches or gearboxes, hot piping, lockout/tagout procedure, verification by blow-down or pressure gauge.

sources.developer: University of Bonn, Autonomous Intelligent Systems group
sources.date: 2017 competition; Journal of Field Robotics paper 2018/2019

sources.claim: The mobile manipulator 'Mario' autonomously detected a manipulation panel in an arena, selected and grasped the correct wrench, and used it to turn a valve stem, winning MBZIRC 2017 Challenge 2 — i.e., autonomous valve actuation with a hand tool in a purpose-built, robot-oriented setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: turning a square valve stem with a wrench in a competition arena. It matches the plumbing task's core physical act (engaging a valve stem/nut with a key or wrench and rotating it) with comparable objects and precision, so it substantiates completion where the valve is presented in a known, machine-oriented setting.

sources.transferJustification: Same physical act (grasping and rotating an industrial valve handle) demonstrated on a bench-mounted valve; supports completion when the valve is fixtured and presented, not in a found facility.

sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' commercially sold Spot Arm turns valves only semi-autonomously: the operator initiates the manipulation (touch-to-grasp / constrained manipulation) and the robot executes the constrained motion.

sources.claim: MHI's EX ROVR is a commercialized explosion-proof plant inspection robot deployed at operating oil and gas assets in ...; it patrols autonomously, but valve manipulation with its arm is described as remote operation and as a future/assisted capability requiring a support device.

tasks.label: Install underground storm, sanitary, or water piping systems, extending piping as needed to connect fixtures and plumbing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New residential construction: underslab sanitary/storm rough-in on a house lot — hand/machine trenching in soil, cutting and solvent-welding PVC DWV pipe to grade with a laser or level, setting closet bends and stub-ups for fixtures, testing, and backfilling before the slab pour.

Replacement/repair of a building sewer lateral or water service at an existing property: locating and excavating a trench across a yard, driveway or street around live utilities, cutting out old clay/cast-iron or galvanized pipe, laying and jointing new PVC/HDPE, tying into the main and the house stub, backfilling and restoring surface.

Commercial/institutional building underground plumbing on an active construction site: larger-diameter underslab sanitary, grease waste and storm lines, floor drains and cleanouts, working around rebar, footings and other trades, sloping to spec and pressure/ball testing before pour.

Site utility / municipal work in roadway or campus right-of-way: deep shored trenches, storm sewer mains, catch basins and manholes or water mains; pipe set by excavator, joints homed and bedded by crew in the trench, grade shot with laser/GPS, compacted backfill and inspection.

Extending piping in and under an existing occupied structure to connect new or relocated fixtures: breaking/saw-cutting slab or working in a crawlspace or tunnel, hand digging around existing footings and utilities, tying new drain and water lines into existing buried piping, then patching.

sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem is a commercial aftermarket kit that makes standard excavators dig trenches autonomously on utility and solar construction sites; the automated scope is excavation (trench cut and spoil placement), not laying, jointing or connecting pipe.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: trenching for buried utilities. sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Leads Major Autonomous Excavation Push | Equipment World

sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk excavation/grading on jobsites. Confirms current construction-site autonomy is limited to earthmoving; it does not cover placing, aligning and sealing buried pipe, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

sources.title: McKinsey: Construction Must Prepare Now for Humanoid Robotics Adoption

sources.transferJustification: Cited only as a negative indicator: pipe installation is described as a projected future capability, confirming no fielded robot performs it today. Not used to support any positive judgment.

tasks.label: Assemble pipe sections, tubing, or fittings, using couplings, clamps, screws, bolts, cement, plastic solvent, caulking, or soldering, brazing, or welding equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential new-construction/remodel rough-in: joining PVC/ABS DWV fittings with primer and solvent cement, PEX with crimp/expansion rings, occasional copper stub-outs, with most joints made in place inside stud bays, joist spaces, crawlspaces and slab trenches of a house under construction.

Service, repair and replacement in occupied homes and small commercial buildings: cutting out a failed section and sweating/pressing in a new valve or coupling, re-piping a trap arm or water-heater connection, joining to existing installed piping in cramped cabinets, closets and crawlspaces.

Commercial/institutional construction, in-place joining: closing grooved couplings on hung sprinkler and chilled-water mains, field butt welds and flange bolt-ups at tie-in points, threaded joints and CPVC/PVC joints made overhead on lifts against a ceiling grid, in an active multi-trade jobsite.

Commercial/industrial jobsite, ground-level fabrication before hoisting: pipe sections and fittings cut, fit up on stands or a site bench, tacked and then welded (carbon/stainless) or brazed (copper) into spools and small rack assemblies for later installation.

Off-site prefabrication / pipe fab shop: producing pipe spools, mechanical-room racks and multi-trade modules from isometrics — beveling, fit-up on positioners, root and fill welding of carbon and stainless pipe-to-fitting joints, plus brazed copper assemblies.

Industrial plant, refinery, power house or hospital central plant maintenance and turnaround: cutting out and replacing spool pieces in situ, in-place welds on congested pipe racks and in confined spaces, bolt-ups and threaded/socket joints on operating systems under permit.

sources.system: Novarc Spool Welding Robot (SWR) with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2

sources.claim: Novarc's Spool Welding Robot with NovEye Autonomy (Gen 2) welds pipe-to-fitting spool joints (root through cap, multi-pass) in pipe fabrication shops, with the spool tacked and mounted on the robot's pipe positioner and no operator intervention during welding.

sources.title: Novarc's Spool Welding Robot | SWR™ | Pipe Welding Robot

sources.title: KRANENDONK strengthens collaboration with JGC through advanced Robotic Pipe Shop installation

sources.title: UltraFlex demonstrates automated robotic induction brazing for copper to brass assemblies

sources.claim: No searched source showed a robotic system making solvent-cemented PVC/CPVC joints or crimped/expanded PEX joints for plumbing assemblies; automation found for plastic pipe is confined to extrusion, fitting manufacture and adhesive dispensing, not joining pipe to fittings.
sources.transferJustification: Documents the manual, time-critical nature of the dominant residential joining method (primer plus cement, joined and held within seconds) for which no robotic system was substantiated.

tasks.label: Locate and mark the position of pipe installations, connections, passage holes, or fixtures in structures, using measuring instruments such as rulers or levels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial/institutional/industrial building under construction (hospital, office tower, data center, plant): plumber/pipefitter transfers the coordinated drawings to the deck or slab — measuring from control lines and grid, then marking sleeve and penetration centers, floor drains, cleanouts, stub-ups, restroom fixture groups and equipment pad outlines before the pour or before rough-in. Tolerances ~1/8 in., dusty active site with other trades working.

Same commercial jobsite, overhead scope: locating and marking the points for pipe hangers, rod inserts, trapeze supports and deck penetrations along overhead piping runs — measured off grid/control with tape, level and laser, marked either as points on the floor for transfer up or directly on the underside of the deck.

Residential new construction (production single-family or multifamily wood frame): after the slab or deck is in, marking wall lines, fixture centerlines (toilet flange, tub/shower drain, lavatory), floor penetrations and stub-up positions from the plan set with tape, square and chalk line, before framing/rough-in.

Rough-in marking on vertical framing and walls in a partially built house or fit-out: measuring and marking bore-hole centers across studs and joists for water lines and DWV, marking stub-out heights, valve and shower-arm heights, and hanger spacing along a wall, using tape, torpedo/spirit level and code height rules; cramped stud bays and irregular framing.

Service/repair or tie-in work in an occupied home or business: locating existing concealed piping in a wall, floor or ceiling (by fixture geometry, sounding, stud/pipe locator or camera), then marking the exact positions for the access cut, the cut point on the pipe, or the new tie-in and hanger positions. Furnished, cluttered, no plan set.

Remodel/finish-stage fixture layout in an existing bathroom or kitchen: marking exact positions and heights for a relocated toilet flange, vanity supply and drain, shower valve and body sprays against existing finished or partially demolished surfaces, working off the fixture's rough-in dimensions and a level, in a small confined room.

sources.title: Dusty Robotics Scales Project Layout Automation | For Construction Pros
sources.claim: Trade press reports the FieldPrinter printed layout on 25 million sq ft of construction in Q1 2022 alone, at roughly 1/16 in. accuracy, and that a single-family residential contractor uses the robots to perform layout for all trades on site.

sources.title: FrameTec Customer Story | Dusty Robotics
sources.claim: FrameTec, a single-family/Type V builder, runs the FieldPrinter on the jobsite slab of individual houses to print multi-trade layout, explicitly including the centerlines of the plumber's fixtures.

sources.title: HP SitePrint FAQ | HP Official Site
sources.claim: HP SitePrint is a commercially available autonomous layout robot (US/Canada/UK/Ireland since July 2023) that navigates real job sites with obstacle and cliff sensors and prints layout lines, points, text and arcs at ±3/32 in. tolerance on concrete, plywood and other site surfaces.

sources.system: Dusty Robotics FieldPrinter (as used by JE Dunn)

sources.claim: General contractor JE Dunn reports from its own projects that layout robots (Dusty FieldPrinters) can mark slab penetrations, in-wall rough-in and overhead MEP installation points in addition to partition layout.

sources.title: Hilti Unveils BIM-Enabled Construction Jobsite Robot (PR Newswire)
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a commercially sold, BIM-driven ceiling robot for MEP contractors that localizes itself indoors from a robotic total station, drills overhead holes and marks them by trade; however an operator drives it by remote control from one drilling area to the next, so its autonomy over a full layout episode is not established.

sources.title: Multifunction Bridge WALLTEQ M-500 | HOMAG
sources.claim: Weinmann/Homag WALLTEQ multifunction bridges are CNC gantries in timber-frame panel plants that automatically mark, label and drill wall, floor and roof elements held on the machine's tables from the digital model.

It is the same act of transferring plan coordinates onto framing members (studs/plates) at millimetre precision, on the same wood workpieces, differing only in that the mark is made by a fixtured gantry rather than by a plumber's tape and level.

sources.title: Multifunction Bridge – Homag Wallteq M-340 | Electro-Tech Machinery
sources.claim: The same machine family automatically performs drilling of openings and electrical-outlet holes in framed wall panels in the factory, i.e. machine-located service penetrations through framing per the digital plan.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatically locating and cutting electrical/service holes in wall panels. Plumbing bore-hole and stub-out marking on studs involves the same workpieces, the same coordinate source (the model) and looser precision than the machine already achieves.

tasks.label: Cut, thread, or hammer pipes to specifications, using tools such as saws, cutting torches, pipe threaders, or pipe benders.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential / light-commercial rough-in: on the jobsite, the plumber measures off framing and cuts copper tube, PEX, CPVC/PVC or ABS to length with tubing cutters, hacksaws or a miter saw, then reams/deburrs the ends; dozens of short odd-length pieces per day, cut where the pipe will be installed amid framing, ladders and other trades.

Commercial/industrial jobsite steel pipe work (including sprinkler fitting): cutting 1/2"-6" black iron, galvanized or carbon steel pipe to length with a portable band saw or oxy-fuel/plasma torch, then threading with a portable power threader (or roll-grooving) at the point of installation, working off spool sheets in a partially built building or plant.

Contractor's prefabrication/fabrication shop: cutting, beveling, threading and grooving pipe to spool drawings or a cut list at fixed workstations (chop saw, power threader, roll groover, CNC profiler), producing labeled spools for delivery to the jobsite.

Bending to specification: forming offsets, 90s and saddles in soft copper tube, EMT/conduit or steel pipe with hand benders, mechanical/hydraulic benders or a shop bender, matching field-measured angles and takeouts.

Service, repair and retrofit: cutting into piping already installed in a building - sawing out a corroded section in a crawlspace, wall cavity, ceiling plenum or occupied mechanical room with a reciprocating saw, tubing cutter or torch, then squaring/threading the remaining end in place for the repair fitting.

sources.title: Machitech Pipe Cut - Fully Automated Pipe Cutting Machine

sources.title: Single machine serves as fully automated pipe cutting shop

sources.claim: BLM GROUP's TS72 automatic tube saw cuts round, square and other sections to length unattended, fed from a bundle loader holding up to 4,000 kg of stock, with automatic production changes - i.e. cut-to-length of tube/pipe to programmed dimensions in a machine cell.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (cutting pipe/tube to specified lengths) on the same diameter range as plumbing pipe; the saw executes the cut list without an operator.

sources.title: BLM GROUP's Smart tube bender can run autonomously
sources.claim: BLM GROUP's all-electric Smart CNC bender bends tube and wire up to 1.1 in. to programmed multi-radius shapes and, with its loading/unloading options, can run without a dedicated operator.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (bending pipe/tube to specified angles and radii) in the copper-tube/conduit size range plumbers bend by hand.

sources.claim: PMC-Colinet's RTP04.5 CNC pipe threading machine threads pipe from 1/2" to 4-1/2" OD (conduit and rebar-connection profiles) with a hydraulically operated dual-clamping chuck and an automated handling table cycling parts in about two seconds, in high-volume production plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-threading pipe ends to a standard thread profile, over exactly the 1/2"-4" diameter range plumbers thread; the machine clamps, chases and gauges the thread under CNC control with automatic part handling.

sources.system: Lancaster/UK dual hydraulic manipulator in-situ pipe cutting system

sources.claim: Cutting pipework that is already installed in place (nuclear decommissioning) is still done with assisted teleoperation: a dual hydraulic manipulator on a mobile base in which the operator selects the pipe on screen, evaluated as a semi-autonomous research system rather than a deployed autonomous one.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the in-place pipe-cutting variant of this task; shows that cutting installed pipework remains operator-driven, not autonomous.

tasks.label: Lay out full scale drawings of pipe systems, supports, or related equipment, according to blueprints.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial/institutional/industrial/multifamily construction: pipefitter lays out the piping drawings full scale on the slab or deck — pipe route centerlines, sleeves and penetrations, stub-ups, floor drains, equipment and housekeeping pads, and support point locations — from coordinated blueprints/BIM and established control points on an active, dusty jobsite floor.

Overhead support layout on a jobsite: transferring hanger, rod, insert and trapeze locations from the blueprints up onto the concrete or metal-deck ceiling/structure along a pipe run, marking anchor points at 8-17 ft height amid deck flutes, beams and other trades' work.

Fabrication shop: developing and drawing a full-scale layout of a pipe spool, a miter/lateral development, or a pipe support assembly on the shop floor or layout table from the blueprint, to serve as a template and fit-up check.

Fabrication shop: transferring blueprint dimensions full scale onto the material itself — marking cut lines, miter/saddle contours, fitting orientation, weld reference lines and part numbers on pipe, strut and support steel staged in the shop.

Retrofit/tie-in work in an existing occupied building or operating plant: field-verifying as-found conditions and marking the new pipe route, penetrations and support points on walls, ceilings, existing racks and equipment, usually from paper prints and field sketches rather than a coordinated model.

Residential and small light-commercial rough-in: plumber marks fixture groups, closet flanges, tub/shower drains, stub-ups and pipe centerlines on the slab or plywood subfloor and on studs, plates and joists in a house or small tenant fit-out, from 2D prints with no digital model on a cluttered, uncontrolled site.

sources.title: Automated Layout for Mechanical | Dusty Robotics
sources.claim: Dusty Robotics' FieldPrinter autonomously prints the coordinated model full scale on jobsite decks for mechanical/plumbing trades, including hanger and support point layouts, duct/pipe centerlines, equipment pads and plumbing stub-ups, floor drains and cleanouts, at 1/16 in. accuracy.

sources.title: Dusty Robotics Case Study - Simplexity Product Development

tasks.label: Fill pipes or plumbing fixtures with water or air and observe pressure gauges to detect and locate leaks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential new-construction/remodel rough-in: plumber caps DWV and water-supply openings, threads on a test gauge/plug assembly, pressurizes with air (or fills with water) to code pressure, watches the gauge over the required hold, and walks the open framing soaping joints to find the leak. Active house under construction, ladders, crawlspace/attic, dust and other trades.

Service/repair call in an occupied home or small business: isolate the existing system at the meter or a fixture, pressurize with air or water, watch the gauge for decay, then narrow down and locate the leak in concealed supply lines, a slab line, a water heater, or a fixture. Cluttered, occupant-controlled space, unknown layout.

Commercial/institutional building under construction: hydrostatic or pneumatic test of new domestic water, hydronic, natural gas, medical gas, or fire-sprinkler piping — fill and vent risers/mains, pump to test pressure (e.g., 200 psi sprinkler hydro), record the gauge for the hold period, then walk down overhead joints from a lift and repair any drips. Multi-trade jobsite.

Process/utility piping in an operating industrial plant, refinery, or power house (new tie-in or turnaround): blind off the loop, fill with water from a test pump, bring up to ASME B31.3/B31.1 test pressure, log gauge/chart-recorder readings over the hold, and walk down welds and flanges for weeping. Institution-controlled plant premises with scaffolding and permits.

Fabrication/prefab shop: hydrostatic or pneumatic test of prefabricated pipe spools, mechanical-room skids, manifolds, or fixture assemblies on a test bench before shipping — cap ends, fill/pressurize, watch the gauge, mark and repair any leaking joint.

sources.system: Cincinnati Test Systems hydrostatic leak test systems
sources.title: Hydrostatic Leak Test Systems — Cincinnati Test Systems
sources.claim: Cincinnati Test Systems builds custom hydrostatic leak-test systems that fill the part with water, vent air, stabilize and use pressure drop to identify leaks; the stated applications include pipe, pipelines, plumbing hydrants, gas ..., and the systems can be supplied with automatic operation and part load/unload automation.
sources.transferJustification: Same task content — fill a pipe or plumbing fixture with liquid, hold pressure, and read pressure decay to detect a leak — performed by machine on fixtured workpieces rather than by a plumber on installed piping.

sources.system: CTS transmission flow-valve automated leak test system
sources.title: Leak Test Systems, Transmission Flow Valve — Cincinnati Test Systems
sources.claim: A delivered CTS six-station indexing-dial system performs automatic leak and flow testing ... valves: a pick-and-place loads parts, test tooling advances to automatically ... ports, air is applied and monitored for leakage at 500 Hz, passing parts are laser-marked and unloaded, rejects diverted, at 600 parts/hour with no operator in the loop.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line pneumatic leak testing of a valve body. It transfers because the machine performs the whole cycle a plumber performs — seal/cap the openings, admit air, monitor pressure for decay, and judge pass/fail — on comparable metal fluid-carrying hardware in a fixtured cell.

sources.system: ATEQ Robotic Sniffing Leak Test System (HE490S sniffer + ABB GoFa CRB 15000)
sources.title: Robotic Leak Testing l Sniffing & Tracer Gas Turnkey Systems — ATEQ Corp.
sources.claim: ATEQ sells a turnkey robotic sniffing leak-test solution pairing an ABB GoFa CRB 15000 collaborative arm with a helium sniffer; the robot guides the sniffing probe along pre-programmed paths over the pressurized assembly to detect and quantify leaks, i.e., to pinpoint where the leak is, in production settings including hoses and pneumatic lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tracer-gas leak localization on pressurized assemblies (hoses, pneumatic lines, fluid systems). It supplies the 'locate the leak' half of the plumber's test — finding which joint is leaking on a charged system — with a robot arm in a fixtured cell.

sources.system: Spot with Spot CAM+IR, FLIR MUVE C360 and Enhanced Autonomy Payload
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas Leaks — Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot performs autonomous inspection rounds at a 40-acre midstream gas plant, including analog gauge reading, thermal inspection and combustible-gas detection; during a round its gas sensor detected a plume from a pinhole leak, but the plant's human safety team then identified and located the leaking asset, and Spot does no blinding, filling, or pressurizing of piping.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous gauge reading and gas-leak sensing in a structured industrial facility. It bounds what mobile robots do at E2 today — read gauges and flag a leak — without setting up, sealing, filling or pressurizing a test, so it cannot complete the whole task.
