tasks.label: Inspect, examine, or test installed systems or pipe lines, using pressure gauge, hydrostatic testing, observation, or other methods.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential new construction/remodel: after rough-in, the plumber caps or plugs openings on the DWV stack and supply lines in an open-framed house, pressurizes with air or water, sets a test gauge, holds the required pressure for the code interval, walks the framing and crawlspace observing joints and listening for leaks, corrects any drop, and presents the held test to the building inspector.

Service call in an occupied home or small business: diagnose a suspected leak or pressure problem - gauge static/working pressure at a hose bib, isolate branches and fixtures, check water heater/boiler relief and expansion setup, observe meter movement, and where needed push a camera through a cleanout to scope a 4-6 in. building drain/lateral, then report findings to the customer.

Commercial building under construction: hydrostatic/pneumatic acceptance test of a fire sprinkler zone (e.g., 200 psi for 2 hours) or of hydronic/domestic risers - install test header and caps, fill and bleed air, pump to test pressure, monitor the gauge over the hold, walk floors and ceiling spaces checking heads, grooved couplings and hangers, and witness the test with the AHJ/insurer.

Industrial plant or turnaround: pressure test of newly installed or repaired process, steam or utility piping - install blinds/spades, isolate valves and instruments, fill, pressurize with a test pump or nitrogen, walk down flanges and welds on racks and at elevation (ladders, scaffold), soap-test joints, hold and chart pressure, then document and drain/depressurize.

Operating industrial/institutional facility: routine condition inspection of in-service piping systems - read pressure and temperature gauges on a fixed route, visually check lines, flanges, steam traps and pumps for leaks or corrosion, thermal/acoustic checks for steam or compressed-gas leakage, and log readings and anomalies for maintenance follow-up.

Pipe fabrication shop: hydrostatic test of shop-fabricated spools/assemblies at a dedicated test bay before shipment - fit test caps/blind flanges, fill with water, pressurize to spec with a test pump, hold and observe the gauge and welds, record the result on the test chart/traveler, then drain and dry.

sources.system: Spot (with Spot CAM+IR, FLIR MUVE C360, Enhanced Autonomy Payload)
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas Leaks | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped is deployed at a 40-acre midstream gas plant running autonomous inspection rounds that include analog gauge reading, thermal inspection and combustible-gas detection on in-service piping and compressor assets; on one round it autonomously detected a pinhole gas leak.
sources.transferJustification: Directly matches the 'inspect installed systems using pressure gauge, observation, or other methods' element of the task, performed on installed process piping in an operating plant.

sources.title: The Next Step in Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics ships automated inspection features for Spot covering thermal monitoring, acoustic leak detection (Fluke SV600-class acoustic imaging) and analog gauge reading, planned and reviewed through Orbit mission software.
sources.transferJustification: Acoustic leak detection and gauge ... the same observation-and-gauge methods a steamfitter uses when checking in-service piping for leaks.

sources.title: ANYmal X Tested for Autonomous Robot Inspections in Ex-zones at BASF
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal X legged robot autonomously runs multi-floor inspection missions in ATEX Zone 1 areas of BASF's Ludwigshafen steamcracker and Oxo plant, visually reading gauge values and liquid levels and performing thermal and acoustic checks on tanks, pumps and furnace walls.
sources.transferJustification: Same activity as the task's gauge-reading and observational inspection of installed piping systems, in a process plant with congested pipe racks and multi-level access.

sources.title: Hydrostatic testing: fast and accurate | Fives Group
sources.claim: Fives supplies Taylor-Wilson hydrostatic pipe testers used on tube/pipe finishing lines: the machine seals pipe ends, applies test pressures from 500 psi to over 25,000 psi with automatic length, grade and pressure settings, holds pressure with dedicated intensifiers, and transmits results through PLC control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mill hydrostatic testing of pipe. Same medium, same test pressures and the same accept criterion (no leak / no pressure decay over a timed hold) as a shop spool hydrotest, with the workpiece fixtured and end-sealed by the machine.

sources.title: Steel Pipe Hydrostatic Testing Equipment
sources.claim: Pipe-mill hydrostatic testing machines run under PLC control that seals the pipe, pressurizes, holds, records the pressure curve and generates the test report automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production hydrotesting of pipe. Confirms the whole test cycle (seal, pressurize, timed hold, record, report) is machine-executed in a purpose-built station, as a fixtured spool hydrotest would be.

sources.title: SOLO Pipeline Inspection Robot CCTV | RedZone Robotics
sources.claim: RedZone Robotics' SOLO robot is launched into a manhole and then autonomously traverses municipal sewer mains collecting CCTV/multi-sensor condition data; it is used in production by utilities such as DC Water and Pittsburgh.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: observational inspection of installed pipe. Shows autonomous in-pipe inspection exists only for manhole-launched municipal mains (8 in.+), not 4-6 in. building laterals entered through a cleanout with tight bends, so it does not transfer to plumbers' drain scoping.

tasks.label: Install pipe assemblies, fittings, valves, appliances such as dishwashers or water heaters, or fixtures such as sinks or toilets, using hand or power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service/replacement call in an occupied home: install or swap a water heater, toilet, sink/faucet, dishwasher supply and drain connection, or shutoff valves. Cramped closets and under-sink cabinets, existing (often non-standard, corroded) piping, homeowner belongings present, must be leak-tested and left clean.

Residential new construction or gut remodel: rough-in DWV and supply pipe assemblies (PEX/copper/PVC) through framing, set hangers and valves, then trim-out - set toilets, lavatories, tubs, hose bibs and water heater. Active, cluttered jobsite shared with other trades, layout differs house to house.

Commercial/institutional new construction (office, school, hospital, retail, data center): install overhead pipe assemblies, fittings, valves and hangers on racks and risers, sprinkler mains and drops, and set commercial fixtures. Work at height from lifts/ladders, coordinated with other trades on a changing site.

Industrial or steamfitting work inside an operating plant, refinery, power house or hospital mechanical room: rig and set fabricated spools, bolt flanges, install valves, steam traps and control assemblies, tie into live systems during a shutdown/turnaround. Institution controls access; layout is congested and as-built.

Shop prefabrication at a mechanical contractor's or fabricator's pipe fab shop: assemble and fit up pipe spools - straight pipe with elbows, tees, reducers, flanges and valve ends - on rollers/positioners and weld or join them, then hydro-test and tag for field delivery.

sources.system: KRANENDONK Robotic Pipe Shop (Apollo Spool Milling Station + Aurora Spool Welding Station, PSWP software)
sources.title: Pipe Spool Automation - KRANENDONK
sources.claim: KRANENDONK's Robotic Pipe Shop is a ... pipe-spool fabrication system (Apollo milling station plus Aurora welding station) that covers cutting/beveling, fit-up, welding and material handling of straight pipe with elbows, tees, flanges and other fittings inside a purpose-built robotic cell.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the shop-prefabrication form of this task: assembling pipe with fittings/flanges into pipe assemblies; same objects (carbon/stainless pipe, elbows, tees, flanges) and joint-quality requirements as a pipefitter's spool work.

sources.system: KRANENDONK Robotic Pipe Shop at JGC Corporation
sources.title: KRANENDONK strengthens collaboration with JGC through advanced Robotic Pipe Shop installation
sources.claim: A fully automated Robotic Pipe ... has been implemented at an industrial customer (JGC Corporation) producing pipe spools with robotic beveling and welding, indicating a real deployment rather than a demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: industrial pipe spool fabrication is the shop form of installing pipe assemblies and fittings; deployment establishes worker-quality, production-rate output.

sources.system: Novarc Spool Welding Robot (SWR) with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2
sources.title: Novarc automates arc welding processes with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2 - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Novarc's Spool Welding Robot with NovEye Autonomy welds pipe joints (flanges, tees, elbows, reducers) in fabrication shops without operator intervention during the weld, and is sold commercially to pipe fab shops.
sources.transferJustification: Joining fittings and flanges to pipe is the core of assembling pipe assemblies in a fab shop; corroborates that robotic joint-making at pipefitter quality is in routine commercial shop use, though the operator still performs fit-up on this system.

tasks.label: Anchor steel supports from ceiling joists to hold pipes in place.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial/institutional construction (offices, schools, hospitals, data centers): pipefitter works overhead from a lift or ladder on an active site, lays out hanger points from prints/BIM, drills anchors into a concrete deck or clamps to steel bar joists/beams, hangs threaded rod, bolts up trapeze/strut and clevis hangers, and sets the pipe in them. Debris, other trades, changing conditions.

Residential and light-commercial: anchoring steel straps, clamps, brackets and small hangers to wood ceiling joists in basements, crawlspaces, attics and joist bays for water, DWV and hydronic lines; overhead drilling and lag/screw fastening in tight, cluttered, as-found spaces.

Retrofit / tenant fit-out and sprinkler work in existing buildings: hanging branch lines and pipe supports from bar joists or wood joists in the plenum above existing ceilings, working around existing duct, conduit and equipment, off ladders or lifts, with concealed and variable structure.

Industrial and institutional plant work (refineries, power, food plants, hospital mechanical rooms): bolting or welding heavier steel pipe supports, brackets and racks to overhead structural steel/joists for large-diameter or high-temperature pipe; congested live plant, hot-work permits, heavy material handling.

Shop prefabrication: in the contractor's fab shop, building trapeze hangers, strut racks and multi-trade rack modules — cutting strut, drilling, and bolting/welding steel support brackets to structural members on benches or jigs before shipment to the site.

sources.developer: fischer group / fischer BauBot Services GmbH
sources.title: Construction Robots Advance Frankfurt Office Build | Walls & Ceilings
sources.claim: fischer's BauBot mobile robots autonomously drill anchor holes in concrete ceilings on an active office construction site, but human crews install the anchors afterwards — the robot performs only the drilling step of hanger/fixing installation.
sources.transferJustification: Same work context (overhead fixing points for suspended building services); cited to show what on-site robots actually complete — hole drilling only, not the steel support assembly.

sources.title: BauBot – fischer Spain
sources.claim: fischer markets the BauBot as able to drill and set anchors overhead in ceilings and walls, though deployment reports describe autonomous drilling with human anchor setting.
sources.transferJustification: Anchor setting into ceilings is the first step of anchoring steel pipe supports; autonomy of the anchor-setting mode is not established, so this item cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Hilti Releases All New Features for the Hilti Jaibot
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a semi-autonomous mobile robot deployed on construction sites worldwide that drills overhead anchor holes from BIM data; it does not install rod, strut or hangers.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the drilling sub-step of overhead MEP hanger installation on real jobsites; establishes the state of on-site (E3) capability as partial.

sources.system: Hitachi dual-arm construction robot (structural part fixation system)
sources.title: Dual-Arm Construction Robot for Automatic Fixation of Structural Parts to Concrete Surfaces in Narrow Environments (arXiv 2403.19948)
sources.claim: Hitachi's dual-arm construction robot autonomously performs the complete fixation of an MEP structural part (bracket/hanger) to a concrete surface — positioning the part, drilling, inserting and hammering the anchor, and torquing the nut — in a purpose-built experimental rig; one side of one part took about 9.5 minutes and the system is described as a concept.
sources.transferJustification: The paper's target task is installation of MEP support brackets and hangers on concrete ceilings/walls — the same objects, anchors and precision as this task — demonstrated on a fixtured concrete test wall, i.e. a purpose-built robotic setup.

sources.title: Robot System for Highly Efficient Work at Heights on Scaffolding under Unstable Installation Conditions
sources.claim: Hitachi reports its dual-arm system inserts anchor bolts into concrete with over 99% success even when the supporting scaffolding is unstable, using machine-learning control and automatic rescheduling on error.
sources.transferJustification: Anchor-bolt insertion into concrete to secure piping fixtures and parts is the load-bearing core of anchoring steel pipe supports; demonstrated in a controlled test setup, not a working jobsite.

sources.system: Zeman Steel Beam Assembler (SBA) / Peddinghaus PeddiAssembler
sources.developer: Zeman Bauelemente / Lincoln Electric, distributed by Peddinghaus
sources.title: Flexible automation meets structural fabrication — The Fabricator
sources.claim: The Zeman Steel Beam Assembler (sold in the US as the Peddinghaus PeddiAssembler) is a commercially deployed fenced robotic cell in structural steel fabrication shops in which robots scan the fixtured beam and automatically fit, position and weld steel connection parts onto it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: attaching steel plates, brackets and fittings to structural steel members. Same objects (steel supports on steel members), same load-bearing quality requirement and comparable placement precision; applies when the member is fixtured and conveyed to the machine (the E1 counterfactual).

sources.title: PEDDINGHAUS PeddiAssembler Robotic Beam Assembler — Akhurst Machinery
sources.claim: The PeddiAssembler robotic beam assembly cell places all welded connection plates on beams with a single operator loading material, in a shop robotic welding cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic attachment of steel connection hardware to fixtured structural members — the fabricated-in-a-cell equivalent of bolting/welding pipe supports to joists and beams.

sources.system: House of Design robotic panel framing / floor truss systems
sources.title: Panel Framing – House of Design Robotics
sources.claim: House of Design supplies commercially deployed robotic panel-framing lines for offsite construction in which robots automatically insert and fasten framing members into wood panels and floor/roof cassettes on fixtured tables.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic fastening of members and hardware to wood framing in a fixtured factory line; transfers to screwing/lagging steel pipe-support brackets to wood ceiling joists presented in a jig, comparable fastening forces and tolerances.

sources.developer: ProBuild Robotics (reseller of a Chinese construction robot)
sources.title: Screw support installation robot – ProBuild Robotics
sources.claim: A vendor markets a 'screw support installation robot' for installing screw hangers for duct, cable tray and light water pipe in underground garage ceilings, claiming automatic drilling, automatic loading and consistent expansion-bolt torque at 30 bolts/hour; independent corroboration and autonomy level are not established.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task (overhead screw hangers for pipe), but the source is vendor marketing with no verified deployment or autonomy evidence, so it is treated as unclear and does not support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Attach pipes to walls, structures, or fixtures, such as radiators or tanks, using brackets, clamps, tools, or welding equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/institutional new construction (hospital, school, office): hanging domestic water, waste, and hydronic mains overhead from a concrete deck or steel joists — setting clevis hangers and threaded rod, building strut trapezes, lifting 2–6 in. pipe into place and tightening clamps, working off scissor lifts among other trades, with cluttered floors, obstructions and field-adjusted elevations/slope.

Residential rough-in (new build or remodel): strapping and clipping copper, PEX, CPVC and PVC DWV to wood studs, plates and joists inside stud bays, crawl spaces and attics using nail-on straps, plastic clips and hangers, in confined, irregular framing with limited access.

Service/repair and retrofit in occupied buildings and homes: re-securing a loose or vibrating pipe to an existing wall or joist, adding or replacing clamps and brackets at a radiator, water heater or tank, in basements, mechanical closets and behind fixtures, working around finished surfaces and live systems.

Industrial/process plant pipefitting (refinery, power, chemical, food plant): welding pipe shoes, trunnions and support lugs, bolting U-bolts, clamps and guides to structural steel on pipe racks and to vessels/tanks, often at height, under hot-work permits during construction or turnaround.

Offsite prefabrication/fabrication shop: building pipe spools, multi-trade racks and skids on benches and jigs — welding supports and attachments onto pipe and bolting clamps and strut hardware so the pipe is fixed to the module frame before shipping.

sources.system: KRANENDONK Robotic Pipe Shop (Apollo milling + Aurora spool welding station, flange mounting robots)
sources.title: KRANENDONK - Robotic Pipe Shop (bendable)
sources.claim: Kranendonk's Robotic Pipe Shop is a commercially supplied, fully automated pipe spool line in which vision-guided robots pick, position and weld flanges and fittings onto pipe without manual setup, in fixtured stations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic welding of steel attachments (flanges, fittings) onto steel pipe in a fixtured cell. Transfers to attaching pipe to supports/structures with welding equipment because the objects (steel pipe and steel attachment hardware), the weld precision required, and the fixtured cell environment are the same as welding pipe shoes, lugs and brackets.

sources.system: KRANENDONK Robotic Pipe Shop at JGC Corporation
sources.title: Robotic Welding & Cutting Automation Company - KRANENDONK
sources.claim: The fully automated Kranendonk Robotic Pipe Shop has been implemented at an industrial customer (EPC contractor JGC Corporation), showing it is deployed rather than a laboratory demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: substantiates that automated welding of attachments onto piping in a fixtured fabrication cell is a working, delivered production system for process-plant piping.

sources.title: Pipe Spool and Skid Automation - KRANENDONK
sources.claim: The Aurora station performs the full welding sequence (TIG root, MIG/MAG fill and cap) on pipe joints automatically, without manual intervention, to code-quality standards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated welding on piping at accepted fabrication quality. Establishes that weld quality in the fixtured cell is at production standard, which is what attaching pipe to structure by welding requires.

sources.system: PD400UR automatic screwdriving cell (UR5e cobot + Nitto Seiko screwdriver); ESTIC ERS robotic workcells
sources.developer: Nitto Seiko America / Universal Robots; ESTIC America
sources.title: New Tech for Robotic Fastening | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Off-the-shelf robotic screwdriving/bolting cells autonomously drive threaded fasteners on fixtured parts in manufacturing, providing the bolted-clamp fastening step of pipe attachment when the work is presented in a fixture.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous threaded-fastener installation on fixtured workpieces. Attaching a pipe with a clamp, strap or U-bolt is the same operation — place hardware over the presented pipe and drive/torque fasteners — at comparable precision, in the same fixtured-cell environment.

sources.developer: Europneumaq Industrial Solutions with INESC TEC
sources.title: Robots Automate Bolt-Tightening on Automotive Assembly Lines | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Robots are routinely used to tighten bolted joints on fixtured automotive assemblies, a deployed industrial application of autonomous torqued fastening.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic torqued bolting of brackets on fixtured assemblies; the clamp/U-bolt fastening used to secure pipe to a support is the same class of operation with comparable torque and positional tolerance.

sources.title: Jaibot - Hilti Corporation
sources.claim: The most advanced field robots for MEP work on construction sites only locate, mark and drill anchor holes in ceilings; the anchors, hangers and pipe are still set by tradespeople.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant negative evidence: the leading jobsite MEP robot performs only the hole-drilling sub-step, not attachment of pipe with brackets, clamps or welds, so it cannot complete the whole instance in an E2/E3 setting.

sources.title: BauBot | fischer
sources.claim: The fischer BauBot drills and automatically sets certified anchors into concrete on site from an anchor magazine, but stops at anchor setting and does not hang or clamp pipe.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic overhead anchor setting, a sub-step of pipe-support installation. Cited only as partial capability — it does not lift, align or clamp pipe, so it cannot substantiate completion of the whole task in the field.

sources.title: Press Announcement: Construction Robot Laboratory Tours (Shimizu)
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy uses sensor-guided dual arms to insert ceiling suspension ... base materials and screw ceiling boards in place on real building projects, showing overhead fastening of ceiling systems but not piping.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous overhead fastening of building-system components at a jobsite. Cited as the strongest field precedent, but the objects differ fundamentally from long, heavy pipe runs needing alignment, slope and clamped/welded supports, so transfer to this task is not claimed.

sources.title: Development of a humanoid robot prototype, HRP-5P, capable of heavy labor
sources.claim: The HRP-5P humanoid autonomously picked up gypsum board and screwed it to a stud wall in a mocked-up residential construction setting, demonstrating robotic fastening of a component to framing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously driving screws to fasten a component to wood/steel studs. Supports the fastening motion for strapping pipe to framing, but as a slow research prototype in a purpose-built mockup it supports only a structured (E1-style) setting, not field-quality work.

tasks.label: Modify, clean, or maintain pipe systems, units, fittings, or related machines or equipment, using hand or power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service call: clearing clogged drain/waste lines and cleaning fouled traps, strainers and fixtures in a private home (kitchen/bath cabinet, basement, crawl space) with hand augers, drum machines or jetters; clog location and pipe condition unknown at arrival.

Residential/light-commercial repair and modification in place: rebuild or swap valves, faucet cartridges, supply stops, water-heater fittings; cut, ream, thread, solder or press short runs of copper/PEX/steel in tight chases and under fixtures, then leak-test.

Commercial/institutional building maintenance (school, hospital, office): in mechanical rooms and restrooms/kitchens, repack or replace valves, replace corroded pipe sections and hangers, clean strainers, service pumps, steam traps and backflow preventers; premises controlled by the facility, standard equipment, fixed layout.

Industrial/power-plant piping maintenance and turnaround work (refinery, chemical plant, powerhouse): hydroblast and clean heat-exchanger tubes and process lines, break and remake bolted flanges, replace steam traps, gaskets and valves on racks and in units under permit control.

Shop/prefab bench work: cut, bevel, thread, groove, ream and deburr pipe and fittings and assemble or modify spools on shop machines (bandsaw, threader, groover, benders) at a contractor's fabrication shop.

Underground/municipal main work: cleaning and maintaining buried sewer or water mains and laterals - jetting, root cutting, descaling, cutting in reinstatements - worked from a truck and manhole in a street or easement.

sources.system: KRANENDONK Robotic Pipe Shop (pipe spool automation, ZEROGAP beveling)
sources.title: Pipe Spool Automation - KRANENDONK
sources.claim: KRANENDONK's Robotic Pipe Shop automates the full pipe-spool workflow - cutting, beveling, fit-up and welding - driven directly from CAD/PCF data without manual programming, inside a purpose-built robotic cell.
sources.transferJustification: Cutting, beveling and fitting pipe and fittings with powered cutting tools is the same physical operation as the 'modify pipe systems, units, fittings ... using hand or power tools' element, on identical workpieces (steel pipe, flanges, fittings) and to the same fit-up/leak-tight acceptance standard.

sources.system: KRANENDONK Robotic Pipe Shop at JGC Corporation
sources.title: KRANENDONK strengthens collaboration with JGC through advanced Robotic Pipe Shop installation
sources.claim: A fully automated Robotic Pipe ... has been installed at an EPC customer (JGC) for production pipe-spool fabrication, i.e. the cell is a deployed system, not a demo.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: production fabrication and modification of pipe spools and fittings with machine tools, fixtured on rollers/positioners in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: StoneAge AutoBox 3L with Sentinel Automation Technology
sources.title: StoneAge releases Sentinel Automation Technology - BIC Magazine
sources.claim: StoneAge's Sentinel/AutoBox automated tube-lancing systems clean fouled pipe/tube interiors hands-free: the machine senses the tube sheet, positions the nozzles itself and runs the lances end to end while operators stand outside the blast zone.
sources.transferJustification: Cleaning scale, sludge and blockage out of the bore of pipes/tubes with high-pressure water is the same physical operation a plumber performs when jetting or descaling a fouled line; objects (fouled steel/copper tubes), tooling (high-pressure jet lances) and the accepted output (clear, free-flowing bore) match.

sources.title: StoneAge Releases the Sentinel Operations System 2.0 to Take your Cleaning Operations to New Heights
sources.claim: The Sentinel operations system learns the tube pattern automatically and visualizes the tube sheet for obstacle avoidance and consistent coverage, i.e. the cleaning cycle is machine-planned rather than joystick-driven.
sources.transferJustification: Substantiates that the automated cleaning cycle is planned and executed by the machine rather than continuously steered, supporting the transfer from tube-bundle cleaning to pipe-bore cleaning.

sources.system: RND Automation hydraulic valve assembly cell
sources.title: Robots assemble hydraulic valves | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Production robotic cells assemble and torque valve bodies and their threaded internals with powered drivers and then place them in leak-test fixtures, with parts presented in collets and pallets.
sources.transferJustification: Rebuilding or replacing valves, cartridges and threaded fittings and proving them leak-tight is the plumber's bench operation in this task; the cell handles the same class of objects (valve bodies, seals, threaded parts), the same powered tooling (torque drivers) and the same acceptance test (leak test).

sources.title: Novarc Technologies' Spool Welding Robot Installed At Seaspan's Victoria Shipyard - Manufacturing AUTOMATION
sources.claim: Novarc's Spool Welding Robot is deployed in real pipe-fabrication shops, including US mechanical contractors' shops and shipyards, welding pipe spools alongside a human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Shows shop-floor pipe modification robots in commercial use, but the SWR is a cobot that works with an operator handling fit-up and adjustments, so it is treated as non-autonomous supporting context only.

sources.title: High-Traction Sewer Robot with Compact DC Motors - FAULHABER
sources.claim: Commercial in-pipe rehabilitation and cleaning robots used in sewers (cutting, milling, jetting) are driven by a human operator from a cable remote control and monitor at the surface.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the buried-main cleaning/maintenance instance; documents that the fielded systems are continuously teleoperated and therefore cannot support a positive judgment in the street/underground setting.

tasks.label: Install automatic controls to regulate pipe systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential / light-commercial service call: plumber installs an automatic control on a home's water or hydronic system - a zone valve and its actuator on a boiler manifold, an aquastat or thermostat wired back to the boiler, a thermostatic mixing valve or pressure-reducing valve at the water heater, or a Wi-Fi leak-detection shutoff valve on the main. Work is in a basement, utility closet, attic or crawl space of an as-found house: congested existing piping, unknown wire routes, kneeling/overhead access, then a functional test.

New commercial construction (office, school, hospital fit-out): pipefitter installs BAS control valves with electric or pneumatic actuators, 2-way/3-way and pressure-independent control valves, sensor thermowells, flow meters and pressure transmitters into chilled-water, hot-water and steam piping in mechanical rooms and above ceilings. Active construction site with scaffolding and other trades; the fitter sets the valve in the line, mounts the actuator, lands control wiring or tubing, and turns it over to the controls contractor.

Sprinkler fitter trims out a fire-protection riser or zone: installs waterflow switches, tamper/supervisory switches on OS&Y and butterfly valves, pressure switches, alarm-check or dry-pipe valve trim and air maintenance devices, then wires to the fire alarm interface and performs flow/trip testing. Usually a new or renovated building still under construction, in a riser room or stair landing.

Service/retrofit in an occupied commercial or institutional building (hospital, campus, hotel): replace a failed control valve and actuator, add a pressure-independent control valve or PRV station, install a mixing valve or automatic makeup-water assembly on existing piping in a mechanical room or penthouse. Facility is staffed and maintained; work requires isolating and draining live systems, as-built congestion, and restoring service the same shift.

Industrial/process plant turnaround (refinery, chemical plant, power house, brewery): pipefitters set heavy flanged control valves with pneumatic diaphragm or piston actuators and positioners into process lines, install pressure regulators and safety/relief trim, bend and fit stainless instrument tubing to actuators and transmitters, and support loop checking. Plant premises with permits, scaffolding, elevated pipe racks and rigging.

Prefabrication / fabrication shop: shop pipefitter builds control assemblies before shipment - mounting control valves, zone valves, actuators, gauges, sensors and boiler/pump-skid trim onto pipe spools, manifolds and packaged skids on shop benches, then pressure- and leak-testing the assembly. Fixed shop layout, benches, jigs, overhead crane.

sources.system: RND Automation MAP valve assembly cell (Epson T3/G3 SCARA + C8 six-axis robots)
sources.title: Robots assemble hydraulic valves | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: A production assembly cell built by RND Automation uses Epson SCARA and six-axis robots to build hydraulic pressure-control valves: robots feed and thread valve components together, dispense thread-locking adhesive, a torque driver completes the joint, and a robot loads each unit into an automated leak-test fixture - fully automated make-up of threaded, leak-tight fluid-control joints inside a fixtured cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated assembly of a pressure-setting hydraulic control valve. It transfers to installing an automatic control on a pipe system at E1 because the objects (metal valve bodies, threaded fluid connections, springs/adjusters), the operations (compliance-assisted thread start, sealant, controlled torque, in-line leak verification) and the precision are the same ones a fitter performs when threading a control valve into a presented, fixtured piping assembly.

sources.system: Cosberg linear assembly line for solenoid valve actuators
sources.title: Linear assembly line - Cosberg SpA - test / for solenoid valve actuators
sources.claim: Cosberg supplies automated linear assembly lines that mount and test solenoid valve actuators: robots load the electrical coil onto the valve, the machine performs an electrical check that the coil is the right one and not open-circuit, and a robot palletizes the finished assembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated mounting and electrical functional testing of solenoid/electric valve actuators. Installing an automatic control includes exactly this actuator-to-valve mounting plus a functional electrical check; the components (valve body, coil/actuator, terminals) and precision are comparable, and the demonstrated setting is a fixtured indexing line.

sources.title: Automated Control Cabinet Wiring Solution for Scalable Renewable Energy Systems (SpringerLink)
sources.claim: Kiesling and Rittal's Averex is a commercially offered robotic wiring centre: a portal robot with a complex end effector that cuts, crimps, routes and lands control wires on devices, supporting both spring-loaded and screw terminals, replacing manual wiring of control panels.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated wiring of control enclosures. Installing an automatic control on a pipe system requires terminating control wiring at actuators, thermostats, flow/tamper switches and controllers - the same cut/strip/crimp/land-on-screw-or-spring-terminal operations Averex performs automatically, at comparable precision, in a fixtured machine environment.

sources.system: Danfoss Nordborg automated line with six Kuka six-axis robots
sources.title: Vision-Guided Robots Process Hydraulic Components | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Danfoss, a maker of heating and cooling valves and controls, runs an automated line at its Nordborg factory where six vision-guided Kuka six-axis robots handle and process hydraulic/valve components of 5-20 kg that were previously handled manually.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling and processing of valve bodies and hydraulic components in the same size and mass class as commercial control valves. It shows a cited system can pick, orient and place valve-scale hardware to assembly tolerances in a fixtured industrial cell - the handling half of installing a control valve at E1.

sources.title: Pipe Spool Automation - KRANENDONK
sources.claim: Kranendonk sells a Robotic Pipe Shop for pipe spool and skid fabrication in which material handling, cutting, beveling, fit-up of fittings and flanges to pipe, and welding are executed as one automated workflow, with a patented zero-gap bevel that removes manual fit-up guesswork.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fit-up and joining of fittings and flanges into pipe spools and skids in a purpose-built robotic cell. That is the piping-connection half of setting an in-line automatic control valve, on comparable pipe sizes and fit-up tolerances; it supports E1 only, since the work must be brought to the machine.
