tasks.label: Inspect structures to assess material or equipment needs, to establish the sequence of pipe installations, or to plan installation around obstructions, such as electrical wiring.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service/repair call in an occupied home: plumber inspects under sinks, in a basement, crawlspace, or water-heater closet to determine what parts, fittings and equipment the repair or replacement will need — identifying pipe material and sizes, valve/trap types, venting, access constraints and clutter, with no drawings available.

Residential new construction or gut remodel rough-in: plumber walks the framed house or opened walls with the plans, locates joists/studs, existing electrical wiring, ducts and structural members, decides pipe routing and drilling/notching locations, the order of DWV vs. supply installation, and lists fittings and materials to stage.

Commercial/institutional building under construction (office, hospital, school, data center): pipefitter or sprinkler fitter walks the floor and ceiling plenum, checks conflicts with ductwork, conduit, cable tray and steel, plans hanger/sleeve locations and the sequence of mains and branches relative to other trades, and notes material and equipment (lifts, rigging) needs.

Existing occupied commercial/institutional facility (hotel, hospital mechanical room, restaurant, school boiler room): inspect existing piping, pumps, boilers and connections to assess equipment and material needs for a replacement or retrofit, including access above ceilings and in chases, shutdown/isolation points, and installation sequence.

Industrial plant walkdown (refinery, power plant, food processing, chemical facility): steamfitter inspects existing process/steam piping to plan a tie-in or repair — verifying line sizes, flange ratings, insulation, supports, obstructions and clearances, and establishing sequence, scaffolding and rigging needs for the installation.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot + Trimble X7 / FieldLink (also HoloBuilder SpotWalk)
sources.title: Trimble Releases Turnkey Autonomous Robotic Scanning Solution for Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot
sources.claim: Trimble's X7 laser scanner integrated with Boston Dynamics' Spot lets the robot autonomously walk repeatable routes on active construction sites and capture 3D scans for progress documentation (used by Hensel Phelps at Denver Airport). It captures reality data only; the assessment of material needs, installation sequence and routing around obstructions is still done by people in the office.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous reality capture / progress documentation on a jobsite. It transfers only partially — the robot traverses the same unstructured construction environment the plumber inspects, but it follows pre-taught routes in open circulation space and produces point clouds, not an assessment of material or equipment needs, an installation sequence, or a route around wiring.

sources.title: AI Startup Using Robots and Lidar to Boost Productivity on Construction Sites - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Doxel deployed an autonomous LiDAR-equipped ground robot that scans construction sites daily (e.g., a Kaiser Permanente hospital project) and compares captured geometry with the BIM model to report installed quantities and quality. It measures what has already been installed against an existing design; it does not survey a structure to decide what materials/equipment are needed or how to sequence and route a new pipe installation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated as-built capture and BIM comparison on construction sites. Closest available analogue to "inspect the structure and judge ...", but the output is progress/quality against a pre-existing design, not the plumber's forward-looking material, equipment and sequencing plan.

sources.title: Quadruped robot boosts safety and maintenance at aging cement plant
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal has run autonomous inspection rounds in an operating cement plant since early 2025, completing over 33,000 inspections — walking predefined routes, climbing stairs and avoiding obstacles while collecting thermal, visual and acoustic data on known checkpoints. This is condition monitoring of fixed assets, not assessment of installation material needs or planning of new pipe runs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous industrial plant inspection rounds inside a structured facility (E2). It shows a robot can perceive plant piping and equipment autonomously, but the deliverable is sensor readings/anomaly flags on predefined checkpoints, not the steamfitter's judgment about line sizes, tie-in materials, clearances and work sequence.

sources.title: Jaibot Semi-Autonomous Drilling Robot - Hilti GB
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot drills ceiling holes for MEP installation from a BIM model on real construction sites, but a human must first lay out the site with a total station and reposition the robot; the robot executes a plan produced by others rather than inspecting the structure to create one.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: BIM-driven MEP hole drilling on a jobsite. It demonstrates model-to-site localization in the same environment, which is a prerequisite for planning work around obstructions, but the planning itself (what to install, in what order, around which conflicts) is supplied by human engineers beforehand.

sources.developer: SuperDroid Robots (and similar vendors, e.g. Uplink Robotics)
sources.title: Plumbing Crawlspace Inspection Robots | SuperDroid Robots
sources.claim: Crawlspace and confined-space inspection crawlers marketed to plumbers and home inspectors are remote-controlled camera platforms: the human drives the robot and makes the assessment from the video feed, so the inspection judgment remains with the worker.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant hardware for the residential inspection instances, but it is continuously teleoperated visual inspection with a human interpreting the feed, so it cannot support a positive judgment under the autonomy rule.

tasks.label: Maintain or repair plumbing by replacing defective washers, replacing or mending broken pipes, or opening clogged drains.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service call to open a clogged drain in an occupied private home: kitchen or lavatory sink, tub/shower, toilet, or main line via a floor-level cleanout. Plumber diagnoses the blockage location, removes a trap or opens a cleanout, runs a cable auger or small jetter through traps and bends, flushes to verify flow, and cleans up the customer's space.

Residential repair of a dripping faucet, leaking valve, or running toilet: disassemble the installed fixture in place (handle cap, screw, packing nut, stem or cartridge), replace worn washers, O-rings, seats, cartridge, or fill/flush valve, reassemble and test for leaks. Parts are often mineral-encrusted or corroded and models vary widely.

Residential repair of a broken or leaking pipe section (copper, PEX, CPVC, galvanized, or cast iron) in a wall cavity, under a floor, in a crawlspace, or in a basement: shut and drain the line, cut out the damaged length, prep, and join in a new section or coupling (solder, press, crimp, solvent weld, or threaded), then pressurize and test.

Commercial or institutional building (office, school, restaurant, hospital, hotel): clear clogged restroom fixtures, floor drains, and grease-laden kitchen waste lines by snaking or jetting from cleanouts, working around building occupants and staff in a facility with standard fixtures and maintained access.

Commercial or industrial building: replace a failed section of pipe or an in-line valve in a mechanical room, above a ceiling, or in a plant piping run — cut out the defective steel/copper pipe or valve, prep the ends, and rejoin by welding, threading, grooved coupling, or brazing; refill and test.

Exterior/buried work on a building sewer lateral or water service: cutting roots or clearing a stoppage from a cleanout in the yard, or making a spot repair on a cracked buried pipe, with excavation or trenchless methods in ground conditions taken as found.

sources.title: StoneAge | AutoBox 3L with Sentinel Automation Technology
sources.claim: StoneAge's AutoBox 3L tractor with Sentinel Automation Technology is a commercially sold automated high-pressure lancing system that positions cleaning nozzles by sensor feedback and cleans fouled/blocked heat-exchanger tubes end to end while the operator stays outside the blast zone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing deposits and blockages from the inside of pipes by high-pressure water lancing. This is the same essential act as jetting/rodding a clogged drain — driving a nozzle down a pipe of comparable diameter until flow is restored — performed on fixtured tube bundles at industrial scale, so it substantiates drain clearing when the pipe is presented to the machine.

sources.title: StoneAge releases Sentinel Automation Technology - BIC Magazine
sources.claim: Sentinel automated exchanger tube cleaning was formally released as a product and reported to outperform traditional (manual/remote) lancing methods, indicating deployed commercial use in refinery and petrochemical cleaning work.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above: mechanized removal of internal pipe fouling/blockage, transferring to drain clearing when the pipe is presented to the machine in a purpose-built cleaning setup.

sources.title: Terydon introduces Apollo to industrial cleaning market - BIC Magazine
sources.claim: Terydon's Apollo tube-cleaning machine with Smart Indexing Technology automatically moves the lance from tube to tube and cleans them with the operator removed from the blast zone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated internal cleaning of pipe runs by water jetting. Comparable objects (small-bore pipe), comparable act (clearing obstruction/deposit), machine-controlled traverse of the pipe interior; supports drain clearing under an E1 presentation.

sources.system: Spool Welding Robot (SWR) with NovEye Autonomy
sources.title: NovEye™ Autonomy - Novarc Technologies
sources.claim: Novarc's Spool Welding Robot with NovEye Autonomy welds pipe joints in fabrication-shop cells with the operator setting up and starting the weld and the robot completing it without intervention, producing X-ray-quality welds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making the pipe joint that mends a cut-out pipe. Joining a fixtured pipe to worker-acceptable (X-ray) quality is the operative step of 'replacing or mending broken pipes' once the work is presented fixtured, as an E1 setting would present it.

sources.system: NovEye Autonomy Gen 2 / Spool Welding Robot
sources.title: Novarc automates arc welding processes with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2 - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Independent trade coverage confirms Novarc's NovEye Autonomy Gen 2 produces high-quality pipe welds without operator intervention and is sold to fabricators across multiple industries.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: autonomous pipe-joint welding in a shop cell is the joining step of replacing a defective pipe section.

sources.system: Robotic Pipe Shop (ZEROGAP beveling + robotic welding line)
sources.title: KRANENDONK strengthens collaboration with JGC through advanced Robotic Pipe Shop installation
sources.claim: KRANENDONK has implemented a fully automated Robotic Pipe ... at JGC Corporation that prepares (cuts/bevels) and robotically welds pipe spools as an integrated automated production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cutting, end preparation and welding of pipe. Mending a broken pipe at E1 — where the pipe arrives fixtured in a positioner — reduces to cutting out the defect, prepping the ends and joining, which this line performs to reproducible quality.

sources.title: Robotic Induction Brazing of Copper to Brass - UltraFlex
sources.claim: UltraFlex's Dragon 15 brazing robot performs automated induction brazing of copper-to-copper and copper-to-brass pipe joints in a fixtured cell for an HVAC manufacturer, moving the coil to each joint and completing the braze on a programmed cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making brazed copper-tube joints, the joining method used on residential water piping. It shows the joint-making step of a copper pipe repair can be done under machine control when the joint is fixtured and presented.

sources.developer: ULC Technologies (deployed by Cadent Gas, National Grid, SGN)
sources.title: CISBOT - Cadent Gas Ltd
sources.claim: In-place repair of buried pipe by robots — sealing leaking joints inside live cast-iron mains — is performed by remotely controlled machines driven by a surface operator, not autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repairing pipe from the inside in the ground. Cited as evidence that the only fielded in-situ pipe-repair robots are continuously operator-driven, so they cannot support a positive judgment for buried lateral repair.

tasks.label: Repair or remove and replace system components.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service call in an occupied home: diagnose and replace a failed small component — faucet or cartridge, toilet fill valve/flapper/wax ring, angle stop, P-trap, hose bibb, garbage disposal. Shut off and drain water, work lying in a cramped sink cabinet or behind a toilet, break loose corroded/over-tightened connections, install the new part with correct sealant/torque, restore pressure and verify no leaks.

Residential/light-commercial major equipment component swap: remove and replace a 40–75 gal water heater, boiler circulator pump, expansion tank, gas control valve or mixing valve in a basement, garage or utility closet. Includes draining, disconnecting gas/water/vent or electrical, hauling the old unit out, setting the new one, making soldered/press/threaded connections, and leak/combustion checks.

Commercial or institutional building service (office, school, hospital, hotel): replace flush valves, backflow preventer internals, circulating pumps, mixing valves, steam traps, or a corroded section of copper/steel above a ceiling grid or in a mechanical room. Work from a ladder or lift in an occupied building, coordinate isolation/shutdown, restore and test.

Industrial process or steam piping (pipefitter/steamfitter) during a shutdown or turnaround: cut out and replace a failed gate/control valve, spool section, gasket, strainer or steam trap on a welded or flanged line in a pipe rack or plant room. Rigging, hot-work permits, cutting, fit-up, welding or bolt-up to torque spec, then hydro/leak test.

Fire sprinkler fitter in a commercial building: drain the system and replace corroded, painted-over, damaged or discharged sprinkler heads and short sections of branch line, or riser/backflow components; re-pressurize, air/hydro test and return the system to service.

Buried service line repair at a residence or in a street/yard: expose and repair or replace a broken water service, sewer lateral, or gas service — install a repair clamp or coupling, cut out and replace a pipe section, or rehabilitate a line trenchlessly; backfill and test.

sources.system: Novarc Spool Welding Robot (SWR) with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2
sources.title: Novarc automates arc welding processes with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2 - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Novarc's Spool Welding Robot with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2 performs autonomous multi-pass pipe welding in fabrication shops, adapting to root-gap and HiLo variation, but it is a cobot that works with a human welder who fits up, tacks and presents the joint; it does not remove failed components or make in-situ repairs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: joining pipe by arc welding, a sub-step of replacing a pipe spool or valve. It does not transfer to the whole task: the robot welds new spools that a human welder has cut, fitted and tacked in a shop fixture, and performs no removal of failed components, no thread/gasket sealing, and no leak testing.

sources.title: Improve tube and pipe welding with artificial intelligence
sources.claim: Novarc's CEO describes the SWR as a welding robot that operates alongside a human welder operator, confirming the human retains fit-up and process control in the fabrication shop.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the prior item (shop pipe welding); cited to show the human's continuing role in fit-up and setup, so the cell does not complete a component replacement end to end.

sources.title: CISBOT - Cadent Gas Ltd
sources.claim: CISBOT is a commercially deployed in-pipe robot that repairs leaking joints in live cast-iron gas mains under city streets (over 50,000 joints sealed since 2009 for National Grid, Con Edison, SGN, Cadent), but utilities describe it as a remotely controlled robot whose operator positions it and triggers injection from a control truck.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ repair of a piping system component (a leaking bell-and-spigot joint) in buried mains, closest existing analogue to the buried-service-line instance. It cannot support a positive judgment because the operator drives the robot and positions the tool head continuously.

sources.developer: University of Sheffield with Birmingham, Bristol and Leeds
sources.title: Tiny robots could help fix leaky water pipes
sources.claim: Pipebots micro-robots developed by University of Sheffield and partners autonomously navigate water pipes and detect cracks/faults; autonomous in-pipe leak repair remains a research project (No Dig Leak Repair) rather than a deployed service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-pipe defect detection and (prospective) sealing of small water mains. Inspection autonomy is demonstrated, but repair of a component to accepted, tested condition is still at project stage, so it does not substantiate completing this task.

sources.system: MEP construction robots (e.g., ceiling-drilling and rebar-tying robots)
sources.title: Humanoid robots in the construction industry: A future vision | McKinsey
sources.claim: As of late 2025, construction-sector robotics for mechanical/electrical/plumbing work is limited to pilots of single-purpose machines such as BIM-guided ceiling drilling and rebar tying; no system performs multi-step MEP component replacement, and these pilots have not scaled.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic execution of MEP trade work on buildings. It shows the frontier is single-step hole drilling and tying, well short of isolating, disassembling and replacing a piping component.

sources.system: Figure 03, Agility Digit, Tesla Optimus, Unitree H1/G1
sources.developer: Figure AI, Agility Robotics, Tesla, Unitree
sources.title: Humanoid Robots in Industrial Manufacturing: What They Can (and Can't) Do in 2026
sources.claim: In 2026 the leading humanoid platforms are in narrow pilots performing material handling, bin picking and ... part insertion, not tool-based maintenance or repair work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general-purpose autonomous manipulation in industrial settings, the capability a robot would need to swap piping components. Demonstrated scope (handling and simple insertion) does not reach tool-based disassembly and leak-tight reassembly.

tasks.label: Cut openings in structures to accommodate pipes or pipe fittings, using hand or power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential (and light-commercial) new-construction rough-in on an active jobsite: boring and notching wood studs, top/bottom plates, and floor joists with a right-angle drill, auger bits and hole saws so DWV, water and gas lines can pass; dozens of openings per house, sized/located to code (nail-plate clearances, joist boring limits).

Service and remodel work in an occupied private home: cutting access openings in finished drywall, plaster, ceramic tile, cabinet backs/bases and subfloor with jab saws, oscillating multi-tools and hole saws to reach or extend piping; unknown wiring/framing behind the surface, dust control and minimal-damage cuts expected.

Commercial/institutional new construction: cutting and punching openings through cold-formed metal-stud partitions, shaft walls, light-gauge joists, structural steel members and fire-rated assemblies so pipe mains, risers and sprinkler branch lines can pass; hole saws, band saws, torches and CNC-punched framing at the fabricator.

Concrete and masonry penetrations on a jobsite: core-drilling 2"–6" holes through cast-in-place slabs, foundation and CMU walls for pipe sleeves, and saw-cutting slab trenches for underground drain, using anchored core rigs and walk-behind saws with GPR scanning for rebar/post-tension.

Retrofit/service inside an occupied institutional or commercial facility (hospital, school, plant, restaurant): cutting openings in existing ceilings, corridor walls or chases for a repipe or new fixture branch, under infection-control/dust barriers and facility work rules.

Prefabrication/fab-shop work: cutting openings in prefabricated wall panels, bathroom pods, pipe racks and skids, and cutting branch openings in headers, on shop tables and CNC equipment before the assemblies ship to site.

sources.title: Home-building robots could help fix the housing crisis | CNN
sources.claim: AUAR's robotic timber micro-factory (an enclosed robot cell shipped in a container) cuts and assembles wall/floor/roof panels from digital plans and drills the holes in the framing for wiring and plumbing runs.

sources.title: AUAR and ABB bring robotic Micro-Factories to U.S. homebuilding - The Robot Report
sources.claim: AUAR micro-factories are a commercially deployed product: units have shipped to US builders, each rated at up to 180 homes per year, built around ABB robots and design-to-manufacturing software.

sources.title: Practical Guide to Web Openings in Cold-Formed Steel Framing
sources.claim: Scottsdale Scotpanel roll-forming steel-framing machines automatically punch pre-engineered plumbing holes (pipe-sized web openings) and smaller service holes in cold-formed steel studs and joists as the members are produced from coil.

sources.title: Steel Framing Machines - FRAMECAD ST950H
sources.claim: FRAMECAD's ST950H automated steel-framing line punches openings in framing members that provide the pass-throughs required for HVAC, mechanical, electrical and plumbing services.

sources.title: WEINMANN multifunction bridges
sources.claim: WEINMANN WALLTEQ multifunction bridges process fixtured timber-frame wall, floor and roof elements on a panel line and cut all openings in the element fully automatically, including routing and drilling operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the machine cuts window, door and outlet openings and drills through fixtured wall elements on a panel line. Same materials (framing lumber, sheathing), same routing/hole-saw class of cut and tolerances as boring a wall element for pipe pass-throughs.

sources.title: SPARTAN™ | Sink & Seam CNC Router - Park Industries
sources.claim: Park Industries' SPARTAN CNC router, working on slabs fixtured on its table in a fabrication shop, cores faucet holes and cuts and polishes sink openings in stone and porcelain using a 19-position tool changer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: coring faucet holes and cutting sink cut-outs is literally cutting openings in a hard mineral building element to accommodate pipes and plumbing fittings, with diamond tooling and fixtured workpieces — the same operation a plumber performs with a hole saw on counters, tile and masonry.

sources.system: Peddinghaus Advantage-2 CNC beam drill line
sources.title: CNC Beam Drill Line | Advantage-2 | Peddinghaus
sources.claim: Peddinghaus CNC beam drill lines automatically drill and mill holes through the webs and flanges of structural steel members fed through the machine in a fabrication shop.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making holes through steel structural members. Beam-web penetrations and sleeve holes that let pipe pass through steel framing are the same cut in the same material at tighter tolerance, performed with the member fixtured and conveyed to the machine.

sources.developer: DEWALT (Stanley Black & Decker) with August Robotics
sources.title: DEWALT and August Robotics launch downward drilling robot - Engineering.com
sources.claim: DEWALT/August Robotics' DALE is a commercially launched autonomous jobsite robot that reads CAD layouts and drills large numbers of holes downward into concrete floors (up to about 1-1/2 in. diameter) for anchoring racks and MEP support legs, with reported 99.97% location/depth accuracy over 90,000+ holes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous drilling of concrete on an active construction site. Cited to bound on-site capability — the holes are small-diameter blind anchor holes drilled downward into floors, not pipe-sized through-penetrations of slabs, walls or decks.

sources.title: Baubot Robot Breaks Guinness World Record for Most Holes Drilled in 24 Hours | Equipment World
sources.claim: fischer's BauBot drills anchor holes semi-autonomously in concrete floors, walls and ... on real projects such as the Koralm tunnel, where it set anchors used to fix and guide water pipes; record run was 3,717 holes of at least 10 mm diameter, 50 mm deep.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic drilling in concrete on a live construction site. Cited to bound on-site capability — 10 mm/50 mm anchor holes for pipe supports are far from the 2–6 in. through-penetrations needed to pass pipe through a structure.

sources.title: Hilti Unveils BIM-Enabled Construction Jobsite Robot
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a commercially available semi-autonomous jobsite robot that positions itself from BIM data and drills overhead anchor/installation holes in concrete ceilings for MEP contractors, with integrated dust removal and marking.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: BIM-driven drilling of holes in concrete for MEP installation on a live jobsite. Cited to bound on-site capability — the holes are small hanger/anchor holes in ceilings, not openings sized to pass pipe through a structure.

tasks.label: Install green plumbing equipment, such as faucet flow restrictors, dual-flush or pressure-assisted flush toilets, or tankless hot water heaters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential retrofit in an occupied single-family home: remove an existing 3.5 gpf toilet in a finished bathroom, clean/inspect the closet flange, set a new dual-flush or pressure-assisted toilet on a wax or foam seal, level and shim on tile, torque closet bolts without cracking china, assemble tank to bowl, connect the flexible supply to the angle stop, test flush and check for leaks, haul off the old fixture.

Residential tankless (on-demand) water heater installation replacing a tank unit in a garage, basement, or utility closet: mount the unit to the wall, run/upsize gas piping and install a sediment trap and shutoff, connect hot/cold with isolation/service valves, install stainless or PVC venting through wall or roof, run condensate drain, make electrical connection, purge, commission, and pass inspection.

Trim-out on an active new-construction or gut-remodel jobsite (multifamily or light commercial): set WaterSense low-flow toilets, faucets with flow restrictors, and low-flow showerheads on rough-ins across many units, working around other trades, dust, partially finished floors, and varying rough-in dimensions per plan.

Water-conservation retrofit inside an occupied institutional building (hotel, school, office, hospital wing): swap flushometer valves or set pressure-assisted/dual-flush toilets in tiled restrooms, install point-of-use tankless heaters in janitor/mechanical closets, coordinate shutdowns around occupants, restore service same day.

Low-flow trim swaps on existing fixtures: unscrew old aerators (often corroded/mineral-fouled) from lavatory and kitchen spouts and thread on flow-restricting aerators, plus low-flow showerheads, across apartments or facility restrooms during a conservation program or as an add-on to a service call; verify no drips and check flow.

sources.system: Estic High-Torque Screwdriving Solution on Universal Robots cobot
sources.date: 2026-07 (product page retrieved); product line marketed since ~2022
sources.title: High-Torque Screwdriving Solution — Universal Robots Marketplace
sources.claim: Commercial cobot screwdriving package (Universal Robots arm + Estic pulse tool) performs torque-controlled threaded fastening automatically in a fixtured workcell, with transducer/encoder feedback that detects cross-threading and floating screws.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic torque-controlled threaded assembly of small metal parts in a fixtured cell. Threading a flow-restricting aerator into a faucet spout is the same class of operation — a small threaded brass/plastic part started by hand-feel and tightened to a modest torque with cross-thread detection — so performance carries over when the faucet is presented fixtured to the machine.

sources.title: Robot screwdriver with screwfeeder | EoAT for assembly automation | OnRobot
sources.claim: Robot end-of-arm screwdriver with automatic screw feeding handles M1.6–M6 threaded parts with precise torque control, i.e. an off-the-shelf autonomous threaded-assembly end effector for fixtured cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated small threaded-fastener assembly. Screwing a flow restrictor/aerator insert into a fixtured spout uses the same motion, torque range and feeding problem, supporting completion only where the workpiece is brought to and held by the machine.

sources.system: Spool Welding Robot (SWR) with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2
sources.title: AI machine learning vision processing system automates pipe welding — The Fabricator
sources.claim: The most advanced automated pipe-joining system in the trades is a shop-based spool welding robot: vision-driven autonomous arc welding of pipe joints inside a fabrication shop, with human operators handling fit-up and loading.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: joining pipe. It shows automated pipe work exists only as fixtured, shop-based welding of spools; it does not extend to mounting appliances, gas/vent connections, seals or commissioning, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion for heater or toilet installation.

sources.title: Top Applications for New Robotic Technology in Plumbing Systems Installations and Repairs | HP Canada
sources.claim: Jobsite construction robots that are actually deployed are limited to layout printing; HP SitePrint marks plumbing fixture and system layouts on floors but does no installation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic work on plumbing projects at the jobsite. It bounds what jobsite robots do today — printing layout lines — and provides no manipulation capability for setting fixtures or connecting piping.

sources.title: Construction Robotics in 2026: 4 Workflows Where Robots Are Actually Working on Construction Site
sources.claim: Industry review of construction robotics finds a small set of working jobsite workflows and expects humanoid/multi-skill robots to be confined to controlled settings rather than general trade work.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the trade generally: no named jobsite system performs plumbing fixture installation; this item cannot support a positive judgment and is cited only to bound the state of the art.

tasks.label: Inspect work sites for obstructions or holes that could cause structural weakness.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential new-construction rough-in: plumber walks the framed house before drilling/notching, sighting along planned supply, waste and vent routes; checks joists, studs, trusses and plates for existing holes, notches, blocking, ducts and wiring, and judges whether the intended penetrations would weaken members. Active framing site with debris, ladders, partial floors and other trades.

Service or remodel work in an occupied existing home or small building: inspecting basements, crawlspaces, attics, chases and opened wall cavities before re-piping or a fixture relocation; confined, dark, dusty spaces, unknown as-built framing, insulation and stored belongings; judgment about where a pipe can pass without cutting a bearing member.

Commercial/institutional building under construction (hospital, school, office, multifamily): pre-installation walk of ceiling plenums, shafts, mechanical rooms and slabs; verifying sleeve and core-drill locations against structural drawings, checking existing penetrations, rebar and post-tension zones, and identifying obstructions from other trades along the planned route.

Retrofit/tie-in survey inside an operating institution-controlled facility (refinery, process plant, hospital mechanical spaces, campus utility building): pipefitter walks the fixed-layout, housekeeping-maintained facility to find obstructions along a new line's route and to assess existing wall/floor/structural-steel penetrations before cutting or drilling.

Fabrication or offsite-prefab shop: inspecting prefabricated assemblies before or after fabrication — multi-trade racks, bathroom pods, wall panels, skids — for openings/holes in members and for clearance conflicts along the pipe run, with the assembly on stands or a fixture in the shop.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot (Autowalk / Orbit site documentation)
sources.title: Automated Construction Site Documentation | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot quadrupeds run programmed autonomous Autowalk missions on live construction jobsites, self-charging from a dock and traversing common jobsite obstacles to capture documentation data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (progress documentation) shows autonomous traversal and imaging of an unstructured jobsite, the locomotion/sensing half of a plumber's site inspection; it does not itself judge structural adequacy of holes or notches.

sources.title: Trimble Spot the Dog - Autonomous Robotic Scanning System
sources.claim: A commercial turnkey package mounts the Trimble X7 laser scanner on Spot for autonomous scanning of construction sites, with point clouds compared to CAD/BIM for deviation and clash detection; used in production by Mace Group.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (as-built capture and clash detection) covers geometric obstruction finding along modelled routes, but the delivered product is a scan/deviation report for human interpretation, not the tradesperson's on-the-spot structural-weakening judgment, and it cannot enter joist bays, attics or closed cavities.

sources.title: NEWS: Doxel uses reality capture and AI to boost construction productivity - AEC Magazine
sources.claim: Doxel's autonomous LiDAR robots scan construction sites daily, indoors and outdoors, and deep-learning software compares installed work with the design-intent model to flag errors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (as-built quality/progress checking against a model) is the closest automated analogue to inspecting a site for deviations; its output is management analytics on installed components, not an assessment of holes or notches that weaken framing.

sources.title: Quadruped robot boosts safety and maintenance at aging cement plant
sources.claim: ANYmal quadrupeds autonomously run inspection routes inside operating industrial facilities, climbing stairs and avoiding obstacles; one unit completed over 33,000 inspections at a cement plant since early 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (routine plant inspection rounds) shows autonomous inspection inside an institution-controlled facility, but the inspection scope is equipment condition — gauges, thermal, acoustic, gas — not structural openings, notches or route obstructions for new pipe.

sources.system: ZEISS AIMax cloud II inline optical 3D sensor (robot-mounted)
sources.title: ZEISS AIMax cloud: Optical 3D sensor for inline measurements
sources.claim: Robot-based inline 3D metrology sensors measure complex features such as holes and bolts on parts presented in a production line, generating point clouds and measurement results within cycle time.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (inline dimensional inspection of fixtured workpieces) transfers to the E1 counterfactual of this task: with the structural assembly presented in a known pose, detecting holes/openings and checking them against the design model is exactly what these cells do, unattended and at production reliability.

sources.title: Manufacturing Quality Control - 3D Machine Vision - Bluewrist
sources.claim: A commercial robot-mounted 3D laser scanning inspection station scans parts for complete coverage, compares them to CAD models, and automatically alerts users when dimensional deviations or defects are detected.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (automated CAD-comparison inspection of a fixtured assembly) matches the E1 form of this task: identifying openings/holes and geometric conflicts on a presented workpiece and issuing an accept/flag decision without an operator.

tasks.label: Install pipe systems to support alternative energy-fueled systems, such as geothermal heating or cooling systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential geothermal heat pump install: plumber runs and joins the HDPE/PEX supply and return lines from the ground-loop entry point through the basement/crawlspace to the flow center and water-to-air heat pump, makes hydronic and condensate connections, purges/flushes and pressure-tests the loop, in an occupied or under-construction single-family home with as-found joists, chases and clutter.

Outdoor ground-loop field work at a residential or small commercial site: butt/socket-fusing 3/4"-1.25" HDPE U-bend loops and header manifolds in a muddy header pit or trench, tying vertical borehole loops or horizontal slinky loops into the header, pressure/flow testing, and routing the header through the foundation wall, alongside drill and excavator crews in weather.

Commercial/institutional geothermal or district-energy distribution piping in a building under construction: welded steel or fused HDPE mains and risers, hangers and supports overhead in ceilings and shafts, mechanical-room headers, pumps, valves and heat-exchanger connections, coordinated around other trades on an active jobsite.

Retrofit tie-in of a new geothermal/heat-pump or solar-thermal system to an existing building's hydronic system: cutting into existing boiler/tank piping in a cramped basement, attic or crawlspace, fitting copper/PEX/steel around existing obstructions, setting a buffer tank and manifold, refilling and commissioning without leaks in an occupied home or small commercial building.

Shop prefabrication for the same alternative-energy job: the contractor's fabrication shop cuts, bevels, fits and welds steel pipe spools, header manifolds and mechanical skids for the geothermal plant, which are then trucked to site for setting and final tie-in.

sources.date: 2020-10 (commercial release; still the flagship MEP jobsite robot as of 2026)
sources.title: Hilti Unveils BIM-Enabled Construction Jobsite Robot
sources.claim: The most advanced commercially deployed MEP-installation robot on building sites drills anchor holes in ceilings from a BIM model; an operator drives it between positions and human trades still install all pipe, hangers and equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: overhead drilling for MEP hanger installation on the same jobsites. It shows the frontier of jobsite MEP robotics is hole drilling only, so it cannot substantiate completion of pipe-system installation instances.

sources.system: KRANENDONK Robotic Pipe Shop (with ZEROGAP beveling)
sources.title: Pipe Spool Automation / Robotic Pipe Shop — KRANENDONK
sources.claim: A fully integrated robotic pipe shop performs the whole spool-fabrication chain — cutting, beveling, fit-up and welding — driven from the CAD/spool model, and has been installed at EPC contractor JGC.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial/shipyard steel pipe spool fabrication. Transfers to shop prefabrication of geothermal header spools and skid piping: same objects (carbon/stainless pipe, elbows, tees, flanges), same joining process and fit-up tolerances, same fixtured cell.

sources.system: Novarc Spool Welding Robot (SWR) with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2
sources.date: 2024-07 (NovEye Autonomy Gen 2 launch); SWR commercial since 2017
sources.title: Maximizing Welder Workforce with Automation featuring Novarc Technologies, Inc. — MCAA
sources.claim: A spool welding robot used in mechanical-contractor pipe fabrication shops welds pipe joints with no operator intervention at code-quality; the operator sets the spool up in the positioner and starts the cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pipe welding in mechanical contractors' fabrication shops (MCAA is the US mechanical contractors' association). Same pipe sizes and code-quality welds required for geothermal plant headers and skids, performed at a fixed welding station.

sources.date: 2023-2025 (commercial; used by Bechtel on solar projects)
sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Retrofitted excavators dig utility trenches autonomously on construction sites, but the automation covers excavation only; laying, fusing and testing the pipe in the trench remains human work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: trenching for buried utilities, the excavation step preceding horizontal ground-loop installation. It does not handle, fuse, header or test loop piping, so it cannot substantiate completion of the ground-loop instance.

tasks.label: Install fixtures, appliances, or equipment designed to reduce water or energy consumption.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied single-family home or apartment: replace an old toilet with a WaterSense 1.28 gpf model — shut off and drain, unbolt and remove old bowl, scrape and inspect the closet flange, set new wax ring and bolts, place, level and shim the bowl, attach tank, connect the supply riser, caulk, and leak-test in a cramped bathroom with unknown existing rough-in.

Home service call: swap faucets, showerheads and aerators for low-flow models and add a hot-water recirculation pump or thermostatic under-sink valve — working overhead inside a base cabinet, threading and taping small connections, dealing with corroded existing supply stops and varied fixture geometry.

Home basement, garage or utility closet: replace a storage water heater with a high-efficiency tankless or heat pump water heater — remove and haul the old tank, set/mount the new unit, run water lines, gas and venting or a dedicated electrical circuit, add expansion tank and condensate drain, then fill, purge, commission and check for leaks.

Commercial/institutional building (office tower, school, hospital, hotel) restroom retrofit: install dozens of low-consumption flush valves, sensor faucets and low-flow or waterless urinals across repeated standard-layout restrooms while the facility is occupied and controlled by building management.

New construction or gut-renovation trim-out on an active jobsite: set high-efficiency toilets, lavatory and kitchen fixtures, tankless heaters and hydronic/heat-pump equipment against roughed-in stubs, coordinating with other trades amid debris, temporary lighting and shifting site conditions.

sources.date: 2020-10 (introduced); still marketed and deployed as of 2026
sources.title: Hilti Unveils BIM-Enabled Construction Jobsite Robot
sources.claim: The most advanced MEP-related jobsite robot in wide use, Hilti's Jaibot, only drills anchor holes in ceilings from BIM data after an operator drives it into position; it does not install fixtures, appliances or piping.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: overhead drilling for MEP installation. Cited to show the frontier of on-site plumbing-adjacent robotics is hole drilling; it does not transfer to setting and connecting fixtures, which requires seal handling, threaded connections and leak testing.

sources.system: Vector Automation fire sprinkler pipe fabrication cell (two-robot weld/plasma cell)
sources.title: Fire Sprinkler Pipe Factory Automation by Vector
sources.claim: Robotic automation of pipe work exists only in fixtured factory cells that cut, fit and weld couplings onto sprinkler pipe spools; no cell installs fixtures or appliances into a plumbing system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shop fabrication of pipe spools in a purpose-built cell. Objects are bare pipe and couplings in fixtures, not fixtures/appliances joined with gaskets, wax seals, thread sealant and torque-critical unions, so it does not substantiate this task even at E1.

sources.system: Robot end-effector concept for hydrogen tube-nut bolting (industrial robot cell)
sources.developer: Ruhr-University Bochum, Chair of Production Systems (LPS)
sources.title: Robot-Based Assembly of Hydrogen Tube Fittings for Large-Scale Electrolyzers
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed production-engineering work states that hose and tube (threaded fitting) connections — the core of connecting a water-saving fixture or appliance — have not yet been automated in a process-safe way, even in factory assembly of electrolyzers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly of threaded tube/hose connections in a fixtured industrial cell. It is the closest analogue to making a fixture's supply connections, and the source reports it as unsolved, so no E1 positive judgment is available.

sources.system: None (survey of climate-relevant robotics; identifies pipe-fitting/installation robots as future work)
sources.title: A Roadmap for Climate-Relevant Robotics Research
sources.claim: A 2025 robotics research roadmap identifies autonomous installation of energy-saving heating equipment (electric boilers, heat pumps) as an open research opportunity rather than an achieved capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing energy-saving heating equipment. Cited as evidence that no fielded robot performs this installation work; supports negative judgments only.

sources.system: Survey of construction robot pilots (rebar tying robots, ceiling drilling robots, humanoid pilots)
sources.title: Humanoid robots in the construction industry: A future vision
sources.claim: As of late 2025, construction-site robotics is limited to single-task, non-humanoid machines (rebar tying, ceiling drilling); humanoids remain at pilot stage without large-scale deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general construction trade work on site. Establishes that no deployed construction robot performs multi-step fixture installation, supporting negative judgments for site and home instances.

tasks.label: Repair hydraulic or air pumps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-place repair of a reciprocating or rotary-screw air compressor serving a plant's compressed-air piping: pipefitter diagnoses low discharge pressure/leakage, isolates and depressurizes, breaks loose oily or corroded fasteners, pulls the head, replaces reed valves, gaskets, unloader or check valve, retorques to spec, refills oil, and runs the unit up to pressure to verify. Plant mechanical/compressor room, hot and confined access, other trades present.

Bench rebuild in the shop of a pump brought in from the field (hydraulic gear/vane pump, jet pump end, or compressor pump): full teardown on a bench with hand and power tools, pressing out bearings and shaft seals, measuring wear, cleaning parts, fitting a rebuild kit (O-rings, seals, gaskets, wear plates), reassembly to torque and clearance spec, then bench/pressure test.

Residential or light-commercial in-place pump repair: shallow-well jet pump, submersible well pump control/pump end, sump pump, or hydronic circulator with a leaking seal or failed cartridge. Work occurs in a basement, crawlspace, pit, or utility closet with tight access, unknown prior workmanship, standing water and corrosion; homeowner present.

Field repair of a hydraulic power unit or hydraulic pump on jobsite equipment (pipe-fusion machine, hydraulic press, jack pump, test pump): troubleshoot low pressure, replace shaft seal, coupling, relief valve or leaking fittings/hoses, bleed and re-prime the system, verify pressure under load. Outdoors or in an active construction area, variable weather and debris.

Institutional/municipal pump repair: lift-station, booster, or process pump in a utility room or wet-well vault — pull the pump, replace mechanical seal, impeller, or wear rings, re-shim and align to the driver, reinstall on the piping with new gaskets, and commission with pressure/flow check. Facility-controlled premises, confined-space and lockout/tagout procedures.

sources.system: Robotic disassembly systems for remanufacturing (industry-wide survey)
sources.developer: Robotics and Automation News (trade press review of the sector)
sources.title: Automation in remanufacturing: how robots are extending product lifecycles
sources.claim: Trade-press review of remanufacturing automation states that robotic disassembly of used products is only beginning to emerge and that used-unit variability — seized bolts, deformed parts, inconsistent assembly — remains a major obstacle, leaving the work with skilled human technicians.
sources.transferJustification: Repairing a used hydraulic or air pump is exactly a teardown-inspect-replace-reassemble cycle on a worn unit; this source characterizes the state of the art for that class of work and shows no system completes it.

sources.system: AI-enabled robotic disassembly (systematic review of 62 peer-reviewed studies)
sources.developer: Ameur et al., Hassan II University / Arts et Métiers (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.title: The future of robotic disassembly: a systematic review of techniques and applications in the age of AI
sources.claim: A 2025 systematic review of 62 studies on AI-enabled robotic disassembly concludes that robots without cognitive reasoning have serious limitations relative to humans when disassembly involves uncertainty; the literature is dominated by research cells and human–robot collaboration rather than fielded autonomous teardown-and-rebuild systems.
sources.transferJustification: Pump repair requires disassembling a used, worn, sometimes corroded assembly under uncertainty — the exact regime this review identifies as unsolved for autonomous robots.

sources.system: Human–robot collaborative disassembly cell (2× KUKA LBR iiwa 14 R820)
sources.developer: Autonomous Remanufacturing Laboratory, University of Birmingham (Pham group)
sources.title: An experimental human-robot collaborative disassembly cell
sources.claim: A laboratory human–robot collaborative disassembly cell using two KUKA LBR iiwa arms was demonstrated on an automotive turbocharger, i.e. disassembly of a rotating fluid machine still requires a human partner and remains a research-lab case study.
sources.transferJustification: A turbocharger is a used rotating machine with shaft, seals and bearings comparable to a pump; the cited work covers only collaborative disassembly in a lab, not autonomous rebuild and test, so it does not substantiate pump repair even at E1.

sources.system: RAISE robot-assisted selective disassembly and sorting system
sources.title: RAISE: A Robot-Assisted SelectIve Disassembly and Sorting System for End-of-Life Phones
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic cell achieves high-rate selective disassembly of end-of-life phones (over 120 units/hour, 98.9% success) in a fixed purpose-built station — the strongest current fixtured-cell teardown capability, but limited to removing components from small consumer electronics, with no reassembly, sealing, torquing or functional testing.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the state of the art in purpose-built teardown cells: the objects (phones) and the scope (disassembly and sorting only) do not transfer to diagnosing a worn pump, fitting seals and bearings, torquing a reassembly, and pressure-testing it.

sources.title: Industrial Inspection Solutions | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot is commercially deployed for autonomous inspection rounds in industrial facilities, collecting thermal, visual and acoustic data (including air-leak detection), but its marketed capability is inspection and data collection, not mechanical repair of equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Shows what mobile robots actually do autonomously inside plant rooms where pumps and compressors live: they inspect and detect leaks; no cited capability to disassemble and rebuild a pump.

tasks.label: Weld small pipes or special piping, using specialized techniques, equipment, or materials, such as computer-assisted welding or microchip fabrication.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop prefabrication in a pipe/mechanical-contractor fab shop: GTAW root plus fill/cap on small-bore (3/4"-2") carbon and stainless spools and stainless tube subassemblies, pipe set on rollers/positioners at a welding bay, fit-up and tack, argon back-purge, welds accepted by visual/RT or borescope and logged.

Semiconductor / microchip fab high-purity work: closed-head orbital autogenous GTAW of 1/4"-1" 316L electropolished tubing for UHP gas and chemical distribution - mostly prefabbed tube racks/assemblies in a controlled workshop, plus final tie-ins made inside the cleanroom/subfab, with coupons, bead-color/oxide criteria and weld data logging.

Pharmaceutical, biotech, or food/beverage plant: orbital welding of 1"-3" sanitary OD tube for process lines and skid hook-ups, largely welded in place along installed runs and in equipment rooms, ASME BPE acceptance criteria, purge control, borescope inspection and weld-log documentation.

Operating industrial plant or building mechanical room maintenance/repair: small-bore socket and butt welds on instrument, sample, steam-tracing and hydraulic lines, in tight, overhead or confined fixed positions (5G/6G), often on shutdown with hot-work permits and existing, sometimes contaminated, pipe.

Jobsite field work on specialty alloy small piping (chrome-moly, duplex, titanium, aluminum) at a construction site, refinery turnaround lay-down yard, or unfinished building: fixed-position welds with tents/purge dams, weather and access variability, hardness/PWHT and NDE requirements.

tasks.label: Operate motorized pumps to remove water from flooded manholes, basements, or facility floors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service call: plumber carries a portable submersible or trash pump down stairs into a flooded basement or crawlspace (sump failure, burst supply line, storm water), sets the pump in the low spot amid stored belongings and debris, routes discharge hose out a window/door or to a floor drain, plugs it in or fuels it, monitors and repositions as the level drops, then removes standing residue and equipment.

Commercial/institutional building interior flood: mechanical or boiler room, elevator pit, retail sales floor, or hospital basement flooded by a burst pipe, backed-up drain, or leaking equipment. Plumber brings a portable pump or wet vacuum, sets suction in the deepest point, runs discharge hose to a drain or outside, and pumps down while the facility stays occupied.

Flooded manhole, valve vault, or meter pit in a street or utility right-of-way must be pumped down before entry for a repair or tie-in. Worker sets traffic control, lowers a submersible or places a suction hose from a trash pump, discharges to a nearby storm inlet or tank, monitors solids/silt and confined-space gas conditions.

Construction-site dewatering during underground pipe installation: keeping a trench or excavation dry with a diesel trash pump or wellpoint/sump setup, laying suction and discharge hoses across the site, priming and starting the pump, and keeping it running (or auto-cycling) through the workday as groundwater and rain refill the hole.

Industrial/plant work by pipefitters and steamfitters: pumping out a pit, tank, condensate sump, or hydro-test water in a controlled plant environment before or after mechanical work, using plant-supplied portable pumps and permanent discharge points.

sources.system: Xylem Godwin Dri-Prime pumps with PrimeGuard 2 controller and Field Smart Technology (FST)
sources.title: Xylem Shows Field Smart Technology at ConExpo — Rental Equipment Register
sources.claim: Commercial dewatering pumps with programmable microprocessor controllers take level, float, flow and pressure inputs and start and stop the pump automatically, without an operator present — i.e., a machine, not a person, performs the pumping operation once the pump and piping are installed at a sump.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (operating a motorized dewatering pump to remove water); the controller performs the start/stop/monitor function the worker would perform, in a setting where the pump and suction/discharge piping are already installed.

sources.system: Zoeller Model M53 'Mighty-Mate' automatic sump pump
sources.title: Model M53 Sump Pump 3/10 HP LED Plug — Zoeller Pumps
sources.claim: Fully automatic float-operated submersible sump pumps are the standard installed means of removing water from basement sumps; the float switch turns the pump on and off with no human action.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (motorized pump removing water from a basement), but only where the space is purpose-built for the machine: floor pitched to a pit, pump seated, discharge piped.

sources.system: Lift-station level sensing and automatic pump control (ultrasonic/submersible/radar transmitters with PLC or float control)
sources.title: Lift Station Level Sensing — Dwyer Omega
sources.claim: Wastewater lift stations and wet wells (the purpose-built equivalent of a flooded manhole) use level sensors feeding a stand-alone or PLC controller that starts and stops the pumps automatically and reports to SCADA, dewatering the structure without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (pumping down a below-grade wet structure) in the purpose-built version of the manhole/vault: fixed pump, fixed discharge main, level control.

sources.system: Mine water and dewatering control systems (submersible hydrostatic level transmitters + control panels/telemetry)
sources.title: Mine Water and Dewatering Control — ICON Process Controls
sources.claim: Underground and open-pit mines run automated dewatering: level transmitters in sump pits and collection wells drive automated pump activation and remote monitoring of plant water pits.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (pumping water out of an industrial pit/sump) executed by machine control in a fixed installation built around the pump.

sources.system: 'Lung Tan Shui' mobile powerful pumping robots (Drainage Services Department)
sources.developer: Hong Kong Drainage Services Department (procured units)
sources.title: Dewatering robots are a boom to fighting floods — The Standard (Hong Kong)
sources.claim: The machines that actually go to arbitrary flooded locations and pump them out — Hong Kong's 'water-pumping dragon' mobile pumping robots deployed to streets, car parks and hospital grounds — are remotely operated by human crews, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task (mobile machine pumping out flooded spaces as found), but remote-operated, so it cannot support a positive judgment at E2/E3.

sources.system: MHI Water Cannon Robot and Hose Extension Robot
sources.title: MHI Develops Autonomous "Water Cannon Robot" and "Hose Extension Robot" for Use in Firefighting
sources.claim: Autonomous robots can lay long runs of hose and position themselves at an industrial site: MHI's hose extension robot automatically deploys up to 300 m of fire hose to a water cannon robot for petrochemical-plant fires.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous hose deployment and water handling at an industrial complex). It covers only hose laying for water delivery — no placement of a suction/submersible pump in a flooded space, no pump-down to completion — so it does not substantiate whole-instance dewatering.

roles.description: Install or repair solar energy systems designed to collect, store, and circulate solar-heated water for residential, commercial or industrial use.

tasks.label: Test operation or functionality of mechanical, plumbing, electrical, and control systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential new-install commissioning, collector side: on a sloped or flat roof of a single-family home, fill and pressure/leak-test the collector loop, purge air, verify circulation and flow rate, check field-made joints and roof penetrations, confirm sensor at the collector outlet. Ladder access, varying roof pitch and weather.

Residential new-install commissioning, mechanical-room side: in a basement/garage/utility closet, pressure-test tank and piping, start the circulator and verify flow and pressure, check differential controller programming and force pump on/off, verify sensor resistance and wiring, test continuity/voltage and GFCI, set and verify tempering valve and backup element/aquastat, record readings.

Service/troubleshooting call on an existing installed residential or light-commercial system: symptom-driven diagnosis (no hot water, leak, noisy or dead pump, degraded glycol, scaled heat exchanger, failed sensor or controller). Legacy, often undocumented equipment; cramped access; technician must isolate the fault and verify the fix.

Commercial/multifamily/institutional building system testing: flat-roof collector array plus mechanical room with multiple pumps, heat exchangers and storage tanks; hydrostatic tests, glycol freeze-point testing, pump and heat-exchanger performance verification, sequence-of-operations functional testing of controller/BAS points, electrical checks at pump panels.

Industrial / large-scale solar thermal installation (process heat, district heating, large institutional plant): periodic functional and performance testing of pumps, valves, instrumentation, safety devices and SCADA/controller logic; verify readings against instruments, exercise valves and interlocks, document results.

sources.system: AMD Machines automated functional test stations
sources.title: Automated Functional Test Stations | AMD Machines
sources.claim: Commercially supplied automated functional test stations perform machine-sequenced actuation, electrical and performance tests on fixtured assemblies, covering valves, motors, solenoids, pumps, pressure/flow, 4-wire continuity, insulation resistance and hipot, with per-part serialized pass/fail records.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line functional testing of manufactured assemblies. It exercises the same physical quantities a solar thermal technician verifies (pump/valve actuation, flow, pressure, continuity, insulation resistance, controller I/O response) on comparable hydronic/electromechanical hardware, at production accept/reject quality.

sources.system: AMD Machines end-of-line test and leak detection systems
sources.title: Automated Test Systems | Leak Detection & EOL Testing | AMD Machines
