sources.title: ANYmal - Autonomous Robotic Inspection Solution - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal is a commercially certified autonomous inspection robot for energy and process plants; its measurements (thermal, acoustic, visual gauge reading) are explicitly taken without physical interaction with the equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous plant inspection. Establishes that fielded E2 inspection robots sense but do not actuate valves, connect test instruments, or exercise control sequences, so they cannot complete in-situ functional testing.

tasks.label: Apply weather seal, such as pipe flashings and sealants, to roof penetrations and structural devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential steep-slope asphalt-shingle roof: at the two collector plumbing penetrations, the technician lifts/cuts shingle courses, slides a pipe flashing (boot) over the supply and return lines, beds it in roofing cement/polyurethane sealant, nails it, and weaves shingles back over the upslope flange. Work at height on 4:12-8:12 pitch, wind and sun exposure.

Residential shingle roof: weather-sealing the collector rack attachment points - 8 to 20 lag-bolt penetrations located over rafters; apply butyl/polyurethane sealant in the pilot hole and under the standoff or aluminum flashing plate, slide each flashing under the shingle course, torque the lag, and tool a sealant fillet around the standoff.

Residential tile or standing-seam/ribbed metal roof: cut or remove a tile (or select the flat of a metal panel), fit a tile-replacement flashing or EPDM pipe boot, bed it on butyl tape, fasten with gasketed screws, and run a UV-stable sealant bead around the boot perimeter and fastener heads.

Commercial/industrial low-slope roof (TPO/EPDM/built-up): flash the piping penetrations and equipment/collector supports through the membrane - pipe boots, target patches or a pitch pocket filled with pourable sealer, plus mastic at curbs and stanchion bases. Roof taken as found, with existing HVAC units, drains, ponding, and varying membrane condition.

Service/repair call on an existing solar thermal installation: locate the failed seal at a penetration or mount, scrape and clean out cracked/aged mastic and debris, prime, and reseal or replace the flashing, then verify watertightness (hose test/visual) before leaving.

sources.system: Arnold Machine automotive windshield glass assembly cell (multi-robot)
sources.title: Automotive Windshield Glass Assembly - Arnold Machine
sources.claim: Commercial robotic assembly cell in which fixtured glass is primed, a robot dispenses a urethane sealing bead with vision verification, and a vision-guided robot then places the mating component and installs a perimeter seal - i.e., apply-bead-then-set-sealing-component on a fixtured workpiece, done autonomously inside the cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic glazing/sealing. The physical act - dispensing a continuous weather-sealing bead of viscous sealant to a controlled profile and then seating a sealing component onto it in a known position - is the same act as bedding a pipe flashing or standoff flashing in roofing sealant, with comparable objects (sheet/rubber parts, mastic beads) and tighter precision than roof work requires.

sources.system: Robotic adhesive dispensing cell (FANUC robot integrated by Pioneer Industrial Systems)
sources.title: Robotic Adhesive Dispensing Cell Case Study | Pioneer Industrial Systems
sources.claim: Deployed FANUC-robot cell that automates the previously manual dispensing of a urethane bead that functions explicitly as a weather seal on bus windshields, with the requirement that the bead be uniform and consistent.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic weather-seal bead application. It is literally the application of a weather seal to a fixtured workpiece; transfer to roof flashing sealant requires the same materials class (urethane/butyl mastics) and lower geometric precision, but only holds where the work is presented to the machine.

sources.system: FANUC dispensing and sealing robots/cobots (e.g., LR Mate 200iD sealing system, CRX dispense cart with Graco metering)
sources.title: Dispensing and Sealing Robots and Cobots | FANUC America
sources.claim: Commercially supported product line of dispensing and sealing robots/cobots that apply sealants, adhesives and gasketing materials, including vision/laser-checked silicone bead placement with part-nest detection, in industrial cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial sealant/gasket dispensing. Establishes that accurate, verified sealant bead application on fixtured parts is a mature, widely deployed capability in purpose-built cells - the E1 counterfactual for applying sealant to a presented roof penetration.

sources.title: Screwdriving Automation: industrial cobots deliver precise and repeatable automotive fastening – Universal Robots
sources.claim: Commercially deployed robotic screwdriving/bolt-driving with torque control at assembly stations, i.e., autonomous mechanical fastening of components once presented in a known position.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic fastening. Pipe flashings and standoff flashings are secured with screws/lags after sealant is applied; torque-controlled robotic driving covers this step when fasteners and workpiece are presented in a fixtured cell.

sources.title: Beacon Announces Partnership with Renovate Robotics | Roofing Contractor
sources.claim: The most advanced field robot for residential roofs installs asphalt shingle courses on the open roof field; it was still at pilot/launch stage with contractors, and no source describes it flashing or sealing roof penetrations.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the E3 judgment: the only named rooftop construction robot addresses repetitive shingle courses, not cutting into courses, sliding a boot over a live pipe, and tooling mastic at a penetration; its autonomy is also not established, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Install solar collector mounting devices on tile, asphalt, shingle, or built-up gravel roofs, using appropriate materials and penetration methods.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied single-family home, pitched asphalt-shingle roof: locate rafters, lay out mount positions for 2-3 solar thermal collectors, lift shingle courses and remove nails, drill pilot holes, apply sealant, set flashings, drive lag bolts into rafters, bolt L-feet and rails; ladder/harness access, variable pitch and weather.

Residential concrete or clay tile roof (Spanish/W/flat profile): remove or cut tiles, install tile hooks or tile-replacement flashings lag-bolted into rafters or battens, reset tiles, mount standoffs and rails without cracking brittle tile.

Low-slope commercial/multifamily built-up gravel or membrane roof (hotel laundry, apartment block): sweep back gravel, set penetrating stanchions or pitch pans with hot-mopped/torched or adhered flashing, or lay ballasted tilt frames; work around HVAC, parapets, drains.
Metal roof (standing seam or through-fastened corrugated panel) on a home, barn or outbuilding: attach seam clamps or bracket feet with butyl-sealed screws into purlins, then rails for collectors.

Difficult retrofit or repair job: two- to three-story steep roof, obstructions and shading, deteriorated deck, or replacing corroded/leaking mounts under an existing collector array, often coordinated with re-roofing; conditions found as-is and diagnosed on site.

sources.title: MIT-based startup launches solar construction robotic system – pv magazine USA
sources.claim: Charge Robotics' Sunrise is a deployed, fully automated solar construction line: solar mounting hardware (tracks, mounting brackets) and panels ... a purpose-built portable factory and automatically assembled and installed, piloted with EPC SOLV Energy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated assembly and bolting of solar mounting hardware (brackets, rails, tracker structure) to structural members inside a purpose-built line where parts are fed in fixtured. Same class of parts, fasteners and torque precision as collector mounting feet and rails, and it is exactly the E1 'work brought to the machine' presentation; it does not, however, address roof decks or waterproofing.

sources.system: Charge Robotics site factory (context on rooftop robots)
sources.title: Robots Make Solar Installation Faster and Easier - Solar Washington
sources.claim: Trade coverage describes Charge Robotics' site factories taking mounting brackets and panels as inputs and assembling them automatically, and notes rooftop solar is markedly harder than solar-farm work because roofs vary in size, shape and steepness.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the Sunrise item: automated fastening of solar mounting brackets in a fixtured, purpose-built line. The article also documents that existing rooftop robots address panel laying, not roof attachment.

sources.system: WEINMANN Multifunction Bridge WALLTEQ M-300 / M-500
sources.title: Multifunction Bridge WALLTEQ M-300 insuFill /M-500 | HOMAG
sources.claim: HOMAG/Weinmann WALLTEQ multifunction bridges are commercially deployed CNC gantries in prefabricated timber-element plants that automatically drill, screw and nail into wall, roof and floor elements clamped on work tables at CAD-specified positions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic pilot-drilling and screw-driving into fixtured timber roof elements from CAD data. Installing a roof mounting foot is the same mechanical act (locate rafter, pilot hole, drive lag screw) on the same substrate at equal or finer precision, given the E1 presentation of a roof element clamped in a known position.

sources.title: AES Maximo robot installs 100 megawatts of solar capacity - The Robot Report
sources.claim: AES/Maximo's autonomous field robot picks, places and attaches utility-scale solar modules to mounting structures outdoors, completing 100 MW of installation at the Bellefield project with version 3.0 exceeding one module per minute.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous outdoor handling and mechanical attachment of solar hardware to mounting structures. It shows solar hardware fastening is automatable outdoors, but only on pre-installed steel racking in prepared rows on graded solar-farm sites — no roof deck, penetration or flashing work.

sources.title: Introducing Rufus, the Automated Roofing Robot from Renovate Robotics | Roofing Contractor
sources.claim: Renovate Robotics' Rufus is a winch-driven gantry robot that navigates roof planes and installs asphalt shingles on residential ... using AI; automating bracket installation for rack-and-panel solar ... is stated only as a future roadmap item.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fastening of roofing material on real pitched asphalt roofs (E3). It does not install structural mounting devices with flashed, sealed penetrations into rafters — that capability is described as a roadmap intent — so it cannot substantiate completion of this task at E3.

sources.system: Buildex rooftop PV module installation robot
sources.title: "Buildex" PV Module Installation Robot | Trinabot
sources.claim: Rooftop solar installation robots offered commercially (Trinabot Buildex in China, Solar D in Thailand) automate transport and laying of modules on residential, commercial and industrial rooftops; the marketed function is gripping and placing modules, not installing roof attachments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: rooftop module placement. Vendor material only and autonomy unverified; the described function begins after mounting structures exist, so it does not substantiate installing mounting devices with roof penetrations.

tasks.label: Install copper or plastic plumbing using pipes, fittings, pipe cutters, acetylene torches, solder, wire brushes, sand cloths, flux, plastic pipe cleaners, or plastic glue.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential rooftop collector loop: on a pitched asphalt-shingle roof of a single-family home, cut and dry-fit 3/4" copper supply/return lines between collector ports and roof penetration, clean/sand/flux joints, solder with an acetylene or MAPP torch while working around shingles and flashing, secure and insulate the run.

Interior routing in an occupied home: drill and thread copper (or PEX/CPVC) lines from the roof penetration down through attic, wall chases, closets or a crawlspace to the tank location; hang and support pipe, solder or glue joints in cramped, poorly lit spaces with combustible framing nearby.

Storage tank / pump station hookup in a garage, basement or utility closet: plumb copper to the solar storage tank, circulating pump, check and isolation valves, expansion tank, tempering valve and drain-down piping; many short soldered joints in tight quarters, then fill, purge and pressure-test the loop.

Solar pool heating with plastic plumbing at a private residence: cut, deburr, prime and solvent-cement 1.5"–2" PVC between the pool pump/filter pad and roof- or rack-mounted polymer panels, install diverter valves and vacuum relief, then leak-test at the equipment pad outdoors.

Commercial/institutional install (hotel, hospital laundry, school, apartment building): larger-diameter copper or steel piping in a mechanical room and up risers to a rooftop array; institution controls the premises, standard equipment layout, work done in-place around existing plant with hot work permits.

Shop prefabrication before the site visit: at the contractor's shop bench, cut copper tube to drawing lengths and braze/solder collector manifolds, pump-station assemblies and pipe spools in jigs, then pressure-test and label for field delivery.

sources.system: Novarc Spool Welding Robot (SWR) / NovEye Autonomy Gen 2
sources.title: Novarc automates arc welding processes with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2 - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Novarc's Spool Welding Robot with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2 autonomously joins pipe sections at a fixed workstation in pipe fabrication shops, controlling the weld pool through multi-pass, multi-layer welds with the operator handling fit-up and loading.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pipe spool fabrication. Joining pipe to fittings to a leak-tight, code-quality standard at a fixtured shop station is the industrial analogue of prefabricating solar-loop pipe assemblies; the process is arc welding of steel rather than torch soldering of copper, so it supports only the shop-prefab instance, not in-building installation.

sources.system: Dragon 15 Robotic Brazing System with Universal Robots UR5
sources.title: Robot Brazing with a Wire Feeder | UltraFlex Power Technologies
sources.claim: A UR5-based robotic brazing cell (Dragon 15) performs induction brazing of copper pipe joints with automatically fed brazing filler wire, with the robot controlling the heating system through its PLC.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated copper-tube brazing in HVAC component manufacturing. Same material and joint type (capillary-filled copper tube-and-fitting joints) as soldered solar plumbing, but performed on small-diameter tube held in fixtures inside a cell, so it transfers only to fixtured shop prefabrication.

sources.system: Robotic unloading turntable automatic flame brazing equipment
sources.title: Robotic Unloading Turntable Automatic Flame Brazing Equipment for High-Efficiency Production - KETCHAN Induction
sources.claim: Commercially sold rotary-turntable flame-brazing cells with robotic unloading braze copper pipe joints, valve bodies ... HVAC and refrigeration production under PLC sequencing with minimal operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production flame brazing of copper pipe joints. It uses the same torch-heated filler-metal joining of copper pipe and fittings called for here, but requires parts loaded into dedicated fixtures on an indexing table, so it substantiates only the purpose-built shop-cell (E1) version.

sources.title: Hilti's Robot Breaks Records on a YIT Construction Site - AEC Business
sources.claim: The most capable field MEP construction robot in commercial deployment, Hilti's Jaibot, only marks and drills BIM-located anchor holes in ceilings for pipe hangers on jobsites; it does not cut, fit, solder or glue pipe.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: overhead drilling for MEP hanger layout on construction sites. It shows the state of in-situ building-services robotics is hole drilling from a BIM model; no pipe cutting, fit-up or joint making transfers, so it supports no positive judgment for this task.

tasks.label: Identify plumbing, electrical, environmental, or safety hazards associated with solar thermal installations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-installation site assessment at a single-family home: technician walks the property, climbs the roof, enters attic/garage/basement, and identifies hazards bearing on the job — roof structural condition and fall/access exposure, deteriorated existing plumbing and water heater venting, panel capacity and old/ungrounded wiring, freeze exposure, asbestos or brittle roofing, overhead lines and shading trees — then reports required mitigations.

Hazard identification while installing a residential or small-commercial system: continuously spotting job-site and system hazards as work proceeds — unstable ladder/anchor points, live circuits during controller and pump tie-in, hot work near combustibles, scald and overpressure risk at fill/commissioning, unsupported piping, missing relief-valve discharge, improper bonding — and correcting or flagging them.

Service/repair visit on an existing residential solar hot-water or pool-heating system: inspect for leaking or corroded fittings and roof penetrations, degraded glycol/failed freeze protection, seized or improperly piped T&P and relief valves, failed expansion tank, chafed sensor or controller wiring, stagnation/overheat damage; hands-on tests and a written list of hazards.

Periodic hazard/condition inspection of an installed commercial or institutional system (hotel, school, hospital, apartment or laundry): walk the mechanical/plant room and rooftop collector array checking for fluid leaks, corrosion and damaged insulation, overheating pumps, motors and electrical connections, abnormal pressure/temperature gauge readings, and report deficiencies.

Hazard inspection round at a large industrial or district-scale solar thermal plant (process heat, district heating, large collector field): survey the collector field and pump house for leaks, hot spots, glycol/steam hazards, electrical faults and fire risk, and document findings for the operator.

sources.system: Spot (with Spot CAM+IR and FLIR MUVE C360)
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot runs autonomous inspection rounds at a 40-acre midstream gas plant with thermal, visual and gas payloads, and detected a combustible-gas pinhole leak during a round — machine identification of leak and thermal hazards on process piping and equipment in a facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the operator's routine hazard/condition round in a process facility. Transfers to identifying plumbing and electrical hazards at a solar thermal plant because the assets (pumps, piping, valves, gauges) and hazard classes (fluid/gas leaks, thermal hot spots) are comparable in a similar plant-room setting.

sources.title: How Swiss Robotics Company ANYbotics and SAP Are Turning Dirty, Dusty, and Dangerous Industrial Inspections into Business Insights
sources.claim: ANYmal performs autonomous multi-modal inspection in industrial facilities, collecting thermal imaging, ultrasonic leak detection, ... and acoustic anomaly data, with automatic anomaly detection and alerting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated condition/hazard inspection rounds of pumps, piping and electrical equipment in plants. The sensing modalities map directly onto the leak, overheating-connection and hot-surface hazards a technician looks for around a solar thermal plant room.

sources.title: ANYmal X Tested for Autonomous Robot Inspections in Ex-zones at BASF
sources.claim: ANYmal X carried out inspection rounds in explosion-hazard zones at BASF Ludwigshafen, reading gauges and lever positions and thermally inspecting tanks and pumps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hazardous-area plant inspection. Gauge reading plus thermal scans of pumps and tanks is the same perception work as checking a solar thermal plant room's pressure/temperature gauges, pumps and storage tanks for hazards.

sources.developer: Boston Dynamics (operated by data center owner)
sources.title: Who's a good bot? Deploying robot dogs at data centers - DCD
sources.claim: Spot is deployed in operating data centers running pre-determined autonomous missions to collect temperature data, monitor equipment and report anomalies, substituting for part of the human routine facility check round.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine facility inspection rounds in a building's equipment halls. Shows a legged robot substituting for a human walking a structured building's mechanical spaces to find thermal/equipment anomalies — the same environment as an institutional solar thermal plant room.

sources.system: Raptor Solar Sentry (drone-in-a-box) with Fire Watch inspection
sources.title: Introducing Autonomous Fire Watch Inspections
sources.claim: Raptor Solar Sentry autonomous drone-in-a-box systems are deployed across more than 12 GW of solar assets and run inspection protocols for fire risk, thermal events and back-of-panel wiring at utility-scale solar sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous thermal/visual hazard scanning of a large solar energy installation (PV). Transfers to the collector-field portion of a large solar thermal plant: same open-air, institution-controlled array setting and IR-detectable hazard signatures (hot spots, wiring faults, fire risk).

sources.title: GAF & Loveland Innovations V2 | Loveland Innovations
sources.claim: IMGING supports fully automated drone flights over residential roofs with AI damage detection, averaging under six minutes per home; it covers roof surface condition only, not plumbing, electrical or mechanical-space hazards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: residential roof condition inspection. It substantiates only the roof-surface part of a residential solar thermal hazard survey; attic, plumbing, water heater and electrical-panel hazards are outside its reach.

sources.title: Home Inspector Crawlspace Inspection Robot | SuperDroid Robots
sources.claim: Robots marketed for residential crawl space and attic inspection are remote-controlled camera rovers that record video for a human inspector to interpret; no autonomous residential hazard-identification system is offered.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: residential sub-space inspection. Shows the residential state of the art is human-driven teleoperation with human interpretation, so it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous hazard identification in homes.

tasks.label: Demonstrate start-up, shut-down, maintenance, diagnostic, and safety procedures to thermal system owners.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-installation handover at a single-family home: the technician walks the homeowner through the mechanical room / pump station of a new solar hot-water system — pointing out the differential controller, isolation and drain valves, pressure/temperature gauges, expansion tank, glycol loop, backup water heater, and explaining how to start it up, shut it down, check for freeze protection, read fault codes, and when to call for service. Purpose is owner comprehension; a printed O&M packet and a verbal or video walkthrough serve the same purpose.

Handover training for a small commercial or multifamily system (hotel, laundromat, restaurant, apartment building): the technician briefs on-site maintenance staff or the building manager in the boiler/mechanical room on start-up and shut-down sequence, stagnation and scald hazards, annual glycol and anode checks, controller diagnostics, and lockout/tagout safety, and hands over the O&M manual.

Residential solar pool-heating handover: technician explains to the homeowner the bypass/diverter valve positions, how to start and stop circulation to the collectors, winterizing/draining the array, filter and flow considerations, and roof-access safety warnings.

Post-repair or service-call explanation: after fixing a failed pump, sensor, controller, or leaking loop, the technician re-explains to the owner what went wrong, how to recognize the symptom again, what routine maintenance was skipped, and how to safely restart the system.

Commissioning handover of a large institutional or industrial system (hospital, school, process-heat plant): a formal training session with facility engineers covering start-up/shut-down sequences, control-system diagnostics and alarms, heat-dump and overtemperature procedures, maintenance schedule, and safety protocols, often with documentation sign-off.

tasks.label: Install circulating pumps using pipe, fittings, soldering equipment, electrical supplies, and hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New residential solar water-heating install in a single-family home: install circulator(s) on the collector loop in a basement/utility closet, cut and ream copper tube, sweat fittings, set isolation/check valves and flow meter, mount pump on existing piping, and wire the pump to the differential controller. Cramped, site-specific layout around an existing tank and plumbing.

Service call replacing a failed circulator on an existing residential solar thermal system: isolate and drain the loop, cut out or unbolt the old pump, fit a replacement with unions/flanges (some joints re-soldered), reconnect power leads, refill/purge and verify flow. Work is entirely on in-place, as-found piping.

Commercial/institutional install (hotel, multifamily, school laundry, industrial process): mechanical room work with larger circulators or flanged base-mounted pumps, threaded/grooved steel or copper piping, hangers, conduit and controller wiring, followed by commissioning. Institution controls the premises; layout is fixed but not built for machines.

Rooftop or exterior mechanical enclosure: mount pump/pump-station near the collector array, run and solder insulated exterior copper piping, weatherproof electrical connections to the controller. Roof access, weather, and site-specific structure.

Shop pre-assembly of pump stations/skids before delivery: build a pump-plus-valves-plus-fittings assembly on a bench or jig, solder/braze the copper joints, bolt the pump, land the wiring in a small enclosure, and pressure-test the module.

sources.system: UltraFlex Dragon 15/20 induction brazing robot (UR5 + W15 induction system)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: making capillary filler-metal joints between copper tube and cast fittings in a fixtured cell. This is the same joint geometry and material as the sweat-soldered copper connections used to pipe a circulating pump into a solar loop, so joining performance carries over when the pipe and fittings are presented fixtured.

sources.claim: A production induction brazing robot cell for copper-to-copper, copper-to-steel and brass-to-copper tube assemblies runs pre-programmed joint-by-joint brazing with optional wire feed and vision-based assembly recognition, used on HVAC/appliance production lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated multi-joint brazing of copper tube assemblies in a purpose-built cell, the same joining operation required to connect pipe and fittings around a circulator when the assembly is fixtured.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: landing and securing conductors on terminals inside an enclosure — the electrical-supplies portion of installing a circulating pump (pump leads to a differential controller / junction box) involves comparable wire handling and terminal insertion at comparable precision, in a fixtured cell.

sources.claim: Novarc's spool welding robot with NovEye Autonomy makes code-quality pipe welds in fabrication shops without operator intervention after setup.
