tasks.label: Install flat-plat, evacuated glass, or concentrating solar collectors on mounting devices, using brackets or struts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential retrofit: two or three glazed flat-plate collectors (each ~4x8 ft, 120-160 lb) hoisted onto an asphalt-shingle pitched roof and bolted to previously installed L-feet/rails or struts, working at height on a slope around vents and valleys.

Solar pool-heating job on a house or small clubhouse: six to twelve semi-rigid unglazed polymer collector panels (4x10-12 ft mats) laid on a pitched or low-slope roof and secured to rails, straps, clamps or brackets screwed into the deck.

Evacuated-tube collector array for domestic hot water: manifold/header frame bolted to roof brackets or a rack, then 20-30 fragile glass tubes seated one by one into grommets and tube clips; roof or ground rack at a home or small business.

Commercial/institutional flat roof (hotel, laundry, multifamily, school): 8-30 flat-plate collectors craned or hoisted up and bolted to strut-channel frames or ballasted mounting devices, navigating parapets, HVAC curbs and membrane protection.

Small ground- or wall-mounted array: two to eight collectors fastened with brackets/struts to a custom-welded or bolted rack in a yard, mechanical enclosure, or south wall, with site-specific footings and clearances.

Large repetitive ground-mounted collector field (industrial process heat, district heating, or concentrating collector loop): dozens to hundreds of identical collectors set in rows onto pre-erected racking/struts at an open, prepared site.

sources.title: Terabase Energy advances automated PV construction with robotics, AI tools - pv magazine Global
sources.claim: Terabase's Terafab is an on-site automated factory line in which robots assemble PV modules onto tracker torque tubes (the mounting structure), with autonomous rovers delivering finished assemblies; first-generation Terafab installed 40 MW across multiple commercial US projects and V2 is in commercial service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastening glass-fronted rigid PV modules to a metal mounting structure. Transfers to mounting flat-plate solar thermal collectors on brackets/struts: same class of object (framed rigid glazed panel ~2 m x 1 m), same bolt/clamp precision, performed inside a purpose-built machine line.

sources.title: The race is on to build solar farms with robots - Renewable Energy World
sources.claim: The Terafab on-site factory bolts modules to the torque tube inside a tent-like temporary factory before carts move them to the field, i.e. the panel-to-mounting-structure fastening happens in a purpose-built robotic work area.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bolting rigid solar panels to their mounting structure. Same manipulation and fastening as bolting a flat-plate collector to brackets/struts; substantiates completion in a purpose-built (E1) setting.

sources.title: Making solar projects cheaper and faster with portable factories | MIT News
sources.claim: Charge Robotics ships portable factories to utility solar sites where tracks, mounting brackets and panels ... in and automatically assembled into completed rows, which an autonomous robotic vehicle then places; prototype deployed with SOLV Energy and $22M raised for first commercial deployments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic assembly of panels to mounting brackets/rails. Objects (rigid glazed panels), fasteners (bracket clamps) and tolerances match collector-to-strut mounting; the machine environment is exactly the E1 counterfactual of work brought to the machine.

sources.title: AES Maximo robot installs 100 megawatts of solar capacity - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Maximo, an autonomous field robot fleet, installed 100 MW of PV modules onto pre-erected torque-tube racking at AES's Bellefield site; it has an end-to-end mode in which the robot performs the whole installation after an operator start, and a supervised mode where people secure the panels.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mounting rigid glazed panels onto pre-erected racking outdoors in rows. Transfers to setting rows of flat-plate collectors on ground racking: same geometry, same clamp/bolt attachment, same open-site conditions; the greater mass of a glazed thermal collector is the main caveat.

sources.title: Robotic Automation for Utility-Scale Solar Installation | KUKA Global
sources.claim: Cosmic-1A, an autonomous all-terrain robot with a KUKA arm, transports and places utility-scale PV modules to +/-1 mm on racking on live US projects, but crews still set up the frames and people fasten the panels; a fastening capability is only planned.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: field placement of heavy panels onto racking. Shows the outdoor state of the art is placement-only, so it does not substantiate whole-instance completion (place plus bracket fastening) at E2/E3.

sources.title: AI robots speed up installation of 500,000 solar panels in Australia - Interesting Engineering
sources.claim: LUMI S4 robots autonomously placed PV modules onto racking at Engie's 250 MW Goorambat East solar farm ahead of schedule, but human crews complete the securing of the modules.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor module-to-rack installation. Confirms that outdoor field systems place but do not fasten, supporting negative judgments for whole-instance completion outside a purpose-built line.

sources.title: Rooftop Photovoltaic Panel Installation Robot - Trinabot
sources.claim: Trinabot markets a rooftop PV panel-laying robot for residential, commercial and industrial roofs that automates transport, alignment and placement, with human operators collaborating to finalize the installation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: rooftop panel mounting. Vendor claim only, with humans finalizing the fastening and no evidence of pitched-shingle-roof work, so it cannot support completion of collector mounting on a roof (E2/E3).

sources.title: News: Schmalz Vacuum Gripping Systems for palletizing and depalletizing - A3/Automate
sources.claim: Schmalz supplies commercially available modular area and layer vacuum gripping systems used on robots and gantries to handle large non-rigid and porous workpieces, the class of handling needed for limp polymer collector mats in a fixtured cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of large limp sheet goods in fixtured industrial cells. Transfers to picking and laying unglazed polymer pool collector mats onto rails in an E1 cell; the fastening step is covered by the assembly-robot evidence.

sources.system: FANUC M-710iC/45M and SCARA-6iA assembly cells
sources.title: Assembly Robots | Assembly Line Robots | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC's commercially deployed assembly cells perform fixtured part insertion and fastening at production rates, e.g. robots orienting rails while SCARA robots insert up to 120 ..., and cells that place covers and load springs into fixtured assemblies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fixtured insertion and fastening of parts into rails/frames. Transfers to E1 versions of collector mounting: seating evacuated glass tubes into manifold grommets and driving bracket bolts when frame and parts are presented in known positions.

sources.title: Terabase Energy advances automated PV construction with robotics, AI tools - pv magazine Global
sources.claim: In current Terafab practice the final step of setting the assembled panel/tube units onto the pre-placed field mounts is still done by workers; automating that step is scheduled for a future version.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (mounting panels on structures). Establishes the boundary: automated mounting is substantiated inside the purpose-built line, not in the open field, supporting E1-only judgments for most instances.

tasks.label: Install solar thermal system controllers and sensors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retrofit solar hot-water system on an existing single-family home: mount the differential controller on a basement/utility-closet wall near the storage tank, install the collector Pt1000 sensor in its well on the roof array, insert the tank sensor in an immersion well, fish and staple sensor cable from roof to controller through attic/chase/conduit, land conductors on screw terminals, wire pump and 120 V supply, power up and program setpoints, verify readings.

New-construction or production residential install: controller and sensors installed in an unfinished mechanical space with clear access and rough-in conduit already run; sensors set in tank and collector wells, controller mounted and terminated, system commissioned and programmed.

Commercial/institutional mechanical room (school, hotel, hospital, multifamily): mount a control panel/controller, install multiple immersion sensors in tanks and piping wells plus flow meters, terminate to a datalogger or building automation system, run conduit, configure and commission.

Service call on an existing installed system: diagnose a failed or drifting Pt1000 sensor or a dead controller, climb to the collector or open the tank jacket, remove and replace the sensor or controller in place, re-terminate field wiring, re-enter programming and verify operation.

Large commercial/industrial or district solar thermal plant: install plant controllers, sensor arrays in field piping and storage, and wiring to SCADA, in a plant room and outdoor collector field, often on prefabricated skids.

sources.title: Automated Control Cabinet Wiring Solution for Scalable Renewable Energy Systems (Springer, GCSM)
sources.claim: Averex, a portal-robot wiring centre from Kiesling/Rittal, performs fully automated control-cabinet wiring in a purpose-built factory cell: cutting and crimping wires, inserting them into screw and spring-loaded terminals, and routing them inside the ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: control-cabinet wiring. Landing a solar controller's sensor, pump and supply conductors on screw/spring terminals and routing cable is the same class of work on the same objects (small stranded conductors, ferrules, terminal blocks) at the same precision, performed in a fixtured cell.

sources.title: Modular Robotic Stations for Control Cabinet Manufacturing | WAGO
sources.claim: WAGO's Wiring Bot is a commercial modular robotic station for control-cabinet manufacturing that prepares conductors and wires mounting plates and rails, supplying pre-wired rails as semi-finished assemblies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: panel wiring in a factory cell. Shows commercial robotic conductor preparation and terminal wiring, the electrical core of installing a controller; its partial coverage also bounds the claim to purpose-built cells.

sources.title: Klippon® Automated RailAssembler – Rail mounting | Weidmüller
sources.claim: Weidmüller's Klippon Automated RailAssembler automatically picks, positions and mounts terminal-block components onto DIN rails in a panel shop, driven by configurator data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mounting electrical devices onto rails/plates in a fixtured cell — the mechanical-mounting half of installing a controller and its terminal hardware, on comparable components and tolerances.

sources.title: Polygon Technologies reduces onsite commissioning time by 70 percent - Tecnomatix (Siemens)
sources.claim: Polygon Technologies' Wirebot combines a portal robot with an articulated arm and vision/tactile sensing to automate wire-harness assembly and wire routing for electrical control panels in production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic wiring of electrical control panels. A second independent commercial system for deformable-cable handling and terminal termination, exactly what wiring a controller and its sensor leads requires, in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Denso VS-series six-axis robot sensor assembly line
sources.title: Robots Assemble Automotive Sensors | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Erwin Quarder Systemtechnik runs a fully automated Denso-robot production line for automotive sensors that inserts sensors onto carriers, makes the soldered electrical connection, and tests and inspects the finished assemblies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic seating of a sensor into its mount plus electrical connection and functional test. Comparable objects (small probe bodies with leads) and insertion precision in a fixtured cell — the E1 analogue of setting a Pt1000 in a well and terminating it.

sources.title: Hilti unveils new robot-powered drilling capabilities | Design World
sources.claim: The most capable field robot used by MEP installation contractors on jobsites, Hilti's Jaibot, is a semi-autonomous mobile ... machine that drills BIM-located holes in ceilings; it does not mount devices, run sensor cable or terminate wiring.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound field capability: the state of the art for in-building MEP robotics is hole drilling from BIM data, which excludes mounting controllers, installing sensors and terminating conductors, so it cannot substantiate E2/E3 completion.

tasks.label: Fill water tanks and check tanks, pipes, and fittings for leaks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New residential solar hot water install: after piping the collector loop and storage tank in a home's basement/garage/attic and on the roof, the tech connects a hose/fill cart, fills the potable tank and the solar loop with water or glycol, purges air, brings the system to test pressure, then walks the roof, attic and mechanical space feeling and eyeing every solder joint, union, valve and tank fitting for weeps, tightening as needed.

Service/repair call on an existing residential system: after replacing a pump, valve, expansion tank or storage tank, the tech refills and repressurizes the system in a cluttered, non-standard home mechanical space and hunts for the leak or verifies the repair holds pressure over a soak period.

Commercial or institutional solar hot water system (hotel, school, laundry, multifamily, hospital): large storage tanks in a mechanical room plus rooftop collector arrays; the tech fills several hundred gallons of tank volume, purges the array, holds a documented pressure test and inspects header fittings, sensor wells and tank connections for leaks.

Solar pool heating system on a residence or small commercial pool: fills the unglazed collector array and header plumbing by running the pool pump, then inspects roof headers, hose clamps, panel connectors and roof penetrations for leaks and drips while the array is under flow.

Industrial process-heat or large district solar thermal array on a controlled plant site: fills storage tanks and long header runs, pressure-tests the loop and inspects flanges, unions and tank fittings across the field and the pump house.

sources.system: CTS custom hydrostatic leak test system
sources.title: Hydrostatic Leak Test Systems — Cincinnati Test Systems
sources.claim: Cincinnati Test Systems builds commercially available hydrostatic leak test systems that automatically fill a vessel or piping assembly with water, vent trapped air, pressurize it and measure pressure drop to identify leaks; they are used on pipe, pipelines, plumbing components and boilers, and can be supplied with automatic operation and part load/unload automation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production hydrostatic leak testing of pressure vessels and piping. It is the same physical act as the worker's task — fill a tank/pipe circuit with water, purge air, pressurize, and determine whether tanks, pipes and fittings leak — on comparable objects (tanks, pipe, plumbing fittings, boilers) at comparable or tighter leak-rate precision, but with the work fixtured in a purpose-built station.

sources.developer: Plastics Extrusion Machinery LLC (PEM), McPherson, KS
sources.title: Hydrotesters | Plastics Extrusion Machinery LLC (PEM)
sources.claim: PEM's hydrotesters are production machines with fully automated loading, testing and ... that clamp a length of water-main pipe between end caps, fill it with water via a centrifugal pump and run a certified proof-pressure test to AWWA specification without an operator performing the test steps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated hydrostatic proof/leak testing of water pipe. Same physical operations as the instance (mechanically seal the circuit, fill with water, pressurize, judge pass/fail on leakage) on water-carrying pipe of comparable size, executed by the machine end-to-end in a purpose-built station.

sources.system: TQC leak test cell with robotic handling (Fanuc 6-axis robot + MALT leak test modules)
sources.title: Case Study - Fully Automatic Leak Test Cell with Robotic Handling — TQC
sources.claim: TQC supplied a production leak-test cell in which a Fanuc 6-axis robot performs all part handling into and out of automated leak-test modules, with vision inspection and automatic pass/fail segregation, showing that robotic loading of parts into pressurized leak-test fixtures is an established, deployed capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-tended automated leak testing. It supplies the missing handling step for the E1 counterfactual — a robot presents and seals assemblies into leak-test fixtures and the cell judges leak-tightness autonomously, the same load-fill-test-verdict sequence the worker performs by hand.

sources.system: ANYmal inspection robot with Gas Leak & Presence Detection
sources.title: ANYbotics Launches New Gas Leak & Presence Detection Solution for its ANYmal Inspection Robot
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal legged robot autonomously patrols industrial plants and, with acoustic-imaging and gas sensing payloads, locates and quantifies leaks and reports them; it performs inspection only and has no capability to connect fill lines, open valves or fill and pressurize a water tank.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous leak inspection inside structured industrial facilities (E2). Cited to bound the E2 judgment: the leak-detection half of the task is demonstrated in facilities, but no cited system performs the filling, valve operation and hands-on fitting checks, so the whole instance is not completed at E2.

tasks.label: Design active direct or indirect, passive direct or indirect, or pool solar systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Determine locations for installing solar subsystem components, including piping, water heaters, valves, and ancillary equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential retrofit of a solar hot-water system on an existing single-family home: the technician walks the site, inspects the roof for collector placement (orientation, shading, rafter layout), looks at the basement/garage/utility closet to pick a spot for the storage tank, pump station, expansion tank and valves, and decides how the supply/return piping will be routed through joist bays, chases or exterior walls. Output is a decision (often sketched, marked, or discussed with the homeowner/inspector) about where each component goes.

Solar pool-heating installation at a home or small club: determining where unglazed collector panels sit on roof or racking, where the diverter/three-way valve, check valve and filter/pump tie-in points go relative to the existing pool equipment pad, and the routing of large-diameter PVC runs. Output is a placement decision constrained by existing pool plumbing and deck layout.

Commercial or institutional solar thermal job (hotel, laundry, apartment building, food plant): reviewing engineered drawings on site, then determining actual field locations for collector arrays, storage tanks, heat exchangers, circulation pumps, mixing and isolation valves, sensors and expansion tanks within a mechanical room and on the roof, reconciling the drawings with as-built conditions, clearances, code setbacks and other trades' equipment.

New-construction or major-remodel coordination: determining component locations before walls, roof penetrations and mechanical spaces are finished, in consultation with the builder, plumber and electrician, so that sleeves, blocking, mounting points and pipe chases are placed correctly.

Service, repair, or component replacement call: determining where a replacement tank, pump, valve, sensor, or section of piping should be relocated or re-sited given a failure, freeze damage, leak, or code/performance problem in an already-installed system.

tasks.label: Perform routine maintenance or repairs to restore solar thermal systems to baseline operating conditions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Annual/on-call service of a residential solar hot-water collector array on a pitched asphalt-shingle roof of a single-family home: climb/ladder access, inspect glazing, glazing seals, absorber, and flashing at roof penetrations, clear soiling and debris, tighten mounts, re-seal a weeping union or penetration, replace a failed roof-mounted collector temperature sensor and its wiring, and verify the loop returns to normal operating temperature/flow.

Service in a residential basement, garage, or utility closet: diagnose no-flow/overheating/pressure-loss complaint, replace failed circulator pump, check valve, expansion tank, or differential controller; drain, flush and recharge propylene-glycol loop to correct freeze point and pressure; purge air; sweat/press or thread new fittings; leak- and pressure-test and restore setpoints on cramped, non-standard piping.

Solar pool-heating system at a home or small club: locate and repair leaks in unglazed polymer collector panels and headers on a roof or ground rack, replace a cracked panel or header, service the diverter/vacuum-relief valves and pump timer, and perform seasonal start-up or winterizing drain-down.

Commercial/institutional solar thermal array on a flat roof of a hotel, apartment building, school, or laundry: walk multiple collector banks, inspect and repair leaks at unions, headers and hose connections, replace a damaged collector or degraded pipe insulation and jacketing, re-secure ballast/mounting, drain and refill the loop, and confirm array output restored.

Commercial mechanical/plant room service: inspect and service storage tanks, external heat exchangers, circulators and mixing/tempering valves; test and replace sensors, rebuild or swap a pump, clean strainers/scale from the exchanger, check anodes and relief valves, restore controller setpoints, and document performance against baseline.

Soiling-removal maintenance visit on a large commercial or industrial collector field (rows of glazed flat-plate collectors serving process heat or a district loop): wash/brush the collector glazing across many rows to restore collector output, with no component repair required.

sources.system: Ecoppia E4 / T4 / H4 robotic cleaning system
sources.title: Check out these robots made specifically for the solar industry - Solar Power World
sources.claim: Ecoppia's water-free cleaning robots operate autonomously on utility-scale solar arrays, traveling across fixed-tilt and tracker rows that are fitted with the robots' own docking/travel hardware, cleaning panel glass on a scheduled basis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cleaning soiling from glazed solar-collector surfaces at a solar plant. Flat glazed thermal collectors present the same planar glass surface at similar tilt, so surface cleaning transfers; the evidence covers only the cleaning-only maintenance visit, not inspection, fluid work, or component repair.

sources.system: CSIRO All Terrain Robot (ATR) solar farm inspection system
sources.title: Robots take the heat for humans maintaining our biggest solar farms - CSIRO
sources.claim: CSIRO's All Terrain Robot autonomously navigates operational solar farms and automatically detects faults (soiling, damage, loose nuts/bolts, hotspots, wiring needing repair), but the robot only inspects — the repairs it flags are still performed by people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine maintenance inspection of a solar energy field. It shows the state of the art for field maintenance robotics on solar assets is autonomous fault detection; the corrective repair steps that define this task are not performed by the robot.

sources.system: Aerones robotic wind turbine maintenance systems
sources.title: Aerones – Leading Robotic Wind Turbine Maintenance Innovator | Latvia.eu
sources.claim: Aerones' robotic systems perform maintenance and repair work on wind turbines (cleaning, lightning protection checks, leading-edge erosion repair), but the repair robots are operated remotely by technicians rather than acting autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repairing energy-collection equipment mounted at height on a structure. The closest commercial analogue to robotic solar-collector repair is teleoperated, so it cannot support an autonomous-completion judgment for this task.

sources.developer: ULC Technologies / ULC Robotics (deployed by Cadent Gas)
sources.title: CISBOT - Cadent Gas Ltd
sources.claim: CISBOT, the leading robot for sealing leaking joints in live cast-iron distribution mains, is a remotely controlled machine, not an autonomous one.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repairing leaking piping joints in a fluid system. It is the nearest deployed robotic pipe-repair capability, and it is human-controlled, indicating no autonomous system performs leak repair on installed hydronic piping.

tasks.label: Install heat exchangers and heat exchanger fluids according to installation manuals and schematics.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential retrofit: installing an external brazed-plate or side-arm heat exchanger in an existing home's basement/utility closet next to a storage tank. Worker mounts the exchanger and brackets, cuts/brazes or threads copper connections to the collector loop and tank ports per the manual's schematic, installs isolation valves and sensor wells, pressure-tests, then charges the closed loop with propylene glycol using a fill/purge cart and bleeds air. Cramped, as-found piping and clearances.

New residential construction / major renovation: solar hot-water rough-in in a house under construction, mechanical wall or closet largely open. Heat exchanger (often part of a pre-plumbed pump/HX station) mounted per manual, piped to tank and collector loop, pressure tested, and charged with glycol at commissioning.

Commercial or institutional mechanical room (hotel, school, apartment building, laundry): larger brazed-plate or shell-and-tube exchanger set on a stand or skid, rigged into place, connected with flanged/grooved/threaded joints to solar and domestic loops per schematic, hydrostatically tested, and charged with drums of glycol via a fill pump; loop balanced and air purged.

Industrial or utility-scale solar process-heat plant: large exchanger or exchanger skid set with rigging, welded pressure piping to the HTF and process loops per P&ID, insulated, leak/pressure tested, and filled with heat transfer fluid from bulk totes with circulation/deaeration.

Service and repair: diagnosing a failed or fouled heat exchanger or degraded glycol in an existing installed system; draining and disposing of old fluid, flushing the loop, cutting out and replacing the exchanger or gaskets in place, refilling with fresh fluid and verifying pH/freeze point with a refractometer.

sources.system: RND Automation Modular Assembly Platform with Epson T3/G3 SCARA and C8 six-axis robots
sources.title: Robots assemble hydraulic valves | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: A production robot cell (RND Automation, Epson SCARA/6-axis robots) autonomously builds fluid-carrying hydraulic valve assemblies: robots feed parts, apply thread-locking adhesive, thread and torque components with compliance devices to avoid cross-threading, and load each unit into an automated leak-test fixture, one valve every 10 seconds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated assembly of threaded, pressure-tight fluid components with adhesive, torque control and leak verification. Heat-exchanger hookup in a fixtured cell involves the same class of objects (threaded/union fluid ports), the same tightness criterion, and the same verification step.

sources.system: Spool Welding Robot (SWR) with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2
sources.title: Novarc automates arc welding processes with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2 - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Novarc's Spool Welding Robot with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2 performs multi-pass autonomous pipe welding in fabrication shops, adapting in real time to fit-up variation such as HiLo and varying root gaps; the cobot is deployed at customer fab shops worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: joining pressure pipe in a shop welding station with a pipe positioner. Commercial/industrial heat-exchanger hookup brought to an E1 cell consists of the same welded pressure-pipe joints at the same sizes and code-quality requirement.

sources.system: Dragon 15 robotic induction brazing system with UR5 robot and automatic wire feeder / UBraze robot-integrated brazing
sources.title: Brazing of Copper to Copper Pipes for Heat Exchanger | UltraFlex
sources.claim: Robotic induction brazing cells are used in production to braze copper-to-copper pipe joints for heat exchangers and copper-to-brass HVAC parts, with the robot positioning the induction coil and brazing wire automatically in a fixture.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making brazed copper joints on heat-exchanger piping, which is exactly the joining method used for residential solar heat-exchanger connections; in a fixtured cell the joints are presented in known positions as in these production cells.

sources.system: Somac automated filling stations (incl. BlueStart) / automated coolant fill adapter tools
sources.title: Dürr Automated Filling Stations - Dürr
sources.claim: Dürr Somac supplies automated/fully automatic filling stations for production lines that fill vehicle fluids and gases including coolant (glycol), brake fluid and refrigerant, with vacuum evacuation, pressure leak testing and level control, integrated into automatic production processes; comparable automated coolant-glycol fill tools with pressure and vacuum leak testing are supplied for radiator/battery-cooling lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: charging a closed fluid circuit with glycol coolant, evacuating air and verifying tightness — the same operation as charging a solar loop with heat-transfer fluid and purging, performed by machine on a fixtured workpiece.

sources.title: Hilti Unveils BIM-Enabled Construction Jobsite Robot
sources.claim: The only mobile robots actually deployed for mechanical/plumbing work on building sites perform drilling of anchor holes from BIM data; the Jaibot is moved between positions by an operator's remote control and then drills the holes within reach automatically. No deployed field robot installs mechanical equipment or makes piping connections.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to characterize the state of field MEP robotics: capability is limited to hole drilling, not to mounting heat exchangers, making fluid-tight joints, or charging loops, so it supports no positive judgment at E2 or E3.

tasks.label: Apply operation or identification tags or labels to system components, as required.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New residential solar water-heating install: after piping up the storage tank, pump station and controller in a basement, garage or mechanical closet, the tech applies self-adhesive pipe markers with flow arrows (solar supply/return, hot/cold), ID labels on valves, pumps, expansion tank, sensors and controller. Cramped, cluttered, varied home layouts; labels wrapped on 1/2"-1" copper and stuck on tank jackets and enclosures.

Code/utility-required placards and warning signage mounted at the install: scald-hazard and 'solar heated water' placards, freeze-protection/glycol notice, emergency shutdown and operating-instruction plaques, and disconnect labels, screwed or adhered to walls, tank stands, panel covers and near roof access at a home or small commercial building.

Commercial/industrial solar thermal plant in a mechanical room: per project spec, engraved brass/plastic valve tags hung with bead chain on dozens of isolation and balancing valves, adhesive or strap-on pipe markers with legends and flow arrows on 2"-4" insulated headers, and equipment ID nameplates on pumps, heat exchangers and storage tanks; tag schedule must match the as-built valve chart.

Rooftop collector array: labeling collector loop supply/return piping and insulation jackets, sensor and pump wiring leads, array/bank identification plates and freeze-drain valves, done outdoors at height on a sloped or flat roof in sun and wind after array plumbing is complete.

Service or retrofit call on an existing installed system: replacing missing, sun-degraded or painted-over pipe markers and valve tags, re-tagging components after a pump, controller or valve replacement, on a system already in place in a home, rooftop or building mechanical space.

sources.system: FOX IV Zebra-based print & apply pipe/tube labeling station with robotic integration
sources.title: Print and Apply Tube Labeling with Robotic Integration | FOX IV
sources.claim: FOX IV built and delivered a print-and-apply labeling station that automatically prints and applies pressure-sensitive labels to the circumference of bent steel and aluminum pipes/tubes of varying diameter (7/8" to 2-1/4") on an indexing table, with industrial robots loading and unloading, inside a factory cell.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class as the rated task's core action - printing an identification label and adhering it to a pipe - on the same object type (small-diameter metal pipe) and to the same acceptance standard (correct legend, firm adhesion), but in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Motion Controls Robotics high-speed robotic case labeling cell (FANUC M-2iA)
sources.title: High-Speed Labeling for Case Labeling - Motion Controls Robotics
sources.claim: A deployed FANUC M-2iA labeling cell uses vision to locate each product on the conveyor and record orientation, prints the label, picks it from the printer, applies it with a spring-backed pad, and vision-inspects placement and data; the cell is fenced with safety sensors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: variable-data identification labeling of discrete items. It transfers because it shows autonomous print-select-place-verify of an ID label on an object whose position and orientation vary, at the mm placement precision needed for component ID labels.

sources.title: Robotic Label Applicator | Signode
sources.claim: Signode sells a robotic label applicator in which the robot picks a printed label and applies it to heavy industrial workpieces (steel coils) at determined positions, with label stock including polyester and vinyl and optional RFID.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: identification tagging of heavy industrial components rather than packages, showing the same pick-and-apply capability on durable label stock similar to industrial pipe and equipment markers.

sources.title: Robotic Hang Tag Applicator Machine | Graphic Packaging
sources.claim: Graphic Packaging supplies a robotic hang-tag applicator that places paper, paperboard or plastic hang tags of various shapes over bottle necks at up to 150 tags per minute, as a standalone machine or integrated into a production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hanging a tag over a cylindrical projection. It transfers to hanging valve tags over valve stems and handles - comparable small tag stock and comparable placement precision - in a fixtured production setting.

sources.date: August 2022 article; platform in commercial use since 2019
sources.title: FieldPrinter autonomous robot automates jobsite layout - Construction Briefing
sources.claim: Dusty Robotics' FieldPrinter is an autonomous construction-site robot that prints BIM layout lines and text on jobsite floors; it marks floors and does not apply tags or labels to installed piping, valves or equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Closest field-deployed marking robot found. It does NOT transfer: it prints on flat floors from a wheeled base and cannot reach, orient to, or adhere labels on installed pipes, valves, tanks or walls, so it cannot substantiate in-situ tagging at E2 or E3.

tasks.label: Connect water heaters and storage tanks to power and water sources.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential retrofit: in an existing home's basement, garage or utility closet, tie the new solar storage tank and backup water heater into the cold supply, hot distribution and solar loop — cut/ream copper or PEX, solder or press fittings, thread dielectric nipples and unions with sealant, install isolation valves and T&P discharge piping — then land the 240 V element/controller circuit and sensor wiring in the junction box; fill, purge, pressure-test and check for leaks in a cramped, cluttered space with existing piping of unknown vintage.

Service/replacement call: an existing tank or backup heater has failed; drain and disconnect it, then reconnect the replacement to the existing (often corroded, misaligned) supply and return stubs with flex connectors or new copper, re-terminate the power whip or plug, refill and leak-check, in a homeowner's mechanical closet or crawl-adjacent space.

Rooftop or exterior installation on a residence or small commercial building: connect an integral-collector or thermosiphon tank to building supply/return lines outdoors, run and insulate the connecting piping, and land pump/controller power and sensor leads at a weatherproof enclosure, working on a pitched or ballasted roof in wind and sun.

Commercial/institutional mechanical room (hotel, school, laundry, hospital): connect large solar storage tanks and backup water heaters with 1.5–4 in. steel/copper piping via grooved couplings, flanges or welded joints, install circulating pumps, mixing valves and expansion tanks, and land power at a disconnect or panel to code; premises are controlled by the owner but the room layout is as-built.

Shop/offsite pre-plumbing: in the contractor's fabrication shop, pre-assemble the tank with its nipples, unions, pump station, sensors and controller wiring on a skid or bracket before delivery, so field hookup is reduced to two pipe joints and one circuit; work is done on a bench with parts staged.

sources.system: KRANENDONK Robotic Pipe Shop (Apollo milling + Aurora spool welding stations)
sources.title: Pipe Spool Automation - KRANENDONK
sources.claim: Fully automated robotic pipe-spool fabrication cells cut, fit and weld pipe, elbows and flanges into finished spools in a fab shop, showing robots can make permanent, pressure-tight pipe joints when the work is fixtured and presented to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic welding of pipe spools in a fab shop. It shows joint-making on comparable steel pipe diameters, but only for welded joints on fixtured, CAD-defined spools — it does not thread, solder, press or seal fittings onto a water heater, install valves, or make any electrical connection, so it covers at most one sub-step of this task.

sources.title: Fire sprinkler welding line - AWL
sources.claim: A robotized welding line for prefabricated fire-sprinkler pipe welds outlet connections at arbitrary positions on the pipe, automating a fitting-to-pipe joining step in a fenced production cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated attachment of outlet fittings to piping in a prefabrication cell. Objects (steel pipe, nipples) are comparable, but the cell only welds pre-programmed outlets onto straight pipe; it does not hook a tank to supply/return lines or handle wiring.

sources.system: Vector Automation fire sprinkler pipe fabrication cell
sources.title: Fire Sprinkler Pipe Factory Automation by Vector
sources.claim: Robots operating in a fire-sprinkler pipe factory place nipples and weld them onto pipe in a start-to-finish automated cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic placement and welding of pipe fittings in a purpose-built cell. Shows fitting placement precision on pipe, but the workpiece arrives cut to length with a barcode and the joints are welded — none of the threaded, soldered or press connections, sealant application, or electrical terminations of a tank hookup are covered.

sources.system: MIRAI robot control system on FANUC/KUKA/UR arms
sources.title: Micropsi's MIRAI Robot Control System Now Available for FANUC Robots - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: AI-vision robot control is sold for production cable-plugging and industrial connector insertion, showing robots can mate electrical connectors autonomously inside a factory cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mating electrical connectors in factory assembly. It covers plug-type mating only; connecting a water heater to power means stripping and landing conductors under terminal screws or wire nuts in a junction box, bonding the ground and closing the enclosure to code, which this system is not shown to do.

sources.system: GE Appliances Camden water heater assembly plant
sources.title: Inside GE Appliance's State-of-the-Art Water Heater Assembly Plant | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Even in a highly automated water heater factory, robots are confined to fabrication, material handling and welding, while assembly of the finished heater remains people-centred.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory assembly of water heaters, the most machine-friendly possible version of attaching fittings and wiring to a tank. The evidence shows fitting installation and final assembly are not robotized even there, which weighs against completion in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Quality control keeps appliance manufacturer out of hot water | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: At a major residential and commercial water heater manufacturer, plugging tank fittings, pressurizing and leak-checking tanks is done by human operators at multiple stations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: attaching fittings to water heater tanks and verifying leak-tightness in a factory. It indicates the accepted-output step of this task (leak-free connections, verified) is still manual in the most structured setting available.

sources.system: NREL Industrialized Construction Innovation robotics pilot
sources.title: Robotics for Systems Integration in Buildings - Pilot Study of Viable Approaches to Install Hygrothermal and Rigid Electrical Systems
sources.claim: Robotic integration of mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems into building assemblies is at the pilot-study stage at NREL, aimed at offsite prefabrication and requiring tight dimensional control before robotic assembly is viable.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic installation of plumbing and electrical systems in buildings. The work is exploratory pilot testing of rigid electrical and hygrothermal systems, with no demonstrated completion of a tank-to-supply plumbing and power hookup.

tasks.label: Cut, miter, and glue piping insulation to insulate plumbing pipes and fittings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential rooftop collector loop: insulating the copper supply and return lines running between collectors, array headers and the roof penetration — measuring, cutting high-temperature elastomeric or mineral-wool sleeve to length, mitering at elbows and around header fittings, gluing seams and butt joints, then jacketing. Sloped roof, sun/wind, pipe already soldered in place on standoffs.

Attic, wall chase, joist bay or crawlspace run: pipe already installed tight against framing; installer kneels or lies in a confined, cluttered space, slits sleeve lengthwise, works it around the pipe past hangers and straps, miters at elbows and offsets, and glues the seams with contact cement.

Residential basement or utility closet at the storage tank and pump station: insulating tees, ball valves, unions, pump flanges, expansion tank and tank nozzles — hand-fabricating mitered fitting covers from sheet or tube stock, dry-fitting, gluing seams, all in tight clearance against walls and other piping.

Commercial or institutional plant (school, hotel, laundry, multifamily mechanical room or rooftop plant) that the building owner controls and keeps to a working standard: larger-diameter piping insulated to spec with mitered fitting covers and glued seams, ladder or scaffold access, other trades present.

Shop or truck-bench prefabrication and repair pieces: working from field measurements or spool drawings, cutting sleeve and sheet insulation to length, cutting miters for elbow covers, gluing up segments and sleeve sections at a bench for transport and final adhesion at the site.

sources.title: Insulation Cutting Machines | Wintech Engineering
sources.claim: Wintech's Fastwire CNC insulation contour cutters cut rigid insulation pipe shells and elbow segments in an insulation fabrication shop, with pre-programmed routines for pipe shells and pipe elbows; the machine only cuts stock — it does not fit, glue or install insulation onto piping or fittings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shop fabrication of insulation pieces. It substantiates only the cutting/mitering sub-step on stock material in a purpose-built cell; it does not present, wrap, adhere or seam insulation onto an assembled pipe run with fittings, so it cannot substantiate completion of the whole instance.

sources.system: Dual Station Copper Insulated Tube Inserting Machine
sources.title: Dual Station Copper Insulated Tube Inserting Machine – BOBO MACHINE
sources.claim: BOBO Machine's dual-station copper insulated tube machine is a factory line that cuts straight copper/aluminum tube to length and feeds foam insulation sleeves onto the bare tube automatically; it handles only straight bare tube and applies no miter cuts or adhesive.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying foam insulation to pipe. Transfer fails for this task because the machine works on straight, unassembled tube fed from a coil in a fixtured production line, with no mitering, no fitting geometry and no adhesive seam work, which are the defining elements of this task.

sources.title: Robotics Underfloor Foam Insulation Technology - Q-Bot
sources.claim: Q-Bot's underfloor insulation robot applies spray foam to the underside of suspended floors in occupied homes, but it is a remotely operated device and applies sprayed foam rather than cutting, mitering and gluing pipe insulation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing insulation in an unstructured building environment. It shows the closest fielded insulation robotics is teleoperated spray application under floors, which does not transfer to cutting, mitering and adhesive-bonding sleeve insulation onto pipes and fittings.

sources.system: Robotic batt insulation installation method (6-DOF arm with custom end effector)
sources.title: A robotic method for installing batt thermal insulation into prefabricated light-frame wood wall panel | Construction Robotics
sources.claim: A 2025 Construction Robotics paper reports a 6-DOF robot arm with a custom end effector installing batt thermal insulation into prefabricated light-frame wood wall panels in a factory setting — a flat, panelized insulation task, not pipe insulation fabrication.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic insulation installation. Objects and geometry differ fundamentally (flat batts pressed into open stud cavities vs. sleeve/sheet insulation cut, mitered and contact-glued around cylindrical pipes, elbows and valves), so it cannot substantiate completion of this task at any tier.

tasks.label: Install plumbing, such as dip tubes, port fittings, drain tank valves, pressure temperature relief valves, or tanks, according to manufacturer specifications and building codes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential retrofit or new build: set an 80–120 gal solar storage tank in a basement, garage or utility closet; insert the dip tube, thread NPT port fittings with sealant, install the T&P relief valve and drain valve to spec, connect cold feed/hot outlet and heat-exchanger loop with soldered or pressed copper, pressure test, leave code-compliant for inspection.

Rooftop/attic side of a residential system: route and join copper supply/return runs between collectors and tank through as-found framing and roof penetrations, install isolation valves, drain-down valves and air vents at field-determined locations, support and insulate the runs.

Commercial/institutional mechanical room (school, hotel, laundry): set 200–500 gal storage tanks, install port fittings, thermometer/sensor wells, ASME relief valves, drain valves and expansion tanks; join threaded or grooved steel and large copper piping per drawings and code.

Service/repair call: replace a failed T&P relief valve, corroded drain valve or broken dip tube on an already installed tank — drain the tank, break in-place corroded threaded joints with wrenches, re-seal, reassemble, refill and test for leaks.

Shop prefabrication before delivery: assemble a pump station/valve manifold or pre-plumb a tank with nipples, unions, relief and drain valves on a bench at the contractor's shop, then pressure test the assembly.

sources.system: UltraHeat W Series with Dragon 15 brazing robot
sources.title: Robotic Induction Brazing of Copper to Brass - UltraFlex
sources.claim: UltraFlex's Dragon 15 brazing robot autonomously positions an induction coil and brazes copper pipe to brass joints for an HVAC manufacturer in a fixtured industrial cell, with a 20-second heat cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: joining copper tube to brass fittings — the same materials and joint geometry as solar-thermal tank port and piping connections; it substantiates leak-tight joining only when the parts are fixtured and presented, i.e. at E1.

sources.system: Felp Assembly Systems automated fitting assembly unit
sources.title: Automated Manufacturing in the U.S. Makes for a Fitting Process | Production Machining
sources.claim: An automated assembly unit built by Felp Assembly Systems installs internal components into brass plumbing fitting bodies from bowl feeders and crimps them, running in a US production plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated assembly of brass plumbing fittings. Comparable objects (brass water fittings) and precision (sealed joints), but only inside a purpose-built fed-and-fixtured cell, so it supports E1 only.

sources.system: Fully Automatic Leak Test Cell with Robotic Handling
sources.title: Case Study - Fully Automatic Leak Test Cell with Robotic Handling
sources.claim: TQC built a fully automatic cell in which a robot handles parts, components are bowl-fed, and assemblies are air-decay leak tested with automatic pass/fail segregation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated leak verification of fluid assemblies, the acceptance step equivalent to pressure-testing plumbing; demonstrated only in a fenced/fed production cell (E1).

sources.system: Toshiba Machine SCARA robot valve assembly system
sources.title: Automated valve fitting | TM Robotics | Case study
sources.claim: Three SCARA robots were integrated into an automated system producing pneumatic valves for a UK manufacturer, raising output on the valve assembly line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated assembly of fluid-control valve components with fed parts and fixtures; comparable insertion/threading precision, but confined to a purpose-built cell (E1).

sources.title: Hilti Unveils BIM-Enabled Construction Jobsite Robot
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot, deployed on construction sites globally since late 2020, is a semi-autonomous mobile robot that drills anchor holes overhead for MEP installation from a BIM plan; it performs drilling only, not pipe, fitting or valve installation.
sources.transferJustification: Closest on-site MEP robot: it establishes that field robots in occupied buildings and jobsites do hole drilling only, and do not handle pipe, fittings, valves or tanks; cited as the boundary of demonstrated field capability.

sources.title: Novarc unveils spool welding robot for pipe fabrication - BIC Magazine
sources.claim: Novarc's Spool Welding Robot is a collaborative, semi-automated welding system used in pipe fabrication shops that welds flanges, tees, elbows and reducers, with the human welder performing fit-up and sharing control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pipe-to-fitting joining in a fabrication shop; however the operator performs fit-up, tacking and part loading, so autonomy of the whole job is not established and it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Install monitoring system components, such as flow meters, temperature gauges, and pressure gauges, according to system design and manufacturer specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New residential solar water-heating installation in a private home: technician mounts a collector-outlet temperature sensor on the roof array, an immersion/strap-on tank sensor at the storage tank, and threads pressure and temperature gauges into the solar pump-station ports in a basement or utility closet, then routes and terminates sensor cable to the differential controller and verifies readings.

Residential service/retrofit call: adding or replacing a failed temperature sensor, pressure gauge, or flow meter on an existing home system in a crawlspace, garage, attic or closet, working around existing insulation, valves and finished surfaces, then re-terminating wiring and confirming the controller reads correctly.

Commercial or multifamily solar thermal system in an operating building's mechanical room: install an inline BTU/flow meter in the solar loop piping, thermowells and immersion sensors, pressure gauges on manifolds per the design drawings, and land sensor wiring to the monitoring panel or BMS.

New-construction commercial or industrial process-heat job site: mounting flow meters and gauges on large-diameter loop piping and headers still under construction, coordinating with other trades, dust, temporary lighting and incomplete layouts, then wiring back to the monitoring cabinet.

Shop prefabrication of pre-plumbed solar pump-station or skid modules: gauges, flow meter and sensor wells assembled and sealed into a manifold on a bench, wired to the controller, pressure/leak checked before delivery to the job site.

sources.system: Epson-robot hydraulic valve assembly cell (integrator-built, 8 stations)
sources.developer: Automation integrator using Epson robots, SCHUNK grippers, ATI compliance devices
sources.title: Robots assemble hydraulic valves | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: A commercial multi-station robotic cell autonomously threads components into hydraulic valve bodies with cross-thread-avoiding compliance, applies thread-locking adhesive, torque-drives the joints and leak-tests each assembly — the same class of threaded-instrument-into-port work as fitting gauges and sensors to a solar loop manifold.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic threaded assembly of fluid-power components with sealant, torque control and leak test. Transfers because installing pressure/temperature gauges and inline meters is threading similar-sized metal fittings into ports to a specified torque with a leak-tight seal, on a fixtured workpiece.

sources.developer: University of L'Aquila (Antonelli & Beomonte Zobel), using Rethink Robotics Sawyer
sources.title: Automated Screwing of Fittings in Pneumatic Manifolds (Int. J. Automation Technology)
sources.claim: A collaborative robot station autonomously picks pneumatic fittings from a feeder, centers them on threaded holes in manifolds held on a rotating fixture, and screws them in — directly analogous to screwing gauges/sensor fittings into a monitoring manifold.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic installation of threaded fittings into manifold ports. Comparable objects (small threaded fluid fittings), comparable precision (thread engagement without cross-threading), in a fixtured purpose-built station.

sources.system: Multi-Robot Engine Cover Assembly System (FANUC robots, TranTek Automation)
sources.title: Assembly Robots | Assembly Line Robots | FANUC America
sources.claim: Multi-robot production cells perform sensor installation together with sealing, leak testing and bolt fastening ... fixtured metal housings, showing that mounting and sealing a sensor to a specification and verifying the result is a routine automated cell capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sensor installation with sealing and leak verification on a fixtured assembly; transfers to fitting temperature/pressure sensors into ports and confirming a leak-tight, functioning installation.

sources.title: Robotic wiring centre will save up to 15 hours per panel - Drives&Controls
sources.claim: A commercial robotic wiring centre cuts, strips, ferrules, routes through cable duct and lands wires on terminal blocks and devices in a fixtured panel, covering the sensor-to-controller wiring portion of monitoring-component installation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated low-voltage wiring and terminations in a fixtured panel. Transfers to landing flow-meter and sensor leads on a solar controller/monitoring panel, with the same conductor sizes and terminal types.

tasks.label: Assess collector sites to ensure structural integrity of potential mounting surfaces or the best orientation and tilt for solar collectors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-family home, pitched asphalt-shingle roof: technician surveys the exterior collector site — measures roof pitch and azimuth, available unshaded area, locates vents/chimneys/dormers, runs a shading analysis for surrounding trees and buildings, and judges condition/remaining life of the roof covering to decide where a solar water-heating or pool-heating collector goes and at what tilt.

Single-family home: verifying the mounting surface can carry glazed collectors plus water — ladder to roof to sound the decking, then attic access to inspect and measure rafters or trusses (size, spacing, direction, rot, prior modifications), locate framing members for lag attachments, and confirm no sag or damage before committing to a mounting layout.

Commercial or multifamily building (hotel, laundry, apartment block, school) with a flat membrane roof: survey the roof plane for available area, HVAC/parapet obstructions and their shadows, membrane condition and ponding, and lay out the orientation and tilt of rack-mounted collector banks.

Commercial/institutional building: structural verification for a rooftop collector array — inspect roof deck, joists and beams from below or in the interstitial space, evaluate existing curbs/attachment points and penetration locations, and confirm the deck will take the array's dead and wind loads.

Ground-mount, wall-mount or open-yard collector site at a residence or small facility: pick the least-shaded location, determine best orientation and tilt, check terrain slope and ground conditions for rack footings, and measure piping run distance back to the tank/mechanical room.

Service/retrofit call on an existing solar thermal array: assess whether existing mounts and the mounting surface are still sound — hands-on tug tests on lag bolts and clamps, lifting flashing and shingles to look for leaks or rotted sheathing around penetrations, and judging whether collectors can be re-mounted or re-tilted.

sources.title: Roof inspection drone tech with EagleView | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio's House Scan software plans a facet-by-facet flight over a residential roof and flies the inspection autonomously, capturing the imagery used for virtual property assessment; deployed commercially with EagleView for residential roof inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: residential roof inspection/measurement. Same physical act of surveying a house roof from the air to document facet geometry, obstructions and surface condition — the data a solar thermal technician gathers to judge mounting surface condition, orientation and tilt.

sources.title: FAQ | Loveland Innovations
sources.claim: Loveland Innovations' IMGING builds an autonomous flight plan from operator-specified scan area and obstructions and then controls the DJI drone through the whole capture flight.

sources.title: IMGING Inspect | Loveland Innovations
sources.claim: IMGING is sold to solar site surveyors and produces comprehensive site survey data from automated drone surveys in a single site visit, intended to be design-grade so no re-survey is needed.

sources.title: Roof Report – DroneDeploy
sources.claim: Drone-captured data is processed into a roof report giving per-face perimeter, area, slope, pitch and ... plus located obstructions, with stated 99.4% measurement accuracy — the orientation-and-tilt output of a collector site assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drone roof measurement for roofing/solar design. The measured quantities (slope/pitch, azimuth, obstruction locations) are exactly the orientation-and-tilt determination this task requires.

sources.title: Scanifly approved tool for solar resource assessments | Energy Trust Insider
sources.claim: A utility program administrator accepts drone-based 3D site models as qualifying documentation for the on-site shade analysis and site assessment requirement, explicitly letting workers stay off the roof during site assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: solar collector site assessment. Establishes that a drone-captured survey meets the accepted quality standard for shade/orientation assessment; Scanifly flights are flown by the surveyor, so autonomy rests on the Skydio/IMGING items.

sources.title: Skydio 3D Scan Autonomous Drone Inspection | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio 3D Scan fully automates the data-capture flight around complex structures, producing comprehensive high-resolution 3D models used for inspection reports of buildings and industrial assets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous structure scanning at commercial/industrial facilities. Produces the same geometric model and surface imagery used to lay out and orient rooftop equipment on a commercial building.

sources.title: Utility Solar Farm Construction Tracking with Drone Inspections | vHive
sources.claim: Autonomous, pre-programmed drone flights over utility-scale solar sites produce topographic maps and terrain contours used to verify site grading, boundaries and clearances before structures go in.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pre-construction solar site survey. Same physical act (autonomous aerial survey of open ground) yielding terrain, slope and obstruction data used to site and orient ground-mounted solar collectors.

sources.title: Civ Robotics spots Series A funding for automated surveying - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Autonomous georeferenced ground robots are deployed at solar construction sites, marking layout points to sub-inch accuracy over challenging terrain and in all weather; more than 100 robots on job sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous field surveying/layout for ground-mount solar. Demonstrates autonomous, survey-accurate ground work in unstructured open sites, supporting the layout/orientation portion of a ground-mount collector site assessment.

tasks.label: Apply ultraviolet radiation protection to prevent degradation of plumbing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New residential solar thermal install: on a pitched shingle roof, wrap the exterior insulated copper/PEX collector supply and return lines with UV-resistant tape or jacketing (or brush/spray a UV-protective mastic), including at elbows, sensor wells and roof penetrations; work at height, variable weather, ladder access, varying roof geometry.

Service/repair call: strip sun-degraded, crumbling foam insulation and old tape from an existing installed system's exterior piping (roof, exterior wall, or tank area), then re-insulate and re-apply UV-protective wrap/coating around in-place pipe already fastened to the building.

Commercial or institutional flat-roof / mechanical-yard install: long runs of insulated piping receiving factory-cut aluminum or PVC jacketing with banding and sealed seams, on an owner-controlled facility roof with controlled access and equipment pads.

Ground-level exterior runs at a residence or small site: piping between ground-mount collectors, storage tank and building wall gets UV-protective jacketing/paint at grade, in a yard with landscaping, uneven footing and weather exposure.

Shop/bench prefabrication before delivery: cutting insulation and applying UV-resistant jacketing, tape or coating to straight pipe assemblies and fittings on a bench in the contractor's fabrication shop or warehouse.

sources.system: Selmers SFBE/DFBE pipe coating application system
sources.title: SFBE/DFBE pipe coating - Selmers
sources.claim: Selmers supplies complete, conveyor-fed in-plant pipe coating lines (SFBE/DFBE) in which pipe is heated, handled and electrostatically powder-coated with a protective layer by automated equipment, with automated systems replacing manual coating labor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory application of a protective coating layer over the full length of pipe. It transfers because the workpiece class (pipe), the act (laying down a continuous protective covering over the pipe surface) and the acceptance criterion (uniform, holiday-free coverage) match applying UV protection to plumbing, with the pipe presented by conveyor as a purpose-built setting would present it.

sources.title: 3LPE/3LPP coating - Selmers
sources.claim: The same class of line extrudes an adhesive plus a polyethylene/polypropylene top-coat layer over the pipe automatically as it passes through the plant, i.e. machine-applied outer protective jacketing on pipe.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine application of a polymer outer layer to pipe. The polyolefin top coat is the weather/environment-facing protective layer, the same function as a UV-protective wrap on solar-thermal plumbing; objects (pipe), motion (continuous wrap/extrusion along the pipe) and quality checks (thickness, adhesion, holiday detection) are comparable.

sources.system: GF Urecon factory-applied insulation and outer jackets (Spiwrap, PE jacket)
sources.title: Insulated Pipes Outer Jackets GF Piping Systems Polyethylene Outer Jacket (fact sheet)
sources.claim: UV protection for above-ground insulated piping is conventionally delivered as a factory-applied outer jacket over the pipe insulation, using UV-inhibited polyethylene or spiral steel jacketing.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the task's output — UV protection over insulated plumbing — is routinely produced by factory jacketing of pipe brought to the plant; cited for the UV relevance of factory-applied jackets, not as the autonomous system (autonomy not established).

sources.title: Painting Robots - Explore FANUC's Paint Robots | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC paint robots autonomously spray-apply coatings to workpieces carried past them on conveyors inside enclosed, fenced paint booths, including tracking parts in motion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic spray application of protective/weather-resistant coatings to fixtured or conveyed parts. Transfers to brush/spray UV-protective coating of pipe presented on a fixture: same act (controlled deposition of a protective film), comparable precision and film-thickness acceptance standards.

sources.system: Komax KT 800 / KT 810 and KTR 1800 harness taping machines
sources.title: Harness Taping | Komax
sources.claim: Komax sells fully automatic taping machines that spiral-wrap tape around elongated flexible bundles held in the machine, including branched, large-diameter harnesses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic spiral tape wrapping of an elongated cylindrical workpiece presented in a fixture — mechanically the same operation as wrapping UV-resistant tape around a pipe run, with comparable overlap/tension quality requirements.

sources.title: PaintJet puts robots to work in construction and maintenance as labor shortage drags on
sources.claim: In-situ robotic coating of building exteriors exists but is remote-controlled and limited to large flat surfaces such as warehouse walls and ship hulls, not wrapping or jacketing small-diameter piping on roofs.
sources.transferJustification: Cited for the negative side: the closest in-situ coating robots on buildings are teleoperated and address broad flat facades, so they cannot substantiate autonomous rooftop wrapping/jacketing of solar-thermal plumbing at E2 or E3.

roles.title: Plasterers and Stucco Masons
roles.description: Apply interior or exterior plaster, cement, stucco, or similar materials. May also set ornamental plaster.

tasks.label: Cover surfaces such as windows, doors, or sidewalks to protect from splashing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Exterior stucco on a single-family home or residential remodel: before scratch/brown/finish coats, the mason masks windows, doors, garage openings, light fixtures, meters and hose bibs with poly film/paper and tape, and covers walkways, driveway, patio, landscaping and A/C units with drop cloths or plastic; work done from ladders and on uneven ground around existing landscaping.

Multi-story commercial new construction with stucco/EIFS: masking installed storefront glazing and window units, curtain-wall frames and door openings from scaffolding or a swing stage, plus covering adjacent sidewalks, entries and finished concrete with poly and plywood; site layout differs building to building and changes daily.

Interior plaster or veneer-plaster work in an occupied private residence (remodel or repair): laying drop cloths and taping poly over floors, furniture, trim, doorways and windows, sometimes erecting a plastic dust barrier, in rooms with varied furnishings and clutter.

Interior plaster patch/repair inside an institution-controlled facility (hotel corridor, school, hospital wing, office building) during maintenance work: covering the corridor floor, doors, hardware, and adjacent finished surfaces with poly sheeting and tape to a facility standard, with the area cordoned off by the facility.

Small ad hoc repair or patch call (stucco crack repair, small interior plaster patch): quickly taping a plastic sheet over one or two windows or a door, and dropping a cloth over the sidewalk or floor immediately below the patch, then removing it after the coat sets.

sources.system: FerRobotics ATK (Active Taping Kit) with Aerobotix robotic cells
sources.title: ATK Active Taping Kit robotic masking tape applicator end effector - FerRobotics
sources.claim: FerRobotics' Active Taping Kit (with Aerobotix) is a commercial robot end-effector that automates masking-tape application before painting, applying tape to large parts and aircraft surfaces with force control and no wrinkles, inside an automated aerospace paint/process facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: masking surfaces before spray coating. Same purpose as the plasterer's masking (keep coating off adjacent surfaces), comparable materials (adhesive tape on rigid surfaces) and precision, but performed on fixtured parts in a robotic paint facility rather than on a building.

sources.title: Glassbuild Connect | PDS IG Equipment
sources.claim: PDS IG Equipment sells a protective-film application system for insulating and monolithic glass that automatically sizes and covers glass units with temporary protective film with no user intervention, running at insulating-glass line speeds in glass fabrication plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: covering window glass with temporary protective film. tasks.label: Apply coats of plaster or stucco to walls, ceilings, or partitions of buildings, using trowels, brushes, or spray guns.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Exterior three-coat cement stucco on a new or re-clad wood-frame house: scratch and brown coats pumped/sprayed or hand-applied over metal lath, rodded and floated to plane around corner beads and control joints, then a colored finish coat; worked outdoors from ground, ladders and scaffold, subject to weather, cure timing and varied elevations.

Exterior stucco or EIFS coats on a multifamily/commercial building: base coat troweled or sprayed over mesh and EPS board, then a textured acrylic or cementitious finish coat, over large elevations reached from scaffold, swing stage or boom lift, with joints, reveals and window returns.

Interior gypsum veneer plaster or full skim/finish coats on walls and ceilings of new commercial/institutional interiors (offices, schools, hospitals, terminals): empty framed-and-boarded rooms and corridors, level floors, temporary power and lighting, large repeated surfaces taken to a flat, paint-ready finish.

Interior plaster or skim coats in new-construction or gut-renovated residential units (apartments, condos, houses): small rooms, closets, ceilings, stair soffits, doorway-limited access, other trades working nearby.

Patch, repair and re-skim of damaged or historic plaster in occupied buildings and homes: cut out failed or water-damaged areas, key new plaster to existing lath, build up coats level with the surrounding wall and blend/match existing texture, while protecting floors and furnishings.

Decorative/specialty finish coats: burnished Venetian or lime plaster, textured or sprayed architectural finishes on feature walls, ceilings and columns in interiors, applied to an aesthetic standard set on site.

tasks.label: Clean and prepare surfaces for applications of plaster, cement, stucco, or similar materials, such as by drywall taping.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Exterior stucco/EIFS prep on new construction (house, apartment block, strip mall): blow/brush dust and debris off CMU, concrete or sheathed walls, remove form oil, laitance or efflorescence, dampen masonry, roll or spray a bonding agent/primer, and mask windows, doors and adjacent finishes; done outdoors from ladders and scaffold in variable weather at an active jobsite.

Re-stucco/repair prep on an existing building exterior: pressure-wash the wall, sound and chip out delaminated stucco, wire-brush and rout cracks, strip failed paint or coatings, vacuum dust, apply bonding agent and mask trim, landscaping and windows; occupied homes and commercial buildings with obstacles and uneven ground.

Interior prep of large flat wall and ceiling fields in open commercial/institutional new construction (office floors, data centers, hospitals, schools): tape and embed board joints, apply a coat/skim of compound, sand to a uniform substrate for veneer plaster or paint; big rooms and corridors, high walls, active jobsite.

Interior detail prep in the same buildings and in dwellings: inside and outside corners, corner and casing beads, soffits, closets, stairwells, bathrooms, and areas around outlets, door frames and penetrations; taping, filling and sanding tight, complex geometry plus punch-list touch-ups.

Repair/renovation prep in occupied interiors (homes, historic buildings, schools): scrape loose and flaking plaster and paint, strip wallpaper, wash and dust walls and ceilings, cut out failed areas, mask floors, furniture and fixtures, and apply a plaster bonding agent before patching or re-skimming.

Shop/plant substrate prep in a fabrication facility: cleaning, sanding and priming panelized wall panels, precast/GFRC panel faces, or ornamental plaster backing and molds before plaster or cement application; fixed layout, standard equipment, controlled access.

tasks.label: Create decorative textures in finish coat, using brushes or trowels, sand, pebbles, or stones.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Exterior finish (color) coat on a single-family or small multifamily home: crew applies the finish coat over brown coat/lath and works it into a specified texture (lace/skip-trowel, sand float, dash) with hopper gun and trowels, around windows, corners, foam trim, soffits and returns, from ladders/pump jacks, matching texture consistently across elevations and joining wet edges before set-up, in ambient weather.

Interior decorative texture on walls and ceilings of a house or commercial interior under construction: spray-applied orange peel/knockdown, hand skip-trowel, swirl or Venetian/polished plaster over plaster or drywall base, including masking, corners, inside/outside angles, and blending texture uniformly across a room.

Patch, remodel and repair: re-creating an existing decorative texture on a damaged or newly patched area of an existing interior or exterior wall, judging and matching the surrounding texture pattern, aggregate size and sheen, and feathering the blend so the repair is invisible.

Large commercial/multifamily exterior: finish-coat texture over large, mostly flat stucco or EIFS elevations from scaffold, swing stage or lift, keeping texture and color uniform across large fields with control joints and reveals.

Shop or plant work: applying and texturing the finish coat on prefabricated EIFS/stucco wall panels or ornamental cast plaster elements staged flat or upright inside a fabrication facility with fixed layout, material staging and controlled conditions.
