tasks.label: Mix mortar and plaster to desired consistency or direct workers who perform mixing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential exterior stucco job (new build or re-stucco): worker batches bagged preblended stucco or portland/lime/sand plus water in a portable mortar mixer or continuous mixer set up in the driveway/yard, judges consistency by look and trowel feel, and keeps mixed material flowing to the scratch/brown/finish crew all day in ambient weather.

Commercial or multifamily cement-plaster/stucco job: bulk or silo-supplied material mixed in a large paddle mixer or continuous mixer feeding a plaster pump, high volume, consistency held constant batch to batch so the pump and spray gun do not clog; work occurs on an active construction site with scaffold and other trades.

Interior gypsum plaster / veneer plaster or finish coat inside a building under construction: bagged plaster mixed with water in barrels or 5-gallon buckets with a drill-mounted paddle, medium batches timed to the material's set, mixed near the work area on floors shared with other trades.

Small patch, repair, or ornamental work in an occupied home or building: a few gallons of patching plaster, gauging plaster, lime putty, or a color-matched finish hand-mixed in a bucket on-site, consistency tuned to the repair and to matching existing texture, with dust and spill control around finished surfaces.

Journeyman/foreman directs tenders who do the mixing: specifies proportions and water, inspects the mix on the board or in the mixer, and orders adjustments (more water, longer mixing, retemper) so batches arriving at the wall meet the desired consistency.

tasks.label: Clean job sites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial or multifamily building under construction: at the end of a plastering/veneer-plaster phase the crew cleans the work area floors — sweeping and vacuuming plaster and sanding dust plus small drops, chips and packaging scraps off large open floor plates and corridors so the slab is dust-free for the following trade (paint, flooring). Layout changes daily; other trades' material is stacked around.

Large slab / parking-deck or big commercial floor after stucco, EIFS or plaster work: wet wash-down and scrub of the concrete to remove cementitious film, splatter and fine dust before hand-over of the area. Open, obstacle-light surface, water available, work done at end of shift.

New residential construction, empty interior rooms: after plastering/patching the crew scrapes dropped mud off the slab and thresholds, gathers scrap lath, mesh, tape, empty mix bags and used buckets into a barrow, wheels them out to the dumpster, then sweeps/vacuums the rooms. Narrow doorways, stairs, uneven surfaces.

Exterior stucco/EIFS job at a house or small commercial building: shovel and scrape stucco droppings off soil, walks and driveway, hose or scrub splatter off windows, walls, hardscape and neighbouring cars/fences, pull scaffold planks' debris, collect paper, lath, mesh and cement bags, load debris into the truck or dumpster, rake and sweep the perimeter and street. Weather, landscaping, parked vehicles and neighbours present.

Mixing station and tool cleanup at the site: wash out the mortar mixer, pump/hopper gun, hoses, hawks, trowels, floats and buckets before the material sets, flush lines, contain and dispose of the washout slurry, and stow the cleaned tools.

Patch/repair or ornamental plaster job inside an occupied institutional building (hospital, school, hotel): after the patch cures, vacuum plaster and sanding dust, wipe adjacent surfaces and fixtures, pull down masking and dust barriers, fold drop cloths, remove debris and restore the corridor or room to service the same day.

tasks.label: Rough the undercoat surface with a scratcher so the finish coat will adhere.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Exterior three-coat stucco on a one- or two-story house (tract or custom): after the scratch coat is applied over metal lath, the mason drags a scarifier/rake horizontally across wall fields to cut ~1/8 in. grooves while the mortar is green; work from ground, ladders or light scaffold; sun, wind and heat shorten the set window; yard cluttered with mixer, hoses and materials.

Exterior stucco on multi-story commercial, hotel or multifamily elevations: scratching large wall areas several stories up from tube scaffold, mast climbers or boom/scissor lifts, moving along the deck as the coat is applied ahead of the scratcher, weather exposed.

Exterior detail and ornamental areas: soffits, arches, columns, parapets, recesses, band/foam trim and the returns around windows and doors, where the scratcher must reach tight geometry, inside corners and edges without gouging accessories or lath.

Interior plaster undercoat (scratch/brown coat over lath, or base coat for veneer plaster) in a building under construction or renovation: flat walls and some ceilings scratched indoors at floor-reachable heights, plus corners and openings, with the crew applying and scratching in sequence.

Patch, repair and tie-in work in existing or occupied buildings (homes, storefronts, historic restoration): small irregular undercoat areas scratched so the finish coat bonds and blends to surrounding intact plaster, often in awkward positions around furniture, trim and existing finishes.

Shop application on prefabricated wall panels or precast elements in a panelization plant or fabrication yard: panels coated on stands or tables in a fixed-layout facility with standard equipment, then scratched before the finish coat.

sources.system: Okibo EG7 (and earlier EP-1000) autonomous finishing robot
sources.title: OKIBO - Smart Robots For Construction Sites
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7 is a self-contained mobile arm robot that scans and models interior walls and executes coating/plaster and drywall-finishing passes autonomously on construction sites, with fleets on European and US jobsites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-applied plaster/coating and drywall finishing on the same wall surfaces a plasterer works. Scratching an undercoat is a coarser tool pass over an identical planar substrate at looser tolerance than the finish passes Okibo already plans and executes autonomously in the same construction-site environment.

sources.title: How a Drywall Robot Is Reshaping Interior Construction | Built (Bluebeam)
sources.claim: The Canvas drywall robot is set at a wall by a worker, then maps the surface, applies an engineered compound profile, and on a later pass re-maps the wall and sands it flush with a vacuum-capped sanding head.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: abrasive contact passes over a coated vertical wall on an interior jobsite. Scratching an undercoat is the same class of operation - a tool held at controlled depth/force and swept over the wall - with far looser depth tolerance than a Level 5 sanded finish.

sources.title: Drywall finishing robot saves time, prevents injuries | Construction Dive
sources.claim: Canvas robots were used by a general contractor on a US commercial project, with the robotic arm taping, spraying and sanding drywall to a Level 5 ... while run by workers on site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wall-coating surface work accepted at the trade's top quality benchmark on a real jobsite, showing that robot-executed contact passes on walls meet employer-accepted quality; a scratched undercoat is a lower-tolerance output of the same kind.

sources.system: Geko G100 automatic wall putty grinding robot
sources.developer: Guangdong Bright Dream Robotics (for Country Garden)
sources.title: Geko G100 - Automatic Wall Putty Grinding Robot - IDSA
sources.claim: The Geko G100 wall-putty grinding robot performs automatic path planning and obstacle avoidance to grind interior wall surfaces on construction sites, and is a commercially produced construction robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous abrasive tooling across vertical wall coatings inside buildings under construction; the coverage planning and wall-contact control are the same competencies a scarifier pass over an undercoat requires.

sources.system: Smooth G1 concrete leveling and troweling robot
sources.title: iF Design - Basement Concrete Troweling and Leveling Robot
sources.claim: Bright Dream Robotics' Smooth G1 system levels and then trowels concrete floors, with the troweling robot starting after the concrete's initial set and planning and driving its own path, needing one person only for auxiliary work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: working fresh cementitious material with a contact tool inside the set-timing window - the same timing and material-state constraint that governs scratching a green scratch coat - executed autonomously on building sites.

sources.system: FerRobotics Active Contact Flange (ACF/ACF-Kit) on industrial robots and cobots
sources.title: Active Contact Flange Kit - FerRobotics
sources.claim: FerRobotics' Active Contact Flange kits give industrial robots and cobots real force-controlled contact for material removal and surface finishing of fixtured workpieces of almost any shape and material, sold as commercial plug-and-play tooling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: force-controlled surface treatment of a fixtured workpiece in a robot cell. Raking a scarifier to a set depth across a fixtured, freshly coated panel is the same programmed toolpath-plus-force-compliance operation on a softer material and looser tolerance.

sources.system: Bright Dream Robotics construction robot fleet
sources.title: Home - Construction Robotics (Bright Dream Robotics)
sources.claim: Bright Dream Robotics states that over 40 of its construction robot types (including plastering, spraying, grinding and concrete finishing machines) are in commercial application across more than 1,100 projects.
sources.transferJustification: Supports the commercial maturity and real deployment scale of the wall-grinding and concrete-troweling robots cited above, whose capabilities are the basis for the transfer to scratching an undercoat.

tasks.label: Set up scaffolds.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential / light-commercial exterior stucco job: crew erects sectional steel frame scaffolding around a one- or two-story house — carrying frames and cross braces over landscaping and soft, sloping soil, setting mudsills and base plates, plumbing and leveling with screw jacks, planking each lift, adding guardrails and wall ties, then dismantling after the finish coat.

Interior plastering: assembling a rolling scaffold tower or sectional interior tower from its components (end frames, braces, deck, casters, guardrails) in a room being plastered, sizing it to the ceiling height and the work at hand.

Light ad hoc staging inside occupied or partly finished spaces: laying planks across trestles/horses or step benches, and repeatedly re-positioning folding towers and planks room to room around furniture, drop cloths, mixing stations and other trades as the plastering progresses.

Multi-story commercial facade: erecting multi-lift modular system or tube-and-clamp scaffolding along a building for stucco/EIFS work — hoisting standards, ledgers and decks lift by lift, installing braces, ties into the structure, toe boards, stair access and debris netting.

Small patch, soffit, gable, chimney and repair jobs: hanging ladder jacks on extension ladders, setting pump jacks on poles, or rigging a plank between a ladder and a wall bracket, on varied residential exteriors and interiors.

Work inside an institution-controlled facility (industrial plant, refinery, school or hospital under a maintenance contract): erecting standard modular scaffolding on prepared paving/floor inside a permitted, access-controlled work area for plaster, stucco or fireproofing repair.

sources.developer: PERI GmbH with University of Southern Denmark (LSP), KU Leuven, RWTH Aachen, UC Leuven Limburg, Jožef Stefan Institute
sources.title: The future of scaffolding is here — University of Southern Denmark (Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute news)
sources.claim: Genio, a mobile dual-arm robot developed by scaffolding manufacturer PERI with SDU, KU Leuven, RWTH Aachen, UC Leuven Limburg and the Jožef Stefan Institute, autonomously positions, lifts and connects PERI UP modular scaffold components from a digital twin and assembly sequence prepared by a scaffolder, with an integrated transport system feeding material to the working level.
sources.transferJustification: Demonstrated on PERI UP modular facade scaffolding; transfer to US sectional frame scaffolds and rolling towers rests on comparable objects (10-25 kg steel frames, ledgers, decks, guardrails), comparable insertion/pinning precision at rosette or pin connections, and the same staged, prepared, machine-built setting.

sources.developer: PERI GmbH / SDU Centre for Large Structure Production
sources.title: Researchers develop new robot: The future of scaffolding is here (SDU press release, Ritzau)
sources.claim: As of mid-2025 Genio remained a prototype that had only been operated in closed, controlled environments (laboratory and the PERI bauma 2025 exhibition hall); a three-year follow-on project was launched to evaluate process reliability, usability and speed on realistic test construction sites.

sources.title: KEWAZO at AFPM NSC26 in San Antonio, May 2026 — KEWAZO LIFTBOT
sources.claim: The only scaffolding robot in routine commercial field use, KEWAZO's LIFTBOT, is a battery-powered, remote-controlled robotic hoist that moves scaffold material vertically along a structure at industrial plants and refineries (e.g., a 52 m flare at BASF Ludwigshafen); human scaffolders still perform the erection and dismantling itself.

sources.title: Robot named Douglas begins work on Tilbury Douglas site — ScaffMag
sources.claim: The first humanoid robot put to work on a live UK construction site by a tier-one contractor performs administrative and data-collection work — autonomous navigation, 360-degree imagery, progress reports — not physical erection tasks, indicating that site-deployed mobile robots in unstructured construction settings do not yet build access structures.

tasks.label: Cure freshly plastered surfaces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New single-family home, three-coat exterior stucco: after the scratch and brown coats, the mason keeps the walls damp — fog-spraying elevations with a hose/fog nozzle two to three times a day for 24–48 hours, moving hoses and ladders/scaffold around the house, adjusting frequency for sun, wind and temperature.

Commercial or multifamily building, cement plaster/stucco on large elevations: curing whole scaffolded or lift-accessed facades — fog misting between coats, or spray-applying a curing compound/membrane, hanging shade cloth or wind screens, and keeping the surface moist per spec over one to two days.

Interior plaster (cement basecoat or veneer plaster) in a building under construction or renovation: controlling the cure/dry-down — closing or covering openings, setting fans, heaters or dehumidifiers, damp-curing cement basecoats, and checking surfaces over several days before the finish coat.

Patch and repair work in an occupied home or building: curing a small freshly plastered/stuccoed patch — dampening the patch and edges, taping plastic sheeting or damp burlap over it, returning to re-mist so the patch does not craze or dry out faster than the surrounding wall.

Shop or plant work: curing plastered/stuccoed prefabricated panels or ornamental plaster casts in a fabrication shop — keeping casts and panels damp or in a curing room at controlled temperature and humidity until they gain strength for handling.

sources.system: Automated concrete curing system (PLC fog-spray curing, Chen/Cai et al.)
sources.developer: Research team published in Journal of Building Engineering (Chinese projects)
sources.title: Theory and application of new automated concrete curing system
sources.claim: A PLC-controlled automated fog-spray curing system keeps cement-based members moist by computing spray intervals from cement hydration models and real-time temperature/humidity sensing; it was field-tested on 20 box-section beams and applied in several real projects (highway T-beams, high-speed rail box girders), with piping and nozzles installed around each member.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moist-curing freshly placed cement-based material. Curing freshly plastered (cement plaster/stucco) surfaces is the same act — holding surface moisture and temperature over the cure period with fine fog on a cementitious surface — with the same low precision demands, so performance carries over when the surface is presented within the fixed nozzle array.

sources.developer: Feng, Jia, Pei, Zhai, Xu, Lacidogna (Developments in the Built Environment)
sources.title: Research on the application of residual networks considering attention mechanism in concrete curing robot - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A concrete curing robot with walking, film-covering and sprinkler modules automates plastic-film curing and water-spray curing of freshly poured concrete, deciding on water spray from a vision model; feasibility was tested on a real building project (Tianjin Lingang Hospital).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: curing freshly placed cementitious surfaces (film covering plus water-spray curing). The curing decision and spray action transfer to plaster, but the demonstrated surfaces are flat, ground-level concrete pours, not vertical plastered walls at height, so it substantiates curing only where the surface is presented to the machine.

sources.title: SmartSet Concrete Curing Systems - Afinitas
sources.claim: Commercial precast concrete curing systems apply misting and computer-controlled, zoned temperature and humidity through the whole cure cycle inside purpose-built kilns, replacing manual watering and environment control for cementitious products.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: controlled curing of cast cementitious products. Curing plaster/stucco likewise means holding humidity and temperature (and misting) until the surface gains strength; the machine performs exactly this function once the element is inside the purpose-built kiln.

sources.system: Okibo EG7 / EP-1 autonomous plastering and painting robot
sources.title: Video | Robot decorator makes its debut - Construction Management
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7/EP-1 robots autonomously navigate active construction sites and spray-apply plaster, render and paint to interior walls, with over a million square feet covered in Europe and use on US sites; no curing (moisture maintenance over 24–48 hours) function is documented.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous spray application of coatings to walls on construction sites. It establishes that mobile autonomy and wall spraying exist at E3, but nothing in the source covers repeated moist curing, covering with sheeting, or drying-environment control, so it does not substantiate completion of this task.

tasks.label: Apply weatherproof, decorative coverings to exterior surfaces of buildings, such as by troweling or spraying on coats of stucco.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New residential build (tract or custom home): apply scratch and brown coats of cement stucco over metal lath on exterior walls from ground and scaffolding — pump/spray or hand-trowel application, scratch/rake the first coat, rod and float the brown coat true and plumb, cut in around windows, doors, weep screed and casing beads; outdoor weather and cure timing govern the work.

Finish/color coat on residential or light-commercial exteriors: apply ~1/8 in. acrylic or cement finish over cured brown coat by hopper-spray and/or trowel, working wall-to-corner without cold joints to a uniform texture (sand float, lace, dash, skip-trowel) and consistent color across the elevation.

Multi-story commercial EIFS / one-coat system from scaffold or swing stage: adhere/prepare insulation board, trowel base coat and embed fiberglass reinforcing mesh with proper laps and back-wrapping, then apply textured finish coat at height on a building under construction.

Repair and patch of existing exterior stucco on occupied homes/buildings: cut out cracked or damaged areas, re-lath and patch base coats, then blend the patch into surrounding wall matching the existing texture and color; access around landscaping, utilities and occupants.

Decorative and architectural detail work: coat and shape foam trim, bands, quoins, arches, columns, window surrounds and sills; hand-trowel profiles, sharp corners and returns as part of the exterior stucco finish.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7 is a commercially deployed, fully autonomous mobile robot that sprays plaster/coatings and finishes walls at active construction sites, having covered over 1 million sq ft in Europe before its US launch.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior wall plastering/coating. Transfer: the same physical act — machine-controlled spray deposition of a wet wall coating followed by a smoothing pass on a vertical planar surface — which is the core of applying a stucco coat when the wall is presented flat to the machine. It does not cover exterior cement stucco over lath, work at height, or texture/color matching.

sources.system: MSP-robot (mortar spraying and plastering integrated robot)
sources.developer: Wang, Xie et al. (published in Automation in Construction)
sources.title: Mortar spraying and plastering integrated robot for wall construction - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A mortar spraying and plastering integrated ... (MSP-robot) autonomously sprayed and screed-leveled plastering mortar on walls in an on-site experiment, with no flakes or voids and quality meeting acceptance criteria.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine plastering of interior walls with gypsum plastering mortar. Transfer: spraying a mortar coat and compacting/leveling it with a scraper to a flat, void-free plane is the same operation as applying and rodding a stucco base coat; the demonstration was on prepared flat interior wall faces, not exterior lath or textured finishes.

sources.system: Robotic Plaster Spraying (RPS), In situ Fabricator mobile robot
sources.title: Robotic on-site adaptive thin-layer printing: Challenges and workflow for design and fabrication of bespoke cementitious plasterwork at full architectural scale (ResearchGate)
sources.claim: ETH Zurich demonstrated Robotic Plaster Spraying at 1:1 architectural scale, with a mobile robot spraying cementitious base-coat plaster in vertical layers to create bespoke decorative plasterwork on walls of an existing building.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic deposition of cementitious base-coat plaster to form decorative wall surfaces. Transfer: shows a robot can spray true cement-based plaster onto a full-scale vertical wall and shape its surface, the material class used in stucco; it is a research demonstration (~24 h per wall) and does not deliver a code-compliant multi-coat exterior stucco assembly.

sources.system: Exterior wall spraying robots (incl. Bright Dream Robotics products) and an HCI gesture-controlled spraying robot prototype
sources.developer: Bright Dream Robotics; authors of Scientific Reports study
sources.title: Control technology research of building wall spraying robot | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: Exterior wall spraying robots developed in China require two to three months of on-site deployment and repeated debugging per building, and cannot hold construction quality in wind, rain or snow or around balconies and window frames.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on point (exterior building-wall spray coating); cited as negative evidence that on-site exterior application at E2/E3 is not achieved autonomously at worker quality, and that the fielded approach is human-in-the-loop control.

sources.title: Oshkosh acquires core technology developed by Canvas - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Canvas's 1200CX is a commercially deployed, worker-controlled construction robot that sprays joint compound on walls and sands to a Level 5 finish; Oshkosh/JLG acquired the technology in January 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior drywall coating/finishing. Context only — the source describes the machine as worker-controlled, so autonomy is not established and it is not used to support any positive judgment.

sources.system: AutoJet E1850+ automated spray coating system on a fiber-cement siding line
sources.title: Fiber-Cement siding manufacturer reduces resin coating consumption with automated spray system | Spraying Systems Europe
sources.claim: A fiber-cement siding manufacturer applies a coating to siding boards with an automated, controller-driven spray header as the boards are conveyed past it on the production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory coating of exterior cladding. Transfer: in the E1 counterfactual the wall surface is presented to the machine on a conveyor/fixture, and machine-controlled spray heads already apply exterior-grade coatings to cladding at production quality — the same deposition step as a sprayed stucco finish coat, though on flat boards rather than a whole building elevation.

tasks.label: Determine materials needed to complete the job and place orders accordingly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Apply insulation to building exteriors by installing prefabricated insulation systems over existing walls or by covering the outer wall with insulation board, reinforcing mesh, and a base coat.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial/institutional construction (school, mid-rise office, retail, multifamily): crew installs EIFS over sheathing or CMU on large elevations from scaffolding, mast climbers or boom lifts - adhesive/mechanically fastened EPS board, rasping, back-wrapped mesh at openings, corner beads and expansion joints, then trowel- or spray-applied base coat with embedded reinforcing mesh; outdoor, weather-dependent, other trades working around.

New single-family or small multifamily residential: foam board plus mesh and base coat (EIFS or one-coat stucco over foam) applied over wood-frame sheathing from ladders/pump jacks/light scaffold; many windows, doors, soffits, bump-outs and trim bands requiring cut-and-fit board and hand mesh wrapping.

Energy retrofit / re-clad of an existing occupied building: substrate prep and leveling over out-of-plane, irregular masonry or old stucco, working around existing windows, pipes, vents, meters, signage and occupants; boards adhered/fastened, mesh and base coat applied to a wall that was never built plumb.

Installation of prefabricated exterior insulation panel systems (factory-made EIFS/insulated panels) over new or existing walls: panels hoisted and set by crane, aligned and fastened to the structure, then field joint treatment - insulation strips, mesh and base coat over joints and returns.

Repair/patch of damaged EIFS on an existing building: cut out and remove damaged insulation board section, fit and adhere replacement board, lap new reinforcing mesh into surrounding mesh, apply base coat and feather/blend into the existing wall, often on a small area reached from a ladder or lift.

sources.title: Video | Robot decorator makes its debut - Construction Management
sources.claim: Okibo's autonomous mobile robot arm plasters and paints interior walls on construction sites, navigating and scanning without prior information; it is limited to interior finishing coats and does not install insulation board or reinforcing mesh.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine application of a plaster coat to a wall. It shows autonomous coating is feasible, but only indoors on interior substrates; it performs none of the board-setting, mesh-embedding or exterior detail work this task requires, so it cannot substantiate completion.

sources.developer: Oak Ridge National Laboratory with industry partners
sources.title: ORNL demonstrates affordable, energy efficient, low-carbon building technologies on National Mall during HUD Innovation Housing Showcase
sources.claim: ORNL and partners demonstrated an autonomous spray foam robot that installs foam insulation into walls; it applies cavity spray foam, not exterior insulation board with mesh and base coat.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of insulation to a building. Transfer fails here: it sprays foam into open cavities rather than adhering rigid boards to a finished exterior and embedding mesh in a base coat, and it was shown as an exhibition demonstration.

sources.developer: Tecnalia / Fraunhofer IPA and H2020 Hephaestus consortium
sources.title: Cable-driven parallel robot for curtain wall module installation - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: The Hephaestus cable-driven parallel robot installed prefabricated curtain wall modules on two demonstration buildings with 4-23 mm placement accuracy; a research demonstrator, not a deployed system, and it performs no coating or mesh work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic placement of prefabricated facade modules onto a building, closest to installing prefabricated insulation systems over existing walls. It remains a project demonstrator with unclear autonomy and no field joint insulation, mesh or base coat capability.

sources.system: Adaptive robotic facade platform for refurbishment panel installation
sources.title: Adaptive robotic platform for the installation of refurbishment panels | Construction Robotics
sources.claim: RWTH Aachen's crane-lifted robotic facade platform placed ventilated rain-screen refurbishment panels in indoor and outdoor tests as a prototype; it places cladding panels only and was not shown completing an insulation, mesh and base coat system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic installation of prefabricated exterior refurbishment panels on existing buildings. Transfer is incomplete: a prototype panel-placing arm does not adhere insulation board, wrap mesh or apply base coat, and no production deployment is reported.

sources.title: Ushering in the Future of Building Retrofits | Grid Modernization | NREL
sources.claim: wall-EIFS, a robotically applied sprayable exterior insulation and finish system, was a US DOE E-ROBOT Prize Phase 1 concept/design award from the University of Arizona; no built, autonomous field system is documented.
sources.transferJustification: Directly targets this task, but the source describes a Phase 1 prize concept and design rather than a demonstrated machine; autonomy and completion cannot be established, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.developer: University of Stuttgart / TUM (Iturralde et al.)
sources.title: Integrated workflow for a semi-automated and robotic facade renovation (Frontiers in Built Environment)
sources.claim: The 2025 state of the art in robotic facade renovation is a semi-automated workflow in which robotic assembly helps manufacture prefabricated facade modules; on-building installation and coating remain manual or human-assisted.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic prefabrication of exterior facade/insulation modules, which is what an E1 counterfactual for this task would require. It reports a semi-automated research workflow for module manufacturing, not a cell that adheres insulation board, embeds mesh and applies a base coat at production quality.

tasks.label: Spray acoustic materials or texture finish over walls or ceilings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Exterior stucco/EIFS finish coat sprayed onto a building exterior (single-family home, apartment block, or commercial building): mixer and rotor-stator pump on the ground, hose run to a spray gun, applicator works from the ground, ladders, scaffold or a lift, spraying dash/lace/acrylic textured finish over the brown coat; wind, sun and temperature affect set, a wet edge must be kept across each elevation, and windows, trim and adjoining surfaces are masked.

Interior texture or finish-coat spray over drywall/base-coat walls and ceilings in new multifamily and commercial interiors (apartment units and corridors, offices, schools, hotels) on an active jobsite: flat floors, elevator or hoist access, standard room heights, other trades working nearby, output sprayed uniformly and then knocked down or left as sprayed before paint.

Interior texture spray in new single-family houses under construction: two-story layouts with stairs, small bedrooms and closets, vaulted ceilings, garages, unfinished floors littered with material, no elevator, hose dragged from a rig parked in the driveway.

Spray-applied acoustic/insulating material over ceilings, metal decks and soffits in a commercial building shell (acoustical plaster, cellulose or mineral-fiber acoustic spray) applied overhead to a specified thickness and density, from lifts or scaffold, in an unfinished, dusty building.

Patch and re-texture repair in an occupied home or tenant space: mask furniture and floors, spray a small area of ceiling or wall after a leak or drywall repair, feather and blend the new texture to match the existing pattern (knockdown, orange peel, popcorn, skip trowel), then clean up.

Texture/plaster finish spray over tall walls and high ceilings in large interior spaces (atriums, lobbies, gyms, warehouses) on a new-construction site, worked from scissor or boom lifts at 15-25 ft, with large uninterrupted surfaces that must be sprayed without lap marks.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7 is a fully autonomous, AI-guided robot that plasters, sprays paint and finishes drywall on walls and ceilings, and is in commercial use on active interior construction sites in Europe and the US, covering over 1 million sq ft.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic spray application of plaster and paint to interior walls and ceilings. Transfer to texture spraying is direct - same surfaces (walls/ceilings), same equipment class (pumped coating through a spray gun on a robot arm), same jobsite environment; texture finish is a coarser variant of the sprayed plaster/finish coat the robot already applies.

sources.title: Video | Robot decorator makes its debut - Construction Management
sources.claim: The Okibo robot maps rooms with 3D scanning without prior information, needs no manual programming and minimal human intervention, and its arm has floor-to-ceiling reach for plastering or painting interiors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous spray plastering of interior walls and ceilings. Same objects and precision class as spraying a texture finish; establishes that the mapping, path planning and spraying run without step-by-step human control.

sources.title: Okibo launches EG7+ autonomous robot for painting and finishing - Engineering.com
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7+ extends to 24 ft, allowing autonomous spraying, painting and Level 4 finishing of high walls with no site preparation or external references.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-reach robotic spray finishing of walls in construction. Same spraying operation and reach envelope needed for tall walls and high ceilings receiving texture finish.

sources.title: Canvas, World's First Robotic Drywall Finishing Company, Launches the 1200CX | Business Wire
sources.claim: Canvas's 1200CX drywall finishing robot spray-applies all joint compound onto walls in one step on real jobsites, including multifamily and tower projects, but is described as worker-operated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic spray application of joint compound over whole wall surfaces (Level 5) on construction sites; corroborates that machines spray wall/ceiling coatings to accepted finish quality in multifamily and commercial interiors, though autonomy is not established from this source.

sources.title: Obayashi Develops a New Fireproof Coating Spray Robot for Wider Use on Construction Sites
sources.claim: Obayashi's second-generation fireproof coating spray robot autonomously moves around construction sites and sprays semi-dry rockwool onto steel beams, matching a skilled sprayer's daily output and meeting thickness and density standards; it was working on Tokyo sites from November 2023.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: overhead spray application of semi-dry mineral-wool material to a specified thickness on building structure. Spray-applied acoustic material uses the same fibrous/cementitious spray equipment, the same overhead ceiling/deck surfaces and the same thickness-uniformity criterion, in the same unfinished-building environment.

sources.title: Crafting plaster through continuous mobile robotic fabrication on-site | Construction Robotics
sources.claim: ETH Zurich researchers mounted a plastering spray gun fed by a standard PFT G4 mortar pump on a 6-DoF robotic arm and sprayed cementitious plaster onto target surfaces along computed, feedback-adapted trajectories in a fixed fabrication setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic spraying of cementitious plaster onto a presented surface in a stationary cell with a standard construction mixing pump and spray gun. Same material family and equipment as stucco/texture finish, demonstrating the spray operation when the work is fixtured and presented to the machine.

sources.developer: DaFang AI / Hong Kong Housing Authority
sources.title: news.gov.hk - Robot boosts construction safety
sources.claim: The Hong Kong Housing Authority deployed an indoor multifunctional construction robot on four public housing projects to perform skim coating, grinding and ... of walls and ceilings; it laser-scans and plans its path with AI vision but the operator controls it remotely from ground level.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine application of skim coat/paint to residential high-rise walls and ceilings on live housing construction sites; corroborates that residential interior coating work is being done by machines, though remote operator control means it cannot by itself establish autonomy.

tasks.label: Install guide wires on exterior surfaces of buildings to indicate thickness of plaster or stucco and nail wire mesh, lath, or similar materials to the outside surface to hold stucco in place.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New single-family / townhome three-coat stucco job: over wood-sheathed exterior walls, staple two layers of building paper and self-furred wire lath, cut and fit around windows, doors and penetrations, nail weep screed, casing beads and corner aid, and string taut ground/guide wires at corners and long runs to set coat thickness; work from ladders, planks and low scaffold on an active jobsite with debris, weather and other trades present.

Multifamily or commercial exterior over metal studs and gypsum sheathing: hang expanded metal lath in overlapping sheets tied/screwed to framing, install control and expansion joint accessories and casing beads, plumb and set screeds and guide wires over multi-story elevations from frame scaffold or swing stage, with wind, height and irregular building geometry.

Repair / re-stucco of an existing occupied building: cut back damaged stucco, patch in new paper and lath tying into existing lath and accessories around windows, chimneys and utility penetrations, match the existing plane using guide wires or spot screeds on out-of-plumb, weathered walls with landscaping, fences and site clutter.

Detail and overhead areas: lathing soffits and eave undersides, arched openings, columns, curved bands and foam trim; bending and cutting lath to curves, working overhead and in tight confined spaces, setting guide wires/screeds on non-planar surfaces.

Off-site panel shop work: prefabricated stucco/EIFS wall panels lying flat on fabrication tables in a controlled fabrication facility; worker rolls out paper and stucco netting or metal lath, staples it to the framed panel, cuts openings and attaches screeds/casing beads before the panel is shipped to site.

tasks.label: Position and secure steel bars, rods, cables, or mesh in concrete forms, using fasteners, rod-bending machines, blowtorches, or hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bridge deck / highway structure flatwork: on an open highway construction site, place top and bottom mats of #4-#8 bars on chairs across a deck between edge forms or screed rails, set spacing per plan, lap and tie intersections to DOT specification, in weather, on an irregular walking surface.

Building foundations and slab-on-grade at a commercial/industrial jobsite: footings, grade beams, pile caps and mat slabs; carry, cut, bend and place bars and welded wire mesh over vapor barrier or in trenches, dodge embeds, dowels, anchor bolts and plumbing penetrations, tie by hand, on muddy or uneven ground.

Vertical elements cast in place: columns, shear walls, retaining walls, bridge piers and abutments; hoist and stand vertical bars, splice to dowels, wrap and tie ties/hoops or horizontal curtains inside or against formwork, often working at height from scaffold or a lift.

Elevated slabs and decks in buildings and parking structures, including post-tensioned slabs: place bars over metal deck or shored formwork at height, weave around PT tendons, MEP sleeves, drops and openings, support on chairs, tie, in a congested, changing overhead-work area.

Shop or laydown-yard prefabrication: assemble pile/column cages, wall mats and mesh panels on jigs or the yard floor from bent bars, tie or weld them, then rig the finished assembly into the form or mould.

Small/light jobs: residential slabs, driveways, sidewalks, curbs, small footings and equipment pads; roll out or cut welded wire mesh and a few bars in wood forms, chair and tie with hand tools, sometimes single-handed in tight access.

instances.label: Active jobsite field trimming: on a bridge deck, footing, wall or slab, the rodbuster shortens bars to fit actual field conditions — trimming dowels, cutting bars around blockouts, embeds and congested laps — with a portable hydraulic bar cutter, gas cutoff saw or hand shears, on uneven ground or standing on a rebar mat, in weather and around other trades.

Jobsite cut station in a laydown area: stock bars from a delivered bundle are rolled onto stands or a bench and batch-cut into required lengths with a bench-mounted hydraulic bar cutter or abrasive chop saw, then bundled and tagged for the placing crew.

Rebar fabrication shop or fabricator's yard: mill-length stock bars (or coil) are cut to the lengths on a bar list using a shear line, hydraulic shear or band saw, then counted, tagged by mark number and bundled for shipment; high volume, repetitive, standard bar sizes #3-#11.

Cutting rebar already embedded in or protruding from hardened concrete: torching off dowels flush, removing misplaced or damaged bars during rework, demolition or repair, with an oxy-acetylene torch or grinder, in place, often at height, in a trench or against formwork.

Cutting welded wire mesh and light rod to fit: trimming mesh sheets around penetrations, columns and slab edges, and cutting short pieces, chairs and tie bars with hand shears or a hacksaw, frequently in congested or confined spots on the deck.

tasks.label: Bend steel rods with hand tools or rod-bending machines and weld them with arc-welding equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field bending in place: on a building deck, footing, wall or bridge deck, the rodbuster bends #3–#6 dowels, hooks and bent-up bars with a hickey bar/manual hand bender so bars clear forms, embeds and conflicts — kneeling in a congested tied mat, outdoors, bars already fixed at one end, shapes judged against drawings and inspector tolerances.

On-site bending station: in the jobsite laydown yard the worker runs a portable electric/hydraulic rod-bending machine, hand-loading straight stock and bending hooks, stirrups, offsets and radius bars per the bar list, then bundling and tagging the output; uneven ground, mud, weather, changing pile locations.

Fabrication shop bending: in a rebar fab shop or precast plant bending area, the worker operates a rod-bending machine (bar bender/stirrup bender) to produce bent shapes to the bar list from racked stock, checking angles and hook dimensions and stacking finished shapes on carts.

Field arc welding: using a stick/engine-drive welder on the jobsite, the worker tack-welds rebar assemblies and column/pier cages, welds bars to embed plates or structural steel, and makes flare-V or lap splice welds on weldable (A706) bar per AWS D1.4 — out of position, in trenches or on decks, with wind, rain and congested access.

Shop/plant welded assemblies: in a fab shop or precast plant, rebar mats, beam/column cages, pile cages and special assemblies are laid out on jig tables and arc-welded at intersections and splices to hold geometry before shipping or casting.

roles.title: Roofers
roles.description: Cover roofs of structures with shingles, slate, asphalt, aluminum, wood, or related materials. May spray roofs, sidings, and walls with material to bind, seal, insulate, or soundproof sections of structures.

tasks.label: Inspect problem roofs to determine the best repair procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential steep-slope shingle roof, active leak call: homeowner reports a ceiling stain; roofer ladders up, walks the roof, lifts and pries shingles, inspects valleys, pipe boots, chimney/skylight flashing, checks the attic underside for wet sheathing and daylight, sometimes runs a hose test, and probes decking for softness to decide the repair method.

Residential hail/wind storm-damage assessment for an insurance claim or repair scope: document damage on every roof facet, count and mark impacts, check ridge caps, vents, gutters and soft metals, measure facets, and determine repair vs. full replacement scope in a documented report.

Residential roof with obvious localized exterior damage (blown-off or creased shingles, cracked pipe boot, lifted step or drip-edge flashing, storm debris impact): inspect and scope the specific repair and materials needed.

Aging residential or small-commercial roof, general condition assessment for a repair-or-replace recommendation: walk the roof feeling for spongy decking, count existing layers, check nail pops, granule loss, sealant and ventilation, and inspect the attic before recommending a repair procedure.

Commercial low-slope membrane/built-up roof on a warehouse, school or similar facility: survey ponding, blisters, open seams, failed penetration details and hidden saturated insulation across a large roof area, and determine patch, recoat, section-replace or full-replacement scope.

sources.transferJustification: Shows the aerial inspection output is accepted in place of an on-roof inspection when scoping storm repairs.

tasks.label: Waterproof or damp-proof walls, floors, roofs, foundations, or basements by painting or spraying surfaces with waterproof coatings or by attaching waterproofing membranes to surfaces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Restoration/recoat of an existing low-slope commercial or industrial roof: after cleaning and priming, spray or roll a silicone/acrylic elastomeric waterproof coating at a specified mil thickness across the field, brushing and reinforcing around HVAC curbs, drains, pipe penetrations, seams and edge metal, outdoors with wind, heat and dew constraints.

Attaching waterproofing membrane to a roof deck (new construction or tear-off re-roof): loading and rolling out self-adhered underlayment, modified bitumen or single-ply TPO/PVC, aligning laps, adhering or mechanically fastening, hot-air welding or torching seams, and hand-detailing flashings at parapets, curbs and penetrations.

Below-grade exterior foundation damp-proofing/waterproofing on a new construction site: spraying or rolling asphalt emulsion or rubberized coating over green concrete foundation walls from inside a muddy excavation, plus sheet membrane at corners/footings, cants and drainage board, coordinating with the backfill schedule.

Interior damp-proofing of an existing basement or crawlspace in an occupied home: patching cracks and tie holes, then brushing, rolling or spraying cementitious/elastomeric waterproof coating onto walls and floor slab in a confined, cluttered, low-headroom space reached by stairs or a hatch.

Waterproofing a deck, balcony, plaza deck, planter or below-tile floor with liquid-applied membrane: priming, embedding reinforcing fabric at corners, drains and terminations, then applying two coats to spec and flood-testing.
Applying elastomeric damp-proof or waterproof coating to above-grade exterior walls or parapets from a boom lift, swing stage or scaffold, cutting in at windows, copings and joints.

sources.title: Duerr sells 2,000th sealing robot: New robot model optimizes sealing application in tight spaces
sources.claim: Duerr's sealing robots apply PVC underbody protection, sill coating and fine seam sealing fully automatically to car bodies fixtured in enclosed paint-shop cells; more than 2,000 such robots had been sold by 2016 and fully automatic sealing is established industry practice.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of waterproof/anti-corrosion sealant and protective coating. The physical act matches this task's spraying of waterproof coatings - depositing a liquid film of controlled thickness over a surface including seams and edges - on a workpiece fixtured and presented to the machine, which is exactly the E1 counterfactual.

It is the closest rooftop system, but it nails discrete shingles at pilot stage and does not handle rolled membrane, adhesives, hot-air seam welding or coating spray, so it does not substantiate this task in the field.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: spraying coatings onto building and structure exteriors. Cited as a negative for the exterior-wall instance because flight is pilot-commanded (semi-autonomous assistance only), which the rating rules treat as teleoperation.

sources.title: Q-Bot / Minimum fuss, maximum insulation - Ashden
sources.claim: Q-Bot's underfloor robot sprays polyurethane insulation onto the underside of floors in occupied homes as a commercial service, but the machine is remote-controlled by an operator using a video feed and a gamepad.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic spray application of a protective/insulating layer to floors and building fabric in a confined domestic void - the closest analogue to basement/crawlspace damp-proofing. Cited as a negative because it is remotely driven throughout.

sources.title: Drywall Finishing Robots Accelerate Construction Schedules - Tech Briefs
sources.claim: Canvas robots autonomously spray and sand drywall compound on walls and ... on US commercial construction sites, delivering Level 4 and Level 5 ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous spray application of a wet coating to interior wall and ceiling surfaces on a jobsite. It shows in-situ coating autonomy is limited to open, level, walk-in interiors, not roofs, excavations or crawlspaces.

tasks.label: Cover exposed nailheads with roofing cement or caulking to prevent water leakage or rust.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Steep-slope residential asphalt shingle roof (new or replacement): after nailing ridge/hip caps, the last course, valley metal and step/counter-flashing at chimneys, walls and vent pipes, the roofer dabs roofing cement over the several dozen fasteners left exposed, working on foot on a 4/12–10/12 pitch, often in heat, with the roof surface littered with granules and debris.

Exposed-fastener metal roofing (agricultural, light commercial, residential panels): the roofer places a controlled dab of butyl/urethane sealant on screw or nail heads across panel fields, ridge caps and trim — often hundreds of fasteners on a restoration or re-screw job — on slick, hot, sometimes oil-canned panels.

Low-slope commercial roof (mod-bit, BUR or mechanically fastened single-ply) on an occupied building: troweling roofing cement over exposed nails and fastener heads at base flashing, gravel stop/drip edge, curb and pipe penetrations, moving around HVAC units, conduit and ponded areas.

Service/repair call on an existing weathered roof: locating backed-out or exposed nails causing leaks or rust streaks (often at ridge, flashing, or a previous patch), cleaning the spot and sealing each with cement or caulk; a handful of scattered locations reached from a ladder or by walking an aged, brittle roof.

Specialty or very steep roof (slate, tile, wood shake, or pitch above 12/12 requiring roof jacks, staging or fall-arrest): sealing exposed fasteners at ridge, hips and flashing, with care not to crack or stain the covering, on an irregular, cut-up roof plane.

sources.system: Kawasaki RS005N / RS010L / RS080N vision-guided assembly and sealant cell (Systematix integration)
sources.title: One-of-a-Kind Vision-Guided Assembly Cell | Industrial Robots by Kawasaki Robotics
sources.claim: A deployed multi-robot, 3D-vision-guided aerospace assembly cell includes a Kawasaki RS005N robot that autonomously applies sealant to a fastener/nutplate assembly for corrosion resistance, with machine-vision verification before and after application — the fixtured-cell equivalent of dabbing sealant on a fastener head.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sealant application over/around rivet-and-nutplate fasteners. It transfers to covering nailheads because the object (a driven metal fastener head on a panel), the material (viscous sealant), and the required accuracy (a controlled deposit fully covering the head, vision-verified) match or exceed roofing requirements; only the environment differs.

sources.system: Broetje-Automation automated sealing system (SOUL OLPS programming, digital twin)
sources.title: Automated sealing of aircraft components reaches industrial maturity
sources.claim: Broetje-Automation's automated aircraft sealing system reached industrial maturity and can run autonomously inside a robotic cell, applying difficult, highly viscous sealants at precise locations on complex components without contaminating surrounding surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated application of viscous sealant to aircraft structures in a fixtured cell. Transfers because roofing cement/caulk over a nailhead is a coarser version of the same deposit-on-a-known-point operation, with far looser tolerance than aerospace sealing.

sources.title: Broetje-Automation presents automated sealer for aircraft components. | CompositesWorld
sources.claim: The same Broetje sealing product line explicitly covers 'cap sealing' — sealing of rivet heads — i.e., robotic deposition of a sealant cap over an installed fastener head, the industrial analogue of covering exposed nailheads.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic cap sealing of rivet heads. Directly comparable to covering exposed nailheads with cement — same geometry (dome of sealant over a protruding fastener head), same purpose (moisture/corrosion protection), tighter precision.

sources.title: RBR50 Spotlight: Renovate Robotics puts Rufus to work on roofs - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The only on-roof construction robot identified, Renovate Robotics' Rufus, is a winch/cable-suspended machine that autonomously places and nails asphalt shingles on real roofs; no source describes it or any other rooftop robot applying roofing cement or caulk to exposed nailheads at flashings, ridges or penetrations.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the E3 judgment, not to support it: Rufus performs shingle placement and nailing along a gantry-like raster path and is not shown detecting exposed fasteners or dispensing roofing cement at flashings, ridge caps and penetrations, so it does not substantiate this task on roofs.

sources.title: Apellix Spray Painting Drone Goes to Work in the Field for State DOTs, Federal Contractors, and Commercial Coating Firms
sources.claim: Aerial coating robots working at height on real structures are semi-autonomous spray systems that hold standoff, perpendicularity and travel speed for area coating; they are not shown making contact-accurate, per-fastener sealant deposits.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the E3/E2 judgment: broad-area coating at height with a piloted, semi-autonomous drone does not substantiate locating individual exposed nailheads and placing a controlled dab of viscous roofing cement on each.

tasks.label: Apply reflective roof coatings, such as special paints or single-ply roofing sheets, to existing roofs to reduce solar heat absorption.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large commercial/industrial low-slope roof (warehouse, big-box store, school), 20,000–100,000 sq ft: after power-washing and repairs, roofer spray- or roller-applies two coats of reflective acrylic/silicone coating to specified mil thickness, working around HVAC curbs, drains, skylights, and vents, in variable wind, sun, and temperature.

Small low-slope roof recoat (small shop, apartment building, mobile home, porch or RV roof), 500–5,000 sq ft: reflective elastomeric coating applied by brush, roller, and small sprayer; ladder access, cluttered surface, many edges, parapets and penetrations.

Prep and detail portion of a coating job: cleaning and priming, caulking, and brushing coating while embedding polyester reinforcing fabric over seams, flashings, drain bowls, pipe boots and curbs before/around the field coat.

Applying reflective single-ply sheets (white TPO/PVC membrane) over an existing roof: laying out and unrolling heavy rolls, mechanically fastening or adhering, hot-air welding seams (often with a self-propelled seam welder), then flashing penetrations and perimeters.

Reflective coating of a sloped or standing-seam metal roof (agricultural, industrial, church): rust and fastener prep, then airless spray of reflective coating on pitch with fall protection or from a lift.

sources.system: RTSS robotic polyurea spray system (FANUC M-710iC/10L + Graco HFR)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic spray application of an elastomeric/protective liquid coating (polyurea, the same chemistry family as roof coatings) at controlled film thickness. At E1 the roof surface arrives as a fixtured panel presented to the cell, which is exactly the material, precision and presentation this system handles.

sources.system: FANUC Paint Series robots (P-250iB, P-40, CRX-10iA/L Paint)

Reflective roof coating is a liquid coating applied to a specified wet-mil thickness; in an E1 presentation (panel fixtured, conveyed to the robot) the operation is the same.

sources.system: SprayWorks Spraybot / Coaterbot roof spray applicator
sources.title: Automated Machine Applicators | Perfect Tool for Roofing, Decking and More | SprayWorks Equipment
sources.claim: Machines that actually apply roof coatings and spray foam on real commercial roofs are operator-guided walk-behind applicators, not autonomous robots: the worker sets the control box and steers the machine across the roof.

sources.title: RBR50 Spotlight: Renovate Robotics puts Rufus to work on roofs - The Robot Report
sources.claim: An autonomous cable-driven robot traverses existing residential roofs and places and fastens asphalt shingles, showing rooftop autonomy for a different roofing task (material placement and nailing), not coating application.

tasks.label: Remove snow, water, or debris from roofs prior to applying roofing materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Steep-slope residential re-roof: after tear-off, the roofer sweeps/blows sawdust, shingle granules, old nails, wood scraps and leaves off the exposed plywood/OSB deck (4:12–10:12 pitch, 15–30 ft up, no fixed anchor points, landscaping and neighbors below) so underlayment can be laid flat the same day.

Low-slope commercial/industrial roof: crew clears dust, insulation scraps, gravel, fastener offcuts and windblown litter from a large flat deck or insulation board with brooms, backpack blowers and shop vacs, working around HVAC curbs, drains, parapets and pipe penetrations, before membrane or adhesive is applied.

Mid-job water removal: overnight rain or a wash-down leaves ponded water and damp substrate; the roofer squeegees, mops or wet-vacs the low spots, pulls tarps, and lets/forces the deck dry to an acceptable moisture level before priming or setting membrane.

Winter start-up: several inches of snow, sleet or ice sit on the deck or on the area to be worked; the roofer shovels, brushes and scrapes snow and ice off the work area and throws it clear of the building before any roofing material goes down.

Detail clearing by hand: picking debris, leaves, old fasteners and torn felt out of valleys, gutters, crickets, and tight areas around chimneys, skylights and pipe boots, and bagging or dropping the debris to a ground container.

sources.system: Dürr EcoClean / cleaning robots (BYD Europe plant)
sources.title: Dürr equips first BYD plant in Europe with sustainable painting technology
sources.claim: Dürr supplies robotic cleaning stations that remove dust and dirt ... vehicle bodies immediately before coating is applied, as standard equipment in new commercial paint shops.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: substrate cleaning immediately prior to applying a coating. Functionally identical to clearing loose debris off a deck before underlayment/membrane — remove loose particulate to a standard that lets the applied layer bond — but with the workpiece conveyed to the machine, i.e. an E1 presentation.

sources.system: Dürr EcoRS Clean F cleaning robots
sources.title: 18,000th Dürr robot will paint vehicles in Ingolstadt
sources.claim: Robot cleaning cells using feather rollers are installed in production paint lines (Audi Ingolstadt top-coat line) to clean car bodies as part of the unattended production sequence.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated removal of loose debris from a surface prior to material application, in a purpose-built line. Same operation and far tighter cleanliness tolerance than a roof deck requires.

sources.system: Taikisha / Encore blow-off systems (machine and robot-mounted)
sources.title: Automation & Robots | Taikisha USA, Inc.

New commercial construction, detail and tapered work: laying out and placing tapered polyiso packages, crickets and saddles per shop drawing, cutting boards to fit around roof drains, curbs, pipe penetrations and perimeter blocking, and sealing the vapor barrier at those details.

Small new-build low-slope roof (small commercial building, addition, or flat deck over new framing): install vapor barrier and one or two layers of insulation on a small, newly built deck with limited access; materials hoisted by ladder or small hoist.

Small existing flat roofs: residential flat/low-slope decks, porch and addition roofs, small older commercial buildings. Irregular shapes, many penetrations, tight access, no staging area; vapor barrier and insulation cut and fitted by hand over an old deck of uncertain condition.

tasks.label: Install, repair, or replace single-ply roofing systems, using waterproof sheet materials such as modified plastics, elastomeric, or other asphaltic compositions.

Open rooftop, wind, heat, changing weather.

Tear-off and replacement on an occupied commercial building: removing wet/failed membrane and insulation, working around HVAC curbs, ducts, drains, skylights, gas lines, conduit and roof hatches; sequencing dry-in each day so the occupied building is watertight overnight.

Detail and flashing work on a single-ply system: cutting and fitting membrane at parapets, curbs, corners, pipe penetrations and drains; hand-welding target patches, pipe boots and inside/outside corners; installing termination bars, sealant and edge metal; probe-testing each detail.

Leak repair or partial replacement on an existing single-ply roof: locating the breach on a dirty, weathered membrane, cleaning and priming, cutting a patch, hand- or machine-welding it, re-securing loose seams or flashings, verifying the repair holds.

Small residential or light-commercial low-slope job: EPDM/TPO or self-adhered modified-bitumen sheet over a porch, garage, dormer or addition deck, or a mobile-home roof; ladder access, tight irregular deck, cut-and-fit around walls, vents and edge metal.

Small jobs and repairs: patching underlayment on a partial tear-off, garage/shed/porch roofs, dormer sections, tying new felt into existing roofing and flashings on an occupied building with tight access.

tasks.label: Set up scaffolding to provide safe access to roofs.

instances.label: Residential steep-slope re-roof: crew erects frame/system scaffold or ladder-jack staging along one or two elevations of an occupied house, working on uneven lawn/soil with landscaping, decks, AC condensers and overhead service drops; base plates leveled with mud sills and screw jacks, planks and guardrails fitted, tied to the fascia/wall.

Small-scale access setup for a short residential job (repair, chimney flashing, gutter/eave work): a rolling scaffold tower or pump-jack/ladder-jack staging set at the eave, moved several times during the day as the work progresses around the building.

Commercial/institutional low-slope re-roof or new build on an active construction site: tube-and-clamp or system scaffold plus a stair tower erected from a paved or graded lot to a 20-40 ft parapet, with debris netting and a loading bay, amid other trades, stored materials and vehicle traffic.

Re-roof at an occupied, institution-controlled facility (school, plant, warehouse, hospital wing): scaffold/stair tower and hoist tower erected on a paved, fenced, standard-layout property with controlled access, marked lay-down area and predictable ground conditions.

Difficult/complex access: tight urban infill or historic building requiring sidewalk shed and overhead protection, cantilevered or hillside setups on sloped terrain, tie-ins around bay windows and balconies, often in wind, cold or wet conditions.

tasks.label: Cement or nail flashing strips of metal or shingle over joints to make them watertight.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Step flashing at a roof-to-wall or dormer intersection on a residential steep-slope asphalt-shingle roof: bending/placing individual L-shaped metal pieces, interleaving one with each shingle course, nailing them to the deck, and dabbing roof cement at laps and terminations. Work is done kneeling on a 4:12-9:12 pitch, outdoors, with varying wall siding and course layout.

Flashing a roof penetration (plumbing vent stack, exhaust or B-vent) on a residential shingle roof: slipping the boot/collar flange over the pipe onto the underlying course, nailing the flange, weaving the next shingle courses over the top half, and sealing nail heads and the collar with roof cement.

Valley flashing on a residential roof: rolling out and nailing metal W-valley or valley membrane along the intersection of two roof planes, lapping successive pieces, then trimming/cementing shingle edges (closed-cut valley) so the joint sheds water.

Chimney or skylight flashing: base, apron and step flashing plus counterflashing let into a saw-cut reglet or mortar joint (or surface-mounted), custom-bent corners, lead wedges/anchors, and sealant or roof cement to close the joint against the masonry or curb.

Low-slope commercial roof: metal edge/drip flashing, parapet coping and curb flashing over membrane laps and joints — fastening the metal to the nailer, lapping and cover-plating joints, and mastic/sealant or membrane target patches to make each joint watertight, on an occupied building's roof deck.

Leak-driven repair on an existing roof: locating the failing joint, cutting out or lifting deteriorated shingles and old flashing, cleaning off cracked mastic, fitting a replacement metal or shingle flashing piece into the existing courses, nailing and re-cementing it, often on an aged, brittle or debris-covered roof.

instances.label: Residential re-roof of an occupied single-family home: after tear-off, roofers sweep the deck, replace bad sheathing, then roll out self-adhered ice-and-water shield at eaves/valleys and synthetic underlayment up a 4/12-8/12 gable-hip roof, cap-nailing courses with correct overlap and cutting/sealing around pipe boots, vents and a chimney, working on the pitched surface with fall protection and weather pressure to dry-in the same day.

Specialty/low-pitch or coating variant: peel-and-stick membrane on a shallow-pitch (2/12-4/12) porch or shed section, high-temp underlayment under metal, or brush/spray-applied plastic coating or fiberglass-reinforced primer over a sloped deck or transition before the finish covering.

Small residential or small-commercial low-slope job (garage, porch, apartment, small store): coating and granule/gravel surfacing of a few squares of modified-bitumen or roll roofing, ladder access, tight work to parapets, walls and edges, homeowner or tenant present.

Large roof under adverse conditions: wind, heat or cold limiting bitumen temperature and set time, roof congested with HVAC units, ductwork, conduit and guy wires; the flood coat must be surfaced with gravel evenly and completely before the asphalt chills.

tasks.label: Smooth rough spots to prepare surfaces for waterproofing, using hammers, chisels, or rubbing bricks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial low-slope job: on a poured concrete roof/plaza deck outdoors at height, the roofer walks the deck and knocks off form fins, hardened mortar droppings, laitance ridges and other high spots with hammer and cold chisel (grinder for stubborn spots), sweeps, and leaves a substrate flat enough for hot-applied or self-adhered waterproofing membrane. Deck is dusty or damp, littered with other trades' debris, interrupted by drains, curbs and penetrations.

Masonry and concrete vertical transitions on the roof: parapet walls, curbs and equipment bases. Roofer chisels off mortar snots and rough joints and rubs the block/brick and concrete face smooth with a rubbing brick so base flashing and membrane adhere without bridging voids; work is done kneeling or standing at the wall, in corners and inside angles, often near the roof edge.

Residential or light-commercial re-roof/new build on a sloped plywood or OSB deck: roofer walks the pitched roof setting protruding nail and staple heads flush, knocking down high panel edges, prying out old fastener remnants, and sanding or scraping splinters and glue ridges before ice-and-water shield and underlayment go down. Pitch, dew and deck condition vary house to house.

Recover or repair of an existing low-slope roof: at patch and tie-in areas the roofer scrapes and grinds rough weathered asphalt/built-up surface, cuts out blisters and scabs, and chisels off remnants of old flashing and mastic ridges to get a smooth plane for new membrane or coating. Surface is aged, gravel-embedded and non-uniform.

Tight detail areas: drain sumps, pipe and conduit penetrations, scupper throats, pitch-pan and curb corners crowded with mechanical equipment. Roofer chisels high spots and rubs the concrete or masonry smooth in confined, awkward positions so the detail membrane can be dressed in without voids.
