sources.title: Life Line Emergency Vehicles deploys robotic sander from GrayMatter Robotics - The Robot Report
sources.claim: GrayMatter Robotics' Scan&Sand cells autonomously scan a presented part and sand or grind it for surface preparation and shape correction across complex geometries without CAD models; deployed at manufacturers including Life Line Emergency Vehicles and BetterWay Products.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous abrasive surface preparation of varied, non-CAD workpieces (including wood and composite panels) in a fixtured cell — the same operation as sanding splinters and high spots off a presented deck panel before a waterproofing layer.

sources.title: True Autonomy: Introducing autonomy in concrete floor polishing | LightWare LiDAR
sources.claim: The ACP-100 retrofits autonomy onto a concrete floor polishing machine so it self-navigates a warehouse floor with LiDAR; its stated value is that humans keep doing the harder hand grinding and detail work in parallel with the machine's open-floor passes.
sources.transferJustification: Closest mobile-robot analogue to in-situ concrete substrate prep inside a facility; cited to show the mobile machine covers open floor while the localized hand grinding a roofer does remains manual.

sources.title: Introducing Rufus, the Automated Roofing Robot from Renovate Robotics | Roofing Contractor
sources.claim: The only roof-deployed roofing robot found, Rufus, is built for automated asphalt shingle installation on residential roofs, traversing the roof on a winch and cable system; no substrate-preparation function is offered.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as context for the E3 judgment: the state of the art on actual roofs is shingle placement, not substrate smoothing.

tasks.label: Apply gravel or pebbles over top layers of roofs, using rakes or stiff-bristled brooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large low-slope commercial/industrial built-up roof (warehouse, school, big-box) on new construction or a full re-roof: hot asphalt flood coat is poured/mopped ahead of the crew and roofers rake and broom 300-400 lb per square of 3/8-5/8 in. roofing gravel into the hot bitumen before it cools, working a wide, largely open field with scattered vents and drains, outdoors in wind, heat and dust, near unguarded edges.

Congested commercial roof: multi-level decks, parapet walls, dozens of HVAC curbs, pipe penetrations, pitch pans, skylights and drain sumps. Much of the gravel work is hand raking and stiff-broom feathering of aggregate up to flashings and walls, keeping gravel out of drains and off walkpads, on a surface cluttered with hoses, kettle lines and material stacks.

Small simple flat roof (garage, porch, apartment block, small retail; roof section under ~20 squares): a plain rectangular deck with one or two vents; gravel is hoisted or carried up in buckets/wheelbarrows through tight access and spread by rake and broom over the flood coat in a single short work session.

Repair and maintenance on an in-place gravel roof: broom existing aggregate aside to expose a leak or blister, patch, then re-spread and re-embed gravel over the new flood coat; also raking wind-scoured or displaced gravel back over bare spots and re-leveling after inspections or rooftop equipment work.

Ballast/pea-gravel surfacing over a protection layer: pea gravel or river-rock ballast dumped in piles from a conveyor, hoist or blower onto a ballasted single-ply or inverted (protected-membrane) roof, then raked out by hand to the specified uniform depth/weight across the field without damaging the membrane.

sources.system: Euroline Slate Mineral Sand Dosing unit (bituminous membrane production line)
sources.title: Bituminous membrane production line - Euroline
sources.claim: Euroline supplies 'Slate Mineral Sand Dosing' equipment for bituminous membrane production lines: a conveyorized, machine-controlled doser that applies slate/mineral/sand aggregate uniformly onto the surface of the hot bituminous waterproofing sheet, with level sensing and inverter-controlled feed rate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying mineral aggregate surfacing onto a bitumen top layer in a factory line rather than on a roof. Transfer: identical materials (crushed mineral aggregate onto hot bitumen), identical acceptance criterion (complete uniform coverage embedded in the bitumen at a controlled spread rate), performed unattended by fixtured, conveyor-fed plant equipment - i.e. exactly the E1 presentation of the gravel-surfacing step, at precision at or above hand raking.

sources.date: c. 2024-2025 product pages and trade coverage, retrieved 2026-07
sources.title: SmartRake - A Robotic Bunker Rake — Robotic Bunker Rakes - BAS-Turf
sources.claim: TurfTroniq's SmartRake is a commercially sold self-contained robot that autonomously rakes and levels loose granular material (bunker sand) to a consistent finish over mapped areas, unattended, on golf courses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous raking/levelling of loose granular material (sand) over a defined area. Transfer is partial - it corroborates that machine-controlled raking of aggregate to a consistent uniform finish is a solved motion - but the machine only smooths material already in place, works on ground-level sand pits, and cannot deposit gravel onto a hot bitumen flood coat, so it is used only as corroboration for the E1 levelling function.

sources.title: RBR50 Spotlight: Renovate Robotics puts Rufus to work on roofs - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most advanced roofing robot working on actual roofs, Renovate Robotics' Rufus, is a winch/cable-driven machine that autonomously places and nails asphalt shingles on steep-slope roofs; no gravel or aggregate surfacing capability is described for it or any other rooftop robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic installation of roofing material on an as-found roof. Cited to establish the state of the art on real roofs (E3): the only fielded roof robot handles discrete shingles on steep slopes and does not spread or embed loose aggregate, which is why no positive E3 judgment is made.

sources.system: ASE 36" Wheels-Under Gravel Spreader 105000 / SPAR Marathon SPA-06SRGS
sources.developer: All Seasons Equipment / SPAR Marathon (sold by Big Rock Supply)
sources.title: Gravel Spreaders & Surfacing Equipment | Big Rock Supply
sources.claim: Rooftop gravel/ballast spreading is currently mechanized only with operator-pushed powered spreaders (e.g. the ASE 36-inch wheels-under gravel spreader and the SPAR Marathon gravel spreader), not with autonomous machines.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (rooftop gravel/ballast spreading). Cited to show that today's rooftop equipment is human-guided powered machinery rather than an autonomous robot; it supports the negative E3/E2 judgments and cannot support any positive judgment.

tasks.label: Install skylights on roofs to increase natural light inside structures or to reduce energy costs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New deck-mounted skylight cut into an existing steep-slope asphalt-shingle roof on an occupied single-family home: lay out and cut the deck opening from above, head/sill framing, set and fasten the unit, install the manufacturer's step/head/sill flashing kit, weave shingles and underlayment back in, seal; work at height on a pitched, sometimes brittle or wet roof with attic obstructions below.

Skylight replacement or re-flashing during a residential reroof: strip shingles around the old unit, remove leaking skylight or curb, repair rotted decking, set the new unit on the existing/rebuilt curb, install new flashing and shingles; conditions unknown until the old work is opened up.

Curb-mounted skylight, dome, or smoke vent installed on a low-slope commercial/institutional roof (TPO/EPDM/BUR or metal deck): cut and frame the deck opening, set the prefabricated curb, hoist and set the unit, flash the curb into the membrane with heat-welded or torched target patches, install safety screen/guard.

Skylight on a tile, slate, standing-seam metal, or low-pitch/complex roof: remove and re-lay tiles or slates, fabricate or fit specialty flashing/soakers, adapt to irregular substrate and unusual pitch, restore the surrounding roof covering to match.

Tubular skylight (sun tunnel) installation: locate rafters, cut a small roof opening and a matching ceiling opening, install the roof flashing/dome, run and seal the reflective tube through the attic, finish the interior diffuser; work split between roof surface and cramped attic.

sources.title: Rufus roofing robot installs shingles three times faster than a human
sources.claim: Rufus, a cable-driven roofing robot, autonomously installs asphalt shingles on residential ... has been piloted on real reroof jobs; its scope is field shingle application, with human crews still doing the detail work such as penetrations and flashing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (field shingle application on the same steep-slope residential roofs). Cited to show the state of the art on roofs; it does not transfer to skylights because no cited capability covers cutting/framing a deck opening, setting a glazed unit, or flashing it watertight.

sources.title: The roofing robot helping contractors — MetalCoffeeShop
sources.claim: Rufus is positioned to handle the repetitive field portion of reroofing while human crews perform detail work; announced roadmap items are tear-off and shingle cutting, not skylight or penetration work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (asphalt shingle installation). Establishes the boundary of demonstrated rooftop robot capability: detail work including penetrations such as skylights remains with human crews.

sources.title: Glazing Robots | GGR Group
sources.claim: Commercially available construction 'glazing robots' are compact operator-controlled vacuum lifting machines that position glass and window units; they are manipulators under continuous human control, not autonomous installers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (placing glazed units into openings). Does not substantiate completion because the machines are continuously operator-controlled lift assists and perform no opening cutting, fastening, flashing, or sealing.

sources.title: WEINMANN multifunction bridges | HOMAG
sources.claim: Automated timber-construction bridges in prefab factories fully automatically fasten sheathing and cut all openings (including roof elements), but the cited capability stops at the opening; no cited system sets and flashes a skylight unit into the panel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (cutting the rough opening in a roof element on a factory line, the E1 counterfactual analogue). Only a sub-step: it does not frame the curb, set the skylight, install flashing, or weatherproof, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion even at E1.

tasks.label: Estimate materials and labor required to complete roofing jobs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential re-roof bid: roofer measures an existing asphalt-shingle house roof (tape/wheel on site, or from an aerial/satellite measurement report), computes squares, waste factor, underlayment, drip edge, ridge/starter, nails and flashing, then estimates crew-days and labor cost and writes the homeowner a priced proposal.

Small repair or partial replacement: after inspecting a leak or wind-damaged section, the roofer tallies a handful of bundles, a roll of underlayment, sealant and flashing pieces, and estimates a few labor hours for one or two workers; quoted verbally or on a one-page ticket.

Commercial low-slope job: from architectural plans, a spec book and a walkthrough, the estimator takes off square footage of TPO/EPDM membrane, insulation boards, fasteners, adhesive, edge metal and drains, and builds labor hours by crew and phase for a competitive bid.

Working foreman ordering for a scheduled job: converts the sold scope into an exact material order (bundle counts, coil nails, ridge vent, ice-and-water) for delivery and rooftop loading, and plans how many workers for how many days to sequence the tear-off and install.

Insurance/storm claim estimate: roofer uses an aerial measurement report and estimating software (e.g., Xactimate-style line items) to quantify damaged slopes, accessories and code upgrades, and to produce labor and material line pricing for an adjuster.

tasks.label: Mop or pour hot asphalt or tar onto roof bases.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field application on a large low-slope commercial/industrial roof (warehouse, school, retail): asphalt heated in a ground kettle to ~450F, hoisted or pumped to the roof, then mopped or spread over the base sheet/insulation at roughly 25 lb per square between plies while felt plies are rolled in behind the mopper; outdoors on an elevated deck with wind, HVAC curbs and pipe penetrations to work around.

Flood-coat pour on a completed built-up roof: hot asphalt poured/spread at heavy rate (about 60 lb per square) over the finished ply stack and gravel or slag broadcast into it while still hot, over the open field of the roof.

Detail and flashing work: hand-mopping hot asphalt at parapet walls, curbs, drains, pipe penetrations, corners and edge metal, setting base flashings and cant strips in the hot bitumen; small, three-dimensional, cut-in areas that vary building to building.

Small or cut-up jobs: residential/light-commercial hot-mop work such as a small flat patio roof, balcony deck, shower-pan hot mop or an addition tie-in; buckets carried up a ladder, tight access, congested surfaces, occupied building below.

Repair, tie-in and patch work on an existing in-place roof: locating and preparing the failed area, then mopping hot asphalt onto the existing roof base to bed a patch or splice into adjoining plies, with unknown substrate condition and the surrounding roof left intact.

sources.system: APP/SBS modified bitumen membrane production line (coating die section)
sources.developer: Wuxi Chengming Machinery Plant (and comparable line builders, e.g. Euroline, Boato)
sources.title: APP membrane production line - Wuxi Chengming Machinery Plant
sources.claim: Commercial APP/SBS bituminous membrane production lines apply hot bitumen compound onto a reinforcement carrier (a roofing base web) through a machine-controlled coating die at set thickness and temperature, with no human spreading the material.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory coating of a roofing base web with hot bitumen rather than field mopping. Same material (hot asphalt/bitumen at coating temperature), same operation (metering and spreading a uniform film onto a felt/mat roof base so a ply bonds), at tighter tolerance than a hand mop. It transfers to the E1 counterfactual, in which the roof base is presented to the machine as the carrier web is.

sources.system: Shingle line asphalt coater and granule applicator
sources.developer: Owens Corning (patent assignee) / standard roofing-plant equipment
sources.title: US Patent 10,584,494 - Asphalt based roofing material with increased infrared reflectivity
sources.claim: Asphalt shingle/roll-goods plants run the base mat through coaters that pour hot melted asphalt onto the mat, and mineral granules are then embedded into the hot coating - the industrial equivalent of a flood coat with aggregate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: plant application of hot asphalt onto a roofing base sheet followed by broadcasting mineral surfacing into the hot asphalt. Same material and same sequence as a roof flood coat and gravel, performed by machine on a presented web.

sources.system: KUKA six-axis robots with Robatech Aero spray heads (Teijin Automotive Technologies plant, Czech Republic)
sources.title: Robots Dispense Hot-Melt Adhesive | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Industrial robots fitted with heated adhesive spray heads apply hot-melt material in a controlled pattern into a formed three-dimensional part inside a production cell, after which a second sheet is bonded into the adhesive.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of hot molten adhesive onto a fixtured substrate with a sheet then bonded into it - the same physical act as mopping hot asphalt onto a roof base and rolling a ply into it, including on shaped 3D geometry comparable to a fixtured curb or flashing detail.

sources.system: Duerr EcoRS sealing robots / EcoGun applicators
sources.date: 2016-06 (2,000th sealing robot sold; process still standard per Duerr, 2025)
sources.title: Duerr sells 2,000th sealing robot: New robot model optimizes sealing application in tight spaces
sources.claim: Fully automatic robotic application of highly viscous seam sealer and underbody coating is standard in automotive plants; robots lay the material more uniformly than manual application along complex three-dimensional edges inside fenced cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine application of hot, highly viscous sealing/coating material along seams, corners and edges of a fixtured workpiece - the closest automated analogue to hand-mopping hot asphalt into flashing details, at far higher precision than roofing requires.

sources.title: MINI MACADEN | SOPREMA
sources.claim: The most advanced field machine for bonding bituminous roof plies is a self-propelled, self-guided welding machine that unrolls and torch-welds membrane on roofs; it runs in operator-controlled manual mode or a laser-guided automatic mode along the lap line, with crew loading rolls and doing all details.
sources.transferJustification: Closest field system to the task (bonding bitumen plies on a roof), but it welds membrane rather than mopping kettle asphalt and is an operator-attended machine, so it cannot support a positive judgment; it documents that field practice remains operator-driven.

sources.title: Rufus roofing robot installs shingles three times faster than a human
sources.claim: An autonomous roofing robot is completing real residential roof jobs, but only for fastening asphalt shingles on steep-slope roofs, and it still requires a ground crew; no comparable field system handles hot kettle asphalt.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the field state of the art: shingle fastening on steep-slope roofs does not transfer to handling and spreading 450F kettle asphalt on low-slope decks, so it supports no positive judgment for this task.

tasks.label: Apply alternate layers of hot asphalt or tar and roofing paper to roofs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large open field area of a low-slope commercial/institutional roof (warehouse, school, hospital wing) in new construction or full reroof: hot asphalt from a kettle/tanker is spread by mop or mechanical felt layer and 2-4 plies of roofing felt are rolled out and broomed in, working across thousands of square feet at 400-475 F.

Field ply application on a cut-up, congested roof of an occupied building: plies must be run and cut in around rooftop HVAC curbs, ducts, skylights, pipe penetrations, drains and multi-level areas, with the crew working around live equipment and obstructions.

Base flashing and detail plies: cutting felt/ply sheets to size and hot-mopping successive layers up parapets, curbs and walls, around drains, vents and pipe penetrations, and at expansion joints, fitting and sealing each layer by hand.

Small low-slope roof on a residential or small commercial structure (porch, garage, addition, small storefront): kettle at street level, materials hoisted up, a few squares of plies applied in a confined area with short runs and many edges.

Field ply application under adverse conditions: cold or windy weather requiring tight asphalt temperature (EVT) control, tapered insulation or an irregular tear-off substrate, damp/dirty deck conditions, and pressure to close the roof in before rain.

sources.title: RBR50 Spotlight: Renovate Robotics puts Rufus to work on roofs - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Rufus is a winch/cable gantry robot that autonomously places and fastens overlapping courses of asphalt shingles on steep-slope residential roofs, with contractor pilot jobs; it does not handle hot bitumen or multi-ply felt.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous asphalt shingle installation on roofs. It shows a machine spanning a roof plane can place overlapping asphalt-based roofing layers autonomously at production rates, which is the layer-placement half of built-up roofing; it gives no evidence for molten-asphalt dispensing or for fitting plies around obstructions, so it supports only machine-structured (E1-style) layup of plain field layers.

sources.system: CH-BMPL SBS/APP modified bitumen membrane production line
sources.title: APP / Sbs Modified Bitumen Membrane Production Line Bitumen Waterproofing Membrane Machine
sources.claim: Commercial modified-bitumen membrane production lines apply metered hot (polymer-modified) asphalt to felt/nonwoven reinforcement, build up the coated layers and roller-form them into finished waterproofing sheet, running in automatic mode inside a purpose-built factory line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory manufacture of bituminous roofing sheet. Materials are the same (hot asphalt at coating temperature, felt/nonwoven roofing reinforcement), the operation is the same (metered hot-asphalt application, ply laydown, roller compaction, repeated to build layers), and the tolerance on coating weight and interply bond is at least as tight as hot-mopped built-up roofing. In an E1 counterfactual the deck is presented to the machine as the line presents its substrate, so the capability carries over to plain field layup; it says nothing about cutting and fitting plies around roof obstructions.

sources.title: Oriental Yuhong launched intelligent hot-melt waterproofing membrane construction equipment -- HotterMan
sources.claim: HotterMan Zandra/Spanker are self-propelled hot-melt bituminous membrane paving machines used on projects such as Beijing Daxing International Airport, but the release describes performance 'under the same condition of two-people operating', i.e. operator-run rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized hot-melt bitumen membrane laying on decks and roofs. It is the closest field machine to hot-asphalt ply application, but it is run by a two-person crew, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion on a roof (E3 or E2).

sources.system: Combination felt layer / mini-mopper / roller-type felt layer
sources.developer: Canadian Roofing Contractors Association (industry reference manual)
sources.title: 2.2.1 Felt Layers - Canadian Roofing Contractors Association
sources.claim: The standard mechanization for this task in the field is the felt layer: an operator-pulled machine that dispenses hot asphalt and rolls out felt behind it; the roofer must control the machine and keep it away from roof edges.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, mechanized: it documents that hot-asphalt dispensing plus felt laydown hardware exists and is routine, but that on real roofs it is pulled and steered by a roofer, with no autonomous guidance, edge protection or detail capability.

tasks.label: Spray roofs, sidings, or walls to bind, seal, insulate, or soundproof sections of structures, using spray guns, air compressors, or heaters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Spray polyurethane foam (SPF) roofing on a low-slope commercial or industrial roof: applicator on the roof pulls hose from a plural-component rig, applies foam in passes to a specified thickness around curbs, penetrations and parapets, then top-coats; work is weather-, wind- and temperature-constrained and the deck condition varies site to site.

Spray-applied elastomeric/silicone or acrylic coating restoration of an existing low-slope commercial roof: field area sprayed to a specified mil thickness after cleaning/priming, with seams, flashings and edge metal detailed, on an aged roof with ponding areas, debris and rooftop equipment.

Small-scale residential or light-commercial spraying: coating or sealing a small low-slope or metal roof section, spraying foam on a small roof deck or its underside, or sealing a residential re-roof; ladder/steep-slope access, tight yard, landscaping and homeowner property to protect.

Spraying exterior walls, parapets or siding with sealant, waterproofing or insulating coating from a lift, scaffold or ground, tying the wall coating into the roof system on a commercial or residential building.

Detail and spot spraying: sealant or mastic at penetrations, drains, flashings, seams and terminations, patch and repair spraying, and spray adhesive for bonding membrane or insulation boards; small volumes, precise cut-in around obstacles and masking of adjacent surfaces.

sources.title: Here's A Robot That Solves For Prefab Wall Panel Spray Foam Insulation
sources.claim: Spray-R is a commercial robotic cell in which a robot sprays closed-cell polyurethane foam insulation onto prefabricated building wall panels while the operator supervises from outside the enclosure, with every panel photographed before and after spraying.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: spray-applied closed-cell foam insulation on building wall panels. Same material class, plural-component spray equipment and purpose (insulate/seal sections of structures) as the roofer's task, performed with the workpiece presented to the machine in a purpose-built cell — the E1 counterfactual.

sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction's Dirty Work Is Going Robotic - Architect Magazine
sources.claim: The Okibo EG7 is a fully autonomous mobile robot that spray-applies paint and plaster and finishes drywall on interior construction sites, operating alongside laborers without site prep or BIM input.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic spray application of plaster/paint coatings to walls and ceilings. Comparable spray equipment, coverage and thickness quality standard, and building surfaces; demonstrated only on floor-accessible interior surfaces, not on roofs or exterior siding at height.

sources.system: Okibo EG7 / EG7+ with BLASTER spray gun
sources.title: Okibo Unleashes BLASTER Technology: A Breakthrough in Autonomous High-Speed Coating for the Construction Industry
sources.claim: Okibo announced commercial availability of a dual-nozzle airless spray gun for its autonomous EG7/EG7+ robots that covers a four-foot board width up to 24 feet high in two passes for painting and priming on large job sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-volume robotic spray coating of wall surfaces to specification. Substantiates autonomous spray coverage of tall wall areas indoors; does not cover exterior at-height or roof-surface spraying.

sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction's Dirty Work Is Going Robotic - Architect Magazine
sources.claim: Legend Robot spray-paints interior walls ... fully autonomously and has been deployed in high-rise apartment buildings in Singapore, covering roughly 200 square meters per hour with one operator supervising two machines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous spray coating of building walls and ceilings inside occupied high-rise buildings. Same spray-application action and surfaces as wall sealing/coating, but indoors and floor-accessible only.

sources.title: Innovation Showcase Features Revolutionary Robotic Painting Solution | Haskell
sources.claim: PaintJet's Bravo system coats exterior walls of large industrial and commercial buildings from a boom lift and has covered over 1.5 million square feet, but its robots are operated by remote control from the ground.
sources.transferJustification: Closest analogue to in-situ exterior wall spraying at height, but explicitly remote-controlled, so it cannot support a positive judgment of autonomous completion.

sources.title: SPF Roofing and Coatings Robot Improves Spray Application Efficiency | SprayFoam Magazine
sources.claim: The SprayWorks Spraybot/Coaterbot is a commercially sold self-propelled machine that lays even passes of spray foam, polyurea or coatings on commercial roofs, bridges and decks; it has user controls and speed settings and is tended by the applicator on the roof.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task (in-situ SPF and coating application to roofs), but autonomy is not established — the machine is set up, steered and tended by the applicator — so it is treated as operator-controlled and cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Torus - RetroFIT for the Future: Q-Bot underfloor insulation
sources.claim: Q-Bot's robots spray foam insulation onto the underside of suspended timber ... in occupied homes, entering through an access hatch or air vent, and are remotely operated by a technician.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ spray foam insulation of a building element in unstructured homes. Shows the deployed state of in-situ spray insulation robotics is remote operation, so it cannot support a positive autonomous judgment.

sources.title: Rufus roofing robot installs shingles three times faster than a human
sources.claim: Renovate Robotics' Rufus is an autonomous cable-driven roofing robot that installs asphalt shingles on steep-slope residential roofs and is performing paid residential jobs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous work on an in-situ residential roof. Shares the environment but not the process — it nails shingles rather than spraying coatings to a mil thickness — so it is cited only as context and not used for a positive spraying judgment.

tasks.label: Attach solar panels to existing roofs, according to specifications and without damaging roofing materials or the structural integrity of buildings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retrofit PV array on a steep-slope asphalt-shingle roof of an occupied single-family home: locate rafters, lift shingle courses to set flashed L-foot attachments with sealant, lag into rafters, level rails, then hoist and clamp 15-30 modules around vents/valleys, all with fall protection on a 4/12-9/12 pitch and no leaks or broken shingles.

Retrofit PV on a residential specialty roof - concrete/clay tile, standing-seam metal, slate, or low-slope membrane - requiring tile removal and replacement hooks, seam clamps, or membrane-welded/ballasted mounts; brittle or slippery surfaces, irregular geometry, tight setbacks.

Small/medium commercial or institutional low-slope roof (school, retail strip, church, office): crane or hoist materials to roof, lay out ballasted or mechanically attached racking around HVAC curbs, skylights and drains, then bolt and clamp several hundred modules without puncturing the membrane.

Large industrial/warehouse flat roof, several hundred kW to MW: long repetitive rows of racking on a wide, mostly clear membrane or metal deck, staged pallets, facility-controlled access, multi-week crew work.

Integrated solar shingle / BIPV product (e.g., nailable solar shingle courses) installed on a residential re-roof: courses nailed to the deck interleaved with conventional shingles and flashing, plus module interconnection.

Service work on an existing rooftop array: detach and re-attach a handful of modules for a roof repair or re-roof, or add a few modules to an existing rail run, matching original specification and re-sealing penetrations.

sources.title: AES Maximo robot installs 100 megawatts of solar capacity - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Maximo's robot fleet autonomously performs mechanical installation of PV modules onto mounting structures at a utility-scale solar construction site, in commercial production (100 MW installed at AES Bellefield, Kern County, CA).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanically attaching PV modules to racking. Same objects (full-size PV modules), same clamp/bolt fastening and sub-millimeter alignment required on a roof; supports the judgment that with the work presented in a fixed, known position a robot can attach modules to worker quality. It cannot reach or work on a roof.

sources.title: Terabase Energy advances automated PV construction with robotics, AI tools - pv magazine Global
sources.claim: Terabase's Terafab is a purpose-built automated assembly line erected on site in which robots unpack modules and move module/torque-tube assemblies through inspection and loading; first-generation used to install 40 MW commercially, V2 field-tested and released for commercial service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly of PV modules to their mounting structure inside a purpose-built line where inputs are presented in known positions - the E1 presentation of module-attachment work. Same modules and mechanical fasteners; the line is on flat ground, not a roof.

sources.title: Rufus roofing robot installs shingles three times faster than a human
sources.claim: Renovate Robotics' Rufus autonomously places and fastens asphalt shingles on real steep-slope residential roofs in New Jersey and Pennsylvania, guided by computer vision, but still needs a ground team and cannot do flat, tile or metal roofs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously fastening roofing material to a sloped residential roof deck. Shows robotic work on real (E3) roofs is emerging, but the product handled is shingles, not racked PV modules, so it does not substantiate solar attachment on roofs.

sources.title: Rufus roofing robot installs shingles three times faster than a human
sources.claim: Renovate Robotics lists bracket installation for rack-and-panel solar and solar-shingle installation as roadmap items, not current capability; full autonomy from setup to ... also a longer-term goal.
sources.transferJustification: Negative evidence: the only robot working on real US residential roofs does not yet install solar mounting brackets or panels.

aliases: AC Sheet Metal Installer (Air Conditioning Sheet Metal Installer)

HVAC Sheet Metal Mechanic (Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning Sheet Metal Mechanic)

roles.description: Fabricate, assemble, install, and repair sheet metal products and equipment, such as ducts, control boxes, drainpipes, and furnace casings. Work may involve any of the following: setting up and operating fabricating machines to cut, bend, and straighten sheet metal; shaping metal over anvils, blocks, or forms using hammer; operating soldering and welding equipment to join sheet metal parts; or inspecting, assembling, and smoothing seams and joints of burred surfaces. Includes sheet metal duct installers who install prefabricated sheet metal ducts used for heating, air conditioning, or other purposes.

tasks.label: Maintain equipment, making repairs or modifications when necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine preventive maintenance on shop fabrication machinery (shear, press brake, roll former, plasma/laser table, spot welder, shop air compressor): lubricate ways/gearboxes, check hydraulic oil level, clear chips and slag, blow out or replace filters, drain the compressor, check belts, guards and safety devices, log the round. Fabrication shop floor, machines in fixed positions, people working nearby.

Corrective repair of a shop machine that has failed or drifted out of tolerance: diagnose the fault, then replace or resharpen shear blades, re-shim/adjust ram parallelism or backgauge, replace a leaking hydraulic hose or seal, swap worn punch and die tooling, replace a limit switch or contactor, and prove the fix with test cuts/bends. Fabrication shop.

Hand and portable power tool service at the bench or gang box: sharpen and adjust aviation snips, crimpers, hand seamers and notchers; replace grinder wheels, cut-off discs and carbon brushes; service pneumatic shears/flangers (oil, replace jaws, fix leaks); repair cords, switches and batteries; clean and oil tools. Shop bench mostly, sometimes site trailer.

Jobsite equipment maintenance and field repair on an active construction site: service the welder/generator, portable brake or roll former, screw guns, vacuum, scissor lift or hoist; fix a broken clamp, hose or cord; conditions are cramped, dusty, weather-exposed, and the layout and clutter differ site to site.

Servicing welding and cutting equipment consumables: ream spatter out of the MIG gun nozzle, cut back wire, apply anti-spatter, replace a burned contact tip or liner, change plasma torch consumables, swap abrasive discs, check gas hoses and regulators. Shop weld booth with the gun and station in fixed known positions.

Modification/upgrade of shop equipment: fabricate and install a custom guard, bracket, table extension, material stop or holding jig on an existing machine; measure, cut, weld or bolt it in place, align it, and verify the machine still runs to tolerance. Fabrication shop.

sources.title: Simplified automated consumables management and manual welds - The Fabricator
sources.claim: Automated consumable-management systems for robotic welding remove and replace nozzles and contact tips and adapt with sensors when a tip is fused, i.e. they handle off-nominal maintenance conditions without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: unattended replacement of worn welding-gun consumables, including recovery from a fused tip, which is the corrective side of consumable servicing.

sources.claim: Robotic systems fielded for industrial plant maintenance programs are inspection platforms: they patrol and collect thermal, visual and gas data to feed predictive maintenance, but do not perform the physical repair or servicing actions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (equipment condition monitoring) cited to bound the state of the art: autonomous plant robots inspect equipment but do not lubricate, adjust, or repair it.

tasks.label: Fabricate ducts for high efficiency heating, ventilating, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems to maximize efficiency of systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial fab shop: producing bare galvanized straight rectangular duct sections for a high-efficiency system from coil stock - decoil, level, bead, notch, cut, plasma-cut taps/collars/access doors, roll TDC/TDF transverse flanges, brake the wrap, close the Pittsburgh/snap-lock longitudinal seam, insert corners, seal the seam and label for shipment.

Commercial fab shop: same straight rectangular sections but internally lined for acoustic/thermal efficiency - liner uncoiled, adhesive applied, liner cut to length and pinned to the sheet before forming, edges treated, then formed, seamed, flanged and sealed to a low-leakage (SMACNA Seal Class A) standard.

Commercial fab shop: round and flat-oval spiral duct and round fittings for a high-efficiency system - spiral pipe rolled from coil and cut to length, plus gored elbows, reducers, taps and collars formed/locked or welded, sized and sealed so the round system meets tight leakage classes.

Commercial fab shop: one-off custom rectangular fittings from shop drawings - transitions, offsets, square-to-round, tees, radius elbows with turning vanes. Blanks nested and plasma/laser cut, hand- or auto-braked, Pittsburgh locks run, pieces mated, hammered, tack-welded or riveted, vanes/rails installed and joints sealed.

Jobsite: fabricating or reworking duct in the field to fit as-built conditions - measuring the actual opening or obstruction, cutting and forming a filler section, transition or offset with portable brake, shears and hand tools on a construction floor or in an occupied mechanical room, then sealing it.

tasks.label: Fasten seams or joints together with welds, bolts, cement, rivets, solder, caulks, metal drive clips, or bonds to assemble components into products or to repair sheet metal items.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fabrication-shop production of rectangular HVAC duct sections and fittings: closing the Pittsburgh/snap-lock longitudinal seam, inserting and crimping TDC/TDF corners, driving pop rivets or screws at cleats and slips, and running mastic/cold sealant on the seams so the section meets SMACNA leakage class. Parts are standard-gauge galvanized, worked at a bench or machine line inside the shop.

Shop fabrication of custom sheet metal products (control boxes, hoods, furnace casings, tanks, kitchen equipment): MIG/spot welding, soldering, riveting and bolting the seams and joints of an assembly held on a bench or in a simple jig, then dressing the joint. Mix of one-offs and short runs, drawings supplied.

Field joining of duct runs in a building under construction: mating slip-and-drive or TDC/TDF flanged sections overhead in a ceiling plenum from a lift or ladder, tapping on drive clips, driving sheet metal screws, bolting flange corners and brushing/gunning sealant on the transverse joint. Congested, variable overhead space, other trades present.

Repair of installed sheet metal items in the field or in the shop's repair bay: welding a cracked seam on a hopper or duct, riveting a patch over corroded metal, re-soldering a leaking joint, re-caulking a failed joint. Item geometry and damage vary case to case; access is whatever the item allows.

Architectural sheet metal: closing single/double-lock standing seams on roof panels, riveting and soldering gutter, coping, flashing and wall-panel joints on the roof or facade, then sealing. Outdoor, on a sloped or elevated surface, weather-dependent.

sources.system: Iowa Precision Fabriduct NEO Full Coil Line (Mestek Machinery)
sources.title: Iowa Precision Fabriduct NEO Full Coil Line | Mestek Machinery
sources.claim: Fully automated HVAC duct coil lines form and close the duct's lock seams and apply cold sealant to those seams in-line, producing finished duct that meets SMACNA Class A leakage; the line runs as a machine-fed, machine-controlled production line in a duct shop.

tasks.label: Transport prefabricated parts to construction sites for assembly and installation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial HVAC run: shop crew pulls a job's prefabricated rectangular duct sections, fittings, hangers and accessories from the fab-shop staging area, loads and straps them on a stake-body or box truck (forklift plus hand loading), drives 10-50 miles in traffic to an active commercial construction site, checks in with site logistics, unloads at the gate/laydown by hand or with a site forklift, and stages the bundles at the crew's work area.

Large/heavy delivery to a multi-story or industrial project: spiral duct, large plenums, fan casings or AHU sections on a flatbed or boom truck; unloaded by site crane, telehandler or material hoist; hoisted or carried floor-by-floor through unfinished, cluttered space and staged near the riser or mechanical room.

Residential / light-commercial run: pickup or van loaded with assorted loose prefab items (boots, take-offs, elbows, flex, registers, hanger strap, sealant) pulled off shop shelves per house, driven to houses under construction on muddy or unpaved lots, then carried by armload into the garage, crawlspace or attic staging point.

Intra-site shuttle: prefab already delivered to the jobsite laydown yard or on-site fab trailer; the sheet metal worker moves bundles and fittings by cart, pallet jack, telehandler or construction elevator to the floor and room where installation is happening that day, through changing, obstructed routes.

Retrofit delivery into an occupied, institution-controlled building (hospital, plant, data center, school): truck backs to a loading dock, parts come off on pallets/carts, then travel by pallet jack through standard corridors and a freight elevator to the mechanical room or ceiling work zone.

sources.system: Seegrid Palion Lift RS1 / CR1 autonomous lift trucks
sources.title: Seegrid Sets the Standard with Industry-Leading Forklift AMR Payload Versatility
sources.claim: Seegrid's autonomous lift-truck AMRs autonomously pick up varied payloads (standard pallets to oversized custom loads), transport them across active manufacturing plants and warehouses, and place them, including 'parts-to-line' delivery in production at automotive manufacturers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility delivery of fabricated parts to the point of assembly. It is the same load-transport-deposit cycle with comparable bulky, palletized/oversized metal parts, differing only in that the route lies inside a controlled facility rather than on public roads and a jobsite.

sources.system: TWA Reach / Extended Reach autonomous forklifts with Shared Autonomy Platform

sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading and unloading a highway trailer with palletized freight at a dock. That is the load/unload half of the sheet-metal delivery cycle, with comparable weights and stacking precision, performed inside a controlled facility.

sources.title: DHL to deploy 1,000 Boston Dynamics Robots in Warehouses
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously unloads floor-loaded trucks and containers in warehouses; DHL has deployed it for container unloading and signed for over 1,000 additional units.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unloading a highway trailer of mixed cases. It substantiates autonomous truck unloading of unfixtured stacked goods, the unloading step of this task, in a structured facility.

sources.title: All-in at TraPac
sources.claim: At the automated TraPac terminal in Los Angeles, unmanned automated straddle carriers move containers across the yard and rail-mounted automated stacking cranes store containers and load and discharge road trucks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving very large, heavy unit loads from a truck through a facility to a precise stacking position. It shows autonomous handling of oversized loads and automated truck load/discharge at a container port, matching the heavy prefab (plenum, AHU casing) delivery leg.

sources.title: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robot showcased at RIA
sources.claim: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robots haul carts of supplies through hospital corridors and service areas and call and ride elevators, deployed in fleets at dozens of US hospitals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cart-based material delivery through the corridors and freight elevators of an occupied institutional building, which is the in-building leg of a retrofit delivery.

sources.system: Aurora Driver (Volvo VNL Autonomous / International trucks)
sources.title: Aurora Expands Driverless Trucking Service from Fort Worth to El Paso
sources.claim: Aurora operates Class 8 trucks driverless on Texas public highways in commercial freight service between terminals, having passed 100,000 driverless miles; loading and unloading at each end is done by people at terminals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the over-the-road leg of a delivery. It covers only terminal-to-terminal highway driving with human loading, unloading and yard work, so it does not substantiate the whole task at a construction site.

sources.system: TRUMPF SortMaster Station / SortMaster Vision with LiftMaster Compact
sources.title: TRUMPF achieves breakthrough in automated sorting
sources.claim: TRUMPF's LiftMaster/SortMaster automation removes cut sheets from the laser cutting machine, separates parts from the skeleton and sorts and stacks the sheet metal parts fully automatically inside the fabrication cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-side handling and stacking of individual sheet metal parts in a purpose-built cell. It substantiates that fixtured, presented sheet metal parts of the kind this task moves can be picked and stacked onto pallets by machine at E1.

sources.system: Bedrock Robotics autonomy retrofit kit on excavators
sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Announces Supervised Autonomy Testing on Active Construction Sites in Move Towards Commercialization
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics runs supervised-autonomy excavators performing excavation work on active US construction sites in pilot programs, with operator-less deployment still a stated future target.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous heavy equipment operation on an active construction site. It marks the current E3 construction frontier as supervised earthmoving, not discrete-part loading, delivery and staging, so it does not substantiate this task at E3.

tasks.label: Install assemblies, such as flashing, pipes, tubes, heating and air conditioning ducts, furnace casings, rain gutters, or downspouts in supportive frameworks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/institutional new construction: hanging and connecting galvanized rectangular and round duct runs overhead from trapeze hangers and threaded rod in an active building under construction, working from scissor lifts; slip-and-drive or TDC joints, screwed and sealed, routed around structure, conduit and pipe installed by other trades.

Residential and light-commercial rigid sheet metal: trunk lines, transitions, plenums, furnace casings, register boots and fittings set into joist bays, attics, crawlspaces, basements and mechanical closets; each run measured and fitted to framing as found, screwed, strapped and sealed.

Residential branch runs in flexible insulated duct: pulling flex through attic framing, sliding the inner liner over a collar or boot, banding/zip-tying, mastic sealing, pulling the insulation and jacket over the joint and supporting the run with saddle straps.

Exterior rainware on houses and small commercial buildings: setting hidden hangers or spikes, hanging seamless gutter to fascia at correct slope from ladders or lifts, sealing end caps and miters, cutting outlets and strapping downspouts to walls.

Roof and wall flashing: step and counterflashing at walls and chimneys, curb, vent and pipe-penetration flashing, coping, drip edge and gravel stop fitted to roof and wall substrates as found, fastened and sealed weathertight, often on sloped or elevated surfaces.

Work inside institution-controlled facilities and prefab shops: mounting duct sections, exhaust connections, hood ductwork and equipment casings onto steel support frames, racks or unit housings in a plant mechanical room, hospital mechanical space, or a fabrication-shop staging bay before shipment.

sources.title: Body-in-White | ABB
sources.claim: Commercial robotic body-in-white cells place and join large sheet metal panels into fixtured supporting structures, performing hemming, self-piercing riveting and spot welding autonomously inside modular, fenced cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: joining formed sheet metal panels to a supporting frame. Objects (large gauge sheet metal), joining methods (mechanical fastening, sealing) and required precision are comparable to setting duct sections and casings into a support framework when the framework and parts are fixtured, as at E1.

sources.system: Automotive BIW robotic weld/assembly cells with workholding fixtures
sources.title: Automotive BIW (Body-in-White) Welding and Assembly Workholding | Reid Supply
sources.claim: In automotive body shops robots pick and place heavy sheet metal panels into precise positions in workholding fixtures inside safety-fenced welding/assembly cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling and positioning large heavy sheet metal panels into a supporting framework. Weight, size and handling demands match duct sections, casings and flashing panels; the cited setting is a fenced, fixtured cell, i.e. E1.

sources.system: ASG AX-40 / AX-10 automatic screwdriving cells
sources.title: Screwdriving | ASSEMBLY digital edition
sources.claim: Off-the-shelf robotic screwdriving cells with frames, part fixtures, screw feeders and safety light curtains automatically drive threaded fasteners in assembly work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic fastening of assembled parts. Sheet metal installation is joined largely with self-drilling screws; a fixtured, light-curtained screwdriving cell supplies the fastening step of the E1 counterfactual.

sources.title: Boeing Introduces New Method for Building 777 Fuselages
sources.claim: Guided robots drilled and installed tens of thousands of fasteners joining large aluminum fuselage panels into a supporting structure in a purpose-built factory cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drilling and fastening large metal skin panels onto a supporting frame. Same class of operation (locate, hold, drill, fasten thin metal to structure) required to secure ducts, casings and flashing, demonstrated in a purpose-built fixtured cell.

sources.title: Robots are the Future of Modular Construction - Modular Building Institute
sources.claim: In an automated modular-housing factory line, robots place and fasten framing and sheathing panels to build wall assemblies, but MEP systems including ductwork are installed by human tradespeople.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic placement and fastening of building components onto a frame on a machine-centric production line. Supports E1 for rigid component installation; the same source shows duct/MEP installation in modules is still manual, so it supports no E2 judgment.

sources.title: Hilti's Overhead Drilling Robot Brings Further Automation to the Jobsite | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: A commercially sold construction robot autonomously drills overhead anchor holes in concrete slabs for MEP hanger installation, working from BIM data on active jobsites, but performs no placement or fastening of ducts or pipes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the anchor-drilling prerequisite of hanging ductwork on real construction sites (E3). It substantiates only hole drilling, not lifting, aligning, joining or sealing assemblies, so it cannot support a positive E2/E3 judgment for this task.

sources.title: RBR50 Spotlight: Renovate Robotics puts Rufus to work on roofs - The Robot Report
sources.claim: A prototype cable/winch-driven roofing robot places and fastens asphalt shingles on residential roofs, covering field shingle courses only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastening roof-covering material on an unstructured residential roof (E3). It handles uniform field shingles on open planes and is a prototype; it does not fit, lap or seal metal flashing at penetrations and walls, so it does not substantiate completion of the flashing instance.

tasks.label: Hire, train, or supervise new employees or apprentices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: A journeyman sheet metal worker supervises one or two apprentices during a duct installation on a commercial job site: assigning the day's hangers and trunk sections, watching their work, correcting technique verbally, checking hanger spacing and joint alignment, and answering questions as they arise.

Hands-on instruction in the fabrication shop: the lead worker shows an apprentice how to set up and run a shear, brake, or Pittsburgh lock former, explains layout marks and drawing symbols, watches the apprentice's first attempts, and critiques the resulting part.

Safety and procedure instruction — toolbox talks, fall-protection and lift orientation, hot-work and PPE rules, explaining a new specification or code requirement to the crew before a task begins, and documenting attendance.

Evaluating and documenting apprentice progress: signing off on hours and competency checklists for a JATC/union apprenticeship, meeting with the apprentice about performance, coordinating with the training coordinator, and recommending advancement or remediation.

Participating in hiring: reviewing applications or union referrals, interviewing candidates about experience with layout, welding, and duct installation, judging a candidate's hands-on tryout, and recommending or making the hire decision.

tasks.label: Lay out, measure, and mark dimensions and reference lines on material, such as roofing panels, using calculators, scribes, dividers, squares, or rulers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop layout on flat sheet stock at a fabrication bench: from a shop drawing or fitting order, measure and scribe cut lines, seam allowances, bend/fold lines and notch marks for rectangular duct fittings (transitions, offsets, tees) on 26-16 ga galvanized sheet, using square, scribe, tape and calculator.

Shop pattern development for a complex or custom piece (round-to-rectangular transition, ogee offset, architectural flashing, casing): develop the flat pattern by triangulation/radial-line development, then transfer and mark stretch-out lines, bend lines and reference marks onto the sheet with dividers, trammel and scribe.

Field measure and mark on roofing/wall panels or flashing at a job site: measure the as-built opening or run on the roof or scaffold, transfer dimensions to the panel lying on the deck or a pair of horses, and mark cut and hem lines, including scribing to an irregular parapet, curb or penetration; wind, weather and uneven support.

Field layout of reference lines and points for a duct run at a job site: from drawings, snap centerlines and elevation reference lines on the deck/structure, and mark hanger, sleeve and penetration locations for the sheet metal crew in an active, cluttered construction area.

Marking on already-formed or curved stock in the shop: laying out and marking tap/collar openings, hole centers and reference lines on round or spiral pipe, elbows, formed casings and curved plenum sections using wraparounds, dividers and templates.

Field fabrication of a one-off filler piece, transition, offset, plenum patch or hanger detail from flat stock at the site: lay out from field dimensions, cut on portable shear/snips, notch corners, brake or hammer-form the flanges over a block, and close the seam so the piece fits an existing opening or obstruction.

Drilling and punching holes at the site: holes in duct flanges, angle iron, unistrut, hanger strap, corner braces and support steel for bolts, tie rods, screws and threaded rod, using a hand drill, magnetic drill or hand punch, sized and located from the as-built support layout.

Architectural/roofing sheet metal: cutting and bending flashing, counterflashing, coping, drip edge, gutter and trim pieces to length and profile on the roof or at a portable brake set up on site, including hammer-forming and soldering-ready corners and miters cut to fit the actual parapet or wall condition.

Residential or light-commercial retrofit: altering an existing installed duct, boot or plenum in place in an attic, crawlspace, basement or above a ceiling grid - cutting a takeoff or access opening in the installed duct, trimming an existing fitting, or drilling in a confined, cluttered, poorly lit space.

tasks.label: Maneuver completed roofing units into position for installation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/industrial metal building: crew maneuvers long (20–40 ft) roll-formed standing-seam or R-panel roof sheets from a bundle staged on the roof or lifted by telehandler, walks/slides each across open purlins, engages the side lap or seam leg with the previously set panel, squares it to the eave, and holds it while it is fastened. Elevated, windy, open framing, fall-protection in use.

Residential or light-commercial sloped metal roof (new or re-roof): two workers hoist cut-to-length panels (8–20 ft) up a ladder/conveyor onto a steep pitch, set the first panel square to the eave and rake, then walk each subsequent panel into position over underlayment and clips, working around occupied homes, landscaping and limited staging.

Architectural sheet metal roofing assemblies: shop-fabricated units such as coping, gravel stops, fascia/edge units, curved or tapered panels, dormer and mansard sections are carried from staging and offered up into position against parapets, corners, hips and penetrations; field dimensions vary and the unit is often nudged, sprung or trimmed to fit before fastening.

Prefabricated roof units and accessories: roof curbs, equipment supports, ventilators, skylight and chimney units are maneuvered across the deck and set square over roof openings, aligned to the opening and to adjoining flashing before being fastened and flashed in.

Rigging and landing: guiding crane- or telehandler-hoisted panel bundles and large prefabricated roof sections from ground level to designated landing points on the roof deck, controlling swing with tag lines, and staging/positioning the load where installation will begin.

sources.title: Smart Handling for Roofing Panels with Comau NJ-110 Robots
sources.claim: Two Comau NJ-110-3.0 industrial robots autonomously load and unload large corrugated roofing panels (up to 1000 x 3000 mm) through a coating line inside EC-certified fenced robotic cells — precise, repeatable positioning of formed sheet-metal roofing panels in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-tending/transfer rather than final installation, but it is the same physical act on the same objects — gripping a large corrugated roofing panel and placing it accurately at a required position — establishing that panel-sized roofing units can be maneuvered into a defined position by robots in a fixtured cell.

sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor

sources.transferJustification: Related task: the panels placed are sheathing boards rather than sheet metal, but the operation is identical in kind — picking a full-size roofing panel, positioning it on a roof element held in a fixture, and securing it — showing the E1 version of 'maneuver roofing unit into position for installation' is done commercially.

instances.label: Shop bench work in an HVAC/fab shop: hand-forming small duct fittings, transitions, offsets, elbow gores and patch pieces by hammering 26–16 ga galvanized sheet over stakes, anvils and hardwood blocks; parts checked against a pattern or template.

Shop dressing of edges, hems and seams: peening, flattening and planishing a hem or lock over a stake or dolly with a mallet/hammer, closing a hemmed edge or a Pittsburgh corner, truing a flange after machine forming.

Custom/architectural sheet metal in shop: forming compound-curved copper/stainless flashing, gutter miters, hoods and ornamental pieces over hammer forms, shot bags, blocks and English-wheel-style tooling; cosmetic surface quality required.

Job-site forming of a new piece to field measurements: on a roof, in a mechanical room or in an attic, a worker forms a flashing, cap, transition or filler from a blank over a portable block, brake stake or scrap form to the dimensions just measured.

Job-site in-place adjustment/repair: hammering a corner or flange of an already-installed duct, curb, gutter or panel over an available form or the structure itself to make it fit, closing a joint in place, or bumping out a dent on installed work in a tight, cluttered space.

Fab shop finishing of welded assemblies: grinding down and blending weld seams and spot welds on stainless kitchen hoods, plenums, welded plenum boxes and architectural panels, then buffing/graining the surface to a specified finish with an angle grinder, belt sander and buffing wheel.

Jobsite (active construction/mechanical room): duct, pipe and fitting pieces cut to length on site are filed and deburred on the deck or on a portable bench before being hung and joined; dust, clutter, other trades present, work often staged on the floor or a gang box.

Jobsite in-situ dressing: grinding, filing and smoothing welds, burrs and rough seams on ductwork, hangers, casings or louvers already hung overhead or fixed in place, from a lift or ladder in a partially built building.

Architectural/roofing sheet metal outdoors: trimming, filing and smoothing edges, hems and soldered/welded seams of flashing, copings, gutters and standing-seam panels formed at a site brake, then buffing them out; weather, heights and staged material on a roof deck.

Specialty precision work in a manufacturing plant: high-spec sanding, polishing and buffing of assembled aerospace, food-grade or laboratory stainless sheet metal components to a stated surface finish, with inspection to Ra/scratch-free standards.

tasks.label: Inspect individual parts, assemblies, or installations, using measuring instruments, such as calipers, scales, or micrometers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fabrication shop: after shearing, plasma-cutting or brake-forming, the worker checks duct sections, fittings, transitions and panels against shop drawings with a tape/steel scale, square and protractor (bend angle, leg lengths, diagonals), to roughly 1/16 in, part mix changing job to job.

Fabrication shop: precision/final inspection of smaller parts and welded assemblies with calipers and micrometers - material gauge/thickness, hole diameters and locations, flange widths, flatness - for first-article and pre-ship QC against a spec sheet.

Active commercial construction site: verify installed duct mains, branches, fittings and equipment against the shop drawings/model - routing, elevations, offsets, dimensions of openings, clearances - and flag deviations for correction before ceilings close.

Field during installation: measure existing conditions and check fit-up from ladders and lifts - inside ceiling plenums, chases and mechanical rooms - taking tape/folding-rule dimensions, checking joint gaps, hanger spacing and levelness before connecting the next fitting.

Architectural sheet metal at height and outdoors: inspect installed roof panels, flashings, copings and gutters - panel lengths, module spacing, hem and seam dimensions, straightness/alignment of runs - in wind and weather.
Residential/light-commercial service call: measure an existing plenum, duct or damaged fitting in an occupied home or small building and check that a replacement part fits.
