tasks.label: Verify that heating, ventilating, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems are designed, installed, and calibrated in accordance with green certification standards, such as those of Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED).

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Walk-through field verification of installed duct systems and HVAC equipment against the project's green/LEED specification on an active commercial construction site: checking seam sealing and mastic, duct insulation type/thickness, hanger spacing, that duct openings are capped per the IAQ construction management plan, and that installed equipment/filters match specified efficiency; requires ladders, above-ceiling and mechanical-shaft access, work amid other trades and debris.

Duct air-leakage testing of installed duct sections to the specified SMACNA leakage class supporting energy/IAQ credits: blanking off branch openings, connecting and setting up a test fan and manometer, pressurizing the section, recording leakage rate against the allowable, locating and resealing failures, retesting, and logging results for the commissioning/LEED record.

Airflow and ventilation verification in a substantially complete or occupied commercial building: flow-hood readings at supply/return diffusers, outdoor-air measurement at the air handler against ASHRAE 62.1 design rates, adjusting balancing dampers and VAV minimums, and recording readings versus design CFM for the balancing report.

Verification of controls and calibration in mechanical rooms and occupied spaces: comparing thermostat, CO2 and temperature sensor readings to a reference instrument, confirming setpoints, economizer and demand-controlled ventilation operation against the sequence of operations, and documenting deviations for the commissioning authority.

Office review of design drawings, shop drawings and submittals against LEED credit and prerequisite requirements (duct leakage class, insulation, filtration, ventilation rates), and compiling the verification paperwork/report package for the commissioning authority or LEED submittal.

sources.title: Trimble X7 Scanner, FieldLink Software Integrated with Spot Robot | Construction Equipment
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot carrying a Trimble X7 laser scanner runs pre-planned autonomous waypoint missions on construction sites to capture scans that are compared with the design model for deviations; sold as a turnkey commercial solution and used by contractors such as Hensel Phelps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous as-built data capture and BIM deviation checking on jobsites. It bears on verifying that ductwork was installed per design geometry, but it only produces scan/deviation data, not a compliance determination about sealing, insulation, filtration or calibration.

sources.title: AI Startup Using Robots and Lidar to Boost Productivity on Construction Sites - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Doxel deploys autonomous LiDAR- and camera-equipped ground robots that scan construction site interiors daily and compare captured data to the BIM to report installed quantities and installation quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated construction quality/progress verification against the model in the same jobsite environment. Transfer is partial: it verifies presence and position of installed MEP elements, not the sealing, insulation, airflow or calibration attributes a green-certification verification requires.

sources.developer: Cai et al. (academic, BuildSys/Automation in Construction)
sources.title: Actively-exploring thermography-enabled autonomous robotic system for detecting and registering HVAC thermal leaks - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A self-navigating research robot (TEA-bot / AcTEA-bot) autonomously detects and registers thermal leaks in HVAC ductwork above ceilings, validated in a purpose-built, true-to-scale in-lab ceiling mock-up with five planted leaks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated inspection of installed HVAC ducts for leaks. It is a laboratory mock-up prototype with ~86% leak-type precision, so it does not substantiate worker-quality verification of an as-built system in a real building.

sources.system: Fully automatic leak test cell with Fanuc robotic handling
sources.title: Case Study - Fully Automatic Leak Test Cell with Robotic Handling
sources.claim: Commercial fully automatic leak-test cells with robotic handling seal, pressurize and measure air-decay leakage on fixtured parts and automatically segregate pass/fail results without an operator performing the test.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated pressure/air-decay leak verification of manufactured assemblies. It maps onto duct leakage-class verification when the assembly is fixtured and presented to the machine: seal, pressurize, measure leakage, record pass/fail; the difference is workpiece size, not the measurement principle.

sources.system: Automated leak test station / robot-tended leak test cell
sources.title: Automated Leak Test Stations | AMD Machines
sources.claim: Automated leak test stations are production machines that present a part to a sealing fixture, clamp, pressurize through a calibrated path, run a measurement sequence and route the pass/reject result, with robot-tended cell variants available.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fixtured automated leakage verification with documented pass/fail output, the machine-side equivalent of verifying a duct assembly against a specified leakage class.

sources.title: ANYmal - Autonomous Robotic Inspection Solution - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal quadruped performs autonomous inspection rounds in industrial plants, collecting visual, thermal, acoustic and gauge-reading data in complex facilities and feeding it into operator systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous instrument/gauge reading and thermal inspection inside plant rooms, the closest analogue to checking HVAC equipment in a mechanical room. It reads existing displays without contact and does not place reference instruments, take flow-hood readings, adjust dampers, or verify sensor calibration.

tasks.label: Perform building commissioning activities by completing mechanical inspections of a building's water, lighting, or heating, ventilating, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New-construction commissioning walkthrough of HVAC distribution in a commercial/institutional building still under construction: verify installed ductwork, sealing, hangers/seismic bracing, fire/smoke and balancing dampers, access doors, AHU/RTU installation checklists; requires ladders and lifts, opening ceiling tiles or working in open plenums, moving through cluttered, partially finished spaces with other trades present, and completing pre-functional checklists against drawings/specs with a deficiency (punch) list.

Functional performance testing of air-handling and terminal equipment in a substantially complete or occupied building: command AHUs, VAV boxes, exhaust fans and heating equipment through modes via the BAS or local controls, watch damper/valve strokes and actuator travel, trip and verify safeties (freezestat, static pressure, smoke shutdown), record temperatures/pressures/amps with hand instruments, and sign off FPT forms.

Airflow verification / test-and-balance style inspection across many occupied or near-complete rooms: place a capture hood on ceiling diffusers, grilles and exhaust registers, take readings, traverse ducts with a pitot tube or anemometer, adjust balancing dampers above ceilings, and record readings against design CFM in a report.

Mechanical room, penthouse and rooftop inspection of central plant and water systems in an existing institution-controlled building: read pressure/temperature gauges, check pumps and seals for leaks, check strainers, filter differential pressure, belts and coils, verify valve positions, insulation and labeling, take thermal readings, and produce a deficiency report for retro-commissioning.

Verification of lighting controls and domestic water/plumbing items during commissioning of an occupied institutional building: trigger occupancy sensors and daylight dimming in each space, verify sweep schedules and light levels with a meter, check fixture flow and water heater/mixing valve temperatures, and log results.

Residential or light-commercial HVAC/duct performance inspection in a private home: set up a duct blaster/blower door, seal registers, run pressurization tests, inspect attic and crawlspace ductwork for leaks and disconnects, measure supply temperatures, and write up findings for the homeowner or program.

sources.system: Spot with Spot CAM/Orbit (automated visual inspection)
sources.title: Automated Visual Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot performs automated visual inspection rounds in industrial facilities, autonomously collecting imagery of assets and reading analog gauges with integrated models; this is condition-monitoring data capture, not commissioning verification or functional testing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine equipment inspection rounds. It covers only remote sensing of accessible equipment faces; it does not include placing instruments on diffusers, opening access panels, stroking dampers/valves, or verifying sequences of operation against design intent, so it does not transfer to a commissioning mechanical inspection.

sources.system: Spot ('Energy Dog') at Simmering power plant
sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / Wien Energie / Smart Inspection GmbH
sources.title: Spot Makes Austria's Largest Power Plant Safer | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot has run autonomous routine inspection rounds inside a large thermal/district-heating power plant since 2022, reading analog displays and using thermal and gas sensors, and reporting faults autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical plant inspection rounds in a structured facility (E2). Transfer is partial only: the robot follows pre-taught missions and captures gauge/thermal data; it cannot open panels, manipulate valves or dampers, attach test instruments, or complete first-time commissioning checklists against design documents.

sources.system: Spot + FieldAI 'field foundation model' autonomy (DPR Construction jobsites)
sources.title: Case Study: Practical Autonomy on Construction Sites | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot with FieldAI autonomy performs jobsite documentation walks on active construction sites without prior maps, collecting photos and scans across multiple floors for progress and inspection reporting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous construction-site inspection/documentation in an unstructured E3 setting. It substantiates navigation and image/scan capture only; commissioning requires above-ceiling access, instrument placement, equipment operation and pass/fail judgment against specifications, which this system does not perform.

sources.title: TEA-bot: a thermography enabled autonomous robot for detecting thermal leaks of HVAC systems in ceilings
sources.claim: Research prototypes (TEA-bot / AcTEA-bot) autonomously navigate ceiling plenums with thermography to detect HVAC thermal leaks, but remain laboratory/testbed demonstrations with limited autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated thermal-leak detection in HVAC ceiling spaces. It is a single sub-step performed in a scale testbed, not a whole commissioning inspection, and is not deployed in real buildings at worker quality.

sources.developer: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (Jiang, Li, Delgoshaei, Liu, Hong)
sources.title: Robotics for HVAC applications: A critical review and future perspectives | Energy Technologies Area
sources.claim: A 2026 peer-reviewed LBNL-led review of 101 studies of robotics for HVAC applications finds the field is dominated by research-stage inspection/monitoring work, with installation/retrofit and other lifecycle tasks little explored and real-world performance limited.
sources.transferJustification: Field-wide survey used as negative context: it shows no fielded robotic system performs whole-building commissioning inspection or functional performance testing; the reviewed inspection robots are research prototypes or narrow data-capture platforms.

sources.system: Duct Botz / GC Inspection Botz duct inspection robots
sources.title: Duct Inspection Robot, Air Duct Inspections, Robot, Wireless, Camera
sources.claim: Commercially available HVAC duct inspection robots are camera crawlers driven by an operator, transmitting real-time video for the technician to interpret.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior duct inspection. Teleoperated and limited to inside-duct video; cannot support a positive judgment and does not cover functional testing, airflow measurement, or checklist sign-off.

tasks.label: Fasten roof panel edges or machine-made moldings to structures by nailing or welding.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New commercial/industrial building: crew lands standing-seam or exposed-fastener metal roof panels on purlins/deck and fastens panel edges and side laps with screws/nails (clips, sidelap fasteners), working at height on an active construction site with wind, crane deliveries, and long (20-40 ft) panels.

Perimeter and detail work: fastening machine-formed moldings/trim — drip edge, rake and fascia trim, coping, ridge caps, gutter and gravel-stop moldings — by nailing/screwing to the structure at roof edges and transitions on commercial or residential buildings, with hand-cut miters and field-fitting at corners and penetrations.

Residential steep-slope metal roofing (standing seam or metal shingle) on a house: panels and trim fastened to sheathing on varied roof geometry with hips, valleys, dormers and pipe penetrations; scaffold/ladder access, changing weather.

Welded metal roofing/flashing work: seam-welding or brazing stainless/lead-coated copper roof panel edges and flashings in place, or welding clips/edge angles and panel edges to structural steel at the roof deck or curb, on site with a portable welder.

Repair/service on an existing roof: re-fastening wind-lifted panel edges, replacing loose or corroded machine-made moldings, re-nailing drip edge and ridge cap, matching existing profiles on an in-service building.

sources.system: WEINMANN WALLTEQ multifunction bridge (M-120/M-300/M-380/M-500), HOMAG Group
sources.title: WEINMANN multifunction bridges — HOMAG
sources.claim: WEINMANN (HOMAG) multifunction bridges automatically fasten (nail, staple, screw) sheathing/planking onto fixtured wall, ceiling, roof and gable elements in prefabricated-house production lines — i.e., panel edges fastened to a supporting structure by nailing, inside a purpose-built gantry line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated nailing/screwing of panel material and battens to a framed roof/wall element on an assembly table. It is the same physical act as fastening roof panel edges and machine-made moldings to a structure by nailing, at comparable scale and fastener precision, with the workpiece fixtured and presented by the line.

sources.title: Multifunction Bridge WALLTEQ M-500 — HOMAG
sources.claim: A WEINMANN multifunction bridge carries interchangeable fastening tools (screwing, stapling, nailing) plus automatic positioning of battens/laths on fixtured roof and wall elements.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fastening of strip/trim members (battens) and panel material to a framed element; the tool set (nailer, stapler, screwdriver) and placement accuracy match nailing machine-made moldings and panel edges to a structure.

sources.claim: Renovate Robotics' cable-driven Rufus robot autonomously navigates residential roof planes and nails asphalt shingles on real roofing jobs; it does not handle metal roof panels, edge trim or machine-made moldings, and crews remain on site for setup, monitoring and material ....
sources.transferJustification: Closest on-roof (E3) system, but transfer to this task is NOT established: it lays flexible asphalt shingle courses in the roof field, whereas this task requires handling long rigid metal panels, aligning clips/side laps, and field-fitting and nailing perimeter moldings (drip edge, rake, coping, ridge cap).

tasks.label: Finish parts, using hacksaws or hand, rotary, or squaring shears.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop fabrication: cutting flat blanks and panels to finished size on a squaring shear — sheet positioned against a back gauge, sheared to layout dimensions for duct sections, plenums, control-box panels; stacked for the next operation.

Shop fabrication: trimming and notching formed or partly formed parts (elbows, transitions, tapers, round fittings, flashings) to a scribed layout line with aviation snips, throatless/rotary shears or a Beverly shear, including corner notches and curved trims.

Jobsite/field: trimming duct sections, end panels, closures and flashing in place to fit as-built conditions — measured in situ, cut with hand snips or a nibbler while working off a lift, ladder, or in a ceiling space, amid other trades.
Cutting stock to length with a hacksaw or portable/benchtop saw: hanger and threaded rod, angle iron, duct stiffeners, small pipe and tube for supports.
Finishing cut edges before assembly: deburring, filing and dressing sheared or sawn edges, removing burrs and slivers, hemming/safing sharp edges on finished parts.

sources.system: Salvagnini S4 punching-shearing machine (with PD destacker / IA stacker automation)
sources.date: 2026-07 (product page retrieved; product line long commercial)

sources.transferJustification: Same operation as the worker's squaring-shear cut: sheet steel/aluminum of gauge thickness sheared to a programmed dimension, with the machine (not a person) positioning the workpiece.

sources.claim: FANUC's high-precision M-800iA/60 laser processing robot is offered for laser trimming of hot-stamped sheet metal components in production stamping shops.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic trimming of formed sheet metal parts to a contour, equivalent to trimming formed fittings with hand or rotary shears; demonstrates path accuracy adequate for finish trim cuts.

sources.claim: Voortman VB CNC bandsaws perform automated straight and miter cutting of structural steel with a full-stop measuring truck that automatically advances material to the next cut length, and can run inside a fully automated integrated processing line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sawing bar, angle and tube stock to length — the machine equivalent of the worker's hacksaw cuts on hanger rod, angle and stiffener stock, with the same tolerance requirements.

sources.title: Deburring is a job that can be easily automated | Teqram
sources.claim: Teqram's EasyDebur robotic cell uses AI vision to identify each workpiece, select a gripper, load and flip parts through a deburring machine without programming, teaching or special fixtures.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the edge-finishing part of the task: removing burrs and sharp edges from laser-cut, punched or flame-cut sheet metal parts, the same finishing the worker does with a file or deburring tool.

sources.title: How vision-guided automation is reshaping high-mix metal fabrication | The Fabricator
sources.claim: A Dutch fabricator has vision-guided robots in production feeding a flat-part deburring machine, sorting cut blanks, and automating plate edge grinding and deslagging in high-mix sheet metal work.

sources.system: FANUC material removal robots / BF-X 500 robotic finishing cell
sources.title: Robotic Cutting, Deburring, Polishing, Buffing & More | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC markets material-removal robots for cutting and finishing metal parts, including plasma and waterjet cutting, deburring, grinding and polishing, and offers a robotic finishing cell built around an M-20iB/25 robot.

roles.title: Structural Iron and Steel Workers
roles.description: Raise, place, and unite iron or steel girders, columns, and other structural members to form completed structures or structural frameworks. May erect metal storage tanks and assemble prefabricated metal buildings.

tasks.label: Read specifications or blueprints to determine the locations, quantities, or sizes of materials required.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Verify vertical and horizontal alignment of structural steel members, using plumb bobs, laser equipment, transits, or levels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Multi-story commercial/institutional steel frame, raising and plumbing-up gang: as columns and beams are hung by crane and temporarily bolted, the worker checks column plumb with a plumb bob, optical plumb or laser and beam level, working on open steel at height and sighting from floors below, and calls turnbuckle/come-along adjustments before final bolt-up. Live crane picks, wind, layout changing hour to hour.

Pre-engineered metal building, warehouse or low-rise frame: two- to four-person crew checks column plumb, rafter and purlin/girt alignment with 4-ft spirit levels, self-leveling laser levels, string lines and tape, working from scissor/boom lifts and a partly poured slab on a muddy, weather-exposed site.

Bridge or heavy-highway girder erection: verifying girder line, elevation, bearing seating and cross-frame/diaphragm alignment with levels, transits or a total station, often at night over traffic, water or rail, with checks taken while the crane still holds the piece.

Industrial/plant steel: verifying plumbness of pipe-rack and equipment-support columns or field-erected tank shell courses with plumb bob, laser and transit at an operating or under-construction plant; congested, at height, frequent obstructions and overhead work.

Post-erection alignment check of a completed tier or bay with metal deck or slab in place: setting up a transit/total station or laser, checking column plumbness and beam elevations against AISC Code of Standard Practice tolerances, recording results, and signing the bay off before final bolt-up or handoff. Structure is stable and floors are walkable.

Fabricator's shop or laydown yard: checking squareness, straightness and fitting alignment of an assembled member or trial-fit subassembly with level, square, tape and laser before shipment or before it is hoisted.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot + Trimble X7 (Trimble FieldLink)
sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / Trimble (deployed by Hensel Phelps)
sources.title: Exploring the use of bio-inspired autonomous robots in construction
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot carrying a Trimble X7 laser scanner performed autonomous walk-and-scan missions on the Denver International Airport Great Hall construction project for Hensel Phelps; scans (2 mm accuracy, self-leveling, auto-registered in the field) were compared to the BIM model to identify deviations from design.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous as-built capture and BIM comparison on a construction site. It transfers to verifying alignment of erected members because the deliverable is the same measurement of built geometry against design, at 2 mm scan accuracy, in the same setting.

sources.system: Trimble X7 + Boston Dynamics Spot autonomous scanning workflow
sources.title: Trimble goes laser scanning with Boston's robot dog - Construction Management
sources.claim: Trimble commercially integrated the X7 scanner and FieldLink with Spot so that scheduled missions follow a predefined waypoint path and collect scans autonomously, tied to the jobsite project coordinate system, for design validation and progress ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous scheduled reality capture referenced to site control. Transfer holds because verifying member alignment requires exactly this georeferenced capture, and the missions are repeated on a schedule without an operator walking the instrument.

sources.title: Verity verifies as-built point cloud data meets design specs (Topcon Positioning)
sources.claim: ClearEdge3D Verity is commercial software that automatically compares as-built point clouds to design and fabrication models and flags installed work that is out of specified tolerance, producing deviation reports and heat maps; it supplies the automated analysis step for robot-captured scans.
sources.transferJustification: Not a robot itself; cited only as the automated analysis component that turns a robot-captured point cloud into the pass/fail alignment verdict the task requires.

sources.title: Robotic Welding for Structural Steel Fabrication | PeddiAssembler | Peddinghaus
sources.claim: The Peddinghaus PeddiAssembler is a commercial robotic structural-steel cell in which a handling robot, a parts-scanning robot and an ABB tacking/welding robot assemble beams, tubes and channels up to 60 ft with fixtured turning devices; the standard Envision system performs 3D measurement and automated inspection of the assembled member.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated dimensional inspection of assembled structural steel members held in fixtures. Objects (wide-flange beams, channels, tubes up to 60 ft) and the checked quantity (position/alignment of members and fittings to about 1 mm) match the verification this task requires, in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Bluewrist inline robotic 3D vision inspection cell
sources.title: Automated 3D Inspection System Detects Weld Defects | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: An automotive OEM deployed a Bluewrist inline 3D inspection system using two FANUC six-axis robots and 3D laser profile sensors to continuously measure welded sheet-steel assemblies in a fixtured production cell and flag defects and dimensional deviations against CAD.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated in-line dimensional verification of welded steel structures brought to the machine in fixtures. Transfers because the measurement (member position/alignment versus model) and precision exceed what steel-erection tolerance checks demand.

sources.title: Built Robotics develops autonomous pile driving system (Heavy Equipment Guide)
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 is a fully ... solar piling system that surveys, distributes and drives steel H-pile foundations on open utility-scale solar sites, with a robotic stabilizer holding piles to plumb and sub-inch position tolerance; a two-person crew supervises over 300 piles per day.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous field measurement and plumb control of a steel member on an unstructured outdoor site. Transfer is partial only: the machine controls plumb of the pile it is itself holding, and does not verify independently erected members.

sources.title: Simulation Study of an Autonomous Steel Bolting Robot - ICCEPM
sources.claim: Autonomous robots for bolting steel structural members remain at the design-and-simulation stage in the research literature, with no fielded system performing in-erection connection or alignment work on steel frames.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as negative context: work on the erected frame during steel erection is not yet performed by fielded robots, so no system supports the in-erection plumbing-up checks at E2 or E3.

tasks.label: Erect metal or precast concrete components for structures, such as buildings, bridges, dams, towers, storage tanks, fences, or highway guard rails.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Structural steel frame erection on a commercial/industrial building site: crane hoists wide-flange columns, beams and joists; connectors ride the iron or work from lifts at height, spud-wrench the members into bolt holes, install and torque bolts, plumb and cable the frame; weather, congested laydown, and changing crane picks throughout the day.

Bridge and highway structure erection: setting steel plate girders, cross-frames and diaphragms (or precast concrete beams) over roadways or water from cranes, often at night under traffic control; bolting splices and bracing at height on a site whose layout changes each pick.

Precast concrete component erection at a building site: rigging and landing multi-ton wall panels, double tees and columns onto bearing pads/embed plates, aligning to survey marks, shimming, bracing, and welding or grouting connections.

Pre-engineered/light metal building assembly: bolting rigid-frame columns and rafters, purlins, girts and bracing for warehouses, agricultural and small commercial buildings on a graded pad, then sheeting; work at moderate height from lifts, outdoors.

Towers, stacks and storage tanks: stacking and bolting transmission or communication tower sections, erecting tank shell plates/roof structures in the field, working at height from the structure itself with tag lines and rigging.

Ground-level linear metal work: installing highway guardrail (driving posts, hanging blockouts and W-beam rails, splice bolting, end terminals), site perimeter fencing, handrail and barrier along roadways and site boundaries, with varied terrain, curves and live traffic.

sources.system: Zeman Steel Beam Assembler (SBA) / Steel Beam Welder
sources.developer: Zeman Bauelemente / Lincoln Electric (installed at CPE Construction)
sources.title: ZEMAN Steel Beam Assembly (SBA) Robot

tasks.label: Bolt aligned structural steel members in position for permanent riveting, bolting, or welding into place.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Multi-story building frame, raising gang: the crane lands a beam on column seats; the connector, tied off on the steel or in a boom lift 30-200 ft up, spuds the holes into line with a drift pin and drives in and snugs two erection bolts at each end so the crane can be released. Wind, mill tolerances, swinging load.

Bolting-up gang on a building frame: following the raising gang through completed bays, filling out the remaining holes in shear tabs, moment plates, gussets and brace connections with high-strength bolts and snugging/tensioning them (TC bolts, turn-of-nut, DTI washers) from beams, ladders and lifts, often overhead and in awkward postures.

Pre-engineered metal building or light industrial frame: bolting rafter splices, column base plates, eave struts, purlins, girts and rod bracing from scissor/boom lifts over a slab or dirt pad; hundreds of small bolts, members held by crane or temporary bracing until bolted.

Bridge and heavy civil steel: bolting field splices in plate girders, cross frames and diaphragms - hundreds to thousands of high-strength bolts per splice - from suspended platforms, man baskets or snoopers over traffic or water, frequently in night lane closures.

Ground pre-assembly in the site laydown yard: bolting trusses, stair towers, joist girders and cross-frames together on cribbing or horses before the pick, working at grade with air impacts and spud wrenches, parts shifted by forklift or crane.

Retrofit / miscellaneous steel inside an existing structure: bolting mezzanine framing, seismic braces, equipment support steel and hangers to existing columns and beams in an occupied or partly finished building, tight access, overhead work off ladders and lifts.

tasks.label: Assemble or inspect hoisting equipment or rigging, such as cables, pulleys, or hooks, to move heavy equipment or materials.
Lift steel beams, girders, or columns using cranes or forklifts, or by signaling hoisting equipment operators to lift or position structural steel members.
Fabricate metal parts, such as steel frames, columns, beams, or girders, according to blueprints or instructions from supervisors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In the contractor's or fabricator's shop: rolled sections (W-beams, columns, channels, tube) are cut to length, coped, beveled, and drilled/punched to the hole pattern shown on shop drawings, then marked and stacked for the next station. Steady work, overhead crane and forklift handling, standard shop tooling.

In the shop: laying out and fitting connection material — shear tabs, clip angles, stiffeners, base and cap plates — onto beams and columns per shop drawings, tacking, then finish welding out the member and grinding it to an acceptable weld profile before it ships.

Shop fabrication of miscellaneous and custom items from a sketch or a supervisor's verbal instruction: brackets, embeds, hangers, shim packs, ladders, handrail sections, small built-up frames — cut from plate/angle/pipe, fit, and weld, usually one-off or a few of a kind.

Field fabrication at the construction site: measuring as-built conditions, then torch-cutting, beveling, drilling, and welding to make or modify a connection part (filler plate, clip, stiffener, brace end) so an erected member fits. Done on the deck, on staging, or at elevation, in weather, around other trades.

Pre-assembly in the jobsite laydown yard: fabricating sub-assemblies on blocking before hoisting — bracing frames, truss or girder sections, stair stringers, column trees — laying out to the erection drawings, fitting, bolting and welding, on uneven ground with mobile crane support.

tasks.label: Connect columns, beams, and girders with bolts, following blueprints and instructions from supervisors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Raising-gang connector on a multi-story commercial/industrial steel frame: rides the load or works from a beam/column at height, catches the incoming beam from the crane, spuds and drift-pins the holes into line at the column seat or shear tab, and installs and snugs the erection bolts before releasing the choker. Wind, swinging loads, tiered floors, changing layout each pick.

Bolt-up (detail) gang finishing connections behind the raising gang on the same building frames: from a boom lift, scaffold, or the steel itself, inserting the full complement of high-strength (often torshear/TC) bolts with washers and nuts into beam-to-column and beam-to-girder connections, snug-tightening, marking, then final tensioning to spec and passing inspection.

Bridge/heavy-civil bolt-up: field splices of plate or box girders and cross-frame/diaphragm connections, thousands of high-strength bolts per splice, worked outdoors from under-bridge platforms or lifts over traffic or water, in weather, with torque/tension verification and documentation.

Pre-engineered metal building or light structural erection on an open site: bolting rafter-to-column moment connections, splice plates, purlins and girts and bracing, mostly from scissor/boom lifts on uneven ground, small crew, blueprint-driven bolt patterns.

Ground-level pre-assembly in the site laydown area: bolting truss or girder sections, column splices, base plates and bracing together on cribbing before the pick, using impact wrenches and torque verification, with members handled by forklift or crane.

tasks.label: Pull, push, or pry structural steel members into approximate positions for bolting into place.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-steel connecting on a multi-story commercial frame: the crane swings a 1–5 ton beam to a column connection; connectors working aloft (astride the steel or from an aerial lift) pull, push and pry the member with spud wrenches and drift pins against wind and load swing until the bolt holes line up and two bolts are started.

Column setting and plumbing-up on an active site: columns dropped onto anchor bolts/splice plates are pushed, pried and barred over shims into approximate position; come-alongs, turnbuckles, wedges and sledges pull the bay square and plumb before final bolt-up. Ground or floor-deck level, weather exposed.

Pre-engineered metal building / secondary steel: joists, purlins, girts, rafters and bracing (50–600 lb) levered into line with sleever bars and drift pins from scissor lifts or from the joists, on semi-rural sites with uneven ground and variable weather.

Bridge and heavy-civil steel: multi-ton girder sections, splice plates and cross-frames brought into alignment with drift pins, jacks, come-alongs and bars over traffic or water, to tight faying-surface and camber tolerances before bolt-up.

Ground-level shakeout and pre-assembly in the site laydown area: trusses, stair towers, frames and tank/plate sections blocked up on dunnage and pried, pulled and barred into alignment for bolting before being flown into place; layout differs job to job.

Fit-up inside a fabrication shop or fab yard (ironworkers doing shop pre-assembly): members and connection fittings delivered by overhead crane to assembly stands, aligned, clamped and pinned for bolting or welding on a fixed-layout, institution-controlled floor.

sources.title: Zeman - Steel Beam Assembler
sources.claim: The Zeman Steel Beam Assembler is a commercial robotic cell in which robots pick structural steel add-on parts weighing up to 200 kg and position them on a main beam directly from 3D model data, then tack and weld them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: positioning structural steel components into a specified position on another member and holding them there for joining. Same physical act as fit-up (bringing a steel member into position relative to a mating member), same objects (structural sections, plates, brackets), and tighter precision than 'approximate position for bolting'; only the fastening method (weld vs bolt) differs, and fastening is outside this task.
