tasks.label: Unload and position prefabricated steel units for hoisting, as needed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Building erection jobsite: flatbed truck arrives with structural beams and columns. Ironworker releases chains/binders, climbs the load, rigs chokers/shackles or beam clamps, signals the crane, guides the piece off the trailer, lands it on dunnage in the laydown area, unhooks. Congested urban site, mud/gravel, weather, other trades present.

Shake-out in the laydown yard: members already offloaded are sorted, turned, and repositioned into erection sequence with a crane or telehandler; blocking and cribbing set; pieces oriented with the connection ends and piece marks facing correctly, tag lines and lifting clutches attached so the raising gang can pick them.

Secondary/bundled prefabricated units — open-web joists, metal deck bundles, girts, purlins, pre-engineered metal building kit components — unloaded from trailers by crane or forklift and staged near the pick point or landed directly on the frame in bundles.

Heavy prefabricated assemblies: bridge plate girders, roof trusses, tank shell courses or prefab pipe-rack modules delivered on lowboys to a bridge, highway or industrial site; unloaded with one or two cranes, set on cribbing, dogged down and oriented for the erection pick, often under traffic control or in a live plant.

Contractor-controlled fabrication/staging yard: steel is received, offloaded from trucks, sorted into racks or shipping sequence, and re-loaded/positioned for the next haul; fixed layout, standing overhead crane or yard forklift, institution controls who enters.

sources.system: Voortman V631 / Multi System Integration (MSI) beam line
sources.date: 2025 (product line in commercial use for years)
sources.title: Voortman V631 | CNC Beam Milling and Drilling Line
sources.claim: Voortman's beam-processing lines move full-size structural profiles automatically between machines with sensored drag-dogs, liftables and cross transports under VACAM control, i.e. the machine positions the steel member itself without an operator handling it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated in-line handling/positioning of structural beams. Same objects (wide-flange profiles up to ~60 ft), same act (bring a member to a defined position and orientation for the next lift/operation), in a purpose-built machine environment.

sources.title: ZEMAN Steel Beam Assembly (SBA) Robot
sources.claim: The Zeman SBA / PeddiAssembler robotic beam assembler uses a scanning robot and a magnetic handling robot to pick loose steel fittings up to 440 lb off a table and position them accurately on all four faces of a beam before tacking; installed and commissioned in commercial fabrication shops.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic pick-and-place of steel members/parts. Demonstrates autonomous magnetic gripping, scanning-based localization and accurate positioning of unfixtured steel pieces, the manipulation core of positioning prefabricated steel units, in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: KASTO UNICOMPACT 5.0 / KASTOecostore automated bar storage
sources.title: Automated Steel Storage System for SPS
sources.claim: KASTO automated long-goods storage systems (e.g. UNICOMPACT 5.0 at Steel and Pipe Supply) store and retrieve bundled steel bars and profiles with automatic stacker cranes, handing bundles to a bridge crane with a magnetic lifting device at the loading/unloading station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling and positioning of bundled long steel product. Same class of object (multi-ton bundles of bars/profiles) and same act (retrieve, transport, deposit at a defined station for the next lift), in a machine-dedicated warehouse.

sources.system: Konecranes automated coil handling cranes with Warehouse Management System
sources.date: 2025 (commercial product; automated coil warehouses in operation)
sources.title: Warehouse Management for Coil Storage Efficiency | Konecranes
sources.claim: Konecranes automated coil-warehouse cranes identify and handle steel coils and can perform truck and rail loading/unloading automatically under warehouse-management control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated crane offloading of heavy steel units from road vehicles and placement in a storage position. Same act as unloading prefabricated steel for later hoisting, but in a machine-dedicated automated crane bay with standardized lifting attachments.

sources.title: Automation for the steel industry | Konecranes
sources.claim: Fully automated overhead cranes are routine in steel plants for heavy loads such as slabs and casting operations, showing multi-ton automated pick-and-place is established in machine-dedicated bays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated crane handling of very heavy steel units (slabs). Supports that the weight class of bridge girders and heavy prefab assemblies is not the limiting factor in a purpose-built setting.

sources.title: Shimizu to deploy robots for high-rise building work in Osaka
sources.claim: Shimizu's jobsite robots represent the frontier of construction-site autonomy: Robo-Carrier moves materials horizontally and via the temporary elevator unmanned, and Robo-Welder welds steel columns, but neither offloads delivery trucks nor rigs and shakes out structural members.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound E3: the most advanced deployed building-site material-handling robot moves palletized supplies on completed floors; it does not release binders, rig chokers, or position multi-ton members for a crane pick.

sources.date: 2023 (first project, Port St. Lucie West Blvd Bridge); ongoing commercial use
sources.title: ACR reveals IronBot, a rebar-placing robot, at ConExpo
sources.claim: IronBOT lifts, carries and places ... bundles up to 5,000 lb on bridge decks, but the machine is positioned on the jobsite by a supervisor with a remote control rather than navigating and rigging autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing heavy steel bundles on a construction site. Cited to show that even this closest jobsite analogue relies on remote positioning and a prepared deck with rails, so it cannot substantiate autonomous E3 completion.

tasks.label: Fasten structural steel members to hoist cables, using chains, cables, or rope.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial building erection: ironworker in the laydown yard selects wire-rope or chain slings and shackles, chokes or basket-hitches a 2–15 ton wide-flange beam or column, judges the center of gravity, hooks the sling eyes onto the crane block, attaches tag lines, and signals the pick. Muddy or uneven ground, mixed dunnage stacks, changing weather, other trades moving nearby.

Heavy or awkward pick on a bridge, stadium, industrial or storage-tank project: multi-point rigging of a plate girder, truss, tank shell course or crane runway beam using shackles at engineered lifting lugs, spreader/equalizer beams, turnbuckles and multiple slings, matched to an engineered lift plan; sometimes tandem cranes.

Bundled and miscellaneous loads on a pre-engineered metal building or warehouse job: choking bundles of bar joists, purlins, roof-deck sheets, bolt baskets and loose secondary steel with nylon or wire slings onto the hoist line off a delivery truck or the laydown area.

Rigging released or reset at height: after a piece is landed and bolted, the connector standing on the steel or in a man basket unhooks the choker from the member and sends the ball back, or re-rigs a member that must be repositioned/rotated in the air.

Fabrication shop or shipping yard: hooking finished members and assemblies to an overhead bridge crane or yard crane with chains, chokers and lifting clamps to shake out, turn over, or load pieces onto trucks for shipment; fixed bays, standard equipment, institution controls access.

Work inside an existing controlled industrial facility (mill, power plant, plant shutdown/retrofit): rigging structural members and equipment supports to the house overhead crane or a chain hoist in a congested but institutionally controlled indoor bay.

sources.system: Morgan Automation automated coil-yard cranes (Morgan Cephas, Siemens controls)
sources.title: US steel mill installs fully automated cranes system - Hoist
sources.claim: A fully automated, unmanned three-crane system at a US steel mill in ... autonomously engages individual 28-ton hot coils with a hoist-mounted grab, moves and places them on saddles or transfer cars, with personnel locked out of the crane quadrants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: securing a heavy steel load to a hoist and releasing it. The grab autonomously engages and releases 28-ton steel loads presented in known positions inside a personnel-excluded crane yard — the purpose-built-environment analog of fastening a structural member to the hoist line, with comparable load weight and the same start-to-finish attach/lift/release cycle.

sources.title: RZR™ Rig Floor Automation Module - Nabors
sources.claim: Canrig's RZR rig floor module with the iRacker robot autonomously grips and handles multi-ton steel tubulars up to 20 in. diameter and presents them at well center hands-free, with crews removed from the red zone; Nabors fully automated an existing land rig (Rig X29, Permian Basin) with it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: latching heavy long steel members and delivering them to the hoist (top drive/elevators). Objects are tons-scale steel of similar length to structural members, engagement and release are machine-controlled, and the work zone is a purpose-built floor from which people are excluded — matching the E1 counterfactual for rigging a member to a hoist.

sources.system: KASTOpick bar (with KASTO automated long-goods storage)
sources.title: Twin-robot KASTOpick bar system for automatically picking up randomly | Handling-Network.com
sources.claim: KASTOpick bar uses a pair of robots with 3D scanning and magnetic grippers to autonomously pick randomly oriented steel bars, tubes and profiles from storage cassettes in steel stockholders' automated warehouses, selecting gripping points without teach-in.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: attaching a steel member to a powered lifting device. The system perceives unfixtured steel long products, chooses attachment points and engages them autonomously — the perception-and-engagement half of rigging — but only inside an enclosed automated storage cell and at loads around 500 kg in the standard version.

sources.system: Roborigger wireless release hook / Ludwig Hook
sources.title: Hooks, Cameras & Accessories - Roborigger
sources.claim: State-of-the-art rigging aids for construction cranes still depend on an operator: the Roborigger/Ludwig wireless release hook releases landed loads at the push of a ... on a remote control, and slings must still be placed on the load by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about the same task (attaching and releasing loads on a construction crane hook): it shows that the commercially available construction-site technology automates only the release step under continuous operator command, so it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous field rigging.

sources.developer: Tilbury Douglas (robot supplier unnamed in report)
sources.title: First humanoid robot on a construction site launched to assist teams
sources.claim: The first humanoid robots put on live construction sites in 2026 are deployed to support site teams with administrative and support duties, not to rig or handle structural steel.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the current state of general-purpose robots on unstructured construction sites; it establishes that no fielded humanoid or mobile manipulator performs load rigging there, supporting the negative E3 judgments.

tasks.label: Cut, bend, or weld steel pieces, using metal shears, torches, or welding equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field welding of column splices / column-to-base connections on an erected steel frame at a building site: thick-plate CJP groove welds on standing columns, backing bars and ceramic tabs, weather exposure, welds subject to UT inspection.

Field welding of beam-to-column moment and shear connections and other member-to-member joints at elevation: welder works from a lift, scaffold or the beam itself, out-of-position (vertical/overhead) welds around weld access holes, variable fit-up, wind and rain.

Field torch cutting (oxy-fuel/plasma) of erected or staged members: trimming beam ends and gussets to make a misfit connection fit, burning holes/slots, cutting off temporary erection lugs, seats and shipping clips, cutting members loose on retrofit work.

Deck- and ground-level welding on the active site: shear studs to beams, embed and base plates, deck puddle welds, welding stairs, landings, handrail, angle and miscellaneous iron in place among other trades.

Site laydown/fab area at grade: cutting stock to length with torch, band saw or shears; bending plate, strap, and small shapes in a portable bender or by heat; making up small pieces and connection material on site.

Fabrication shop or prefab assembly yard work performed by the erector's crew: cutting members to length and bevel, and welding clips, stiffeners, gussets and plates to members before shipment or lift.

sources.title: Shimizu Begins Collaborating People and Autonomous Robots at Construction Site, Toranomon-Azabudai Project
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Welder, an AI-equipped autonomous welding robot, was put into operation on an actual Tokyo high-rise construction site welding the groove joints of standing steel columns, including 100 mm thick column plates, with laser groove-shape sensing driving the torch.

sources.title: Path Robotics raises $100M to automate welding - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Path Robotics' AW-3 and AF-1 robotic welding cells autonomously scan and weld steel parts, including parts up to ~70 ft long, and are in commercial use in fabrication shops in the US and Canada.

sources.system: BeamMaster robotic beam welding cell (FANUC Arc Mate robots, Cortex software)
sources.developer: AGT Robotics / FANUC America (user: Steelway Building Systems)
sources.title: Steelway Boosts Beam Welding Productivity with New Robotic Integration | FANUC America
sources.claim: Steel building manufacturer Steelway installed AGT Robotics' BeamMaster cell with dual FANUC Arc Mate robots, which welds all four sides of built-up beams (three-plate beams up to 60 ft) with auto-programming from model files, replacing manual welding labor in production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shop welding of plates/attachments to beams. Same joints, materials and code-quality welds that ironworkers make on connection material; transfer is to the welding portion of the task with the member clamped and presented to the machine.

sources.system: PeddiBot-1250ST / PeddiBot-1250 robotic CNC beam coper
sources.title: Robotic CNC Beam Coper | PeddiBot-1250ST | Peddinghaus
sources.claim: Peddinghaus sells robotic CNC beam copers that plasma and oxy-fuel cut, cope, bevel and mark structural members fed and clamped in the machine line, using a camera system that measures material deviation and adapts the cutting path.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: thermal cutting of structural steel (coping, hole burning, bevelling, trimming to length) — the same oxy-fuel/plasma cuts ironworkers make with a torch, performed on members clamped and conveyed into the machine.

sources.system: ARCMAN welding robot series with SENSARC power sources
sources.title: Kobelco's ARCMAN welding robots and SENSARC power sources (Technical Highlight Vol.7)
sources.claim: Kobe Steel's ARCMAN robotic arc welding systems, with groove-searching sensors, positioners and sliders, are used in production for medium- and heavy-thick plate welding of building steel structures and bridges.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: multipass heavy-plate structural welding in a fixtured cell — the same thick-section groove and fillet welds required at structural connections, showing robotic systems reach code-quality on this joint class when the work is presented to them.

sources.title: Automated Press Brake, Robotic Press Brake | B3 | Salvagnini
sources.claim: Salvagnini supplies robotized bending cells in which a robot manages all handling and bending on the press brake unattended, forming sheet and plate parts to program.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bending steel stock. Ironworkers bend plate, strap and small shapes; a robotized press-brake cell performs the same forming operation when the blank is presented to the machine.

tasks.label: Force structural steel members into final positions, using turnbuckles, crowbars, jacks, or hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Connector on a multi-story/high-rise steel frame: a crane holds a beam near a column at elevation; the ironworker straddles the steel or works from a lift, swings and pries the member with a spud wrench and bull/drift pins, forces the connection holes into line, and installs fit-up bolts. Open site, wind, weather, mill tolerances, no two connections identical.

Bolt-up / detail crew working behind the raising gang on the erected frame: misaligned holes at beam-to-column and beam-to-beam connections are drawn into position with sledges, pry bars, come-alongs, drift pins and small jacks so bolts can be driven and torqued; access from decking, ladders or MEWPs.

Plumbing up and squaring the frame: rigging plumbing-up cables with turnbuckles and come-alongs between columns, tensioning and releasing them under instrument/laser or transit feedback until columns are plumb and bays are square, then holding the bracing until final connections are made.

Bridge / heavy-civil erection: girder segments, cross-frames, diaphragms and splice plates are drawn into alignment with hydraulic jacks, come-alongs, drift pins and bars, often over water, traffic or uneven ground, with camber and temperature movement to fight.

Pre-engineered metal building or light structural work on a low-rise slab site: rafters, purlins, girts, eave struts and X-bracing forced into position with drift pins, pry bars, ratchet straps and hand tools, working from lifts or ladders in a partially cluttered site.

Ground-level or shop pre-assembly: sub-assemblies (truss sections, stair stringers, girder web/flange fit-up, handrail and embed assemblies) laid out on horses or jigs in a fabrication shop or lay-down yard and forced into final position with clamps, dogs, wedges and jacks before welding or bolting.

sources.system: Zeman Steel Beam Assembler (SBA) robotic fitting/welding line
sources.developer: Zeman Bauelemente (marketed with Peddinghaus / Lincoln Electric)
sources.title: Flexible automation meets structural fabrication
sources.claim: Zeman Steel Beam Assembler robotic lines installed at US structural fabricators (Lexicon, Prospect Steel) automate fitting as well as welding: a part-handling robot scans randomly placed cut parts on a table, matches them to the 3D model, carries each part to the conveyor-fed beam, positions and secures it, while the welding robot scans and makes fit-up adjustments for mill tolerances before tacking and welding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shop fit-up of structural steel. The robot delivers the same output as the fitter's 'force the member into final position and secure it' step - bringing steel parts to the modelled position, correcting fit-up within mill tolerance, holding them there - but only inside a fenced, conveyor-fed cell with the beam fixtured on a rotating table.

sources.system: 3-in-1 H-beam assembly machine (assembly / welding / straightening line)
sources.developer: ZMDE Steel Machinery (comparable lines from Jinggong, Yomi)
sources.title: What Is a 3-in-1 H Beam Machine and How It Works
sources.claim: Commercial CNC H-beam assembly machines automatically centre, clamp and force web and flange plates into their final relative position with hydraulic/servo-driven pressure and then tack weld them - multi-ton steel members forced into final position under machine control in a purpose-built line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: forcing steel plate members into final assembled position before tacking. Comparable objects (multi-ton structural sections) and comparable forcing action (hydraulic clamping against mill tolerance), but only with the work fed on a roller line and held by fixtures.

sources.title: H Beam Assembling Machine | JINGGONG
sources.claim: A second vendor line confirms that automatic alignment, clamping and tack welding of web and flange plates is standard commercial equipment in fabrication plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shop fit-up/forcing of steel members into final position; the alignment force is applied by fixtures and hydraulics in a purpose-built line, not by a machine working an erected frame.

sources.title: Shimizu Begins Collaborating People and Autonomous Robots at Construction Site, Toranomon-Azabudai Project
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Welder has been used on a live Tokyo high-rise site (Toranomon-Azabudai) welding steel column splices; in the Smart Site concept a crane holds the column in position while the robot welds - the robot does not align or force the member into position.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-site work on erected steel. It shows the most advanced deployed site robot for steel frames performs welding on members already held in final position by crane and connectors, providing no capability for forcing or aligning members; it therefore does not substantiate the task at E3.

sources.system: RAS robotic assembly system for steel structure erection and assembly
sources.developer: academic research group (Int. J. Intelligent Robotics and Applications)
sources.title: RAS: a robotic assembly system for steel structure erection and assembly
sources.claim: Research on robotic steel-frame erection and bolting remains laboratory scale and requires the connection itself to be redesigned (extra guide holes above each bolt hole) for a robot to achieve alignment.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task (bringing a beam into final connected position); cited as evidence that autonomous alignment of steel members is a redesigned-connection laboratory capability rather than a field capability.

sources.system: JLG 'Job Site of the Future' semi-autonomous MEWP demonstration
sources.title: JLG Technology Strategy 2026: ClearSky, Automation, and Smart Equipment
sources.claim: The state of the art shown at CONEXPO 2026 for moving and placing a steel beam was a staged booth demonstration with semi-autonomous scissor lifts and a boom-mounted welding end-effector supervised by a single operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transporting and positioning a steel beam for installation. Cited as non-supporting context: operator-supervised, staged on a trade-show floor, and stopping at placement rather than forcing the member into its final connected position.

tasks.label: Ride on girders or other structural steel members to position them, or use rope to guide them into position.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Multi-story commercial/institutional building frame: an ironworker on the deck or ground holds a tag line on a 20-40 ft wide-flange beam as the crane swings it into the bay, checks spin and pendulum in wind, walks it past columns, hoses and other trades, and guides it down onto the seats where connectors take it.

Connector work at elevation: the ironworker perched on a column top or straddling the erected beam receives the suspended member, sometimes riding the load or a hoisted member to reach the point, and hand-guides or short-ropes it into the connection so drift pins can be driven; harnessed, exposed, wind and swing are the hazards.

Heavy/long-span work: bridge plate girders, trusses or heavy industrial members handled with two tag lines by a ground crew, often tandem crane picks, over live roadway, water or a plant yard, frequently on night shifts or short closures, with the member landed on bearings or splice points.

Pre-engineered metal building, warehouse or big-box job: lighter rafters, columns, joist bundles and purlins guided by rope from the ground or from a lift, many nearly identical bays, muddy open site, small crew, fast repetitive cycles.

Miscellaneous, retrofit and tank work: stair towers, equipment platforms, mezzanine steel or tank shell plates guided with hand lines, come-alongs and tag lines through tight access inside or alongside an existing structure, with non-standard pieces and improvised rigging points.

sources.title: Robotic Welding for Structural Steel Fabrication | PeddiAssembler | Peddinghaus
sources.claim: Commercial robotic structural-steel assembly cell (ABB robots) autonomously scans loose steel parts, picks them with a magnetic gripper and positions them on beams, columns and tubes to model tolerance, then tack welds; handles parts to 440 lb on profiles to 60 ft and 11,000 lb.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic fit-up of structural steel in a fabrication cell. The machine performs the same function the tag-line worker performs at E1 scale - bringing a steel member into its mating position against another structural member and holding it there until it is joined - on the same class of objects (beams, columns, tubes, connection plates) and to tighter precision than manual fitting.

sources.title: Flexible automation meets structural fabrication
sources.claim: A US fabricator (Lexicon) runs a Zeman Steel Beam Assembler line in which conveyors feed beams to the cell, the robot scans the beam to find its zero point, and the robots fit and assemble parts that operators dumped on a table in no particular order.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fitting of structural steel members. Positioning parts to a beam per the 3D model, with the workpiece brought to the machine on a conveyor, is the E1 form of guiding a member into position; the parts are unfixtured and located by robot scanning, so it is not a blind scripted pick.

sources.title: Zeman - Steel Beam Assembler
sources.claim: The Zeman SBA is a mature commercial product line handling parts up to 200 kg with direct 3D data flow to ... and no teaching, with dozens of lines installed worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (robotic fit-up of structural steel); cited to establish that the capability is fielded at scale rather than a one-off demonstration.

sources.system: Zeman Steel Beam Assembly (SBA) robot at CPE Construction
sources.title: ZEMAN Steel Beam Assembly (SBA) Robot
sources.claim: An Australian steel fabricator commissioned a Zeman SBA robot in 2024 with automated infeed/outfeed; robotic arms position stiffeners, brackets and other components ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic positioning of steel members onto a beam in a purpose-built cell, i.e. the E1 form of guiding a member into position for connection.

sources.system: Konecranes Automated Stacking Cranes with Active Load Control
sources.title: Konecranes to deliver 20 Automated Stacking Cranes to Global Terminal in USA
sources.claim: Automated stacking cranes with 40 t capacity operate unmanned in fenced automated blocks at container terminals, using automatic sway control and horizontal fine ... to land heavy suspended loads without a ground crew on tag lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous placement of a heavy crane-suspended load. The tag-line worker's function is damping spin/pendulum and steering the suspended load to its landing point; ALC-equipped ASCs do exactly that for 40 t loads, but only inside a purpose-built, fenced, human-excluded automation block.

sources.title: A brief guide to container terminal automation - Thetius
sources.claim: Automated stacking cranes place containers to roughly 50 mm of the intended position using lidar-based systems, with anti-collision stopping for intrusions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous heavy suspended-load landing. Establishes the placement accuracy achievable without a tag-line crew, which is adequate for landing a member on seats but is demonstrated only in fenced automated stacking blocks.

sources.system: JLG leader-follower scissor lifts and autonomous end-effector boom lift
sources.title: JLG Brings "Job Site of the Future" Demo and Robotics Preview to CONEXPO/CON-AGG
sources.claim: At CONEXPO 2026 JLG staged a booth demonstration in which two scissor lifts transported and positioned structural material and a boom lift with a welding end-effector welded it, with one operator overseeing the machines via leader-follower and ClearSky connectivity.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (moving a structural member into position at a site), but the scissor lifts follow a human-operated leader machine in a staged trade-show scenario, so it is treated as teleoperated and cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Verton EVEREST / SpinPod load orientation system
sources.date: 2024-04-03 (Hale Steel distribution-centre case study; product in market since ~2020)
sources.title: Hale Steel incorporates Verton's EVEREST series to improve safety and efficiency in lifting operations at a distribution center construction
sources.claim: Gyroscopic load-orientation pods are used commercially on steel erection and other lifts to replace tag lines, but the load's orientation is commanded by a rigger with a hand-held remote.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task: it replaces the rope. But orientation is continuously commanded by a human remote operator, so under the autonomy rule it cannot substantiate autonomous completion on a construction site.

sources.title: Report "Obayashi Automated Crane" | CIFE | Center for Integrated Facility Engineering
sources.claim: Obayashi's autonomous crane, fitted with lidar and the Skyjuster suspended-load direction control device, ran lifting operations at the Kawakami Dam project with the operator supervising remotely; Stanford CIFE recommends future application to steel beam installation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous crane lifting with automatic suspended-load orientation at a real (E3) construction site. It is cited as the closest field evidence, but the demonstrated loads were dam construction lifts, and steel beam installation is a recommendation for future work, not a demonstrated result.

sources.system: ISC-Perception (research dataset for robotic steel assembly)
sources.title: ISC-Perception: A Hybrid Computer Vision Dataset for Object Detection in Novel Steel Assembly
sources.claim: A 2025 research paper on robotic steel assembly states that robotic manipulators' impact on construction remains modest because building sites are unstructured and weather-exposed, complicating autonomous operation of steel frame erection.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the negative E2/E3 judgments: as of late 2025 robotic steel frame erection remains a research problem, consistent with the absence of any fielded autonomous system that lands members into connections.

tasks.label: Drive drift pins through rivet holes to align rivet holes in structural steel members with corresponding holes in previously placed members.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Multi-story/high-rise building frame: a connector standing on a beam flange or in a bucket receives a crane-suspended beam, drives a tapered drift pin (spud wrench handle or bull pin) through the beam-web holes and the column shear-tab holes to pull the holes into line, then inserts erection bolts. At height, exposed to wind, load swinging, no fixed layout.

Low-rise commercial / pre-engineered metal building: erecting joists, girts, purlins, rafters and light framing from a scissor or boom lift; lighter members, pinning bolt holes of clip angles and splice plates into alignment before bolting. Site conditions as found, uneven ground, weather.

Bridge or heavy industrial steel: bolted field splices of plate girders, trusses, or crane runways; many holes through thick splice plates, drift pins driven with sledge or pneumatic hammer to draw the mating holes into line, often over water, traffic, or in a running plant.

Ground-level pre-assembly in a site laydown yard: trusses, tower sections, tank shell courses or column trees assembled on cribbing/dunnage before the pick; drift pins used to align mating hole patterns, then bolted up. Outdoor, layout varies by site.

Fabrication shop or pre-assembly bay: trial fit-up of bolted assemblies on assembly tables/horses with overhead crane; drift pins align hole patterns of plates, gussets and splices before bolting or welding. Indoor, controlled premises, standard equipment.

Retrofit, repair, or reinforcement of an existing structure: new steel pinned to as-found members whose holes are rusted, mismatched, or field-drilled; drifting, reaming and re-drilling as needed, in confined or occupied space.

sources.system: Electroimpact automated production fastening system (737 wing panel assembly line)
sources.title: 2015-01-2514: An Automated Production Fastening System for LGP and Hi-Lok Titanium Bolts for the Boeing 737 Wing Panel Assembly Line
sources.claim: Electroimpact's automated production fastening system installs LGP and Hi-Lok titanium bolts into holes in fixtured wing panel assemblies on a production line — machine-controlled insertion of a fastener through holes in stacked metal structural members inside a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fastener installation through holes in a fixtured metal structural assembly. It transfers to driving a pin through mating holes at E1 because the machine must locate the hole, present the pin coaxially and drive it home to depth at production reliability; aerospace tolerances are tighter than structural steel drift-pin work, and the setting is a purpose-built fixtured cell exactly as the E1 counterfactual assumes.

sources.title: ZEMAN Steel Beam Assembly (SBA) Robot — CPE Construction
sources.claim: The Zeman Steel Beam Assembler is a commercially installed robotic cell that autonomously picks heavy steel attachment parts (magnet pick-up), positions them on a beam using 3D scanning and CNC data, and welds them, with automated in/out feed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fit-up of structural steel parts to a beam in a purpose-built cell. It substantiates the handling and alignment half of the drift-pin task — grasping heavy steel plate, locating the beam by scanning, and placing the part to fabrication tolerance — on the same class of objects (rolled beams, plates, gussets) the ironworker pins.

sources.title: Zeman - Steel Beam Assembler
sources.claim: Zeman SBA lines run structural steel production with essentially one attending worker and handle attachment parts up to 200 kg, indicating production-rate autonomous operation on heavy steel parts.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (robotic structural-steel fit-up); the payload and cycle figures show the cell works at worker-replacing throughput on heavy steel components rather than as a laboratory demonstration.

sources.system: Visumatic VIM-700 automatic pin insertion system
sources.title: Automatic Pin Insertion | Visumatic Industrial Products
sources.claim: Visumatic's VIM-700 is a commercial robot-integrated pin insertion system that feeds steel pins and repeatably inserts them to a set depth, with sensors verifying insertion depth.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated feeding and driving of non-threaded steel pins into holes to a verified depth on 6-axis robots. This is the pin-driving half of the drift-pin task, executed under machine control in a fixtured cell; scale is smaller, so it supports E1 only in combination with the heavy-steel handling evidence.

sources.developer: research group, published in Automation in Construction
sources.title: Tower-crane robotic arm bolting system for modular integrated construction - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Robotic bolting of steel module/beam connections on construction sites has only been validated in laboratory experiments; on-site bolting of steel connections is still done manually.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related task (making bolted steel connections in the field). Cited only as negative context: the state of the art for field steel connection work is lab validation, so no E3/E2 field capability is substantiated.

sources.system: RAS (Robotic Assembly System for steel structure erection)
sources.title: RAS: a robotic assembly system for steel structure erection and assembly
sources.claim: A robotic assembly system for steel structure erection was validated only at reduced scale and required purpose-modified connections with extra guide holes above each bolt hole.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related task (aligning and bolting erected steel members). Cited as negative context: scaled lab validation with redesigned connections does not meet worker-quality completion on real erection work.

tasks.label: Dismantle structures or equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Taking down the structural steel frame of a building slated for demolition or heavy renovation: burners cut columns, beams and connections with oxy-fuel torches while riggers choke each member, a crane picks it out, and pieces are lowered to grade. Work is at height on a partially dismantled, progressively unstable frame with changing load paths, weather exposure, and adjacent trades.

Removing steel bridge superstructure (girders, floor beams, trusses, bearings) during rehabilitation or replacement: torch-cutting members over live traffic or water during night closures, rigging picks with mobile or barge cranes, controlling debris and load stability on a site whose geometry differs at every span.

Dismantling process equipment, tanks, vessels, ductwork, hoppers or conveyor structures at an operating refinery, power plant, paper mill or steel mill during a turnaround or decommissioning: isolate and disconnect, burn or unbolt supports and shell sections, rig each piece out through congested pipe racks under permit and confined-space rules.

Dismantling temporary erection equipment at the end of a job: tower cranes and climbing masts, material hoists, derricks, falsework, shoring towers and heavy scaffold—unpinning/unbolting sections at height, rigging them to an assist crane, and lowering and stacking them on an active jobsite.

Small in-facility removals and retrofits inside an existing building: cutting out a damaged or obsolete beam, mezzanine, monorail, machine base, storage rack or equipment frame; shoring adjacent steel, burning the member free, and rigging it out through doorways or roof openings while the facility stays occupied.

sources.title: Why Brokk Original demolition power
sources.claim: Brokk's demolition machines—the dominant robotic tool used in structural/industrial demolition, including steel cutting and nuclear work—are continuously remote-controlled by a human operator with a handheld control box; no autonomous dismantling mode is offered.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task family (demolition/dismantling of concrete and steel), used to establish that the leading fielded demolition machines are teleoperated rather than autonomous.

sources.system: Cyan Tec skip sorting and laser cutting cell (FANUC ARC Mate 120iC + M-900iB/360)
sources.developer: Cyan Tec Systems with FANUC UK / TKE Nuclear for Sellafield Ltd
sources.title: Autonomous laser cutting cell installed at Sellafield nuclear site
sources.claim: A deployed robotic cell at Sellafield autonomously dismantles steel nuclear-waste skips: two FANUC robots scan the item, compare it to a reference model, choose a cutting pattern, laser-cut it, and handle the cut steel panels with an electromagnet inside a purpose-built shielded bunker.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic size-reduction (dismantling) of steel weldments. It transfers to dismantling steel equipment brought to a machine—same operation of thermal cutting a steel enclosure into pieces plus mechanical handling of the cut pieces—but only at cell scale (360 kg handling, ~2.6 m reach), not for in-situ structures.

sources.system: Cyan Tec autonomous laser-cutting and handling system
sources.title: Fanuc robots enable autonomous nuclear waste size reduction at Sellafield
sources.claim: The Sellafield cutting/handling system operates autonomously inside the bunker with supervision from a control room 100 m away, rather than under continuous manual joystick control.
sources.transferJustification: Same system as evidence 1; cited to establish autonomy status of the cell.

sources.title: Autonomous excavators – a new era - HitachiCM Europe
sources.claim: Fully autonomous heavy earthmoving/demolition-class machines remain developmental: Hitachi's fully autonomous 15-tonne excavator was a Bauma 2025 exhibit and is not yet a fielded jobsite product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous operation of heavy demolition-capable plant on real sites. Cited as negative context showing no fielded autonomous machine performs in-situ structural takedown.

sources.title: KEWAZO - Projects with the scaffolding elevator LIFTBOT
sources.claim: The leading scaffolding robot used during erection and dismantling only hoists components vertically; the dismantling itself is still done by the human crew (crew size reduced from four to two on a 40 m power-plant scaffold).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dismantling temporary steel structures. Cited as negative evidence that the robot performs material transport, not the unpinning, rigging and takedown that constitute the instance.

tasks.label: Insert sealing strips, wiring, insulating material, ladders, flanges, gauges, or valves, depending on types of structures being assembled.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-engineered metal building erection: worker sets closure strips, foam/rubber sealing strips and butyl mastic tape along panel laps, eave and ridge lines while working on purlins or a lift, matching strip type to panel profile, in wind and weather.

Metal building erection: worker unrolls and positions fiberglass blanket insulation with vapor-barrier facing over purlins/girts ahead of roof and wall sheeting, cutting to length, lapping and sealing the facing, working at height over open framing.

Field-erected storage tank or structural frame: worker rigs, aligns and bolts or tack-welds steel ladders, safety cages, handrail sections and stair/platform stringers to the erected shell or frame at height, drilling/reaming where holes do not line up.

Field-erected tank or vessel: worker fits gaskets and installs flanged nozzles, manway covers, level gauges and valves to shell openings, aligning bolt patterns and torquing bolt-up in sequence, often at elevation on the tank exterior.

Prefabricated metal building or tank: worker pulls grounding cable, lighting/heater wiring and conduit through frame members, installs hangers/clips and grommets through purlin holes, coordinating with electricians on an active site.

Fabrication shop or lay-down yard pre-assembly before shipment: worker fits sealing strips, gaskets, flanges, gauges and short ladder/handrail sections onto tank courses, skids or prefabricated modules staged on stands under crane coverage.

sources.system: Sonderhoff FIPFG gasketing cell (Fermapor K31, Henkel)
sources.title: System solution for sealing with high process reliability
sources.claim: Henkel/Sonderhoff FIPFG production cells apply sealing gaskets automatically to fixtured components: a rotary indexing table presents housings and a 6-axis robot traverses the part contour dispensing the seal, with camera-based quality control and conveyor unloading.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: forming/placing an elastomeric weather seal on a fixtured sheet-metal component. Comparable objects (compressible seal material on metal panels), comparable precision (bead placed to sub-mm repeatability along a panel contour), in a purpose-built cell — the same operation a metal-building closure/sealant strip performs.

sources.system: GLPPR robotic batt-insulation installation cell (6-DOF arm + custom end effector)
sources.developer: University of Alberta (Han, Yang, Chen) with Tecnológico de Monterrey
sources.title: A robotic method for installing batt thermal insulation into prefabricated light-frame wood wall panel
sources.claim: A 6-DOF robot arm with a custom end effector autonomously inserts mineral-wool and fiberglass batt insulation into fixtured prefabricated wood wall frames of varying sizes, achieving tight fits without visible gaps at a 92.5% success rate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing fiberglass blanket insulation into a framed cavity in a prefabrication setting. Same material (fiberglass/mineral wool batts), same handling problem (limp, deformable material pressed into a frame), differing only in that the frame is fixtured rather than an erected purlin roof.

sources.title: Pipe Spool and Skid Automation - KRANENDONK
sources.claim: Kranendonk's Robotic Pipe Shop is an ... covering material management, cutting, beveling, fit-up and welding of pipe spools and skids, including dedicated flange preparation stations for exact fit-up.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fitting flanges and fittings to heavy steel pipe and skid frames. Same components (flanges, nozzles, heavy steel weldments), same joining operations (align to bolt/weld line, fit-up, weld), performed in a fixtured, purpose-built line rather than on an erected tank.

sources.title: Boltron Flange Bolting Robot | Total Marine Technology Products
sources.claim: Boltron is an automated/autonomous flange-bolting robot used on industrial sites, refineries, ... to tighten and loosen flange bolts across a range of flange diameters; a unit was contracted to an alumina refinery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making up bolted flange joints on plant equipment. It covers only the bolt-up step (not hanging the flange, gasket or valve), so it supports the fastening portion of flange/valve installation, not the whole instance in an as-found plant.

sources.system: ESTIC ERS robotic workcell; ASG AX-40 screwdriving cell
sources.developer: ESTIC America; ASG, Division of Jergens
sources.title: New Tech for Robotic Fastening | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Preconfigured robotic screwdriving/nutrunning workcells are sold for automatic installation of threaded ..., built as enclosed cells with conveyor, feeder and light curtain, with optional vision guidance that corrects tool-to-fastener misalignment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving threaded fasteners to torque on a fixtured workpiece with vision correction for hole misalignment — the fastening step common to bolting ladders, handrails, gauges, flanges and closure trim, done in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: FANUC assembly robot systems (M-710iC/70, R-2000iC/270F, SR-series)
sources.title: Assembly Robots | Assembly Line Robots | FANUC America
sources.claim: Multi-robot FANUC systems in production perform sealing, sensor installation, riveting and torquing on fixtured assemblies, and assemble automotive parts using vision-guided nesting and precision screw driving with end-of-line testing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing instruments/sensors and applying seals onto a fixtured metal assembly, then torquing fasteners and leak-testing — the same class of operations as fitting gauges, valves and sealing strips, in a fenced industrial cell.

sources.title: Q5d unveils robot for automating wiring harness manufacturing - New Electronics
sources.claim: Q5D's CY1000 is a 5-axis robotic production cell that automatically adds wiring, connections and components into or onto fixtured parts; the first units are shipping and are being used to assemble a vehicle roof-lining harness.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routing and terminating wiring onto a fixtured metal structure. Comparable objects (insulated conductors, clips, terminations) and comparable placement precision; differs only in that the structure is presented in a cell rather than an erected frame.

tasks.label: Place blocks under reinforcing bars used to reinforce floors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Poured-in-place floor slab at a commercial building site: workers walk the deck/subgrade and set plastic or concrete chairs and dobies at plan spacing (typically 3-4 ft) under the bottom mat of rebar or welded wire mesh, on vapor barrier, gravel or metal deck, in open weather with other trades working nearby.

Bridge or parking-structure deck: setting slab bolsters, individual bar chairs and dobies on stay-in-place forms or deck panels ahead of the mat, outdoors at height, often over live traffic, with camber and varying deck geometry.

Two-layer deck top mat: placing upper continuous high chairs / slab bolsters standing on the bottom mat to hold the top layer at cover, working around post-tension ducts, embeds and congested intersections on an in-place deck.

Remedial/adjustment work before the pour: sliding blocks or chairs under bars already laid and tied where the mat has sagged, cover checks failed, or a chair was crushed, in a congested area with penetrations, sleeves and embeds.

Indoor precast/prestressed concrete plant: setting wheel spacers, plastic chairs and blocks under bars/mesh in a casting bed or on a production pallet for floor planks and slab elements, on a level shop floor under overhead cranes.

Small light-commercial or residential floor pour (garage slab, small addition): a handful of chairs and brick/concrete dobies set under mesh and a few bars in tight quarters on an uncontrolled small site.

sources.title: Mesh Spacer | Progress Maschinen & Automation
sources.claim: Progress Maschinen & Automation's Mesh Spacer is a commercially offered robot system that places spacers for reinforcing mesh fully automatically on the ... in precast concrete plants, positioning them per CAD-CAM data with laser control so the reinforcement gets uniform concrete cover.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: the spacers it sets on the pallet are the blocks that hold floor-slab reinforcement at cover, replacing rings, plastic strips and spacer bars previously placed by hand.

sources.title: Mesh Spacer und Insert Placer: automated to higher efficiency - BFT International
sources.claim: Trade press describes the same Progress system: spacers for wire mesh mats that were previously placed manually as rings, plastic strips or spacer bars are now positioned on the production pallet fully automatically by ..., one of the last manual steps at the start of the precast production cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Same task and same objects (spacers/blocks under mesh and bars for slab elements); the article covers precast floor slab production lines.

sources.system: Wire Center / reinforcement automation portal robots
sources.title: Automation of Reinforcement | Progress Maschinen & Automation
sources.claim: Progress's Wire Center portal-robot reinforcement station in pallet carousel precast plants places cross reinforcement with and without ... on the formwork to CAD specifications, fully automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic placement of the spacer-carrying bars and lattice girders that set layer height and cover in floor-slab reinforcement - same objects, same cover tolerances, same fixtured pallet setting as placing blocks under bars.

sources.title: Rebar Tying Construction Robot Evolves | For Construction Pros
sources.claim: On real construction sites the leading autonomous rebar robot (TyBOT, used on bridge decks) only ties intersections and presupposes that bar chairs have already been installed by workers; it requires a minimum bar chair .... No cited jobsite robot places the chairs.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed jobsite rebar robot; cited as context that chair/block placement on decks remains a manual precondition rather than a demonstrated robot capability.

tasks.label: Hold rivets while riveters use air hammers to form heads on rivets.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field riveting during rehabilitation of a historic steel truss bridge: the worker stands on staging, a lift, or inside the truss and backs a hot 3/4"–1" rivet, placed in a splice or gusset connection, with a heavy dolly/holder-on while a partner drives the head with a pneumatic rivet hammer; work is outdoors, elevated, with awkward reach and tight clearances, coordinated with a heater/catcher and inspected for head form and tightness.

Shop riveting in a bridge/steel fabrication shop: restored or replacement built-up girders, floor beams and truss members sit on trestles or assembly jigs; the holder-on backs each hot rivet with a bucking bar or holder-on snap while a riveter drives it with an air hammer (or the pair works with a hydraulic squeezer), moving rivet to rivet along a connection.

Field riveting or rivet replacement on other legacy riveted structures — bolted/riveted water and oil storage tanks, penstocks, elevated water towers, mill and historic building steel frames — often in confined interiors, overhead, or from swing staging, with limited access to the far side of the joint.

Apprenticeship training and heritage demonstration riveting at a union training center, shop safety class, or public demonstration: repeated rivets driven into sample plate/angle assemblies clamped on a bench or stand, under controlled indoor conditions, with an instructor judging head quality.

sources.system: Electroimpact Automatic C-Frame Riveter (riveting product line)
sources.title: Riveting - Electroimpact
sources.claim: Electroimpact's automatic C-frame riveting machines run a CNC part program that drills, inserts and upsets rivets with automatically changed upper and lower rivet anvils, with the part held and indexed by a fixture/barge and no operator intervention required — the lower anvil performs exactly the backing (holder-on) function of this task.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is automated solid-rivet installation on fixtured aerospace panels: the machine's lower anvil backs the rivet while the upper head upsets it, which is the same mechanical function (holding/backing the rivet while a head is formed) demanded here; transfer is limited to fixtured presentation, i.e. E1.

sources.system: Electroimpact E7000 CNC fuselage riveting cell
sources.date: 2013 (SAE technical paper), machines in production use since
sources.title: E7000 High-Speed CNC Fuselage Riveting Cell
sources.claim: The E7000 CNC riveting cell fastens fixtured aircraft panels at 15 rivets per minute, with the cycle including drilling, rivet insertion and upset of the formed head — machine-formed rivet heads without a human holder-on.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is automated riveting of fixtured panels; the machine performs both the driving and the backing of each rivet, replacing the two-person riveter/holder-on pair, but only where the workpiece is presented in a purpose-built fixture.

sources.system: Robotic percussive riveting system (6-DOF robot + 5-axis CNC gantry bucking bar)
sources.developer: Concordia University / Advances in Manufacturing (Zhu et al.)
sources.title: Framework on robotic percussive riveting for aircraft assembly automation
sources.claim: A robotic percussive riveting system was built in which an industrial robot holds the pneumatic rivet gun and a CNC gantry replaces the second worker who holds the bucking bar, with the whole percussive riveting process automated by synchronizing the two machines.
sources.transferJustification: This is the same operation as the task — percussive (air-hammer) riveting with a bucking bar held against the rivet — automated for aircraft sheet; it substantiates machine performance of the holder-on role only with the workpiece jigged on the gantry (E1).

sources.system: Robotic self-piercing riveting (C-frame squeeze riveting) systems
sources.developer: automotive industry suppliers (e.g. Henrob/Atlas Copco, Böllhoff RIVSET)
sources.date: 2013 (review statement); technology in volume production since
sources.title: Framework on robotic percussive riveting for aircraft assembly automation
sources.claim: Squeeze-type robotic riveting with a C-frame whose opposite end acts as the anvil/die is fully developed and commercialized for ... in automotive body plants, i.e. robots routinely form structural rivet joints while providing the backing themselves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is robotic structural riveting of steel/aluminium sheet in fenced body-shop cells; the C-frame's die side replaces the holder-on, showing the backing function is a solved, deployed capability inside purpose-built cells.

sources.system: Fuselage Automated Upright Build (FAUB) robotic riveting line
sources.title: Boeing abandons its failed fuselage robots on the 777X, handing the job back to machinists
sources.claim: In Boeing's Fuselage Automated Upright Build line at Everett, paired robots worked opposite sides of the fuselage: one inserted the rivet while the robot on the other side simultaneously flattened (upset) its far end, installing tens of thousands of fasteners that had been driven by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is two-sided robotic riveting of a large fixtured structure: one machine drives, the other backs/forms the far head — the holder-on role — demonstrating it in a production factory cell, though Boeing later returned the work to machinists.

sources.title: Hot Upset Forming | High-Strength Metal Joining Solutions
sources.claim: Industrial hot upset forming/riveting machines heat a steel fastener and form its head under press pressure in a tooled machine, showing that heat-softened heavy steel rivets are headed by fixtured machines rather than by a hand hammer and holder-on.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is machine hot riveting of heavy steel fasteners; it addresses the material/temperature gap between small aerospace rivets and hot-driven structural rivets, again only for parts fixtured in the machine (E1).

tasks.label: Catch hot rivets in buckets and insert rivets in holes, using tongs.

aliases: Journeyman Electrician PV Installer (Journeyman Electrician Photovoltaic Installer)

roles.description: Assemble, install, or maintain solar photovoltaic (PV) systems on roofs or other structures in compliance with site assessment and schematics. May include measuring, cutting, assembling, and bolting structural framing and solar modules. May perform minor electrical work such as current checks.

tasks.label: Install photovoltaic (PV) systems in accordance with codes and standards, using drawings, schematics, and instructions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retrofit array on an occupied single-family home: 15-30 modules on a pitched asphalt-shingle roof. Crew locates rafters, installs flashed standoffs/L-feet, levels rails, sets and clamps modules, runs conduit, lands microinverter/rapid-shutdown wiring, mounts inverter and disconnect, and passes AHJ inspection to NEC 690. Two- to three-person crew, one to two days, varying pitch, vents/obstructions, weather.

Small distributed array up to roughly 100 kW at a farm, small business, school or carport (ground-mount or low-slope roof): set piers/posts or ballast, assemble bespoke racking, mount modules, trench and pull DC/AC circuits, terminate at string inverter per stamped drawings and local code.

Large commercial/industrial flat roof, 250 kW-2 MW: crane-hoist ballasted racking and 400-600 modules to roof, lay out rows per stamped drawings around HVAC curbs and setbacks, set ballast, clamp modules, install cable management, string to combiners/inverters, torque and QC to code.

Utility-scale site foundations: survey/stake pile locations from the plan set, distribute steel H-piles along rows, drive thousands of piles to plumb, embedment and reveal tolerance on uneven graded terrain, and inspect each for tolerance before racking crews follow.

Utility-scale mechanical row build: assemble single-axis tracker torque tubes, bearings and module rails onto driven piles, then place and bolt hundreds of 60-80 lb modules per crew-day into long repetitive rows in an open field with dust, wind and heat, per drawings and torque specs.

Utility-scale DC/BOS electrical scope: mate string connectors, route and secure harnesses and cable management, bond/ground rows, terminate combiner boxes and inverter skids, torque-mark and test/verify per NEC and the project QC plan.

sources.title: AES Maximo robot installs 100 megawatts of solar capacity - The Robot Report
sources.claim: AES-incubated Maximo installed 100 MW of utility-scale solar at the Bellefield complex in Kern County, California with a fleet of four ...; the system has an end-to-end autonomous mode in which the robot performs the module installation after an operator start command, using AI vision to adapt to lighting, mounting structures and configurations in dust and wind.

sources.title: Meet Maximo, the AI-enabled solar installation robot
sources.claim: Maximo automates both placing and attaching of utility-scale solar modules and had its first utility-scale deployment at the Oak Ridge Solar project in Louisiana, installing about 10 MW before scaling to a fleet.

sources.title: Making solar projects cheaper and faster with portable factories | MIT News
sources.claim: Charge Robotics' Sunrise portable field factory robotically assembles steel tracks, mounting brackets, fasteners and panels into completed 800-lb solar bays, machine-vision QCs them, and a robotic vehicle autonomously places each bay on the driven piles; it automates the entire mechanical installation scope other than pile driving, first deployed building a solar farm with SOLV Energy.

sources.title: Terafab Solar Construction Automation | Terabase Energy
sources.claim: Terabase's Terafab automated on-site field factory plus installation rovers has built more than 100 MW across multiple commercial US utility-scale projects, roughly doubling installation productivity; next-generation v2 adds fully automated table assembly and in-line module QC.

sources.title: Robotic Automation for Utility-Scale Solar Installation | KUKA Global
sources.claim: Contractor Sunstall uses Cosmic Robotics' Cosmic-1A, an autonomous all-terrain mobile robot with a foundry-rated KUKA arm and in-house computer vision, to pick 80-lb modules and place them on tracker racking at US utility-scale solar fields in rain, dust and extreme temperatures; human crews still erect racking and fasten modules.

sources.title: Built Robotics develops automated pile driver for large-scale solar construction
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 is a fully ... solar piling system that performs survey, pile distribution, pile driving ..., installing 300+ piles per day to tolerance with a two-person crew on utility-scale solar sites.

sources.system: Built Robotics Exosystem / autonomous piling machines
sources.title: Top 10 robotics companies building the solar power future
sources.claim: Trade press review of solar construction robotics reports Built Robotics' autonomous excavator-based trenching and piling machines are in regular use on solar energy projects with minimal human oversight.

sources.title: Robots speed installation of 500,000 panels at solar farm in Australia - pv magazine Global
sources.claim: Luminous Robotics' LUMI pick-and-place robot autonomously placed modules onto racking during construction of a large solar farm at Goorambat, Australia (about 500,000 panels), with site workers doing final securing.

sources.title: Trinabot offers installation robots for large PV projects – pv magazine International
sources.claim: Trinabot's Buildex module-installation machines (the company also markets a rooftop version for residential, commercial and industrial roofs) carry and position modules but do not perform bolt fastening, so the mechanical attachment and all electrical work remain manual.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (PV module installation); cited to show the limits of rooftop-oriented machines, which position modules only.

tasks.label: Check electrical installation for proper wiring, polarity, grounding, or integrity of terminations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential pitched-roof array, DC side: after modules are set, the installer walks/kneels on a shingle roof, meters string open-circuit voltage and confirms polarity at the string leads or rapid-shutdown device, tug-tests MC4 connections, and confirms module frame bonding clips/lay-in lugs and the EGC path. Hot, sloped, cluttered roof; layout differs at every house.

Residential balance-of-system at the wall/garage: inverter, rapid-shutdown box, DC/AC disconnects, load center and grounding electrode. Verify conductor landings are torqued to spec, correct polarity/phasing, neutral-ground separation, EGC/GEC continuity with a meter, and sound terminations before energizing and again for the AHJ inspection.

Commercial/industrial flat-roof array during installation: dozens of strings landed in several combiner boxes, conduit and raceway bonding, homerun polarity/voltage checks, insulation-resistance (megger) test on DC circuits, torque-mark and label verification across many circuits, on an active construction roof.

Utility-scale solar farm commissioning/O&M: string polarity and voltage checks at combiners and inverter skids, torque audit of DC and AC lugs, harness/whip connector checks along tracker rows, grounding/bonding continuity to the ground grid, IR scan of terminations. Fenced, access-controlled site with standardized repeated rows, outdoors on graded terrain.

Service call on an existing installed system at a customer site: chase a ground fault, arc fault, reverse-polarity string, or loose/burned lug reported by the inverter. Isolate circuits, open enclosures, meter at multiple points on roof and at equipment, identify and re-terminate the defect, then re-verify.

sources.system: Ecoprogetti solar module production line / ECOHI-POT in-line hi-pot tester
sources.title: Solar module production line - Ecoprogetti.com
sources.claim: Commercial PV module production lines include in-line hi-pot stations that automatically perform insulation-resistance measurement and ground-continuity verification on each module as it moves through the line, without an operator making the measurement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory electrical safety verification of PV assemblies. The measurement content (insulation integrity, grounding/bonding continuity of a PV circuit and frame) is the same content the installer verifies in the field, performed automatically when the work is fixtured and conveyed to the machine.

sources.title: Averex wiring centre from Kiesling | Rittal - The System.
sources.claim: A portal robot wiring centre inspects a fixtured control-panel mounting plate against its digital design and then routes, cuts, crimps and lands wires on device terminals automatically and autonomously inside a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated wiring and verification of an electrical panel. It checks the as-built assembly against the schematic and makes screw-terminal landings on the same class of low-voltage gear an installer checks (disconnects, terminal blocks, load-center style terminations), with the panel fixtured.

sources.system: Crimp Force Monitoring (ACO 08) on Komax/Schleuniger crimping presses
sources.title: Crimp Force Monitoring | Komax
sources.claim: Automated wire-processing machines continuously monitor crimp force on every termination cycle and flag defective terminations (missing strands, faulty terminals) in real time as a production quality gate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine verification of termination integrity. The installer's 'integrity of terminations' check (sound crimp/landing, no missed strands) is performed instrumentally and automatically when the conductor and terminal are presented to the machine.

sources.system: Cirris Easy-Touch Pro cable/harness tester (and Cirris CH2 automated harness test)
sources.title: Easy-Touch ® Pro High Voltage Cable Tester | Cirris
sources.claim: Automated harness/cable test systems verify continuity, isolation, correct routing (miswires) and hipot on a fixtured assembly and report the location of opens and shorts, executing programmed test sequences under machine control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: electrical verification of a wired assembly. Checking 'proper wiring, polarity, grounding' is a continuity/isolation/miswire test against the schematic; the machine performs it and localizes faults once the circuit ends are presented at the fixture.

sources.system: Autonomous contact-probe robot (self-supervised robotic system for contact-based spatial mapping of semiconductor properties)
sources.developer: MIT (Buonassisi group) and collaborators, published in Science Advances
sources.title: Robotic probe quickly measures key properties of new materials | MIT News
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robotic probe positions physical contact probes onto selected points of a sample and takes thousands of electrical measurements over a 24-hour unattended run, choosing where to probe with learned models.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous contact electrical probing. It demonstrates the manipulation skill an instrument check needs — bringing probes into reliable electrical contact at chosen points and recording the reading — on a fixtured workpiece in a bench-scale purpose-built setting.

sources.system: Spot with thermal payload (Consumers Energy substations; Avangrid/United Illuminating pilot with Levatas)
sources.title: How Spot Helps the ENR Sector | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Quadruped robots run autonomous inspection routes inside utility substations and industrial plants, capturing thermal images of electrical connection points to find overheating; they perform no contact measurement of polarity, continuity or torque.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic electrical-asset inspection in an institution-controlled facility (E2). instances.label: Pre-job site walk and job hazard analysis before a residential rooftop install: the installer surveys roof pitch and condition, anchor points, overhead service drops and power lines, ladder set-up area, attic/service panel access, and weather, then records the hazards on a JHA/toolbox-talk form and briefs the crew. Output is an identified and communicated hazard list, not a physical change to the site.

Ongoing hazard recognition during a residential rooftop installation: recognizing that modules are energized whenever illuminated (live DC strings, ungrounded conductors), spotting damaged insulation or improperly seated MC4 connectors, wet or slippery surfaces, brittle tiles, unsecured tools and trip hazards from cabling, and calling them out or stopping work.

Commercial rooftop or ground-mount/utility-scale array: identifying arc-flash and high-voltage DC hazards at combiner boxes, recombiners and inverters, working-clearance and labeling deficiencies, trenching/excavation and heavy-equipment traffic hazards, heat stress and lightning exposure, and documenting them for the site safety plan.

Service, troubleshooting, or O&M visit on an existing system: identifying hazards such as burnt or corroded connectors, ground faults, rodent-chewed wiring, backfeed from batteries or the grid, degraded rooftop penetrations, and mislabeled disconnects, and reporting them to the customer/supervisor.

Environmental and site-condition hazards specifically: wasp/hornet nests and wildlife under arrays, vegetation and wildfire risk, high wind or approaching storms, extreme heat, dust and glare, contaminated or unstable soil, and flagging these conditions to the crew lead.

tasks.label: Identify installation locations with proper orientation, area, solar access, or structural integrity for photovoltaic (PV) arrays.

instances.label: Single-family home, pitched asphalt-shingle roof: assessor arrives at the property, gets on/over the roof, measures each roof plane's dimensions and usable area, records azimuth and pitch, maps obstructions (vents, chimneys, skylights, setbacks) and performs a solar-access/shading analysis of surrounding trees and neighboring structures to mark which planes can host the array.

Same residential job, structural leg: enter the attic or inspect the roof deck to identify rafter/truss size, spacing and span, check sheathing and framing condition and load path, and confirm the identified roof planes have the structural integrity to carry the array and mounts.

Commercial or institutional flat/low-slope roof (warehouse, school, big-box store) whose owner controls access: measure available membrane area, note parapets, HVAC units and skylights and their shadow footprints, confirm orientation and row spacing, and mark array zones with adequate solar access.

Small ground-mount or accessory-structure site on residential/farm property (back yard, pasture, barn or carport): pace off the open area, judge terrain slope and orientation, map shading from tree lines and outbuildings across the day and season, and identify where the array can be sited.

Large ground-mount / utility-scale greenfield parcel: survey acres of raw land for topography, slope, drainage, tree lines and access, and verify which portions of the parcel can host rows at proper orientation and spacing with adequate solar access.

instances.label: Residential new install on a sloped asphalt-shingle roof: at each of 20-40 attachment points, lift the shingle course, inject sealant into the pilot hole, slide the flashing (or butyl-pad mount) under the shingles, bed and seal the lag/bolt head and flashing perimeter; also boot and seal the conduit roof jack. Ground-mount / utility-scale or exterior balance-of-system work: weatherproofing conduit entries into combiner boxes, inverter enclosures and disconnects with sealing hubs, duct seal and gaskets; sealing the wall or roof penetration where conduit enters the building; sealing junction boxes and exposed support hardware. tasks.label: Install module array interconnect wiring, implementing measures to disable arrays during installation.

instances.label: New residential install on a sloped asphalt-shingle roof: after modules are set, the installer mates module MC4/H4 leads to microinverter or optimizer trunk cables, dresses and clips wire to racking rails off the roof deck, runs the string/branch home run to a junction or rapid-shutdown device, and keeps the array disabled (breaker and DC disconnect open, last connector left unmated or modules covered) until commissioning. New commercial flat-roof array (100 kW-1 MW, ballasted or attached racking): installer plugs module-to-module connectors in long rows, installs module-level rapid shutdown devices, secures PV wire in clips/cable trays under modules, lands home runs in combiner boxes, and implements array disable measures (open combiner fuse holders/DC disconnects, opaque covers) while other trades work the roof.

Utility-scale ground-mount tracker rows: crew plugs module leads into string harnesses along the torque tube, routes and secures cable with clips/messenger wire, connects whips to combiner boxes or string inverters, and keeps strings de-energized by leaving harness ends unmated and fuse holders/disconnects open. Outdoor field, dust, mud, heat, uneven terrain.

Small ground-mount, carport, pole-mount or barn/garage array at a home or farm (5-30 kW): interconnect wiring between modules, routing conductors into conduit down the structure, disabling the array with disconnects/covers during the work. Site conditions and structure vary widely.

Service, repair or add-on work on an existing installed array: safely disabling the live array (shut down inverter, open DC disconnect, cover modules), unmating and re-mating connectors, replacing damaged interconnect wiring or a failed connector/optimizer, re-securing wire management, then re-energizing and verifying strings.

Commercial rooftop or carport array (roughly 100 kW to 2 MW) on an occupied building undergoing retrofit: string-by-string Voc/Isc and insulation-resistance testing per IEC 62446/NEC before energization, closing combiner and inverter disconnects, sequential inverter startup, verifying data acquisition/SCADA points and utility interconnection settings, and documenting commissioning results, often with a utility or engineer witness.

Utility-scale or large ground-mount plant block: crews IV-curve trace and megger strings, energize combiner boxes and inverter skids, start trackers, close medium-voltage breakers on a block, and verify block output and telemetry against expected performance across uneven outdoor terrain in an active construction site.

Service/callback reactivation on an existing home or small commercial system: after an inverter swap, breaker trip, or module/optimizer replacement, the tech re-energizes the system, checks voltages and currents with meter and clamp, clears faults, and confirms restored production on the monitoring portal against expected output.
