tasks.label: Identify and resolve any deficiencies in photovoltaic (PV) system installation or materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential rooftop new-install QA walk and punch-list correction: on a sloped shingle or tile roof of a private home, the installer checks the finished array against plans — clamp torque, rail alignment, flashing/penetration seals, wire management and clips, conduit runs, grounding, labeling — and remedies what is wrong (reseal a leaking penetration, re-torque or re-set clamps, re-route sagging home runs, swap a scratched or cracked module). Ladder access, pitched surface, weather, homeowner property.

Residential or small-commercial service/troubleshooting call: system underproducing or inverter/rapid-shutdown fault. Installer reads monitoring data and error codes, meters strings, uses an IR camera or curve tracer, traces the fault to a failed microinverter/optimizer, a burned or unmated MC4 connector, a chewed conductor, a ground fault, or a bad module; accesses roof/attic/wall equipment, replaces or re-terminates, retests and restores production.

Commercial rooftop, carport or small ground-mount deficiency correction from an AHJ inspection or commissioning punch list: misaligned or under-ballasted racking, wrong conductor routing or bend radius, missing labels/placards, loose combiner terminations, damaged modules to replace — on a flat roof crowded with HVAC units, curbs and edges, or on a partly built ground array.

Utility-scale plant: replace mechanically defective modules and correct mounting-hardware deficiencies flagged by QC or thermal/EL inspection — cracked or hot-spot modules in tracker rows, loose or under-torqued clamps and torque-tube bolts, misseated modules — walking fenced, access-controlled rows on graded terrain.

Utility-scale plant: diagnose and repair electrical/BOS deficiencies found in commissioning or O&M — open or cross-mated string harness connectors, damaged whips and jumpers, combiner/fuse faults, ground faults, tracker drive or wiring faults — using meters, curve tracers and IR, then repairing or replacing in the field.

Materials inspection at the laydown yard, warehouse or staging area: open pallets of modules, racking and inverters, check against the BOM and for shipping damage — cracked glass, bent frames, damaged junction boxes, wrong SKUs — segregate and swap out defective units, document for RMA so only good material reaches the array.

sources.claim: On active utility solar sites the Terafab field factory runs palleted panels through an automated inspection line ... with defects caught in real time, and robotic arms load only approved assemblies onto unmanned rovers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated defect detection plus physical segregation of non-conforming assemblies (only approved units are loaded out) is the machine equivalent of the installer's incoming-material and pre-install deficiency screening, performed on fixtured work in a purpose-built line.

Fenced, operator-controlled site with standardized rows.

Module receipt and pre-installation QC at the laydown/staging area and during mounting: unpack pallets, inspect each module for shipping damage (broken glass, bent frames, damaged junction box/connectors, visible cell defects), screen out rejects, and spot-check open-circuit voltage before the module goes on the racking. instances.label: Residential grid-tied rooftop PV handover: after final inspection the installer walks the homeowner around the house (exterior AC disconnect, inverter on garage/side wall, main service panel, roof-mounted rapid-shutdown initiator), energizes the system in sequence, shows the inverter boot-up and status LEDs/display and live production, then opens the disconnects to shut it down, restarts it, and shows the emergency/firefighter shutdown procedure and the monitoring app. Layout, equipment brands and clutter differ at every house.

Residential PV + battery storage (ESS) handover: installer additionally demonstrates the backup gateway, simulates a grid outage by opening the main breaker to show islanding and which loads stay live, shows battery reserve settings, the ESS service/bypass disconnect and the battery emergency stop, then restores grid connection and verifies normal operation. Equipment sits in a garage, basement or exterior wall of a private home.

Follow-up or inspection-day demonstration at a home: showing the AHJ inspector or utility that rapid shutdown and labeled disconnects work as designed, or re-walking a new/confused homeowner through start-up, shut-down and restart after a fault or outage during a service call.

Small/medium commercial rooftop or carport system turnover to a facility manager and maintenance staff: roof access by hatch or ladder, multiple string inverters and combiner boxes, labeled AC/DC disconnects and an emergency shutdown at the service entrance; installer runs the start-up and shut-down sequences, trips and resets the rapid shutdown, verifies string currents/output, and shows the monitoring portal.

Large ground-mount / utility-scale plant commissioning demonstration to the owner's engineer: start and stop inverters at the HMI or SCADA, verify ramp-up and expected performance against irradiance, perform emergency stop and DC disconnect trip tests, demonstrate restart and bypass operation, and sign off the commissioning checklist inside a fenced, controlled plant.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: operating medium/low-voltage switchgear (tripping and racking a breaker). It is the closest demonstrated robotic analogue to opening/closing PV disconnects, but it is a single engineered procedure rather than a full start-up/shut-down/emergency demonstration across a site.

tasks.label: Identify methods for laying out, orienting, and mounting modules or arrays to ensure efficient installation, electrical configuration, or system maintenance.

instances.label: Residential steep-slope (composition shingle) rooftop: before mounting, the lead installer determines the module layout method — portrait vs. landscape orientation, number of rows, rail runs relative to rafter spacing, code-required fire setbacks and access pathways, and where conduit/string runs will drop to the inverter — reconciling the design drawing with what is actually on the roof.

Commercial low-slope/flat roof: determining the array layout method for a ballasted or attached racking system — row pitch to avoid inter-row shading, tilt and azimuth, block grouping into strings, ballast/attachment pattern within roof load limits, and placement of combiners and walkways for future maintenance.

Ground-mount, carport, or tracker array: identifying pier/foundation spacing and row pitch, module orientation and tilt, table-to-string mapping, trench and conduit routing, and vehicle/personnel access lanes for O&M.

Mid-installation field adjustment: an unforeseen condition (plumbing vent, dormer, new shading obstruction, unexpected rafter spacing, damaged decking) forces the crew to re-identify a mounting/layout approach on the spot, decide whether to shift, rotate, or drop modules, and confirm the revised electrical configuration with the crew lead or designer.

Maintenance/retrofit on an existing array: identifying how a failed module or racking component can be demounted and remounted, whether the existing layout permits access, and what mounting method preserves the string configuration and weatherproofing.

instances.label: Residential rooftop system commissioning/startup: installer climbs to roof and inverter location, verifies polarity, measures each string's open-circuit voltage and operating current with a multimeter and clamp meter at the inverter or rapid-shutdown combiner, performs an insulation-resistance test, verifies inverter AC voltage/frequency and startup, confirms expected production on the monitoring app, and records results on a commissioning sheet. Occupied single-family home, sloped shingle roof, ladder access, variable weather.

Residential service/troubleshooting call: homeowner reports low or zero production. Technician reviews monitoring data and inverter fault codes, then measures DC string voltage and current, module-level optimizer/microinverter readings, and AC output at the disconnect, sometimes with an IR camera, to isolate a failed module, optimizer, connector or breaker, and re-measures after the fix. Private home, cluttered attic/garage/roof access.

Commercial or institutional rooftop / small ground-mount array (school, warehouse, municipal site): commissioning verification or periodic O&M performance check — walk the array with an IR camera, clamp-meter string currents at each combiner, measure Voc and insulation resistance on suspect strings, compare readings and irradiance against inverter/monitoring data, and log results. Fixed layout, owner-controlled premises, roof or fenced yard.

Utility-scale or large ground-mount plant: array-wide performance assessment — thermal/visual survey of tens to hundreds of thousands of modules to find hot cells, diode failures, string outages, soiling and tracker faults, cross-checked against production data, producing a ranked anomaly/loss report for the O&M crew. Fenced plant with graded rows and controlled access.

Utility-scale/large commercial commissioning electrical testing: string-by-string polarity, Voc, Isc, insulation resistance and sampled IV-curve tracing at hundreds of combiner boxes, plus inverter commissioning parameter checks and data logging against design expectations. Fenced plant, hot and dusty outdoor conditions.

Balance-of-system equipment condition check at a plant or facility electrical yard/room: thermal scan of inverters, combiners, disconnects, transformers and switchgear for hot connections, reading inverter displays/meters and logging operating parameters (voltages, currents, temperatures, error states) into the maintenance record. Institution-controlled, fixed-layout equipment pad or electrical room.

instances.label: Residential rooftop service visit at a customer's home (pitched composition-shingle roof, 5-8 kW array): visual inspection of modules for cracks/hot spots, washing/rinsing panels, checking and re-torquing rail clamps and lag/flashing penetrations, resealing weather-sealed penetrations, verifying string voltages and inverter/rapid-shutdown operation, clearing debris, and writing up the service report.

Commercial/industrial flat-roof array preventive maintenance visit (100 kW-1 MW, ballasted or attached racking on a warehouse/school roof): module wash-down, IR scan of modules and combiner boxes, connector and conduit inspection, torque checks on racking and lugs, inspection of roof penetrations and ballast blocks, DC string testing, and log-out of findings.

Scheduled soiling removal (module cleaning) campaign across a utility-scale ground-mount plant (tens to hundreds of MW, fixed-tilt or single-axis tracker rows on graded, fenced land) to restore transmittance ahead of a performance-guarantee check.

Utility-scale plant preventive maintenance on array electrical and structural balance-of-systems: opening and inspecting combiner boxes, replacing blown string fuses and damaged MC4 connectors, re-torquing module clamps, pier and tracker fasteners, greasing/adjusting tracker drives and dampers, and replacing individual failed modules found by the IR report.

Power-conditioning equipment servicing at commercial and utility sites: string/central inverter annual PM — cleaning heat sinks and cabinet interiors, replacing air filters and cooling fans, torque-checking AC/DC lugs, clearing ground faults and arc-fault trips, firmware/monitoring checks, and swapping failed inverter modules.

Battery and safety-system maintenance on stored-energy PV systems (residential garage/wall-mount packs, small commercial cabinets, off-grid lead-acid banks): terminal cleaning and torque, electrolyte/state-of-health checks, capacity and insulation testing, ventilation and enclosure inspection, and verifying disconnects, breakers, and rapid-shutdown/labeling compliance.

sources.title: Ecoppia installs solar panel cleaning robots for AES project in California
sources.claim: Ecoppia's rack-mounted T4 cleaning robots were installed at an AES Clean Energy utility-scale solar site in California and clean tracker rows autonomously every night without operators or water, i.e. autonomous, deployed module cleaning inside an operating PV plant.

sources.title: Smarter E Products: New solar module cleaning solution from Ecoppia
sources.claim: Ecoppia's H4 robot is a fully ... module cleaning robot marketed for PV O&M fleets, confirming commercially available autonomous cleaning of fixed arrays.

sources.title: BVLOS Drone-in-a-Box Systems to Inspect Solar Power Plant
sources.claim: Percepto's drone-in-a-box performs highly automated BVLOS inspection flights over a large Texas solar power ... — automation of the aerial inspection portion of PV O&M only, with no physical service actions on modules, combiners, inverters or batteries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scheduled aerial thermographic/visual inspection of a PV plant. It shows autonomous data collection carries over, but it does not carry over to the hands-on service steps (fuse and connector replacement, torqueing, resealing) that the maintenance instances require.

sources.title: Automating utility-scale solar vegetation management can increase profitability
sources.claim: Renu Robotics' Renubot is an autonomous, RTK-GPS and lidar guided electric mower used for vegetation management at utility-scale solar plants — autonomous ground mobility among array rows, but only groundskeeping, not work on PV equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: solar-plant grounds maintenance. Demonstrates autonomous navigation of the same outdoor plant environment, but the manipulation demands (mowing vs. opening combiner boxes and torqueing hardware) do not transfer.

sources.developer: AES / Maximo (robotics startup incubated by AES)
sources.title: Meet The Robot Replacing Four Workers At A Time On Solar Projects
sources.claim: AES's Maximo robot autonomously drives through utility-scale arrays and places/mounts PV modules on racking, and has been deployed at a California site; it handles module placement but not the electrical service work of maintenance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: new module installation on utility racking. Module handling and clamping partially resemble replacing a failed module, but Maximo does not remove existing modules, make or break DC connections, test strings, or service combiners/inverters, so it cannot complete a maintenance instance.

sources.title: Fully autonomous robot for solar O&M
sources.claim: Mobile (non rack-mounted) solar array cleaning vehicles offered for PV O&M remain tele-operated rather than autonomous, indicating cleaning outside purpose-fitted rack systems still needs continuous human control.

tasks.label: Compile or maintain records of system operation, performance, and maintenance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Install active solar systems, including solar collectors, concentrators, pumps, or fans.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential pitched-roof PV array (12–30 modules) on a private home: locate rafters, set flashed roof attachments, mount rails, carry and hoist 20–30 kg modules up a ladder/hoist, set and torque clamps to spec, keep rows square on an irregular, sloped shingle or tile roof with vents, chimneys and setbacks.

Utility-scale ground-mount field: attach hundreds of thousands of modules to tracker torque tubes/rails in long repeated rows on a graded, fenced construction site, with pile foundations and racking installed ahead of module placement; dust, heat, mud and crew traffic.

Commercial/institutional flat roof (warehouse, school, big-box store): lay out and set ballasted or attached racking, hoist modules by crane/conveyor to the roof, place and clamp modules in arrays around HVAC units, curbs and walkways; building owner controls roof access.

Small ground-mount, pole-mount or carport/canopy array at a home or small business: set posts/foundation brackets, assemble frame, lift and bolt 8–40 modules onto the structure in a yard, field or parking lot taken as found.

Active solar thermal system on a home: mount flat-plate or evacuated-tube collectors on the roof, run and insulate supply/return piping, install circulating pump, expansion tank, differential controller and sensors, connect storage tank, fill and purge the loop.

Balance-of-system for an active solar installation: mount inverters/combiners and pumps or fans, run conduit and mounting hardware on walls and roofs, set and secure equipment, then check currents and commission the system.

sources.title: AES Maximo robot installs 100 megawatts of solar capacity - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Maximo's solar installation robot has an end-to-end mode in which the machine performs the whole module installation after an operator start, using AI vision to handle lighting, module and mounting-structure variation.

sources.title: Robots install 100 MW of solar panels on 1-GW AES project – Solar Power World
sources.claim: A fleet of four Maximo robots installed 100 MW of modules at the under-construction 1 GW Bellefield project in Kern County, California — sustained commercial module installation on an open utility-scale construction site.

sources.title: AES' Maximo: AI Solar Robot for Clean Energy
sources.claim: Maximo's lower robotic arm tightens the module clamps, i.e. the robot both places and mechanically fastens modules to rails/trackers, with lidar and cameras for placement.

sources.system: Leapting Automatic Navigation Solar Module Mounting Robot (Litian Intelligent)
sources.title: Leapting robot completes install of 10,000 PV modules – pv magazine Australia
sources.claim: Leapting's autonomous module-mounting robot completed its first commercial deployment at the 350 MW Culcairn Solar Farm in Australia, installing about 10,000 modules with complete automation of the installation ....

sources.title: Chinese robot does job of three to four humans installing thousands of panels at Australian solar project – RenewEconomy
sources.claim: The Leapting robot is a self-guided crawler with a robotic arm that lifts modules from a stack and places them into brackets, adapting to varying terrain and outdoor conditions at the solar farm.

sources.title: Terabase Energy's Next-Generation Terafab Completes Field Testing, Ready for Deployment (Business Wire)
sources.claim: Terabase's Terafab automated field factory autonomously assembles and installs utility-scale solar arrays in the uncontrolled conditions of active construction sites; its next generation installed 17 MW of the 225 MW White Wing Ranch project in Arizona.

sources.title: Terafab Solar Construction Automation | Terabase Energy
sources.claim: Terafab, an on-site automated assembly line for attaching solar modules to mounting structures, has installed more than 100 MW across multiple commercial US projects.

sources.title: Making solar projects cheaper and faster with portable factories | MIT News
sources.claim: Charge Robotics' portable factory is a purpose-built assembly line into which tracks, mounting brackets and panels ... and automatically assembled into complete solar bays with machine-vision quality control, then placed by an automated robotic vehicle; it automates all mechanical installation except pile driving.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly of racking-plus-module bays on a fixtured line. It substantiates that modules and mounting hardware presented to a machine can be joined and torqued autonomously — the same objects and precision as rooftop or small-array module mounting.

sources.title: Robotic solar pile driver three times faster than humans – pv magazine USA
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 is a fully ... solar pile driver covering survey, pile distribution, driving and inspection, installing the structural foundations of utility-scale arrays to sub-inch accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing the array's structural foundations at the same utility-scale outdoor sites, showing the structure-erection portion preceding module mounting is also autonomously handled there.

sources.system: Trinabot Rooftop Photovoltaic Panel Installation Robot
sources.title: Rooftop Photovoltaic Panel Installation Robot – Trinabot
sources.claim: Rooftop-oriented installation robots offered commercially handle transport, alignment and placement of panels but require human operators to finish the installation; autonomy of the whole rooftop job is not established.

roles.title: Helpers--Brickmasons, Blockmasons, Stonemasons, and Tile and Marble Setters
aliases: Firebrick and Refractory Tile Bricklayer Helper
Firebrick or Refractory Tile Bricklayer Helper
roles.description: Help brickmasons, blockmasons, stonemasons, or tile and marble setters by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

tasks.label: Mix mortar, plaster, and grout, manually or using machines, according to standard formulas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial masonry jobsite (school, warehouse, mid-rise): helper hauls 60-80 lb bags of preblended Type S mortar (or cement, lime and shoveled sand) to a gas or electric drum/paddle mixer set up in the laydown area, doses water from a hose, judges consistency by eye/feel, retempers, discharges into wheelbarrow and mortar tubs at the mason's pace, then washes out the drum. Weather, sand moisture and crew demand vary through the day.

Large commercial masonry or stucco job served by a bulk system: preblended mortar/grout arrives in a portable silo or 3,000 lb bulk bags; helper runs a silo-mounted continuous mixer (e.g., SPEC MIX D2W type), sets water flow, and produces mixed mortar/grout continuously into tubs, pumps or grout delivery systems all day, with automatic wash-out at the end.

Small residential/repair masonry or stonework (patio, chimney, veneer, tuckpointing, historic repointing): helper mixes modest batches by hand in a mortar box or wheelbarrow with a hoe, or in a small portable mixer, from bagged mix or site sand, matching a specified or color-matched formula; work occurs in a yard, driveway or occupied building with no fixed setup.

Tile and marble setter's helper: mixes 3-5 gallon bucket batches of thinset/medium-bed mortar and sanded/unsanded grout with a drill-mounted paddle in a bathroom, kitchen, or commercial interior fit-out; must hit the bag's water ratio, slake, remix, keep batches small so they do not skin over, and clean buckets and paddles between colors.

Plaster/stucco work: helper mixes plaster, stucco scratch/brown coat or veneer plaster, either in a plaster mixer or by feeding a continuous mixing pump (bag- or silo-fed) that hydrates and delivers material to the plasterer's hose or hawk, keeping supply matched to the applicators.

sources.title: Vulcan | ICON
sources.claim: ICON's Magma is an automated portable mixing unit that combines dry cementitious material, admixtures and water to a controlled formula and supplies the mix to Vulcan printers on site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: batching/mixing a cementitious mortar-like material (portland cement, fillers, admixtures, water) to a specified formula for immediate use by masons/printer. Same material class, same 'standard formula' requirement, and the mix must stay workable and pumpable, as jobsite mortar must.

sources.system: ICON Magma / Vulcan at Wolf Ranch
sources.title: Robots Building Neighborhoods: Inside the Technology Transforming Construction at Wolf Ranch in Texas
sources.claim: Magma performed formula-controlled mixing on an active residential construction site, adjusting hydration in real time to site temperature and humidity, across a 100-home build.
sources.transferJustification: Related task as above: on-site production of correctly proportioned cementitious mix. Shows the mixing station works outdoors on an unstructured construction site, fed from bulk bags, not only in a plant.

sources.system: PFT G 4 / RITMO mixing pumps (with SILOMAT silo feed)
sources.title: Knauf PFT - Mixing pumps
sources.claim: Knauf PFT continuous mixing pumps hydrate and mix machine-grade dry gypsum, lime and cement mortars fully automatically, fed from bags, buckets or a silo via the SILOMAT conveying system.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task for plaster/stucco: the machine doses water and mixes dry mortar to the product's specified ratio and delivers ready material; the human role reduces to feeding and setup.

sources.system: Automated grout batch/colloidal plants (AMIX Systems, ChemGrout class)
sources.title: Automated Batching System Technology for Grout Mixing - AMIX Systems
sources.claim: Modern grout mixing plants perform batching fully automatically under PLC control, with load cells weighing cement to a fraction of a percent and calibrated flow meters dosing water to the programmed water-to-cement ratio.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: proportioning and mixing cement grout to a specified formula. Same material class and a tighter proportioning tolerance than hand mixing; inputs must be presented through silos/weigh hoppers, i.e. a purpose-built feed.

sources.system: Matest E093 Automatic Mortar Mixer (and equivalents from Humboldt, NextGen)
sources.title: Automatic Mortar Mixer - Cement & Mortar Laboratory Equipment | Matest
sources.claim: Laboratory-grade automatic mortar mixers run standard mixing programs (EN 196-1/ASTM C305) with an automatic sand dispenser and machine-managed speed changes and mixing sequences, producing small mortar batches to a standard formula without an operator running the cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mixing a small batch of cementitious mortar to a written standard formula, including timed slake/remix steps analogous to thinset slaking. Materials must be presented in the machine's bowl and hopper, a purpose-built presentation.

sources.system: SPEC MIX D2W continuous mixing system on G7000/Ten Bagger silo
sources.title: D2W - CONTINUOUS MIXING SYSTEM (operating and safety instructions)
sources.claim: SPEC MIX silo-mounted continuous mixers act as an on-site batch plant producing mortars, grouts, stucco and shotcrete at jobsites, with water flow set by valve and flow meter and a push-button self-clean cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task (silo-fed jobsite mortar/grout mixing), but water is set and consistency judged by an attending operator, so autonomy is unclear and this item is used only as context.

sources.title: Startup emerges from stealth with $25 million for robots that lay bricks as fast as humans
sources.claim: Monumental's autonomous ground robots work on real construction sites laying brick, with one robot dedicated to ferrying mortar that is dispensed from a bulk site silo.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: jobsite mortar supply. It shows silo-dispensed mortar is the machine-compatible supply mode on real sites, but the mixing itself is done by the silo system, not by a mobile robot.

tasks.label: Cut materials to specified sizes for installation, using power saws or tile cutters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential remodel (kitchen/bath): helper sets up a wet tile saw in the garage, driveway or the room itself and cuts ceramic/porcelain field tile to the setter's marks - straight rips, L-cuts around door jambs, notches and hole cuts for pipes and outlets - handing pieces back within a minute or two as the setter works. Dusty, cluttered, occupied home; layout differs house to house.

Masonry jobsite (house foundation, commercial CMU wall): helper runs a table masonry saw at a cut station, cutting standard concrete block and brick to length to fit the course layout (half blocks, closures, jamb blocks) and stacking cut units for the masons. Open ground, weather, dust, other trades moving nearby.

Same masonry jobsite, irregular field cuts: bevels and angled/rake cuts for gables and sills, notches around rebar, ties and openings, and cutting brick veneer pieces with a handheld cutoff saw or grinder in tight spots or up on the scaffold, to marks made from field measurements.

Marble/large-format work: helper cuts natural stone tile, marble thresholds or large-format porcelain slabs on a bridge/rail saw set up at the jobsite or in a staging area - long straight cuts, miters for outside corners, sink or pipe openings - where a chipped or off-square piece scraps expensive material.

Contractor's stone/tile shop or fabrication bay: helper loads slabs and stone tile onto a bridge saw and cuts pieces to the dimensions on the cut list before they are palletized and delivered to the site. Fixed layout, standard equipment, company controls who is present.

Hardscape/exterior masonry: helper cuts concrete pavers, segmental retaining-wall block and flagstone with a table saw or cutoff saw on an outdoor site - curve cuts on paver fields, tapered wall block, trimming irregular natural stone to a chalk line - on uneven ground in the weather.

sources.title: Bricklaying robots can now build tennis-court-sized walls in 4 hours
sources.claim: FBR's Hadrian X blocklaying robot works from a CAD plan on outdoor building sites; workers feed pallets of masonry blocks into the truck and onboard 'dehacker' robots unpack the blocks and cut them to size as required with an internal circular saw before they are laid.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is robotic blocklaying, but the cited step is literally this task: masonry units are cut to the sizes the wall plan specifies, immediately prior to installation, by a machine-controlled saw on the jobsite.

sources.title: Hadrian X bricklaying robot builds first homes in demo program (RBR50 2025)
sources.claim: Hadrian X is a mobile blocklaying machine that works outdoors in uncontrolled environments building from a 3D CAD model; in 2024 it completed the first five homes of a US demonstration program with CRH ....
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the environment (real outdoor US residential building sites) and autonomy level of the machine whose internal saw performs the cut-to-size step.

sources.title: FAQs | FBR
sources.claim: FBR states Hadrian builds directly from a ... and can cut blocks to size for ..., reducing on-site waste and over-ordering.
sources.transferJustification: Developer documentation that the machine's cut-to-size output can be produced as cut blocks for later installation, i.e. the helper's deliverable, not only blocks the machine lays itself.

sources.title: Autocut Line - Automated Systems | BACA Systems
sources.claim: BACA Systems' Robo SawJet is a commercially sold KUKA-robot sawjet cell used by stone fabricators to cut granite, quartz and porcelain slabs into finished pieces (straight cuts, miters, sink and hole cutouts); the Autocut Line adds robotic loading and unloading of ... for about 2,000 sq ft per shift ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task is stone countertop fabrication: the same materials a marble/tile helper cuts (granite, marble, engineered stone, porcelain slab), the same cut types (rips, miters, notches, holes) and tighter tolerances, with the workpiece brought to a purpose-built cutting cell.

sources.system: OMAX / MAXIEM / OptiMAX abrasive waterjet with IntelliMAX software
sources.title: Transform Your Cutting: OMAX Waterjets for Marble, Tile, Ceramic, and Stone
sources.claim: OMAX abrasive waterjets are commercial CNC machines used to cut marble, tile, ceramic and stone for countertops, backsplashes and architectural stone, including multi-axis bevels and 3D shapes, without cracking or chipping.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is CNC waterjet fabrication of tile/stone pieces: identical materials (ceramic tile, marble, porcelain) and identical geometry to a setter's cut list - rips, L-cuts, pipe/outlet holes - cut to CAD-specified dimensions once the piece is on the machine table.

tasks.label: Erect scaffolding or other installation structures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Exterior multi-lift frame or system scaffold erected around a commercial/institutional masonry job: helper sets mudsills and base plates on graded, uneven ground, stacks frames, pins cross braces, lays planks, adds guardrails and toeboards, and ties the run to the building as the wall rises; weather, mud, deliveries and other trades present.

Interior staging for tile, marble or block work in a building under construction or renovation: helper rolls out and assembles baker's/rolling scaffold towers or plank-and-trestle platforms, levels them on finished or rough floors, and repositions them repeatedly around fixtures, doorways and stacked materials.

Raising, adjusting and striking scaffolding as the work progresses: adding lifts and planks so masons stay at working height, moving guardrails, relocating a bay, then dismantling the run, handing components down and loading them on a truck at job end.

Residential job: helper sets pump jacks, ladder jacks or a small tubular tower on lawn, soil or a sloped driveway for brick veneer, chimney or stone work, shimming and blocking to get plumb and level on soft ground around landscaping.

Other installation structures and staging built on site: mortar board stands, mixing/cutting station and tile-saw bench, a plank work platform on trestles, temporary braces and dust/weather enclosures set up near the work face.

sources.title: KEWAZO LIFTBOT - Edison Awards
sources.claim: Kewazo's LIFTBOT, the leading commercially deployed scaffolding robot, is a robotic hoist that climbs the scaffold and moves scaffold components and materials vertically; human erectors still assemble the scaffold.
sources.transferJustification: This is a sub-step (material transport) of scaffold erection, not completion of it: the robot delivers parts to human erectors who perform all assembly, so it cannot support a positive judgment on this task.

sources.title: Meet the robot that transports scaffolding
sources.claim: The Kewazo scaffolding robot delivers scaffold parts to human scaffold erectors on site; erection itself remains manual.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (scaffolding), but the demonstrated function is component transport only; the structure is still erected by workers, so it substantiates no environment for the task itself.

sources.title: Automated Floor Truss Systems – House of Design Robotics
sources.claim: In offsite-construction factories, robotic cells autonomously assemble rigid structural frames from standardized members: robots lay out chords and pick and place webs into an assembly jig on automated roof/floor truss lines sold to major producers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling a load-bearing wooden frame from standardized members presented in a jig. It transfers to the E1 counterfactual of building a simple plank/trestle work platform from fixtured members (comparable members, payloads and placement precision), but not to erecting multi-lift pinned steel scaffold towers in situ.

sources.title: Watch A Robot Assemble Its Own IKEA Chair (VIDEO) – Asian Scientist Magazine
sources.claim: Two industrial arms with a 3D camera autonomously assembled an IKEA chair from its parts, including peg-in-hole insertion under force control, in a laboratory cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous assembly of a small rigid support structure from standard parts with pin/dowel insertion in a structured cell — the closest demonstrated analog to assembling a bench or trestle stand when parts are presented; it does not scale to heavy, multi-lift scaffold structures.

tasks.label: Locate and supply materials to masons for installation, following drawings or numbered sequences.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/institutional brick-and-block wall on an active construction site: the tender reads the elevation/spec to identify the right unit (blend, size, color, special shapes), finds the correct cubes among pallets scattered in the lay-down area, moves them with a telehandler/pallet jack over uneven ground and mud, and keeps masons stocked with units along the scaffold as the wall rises.

Tile/marble setter's helper on interior finish work in a building under construction or renovation: locate the correct cartons of field tile, trim, bullnose and accent pieces in the staging room per the tile layout drawing and pattern schedule, carry 30-60 lb cartons through corridors and stairs to the room, open them, and hand the setter the right pieces in the plan's order.

Cut/dimension stone or architectural veneer with numbered pieces: match stamped piece numbers on crated stone in the site lay-down yard against the shop-drawing elevation, unband crates, rig and move irregular 50-400 lb pieces on carts, dollies or hoists, and deliver them to the setter in the erection sequence amid crane and forklift traffic.

Residential or small-job masonry/hardscape at an occupied home: chimney, fireplace, patio or retaining wall; locate the specified stone/brick/paver on pallets in the driveway, sort by size, shape and color per the mason's sketch or plan, and haul it by wheelbarrow or buggy across lawn, steps and tight side yards to keep one or two masons supplied.

Shop, yard or warehouse staging: in a masonry supply warehouse, stone fabrication shop or prefab panel plant, pull materials against drawings/cut lists, stage cartons, pallets and numbered pieces on carts by piece number for the setters or for load-out to the job.

sources.system: Seegrid Lift CR1 / Lift RS1 / Palion AMR lift trucks
sources.title: Seegrid Sets the Standard with Industry-Leading Forklift AMR Payload Versatility
sources.claim: Seegrid's autonomous lift-truck AMRs move pallets and bins (up to several thousand pounds) inside manufacturing plants and warehouses, autonomously executing putaway and parts-to-line replenishment, i.e., locating stock and delivering the right load to the point of use on schedule.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: parts-to-line material replenishment in a plant. It is the same act as a mason tender's core function - identifying the required load from stock and delivering it to the installer's work position at the pace of the work - with comparable payloads (48x40 pallets, 3,500-8,000 lb) to cubes of brick or block.

sources.title: Warehouse Automation | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously identifies, picks and places cases up to 50 lb, unloading trailers and building palletized orders (i.e., selecting cases per an order list) in warehouses; it is sold commercially.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order-driven case picking. Cartons of tile (30-60 lb) are within Stretch's 50 lb case range, and 'build palletized orders' is the same select-per-list-and-stage function as pulling the cartons a tile setter's drawing calls for.

sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Stretch robots are in multi-site commercial service unloading cases for DHL, with ten units across three countries as of mid-2025 and rates of about 700 cases per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (case handling per order); this item establishes real multi-site deployment and throughput, not just a demo.

sources.title: Amazon tops 1 million robots: Here's what they do
sources.claim: Amazon operates fleets of autonomous systems in fulfillment centers that retrieve stored inventory and bring it to human workstations, and robotic arms (Sparrow) that pick specified individual items from containers into the tote for a given order.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: goods-to-person order fulfillment. 'Locate the specified item and supply it to the human worker who will use it, in the order's sequence' is the same information-plus-handling loop as supplying a mason per a numbered sequence, in an institution-controlled facility.

sources.title: Breton Jot | Handling robot marble granite Lapitec ceramic quartz
sources.claim: Breton's Jot is a numerically controlled handling robot used in stone fabrication plants to load, unload, relocate and flip marble, granite, ceramic and quartz slabs, including 'block recomposition' mode in which semi-finished slabs are returned to their exact original position in the sequence.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated slab handling in a purpose-built fabrication line. It handles the same heavy, fragile stone the helper stages and keeps pieces in a numbered/original sequence, but only with slabs presented on racks, conveyors and turntables built around the machine.

sources.system: EKOSORT DINAMICA sorting/stacking and gantry palletizing lines
sources.title: EKOSORT DINAMICA | SACMI
sources.claim: Sacmi supplies automatic sorting, stacking, packaging and palletizing lines that handle ceramic tiles and slabs of any size and sort them by grade/type before palletizing, running as fixed automation in tile plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sorting and stacking tile/slab product by class in a plant. Shows machine handling of exactly the materials in question (tile, large slabs) when the material is conveyed to the machine in a purpose-built line - the E1 counterfactual - but not selection and delivery in a human work setting.

sources.title: MULE Lifting System | R.I. Lampus
sources.claim: On real masonry jobsites the state of the art for handling block and stone is the MULE, a mason-operated lift-assist arm mounted on the scaffold that makes units up to 135-150 lb feel weightless; the worker still locates, guides and places every unit.
sources.transferJustification: Same task and setting (supplying masonry units on a jobsite). Cited as a negative bound: the commercially deployed jobsite device is a human-guided lift assist, not an autonomous locate-and-supply system.

sources.title: KEWAZO LIFTBOT - Edison Awards
sources.claim: Kewazo's LIFTBOT is a battery-powered robotic hoist that climbs scaffolding and moves scaffolding parts and materials vertically on construction and industrial sites; loading and unloading at each level is done by workers and the unit is remote-controlled/app-directed.
sources.transferJustification: Same setting (jobsite material movement). Cited as a bound: it automates only a vertical transport leg on a fixed rail, with humans locating, loading and unloading the material, so it does not complete the locate-and-supply task.

tasks.label: Clean installation surfaces, equipment, tools, work sites, or storage areas, using water, chemical solutions, oxygen lances, or polishing machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: On an active jobsite, cleaning newly installed masonry/tile surfaces: sponging grout haze off a just-grouted tile or marble floor/wall, wiping mortar smears off block and brick, and detergent/acid wash-down and rinse of a brick veneer wall after the mason finishes, working around scaffolding, drop cloths and adjacent finished work.

Cleaning tools and equipment during and after the shift: hosing out and scraping the mortar mixer, buckets, hawks, trowels, mortar boards and wheelbarrows, flushing the wet saw and grout sponges, at a hose bib or wash-out area on the jobsite or in the truck/yard.

Cleaning the work area floor: sweeping and vacuuming brick dust, cut-tile chips and mortar droppings, wet-vacuuming saw slurry and hosing/squeegeeing the slab so the next trade can work, amid cords, hoses, stacked material and other trades.

Clearing and removing scrap and rubble: shoveling hardened mortar lumps, broken brick/tile, banding, mortar bags and pallet scrap into buckets or a wheelbarrow and hauling it to a dumpster or debris chute; cleaning up spilled sand or mortar.

Cleaning and tidying the employer's shop, tool crib, storage areas and material yard: sweeping/scrubbing shop and storage-room floors, washing down the slab-storage area, rinsing racks and staging areas between jobs.

On-site grinding and polishing of installed stone or concrete: helper changes grit sequence, pad/segment type, wet vs. dry, machine speed and water feed for the material (concrete vs. marble vs. terrazzo) and the specified finish, including edge and corner work in occupied or partially finished buildings.

Stone/tile fabrication or staging shop with fixed layout and standard machines: helper adapts the grinding, polishing and washing routine to the slab or piece at hand (granite vs. marble vs. engineered quartz), changing abrasives, feed and cleaning method for the material and required finish.

Brick/block masonry: helper cuts off mortar squeeze-out with a trowel, strikes/tools the bed and head joints, and brushes and cleans mortar smears from the brick or block face, on scaffold or at grade, exterior weather, following the mason up the wall.

Post-cure residue: removing hardened grout haze or mortar/efflorescence residue after the joints have set — cheesecloth/pad buffing of tile and stone, scraping stray grout from joints, dilute-acid or proprietary wash-down of brick and stone faces with rinse.

Ad hoc fetching inside the site: helper is sent to bring a specific tool or machine (wet saw, mixer, grinder, blades, buckets, levels) from the gang box or truck to the setter's current location.

Residential or occupied-building tile/stone job: unload the van at the curb or driveway and carry boxes of tile, bags of mortar, a wet saw and hand tools through doorways, stairs and finished rooms to the work area, protecting finishes.
Vertical supply to masons working at height: load block, brick and mortar onto a scaffold hoist or mast climber, ride up, and stack the material on the narrow scaffold deck within the masons' reach.

tasks.label: Provide assistance in the preparation, installation, repair, or rebuilding of tile, brick, or stone surfaces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New-construction masonry tending (commercial/institutional and residential): helper mixes mortar in a paddle mixer, loads mud boards and brick/block onto scaffold or forklift, hauls units over rough ground, wets/cuts units on a masonry saw as the mason calls for them, strips scaffold and cleans the wall and work area at day's end. Weather exposed, layout changes daily.

Stone work at homes and commercial exteriors: helper carries and stages heavy irregular natural or manufactured stone for veneer, steps, patios and mortared garden walls, mixes and delivers mortar, wet-saws pieces to the mason's marks, points and washes the finished stone.
Landscape/retaining walls built from large boulders and rubble on grading or park sites: helper rigs and stages stone for machine placement, sorts and shims pieces, backfills and cleans the site.

Commercial interior tile installation (hotel, hospital, school, retail fit-out under construction): helper moves tile pallets and setting materials into the space, mixes thinset batches continuously, feeds tile and mortar to the setter across large open floors, cuts field and edge tiles, sponges and cleans grout haze.

Residential tile work in occupied homes and new houses: helper carries material up stairs into a small bathroom or kitchen, demos old tile, mixes small thinset and grout batches, cuts tile around toilets, drains and cabinets, holds and hands tools to the setter, protects finishes and cleans up.

Repair, repointing and rebuilding of existing tile, brick and stone: helper grinds out and refills deteriorated mortar joints, cuts out and replaces spalled brick or stone units, patches cracked tile and regrouts, works from scaffold/ladders in dusty conditions in occupied or older structures with non-standard materials.

sources.claim: Monumental's electric robots autonomously lay bricks and apply mortar for masonry walls on active construction sites; the company works as a subcontractor and its robots have built walls for over 100 homes, a school, a hotel and canal walls in NL/UK.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the bricklaying the helper tends. Same objects (brick, mortar), same wall, same jobsite; if the machine both places units and applies mortar, the assistance the helper supplies at the wall is largely absorbed by the machine.

sources.title: With new funding, Monumental plans to bring its construction robots to the U.S. - The Robot Report
sources.claim: In Monumental's deployments the human crew retains the tending duties: operators deploy and oversee the ... and intervene, while the site crew prepares the site and does all work outside the masonry process.

sources.title: Hadrian X bricklaying robot builds first homes in demo program - The Robot Report (RBR50 2025)

tasks.label: Move or position materials such as marble slabs, using cranes, hoists, or dollies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outdoor jobsite supply at ground level: a masonry helper moves pallets of brick/CMU, bags of mortar and stone units from the delivery/laydown area to the masons at the wall using a two-wheel dolly, brick cart, wheelbarrow or pallet jack, over mud, ruts, hoses, rebar and shifting stockpiles, restocking as the crew advances.

Commercial/institutional building interior under construction: helper moves palletized and boxed tile, marble tile, thinset and setting materials from the ground-floor delivery point up the freight/temporary elevator and along corridors to the tile setters' staging point on the work floor, using a dolly or pallet jack on bare concrete floors amid other trades.

Residential or occupied-building renovation: helper carries and dollies boxes of tile and small marble pieces up stairs, through narrow doorways and cluttered furnished rooms, protecting finished floors, staging material where the setter is working.

Hoisting on site: helper rigs a load (pallet of block, crated slab, bundle of stone) to a crane hook, mast-climber or material hoist with slings/forks, signals the operator, then receives, lands and unhooks the load on scaffold or an upper floor.

Stone fabrication shop or slab warehouse: helper moves 300-800 lb marble/granite slabs between A-frame racks, slab carts and the saw or CNC table using an overhead gantry crane with clamp or vacuum lifter, and loads finished pieces onto transport racks.

Final precise positioning: helper handles a large marble slab, countertop or stone panel with suction lifters/clamps and hand-guides it into its final position on a setting bed, cabinet run or wall, aligning edges to adjacent finished work without chipping it.

tasks.label: Apply caulk, sealants, or other agents to installed surfaces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential bathroom/kitchen: helper guns silicone caulk into tile change-of-plane joints (tub/shower corners, tile-to-tub, backsplash-to-countertop), then tools/smooths the bead and wipes excess, in an occupied or nearly finished home with fixtures, varied joint widths and tight access.

Applying impregnating grout/stone sealer to just-installed tile, natural stone floors, wall tile and countertops with roller, pad or pump sprayer, working section by section, then wiping/buffing residue off faces before it hazes; in homes or commercial interiors under construction.

Spray-applying masonry water-repellent/sealer to a brick or CMU wall at grade or from ground level on a commercial jobsite: saturating coverage, overlapping passes, back-rolling runs, masking adjacent surfaces, outdoors with wind and weather.
Spray-applying water repellent or sealer to a multi-story masonry facade from a scaffold, swing stage or boom lift, repositioning the platform, working at height around windows, ledges and trim.

Commercial jobsite: preparing masonry expansion/control joints and joints between dissimilar materials - cleaning the joint, inserting backer rod, gunning polyurethane sealant and tooling the bead concave, along irregular wall runs and around penetrations.

Detail work: caulking/sealing around fixtures, thresholds, saddles, window sills, pipe penetrations and trim edges after tile or stone work, small runs in varied orientations, followed by cleanup of the work area.

sources.system: FANUC dispensing/sealing robots (LR Mate 200iD robotic sealing system, Adaptec Solutions integration)
sources.title: Dispensing and Sealing Robots and Cobots | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC's dispensing and sealing robot line includes fielded systems that place accurate silicone beads on fixtured parts held in nests, with laser inspection of the bead - i.e., automated caulk-bead application in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial silicone/sealant bead dispensing. It is the same physical act as caulking - extruding a controlled bead of viscous sealant along a joint on a workpiece - at bead tolerances tighter than a caulked tile joint, but only with the workpiece fixtured and presented in a nest (E1).

sources.title: Paint solutions for Automotive | ABB - sealing robots
sources.claim: ABB supplies turnkey robotic seam-sealing systems that apply and smooth sealant over visible seams on car bodies inside automated paint-shop cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive seam sealing, which is bead application into and over joints with cosmetic (visible-seam) quality requirements. It transfers to caulking joints only where the workpiece arrives fixtured on a conveyor in a fenced booth, i.e. E1.

tasks.label: Correct surface imperfections or fill chipped, cracked, or broken bricks or tiles, using fillers, adhesives, or grouting materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Punch-list touch-up on a residential or light-commercial job site: helper finds chipped corners, gouges and hairline cracks in installed glazed ceramic/porcelain wall and floor tile in a bath, kitchen or lobby, cleans the void, mixes a color-matched epoxy/ceramic filler, packs it, strikes it flush and wipes the surrounding tile clean. Repairs must be visually invisible at handover; work is done in place, in a partly finished, cluttered interior.

Natural stone on a job site: filling the pits, voids, worm holes and hairline fissures in installed travertine, marble or limestone floor/wall tile with grout or color-matched polyester/epoxy filler, then razoring, honing or buffing the fill flush with the stone face. Dozens to hundreds of small defects scattered over a floor, each a different size and shade.

Exterior masonry: patching chipped, spalled or broken brick and block faces and filling cracked units with repair/patching mortar or sealant, color- and texture-matched to the existing wall, worked from ground level, ladder or scaffold on an occupied or under-construction building, in variable weather and dust.

New tile floor at grouting stage: filling voids, pinholes, gaps and low spots in the joints across a freshly grouted floor with grout material (a further pass with a float), then wiping haze and excess off the tile faces before the mason inspects. Bulk, repetitive area work in an empty room of a building under construction.

Maintenance repair in an occupied institutional or commercial facility (school, hospital, hotel, store): routing out a cracked or chipped floor or wall tile and the failed grout around it, filling with epoxy/grout, matching color, and cleaning the area, working around furniture, fixtures and passing occupants during a service window.

Shop or staging-area bench work: pre-filling chips, fissures and open seams in stone tiles, slabs or fabricated countertops with color-matched polyester/epoxy resin before or during installation, then scraping and polishing flush, at a fabrication shop or contractor's staging table.

sources.system: Prometec GALILEO robotic resin application system
sources.title: Galileo automatic system for resin application | Prometec
sources.claim: Prometec's GALILEO is a commercial robotic cell for stone plants in which a high-resolution 3D scanner locates hollow spots and fractures in a slab and an anthropomorphic robot then applies resin along computed trajectories and performs retouch work, replacing manual resin filling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: filling cracks, fissures and voids in stone with resin filler. It is the same operation the helper performs on chipped/cracked stone and tile units — vision-located defect, curable filler packed into the void, then finished flush by the downstream grinding/polishing stage — on the same class of flat, brittle masonry workpieces, at comparable sub-millimetre precision, but with the workpiece conveyed and fixtured in a plant.

sources.system: IonBreton resin line (with Breton Okto slab-loading robot)
sources.title: IonBreton | Resin Line For Repair Marble Granite Slabs
sources.claim: Breton's IonBreton resin line is a commercial slab-repair line for marble and granite in which slabs are loaded by a suction-cup robot, epoxy components are dosed automatically, and fresh resin is added in a later station to fill cracks and voids revealed after the first application.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine repair of cracked/chipped stone units with filler. Same materials (epoxy/polyester fillers), same workpieces (stone slabs and tiles) and same accepted output (voids filled and surface finished flush) as the helper's stone-filling work, achieved with the work presented to the machine on a line.

sources.system: Fabrica AI V5 autonomous tile grouting robot
sources.title: Press information - Fabrica AI's V5 Grouting Robot Makes Waves at BCA Tech Exchange (bauma 2025 exhibitor press release)
sources.claim: Fabrica AI's V5 tile grouting robot autonomously fills all grout lines on tiled floors and cleans off excess grout in apartments under construction, navigating obstacles without BIM or prior setup; humans only move it between rooms, reload grout and change water.
