sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying grouting material to fill the joints of a newly tiled floor and cleaning the tile faces. It uses the same grout material, the same floors, and delivers the same accepted output as the helper's joint void-filling/wipe-down pass, on live construction sites.

sources.title: 3M Finesse-it Robotic Paint Repair System wins another international SURCAR award (PR Newswire)
sources.claim: 3M's Finesse-it Robotic Paint Repair ..., commercialized in 2021, uses a vision system to identify surface defects on vehicle bodies on the assembly line and robotically sands and polishes each defect out to a consistent finish.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously correcting localized surface imperfections to an aesthetic standard on a fixtured workpiece. It shows vision-driven defect finding plus abrasive finishing at cosmetic quality inside a purpose-built cell, the finishing half of a fill-and-level repair, though on painted steel rather than masonry.

sources.title: Travertine Tile Production | Stone Tile Depot
sources.claim: Travertine tile plants use dedicated filling machines that spread filler with multiple blades to fill the holes across the tile surface before the tiles are cured and polished.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: filling voids in stone tiles with filler at tile scale rather than slab scale; corroborates the Prometec/Breton evidence that this repair is executed by machines in a purpose-built plant, but its degree of automation is not established so it is treated as non-supporting.

roles.title: Helpers--Carpenters
roles.description: Help carpenters by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

tasks.label: Erect scaffolding, shoring, or braces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Exterior frame/system scaffold at a residential or light-commercial jobsite: helper hauls and hands up 20–35 kg steel frames, cross-braces, base plates and planks over uneven ground, sets mudsills and levels bases, pins frames as the stack rises, lays planks, adds guardrails and wall ties, in weather and around other trades.

Interior rolling/baker scaffold or pump-jack setup inside a building under construction or fit-out: assemble tower from frames, casters, outriggers, planks and guardrails on a cluttered, partly finished floor; level on an uneven slab; break down and reposition repeatedly through the day.

Temporary bracing during framing: cut 2x4 kickers and stakes, hold and position diagonal braces while the carpenter plumbs a stick-framed or tilt-up wall, then nail braces to studs and to the deck, stakes or ground; also brace formwork panels and door/window bucks.

Shoring for concrete work: set adjustable steel post shores or frame shoring towers under deck/beam formwork per an engineered layout, place stringers and joists, plumb posts, screw-jack them to grade, and install X-braces and diagonal ties on mud, gravel or a green slab.

Temporary shoring in remodel/repair: install jack posts on pads, build temporary stud shoring walls, or set needle beams to carry floor or roof loads while a bearing wall or beam is removed, inside an existing, often occupied building with irregular framing, finishes and tight access.

sources.title: Robotics firm Kewazo gets a $10M lift | Construction Dive
sources.claim: The most advanced fielded scaffolding robot, Kewazo LIFTBOT, is a battery-powered hoist that climbs the scaffold and moves components to height; human scaffolders still perform all assembly (pinning frames, bracing, planking).
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (scaffolding erection): it establishes that the deployed robotic capability is vertical material transport, not assembly of the scaffold itself.

sources.developer: WEINMANN Holzbausystemtechnik / HOMAG (distributed by Stiles Machinery)
sources.date: 2025-01 product page (systems in commercial use for years)
sources.title: WEINMANN FRAMETEQ Framing Stations - Stiles Machinery
sources.claim: WEINMANN FRAMETEQ framing stations in offsite-construction plants automatically position, index, cut and nail dimensional lumber into wall frames held in the machine's fixtures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-fed positioning and nailing of 2x lumber members into a fixtured frame. Same objects (dimensional lumber), same fastening (nails), and equal-or-tighter placement tolerance than nailing temporary braces, so it substantiates brace installation when the work is fixtured and presented to the machine (E1).

sources.system: House of Design robotic roof/floor truss assembly systems
sources.title: Video Showcase: Robots at the truss plant | HBS Dealer
sources.claim: Fully automated robotic truss lines pick, position and fasten lumber chords and diagonal web members in jigs at production plants in the US.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robots place and fasten diagonal lumber bracing members (truss webs) into a jigged assembly. Comparable members, comparable precision, work presented by conveyor/fixture — supports brace erection only in a purpose-built cell (E1).

sources.system: Robotic collaborative system for reciprocal frame structures (Chea et al.)
sources.developer: Nanyang Technological University / Kyoto (published CACAIE; reviewed in TSE)
sources.title: An integrated review of automation and robotic technologies for structural prefabrication and construction | Transportation Safety and Environment
sources.claim: A research mobile-manipulator system (UR10/UR10e arm on a MiR100 base) autonomously placed temporary supports and then assembled a small reciprocal-frame timber structure in a laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing temporary supports for a structure under assembly. It is lab-scale with ~10 kg-payload arms and light members, so it does not substantiate erecting load-rated steel shoring or scaffold frames.

sources.title: DokaXbot Lift - Doka
sources.claim: The most advanced formwork-shoring robot on the market positions slab formwork panels overhead but is semi-automated and remote-controlled by a worker on the ground.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task for slab shoring/formwork erection; it is remote-controlled, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Tilbury Douglas becomes first contractor to launch a humanoid robot on a construction site
sources.claim: The first humanoid robot deployed by a tier-one contractor on a live construction site performs autonomous navigation and data capture, not material handling or structure erection.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the state of general-purpose humanoids on jobsites as of 2026: inspection/data capture, with no demonstrated erection of scaffolding, shoring or braces.

tasks.label: Clean work areas, machines, or equipment, to maintain a clean and safe job site.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interior of a commercial or multifamily building under construction: at end of shift the helper sweeps/vacuums sawdust, wood offcuts, nails and screws and fine dust off large open concrete floors and around stacked material, with other trades working nearby and the layout changing daily.

Single-family home build or occupied remodel: broom-and-shop-vac cleanup of sawdust, cut-offs and packaging in tight, cluttered rooms, on stairs, around furniture, tool cases, cords and drop cloths, without damaging finished surfaces.

Gathering and hauling scrap: picking up cut-offs, broken lumber, drywall and sheathing scrap, banding and packaging; loading a wheelbarrow, cart or debris chute; carrying it to the dumpster; stacking still-usable stock out of the way.

End-of-day cleaning of machines and equipment: blowing and brushing sawdust off miter saw and table saw tables, guards and dust ports, clearing chop-saw stands and benches, emptying dust-extractor/shop-vac canisters, wiping tools down before they go back in the gang box.

Millwork, cabinet or prefab-component shop: end-of-shift sweeping and vacuuming of sawdust and small offcuts from shop floors, aisles and the areas around stationary saws and CNC routers in a fixed-layout facility.

Final construction clean of a finished interior before punch-list/handover: vacuuming fine drywall and sawdust from floors and picking up remaining nails, screws and small debris so floors pass the superintendent's inspection.

sources.title: 自律走行清掃ロボットシステム「T-CleanX」を開発 | 大成建設株式会社
sources.claim: Taisei's T-CleanX autonomous cleaning-robot system (ARAMECLEAN rough-cleaning and KOMAMECLEAN dust-vacuum robots) cleans active building construction sites, generating its own routes without prior mapping or teaching in an environment that changes daily.

sources.title: 大成建設、自律走行清掃ロボットシステム「T-CleanX」を開発 - ドローンジャーナル
sources.claim: ARAMECLEAN collects relatively large debris such as wood offcuts, nails and screws as well as fine dust in one pass; the KOMAMECLEAN suction robot achieved a finish equivalent to the cleaning previously done by workers.

sources.title: 大成建設がケルヒャーの床洗浄ロボットを導入 国内建設現場での導入は初 - ロボスタ
sources.claim: Kärcher's KIRA B 50 autonomous scrubber, already used in airports and shopping malls, was adopted by Taisei as KIRAMECLEAN after trials on multiple construction sites with wood offcuts, nails and heavy dust and daily-changing conditions.

sources.title: Kajima and PFN Develop Autonomous Navigation System for Construction Site Robots
sources.claim: Kajima and Preferred Networks' AI cleaning robot 'Raccoon' autonomously cleans concrete floors of building construction sites; it was tested and introduced at multiple sites in the Tokyo ..., cleaning about 500 m2 in 100 minutes of continuous operation.

sources.developer: Takenaka Corporation / Okaya & Co. / Rental no Nikken
sources.title: ロボ本体とコーン4つですぐに工事現場を清掃、時間を半減 | 日経クロステック
sources.claim: The 'TO Gather' autonomous cleaning robot sweeps material that has fallen on construction-site floors into a pile; it was put into practical use in 2017 and has been rented and sold commercially since April 2018.

sources.title: Avidbots Neo Cleaning Robot Used by Many of the Newly Named Top Cleanest Global Airports
sources.claim: Avidbots' Neo autonomous floor-scrubbing robot is deployed at scale (over 1,000 units) in institution-controlled facilities including manufacturing plants, warehouses, airports and retail.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous sweeping/scrubbing of dust and loose floor debris in a facility. Same accepted output (a floor cleared of dust and small debris) and the same environment class as the shop or facility floor a carpenter's helper sweeps.

sources.title: Heavy Picker | Sorting Robot | ZenRobotics
sources.claim: ZenRobotics Heavy Picker robots sort bulky construction and demolition waste (wood, metal, stone) from a conveyor into chutes, working unmanned around the clock in sorting facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grasping heavy irregular C&D waste items (wood offcuts, board scrap, packaging) and depositing them into waste containers — the same object class and accepted output as a helper throwing scrap into a dumpster, but with material presented on a conveyor as an E1 setting presents work.

sources.system: Kawasaki machine-tending robot cells (air blow-off cleaning)
sources.title: Machine Tending | Robotic Applications | Complete Guide - Kawasaki Robotics
sources.claim: In fenced CNC machine-tending cells the robot routinely performs air blow-off to remove chips and dust from the machine fixture after each cycle as part of an unattended automated cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: clearing chips and dust off a production machine and its fixture with a blow-off nozzle in a purpose-built cell — comparable to blowing sawdust off a saw table and dust ports: coarse debris removal, no fine precision, machine in a known fixed position.

tasks.label: Align, straighten, plumb, or square forms for installation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/light-commercial foundation and basement walls at a house site: helper sets aluminum/steel panel forms or ICF blocks on footings, pulls string lines, squares corners by diagonal measurement, plumbs panels with a level, and holds/adjusts them with a sledge, wedges, ties and kicker braces while the carpenter fastens them. Uneven ground, mud, weather, changing layout each job.

Flatwork and footing edge forms: 2x lumber or steel edge forms, curb and sidewalk forms staked to line and grade; helper drives stakes, straightens the form between stakes to a string, checks grade with level/laser, squares the perimeter by diagonals, and nails/clamps braces. Outdoor, ground conditions vary.

Commercial/heavy-civil cast-in-place work: crane-set gang wall forms, column boxes, deck edge forms and bulkheads on a multistory building or bridge; helper guides the hanging panel, aligns panel joints and hardware, plumbs with turnbuckle kickers and plumb bob/laser, wedges and pins ties. Multi-ton assemblies, congested deck, other trades working.

Precast/prefab plant or on-site tilt-up casting bed: helper sets and squares steel/magnetic side forms and blockouts on a flat casting pallet or slab to a shop drawing, aligns joints between profiles, checks diagonals, repetitive standard panel and slab shapes.

Small, awkward one-off forms: stair landings, equipment pads, patch pours, curbs around obstacles; work in basements, crawlspaces, occupied buildings or tight excavations, irregular geometry, improvised bracing against existing structure.

sources.date: 2026-07 (product page, commercially offered for over a decade)
sources.title: Shuttering Robot | Progress Maschinen & Automation
sources.claim: Progress Group's Form Master shuttering/deshuttering robot is a commercially sold, fully automatic gantry robot in precast pallet-circulation plants that selects shutters from storage per CAD data, positions them precisely on the mould surface and activates their magnets, then strips and re-sorts them.
sources.transferJustification: Same task content as the helper's: positioning and squaring the side forms that define a concrete wall or slab element, to model dimensions, before pouring. Objects (steel side forms/shutters, blockouts) and required precision are comparable to jobsite panel forms; only the setting (fenced pallet line) differs.

sources.title: Robot for automatic shuttering in precast wall production | Elematic
sources.claim: Elematic's Shuttering Robot E9 is a commercial fenced robotic station that plots opening locations, places shutters on the mould table per the production plan and automatically optimises gaps and aligns shutters on the push edges for double wall, solid wall, sandwich panel and slab production.
sources.transferJustification: The listed functions are literally aligning and squaring forms for a concrete element; the station is surrounded by a safety ... and fed by a pallet conveyor, marking it as a purpose-built robotic cell (E1).

sources.title: Plotter/shuttering robot | Vollert Anlagenbau GmbH
sources.claim: Vollert's plotter/shuttering robots work fully automatically, placing shutters on the casting pallet to CAD data; the Smart Set shuttering robot installed in the M3SP precast plant in Cotia, Brazil achieves positioning accuracy within ±0.4 mm in daily production.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes worker-quality accuracy (±0.4 mm) and real production deployment for machine placement/alignment of concrete side forms, the same output the helper produces when squaring and straightening forms.

sources.title: Highly dynamic shuttering robot of the third generation - Concrete Plant Precast Technology
sources.claim: Weckenmann supplies fully automated shuttering robots handling double wall, floor slab and solid wall formwork in operating precast plants, including scanning the formwork surface and demolding shutters.
sources.transferJustification: Independent confirmation that automated placement/alignment of wall and slab formwork is standard practice in purpose-built precast lines, covering wall forms as well as flat slab forms.

sources.title: How Robots are Revolutionizing Formwork Assembly - Doka
sources.claim: The most advanced jobsite formwork machine from a major formwork supplier, Doka's DokaXbot Lift, is only semi-automated: an operator works it from ground level while the machine makes automatic fine adjustments to position slab formwork elements; it was shown as a reengineered prototype at bauma 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Closest jobsite system to this task; cited only to show that in-situ formwork positioning on construction sites (E3) remains operator-guided, supporting the negative E3/E2 judgments.

tasks.label: Select tools, equipment, or materials from storage and transport items to work site.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential jobsite (new framing, additions, decks): helper pulls dimensional lumber, sheathing, joists or trim from stacks on the ground, from the delivery bunk or from the truck/trailer, selects the right lengths and counts, and carries or wheels them across mud, scrap and uneven grade, up stairs or through the framed shell to the carpenter's work point.

Commercial/institutional jobsite interior (metal stud framing, doors and hardware, casework, finish carpentry): helper draws material from a floor staging area or laydown yard, loads a cart or pallet jack, moves it via hoist, elevator or ramp through corridors shared with other trades, and stacks it where the carpenter is working.

Tool and consumable runs: carpenter calls for a specific item (impact driver and bits, circular saw blade, chalk box, particular box of screws/nails, extension cord, level); helper identifies it in the gang box, job trailer or truck bed, retrieves it and brings it to the carpenter at the work point, then returns it to storage.

Shop or yard based helper (cabinet/millwork shop, truss or panel plant, lumberyard): pulls sheet goods, hardwood stock, hardware and fasteners from racks and bins per a cut list, and moves them by cart, pallet jack or forklift to a bench, saw or assembly table inside the facility.

Occupied-home remodel/service work: helper carries tool bags, power tools, sawhorses and small quantities of material from a van parked at the curb, through the front door, around furniture, floor protection and pets, up interior stairs to the room being worked, and hauls tools back out at day's end.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Moxi, a mobile manipulator, autonomously picks supplies out of hospital supply closets and delivers them to patient rooms in commercial hospital operation — the fetch-from-storage-and-deliver pattern of this task, for small items, in a structured human facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply fetch-and-delivery. It matches this task's structure — select a requested item from a storage location, transport it through the building, hand it off at the work point — with comparable object sizes to the tool/consumable runs and comparable precision demands (grasping loose items from shelving).

sources.title: Moxi reaches milestone of 100,000 autonomous elevator rides in hospitals - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi fleets run continuous autonomous deliveries across US health systems, including riding elevators between floors, with over 100,000 autonomous elevator trips logged — evidence the fetch-and-deliver capability is a sustained deployment, not a demo.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (supply/specimen transport); establishes reliability and multi-floor transport in an institution-controlled facility, which is what the commercial-interior and in-home carry instances reduce to under the E2 counterfactual.

sources.title: Third Wave Automation picks up Series C funding for robotic forklifts - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The TWA Reach autonomous high-reach forklift operates in fully autonomous mode to ... through an active warehouse, and is being deployed by Holman Logistics for inbound, racking, picking and replenishment moves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse unit-load handling. Inside a structured facility, building material is stored and moved as unitized loads on pallets or bunks exactly as warehouse goods are, so retrieving a load from a rack and delivering it to a designated work position is the same act at the same precision.

sources.title: Digit Moves Over 100,000 Totes in Commercial Deployment | Agility
sources.claim: Agility's Digit humanoid has moved more than 100,000 ... commercial operation at GXO's Flowery Branch facility, picking totes on and off AMRs and conveyors in a warehouse shared with people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse tote handling. It demonstrates legged mobile manipulation carrying containerized loads between storage/staging points and work stations in a human-occupied facility, the transport half of this task at E2.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously identifies and picks individual, varied products out of containers and places them into specific totes in fulfillment centers — item-level selection from storage in a purpose-built robotic cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order picking. It substantiates the 'select the correct item' element of this task — recognizing a requested SKU among mixed inventory and handling it — for the tool/fastener runs when the work is presented in bins at a station.

sources.system: House of Design robotic roof/floor truss systems
sources.developer: House of Design Robotics (installed at Builders FirstSource, Louws Truss)
sources.title: Video Showcase: Robots at the truss plant | HBS Dealer
sources.claim: Builders FirstSource operates fully automated House of Design robotic truss lines in which robots do the lifting, preplating and assembly of lumber components, moving cut lumber from feed positions into assembly jigs inside fenced cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: truss component manufacturing. It shows robots selecting and transporting the very materials of this task — dimensional lumber — from presentation racks to a work position, which is what the task reduces to when the work is fixtured and presented (E1).

sources.title: Construction | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: On active construction sites, the deployed autonomous capability of Spot is navigation for reality capture and surveying; Boston Dynamics markets it as a data-capture solution, not a material or tool fetching system.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to characterize the state of jobsite (E3) autonomy: the only established autonomous construction-site work is sensing/inspection, so no cited system selects and hauls tools or materials on an unstructured site.

tasks.label: Fasten timbers or lumber with glue, screws, pegs, or nails and install hardware.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rough framing on an active residential/light-commercial jobsite: helper holds studs, plates, blocking, headers and joists in place and nails them off with a pneumatic nailer under the carpenter's direction; nails plywood/OSB sheathing and subfloor; drives joist-hanger and hurricane-tie nails. Lumber is crowned or warped, layout changes as the crew works, and weather, debris and other trades are present.

Interior finish assist in an occupied or renovated building: gluing and nailing baseboard, casing, jamb extensions and shoe with a finish nailer; clamping and gluing mitered returns; hanging prehung doors and screwing hinges, strike plates, locksets, closet hardware, and cabinet hinges/pulls. Tight tolerances, visible surfaces, furniture and occupants nearby.

Exterior site carpentry: decks, stairs, fences and arbors - screwing down deck boards, lag-bolting ledgers, nailing rails and pickets, installing post bases, joist hangers and other galvanized hardware, outdoors on uneven ground and in variable weather.

Concrete formwork, shoring and temporary structures on site: nailing plywood to 2x lumber to build form panels, nailing wales, kickers and bracing, screwing walers and strongbacks, installing form ties and hardware; rough tolerances but muddy, congested, constantly changing site conditions.

Shop or component-plant prefabrication: helper works at benches or on a panel/truss line in a millwork shop, cabinet shop, component plant or crate shop - gluing, screwing, nailing and doweling lumber assemblies, boring and setting hinges and other hardware, on a fixed layout with standard equipment and controlled access.

sources.system: WEINMANN framing machine + WALLTEQ multifunction bridge at Bensonwood
sources.title: From Lumber to Bundle: The Prefabrication of a Bensonwood Panel
sources.claim: In Bensonwood's prefab plant a worker loads lumber into a WEINMANN framing machine, which automatically aligns and spaces the studs and nails the top and bottom plates to them; a WEINMANN multifunction bridge then nails the OSB sheathing to the panel from digital fabrication files.

sources.system: WEINMANN WALLTEQ M-300 / M-380 multifunction bridge
sources.title: WEINMANN Multifunction Bridge WALLTEQ M-300
sources.claim: The WEINMANN WALLTEQ multifunction bridge is a commercially sold CNC gantry that staples, nails, saws, marks and trims timber-frame wall, roof and floor elements in prefabrication plants.

sources.system: WEINMANN multi-function bridge panel line at Schwieters
sources.title: Schwieters Success Story - Stiles Machinery
sources.claim: A US component manufacturer (Schwieters) runs a WEINMANN-based panel line whose multifunction bridge performs automated nailing and stapling with accurate nail patterns and depth, with transfer tables moving panels between stations.

sources.system: Automated door machining and assembly line (Beth reference project)
sources.title: Automated door production line - machining and assembly
sources.claim: An installed turnkey automated door line at a Dutch door manufacturer bores and mounts hinges on door leaves automatically and machines the lock and handle side, running up to 3.3 doors per minute.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing door hardware. Same hardware (hinges, lock and handle furniture) and the same screw-driving precision on wood doors and jambs that a carpenter's helper performs by hand.

sources.system: GANNOMAT Express S1 CNC bore and hinge insertion machine
sources.title: GANNOMAT Express S1 CNC Bore and Hinge Insertion Machine
sources.claim: CNC bore-and-insert machines automatically drill for and insert hinges and other cabinet-door hardware into wood parts in seconds in ordinary shop production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing cabinet and door hardware. Same objects (hinges, mounting plates) and tolerances as the helper's hardware-setting work, on fixtured wood workpieces.

sources.system: HOMAG DRILLTEQ D-510 CNC drilling and dowel inserting machine
sources.title: CNC-Drilling and Dowel Inserting Machine DRILLTEQ D-510
sources.claim: CNC drilling and dowel-inserting machines automatically feed dowels, apply glue with monitored flow, drive the dowels and set fittings in wood workpieces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastening wood with glue and pegs (dowels). Identical fastening media and comparable wood components to the helper's glue-and-peg work, with the workpiece fixtured.

sources.system: Viking Turbo 505 / Voyager nailing machines with Joutech automated lumber feeding
sources.title: Joutech Explains More Details on Its Automation Partnership with Viking Engineering
sources.claim: Automated pallet nailing machines nail boards across stringers and blocks in lumber assemblies; Viking's Turbo 505 and Voyager nailers are now paired with automated lumber feeding for hands-off production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: nailing boards across supporting members, the same operation as nailing deck boards to joists or sheathing to framing, with construction-grade lumber at production reliability in a fixtured line.

sources.title: Adaptive Robotic Construction of Wood Frames
sources.claim: A perception-driven robotic cell assembles wood light-frame walls from real framing lumber, estimating stud poses and building two wall designs with better-than-code precision using both low- and high-quality lumber.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (assembling framing lumber into walls); shows that warped, variable construction lumber can be perceived and positioned by a robot cell, the main obstacle to automated fastening of framing.

sources.system: Robotic nailing cell for off-site mass timber assembly (KUKA KR250 with nail-gun multi-tool)
sources.title: Automated Nailing in Off-site Mass Timber Construction: Toward Robotic Assembly Solutions
sources.claim: A research robotic cell combining a KUKA KR250 with grippers and a nail gun performs automated nailing of mass-timber stud assemblies, validated on a six-stud configuration.

sources.title: Renovate Robotics Reveals Roofing Robot Prototype
sources.claim: The closest on-site nail-driving robot for wood construction, Renovate Robotics' Rufus, was a cable-suspended prototype directed by a technician with a tablet, nailing shingles on a mock roof inside a warehouse.
sources.transferJustification: Closest on-site nail-driving system to this task; cited to show the jobsite (E3) frontier is a technician-directed prototype, so it cannot support a positive E2 or E3 judgment.

tasks.label: Position and hold timbers, lumber, or paneling in place for fastening or cutting.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New residential framing on an open jobsite: helper lifts and holds studs, plates, headers, joists, blocking or a rafter plumb/square against variable, out-of-level existing work while the carpenter nails it off; mud, weather, ladders, changing layout.

On-site cutting support: helper steadies boards, timbers or sheet goods on sawhorses, a miter-saw stand or a table/track saw, feeding and holding the stock and supporting the offcut while the carpenter cuts.

Interior finish or remodel work in occupied homes / nearly finished buildings: helper holds paneling, plywood, trim or board tight and level to walls, soffits and ceilings (often overhead, around obstacles and finished surfaces) while the carpenter fastens.

Commercial or heavy construction: helper positions and holds formwork panels, blocking, ledgers, glulam or large timbers, often at height on scaffold or lifts and with crane assistance, while they are braced and fastened.
Off-site prefab shop or carpentry/millwork shop built for human work: helper holds lumber or panel stock against a jig, table or bench for nailing or cutting, with material stacked on the shop floor.

sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: Randek's commercially sold ZeroLabor robotic framing system automatically cuts and places studs ... and lifts, positions and secures studs in timber wall frames inside an offsite factory line.

sources.title: LIGNA Product 2025: ZeroLabor Robotic System (Randek)
sources.claim: Randek ZeroLabor sheet handling picks sheathing panels from stacks with vacuum cups, places them on the building component per the CAD file and fastens them by screwing, stapling or nailing; a squaring table first aligns deviations in the studs.

sources.system: Kawasaki BX250L wall sheathing cell (integrator SCADAware)
sources.title: Assembling Walls for Prefabricated Homes | Industrial Robots by Kawasaki
sources.claim: A four-robot Kawasaki/Guedel cell at prefab homebuilder Rehkemper positions heavy OSB sheathing onto pre-framed walls and nails it, with servo fingers straightening warped studs and a squaring table holding the frame to 1/16 in.

sources.title: Hundegger's Multi-tasking - Timber Trades Journal
sources.claim: Hundegger CNC timber machining centres grip, feed and hold timber components in position for automatic sawing, milling and drilling to +/-0.5 mm, single-operator, in timber-frame and truss plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine feeding and holding of stock for cutting. It is the same act the helper performs in the cutting-support instance - presenting and holding a timber or board rigidly while it is sawn - on the same objects and to tighter precision, with the work brought to the machine.

sources.system: Spatial Timber Assemblies (ETH Zurich / NCCR Digital Fabrication)
sources.developer: ETH Zurich Chair of Architecture and Digital Fabrication
sources.title: Robotic collaboration in timber construction | ETH Zurich
sources.claim: At ETH Zurich's Robotic Fabrication Laboratory two industrial robots hold a timber beam while it is sawn, drill it, and then jointly position beams in the precise spatial ... for connection; the assemblies were built into the DFAB HOUSE with partner Erne AG Holzbau.

sources.title: Japanese robots to work on high-rise buildings | The Construction Index
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy is a two-armed autonomous mobile robot that lifts a ceiling board into position with one arm and screws it to the base material with the other; it was in trials for installing boards at a high-rise site in Osaka and, at 1.6 t, requires dedicated walkways on site.
sources.transferJustification: Closest on-site analogue to holding paneling for fastening; cited to show the on-site state of the art is limited trials on prepared high-rise floors with dedicated walkways, not general finish carpentry in as-found buildings.

sources.title: Development of a humanoid robot prototype, HRP-5P, capable of heavy labor
sources.claim: AIST's HRP-5P humanoid performed autonomous gypsum board installation only at a simulated residential construction ... in the laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting and holding a board against framing for fastening. Cited as the closest humanoid capability and as evidence that it exists only as a laboratory mock-up demo, not on real sites.

sources.system: Adaptive robotic wood frame construction (industrial arm with eye-in-hand RGB-D)
sources.title: Adaptive robotic construction of wood frames | Construction Robotics (Springer)
sources.claim: Autodesk Research's adaptive wood-frame robot picks and places studs positioned randomly in the workspace using vision, but the technology is deployed in a factory-type robotic setting, not on site.

tasks.label: Cut timbers, lumber, or paneling to specified dimensions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential framing on an active job site: helper cuts 2x4/2x6 studs, plates, blocking, headers and rafter tails to lengths called out by the carpenter, using a circular saw or miter saw set on sawhorses amid mud, debris, cords, weather and moving trades.

Cutting sheet goods on site: ripping/crosscutting plywood, OSB sheathing, MDF or wall paneling to size with a circular ... and straightedge or track saw on a temporary cut station, matching field-measured openings.

Interior trim/finish work in a nearly finished or occupied building: cutting baseboard, casing, jamb stock and wall paneling to length and angle on a portable miter saw, tight tolerances and scribe-to-fit cuts, in furnished or dust-controlled rooms.

Heavy stock outdoors: cutting timbers, beams, posts, deck joists, and formwork lumber to dimension with circular saw, beam saw or chainsaw, often on the ground or on a stack, in weather and on uneven terrain.

Shop/prefab cutting: helper at a millwork, cabinet or component shop cuts lumber and panel stock to dimension at a chop-saw or panel-saw station from a cut list, with racks of stock and a fixed shop layout.

sources.system: Hundegger K2 / K2i CNC joinery machine
sources.title: High-Tech Timber-Frame Joinery Machine - Fine Homebuilding
sources.claim: Hundegger K2i CNC joinery machines are in routine commercial use in timber-framing shops, cutting timbers to length and performing joinery from a digital design, i.e. the exact 'cut timbers to specified dimensions' work in a purpose-built machine environment.

sources.system: Hundegger ROBOT-Compact / K2-Industry with automatic infeed
sources.title: ROBOT-Compact | Hundegger
sources.claim: Hundegger sells automatic infeed/handling packages that connect the timber stock in the factory to the joinery machine, so stock is presented to the saw and processed without a human making each cut.

sources.system: MiTek MatchPoint BLADE II linear saw
sources.title: MatchPoint BLADE II - MiTek Residential Construction Industry
sources.claim: MiTek's MatchPoint BLADE II is a commercially deployed, fully automated linear saw in truss/wall-component plants that cuts framing lumber (studs, chords, webs) to specified lengths and angles at 1/32-inch accuracy inside a guarded cutting chamber, with automated material handling.

sources.system: WEINMANN cutting and joinery systems / BEAMTEQ, timber frame production lines
sources.title: WEINMANN Timber Construction Machinery | High-Precision Solutions for Timber House Production
sources.claim: WEINMANN (HOMAG) timber-construction lines automatically saw rafters, beams, posts and studs to dimension in prefabricated house plants, driven directly from the CAD/CAM model.

sources.title: WEINMANN Multifunction Bridge WALLTEQ M-300
sources.claim: The WEINMANN WALLTEQ M-300 multifunction bridge saws sheathing and panel layers (plywood/OSB/plasterboard) to size and cuts openings automatically over a fixtured assembly table — the panel-cutting portion of the task in a purpose-built gantry cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sizing/trimming of sheathing and paneling on a wall element. Same materials (plywood, OSB, gypsum, panel stock) and same required precision as a helper cutting paneling to specified dimensions.

sources.system: Cosmic Buildings mobile robotic microfactory with ABB IRB 6710
sources.title: ABB and Cosmic use AI-powered robots to rebuild homes in Los Angeles area
sources.claim: ABB IRB 6710 robots in Cosmic Buildings' mobile microfactory fabricate structural wall panels to millimeter precision at a wildfire rebuild site in Pacific Palisades — but the robots work inside a purpose-built enclosed robotic cell trucked to the site, not on the site as found.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic fabrication of framed wall panels including member sizing. Shows that even site-adjacent robotic woodworking is done inside a machine-built cell, supporting E1 rather than E3.

sources.system: AutoSaw (Roomba Create with jigsaw + two KUKA youBots)
sources.title: Custom carpentry with help from robots | MIT News
sources.claim: MIT CSAIL's AutoSaw used mobile robots to cut lumber with a jigsaw and to load and cut beams on a chop saw, but only as a semi-autonomous laboratory demonstration with motion-capture tracking, not at worker quality on a job site.

sources.system: Mobile robot platform for on-site timber fabrication (ABB IRB4600 on track vehicle)
sources.title: Computational design and on-site mobile robotic construction of an adaptive reinforcement beam network for cross-laminated timber slab panels
sources.claim: On-site mobile robotic timber processing exists only as research: a track-vehicle-mounted ABB IRB4600 arm with a timber tool station, operating relative to a preinstalled panel surface as a semi-controlled environment — no deployed system cuts framing lumber on a job site as found.

tasks.label: Hold plumb bobs, sighting rods, or other equipment to aid in establishing reference points and lines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential jobsite, exterior: helper holds a leveling/grade rod on grade stakes, batter boards, and footing bottoms while the carpenter sights a builder's level or transit to set site grades and excavation/footing depths; muddy, sloped, uneven ground, hand-signal communication.

Elevation/reference transfer onto built work: helper holds the rod, target, or story pole against a foundation top, deck, ledger, or header while the carpenter shoots and marks a reference elevation to 1/8 in., often at height or on a ladder.

Helper holds a plumb bob, spirit level, or straightedge against a post, stud wall, door jamb, or concrete form and calls the reading while the carpenter racks, shims, and nails the brace; object must be held steady against wind, bumping, and the carpenter's adjustments.

Helper holds the dumb end of a chalk line, string line, or tape at a mark on a floor deck or slab so wall lines, partition lines, and reference points can be snapped and marked across a room or floor plate; debris, rebar, and other trades present.

Commercial jobsite: helper holds a prism pole or laser-receiver rod plumb over control points and layout points while the foreman runs a total station or rotary laser to lay out column lines, wall lines, and anchor points on a floor with active trades and clutter.
Interior finish stage: helper holds targets, story poles, or a laser receiver for ceiling-grid heights, soffit lines, and cabinet/casework reference lines inside a partially finished building.

sources.title: BIM-Driven Layout for Construction | Dusty Robotics
sources.claim: Dusty Robotics FieldPrinter is an autonomous jobsite robot that prints BIM-derived wall lines, points and text directly on construction-site floors to 1/16 in., replacing the two-person string-line-and-chalk layout crew.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated construction layout. The helper's rod/chalk-line holding exists only to establish reference points and lines on the deck; the robot produces the same accepted output (marked reference lines and points) on the same jobsite floors, at carpenter tolerances.

sources.title: Dusty Robotics Case Study | Simplexity Product Development
sources.claim: FieldPrinters have been deployed at production scale on real construction sites with major general contractors, indicating deployed, non-demo reliability in unstructured jobsite conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (construction layout) as above; establishes deployment maturity on ordinary jobsites rather than demos.

sources.title: How to Implement Construction Layout Robots at Your Worksites | HP Official Site
sources.claim: HP SitePrint is a commercially available autonomous layout robot that positions itself from a total station and prints layout lines, arcs, points and text on construction-site floors, traversing site conditions and avoiding obstacles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: total-station-referenced jobsite layout. The robot carries its own prism and self-positions, eliminating the rod/prism-pole holder while delivering the same marked points and lines.

sources.title: HP SitePrint Case Studies | HP Official Site
sources.claim: HP SitePrint has been used by contractors for interior layout of a 110,000 sq ft facility, holding 1/8-inch tolerance across the rack ..., i.e. finish-stage interior reference lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior layout printing inside a building under construction; the accepted output (reference lines/points to 1/8 in.) is what the helper's target/story-pole holding is meant to produce.

sources.title: These little robots are changing the way solar farms are built, saving time and money (CNBC)
sources.claim: CivDot is an autonomous four-wheeled marking robot that stakes out coordinate points with 8 mm accuracy on rugged outdoor construction terrain and is in commercial use by Bechtel in Texas and Nevada.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor construction staking. The rod-and-instrument pair exists to fix ground reference points and elevations; CivDot autonomously establishes and marks those points (with elevation data) on unimproved, sloped, muddy terrain.

sources.title: Civ Robotics FAQ | Construction Layout Robots
sources.claim: CivDot handles unimproved terrain up to 30-degree slopes and harsh weather, and works from point files carrying northing, easting and elevation, i.e. the same reference data a rodman helps capture.
sources.transferJustification: Supports the same related task (construction staking) by establishing that the outdoor conditions of residential/site grade work are within the robot's operating envelope.

sources.system: Spatial Timber Assemblies (DFAB HOUSE robotic timber assembly)
sources.developer: ETH Zurich / NCCR Digital Fabrication with Erne AG Holzbau
sources.title: Spatial Timber Assemblies: Architecture, Robotics, and Craftsmanship - urbanNext
sources.claim: Two cooperating industrial robot arms held and positioned 487 timber beams in precise computed spatial positions in ETH's Robotic Fabrication Laboratory while human workers bolted the connections - the machine equivalent of holding a member to its reference line while a carpenter fastens it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic holding of a structural member at a surveyed reference position while a human fixes it. This is functionally what holding a plumb bob/level/rod against a post does - keep the member on its reference line until braced - with comparable objects (timber members) and tighter precision, but only in a purpose-built robotic cell.

sources.title: Jaibot Semi-Autonomous Drilling Robot - Hilti GB
sources.claim: Hilti Jaibot is a commercially sold, BIM-driven jobsite robot that localizes itself indoors from a total station and then marks and drills ceiling and wall points per plan inside buildings under construction; an operator positions it and it executes the point sequence.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: overhead/wall reference-point marking from the model. It substitutes for the helper who holds targets or rods so overhead reference points can be located, in the same interior jobsite environment and at installation tolerances.

sources.title: Robotic Concrete Marking Case Study | REA JET
sources.claim: Rugged Robotics fields a small autonomous ground vehicle that marks fully coordinated architectural/engineering layout directly onto unfinished concrete floors and is scaling commercially with large contractors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: field layout on jobsite decks, the same output the helper's chalk-line/tape holding serves; corroborates that multiple vendors do this autonomously on ordinary construction floors.

tasks.label: Cut or weld metal.
Drill holes in timbers or lumber.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Light-frame residential jobsite: boring holes through studs, top/bottom plates and floor joists for electrical/plumbing runs and for bolts or hold-downs, using a right-angle drill with auger or self-feed bits. Members are already nailed in place; the helper works in stud bays, overhead and in awkward postures, following the carpenter's or trade's marks.

Jobsite bench work: drilling pilot and clearance holes in dimensional lumber laid on sawhorses or a plank table (deck ledgers, stair stringers, posts, rails, bolted splices). Layout is marked by hand, the piece is held by hand/knee or a clamp, and work is outdoors in variable weather and footing.

Commercial/industrial site formwork and temporary structures: drilling holes in lumber and plywood forms, walers, bracing, blocking and shoring for form ties, anchors and lifting hardware; congested, dusty conditions with other trades working around the helper.

Heavy-timber frame shop or fabrication yard: boring large-diameter through-bolt, lag and peg holes in beams, posts and glulam members laid on racks or sawhorses, to marks or templates supplied by the timber framer, inside a company-controlled shop.

Component plant (roof-truss, wall-panel or millwork facility): drilling holes in lumber members at a station on the plant floor — pilot holes in chords and studs, holes for hardware, service penetrations — on standard equipment with a fixed layout and supervised workflow.

sources.system: Hundegger K2-Industry CNC joinery machine (drilling/slotting units)
sources.title: Options | Hundegger K2-Industry
sources.claim: Hundegger CNC joinery machines used in timber-construction factories carry configurable drilling units that bore blind holes, countersinks and dowel holes in solid timber automatically from the digital model.

sources.title: Joinery machines | Hundegger
sources.claim: Hundegger joinery machines are fully automatic machines installed in timber construction factories, with timber fed and clamped by the machine line rather than hand-held.

sources.system: Hundegger K2i CNC joinery machine (in-shop deployment)
sources.title: High-Tech Timber-Frame Joinery Machine - Fine Homebuilding
sources.claim: A US timber-frame shop produces frame members on a Hundegger K2i CNC machine that cuts the joinery including the peg holes in mortises; framers only match-drill the tenons at dry-fit.

sources.system: Spatial Timber Assemblies (two-robot timber fabrication cell)
sources.developer: ETH Zurich / NCCR Digital Fabrication with Erne AG Holzbau
sources.title: spatial timber assemblies, a digital timber construction method developed by ETH zurich
sources.claim: In ETH Zurich's Spatial Timber Assemblies process, industrial robots in the Robotic Fabrication Laboratory saw timber beams to size and a second robot drills the holes needed to bolt the beams together, working from the computer layout; the modules were built into the real DFAB House.

sources.developer: HOMAG / WEINMANN (distributed in US by Stiles Machinery)
sources.title: WEINMANN multifunction bridges | HOMAG
sources.claim: WEINMANN multifunction bridges on timber-frame element lines process wall, roof and floor elements fully automatically, including routing and drilling of openings and penetrations in the fixtured element.

sources.title: Hilti Unveils New Drilling Capabilities to BIM-Enabled Construction Jobsite Robot
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a mobile drilling robot deployed on construction sites worldwide, but it drills anchor holes in concrete ceilings, corrugated metal deck and concrete walls from BIM data, and is positioned by a worker with a remote control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-site machine drilling of holes to a digital layout. Transfer to drilling timbers is limited — Jaibot hammer-drills small anchor holes in concrete/metal deck overhead, is driven into place by a worker, and does not bore wood members inside stud bays, so it cannot substantiate E3 for this task.

tasks.label: Glue and clamp edges or joints of assembled parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/light-commercial job site, finish carpentry: helper spreads wood glue on mitered casing returns, scarf joints in base/crown, built-up trim and jamb extensions on sawhorses or the floor, then holds/clamps (spring clamps, band clamps, tape, hand pressure) while the carpenter nails; varied profiles and species, dusty room, other trades around.

Cabinet/millwork shop bench work: helper injects or spreads glue in dowel holes, dados, biscuit slots and face-frame joints of cabinet and drawer boxes, assembles the box and clamps it square in bar clamps or a case clamp until cure; repeated similar parts, standard shop layout.

Shop edge and panel gluing: applying adhesive to panel edges, edge banding, laminate/countertop buildups and solid-wood panel glue-ups, then clamping in clamp racks, presses or under pressure rollers until set.

Prefab component plant (wall-panel, truss, stair, glulam/laminating shop): helper runs beads of construction adhesive/glue on framing members, lamellas or stair stringers and presses/clamps the assembly in a jig, press or clamp table before fastening.

Glue-up of joints on parts already installed or being installed in place: re-gluing a loose handrail/newel or balustrade joint, squeezing glue into a split installed trim miter or loose stair tread, clamping an out-of-line joint on installed casework in an occupied home or building.

sources.system: JR Automation / Stiles Machinery robotic face-frame assembly cell
sources.developer: JR Automation Technologies LLC with Stiles Machinery Inc.
sources.title: Automation Profiles: Cabinet Assembly Moves Into 21st Century | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Two-robot cell at a cabinetmaker glues and assembles wooden cabinet face frames of many sizes: a load robot presents each board to a glue dispenser, an assembly robot places and holds the part while pilot drilling and screwing the joint.
sources.transferJustification: Same operation on comparable objects: wood frame members (1.5-6 in wide, 4-20 pieces, various species) are glued at the joint and held under machine pressure while fastened - the helper's glue-and-clamp step for trim and face-frame subassemblies.

sources.title: Drill Glue and Dowel Machine - GANNOMAT Index
sources.claim: Commercial CNC machine performs automatic boring, glue injection into the joint holes and dowel driving for cabinet and furniture parts.

sources.system: Italpresse SP/1-A automatic through-feed case clamp
sources.title: New Italpresse Model SP/1-A Automatic Through Feed Case Clamp
sources.claim: Through-feed case clamp squares and clamps glued, dowelled cabinet cases with a fully automatic cycle including automatic loading and unloading, holding the box under pressure while the glue sets.

sources.system: HOMAG ABD 260 drilling and dowelling machine (ECF Ltd production cell)
sources.title: HOMAG production cell at ECF Ltd | HOMAG
sources.claim: Deployed HOMAG production cell at a cabinet manufacturer performs horizontal drilling, glue injection and dowel insertion on cabinet parts with a dedicated machine in the line.

sources.system: BIESSE VC 511 gluing unit on Akron edgebanders
sources.title: BIESSE VC 511 - Hoechsmann woodworking machinery lexicon
sources.claim: Edgebanding gluing unit automatically applies hot-melt adhesive to the panel edge and presses the edge material against the workpiece.
sources.transferJustification: This is the machine form of 'glue and clamp edges': adhesive is applied to the edge of an assembled panel and the edge member is held under roller pressure until the bond sets.

sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: Robotic gluing cell in offsite house-element factories applies glue beads to timber wall, floor and roof panel assemblies from CAD data, ahead of the robotic sheathing station that lays and fastens the sheets.

sources.system: Randek ZeroLabor robotic wall production line (KUKA robots) at Kodumaja
sources.title: Autowall, Robotic wall production line for production of exterior walls | KUKA Sweden
sources.claim: Randek ZeroLabor robotic wall-element lines are installed and producing wall panels at a prefabricated house manufacturer.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes real factory deployment of the ZeroLabor robotic panel line whose gluing station performs the glue-then-press step on timber assemblies.

sources.title: LHF press line for glulam production - Kallesoe Machinery
sources.claim: Glulam press line automatically applies glue to lamellas, lays them up and clamps them in a hydraulic radio-frequency press until cured, with glue application and pressing under central automatic control.
sources.transferJustification: Face-gluing and clamping laminated timber members is the same glue-and-clamp operation on wood assemblies, at equal or larger scale, held to a cured-bond quality standard.

tasks.label: Install handrails under the direction of a carpenter.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interior stair handrail in a single-family house under construction or being remodeled: helper locates studs/blocking, marks code height along the stair rake, cuts the wood rail to length with mitered returns, screws brackets to the wall, mounts and levels the rail, and fastens it so it passes an inspector's load check; dusty, cluttered, occupied or partly finished rooms.

Exterior deck, porch or ramp railing at a residence: helper sets or plumbs posts, fits top rail/graspable handrail and balusters between posts, drills and drives fasteners outdoors on uneven decking, in weather, with rails often scribed to fit non-square framing.

Commercial jobsite interior: long runs of wall-mounted handrail in stairwells and corridors of a building under construction — anchoring brackets to metal studs, blocking or concrete, splicing rail sections, adding ADA end extensions and returns, working from ladders amid other trades.

Temporary safety handrails/guardrails on the jobsite: 2x4 top rails, midrails and posts around floor openings, stair towers, ramps and scaffold landings, or system guardrail components, built to OSHA height and strength requirements on rough, changing site conditions.

Grab bars and short ADA handrails installed in occupied institutional buildings (senior living, hospital, school restrooms and corridors) during renovation or service work: existing tiled or drywall walls, blocking to be found, work sequenced around occupants and facility rules.

Shop or prefab-plant work: pre-assembling handrail sections and balustrades on a bench or panel line — cutting and joining rail lengths, attaching brackets, newels and balusters to components before shipment or on-site mounting.

sources.developer: AIST (National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology, Japan)
sources.title: Development of a humanoid robot prototype, HRP-5P, capable of heavy labor
sources.claim: AIST's HRP-5P humanoid autonomously picked up, carried and fastened a large gypsum board to a wall frame using a power screwdriver in a mock residential construction setup, showing autonomous positioning of a bulky building element against structure and screw-fastening it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior board installation. Transfer to handrail mounting is partial but direct in kind — a long, heavy wooden element is held against wall framing at a target position and fastened with a powered screwdriver, the core physical act of mounting a rail or bracket; the demo environment was a purpose-built mock-up, supporting only a machine-structured (E1) setting.

sources.title: LIGNA Product 2025: ZeroLabor Robotic System (Randek)
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor is a commercially sold, fully automatic fenced robot cell for timber house components that performs assembly, framing, sheathing, gluing and insulation of wall elements presented to it on a production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic framing/assembly of timber building elements in a fixtured factory cell. Transfer: the objects (dimensional lumber and boards), the fastening operations (positioning a member on a fixtured assembly and driving nails/screws to layout) and the tolerances are those of mounting rails, brackets and balusters when the work is brought to the machine.

sources.system: House of Design automated truss assembly system (ABB robots), e.g. at Louws Truss
sources.developer: House of Design Robotics with Alpine (ITW)
sources.title: Alpine & House of Design are Partnering to Bring the Latest in Automated Solutions to CMs
sources.claim: House of Design's ABB-robot truss lines, installed in US plants, autonomously pick, position and fasten dimensional lumber members into finished building components inside fenced robotic cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly of wood-member frames. Transfer: placing long wooden members at commanded positions on a fixtured jig and mechanically joining them is the same manipulation and precision class as fitting a rail between posts or onto brackets in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: WEINMANN WALLTEQ M-300 / M-380 multifunction bridge
sources.title: WEINMANN Multifunction Bridge WALLTEQ M-300
sources.claim: WEINMANN multifunction bridges used in timber-frame plants automatically saw, trim, drill, mark, nail and staple on panels held on a production table, i.e. CNC-controlled cutting-to-length and fastening of wood at commanded layout positions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cutting and fastening on fixtured wood assemblies. Transfer: the sub-operations a handrail install needs when the work is fixtured — mark layout, cut rail stock to length, drill pilot holes, drive fasteners — are exactly this machine's operations at higher precision than hand carpentry.

sources.title: Robots under Autonomous Control at Robot Lab | Shimizu Corporation
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Buddy uses sensors to locate ceiling grid framing and, with two 6-axis arms, lifts a board into position and screws it in place, as part of a construction-site robot system used on Japanese high-rise projects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous board installation on active building sites. It shows site-capable lift-and-screw robots exist, but the system is dedicated to repetitive ceiling/floor board grids and provides no evidence of one-off rail layout, cutting, splicing or finish-quality mounting, so it does not substantiate handrail installation at E2/E3.

sources.system: Schindler R.I.S.E (Robotic Installation System for Elevators)
sources.title: Robots rise at Schindler — The Construction Index
sources.claim: Schindler R.I.S.E works autonomously inside elevator shafts on high-rise construction sites, measuring positions, drilling and setting anchor bolts; the brackets and rails themselves are still fitted by human installers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous drilling and anchor setting on real construction sites. It covers only the hole-and-anchor step of rail mounting — published work on this class of system notes brackets are afterwards fixed by humans — so it cannot substantiate whole handrail installation in a built environment.

tasks.label: Construct forms and assist in raising them to the required elevation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/light-commercial foundation at a house lot: helper cuts plywood and dimension lumber and assembles footing and foundation-wall forms (or sets modular panel forms), then helps stand, align, stake and brace them to the grade/elevation marks on uneven, muddy ground in open weather.

Flatwork on a jobsite: helper builds and sets edge/screed forms, bulkheads, curb and stair forms for slabs-on-grade, sidewalks and steps - cutting boards to length, driving stakes, nailing, and setting the top of form to the required grade with string line or laser.

Commercial concrete structure: helper assembles prefabricated gang/panel wall and column forms (panels, walers, ties, strongbacks), rigs them to a crane, guides and holds them as they are raised, then helps plumb, align and brace them at the required elevation.

Elevated slab deck formwork: helper erects shoring frames/post shores and stringers, joists and plywood decking overhead inside a partially built structure, then adjusts screw jacks and re-shores to bring the deck to the required elevation.

Heavy civil / high-rise core: helper works on bridge pier, abutment or wall forms, falsework and jump/climbing forms - handing up material, bolting sections, rigging and tag-lining large forms as cranes or climbing hydraulics raise them to the next elevation, at height and in weather.

sources.system: Form Master shuttering / deshuttering / storage robot
sources.developer: Ebawe Anlagentechnik / Progress Maschinen & Automation (Progress Group)
sources.date: 2026-07 (product documentation; product line in service since ~2020)
sources.title: Shuttering & deshuttering robot - Ebawe - Progress Group
sources.claim: The Form Master gantry robot in precast carousel plants autonomously selects steel shuttering profiles from storage per CAD data, positions them precisely on the casting pallet to form the mould outline, and locks them with integral magnets; a deshuttering robot removes them afterwards.
sources.transferJustification: This is form construction itself - assembling the formwork perimeter to dimensioned drawings and fixing it in position - performed in a purpose-built plant on a horizontal casting bed rather than in situ.

sources.system: Form Master at Schwoerer Bausysteme GmbH
sources.title: Schwoerer Bausysteme relies on modernization in the precast plant - Concrete Plant Precast Technology (BFT International)
sources.claim: A Form Master shuttering/deshuttering/storage robot was installed and put into operation in a working precast plant (Schwoerer Bausysteme, Haigerloch-Stetten), performing fully automated positioning of shuttering magnets and mounting parts.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: the deployed machine builds the concrete form (shuttering) to drawing in a purpose-built plant; it substantiates real production use rather than a demonstration.

sources.title: Shuttering Robots for Precast Concrete Plants - Sommer Anlagentechnik
sources.claim: Multi-function shuttering robots sold for precast plants place shuttering profiles, align them and activate their magnets, and place additional magnets for insert parts and frames, working from element geometry.
sources.transferJustification: Independent commercial confirmation that automated form (shuttering) assembly and alignment is standard capability inside purpose-built precast plants.

sources.date: 2026-07 (product documentation; systems sold to panel factories)
sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor robotic framing and sheathing cells automatically cut and place studs and noggings, and sheet wall, floor and roof elements with OSB/plasterboard, including robotic sawing, gluing and routing of openings, in prefab factories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic framing and sheathing of timber wall panels. Job-built concrete forms use the same materials (dimension lumber studs/walers plus plywood or OSB sheets), cut and nailed to dimensioned layouts at comparable tolerances, so the fabrication capability carries over when the work is brought into a fixtured cell.

sources.system: Wall sheathing robot cell (Kawasaki BX250L with SCADAware software)
sources.title: Assembling Walls for Prefabricated Homes | Industrial Robots by Kawasaki
sources.claim: Four Kawasaki BX250L robots on rails in a fenced cell at prefab home builder Rehkemper handle full-size OSB sheets, place them on framed walls and nail them to the studs and beams from the electronic wall design, then cut openings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sheathing and nailing timber panels in a fixtured factory cell. Building plywood-faced concrete forms requires the same heavy-sheet handling, nailing into hidden framing members and CAD-driven accuracy, so the capability transfers to form-panel fabrication at E1.

sources.system: Robotic hot-blade / hot-wire formwork cutting (incl. containerised 'Factory on the Fly')
sources.title: Odico's Factory on the Fly is a pop-up robotic manufacturing unit for construction sites | Dezeen
sources.claim: Odico's industrial robot cells produce concrete formwork moulds by robotic hot-wire/abrasive wire cutting of EPS blocks, and those moulds were used for load-bearing concrete structures in a completed building (Fjordenhus).
sources.transferJustification: Directly form construction (fabricating concrete formwork) executed by robots, but inside an enclosed robot cell/container rather than in situ.

sources.title: Super Climber SCP - Doka
sources.claim: Self-climbing formwork systems raise entire core formwork and platforms to the next elevation hydraulically without a crane, but the lift is initiated and supervised by the site crew, and the forms themselves are assembled, tied, cleaned and stripped by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Covers only the 'raising to elevation' half of the task and is an operator-actuated hydraulic appliance rather than an autonomous robot, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Secure stakes to grids for constructions of footings, nail scabs to footing forms, and vibrate and float concrete.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/light-commercial footing layout: helper drives and secures wood grade stakes along string/grid lines in and beside a shallow excavated footing trench or building pad, sets them to line and grade off the carpenter's marks, and holds/attaches form boards to them. Muddy, uneven, sloped ground; rebar, spoil piles and equipment in the way.

Nailing scabs, cleats and kickers to footing and low wall forms: short boards nailed across form-board joints and to stakes to keep forms straight and prevent blowouts, using a hammer or nail gun while kneeling in or over the trench; done just before and during the pour.

Consolidating fresh concrete during a footing, grade-beam, pier or short wall pour: helper works an immersion (stinger) vibrator into the form ahead of the chute/pump hose, spacing insertions, watching for honeycombing and form pressure, moving continuously with the pour crew.

Hand screeding and floating narrow or small work: striking off and bull-floating/darbying footing tops, pier caps, curbs, sidewalks, stoops and small slabs; edging and working around anchor bolts, dowels and form edges on grade.

Large commercial slab-on-grade or structural deck pour inside a building shell or on an open pad: helper assists with screeding, bull floating and running/ tending walk-behind or ride-on power trowels over a large open flat area on a tight finishing window.

sources.title: Plotter/shuttering robot | Vollert Anlagenbau GmbH
sources.claim: Vollert's plotter/shuttering robots in precast pallet-circulation plants place formwork profiles onto the casting pallet fully automatically at CAD-defined positions, i.e. they set and magnetically secure the elements that fix the form line to a layout grid.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: setting and securing the elements that hold a concrete form on the design layout. Footing grade stakes exist to fix form-board line and grade; the shuttering robot performs the equivalent function (position + magnetically lock edge profiles to the plotted grid) at millimetre precision on a fixtured pallet, which is how the work is presented at E1.

sources.title: Shuttering Robots for Precast Concrete Plants
sources.claim: Sommer's multi-function shuttering robot automatically plots the layout, places and aligns shuttering profiles and activates their magnets on the casting pallet.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the Vollert item: plotting the grid and securing the form-locating hardware to it is the E1 analogue of staking a footing form line.

sources.title: Robotic solar pile driver three times faster than humans – pv magazine USA

sources.title: This Plant Runs Itself - Offsite Builder Magazine

tasks.label: Perform tie spacing layout and measure, mark, drill or cut.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wood-framing jobsite (house/light commercial): helper reads the plan, lays out stud/joist/rafter and tie (blocking, strap/collar tie) spacing on plates and rims with tape and square, pencils the marks, then measures, marks and cuts members to length at an on-site saw station. Uneven decks, weather, scattered material stacks, other trades moving through.

Concrete formwork on a commercial jobsite: helper lays out snap-tie/she-bolt spacing on plyform wall panels and walers per the form drawing, marks hole centers, drills the tie holes with a hand drill, and cuts panels/walers/fillers to fit. Work done on horses in a staging area or on standing forms, outdoors, dirty and dusty.

Contractor's shop or panel/prefab shop cut station: helper works from a cut list or shop drawing, measures and marks lumber and plywood on benches, drills bolt/tie holes, and cuts pieces on a shop chop saw or table saw. Fixed layout, standard equipment, company controls who is on the floor.

Commercial interior fit-out: helper lays out partition track, backing and anchor/tie spacing per plan, marks hole positions on the concrete deck, slab or wall, and drills the anchor/tie holes with a rotary hammer at the marked spacing. Building shell under construction, lighting and access variable.

Outdoor heavy/civil timber work (bridge or trestle decking, dock, boardwalk): helper lays out tie spacing on stringers or caps, measures and marks each tie position, bores bolt/drift-pin holes with an auger or heavy drill, and cuts timbers to length. Exposed site, heavy timbers, no fixed workstation.

Residential remodel/deck work at an occupied home: helper lays out joist and ledger tie spacing, marks hole and cut locations, drills ledger/rim bolt holes, and cuts deck framing and boards to length. Cramped, cluttered site with existing construction and homeowner property present.

sources.system: Hundegger ROBOT-Drive / ROBOT-Compact CNC joinery machine

sources.transferJustification: Same operations as the task (measure, mark, drill, cut) on the same material (structural lumber and heavy timber), executed automatically from the digital plan inside a fenced machine cell rather than by hand on site.

sources.transferJustification: Covers the marking, drilling and cutting portion of the task on plywood/OSB sheathing and framing lumber — the same materials a helper marks and drills for form ties or framing — but with the panel fixtured on a machine table.

sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor robotic system is a ... cell for panelised timber production that cuts, frames, sheathes and glues wall, floor and roof elements with minimal human input; the subassembly version was launched at LIGNA 2025.

sources.title: Skanska Case Study | Dusty Robotics

sources.transferJustification: Related task: building layout marking on jobsite decks. It substantiates only the layout/marking element on floors from the digital plan; it does not mark lumber, drill, or cut, so it cannot by itself complete instances that end in a drilled or cut piece.

sources.date: 2020-10 (launch); new concrete-wall and metal-deck drilling features 2022-06

sources.transferJustification: Related task: anchor-hole layout and drilling from a digital plan on an active jobsite. It transfers to the helper's anchor/tie-hole work because the deliverable is the same — holes at the planned spacing, marked and drilled to position tolerance in the structure as found.

tasks.label: Smooth or sand surfaces to remove ridges, tool marks, glue, or caulking.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential remodel in an occupied home: helper hand- and orbital-sands installed interior trim, door casing, baseboard and stair parts after the carpenter sets them — knocking down filler over nail holes, glue squeeze-out at miters, and excess caulk — working around furniture, finished floors and dust containment before paint.

New single-family/townhome construction at the finish stage: sanding installed jambs, casing, crown, closet shelving, handrails and stair treads in place, smoothing filler and glue at joints and tool/planer marks, on a cluttered site with other trades, ladders and temporary power.

Cabinet/millwork shop or a dedicated shop bench: sanding loose cabinet doors, drawer fronts, face frames, panels, tabletops and trim stock on benches or a downdraft table, removing mill marks, ridges and glue squeeze-out before finishing or installation.

Commercial or institutional interior build-out: sanding installed casework, wood doors, handrails, window stools and plywood/laminate edges in place, plus smoothing filler and caulk at reveals, often from ladders or lifts while the GC controls access to an active jobsite.

Exterior/rough work: sanding deck boards, railings, fascia and exterior trim before paint or stain, easing splintered edges on framing lumber and plywood, and knocking down burrs and form marks, outdoors in variable weather.

Interior finish support on a commercial project: sanding joint compound and skim coat over large wall and ceiling areas (around installed carpentry, patches and framing penetrations) to a Level 4/5 smoothness before paint.

tasks.label: Cover surfaces with laminated plastic covering material.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In a millwork/cabinet or countertop fabrication shop, the helper covers a flat particleboard/MDF panel or countertop blank with HPL sheet: cleans the substrate, spreads contact cement or PVA on substrate and laminate, lays the oversize sheet, rolls/presses it, then flush-trims the overhang with a router and files the edges. Portable workpiece, fixed shop layout, standard equipment.

In the shop, the helper applies laminate edging/edge banding strips to the edges of panels, cabinet parts and countertop build-downs: glue on the strip, press it to the edge, trim the overhang flush, scrape and buff the joint. High-volume, repetitive, portable parts.

At a residential or light-commercial jobsite, the helper builds and laminates a top on sawhorses or a bench in the garage/staging area: cuts the substrate blank to the measured size, applies contact cement, positions and rolls the laminate, self-edges it, trims flush and eases edges, then it is carried in and set. Portable workpiece, but dusty, variable jobsite conditions.

On a commercial construction site, the helper laminates surfaces already fixed in the building: wall panels and wainscot, column wraps, window sills, the face of an installed reception desk or built-in casework. Sheets must be scribed and cut around outlets, corners and returns, glued and rolled in place, and trimmed in situ overhead or at floor level, working around other trades.

In an occupied facility (school, office, hospital, restaurant), the helper re-covers or patches worn installed laminate surfaces: strips or scuffs the old laminate on fixed counters, casework ends and desktops, cuts new pieces to fit around existing sinks, backsplashes and fillers, bonds and trims them in place with minimal disruption during off-hours.
