tasks.label: Cut and install insulating or sound-absorbing material.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New residential construction site: helper cuts fiberglass or mineral-wool batts with a utility knife and friction-fits/staples them into wood stud bays, floor joists and ceiling cavities of a house under framing, working off ladders, around wiring, plumbing and blocking, trimming batts around outlets and irregular bays.

Commercial/institutional interior fit-out on an active job site: helper cuts and stuffs sound-attenuation batts into metal-stud partitions and above ceilings, and cuts/drops sound-absorbing acoustic ceiling panels and wall panels into grid or onto furring, trimming perimeter pieces to fit.

Rigid insulation board work: helper cuts rigid foam, mineral-wool or wood-fibre board to size and fastens it to exterior sheathing, roof decks, foundation/basement walls or as continuous insulation, cutting around penetrations and taping seams.

Retrofit in an existing or occupied house: helper cuts and installs batts or board insulation in an attic, crawl space, basement rim joists, or around new windows/doors during a remodel; cramped, cluttered, variable access.
Prefabrication/modular panel shop: helper cuts and installs insulation into wall, floor or roof panels laid flat on assembly tables before sheathing, following a cut list for repeated panel types.
Small finish/acoustic jobs: cutting and mounting sound-absorbing panels in a home theater, studio or conference room, cutting sound board, or wrapping duct and pipe insulation in a finished space.

tasks.label: Cut tile or linoleum to fit and spread adhesives on flooring for installation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential remodel (occupied home): helper measures, marks and cuts ceramic/porcelain tiles on a wet saw or snap cutter to fit around a toilet flange, vanity, out-of-square walls and door casings in a small bathroom or kitchen, mixes thinset and spreads it with a notched trowel in confined areas amid furniture, dust control and homeowner traffic.

New residential construction: helper spreads thinset over entry, mudroom, laundry or bath floors on a partially finished slab/subfloor, sets and beats in full field tiles, and cuts perimeter and border pieces at a wet saw; site has debris, other trades working nearby, temporary lighting.

Large commercial interior (lobby, corridor, school, retail box) under construction: helper spreads mortar/adhesive with a notched trowel or applicator over large open prepared field areas ahead of the setters, using full-size tiles on a laid-out grid; perimeter and cut pieces handled separately by others.

Resilient flooring (sheet vinyl, linoleum, LVT or VCT) in homes, offices, clinics or schools: helper scribes and knife-cuts sheet goods or tiles to fit walls, columns, cabinet toe-kicks and door casings, then spreads pressure-sensitive or wet-set adhesive with a notched trowel or roller over the area before the sheet is rolled out and rolled in.

Small repair, patch and odd-shape work: replacing cracked tiles in an existing floor, cutting pieces around pipes, floor drains, thresholds and stair nosings, and buttering/spreading adhesive in small confined spots in occupied homes or working offices.

tasks.label: Strip insulation from wire ends, using wire stripping pliers, and attach wires to terminals for subsequent soldering.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential rough-in/trim on an active jobsite: helper strips 14/12 AWG NM-B or THHN conductor ends with strippers and lands them on screw or push-in terminals of receptacles, switches and fixture leads in device boxes; boxes are at varied heights, dust/debris present, other trades working nearby.

Commercial/institutional construction site: stripping THHN branch-circuit conductors and landing them on terminal screws/lugs inside panelboards, disconnects, junction boxes and light fixtures, often overhead from a ladder or lift, in a partially built space with changing layout.

Contractor prefab shop or panel shop bench work: cut, strip, ferrule/tin and land control and power conductors on DIN-rail terminal blocks, relays and contactors in control panels or prefabricated assemblies; fixed benches, standard components, drawings supplied.

Maintenance/retrofit inside an operating facility (plant, hospital, school): re-terminating small-gauge control and instrumentation wires at terminal strips in existing MCCs, control cabinets and junction boxes; cramped existing enclosures, congested legacy wiring, work permits and lockout.

Small-gauge / low-voltage lead work: stripping and tinning fine stranded conductors and attaching them to terminal tabs, pins or lugs for subsequent soldering (fixture leads, control devices, sensor pigtails), usually at a bench or tailgate with a helping hand and iron.

Heavy feeder terminations on site: stripping insulation from large conductors (2/0 to 250 kcmil) and landing them on mechanical lugs/compression lugs in switchgear, transformers or service equipment, using large strippers and hydraulic crimpers in an electrical room.

sources.system: Rittal Wire Terminal WT C5 / WT C10
sources.title: 4051210 Fully automated wire cabling machine Wire Terminal WT C10
sources.claim: Rittal's Wire Terminal WT C5/C10 are commercially sold, fully automated wire-processing machines that cut, strip, print and crimp ferrules onto wires (0.5–6 mm², i.e. AWG 20–10) with no manual intervention inside a purpose-built machine enclosure.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical operation as the task's first half plus terminal attachment: insulation stripping of building/control-gauge conductors and attachment of a ferrule/terminal to the stripped end, at the same wire gauges a helper handles.

sources.title: Rittal: 10x faster wire processing with Rittal machine | Control Global
sources.claim: Trade press confirms the Rittal WT C machine performs programmable insulation stripping (partial or full, up to 20 mm) and servo-driven crimping of wire-end ferrules, i.e. the strip-and-terminate sequence, automatically.

sources.title: Cable stripping and crimping machine - Alpha 560 - Komax AG - fully-automatic
sources.claim: Komax's Alpha-series machines are fully automatic wire-processing machines that strip and attach terminals to conductors up to 16 mm² (AWG ...), with integrated quality monitoring from stripping through the finished crimp.
sources.transferJustification: Attaching a crimp terminal to a stripped conductor end is the mechanical equivalent of the task's 'attach wires to terminals', on the same conductor sizes (AWG 14–6) that electrician helpers strip.

sources.title: Automatic Crimping | Komax
sources.claim: Komax automatic crimping machines integrate cutting, stripping, crimping, seal insertion, ... in one machine — including the tinning/solder-preparation step implied by 'for subsequent soldering'.

sources.system: Weidmüller SNAP IN robotic wiring cell
sources.title: How Weidmüller SNAP IN Enables Faster, Automated Cabinet Wiring | Machine Design
sources.claim: At Automate 2026 Weidmüller demonstrated a robotic wiring cell that cut, stripped and measured wire and then routed and terminated it into a power supply and SNAP IN terminal blocks inside a control panel — automating the strip-and-land-on-terminal sequence in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Fully automatic crimping machines - Schleuniger
sources.claim: Schleuniger sells fully automatic CrimpCenter machines that cut, strip, crimp, seal, twist and tin wires, and MegaStrip automatic cut-and-strip machines that process cables up to 35 mm outer diameter (heavy feeder-size conductors).

sources.system: Kingsing automatic wire stripping, twisting and tin-soldering machines
sources.title: Automatic Wire Stripping and Tin Soldering Machine
sources.claim: Commercial fully automatic machines strip fine-stranded wire ends and tin/solder them (flux and solder bath) in one servo-controlled sequence, covering the strip-and-prepare-for-soldering variant of the task.

sources.system: Kingsing heavy-duty servo lug crimping machine
sources.title: Heavy Duty Cable Lug Crimping Machines
sources.claim: Heavy-gauge terminals: large-tonnage servo lug-crimping machines terminate conductors up to 120 mm² (about 4/0 AWG) onto cable lugs on a bench/machine station.
sources.transferJustification: Landing a large conductor on a compression lug is the heavy-gauge form of 'attach wires to terminals'; the machine performs the same termination on the same conductor sizes used for feeders.

tasks.label: Trace out short circuits in wiring, using test meter.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service call in an occupied home or apartment: breaker trips repeatedly; helper works with the electrician using a multimeter/continuity tester at the load center, pulling receptacles, switches and fixtures, disconnecting devices and splitting the circuit at junction boxes to isolate a hot-to-ground or hot-to-neutral short in cable buried in finished walls, attics or crawlspaces.

New construction / rough-in jobsite (house or building under construction): after wire pull, homeruns and branch runs are tested at the temporary panel for shorts caused by staples, drywall screws or damaged insulation; work occurs amid other trades, debris, partial lighting, unfinished framing.

Occupied commercial building (office, retail, school) under facility management: tracing a short on a lighting or receptacle branch circuit at panelboards, conduit runs, junction boxes above ceiling tile; helper holds/uses the meter, records readings, and helps isolate the faulted segment while the building stays in use.

Industrial plant maintenance: tracing shorts in machine control wiring, MCC buckets, motor leads and terminal strips inside control cabinets, with the equipment locked out; helper uses meter for continuity/insulation readings on numbered conductors against a wiring diagram.

Shop or bench work: a removed fixture, motor, extension cord, portable tool or prefabricated panel/harness assembly is tested at the shop bench with a meter to find a short before repair or installation.

sources.developer: Multiple (Takaya, Seica, Acculogic); described by JLCPCB
sources.title: Flying Probe Testing: Modern PCB Quality Assurance
sources.claim: Flying probe testers are commercial automated machines whose motor-driven probes move across a fixtured circuit assembly, contact test points, and measure resistance/continuity to detect short circuits, without custom fixtures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated electrical test of a fixtured circuit assembly. The act is the same as the helper's — place test probes on conductors, measure resistance/continuity, and identify which conductors are shorted — at finer precision than building-wiring terminals, in a purpose-built machine (E1).

sources.system: Seica Pilot V8 flying probe tester in production at Sierra Circuits
sources.title: Flying Probe Testing for PCB Assembly | Sierra Circuits
sources.claim: A US contract manufacturer runs Seica Pilot V8 flying probe machines in production, testing assemblies for shorts, opens and component ..., i.e. deployed robotic probing that locates short circuits.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fixtureless in-circuit electrical test. Same diagnostic output as the task — identifying the shorted conductors/nets by probing them with a meter-equivalent instrument — performed autonomously inside a purpose-built test machine.

sources.system: Robotic Arm-Assisted PCB Diagnostic and Measurement System
sources.developer: Universiti Malaysia Perlis (H. F. Hawari et al.)
sources.title: Implementation of a Robotic Arm-Assisted PCB Diagnostic and Measurement System (IJARIS)
sources.claim: A robotic arm carrying test probes autonomously took voltage and resistance measurements at circuit test points and identified faults including short circuits, validated against a calibrated digital multimeter.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic meter probing of a fixtured circuit. It is the task's core act — positioning probes on conductors and reading a meter to find a short — done by a programmed (not teleoperated) manipulator on a bench fixture.

sources.title: ANYmal - Autonomous Robotic Inspection Solution
sources.claim: Autonomous legged inspection robots deployed in industrial plants carry only non-contact sensors (visual/thermal cameras, ultrasonic microphone, lidar); they perform inspection rounds but do not attach test leads to conductors or trace shorts.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to characterize the state of autonomous robots inside structured human facilities (plants, substations): sensing is non-contact, so this does not substantiate meter probing or short-tracing at E2; it supports the negative E2 judgments only.

tasks.label: Measure, cut, and bend wire and conduit, using measuring instruments and hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/institutional new-construction rough-in: helper measures a run in place (point-to-point, around beams and ductwork), cuts 1/2"–1" EMT with hacksaw or portable band saw, reams, and bends 90s, offsets and saddles with a hand bender to fit; active jobsite with debris, ladders, other trades, changing layout.

Residential rough-in and service work: measuring and cutting NM cable/THHN off spools to length for runs, cutting short pieces of EMT/flex/greenfield, bending small offsets and ground pigtails, inside a partially framed or occupied house with tight, varied spaces.

Industrial plant or retrofit work: measuring, cutting (band saw), and bending 1"–4" rigid/IMC conduit with mechanical or hydraulic bender for racks and equipment feeds, in mechanical rooms and around existing pipe racks and live equipment.

Batch fabrication in the contractor's prefab shop or on-site prefab trailer: helper works from a cut list/BIM spool sheet at a bench, measures and marks conduit stock, cuts on chop saw/band saw, bends stubs and offsets on a programmable or hydraulic bender, and cuts/coils/labels wire lengths for kits.

Cutting conductors to length for pulls: measuring feeder/branch conductors off reels on a reel rack or gang box using a measuring wheel or tape, cutting to length with cable cutters, and coiling/tagging them for the pull.

sources.title: New Fully Automated Production Cell with eMOB 150
sources.claim: AMOB's fully automated tube-bending production cell built around the all-electric eMOB 150 bender loads tube bundles automatically, orients each tube with a vision system, bends it, and robot-unloads and palletizes the finished parts in a fabrication shop.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: CNC bending of steel tube in a fabrication cell. EMT/IMC/rigid conduit is thin- and heavy-wall steel tube in the same diameter range (the cell handles round tube to 50 mm; the eMOB series to 225 mm OD), and the required bend geometry (90s, offsets, saddles) and ±degree precision are the same class of work as conduit bending.

sources.system: Unison Breeze automated tube bending and punching cell (Olicana Products)
sources.title: Unison builds automated tube bending cell for UK metalworking contractor
sources.claim: A Unison Breeze all-electric CNC tube bender integrated with automatic hopper feeding and robot unloading fabricates multi-bend tubular frames unattended overnight from a loaded program, with completely automatic batch set-up.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: programmed multi-bend fabrication of steel tube from raw stock. The helper's conduit bends (multiple bends per stick to specified dimensions) are the same operation; the cell measures feed length by servo and performs up to six bends per part without an operator.

sources.system: BLM GROUP E-TURN all-electric tube bender
sources.title: E-TURN All-Electric Tube Bender - SME.org
sources.claim: BLM Group's E-TURN all-electric CNC tube bender automatically loads, bends and unloads tube in one machine, and BLM benders are designed to be integrated ... cells with saw-cutting and laser tube-cutting machines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic loading and CNC bending of round steel tube, the same stock geometry as EMT/rigid conduit; the machine's own feed axis sets bend-to-bend distances, which is the measuring step of the helper's task performed by the machine.

sources.system: Komax Kappa 322 / Kappa 340 automatic cut-and-strip machines
sources.title: Automatic Cutting and Stripping Machines | Assembly Magazine
sources.claim: Komax Kappa automatic cutting-and-stripping machines measure and cut insulated conductors to programmed length from reels and strip them, running in production at high rates; the Kappa 340 cuts to length conductors from 0.22–70 mm² (AWG 24–2).
sources.transferJustification: Same act as the helper's wire work: measuring building wire/cable to a specified length and cutting it. Conductor sizes overlap the branch-circuit wire helpers cut (Kappa 340 covers up to AWG 2), and machine length accuracy exceeds tape-measure practice.

sources.title: Industrial Automatic Bandsaw Machines - Auto Feed Saws | Sawcraft UK
sources.claim: Industrial automatic band saws are fully programmable, feed and clamp stock themselves, and cut batches to programmed length unattended overnight in fabrication shops.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting metal tube/bar to measured length. Cutting EMT, IMC and rigid conduit to length is the identical operation on the same stock; the saw's programmable feed performs the measuring.

sources.system: Greenlee AutoBend 3D / programmable electric benders in distributor prefab shops
sources.developer: Greenlee (Emerson) / Walters Wholesale, Electrical Wholesalers Inc.
sources.title: Pipe Bending | Electrical Wholesalers Inc. — Prefabrication Solutions
sources.claim: Electrical prefabrication shops run Greenlee AutoBend, a digitally driven conduit bender that positions conduit with an embedded laser sensor from BIM-derived bend data and bends 1/2" to 4" EMT, IMC, rigid and stainless conduit; the conduit is still loaded and handled by a shop worker.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task (conduit measuring and bending) on conduit-specific equipment, but the machine is operator-fed and operator-tended, so it is treated as non-autonomous and used only as context that conduit bending is executed from digital dimensions in shops.

sources.title: Hilti Unveils BIM-Enabled Construction Jobsite Robot
sources.claim: The most capable electrical/MEP jobsite robot deployed on construction sites, Hilti's Jaibot, is driven between positions by an operator with a ... and only drills BIM-located holes automatically; no cited jobsite robot measures, cuts or bends conduit in the field.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic MEP work on an active construction site. It shows the ceiling of jobsite (E3) electrical-helper automation today — remote-driven positioning and a single drilling operation — and no capability to measure, cut or bend conduit in the field.

tasks.label: Examine electrical units for loose connections and broken insulation and tighten connections, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New residential construction trim-out and pre-energization: helper works through newly installed receptacles, switches, fixture whips and the new panelboard, checking that terminal screws, breaker lugs and neutral/ground bar screws are tight and that no conductor insulation was nicked during pulling; screwdrivers/torque screwdriver on standard modern devices in an unfinished house.

New commercial/industrial installation on an active jobsite: helper checks and tightens terminations in new panelboards, disconnects, junction boxes, motor connection boxes and control cabinets to labeled torque specs before energizing; standard specified components, but work is on ladders/lifts in a partially built, cluttered structure.

Contractor prefab shop / panel shop bench work: helper inspects and torques terminations on control panels, gear assemblies and prefabricated racks built in-house, working at a bench with the assembly laid flat and documentation at hand.

Occupied commercial/institutional building (school, office, hospital) service and maintenance: helper opens as-found aged panelboards, disconnects, lighting circuits and receptacles in electrical rooms and above ceilings, looks for discolored/loose lugs, brittle or chafed insulation, and re-tightens; equipment vintage, brand and layout vary building to building.

Industrial plant preventive maintenance under lockout/tagout: helper assists with annual checks of motor control centers, control cabinets, terminal strips and disconnects — following thermography findings, inspecting for heat damage and broken insulation, and re-torquing lugs and terminal screws on installed, as-found equipment.

Residential/light-commercial service and repair call on an existing property: helper examines an old panel, junction boxes and devices while troubleshooting (loose neutrals, backstabbed receptacles, cloth- or rubber-insulated conductors, wire nuts), often in attics, crawlspaces or cramped closets, tightening what is found loose.

sources.title: Robotic wiring centre will save up to 15 hours per panel - Drives&Controls
sources.claim: Kiesling's Averex robotic wiring centre (Rittal/Friedhelm Loh group) wires control and switchgear panel mounting plates inside the machine, attaching conductors to terminal blocks, contactors and motor ... with torque-controlled screwing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic panel wiring. Same objects (terminal blocks, contactors, breakers, insulated conductors), same tool action (driving terminal screws to controlled torque) and same acceptance criterion (a connection tight to spec) as 'tighten connections, using hand tools'.

sources.title: Robotic wiring centre will save up to 15 hours per panel - Drives&Controls
sources.claim: The Averex machine first checks the fixtured mounting plate against digital component and position data using lasers, then wires and screws the components automatically and autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine inspection of an assembled mounting plate. It substantiates the 'examine' half of the task — machine verification of an electrical assembly against spec before terminations are made and torqued — in the same fixtured panel-building setting, and establishes autonomy.

sources.date: 2024 (shown at Hannover Messe 2024); product page current 2026
sources.title: More Efficient Control Cabinet Wiring | WAGO
sources.claim: WAGO's Cabinet Wiring Robot wires control cabinets and verifies every connection it makes: screw connections get a pull-out test, spring connections are force-torque monitored, and a camera/laser system compares the actual assembly to the digital order data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated control-cabinet wiring with in-process connection verification. Testing that every screw connection holds and that the assembly matches spec is functionally the helper's examine-and-tighten step on the same class of electrical units.

sources.system: ASG AX-10 robotic assembly cell with X-PAQ screwdriving system
sources.developer: ASG, a Division of Jergens Inc.
sources.title: Robotic Cell Automates Screwdriving Process | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Commercially available robotic screwdriving cells (ASG/Jergens AX-10) fixture the workpiece and drive fasteners under closed-loop torque and angle control with traceability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic screwdriving in a fixtured cell. Tightening a terminal screw to a specified torque is the identical physical action and acceptance criterion; the cell supplies the fixtures and part presentation assumed by the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: Averex portal robot (control cabinet wiring automation)
sources.title: Automated Control Cabinet Wiring Solution for Scalable Renewable Energy Systems | SpringerLink
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed review of control-cabinet manufacturing confirms fully automated portal-robot wiring (Averex) covering wire cutting, crimping, connecting and routing inside cabinets is fielded practice.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cabinet wiring; cited to date the capability to 2025 and confirm it is a fielded industrial solution rather than a one-off demonstration.

sources.system: DEEP Robotics X30 / Jueying quadruped substation inspection robot
sources.title: DEEP Robotics' Robot Dogs Successfully Deployed for Substation Inspection Scenarios
sources.claim: Deployed field robots in electrical facilities are inspection-only: DEEP Robotics quadrupeds autonomously patrol substations with visual and thermal sensors, but carry no manipulator and do not open equipment or tighten terminations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inspection of electrical equipment inside a facility. Cited to show the ceiling of field capability — patrol and imaging only, no hand-tool manipulation — which is why in-facility (E2) and as-found (E3) completion of this task is unsubstantiated.

tasks.label: Maintain tools, vehicles, and equipment and keep parts and supplies in order.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-shift tool round-up and clean-down at an active job site (commercial build-out, residential rewire, occupied building): gather hand and cordless tools scattered across the area, coil 50-100 ft extension cords and leftover wire, separate reusable material from scrap, stow everything in the gang box or van.

Keeping the service van/truck in order: replenishing bins of wire nuts, connectors, straps, breakers and fittings from stock, loading conduit, spools, benders and ladders, re-sorting shelving after a job, done in the yard and curbside between calls.

Shop stockroom/warehouse work: receiving supply-house deliveries, putting stock away in labeled bins and racks, pulling and staging material for the next day's jobs, counting inventory and flagging reorders.

Tool and equipment maintenance at the shop bench: wiping down and cleaning tools, charging and rotating battery packs, changing bits/blades, lubricating benders, threaders and hydraulic knock-out sets, inspecting cords and GFCIs, tagging out damaged tools, servicing generators and compressors.
Keeping the service vehicle clean and fueled: running the van through a wash, fueling or charging it at the end of the week.
Vehicle condition checks and servicing logistics: checking oil, coolant and washer fluid, tire pressure and tread, lights, noting defects and getting the van to scheduled service.

sources.title: Amazon unveils the next generation of fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously picks and places individual items spanning over 200 million distinct products in fenced robotic cells inside fulfillment centers, sorting and consolidating stock into containers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse item putaway/sortation. Transfer to 'keep parts and supplies in order': the objects (small hardware, packaged fittings, boxed goods) and required precision are comparable to sorting electrical parts into labeled bins when items are presented to the machine.

sources.system: ZOLLER roboSet 2 / cora automated tool room
sources.title: Automated Tool Handling 24/7 | ZOLLER
sources.claim: ZOLLER's roboSet/cora tool-room automation autonomously picks, assembles, clamps, cleans, labels, measures and stores cutting tools in an enclosed automated tool room, running unattended around the clock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-shop tool room upkeep. Transfer: same work content as this task's tool maintenance - cleaning, inspecting, labeling and storing tools in known locations - performed on tools presented in pallets/fixtures, i.e. the E1 form of the instance.

sources.system: ABICOR BINZEL TCS Compact torch cleaning station (also Lincoln Electric Power REAM)
sources.title: TCS Compact Nozzle Cleaning Station | ABICOR BINZEL
sources.claim: Automatic torch cleaning/maintenance stations service a robot's welding torch inside a fenced weld cell - reaming spatter from the nozzle, cutting wire and spraying anti-spatter - as an unattended, machine-controlled maintenance cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated maintenance of a working tool (clearing debris, replacing/servicing consumables) in a purpose-built station; comparable to the cleaning and consumable-changing portion of tool upkeep when the tool is brought to the machine.

sources.title: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid hits 100,000-tote milestone in commercial warehouse use
sources.claim: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid autonomously moves totes in live commercial logistics facilities, passing 100,000 totes at GXO's Georgia site and deployed with Schaeffler and Toyota.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: material movement in a structured facility. Shows tote-level transport in an E2 warehouse but not putaway of heterogeneous stock onto human shelving, so it bounds rather than establishes E2 capability for this task.

sources.title: Figure AI's Robots Work 17-Hour Shift, Sort 22,000 Packages
sources.claim: Figure's Helix-powered humanoids ran an autonomous multi-hour package-sorting shift at a logistics customer, handling tens of thousands of varied parcels from a fixed workstation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: parcel sortation at a fixed station. Transfer: shows sustained autonomous handling of varied packaged items where the flow is engineered to the machine, matching the E1 form of stocking/kitting parts.

sources.title: AutoStore Named to TIME's Best Inventions 2025
sources.claim: AutoStore's cube-based automated storage and retrieval system uses robots to store and deliver parts bins to picking workstations, with an AI robotic piece-picking workstation (CarouselAI) added in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated stockkeeping. Transfer: 'keeping parts and supplies in order' is what the grid does - maintaining known locations, inventory counts and retrieval of small parts - in a purpose-built machine environment.

sources.system: Touchless automatic car wash (Shinewash; InterClean drive-through)
sources.title: Touchless Car Wash Technology: A Revolution in Vehicle Care
sources.claim: Touchless automatic car wash systems clean a vehicle end-to-end without an attendant: sensors profile the vehicle and a controller sequences detergent, high-pressure wash and drying in a purpose-built bay.

sources.title: What is robotic refueling? | MobilityPlaza
sources.claim: Autofuel's robotic arm refuels vehicles at gas stations without human involvement, using plate recognition and an app for identification and payment; introduced at a station in Espoo, Finland.

sources.title: Rocsys demonstrates hands-free charging of an electric self-driving truck
sources.claim: Rocsys robotic charging arms perform autonomous hands-free plug-in charging of trucks at container terminals, including at APM Terminals Maasvlakte II and rollouts for port fleets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: energizing/fueling a work vehicle without a human. Transfer: same end state as topping up the service van, achieved at a purpose-built stall.

tasks.label: Drill holes and pull or push wiring through openings, using hand and power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential rough-in (new house or addition): helper bores 3/4"-1" holes through wood studs, top plates and joists with a right-angle drill and auger/self-feed bits, then pulls NM-B cable from the panel location to device boxes through those holes, working off ladders and in attics/crawlspaces amid framing debris, other trades and changing plans.

Commercial new construction (office/retail/school shell): helper drills through metal studs, top tracks and CMU/concrete for penetrations and support anchors, then feeds fish tape or a vacuum string through installed EMT/conduit and pulls THHN conductors with soap and a tugger, coordinating with an electrician at the far box.

Drilling-only shift on a commercial jobsite: helper lays out and drills the overhead hole pattern in the concrete deck/soffit (anchor and small penetration holes) for an upcoming conduit and cable-tray run, hundreds to thousands of holes per BIM/layout, with dust control, before any wire is pulled.

Industrial/utility work: helper drills anchor holes in concrete or steel for supports, then helps pull heavy feeder cable or multiple large conductors through long conduit runs, duct banks between handholes, or cable tray, using a power cable puller, rope, rollers and lubricant, in plant/site conditions with confined spaces and mud.

Retrofit/service in finished, occupied buildings (homes, small businesses): helper drills blind through plates and framing with flex bits and fishes cable through finished wall and ceiling cavities using glow rods, fish tape and magnets, working around insulation, furniture, obstructions and unknown existing conditions with minimal damage.

Contractor prefab shop: helper drills and punches holes in panel backpans, boxes, strut racks and enclosures at a bench, then pulls and routes conductors/whips into the assemblies for shipment to the jobsite, with standard parts, drawings and a fixed workstation.

sources.title: Hilti Releases All New Features for the Hilti Jaibot
sources.claim: Hilti Jaibot is a commercially sold, semi-autonomous mobile robot that navigates a construction site and drills thousands of BIM-planned overhead anchor holes in concrete with dust control; deployed on real MEP projects since late 2020.

sources.title: Jaibot Semi-Autonomous Drilling Robot - Hilti GB
sources.claim: Hilti states the Jaibot drills the planned holes autonomously once positioned, with the worker operating and supervising it rather than drilling by hand.

sources.title: Things look up for nLink's Mobile Building Robot - The Robot Report
sources.claim: nLink's Mobile Building Robot drills holes in concrete ceilings on construction sites from BIM data, commercialized for electricians and plumbers who otherwise drill thousands of overhead holes.

sources.title: Automated Control Cabinet Wiring Solution for Scalable Renewable Energy Systems (SpringerLink)
sources.claim: Kiesling/Rittal's Averex is a portal-robot wiring centre that automatically cuts, crimps, connects and routes wires inside a fixtured control cabinet.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated control-cabinet wiring. It handles the same class of object (insulated building-gauge conductors) threaded through openings and ducts of a fixtured metal enclosure and landed on terminals, i.e. the 'push wiring through openings' half of this task, in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Averex wiring centre from Kiesling | Rittal
sources.claim: Averex was launched by Kiesling in 2014 as the first robotic wiring centre for control enclosure and switchgear manufacturing, replacing manual wiring of mounting plates.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (control-cabinet wiring): establishes the system is a marketed machine, not a concept, for automatically running wires in a fixtured enclosure.

sources.title: Automated Enclosure Machining & Wire Processing | Rittal
sources.claim: Rittal Automation Systems sells CNC machining equipment (milling/laser/cutting centres) that automatically produce holes and cut-outs in panel backplates and enclosures from CAE data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated enclosure/backplate machining. It is the drilling half of this task performed on a fixtured metal workpiece to drawing tolerances, the same holes a helper drills in a prefab shop.

sources.title: Rick Murdock's dream multifamily housing factory | Building Design + Construction
sources.claim: In the most automated modular-housing factory line, robots frame walls and rout out electrical box and other openings, but MEP and finish trade work is done by tradespeople.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic framing and routing of wall panels. It shows the hole/opening-making half is automated on fixtured timber panels, while cable installation in those panels is still performed by tradespeople.

sources.system: Autovol / House of Design robotic wall line
sources.title: Robots are the Future of Modular Construction - Modular Building Institute
sources.claim: Robots in the same modular factory pick, stage and fasten framing lumber and complete wall sections without human hands; humans and tradespeople take over for assembly and trade installation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated wall-panel fabrication, which includes cutting/drilling openings in fixtured framing; establishes the E1 drilling capability and the boundary where wiring remains manual.

sources.title: WEINMANN WALLTEQ multifunction bridges (brochure, Stiles Machinery)
sources.claim: WEINMANN WALLTEQ multifunction bridges are commercial CNC gantries over prefab wall panel lines that saw, trim, drill and mark timber elements, including rough openings and outlet holes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: CNC processing of fixtured wall panels. It substantiates that the drilling half of this task is fully automated when framing is brought to the machine, but the machine does no cable pulling.

sources.system: Multistage cable routing hierarchical imitation-learning system
sources.title: Multistage Cable Routing Through Hierarchical Imitation Learning | IEEE Transactions on Robotics
sources.claim: Berkeley researchers demonstrated autonomous multistage robotic cable routing, threading a cable through a series ... on a fixtured bench setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic routing of a flexible cable through fixed retention points in a purpose-built bench cell; the closest research analog to pushing wiring through openings, but only short lengths in a lab fixture.

sources.title: The fleet — Wattson and Tyler | Human Friendly Robotics
sources.claim: A startup markets an autonomous wire-pulling robot (Wattson) for data-center buildout, but as of mid-2026 it is described only as being in pilots, with the chassis validated by a separate flooring robot.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related (jobsite cable pulling), but the vendor states only pilot status with no independent evidence of completed autonomous pulls, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Clean work area and wash parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential new construction, remodel, or service call: at breaks and end of day the helper cleans the work area in a house or apartment — sweeps up wire clippings, insulation scraps, knockout slugs, drill and drywall dust; collects cardboard fixture boxes, wire-spool cores and scrap conduit; bags trash and carries it to the dumpster or truck; coils cords, moves ladders and material out of walkways; wipes new fixtures and devices clean of dust and fingerprints before the homeowner walks through.

Commercial or institutional construction site / tenant fit-out (office, school, warehouse, hospital shell): helper broom-cleans around electrical rooms, panel walls and overhead work, sweeps up conduit cuttings, metal shavings, tie-wrap tails and packaging; loads scrap conduit, strut and wire reels into rolling bins; hauls debris to the site dumpster; keeps aisles, ladders and cords clear for the daily housekeeping/safety walk and pre-inspection cleanup. Site layout changes daily; other trades and stacked material are present.

Service or maintenance call in an occupied commercial/institutional building (retail store, office suite, school, clinic): after fixture, device or panel work the helper vacuums drilling and ceiling-tile dust from floors, counters and shelving, picks up small debris and packaging, carries out old fixtures/ballasts and boxes, wipes lenses and cover plates, and puts furniture, ceiling tiles and floor protection back as found before the space reopens.

Industrial plant, utility or contractor shop: after motor, switchgear, or control-panel work the helper cleans the work area — vacuums/sweeps debris and dust from around the equipment, wipes grease, dust and coolant from enclosures and components — and washes parts: degreasing motor housings, contactors, terminal blocks, conduit fittings and hand tools in a solvent parts washer, ultrasonic tank or with a pressure washer, then drying and laying them out.

Open-floor sweeping/vacuuming pass in a warehouse, plant bay, garage or contractor shop: after core drilling, conduit cutting or overhead rough-in the helper sweeps or shop-vacs a large clear floor area of concrete/silica dust and small debris so the floor is left clean; open, uncluttered floor, standard surfaces, no manipulation of scrap or tools required beyond the floor pass.

instances.label: Residential rough-in help on a house under construction or a remodel: carry NM cable coils, boxes and panels in from the truck, drill holes through studs/joists, nail on device and fixture boxes, pull and staple cable back to the panel, sweep up scrap. Commercial/institutional interior rough-in: lay out and drill hundreds of anchor holes in concrete decks and walls and set anchors for conduit hangers, cable tray and fixture supports across a floor, working from a lift or ladder with dust control.

Cable pulls: set up jacks and reels, feed and lubricate conductors into installed conduit or tray, tend the puller and coordinate hand signals with the electrician at the far end, coil and dress the pulled wire.

Service/repair call help at occupied homes and small businesses: carry tools, ladder and parts in, hold fixtures, ladders and lights while the electrician works, fetch parts from the truck, clean the work area and wash parts before leaving.

Outdoor underground and solar electrical labor: dig and clean trenches for conduit runs, ground rods and site lighting, place and bed conduit, backfill and tamp, haul equipment across the site in dirt, heat and weather.

tasks.label: Thread conduit ends, connect couplings, and fabricate and secure conduit support brackets, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial building rough-in on an active new-construction jobsite: helper measures, cuts and threads ends of rigid/IMC conduit on a portable pipe stand with a power or ratchet threader, reams, dopes and spins on couplings, then cuts strut/angle to length, drills it, and anchors brackets to concrete deck or steel from a ladder or scissor lift amid other trades, dust, and shifting layout.

Work inside an operating industrial or institutional plant (refinery, water treatment, manufacturing, data center, hospital plant room): 1"-4" rigid conduit threaded in place with a portable power threader, couplings and unions made up, Kindorf/strut brackets fabricated and bolted or clamped to structural steel and existing pipe racks in congested, access-controlled areas.

Electrical contractor prefabrication shop: bench work cutting conduit to length on a chop saw, threading ends on a shop threading machine (e.g., Ridgid 300), making up couplings, cutting/punching strut and fabricating bracket and hanger assemblies, and assembling prefabricated conduit racks for delivery to site.

Outdoor and underground site work: service risers, meter masts, pole and site-lighting bases, duct-bank stub-ups; threading rigid conduit at the trench or pole, coupling sections, and fabricating/securing straps and support brackets to walls, poles or concrete, in weather, mud, and uneven ground.

Residential and light-commercial small jobs and retrofits in occupied buildings: short rigid nipples and mast sections hand-threaded with a ratchet threader, couplings made up, and straps/brackets fabricated and fastened to studs, block, or joists in tight, cluttered spaces with furniture and occupants present.

tasks.label: Disassemble defective electrical equipment, replace defective or worn parts, and reassemble equipment, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/institutional building (office, school, hospital, retail): a defective interior lighting unit — recessed troffer, high-bay, exit sign, ceiling fan — is opened from a ladder or lift; helper removes lens/trim and ballast cover screws, disconnects leads, swaps ballast/LED driver, lampholder or occupancy sensor, and reassembles the fixture.

Occupied home or small tenant space service call: defective in-wall/in-box work — receptacles, switches, dimmers, GFCIs, hardwired smoke alarm bases, doorbell/thermostat transformers — pulled from cramped boxes with existing building conductors, worn parts/terminals replaced, device reseated and cover reinstalled amid furniture, pets and occupants.

Industrial or large-commercial facility, in place inside installed gear: after lockout/tagout, opening a panelboard, disconnect, junction box, control panel or MCC lineup with landed feeders and busbars to replace burnt contactor contacts and coils, relays, breakers, fuse clips or terminal blocks, then reassembling covers and torquing terminations.

Contractor shop bench: portable job-site electrical equipment brought in for repair — power tools with worn brushes/switches/cords, extension cord sets, GFCI spider boxes, temporary lighting strings, task lights — disassembled with hand tools, worn parts replaced, reassembled and tested.

Shop or truck bench work on removed electromechanical units: fan and pump motors, blowers, small appliances and unit heaters — housings opened, run capacitors, contactors, brushes, bearings, thermal switches or terminal boards replaced, unit reassembled and bench-tested; parts are greasy, dirty and of varied make.

Outdoor construction site or building exterior: repairing weather-exposed discrete equipment — pole/wall-pack and sign fixtures, temporary power distribution boxes, cord reels and portable generators — corroded fasteners, dirt, wind and lift/ladder access, work brought back to a gang box or truck when possible.

sources.transferJustification: Covers only the driving sub-step of the 'motorized truck' instance; it does not substantiate loading or unloading assorted material.

sources.claim: Kodiak-equipped driverless RoboTrucks owned by Atlas Energy deliver proppant to well sites across the Permian Basin without a driver, with loading handled by fixed loadout infrastructure.
sources.transferJustification: Delivery of bulk material to a work site by heavy truck; the load is handled by silo loadout and site equipment, not by the vehicle, so it does not cover hand loading/unloading of assorted supplies.

sources.title: Digit is first humanoid deployed in a commercial application
sources.claim: Agility's Digit humanoid is commercially deployed at a GXO-run Spanx facility moving standardized totes between AMRs and conveyors — the current frontier of autonomous mobile manipulation of goods, limited to uniform containers in a fixed workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest deployed analog to hand-carrying items; it establishes the ceiling — standardized totes on known fixtures, not assorted tool bags, conduit bundles or wire reels.

sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Stretch autonomously unloads cases from trailers and containers at DHL sites, at roughly 700 cases per hour, but handles only uniform boxed cases.
sources.transferJustification: Truck unloading is a sub-step of the supply-run instance; it transfers only for uniform cases inside a dock, not for mixed conduit, reels and ladders at a jobsite.

sources.title: Unlocking Jobsite Data with Spot
sources.claim: On active construction sites, Spot autonomously walks pre-taught routes over changing terrain to capture scans and photos; its role is data capture with a small sensor payload, not carrying or placing materials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous navigation of an active jobsite) shows mobility transfers, but the ~14 kg fixed sensor payload and lack of load pickup/placement mean it cannot substitute for a helper hauling materials.

sources.system: Teleo Supervised Autonomy on articulated dump trucks
sources.title: Teleo deploys dump trucks equipped for supervised autonomy
sources.claim: Material-moving machines on active construction sites operate under supervised autonomy with a human remote operator able to take control, hauling bulk earth rather than tools and supplies.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to document the state of jobsite material movement (bulk earthmoving under remote supervision); it does not substantiate autonomous transport of tools and supplies.

tasks.label: String transmission lines or cables through ducts or conduits, under the ground, through equipment, or to towers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/institutional new construction: helper pulls THHN/XHHW conductors through EMT or rigid conduit runs (multiple 90s, LBs, long horizontal runs above ceilings and in walls) from panel to junction boxes — fishing a tape or pull line, taping and lubing the head, feeding from spool carts, tending the tugger, and leaving tails at each box. Active jobsite with ladders/lifts, other trades, debris, changing layout.

Residential rough-in: helper pulls NM-B (Romex) cable from the panel through drilled holes in studs and joists to device and fixture boxes, in an unfinished framed house or apartment unit; also fishing cable in existing walls on remodels.

Underground: helper strings feeder/primary cable through duct banks between manholes, handholes, or building entries — rodding the duct, rigging the pull rope, setting sheaves and rollers, feeding cable off a reel with a winch, monitoring tension at street or site-yard locations, in the weather and in confined spaces.

Industrial plant, data center, or hospital fit-out/retrofit: helper pulls power and control cables through cable tray, ladder rack and sleeves, and into equipment (switchgear, MCCs, panels, racks), dressing and combing the cables and leaving service loops; fixed-layout facility controlled by an owner, partly energized/occupied.

Outdoor overhead: helper assists stringing conductor, shield wire, or communications cable to poles/towers along a right-of-way — handling the pilot line and pull rope, setting up reels/blocks, tailing at ground level under a lineman crew.

sources.title: Facebook robot crawls along power lines to deliver fiber optic cable
sources.claim: Meta's Bombyx robot helically wraps fiber-optic cable onto energized medium-voltage distribution lines outdoors; the target was autonomous obstacle passing, but the functional prototype still had to be steered around obstacles by a remote operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing (stringing) a communications cable along overhead power line infrastructure, the closest robotic analogue to stringing cable to poles/towers; cited to show the state of the art ... its remote-control dependence.

sources.title: Making aerial fiber deployment faster and more efficient
sources.claim: Meta's engineering description of the aerial fiber deployment system states autonomous obstacle passing as a design goal, with human crews still performing setup, loading/unloading and transitions; deployment was prospective at the time of writing.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (aerial cable stringing on distribution lines); quoted because the capability is stated in the future tense, i.e., not yet demonstrated as completed autonomous work.

sources.system: Drone-assisted pilot line pull (shield wire installation)
sources.title: FirstEnergy Pioneers Drone-Assisted Line Work
sources.claim: Utilities use piloted drones to fly a lightweight pilot line between transmission structures; crews then attach and pull the heavier rope and the shield wire with conventional equipment, so the drone performs only one step of the stringing operation.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the aerial variant of this task; shows the only fielded robotic element (a piloted drone) covers the pilot-line step, with human crews doing the rest.

sources.system: Cable-laying robot based on reconfigurable single-actuator-wave units
sources.title: Development of Cable-Laying Robot Based on Reconfigurable Single-Actuator-Wave Units
sources.claim: A 2026 journal paper reports a laboratory prototype cable-laying robot intended to pull lead cables over ... in ceiling spaces at construction sites — i.e., robotic cable pulling in buildings is still at the prototype ....
sources.transferJustification: Same task (pulling cable over racks/ceilings on construction sites); cited to establish that the capability exists only as a research prototype pulling lead (pilot) cables, not as accepted worker-quality installation.

sources.system: Robotic Cable Pulling in Conduit Systems (open innovation challenge)
sources.developer: BEAMP (Built Environment Accelerate to Market Programme, Singapore)
sources.title: Robotic Cable Pulling in Conduit Systems
sources.claim: Robotic pulling of cable through building conduit systems is posed as an unsolved industry challenge, with the incumbent method being manual fish-tape/wire-spring pulling that frequently jams at bends.
sources.transferJustification: Exactly this task (pulling cable through conduit); cited as evidence that no fielded robotic solution exists and the problem is still being solicited from industry.

sources.system: WireSCoutE automatic control cabinet wiring (human-robot cooperation)
sources.title: Automatic control cabinet wiring in a human-robot cooperation
sources.claim: Automated wiring of electrical control cabinets remains a research topic requiring human-robot cooperation, with the worker intervening to help the robot during wire routing and insertion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routing and landing conductors inside equipment enclosures (the 'through equipment' portion of this task) in a fixtured, purpose-built setting; cited because even there the system depends on human assistance.

sources.system: S.A.M. sewer robot (KA-TE) used by CityNet/CableRunner
sources.title: CityNet signs agreement with city of Vienna, Austria for last-mile fiber optic deployment
sources.claim: Fiber has been installed in municipal sewer ducts using remotely operated sewer robots that fix rings and conduit inside non-man-accessible pipe, with human crews doing the man-accessible portions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing cable/conduit in underground ducts; cited as the closest fielded underground system, but it is a remotely operated pipe robot installing supports, not an autonomous duct cable pull.

tasks.label: Install copper-clad ground rods, using a manual post driver.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service entrance or service upgrade: helper carries two 8-ft copper-clad rods to the meter/panel side of an occupied house, picks spots at least 6 ft apart clear of the foundation, buried services, sprinkler lines and landscaping, and drives each rod flush or slightly proud with a manual slide-hammer driver or rotary-hammer driver bit, working in a narrow side yard against fences, shrubs and A/C pads.

Commercial/industrial construction site, open machine-accessible areas: rods driven at transformer pads, generator pads, and grounding-ring locations in graded, staked-out ground before paving/landscaping, several rods per location, soil compacted fill, other equipment working nearby.

Commercial/industrial site, congested locations: rods driven tight to building walls, in trenches or beside pipe racks, inside fenced electrical yards after paving, amid other trades, formwork and stored material, using a hand driver from a kneeling or awkward stance.

Temporary power poles, jobsite trailers, light poles, sign/EV-charger/pool-equipment pads: a single rod driven at a spot chosen on the day, ground varying from lawn to gravel to compacted subgrade, work done quickly with a manual driver and the rod left for the electrician to clamp.

Utility-scale/repetitive grounding: dozens of rods on a solar farm, cell-site compound, substation yard or transmission structure, driven at surveyed grid locations in open, cleared terrain, often into an open trench line for the counterpoise conductor.

Constrained or adverse conditions: rod driven in a crawlspace, unfinished basement, mechanical pit or manhole; from a ladder/bucket beside a pole; or in rocky, root-bound or frozen ground where the rod hits refusal and the helper must reposition, cut the rod, angle it at 45 degrees, or switch to a buried electrode.

sources.system: Built Robotics RPD 35 / RPS 25 autonomous piling system
sources.title: Blattner Picks Autonomous Pile Drivers From Built Robotics for Solar Projects — Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 autonomous pile-driving excavators carry steel piles onboard and install them unaided at utility-scale solar construction sites; EPC contractor Blattner (Quanta) signed a nationwide deal in Sept 2025 after use on multiple projects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously driving steel members vertically into native soil at surveyed points on an open construction site. It transfers to ground-rod driving because the operation class is identical (navigate to a marked point, hold the member plumb, hammer to depth, verify), the terrain is the same graded outdoor site, and a ground rod demands far looser placement precision (feet) than the sub-inch pile tolerances demonstrated; the object is smaller and lighter, requiring a different driving head rather than a different capability.

sources.title: The World's First Autonomous Piling System for Utility-Scale Solar — Built Robotics
sources.claim: The RPD 35 is marketed and specified as a fully autonomous robot that ... in one machine, with a 40,000 lb hammer impulse and compatibility limited to W6x7–W8x28 wide-flange sections (i.e., its current chuck/head is pile-specific, not rod-specific).
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (autonomous pile driving). Cited both to establish autonomy of the whole cycle and to record the tooling limit: the demonstrated head handles wide-flange piles, so driving a 5/8-in ground rod would need a rod head, which is why I do not credit this system in settings where an excavator-class machine cannot reach.

sources.system: Autonomous vineyard post-driving robot (Ly, Gimbert, Passault, Baron)
sources.title: A Fully Autonomous Robot for Putting Posts for Trellising Vineyard with Centimetric Accuracy — IEEE Xplore
sources.claim: A robot built on a small backhoe loader autonomously navigated to marked post locations in a vineyard and drove trellis posts into the earth with centimetric accuracy, with a human only handing it the post.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving a slender post (a few inches across, ~2 m long) into native soil at a specified point from a compact machine. Object scale and driving forces are much closer to an 8-ft ground rod than utility piles are, and the compact backhoe base shows the operation does not require a full-size piling excavator; it is a 2015 research demo, so it supports feasibility in controlled, open, machine-accessible ground rather than deployment-grade reliability.

sources.system: Vibe Drive Vibrating Ground Rod Driver attachment
sources.title: Vibrating Ground Rod Driver | Vibe Drive Technologies
sources.claim: A commercially sold ground-rod driving head attaches to vibratory post and pile drivers, so the machine-mounted tooling needed to drive copper-clad ground rods from a driver-equipped machine exists (operated manually, not autonomously).
sources.transferJustification: Not an autonomous system and cannot by itself support a positive judgment; cited only to show that the end-effector gap between demonstrated autonomous pile driving and ground-rod driving is a standard attachment, supporting the transfer argument in evidence 0 and 1.

tasks.label: Dig trenches or holes for installation of conduit or supports.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/light-commercial service work: helper hand-digs (shovel, mattock, sometimes a rented walk-behind trencher) a 12-24 in deep, 40-100 ft conduit trench across an occupied homeowner's yard to a garage, pool panel, or post light; must work around finished landscaping, tree roots, sprinkler lines and a fence gate with narrow access, keep spoil on a tarp, and restore sod.

New commercial/industrial/solar or utility construction site: helper and crew dig long open-ground trenches (hundreds to thousands of feet, 24-48 in deep) with an excavator or trencher for feeder conduit, duct bank, or direct-burial cable, cutting to grade and depth, piling spoil, and hand-cleaning/grading the trench bottom before conduit is laid.

Digging holes for supports on open ground at a new site: auger or excavator-dug footings for light-pole and sign bases, equipment-rack/transformer pad piers, guy anchors and ground-rod pits, dug to specified diameter, depth and location from stakes or layout.

Excavating near existing/live buried utilities: helper hand-digs or vacuum-excavates test holes (potholing/daylighting) inside the tolerance zone of marked gas, water, telecom and power lines in a street shoulder, parking lot, or campus lawn, exposing the line undamaged, then backfilling and compacting.

Hard-surface excavation at an operating facility: saw/jackhammer through asphalt or a concrete apron in a plant yard, campus walk, or parking lot, then dig the hole or short trench beneath for a conduit stub-up, hand hole, or support footing, and backfill/patch.

Interior retrofit: break out a section of building floor slab in a mechanical room, back-of-house corridor, or store during off-hours and dig a shallow trench/hole in the fill below for conduit runs or an equipment support, working in tight quarters with dust control and no machine access.

sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofit turns standard excavators into fully autonomous trenching machines, marketed with 180 ft/hr production and 0.1 ft digging accuracy for DC/AC cable trenches on utility-solar jobsites.

sources.system: Built Robotics AI Guidance System / Exosystem on excavators
sources.title: Construction Jobs Accelerate With Autonomous Robot Use : CEG
sources.claim: Black & Veatch used Built Robotics-equipped excavators to autonomously dig 1,000 linear feet of cable trenches at a solar energy ...; Built staff supervised on site rather than operating the machines.

sources.system: Built Robotics AI Guidance System on excavators
sources.title: Construction Jobs Accelerate With Autonomous Robot Use : CEG
sources.claim: Mortenson used Built Robotics-equipped excavators on wind farm sites in eastern Colorado to autonomously excavate turbine foundation holes to specified dimensions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: excavating foundation holes for wind turbines. Same machine class, same medium (native soil on an open outdoor site), same output (a hole of specified diameter/depth at a staked location for a structural support), so it transfers to digging holes for supports such as pole bases and piers.

sources.title: Blattner Deploys Robots on Solar Projects | Construction Equipment
sources.claim: Built Robotics' autonomous machines remain in commercial fleet use in 2025: Blattner signed a three-year agreement to ... the robots on US solar projects for piling, surveying, drilling and trenching.

sources.system: Built Robotics RPD 35 robotic pile driver
sources.date: 2026-07 (page live; product launched 2023, deployments from Q4 2023)
sources.title: The World's First Autonomous Piling System for Utility-Scale Solar — Built Robotics
sources.claim: The RPD 35 is a ... surveys, distributes, drives and records piles — the ground-penetrating structural supports for solar racking — and has been used by US contractors since 2023.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing solar piles. It autonomously puts structural supports into the ground at surveyed locations to tight tolerance on open outdoor sites, which is the same output as digging holes for supports.

sources.title: The Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System (RRES): From Innovation Funding to Field Trials – ULC Technologies
sources.claim: In UK field trials on SGN's gas network, the RRES robot scanned below ground, located a buried pipe, cut a keyhole in the surface, and excavated down to expose the live asset undamaged, then backfills and reinstates the surface.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: keyhole excavation to expose a buried gas main. Same objects (buried utilities in soil under pavement), same precision requirement (expose without strike), same setting class, so it transfers to potholing/daylighting before conduit installation.

sources.title: The Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System (RRES): From Innovation Funding to Field Trials – ULC Technologies
sources.claim: RRES carries a road-cutting device on its robotic arm that cuts and removes a core of the paved surface, sensing material hardness and adjusting cutting speed, before the soil beneath is vacuum-excavated; ULC's trials ran at SGN's gas holder site in ..., Surrey.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting pavement and excavating beneath it for utility work. Same hard-surface breaking plus soil removal sequence required when a helper saws/jackhammers asphalt or concrete to dig for a conduit stub-up.

sources.title: Roadwork Robot Autonomously Digs Out, Repairs, Buried Utility Lines | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Trade press describes RRES as a stand-alone battery-powered robot performing the full excavate-repair-rebury cycle on buried utility lines under roadways autonomously; it was a working prototype in field trials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic street excavation over buried utilities; the excavation and reinstatement steps are the same physical work a helper performs when digging near existing lines.

tasks.label: Raise, lower, or position equipment, tools, and materials, using hoist, hand line, or block and tackle.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/institutional new construction: helper ties bundles of conduit, wire spools, strut, boxes and tool buckets to a hand line or rope-and-pulley rigged over a floor opening, scaffold, or steel deck and raises them to the electrician working on a lift or upper floor, then lowers empties; load must clear obstructions and be handed off at height amid other trades.

Setting heavy electrical gear: helper rigs slings/chain hoist, come-along or block and tackle to a panelboard, transformer, switchgear section, cable reel or motor and raises, skids and positions it onto a housekeeping pad, wall or rack, aligning to anchor bolts and conduit stubs under the electrician's direction, in an electrical/mechanical room of a building under construction or renovation.

Residential and light-commercial service or remodel: helper raises and lowers tools, fixtures, coils of wire and small equipment on a hand line to a worker on a ladder, in an attic, or on a roof; cluttered, occupied, variable spaces with no fixed rigging points.

Industrial or institutional plant work (factory, refinery, hospital, data center) during maintenance or retrofit: helper uses the facility's overhead bridge crane, jib crane or chain fall to lift a motor, transformer, cable reel or enclosure off a pallet or truck and position it at the installation point; premises and traffic controlled by the plant.

Outdoor utility, site-lighting or building-exterior work: helper uses a hand line, block and tackle or truck-mounted hoist to raise tools, hardware, fixtures and small equipment to a worker on a pole, tower, light standard or parapet, and lowers removed equipment; weather, uneven ground, and public traffic nearby.

sources.system: Morgan Automation automated crane system with Morgan Cephas logistics control (Siemens drives/PLC)
sources.title: US steel mill installs fully automated cranes system - Hoist
sources.claim: A US steel mill operates a fully automated, unmanned three-crane overhead system that autonomously engages heavy loads (28-ton coils) with a crane grab, raises them, and places them on transfer cars or floor saddles at laser-determined positions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated overhead-crane material handling. It is the same physical act as the helper's hoist work — raising, lowering and precisely positioning heavy material with a hoist — but only where loads arrive at known positions in an unmanned bay and are engaged by a dedicated grab rather than field-rigged slings.

sources.title: Automated Stacking Cranes (ASC) | Konecranes
sources.claim: Automated stacking cranes lift, move and precisely stack heavy containers without an operator in the machine, with more than 550 units in commercial service at container terminals worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated hoisting and placement of heavy unit loads. Demonstrates autonomous raise/lower/position of multi-ton loads to millimetre-level placement, but with standardized loads, a dedicated engaging device, and a machine-only stacking yard.

sources.system: Dual-arm robot with crane pulley blocks (Hayakawa, Wan, Koyama, Harada)
sources.title: A Dual-arm Robot that Autonomously Lifts Up and Tumbles Heavy Plates Using Crane Pulley Blocks (arXiv:2101.09526)
sources.claim: A dual-arm robot autonomously plans and executes the operation of crane pulley blocks (block and tackle) to lift and tumble heavy plates beyond its own arm payload, in a laboratory setup.
sources.transferJustification: Direct match to the 'block and tackle' element of the task: the robot rigs and pulls a pulley-block rope to raise a heavy object, but only for a known plate in a fixtured laboratory bench setup.

sources.title: Featured in ENR: LIFTBOT transforming site logistics - KEWAZO LIFTBOT case study
sources.claim: Kewazo's LIFTBOT robotic hoist climbs scaffolding to carry materials to height on real construction and industrial sites, including the US Capitol facade reconstruction, but it is remote-controlled and workers load and unload it.
sources.transferJustification: Closest fielded construction-site analogue to hoisting materials to height; it is human-controlled and human-loaded, so it does not substantiate autonomous completion of the task on a jobsite.

sources.system: Konecranes Automated Storage and Retrieval System (ASRS) cranes
sources.title: Automatic Storage and Retrieval System | Konecranes
sources.claim: Fully automated storage-and-retrieval cranes handle paper rolls in mill warehouses, autonomously picking, raising and stacking rolls and tracking their positions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unmanned crane handling of heavy cylindrical stock (comparable to cable reels) inside an industrial plant, showing autonomous raise/lower/position where the storage bay is engineered for the crane.

tasks.label: Bolt component parts together to form tower assemblies, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ground assembly of lattice steel transmission tower sections in the laydown/assembly area of a line construction right-of-way: helper sorts match-marked galvanized angle members from bundles, holds and aligns them while the electrician/lineman drifts holes, then inserts and runs hundreds of bolts/nuts with spud wrench and impact wrench to spec. Uneven ground, mud, wind, weather, layout differs at every structure site.

Bolting members into a partially erected tower at height (climbing the lattice or working from a bucket/crane-held section): attaching leg extensions, bracing, crossarms and step bolts, passing and starting bolts overhead and torquing them while tied off.

Bolting crossarms, davit arms, braces and hardware onto steel/concrete poles or bolting substation structural steel (bus supports, dead-end and switch stands) together on the ground in a fenced substation yard or at the pole site.

Shop or contractor's-yard prefabrication: sub-assembling tower sections, crossarm assemblies or tower legs on a fabrication shop floor or laydown yard with wooden/steel jigs, sawhorses, overhead crane and standard equipment under an institution's control before shipment or erection.

Assembly of smaller bolted tower structures at the site: communication/antenna tower sections, light or camera towers, temporary steel masts — modular sections bolted flange-to-flange or leg-to-leg on staging ground before lifting.

sources.system: MIRAI AI-vision software on Universal Robots cobots with automatic torque wrench
sources.title: Leading US automotive OEM — Automated bolt torquing | MIRAI Use cases
sources.claim: A US automotive OEM runs seven vision/AI-guided Universal Robots cobots that autonomously locate and torque bolts on four seating assembly lines despite variance in bolt position, part presentation and lighting — deployed robotic bolt fastening inside a fixtured production station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: running down and torquing threaded fasteners on a fixtured assembly. It transfers to bolting tower members at E1 because the machine locates the hole, drives the fastener and verifies torque, which is the fastening core of the tower-bolting task once parts are presented in fixtures.

sources.system: Automated production fastening system for LGP and Hi-Lok titanium bolts (737 Panel Assembly Line)
sources.title: 2015-01-2514: An Automated Production Fastening System for LGP and Hi-Lok Titanium Bolts for the Boeing 737 Wing Panel Assembly Line
sources.claim: Electroimpact's automated production fastening system on Boeing's 737 wing panel assembly line inserts bolts through holes in fixtured structural assemblies and sets the collars/preload automatically at production rate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bolting structural members of an airframe together in a fixtured cell. Transfers to bolting tower steel at E1 because the operation is the same class — driving a metal bolt through aligned holes in two rigidly held structural members and setting it to a specified preload, with automatic fastener feeding — at tighter precision than tower bolting requires.

sources.title: Boeing automates 737 wing assembly job to reach production targets
sources.claim: Boeing installed the Electroimpact panel assembly line machines on the 737 wing production line in Renton, confirming factory deployment rather than a laboratory demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the Electroimpact fastening-system item; this source establishes that the automated bolt-installation machinery is in production use in a purpose-built assembly cell.

sources.system: WEBER automatic fastener feeding systems and screwdriving spindles for robot applications
sources.title: Feeding technology with automatic screw feeding - WEBER
sources.claim: Commercial automatic feeding systems deliver bolts, nuts and washers to robot-mounted screwdriving/nutrunning spindles, so a robotic cell can present and drive its own fasteners rather than having them pre-started by a human.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fastener presentation for robotic assembly. It supplies the part of tower bolting that consists of picking a bolt and a nut and starting them, closing the gap between torque-only cells and full bolt-up in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Tightening Cell Robotics (TCR) / automated tightening solutions
sources.title: Automated tightening - Atlas Copco USA
sources.claim: Atlas Copco markets turnkey robotic tightening cells (Tightening Cell Robotics) configured around production rate, station layout, part torque/position specs and part handling, i.e. purpose-built fenced/fixtured robotic bolting stations sold as standard equipment, including for heavy components.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic bolt tightening of heavy fixtured components. Shows that a purpose-built cell able to place heavy parts and torque large fasteners is off-the-shelf, which is what the E1 counterfactual for tower-section bolting requires.

sources.system: Transmission tower climbing robot (3D-model-based visual positioning)
sources.title: A New Positioning Method for Climbing Robots Based on 3D Model of Transmission Tower and Visual Sensor
sources.claim: Robots that would tighten bolts on transmission towers in the field are still research designs: work published on tower-climbing robots addresses clamping mechanisms and visual positioning on the tower, not fielded bolt-up of tower assemblies.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-topic (bolting on transmission towers) but prototype-stage; cited as the state of the art for the in-field environment, which is why no E2/E3 judgment is made.

sources.title: Robots under Autonomous Control at Robot Lab | Shimizu Corporation
sources.claim: The closest autonomous fastening robot working on a real building site senses ceiling grid position, inserts ceiling suspension bolts and screws up lightweight ceiling boards; it does not mate and bolt heavy structural members.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fastening on a construction site. It bounds what is fielded — light interior components fastened to an already-installed grid inside a weather-tight shell — and therefore does not substantiate assembling and bolting heavy galvanized angle members in a yard or at height.

tasks.label: Erect electrical system components and barricades, and rig scaffolds, hoists, and shoring.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial
