instances.label: Commercial/institutional new construction or fit-out: helper erects supports and mounts electrical system components with the electrician — unistrut/hanger racks, conduit supports, junction/pull boxes, disconnects, panelboard cans, cable-tray sections, light fixtures — on an active jobsite with other trades, dust, temporary lighting, uneven floors and changing layouts.

Residential or light-commercial work: helper erects service mast, meter socket, temp-power pole/panel, exterior disconnects and small equipment at an occupied house or small tenant space; each site differs, surfaces and access are as found.

Utility-scale outdoor electrical construction (solar farm, substation yard, site electrical): helper erects array/racking-mounted modules, combiner boxes and field-mounted equipment onto prepared foundations/mounts, outdoors in heat, wind and dust.

Barricading and work-zone protection: helper sets cones, barrier stands, caution tape, temporary fencing/plywood barriers around an open panel, floor opening, trench or lift zone, or a lane/parking-lot work zone for street-light or signal work, and removes them afterward.

Rigging scaffolds and shoring: helper erects and dismantles a Baker/rolling scaffold or sectional frame scaffold, sets planks, outriggers and guardrails, and installs shoring/trench-box support so electricians can work at height or in an excavation.

Rigging hoists and lifting gear: helper attaches chain falls, slings, come-alongs and tag lines to hoist heavy electrical equipment (transformers, switchgear sections, motors, cable reels, large fixtures) into position on brackets, pads or overhead steel.

sources.title: AES Maximo robot installs 100 megawatts of solar capacity - The Robot Report
sources.claim: AES Maximo, a robotic solar-module installation system, works on utility-scale solar construction sites; in end-to-end mode it performs the module installation itself under button-push supervision, and had installed 100 MW by early 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Erecting field-mounted electrical system components (PV modules on racking) is the outdoor variant of this task: heavy rigid components lifted from a stack and fastened onto structural mounts.

sources.title: AES sends world's first AI-powered solar robot fleet to California project
sources.claim: Maximo fleets have been sent to utility-scale projects (Bellefield, CA; Oak Ridge, LA) and had installed more than 35 MW of modules by September 2025, working alongside union field crews.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: field erection of electrical system components at commercial scale on real construction sites.

sources.title: Terabase Energy invests in automation and engineering to streamline solar construction – pv magazine USA
sources.claim: Terabase's Terafab is an on-site automated 'field factory' line that assembles module and tracker torque-tube assemblies and places them on prepositioned tracker mounts; the first generation was deployed on five power-plant projects and V2 completed field testing in 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated lifting, carrying and precise seating of large heavy electrical-array assemblies onto prepared mounts, i.e. the machine equivalent of hoisting equipment into place where the load is staged and presented to the line.

sources.system: ABB Smart Power switchgear assembly line (ABB robots, JOT Automation)
sources.title: Automated assembly line helps ABB Smart Power launch next-generation switching products
sources.claim: An automated fenced assembly line built by JOT Automation with ABB robots assembles ABB Smart Power's industrial switchgear product family in a factory cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic assembly and mounting of electrical gear components in a fixtured cell; comparable objects (switchgear parts, enclosures) and fastening precision to mounting boxes, panels and devices, with the work presented to the machine.

sources.title: Automated Electrical Box Assembly Cell | HowToRobot
sources.claim: A commercial robotic cell assembles electrical enclosures of various sizes: three six-axis robots install inserts, place covers and drive screws, with parts presented by feeders.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = fixtured pick-place-and-fasten of electrical enclosure hardware; transfers to mounting electrical components and to setting light rigid objects (cones, barrier stands) at defined positions when the work is presented to the machine.

sources.title: KEWAZO LIFTBOT - Edison Awards
sources.claim: Kewazo's LIFTBOT is a battery-powered robotic hoist that clamps to scaffolding and autonomously carries scaffold parts and other materials vertically; it is in regular use on industrial plant sites (ExxonMobil, BASF, Dow, TotalEnergies) but is itself installed by two workers and does not erect scaffolds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = hoisting materials to elevation at a work site; covers the hoisting portion once the hoist is in place, but not human erection of the scaffold or the rigging of the hoist itself.

sources.system: Genio (PERI UP Robotics) / Robot-Aided Scaffold Assembly demonstrator
sources.title: Symposium 2025: Smart Manufacturing - Flanders Make
sources.claim: Robot-aided scaffold assembly (PERI 'Genio' platform with Flanders Make) exists only as a prototype/demonstrator shown at bauma 2025 and research symposia; the scaffolder still prepares, monitors and secures the assembly.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the scaffold-rigging instance, but a prototype demonstrator in which the human scaffolder secures the structure, so it does not substantiate whole-instance completion at worker quality.

sources.title: Hilti Unveils BIM-Enabled Construction Jobsite Robot
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot, the leading MEP construction-site robot, only drills and marks overhead anchor holes: it is driven from location to location by a remote-control operator and then drills automatically; it does not mount or erect components.
sources.transferJustification: Closest construction-site robot for electrical installation work; establishes that on-site automation stops at anchor-hole drilling and does not extend to erecting supports or mounting electrical components.

sources.developer: Hong Kong Highways Department with Hong Kong Productivity Council
sources.title: Highways Department - Robot System for Placement and Collection of Traffic Cones and Warning Lanterns at High Speed Roads
sources.claim: Robotic placement of traffic cones and warning devices on real roads remains prototype work: Hong Kong's Roadbot 1 is described as a prototype and Roadbot 2 as anticipated for future use.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the barricading instance (delineating a work zone), but only a prototype with unestablished autonomy, so it cannot support a positive judgment in an unstructured or facility setting.

sources.system: Automated cone laying vehicles (Highway Care; King Highway Products)
sources.developer: Highway Care / King Highway Products for Highways England
sources.title: Highways Magazine - Automated cone laying moves forward with road trials
sources.claim: UK automated cone-laying vehicles trialled on the strategic road network place cones mechanically but are operated by the driver, i.e. operator-run machines rather than autonomous robots.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the roadway-barricading instance; shows the deployed technology is a driver-operated machine, not autonomous barricade erection.

tasks.label: Trim trees and clear undergrowth along right-of-way.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Clearing undergrowth in a rural/wooded distribution or transmission right-of-way: cutting briars, brambles, saplings and light woody brush (mostly under ~2 in. stems) with a brush saw, string trimmer or chainsaw, cut material left mulched/scattered in place. Uneven ground, stumps, rocks, slopes, farm fences, ticks and poison ivy; terrain and vegetation taken as found.

Trimming tree limbs and branches encroaching on energized conductors and service drops: pole pruner/pole saw work from the ground, handing tools/ropes and rigging for a climber or bucket operator, dropping and directing limbs away from houses, cars, fences and traffic on residential streets and roadsides while maintaining approach distances from energized lines.

Debris handling and site cleanup after trimming: dragging cut limbs and brush from where they fell to the truck, feeding the chipper butt-first, loading logs and chips, raking and blowing chips off lawns and pavement, keeping the roadway clear at a roadside or residential worksite.

Mechanized corridor clearing along a maintained right-of-way or access road: running a mower/brush hog or mulching head over grass, weeds and light brush along pole lines, easements and roadside ditches; slopes, culverts, guy wires, boulders and hidden debris.

Vegetation clearing inside institution-controlled utility facility grounds: mowing and cutting weeds and brush inside a fenced substation yard, generating-plant grounds, solar array or service-center yard, around equipment pads, structures, fences and pole bases, on a graded site with a fixed layout and controlled access.

sources.system: Swap Robotics vegetation cutting robot (rough-cut deck)
sources.title: SOLV Energy partners with Swap Robotics to tackle thick vegetation on solar sites
sources.claim: Swap Robotics fields autonomous electric vegetation-cutting robots on utility-scale solar sites; their 'rough cut' deck cuts thick grass and woody vegetation up to two inches in ... over variable terrain, after a pre-mapping teaching run.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is vegetation management on a utility-scale solar site: same class of work (cutting brush/undergrowth, woody stems up to ~2 in.), same implement class (rough-cut mowing/mulching deck), same outdoor uneven terrain, differing mainly in that the solar site is an institution-controlled facility rather than an as-found ROW.

sources.title: Swap Robotics | LinkedIn company page
sources.claim: Swap Robotics reports a deployed fleet operating autonomously outdoors on utility-scale solar sites.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployment maturity of the same solar-site vegetation cutting work cited above.

sources.title: RenuBot drives autonomously with the help of mosaic-X5
sources.claim: Renu Robotics' RenuBot is a fully autonomous electric machine that performs vegetation management (mowing) at utility-scale solar farms and other energy facilities, navigating with GNSS.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is vegetation management at an energy facility; same outdoor cutting work around fixed equipment (panel rows, piers) as clearing vegetation in a substation or plant yard.

sources.title: Southern Company deploys electric, semi-autonomous lawn mowers at power plants
sources.claim: Southern Company deployed Scythe Robotics electric autonomous mowers to maintain grounds at six power plants; the machines use eight cameras and sensors to work safely around people, animals, trees and shrubs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is grounds vegetation maintenance at an electric utility generating facility — the same institution-controlled utility yard setting and obstacle-dense mowing/trimming work as clearing vegetation inside substation and plant grounds.

sources.title: Scythe Robotics launches latest generation of M.52
sources.claim: The Scythe M.52 is marketed and shipped as a fully autonomous commercial mower rolling out to landscape contractors across multiple US states.
sources.transferJustification: Corroborates autonomy level of the mower deployed at utility plant grounds.

sources.system: Greenzie Powered Autonomy (Bobcat, Wright, Mean Green mowers)
sources.title: Greenzie releases Version 5.0 software to advance commercial-ready autonomy
sources.claim: Greenzie's autonomous mowing systems are in commercial use on campuses, parks and athletic fields, but perform best on large, flat, low-obstacle grounds — i.e., institution-maintained sites rather than as-found rough terrain.
sources.transferJustification: Same class of autonomous outdoor vegetation cutting; cited to bound the environment in which current autonomy is reliable (kept grounds, not as-found brush terrain).

sources.title: Right-of-way robots could mow along Minnesota highways
sources.claim: Mowing of steep, rough highway right-of-way slopes is currently done with radio-controlled machines operated by a person in line of sight, not autonomous ones; legislators were only funding a study of autonomous roadside mowing.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the ROW brush/slope mowing instance; shows the state of practice in as-found corridors is remote control, which cannot support a positive autonomy judgment.

sources.title: Aerial Saw Tree Trimming Work Begins Along Hard-to-Access Corridors in Northern and Central Pennsylvania
sources.claim: Mechanized trimming of trees along transmission rights-of-way is performed by a human-piloted helicopter carrying a saw boom, not by an autonomous machine.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the limb-trimming instance; shows the only mechanized ROW limb-cutting in service is a piloted aircraft, i.e. not an autonomous robotic system.

sources.system: ARSS aerial robot with suspended saw
sources.title: ARSS: A Novel Aerial Robot Performs Tree Pruning Tasks
sources.claim: Robots that cut tree branches near electric power lines from the air remain research prototypes evaluated in controlled tests, not fielded systems.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the limb-trimming-near-conductors instance; demonstrates only prototype-level capability, supporting a negative judgment.

sources.developer: La Hera et al., Umeå University (Journal of Field Robotics)
sources.title: Exploring the feasibility of autonomous forestry operations: Results from the first experimental unmanned machine
sources.claim: Autonomous handling and loading of felled woody material by forestry machines is still experimental research rather than fielded capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is picking up and loading cut timber with a grapple — the nearest analogue to dragging brush and feeding a chipper; its experimental status supports a negative judgment for debris handling.

tasks.label: Requisition materials, using warehouse requisition or release forms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Solder electrical connections, using soldering iron.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop/prefab bench work: helper solders lead wires to lugs, terminals, pigtails and small connectors on the contractor's shop bench or a prefab table, using a soldering iron, flux and a helping-hand vise; parts vary job to job, positions taught by eye, joint then heat-shrunk and inspected by the journeyman.

Occupied commercial/institutional building: helper solders low-voltage, control or signal splices in situ — inside a junction box, device box, or above a suspended ceiling on a ladder — wires already pulled and terminated in place, working overhead or in a cramped enclosure with live adjacent circuits.

Industrial plant maintenance: helper solders leads, sensor wiring or component connections on machinery, motor control gear or inside a panel enclosure on the plant floor, often in awkward posture inside a cabinet, with plant housekeeping standards and lockout in force.

Residential/light commercial service or remodel: helper solders splices or fixture/thermostat/doorbell leads inside a private home — attic, crawlspace, wall cavity or ceiling box — dusty, cramped, poorly lit, layout differs house to house.

Outdoor/rough construction site: helper solders bonding jumpers, ground straps, or heavier conductor-to-lug connections on site equipment or exterior gear, in wind, temperature swings and dirt, using a heavy iron or torch-assisted heating.

sources.system: Japan Unix automatic soldering robots (UNIX-DF / laser robots)
sources.title: Let's Try Soldering of DB Connector with an Automatic Soldering Robot [YouTube Tech Article]
sources.claim: Commercial automatic soldering robots (Japan Unix desktop/gantry/articulated) solder lead wires onto the terminals of a D-sub (DB) connector under program control, with iron and laser heads; the vendor reports over 1,000 implementations worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: soldering stranded lead wires to metal terminals with a soldering iron; the objects (wire, terminal, solder, flux) and precision are those of an electrician-helper's soldered connection, done in a fixtured benchtop cell.

sources.system: Hakko soldering kit (FU-601/FU-500) on Universal Robots cobots; tabletop soldering robots
sources.title: What's New With Robotic Soldering? | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Robotic soldering with iron plus automatic solder-wire feeder is a mature commercial automation category in US manufacturing: Hakko's soldering kit (iron + FU-500 feeder) lets Universal Robots cobots run hand-soldering processes on plant benchtops.

sources.system: Robotic soldering cell for electrical/electronic cables (cobot + rotating table + vision)
sources.title: New Product Development of a Robotic Soldering Cell Using Lean Manufacturing Methodology
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed engineering paper documents a built robotic soldering cell for multi-wire electrical cables: wires are held in a wire-fixing device on a rotating table, a vision camera verifies wire insertion, and the cobot then performs the soldering cycle automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Same task on the same objects an electrician's helper solders: multi-conductor cable wires soldered to terminals, with fixtures presenting the wires — an E1 presentation of the instance.

sources.system: Ambrell EASYHEAT LI 3542 / EKOHEAT induction soldering systems with application-specific coils
sources.date: application notes, retrieved 2026-07; systems commercially sold for years
sources.title: Soldering a fine copper wire to an electrical connector assembly | Ambrell Induction Heating
sources.claim: Automated induction soldering stations solder heavier electrical joints — a battery cable to its terminal and copper wire to a connector assembly in 1-2 seconds, and grounding lugs — with a purpose-built coil and fixed cycle, replacing flame/hand methods.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled soldering of larger-gauge conductors and grounding lugs, the heavy-conductor end of the helper's soldering work; same materials (copper conductor, lug, solder, flux) and same accepted joint quality, in a fixtured station.

sources.system: Komax X1585 fluxing-tinning module on fully automatic wire processing machines
sources.title: Options for Tinning Wire | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Fully automatic wire-processing machines cut, strip and tin (flux + solder) stranded wire ends as a standard production module, automating the preparation step of a soldered electrical connection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fluxing and tinning stranded conductor ends is the preparation half of 'solder electrical connections'; it uses the same materials and joint-quality standard and shows the whole strip-flux-solder sequence is machine-executable when wires are fixtured.

tasks.label: Paint a variety of objects related to electrical functions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Active commercial/industrial construction site: helper spray- or brush-paints already-installed EMT/rigid conduit runs, straps, hangers, cut ends and surface-mounted boxes overhead and along walls — masking adjacent finished surfaces, priming cut/threaded ends, matching architect-specified or galvanizing-repair coatings, working amid other trades, scaffolds and clutter.

Occupied institutional or industrial facility (school, plant, hospital, warehouse) during retrofit or maintenance: helper applies identification/color-code paint — red on fire-alarm conduit and boxes, orange/yellow on emergency or high-voltage raceway, painted panel covers, safety striping around gear — brushing or spraying in-place equipment while the facility keeps operating.

Outdoor customer sites and utility yards: helper wire-brushes and repaints installed exterior electrical hardware in place — pole bases and light standards, meter enclosures, disconnect switches, pedestals, cable tray and strut, transformer cabinets — with primer/enamel or cold-galvanizing spray under variable weather.

Contractor shop or designated jobsite paint area: helper paints loose items before installation — pull boxes and junction boxes, panel covers, mounting brackets, unistrut, threaded rod, pole sections, plywood backboards — set on racks/sawhorses or hung, primed and sprayed, then set aside to dry.

Occupied residence or small tenant space: helper paints exposed surface conduit, meter socket, service mast, weatherhead or device cover plates to match the existing wall/trim finish, working around furniture, landscaping and homeowner property with drop cloths and masking.

sources.system: Häwa powder coating line with painting robot in powder booth
sources.date: 2024-08 (plant commissioned mid-2024; article undated, corroborated by 2026 trade report)
sources.title: Powder coating system for electrical enclosures and control cabinets - Surface Technology Online
sources.claim: Häwa's new powder coating plant for electrical enclosures, control cabinets and electrical-component housings uses a robot in an automated powder booth to apply pre-coating and corner coating on parts conveyed through the line — direct evidence that electrical enclosures and boxes are painted by robots in a purpose-built booth.
sources.transferJustification: Same class of objects as the task (electrical enclosures, cabinets, housings) and same operation (applied coating), but the work is brought to a fixtured conveyor booth rather than painted in place.

sources.system: Häwa Lackierroboter / new powder coating plant
sources.title: Schaltschrank- und Gehäusehersteller häwa investiert 20 Millionen
sources.claim: German trade press (Feb 2026) confirms the Häwa plant is in production with painting robots and cobot stations in its new powder coating line for switch cabinets and enclosures.
sources.transferJustification: Corroborates that the robot painting of electrical cabinets/enclosures described above is an operating production installation, not a concept.

sources.system: FANUC P-50iB paint robots, multi-zone conveyor-fed line integrated by Robotic Technical Support Services (RTSS)
sources.developer: FANUC America / RTSS at Regal Finishing
sources.title: Painting in Partnership: Regal Finishing Elevates Its Paint Operations with RTSS' Automation Solution | FANUC America
sources.claim: A US job-shop finisher runs a fully automated, conveyor-fed robotic paint line that applies primer, base, specialty finishes and ... to a mix of customer parts, halving the number of painters and improving first-run quality — evidence that varied fabricated metal parts presented on a conveyor can be painted to accepted commercial quality by robots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: job-shop spray painting of assorted fabricated metal workpieces hung on a conveyor. Objects (brackets, covers, boxes, tubular parts), coatings (primer/enamel) and finish tolerances match the helper's shop painting of loose electrical hardware; only the presentation is fixtured.

sources.system: Ventherm automated paint systems using ABB IRB 5500/5510 ATEX paint robots on gantry or floor rails
sources.title: Automated Paint Systems – Gantry, Floor & In Line | Ventherm
sources.claim: Commercially supplied paint cells put six-axis ATEX paint robots on gantries or rail wagons inside booths to coat large steel workpieces such as long cylindrical structures — the configuration used for pole- and tube-shaped items brought into a booth.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: booth coating of large steel weldments and cylindrical sections; transfers to pole sections, strut and large pull boxes the helper would paint in a shop, provided the work is conveyed into the booth.

sources.system: Okibo EG7 / EG7+ autonomous plastering and painting robot
sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction's Dirty Work Is Going Robotic - Architect Magazine
sources.claim: The most capable field painting robots on construction sites are autonomous wall-and-ceiling finishers: Okibo's EG7 plasters, sands and paints large flat interior surfaces while navigating jobsites, but performs surface coating of walls, not masked detail painting of installed conduit, boxes and hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to characterize the state of the art for in-situ painting on jobsites; it does not substantiate completion of masked detail painting of installed electrical components, so it supports no positive judgment here.

sources.title: Apellix Spray Painting Drone Goes to Work in the Field for State DOTs, Federal Contractors, and Commercial Coating Firms | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: Drone-based coating systems are entering field service for painting tall exterior structures (bridges, tanks, high walls) with contractor pilots on the ground; the work is large-area exterior surface coating rather than detail painting of small in-place electrical hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only to bound outdoor in-situ coating capability; the system is pilot-supervised (semi-autonomous) and aimed at large flat exteriors, so it cannot support a positive judgment for painting installed electrical hardware.

tasks.label: Break up concrete, using airhammer, to facilitate installation, construction, or repair of equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/institutional construction or renovation site: helper uses a pneumatic/electric jackhammer to cut a channel or opening through a 4-8 in. interior floor slab (often with rebar or wire mesh) so the electrician can run conduit, set floor boxes, or pour an equipment base; dust control, adjacent finished work, and unknown embedded services in play; helper also clears the rubble.

Operating industrial plant, substation, or data center under an institution's control: helper breaks out a concrete housekeeping pad, breaks around anchor bolts, or chips concrete away from an embedded conduit stub so a motor, panel, transformer, or switchgear can be removed/reinstalled; fixed plant layout, controlled access, live equipment nearby.

Exterior sidewalk, driveway, or parking-lot slab in a public right-of-way: helper breaks out a strip/section of concrete along a marked route with a jackhammer (sometimes a skid-steer hammer) to run new underground conduit, set a pull box, or drive a ground rod; traffic control, weather, unknown buried utilities, rubble hauled off.

Small keyhole/access breakout in pavement or sidewalk directly over a buried duct, conduit, or handhole to reach and repair existing underground electrical equipment; opening is limited in size, work includes exposing the asset without damaging it and backfilling/patching afterward.

Vertical and overhead concrete work at a site taken as found: breaking a penetration through a concrete wall, foundation, or slab edge for a service entrance or conduit sleeve, or chipping concrete encasement off a duct bank in an open trench, using a handheld chipping/air hammer in awkward positions.

sources.system: Normet Xrock Autobreaker (autonomous module for Xrock breaker booms)
sources.title: Normet Xrock launches fully autonomous underground rock breaker - International Mining
sources.claim: Normet Xrock's Autobreaker autonomously perceives a rock pile, identifies oversize material, plans strike positions and breaks it with a hydraulic hammer on a fixed breaker boom at a mine grizzly, with people excluded from the area and an operator supervising remotely; commercially available.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous secondary breaking of oversize rock with a hydraulic hammer. It uses the same tool class as an airhammer/breaker on material at least as hard as structural concrete, and autonomously selects and executes strike sequences on an unfixtured mass. It substantiates only the purpose-built-station case (E1 counterfactual: the concrete brought to a fixed, fenced hammer installation), not in-situ breaking of a building floor, wall, or pavement.

sources.title: Normet Xrock Launches the World's First Autonomous Rock-Breaking System, Xrock Autobreaker
sources.claim: Corroboration that the autonomous rock-breaking system is a released commercial product rather than a concept, sold for grizzly breaker-boom installations.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the preceding item (hydraulic-hammer breaking of hard material at a fixed station); cited to establish product maturity.

sources.title: Transforming roadworks with our all-electric excavation robot | SGN
sources.claim: The Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System (RRES), a robot-arm platform on an electric tracked base, autonomously cuts the road/pavement surface and performs vacuum excavation at utility worksites in the public roadway during SGN network trials in the UK.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: keyhole access excavation to reach a buried utility. The concrete/asphalt surface removal and soil excavation produce the same accepted output as a helper breaking out pavement over a buried duct so equipment can be reached and repaired, in the same public-street setting.

sources.title: Robotic Roadworks – ULC Technologies
sources.claim: RRES uses a custom concrete-cutting chainsaw end effector to make flexibly shaped cuts in road surface materials, drills a pilot hole to lift out the cut core, vacuum-excavates through the keyhole, and reinstates the core; the developer describes the process as end-to-end autonomous excavation including concrete ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic removal of a pavement/concrete section to gain below-ground access for utility installation and repair; comparable material (concrete road surface), comparable opening size to a keyhole breakout, same unstructured street environment.

sources.title: Husqvarna launches new remote-control demolition robots (Video) | Equipment World
sources.claim: The demolition machines that actually break concrete on jobsites (Husqvarna DXR, Brokk) are remote-controlled: an operator drives the boom and hammer continuously from a handheld console, so concrete breaking on site is teleoperated rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same task (breaking concrete with a hydraulic hammer on jobsites), cited to show the mode of control is continuous teleoperation, which cannot support a positive judgment at E2 or E3.

sources.title: Hilti Releases All New Features for the Hilti Jaibot - Hilti Corporation
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a semi-autonomous mobile robot deployed commercially on construction sites that autonomously drills anchor holes in concrete ceilings and walls from BIM data, showing that jobsite concrete work autonomy today is limited to drilled holes, not removal of concrete volume.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous drilling into concrete on construction sites for MEP installation. It does not transfer to breaking up concrete: the Jaibot only produces small-diameter anchor holes and cannot demolish, trench, or remove a section of slab or wall; cited to bound the E3 judgment rather than support it.

tasks.label: Operate heavy equipment, such as backhoes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-ground trenching at a large greenfield/industrial site (solar farm, warehouse pad, campus expansion): helper runs a backhoe or mini-excavator to cut long conduit/duct-bank trenches to plan depth and grade, piling spoil alongside, in a surveyed area away from existing structures.

Excavation in congested developed areas: trenching across an occupied parking lot, sidewalk, street cut, or beside an existing building; known and unknown live buried utilities, potholing and hand-dig exposure, pavement breaking, small pull-box or pole-base pits, traffic and pedestrians nearby.

Backfilling and compacting after conduit/duct bank is laid and inspected: pushing spoil back in lifts with the backhoe or skid steer, running a plate compactor or roller, spreading remaining spoil, rough grading and site cleanup.

Moving standard palletized and boxed material around a laid-out site with a rough-terrain forklift, telehandler or skid steer: pallets of fittings, boxes, strut, staged along established haul routes from laydown yard to work areas.

Handling odd, heavy, non-palletized items: unloading a strapped flatbed of conduit bundles and 3,000-lb wire reels, carrying switchgear or transformer sections, setting reels at pull points and placing gear in tight interior or curbside locations.

Operating an aerial lift (scissor lift, articulating boom, or bucket) to raise the electrician and materials for overhead conduit, cable tray, and fixture work inside a building under construction or on a site, repositioning repeatedly as the work advances.

sources.system: Built Robotics Exosystem (retrofit autonomy kit for excavators)
sources.title: Built Robotics raises $64 million for robotic excavator Exosystem | Equipment World
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofit kit turns standard excavators into fully autonomous trenching machines that dig to an uploaded design (depth, grade) inside a geofenced area with nobody in the cab.

sources.system: Built Robotics Exosystem / RPD pile driver (used by Bechtel)
sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Moves Earth with Autonomous Excavators | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Autonomous Built Robotics excavators have been used by major contractors for trenching on live solar construction projects in Texas, and autonomous pile drivers on other projects.

sources.title: Exosystem | Robots in Construction
sources.claim: The Exosystem performs survey, excavation and grade checking with no operator in the ...; one remote Robotic Equipment Operator supervises several machines from a nearby trailer, i.e., limited intervention rather than continuous teleoperation.

sources.title: Robotic pile driver faster than manual versions, says US startup – pv magazine International
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 autonomously surveys, distributes, drives and inspects foundation piles at surveyed points on utility-scale solar construction sites, at roughly 300 piles/day with a two-person crew.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving foundation piles/posts at surveyed points. Same class of heavy machine, same open construction-site environment, and the same requirement to reach surveyed ground positions and work to tolerance, as when a helper augers or excavates discrete foundation points.

sources.system: RPD 35 robotic pile driver (Blattner three-year agreement)
sources.title: Building Safer, Smarter Solar Projects (Sumitomo Corporation of Americas, Visions)
sources.claim: The RPD 35 is in contracted field use with EPC contractor Blattner, with crews supervising the robots from a distance rather than operating the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (autonomous foundation/pile installation on open construction sites), cited here to establish real deployment rather than demonstration.

sources.title: Bluelight Machines brings affordable autonomy to construction | Equipment World
sources.claim: Bluelight Machines' Autopilot retrofit kit runs soil compactors and articulated haul trucks autonomously and is in use on dozens of contractor jobsites across the US.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous compaction and material hauling on earthmoving jobsites, which is the compaction/spoil-hauling portion of trench backfill work; same machines a helper would run, same site conditions.

sources.system: Bluelight Machines Autopilot on Cat GC rollers
sources.title: Bluelight Machines Expands Autonomy Platform to Volvo G-Series ADTs, Caterpillar GC Rollers : CEG
sources.claim: Bluelight-equipped Caterpillar GC rollers are operating on jobsites in several US states, and the platform has been extended to Volvo articulated haulers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous compaction on active earthmoving sites, i.e., the compaction step of trench backfill.

sources.title: Real-X excavator marks major step towards autonomous construction - Materials Handling World News
sources.claim: Develon's Real-X crawler excavator was shown carrying out trench excavation, earthworks and ..., but as an exhibition/demonstration machine rather than a fielded product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous bulk earthmoving and truck loading, i.e., moving spoil back into and away from a trench; same machine class and material as backfilling, but shown only in a prepared demonstration area.

sources.system: Third Wave Automation TWA Reach / Armada shared-autonomy lift trucks
sources.title: THIRD WAVE AUTOMATION ANNOUNCES TECHNOLOGY PARTNERSHIP WITH THE RAYMOND CORPORATION
sources.claim: Third Wave Automation's autonomous lift trucks run pallet workflows in warehouses with a remote operator supervising up to ten vehicles, and are being scaled through Raymond's lift-truck line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: powered lift-truck material handling. Same machine type and load class (pallets/unit loads) a helper moves with a rough-terrain forklift, demonstrated inside a structured facility.

sources.system: Third Wave Automation autonomous forklifts at Holman Logistics, Spokane
sources.title: Holman Logistics announces autonomous forklift initiative with Third Wave Automation - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Autonomous forklifts from Third Wave were deployed in a Holman Logistics warehouse to handle full-pallet inbound movements, racking and picking to outbound dock positions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: full-pallet lift-truck movement in a structured facility, matching the palletized share of a helper's jobsite material handling.

sources.system: Moog Construction autonomous compact track loader
sources.title: Moog Construction track loader automates solar panel delivery on site
sources.claim: Moog Construction demonstrated an autonomous ... delivering solar panels around a US utility-scale solar site; ENR reports autonomous Moog skid steers were used for just-in-time panel delivery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous jobsite material delivery with a compact track loader, the same machine helpers use to move material, but shown for one uniform load type in a pilot.

tasks.label: Operate cutting torches and welding equipment, while working with conduit and metal components to construct devices associated with electrical functions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cutting stock steel to length/shape for electrical supports: burning strut, all-thread, angle iron, channel and plate with an oxy-acetylene or plasma torch (or band/chop saw) at a job-site laydown area or contractor cut station, working from marks and a cut list from the journeyman; rusty mill stock, dust, weather, variable lighting.

Bench fabrication in a contractor prefab/fab shop or on-site fab bench: tack and MIG/stick welding cut pieces into conduit racks, trapeze hangers, pipe stands, equipment stands, gusseted brackets and modified pull-box/enclosure parts; parts clamped in a vise or on a welding table, one-off or small batches to a sketch or BIM spool drawing, then ground and painted.

Field welding attachments at an active commercial construction site: burning and welding conduit support brackets, strut clips, embed plates and sleeves onto already-erected structural steel, deck angle or embeds, frequently overhead from a scissor lift or ladder, in awkward positions under hot-work permit with fire watch.

Industrial plant retrofit/maintenance: torch-cutting existing conduit, cable-tray hangers and rusted supports in place and welding replacement supports in a live operating facility, in tight pipe racks, elevated platforms or confined spaces, with LOTO, spark containment and hot-work permitting.

Grounding and bonding: exothermic (Cadweld) connections of grounding conductors to driven ground rods, rebar, ground rings and building steel in open trenches, ductbank excavations and electrical rooms; setting molds, packing powder, igniting, then inspecting and cleaning the connection.

sources.system: Path Robotics AW-3 (Obsidian AI welding cell)
sources.title: Intelligent Welding Cells | Path Robotics
sources.claim: Path Robotics' AW-3 intelligent welding cell uses AI vision to scan each part, find seams and plan weld paths without programming, targeting one-off and high-mix steel weldments in fabrication shops.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical act as the helper's bench fabrication: arc welding cut steel members and plate into fabricated assemblies, at comparable size, joint type and precision.

sources.system: Path Robotics welding cell at AMSi Inc.
sources.title: Path Robotics | Resources / Blog
sources.claim: A Path Robotics cell passed factory acceptance for AMSi, a builder of E-houses, switchgear and portable substations, welding heavy electrical equipment weldments by scanning seams and planning in real time.
sources.transferJustification: The welded products are electrical enclosures and substation structures - the same class of metal 'devices associated with electrical functions' a helper fabricates from conduit, strut and plate.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic weld cells (class; incl. Path Robotics, ABAGY)
sources.title: Uncovering the potential of autonomous robotic welding - The Fabricator
sources.claim: Trade press confirms autonomous robotic weld cells - robots that look at the part and then weld, without precisely fixtured, pre-programmed setups - are now a commercially available class of equipment in metal fabrication.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that high-mix, one-off steel weldments - the helper's fabrication work - are handled by commercial autonomous cells, not only by high-volume fixtured production lines.

sources.title: BeamMaster - Robotic Welding - Structural Steel
sources.claim: AGT Robotics' BeamMaster robotically welds fittings, plates and clips onto structural steel beams in fabrication shops, adapting to varied beam types without programming expertise and repositioning welds automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Welding a small steel bracket or clip to a structural member is the same joint, material and precision class as welding a conduit support bracket to building steel, when the member is presented to the machine.

sources.title: CNC Angle Line | Anglemaster-863 | Peddinghaus
sources.claim: Peddinghaus CNC angle lines cut angle and flat bar to length, punch and mark automatically with automated loading, producing finished cut parts continuously from mill stock.
sources.transferJustification: Cutting angle, flat bar and strut stock to length with marked hole layout is exactly the helper's cut-list work; the machine delivers the same finished pieces to tighter tolerance.

sources.system: HGG RPC 1200 Mk3 / APC robotic plasma coping
sources.title: RPC 1200 Mk3 Plasma Cutting Machine | HGG Group
sources.claim: HGG's robotic plasma coping machines position a plasma torch with an industrial robot to cut and bevel steel profiles (beams, channel, angle, tube) automatically from CAD data.
sources.transferJustification: Thermal (plasma/oxy-fuel) torch cutting of structural profiles to length and shape is the same operation the helper performs with a hand torch, at higher accuracy.

sources.title: Over 1 Million Welds Achieved with Cobot Welding | AWS Welding Digest
sources.claim: A Vectis/Universal Robots cobot welding system has run over one million production MIG welds on heavy-duty steel brackets at Centerline Brackets, letting two welders plus the cobot match the previous output of eight welders.
sources.transferJustification: Fillet welding flat-bar steel brackets on a fixtured welding table is the same operation, material and weld quality standard as a helper fabricating conduit-support brackets at a bench.

sources.title: Shimizu Begins Collaborating People and Autonomous Robots at Construction Site, Toranomon-Azabudai Project
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Welder autonomously welds thick steel column butt joints at an actual high-rise construction site using laser shape recognition and its own torches, but is set onto one prepared column joint and performs only that groove-weld operation.
sources.transferJustification: Closest field-welding analogue; cited to bound field capability - it welds a pre-set, fixtured column joint and neither fetches, fits nor holds small brackets at arbitrary overhead locations.

sources.developer: Inrotech / Lincoln Electric (deployed at Seaspan Vancouver Shipyards)
sources.title: Welding smarter: How robotic technology is advancing shipbuilding at Seaspan
sources.claim: Inrotech's Crawler is a mobile welding robot hand-placed on the workpiece in a shipyard block assembly shop; it 3D-scans the joint and welds long groove seams, i.e. in-situ welding inside a human facility but restricted to prepared continuous seams.
sources.transferJustification: Bounds in-facility mobile welding: the robot is placed on a long prepared seam by workers and does not locate, fit or hold small conduit-support brackets, nor perform torch cutting.

roles.title: Helpers--Painters, Paperhangers, Plasterers, and Stucco Masons
roles.description: Help painters, paperhangers, plasterers, or stucco masons by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

tasks.label: Clean work areas and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-day cleaning of painting tools and equipment: washing out brushes, roller covers, frames, trays and 5-gallon buckets; flushing an airless or HVLP sprayer with water or solvent and cleaning the gun, tip, screens and filters; wiping and racking tools. Done at a job-site utility sink, an outdoor hose bib, or back at the contractor's shop, with solvent/waste-water rules to follow.

End-of-day / end-of-job work-area cleanup on an occupied residential interior repaint: pulling masking tape, paper and plastic off trim and fixtures, folding and shaking out drop cloths, scraping paint spatter off floors, glass and hardware, sweeping and shop-vaccing sanding dust, gathering rags, cans and scrap, and hauling debris to the truck. Furniture, flooring and homeowner belongings are present and must not be damaged.

Final floor cleaning of a large commercial/institutional interior after painting is finished and ladders, staging and materials have been removed: sweeping, vacuuming, dust-mopping and damp-mopping/scrubbing wide runs of hard floor in school corridors, office suites, retail sales floors or a hospital wing, clearing dust film and grit before the space is turned back over. Access is controlled by the facility or the general contractor.

Cleaning plastering/stucco equipment: washing out the mortar mixer drum and paddles before the mud sets, rinsing hoppers, pumps and hoses, scraping and washing hawks, trowels, darbies and mud pans, and cleaning buckets. Done with a hose at the mixing station on site or at the shop's washout area.

Exterior job-site cleanup on a stucco/plaster or exterior painting job: shoveling and bagging dropped mortar and sand, hosing and scrubbing splatter off walkways, driveways, windows and scaffold planks, sweeping around the mixing station, picking up scrap lath, empty bags and banding, and loading waste. Uneven ground, landscaping, weather and vehicles in the way.

sources.title: Avidbots Designs Fully Autonomous Cleaning Robots for Airports and Hospitals (Onshape case study)
sources.claim: Avidbots Neo autonomous floor-scrubbing robots clean large hard-floor areas without an operator and are in service across airports, malls, hospitals, factories, schools and warehouses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine facility floor care. The painter helper's final floor pass is the same physical act on the same surfaces - removing dust and light debris from large hard floors in a facility - so performance carries over to the floor-cleaning instance.

sources.title: Brain Corp: Sam's Club Deploying Autonomous Robots
sources.claim: Autonomous floor scrubbers built by Tennant and running Brain Corp autonomy are deployed at fleet scale in US retail facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial floor cleaning. Same surfaces, same soil (dust, grit, scuff marks) and same acceptance standard as the helper's final floor clean in a controlled facility.

sources.system: POSCO E&C / Clobot autonomous cleaning robot
sources.title: POSCO E&C deploys autonomous robots for post-construction cleanups - The Korea Times
sources.claim: POSCO E&C is running AI-powered autonomous cleaning robots (developed with Clobot) to clean community spaces and underground parking of an apartment redevelopment project in the pre-handover, post-construction phase, unsupervised and around the clock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: final cleaning of a building at the end of construction - the same job phase and the same floors a painter helper cleans after finishing work, on a site whose access and layout the builder controls.

sources.title: JFE Steel Develops Efficient, Autonomous Cleaning Robot to Reduce Human Labor and Improve Safety and Productivity
sources.claim: JFE Steel's GAZMASTAR-S autonomously clears clumps, dust, powder and other ... from road surfaces and is in operation performing heavy-duty cleaning at its West Japan Works.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk debris and dust clearing in an industrial work area. Comparable material (dropped clumps, powder, grit) and comparable precision demand to sweeping out a work area, inside premises the operator controls.

sources.system: FANUC Paint Mate parts washing system (Prime Test Automation)
sources.title: Robotic Cutting, Deburring, Polishing, Buffing & More | FANUC America
sources.claim: A production parts-washing cell uses a FANUC Paint Mate ... soiled parts inside a purpose-built enclosure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing soiled hardware presented to a machine inside a fenced enclosure. Cleaning painting and plastering tools is the same act - flushing and spraying soiled items and repositioning them until clean - at equal or lower precision.

sources.title: Herkules Deluxe Gun Washer - G200 | Spray Gun Cleaners
sources.claim: Commercial automatic gun washers clean paint spray guns and cups on an unattended timed cycle once the equipment is loaded into the cabinet.
sources.transferJustification: This is the equipment-cleaning half of the task itself: paint spray guns, cups and internal passages cleaned of wet paint by machine, to the standard a paint shop accepts before the next job.

sources.system: Floor mortar cleaning robot / building cleaning robot
sources.title: Construction Cleaning Robots: Revolutionizing Construction Site Cleaning - ProBuild Robotics
sources.claim: A construction floor mortar cleaning robot sold for job-site use is described as cleaning fallen mortar from building floors using self-built maps, path planning and obstacle avoidance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing dropped plaster/mortar from the floors of a building under construction - the same material and the same clean-up-after-the-trade purpose as the helper's work-area cleaning, on floors of a builder-controlled site.

tasks.label: Supply or hold tools and materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential repaint / plaster patch at a private, often furnished and occupied home: helper unloads the van, carries 5-gallon pails, ladders, drop cloths and a sprayer through halls and up stairs, opens/stirs and pours paint, keeps trays and cut buckets filled, and hands brushes, rollers, tape, caulk and rags up to the painter on the ladder while steadying the ladder and holding a work light.

Active commercial or multifamily construction site during drywall finishing and painting: helper hauls buckets of joint compound, boxes of board/mesh/tape, sanding poles and hoses across a cluttered floor and up several levels, mixes and refills mud for the finishers, drags and holds spray hoses and lights, and passes tools up to workers on stilts, scaffolds and scissor lifts.

Exterior stucco/plaster jobsite: helper tends the mixer, shuttles mortar in wheelbarrows/hods to the scaffold, loads hawks and the pump hopper, carries 80-lb bags and bundles of lath, hands trowels, darbies and corner bead up the scaffold, and holds lath, bead and trim in place while the mason fastens it, in wind, heat and changing site layout.

Repaint or wallcovering work inside an occupied institution (hospital wing, hotel corridor, school, office tower): helper stages materials from a locked supply room, ferries pails, ladders and drop cloths through corridors around staff and the public, keeps the painter/paperhanger stocked, and holds pasted wallcovering strips, trim pieces or a light while the tradesperson positions and finishes them.

Shop or plant finishing operation (industrial coating shop, cabinet/furniture finishing line): helper draws stock from the storeroom and keeps the spray booths supplied — moving cases and pails of coating, abrasives, masking paper and tape on carts to booth-side, returning empties and waste to a fixed collection point on a repeating schedule inside a controlled-access facility.

sources.system: Dürr EcoRP / SCARA opener (handling) robots in Ecopaint painting stations
sources.title: Ecopaint Robot PAINTING STATIONS (Dürr brochure)
sources.claim: In automotive paint booths, dedicated handling robots grip and hold vehicle hoods, doors and trunk lids open in position for the whole duration of the automated painting operation — i.e., a machine holds the material for the painting operation in a purpose-built, fixtured cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: holding a workpiece/part steady for a painter. The helper's 'hold materials' duty is the same act — gripping and maintaining an item in position throughout a coating operation — performed here on comparable-size, comparable-weight sheet items in a paint booth, unattended in production.

sources.title: Digit's Next Steps | Agility
sources.claim: A humanoid robot has worked full-time for over a year at a GXO fulfillment site, autonomously unloading totes of product delivered by mobile robots at its station and placing them onto a ... for downstream stations — routine material supply inside a human work facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: supplying standardized material containers between a delivery point and a work station. Transfers to the 'supply materials' duty for containerized goods of similar weight, but only where items are presented at a fixed station.

sources.title: Amazon debuts first fully autonomous mobile robot in supply chain
sources.claim: Amazon's Proteus autonomously moves wheeled carts of goods (up to ~400 kg) through fulfillment centers, operating outside restricted areas and around employees; it has been rolled out across roughly 25 U.S. fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transporting heavy loaded carts of materials to a point of use in a facility shared with people — the transport half of 'supply materials' at comparable weights, in a structured human work facility.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Diligent's Moxi mobile manipulator autonomously fetches and delivers supplies, medications and lab specimens to clinical staff in hospitals, including autonomous elevator rides; deployed in more than 25 ... with over one million deliveries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fetching and delivering supplies to human workers inside a structured facility. It covers packaged, drawer-sized supplies on mapped routes; it does not carry ladders, open pails, or hand tools on demand.

sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously unloads cases from trailers and containers into warehouse handling systems at commercial rates, deployed at DHL sites in three countries with 1,000+ more units contracted.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk handling of cased materials (comparable weights to paint cases) between a delivery vehicle and the facility's handling system — the loading/unloading half of material supply inside a controlled facility.

sources.title: US: BMW deploys Figure 03 humanoid at smart factory for logistics
sources.claim: BMW has begun using Figure's humanoid at Plant Spartanburg for logistics: picking parts from unsorted containers and sequencing them into trolleys that are then taken to assembly stations, after a prior ten-month body-shop deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: kitting/sequencing materials so they arrive at a human work station — the 'supply materials' duty for factory parts, in a fixed-layout plant with presented containers.

sources.title: Shimizu Begins Collaborating People and Autonomous Robots at Construction Site, Toranomon-Azabudai Project
sources.claim: On the Toranomon-Azabudai high-rise project, Shimizu's Robo-Carrier system autonomously picked up palletized materials, loaded them into a freight elevator and transported them to designated locations on the working floor of an active construction site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: jobsite material logistics. It substantiates only palletized point-to-point transport (largely outside working hours), not fetching individual items, handing tools to a tradesperson, or holding materials.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7 autonomously navigates active construction sites and applies plaster, drywall compound and paint, covering over a million square feet and used by a major U.S. specialty contractor.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the current limit of jobsite autonomy in this trade: the robot performs the finishing itself from a lift, but does not fetch, carry, hand or hold tools and materials for a tradesperson, so it is not used to support a positive judgment.

sources.title: KEWAZO LIFTBOT - Edison Awards
sources.claim: Kewazo's LIFTBOT is a battery-powered robotic hoist that climbs scaffolding to move scaffold parts and other materials vertically on construction sites and industrial plants (ExxonMobil, BASF and others); the company describes it as remote-controlled, with workers loading and unloading it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: supplying materials to workers at height on scaffolds. Autonomy is unclear (vendor materials call it remote-controlled) and humans still load, unload and place items, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid
sources.claim: 1X's NEO home humanoid, the leading attempt at a general household helper, relies on remote human operators for most tasks rather than autonomous execution.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general fetch-and-carry assistance in unstructured interiors. It shows that fetching/holding varied objects in homes is currently teleoperated, supporting the negative judgment at E3.

tasks.label: Apply protective coverings, such as masking tape, to articles or areas that could be damaged or stained by work processes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied private home, interior repaint: helper masks door and window trim, baseboards, hinges, outlet and switch plates with tape, spreads canvas drop cloths over finished floors and carpet, and tapes plastic over furniture, appliances and light fixtures, working around the homeowner's possessions and varied room layouts before the painter sprays or rolls.

Occupied institutional or commercial building (office suite, school, hotel corridor, retail store, hospital wing) maintained by a facility owner: helper tapes off door frames, casework, signage, sprinklers, thermostats and fixtures, lays floor protection paper/runners and tapes edges, and hangs poly barriers at entrances before repainting during off-hours.

New-construction or gut-renovation interior, unfinished job site: helper masks installed window units, door hardware, HVAC diffusers and electrical boxes, tapes plastic sheeting over floors and openings, and builds temporary containment before spray painting or plastering, amid scaffolds, stacked materials and other trades.

Exterior of a house or small commercial building: helper masks window glass and frames, tapes off gutters, light fixtures, meters and hose bibs, and covers shrubs, walkways, driveways and adjacent siding with plastic and drop cloths, working from ladders in wind and sun before spraying.

Contractor's shop or spray booth: helper masks discrete articles brought to the booth (cabinet doors, millwork, metal railings, machine parts) with tape, paper, film and plugs on benches or racks before finish coating, then removes masking after cure.

sources.system: Active Taping Kit (FerRobotics ACT end-effector on six-axis robot, integrated by Aerobotix)
sources.title: New End-Effector Applies Masking Tape | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Aerobotix and FerRobotics' Active Taping Kit lets a six-axis industrial robot apply masking tape automatically and precisely to aircraft assemblies and other ... parts, with force-controlled compliance, tested in Aerobotix's robotic process laboratory (paint/cure/sand/inspect cells) and on aircraft.

sources.system: FANUC robots with end-of-arm tape applicators (TPC Automation integration)
sources.title: Robotic Tape Application | FANUC Authorized System Integrator
sources.claim: A FANUC authorized integrator sells production robotic tape-application cells whose common automotive application is masking for painting: applying protective tape with precision to parts presented in the cell before paint shop processes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (industrial masking/taping of parts before coating) transfers to shop masking of articles: same material (masking tape), same purpose (protecting surfaces from coating), same fixtured presentation of the workpiece in a cell.

sources.title: FAQ - Les Companions
sources.claim: PACO, a commercially sold/rented autonomous interior painting robot deployed on new-build and renovation sites including schools, offices and hospitals, still depends on humans to mask the unpainted areas; the robot merely overlaps the tape line.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed in-building painting robot; it shows that masking and protective covering in occupied buildings and construction interiors remains a manual prerequisite, i.e. no cited system performs this task there.

sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction's Dirty Work Is Going Robotic - Architect Magazine
sources.claim: Okibo's fully autonomous construction robot paints, applies plaster and finishes ... on interior job sites using AI 3D scanning; its capability set covers coating application, not applying masking tape or protective coverings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous interior painting/plastering on construction sites) marks the state of the art in unstructured building interiors; no masking or protective-covering capability is claimed, supporting the negative judgment for site masking.

tasks.label: Smooth surfaces of articles to be painted, using sanding and buffing tools and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New construction or gut-remodel interior: pole-sanding / vacuum-sanding taped and mudded drywall or plaster over full walls and ceilings of ordinary and large open rooms (commercial, institutional, multifamily, single-family), building empty of furnishings, contractor-controlled, to Level 4/5 paint-ready smoothness.

New construction interior, tight and irregular work: sanding closets, stairwells, small bathrooms, soffits, inside corners, areas behind ducts and fixtures, plus hand-sanding installed wood trim, casings, jambs and doors on site before priming.

Repaint prep in occupied private homes: feather-sanding spackled patches, scuff-sanding glossy trim, doors, cabinets and window sash, sanding old peeling paint, working around furniture, floors and occupants with block/orbital sanders and sponges.

Repaint prep in institution-controlled buildings (schools, hospitals, offices, hotels, apartment turnovers): sanding patched corridor and room walls, door frames, doors, handrails and metal fixtures, often off-hours around furnishings and occupants.

Exterior prep before painting: sanding/scraping and feathering wood siding, fascia, trim, stucco patches and metal railings from ladders, planks or scaffold, in variable weather and lighting on a residential or commercial site.

Shop/bench work: sanding and buffing removable articles (door slabs, cabinet doors, shutters, trim stock, metal railings, furniture pieces) at the contractor's shop or a finishing shop before spraying.

sources.title: Drywall finishing robot saves time, prevents injuries | Construction Dive
sources.claim: Canvas drywall finishing robots taped, sprayed and sanded drywall surfaces to a Level 5 finish ... occupied-by-trades commercial construction projects for Webcor, and have been used at SFO's Harvey Milk Terminal, UCSF and Chase Center Towers.

sources.title: More Contractors See Benefits of Drywall Finishing Robot | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Trade press reports the Canvas machine finishes and sands large sections of drywall semi-autonomously on jobsites, with workers handling taping and complex geometries.

sources.title: Solution | Autonomous Drywall Finishing Robotic System | CPWR Construction Solutions
sources.claim: CPWR's construction-solutions database classifies the Canvas system as an autonomous drywall finishing robot that automates the sanding portion of drywall finishing, with a vacuum sanding system controlling silica dust.

sources.title: Canvas' new compact drywall finishing robot fits into smaller construction spaces - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Canvas released a compact model sized to fit smaller construction spaces such as multifamily and ... projects; it carries an interchangeable sanding head with 99.9% dust capture, but is still a 1,200 lb rolling platform with a 12-ft finishing height.

sources.title: Okibo and PCI team up on Netflix House project in Pennsylvania - Engineering.com
sources.claim: Performance Contracting Inc. used Okibo's drywall and painting robots for surface sanding on the Netflix House construction project in King of Prussia, ..., reporting over 300% higher sanding production; the robots run nearly autonomously with an operator, guided by onboard 3D scanning.

sources.title: Okibo launches autonomous, AI-guided painting and drywall finishing EG7+ robot - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Okibo launched the EG7+ in the US for sanding, painting and Level 4/5 drywall finishing up to 24 ft, with customers reporting large productivity gains on sanding jobs while meeting quality standards; it needs no site preparation, markers, BIM or Wi-Fi.

sources.system: Dynabrade Automated Cabinet Door Sanding Cell with FerRobotics Active Contact Flange Kit
sources.title: Dynabrade Automated Cabinet Door Sanding Cell - FerRobotics
sources.claim: A commercially offered automated cell sands complete cabinet/shaker doors of any wood type, including corners, edges, rails and ..., using force-controlled random-orbital tools with no programming required.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sanding of wooden cabinet/shaker doors to a finish-ready surface. Same articles (doors, panels, trim stock), same abrasive tools and same paint-ready smoothness standard as a painter's helper sanding removable articles in a shop.

sources.title: The World's First Dual-Arm Autonomous Robotic Sanding Cell (PR Newswire)
sources.claim: BetterWay Products deployed GrayMatter Robotics' dual-arm autonomous sanding cell on its shop floor; the system scans each part and generates ... sanding program for high-mix composite parts, yielding a 4x throughput increase.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous abrasive sanding of large composite parts to a paint-ready finish in a manufacturing cell. Comparable objects (large panels/bodies), comparable surface-finish precision, and it substantiates that fixtured articles can be sanded autonomously at production quality.

tasks.label: Erect scaffolding.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interior residential/light-remodel work: helper carries a rolling 'baker's' or aluminum tower scaffold in pieces through doorways of an occupied home, assembles frames, cross braces, deck and guardrails on a finished floor around furniture, levels it with casters/outriggers, locks wheels, and repositions it repeatedly as the painter/plasterer works a ceiling or stairwell.

Exterior residential painting or stucco patch: helper sets mud sills/base plates on uneven soil or landscaping, erects one to two lifts of frame or system scaffold along a house wall (or sets pump-jack/ladder-jack poles and planks), plumbs and levels it, planks the deck, adds guardrails and wall ties, in weather and around shrubs, hose bibs, AC units.

Interior of a commercial/institutional building under construction: helper erects and moves frame or system scaffold bays for drywall finishing, plastering or spray work, working amid other trades, debris and floor penetrations, with layout changing day to day; components are staged on the floor and hauled by hand.

Large multi-lift exterior scaffold for stucco/EIFS or repaint on a multistory commercial building: crew erects 3+ lifts of frame or system scaffold from grade with screw jacks, base plates, planking, guardrails, toeboards, wall ties, stair tower and debris netting, to an engineered/OSHA-inspected standard.

Maintenance painting inside an occupied institution the owner controls (school gym, hospital corridor, hotel atrium, airport concourse): helper erects a mobile tower scaffold on a level finished floor inside a barricaded work zone, to a standard layout, coordinating with facility staff and moving it between work areas.

sources.title: Robotics firm Kewazo gets a $10M lift | Construction Dive
sources.claim: The only scaffolding robot in commercial site use, Kewazo LIFTBOT, is a robotic hoist that clamps to erected scaffold and carries components to height; the scaffold itself is still assembled by scaffolders.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about scaffolding work: it establishes that the deployed state of the art on real sites is autonomous material transport for scaffold erection, not autonomous assembly, so it cannot substantiate completion of the erection task at E2 or E3.

sources.title: KEWAZO LIFTBOT - Edison Awards
sources.claim: LIFTBOT autonomously transports scaffolding parts vertically on industrial construction and maintenance sites, reducing but not eliminating the human erection crew.
sources.transferJustification: Same task domain (scaffold erection). Confirms the commercial system automates hauling of components only; workers still connect frames, braces, decks and guardrails.

sources.title: GITAI tests robotic construction of lunar comms tower in desert simulation exercise
sources.claim: A team of GITAI robots autonomously assembled a 5-metre modular tower from staged structural members, attached hardware at its apex, and then disassembled it, in a prepared desert analog site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous erection of a vertical modular tower from standardized members with robot-compatible connectors, from a staged kit of parts in a purpose-arranged setting. This is the closest demonstrated analogue to building a scaffold tower when components are presented as an E1 cell would present them; it does not transfer to found sites because parts, interfaces and layout were engineered for the robots.

sources.system: Randek ZeroLabor robotic framing system (FrameTec plant)
sources.title: FrameTec builds scalable framing model with Randek automation | Built Offsite
sources.claim: Robotic framing cells assemble structural timber/steel frame assemblies from raw stock presented in fixtured lines, running as commercial production systems in offsite factories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly of load-bearing structural frames from standard members inside a fenced, fixtured cell. Member weights (2-30 kg), positioning tolerances and repetitive modular joining are comparable to assembling scaffold bays, supporting the E1 counterfactual in which scaffold components arrive fixtured and presented.

sources.system: House of Design automated truss / floor truss systems
sources.title: Floor Truss Systems - House of Design Robotics
sources.claim: Purpose-built robotic cells commercially build floor and roof trusses (multi-metre structural frames) from presented lumber with automated plating and assembly sequencing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fixtured robotic assembly of large modular structural frames. Supports the E1 claim that, with components fixtured and presented, robots assemble scaffold-scale frame structures; it says nothing about erection in found settings.

sources.title: VIDEO: NASA's Valkyrie Robot Can Erect Scaffolding | ScaffMag.com
sources.claim: A humanoid erecting scaffolding has been shown only as a slow, semi-autonomous demonstration, not as reliable work.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task, but semi-autonomous and far below worker speed and reliability, so it cannot support a positive judgment at any tier.

sources.title: Hadrian X bricklaying robot builds first homes in demo program - The Robot Report
sources.claim: FBR's Hadrian X autonomously places heavy standardized blocks to build house walls outdoors on real sites, showing outdoor autonomous placement of building elements but not scaffold assembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous placement of heavy standardized elements at a found building site. It does not transfer to scaffold erection - the machine lays adhesive-bonded blocks from a boom and cannot set base jacks, pin frames and braces, lay planks, fit guardrails or tie into a wall - so it does not substantiate E3 or E2 for this task.

tasks.label: Perform support duties to assist painters, paperhangers, plasterers, or masons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Set up and support an interior repaint in an occupied home or office: move and cover furniture, spread drop cloths, mask trim, windows, floors, outlets and fixtures with tape and plastic, set ladders, open/stir/pour paint, keep the painter's cut buckets and roller trays filled and hand up brushes and rollers on request.

Tend a plasterer or stucco mason: load and run the mixer, mix batches of plaster/stucco/mortar to the right consistency, fill buckets/hawks/hods, carry material up ladders and scaffolds, keep a continuous supply at the work face, and hose out the mixer and tools between batches.

Fetch, carry and stage materials and tools on a commercial construction or renovation site: unload the truck, move 5-gallon pails, compound boxes, ladders, planks, baker scaffolds, hoses, cords and work lights to the right rooms and floors, and hand tools and material up to workers on stilts or staging.

End-of-day cleanup on a residential or commercial job: clean brushes, rollers, buckets, spray guns, hoses and pumps; pull and dispose of masking tape and plastic; scrape spatter; sweep/vacuum debris and dust; bag and haul waste; restore furniture and leave the area presentable to the client.

Assist a paperhanger: measure, cut and match strips, run them through paste or a pasting machine, book them, hand the limp strip up to the hanger, hold and steady the bottom while it is positioned, wipe seams and squeeze-out, and keep the pasting table clean.

Support finishing work inside an industrial shop or prefab plant (fab shop, rail/marine/aerospace or cabinet finishing): mask parts before coating, stage and hang parts for the painter, blast or sand surfaces for prep, mix and supply coating, and clean guns and the booth.

sources.system: Active Taping Kit (ATK) on Aerobotix robotic coating cells
sources.title: Aerobotix, FerRobotics Launch Robotic Tool for Applying Masking Tape
sources.claim: Aerobotix and FerRobotics' Active Taping Kit is a robot end-effector that applies masking tape to aerospace parts of varying shape in robotic coating cells, automating the masking prep step normally done by hand before painting.
sources.transferJustification: Masking surfaces with tape before a painter sprays is a core helper support duty; the robot performs it on fixtured workpieces with comparable tape-line precision.

sources.system: Scan&Sand dual-arm autonomous robotic sanding cell
sources.title: The World's First Dual-Arm Autonomous Robotic Sanding Cell
sources.claim: BetterWay Products runs a dual-arm autonomous robotic sanding ... that scans a part and sands it, replacing manual surface prep in production.
sources.transferJustification: Sanding and surface prep ahead of coating is a helper duty; the cell does it autonomously on presented workpieces to production quality.

sources.system: Blastman B20 series blast cleaning robots
sources.title: BLASTMAN BLAST CLEANING ROBOTS IN DIFFERENT INDUSTRIES
sources.claim: Blastman gantry blasting robots perform abrasive blast cleaning of large workpieces inside blast chambers, running programs that automatically follow component contours with no human in the chamber.
sources.transferJustification: Blast cleaning is the industrial form of the helper's scraping and surface-prep work before coating, performed inside a purpose-built chamber.

sources.title: Autonomous Mobile Robots MiR (Universal Robots)
sources.claim: MiR autonomous mobile robots are deployed at scale in factories, autonomously transporting components and materials between production cells and stations.
