sources.system: Winton Machine RT23 rotary transfer tube forming system
sources.title: Automated Coil-Fed CNC Tube Cutting & Bending for HVACR OEMs - Winton Machine
sources.claim: Coil-fed CNC tube systems cut copper/aluminum tubing to length and form it with six-axis robotic transfer between stations for unattended operation.
sources.transferJustification: Measuring and cutting copper tube to length and moving it to assembly stations is the same physical operation on the same material as residential copper water-line work, done in a fixtured cell.

sources.title: UltraFlex demonstrates automated robotic induction brazing for copper to brass assemblies
sources.claim: Robotic arms perform automated induction brazing of copper and brass HVAC pipe assemblies, replacing manual torch brazing of copper joints.
sources.transferJustification: Joining copper pipe to fittings by heat (brazing/soldering) is the assembly step of residential copper piping; the cell does it on comparable copper parts in fixtured positions.

sources.title: Hilti's Overhead Drilling Robot Brings Further Automation to the Jobsite | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: The most capable pipe-related construction-site robot in commercial use drills overhead anchor holes for MEP hangers from BIM data; no cited site robot measures, cuts, threads, assembles pipe or lands it in hangers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (drilling hanger anchor holes on jobsites) shows the state of the art in field MEP robotics; it does not include pipe measuring, cutting, threading, assembly or placement, so it cannot substantiate completion at E2/E3.

sources.system: Tele-robotic pipe installation concepts (open-trench pipe laying)
sources.developer: academic research published in Automation in Construction
sources.title: Control schemes for tele-robotic pipe installation - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Robotic installation of buried pipe in open trenches has been pursued only as tele-robotic concepts, with handling and jointing of varied pipe types noted as not readily replaceable by remote devices.
sources.transferJustification: Directly addresses the trench pipelaying instance; only teleoperated concepts exist, supporting a negative judgment.

tasks.label: Assist pipe fitters in the layout, assembly, and installation of piping for air, ammonia, gas, and water systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/institutional new-construction rough-in: helper works with a fitter overhead on scissor lifts or scaffold, carries and hoists 2"-6" black steel, copper and CPVC lengths from the staging area, cuts pipe to length, preps ends, holds pipe in trapeze hangers while the fitter aligns and joins (grooved couplings, press, braze, weld), fetches fittings and tools. Active site with other trades, debris, changing layout.

Layout support on a commercial job: helper works with the fitter to transfer coordinated drawing/BIM dimensions to the deck and structure - pulling tape, holding the rod/laser target, snapping chalk lines, and marking hanger, sleeve and penetration locations for the pipe runs before installation begins.

Industrial process piping in an operating plant (ammonia refrigeration in a food plant, compressed air, gas headers): helper rigs and positions prefabbed spools, holds flanges and fit-ups for the fitter/welder, torques bolts, grinds and cleans joints, works in mechanical rooms and on elevated racks under permit conditions amid scaffolding and existing equipment.

Contractor's fabrication shop or on-site fab yard: helper loads pipe onto stands and the cut/bevel or threading machine, cuts and bevels lengths, deburrs and cleans, holds fittings for the fitter to tack, assembles spools and multi-trade racks on jigs, and stages finished assemblies for delivery.

Residential and light-commercial rough-in/service: helper assists in an occupied or under-construction house - crawl space, attic, joist bays - carrying materials, cutting and dry-fitting PVC DWV and PEX/copper water lines, applying primer/cement, holding pipe while the plumber joins and straps it, cleaning up.

Underground site utility work: helper assists a pipelayer laying gravity sewer, water main or gas line in an open trench - guiding pipe sections down from the excavator, seating bell-and-spigot joints, checking grade with laser/level, placing bedding, handling fusion/joining equipment.

sources.system: KRANENDONK Robotic Pipe Shop (Apollo bevel station + ZEROGAP + robotic welding)
sources.title: KRANENDONK strengthens collaboration with JGC through advanced Robotic Pipe Shop installation
sources.claim: KRANENDONK's Robotic Pipe Shop is a ... pipe-spool fabrication line (automated bevel prep of pipe ends, elbows and tees, upstream assembly/fit-up, robotic welding) driven directly from PCF model files with minimal operator input; installed with JGC Corporation for process piping spools.
sources.transferJustification: Same work content as the assembly half of this task - fitting up and joining pipe, elbows, tees and flanges into piping assemblies for process/air/gas/water service - but performed in a fixtured robotic cell rather than by a fitter-and-helper pair.

sources.system: Spool Welding Robot (SWR) with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2
sources.title: AI machine learning vision processing system automates pipe welding
sources.claim: Novarc's Spool Welding Robot with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2 performs pipe joint welding autonomously using real-time machine-vision seam tracking in pipe fabrication shops; more than 80 units were installed across North America, the UK, Germany, Saudi Arabia, Australia and ... by 2023.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the joining step of pipe assembly (the fitter-and-helper fit-up-and-weld operation) on the same carbon/stainless pipe sizes used in air, gas and water piping, but with the spool held in a powered positioner.

sources.system: Rotoweld 3.0 automated pipe spool welding cell
sources.title: Covering all the pipe fabrication bases with automated welding technology
sources.claim: Automated pipe-spool welding work cells are in production use in US/Canadian pipe fabrication shops: INfab's Rotoweld cell welds large-diameter spools loaded into the cell and replaces several manual welders' output.
sources.transferJustification: Demonstrates that pipe assembly work presented to a fixtured cell is completed at commercial quality and throughput, the E1 counterfactual for the assembly content of this task.

sources.title: Hilti Unveils BIM-Enabled Construction Jobsite Robot
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a commercially available semi-autonomous jobsite robot that takes BIM-coordinated hanger and sleeve points, marks them and drills the overhead anchor holes automatically on active construction sites; an operator repositions it by remote control between drilling zones and it references a robotic total station.
sources.transferJustification: Overhead marking and drilling of MEP hanger/sleeve points is the field-layout output a pipefitter's helper produces before pipe is hung; same building, same tolerances, same drawings.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Layout with Dusty Robotics | Turner Construction Company
sources.claim: Dusty Robotics' FieldPrinter is an autonomous layout ... used on active construction sites by general contractors such as Turner, printing the coordinated BIM model at full scale directly on the deck.

sources.title: Automated Layout for Mechanical | Dusty Robotics
sources.claim: Dusty's FieldPrint Platform is marketed and used for mechanical/piping trades specifically, printing coordinated model and shop-drawing intent on the deck so pipefitting crews no longer measure and shoot layout points by hand.

sources.title: Induction Brazing Robot - Dragon 15 | UltraFlex Power Technologies
sources.claim: UltraFlex's Dragon 15/20 induction brazing robot automatically brazes multiple copper/brass tube joints held in predefined positions in a fixtured assembly, sold to HVAC/refrigeration manufacturers to replace manual torch brazing.
sources.transferJustification: Brazing copper tube-and-fitting joints in a fixture is the joining operation used for copper water and refrigerant lines; the objects (copper tube, sweat fittings) and precision match residential/light-commercial piping assembly.

tasks.label: Requisition tools and equipment, select type and size of pipe, and collect and transport materials and equipment to work site.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/institutional construction site: helper takes the fitter's list, pulls the right pipe (e.g., 2" copper, 4" cast iron, 3" PVC sticks), fittings, hangers, solder, and power tools from the job trailer or laydown yard, loads a cart or hoist, and moves them through an active, cluttered, multi-floor site (mud, temporary stairs, buck hoists, other trades) to the fitter's work area.

Residential/light-commercial service and repair: helper loads the service van at the shop with the day's tools, fixtures, and assorted pipe/fittings, rides to customer addresses, then unloads and carries what's needed through driveways, yards, doorways, basements, and crawlspaces to the work spot inside a private home or small business.

Industrial plant or institutional campus maintenance: helper draws requisitioned tools from the tool crib and pipe/valves/fittings from the maintenance stockroom, loads a cart, and moves them through plant aisles, corridors, and freight elevators to the job location inside the facility.

Wholesale supply house / warehouse pickup: helper presents the requisition at the counter or pulls stock himself, selecting correct pipe type, size and schedule plus boxes of fittings from racks and bins, verifies the order, and loads it onto the truck or trailer for the crew.

Underground utility / pipelaying work: helper collects bell-and-spigot pipe joints, gaskets, lube, bedding stone, and shoring hardware from the roadside stockpile and moves them along the open trench line (uneven ground, spoil piles, traffic control) to the laying crew and the excavator operator.

sources.system: KASTO UNICOMPACT 5.0 automated long-goods storage with KASTOlogic WMS (Steel and Pipe Supply, Kansas City)
sources.title: Automated Steel Storage System for SPS
sources.claim: KASTO automated long-goods storage systems at a US steel and pipe distributor automatically store and retrieve bar stock and tubes by size under warehouse-management software, with a bridge crane and magnetic lifter handling the retrieved bundles — i.e., machine selection and retrieval of specified pipe/tube in a purpose-built automated storage setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated storage/retrieval of bar and tube stock at a pipe distributor. It is the same physical act as 'select type and size of pipe and collect it' — same objects (tubes/pipe bundles), same size/grade discrimination driven by an order record.

sources.system: KASTOsort robot handling system plus AGVs (KASTO material flow installations)
sources.title: Kasto: pioneering automation, storage and sawing solutions since 1844
sources.claim: In the same KASTO material-flow installations, a robotic handling system sorts and stacks cut long-goods pieces and AGVs then move the containers to their destination workstations, showing machine-side collection plus transport of pipe/bar material inside a purpose-built material-flow system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: kitting and internal delivery of cut pipe/bar. Transfers because the objects are the same (pipe/tube lengths in containers) and the output is the same — correct material delivered to the point of work.

sources.system: Canrig Red Zone Robotics (RZR) Rig Floor Module on Nabors rig X29
sources.title: Nabors retrofits robotics module onto existing land rig to achieve full automation
sources.claim: Nabors' Canrig Red Zone Robotics rig-floor module autonomously handles tubulars — picking up, moving and delivering drill pipe and casing to well center and racking it back — on land rigs drilling commercial wells, i.e., heavy pipe selection and delivery to the work point in a purpose-built machine setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated tubular handling. It covers the heaviest physical element of this task — selecting a joint of pipe of the right size from a rack and delivering it to the work point — with pipe far heavier than plumbing stock, in a fixtured setting.

sources.title: Shimizu Begins Collaborating People and Autonomous Robots at Construction Site, Toranomon-Azabudai Project
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Carrier system autonomously picks up palletized construction materials at ground level, loads them into a linked autonomous elevator, and transports them to designated locations on the working floor of a high-rise construction project; it was put to work with human crews on the Toranomon-Azabudai project.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: jobsite material logistics. Directly comparable transport leg, but limited to pre-palletized unit loads on prepared routes — it does not select pipe by size or gather loose tools and fittings.

sources.title: KEWAZO LIFTBOT - Edison Awards
sources.claim: KEWAZO's LIFTBOT is a commercially offered, battery-powered robotic hoist that autonomously moves scaffolding and other materials vertically on industrial construction and maintenance sites; it runs on a rail installed on the scaffold and is loaded and unloaded by workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vertical material transport on jobsites. Shows only the hoisting leg on a purpose-installed rail; workers still select, gather and load the materials.

sources.title: UTMB deploys robots to support hospital staff
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator autonomously navigates hospital corridors, doors and elevators to fetch and deliver supplies, lab samples and medications, with nearly 100 robots and over 1.25 million deliveries; staff load the items into its locked drawers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility supply delivery in a structured human facility. It substantiates autonomous transport of small supplies through corridors and elevators, but the items are loaded by people, so it does not cover selecting and gathering pipe, fittings and tools.

sources.title: FoxBot Mk3 Takes on More Warehouse Work with New Capabilities and Industry Applications
sources.claim: Fox Robotics' FoxBot Mk3 autonomous forklift picks, moves and loads or ... in warehouses using onboard cameras and lidar, integrated with warehouse management systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse pallet retrieval and truck loading. Covers unit-load handling in a supply warehouse, but only palletized loads identified by the WMS — not picking individual pipe lengths or mixed fittings from racks and bins.

sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch is a fully autonomous mobile case-handling robot deployed by DHL for unloading boxes from trucks and containers in warehouses, with ten units in service across three countries by mid-2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading/unloading boxed materials from a vehicle in a facility. Comparable object class (cartons up to ~50 lb) and shows autonomous vehicle loading work, but it does not select items by type or move them to a remote work site.

sources.system: RoboCrib VX1000 / AutoLocker FX industrial vending
sources.title: Mars Supply | AutoCrib Vending & Tool Crib Management
sources.claim: AutoCrib RoboCrib industrial vending machines automatically issue requisitioned tools and supplies — including power tools, gauges and oversized items via attached automated lockers — to workers who authenticate at the machine, performing the recordkeeping a tool-crib attendant would.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated tool-crib issuance. It directly covers the 'requisition tools and equipment' element in a purpose-built dispensing machine, though the worker still carries the tools onward.

tasks.label: Disassemble and remove damaged or worn pipe.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service call or repipe in an occupied house: helper cuts out and removes corroded galvanized supply lines, old copper, or cast-iron/ABS drain sections under a sink, in a crawlspace, basement joist bay, or opened wall; joints are seized or corroded, access is confined, pipe is cut with a recip saw or snap cutter, unions and hangers are undone, and the sections are carried out to the truck.

Commercial building renovation / tenant strip-out: helper works from a ladder or lift removing abandoned or worn hydronic, steam, or domestic water piping above ceilings and in mechanical rooms; must strip insulation and hangers, unbolt flanges or cut welded/threaded joints, and lower and haul away pipe amid other trades and varying as-built layouts.

Industrial or institutional plant maintenance/shutdown (refinery, power plant, food plant, campus steam tunnel): helper assists in removing worn process or steam pipe spools - unbolting flanges, breaking unions, cutting with a bandsaw or torch under hot-work permit, rigging the spool out with a chain hoist, and moving it to a laydown area.

Underground utility work in an open trench or street cut: helper cuts out and removes a broken or worn section of water main, sewer, or gas line - pulling bell-and-spigot or gasketed joints apart, cutting ductile iron, clay or PVC, slinging the piece to an excavator, in mud, groundwater, and shoring.

Fabrication shop or contractor yard: helper breaks down removed or salvaged pipe at a bench - unthreading fittings in a pipe vise with wrenches, cutting spools into shorter scrap lengths on a saw, stripping valves and fittings for reuse, and loading pieces into scrap bins.

sources.system: Canrig Red Zone Robotics (RZR) Rig Floor Module
sources.title: Nabors retrofits robotics module onto existing land rig to achieve full automation - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: Canrig RZR rig-floor robotics module autonomously performs hands-free tubular handling on a drilling rig floor, including breaking out and making up threaded steel pipe connections and tripping pipe in and out of the hole, with crews cleared from the red zone; deployed commercially on Nabors rig X29 drilling wells for ExxonMobil.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tripping out of hole is unscrewing high-torque threaded steel pipe joints and removing heavy pipe sections from the ground, then racking them. Objects (heavy-wall steel pipe, threaded/galled joints, hundreds of kg), forces and the disassemble-then-remove action match helper pipe removal, and the pipe is presented fixtured (spider/rotary table) as a purpose-built cell would present it.

sources.title: FlexRobotics Hands-Free Rig Floor | H&P, Inc.
sources.claim: H&P FlexRobotics, a three-arm rig-floor system built on NOV Atom RTX / Yaskawa six-axis manipulators, performs hands-free drilling and tripping connections - moving pipe stands between mousehole, well centre and setback and servicing the connection - with personnel removed from the red zone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic arms grip, unthread and transport heavy steel pipe during tripping - the same grip / break-joint / carry-away sequence as disassembling and removing worn pipe - inside a machine-built work envelope from which humans are excluded (mark of E1).

sources.system: autonomous disassembly demonstrator cell for e-waste (reported by Tech Xplore)
sources.developer: European research consortium reported by Tech Xplore
sources.title: Robots to the rescue: Automated disassembly for e-waste recycling
sources.claim: A purpose-built robotic disassembly cell for end-of-life electronic products executes disassembly sequences - unscrewing, cutting, levering, extracting and lifting parts out - fully autonomously from vision-driven plans, on used and degraded units.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous take-apart of worn, degraded assemblies in a fixtured cell, including cutting and unfastening steps a pipe teardown needs; it supports the cut/unfasten half of the E1 counterfactual while the rig-floor systems supply the heavy-pipe force and handling half.

sources.system: Brokk demolition robot with BGS65 Grapple Saw
sources.title: Brokk: Transforming Nuclear Decommissioning Through Innovation - Brokk Global
sources.claim: In-situ removal of plant piping at the Agesta nuclear plant used a Brokk demolition machine with a custom BGS65 grapple saw that cuts and grips pipe runs 3-5.5 m overhead; the machine is remote-controlled by an operator at a distance, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (cutting out and removing worn pipe inside a facility), but under continuous remote control, showing that the state of the art for in-situ pipe removal in a structured facility (E2) and in unstructured settings (E3) remains teleoperated.

tasks.label: Cut or drill holes in walls or floors to accommodate the passage of pipes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wood-framed residential or light-commercial rough-in on an active build/gut-remodel: helper bores 1 in.-2.5 in. holes with auger bits and hole saws through studs, top/bottom plates, blocking and floor joists so the plumber can pull PEX, copper and DWV lines; positions marked by the journeyman, must respect notching/boring limits, work is overhead and in tight bays.

Service, repair or small remodel in an occupied, finished home or small business: cut an opening through finished drywall, plaster, tile, cabinet back, wood subfloor or basement slab to pass a new supply, drain or vent line; furniture and finishes present, concealed wiring/pipes unknown, dust control and patch-ready edges required.

Large open commercial/industrial building shell under construction (warehouse, data center, big-box, plant): drill many small-diameter (roughly 1/2 in.-1.5 in.) holes into the bare concrete floor slab from a digital layout for small pipe/conduit penetrations and for the anchors of pipe supports, with dust extraction and rebar avoidance.

Commercial/institutional new construction: wet core-drill 2 in.-8 in. penetrations through concrete floor slabs and metal-deck floors for pipe sleeves, stacks and risers on an active multi-trade site - scan for rebar/post-tension, set the rig, manage water and slurry, remove and dispose of the core, prep for sleeving/firestop.

Penetrations through masonry, poured foundation or exterior walls: core or hammer a hole through a CMU/concrete foundation wall for a water service or through an exterior wall for a vent or hose bibb, working from a crawlspace, trench or ladder with a hand-held or rig-mounted core drill.

Prefab/modular shop or MEP fabrication facility: cut and drill the pipe-passage holes in wall panels, floor cassettes, precast elements or module framing at a fixed station before the assembly is shipped to site, working from shop drawings on staged, jigged workpieces.

sources.system: DALE (DEWALT + August Robotics autonomous downward drilling robot)
sources.developer: DEWALT (Stanley Black & Decker) with August Robotics
sources.title: 9 weeks to 9 days: How autonomous drilling is transforming data center construction - The Robot Report
sources.claim: DALE, an autonomous mobile drilling robot (DEWALT drilling rig on August Robotics' Lionel AMR), drills holes in bare concrete floor slabs on data-center and other building construction sites straight from CAD hole layouts; 12 robots were in the field having drilled ... at 99.97% placement accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic drilling of holes in a concrete floor on a jobsite. Material (structural slab), tool (industrial rotary hammer with dust extraction), diameter range and location tolerance overlap the small floor penetrations a plumber's helper drills for pipe/conduit passage; demonstrated holes are for rack stops and legs supporting overhead MEP rather than through-holes for pipes.

sources.title: Robotic Downward Drilling for Data Centers and General Construction | August Robotics
sources.claim: The DALE platform drills 1/2 in. to 1-1/2 in. ... holes up to 14 in. deep in concrete, executes autonomously from an uploaded CAD/CSV of drill points, detects and cuts rebar, and extracts dust.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: establishes a hole diameter/depth envelope covering small pipe and conduit penetrations through a normal 6-8 in. slab, and confirms autonomous execution rather than teleoperation.

sources.title: Automatic hollow core machine Modifier E9 - Elematic precast technology
sources.claim: Elematic's Modifier E9 is an automatic ... on a hollow-core slab production line that digs openings and recesses for HVAC ducts and plumbing, and drills holes, in concrete floor slabs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: forming the pipe-passage opening in a concrete floor element, done on a purpose-built production line with the slab presented to the machine rather than core-drilled in place; same accepted output (a correctly located, correctly sized opening in a floor for plumbing).

sources.developer: WEINMANN Holzbausystemtechnik (HOMAG Group), distributed by Stiles Machinery
sources.title: WEINMANN WALLTEQ Multi-Function Bridges - Stiles Machinery
sources.claim: WEINMANN WALLTEQ multifunction bridges are CNC-controlled gantry machines on prefab wall/floor/roof element lines that rout, saw and drill wall elements, cutting rough openings such as window, door and outlet openings, from the digital element model.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-cut service openings in a fixtured timber wall element. Same materials (framing lumber and sheathing), comparable hole sizes and tolerances to the 1-2.5 in. bores a helper makes for pipes, and the machine works from the same digital model that carries plumbing penetrations.

sources.system: Kawasaki BX250L robotic wall sheathing and cutting cell (SCADAware / Rehkemper)
sources.title: Assembling Walls for Prefabricated Homes | Industrial Robots by Kawasaki
sources.claim: A cell of four Kawasaki BX250L robots on Gudel rails at Rehkemper (integrated by SCADAware) fastens OSB sheathing to framed wall panels held on an aligning table and carves window and door openings into the panels from the digital wall design, locating studs to within 1/16 in.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic cutting of openings through a wall assembly held in a fixture. Same wood substrate and comparable positional precision (1/16 in. relative to framing) as cutting a pipe-passage hole in a wall; performed in a robotic cell with the panel presented to the robot.

sources.system: Hundegger K1 / Robot Drive CNC joinery machine
sources.title: Our Timber Frame CNC - Woodhouse The Timber Frame Company
sources.claim: Hundegger CNC joinery machines used in timber-frame shops size timber members and use horizontal and vertical drills and slot cutters to produce holes and slots in the members at a fixed machining station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: CNC drilling of holes in structural timber members fed and clamped by the machine - the same operation, material and accuracy class as boring studs, plates and joists for pipe passage, but with the member brought to the machine.

sources.title: Hilti's Robot Breaks Records on a YIT Construction Site - AEC Business
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a semi-autonomous mobile ... used on construction sites that drills and marks MEP holes in concrete ceilings and (since 2022) concrete walls and metal deck from BIM data; an operator drives it into position by remote control and sets up a PLT 300 total station, after which holes within reach are drilled .... Hole diameters are about 3/16 in. to 3/4 in.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drilling MEP holes in concrete walls/ceilings on a live jobsite. Not used to support a positive judgment: the operator repositions the machine throughout, and its 3/16-3/4 in. anchor holes are smaller than pipe-passage holes.

tasks.label: Clean shop, work area, and machines, using solvent and rags.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-day cleanup at a residential job site (occupied home: bath/kitchen remodel, water-heater or drain replacement): pick up copper/PVC offcuts, fittings, cardboard and packaging, sweep or vacuum cutting dust and sawdust, wipe flux, pipe dope, solvent cement and water off floors, fixtures and cabinets with rags, and carry debris out to the truck.

Cleanup of the work area on a commercial/institutional job site (mechanical room, new building floor, hospital or school renovation): clear scrap pipe, hanger stock and insulation offcuts, sweep dust and metal cuttings, wipe cutting oil and grease spots off the deck with solvent and rags, and put used rags in the approved waste container before inspection.
General housekeeping of the contractor's pipe-fabrication shop: sweeping/mopping open floor areas and aisles covered with metal chips, cutting-oil film, dust and shop dirt at the end of the shift.

Wiping down and degreasing shop machines in place: pipe threading machine, cut-off saw, roll groover and bender caked with thread-cutting oil, chips and swarf — wiping housings, ways, chucks and dies with solvent-soaked rags and picking chips out of trays.

Cleaning hand tools and equipment with solvent and rags at the shop bench or truck: wrenches, threader dies and heads, torch tips, drain-machine cable, levels and pipe stands, then drying and returning them to the gang box or rack.

sources.title: Tennant Company Unveils X16 SWEEP for Autonomous, Around-the-Clock Industrial Sweeping
sources.claim: Tennant's X16 SWEEP, powered by Brain Corp autonomy, is a commercially launched autonomous robotic sweeper for industrial floors in warehouses, logistics centers and light ... plants — i.e., autonomous shop-floor debris and dust removal in a facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous industrial floor sweeping. It covers the shop-floor housekeeping instance directly — same surfaces (concrete industrial floor), same soils (dust, chips, shop dirt), same institutional facility.

sources.title: Avidbots: Neo 2W - Material Handling 24/7
sources.claim: Avidbots Neo 2W is a fully autonomous floor-scrubbing ... built for and deployed in warehouses, distribution centers and manufacturing facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous scrubbing of industrial floors. Transfers to mopping/degreasing a fab-shop floor: same oily concrete surfaces and same type of institutionally controlled industrial premises.

sources.title: Robot Laser Cleaning Machine | Laserax
sources.claim: Turnkey robotic laser-cleaning workcells (enclosed, safety-interlocked) autonomously remove oils, grease, residue and coatings from metal parts, tooling and equipment presented in the cell, and run continuously in industrial plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic degreasing/decontamination of machine parts and tooling in a fenced cell. Same objective as wiping oil and grease off shop machines and tools with solvent and rags — removal of oil films from metal surfaces — but with the workpiece brought to and fixtured at the machine, which is exactly the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: KUKA KR 210 R3100 F ultra dry-ice blasting cell
sources.title: KUKA: robots-based dry-ice blasting
sources.claim: A KUKA foundry robot in an enclosed cell cleans permanent casting molds with dry ice, executing the cleaning path automatically after teach-in; molds are brought to the station and returned to production after the ~30-minute cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic cleaning of production tooling/equipment surfaces fouled with release agents and residue, replacing manual solvent-and-rag cleaning. Comparable objects (large greasy metal machine components) and comparable acceptance standard, performed with the equipment brought into a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Kawasaki machine-tending robot cells (air blow-off end effector)
sources.title: Machine Tending | Robotic Applications | Complete Guide
sources.claim: In commercial robotic machine-tending cells, the robot itself performs work-zone housekeeping: an air blow-off on the ... removes chips, dust and coolant from the fixture after every cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated clearing of chips, swarf and coolant/oil from the machine and its work zone — the same soils and objective as a helper cleaning a machine and its work area, done inside a purpose-built cell where the work is presented to the machine.

sources.system: AMD Machines robotic machine-tending cells with integrated parts washer
sources.title: Robotic Machine Tending Cells | AMD Machines
sources.claim: System integrators build robotic cells in which one robot tends machines and a parts washer in sequence, with air-knife blow-off stations and a dedicated parts washer inside ... to clean chips and coolant off parts and fixtures automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated washing/blow-off of oily metal parts and tooling handled by a robot inside a cell. Comparable objects (oil- and chip-covered steel tools and fixtures) and comparable accepted output (clean, dry, oil-free) to cleaning hand tools and threader dies with solvent and rags.

sources.title: Figure’s Humanoid Robot Picks Up Toys, Wipes Surfaces in New Demo
sources.claim: Figure's Figure 03 humanoid, running Helix 02, was shown in a March 2026 video demo autonomously tidying a living room: spraying a surface, wiping it with a towel, gathering trash and putting objects away. It is a company demo in a staged home, not a deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Closest available evidence for mobile-manipulator wiping and debris pickup in an unstructured room; cited to show the state of the art is a staged single demo, not sustained worker-quality job-site cleanup with construction debris and solvents.

sources.system: Clobot autonomous cleaning robot (POSCO E&C deployment)
sources.title: POSCO E&C deploys autonomous robots for post-construction cleanups
sources.claim: POSCO E&C deployed AI-powered autonomous cleaning robots (with Clobot) at an apartment redevelopment project for pre-handover cleaning of parking areas and community spaces; the robots map the space, ride elevators and run unsupervised, but they are floor-cleaning machines only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous floor cleaning in a building at the final construction stage. It covers only the floor-washing portion of job-site cleanup; it does not pick up pipe offcuts and packaging or wipe residues off fixtures with rags.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's bathroom cleaning robot is sold as a monthly service and autonomously cleans fixtures and floors and picks up trash in office-building restrooms without direct supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cleaning of surfaces, fixtures and floors plus trash pickup inside a structured facility. Cited to bound the E2 case: the fixtures are standardized restroom items in a maintained room, not oil-caked pipe machinery or a debris-strewn work area under renovation.

tasks.label: Excavate and grade ditches, and lay and join pipe for water and sewer service.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Municipal gravity sewer or storm-drain main in a street/right-of-way: excavator opens a 6–15 ft trench with a trench box, helper checks depth with laser/GPS rod, spreads and fine-grades stone bedding to line and grade, rigs and guides each bell-and-spigot pipe section into the trench, lubricates the gasket, seats the joint with the machine or come-along, checks alignment before backfill. Existing utilities, traffic control, wet/caving soils.

Water main run in a new subdivision or greenfield corridor: trench 4–6 ft deep, bed the bottom, lay ductile-iron or PVC push-on pipe, set fittings, valves, restraints and thrust blocks, join by pushing spigot into bell, occasional cut-to-fit with saw, then partial backfill for pressure test.

Residential water service line or sewer lateral: mini-excavator plus hand digging near foundation, driveway, tree roots and existing utilities; lay small-diameter PVC/HDPE/copper, join with solvent weld, fusion or compression couplings, tie into main or building stub, grade bedding, backfill and restore the yard. Tight, cluttered private property.

Emergency repair or tie-in on an existing water/sewer line: excavate a small pit to expose the broken pipe (hand digging around live utilities, pumping out water/mud), grade the pit bottom, cut out the damaged section and install a repair sleeve, coupling or saddle, then bed and backfill. Unknown conditions, no as-built certainty, urgency.

Trench-and-grade assignment on an open site ahead of the pipe crew: excavate and grade a long, straight ditch to specified depth and line (utility/pipe corridor on a greenfield, solar, industrial or subdivision site), place spoils along the trench, keep the floor smooth for later bedding; no existing utilities in the corridor, open working room.

sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofit turns standard excavators into fully autonomous trenching machines that dig trenches with smooth floors and clean walls for later installation of buried infrastructure.
sources.transferJustification: Trenching for buried electrical infrastructure is the same excavate-and-grade-a-ditch operation as trenching for pipe: same machines, same soils, same depth/line/grade control, differing only in what is later placed in the trench.

sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Moves Earth with Autonomous Excavators | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Autonomous Built Robotics excavators have been used by a major contractor (Bechtel) for trenching on real solar construction projects in Texas, i.e., deployed field use rather than a demo.
sources.transferJustification: Utility trenching on a solar site is the excavation-and-grading half of this task performed with the same equipment on an open outdoor construction site.

sources.title: Autonomous construction bots are building the solar infrastructure behind Meta's massive Hyperion data center
sources.claim: Built Robotics machines operate autonomously inside defined work zones on active construction sites and the company has completed over 40 deployments in utility-scale solar and data-center projects, covering trenching, pile driving and pre-drilling.

sources.system: Bedrock Robotics autonomy kit on 20–80 ton excavators
sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Announces Supervised Autonomy Testing on Active Construction Sites in Move Towards Commercialization
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics runs supervised-autonomy excavators on active construction sites, moving more than 65,000 cubic ... earth on a 130-acre facility site, but full (unsupervised) autonomous customer deployments were still a 2026 target.
sources.transferJustification: Mass excavation with an autonomous excavator shares the digging and earth-grading component of this task, though it does not include pipe handling or jointing.

sources.developer: ETH Zurich (Gramazio Kohler Research, Robotic Systems Lab)
sources.title: Autonomous excavator constructs a 6-meter-high dry-stone wall
sources.claim: An autonomous excavator (HEAP) autonomously scanned, grabbed and placed multi-ton boulders to centimetre precision to build a 65 m dry-stone wall within an autonomously excavated landscape — the closest demonstrated capability to machine placement of heavy objects into prepared ground.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous pick-and-place of heavy irregular objects by an excavator. It bears on 'laying' pipe, but not on grading a bedded trench bottom to sewer tolerances or seating a gasketed bell-and-spigot joint, which require in-trench alignment, lubrication and controlled axial insertion not demonstrated here.

sources.system: CRC Evans automatic/mechanized pipeline welding systems
sources.title: ADIPEC 2025: CRC Evans CEO talks offshore welding for a digital future | Offshore Magazine
sources.claim: Field pipeline joining by the leading automatic-welding supplier remains semi-automated with human operators; fully robotic, autonomous joint-making is stated as a future vision, not a current capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making pipeline field joints. Even in the most automation-intensive pipe-joining niche, the joint-making step is operator-loaded and semi-automated, indicating no autonomous field jointing capability transferable to water/sewer joints.

sources.system: Novarc Spool Welding Robot (SWR) with NovEye Autonomy
sources.title: Novarc automates arc welding processes with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2 - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Even in a fixtured fabrication-shop setting, pipe joining robots are collaborative systems in which an operator handles fit-up and loading while the robot performs weld passes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: joining pipe in a purpose-built cell. Relevant to the E1 counterfactual, but the operator performs fit-up/handling and the workpieces are shop spools, so it does not substantiate autonomous laying and joining of buried water/sewer pipe.

tasks.label: Immerse pipe in chemical solution to remove dirt, oil, and scale.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mechanical/pipe-fabrication shop: helper rigs a welded stainless steel pipe spool to a hoist or hand-carries it, lowers it into an acid pickling/passivation tank, times the soak, lifts it out, rinses/neutralizes it, and racks it to dry. Pipe sizes and weld-scale severity vary batch to batch; PPE, fume hood/ventilation, spill controls.

Shop cleaning bench/dip tank or parts washer: helper drops a batch of nipples, fittings, valves, and short pipe lengths into a basket of alkaline/solvent degreasing or acid solution to strip cutting oil, dirt, and rust, agitates or brushes them, rinses, and dries them before threading, brazing, or painting.

Job site (unfinished building, trailer, or outdoors): helper dips copper tube ends, fittings, or threaded nipples into a bucket/pan of cleaning solution (e.g., dilute acid or solvent) staged on the ground near the work, swirls and wipes them, and hands them to the plumber for soldering or assembly. Layout changes daily, weather and debris present.

Galvanizing/coating shop: helper hooks bundles or racks of pipe to an overhead crane and lowers them in sequence through degreasing, acid pickling, rinse, and flux tanks, watching soak times and drainage before the pipe goes to the dryer/kettle or paint line.

High-purity/oxygen-service prep in a controlled shop area: helper immerses pipe and fittings in a specified degreasing solution (cleaning to CGA/ASTM-type spec), rinses with clean/deionized water, dries, and stages the parts for inspection so no oil or particulate remains.

sources.system: GIMECO tubes and pipes hot-dip galvanizing line (automatic pretreatment tanks, racks, bundle conveyors)
sources.date: 2024-06 (page updated); product line commercially installed for years
sources.title: Tubes and pipes hot-dip galvanizing | GIMECO Impianti
sources.claim: Commercial hot-dip galvanizing lines for tubes and pipes run the chemical pretreatment sequence (degreasing, acid pickling, fluxing immersion tanks) and bundle handling entirely automatically, with only occasional operator supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: pipe is immersed in chemical solutions (degreasing, pickling acid, flux) to remove dirt, oil, and scale; the line performs the immersion, soak timing, extraction, and rinsing on real pipe bundles.

sources.system: Best Technology Automated Passivation System for High-Volume Production (gantry-rail hoist automation)
sources.title: Automated Passivation Systems for High-Volume Production
sources.claim: Commercial automated passivation/pickling systems move baskets or racks of metal parts through immersion cleaning, acid, rinse, and dry tanks under PLC recipe control, without an operator handling the loads between tanks.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical act on comparable workpieces: stainless steel parts (including welded assemblies and fittings) are immersed in chemical solution to remove oil, dirt, and weld scale, then rinsed and dried; the system supports pickling/descaling chemistries.

sources.system: Best Technology automated ultrasonic cleaning and pickling line
sources.title: Automated Pickling and Cleaning System Case Study
sources.claim: An automated cleaning-and-pickling line integrating cleaning, rinsing, chemical descaling, and post-pickle steps was engineered and delivered for a production manufacturer.
sources.transferJustification: Chemical descaling and degreasing of metal parts by immersion is the same operation the helper performs on pipe and fittings; the line covers the full sequence from load to rinsed, descaled output.

sources.system: Best Technology Automated Passivation System (gantry monorail on fiberglass I-beams)
sources.title: Automated Passivation for High-Volume Production: Case Study
sources.claim: A high-output stainless steel component manufacturer installed a gantry-monorail automated passivation system that carries parts loads through the corrosive chemical tanks.
sources.transferJustification: Demonstrates a real deployment of machine-handled immersion chemical processing of stainless parts, the same handling problem as dipping pipe spools and fittings in a cleaning bath.

sources.system: Siedentop Rotainer / Tube Blue Rotainer pickling system
sources.title: Automated container-type pickling systems - Stainless Steel World
sources.claim: A fully automated, computer-controlled tube pickling system processes bundles of stainless steel tubes through degreasing, pickling, passivation and rinsing steps with a dedicated hoist-rotation lift, without operators contacting the acid.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: chemical pickling/degreasing of steel tube bundles to remove oil and scale, delivered by enclosed spray rather than open bath, with automated hoist handling of the tube bundles — same workpieces, chemistry, and cleanliness acceptance.

tasks.label: Clean and renew steam traps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Industrial/process plant (food plant, refinery, paper mill, chemical plant): helper works with a pipefitter on steam traps at drip legs and process equipment, many on elevated pipe racks or outdoors. Isolate and bleed the trap, break the union/flange, blow down and clean the strainer screen, scrape scale and rust from body and seat, install a repair kit (disc/seat, bimetal or float assembly, gasket), torque up, restore steam and check for blow-through or leaks. Hot, dirty, seized fasteners are common.

Institutional/commercial mechanical room (hospital, university, office boiler plant): F&T and thermostatic traps on heating coils, unit heaters, converters and humidifiers in a boiler room or ceiling space. Helper isolates the trap, removes the cover bolts, cleans out sludge and scale, fits a manufacturer's rebuild kit or swaps the whole trap on unions, then leak-checks. Tight clearances around piping and insulation removal/replacement.

Older multifamily/residential steam heat: replacing or rebuilding radiator thermostatic traps and cage units in occupied apartments and basements. Helper carries kits, cracks the seized cap with heat or a wrench, cleans the seat, drops in the new cage unit and gasket, reassembles, and cleans up in the tenant's space. Layouts, trap brands and access differ apartment to apartment.

Shop/bench work: traps pulled from the system are brought to the shop bench for cleaning and renewal — disassembly, wire brushing/soaking or ultrasonic cleaning of body and screen, inspection of seats and orifices, installation of new internals and gaskets, reassembly and bench/pressure test before the trap goes back on the line.

Campus district-steam tunnels, pits and crawl spaces: cleaning and renewing traps and their strainers in hot, cramped, poorly lit underground vaults, often with confined-space procedures, condensate underfoot, and traps mounted low or overhead among congested piping.

sources.title: Spot Arm | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: The most capable commercially deployed mobile manipulator for industrial plants (Spot with arm) is marketed for turning valves, flipping levers and opening doors semi-autonomously or by telemanipulation — not for disassembling, cleaning and rebuilding piping components.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-plant valve/lever manipulation. It is the closest field manipulation capability to steam-trap work; it shows current plant robots handle single constrained motions under operator initiation, far short of disassembling and rebuilding a fouled trap.

sources.title: ANYmal - Autonomous Robotic Inspection Solution - ANYbotics
sources.claim: Deployed autonomous quadrupeds in refineries, chemical plants and power stations perform sensor-based inspection rounds only (visual, thermal, ultrasonic); they carry no manipulator for maintenance work such as cleaning or renewing steam traps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous steam-trap and equipment inspection rounds in the same plants where this task occurs. It establishes that robots in these settings gather data rather than perform mechanical repair, so it cannot substantiate completion of cleaning/renewal.

sources.system: Robotic unscrewing cell for e-waste disassembly
sources.developer: academic research group (published in Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing)
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic unscrewing of end-of-life products has been demonstrated in laboratory cells with 91–100% per-screw success, but only for the fastener-removal sub-step on electronics testbeds, with acknowledged remaining challenges.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly of used products. It covers only fastener removal on clean, small electronics — not breaking seized steam-trap caps, descaling bodies, fitting gaskets and internals, or achieving a pressure-tight rebuild.

sources.system: Epson robot valve assembly cell (Dotson/AutomateElite integrator)
sources.title: Robots assemble hydraulic valves | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Industrial robots reliably assemble new hydraulic valves (O-rings, screws, adjustment parts) in fixtured, feeder-fed cells — but this is assembly of clean new components, not renewal of fouled used units of variable condition.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated valve assembly in a purpose-built cell. Transfer fails for this task because the inputs here are used, scaled and corroded traps of mixed models requiring cleaning, condition judgment and seized-fastener removal, none of which this cell handles.

sources.title: Cat Reman | The Remanufacturing Process | Caterpillar
sources.claim: Remanufacturing of used mechanical cores (disassembly, cleaning, salvage, inspection, reassembly and test) is described by the largest industrial remanufacturer as a technician- and inspector-driven process; automation is established for washing/blasting rather than for full disassemble-clean-rebuild autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bench renewal of used fluid-handling components. Industry-scale reman of comparable used parts is still performed by human technicians with automated washing support, indicating no cited system completes an equivalent clean-and-rebuild cycle autonomously.

sources.title: The future of robotic disassembly: a systematic review of techniques and applications in the age of AI
sources.claim: A 2025 systematic review of robotic disassembly finds robots deployed across a spectrum from narrow autonomous tasks to human-robot collaboration, with product-condition uncertainty in end-of-life items still the central obstacle; no fielded system performs whole used-component rebuilds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly/remanufacturing generally. It documents that autonomy is confined to specific sub-tasks under controlled conditions, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance steam-trap cleaning and renewal at any tier.

tasks.label: Fill pipes with sand or resin to prevent distortion, and hold pipes during bending and installation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/institutional jobsite: helper steadies and feeds 1/2"-2" conduit, copper or steel pipe into a hand, ratchet or hydraulic bender, holds it against the shoe while the journeyman pulls the bend, and repositions/re-marks it between bends on a cluttered, changing floor.

Commercial/institutional jobsite: helper bears the weight of a 10-21 ft length of pipe overhead, in a chase or on a rack, aligning it to hangers and to the mating fitting and holding it steady while the fitter tacks, solders, presses, threads or bolts it up; ladders, lifts, dust and other trades present.

Residential or light-commercial service/remodel: helper holds pipe or tubing steady in a basement, crawl space, joist bay or under a fixture while the plumber cuts, bends with a hand bender, joins and fastens it; tight, unmodified, occupied space.

Trench/pipelaying: helper guides and holds a large-diameter sewer, water or gas pipe as it is lowered by excavator or sideboom, keeps it aligned while it is homed into the bell or lined up for welding, and steadies it while the joint is made in an open, muddy trench.

Contractor fabrication shop or prefab facility: helper packs pipe with sand/packing (or sets up the mandrel), caps ends, loads and holds pipe on the shop bender, and holds/positions spool pieces in a jig while the fitter bends, fits and tacks; fixed layout, standard equipment.

sources.system: fischer group automated bending cells (CNC mandrel benders with load/unload robots)
sources.title: Making the most of tube bending automation in a metal fabrication shop
sources.claim: Fully automated CNC tube/pipe bending cells in production use comprise a tube magazine with weld-seam detection, internal lubrication, a robot that loads and unloads the mandrel bender, and an outfeed conveyor - the machine presents, clamps and supports the pipe through the bend with no human holding it.
sources.transferJustification: Same task element: the helper's job of holding and feeding pipe through bending is performed by the cell's magazine, loading robot and clamp/pressure dies, and the internal mandrel performs the anti-distortion role of sand or resin fill.

sources.system: ball mandrel tooling for rotary-draw pipe/tube bending
sources.title: Inside the world of tube bending
sources.claim: An internal mandrel inserted in the pipe during bending is the machine equivalent of packing a pipe with sand or resin: it supports the wall and prevents collapse, kinking and ovality.
sources.transferJustification: Substantiates that the anti-distortion purpose of filling pipe with sand or resin is served inside automated benders by internal mandrels; used as context only, not as a decisive system.

sources.system: Ercolina EB76 CNCV7S mandrel bender (CML USA)
sources.title: EB76 CNCV7S Mandrel benders - Ercolina
sources.claim: Commercial CNC mandrel benders are fully automatic multi-axis machines that clamp and bend pipe up to roughly 3 in. OD under program control, with the wider NC/CNC mandrel line covering capacities to 6-1/2 in.

sources.system: Valk Welding two-robot sprinkler pipe cell at Tyco Building Services Products AB
sources.title: Welding robot installation 4.0 for the production of sprinkler pipes
sources.claim: In a deployed sprinkler-pipe prefabrication cell, a robot-controlled positioner with a chuck clamps, rotates and positions pipes up to 7.5 m long while one robot handles couplings and another cuts holes and welds the couplings on - machines hold the pipe throughout fit-up and joining.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (prefabrication of sprinkler piping) covers the same element: holding and positioning pipe steady and in alignment while a fitting is joined to it, on the same class of objects (steel pipe with couplings) at fixtured-cell precision.

sources.system: Nabors RZR robotics module / PACE-R rigs
sources.title: Retrofit Kit Makes Robotic Drilling a Reality for Existing Rigs (JPT)
sources.claim: Nabors' RZR robotics module gives completely hands-free pipe handling on a land rig floor: it autonomously grips, positions and makes up drill pipe and casing (3-1/2 in. to 13-3/8 in.) with no crew member on the floor, and drilled multiple horizontal wells for ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task (making up tubular connections) is the heavy-pipe analogue of holding pipe during installation: the machine lifts, stabs and holds large-diameter heavy pipe in alignment while the joint is made, in a machine-controlled zone kept clear of people.

sources.title: Hilti Releases All New Features for the Hilti Jaibot
sources.claim: The most capable robot fielded on real construction sites for the MEP/pipe trades is a semi-autonomous mobile drilling ... that drills BIM-planned anchor holes; it does not lift, hold or install pipe.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to characterize the state of jobsite robotics for the pipe trades: capability is limited to drilling anchor holes, so it does not substantiate holding or bending pipe at E3.

tasks.label: Install gas burners to convert furnaces from wood, coal, or oil.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-family home basement/utility room: helper assists a plumber converting an oil-fired warm-air furnace or boiler to gas — carries the conversion burner down stairs, helps pull the old oil burner and clean the combustion chamber, holds the new burner against the front plate while it is bolted/gasketed, hands wrenches and pipe dope, helps run and support threaded black-iron gas pipe with drip leg and shutoff, then cleans soot and debris. Cluttered, low-headroom basement with stored household goods, varying furnace makes and clearances.

Older or rural dwelling with a wood/coal-fired furnace, gravity 'octopus' furnace, or crawlspace/mobile-home unit being converted to a gas or LP burner: extremely dirty and confined, ash and clinker removal, improvised access, hand-fitting of the burner and refractory/blockoff plate, propane tank piping outside; helper does most fetching, holding, and cleanup in tight quarters.

Small commercial/institutional boiler room (apartment building, school, church, small plant): oil-to-gas power-burner conversion on a cast-iron or steel boiler; helper rigs and skids the heavy burner into place, holds it while mounted to the boiler front, supplies gaskets/bolts, assists in assembling the gas train (cocks, regulator, safety shutoff valves) and running the pipe, and cleans the room after. Building-owner-controlled mechanical room, fixed layout but congested with existing piping.

Large industrial or utility boiler house: replacement of a coal/oil burner with a gas burner assembly on a large boiler — crane or chainfall rigging, heavy flanged gas train, refractory work, and commissioning with combustion analysis; helper tends rigging, supplies material and tools, holds parts during fit-up, and cleans the work area under permit conditions.

Shop/prefabrication work ahead of the field conversion: helper cuts and threads black iron pipe, assembles the gas train and burner mounting/adapter plate on a bench, tags and loads the assembly for delivery to the job. Contractor-controlled shop with pipe vise, threading machine, and benches.

sources.system: SDC gas burner assembly machine (FANUC SCARA robots, SDC Flex Feeders, indexing ring)
sources.title: High-Speed Gas Burner Assembly Machine – Robotic Automation
sources.claim: Fixtured factory cells with SCARA robots and vision-guided pick-and-place assemble gas burner components at high speed, but this is manufacture of burner parts on a dedicated line, not mounting a conversion burner onto an existing furnace with gas piping, wiring, and commissioning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory assembly of gas burner components in fixtures. Transfer is insufficient — the cell handles identical, feeder-presented parts on one product family and performs press/pick-place operations only; it does not mount a burner to a heterogeneous furnace, make up threaded gas piping with sealant, wire controls, or leak-test and commission the appliance.

sources.title: Hilti Releases All New Features for the Hilti Jaibot
sources.claim: The most capable field robot in the mechanical/plumbing trades performs only BIM-planned overhead anchor-hole drilling on construction sites; no cited field system installs heating equipment or makes gas connections.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: MEP jobsite drilling. Shows that deployed trade robots in these buildings are limited to a single repetitive drilling operation from a digital plan; it provides no manipulation, fitting, piping, or commissioning capability needed to install a gas burner.

sources.system: Spool Welding Robot (SWR) with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2
sources.title: Novarc Launches NovEye™ Gen 2 for Full Welding Automation
sources.claim: Pipe-shop automation for joining pipe is limited to welding of prepared spools inside fabrication shops with operator setup; there is no cited system that makes up threaded gas-train piping or assembles a burner and gas train end-to-end.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic pipe welding in fab shops. Transfer is insufficient — the robot welds joints that a human fits up and loads on a positioner; it cannot cut/thread pipe, apply sealant, torque threaded fittings, mount a burner, or pressure/leak test the finished gas train.

roles.title: Helpers--Roofers
roles.description: Help roofers by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

tasks.label: Check to ensure that completed roofs are watertight.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential steep-slope asphalt shingle re-roof: helper walks the finished roof with the lead roofer doing the hands-on watertightness check — inspecting valleys, step and counter flashing at chimneys and walls, pipe boots, skylight curbs and ridge; pressing/tugging courses to confirm adhesion, feeling for high or exposed fasteners, and dabbing sealant on any exposed nail heads before sign-off.

Residential job: purely visual final look-over of the completed roof (from ladder, ground, or aerial photos) to confirm no missing, lifted, or misaligned shingles, no gaps at penetrations, no debris left, and to capture photo documentation for the foreman/homeowner file.

Low-slope commercial roof (TPO/PVC/EPDM or modified bitumen) on an active re-roof job: helper probes every field seam and flashing lap with a seam probe, checks welds, pipe boots, curb flashings, terminations, drains and scuppers, marks voids with a crayon, and holds materials while defects are re-welded or patched.

Water testing suspect details: helper runs a hose over chimney, wall and skylight flashings, valleys, or a repaired area in stages while a co-worker watches from inside the attic or below; helper also climbs the attic/goes into the room after the job or after rain to look for drips, stains, or daylight at penetrations, and reports findings.

Flood test on a small flat roof, deck, or balcony: helper plugs the drains, fills the surface to ~2 inches of water, monitors the level and the ceiling/underside for 24–48 hours, then pulls the plugs, drains and dries the area.

Instrument/aerial survey of a completed low-slope roof for close-out: capturing overhead imagery or an infrared moisture scan to confirm no ponding, no visible membrane defects, and no entrapped moisture, delivered as a documented report to the foreman or building owner.

sources.title: EagleView Announces Launch of EagleView Assess Autonomous Drone-Sourced Property Intelligence
sources.claim: EagleView Assess is a commercially available autonomous drone product that launches from the ground and captures high-resolution imagery of residential roofs with AI anomaly detection, used by roofing contractors and adjusters at private homes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drone roof damage/anomaly inspection. Same object (shingle roof facets, flashings, penetrations) in the same setting (occupied private homes), and the output — an imagery-backed report flagging openings/defects on a roof surface — is the same kind of visual determination a helper makes when looking a finished roof over.

sources.title: Roof inspection drone tech with EagleView | Skydio
sources.claim: The EagleView/Skydio system builds a facet-by-facet flight plan and flies the residential roof inspection autonomously, without a human piloting it.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the autonomy of the capture step for the same drone roof-inspection task cited above; the machine, not an operator, executes the survey of the roof.

sources.title: Eagleview Assess™ Expands Drone Roof Inspection Solution
sources.claim: Eagleview extended the autonomous Assess drone inspection product to large, multi-faceted and commercial buildings, producing photo capture and anomaly reports ... such roofs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial condition/anomaly reporting on large low-slope and complex roofs. Same environment (building rooftops) and same deliverable (defect report on a completed roof surface) as the close-out survey instance.

sources.system: Zeitview Property Insights Platform (drone thermal + AI)
sources.title: Drone Based Roofing Inspections: Zeitview Expands Software Platform
sources.claim: Drone-borne thermal/visual survey services are commercially offered for commercial roofs and are used to find moisture under a roof ... other rooftop anomalies such as ponding water, with AI-based anomaly detection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: non-destructive moisture survey of low-slope roofs (ASTM C1153-style infrared). Same objects and rooftops as the close-out survey instance; cited only as corroboration since capture autonomy is not established.

sources.developer: NYU (Kevin Lee, Wei-Heng Lin, Talha Javed, Chen Feng)
sources.title: Roofus: Learning-based Robotic Moisture Mapping on Flat Rooftops with Ground Penetrating Radar
sources.claim: The state of the art for contact-based rooftop moisture/leak detection robotics is a research prototype that is remotely controlled, not autonomous, and only maps subsurface moisture rather than verifying seams or flashings.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related task: on-roof moisture detection. Cited to show that on-surface rooftop inspection robotics remain teleoperated research prototypes, so they cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Renovate Robotics puts Rufus to work on roofs - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The only robot piloted on residential roofs is a shingle-installation machine, not an inspection system; it is a cable-suspended prototype in contractor pilots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic work on steep-slope residential roofs. Shows machine locomotion on roofs exists, but the system installs shingles and performs no watertightness verification, so it does not transfer to the inspection instances.

tasks.label: Set ladders, scaffolds, and hoists in place for taking supplies to roofs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential steep-slope re-roof: helper carries a 24-32 ft fiberglass extension ladder from the truck across a lawn, sets the feet on soft/uneven ground beside shrubs or a deck, levels the footing, raises and extends the fly section, sets the correct 4:1 angle above the eave, and ties off the top rail so the crew can climb and carry bundles.

Residential re-roof: setting a ladder hoist / shingle conveyor at the eave - positioning the trailer-mounted or knock-down hoist on the driveway or lawn, extending and angling the track to the roof edge, leveling and stabilizing the base, attaching the eave hook/roof-top standoff, and running power so bundles can be sent up.

Low-rise multi-family or light commercial roof job: erecting frame scaffolding or pump jacks along a wall - laying mud sills and base plates on gravel/asphalt, stacking and pinning frames, installing cross braces, planks and guardrails to parapet height, and tying the run to the structure.

Re-roof at an institution-controlled facility (school, warehouse, plant): setting a ladder or fixed access tower and a material hoist in a paved staging area cordoned off by the owner, anchoring the hoist to the parapet, and setting a roof-edge ladder for supply runs.

Repositioning during the workday and takedown: moving ladders and light scaffold sections repeatedly around the building as the crew works each elevation, working past landscaping, driveways, HVAC units and dropped debris, then striking all access equipment and loading it at day's end.

sources.system: House of Design robotic truss assembly line (Builders FirstSource Villa Rica)
sources.developer: House of Design Robotics / Builders FirstSource
sources.title: BFS shares its high-tech aspirations | HBS Dealer
sources.claim: Deployed industrial robot lines in US truss plants (House of Design systems at Builders FirstSource's Villa Rica, GA facility) autonomously lift long dimensional lumber, pre-plate it and assemble roof/floor trusses inside fenced plant cells with a small human crew.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling and assembly of long structural lumber members. Transfer: the objects (long, heavy, unwieldy rigid members of ladder-like scale), the required placement precision, and the fixtured, fenced-cell presentation match the E1 counterfactual of setting a ladder or scaffold component that is presented to the machine in a known pose.

sources.system: Spatial Timber Assemblies / Robotic Fabrication Laboratory robots
sources.developer: ETH Zurich (NCCR Digital Fabrication) with Erne AG Holzbau
sources.title: Robotic collaboration in timber construction | ETH Zurich
sources.claim: Two large industrial robots in ETH Zurich's Robotic Fabrication Laboratory cut, drilled and cooperatively positioned long timber beams into precise three-dimensional frame arrangements for load-bearing modules of a real building (DFAB HOUSE), with collision-free paths recomputed as the structure grew.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic erection of a three-dimensional frame from long beams. Transfer: erecting a scaffold bay or leaning/positioning a ladder in a purpose-built cell involves the same class of long rigid members, similar payloads, and spatial positioning against a fixed reference structure.

sources.system: Robotic windshield insertion cells (e.g., EzRG 3D-vision guided insertion)
sources.developer: Automotive OEM integrators / LMI Technologies (Gocator sensors)
sources.title: Sensors Make Robots Smarter When Inserting Vehicle Windshields | Assembly Magazine
sources.claim: In automotive final-assembly cells, large six-axis robots pick a bulky rigid panel (a windshield) from a fixed presentation point with suction tooling and insert it at a predetermined location, with 3D-vision guidance achieving sub-millimetre placement accuracy.

tasks.label: Clean work areas and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential steep-slope tear-off in progress: helper clears torn-off shingles, felt and nail-studded scrap from tarps and the ground into a roll-off dumpster or dump trailer, drags and shakes out tarps, and keeps walkways and the ladder area clear through the day.

Residential steep-slope roof surface clean-down: sweeping and blowing loose granules, cut-off shingle scraps and stray nails off the exposed deck before underlayment and off the finished shingles at day's end, working on a pitched surface at height.

Commercial low-slope reroof: sweeping/vacuuming a large flat deck and membrane free of dust, insulation scraps, old fasteners and cut-offs before the next layer goes down, and keeping the material staging area on the roof tidy.
Job completion on paved surfaces: rolling a magnetic sweeper over the driveway, walkways and street and blowing them off so no nails or shingle grit remain before the homeowner walk-through.
Job completion on landscaping: hand-picking shingle scraps, felt pieces, wrappers and nails out of lawn, mulch and rock beds, shrubs and window wells around the perimeter of the house.

Cleaning tools and equipment at day's end: scraping hardened asphalt, tar and mastic off shovels, spud bars and tear-off bars, cleaning the kettle, hoses and buckets, washing brushes, rollers and sprayers, wiping down power tools, and sweeping out the truck bed and trailer.

sources.title: Tennant Company Unveils X16 SWEEP for Autonomous, Around-the-Clock Industrial Sweeping

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous machine sweeping of work-area floors. It transfers to the roofer helper's surface clean-down because the action (driving a powered sweeper over a flat work surface to remove grit, dust and small hard debris such as nails and scrap) and the accepted output (a debris-free work surface) are the same; only the surface's location differs.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cleaning of work-area floors in occupied facilities. sources.title: Trombia Free - Autonomous Street Sweeper

tasks.label: Maintain tools and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-day cleaning of hand tools and equipment fouled with roofing cement, hot asphalt, mastic, sealant and shingle grit — trowels, spud bars, tear-off shovels, brooms, buckets, mop carts, kettle/melter parts — scraped, wire-brushed and solvent- or diesel-wiped in the driveway, on the tailgate or back at the contractor's yard, with tools pulled at random from a pile.

Routine fluid service of powered equipment on the job: refueling the gas compressor, generator, and shingle-hoist/ladder-lift engines from cans, checking and topping engine oil, oiling pneumatic nailers at the air fitting, greasing hoist rollers and cart wheels, draining compressor tank condensate.

Fault servicing and minor repair of tools: clearing jammed nail guns, replacing worn or torn air hoses, couplers and O-rings, cleaning or replacing air filters and spark plugs, retightening loose fasteners, swapping damaged handles or driver tips, and flagging tools that need shop repair.

Inspecting and maintaining fall-protection and access equipment: checking harnesses, lanyards, lifelines and rope grabs for cuts, tar contamination and wear, wiping and cleaning them, checking ladder rungs/feet, roof brackets and jacks, tagging and removing defective gear from service, then coiling ropes and storing the gear.

Blade and cutting-edge maintenance: changing utility-knife and shingle-cutter blades, swapping and sharpening circular-saw and cut-off blades, filing or grinding shovel, spud-bar and hatchet edges — done at the truck, in the shop, or at the company yard's bench grinder.

Housekeeping and stowage of the tool inventory: washing down equipment, coiling and hanging air hoses and cords, sweeping out the tool trailer/truck bed, restocking and organizing gang boxes and racks, charging tool batteries, and checking that all tools came back from the job.

tasks.label: Provide assistance to skilled roofers installing and repairing roofs, flashings, and surfaces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Steep-slope residential reroof: helper hauls and stages shingle bundles, underlayment rolls and nail coils on a pitched roof, hands shingles/fasteners/tools to the skilled roofer as he courses, holds drip edge, underlayment and starter pieces while they are nailed, and repositions ladders, hoses and compressors as the crew moves around the roof.

Tear-off support on a reroof: helper strips old shingles and felt with a shovel/spud bar, pries out fasteners, pushes debris to the edge into a dumpster or Equipter, and preps the deck so the skilled roofer can begin dry-in.

Low-slope commercial reroof (TPO/EPDM/mod-bit): helper carries and stages insulation boards, membrane rolls, fastener buckets and adhesive across a flat deck, feeds sheets and plates to the roofer, holds membrane edges and flashing while they are welded or torched, and keeps the deck swept ahead of the work.

Ground and staging support: helper unloads a material delivery, stages bundles/rolls/coil near the structure, loads and runs a ladder hoist or conveyor to send material up, fetches specific tools and cut trim/flashing pieces on request, and keeps fasteners and sealant flowing to the roof crew.

Service call / detail repair assist: on a small repair (chimney, valley, skylight, pipe boot), helper holds step or counter flashing and patch pieces in position at awkward angles while the roofer fastens and seals, passes sealant, snips and small metal pieces, and steadies material in wind.

End-of-job cleanup of the work area: sweeping granules, nails, scrap and debris off decks, walkways and the staging area, collecting scrap into bins, and wiping down/cleaning tools and equipment before loading out.
