tasks.label: Locate worn or torn areas in roofs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential steep-slope asphalt-shingle roof at a repair/estimate or storm-claim call: get on/over the roof and find missing, torn, curled, blistered or hail-bruised shingles, worn granule loss and damaged flashing, then report/mark each location for the roofer. Roof is a private home taken as found (trees, pitch, varying facets).

Low-slope commercial or institutional roof (EPDM/TPO/BUR on a store, school, warehouse): survey a large field of membrane for splits, punctures, open seams, blisters, ponding areas and worn spots around penetrations and curbs; sometimes a thermal scan for suspected wet insulation. Rooftop is weathered and cluttered with HVAC units, taken as found.

Leak call: trace an active leak from an interior water stain back to its source — inspect the attic/underside, then check flashing, valleys, penetrations and laps on the roof by hand, lifting shingles or probing sealant, sometimes running a hose test, to pinpoint the torn or worn spot.

During tear-off/repair on an active job: after shingles and felt are stripped, walk the exposed deck amid crew, tools and debris, feeling for spongy/soft sheathing and spotting rot, delamination and holes, and chalk-mark the sections needing replacement before dry-in.

Steep, tall or complex roofs and non-shingle materials (tile, slate, standing-seam metal, multi-story or cut-up roofs with dormers): locate cracked or slipped tiles, rusted or torn panels, worn coatings and damaged flashing where footing/access is hazardous.

tasks.label: Sweep and clean roofs to prepare them for the application of new roofing materials.

instances.label: Steep-slope residential re-roof: after tear-off, the helper sweeps the exposed deck clear of loose nails, old granules, shingle fragments and sawdust with broom, magnetic sweeper and blower, working on a 4:12-8:12 pitch in a harness, so underlayment can go down the same day.

Low-slope commercial/industrial roof (warehouse, school, retail): before membrane, coating or adhesive is applied, the helper sweeps and power-blows a large flat deck clear of dust, grit, gravel, torn insulation scraps and fasteners, leaving it clean enough for adhesion.

Residential recover/repair prep without full tear-off: the helper brooms and blows leaves, pine needles, moss, dirt and loose granules off existing shingles or tile and out of valleys, so new material or patching can be applied over a clean surface.

Detail cleanup: scooping packed wet leaves and grit out of gutters, valleys, crickets and around chimneys, vents and HVAC curbs by hand and scoop, then carrying or shoveling the collected debris to a chute, tarp or ground dumpster.

Adverse conditions and cut-up geometry: cleaning a damp, windy or very hot roof with multiple planes, dormers, hips and steep pitch, tight access, and clutter of tools and material bundles, with the crew moving on the same surface.

tasks.label: Remove old roofing materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential steep-slope tear-off: on a single-family house (pitch roughly 4/12–10/12), the helper drives a tear-off shovel/pitchfork under 1–3 layers of asphalt shingles and underlayment, pries them free with nails, works around valleys, vents, skylights and chimneys, and pushes the debris down to tarps or a dumpster while staying tied off on a sloped, slippery surface.

Deck detail work after the field shingles are off the same residential roof: pulling remaining nails and staples, prying off drip edge, step and valley flashing, ridge cap and stuck ice-and-water shield, sweeping/blowing the deck clean, and flagging soft or rotten sheathing for the roofer.

Commercial low-slope tear-off: on a warehouse, school or strip-mall roof, cutting built-up/gravel, modified bitumen or EPDM/TPO membrane and insulation into strips with a powered cutter, prying strips and fasteners off a metal, wood or concrete deck, and moving the wet, heavy debris around HVAC curbs, pipes and drains to a chute, crane bucket or debris trailer.

Specialty or heavy material removal: clay/concrete tile, slate, wood shake or standing-seam metal panels stripped from a residential or institutional roof, often with pieces salvaged intact and stacked, on fragile or high-pitch surfaces where foot placement and breakage matter.

Partial/selective removal for repair or storm damage: opening a limited area around a leak, hail-damaged section or blown-off patch — cutting straight lines, removing only the damaged shingles, underlayment and sometimes a sheet of decking, on a roof of unknown condition, often on short notice and under tarps.

sources.title: Introducing Rufus, the Automated Roofing Robot from Renovate Robotics | Roofing Contractor
sources.claim: Renovate Robotics' Rufus is a cable-driven robot that autonomously installs asphalt shingles on residential ...; shingle tear-off is only a roadmap item, not a demonstrated capability.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task: autonomous shingle installation on the same residential steep-slope roofs with the same materials. Transfer fails for this task — removal requires prying fastened, brittle, unknown-condition layers loose and clearing debris, and the developer itself lists tear-off as future roadmap capability, so no completion of removal is substantiated.

sources.title: Beacon Announces Partnership with Renovate Robotics | Roofing Contractor
sources.claim: As of mid-2025, after a distribution partnership with Beacon, Rufus's marketed capability is still asphalt shingle installation on residential roofs, with tear-off described as a plan.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (shingle installation) and same environment (residential roofs); cited to date the state of the art in 2025 and to show removal is still an announced intention rather than a demonstrated capability.

sources.date: 2025-08 (page), models in commercial use for years
sources.title: Why Brokk – Original demolition power
sources.claim: Brokk machines, the standard 'demolition robots' used for selective demolition including stripping decks and coverings, are remote-controlled by a human operator throughout the work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: selective demolition/stripping of building surfaces, sometimes on roof decks. It cannot support a positive judgment because operation is continuous teleoperation, not autonomous work.

sources.title: The Machine – Robotics & AI Helping Reclaim Waste Wood | Urban Machine
sources.claim: Urban Machine's container-sized machine autonomously locates and extracts nails, screws and staples from reclaimed dimensional lumber using vision, gantries and robotic end-effectors; it is in commercial operation at a California C&D recycling facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fastener removal from old construction wood inside a purpose-built, fixtured machine — the nearest E1 analogue. Transfer to roof tear-off fails: it processes loose, clamped boards fed on a conveyor, and does not strip bonded shingle/felt/membrane layers off an intact roof assembly or handle the resulting debris.

tasks.label: Perform emergency leak repairs and general maintenance for a variety of roof types.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential steep-slope asphalt-shingle roof at an occupied single-family home: homeowner reports a ceiling stain; helper carries tools/materials up a ladder, works with the roofer to trace the leak to a pipe boot, valley, chimney flashing or nail pops, lifts and replaces cracked shingles, sets a new boot, applies roof cement, then cleans debris from roof and yard. Varied pitch, ladder access, weather-limited window.

Post-storm emergency call-out on a damaged residential roof: wet, windy conditions, blown-off shingles and exposed decking; helper hauls and unrolls heavy tarps, holds them while they are battened and nailed to sound framing, seals temporary patches, and clears blown debris, all on a same-day urgent schedule.

Low-slope commercial roof (TPO/EPDM/modified bitumen) at a school, warehouse or retail center under a maintenance contract: access by roof hatch, walk the roof to find punctures and open seams around HVAC curbs and drains, clear ponded debris and drain strainers, clean and prime the area, cut and hot-air-weld or adhere patches, re-caulk pitch pans and reseal fastener plates.

Specialty roof types — clay/concrete tile, slate, or standing-seam metal on homes and small commercial buildings: replace cracked tiles or slates without breaking neighbors, reseal exposed fasteners and lap seams on metal panels, rebuild flashing at walls and skylights; fragile, slippery, steep surfaces requiring walkboards and fall protection.

Routine preventive-maintenance visit: clear gutters, downspouts and valleys of leaves and grit, remove moss and debris, re-caulk penetrations and exposed nail heads, touch up small flashing defects, and afterward load leftover material, clean sealant guns and tools, and police the site.

sources.title: Rufus roofing robot installs shingles three times faster than a human
sources.claim: Rufus, a cable-driven gantry robot, installs asphalt shingles autonomously on steep-slope residential roofs and is doing paid roofing jobs in New Jersey ...; its scope is new shingle placement on a prepared deck, with tear-off still a roadmap item.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: asphalt shingle installation during re-roofing, on the same residential roof surfaces. It does not transfer to emergency leak repair or maintenance: the robot places new shingles on a stripped deck in bulk and cannot locate a leak, selectively remove damaged material, replace a pipe boot, rebuild flashing, or apply sealant; the company lists automated tear-off as future work.

sources.title: Rufus Roofing Robot Explained: What Does It Change?
sources.claim: Independent coverage confirms Rufus is limited in autonomy and requires a ground team to ... that its function is asphalt shingle installation on steep-slope ....
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (shingle installation); cited to bound the autonomy claim, showing the frontier roofing robot still depends on a ground crew and covers only shingle laying, not leak diagnosis or repair.

sources.title: Sherpa Cleaning Drone | Exterior Building Washing Robot | Lucid Bots
sources.claim: The most widely deployed commercial exterior-cleaning drone in North America performs roof and facade washing but is flown by a certified pilot with a ground crew member, i.e. it is teleoperated and does no repair work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: exterior roof/facade cleaning, part of general building maintenance at height. It does not substantiate leak repair: the platform only sprays water/soap under continuous pilot control and carries no fasteners, patches, or sealant tooling.

sources.title: Apellix Spray Painting Drone Goes to Work in the Field for State DOTs, Federal Contractors, and Commercial Coating Firms
sources.claim: Apellix's aerial coating system sprays paint and coatings on tilt-up warehouses, bridges and tanks in the field, but is described as semi-autonomous and operated with a ground-based crew.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying protective coatings to building exteriors, adjacent to roof coating/maintenance. It does not transfer: coating a large surface under pilot supervision does not include leak location, surface repair, membrane patching, or flashing work, and the system is not autonomous.

sources.title: Welding roofing membranes on flat roofs | Leister
sources.claim: Automated hot-air welding machines for thermoplastic roof membranes are self-propelled seam welders used by roofing crews on flat roofs; they weld overlap seams but are positioned, steered along the lap and supervised by an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hot-air welding of single-ply membrane seams, the core joining step in low-slope roof patching. It does not substantiate the repair instance: the machine is a hand-placed, operator-guided tool that welds straight laps only, and cannot survey a roof, find punctures, clear drains, cut patches, or detail around curbs and pitch pans.

tasks.label: Unload materials and tools from work trucks, and unroll roofing as directed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential re-roof: helper unloads loose 70–80 lb asphalt shingle bundles, rolls of felt/synthetic underlayment, drip edge and starter, plus a nail gun, hose and compressor from a pickup/flatbed parked in a sloped driveway; carries and stages them on the lawn or hands them up a ladder, working around parked cars, landscaping and homeowners.

Residential steep-slope deck: helper positions a roll of felt/synthetic underlayment at the eave and unrolls it across the deck as the roofer directs, keeping the run straight, holding the specified head/side laps to the chalk line, and tacking it while working on a pitched, sometimes windy surface.

Commercial flat roof: helper unloads palletized/banded bulk material — TPO or EPDM membrane rolls, polyiso insulation boards, cartons of plates and fasteners — from a box truck or delivery trailer at the jobsite and stages it at the crane/hoist point on uneven ground.

Commercial flat roof: helper drags heavy (150–250 lb) membrane rolls into position on the deck and unrolls them to the layout lines as directed, letting them relax, squaring the sheet and aligning the seam overlap before the roofer fastens or welds.

Tools and consumables only: helper unloads hand tools, buckets of roof cement, torches and propane bottles, tear-off shovels, brooms, magnets, tarps and ladders from the truck bed and stages them where the crew wants them at the start or end of the day.

sources.title: Walmart brings autonomous forklifts to 4 distribution centers | Grocery Dive
sources.claim: FoxBot autonomous forklifts unload palletized freight from trailers at Walmart distribution center docks, using machine vision and planning, in commercial deployment across four DCs after a 16-month proof of concept.

sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics — Automated Warehouse

sources.title: Bundle Palletizer Equipment - shingle production
sources.claim: Reichel & Drews supplies an automatic bundle palletizer for asphalt shingle plants that receives shingle bundles off the line, positions them and stacks them on pallets in a controlled sequence.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine handling of the exact object the helper carries (asphalt shingle bundles), transferring them from a presented position to a stack. It substantiates bundle handling only where a purpose-built line fixtures and presents each bundle.

sources.title: FANUC M-410iB/700 | 700 kg Payload Palletizer Robot | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC's M-410 family of dedicated palletizing robots handles payloads up to 700 kg with ... in end-of-line cells, stacking boxes, bags, pails and drums.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heavy, repetitive material transfer in a fenced cell. Transfers to unloading heavy roofing bundles, rolls, buckets and tool cases only when each item arrives at a known, fixtured position, which is the E1 presentation condition.

sources.system: Automated Fiber Placement / Automated Tape Laying machines
sources.title: Today's Reality - Aerospace Manufacturing and Design

sources.title: Beacon Announces Partnership with Renovate Robotics | Roofing Contractor

sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing roofing material on a real residential roof (E3). tasks.label: Hoist tar and roofing materials to roofs, using ropes and pulleys, or carry materials up ladders.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential steep-slope tear-off/re-roof at a private home: helper repeatedly shoulders 60-80 lb asphalt shingle bundles from a driveway stack, climbs an extension ladder set on lawn/driveway, walks a 4:12-8:12 pitch, and stacks bundles along the ridge and on staging brackets; wind, heat, landscaping and debris underfoot.

Residential or light-commercial job using a ladder hoist/shingle elevator or conveyor truck: helper loads bundles, rolls of underlayment and drip edge onto the hoist carriage at ground level, climbs to the eave, unloads each carriage load at the roof edge and stacks it on the deck, keeping pace with the crew.

Low-slope commercial re-roof: rolls of modified bitumen/TPO, insulation boards, fastener buckets and adhesive pails are hoisted by rope-and-pulley, roof hoist or crane/telehandler-placed pallets; helper rigs loads below, receives and unrigs them at the parapet, then carts and distributes material across a large deck cluttered with HVAC curbs, pipes and torn-off debris.

Frequent short trips up ladders during the day carrying tools, nail boxes, flashing, ridge cap, sealant tubes, small buckets and a rope-hauled tool bucket; hands partly occupied, ladder footed on varied ground, roof edge transition at the top.

Hot built-up roofing/tar work: helper fills and hoists 5-gallon buckets of hot asphalt from a ground kettle by rope and pulley (or tends the mop cart and felt rolls), managing heat, fumes and spill hazards at the roof edge.

sources.title: Bundle Palletizer - Shingle Production Equipment - Reichel Drews
sources.claim: A commercially supplied, fully automatic palletizing system receives asphalt shingle bundles on a conveyor, orients them and stacks them layer by layer onto pallets inside a purpose-built shingle production line — i.e., autonomous handling of exactly the heavy bundles roofer helpers carry, when the work is presented to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory palletizing of shingle bundles. Same objects (asphalt shingle bundles, ~70 lb) and same act (lift, transport, stack at a designated position) as the helper's staging of material, in a machine-built cell.

sources.system: Interlake Mecalux Unit Load AS/RS (pallet stacker cranes)
sources.title: Stacker Cranes (AS/RS for Pallets) - Interlake Mecalux
sources.claim: Unit-load AS/RS stacker cranes autonomously lift and place full pallets of material at heights approaching 100 ft in purpose-built rack aisles, under warehouse-management software with no human in the aisle — vertical transport of heavy palletized loads to an elevated placement point.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated high-bay pallet putaway. It is the E1 form of 'hoist materials to height': loads arrive fixtured on pallets at a conveyor infeed and the machine raises and deposits them at a defined elevated location, well above roof heights and at far greater weights.

sources.system: Motion Controls Robotics roofing-industry robot cells (FANUC M-410, R-2000)
sources.title: Robots for Roofing Material Manufacturing - Motion Controls Robotics
sources.claim: FANUC-based robotic cells built by a certified integrator handle roofing materials specifically — palletizing rolls of roofing sheet, bundles of shingles and containers of roof sealant/coating — with vision-guided picking and conveyor infeed in fenced cells.

sources.system: Foundry pouring/ladling robot cells (e.g., Motoman/Comau foundry robots)

Transfers to hoisting/pouring hot asphalt in an E1 cell: comparable hot-liquid vessels handled at far higher temperatures with fixtured presentation; only the vertical transport is added, covered by the AS/RS evidence.

sources.title: KEWAZO LIFTBOT - Edison Awards
sources.claim: A commercially deployed robotic hoist clamps to scaffolding and moves scaffold parts and materials vertically on construction sites and in industrial plants (including a BASF plant), but workers still load and unload it and the company describes it as remote-controlled, so it automates only the vertical leg of the material-supply task.
sources.transferJustification: Closest jobsite analogue to hoisting materials to height, but loading and unloading remain manual and control mode is remote/unclear, so it cannot support a positive judgment for the whole instance.

sources.title: Introducing Rufus, the Automated Roofing Robot from Renovate Robotics | Roofing Contractor
sources.claim: The only robot working on actual asphalt-shingle roofs is a cable-driven gantry that is placed on the roof and installs shingles; it is a prototype in testing, and material still has to be brought to the roof by the crew, so no on-roof system performs the hoisting/carrying task.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-roof shingle installation. Cited to show that even the most advanced roof robot does not transport material from ground to roof, supporting the negative E3/E2 judgments.

tasks.label: Clear drains and downspouts and clean gutters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-story or story-and-a-half house on a re-roof or service call: helper works off an extension ladder, hand-scoops and blows wet leaves, pine needles, shingle grit and mud out of the K-style gutter trough, bags it, and repositions the ladder every 8-10 ft around the house.

Clearing a blocked downspout/leader or drain leader: flushing with a hose, running a snake or blower down the pipe, sometimes disassembling elbows or a drain strainer to break out compacted sludge, roots or a nest, then verifying flow at the outlet or underground line.

Two- or three-story house or steep-slope roof with dormers and valleys: gutters reached from a tall ladder, from the roof on a harness, or from a lift; helper clears packed needles and grit from long runs and from valleys above the gutter line, in wind and on pitched footing.

Low-slope commercial/institutional roof (school, warehouse, apartment block, retail center) under facility control: helper pulls strainer domes on internal roof drains, scoops out ponded leaves and sludge, clears scuppers and overflow drains, and checks that each drain runs before leaving.

End-of-job cleanup after a tear-off: flushing shingle granules, nail heads, tar chunks and underlayment scraps out of gutters and roof drains, picking debris from the ground at the downspout discharge, and confirming the drainage system flows before sign-off.

sources.title: iRobot Looj 330 Gutter Cleaning Robot Fast Facts (iRobot media)
sources.claim: The iRobot Looj 330 is a commercial gutter-cleaning robot that drives along a rain-gutter trough and augers/ejects leaves, clogs and grit; it has an autonomous CLEAN mode in which it travels and cleans the trough on its own after a person places it in the gutter.

sources.title: iRobot Looj M330 Gutter Cleaner Review - Trusted Reviews
sources.claim: Independent trade-press testing of the Looj in real house gutters confirms it runs in 'Auto' and clears heavy leaf/mud/moss loads, though it ejects debris messily onto the roof and surroundings and can bog down in compacted wet muck.

sources.title: Looj 330 Gutter Cleaning Robot Review - A & A Services Home Improvement
sources.claim: The Looj does not perform the whole job on a building: a person must still climb the ladder to place, retrieve and reposition it for each gutter run, and it does not clear downspouts.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (gutter cleaning) - documents the human ladder and placement work the robot does not do, bounding the E3 judgment.

sources.title: Beacon Announces Partnership with Renovate Robotics | Roofing Contractor
sources.claim: Renovate Robotics' Rufus is a cable-suspended robot that autonomously installs asphalt shingles on residential ... being piloted with contractors; it is the closest autonomous system working on real house roofs, but it works on the roof plane and does not reach into gutters or clear drains.
sources.transferJustification: Related roofing task in the same E3 setting (residential roofs); cited to show that the state of the art on real roofs does not extend to scooping debris from gutters or servicing drains.

sources.title: Skyline Robotics deploys Ozmo window cleaning robot in New York City - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Skyline Robotics' Ozmo autonomously cleans glass on a high-rise facade from a building maintenance unit with a human supervising on the roof - at-height exterior cleaning autonomy exists, but it is limited to wiping flat glass on a BMU-equipped tower, not removing debris from gutters or roof drains.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous exterior building cleaning at height in an institution-controlled facility); cited to show the only deployed at-height cleaning autonomy handles flat glass via a BMU and does not transfer to scooping wet debris from gutters or drain sumps.

sources.title: Sherpa Cleaning Drone | Exterior Building Washing Robot | Lucid Bots
sources.claim: Commercial drone-based exterior building cleaning, the method marketed for gutter and roof cleaning at height, is flown by a human pilot with ground crew - teleoperated, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (washing/clearing building exteriors at height, sold as gutter and roof cleaning); cited to establish these systems are pilot-flown and cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Cover roofs with layers of roofing felt or asphalt strips before installing tile, slate, or composition materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Simple residential re-roof: after tear-off on a single-family home's gable roof, the helper snaps chalk lines and rolls out 36-in synthetic underlayment (or 15# felt) course by course up the slope, keeping it flat and square, lapping 2-4 in, cutting rolls at rakes/hips, and fastening with cap nails; working on a 4:12-8:12 pitch at height, in wind and sun, around the crew and hoses.

Cut-up residential roof: same underlayment work but on a complex deck with dormers, valleys, hips, skylights, chimneys and plumbing vents, plus self-adhered ice-and-water shield at eaves and valleys; requires trimming, weaving into valleys, cutting around penetrations and tying into drip edge and step flashing on steep (8:12+) planes.

New-construction tract housing: fresh plywood/OSB deck on an active jobsite; helper drags rolls up, dries in the whole roof with underlayment ahead of the shingle crew, often on multiple planes of a two-story house, with debris, staged materials and other trades present.

Tile or slate roof prep in the Southwest/coastal markets: laying two-ply or high-temp/self-adhered underlayment over a steep deck, hot conditions, followed by battens or anchor sheet before heavy tile is loaded and set.

Small commercial or multifamily steep-slope roof (apartment buildings, strip retail, church): larger, mostly uninterrupted decks covered with felt/base sheet before composition shingles; roof accessed by ladder or lift, curbs, HVAC penetrations and parapets present, work coordinated with a building owner or GC.

sources.title: Rufus roofing robot installs shingles three times faster than a human
sources.claim: Renovate Robotics' Rufus is an autonomous cable-driven roofing robot that installs asphalt shingles on real residential roofs in New Jersey and Pennsylvania — the most advanced deployed steep-slope roofing robot, but its work is shingle placement and nailing, not underlayment.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic system to this task (same roofs, same trade), cited to establish the frontier; it starts only after the underlayment step this task covers.

sources.title: Robots Revolutionize Construction: A New Era of Building Efficiency and Safety
sources.claim: Rufus begins work only after humans have installed the underlayment and dried in the roof; the robot places and nails shingles on the already-covered deck.
sources.transferJustification: Directly delimits the frontier system's scope: felt/underlayment application is excluded from the robot's work.

sources.title: Robotics in Roofing | Roofing Contractor

sources.transferJustification: Explicitly identifies underlayment installation as outside current roofing-robot capability.

sources.title: Beacon Announces Partnership with Renovate Robotics | Roofing Contractor
sources.claim: Renovate's commercial launch and published roadmap cover shingle installation, tear-off, shingle cutting and solar bracket/shingle work — no underlayment capability.
sources.transferJustification: Confirms the deployed product scope is shingle installation only, so no cited system covers the felt/underlayment step.

sources.title: WEINMANN multifunction bridges | HOMAG
sources.claim: Factory panel lines (WEINMANN multifunction bridges) automatically fasten and format rigid sheathing on fixtured wall, roof and floor elements, but the documented processes are boards, battens and insulation — not unrolling, lapping and cap-fastening rolled roofing felt or underlayment.

tasks.label: Attach sheets of metal to roof boards or building frameworks when installing metal roofs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Steep-slope residential/light-commercial metal roof over solid deck and underlayment: helper hauls exposed-fastener ribbed panels up a ladder or hoist, sets them to a chalk line, laps ribs, and drives self-drilling screws with EPDM washers to correct depth while working on a pitched surface with fall protection, wind and heat.

Large low-slope commercial/industrial roof (warehouse, school, big-box): bundles craned onto the roof, helper positions wide panels or metal deck over insulation/purlins, screws long fastener rows in repetitive field areas, working around curbs, skylights, HVAC units and open edges.

Cut-up or retrofit work: dormers, hips, valleys, panels field-measured and cut around chimneys, vents, skylights and existing walls; small tear-off/repair jobs replacing individual damaged sheets on an existing roof with varied, non-standard geometry.

sources.title: LIGNA Product 2025: ZeroLabor Robotic System (Randek)

sources.system: ABB IRB welding robot line at CIMC container plant (Fenggang)

sources.system: KUKA KS Framer body-in-white framing station
sources.title: KS Framer: the best basis for vehicle bodies | KUKA Austria

tasks.label: Apply shingles, gravel, or asphalt over the top layer of tar to protect the roofing material.

instances.label: Residential steep-slope reroof: helper lays and nails courses of asphalt shingles across the open field of large, walkable-pitch gable/hip planes over underlayment (and roof cement at low-slope transitions), keeping courses straight and offsets correct, working with the crew on a suburban house.

Residential cut-up roof: shingles must be cut and fitted at valleys, dormers, skylights, pipe/vent penetrations and step flashing, bedded in roofing cement/tar, plus hip and ridge caps; steeper pitches, small planes, obstructions.

Commercial/industrial low-slope built-up roof: after the kettle-fed hot asphalt flood coat is poured/mopped, the helper broadcasts pea gravel or slag ballast evenly into the hot bitumen across a large flat roof (buckets, shovels, wheeled spreader), around drains, curbs and equipment.

Low-slope roof top ply: helper rolls out and embeds a mineral-surfaced cap sheet / modified-bitumen top ply into hot mopped asphalt (or spreads a flood/asphalt coating as the final protective layer) over the built-up plies, brooming it in.

Repair and patch work: applying a few shingles, a gravel top-dressing, or asphalt/mastic over tar patches at flashings, penetrations, blisters or a small torn-off section, on either a house or an occupied commercial building; irregular geometry, ladder access, cluttered rooftop.

sources.system: Granule applicator / high-speed granule delivery system on asphalt roofing production lines
sources.developer: Owens Corning (patented granule delivery systems used in asphalt roofing plants)
sources.title: High speed granule delivery system and method (US 9,555,439)
sources.claim: Automated granule applicators in asphalt roofing plants broadcast protective mineral granules onto a hot asphalt-coated web under machine control — the same protect-the-bitumen surfacing operation performed by hand on a built-up roof.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory mineral surfacing of bitumen roofing. Same materials (hot asphalt and mineral gravel/granules), same purpose (embed a protective mineral layer in the hot bitumen before it cools) and the same coverage-uniformity tolerance; the difference is only that the roofing sheet is conveyed to the applicator instead of the applicator being carried onto the roof, which is exactly the E1 counterfactual.

sources.claim: Commercially sold, fully automated bituminous membrane and shingle production lines coat reinforcement sheet with hot bitumen and dose mineral granules onto its surface; Euroline supplied such a line to roofing manufacturer Tarco in Belton, Texas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine application of the hot-bitumen top layer and its protective mineral surfacing to roofing sheet. Materials (hot asphalt, granule surfacing, cap-sheet ply), the bonding-while-hot constraint and the uniform-coverage quality standard match the roof-top flood-coat/cap-sheet operation; the work is brought to the machine, as the E1 counterfactual specifies.

sources.system: Euroline High-speed Combination Production Line at Tarco, Belton TX
sources.title: Tarco Announces Manufacturing Capability Enhancement
sources.claim: The Euroline line installed at Tarco's Belton, Texas plant to make bituminous roofing membrane is fully automated and electronically controlled with thickness measurement and auto-correction.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above: this is a deployed instance of a machine that applies the hot bitumen top layer and mineral surfacing to roofing material under machine control in a purpose-built setting.

tasks.label: Chop tar into small pieces, and heat chopped tar in kettles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial low-slope built-up reroof: kettle on a trailer in the building's parking lot or lay-down area. Helper breaks 100-lb paper-wrapped asphalt kegs into chunks with an axe/spud bar, lifts and drops chunks through the kettle lid, lights and tends the burners, watches the thermometer to hold roughly 425-500 F below the flash point, tops the kettle off through the day, and keeps combustibles clear.

Urban tight-access job: kettle staged on a closed street lane, alley, or sidewalk closure beside a downtown building, with traffic, pedestrians, parked cars and curbs around it. Chopping and charging done in cramped space, kettle repositioned during the day, hot asphalt pumped or hoisted to the roof.

Small residential or small commercial repair/tear-off: kettle parked in a driveway or on a lawn edge with sloped, uneven ground and homeowner property nearby. Small batches of asphalt chopped from partial kegs, kettle heated, allowed to cool and reheated between intermittent mopping runs.

Coal-tar-pitch built-up roof on an institutional or industrial building: pitch delivered in kegs/cartons, broken up and charged at ground level near a loading dock, with tighter temperature limits than asphalt and heavy fume/burn exposure requiring careful, attentive tending.

Hot rubberized asphalt waterproofing (plaza deck, parking structure, or below-grade): 40-60 lb wrapped blocks or slabs are broken/unwrapped and fed into an oil-jacketed double-boiler melter on a trailer at grade, agitator run, material held at 350-400 F and drawn off as crews need it.

sources.system: Polygonmach PBD bitumen drum decanter / barrel heater series
sources.title: Bitumen Barrel Heaters and Drum Decanters - Polygon Machine
sources.claim: Polygonmach PBD-series bitumen barrel heaters / drum decanters are commercial plant machines that take solid bitumen packed in drums, feed it via an automated drum-feeding conveyor on the larger models (PBD-25 listed as 'Full Automatic' drum handling), melt it in a thermal-oil heated chamber held to +/-1 C, and pump the molten binder out automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Same material and same accepted output as the task: solid packaged asphalt/bitumen converted to hot liquid binder held at a controlled working temperature, with the solid charged into the heated vessel by machine rather than chopped and shovelled by hand.

sources.system: Kesar Bitumen Drum Decanter / Asphalt Drum Melter
sources.title: Bitumen Drum Decanter, Asphalt Drum Melter
sources.claim: Kesar bitumen drum decanters reheat and melt bitumen packed in drums and automatically transfer the melted bitumen from the decanter reservoir to bulk storage during the decanting process, at a set temperature.
sources.transferJustification: The task's purpose is producing hot, pumpable asphalt from solid asphalt at the right temperature; a drum decanter performs exactly that conversion and delivery step by machine in a purpose-built installation.

sources.title: Bitumen Decanting Machines | Bitumen drum melting Plants
sources.claim: Site bitumen decanting machines use a hydraulic flip-over device and hydraulic arm to move drums into the melting chamber, i.e. the heavy drum handling into the hot vessel is done by powered machinery rather than by a laborer.
sources.transferJustification: Describes machine handling of the heavy solid-asphalt package into the heated vessel, the mechanical equivalent of the helper lifting chopped chunks through the kettle lid; operator involvement in placing the drum is unclear, so it is treated as non-autonomous.

sources.title: Road Construction Bitumen Melter, Bitumen Heating Equipment For Bag / Box Packing
sources.claim: Commercial road-construction bitumen melters for bag/box-packed solid bitumen run closed-loop thermostatic heating: the burner cycles automatically to the set asphalt and thermal-oil temperature, and the circulation filter removes slag automatically.
sources.transferJustification: The 'heat chopped tar in kettles' half of the task is temperature tending of a fired melting vessel; this machine performs that closed-loop without an attendant watching a dial thermometer.

sources.title: Bitumen Melting Machine Manufacturer | Bitumen Melting Machine for Sale
sources.claim: Bitumen melting machines are built to extract solid bitumen by melting it out of its shipping packages - barrels, bags and wooden cases - so the packaged solid does not have to be chopped up by hand before heating.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that machine melting handles the same packaged solid asphalt forms the helper chops (kegs, blocks, cartons); autonomy of the feed is not stated, so it is not relied on alone.

sources.title: Robotic Furnace Tending Cell | Midwest Engineered Systems
sources.claim: Midwest Engineered Systems builds fenced robotic furnace-tending cells in which an industrial robot loads and unloads heavy steel workpieces into and out of furnace, quench and temper lines and runs continuously with minimal human involvement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: charging heavy solid material into a hot, fired vessel and tending it. Comparable object weight and hazard, comparable coarse placement precision, in a purpose-built fenced cell - the E1 analogue of loading a tar kettle.

sources.title: Industrial Robot Automatic Loading System - Join Industrial
sources.claim: Standard industrial robotic loading cells deliver raw material to a loading station by conveyor, tray or feeder, verify part presence and position with vision or sensors, and have the robot pick and place it, all coordinated by a cell PLC.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-fed charging of bulk workpieces in a fenced cell. It substantiates the E1 counterfactual premise that the asphalt kegs/blocks arrive fixtured and presented to the machine rather than being found in a stack on a job site.

sources.title: Renovate Robotics puts Rufus to work on roofs - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The only roofing-site robot in the field, Renovate Robotics' Rufus, is aimed at cable-suspended asphalt shingle installation on sloped residential roofs and is still in trial; no fielded roofing robot chops asphalt kegs or charges and tends a tar kettle at a job site.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only as the state of the art for robots working on roofing job sites; it handles light shingles, not 100-lb asphalt kegs, axes or 500 F kettles, so it supports no positive judgment at E2 or E3.

tasks.label: Attach roofing paper and composition shingles, using nails.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dry-in on a residential job: after tear-off or on a new deck, the helper rolls out felt or synthetic underlayment (plus self-adhered ice-and-water at eaves/valleys), laps courses to the printed lines, cap-nails it off, and cuts it around vent pipes and walls, working over a pitched deck outdoors.

Re-roof of an ordinary suburban house: on large, open, walkable planes (roughly 4:12-8:12), the helper snaps lines and lays and nails course after course of three-tab or architectural shingles with a coil nailer, keeping exposure and offsets, while the lead roofer handles flashings.

New-construction tract or custom home: clean plywood/OSB deck, dried in, simple gable or hip planes; the helper nails off the field courses of composition shingles on a builder-run site with other trades around.

Field shingling on hard roofs: steep pitch (10:12 and up) or two- and three-story planes needing roof jacks, toe boards and harnesses, or planes broken up by dormers, low overhead branches and tight access, where footing and staging dominate the work.

Detail and cut-in shingling: starter strips, cutting shingles with a hook blade at rakes and valleys, weaving or closed-cut valleys, fitting courses around chimneys, skylights, pipe boots and wall step flashing, and nailing hip and ridge caps.
Small jobs: patching wind- or hail-damaged sections and tying new shingles into existing courses, or shingling a garage, shed, porch or dormer roof of a few squares where setup time dominates.

tasks.label: Place tiles, nail them to roof boards, and cover nailheads with roofing cement.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field-tile courses on a new or replacement residential concrete/clay tile roof (Sun Belt): helper works off stacks of tiles already loaded on the deck, sets each tile on battens or direct-to-deck in offset courses, drives a nail through the pre-formed hole into the roof boards, and dabs roofing cement/mastic over exposed nailheads. Large open plane, moderate pitch, dry weather, highly repetitive.

Tile roof on a new commercial or multifamily building (apartments, hotel, HOA blocks): tiles hoisted and stocked mechanically, very long repetitive runs on large simple planes, same place-nail-cement cycle, sequenced by a GC on an active construction site.

Cut-up residential tile roof: tiles cut and fitted at hips, valleys, rakes and around chimneys, vents and skylights; hip and ridge tiles bedded in mortar/foam and nailed; exposed nails and cut edges sealed with roofing cement. Requires measuring, sawing brittle tile, and weathertight detailing on irregular geometry.

Repair/replacement on an existing occupied roof: locating and swapping cracked or slipped tiles/slates, lifting adjacent tiles, re-nailing into old roof boards, sealing nailheads and lifted edges with roofing cement, often an emergency leak call in marginal weather with unknown deck condition.

Slate roofing on steep-slope or historic homes (Northeast/Mid-Atlantic): placing slates in staggered courses on an uneven old deck, hand-nailing without over-driving or cracking, cementing nailheads and repair slates, working from staging on a steep pitch.

sources.title: Rufus roofing robot installs shingles three times faster than a human
sources.claim: Rufus is an autonomous cable-driven roofing robot that places and fastens asphalt shingles on real steep-slope residential roofs in New Jersey and Pennsylvania, but tile roofing is explicitly outside its scope and a ground team is still required.
sources.transferJustification: Closest on-roof system to this task (placing and fastening roofing units on a pitched roof). It shows in-situ roof automation exists only for asphalt shingles; the developer excludes tile, so it cannot substantiate tile placement, nailing and cement sealing at E2/E3.

sources.title: WEINMANN multifunction bridges
sources.claim: WEINMANN multifunction bridges perform planking of fixtured wall, ceiling, roof and gable elements fully automatically in a factory line, including fastening (nailing/stapling), formatting and cutting openings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatically nailing covering material onto a roof element held on a fixtured assembly table. This is the 'nail them to roof boards' step performed with the work brought to the machine, at production quality with CAD-driven positioning.

sources.title: LIGNA Product 2025: ZeroLabor Robotic System (Randek)
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor is a fully automatic robotic cell used in offsite housing plants that picks and places sheet material with vacuum grippers and fastens it on wall, floor and roof elements.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous pick-and-place plus fastening of covering material onto fixtured roof elements in a purpose-built cell — the same place-then-fasten cycle as laying and nailing tiles when the roof plane is presented to the machine.

sources.system: KUKA robot tile handling line at Creaton (Autenried II plant)
sources.title: Robotic Solutions for Ceramic Tile Handling
sources.claim: KUKA industrial robots run the handling line for large clay roofing tiles at Creaton's plant, gripping and placing brittle roof tiles at high production rates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic gripping and precise placement of clay roofing tiles — the identical objects handled in this task — inside a fenced industrial cell, showing the placement half of the task is routine when tiles are presented in known positions.

sources.title: Hadrian X – World's first mobile robotic blocklaying machine
sources.claim: FBR's Hadrian X autonomously lays heavy blocks from a 3D CAD model, applying a bonding adhesive to the units, and compensates for wind and vibration to hold placement accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine placement of heavy rigid masonry units in a repeating bond pattern with cementitious adhesive applied to them — comparable objects and precision to setting roof tiles and applying roofing cement, supporting the place-plus-cement steps in a structured cell.

roles.title: Construction and Building Inspectors
aliases: Site Damage Prevention Technician (Site Damage Prevention Tech)
roles.description: Inspect structures using engineering skills to determine structural soundness and compliance with specifications, building codes, and other regulations. Inspections may be general in nature or may be limited to a specific area, such as electrical systems or plumbing.

tasks.label: Approve building plans that meet required specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Review and interpret plans, blueprints, site layouts, specifications, or construction methods to ensure compliance to legal requirements and safety regulations.

tasks.label: Inspect bridges, dams, highways, buildings, wiring, plumbing, electrical circuits, sewers, heating systems, or foundations during and after construction for structural quality, general safety, or conformance to specifications and codes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Structural inspection during construction of a residential or light-commercial building: inspector walks a muddy, partially built site (footings/rebar/anchor bolts, framing members, sheathing, hold-downs, joist notching), climbs ladders and enters crawlspaces/attics, measures spans and spacing, compares to approved stamped plans and the IRC/IBC, and issues a pass/correction determination on site.

Rough-in trade inspection (electrical, plumbing, mechanical) in open walls of a house or small commercial building: verify conductor type/size, box fill, grounding/bonding, GFCI/AFCI, panel work, drain slope and venting, pipe supports, witness a pressure/air test on a gauge, check duct and gas-line work; requires reaching into stud bays, opening panels, and reading gauges in tight, cluttered spaces.

Final/occupancy inspection of a completed building: walk the whole structure checking egress, stair/handrail geometry, smoke and CO alarms, fixtures, guards, fire separations, accessibility, operating devices and switches, and confirming prior corrections before sign-off for a certificate of occupancy.

Public-works inspection in the right of way: trench depth, bedding and backfill compaction, water/sewer main installation, manholes, curb, subgrade and paving on an active street project with traffic control, weather, and heavy equipment moving around the inspector.

Post-construction / condition inspection of a buried sewer or storm pipeline: launch an inspection unit at a manhole, traverse the pipe segment capturing continuous imagery, and deliver a NASSCO PACP/MACP-coded defect and acceptance report for the newly installed or existing line.

Routine condition inspection of a highway bridge or dam: NBIS-style element-level review of deck, superstructure, substructure, bearings and joints, including hands-on/tactile checks (sounding, chain drag) of fracture-critical or concrete elements, under traffic control and difficult access, ending in element condition ratings in the inspection report.

sources.title: SOLO® Pipeline Inspection Robot CCTV | RedZone Robotics
sources.claim: RedZone Robotics' SOLO is a commercially deployed, fully autonomous small-diameter sewer inspection crawler: it is launched at a manhole and traverses the pipeline on its own using onboard sensors, with deliverables in NASSCO PACP/MACP coding format.

sources.title: Redzone Robotics Conducts Autonomous Pipeline Inspections (AMD case study)
sources.claim: Independent case study confirms RedZone's Solo units are fully autonomous sewer pipeline ... used in municipal field operations, with embedded AI routines running onboard.

sources.title: Inside the Sewer Infrastructure Ecosystem | SewerAI
sources.claim: The assessment/coding half of a pipeline inspection is produced automatically by computer-vision software that applies NASSCO PACP defect codes, in production use by utilities and contractors, so the robot-plus-software pipeline yields the accepted inspection deliverable.
sources.transferJustification: Not a robot itself; cited only as the analysis layer paired with the autonomous SOLO crawler, which supplies the physical traverse and imagery capture inside the pipe.

sources.developer: Skydio (Alaska, North Carolina, New York DOTs)
sources.title: How Transportation Departments Are Using Advanced Drone Technology for Infrastructure Inspections
sources.claim: State DOTs fly Skydio autonomous drones with 3D Scan for routine bridge and infrastructure inspection data capture; the drone automates the imagery/model capture, while the condition assessment and NBIS report remain with the qualified inspector.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous aerial data capture for bridge inspection. Cited to show the state of the art on bridges is capture only — no tactile sounding, no element condition ratings — so it does not complete the inspection instance.

sources.title: Trimble Releases Turnkey Autonomous Robotic Scanning Solution for Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot
sources.claim: Trimble sells a turnkey autonomous scanning solution pairing Boston Dynamics' Spot with the X7 laser scanner for repeated jobsite data capture on construction sites; the product automates capture and documentation, not code-compliance determinations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous navigation and reality capture on active construction sites. Cited to show mobility on E3 sites is solved, but the output is scan data for progress documentation, not a code/spec conformance inspection.

sources.title: AI Startup Using Robots and Lidar to Boost Productivity on Construction Sites - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Doxel operates lidar-equipped autonomous robots that scan construction sites daily and use deep learning to check whether installed work matches the model, producing progress and installation-quality metrics rather than code-compliance sign-offs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated verification of installed work against design on construction sites. Cited as the closest analogue to structural/rough-in inspection; it covers geometry and presence of visible elements only, not concealed connections, fastening, testing, or code judgment.

tasks.label: Monitor installation of plumbing, wiring, equipment, or appliances to ensure that installation is performed properly and is in compliance with applicable regulations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rough-in inspection at a single-family home under construction: inspector walks the open-framed house (including crawl space and attic), checks electrical rough-in (box fill, cable support and protection plates, grounding/bonding, circuit layout) and plumbing rough-in (DWV slope and venting, pipe supports, water-line materials), verifies the pressure/water test gauge is holding, and issues a pass or a written correction list on the spot.

Final/mechanical inspection of installed equipment and appliances in a newly completed house: water heater (T&P discharge, seismic strapping, pan/drain, gas connection and sediment trap), furnace/HVAC (venting, combustion air, condensate, disconnect), panel and device finish-out (GFCI/AFCI testing, cover plates, labeling). Inspector operates devices and testers and signs off for occupancy.

MEP inspection on an active commercial/institutional construction site (medical office, school, retail core-and-shell): inspector coordinates with trades, climbs ladders/lifts, inspects above-ceiling conduit, cable tray, sprinkler and piping supports and seismic bracing, mechanical rooms, switchgear and feeder installation, often in phased areas with ongoing work, dust, and temporary lighting.

Repetitive rough-in inspections of many similar units in a multifamily or hotel project under construction: same unit layout floor after floor, inspector spot-checks wiring and plumbing rough-in per unit, notes deviations, and tracks re-inspections of previously failed items.

Alteration/replacement permit inspection in an existing occupied home or small business: service-panel upgrade, re-pipe, water heater or A/C changeout, kitchen remodel wiring. Cramped, cluttered, occupied spaces; hidden and legacy conditions; inspector must judge existing-versus-new work and grandfathered conditions before approving.

sources.title: AI Startup Using Robots and Lidar to Boost Productivity on Construction Sites - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Doxel's autonomous lidar-equipped rover scans active construction site interiors daily after hours and its deep-learning pipeline checks that components have been installed in the right place per the design model; it reports deviations to human managers rather than making code-compliance determinations or performing physical tests.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated verification of installed MEP components against the design model on a construction site. It shares the environment and the objects (conduit, pipe, hangers) with the inspector's task, so it bounds how far autonomous machines get: presence/location checking, not the code judgments, physical tests, or sign-off the inspection task requires.

sources.system: Spot (with Trimble X7 / 360° camera payloads, Autowalk missions)
sources.title: Construction | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot is commercially deployed with contractors (Turner, Suffolk, Strabag) to autonomously navigate construction sites on scheduled routes and capture 360° imagery and laser scans of progress and as-built state; the deliverable is documentation for human decision-makers, not an inspection determination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous jobsite reality capture on active construction sites. Same environment and comparable access requirements (stairs, clutter), so it shows autonomous mobility is solved while the inspection judgment, manipulation (opening panels, operating devices) and testing steps of this task are absent.

sources.system: BIM-driven autonomous quadruped inspection framework (ANYmal/Spot-class quadruped)
sources.developer: Aalto University (published in Automation in Construction)
sources.title: Automating on-site object inspection with a quadruped robot and BIM
sources.claim: A research framework demonstrates a quadruped robot autonomously navigating a real building using BIM and inspecting objects with next-best-view planning and a vision-language model, verifying whether modeled elements are present; validation is research-grade object presence/condition inspection, not regulatory compliance inspection of plumbing or wiring installations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous on-site object inspection against BIM in construction and facility-management settings. It is the closest published attempt at robotic construction inspection; it establishes autonomous navigation and object-level checking but stops short of code interpretation, physical testing, and issuing pass/fail results.

sources.title: Quality Control in Construction: Prevent Rework with AI | Doxel
sources.claim: Doxel's current quality-control product compares captured reality data against the BIM at component level to flag missing or mislocated components across trades; capture method for the flagged data is not established as robotic in this source, and the output is a deviation list for human follow-up rather than a completed compliance inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated construction quality control of installed work. Shows the state of the art in automated checking of installed plumbing/electrical is design-conformance flagging for human review, which does not carry over to the inspector's code determination, tests, and approval.

tasks.label: Inspect and monitor construction sites to ensure adherence to safety standards, building codes, or specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Municipal/third-party residential code inspection at a house or small multifamily project under construction: foundation/rebar, framing, rough electrical-plumbing-mechanical, insulation, and final. Inspector climbs ladders, enters crawlspaces and attics, measures spans, hangers, nailing patterns and clearances against approved plans, and issues a pass/fail with correction notices, often 8-15 sites a day.

Commercial, institutional or multi-story building inspection, including special inspections: pre-pour rebar placement and cover, structural steel bolting/welds, shear walls and anchorage, fire-rated assemblies, firestopping, sprayed fireproofing thickness, egress and accessibility items. Requires access to elevated and concealed work, measurement, sampling and signed reports on an active, congested site.

Routine, repeatable progress and specification-conformance documentation round on a large, well-managed commercial project (data center, hospital, terminal) with mapped floors and consistent routes: capture the as-built condition floor by floor, compare installed work to drawings/BIM, log deviations and visible hazards, and distribute a dated record/report to the project team.

Owner's-rep or GC quality walkthrough and punch verification on a mixed project: close-up checks of hanger spacing, sealant, flashing, glazing, waterproofing laps, tolerances and finishes; touching, opening and measuring work; writing non-conformance items with photos and conferring with trade foremen on the spot.

Site safety monitoring round on an active construction site: fall protection and leading edges, ladders and scaffolds, excavation shoring and access, crane and rigging operations, electrical/GFCI, housekeeping and PPE across a site in early or structural phases; includes interviewing crews, checking permits/tags, and stopping unsafe work.

Public works / heavy civil field inspection: subgrade and grades, utility trench bedding and shoring, pipe installation, compaction and concrete field tests (slump, air, cylinders), asphalt placement and paving temperatures, quantity measurement for pay items, in traffic, weather and mud, documented in a daily report.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot + DroneDeploy Robotics (with StructionSite)

tasks.label: Measure dimensions and verify level, alignment, or elevation of structures or fixtures to ensure compliance to building plans and codes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Framing/rough inspection of a single-family house or townhouse under construction: measure stud and joist spacing, header and beam sizes, stair rise/run, guard and handrail heights, opening dimensions; check walls plumb and floors level against 2-D residential plans and the IRC. Partially built structure with debris, ladders, temporary lighting, no 3-D model.

Foundation / pre-pour inspection on a residential or light-commercial lot: measure trench and footing depth and width, form dimensions, top-of-form and slab elevations relative to a benchmark, rebar spacing and cover, and building setbacks from property lines. Muddy excavated ground with open trenches and equipment.

Commercial or institutional building under construction: verify column and wall locations, plumb and alignment, slab elevations and floor flatness, ceiling heights, embed and opening dimensions, and hanger/MEP layout against the design drawings or BIM model. Large active site controlled by a general contractor, multiple trades working.

Civil/site work inspection: verify subgrade and finished-grade elevations, pipe invert elevations and slopes, curb and sidewalk cross-slopes and curb-ramp running slopes, and pavement/base thickness at stations, using level and rod, total station or GNSS rover. Open outdoor site with traffic, stockpiles and moving equipment.

Final or accessibility inspection inside a completed or occupied commercial building: measure door clear widths and maneuvering clearances, grab bar, counter and fixture mounting heights, ramp and landing slopes, stair riser/tread uniformity and egress widths against approved plans and ADA/IBC. Finished, cleaned, institution-controlled interior with a fixed layout.

Alteration/remodel or home inspection in an occupied private home: measure ceiling heights in finished rooms, egress window opening dimensions, deck and guard heights, and verify newly installed fixtures are level and aligned. Furnished, cluttered rooms plus tight crawlspaces and attics.

tasks.label: Maintain daily logs and supplement inspection records with photographs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Municipal/county building inspector on a route of 8-15 short field visits per day (new houses, remodels, tenant improvements, occupied dwellings): at each address photographs the specific conditions inspected or cited (footing rebar, framing straps, panel labeling, fire-blocking, an unpermitted deck), then enters the result and log entry into the permit system from the truck. Addresses are new each day; access via lockbox, homeowner or contractor.

Resident/construction inspector assigned to one active commercial or public-works project: keeps the daily inspection log (weather, contractor crews and equipment on site, work performed by location, materials delivered, tests witnessed, directives given, delays, non-conformances) and attaches photographs of the day's work and of any deficiencies to the project record.

Special/trade inspector documenting concealed or hard-to-reach work before cover-up: close-up photographs of welds, bolted connections, rebar placement, ductwork and rough plumbing/electrical in crawlspaces, attics, above ceilings, trenches and mechanical rooms, plus a log entry keyed to the drawing location and code section.

Exterior/infrastructure condition documentation: bridge spans and undersides, roofs, facades, retaining walls, towers. Inspector systematically photographs structural elements and observed distress with location referencing and files the indexed image set with the inspection record.

Routine repeat-interval visual record of a large active jobsite (weekly/daily walk of the same floors and exterior on a fixed route) captured as 360 degree or aerial imagery, pinned to floor plans/site maps, to supplement inspection and as-built records for progress and cover-up disputes.

tasks.label: Conduct inspections, using survey instruments, metering devices, tape measures, or test equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Municipal/third-party code inspection at a residential jobsite (footing, framing, insulation, final): inspector walks a partially built, cluttered house, uses tape measure and level to check stair rise/run, guard and handrail heights, egress opening sizes, header/joist sizes and spans, stud and fastener spacing, clearances; issues pass/fail with a correction list.

Electrical, plumbing, mechanical and energy-code inspections using test equipment: receptacle/GFCI tester and multimeter at outlets and panels, air/water pressure gauge on rough plumbing, gas-line pressure test, combustion analyzer at appliances, duct-leakage/blower-door test - instruments must be physically connected in tight, varied locations in a building under construction or renovation.

Special/materials inspection on a commercial or institutional jobsite: rebar cover meter scans, casting and testing concrete cylinders plus slump/air tests, bolt torque and weld NDT checks, sprayed fireproofing thickness gauge readings, soil compaction (nuclear density gauge) - hands-on placement of instruments and sampling, results compared to approved specifications.

Dimensional/as-built verification of an active jobsite against plans: laser scan or total-station/GNSS/drone survey of interiors and site to verify layout, elevations, grades, setbacks, plumbness and whether installed work is in the specified position; deviation report delivered to the project team.

Home inspection or inspection of an existing occupied building: moisture meter on walls and roof leaks, infrared camera, outlet tester, CO/gas detector, crack gauges and tape measurements in basements, attics, crawlspaces and around occupants' belongings; written condition report.

Off-site inspection at a fabrication plant of building components (precast panels, structural steel, modular/manufactured housing units): dimensional QA against approved shop drawings with tape/laser measurement plus weld or embed verification, in a plant controlled by the manufacturer.

tasks.label: Monitor construction activities to ensure that environmental regulations are not violated.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine weekly and post-rain-event stormwater/SWPPP inspection on an active land-disturbing site: walk the perimeter, ditches, slopes and outfalls; check silt fence integrity and toe-in, inlet protection, stabilized construction entrance, stockpile covers, sediment basins and dewatering; look for offsite sediment discharge and turbid runoff; complete the permit inspection report with photos, corrective actions and deadlines. Muddy, sloped, wet terrain; heavy equipment working.

Routine environmental compliance walk on an active building/vertical construction site: dust control, concrete washout containment, fuel and chemical storage with secondary containment, spill kits, covered dumpsters and waste segregation, tracked mud at the exit, noise and work-hour limits; documented with photographs and a checklist against permit conditions.

Demolition or renovation environmental checks: asbestos/lead abatement containment integrity and negative-pressure verification, wetting/dust suppression during demolition, handling and disposal of regulated waste, and review of disposal manifests and notifications, often inside a partially occupied building.

Complaint or enforcement response: mud tracked onto a public road, a sediment plume entering a storm drain or stream, or an illicit discharge; the inspector traces the source across and beyond the site, documents conditions, discusses corrective action with the contractor, and issues a notice of violation or stop-work order.

Environmental commitment monitoring on a linear/heavy infrastructure project (highway, pipeline, utility corridor): driving and walking miles of corridor to check wetland and stream buffer limits, tree protection fencing, clearing limits, dewatering operations and staging/fueling areas, with off-road access and remote locations.

Pre-disturbance verification that erosion and sediment controls were installed in the quantities and locations shown on the approved plan before grading begins, plus periodic aerial or walk-over documentation of site conditions compared against the plan.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with FieldAI Field Foundation Models
sources.title: Case Study: How FieldAI and Boston Dynamics Made Autonomy Practical on Construction Sites
sources.claim: Spot quadrupeds running FieldAI's Field Foundation Models are deployed on active construction sites in Asia, Europe and North America, autonomously executing inspection, mapping and monitoring job walks without prior maps or pre-planned routes, surfacing site conditions including safety observations (holes, drop-offs, PPE compliance, slippery surfaces).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous progress/condition documentation and hazard observation on as-found construction sites. It shows a robot can traverse and image an unstructured jobsite autonomously, but the observations it delivers are progress, quality and safety hazards feeding human decision-making, not permit-compliance determinations about erosion controls, containment or discharges.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with DroneDeploy Ground Robotics

sources.claim: Turner Construction runs Boston Dynamics Spot on scheduled autonomous overnight missions on data center construction sites to capture 360-degree walkthroughs that feed DroneDeploy and StructionSite for comparison against plans and BIM.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeatable autonomous reality-capture rounds on a construction site. It substantiates autonomous traversal and photo documentation of a jobsite, but the deliverable is imagery for human review of progress, not an environmental compliance finding.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: scheduled autonomous inspection rounds over a large controlled industrial site, imaging fixed installations and flagging spills, leaks and hazards. Comparable to a scheduled visual compliance round of site installations in a facility with a fixed layout and controlled access, at similar (coarse visual) precision.

sources.system: ANYmal with Gas Leak and Presence Detection
sources.title: ANYbotics Launches New Gas Leak & Presence Detection Solution for its ANYmal Inspection Robot
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal quadruped performs autonomous inspection missions in industrial facilities and, with its 2025 gas leak and presence detection payload, localizes and quantifies fugitive gas leaks and alerts personnel in real time.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous detection of fugitive emissions, an environmental-regulatory monitoring function, inside refineries and plants. Shows robots can carry out environment-related compliance sensing rounds, but only on fixed industrial assets in institution-controlled facilities.

sources.title: Climate Investment backs ANYbotics to advance industrial decarbonization
sources.claim: More than 200 ANYmal units ... shipped and perform thousands of inspections weekly across oil and gas, mining, ... sites, autonomously detecting indicators such as overheating and fugitive gas emissions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: at-scale autonomous inspection rounds in structured industrial facilities; establishes deployment maturity of the environment (E2) in which such robotic monitoring rounds are actually completed.

sources.system: UAS-based deep-learning detection of construction stormwater practices (Auburn University study)
sources.title: Deep Learning-Based Object Detection for Unmanned Aerial Systems (UASs)-Based Inspections of Construction Stormwater Practices
sources.claim: Research applying deep-learning object detection to UAS imagery of active construction sites detected four types of stormwater practices for site-plan comparison, but the approach identifies the quantity and location of installed practices rather than judging their condition or compliance, and the aerial data collection was flown for the study rather than by a fielded autonomous system.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related to the stormwater inspection instance, but it substantiates only detection of practice type and location in imagery; flight autonomy is not established, so under the rules it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Inspect facilities or installations to determine their environmental impact.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Erosion and sediment control / stormwater (SWPPP, NPDES) inspection at an active construction site: inspector walks disturbed areas and the perimeter in mud and traffic, checks silt fence keying and repair, inlet protection, stabilized entrance and off-site tracking, concrete washout, dewatering discharge points and any sediment reaching a ditch or stream, photographs deficiencies and issues a written report with corrective actions.

Periodic environmental-condition compliance inspection of an operating industrial or commercial facility (plant, fuel depot, shop, process building): walk the property checking fuel and chemical storage, secondary containment, waste accumulation areas, floor drains and outfalls, visible leaks/spills, dust and emissions points; document findings in a compliance report.

Onsite wastewater/septic system inspection at a residential or rural property: verify setbacks to wells, streams and property lines, inspect the open excavation, tank, distribution box and drainfield before backfill, probe soil, check for surfacing effluent or failure; approve or reject the installation.

Pre-demolition or pre-renovation hazardous-materials survey of an existing building (asbestos/lead/mold): access attics, crawl spaces, boiler and mechanical rooms, identify suspect materials, collect bulk samples of pipe insulation, flooring and roofing, and document for the demolition permit.

Inspection of a newly installed or existing buried utility installation for leakage/environmental effect: run CCTV through new sanitary sewer or storm drain lines and structures, check joints, infiltration, offsets and connections, and report defects requiring correction before acceptance.
