tasks.label: Examine lifting or conveying devices, such as elevators, escalators, moving sidewalks, hoists, inclined railways, ski lifts, or amusement rides to ensure safety and proper functioning.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Periodic (annual/semi-annual) elevator inspection in an occupied commercial or institutional building (office tower, hospital, school, apartment high-rise). Inspector rides the car, checks leveling and door reversal/restrictors, tests firefighters' emergency operation and emergency communications, enters the machine room to check machine, brake, governor and controller wiring, works from the car top with the inspection station, descends into the pit to check buffer, stop switch and travel cables, then writes up violations and signs the certificate.

Periodic escalator or moving-walkway inspection at a mall, airport, transit station or stadium. Inspector runs the unit, checks handrail speed and entry guards, gauges comb-step impact and step/skirt clearances, actuates emergency stops and safety switches, has steps/panels removed to view drive, chains and brake, inspects the truss pit, and documents violations.

Acceptance or witness testing of a newly installed or modernized elevator/escalator in a building under construction or renovation. Inspector verifies installation against approved drawings and witnesses full-load running, car and counterweight safety and governor trip tests with test weights loaded into the car, buffer, brake and unintended-movement tests, amid an active job site with dust, temporary lighting and other trades.

Amusement ride inspection at a fixed-site park or a traveling carnival/fair setup: walk-down of structure, welds, pins, fasteners and cables (often with NDT), restraint and lap-bar tests on every seat, block/brake and control-system checks, ride envelope and fencing, plus empty and loaded test cycles; carnival units inspected after each setup on grass or gravel lots in variable weather.

Ski lift, aerial tramway or inclined railway inspection at a mountain resort: accessing towers to check sheave assemblies and rope alignment, haul-rope and splice examination, grip and carrier checks, drive/auxiliary/emergency brake and evacuation tests, terminal machinery inspection, on steep snow-covered or summer alpine terrain in wind and cold.

Small or residential conveyance inspection: private-residence elevator, LULA, wheelchair/platform lift, stairlift or dumbwaiter in a home or small commercial space, plus temporary construction personnel/material hoists on job sites. Cramped, non-standard installations, frequently no machine room, homeowner or contractor escorting, followed by a violation report.

sources.title: Industrial Inspection Solutions | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot performs autonomous, repeatable inspection rounds in industrial facilities (plants, substations, refineries), collecting visual, thermal and acoustic data and reading gauges on preprogrammed routes; commercially deployed, but its scope is sensor data capture, not functional safety testing or code adjudication of conveyances.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous facility inspection rounds. It is the most mature deployed autonomous inspection robot, but it only captures sensor readings along taught routes; it cannot open machine-room panels, operate car-top inspection stations, gauge step/skirt clearances, load test weights or trip safeties, so capability does not transfer to a conveyance safety inspection.

sources.title: Schindler's Robotic Installation System for Elevators | Schindler Group
sources.claim: Schindler R.I.S.E. is a commercially used robot that works autonomously inside elevator hoistways of buildings under construction, drilling holes and setting anchor bolts around the clock with an operator on site only for quality control and support; it performs installation work, not inspection or compliance judgment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous work inside an elevator hoistway. It shows a robot can self-position and drill in a shaft, but the work is a single repetitive drilling/anchoring operation on a bare shaft wall; it demonstrates no inspection perception, no testing of safety devices and no code-compliance decision.

sources.title: Drone-Based Inspection and Surveying, Far and Away - Inside Unmanned Systems
sources.claim: Drone service providers inspect elevator shafts in occupied high-rise buildings with collision-tolerant indoor drones, capturing imagery of shaft conditions; missions are flown by a professional pilot and deliver visual data only, not a completed conveyance safety inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hoistway visual inspection. Even the visual portion of an elevator inspection is pilot-flown here, and it covers none of the functional tests (door reversal, fire service, governor/safety trips) required to complete the task.

sources.title: Advanced Drone Autonomy for Indoor Inspection: Inside the Elios 3
sources.claim: Indoor confined-space inspection drones remain pilot-operated; the manufacturer states its autonomy features assist rather than replace the pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Confirms the leading confined-space inspection robot for shafts and machinery spaces is not autonomous, so it cannot support a positive judgment for any instance of this task.

sources.system: Multifunctional roller coaster track detection robot
sources.title: Development of Multifunctional Detection Robot for Roller Coaster Track
sources.claim: A research prototype robot that travels along roller-coaster track carries cameras, electromagnetic-acoustic and eddy-current probes to detect appearance defects, wall-thickness loss and cracks; validated in machine testing and addressing only the track-NDT portion of a ride inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: amusement-ride structural NDT. It covers one sub-step (track flaw detection) of a ride inspection, is a laboratory-stage prototype with unstated autonomy, and does not test restraints, brakes, controls or run acceptance cycles.

sources.title: Drones for Inspection and Monitoring - Seilbahnen International
sources.claim: Ropeway operators use drones to support routine lift inspections, with the operator watching the live feed on an office PC and reviewing images afterwards; the drone supplies imagery for human assessment rather than completing the lift inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: ropeway visual inspection. Only aerial imagery is produced; grip, brake, evacuation and rope-splice testing plus the compliance determination remain with the human inspector, and the flights' autonomy is not established.

tasks.label: Conduct environmental hazard inspections to identify or quantify problems, such as asbestos, poor air quality, water contamination, or other environmental hazards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-renovation/demolition asbestos and lead survey of an existing building (single-family home, small commercial space, school wing): inspector walks the whole structure including attic, crawlspace, boiler room and ceiling plenums, visually classifies suspect materials by homogeneous area, cuts/scrapes bulk samples (pipe lagging, floor tile and mastic, joint compound, roofing) with knife or corer, bags/labels them with chain-of-custody, takes XRF lead readings on painted components, and writes the survey report.

Indoor air quality inspection of an occupied institutional or commercial building (school, office, hospital wing) after a complaint or as periodic monitoring: walk a route through rooms and mechanical spaces taking calibrated readings (CO2, CO, VOC, particulates, temperature, humidity), check ventilation supply/return and filters, flag locations exceeding thresholds, and document findings.

Asbestos abatement project monitoring and final clearance in an active work area: set out area air-sampling pumps with filter cassettes inside and outside the containment, verify barriers/negative pressure, walk the containment for visual clearance (no residual dust or debris on surfaces), run aggressive air sampling with a fan/blower, and sign off the clearance.

Potable water contamination sampling in a building (school, childcare center, apartment building): collect first-draw and flushed samples at multiple fixtures for lead/copper or bacteria, take field measurements (chlorine residual, pH, temperature), preserve, label and log bottles with chain-of-custody, and report results against action levels.

Environmental compliance inspection of an active construction or demolition site: check erosion and sediment controls, dust suppression, concrete washout and spill/contaminated-soil conditions, sample stormwater discharge at outfalls, and issue notices; layout, equipment and stockpiles change daily and workers and machines are moving throughout.

Residential environmental hazard inspection of an occupied home: moisture and mold assessment with moisture meter and IR camera including crawlspace and attic entry, tape-lift or spore-trap sampling, placement and retrieval of a radon monitor, and collection of a private well water sample, with a written report to the homeowner or lender.

sources.system: Spot with MUVE C360 gas detection payload (MFE Inspection Solutions)
sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / MFE Inspection Solutions / Teledyne FLIR
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas Leaks | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot, carrying a Teledyne FLIR MUVE C360 gas sensor, ran autonomous inspection rounds across a 40-acre midstream gas plant and detected a combustible gas plume from a pinhole leak, autonomously shutting down at the LEL threshold and alerting the safety team.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine atmospheric-hazard monitoring rounds in a plant. It transfers to an indoor air quality inspection because both consist of traversing a human-built, institution-controlled facility on a defined route with calibrated gas/air sensors and flagging locations where airborne contaminant concentrations exceed thresholds.

sources.title: Meet Chevron's New Energy Watchdog | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Chevron moved Spot into a ... Bakersfield cogeneration facility, where robots perform daily inspections walking autonomous routes and collecting visual and thermal data, and can carry an explosive-gas sensor allowing autonomous operation in hazardous, electrically classified areas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: recurring facility inspection rounds with sensing payloads. Transfers to periodic air-quality/hazard monitoring inside a structured building because the robot navigates human-occupied plant interiors and yards unattended and returns the measurement record the inspector would produce.

sources.title: ANYbotics launches Gas Leak and Presence Detection for ANYmal inspection robot - The Robot Report
sources.claim: ANYbotics launched a gas leak and presence detection ... the ANYmal legged inspection robot, combining modular gas detectors with acoustic imaging so the autonomous robot can locate leak sources and measure ambient gas concentrations in industrial plants built for humans.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous gas-hazard survey inside multi-floor process plants. Transfers to quantifying poor air quality in a structured building: same class of mobile robot, same calibrated gas sensing, same indoor human-built environment.

sources.system: USV water quality monitoring and sampling system (4th generation)
sources.developer: Hong Kong Water Supplies Department / OceanAlpha
sources.title: WSD - Use of Unmanned Surface Vessel System for Water Quality Monitoring and Sampling at Impounding Reservoirs
sources.claim: Hong Kong's Water Supplies Department operates four unmanned surface vessels that automatically navigate preset routes in impounding reservoirs, collect water samples and measure water quality parameters, and since 2024 automatically add monitoring points and extra samples when water quality changes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended collection of water samples plus in-situ quality measurement for a water utility. Shows machine-controlled sample capture and reporting, but only on open water at fixed sampling points, not at plumbing fixtures inside buildings.

sources.title: Automatic Water Samplers | Teledyne ISCO
sources.claim: Teledyne ISCO automatic water samplers are programmed to collect and bottle water samples unattended at set intervals or on trigger events (rainfall, level, flow) at fixed monitoring stations, and are used for municipal stormwater and industrial discharge regulatory compliance sampling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine collection of compliance water samples. It substantiates only the purpose-built case where water is piped to the machine at a fixed sampling station with in-line parameter sensors; it cannot walk a building and operate fixtures.

sources.system: Gopher (GPK-32) confined space inspection robot; TOBOR Hellcat Xplorer
sources.title: Gopher Confined Space Inspection Robot | SuperDroid Robots
sources.claim: Inspection robots marketed to home inspectors for crawlspaces and confined spaces are human-driven camera crawlers that carry a camera into the space while the inspector watches and interprets the video; they perform no autonomous survey or sampling.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to residential mold/moisture inspection: this is the state of practice for robotic help under houses, and it is continuous teleoperation with human interpretation, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Evaluate premises for cleanliness, such as proper garbage disposal or lack of vermin infestation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied rental dwelling unit (housing-code / HQS-NSPIRE-style inspection): inspector enters a tenant-occupied apartment or single-family rental, works around furniture and clutter, checks kitchen and bath for accumulated refuse and improper garbage storage, looks under sinks, behind and under appliances, in cabinets and closets for roach droppings/egg cases, rodent droppings, gnaw marks and harborage, and records cited violations with photos.

Common areas and refuse-storage areas of a managed multifamily or mixed-use building: trash rooms, chute rooms, basements, dumpster enclosures and alcoves. Inspector opens enclosure gates and container lids, judges whether containers are adequate/covered/overfilled, checks for spilled refuse, standing liquid, rodent runways, burrows and droppings behind bins, and issues a compliance determination to the owner.

Exterior premises / property-maintenance complaint on a residential lot or vacant property: inspector walks the yard, alley and perimeter, evaluates accumulated junk, bagged refuse, overturned or missing containers, overgrowth and rodent harborage, documents conditions from lawful vantage points, and writes a notice of violation.

Commercial or institutional premises (restaurant, grocery, retail strip, school, care facility, warehouse) as part of a general or occupancy inspection: check refuse handling area and grease/recycling bins, storage and stock rooms, back-of-house housekeeping, and evidence of vermin activity in storage and utility spaces; issue findings to the operator.

Active construction or renovation jobsite during a progress inspection: verify debris is contained rather than scattered, dumpsters are serviced, food waste and standing water are not creating harborage, sanitary facilities are maintained, and note sanitation deficiencies in the inspection report.

sources.title: Cargill Deploys AI-Powered Robot Dog 'Spot' at Amsterdam Facility to Enhance Safety, Reliability and Workplace Innovation
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot runs high-frequency autonomous inspection rounds inside a working food-processing plant, capturing thermal/acoustic/visual data and flagging hazards such as leaks and overheating.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine facility walkthrough inspection. It shares locomotion through a human work facility and automated visual condition assessment at fixed checkpoints, which is the sensing half of a premises-condition check; it does not cover refuse-container or vermin-evidence judgments.

sources.system: Levatas Cognitive Inspection Platform on Boston Dynamics Spot
sources.title: Boston Dynamics Adds Capabilities to Spot Robot, Names Levatas as Certified Technology Partner
sources.claim: Levatas' certified AI models for Spot include liquid spill detection and detection of unexpected environmental changes, run automatically on Spot's inspection missions in industrial facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated housekeeping/hazard detection on inspection rounds. Detecting spills and unexpected changes at mapped checkpoints is the closest demonstrated analogue to judging whether an area is kept clean and refuse is contained.

sources.title: AI Inspections - Levatas.com
sources.claim: Levatas markets an 'Unexpected Debris Detection' visual AI inspection model alongside spill and fire-safety models for robot-borne inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated detection of debris/spills during robotic inspection routes; comparable perception target (loose material on floors) to the litter/refuse component of a cleanliness check, but limited to what is visible from a mapped route.

sources.title: Quadruped robot boosts safety and maintenance at aging cement plant
sources.claim: ANYmal performs unattended nightly inspection rounds of a cement plant, visiting hundreds of predefined checkpoints across multiple levels and reporting anomalies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeatable checkpoint inspection rounds in an industrial facility. Establishes that a legged robot can autonomously reach and image predefined stations, which is what an E1-style presentation of refuse/housekeeping checkpoints would require.

sources.system: Cleaning-audit robot (dirt-probability-driven exploration with touch-and-inspect sensor)
sources.developer: Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD)
sources.title: An Autonomous Robot-Aided Auditing Scheme for Floor Cleaning
sources.claim: A research mobile robot autonomously audits the cleanliness of built-environment floors, exploring dirt-likely regions and assigning an audit score.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic cleanliness auditing. Directly targets 'how clean is clean' for floors, but is a laboratory-scale demonstration scoring surface dirt, not a refuse-handling or vermin-infestation determination.

sources.title: AI Enabled IoRT Framework for Rodent Activity Monitoring in a False Ceiling Environment
sources.claim: A research robot ('Falcon') carries a camera into building false ceilings and an AI model classifies signs of rodent activity; validation used real ceilings plus 3D-printed rodents.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic detection of vermin evidence in a building void. Closest published analogue to the vermin half of this task, but platform autonomy is not established and results are demo-grade, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: The implementation of robotic dogs in automatic detection and surveillance of red imported fire ant nests - PubMed
sources.claim: A quadruped robot platform with a YOLOX vision model detected and geolocated fire-ant nests in field trials, finding more nests than trained human inspectors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic pest-infestation survey on open ground. Shows automated infestation detection outdoors, but locomotion autonomy is not documented and the target (visible ant mounds in open turf) differs from rodent harborage in cluttered as-found premises.

sources.title: Angsa Robotics | LinkedIn
sources.claim: An autonomous outdoor robot detects and picks up small litter items on grass and gravel in parks and event grounds using onboard AI perception.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous outdoor litter detection. Demonstrates recognition of small waste items on unpaved ground, relevant to spotting scattered refuse outdoors, but it collects litter rather than producing a premises sanitation determination.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with 360 camera / HoloBuilder
sources.title: Pomerleau First in The World to Use Spot Robot on Construction Site
sources.claim: Spot was used on a Montreal construction site to walk routes with a 360-degree camera and produce site documentation linked to progress-tracking software.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous jobsite documentation walks. Shows a robot can traverse an active construction site and capture imagery, but interpretation and any deficiency determination are made by humans reviewing the captures.

tasks.label: Sample and test air to identify gasses, such as bromine, ozone, or sulfur dioxide, or particulates, such as mold, dust, or allergens.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential mold/particulate air sampling: after a water-loss or 'musty smell' complaint, the inspector places a calibrated pump with spore-trap cassettes in several occupied rooms plus an outdoor control, runs timed volumetric samples, seals and labels cassettes, completes chain-of-custody to an accredited lab, and interprets the returned spore counts. Furnished private home, occupants and pets present, no fixed layout.

Direct-reading gas/particulate screening during a home or dwelling inspection: handheld multi-gas/IAQ meter used for CO around furnaces, water heaters and attached garages, plus CO2, VOC, PM and humidity readings room by room, including crawl space, attic and basement; readings logged by location and compared to an outdoor baseline.

Indoor-air-quality complaint investigation in an institutional or commercial building (office floor, school, hospital wing, multifamily common areas): walkthrough with a multi-gas/IAQ instrument taking breathing-zone CO2, CO, ozone/VOC, PM2.5, temperature and RH readings at dozens of mapped locations over a floor or wing, plus outdoor reference, during occupied hours.

Active construction/renovation site air monitoring: real-time dust monitoring during demolition, concrete cutting or grinding; CO/NO2 from fuel-burning equipment in enclosed or partially enclosed areas; and pre-entry atmospheric testing (O2, LEL, CO, H2S) of vaults, tanks, manholes and crawl spaces. Changing layout, weather, traffic and other trades working nearby.

Post-remediation / post-abatement clearance air sampling inside a sealed containment (asbestos PCM or mold clearance): calibrate pumps, run aggressive sampling with a blower, collect filter cassettes at set flow and volume, take field blanks, chain-of-custody to lab, and issue a pass/fail clearance decision.

sources.system: Spot with FLIR MUVE C360 gas detection payload
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot, carrying the Teledyne FLIR MUVE C360 multi-gas sensor plus the Enhanced Autonomy Payload, ran autonomous inspection routes across a 40-acre midstream gas plant, sampling plant air for combustible gas and shutting down when it detected a plume.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class: a mobile machine carries a calibrated gas-sensing instrument through a facility and logs/flags airborne gas concentrations, which is the measurement core of the inspector's air sampling and testing task.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics' Robot Dog Detects Gas Leaks | IoT World Today
sources.claim: Independent trade coverage of the same deployment confirms the robot roamed the 40-acre facility autonomously while carrying the gas detection sensor.

sources.title: FLIR MUVE C360 Protects First Responders From a Wide Range of Hazards | Teledyne FLIR
sources.claim: The MUVE C360 payload carried by Spot and by UAS is an 8-channel multi-gas detector whose sensor suite covers the gas families an inspector screens for, including sulfur dioxide, chlorine (a halogen), nitrogen dioxide, CO, H2S, O2 and VOCs by PID.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the robot-mounted instrument measures the same toxic-gas species (SO2, a halogen, NO2, CO) named in the inspector's task, at real-time direct-reading quality.

sources.system: ANYmal with gas leak and presence detection
sources.title: ANYbotics launches new gas leak, presence detection solution for inspection robots | International Mining
sources.claim: ANYbotics released a gas leak and presence detection ... the ANYmal inspection quadruped used at oil, gas and chemical facilities: swappable, on-site calibrated gas detectors (oxygen, hydrocarbons, ammonia and others) that log concentrations continuously during autonomous inspection missions.

sources.title: Robosecurity Is Here: How Robots Can Save Money and Lives - Cobalt Robotics
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor patrol robot, deployed in commercial buildings and laboratories, autonomously patrols routes carrying an environmental sensor bay and flagged an elevated carbon monoxide level inside a biopharma laboratory, prompting evacuation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous indoor patrol with environmental sensing) transfers: the robot traverses an occupied human work building on a mapped route and reports airborne gas/particulate concentrations, the same physical act as an inspector's direct-reading IAQ walkthrough.

sources.title: Cobalt - ROBOTS: Your Guide to the World of Robotics
sources.claim: The Cobalt robot's sensor complement for those indoor patrols includes gas and particulate sensing - smoke, carbon monoxide, humidity, temperature ... airborne dust - carried in a dedicated environmental sensor bay.
sources.transferJustification: Documents that the deployed indoor robot measures both gases and airborne dust, matching the gas-and-particulate scope of the inspector's screening measurements.

sources.title: Short communication: automatic real-time monitoring of fungal spores: the case of Alternaria spp (bioRxiv)
sources.claim: MeteoSwiss operates a national network of automatic Swisens Poleno instruments that continuously draw ambient air, image individual airborne particles and classify allergenic pollen and fungal spores (e.g., Alternaria) in real time, validated against manual Hirst-type spore traps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (automatic bioaerosol sampling and identification) transfers to the particulate half of the inspector's task: the machine performs the sample-and-identify step for airborne spores/allergens, but only at a fixed, purpose-built installation to which the air is brought.

tasks.label: Identify any health or safety issues related to planned weatherization projects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied single-family home in a low-income weatherization (WAP) or utility program: auditor performs the health-and-safety portion of the audit — ambient CO monitoring, worst-case combustion appliance zone depressurization (closing doors, firing dryer/exhaust fans), draft/spillage and flue-gas CO measurement on gas furnace and water heater, gas-line leak check with a detector, checking for unvented heaters, missing CO/smoke alarms, moisture/mold, pest/sewage, and deferring measures if hazards found. Cluttered, occupied rooms; basement or utility closet access.

Pre-insulation hazard inspection of attic, crawlspace or basement in a single-family home: entering a dark, tight, unconditioned space to look for vermiculite/asbestos insulation, active knob-and-tube wiring, recessed cans and chimney clearances, bath fans venting into the attic, standing water/damp, rot, rodent droppings, and structural defects that must be corrected before air sealing or insulating.

Manufactured/mobile home audit: checking unvented space heaters, sealed-combustion furnace and water heater venting, gas leaks at connectors, duct crossover and belly damage under the home, and confirming that planned air sealing will not create backdrafting or moisture problems in a very tight, small structure.

Small multifamily building (older 4–24 unit apartment property): assessing shared boiler/water-heater room combustion safety and common venting, corridor and unit-level ventilation, dryer venting, asbestos-suspect pipe lagging, mold/moisture in units, and unit-by-unit spot checks in occupied apartments before a building-wide weatherization retrofit.

Commercial or institutional building (school, office, small retail, church) energy audit: identifying asbestos-containing pipe and boiler insulation, combustion venting and make-up air adequacy in the mechanical room, ventilation/IAQ implications of tightening the envelope, roof and confined-space access hazards, and electrical hazards, documented in the audit report as prerequisites to the recommended measures.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with gas-detection and thermal payloads
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas Leaks | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot runs autonomous inspection rounds at a 40-acre midstream gas plant with thermal, visual and gas-detection payloads, and autonomously detected a combustible gas leak — showing autonomous hazard sensing on pre-taught routes inside an industrial facility, not a whole building health-and-safety assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous facility safety rounds (gas leak, thermal anomaly, gauge reading). It substantiates autonomous sensing of one hazard class along fixed routes in a controlled industrial plant, but not the multi-modal, instrumented, judgment-based hazard identification (combustion appliance zone depressurization, asbestos identification, moisture/mold, ventilation adequacy) required by this task.

sources.title: Q-Bot / Minimum fuss, maximum insulation — Ashden
sources.claim: Q-Bot's underfloor robot is inserted into crawlspaces of occupied UK homes to survey the void and flag problems such as damp or damaged floorboards before insulation — the closest analogue to pre-weatherization hazard identification in a home — but it is driven remotely by a trained operator over a tethered data cable.
sources.transferJustification: Same setting and purpose (identifying defects/hazards under a floor before a weatherization measure) in real homes, so it bears directly; but continuous remote control by an operator means it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Crawlspace inspection robots (home inspection crawlers, e.g. SuperDroid/Inspector Bots units)
sources.title: Crawlspace Inspection Robots: Are they worth the investment?
sources.claim: Crawlspace inspection robots marketed to home inspectors are remote-controlled camera vehicles; they capture imagery of the space for a human to interpret rather than autonomously identifying hazards.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same sub-setting (residential crawlspaces inspected for defects), establishing that the commercially available residential inspection robots are teleoperated camera platforms, not autonomous assessors.

sources.title: TEA-bot: a thermography enabled autonomous robot for detecting thermal leaks of HVAC systems in ceilings
sources.claim: TEA-bot / AcTEA-bot is an autonomous thermography robot that navigates ceiling plenums to detect and register HVAC thermal leaks, validated in a purpose-built in-lab, true-to-size ceiling test site — a research demonstration limited to thermal leak detection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated building/HVAC energy-related data collection. It shows autonomy exists for a single thermal-imaging sub-step in a purpose-built test rig, not for identifying combustion, asbestos, moisture or electrical hazards in a real building.

sources.title: Security Robot: New Spill and Leak Detection Technology | Buildings
sources.claim: Cobalt Robotics' indoor robots autonomously patrol offices and other human-occupied facilities and can flag leaks and spills within predefined areas, with alerts routed to a remote human specialist — autonomous anomaly sensing in an E2 facility, limited to pre-defined anomaly classes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous indoor facility patrol with environmental anomaly detection in commercial buildings. It shows autonomous navigation of an E2 human work facility, but detection is limited to predefined anomalies and does not include instrumented combustion-safety testing or hazardous-material identification.

sources.title: Autonomous Robots for Industrial Inspection in Hazardous Zones | Ghost Robotics
sources.claim: Ghost Robotics Vision 60 quadrupeds autonomously patrol refinery grounds with gas detection, thermal imaging and ... inspection payloads, reporting hazards in an industrial facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hazard patrol in an institution-controlled industrial facility. Establishes the current ceiling of autonomous hazard sensing (fixed routes, sensor thresholds), which falls short of the diagnostic testing and multi-hazard judgment this task requires.

tasks.label: Identify opportunities to improve the operation, maintenance, or energy efficiency of building or process systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial office building (ASHRAE Level I/II style): auditor synthesizes walk-through observations, nameplate data, HVAC/BAS schedules, lighting inventory and 12-24 months of utility bills to identify energy conservation measures (setpoint and schedule changes, lighting retrofit, economizer repair, filter/belt maintenance) and lists them with estimated savings.

Single-family or small multifamily home audit: auditor interprets blower-door and IR-camera results, insulation/appliance/HVAC observations and occupant behavior to identify air-sealing, insulation, duct-sealing, water-heater and equipment-replacement opportunities, and prioritizes them for the homeowner or weatherization program.

Investment-grade audit of a large facility or portfolio: auditor calibrates an energy model, runs measure-by-measure savings and life-cycle-cost analysis, and identifies the package of operations, maintenance and capital measures that meets the client's payback/IRR criteria for a performance contract.

Industrial or process facility (plant utilities): auditor reviews compressed-air, steam, boiler, motor/drive, refrigeration and process-heat data plus logged measurements to identify leak repair, VSD retrofits, steam-trap maintenance, heat-recovery and load-scheduling opportunities.

Retro-commissioning / ongoing monitoring-based commissioning: auditor mines building automation system trend logs, submetering and fault-detection outputs (simultaneous heating and cooling, stuck dampers, schedule overrides, drifting setpoints) to identify low-cost operational and maintenance corrections.

tasks.label: Calculate potential for energy savings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Inspect or evaluate building envelopes, mechanical systems, electrical systems, or process systems to determine the energy consumption of each system.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-family home audit: auditor walks an occupied private house, inspects attic and crawlspace insulation, rim joists, windows/doors, ducts; records furnace, water heater and AC nameplate data and ages; runs blower door and duct blaster, IR-scans walls/ceilings, checks combustion appliance draft, counts lighting/appliances, then estimates consumption by end use.

Multifamily building audit: auditor samples occupied apartments (kitchens, closets, radiators, in-unit heaters) and inspects the common boiler/DHW room, distribution piping, laundry and corridor lighting, roof equipment, and house-meter/panel setup to apportion energy use among heating, DHW, and common loads.

Small commercial walk-through (retail store, restaurant, small office): auditor inventories lighting, climbs to the roof to check packaged RTUs and record nameplates, opens/reads electrical panels and utility meters, inspects refrigeration, water heating and envelope condition, and interviews the manager on schedules.

Large commercial/institutional ASHRAE Level II audit (office tower, hospital, campus, school): auditor tours central plant (chillers, boilers, pumps), AHU rooms and shafts, reads panel meters and BAS trends, spot-measures amperage and temperatures, installs data loggers, checks envelope and lighting by floor, and builds system-level energy breakdowns.

Full industrial/process facility audit: auditor surveys compressed air generation and distribution, boilers and steam traps, process heat, motors and drives, ovens/furnaces; performs combustion analysis, motor amperage/power measurements, insulation thermography, and quantifies consumption per process system.

Targeted plant energy-loss survey inside a manufacturing plant: repeat route through packaging/process lines and utility areas with acoustic imaging and thermography to find and locate compressed air/gas leaks and overheating motors/bearings, logging each finding for repair and loss accounting.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Spot CAM+IR and Fluke SV600 acoustic payload
sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / Fluke Process Instruments (customer: AB InBev)
sources.title: Energy Savings & Predictive Maintenance at AB InBev's Largest European Brewery | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot quadruped runs autonomous thermal and acoustic inspection rounds at AB InBev's Leuven brewery packaging lines, finding compressed air/gas leaks and overheating motors and feeding work orders; deployed since 2023 with ~1,800 inspections/week.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: acoustic/thermal leak-and-hotspot survey of plant utility and process equipment. instances.label: Small to mid-size commercial building (retail store, restaurant, bank branch, small office) with packaged rooftop HVAC and no central BMS. Auditor walks sales floor and back-of-house, climbs to the roof to inspect RTUs and read nameplates, checks thermostats, lighting panels, the main service panel and utility meter for spare breaker space and CT locations, and interviews the manager; determines whether smart thermostats, a DR controller and load-shed relays can be installed and which loads can be curtailed at peak.

Mid-size to large office or institutional building with an existing building automation system. Auditor tours mechanical rooms (chillers, boilers, air handlers, VFDs), electrical rooms and switchgear, reviews the BMS graphics, point list, schedules and trends with the building engineer, checks controller models, spare I/O, BACnet/network infrastructure and submetering; determines feasibility of an OpenADR gateway and curtailment sequences.

Grocery store or big-box retail with refrigeration racks and multiple rooftop units and an existing EMS. Auditor inspects compressor racks, condensers, walk-in cases, anti-sweat heaters, roof units, the EMS panel and submeters; assesses which loads can be shed without product-temperature or comfort violations and whether added control points and metering are feasible.

Warehouse, distribution center or light manufacturing plant. Auditor walks production and dock areas, inspects motor control centers, air compressors, process equipment, high-bay lighting and charging rooms, discusses production constraints with plant staff; determines which loads are interruptible and where curtailment controls, metering and communications hardware could be installed.

Large campus, hospital or data center with a central plant. Auditor examines chillers, pumps, towers, thermal storage potential, main switchgear, standby generators, paralleling gear and transfer switches under escort and PPE rules; assesses curtailment, generator dispatch or storage participation given life-safety and uptime constraints, coordinating with facilities engineering.

sources.title: Automated Inspections Made Simple | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot performs autonomous inspection missions in industrial facilities, capturing thermal images, gauge readings and visual data, but the route and every inspection action must first be recorded by a human operator manually driving the robot through the site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine equipment inspection rounds in a facility, involving the same objects an energy auditor examines (motors, gauges, electrical gear) in the same kind of building. Transfer is limited to repeat data capture along a human-taught route; it does not cover a first-visit examination, and the output is sensor data, not an installation-feasibility determination.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inspection of electrical equipment, the closest deployed analog to an auditor examining switchgear and electrical rooms. Missions are pre-configured against known assets in an institutionally controlled facility and report anomalies, rather than assessing whether new control hardware could be installed.

instances.label: Single-family home audit: auditor arrives at an owner-occupied house taken as found (clutter, pets, occupants), sets up and runs a blower-door depressurization test in an exterior doorway, scans walls/ceilings with an infrared camera, climbs into attic and crawlspace to measure insulation depth and check ducts, records furnace/water-heater/appliance nameplate and combustion-safety readings, reads the utility meter, photographs conditions, then enters the data into modeling software to produce savings estimates.

Small commercial building (retail store, restaurant, small office) walkthrough audit: escorted by the manager, count and identify lighting fixtures and controls, climb a ladder to the roof to record rooftop HVAC unit nameplates and filter/condition data, read the utility meter and electrical panel schedules, take clamp-meter spot readings on selected circuits, log equipment operating schedules, then compile a Level 1 report.

Large commercial/institutional building (office tower, school, hospital, campus): tour mechanical rooms to record boiler, chiller, pump and air-handler data; pull trend data from the building automation system; install portable data loggers and current transformer clamps on panels and equipment for one to two weeks; thermal-scan roof and facade for envelope losses; retrieve loggers and reconcile the field data with utility billing for an ASHRAE Level 2 analysis.

Industrial/process plant full energy audit: measure motor loads and power factor with clamp-on meters, run a boiler combustion-efficiency test, conduct a steam-trap survey, measure compressed-air system pressure, flow and leakage, sample process heat and ventilation loads, interview operators about production schedules, then build an energy balance and investment-grade measure list.

Recurring targeted energy-loss survey along a fixed route in an industrial or utility facility: walk the plant with an ultrasonic/acoustic leak detector and thermal camera to find compressed-air and steam leaks and hot electrical/mechanical equipment, log locations and readings, and compile a leak list with estimated annual energy loss and repair priority.

Multifamily building audit: sample a set of occupied apartment units (each taken as found, with tenants' belongings), running blower-door and infrared checks in units, inventorying in-unit appliances and heating equipment, plus common areas and the central boiler/domestic-hot-water room, then aggregate the field data into a building-level energy model.

instances.label: Walkthrough spot measurements during a commercial/institutional audit (office, school, retail): illuminance readings with a light meter at workstations and in corridors, air temperature/RH with a thermometer or psychrometer, surface temperatures with an IR thermometer, and reading utility/sub-meter and equipment displays. Occupied, staffed building, standard layout.

Multi-day ambient monitoring in a commercial/institutional facility: distributing temperature/RH, light and occupancy data loggers across zones for one to two weeks, then retrieving them and downloading the time series used for the energy model.

Electrical measurements in mechanical/electrical rooms of a commercial or industrial facility: clamp-on amp probe and volt meter spot readings on motors, pumps, panels and MCCs, plus installing a three-phase power/watt logger with current transformers on live conductors for a week and removing it. PPE and live-panel safety procedures.

Boiler/furnace combustion testing in a plant or central boiler room: inserting a flue gas analyzer probe into the stack test port, measuring O2/CO/stack temperature and draft, and computing combustion efficiency across firing rates.
Industrial energy-loss survey on a plant floor: ultrasonic/acoustic compressed-air and steam leak detection and thermal scanning of hot equipment, electrical gear and insulation, logged by asset.

Residential/small-building audit in an occupied home: handheld light meter and thermometer/psychrometer readings, plug-load watt meter on appliances, clamp-on amp reading at the load center, reading the house utility meter, and temperature/humidity readings in attic and crawlspace. Cluttered, unstandardized, occupants and pets present.

instances.label: Occupied existing single-family home, residential energy audit / weatherization assessment: auditor preps the house (closes windows and exterior doors, opens interior doors, shuts dampers, covers fireplace ash), fits the adjustable aluminum frame and fabric panel into an exterior doorway, mounts the calibrated fan, runs hoses to the manometer, performs a multi-point depressurization to 50 Pa, then walks the house with a smoke pencil, IR camera and hand to locate and document leaks (rim joists, attic hatch, outlets, penetrations), and removes the rig. Furniture, clutter, pets and occupants present; varied door sizes and floor plans.

Newly built single-family home at a construction site or just before closing, blower-door test for IECC code compliance / HERS rating: dusty unfinished or newly finished interior, temporary power, other trades present, must verify HVAC registers and dryer/bath fans are configured, install the frame in a job-site door, run the test to a pass/fail ACH50 threshold and report the result.

Individual apartment or condo unit in a multifamily building, compartmentalization test: small-capacity fan/MiniFan carried through corridors and stairs, frame fitted into a unit entry door or balcony door, corridor and adjacent-unit pressures considered, unit-by-unit repetition; units are occupied or partly furnished with varied layouts.

Small commercial or institutional building (office suite, school wing, retail, clinic) whole-building air leakage test, often multi-fan setups in a large entry door or a temporary panel, performed off-hours with facility staff controlling access; auditor coordinates HVAC shutdown, seals intentional openings, runs the test and locates leaks at doors, curtain wall joints and roof/wall interfaces.

Duct leakage (duct blaster) test and zone pressure diagnostics in a home: taping off supply registers, connecting the calibrated fan to a return grille or air handler cabinet, pressurizing the duct system, reading CFM25, and pinpointing duct leaks with smoke or pressure pans.

sources.system: Blower door test procedure (Minneapolis Blower Door / Retrotec-class equipment)
sources.title: Blower Door Testing - InterNACHI
sources.claim: A blower door test requires a technician to temporarily mount a variable-speed calibrated fan into an exterior door frame; leak locations are then pinpointed while the building is depressurized. This defines the manual setup and walkthrough work the task requires.

sources.transferJustification: Directly the same task's instrumentation: it shows the automated portion covers only fan control and data logging, not rig installation, enclosure preparation, or leak localization.

instances.label: Post-installation QA inspection at an occupied single-family home after a weatherization/retrofit job: verify attic and wall insulation coverage and depth, inspect air-sealing work, check the new heat pump/furnace/water heater (mounting, line set, refrigerant charge, venting/combustion safety, filter and airflow), inspect duct sealing, and re-run blower-door and duct-leakage tests; requires crawling attics/crawlspaces and setting up portable test instruments amid occupants' belongings.

Verification inspection on a new-construction or gut-rehab jobsite before occupancy (HERS-rater style): grade installed insulation, inspect envelope and window details, confirm installed HVAC/water-heating equipment model numbers and capacities match spec sheets, and perform blower-door and duct-leakage testing amid ongoing trade work, debris, and partial finishes.

Verification of a lighting and lighting-controls retrofit in an institution-controlled commercial building (office, school, warehouse): sample-count installed LED fixtures against the measure spec, verify fixture type/wattage and labeling, measure illuminance, functionally test occupancy sensors and daylight dimming, and spot-measure circuit power; work from ladders/lifts during or after hours.

Verification of newly installed commercial HVAC and controls measures (rooftop units, VFDs on fans/pumps, economizers, new BAS sequences) in a commercial or institutional building: inspect the installation on the roof and in mechanical rooms, measure supply/return temperatures, airflow and amp draw, exercise control sequences, and trend BAS points to confirm performance against design specification.

Verification of newly installed efficiency measures in an industrial/process plant (premium-efficiency motors, VFDs, compressed-air upgrades, heat recovery): inspect installation, piping and wiring, log kW with a portable power meter, read pressures/temperatures/flows, run a leak survey, and compare in-situ performance to the design/savings specification while escorted under plant PPE rules.

instances.label: Occupied single-family home on a weatherization/direct-install job: the auditor directs the install crew (and personally installs several measures) — low-flow showerheads and faucet aerators, a water heater blanket around a tank in a cramped closet or basement, foam/fiberglass sleeves on accessible hot-water piping, weatherstripping and a door sweep on exterior doors. Clutter, pets, occupants present, non-standard fixtures, corroded threads, gas-appliance clearance rules.

Multifamily property, unit-by-unit direct install: the auditor walks the crew through dozens of similar apartments installing showerheads, aerators, pipe wrap and door weatherstripping/sweeps, coordinating tenant access, resolving unit-to-unit differences (fixture types, door conditions), and logging measures per unit for program records.

Small commercial or institutional building (office, retail, school, church): auditor oversees a contractor insulating mechanical-room domestic hot-water piping and storage tanks, weatherstripping exterior/vestibule doors, and swapping restroom fixtures to low-flow; ladder work, boiler rooms, facility staff escort, work scheduled around occupants.

Post-installation QC/verification visit at a home: inspect each installed measure against spec — tug and gap-check weatherstripping, confirm the door sweep contacts the threshold, verify blanket coverage without blocking controls/vents, check pipe sleeve seams, bag-test or verify showerhead flow rate — photo-document, write up deficiencies, and direct rework.

On-site coaching and spec enforcement with the installation crew: demonstrating correct technique for a measure, deciding field deviations (e.g., skip a wrap on a gas water heater for draft-hood clearance, substitute a different sweep on a warped door), and adjusting the work order scope on the spot.

sources.title: E.ON and Q-Bot team up to use robotics and AI to help insulate Britain's homes
sources.claim: Q-Bot's building-retrofit robot, used commercially in UK homes with E.ON, applies spray-foam insulation beneath suspended floors, but it is a remotely operated device — the closest fielded robot to residential energy-efficiency retrofit work, and it is teleoperated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing insulation retrofit measures in occupied homes — the same buildings and measure class as this task. It shows the state of the art in home retrofit robotics is remote human operation, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid
sources.claim: Consumer home humanoids that might otherwise perform multi-step household installation work rely on human teleoperators for complex tasks; no humanoid has been shown completing a household chore end-to-end autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general in-home manipulation of ordinary household objects and fixtures, the capability class needed to install or hands-on-verify showerheads, wraps and door sweeps in homes. Teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Roboattic / PARIS (Precise Air-sealing Robot for Inaccessible Spaces)
sources.title: Ushering in the Future of Building Retrofits | NREL
sources.claim: Robotic systems for attic air-sealing and insulation in existing buildings exist only as DOE/NREL-funded research prototypes (Roboattic, PARIS), not fielded systems performing accepted retrofit work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying air-sealing/insulation energy-efficiency measures inside existing buildings. Research prototype with unclear autonomy, so it cannot substantiate completion of an oversight-and-install visit.

sources.title: Case Study: Practical Autonomy on Construction Sites | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: FieldAI-powered Boston Dynamics Spot performs autonomous inspection and progress-monitoring walks on active construction sites, capturing site data without pre-planned routes — but it only collects data; it does not install measures, make acceptance judgments on installed weatherization work, or direct rework.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous walk-through inspection/documentation of building work in progress. It covers only the data-capture portion of oversight, with no manipulation of installed measures and no accept/reject or rework direction, so it does not carry over to completing this task.

sources.system: Robotic gasket dispense station (Fanuc LR Mate 200iD + Graco Therm-O-Flow)
sources.title: Robotic Gasket Dispense - Flexible Automation Inc.
sources.claim: In fenced industrial cells, robots autonomously handle seal-related work on fixtured automotive parts — a Fanuc LR Mate 200iD ... Graco dispensing applies butyl mastic into the channel of a rubber ... weatherstrip — demonstrating E1-level seal work limited to one known part geometry presented to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated application/inspection of elastomeric weatherseal material on a fixtured workpiece. It is single-part, single-material adhesive dispensing, not fitting weatherstrip and sweeps to varied doors nor overseeing a multi-measure job, so the transfer to this task fails.

sources.system: Cognex In-Sight vision system on a robot arm (assembly verification)
sources.title: Assembly Verification with Vision Guided Robotics | Cognex
sources.claim: Vision-guided robotic assembly verification (Cognex In-Sight carried on a robot arm) autonomously inspects fixtured automotive assemblies for the presence and position of components in factory cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated verification that components were correctly installed. It is limited to taught inspection points on identical fixtured parts, whereas this task requires tactile/functional checks of varied measures in buildings and direction of rework, so it does not carry over.

sources.title: How Automation Is Transforming Door Manufacturing - ELMENS
sources.claim: Even inside door-manufacturing plants — the most structured possible setting for weatherstrip and hardware fitting — hardware installation remains a manual, variable operation rather than an automated one.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fitting weatherstrip/hardware to doors in a purpose-built production setting. It indicates that even fixtured door hardware fitting is not generally automated, supporting a negative judgment at E1.
