roles.title: Elevator and Escalator Installers and Repairers
aliases: Accessibility and Private Residence Lift Technician (Accessibility and Private Residence Lift Tech)
Accessibility and Private Residence Lift Tech
Elevator Repair and Maintenance Technician (Elevator Repair and Maintenance Tech)
roles.description: Assemble, install, repair, or maintain electric or hydraulic freight or passenger elevators, escalators, or dumbwaiters.

tasks.label: Inspect wiring connections, control panel hookups, door installations, and alignments and clearances of cars and hoistways to ensure that equipment will operate properly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled maintenance/annual inspection of an in-service passenger elevator in an occupied office, hospital or hotel building: open the controller in the machine room and check wiring terminations, terminal tightness and panel hookups; ride the car top through the hoistway at inspection speed checking door operator, hangers, gibs, interlocks, sill-to-sill and running clearances; verify leveling and proper operation.

Final check-out of a new elevator installation in a building still under construction: verify rail alignment/plumbness, car-to-hoistway and car-to-counterweight clearances, landing door sill and door installation clearances, field wiring into the controller and travel cable hookups, then run the car to confirm proper operation. Dust, temporary lighting, other trades and debris in the shaft.

Callback/troubleshooting visit in an occupied building: elevator shut down or doors misbehaving; inspect control panel hookups and wiring connections for loose, burnt or chattering terminals/relays, check door installation, alignment and clearances, isolate the fault and confirm the equipment will operate properly after adjustment.

Escalator or moving-walk inspection in a mall or transit station during off hours: check controller cabinet wiring and hookups in the truss, step-to-skirt and step-to-comb clearances, step band alignment, handrail tracking and safety switch operation; work partly from the pit/wellway with the unit barricaded.

Modernization or legacy/one-off equipment: pre-mod survey or post-mod check on a decades-old relay-logic or hydraulic elevator in a small commercial building, or a limited-use/residential elevator in a private home — cramped hand-built machine space, no as-built documentation, nonstandard door and rail configurations.

sources.system: Cognex In-Sight vision system on Fanuc robot (Piston Group inspection station)
sources.title: Robot Vision System Increases Quality and Reduces Costs for Piston Group
sources.claim: A Cognex In-Sight vision system mounted on a Fanuc robot performs the complete end-of-line inspection of automotive front-end modules in an automated check station, verifying build variant, that all electrical connectors are fully seated and engaged, and dimensional requirements to about 1 mm — a robotic cell that inspects wiring/connector hookups and dimensional conformance on a fixtured assembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line inspection of wiring-harness/connector hookups and dimensional tolerances on an assembled module. Transfers to inspecting elevator controller hookups and door/car dimensional conformance because the objects (harnesses, connectors, sheet-metal assemblies), the mm-level tolerances and the pass/fail conformance judgment are comparable, provided the work is presented fixtured in a cell.

sources.system: Comau RACER-5 COBOT gap & flush inspection system with EDIXIA vision
sources.title: Stellantis Gap and Flush case study - Comau
sources.claim: Comau's RACER-5 collaborative robot with an integrated EDIXIA vision system fully automates gap-and-flush (panel alignment/clearance) inspection on car bodies at Stellantis final assembly, measuring alignment points along the whole body with repeatability of a few tenths of a millimetre — better than the manual method.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated measurement of door/panel gaps, flush and alignment on an assembled product. Elevator work of 'door installations, and alignments and clearances' is the same class of measurement (mm-level gaps between sheet-metal doors, sills and frames) on a presented assembly.

sources.system: Perceptron HELIX scanning sensor; Hexagon 360° Smart Inline Measurement Solutions (SIMS)
sources.title: Perceptron Adds HELIX HDR for Automotive and Aerospace Measuring Applications
sources.claim: Robot-carried laser scanning sensors are used across the automotive industry for in-process dimensional and gap-and-flush measurement of car bodies in inline measurement cells; Hexagon markets 360° SIMS robotic 3D metrology cells for fully automated dimensional quality control in automotive plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated dimensional inspection of clearances and alignment on large assemblies in fenced measuring cells. Comparable to checking car/hoistway running clearances and door alignment when the workpiece is presented in a known, fixtured position.

sources.system: Schindler R.I.S.E (Robotic Installation System for Elevators)
sources.title: Pioneering robotic system Schindler R.I.S.E now operational | Schindler Group
sources.claim: Schindler R.I.S.E, a self-climbing robot that works autonomously inside elevator shafts on construction sites, has been deployed commercially at dozens of job sites; its function is drilling holes and setting anchor bolts for guide-rail brackets, not inspecting wiring, control panels, doors or clearances.
sources.transferJustification: Same environment (an elevator hoistway during installation) as instance 1; cited to show the scope of what is actually deployed in hoistways — drilling and anchor setting under BIM guidance — and that no deployed in-shaft robot performs the wiring, control-panel, door and clearance inspection this task requires.

sources.title: From Robot to Colleague: True Autonomy in Industrial Inspection - Inside Unmanned Systems
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal legged robot runs autonomous inspection rounds in industrial plants, refineries and substations, collecting visual, thermal, acoustic and lidar data (e.g. thermal readings on electrical equipment), but the work is sensor-based data collection on a route, not hands-on inspection of wiring terminations, door hardware or dimensional clearances.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inspection rounds in a structured human facility (E2), including thermal checks of electrical equipment. Cited to bound what E2 inspection robots do today: they cannot open control panels, check terminal connections, ride car tops or gauge door/hoistway clearances.

tasks.label: Assemble, install, repair, and maintain elevators, escalators, moving sidewalks, and dumbwaiters, using hand and power tools, and testing devices such as test lamps, ammeters, and voltmeters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled preventive-maintenance visit on passenger elevators in an occupied commercial or institutional building (office tower, hospital, hotel): ride the car, inspect machine-room controller and brake, work from the car top in the hoistway, lubricate rails and bearings, adjust door operator and safety edges, clean the pit, test safeties with meters and test lamps, log results.

Trouble call / repair in an occupied building (a minority in private homes, small residential elevators and dumbwaiters): release an entrapment, diagnose an intermittent fault with voltmeter/ammeter across relays, door restrictors, hoistway switches or a controller board, replace the failed part (door operator belt, roller guides, contactor, board, hydraulic valve), retest and return the unit to service.

New elevator installation in a building under construction (main erection phase): set guide-rail brackets and align rails, install machine or hydraulic jack, assemble car sling, cab and counterweight, hang ropes, set landing door frames, sills and operators, run hoistway wiring and travelling cable, mount and wire the controller, then adjust and test.

New high-rise construction, shaft-preparation phase: survey and lay out the concrete hoistway, drill the several hundred to several thousand fixing holes in the shaft walls and set anchor bolts for guide-rail brackets and landing door frames, working in a dusty, noisy shaft off a temporary platform.

Modernization in an existing occupied building: strip out old controller, machine, door operators and fixtures in a cramped legacy machine room and hoistway, install and wire new equipment matched to the existing shaft, then test and adjust to code with instruments.

Escalator or moving-walk maintenance and repair in a mall, transit station or airport: remove steps/pallets for inspection, check and tension the step chain, replace combplates, handrails or rollers, adjust drive and brake, clean the truss and pits, test safety switches, all inside a barricaded work zone in a public facility.

sources.system: Schindler R.I.S.E (Robotic Installation System for Elevators)
sources.title: Pioneering robotic system Schindler R.I.S.E now operational
sources.claim: Schindler R.I.S.E is a self-climbing, autonomous robot that performs the shaft-wall preparation part of elevator installation (locating positions, drilling holes, setting anchor bolts) in hoistways of buildings under construction; commercially deployed on customer projects since 2020.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (elevator installation) but only the layout/drilling/anchor-setting portion; cited to substantiate the shaft-preparation instance only, not full installation.

sources.developer: Schindler with ABB Robotics and ETH Zurich
sources.title: Autonomous drilling robot debut | News center | ABB
sources.claim: Technical account of R.I.S.E: an ABB IRB 2600 on a self-hoisting platform scans the shaft wall for rebar, recomputes hole coordinates to tolerance, then drills and hammers in anchor bolts repeatedly with no operator monitoring or controlling it.

sources.title: Robots rise at Schindler | The Construction Index
sources.claim: As of June 2026 Schindler runs seven R.I.S.E robots, deployed at 36 job sites ... with roughly 50,000 anchor bolts installed; the robot works to a pre-uploaded digital plan, and its scope remains measuring, drilling and anchor-bolt setting for guide rails and landing doors — not rail erection, car assembly, roping or wiring.

sources.title: Jaibot Semi-Autonomous Drilling Robot - Hilti GB
sources.claim: Hilti Jaibot is a commercially available construction drilling robot that, after total-station site layout, drills large numbers of anchor holes in concrete to a BIM-derived plan on active construction sites without step-by-step operator control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: BIM-driven anchor-hole drilling in concrete on active construction sites. Same materials (concrete, anchors), comparable millimetre layout precision, and the same unstructured jobsite conditions as elevator shaft-wall preparation.

tasks.label: Disassemble defective units, and repair or replace parts such as locks, gears, cables, and electric wiring.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/institutional building (office tower, hospital, hotel): troubleshoot a door fault and disassemble the car/landing door system — replace hoistway door interlocks, contacts, rollers, gibs, door-operator belts, linkages and limit switches — working from the car top or at the landing in a confined hoistway on equipment of mixed vintage and manufacturer.

Machine room or machine-roomless overhead space: open the traction machine or controller and replace defective mechanical parts — brake pads/coils and springs, worn gears and bearings in a geared machine, sheave liners, contactors and relays in the controller cabinet — with the car parked and power locked out.

Electrical repair: trace an intermittent circuit and replace burnt or chafed electric wiring, terminals, traveling cable, harness sections, fuses, relay boards or a controller PC board; re-terminate, land conductors, and verify safety-circuit operation before returning the unit to service.

Hoist cable/rope work: rig and replace worn hoist ropes, compensating ropes or governor rope, including hitch/wedge socket rebuilds, shackle and spring assembly, rope tensioning/equalizing, and associated sheave or governor overhaul in the hoistway and overhead.

Escalator/moving walk in a transit station, airport or mall: pull steps and open the truss, disassemble the drive — replace step chain, step rollers, drive chain, sprockets/gears, handrail drive components and worn wiring/switches — in a greasy, confined pit with the unit barricaded off from the public.

Private residence or small building: repair a home elevator, LULA or dumbwaiter — replace a worn drive belt/chain, gearbox part, door lock, limit switch or damaged wiring — in a cramped closet/basement machine space taken as found, with non-standard, sometimes obsolete equipment.

sources.system: Schindler R.I.S.E (Robotic Installation System for Elevators)
sources.title: Pioneering robotic system Schindler R.I.S.E now operational | Schindler Group
sources.claim: Schindler R.I.S.E, the closest robotic system to elevator field work, autonomously drills holes and sets anchor bolts for guide-rail brackets and landing doors in new elevator shafts; it performs no disassembly, part replacement or repair of defective units.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: elevator installation drilling/anchoring inside a hoistway. It shows an autonomous robot can work in a shaft, but capability does not transfer: R.I.S.E executes a pre-uploaded drilling plan on bare concrete and never disassembles an existing unit, diagnoses a fault, or replaces locks, gears, cables or wiring.

sources.title: Robots rise at Schindler | The Construction Index
sources.claim: R.I.S.E operates autonomously in the shaft from a pre-uploaded digital work plan, and its demonstrated scope is limited to measuring positions, drilling and installing anchor bolts.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (shaft installation drilling); cited to establish autonomy and to bound the demonstrated scope, which excludes disassembly of defective units and replacement of parts.

sources.title: How Apple Uses Robots to Reduce E-Waste | Sustainability Magazine
sources.claim: The most capable fixtured product-teardown robot, Apple's Daisy, disassembles a fixed set of known iPhone models on a purpose-built line for material recovery; it separates parts but does not diagnose faults, replace components, or reassemble a working unit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly of an end-of-life/defective unit fixtured in a purpose-built cell — the E1 counterfactual for this task. Transfer fails because Daisy handles only pre-identified standardized models and its output is separated scrap, not a repaired unit returned to service.

sources.developer: University of Birmingham (Journal of Remanufacturing case study)
sources.title: An experimental robotic cell for the disassembly of electric vehicle battery modules | Journal of Remanufacturing
sources.claim: Robotic disassembly of used assemblies remains prototype-stage even inside a purpose-built fenced cell, and the demonstrated process is disassembly only, validated on a mock-up module, with no fault repair or reassembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous teardown of a used assembly with fasteners, cabling and connectors fixtured in a cell — the closest analogue to the E1 counterfactual here. It shows the state of the art stops at disassembly of a single known design on a mock-up, short of repair and reassembly.

tasks.label: Check that safety regulations and building codes are met, and complete service reports verifying conformance to standards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine periodic (monthly/quarterly) maintenance visit on passenger elevators in an institution-controlled commercial building (office tower, hospital, hotel): mechanic rides the car and car top, enters the pit and machine room, verifies door restrictors, door reopening devices and closing force, leveling, emergency light/phone, firefighter Phase I/II operation, signage and machine-room code items, notes deficiencies, then writes and signs the service report/compliance ticket.

Annual Category 1 no-load safety test on a traction or hydraulic elevator in a commercial building, commonly witnessed by a licensed QEI inspector: trip the overspeed governor, set the car safeties, test buffers, brake, emergency terminal devices, hydraulic relief valve and low-oil protection, then reset, tag the equipment and complete the signed test/conformance report.

Periodic safety inspection of an escalator or moving walk in a mall, transit station or airport: check comb impact and missing-step devices, skirt obstruction switches and clearances, handrail speed and entry guards, step chain tension/wear, run a brake stopping-distance test, verify guards and signage, and complete the inspection/service report.

Acceptance/final inspection of a new or modernized elevator at an active construction or renovation site before the AHJ certificate: verify hoistway, pit and overhead running clearances, guarding, fire alarm and sprinkler interfaces, emergency power, ADA/code items and required data plates; produce punch list and conformance documentation for the inspector.

Compliance check on residential or light-commercial equipment in an uncontrolled setting — private-home elevator, LULA, small apartment building elevator or dumbwaiter — typically after a repair or callback: verify gate switches, door interlocks, clearances/space guarding, emergency communication and code-required devices, then complete the service report.

Five-year Category 5 full-load, rated-speed test on a traction elevator in a commercial building: load the car with certified test weights, run the governor overspeed trip and safety test at rated speed, test brake with full load, verify buffer and emergency brake operation, unload, and complete the signed test report.

sources.system: Schindler R.I.S.E. (Robotic Installation System for Elevators)
sources.title: Robots rise at Schindler — The Construction Index
sources.claim: Schindler R.I.S.E. is a real, autonomously operating robot deployed in elevator hoistways on construction sites, but its function is measuring, drilling and setting anchor bolts for rail and door brackets — it performs installation work, not safety/code inspection or conformance reporting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic work inside an elevator hoistway. It shows a robot can operate in the shaft environment, but the task here requires functional safety testing (governor trips, door force, brake tests), code-conformance judgement and a signed service report, none of which R.I.S.E. performs; so it does not substantiate completion of this task at any tier.

sources.title: Schindler's Robotic Installation System for Elevators | Schindler Group
sources.claim: Schindler states the R.I.S.E. robot operates fully autonomously once installed in the shaft, with remote monitoring — establishing the autonomy of the closest elevator-domain field robot, which nonetheless only installs anchors.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (hoistway installation drilling); cited to document the frontier of autonomous elevator-shaft robotics and to show it does not extend to inspection, testing or compliance reporting.

sources.title: Thermal Sensing & Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot performs autonomous, scheduled inspection rounds in industrial facilities, capturing thermal/visual/acoustic data on equipment and feeding it to asset-management systems; it collects condition data rather than performing functional safety tests or issuing code-conformance verdicts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous routine equipment inspection rounds inside a structured facility (E2). Transfer fails for this task because elevator/escalator code verification requires actuating safety devices (tripping governors, applying force gauges, key-switch fire service tests), entering pits and riding car tops, and rendering a signed conformance judgement — capabilities not shown for Spot.

sources.title: The Next Step in Safe, Autonomous Robotic Inspection — Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Autonomous manipulation on Spot inspection missions was, as of late 2025, limited to newly released door-opening during Autowalk missions, indicating that autonomous contact tasks by inspection robots remain very narrow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation during inspection rounds. Cited to bound the frontier: the manipulations required to test elevator safety devices are far beyond autonomous door opening, so no transfer to this task is supported.

sources.title: Advanced Drone Autonomy for Indoor Inspection: Inside the Elios 3
sources.claim: Flyability's Elios confined-space inspection drones are the mainstream tool for visual data capture in shafts and other confined spaces, but they are pilot-operated data-capture platforms with only assistive autonomy features, and the manufacturer does not provide inspection services or compliance determinations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: confined-space visual inspection, the closest analogue to hoistway survey. It is pilot-flown and produces imagery only, so under the teleoperation rule it cannot support a positive judgement for this task.

tasks.label: Locate malfunctions in brakes, motors, switches, and signal and control systems, using test equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Callback on a stalled or misbehaving traction passenger elevator in an office, retail, hospital or apartment building: the mechanic reads controller fault codes, then traces the fault with a multimeter/tester through the safety string, door locks and gate switches, relays/contactors, drive and encoder feedback, working in the machine room, on the car top, in the hoistway and pit. Cramped, dirty, layout differs building to building; live 120/480V circuits.

Escalator or moving walk in a transit station, airport or shopping mall that has shut down or trips intermittently: mechanic opens step-band/floor plates and works inside the truss and pit with a meter to find which safety device (comb impact, handrail speed, step upthrust, skirt obstruction, drive-chain switch), brake coil/microswitch, motor winding or controller input is at fault, often an intermittent fault with the public nearby.

Scheduled preventive-maintenance electrical testing to find developing faults in discrete components: megger/insulation and winding tests on the hoist or pump motor, brake coil resistance and current draw, contact resistance on contactors and relays, continuity of limit and interlock switches, signal/control voltages on the controller board and door operator, in a commercial building machine room.

Hydraulic elevator in a low-rise or apartment building that drifts, fails to level or will not run: diagnosing the power unit (pump motor starter, valve solenoid coils, pressure/leak behaviour) and associated control wiring with meter and pressure gauge in a small machine room next to the shaft.

Private-residence home elevator or LULA lift: diagnosing a controller, interlock/limit switch, door contact or drive fault in a homeowner's basement, garage closet or under-stair machine space; unpredictable layout, non-standard equipment, occupants and pets present.

New installation or modernization commissioning on an active construction/renovation site: locating wiring errors, mis-landed control signals, faulty switches or drive parameter/feedback faults with test equipment in an unfinished hoistway and temporary machine room, amid dust, temporary power and other trades.

sources.system: SPEA flying probe testers (4x/6x flying probe board test systems)
sources.title: Electronic Board Testing: ICT, Flying Probe & Functional | SPEA
sources.claim: SPEA flying-probe board testers are commercial machines whose independently moving probes automatically contact an electronic board and produce a component-level diagnostic report identifying the faulty part, used by repair centres as well as production lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: locating faults in electronic control boards with automated test equipment. Elevator 'signal and control system' fault-finding at board level involves the same objects (populated PCBs) and measurements (continuity, resistance, in-circuit parameters) at finer precision than hand probing, but only when the board is removed and presented fixtured to the machine.

sources.system: Takaya APT-9411 / APT-1600FD flying probe test systems
sources.date: 2020-06 distributor page; series in production use through 2025
sources.title: FLYING PROBE Testers - TAKAYA — CPS-IEP
sources.claim: Takaya APT-9411 flying probe systems automatically detect defects on assembled printed circuit boards with four independently moving probes, without a bed-of-nails fixture, in an enclosed conveyor-fed machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated probing and electrical fault detection on circuit boards; transfers to the control-board portion of elevator troubleshooting only inside a purpose-built cell where the board is fixtured and its netlist known.

sources.system: Klotz EOL test benches for high-performance electric motors
sources.title: End-of-line testing for high-performance electric motors | Klotz
sources.claim: Klotz end-of-line test benches for electric motors perform fully automatic set-up and electrical contacting and run performance and leakage tests autonomously, i.e. the machine itself makes the measurement connections and evaluates the unit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated electrical testing of a motor brought to a fixtured station. Elevator PM testing of a hoist or pump motor uses the same measurements (winding resistance, insulation, current draw, performance) on comparable machines; carries over only when the motor is presented to the bench.

sources.system: Marposs E.D.C. AMT320/W motor functional test systems
sources.title: End-Of-Line Testing Of Electric Motors | Marposs
sources.claim: Marposs AMT320/W functional test systems perform automatic end-of-line testing of assembled electric motors (DC, AC, synchronous, asynchronous) in production environments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated functional/electrical fault screening of complete motors on a fixtured station, comparable to a mechanic's electrical tests on an elevator machine once the unit is presented to the tester.

sources.system: Robotic Arm-Assisted PCB Diagnostic and Measurement System
sources.title: Implementation of a Robotic Arm-Assisted PCB Diagnostic and Measurement System | IJARIS
sources.claim: A robotic-arm system automatically positions probes on predefined PCB test points and takes voltage and resistance measurements for diagnosis, showing machine-performed meter measurements rather than fixed-fixture testing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: taking meter measurements at electrical test points with a robot arm — the same instrument and measurements as elevator control-circuit testing, but only at predefined points on a board held in a known position.

sources.title: Hydraulic Test Stands - hainzl.at
sources.claim: Hainzl hydraulic test stands run automated pressure, leakage and friction test sequences on valves, cylinders and hydraulic components inside a closed test cell with continuous system monitoring.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated functional testing of hydraulic valves and cylinders in a fixtured cell — comparable components to a hydraulic elevator power unit's control valve; supports fault screening only when the unit is removed and connected to the stand.

sources.system: Spot with thermal / acoustic imaging inspection payloads
sources.title: Boston Dynamics’ robot dog patrols 1.5 million-square-foot factory
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot is deployed to autonomously patrol a 1.5-million-sq-ft manufacturing facility with thermal and acoustic imaging payloads, flagging overheating components, abnormal vibration and leaks; it does not perform circuit-level electrical fault tracing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous condition monitoring of machinery in a structured facility (E2) — the closest field capability, but it only reports sensor anomalies on accessible equipment and cannot probe safety strings, switches or controller terminals, so it does not complete this task's instances.

sources.system: Schindler R.I.S.E (Robotic Installation System for Elevators)
sources.title: Robots rise at Schindler | The Construction Index
sources.claim: Schindler R.I.S.E, a self-climbing robot, works autonomously inside elevator hoistways on real job sites, having set roughly 50,000 anchor bolts across 36 sites; its demonstrated work is drilling and installation, not electrical fault diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Shows a robot can physically operate in the elevator hoistway environment, but the demonstrated work is scanning, marking, drilling and bolt setting; no evidence of fault localization in brakes, motors, switches or control circuits.

tasks.label: Adjust safety controls, counterweights, door mechanisms, and components such as valves, ratchets, seals, and brake linings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Passenger elevator door system out of adjustment in a commercial or institutional building (office tower, hospital, school): mechanic works from the car top and at landings, adjusting the door operator cam/clutch, hanger rollers, up-thrust and gib clearances, closing speed and force, restrictor and interlock engagement, then re-tests door cycling and code-limit closing force at several floors on legacy equipment of varied make and vintage.

Adjustment and verification of safety controls during scheduled maintenance or a periodic (Cat 1) test: normal and final limit switches, terminal slowdown, door lock and gate switches, pit and car-top stop switches, overspeed governor trip setting and safety-gear linkage, load-weighing device; work spans machine room, hoistway and pit with repeated run-and-check cycles and code documentation.

Traction machine brake service in the machine room: measuring and setting brake shoe clearance, spring compression and torque, adjusting or replacing worn brake linings and running a drag/stopping test, on geared or gearless machines of many makes, in a cramped, oily equipment room with the car parked.

Hydraulic elevator: adjusting the control valve (up/down leveling and acceleration screws, relief pressure setting) so the car levels and rides to spec, and replacing packing/O-ring seals on the valve block, jack head or cylinder; performed on the pump unit in the machine room and at the jack in the pit, with oil, temperature drift and iterative run-and-adjust cycles.

Counterweight adjustment during modernization or after a cabin/interior change: balance check, then adding or removing cast filler weights in the counterweight frame in the hoistway, re-securing tie rods and rechecking balance by running the car with test loads.

Escalator/moving walk adjustments at a transit station or mall: step chain and handrail tension, drive chain, brake torque and stopping distance, comb plate and step-to-skirt clearance, safety switch actuation, working inside the truss and pits during an off-hours shutdown.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: elevator installation drilling/anchoring in the same hoistway environment. Cited to show the frontier of robotics inside elevator shafts is repetitive drilling and bolt setting on a mapped shaft, which does not transfer to diagnostic mechanical adjustment of doors, brakes, safeties or valves.

sources.title: Schindler expands fleet of elevator shaft robots - Construction Management
sources.claim: After five years of deployment the R.I.S.E fleet has worked at 36 job sites and installed about 50,000 anchor bolts; the deployed capability remains drilling and anchor installation in construction shafts.

sources.system: RND Automation hydraulic valve assembly cell (Epson robots, SCHUNK gripper, ATI compliance device)
sources.title: Robots assemble hydraulic valves | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: An eight-station robotic cell built by RND Automation with Epson robots assembles hydraulic valves in a fixtured cell: robots fit O-rings onto adjustment screws, thread and drive the adjustment screws, load springs selected for the desired cracking pressure, and load finished units into a leak-test fixture, running with almost no operator intervention.

Objects (hydraulic valve bodies, adjustment screws, springs, O-rings), precision (threaded adjustment, leak-tight sealing) and the fixtured cell match the E1 counterfactual for adjusting an elevator hydraulic control valve and renewing its seals.

sources.title: Automated Assembly & Testing Line for Electro-Hydraulic Servo Valves

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic build-and-test of precision hydraulic valves. Shows a purpose-built robotic cell can bring a hydraulic valve to a verified functional specification - the closed loop a mechanic performs when setting an elevator valve - provided the valve is fixtured and presented to the machine.

sources.system: OHRMANN Internal O-Ring Installation Machine Series
sources.title: Internal O-Ring Installation Machine Series | OHRMANN
sources.claim: Ohrmann supplies automatic machines that install internal O-rings deep inside components with controlled insertion forces and repeatable quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated seal (O-ring) installation into recessed bores. Same class of object and precision as renewing packing/O-ring seals in an elevator hydraulic valve block or jack head when the part is fixtured in a purpose-built station.

instances.label: New-construction mid/high-rise traction passenger elevator: mechanics in a bare concrete hoistway of a building under construction reeve several hundred-foot 1/2"–5/8" steel hoist ropes from the overhead machine/sheaves, thread them over the traction sheave and deflector sheaves, cut to length, form babbitt or wedge-socket terminations, and hang the car frame crosshead hitch plate and counterweight hitch with shackle rods, springs, nuts and cotter pins, then equalize rope tension.

New-construction low-rise machine-room-less traction elevator (2–6 stops, small office, retail or apartment building under construction): reeve 2:1 roped car and counterweight over car-frame and counterweight sheaves and the compact machine, terminate ropes/belts at dead-end hitches in the overhead, tension and equalize, working from a work platform in a tight shaft.

Scheduled re-roping / hoist-rope replacement in an occupied existing building (office tower, hospital, hotel): mechanics work from the car top and in the machine room, use come-alongs and rope clamps to hold the load, pull new ropes with the old, socket the new ropes, reconnect car crosshead and counterweight hitches, and equalize tension before returning the car to service.

Modernization in an older existing building: car sling/frame or counterweight is replaced or rebuilt in a cramped, greasy legacy hoistway with non-standard geometry; new ropes are installed and connected between the new car frame hitch and counterweight hitch, often with rigging beams and hand-hoists in confined overheads.

Small residential/home traction elevator or counterweighted dumbwaiter: connect the light-duty steel cables between the car frame and counterweight in a private residence or small commercial back-of-house shaft, with limited access, no machine room, and site-built shaft conditions.

sources.system: Schindler R.I.S.E. (Robotic Installation System for Elevators)
sources.title: Schindler's Robotic Installation System for Elevators
sources.claim: Schindler R.I.S.E., the most advanced fielded elevator-installation robot, self-climbs a hoistway and autonomously drills holes and sets anchor bolts for landing doors, divider beams ...; its scope does not include reeving hoist ropes or connecting car frames to counterweights.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task: robotic work inside elevator hoistways during installation. It substantiates only drilling/anchor setting against a pre-programmed digital layout; it does not handle heavy deformable steel rope, sheave reeving, socketing or hitch assembly, so capability does not transfer to this task.

sources.title: Schindler expands RISE robot fleet as automated elevator installation demand grows
sources.claim: As of mid-2026 Schindler is expanding its R.I.S.E fleet, but the robot's work remains drilling holes and installing anchor ... at pre-programmed positions following a digital layout prepared in advance.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (in-hoistway installation robotics); confirms the state of the art in 2026 is limited to rigid drilling/bolting operations, not rope reeving and hitching.

sources.transferJustification: Not a robotic system; cited only to characterize the manual, damage-sensitive nature of the roping work that would have to be replicated at worker quality.

instances.label: New-construction installation: in an unfinished building, the mechanic lands hoistway riser conductors, car traveling-cable conductors and machine-room device wiring onto the terminal strips, contactors and drive terminals of a new elevator controller, per the job's wiring prints, then labels and torques the terminations. Dust, temporary lighting, shared shaft with other trades.

Modernization in an occupied building: a new controller replaces a legacy one in the machine room; the mechanic identifies and re-lands existing hoistway, car, safety-circuit, encoder and brake conductors on the new panel's terminal blocks and drive, working from as-built and new prints in a cramped legacy machine room.

Service/repair call: diagnose an intermittent or burned connection in an energized-or-locked-out controller (machine room or MRL cabinet at a landing), remove the failed conductor/contactor/connector and reconnect new wiring at the terminals, then verify operation. As-found wiring, no CAD model of the actual panel.

Power termination at the machine: connect heavy three-phase hoist-motor leads, brake coil and thermal/encoder cables at the motor terminal box and drive output — large-gauge conductors, crimped lugs, bolted terminals, overhead or tight access beside the machine.

Escalator/moving walk: connect wiring to the escalator controller and drive-motor circuit inside the truss, pit or head-end enclosure at a mall or transit station — confined, greasy, working from unit-specific prints.

Residential home elevator or dumbwaiter: connect wiring to the small controller and motor/pump unit located in a garage, closet or basement of a private home, tying in the disconnect, car wiring and call stations.

sources.system: Averex robotic wiring centre (Kiesling Maschinentechnik / Rittal)
sources.title: CDA Magazine - How automation became a reality
sources.claim: Kiesling/Rittal's Averex robotic wiring centre automatically wires control-panel mounting plates: it cuts, strips and ferrules wire, routes it in the duct and connects it to terminal blocks, contactors and motor ... with torque-controlled screwing, working autonomously from ECAD data inside a purpose-built machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory wiring of switchgear/control panels. It transfers to the elevator task because the objects (stranded control conductors, ferrules, DIN-rail terminal blocks, contactors, screw terminals) and the required precision and torque control are the same as landing conductors in an elevator controller; only the setting differs, which the E1 counterfactual supplies.

sources.title: Rittal Kiesling Product portfolio
sources.claim: The Averex wiring centre is offered as a product for fully automated wiring of controlgear mounting plates, performing wire cutting, stripping, ferruling, duct routing and connection to components, with laser scanning to correct assembly tolerances and a capacity of about 300 wires per plate.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (control-panel wiring in a panel shop machine); the terminations made are the identical class of connection an elevator mechanic makes at a controller's terminal strips.

sources.title: Modular Robotic Stations for Control Cabinet Manufacturing | WAGO
sources.claim: WAGO sells the Wiring Bot, a modular robotic station with an automated conductor preparation unit that cuts, strips, crimps and prints conductors and then wires DIN rails and mounting plates carrying terminal blocks, breakers, controllers and automation products, cutting manual wiring labour by about 60%.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: series wiring of control cabinets and distribution boards. Objects (ferruled control conductors into push-in/rail-mount terminal blocks and breakers) and precision match elevator controller terminations; the robot needs the plate or rail presented in its station, i.e. an E1 setting.

sources.title: Automated Control Cabinet Wiring Solution for Scalable Renewable Energy Systems | SpringerLink
sources.claim: A 2025 review of automated control-cabinet wiring reports Rittal's current solution as an articulated collaborative robot with a gripper that stores a pre-assembled wire, connects both ends to the terminals ... routes the wire inside the cabinet.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: connecting wire ends into cabinet terminals. Same manipulation problem (deformable conductor end into a screw or push-in terminal) as landing wires in an elevator control panel, performed with the cabinet fixtured in a robot cell.

sources.system: Schindler R.I.S.E. (Robotic Installation System for Elevators)
sources.title: Schindler's Robotic Installation System for Elevators | Schindler Group
sources.claim: Schindler's R.I.S.E. robot works autonomously inside elevator hoistways on live construction projects, but its tooling measures, drills holes and sets anchor bolts for guide rails and doors; no wiring or terminating function is described.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only to characterise the state of in-situ elevator field robotics: R.I.S.E. performs drilling and anchor setting, a rigid-tool operation on concrete, which does not transfer to terminating flexible conductors in a control panel. It supports no positive judgment for this task.

sources.system: Robot tool for full-automatic handling and wiring of deformable linear cables

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic insertion of prepared conductor ends into cabinet component terminals; supplements the commercial evidence that wire-to-terminal connection is automatable when the panel is fixtured and sensed (E1 conditions).

instances.label: Final adjusting and acceptance run of a newly installed traction passenger elevator in a mid/high-rise under construction: mechanic runs the car to every landing, verifies floor-level accuracy within tolerance, times door dwell/open/close, tests door reopening devices (photo eye, safety edge), verifies car and hall call registration and dispatching, ride quality, emergency stop, alarm and two-way phone, and fire service Phase I/II with keys. Hoistway, machine room and lobbies still in construction finish, dusty, protected openings, other trades present.

Code-required acceptance safety tests on a new traction unit witnessed by an AHJ or third-party inspector (ASME A17.1/A17.2): loading rated test weights into the car, tripping the speed governor and testing car safeties at governor tripping speed, buffer test, brake test, emergency terminal stopping and slowdown devices, checking rail marks and clearances, riding the car top on inspection operation and temporarily jumpering circuits.

Testing a newly installed or modernized hydraulic elevator in a low-rise commercial, retail or medical-office building: relief valve pressure setting test with load, leveling and re-leveling accuracy, dwell/timing, low-oil and anti-creep protection, manual/emergency lowering, plunger drift check, door interlocks and phone. Small machine room, pit access, tight lobby.

Commissioning tests on a newly installed escalator or moving walk in a mall, airport or transit station: comb-impact and skirt-obstruction devices, handrail speed and entry guards, step-to-skirt clearances and step level measured with gauges, stopping-distance/brake test with loaded steps, missing-step and broken-chain devices, emergency stop buttons, run in both directions. Wellway barricaded off inside a facility controlled by the operator.

Testing a newly installed residential home elevator, LULA, or dumbwaiter in a private house or small business: run the car through its travel, check leveling, gate/door interlocks and locks, slack-rope or safety device, emergency lowering and battery lowering, alarm and phone, and confirm timing/operation against the manufacturer's specification. Varied, cramped, occupant-owned space.

sources.system: Schindler R.I.S.E (Robotic Installation System for Elevators)
sources.title: Pioneering robotic system Schindler R.I.S.E now operational

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic elevator installation in the same hoistway environment. sources.title: Robots rise at Schindler
sources.claim: As of mid-2026 Schindler R.I.S.E. has been used on 36 job sites and installed roughly 50,000 anchor bolts, operating autonomously in the shaft from a pre-uploaded digital work plan with operators monitoring by tablet; its task scope remains measuring, drilling and anchor-bolt setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated elevator installation work. Cited to show the current, updated scope of the only fielded hoistway robot — anchor-bolt installation — which does not include running acceptance tests, load/safety-gear tests, or verifying door dwell times, so it does not substantiate completion of this task.

sources.title: Autonomous Robot Completes 110,000-Plus Elevator Rides - Elevator World
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi autonomously calls and rides elevators in US hospitals, physically pushing elevator buttons with its arm, having completed over 110,000 autonomous elevator rides; it uses elevators as a passenger and performs no measurement or verification of elevator performance against specification.

This covers only a sub-step of the test instance; it provides no leveling measurement, door-force or dwell-time verification, safety-device tripping, load testing, or documented pass/fail judgment, so it cannot substantiate completion.

tasks.label: Operate elevators to determine power demands, and test power consumption to detect overload factors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine preventive-maintenance power check on a geared/gearless traction passenger elevator in a commercial office building or hospital: mechanic enters the machine room, opens the controller/disconnect area, clamps an ammeter or power analyzer on the drive or motor leads, runs the car up and down empty and with a partial load from the machine-room inspection station, reads starting and running current, compares to motor nameplate and overload-relay settings, logs results.

Acceptance or periodic full-load/overload test on a new or modernized traction elevator: car is loaded with test weights to rated and 125% load, run through duty cycles while the mechanic measures line current, voltage and power draw, checks phase balance and demand against feeder and overload-protection sizing, and documents results for the inspector.

Hydraulic elevator in a low-rise commercial or small residential building tripping overloads or running hot: mechanic works in a cramped machine-room closet, clamps a meter on the pump motor leads, runs the car up under load, measures starting and running amperage and phase balance, correlates with relief-valve pressure, and determines whether overload heaters or motor are undersized or the unit is overloaded.

Freight elevator in a warehouse, factory or loading dock: verify power demand of the hoist motor under heavy rated loads, measure running current over repeated hoisting cycles, and detect overload factors such as habitual over-loading, a dragging brake or an out-of-balance counterweight.

Machine-room-less or residential/home elevator with drive and controller in a hallway cabinet, hoistway or under-stair closet: no dedicated machine room, layout differs at every site; mechanic works from the car top or a cramped cabinet to hook up a meter, runs the car on inspection, and checks power draw against the unit's ratings.

sources.title: Traction Machine Test Bench | High-Precision Motor Testing System
sources.claim: Commercial dynamometer test bench purpose-built for elevator and escalator drive units: it fixtures the traction machine, simulates the car/counterweight load, runs it through duty cycles under automatic program control, and continuously measures torque, speed and power to verify rated parameters and power consumption.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bench validation of elevator/escalator hoist machines. It performs the same operation as the worker's task - running the elevator drive under simulated car load while measuring power consumption and comparing with rated parameters to flag out-of-spec/overload conditions - on the same class of object (elevator traction machines), in a purpose-built (E1) test cell.

sources.system: KLOTZ EOL test benches for electric motors/power packs
sources.title: End-of-line testing for high-performance electric motors
sources.claim: Fully automated end-of-line test benches for high-performance electric ... that automatically set up and make electrical contact with the unit under test, run performance tests, and can operate autonomously; test cells are designed for robot loading with sub-20-second cycle times.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated electrical performance testing of motors. It shows that the manipulation the mechanic performs by hand - making the electrical connection to the machine and energising it to measure electrical performance against pass/fail limits - is done automatically and without an operator in a fixtured, fenced cell.

sources.system: Power Test hydraulic test benches (H-H900 / HTS-200)
sources.title: Hydraulic Test Benches - Power Test, LLC
sources.claim: Commercial hydraulic pump/motor production test stands that drive and load hydraulic pumps and motors through fully automated test processes, measuring performance and power under simulated working conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated bench testing of hydraulic pump/motor units, the same power unit used on hydraulic elevators. The stand runs the unit under load and records power/performance against rated specifications, which is what the mechanic does when measuring pump-motor amperage to detect overload.

sources.title: Relay Robotics Introduces New Hospital Delivery Robot
sources.claim: Hospital delivery robots autonomously call and ride passenger elevators of all major makes in occupied buildings, so the 'operate the elevator' element alone is automated in situ, but these robots carry no test instrumentation and take no electrical measurements.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous elevator operation by a mobile robot in a structured facility. It substantiates only the car-operation half of the task; it provides no capability to connect instruments or measure power consumption, so it cannot support completion of any instance.

sources.title: ANYmal Robots Transform Power Industry with GMV and Elewit Collaboration
sources.claim: Legged inspection robots run autonomous rounds in electrical substations and process plants collecting thermal, visual and acoustic data, but their electrical inspection is non-contact sensing - they do not attach clamp meters or power analysers or run machinery through instrumented power-demand tests.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-situ electrical equipment inspection in an E2 facility. It bounds what field robots do today - camera/thermal/acoustic readings only - and therefore does not substantiate the contact instrumentation and load-cycle power measurement this task requires.

tasks.label: Install electrical wires and controls by attaching conduit along shaft walls from floor to floor and pulling plastic-covered wires through the conduit.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New-construction mid/high-rise hoistway rough-in: constructor works from a temporary platform or scaffold inside an active construction shaft, measures and lays out runs, drills concrete/block, anchors straps, cuts/bends/couples EMT or rigid conduit floor to floor, mounts hall-station, door-lock and junction boxes, fishes and pulls THHN wires between floors, and lands them at devices. Dust, debris, poor light, other trades adjacent.

Low-rise commercial/institutional new construction (2-6 stop hydraulic or MRL): conduit run from machine room/controller through wall penetrations into the hoistway and along shaft walls to each landing, wires pulled and terminated at hall buttons, door interlocks and pit switches. Site partially finished, layout differs per building.

Modernization/rewire in an occupied existing building: working from the car top or in a blocked-off shaft, mechanic removes or reuses legacy conduit and raceway, adds new conduit runs and boxes on as-found shaft walls (brick, block, poured concrete, steel), pulls new control and safety wiring floor to floor, keeping adjacent cars in service.

Small residential/home elevator, LULA or dumbwaiter installation in a private home or small business: shallow tight shaft framed in wood or block, surface-mounted conduit or raceway attached along the shaft wall between two or three landings, wires pulled and connected to the controller and landing fixtures; access via ladders and cramped openings.

Machine-room / control-space side of the same job in an existing institutional building: conduit run from the controller cabinet and disconnect through the wall into the hoistway or pit, wires pulled through and terminated on controller terminal strips, with labeling and continuity checks before energizing.

sources.system: Schindler R.I.S.E (Robotic Installation System for Elevators)
sources.title: Robots rise at Schindler — The Construction Index
sources.claim: Schindler R.I.S.E is a self-climbing robot deployed commercially in elevator hoistways on construction sites that autonomously measures, drills and sets anchor bolts for guide-rail brackets and landing doors; its documented capability set stops at drilling and anchoring and does not include mounting conduit, pulling wire, or terminating controls.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastening hardware to hoistway walls in the same environment (the elevator shaft) that this task's conduit straps would occupy. It substantiates autonomous drilling/anchoring only; it handles no conduit, no plastic-covered wire, and no device terminations, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

sources.title: Schindler's Robotic Installation System for Elevators — Schindler Global Large Projects
sources.claim: Schindler's own product documentation defines the R.I.S.E work scope as drilling holes and setting anchor bolts on a floor, operating without an on-platform operator; no conduit installation or wiring step is listed.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (wall drilling/anchoring inside the hoistway). Cited to bound the frontier: the only elevator-shaft installation robot in commercial service performs neither conduit attachment nor wire pulling.

sources.title: Jaibot — Hilti Corporation media release
sources.claim: The most advanced commercial MEP rough-in robot for buildings, Hilti's Jaibot, performs semi-autonomous BIM-driven ceiling drilling and marking only; it does not mount conduit or pull conductors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: electrical/MEP rough-in preparation on jobsites. Transfer fails for this task because Jaibot only drills and marks holes; the conduit fastening, bending/coupling, box mounting and wire pulling that define this task are outside its demonstrated scope.

sources.title: Construction Robotics Report 2026 — Zacua Ventures
sources.claim: Industry survey of construction robotics as of 2026 characterises installation and MEP robots as an early-stage category, with specialised drilling/layout machines rather than general installation robots doing the field work.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the absence of any fielded conduit-installation or wire-pulling robot; used only to support negative judgments, not to establish capability.

tasks.label: Attach guide shoes and rollers to minimize the lateral motion of cars as they travel through shafts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New elevator installation in a mid- or high-rise building under construction: after the car sling/platform is erected, the mechanic bolts four roller-guide assemblies (typically 10-25 kg each) to the top and bottom of ... car frame stiles and shoe assemblies to the counterweight frame, shims them, sets roller spring preload to the rail gauge, and checks the car runs plumb in the hoistway. Dust, temporary lighting, staging on the shaft floor or from the car top.

Modernization / car replacement in an occupied existing commercial building: legacy sliding guide shoes or worn roller guides are unbolted from an old car frame and new units fitted, often with adapter plates and shims to match non-matching hole patterns; work done from the car top and in the pit with the hoistway isolated, in tight, greasy, poorly lit space that differs building to building.

Routine maintenance/repair service call on an in-service elevator in an office, hospital, hotel or retail building: replace worn gib liners in sliding guide shoes or worn roller tires, re-attach and re-adjust roller guide spring tension to cure lateral sway, vibration or noise complaints; performed from the car top or pit during a short service window.

Freight or heavy-duty/industrial elevator and counterweight work: attaching heavy cast sliding shoes or oversize rollers on freight car frames and counterweight frames in warehouse, plant or parking-structure hoistways; heavy parts, confined pit access, dirt and grease.

Small hydraulic or residential/home elevator: fitting nylon or roller guide shoes to a light car sling in a private home, small apartment building or small low-rise commercial unit; very tight shaft, non-standard site conditions and improvised access.
