sources.transferJustification: Related task: drilling and anchor-setting on hoistway walls. It shares the environment (the shaft) but not the work: it does not retrieve a multi-part guide-shoe assembly, align it to a car-frame stile, bolt it up or set roller preload, so it does not substantiate completion of this task in the hoistway.

sources.system: Vision-guided lug-nut fastening cell (FANUC robot + machine vision, integrated by Radix Controls)
sources.title: Vision-guided Robot Key To Automated Lug-nut Fastening - Manufacturing AUTOMATION
sources.claim: A vision-guided FANUC robot in an automotive plant locates a wheel in six degrees of freedom, positions a nutrunner onto the studs and torques the lug nuts to specification, running in production for 18 months at greater than 99.6% uptime - deployed, autonomous bolted fastening of a component onto a large frame.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: torquing a bolted component onto a vehicle hub. Comparable objects (steel component, multiple bolts) and precision (vision pose correction then torque to spec), matching the act of bolting a roller-guide assembly to a car-frame stile when the frame is fixtured in a cell.

sources.system: 3D-vision robotic bolt-tightening station for rear axle dampers
sources.developer: INESC TEC (Institute for Systems and Computer Engineering, Technology and Science) with an automaker
sources.title: Robots Automate Bolt-Tightening on Automotive Assembly Lines | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Robots fitted with 3D vision and force sensors tighten the bolts fastening rear axle dampers to van undercarriages on a production line, compensating for vehicle position variation caused by conveyor tolerances.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastening a suspension component to a vehicle frame at two attachment points. Same class of work as bolting a guide shoe to a car stile - steel part, few bolts, torque spec - executed with vision- and force-corrected pose in a factory cell.

sources.title: Inbolt and FANUC Pioneer Robots that Think and Act on the Fly at Moving Assembly Line Speeds
sources.claim: FANUC robots using Inbolt's on-arm 3D vision perform screw insertion and bolt rundown on parts in automotive general assembly; Inbolt reports customers including Stellantis, Toyota and Volkswagen across more than 70 factories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided bolt rundown on car bodies in general assembly. Demonstrates autonomous fastener starting and torquing on variable-pose steel structures, the core motion of attaching guide shoes when the car frame is presented in a cell.

sources.title: Inbolt provides vision guidance in real time for new bin-picking system - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Inbolt's bin-picking system picks parts from unstructured bins with 95% success and sub-second cycles in live automotive production and runs in more than five factories, showing robots can retrieve the component to be installed as well as fasten it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving components from bins in a factory cell. Supplies the part-retrieval half of attaching a guide shoe or roller in the E1 counterfactual where the car frame is fixtured and parts are presented.

sources.system: Recirculate project robotic disassembly cell (KUKA KR10 on linear track)
sources.developer: Centria University of Applied Sciences (Recirculate project)
sources.title: Recirculate tests AI-driven robotic system for EV battery disassembly - electrive.com
sources.claim: A KUKA-based robotic cell detects, unscrews and removes bolted components from heavy EV battery packs autonomously using purpose-built tools and a depth camera, showing robotic removal of worn bolted hardware in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous unscrewing and removal of bolted parts from a heavy steel assembly. Covers the removal step preceding attachment of a replacement guide shoe or roller, at comparable fastener sizes, in a fixtured cell.

tasks.label: Install outer doors and door frames at elevator entrances on each floor of a structure.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New high-rise/commercial construction (10+ landings): mechanic works from a hoistway platform or car top in an active construction shaft, sets the entrance sill and struts, plumbs and welds/bolts the steel door frame to shaft anchors within a few millimetres of the car-sill line, hangs the door panels on hanger rollers, fits gibs, interlock and closer, then adjusts running clearances at every floor. Dust, temporary lighting, open shaft edges, other trades working nearby.

New low-rise construction (2-6 stops: schools, medical office buildings, apartments, retail): same entrance package installed into block or drywall shaft openings, often after rough-in, with a two-person crew hoisting frames and door panels by hand or with a chain fall in a partially finished building.

Modernization / entrance replacement in an occupied building (office tower, hospital, hotel): barricade the landing, strip out legacy frames, sills and panels, cut and weld to existing out-of-plumb structure, shim and grout the new frame to match finished walls and fire-rating details, hang new panels, one bank of landings at a time while the building stays in service.

Residential install: private-home elevator or small 2-3 stop residential building, tight and irregular framing, lightweight swing or slide hoistway doors and frames fitted to wood or light-steel rough openings in a house or small building under construction or renovation.

Service/repair call: replace a damaged hoistway door panel, sill or frame section at a single landing (parking garage, apartment lobby, retail) - assess the damage and existing hardware, remove the damaged part, refit and realign the panel to gibs and interlock, restore code clearances, return the car to service the same day.

sources.system: Schindler R.I.S.E (Robotic Installation System for Elevators)
sources.title: Schindler's Robotic Installation System for Elevators | Schindler Group
sources.claim: Schindler R.I.S.E is a self-climbing robot that works inside real elevator shafts on construction sites, but its autonomous work is limited to scanning, drilling and setting the anchor ... that landing doors, divider beams and ... are later fixed to - it does not set frames or hang door panels.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shaft anchor preparation for landing doors. It is the closest in-situ robotic capability to this task, but it is a preparatory sub-step (hole drilling and anchor setting) and does not install the doors or frames, so it cannot substantiate completion of the whole instance.

sources.title: Robots rise at Schindler - The Construction Index
sources.claim: After five years of commercial use the R.I.S.E fleet is seven robots that have worked 36 job sites, and the reported output is anchor bolts, confirming that in-situ elevator-shaft robotics has not extended to entrance door and frame installation as of mid-2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic elevator-shaft installation work on live construction sites. Cited to establish the ceiling of demonstrated in-situ capability (anchor setting only), which underpins the negative judgments at E2 and E3.

sources.system: Bluewrist EzRG robot guidance with LMI Gocator 2300 sensors on a six-axis assembly robot
sources.title: Sensors Make Robots Smarter When Inserting Vehicle Windshields
sources.claim: On automotive assembly lines a six-axis robot with 3D laser sensors picks a large glass panel, measures the panel and the body aperture, and inserts it with ±0.2 mm guidance accuracy; the same system is used for hanging hoods, trunk lids and doors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided robotic mounting of doors and glazing panels into apertures on a fixtured assembly line. Objects are comparable (large, heavy rigid panels), required precision is tighter than the few-millimetre clearances of an elevator entrance, and the environment is exactly the fenced, fixtured E1 cell the counterfactual assumes.

sources.system: Kawasaki BX250L robots on Güdel TrackMotion rails with SCADAware control software (Rehkemper & Son prefab plant)
sources.title: Assembling Walls for Prefabricated Homes | Industrial Robots by Kawasaki
sources.claim: Four 250 kg-payload Kawasaki robots on rails autonomously handle and fasten large heavy building panels onto framed wall assemblies held square on a motorised fixture table, aligning to the digital design within about 1/16 inch and cutting the window and door openings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling and mechanical fastening of large, heavy building components onto a frame in a purpose-built, fixtured factory cell. Payload class (250 kg) and fastening tolerances match elevator entrance frames and door panels once the workpiece is presented fixtured.

sources.system: Otis / Max Bögl prefabricated elevator shaft
sources.title: "Marriage" of Shaft and Elevator - Elevator World
sources.claim: Prefabricated elevator shaft modules are produced with the elevator components, including the entrance doors, already installed in the factory before the shaft is delivered to site, showing that entrance door and frame installation can arise as factory work on a fixtured module rather than in the building.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only to show that the E1 counterfactual can arise - entrance doors are in fact fitted to shaft modules in a factory - not to show robotic capability; the robotic capability for that setting rests on the Bluewrist and Kawasaki items.

tasks.label: Assemble elevator cars, installing each car's platform, walls, and doors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New-construction mid/high-rise passenger elevator: in the hoistway, the crew bolts the platform to the car sling, then erects the steel cab shell (side and rear walls, ceiling, front return), hangs the car doors on the header/hanger rollers, sets the sill and gibs, and mounts the door operator. Parts are hoisted in through the shaft opening; work is done from the car top or a temporary platform amid dust, other trades, and varying shaft geometry.

Low-rise hydraulic or MRL elevator (2-6 stops) in a small commercial building or private residence: tight, non-standard shaft; cab platform and walls assembled in the shaft or partly outside and slid in; single car door and operator fitted; limited staging space, residential/finished-space protection, no fixturing.

Modernization / cab refurbishment in an occupied, institution-run building (office tower, hospital, hotel): existing car parked at a landing, old interior stripped, new wall panels, ceiling, handrails and flooring installed on the existing platform, and new car doors, sill and operator fitted; work scheduled around building operations.

Freight, service or specialty car in an operating industrial or institutional facility: heavy steel wall panels and channel-reinforced platform, bi-parting or vertical-slide car gates, heavy-duty door operator; larger, heavier components handled with chain falls inside the shaft.

Shop or staging pre-assembly: at the contractor's shop, warehouse, or laydown area, cab shells, platforms, and door/header assemblies are bolted together on horses or simple jigs (or an entire small cab is built up) before being trucked to site and hoisted into the shaft.

sources.system: Schindler R.I.S.E (Robotic Installation System for Elevators)
sources.title: Schindler's Robotic Installation System for Elevators | Schindler Group
sources.claim: Schindler R.I.S.E is the state of the art in autonomous elevator-installation robotics: a self-climbing robot that works unattended inside the hoistway, but its scope is limited to measuring, drilling and setting anchor bolts for landing doors, divider beams ... — it does not assemble car platforms, walls or doors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (hoistway preparation) in the same environment as this task; cited to show what field elevator-installation robots do and do not do — no cab assembly capability is demonstrated in the shaft.

sources.title: Schindler expands elevator installation robot fleet as demand for construction automation grows
sources.claim: Schindler's hoistway robot has been used on 36 construction sites and has set ~50,000 anchor bolts, confirming real field deployment but again only for shaft preparation, not car assembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (drilling/anchor setting in the hoistway); establishes the ceiling of demonstrated in-shaft robotic capability relevant to judging E3/E2 for cab assembly.

sources.system: Flexible Intelligent Door/Hood/Lid Assembly Line (Risong Technology) at Changan Mazda
sources.title: Flexible Intelligent Door Assembly Line of Changan Mazda Automobile Co., Ltd. (IFR case study)
sources.claim: A fully automated, vision-guided robotic line in mass production hangs and bolts large door, hood and lid panels onto a conveyed body, measuring gaps and automatically tightening 64 screws per unit across 8 mixed models.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hanging vehicle doors and bolting large sheet-metal panels onto a fixtured structure with millimetre gap control. Objects (large steel/aluminium panels and doors), fastening method (bolted, torque-monitored) and required alignment precision are comparable to bolting an elevator cab's platform and wall panels and hanging car doors on their header — and the line runs mixed models, showing the fixtured cell tolerates variant geometry.

sources.system: Randek ZeroLabor robotic wall production line (KUKA robots) at Kodumaja
sources.title: Autowall, Robotic wall production line for production of exterior walls | KUKA Sweden
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor robotic system, built on KUKA robots, runs a commercial factory line that autonomously produces multi-layer wall panel elements for a modular building manufacturer, replacing manual operations and quality checks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory assembly of building wall panels — picking, positioning and fastening large flat panels onto a frame in a fixtured line. Panel size, weight class and fastening are comparable to assembling an elevator cab shell when the work is brought to the machine.

sources.system: Robotic wall-frame assembly cells in modular construction factories
sources.title: Automation in Modular Construction Manufacturing: A Comparative Analysis of Assembly Processes
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed comparison of modular-construction factories documents robotic cells that place studs, nail wall frames and add sheathing boards with vacuum lifters at roughly 55 wall elements per day.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory-based structural panel assembly with automated fastening and large-panel handling; supports that walls/platform sub-assemblies of an elevator cab could be built up autonomously when parts are fixtured and presented in a purpose-built line.

tasks.label: Bolt or weld steel rails to the walls of shafts to guide elevators, working from scaffolding or platforms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New-construction mid-rise concrete hoistway (roughly 4-10 stops): mechanic works from a false car/temporary platform, sets rail brackets on anchors, hoists 16-ft steel T-rails (~100-200 lb) into place, bolts fishplates and rail clips, and aligns the rail line plumb and to gauge within about 1 mm before final torquing. Active jobsite: dust, debris, other trades, varying wall condition.

High-rise new construction (10+ floors, express zones): hundreds of rail sections stacked in one shaft from suspended platforms or a climbing false car, tighter alignment tolerance for high-speed cars, seismic bracket detailing, rail deliveries staged by floor.

Steel-framed hoistway or steel divider beams: rail brackets/rail backing welded (stick or MIG) to structural steel inside the shaft, working from scaffold or platform, hot work with fire watch, fit-up varying with as-built steel tolerances.

Modernization/rail replacement in an occupied existing building (office, hospital, apartment): old rails and brackets removed and new rails bolted into a legacy shaft from the car top, working around existing wiring, out-of-plumb walls, and irregular masonry/concrete, with shaft access controlled by building management.

Low-rise hydraulic or small MRL elevator (2-3 stops) in a small commercial or residential building: two car rails and bracket sets bolted to block or concrete walls in a cramped shaft, working from ladders, staging, or a small platform, often a two-person crew.

sources.system: Schindler R.I.S.E. (Robotic Installation System for Elevators)
sources.title: Schindler's Robotic Installation System for Elevators | Schindler Global Large Projects
sources.claim: Schindler R.I.S.E. is a self-climbing robot that works autonomously inside elevator shafts on high-rise construction sites, but its scope is measuring, drilling and setting/pre-tightening anchor bolts for rail brackets and landing doors - not mounting the rails themselves.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (elevator guide-rail installation in a hoistway); cited to establish the in-shaft state of the art and to bound it - the robot prepares walls but does not bolt rails.

sources.title: Technology Redefining the Future of Elevator Installation Methods for High-Rise Buildings - Elevator World
sources.claim: Trade/symposium paper on high-rise installation methods states explicitly that after the robot drills and sets anchors, the human installation team installs the rails and brackets from a false car or lift car platform.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about this task; establishes that the rail-bolting step itself remains manual even where the most advanced in-shaft robot is deployed.

sources.title: Schindler expands elevators installation robot fleet - Elevatori Magazine
sources.claim: As of mid-2026 Schindler operates seven R.I.S.E. robots across 36 job sites; the system is explicitly designed to leave precision alignment and guide rail installation to human technicians.
sources.transferJustification: Same task; confirms current-generation elevator installation robots do not perform rail mounting or alignment in the shaft.

sources.title: Robotic Welding for Structural Steel Fabrication | PeddiAssembler | Peddinghaus
sources.claim: The PeddiAssembler/Zeman SBA is a commercial fenced robotic cell in which a handling robot laser-scans and positions steel parts up to 440 lb onto profiles up to 60 ft long and a second robot tacks and welds them per 3D/BIM data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: positioning and welding steel attachments (brackets, plates, stiffeners) onto long steel members in a fixtured cell. Objects are comparable in size and weight to elevator guide rails and brackets (a 16-ft T-rail is roughly 150 lb), placement is scanner-referenced to model data, and the setting is a purpose-built fenced cell - the E1 counterfactual for fastening rails to a fixtured shaft structure.

sources.title: ZEMAN Steel Beam Assembly (SBA) Robot | CPE Construction
sources.claim: A Zeman SBA robotic cell was installed and commissioned in 2024 at a fabricator, using robotic arms with 3D scanning to position and weld brackets and other attachments onto steel beams with automated in/outfeed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic placement and welding of brackets onto steel members in a production cell - the same physical operation as welding rail brackets or rails to a fixtured steel shaft structure, in an E1 setting.

sources.system: MIRAI-guided Universal Robots cobots with automatic torque wrench
sources.title: Leading US automotive OEM Automated bolt torquing | Micropsi Industries
sources.claim: Seven production robots at a North American automotive plant perform bolt torquing on a moving assembly line, using AI vision to absorb positional variance, with near-100% success and little manual intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous torquing of structural fasteners under real positional variance in a production cell - the fastening half of bolting rail clips and fishplates once the work is fixtured and presented, i.e. the E1 counterfactual.

tasks.label: Assemble electrically powered stairs, steel frameworks, and tracks, and install associated motors and electrical wiring.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New-construction escalator install in a building under construction (office tower, mall, stadium): truss sections rigged into the wellway by crane, bolted/welded and shimmed to supports, step tracks and angles aligned to tolerance, drive machine, step chain, steps, handrail drive and balustrades assembled, controller and safety-switch wiring pulled and terminated, then run-in and code inspection. Dust, overhead trades, temporary power, plumb/level references off building steel.

Modernization/replacement of an existing escalator inside an operating facility (transit station, airport, mall) behind hoarding, often night shifts: old unit stripped out or truss retained, new tracks, step chain, drive unit, controller and complete rewiring installed inside the existing pit and wellway, alignment to existing landing plates, then safety testing and return to service.

Component-level rebuild on an in-service unit in a controlled facility: replacing worn track sections and step-chain, swapping a drive motor/gearbox or handrail drive, re-terminating motor leads and safety-circuit wiring in the controller, re-tensioning and testing. Cramped pit and truss interior, greasy legacy hardware, unit taken out of service for a shift.

Moving walkway or short-rise unit delivered largely factory-assembled, set into a new terminal, store or renovation opening: rigging into the pit, leveling and anchoring, joining truss sections for long walks, connecting the power feed, controller and remote station wiring, commissioning tests.

sources.system: Schindler R.I.S.E (Robotic Installation System for Elevators)
sources.title: Robots rise at Schindler
sources.claim: Schindler R.I.S.E is an autonomous self-climbing robot deployed on real construction sites, but its scope is measuring, drilling holes and setting anchor bolts in elevator shaft walls — it does not assemble structural frames, tracks, drives or wiring.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task: robotic elevator installation work by the same occupation. It does not transfer to this task — it performs only concrete drilling and anchor setting on a flat shaft wall, with no component assembly, track alignment, motor mounting, wire pulling or termination, so it cannot substantiate completion of escalator assembly at any tier.

sources.title: Schindler expands RISE robot fleet as automated elevator installation demand grows
sources.claim: Schindler R.I.S.E fleet remains small (seven robots, 36 job sites over five years), confirming the only fielded elevator-trade robot is limited to shaft anchor-bolt work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (elevator shaft preparation) in the same occupation; cited to show the state of the art in trade-specific field robotics, which covers drilling/anchoring only and therefore does not carry over to assembling escalator frameworks, tracks, motors and wiring.

sources.title: Humanoid Robots Complete Trial Project at BMW Assembly Plant
sources.claim: The most mature humanoid factory deployment (Figure 02 at BMW Spartanburg) was limited to loading/inserting sheet-metal parts in a fixtured body shop over an 11-month pilot; no multi-step mechanical assembly with fastening and electrical termination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general-purpose humanoid assembly support in a purpose-built industrial cell. Cited to test the E1 counterfactual — even with work presented on a fixtured line, demonstrated capability is part loading, not structural assembly, precision track alignment, motor mounting or wire termination, so it cannot substantiate completion.

sources.title: Hilti robot can drill on corrugated metal deck ceilings and more
sources.claim: Construction-site robots marketed for MEP work, such as the Hilti Jaibot, are semi-autonomous drilling machines driven to position by an operator and limited to drilling BIM-specified holes; they perform no wiring or mechanical installation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical/electrical rough-in on building sites. Operator-positioned, drilling-only, and therefore does not substantiate autonomous completion of escalator framework, track, motor or wiring installation.

tasks.label: Cut prefabricated sections of framework, rails, and other components to specified dimensions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New-construction install: mechanic field-measures the hoistway, then cuts steel guide rails (T-rails, ~16 ft, 30-60 lb) and rail-bracket/backing steel to length with an abrasive chop saw or portable band saw on the staging floor or inside the hoistway; dust, temporary power, cramped access, cut ends deburred and matched to the mating rail.

Cutting framework and support steel to specified dimensions at the jobsite: angle, channel, tube, Unistrut, threaded rod and all-thread for machine-room, pit, overhead, divider-beam and counterweight supports; lengths taken from field conditions and cut with chop saw, band saw, or torch.

Modernization in an occupied building: new rails, brackets, and structural steel cut to fit an existing hoistway; cutting done in the machine room, at a landing, or on a protected staging area of a building that is still operating, with dimensions dictated by the existing shaft.

Cutting non-structural components to dimension at the jobsite: EMT/conduit, wireway and duct, sill angle, hoistway-door trim, sheet-metal and laminate cab and entrance panels, cut with portable band saw, hacksaw, shears/snips, or circular saw and fitted on the spot.

Escalator/moving-walk install or repair in a mall, airport, or transit station: cutting truss cladding, skirt and deck panels, balustrade trim, comb-plate and angle stock to fit the opening, usually during off-hours behind barricades in an operating facility.

Cuts that must be made in place on material already fixed in the structure: trimming an installed rail or bracket flush, cutting hoistway steel or a set sill to dimension, notching in situ, often overhead or at height in a cramped shaft.

sources.system: Machitech Beamcut BC25 robotic beam cutting system
sources.title: Robotic beam cutting machine performs automated cutting of structural parts
sources.claim: Beamcut BC25 is a commercially sold 6-axis FANUC robotic plasma cell that automatically cuts structural steel profiles (beams, channel, angle) to length, plus holes, copes and bevels, from CAD data in a fabrication-shop cell, eliminating manual layout.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, different setting: cutting prefabricated steel profiles to a specified dimension. Elevator guide rails are steel T-profiles and rail brackets are angle/channel of the same size class and tolerance.

sources.title: Automated cutting system improves fit-up, efficiency for structural fabricator
sources.claim: A deployed Beamcut BC25 installation at structural fabricator ProSteel is described in trade press as purpose-built automated structural steel processing that improves fit-up and efficiency.
sources.transferJustification: Same cut-to-dimension operation on structural steel members; demonstrates production deployment at worker-acceptable quality, not just a demo.

sources.title: CNC Bandsaw Machine | Cutting Beams | Voortman Steel Machinery
sources.claim: Voortman VB series CNC band saws are conveyor- and bundle-fed machines that saw structural profiles to length automatically in steel service centers, with bundle stops and clamps ensuring accurate length on multiple profiles at once.
sources.transferJustification: Cut-to-length sawing of steel profiles is the same operation performed on elevator guide rails, divider beams and bracket steel; material, section size and length tolerance are comparable.

sources.system: Automatic programmable band saw with bundle/infeed magazine
sources.title: Band Saw Machine Types Explained | KEENSAW Guide
sources.claim: Automatic band saws with infeed magazines feed, measure, clamp, cut and unload each piece to a programmed length without operator intervention, and can run unattended.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the cutting-to-specified-dimension step for bar, tube, conduit and profile stock used for elevator framework and supports.

sources.title: CNC Angle Line | Anglemaster-863 | Peddinghaus
sources.claim: Peddinghaus Anglemaster-863 CNC angle line automatically loads angle, flat bar and channel and shears it to length, running unattended for extended periods.
sources.transferJustification: Elevator bracket, backing and support framework is angle, flat bar and channel of exactly these sizes; cutting to a programmed length is the same operation.

sources.system: Eagle laser automation (tower-fed fiber laser cutting line)
sources.title: Sheet Metal Automation Systems for Laser Cutting | Eagle
sources.claim: Fiber laser cutting cells with tower storage and automatic load/unload cut and sort sheet parts to programmed dimensions in unattended, lights-out operation.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the sheet-metal share of the task: cab and entrance trim panels, escalator skirt/deck cladding and similar flat components cut to a specified dimension.

sources.title: Schindler's Robotic Installation System for Elevators
sources.claim: Schindler R.I.S.E. is a self-climbing robot that works fully autonomously inside elevator shafts on live construction sites, but its tooling is limited to drilling holes and installing anchor ...; it does not cut rails or framework to dimension.
sources.transferJustification: Closest field-deployed elevator-installation robot; cited to bound the E2/E3 judgment, since its demonstrated capability is drilling and anchoring, not measuring and cutting components to dimension.

roles.title: Fence Erectors
roles.description: Erect and repair fences and fence gates, using hand and power tools.

tasks.label: Establish the location for a fence, and gather information needed to ensure that there are no electric cables or water lines in the area.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New residential fence at a single-family home: worker walks the yard with the homeowner, finds property pins/plat references, measures offsets, pulls a string line and stakes/paints corner, gate and post locations around trees, slopes, sheds, A/C pads and driveways; submits the 811 locate ticket and reads the utility flags/paint (gas, electric, irrigation, water service) before digging.

Chain-link or ornamental fence on a commercial/institutional property (school, warehouse yard, apartment complex, business lot): layout taken from a site plan supplied by the owner, mostly open turf or pavement, line marked with paint/stakes, coordinated with the facility manager and with utility locate markings and as-built drawings.

Agricultural/rural fence line on a ranch or farm: long runs across open pasture and rolling ground, sighting in the line between corners, setting corner/brace and post marks at spacing, checking for buried water lines to troughs and electric service near gates and wells.

Perimeter fencing on a large open construction or energy site (solar farm, substation, industrial build, temporary construction fence): fence line laid out from design coordinates over a large graded or raw site, hundreds to thousands of post points marked, utility corridors identified from plans and locate markings.

Repair, replacement or extension of an existing fence: re-establishing the line of an old fence from remnant posts and post holes, matching spacing and tie-in points at a home or rural property, and verifying that no cables or water lines run in the old line before re-digging.

sources.title: Solar Farm Layout Tool & GPS Surveying Equipment | Civ Robotics
sources.claim: Civ Robotics' CivDot layout rovers are used on solar sites specifically to mark out the fence perimeter and locate fence points, i.e. exactly the 'establish the location for a fence' output.

sources.title: CivDot Or CivDot+: Which Robotic Surveyor Fits Your Needs?
sources.claim: Vendor use-case documentation states the robots mark perimeter lines for fencing and locate individual fence post points to plan, without gaps or overlaps.

sources.title: These little robots are changing the way solar farms are built, saving time and money (CNBC)
sources.claim: CivDot is in commercial field use by a major contractor on rugged open outdoor sites, marking thousands of layout points per day at centimetre-level accuracy.

sources.title: Automated Layout Startup Civ Robotics Secures $7.5M Series A Funding Round | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Trade press confirms the layout marking is autonomous with only minimal human oversight on large outdoor sites.

sources.title: Robots Powered with Reach Speed up Stakeout for Construction Projects - Emlid Blog
sources.claim: Technical description of CivDot's autonomy: it navigates to programmed coordinates under autopilot with RTK GNSS and marks each point to 1-2 cm.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class: driving to design coordinates on open ground and marking them is the stakeout step by which a fence line and its post positions are established.

sources.title: TinySurveyor Terra | TinyMobileRobots | Monsen Engineering
sources.claim: A second commercial autonomous stakeout robot (TinySurveyor Terra) drives itself and paints layout points to 1-2 cm on job sites and roadways, showing the capability is not vendor-unique.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (survey stakeout / road pre-marking) uses the same coordinates-to-ground-marks workflow and precision needed to set out a fence line and post points.

sources.developer: ULC Technologies (with SGN and Transport for London)
sources.title: AUSMOS | Robotic GPR Mapping Services | ULC Technologies
sources.claim: AUSMOS is a fielded robotic GPR/EM platform that detects buried power cables and pipes and paints the mark-out on site, covering the physical half of 'ensure there are no electric cables or water lines'; it has been run through scan-to-mark-out operations on London streets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (utility locate and mark-out) is the on-the-ground portion of gathering information that no electric cables or water lines lie in the fence area; same ground surface and same paint mark-out output.

sources.system: Roto-Fence (Kidd post driver + Farmscan AG autonomy)
sources.developer: Farmscan AG / Kidd Farm Machinery / Harper Adams University
sources.title: Roto-Fence Project: Autonomous Fencing for Smarter Grazing - Farmscan AG
sources.claim: An autonomous tractor-mounted fencing system placed posts one after another at pre-set points in a field during a live demonstration, showing point-to-point fence setting-out in pasture conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous post setting to planned points in a pasture) shows a machine can follow a farm fence line and hit each planned post position, which is the output of rural fence layout.

tasks.label: Set metal or wooden posts in upright positions in postholes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential wood privacy/picket fence: setting 4x4 or 4x6 treated wood posts into 10-inch augered holes 24-36 in deep in a homeowner's back yard; each post is dropped in, held to a string line, checked plumb with a level, braced, and concreted. Access is through a 3-ft gate, with lawn, roots, slopes, sprinkler lines and buried utilities present.

Residential / small-commercial metal-post fencing (chain link, ornamental aluminum or steel, vinyl over steel): 1-5/8 to 2-7/8 in pipe terminal, corner and line posts set in augered holes with concrete, aligned to a string line and plumbed, on small lots with driveways, walls, landscaping and grade changes.

Commercial / industrial / institutional perimeter fencing: long straight runs of galvanized pipe or ornamental steel posts around warehouses, substations, schools, ball fields and utility yards; holes machine-augered from a skid steer or auger truck on open, machine-accessible graded ground; posts set plumb to a surveyed layout and concreted, often hundreds per job.

Agricultural / ranch fencing: line, corner and brace posts (wood rounds or steel) along long pasture and field boundaries; holes augered (or posts driven where soil allows) in uneven, rocky or muddy terrain, posts set to depth, plumbed and tamped or concreted, far from improved access.

Repair / replacement work: setting one or a few replacement posts into re-dug holes in an existing fence line (storm damage, rot, vehicle impact) in a yard, farm lane or commercial lot; the new post must match the existing line, height and spacing before backfill.

sources.system: Built Robotics RPD35 + RPS25 autonomous piling system
sources.title: Fortescue Innovation Hub Trial Report: Built Robotics — Pilbara Solar Innovation Hub (ARENA)
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD35 pile driver and RPS25 pile stabiliser autonomously retrieved steel piles from onboard baskets and set them into pre-drilled holes filled with cement stabilised fill at Fortescue's Cloudbreak Solar Farm, an open outdoor construction site in the Pilbara (trial Aug-Oct 2025).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: solar foundation piling. It is the same physical act as this task — placing a long steel post upright into a pre-drilled hole with cement backfill at a laid-out position and holding it vertical — with heavier members (12-19 ft, ~200 lb steel sections) and tighter tolerances than fence posts, in an outdoor field setting.

sources.system: Built Robotics RPD35 + RPS25 autonomous piling system
sources.title: Fortescue Innovation Hub Trial Report: Built Robotics — Pilbara Solar Innovation Hub (ARENA)
sources.claim: The same trial found the autonomously set piles met positional accuracy, verticality and embedment tolerances, and that one operator supervised up to three piling rigs from a central station (about 67% manning reduction).
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above; establishes accepted output quality (verticality/position) and that operation is supervisory rather than continuous teleoperation.

sources.title: Robots that Build the World — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics publishes that its robotic pile stabiliser holds posts to within 1.0 degree of plumb and 15 mm of design elevation, for members up to 19 ft long, with fleets running up to 24 hours a day.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: solar piling. Quantifies the plumb/position precision achieved when standing a long post upright, the core quality criterion of setting fence posts.

sources.title: Meta's Largest Data Center Project Is Bringing in 72-Ton Robots | eWeek
sources.claim: Ten 72-ton Built Robotics machines are autonomously driving roughly 1,000 steel piles per day at the Louisiana solar site serving Meta's Hyperion data center, handling more than half of ... site's pile-driving work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: solar piling at commercial scale on a live outdoor jobsite; shows the post-handling-and-standing capability is deployed, not merely demonstrated, in an unstructured field environment.

sources.developer: Farmscan AG / Kidd Farm Machinery / Harper Adams University
sources.title: Roto-Fence Project: Autonomous Fencing for Smarter Grazing - Farmscan AG
sources.claim: The Roto-Fence system (Farmscan AG, Kidd Farm Machinery, Harper Adams University, Innovate UK) autonomously drove a tractor along a planned fence line and operated a modified Kidd 340 post driver, placing fence posts one after another with centimetre-level accuracy in field trials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing fence posts by driving rather than in a dug hole. Same objects (farm fence posts), same output (post standing upright at a laid-out position to depth), same pasture environment; only the hole-forming step differs.

sources.system: WEINMANN framing station with KUKA six-axis robot / FEEDBOT F-500
sources.title: Robots in production — a new trend? | HOMAG
sources.claim: In WEINMANN/HOMAG timber-frame production cells (e.g. Bien-Zenker, Lindbäcks), a six-axis KUKA industrial robot autonomously picks wooden studs from collection stations and inserts them into the fixtured frame, completing wall elements in minutes with better dimensional accuracy than manual work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated insertion of dimensional lumber into fixtured positions in a purpose-built cell. This is the E1 analogue of placing a wooden fence post into a fixtured posthole — same object class (sawn timber members), machine-presented stock, positions known to the controller.

sources.title: Publications | Designing Emergence Laboratory (Harvard)
sources.claim: Romu, an autonomous wheeled robot from Harvard's Wyss Institute, uses a vibratory hammer and its ... weight to drive posts and sheet piles into soil in natural outdoor terrain without human control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous anchoring/post driving in unimproved outdoor terrain; corroborates that standing posts upright in soil is achievable autonomously outdoors, though at research scale.

tasks.label: Measure and lay out fence lines and mark posthole positions, following instructions, drawings, or specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New residential fence at a private home (wood privacy, vinyl, ornamental or chain link): crew locates property pins and existing corners, measures with tape/wheel from a sketch or contract drawing, sets corner stakes, stretches a string line, and paints or stakes each posthole position, adjusting around trees, slopes, decks, AC units, driveways and gate openings in a small enclosed yard.

Small-to-medium commercial or institutional job (parking lot, car dealership, storage yard, school ballfield, warehouse perimeter) laid out from a civil site plan: measure the perimeter and gate locations off curbs/building lines or survey control, string the fence line and mark post positions on dirt, gravel or asphalt on an active but open site.

Large industrial / utility-scale project (solar farm, substation, plant, data center, highway right-of-way) with CAD drawings and surveyed coordinates: lay out miles of fence line and mark hundreds to thousands of posthole positions on graded open ground, coordinating with the project surveyor and other trades.

Agricultural or ranch fencing across pasture, cropland or rangeland: sight and lay out long runs over uneven, vegetated terrain, set corner and brace positions from the field boundary or a farm plan, and flag/mark line-post positions at 12-16 ft spacing, often with no georeferenced drawing.

Repair, replacement or short extension work: measure off an existing fence or structure to match post spacing and line, mark one to a few posthole positions in tight, obstructed spaces (between buildings, along an existing fence line, behind landscaping).

sources.title: Solar Farm Layout Tool & GPS Surveying Equipment | Civ Robotics
sources.claim: Civ Robotics' GNSS layout robots are used on solar farm construction sites specifically to locate fence points and mark the project perimeter for fence installation.

sources.title: Automated Layout Startup Civ Robotics Secures $7.5M Series A Funding Round | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Third-party trade press reports that the CivDot+ autonomously marks layout points across large outdoor construction sites with minimal human oversight, reducing the crew needed to mark out sites.
sources.transferJustification: Marking surveyed layout points (piles, foundations, fence perimeter) on an outdoor site is the same act as marking posthole positions from drawings: same medium (paint/flag on ground), same tolerance, same site type.

sources.title: Civ Robotics provides CivNav AI navigation for solar construction systems - The Robot Report
sources.claim: CivDots are in production use by large contractors: a project executive at Boldt reports the robots laid out over 300,000 point locations on ... construction projects.
sources.transferJustification: Point layout on heavy-civil sites transfers to marking posthole positions: identical output (ground marks at designed coordinates) at tighter tolerance than fence work requires.

sources.title: High-precision construction layout robot | Civ Robotics
sources.claim: CivDot is a rugged 4WD outdoor rover with 10-inch ground clearance that marks up to 3,000 points per ... at 30 mm accuracy using a spray-paint mechanism, driven by an AI navigation algorithm with modes for different terrains.

sources.title: Surveying Upgrade: Six Points a Minute with CivDot | Civ Robotics
sources.claim: Vendor success story describes CivDot marking coordinates while navigating variable topography with mud, rocks and challenging landscapes, with the crew simply installing flags behind it.
sources.transferJustification: Rough-ground coordinate marking is the layout step of fencing: the robot places the ground marks a fence crew would paint or flag before digging.

sources.title: TinyMobileRobots marks one million sports fields | SportsField Management
sources.claim: TinyMobileRobots' GPS-RTK line-marking robots autonomously mark out designs on turf at grounds-maintained facilities (clubs, schools, universities, municipalities); the company had marked its one-millionth sports field by 2022.
sources.transferJustification: Setting out a stored geometric design on maintained turf with cm-level paint marks is the same operation as measuring out a fence line and marking post positions on grounds; comparable precision and marking medium.

tasks.label: Align posts, by lines or sighting, and verify vertical alignment of posts, using plumb bobs or spirit levels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential backyard wood or vinyl privacy fence: string a line between set terminal posts, drop each 4x4 into an augered hole, align its face to the string, plumb both faces with a spirit level, brace it, then concrete. Sloped, landscaped yard with tight access, tree roots, utilities and property-line constraints; 15-30 posts.

Chain-link or ornamental steel fence on a commercial/institutional lot (school grounds, warehouse yard, substation): terminal posts set first, a taut line run between them, line posts set in concrete footings on graded ground at uniform spacing, each checked plumb with a level and sighted down the run before the concrete sets.

Agricultural/ranch wire fencing: hundreds of wood or steel posts driven along a sighted line across open pasture, corners and braces set first, line-of-sight and mast-angle used to keep posts on line and vertical over rolling, uneven ground.

Large-site or right-of-way perimeter fencing (solar farm, industrial construction site, highway ROW): posts driven at surveyed coordinates along long straight runs on open, ungraded ground, position and plumb verified against layout stakes/GPS points.

Repair/replacement: a leaning, frost-heaved or broken post in an existing fence is re-plumbed or dug out and replaced, then re-aligned to the existing fence line with the adjacent fabric, rails or wire still attached; typically one to three posts in a homeowner's yard or along an existing farm fence.

sources.title: The World's First Autonomous Piling System for Utility-Scale Solar — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 autonomous pile driver, paired with the RPS 25 stabilizer, drives steel posts into the ground on open solar-farm sites to surveyed positions with controlled plumbness and z-height, combining surveying, pile distribution, driving and inspection in one robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: solar pile driving. Both tasks place a long vertical member at a surveyed point on a line at fixed spacing and verify it is plumb; the robot's own metric is plumbness and position (sub-inch), comparable to or tighter than fence-post line-and-level work, and the objects (steel posts, 200 lb, 12-19 ft) resemble driven fence posts.

sources.system: Built Robotics autonomous pile drivers (Louisiana solar site, Meta Hyperion)
sources.title: Autonomous construction bots are building the solar infrastructure behind Meta's massive Hyperion data center
sources.claim: Built Robotics' retrofitted excavators are deployed on real, muddy outdoor solar construction sites, driving roughly 1,000 steel piles per day with a human acting only as fleet supervisor, across 40+ deployments nationwide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pile driving on an unstructured construction site. It establishes that the plumb/position-controlled post-setting capability runs unattended on terrain taken as found, which is the environment fence erectors work in for driven-post runs.

sources.developer: Farmscan AG / Kidd Farm Machinery / Harper Adams University
sources.title: Roto-Fence Project: Autonomous Fencing for Smarter Grazing - Farmscan AG
sources.claim: The Roto-Fence system (Farmscan AG, Kidd Farm Machinery, Harper Adams University) drives farm fence posts along a pre-planned fence line from an autonomous tractor with a sensor-equipped post driver, achieving centimetre-level placement accuracy in field trials.

sources.title: Solar Farm Layout Tool & GPS Surveying Equipment | Civ Robotics
sources.claim: Civ Robotics' CivDot autonomous survey robots mark pile and fence-perimeter points on solar construction sites, marking up to 3,000 points ... to within about four inches, replacing manual line-and-stake layout for contractors such as Bechtel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: construction layout. It covers the 'align by lines or sighting' half of the task — autonomously establishing the fence line and post positions in the field — which fence erectors do with string lines and sighting.

sources.system: SCADAware prefabricated wall assembly cell (Kawasaki BX250L / Güdel TMF-3)
sources.title: Assembling Walls for Prefabricated Homes | Industrial Robots by Kawasaki
sources.claim: A purpose-built robotic cell at builder Rehkemper & Son (integrator SCADAware, Kawasaki BX250L robots on Güdel rails) squares wooden framing members against fixed stops and servo fingers and positions them to within 1/16 inch of the digital design before robots fasten sheathing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic timber framing in a fixtured cell. The act is the same as the fence task's core — bringing a long wooden member onto a reference line and verifying its alignment — with comparable objects (dimensional lumber) and tighter precision, but only when the work is fixtured and presented, i.e. an E1 setting.

sources.system: BUILT to BUILD automated panel framing
sources.title: Automated Panel Framing – House of Design Robotics
sources.claim: House of Design's automated panel framing systems use robots to insert and fasten plates and span members for wall panels inside a purpose-built robotic cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic placement of framing members in a jig. Supports that, with the workpiece fixtured and presented (E1), commercial robot cells reliably place and hold linear wooden members in correct alignment, the equivalent of setting a post to line and plumb.

tasks.label: Attach rails or tension wire along bottoms of posts to form fencing frames.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential wood privacy or picket fence in a homeowner's back yard: after posts are set in concrete, the erector measures, cuts and fastens 2x4 bottom (and mid) rails between posts with screws, nails or brackets, stepping or racking the rails to follow sloped, landscaped ground and working around trees, AC units, sheds and neighbors' fences.

Residential or light-commercial chain-link fence on a small lot: attaching a bottom rail into rail ends/brace bands at terminal posts, or stretching bottom tension wire from terminal to terminal with a come-along and securing it at each line post before the fabric is hung and hog-ringed.

Commercial/industrial or highway perimeter chain-link fence on an active construction site or road right-of-way: long runs of heavy 21-ft top/bottom rails or coiled tension wire carried along a rough, muddy or rocky, partially cleared fence line, with grade changes, spoil piles and traffic nearby.

Agricultural/ranch fencing: running and tensioning bottom and line wires along wood posts and T-posts across pasture, stapling to wood posts or clipping to steel posts over long undulating runs with vegetation, livestock and no prepared work surface.

Ornamental aluminum/steel or chain-link fence on maintained institutional premises (paved warehouse yard, school sports complex, parking lot): pre-fabricated panels with horizontal rails bolted or bracketed to posts along a level, graded, groundskept line with standard hardware and controlled access.

Repair call: replacing a broken or sagging bottom rail, or re-tensioning and re-attaching a slack bottom tension wire, on an existing weathered fence — cutting out damaged members, freeing rusted bands and fasteners, and refitting to posts already in the ground.

sources.system: KCR Systems 300 robotic welding cell (KUKA KR16 L6)
sources.title: Robotic Aluminum Arc Welding Case Study for Flexible Robotic System
sources.claim: A turnkey KUKA robotic arc-welding cell built by KC Robotics welds an aluminum fencing manufacturer's fence posts and gate frames from parts held in dedicated fixtures, inside a fenced, light-curtained cell, running with one operator instead of 4-6 welders.
sources.transferJustification: Same objects and joint as the task: horizontal rails/members joined to fence posts and into gate/fence frames. The cell performs the joining autonomously once posts and rails are clamped in fixtures, which is exactly the E1 counterfactual (work brought to the machine).

sources.system: BOS-FENC FE/LP7/LP9 and BOS-FENC H fencing panel nailers
sources.title: Bostitch Automated Solutions — Specialist Machines: Fencing
sources.claim: The BOS-FENC fence-panel nailing machines assemble wood fence panels (rails plus feather-edge/lapped boards): an operator loads the jig and a machine-controlled nailing bridge drives the fasteners in one pass, with quick changeover between panel dimensions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory assembly of wood fence frames. Same members (fence rails and boards), same fasteners (nails) and same tolerance as fastening rails to posts on site; it is done with the parts fixtured in a jig, i.e. the E1 presentation of the work.

sources.system: UNIFEWEL / FEWEL mesh welding machines for fence panels
sources.title: Mesh Welding Machines | 358 Security Panels Mesh Welding Machine
sources.claim: Fully automated fence-panel welding lines feed line wires from coils through servo-driven rollers, straighteners and tension control and weld them to cross members to produce finished 2D/3D/358 security fence panels, run by one operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine attachment of tensioned horizontal wire to fixtured vertical members in fence manufacture. It is the purpose-built-line analog of running and tensioning wire along posts, supporting the E1 counterfactual for the tension-wire variants of this task.

sources.system: House of Design automated roof/floor truss systems (ABB robots)
sources.title: Louws Truss turns to tech and robotics | HBS Dealer
sources.claim: Robotic truss lines from House of Design, installed in US component plants (e.g. Louws Truss, 2022; Builders FirstSource orders), handle dimensional lumber and embed nail plates to assemble wood frames on jigged tables.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic fastening of wood framing members into frames on fixtured tables. Comparable members (nominal lumber), comparable fastening precision, and the parts are presented by conveyors and jigs — the E1 form of attaching wood rails to posts.

sources.system: Charge Robotics portable solar factory / Sunrise system
sources.title: Making solar projects cheaper and faster with portable factories | MIT News
sources.claim: Charge Robotics deploys a portable robotic assembly line to utility-scale solar construction sites that assembles steel tracks, brackets, fasteners and modules into 40-ft bays, with a robotic vehicle delivering and fastening each bay onto driven piles; the company says everything except pile driving is automated.
sources.transferJustification: Closest outdoor analog (fastening horizontal steel members onto driven posts in a field). It does not transfer to this task: it requires a shipped-in assembly line, one standardized racking product and GPS-surveyed piles on graded ground, and it never cuts/threads fence rails or stretches and ties tension wire, so it substantiates completion only where the work is presented to a purpose-built line.

sources.system: Roto-Fence autonomous fencing system (Farmscan AG guidance + Kidd post driver)
sources.developer: Farmscan AG / Smart Ag Systems / Kidd Farm Machinery
sources.title: Roto-Fence Project: Autonomous Fencing for Smarter Grazing – Farmscan AG
sources.claim: The Innovate UK Roto-Fence project demonstrated an autonomous tractor and post driver that follows a digitally planned fence line and places farm fence posts at planned intervals; the automation covers post placement, not attaching rails or running and tensioning wire.
sources.transferJustification: Same trade, adjacent step (setting posts). Cited to show that on-site fencing automation as of 2026 stops at post placement — no cited system attaches rails or stretches/secures tension wire along posts in the field — supporting the negative E2/E3 judgments.

tasks.label: Dig postholes, using spades, posthole diggers, or power-driven augers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential job: digging 15-40 holes (~8-12 in dia., 24-36 in deep) along a staked line in a homeowner's yard for a wood privacy or chain-link fence, using a two-man gas auger or clamshell diggers; tight access through a 36-in gate, lawn/landscaping and sprinkler lines to protect, tree roots, buried service laterals, holes hard against the house, deck or neighbor's fence.

Farm/ranch line fence across open pasture: augering corner, brace and line-post holes along a long run with a tractor 3-point or skid-steer auger; uneven, sloping ground, rocks and hardpan, sod and brush, livestock and gates, spoil left beside each hole, depth varied by post type.

Commercial/industrial perimeter on an open, machine-accessible new-construction site (warehouse yard, school field, substation, solar or park perimeter): surveyed layout, 10-12 in dia. holes 30-42 in deep for chain-link line and terminal posts, graded bare ground, room for a skid steer or mini-ex auger, spoil hauled off, coordination with other trades.

Commercial infill fencing on a congested urban lot: postholes along a property line squeezed between existing buildings, curbs, parking-lot asphalt, landscaping and marked utilities; frequent hand digging or hydro-excavation near utilities, obstructions requiring holes to be shifted or chipped through old concrete.

Repair/replacement work: digging out one or a few holes to replace a broken or rotted post in a standing fence, breaking out or working around the old concrete footing with bar and clamshell diggers, working in a confined pocket between existing panels or rails.

Highway right-of-way / roadside fencing: augering line-post holes along a shoulder, ditch slope or airport/utility boundary, in gravel and rocky fill, within a traffic-control zone next to live traffic, following the road grade over long distances.

sources.system: Epiroc SmartROC D65 MKII (autonomous surface drill)
sources.title: Epiroc and Luck Stone launch first fully autonomous SmartROC D65 drill rig in U.S. aggregate market
sources.claim: Epiroc's SmartROC D65 MKII surface drill rig executes complete drill patterns in a quarry with no operator in the ..., under remote supervision, deployed commercially at Luck Stone in Virginia.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drilling a planned pattern of holes into the ground outdoors. Like posthole digging, the machine positions itself at surveyed hole locations on natural ground, penetrates to a specified depth, withdraws and moves to the next hole; hole diameters (roughly 4-6 in) and depths are of the same order as fence postholes, though in rock rather than soil.

sources.title: Built Robotics Unveils Autonomous Pile Driving Robot, Expediting Solar Rollout (Forbes)
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 autonomously surveys a utility-scale solar site, distributes and installs foundation piles into native ground and inspects them, working with a two-person crew present.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: setting post foundations into native ground at surveyed positions on an open outdoor site. It is the same ground-engaging foundation step a fence erector performs when digging and setting posts, at similar or larger post size and to tighter position/plumb tolerance, on unimproved graded terrain.

sources.title: Blattner Picks Autonomous Pile Drivers from Built Robotics for Solar Projects (ENR)
sources.claim: Solar EPC contractor Blattner (Quanta) is adopting dozens of Built Robotics' autonomous pile-driving excavators for solar foundation installation on U.S. projects, indicating commercial-scale field use.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the RPD 35 item: autonomous installation of ground-embedded posts at surveyed locations across open outdoor construction sites; this source establishes commercial-scale deployment rather than a one-off demonstration.

sources.title: Robotic soil sampler is slow but consistent (The Western Producer)
sources.claim: Rogo's SmartCore, a self-driving Bobcat-chassis robot, autonomously drives farm fields and augers soil at RTK-GPS-specified points to a controlled depth, at commercial scale (about 100,000 acres sampled in one season with four machines).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously navigating an open field taken as found and augering into soil at prescribed locations and depth. Same physical operation as augering a posthole (soil engagement, depth control, repositioning between holes), though at much smaller hole diameter and depth.

sources.system: DEWALT autonomous downward-drilling robot (August Robotics platform)
sources.title: DEWALT Unveils the World's First Downward Drilling, Fleet-Capable Robot to Accelerate Data Center Construction
sources.claim: A DEWALT drilling rig mounted on an August Robotics autonomous mobile robot drills thousands of holes to a CAD layout on active data-center construction floors, reporting 99.97% accuracy over 90,000+ holes in a hyperscaler pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously drilling large numbers of downward holes at surveyed layout positions inside a facility under construction, with other trades present. Supports hole-to-layout autonomy in a structured human work facility (E2), though the medium is concrete slab rather than soil.

tasks.label: Attach fence rail supports to posts, using hammers and pliers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential chain-link fence install in a homeowner's back yard: worker slides brace bands/rail-end bands over set terminal and corner posts at the required height, seats rail-end cups, threads and tightens carriage-bolt nuts with pliers, and taps the top rail into loop caps with a hammer, working on turf, slopes and around landscaping.

Residential wood privacy or picket fence: worker nails or screws rail hangers/brackets (or toenails 2x4 rails) onto 4x4 posts at marked heights with a hammer, checking level and adjusting spacing for out-of-plumb posts and uneven ground.

Commercial/institutional chain-link perimeter (school yard, warehouse lot, substation, ball field) on an institution-controlled site: many identical line and terminal posts, brace bands and rail ends bolted and tightened along long straight runs, some work at height from a ladder or lift, crew and equipment staged on the premises.

Agricultural, ranch or highway right-of-way fencing across open uneven terrain: attaching brackets, clips, stays or staples to wood or steel posts with hammer and pliers, in weather, at distance from vehicles, with variable post spacing and terrain.

Repair/replacement work on an existing standing fence: cutting or knocking off a corroded or bent rail support/band, fitting and bolting or nailing a replacement onto the in-place post, matching the existing fence's height and hardware.

sources.system: Robotiq Screwdriving Solution / Screwdriving Workcell (UR cobot + screw feeder + force sensing)
sources.title: Screwdriving Solution | Robotiq
sources.claim: Robotiq's Screwdriving Workcell is commercially deployed at Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories, where cobot cells autonomously pick fasteners from a feeder and drive them into fixtured assemblies with torque control at production volume across 27 stations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: powered fastener driving onto fixtured workpieces in a purpose-built cell. Attaching a fence rail support means positioning a band/bracket on a post and running a bolt or screw to torque - the same class of hardware placement plus fastener drive at comparable precision, which this workcell performs autonomously with feeders, torque control and error-proofing.

sources.system: House of Design dynamic automation / Automated Truss and Wall Panel Systems (ABB robots with nail guns)
sources.developer: House of Design Robotics (Nampa, Idaho), deployed at Autovol
sources.title: Dynamic Automation Helps Company Create "Snowflakes" - Modular Building Institute
sources.claim: ABB robot cells built by House of Design run nail guns to assemble dimensional-lumber wall and truss assemblies in an offsite factory (Autovol), building assemblies of varying geometry from 3D models without a human holding the nailer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic nailing of wood framing members into fixtured assemblies. Attaching a wood fence rail bracket or toenailing a rail to a 4x4 post uses the same materials, the same nail-driving action and comparable (few-mm) placement precision; the truss/wall cells do it autonomously at production quality.

sources.system: FANUC M-20iD/25 robot cells for clip insertion
sources.title: FANUC Robots Automate Precise Automotive Process | Case Study
sources.claim: FANUC M-20iD/25 industrial robots in four fenced cells autonomously feed, insert and fasten (weld) plastic clips onto an automotive product with dimensional and geometric positioning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous feeding and installation of small hardware onto a fixtured part in a guarded cell - structurally the same operation as presenting a brace band/rail-end and securing it to a fixtured post.

sources.title: AES Maximo robot installs 100 megawatts of solar capacity - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most advanced outdoor construction manipulator deployed at scale (Maximo, 100 MW installed at the AES Bellefield solar site) focuses on placing modules; in its supervised mode humans, not the robot, secure the modules to the structure, and the company describes its core function as module placement.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest outdoor analogue (attaching hardware to structural members on unimproved ground). It shows placement is automated but fastening on repetitive, surveyed racking is still largely human, so it does not substantiate autonomous bracket-and-bolt attachment on fence posts in the field.

sources.system: Roto-Fence autonomous fencing system (Kidd post driver + Farmscan AG control)
sources.developer: Farmscan AG, Kidd Farm Machinery, Harper Adams University (Innovate UK)
sources.title: Roto-Fence Project: Autonomous Fencing for Smarter Grazing - Farmscan AG
sources.claim: The Roto-Fence project automates field fencing only to the extent of driving posts to a planned layout; hardware attachment along the fence line is not automated.
sources.transferJustification: Closest fence-specific field automation found. It covers post installation, not attaching rail supports to posts, so it supports no positive judgment for this task in E2/E3 settings.

tasks.label: Assemble gates, and fasten gates into position, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential wood privacy/picket gate: on a homeowner's back-yard fence line, cut and fasten a braced wood frame, screw/nail on pickets, lag hinges to an already-set wood post, hang the leaf, shim to gap and swing clear of sloped ground, install latch and drop rod.

Chain-link gate delivered as a complete prefabricated leaf: bolt hinge hardware (male/female hinges) to the terminal post, lift and hang the leaf, plumb it, set the latch fork and drop rod, adjust to swing clear of the drive.

Chain-link gate built on site: cut tubing, assemble the frame with rail-end/corner fittings or field welds, stretch chain-link fabric across the frame with tension bars and bands, tie it off, then hang the finished leaf on the post.

Commercial/industrial perimeter at a controlled facility (plant, distribution yard, school): hang a heavy double-swing or cantilever slide gate — bolt or weld heavy hinges/roller trucks to steel posts, set the leaves with a helper or machine, install drop rods, latch and hardware, adjust plumb and level.

Farm/ranch tube gate on uneven pasture ground: bore and set lag/bolt hinge pins in a wood brace post (or bolt to steel post), lift the pre-made tube gate onto the pins, adjust height for terrain, hang chain/latch on the far post.

Shop or yard pre-assembly before delivery: build ornamental steel or aluminum gate leaves in the contractor's fabrication shop — assemble frame members and pickets, weld or bolt them, fit hinges, latch and hardware to the leaf.
