sources.transferJustification: Directly the fabrication of alternate-panel (hit-and-miss) fence sections named in the task; only the on-site post setting and hanging fall outside it.

sources.system: BOS-FENC FE/LP7/LP9 and BOS-FENC H fencing panel machines
sources.title: Automated Solutions / Sectors / Specialist Machines / Fencing — Bostitch UK
sources.claim: Bostitch's BOS-FENC family are purpose-built fence-panel nailing machines used in fence panel production; an operator loads the jig or table and a programmable nailing bridge fastens the whole panel in one movement.
sources.transferJustification: Same workpiece as the task (wood fence panels of lapped/feather-edge type); listed as supporting context only, since the operator lays the boards so machine autonomy over the whole panel is not established.

sources.date: product page retrieved 2026-07; LIGNA launch of sub-assembly cell June 2025
sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - ZeroLabor
sources.claim: Randek's ZeroLabor is a commercially sold multi-robot cell that performs fully automated sub-assembly and sheathing of timber wall elements (studs, noggings, rough openings, multi-layer sheeting) in offsite construction factories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly and fastening of dimensional lumber members into flat panels in a fixtured factory line — the same materials, fastening operations and tolerances required to build a fence panel or fence section in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: SCADAware robotic wall sheathing cell (Kawasaki BX250L robots) at Rehkemper & Son
sources.title: Assembling Walls for Prefabricated Homes | Industrial Robots by Kawasaki
sources.claim: Four Kawasaki BX250L robots on Güdel rails autonomously nail sheathing boards onto pre-framed timber walls and cut openings in a prefabricated-home factory cell, driven by software generated from the wall's digital design, handling warped, imprecise wood.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic nailing of boards to a timber frame held in a factory fixture, with vision/model-driven placement on imprecise lumber — the same operation as fastening fence boards or louver slats to rails in a jig.

sources.date: launched March 2023; commercial solar site deployments reported 2023-2025
sources.title: Robotic solar pile driver three times faster than humans – pv magazine USA
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 autonomously surveys, distributes, drives and inspects foundation piles on utility-scale solar construction sites, at roughly 300 piles per day with ..., but it only drives posts and performs no board or panel attachment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously driving posts into the ground outdoors at surveyed positions — covers only the post-setting sub-step of fence erection; nothing in the system attaches rails, boards, louvers or woven panels, so it cannot complete the whole task outdoors.

tasks.label: Insert metal tubing through rail supports.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential chain-link fence: after line posts are set and loop-cap (eye-top) rail supports are placed, the erector lifts 21-ft, 1-3/8" galvanized top rail overhead in a fenced-in backyard, threads it through the loop caps on successive posts, swages/couples it into the previously installed length, and cuts the last stick to fit the rail end at the terminal post; uneven grade, trees, AC units, sheds and slopes.

Commercial/industrial perimeter chain-link (warehouse yards, substations, storage lots, jobsite security fence): long, mostly straight runs on graded ground, heavier 1-5/8" or 2" top rail and sometimes mid-rail, threaded through loop caps on 10-ft-spaced posts, joined stick to stick and braced at corner/terminal posts; work amid other trades, traffic and weather.

Sports and recreation fencing (ball field backstops, tennis/pickleball courts, playgrounds): tall 10-20 ft fabric with top, mid and bottom rails plus backstop framework; rails threaded through eye tops and rail-end bands often from ladders or lifts, with corner and radius sections requiring cut-to-fit tubing.

Repair/retrofit: replacing a bent or rusted section of top rail on an existing fence — cutting out the damaged tube, sliding a new length through the existing loop caps, sleeving/swaging it into the remaining rail, in situ against standing fabric that must be loosened and re-tied.

Shop/yard prefabrication: at the contractor's fabrication shop, assembling gate frames and prefabricated fence sections on layout tables — inserting tubing through frame rail supports/brackets and fittings before welding or bolting, then staging for delivery.

sources.system: OCTA Group ITS M25 tube insertion machine
sources.title: Tube insertion machine - Precise and automatic threading on heat exchangers | OCTA Group
sources.claim: OCTA Group's ITS M25 is a commercial factory machine that automatically threads long metal tubes lengthwise through a series of aligned holes in a pre-assembled stack, with an automatic positioning system finding the holes and a track drive pushing the tube the full length.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inserting heat-exchanger tubes through the aligned holes of a finned/baffled stack. It is the same motion and object class as threading a fence top rail through loop-cap rail supports — a long, slender metal tube pushed lengthwise through a series of coaxial support holes — at tighter tolerances than a 1-3/8" rail in a loop cap, in a fixtured machine setting.

sources.system: Canrig iRacker / RZR Rig Floor Automation Module
sources.title: RZR™ Rig Floor Automation Module - Nabors
sources.claim: Canrig/Nabors' iRacker is a commercially deployed, fully autonomous tubular-handling system that picks, moves and stabs long heavy steel pipe on the rig floor with no workers present in the handling zone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous handling and stabbing of 30-ft steel tubulars into fixed receptacles (well center, mousehole) on a purpose-built rig floor. Object length, weight and the insert-into-a-known-aperture precision exceed those of a 21-ft fence top rail entering a loop cap, showing machines can manipulate and insert long tubing when the receiving features are held in known positions.

sources.title: MIT-based startup launches solar construction robotic system – pv magazine USA
sources.claim: Charge Robotics' Sunrise system, first deployed in 2024, autonomously assembles steel tracker hardware (torque tubes and modules) into completed solar bays inside a portable on-site factory line and performs field installation of the assemblies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated assembly of long steel torque tubes and brackets into tracker rows. Comparable objects (multi-metre galvanized steel tubing and their support fittings) and bolt-level precision, but the assembly is done on a purpose-built portable factory line fed with fixtured, standardized parts, not by threading tube through supports already standing in the ground.

sources.title: Terabase Energy's Next-Generation Terafab® Completes Field Testing, Ready for Deployment
sources.claim: Terabase's Terafab V2, field-tested and released for commercial shipment in 2026 after first-generation deployment on five solar projects, is an automated on-site line that assembles modules onto tracker torque tubes and delivers the assemblies to prepositioned tracker mounts using robotics.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling and assembly of long steel torque tubes onto engineered supports at a solar site. It shows tube-and-support assembly is automated only inside a purpose-built line whose feedstock is standardized and fixtured; the outdoor step is lowering finished rows onto surveyed mounts, not threading tubing through in-place rail supports.

tasks.label: Nail pointed slats to rails to construct picket fences.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New residential picket fence: after posts are set and 2x4 rails are hung between them in a homeowner's back or front yard, the erector face-nails uniform pointed pickets to the rails with a pneumatic coil/siding nailer, using a spacer jig and string line to hold spacing, plumb and top height over uneven turf, working around shrubs, AC units and slopes.

Shop/yard prefabrication: at the fence contractor's or lumberyard's covered shop, pickets and rails are laid on a bench jig and nailed into 6- or 8-ft picket sections that are stacked and hauled to jobs; uniform, pre-pointed pickets, standard spacing, indoor level floor.

Repair work: replacing broken, split or rotted pointed pickets on an existing standing picket fence at a home, matching the old picket profile and spacing, nailing to rails that are in place (sometimes warped), often with limited access from one side and landscaping in the way.

Commercial/institutional/municipal job: long straight runs of standard picket fence at a school, park, HOA or apartment complex on a graded, staked and cleared line; large volumes of identical pointed pickets nailed to installed rails, quality checked against a spec.

Custom/decorative picket work on site: scalloped or arched picket tops, varying picket lengths, racked or stepped panels on sloping ground, curves, gate leaves and end panels ripped to fit; pickets cut and pointed on site with a saw, then nailed to rails.

sources.system: GBN Excalibur stringer pallet system (GBN Machine and Engineering Corp.)
sources.title: Nailing Machine Guide: What to Look for in a Nailing Machine - Pallet Enterprise
sources.claim: Commercial pallet-assembly nailing systems with automatic stringer and deck-board feeders position boards on stringers at programmed spacing and nail them automatically inside a guarded machine cell, with operators only tending magazines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: nailing wooden deck boards across stringers at a set spacing. This is mechanically the same operation as nailing pointed slats to fence rails - same softwood members, same collated/bulk nails, same few-millimetre placement tolerance - so a machine that feeds, spaces and nails deck boards can nail pickets to rails when the work is presented on a fixture.

sources.system: Viking Voyager / Turbo 505 tandem nailing machines
sources.title: Nailing Machine Guide: What to Look for in a Nailing Machine - Pallet Enterprise
sources.claim: Viking's automated nailing machines feed boards from hoppers and position them for nailing at rates of thousands of assembled units per shift; they are the standard nailing equipment in US pallet plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic positioning and nailing of boards onto parallel stringers. Board-to-rail fastening geometry, lumber dimensions and nail types match picket-to-rail fence assembly; the machine supplies the board placement that the human fence erector does by hand with a spacer jig.

sources.title: Fence Panel Machine | Pallet Chief Manufacturing
sources.claim: A US machinery maker sells a purpose-built automated fence panel machine that performs the nailing, cutting and flipping of wooden fence panels in a fixtured cell.
sources.transferJustification: Direct task match at panel scale: the machine nails wooden slats to rails to produce a finished fence panel; only the loading of the jig is attributed to an operator.

sources.title: BOS-FENC FE/LP7/LP9 - Bostitch Automated Solutions, Fencing
sources.claim: Dedicated fencing-panel nailing machines with 7-9 nailing tools on a moving bridge nail up wooden fence panels in a jig; an operator loads the jig and ... machine completes the nailing cycle automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, factory form: wooden slats fastened to rails to make a fence panel. Shows fence-panel nailing is a standard fixtured-cell operation; slat placement here is still manual, so it corroborates rather than carries the judgment.

sources.title: Panel making machine - BOS-FENCE - HANDSAEME MACHINERY - automatic / for the wood industry
sources.claim: Semi-automatic garden/fence panel machines are sold in which an operator places the wooden slats in a mold and the machine's tools automatically join them.
sources.transferJustification: Same task in a factory cell (slats fastened to rails to form fence panels); confirms the operation is routinely machine-executed once the workpieces are fixtured.

sources.system: Automatic American stringer-type wood pallet nailing machine (fully automatic configuration)
sources.title: Automatic Stringer Pallet Nailing Machine - High-Efficient Wood Pallet Making Machine
sources.claim: Fully automatic stringer-pallet nailing lines feed stringers and boards by conveyor/indexing into a clamping fixture and nail them without manual handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic feeding, clamping and nailing of boards onto rails/stringers - the E1 presentation of picket-to-rail nailing, with identical materials and fastening precision.

tasks.label: Construct and repair barriers, retaining walls, trellises, and other types of fences, walls, and gates.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential wood or vinyl privacy fence at a private home: lay out the line on an irregular, sloped yard, dig/auger 10-20 post holes around buried utilities and tree roots, set posts in concrete, cut and fasten rails and pickets to follow grade, and build and hang a matching gate.

Chain-link, welded-mesh or ornamental steel fence with gates around a commercial, industrial or school property: run the line along a boundary with brush, curbs and slope, set line/terminal posts, hang panels or stretch fabric with top rail and tension bars, and install swing or cantilever gates.

Agricultural/ranch fencing: long runs of woven-wire, barbed-wire or high-tensile fence across pasture and rough terrain — driving wood and steel posts, building H-brace corners, stretching and stapling wire, and hanging farm gates.

Repair calls on existing fences, walls and gates in place: replacing storm-broken pickets or panels, resetting or splicing a rotted/leaning post, patching torn chain-link fabric, re-tensioning wire, and re-hanging or re-welding a sagging gate and its hardware.

Landscape barriers in yards and light commercial grounds: segmental block or timber retaining walls (excavate, base course, backfill, drainage), decorative masonry garden walls, and building/installing trellises, arbors and lattice screens.

Temporary and roadside barriers: standing and clamping temporary mesh fence panels around a jobsite or event, and installing highway guardrail/barrier posts and rail along a road shoulder under traffic.

sources.system: IGS mesh welding line for fencing panels
sources.title: 3D fence panels mesh welding machine production off coils
sources.claim: Fully automatic production lines weld complete metal fence panels (2D, 3D V-bend, 358 security, 4D) end to end from wire coils in a factory cell with one attending operator — i.e., machines construct the finished fence sections human fence builders otherwise assemble.

sources.system: RKM fully automatic fence panel production line
sources.title: Fence Mesh Welding Machine | 3D Welded Fence Panel | RKM
sources.claim: A commercially sold fence-panel line takes wire from coils to finished, V-bent security fence panels automatically under PLC control, at 120 welds/min, for highway and municipal barrier projects.

sources.system: Ameristar Tulsa plant robotic welders (ornamental steel fence/gate production)
sources.title: Ameristar Fence Products Inc — Manufacturing Today
sources.claim: The largest ornamental fence manufacturer builds its steel fence sections and gates in-house on tube mills, roll formers and robotic welders inside a purpose-built plant.

sources.date: 2025-06 (LIGNA launch of subassembly cell); product line commercial earlier
sources.title: Randek - House Production Technologies - Wall, Floor and Roof Production Lines
sources.claim: A commercially sold robotic cell fully automatically frames, nails, sheathes and glues timber panels (studs, rails, openings) in a factory, handling dimensional lumber assemblies to millimetre precision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic framing and nailing of timber wall panels. A wood fence panel or trellis is the same operation on the same material — rails/stiles and pickets or lattice nailed in a jig to set spacing — at equal or lower precision, in the same purpose-built factory cell, so performance carries over to fabricating fence sections and trellis panels.

sources.title: Hadrian X bricklaying robot builds first homes in demo program - The Robot Report
sources.claim: A mobile robotic block-laying machine builds structural block walls outdoors from a 3D CAD model, laying blocks with adhesive without worker intervention; it completed five single-storey homes in a US demonstration program in Florida.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying masonry blocks into a wall from a CAD model. A segmental garden/retaining wall is the same operation with comparable units and tolerances; it substantiates machine construction of a block wall when blocks are fed to the machine on a prepared base, though it does not perform the excavation, drainage or backfill of a full retaining wall.

sources.date: 2023-03 launch; deployed on US solar sites since
sources.title: Robotic solar pile driver three times faster than humans – pv magazine USA
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic pile driver surveys, distributes, drives and inspects steel H-beam piles into as-found ground on utility-scale solar construction sites, ~300 piles/day with a two-person crew — the post-setting step of fence building, but not rail, mesh, wire or gate work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving posts/piles into unprepared outdoor ground. It transfers to setting fence posts in a field, but covers only that sub-step — no cited system then attaches rails, stretches wire or hangs gates on site.

sources.developer: Farmscan AG with Kidd Farm Machinery and Harper Adams University
sources.title: Roto-Fence Project: Autonomous Fencing for Smarter Grazing - Farmscan AG
sources.claim: An autonomous tractor with a sensor-equipped post driver placed fence posts one after another to centimetre accuracy in a UK pasture at a live demonstration of the Innovate UK Roto-Fence project.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous placement of fence posts in a grazing paddock. It shows machine post-setting in an as-found field, but is a prototype limited to temporary grazing fence posts; no wire stretching, bracing, stapling or gate hanging is substantiated.

tasks.label: Weld metal parts together, using portable gas welding equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/light-commercial ornamental steel or aluminum fence installation in a customer's yard: the erector torch-welds or arc-welds rails and pickets to set posts, welds post caps and rack-adjusted panel ends, working outdoors on uneven ground, over dirt/landscaping, around plants, pets and homeowners, in whatever weather the day brings.

On-site welding of gate hardware at a driveway, industrial yard or school: tacking and welding hinges, latch plates, drop-rod keepers and diagonal braces onto set steel gate posts and gate frames, holding parts by hand/clamp for fit-up, welding in awkward positions near the ground.

Shop fabrication at the fence contractor's fab shop: cutting tube to length and laying a custom gate frame or panel out on a welding table/jig, tacking the corners, then welding the frame joints, pickets and hinge tabs before the gate goes out to the site.

Field repair of damaged fence or gate: judging what is bent/broken, cutting out the damaged member or old hinge with an oxy-fuel torch, grinding, fitting a salvaged or newly cut replacement piece, and welding it in, on a fence that has been hit, rusted or vandalized.

Agricultural or heavy perimeter work: welding pipe rails to pipe corner posts on a ranch continuous-fence line, or welding brackets/anti-climb plates and posts for a security or highway fence, outdoors on rough terrain, often far from power with a truck-mounted engine drive and torch set.

sources.system: Path Robotics AW-3 / AF-1 (Obsidian AI) welding cells
sources.title: Path Robotics raises $100M to automate welding - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Path Robotics' AW-3 and AF-1 intelligent welding cells scan parts, generate weld paths without programming, and autonomously weld steel parts; they are deployed commercially in fabrication shops across the ..., including high-mix, one-off work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: arc welding of steel weldments (frames, chassis, brackets) inside a fenced cell. Materials (mild steel tube/plate), joint types (fillet/lap tacks and seams) and precision are the same as fence gate frames, pickets and hardware; the system's scanning handles part-to-part variation typical of one-off fence work.

sources.title: ZEMAN Steel Beam Assembly (SBA) Robot — CPE Construction
sources.claim: A Zeman Steel Beam Assembler installed in a fabrication shop uses robotic arms to pick, position, tack and finish-weld attachments such as stiffeners and brackets onto steel members, with automated infeed/outfeed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fitting and welding small steel attachments onto long structural members. This is the same operation as welding hinges, latch plates, brackets and rails onto fence posts and gate frames — same steel, similar weld sizes — and the robot performs the fit-up (part placement) as well as the weld.

sources.title: ZEMAN SBA: automatic steel beam production
sources.claim: Zeman's SBA assembly-and-welding lines are a mature commercial product with dozens of installations worldwide in structural steel shops.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (robotic fit-up and welding of steel attachments to members); this item establishes commercial maturity and installed base rather than a new capability.

sources.system: Novarc Spool Welding Robot (SWR) with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2
sources.title: Novarc automates arc welding processes with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2 - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Novarc's Spool Welding Robot with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2 performs pipe and tube arc welding at a shop workstation with roller positioners, adapting parameters in real time and completing welds with no operator intervention after setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous arc welding of round pipe/tube joints on a purpose-built positioner. Ranch pipe fence and tube gate frames use the same round-section joints and comparable weld quality demands, supporting completion when the work is presented fixtured at a machine.

sources.title: Shimizu Begins Collaborating People and Autonomous Robots at Construction Site, Toranomon-Azabudai Project
sources.claim: Shimizu's Robo-Welder is an autonomous welding robot that welds steel column joints at high-rise construction sites, using laser shape-recognition sensors to manipulate torches; it has been used on actual Shimizu projects. It welds only pre-erected, pre-prepared column groove joints and does not fit up or hold arbitrary parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: field welding of structural steel joints. Transfer to fence work is limited — the robot is clamped to a standardized column groove that others have erected and aligned, whereas fence field welding requires locating, holding and fitting varied small parts on uncontrolled terrain.

sources.title: Path Robotics Launches Rove, Bringing Mobility to Welding Automation Powered by Physical AI
sources.claim: Path Robotics announced Rove, a quadruped-mounted mobile welding system intended for large assemblies and immovable structures ... shipyards and construction, launched with an early-adopter program rather than documented autonomous field completions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile arc welding away from a fixed cell. Recorded because it bears on whether welding outside a cell is substantiated; as a product launch with an early-adopter program and no documented autonomous job completions, it does not support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Blast rock formations and rocky areas with dynamite to facilitate posthole digging.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ranch/farm fence line crossing shallow bedrock or a boulder ledge: crew locates post spots on uneven pasture, drills a few small holes in rock with a hand-held or skid-steer rock drill, loads a stick or partial stick of dynamite with cap and fuse, stems, clears livestock/personnel, fires, then checks and cleans the shattered hole so a posthole digger or bar can finish it. Remote, no site control, weather and soil vary hole to hole.

Residential or small-commercial property fence in rocky ground: suburban/exurban lot with houses, driveways, buried utilities and landscaping nearby; very small, tightly confined charges (or the decision to shoot only one or two obstructing rocks), blast mats/covering, neighbor notification and vibration limits, then hand cleanout of the hole.

Right-of-way fencing along a highway, railroad or utility corridor over rocky terrain: contractor work zone with traffic control, long line of posts, mixed rock and soil, blasting subcontractor drills and shoots a series of post locations ahead of the post-setting crew, then the fence crew digs and sets posts.

Long boundary or wildlife fence in mountainous/remote terrain: steep, brushy, access by ATV or on foot, equipment and explosives packed in, posts spaced over miles, rock encountered irregularly; blast a scattering of holes per day under changing weather and no site infrastructure.

Perimeter or internal fence on an institutionally controlled industrial property (quarry, mine, plant, substation, airport): access-controlled premises with on-site blasting crews, magazines and established shot procedures; rock along the fence alignment is drilled and shot to allow posts to be set.

sources.system: SmartROC D65 MKII autonomous surface drill rig
sources.developer: Epiroc (deployed at Luck Stone quarry, Virginia)
sources.title: Epiroc and Luck Stone launch first fully autonomous SmartROC D65 drill rig in U.S. aggregate market
sources.claim: Epiroc's SmartROC D65 MKII surface drill rig executes complete blast-hole drill patterns autonomously (GMG Level 4) under remote supervision, deployed at a US quarry — showing autonomous rock drilling exists, but only on prepared quarry/mine benches with surveyed patterns, and it performs no explosive charging or firing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous drilling of blast holes in rock. It is the drilling half of the fence-erector blasting cycle, but it operates only on graded, access-controlled quarry benches with pre-designed patterns and does not load explosives, stem, tie in or fire.

sources.title: ABB, Boliden and LKAB complete successful testing of industry-first automated robot charger for increased safety in underground mines
sources.claim: ABB's Robot Charger detects drilled holes ... an underground rock face with machine vision and loads explosive charges with the charging cycle automated; testing was completed at Boliden Garpenberg mine, with the full blasting sequence still a subsequent development stage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic loading of explosives into pre-drilled holes. It covers only the charging step, requires an already-drilled pattern on a tunnel face inside a controlled mine, and the announcement states the full blasting sequence was still to be handed over for later development.

sources.system: Avatel development charging system (Epiroc Boomer M2 carrier)
sources.title: Epiroc, Orica co-create semi-autonomous explosives system - Australian Mining
sources.claim: Orica and Epiroc's Avatel underground charging unit is semi-autonomous: a single human operator completes the entire charging cycle from an enclosed cab, so explosive loading and blasting still depend on continuous operator control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanised explosive charging and blasting underground. It is the most commercially advanced charging machine, yet it keeps a human operator in the loop for the whole cycle, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment for field blasting.

sources.system: Drill-and-blast automation (industry survey incl. Avatel, autonomous drills)
sources.developer: Various (Orica, Epiroc, Sandvik) reported by Mining Technology
sources.title: What's new in automated drilling and blasting?
sources.claim: Trade-press review of drill-and-blast automation as of 2024 reports that autonomous drilling has been widely adopted while automation of blasting itself remains at an early stage, with charging machines still operator-controlled.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the mining drill-and-blast cycle, the only domain where explosive placement is being automated. It establishes that no fielded system autonomously performs the complete charge-and-fire sequence, even in the best-instrumented settings.

roles.title: Hazardous Materials Removal Workers
aliases: D and D Operator (Decontaminate and Decommissioning Operator)
D and D Operator (Decontamination and Decommissioning Operator)
roles.description: Identify, remove, pack, transport, or dispose of hazardous materials, including asbestos, lead-based paint, waste oil, fuel, transmission fluid, radioactive materials, or contaminated soil. Specialized training and certification in hazardous materials handling or a confined entry permit are generally required. May operate earth-moving equipment or trucks.

tasks.label: Remove asbestos or lead from surfaces, using hand or power tools such as scrapers, vacuums, or high-pressure sprayers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Asbestos thermal system insulation removal in building mechanical spaces: pipe lagging, boiler and breeching insulation, duct wrap and fittings in basements, crawl spaces and tunnels of commercial/institutional buildings; glovebags or full containment with negative air, wet methods, hand scraping and HEPA vacuuming; congested overhead runs with valves, elbows, tees and hangers.

Asbestos surfacing and flat-material removal in institutional/commercial buildings under renovation: vinyl floor tile and black mastic, sheet flooring, textured/plaster wall coatings, sprayed-on fireproofing and transite panels; large planar areas worked with scrapers, power scrapers, shrouded grinders, wet methods and HEPA vacuums inside a poly containment.

Asbestos removal at industrial sites - power plants, refineries, shipyards, nuclear decommissioning: insulation and refractory on boilers, turbines, vessels and process piping, worked under permit inside institution-controlled plant premises with scaffolding, wet removal and HEPA vacuums.

Lead paint abatement in housing and child-occupied facilities: wet scraping, HEPA-shrouded sanding/needle scaling, heat and chemical stripping of window sashes and casings, doors, trim, porches, stair rails and exterior siding; varied wood/plaster/metal substrates, furniture and occupants nearby, must pass clearance dust-wipe testing.

Lead paint removal from steel structures: bridges, water towers, storage tanks, transmission towers, industrial steelwork and ship hulls; containment and negative air erected, then abrasive blasting, ultra-high-pressure water jetting or needle guns to a specified SSPC surface-preparation standard, often at height or in confined box sections.

sources.system: SABRE / UTS 'Rosie' and 'Sandy' autonomous grit-blasting robots
sources.developer: University of Technology Sydney Centre for Autonomous Systems / Sabre Autonomous Solutions, with NSW Roads and Maritime Services
sources.title: Revolutionising steel bridge maintenance | University of Technology Sydney
sources.claim: Two autonomous grit-blasting robots (Rosie and Sandy), developed by UTS with NSW Roads and Maritime Services, strip old lead-bearing paint and corrosion from the steelwork inside the Sydney Harbour Bridge spans; they sense and 3D-map the found geometry, plan nozzle positions, and blast while the operator stays clear.

sources.title: Sydney Harbor Bridge Gets Blasted By Robots - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Trade-press account of the same deployment: the lightweight SABRE arms are manually placed on a rail, then automatically scan the steel and blast dirt, rust and old ... girders, with blasting consistency reported to exceed that of experienced workers and one operator supervising.

sources.system: SABRE Alpha1 autonomous abrasive blasting robot
sources.title: Solution | Autonomous Abrasive Blasting Robot | Construction Solutions (CPWR)
sources.claim: CPWR's construction-solutions database documents the commercial SABRE Alpha1 as an autonomous abrasive blasting robot that scans and 3D-maps a surface and then blasts it automatically, used for example inside storage tanks, and cites removal of lead-containing coatings as the exposure it eliminates.

sources.system: Blastman B-series blast cleaning robots (blast room with conveyor-presented workpieces)
sources.date: accessed 2026-07 (product line commercial for decades; company news 2025)
sources.title: Rail Industry - Freight Cars - Blastman Robotics Ltd
sources.claim: Blastman's commercial blast-room robots strip steel workpieces (e.g. rail wagons brought into the blast room on conveyors) automatically from a stored program, unattended, meeting strict surface-preparation quality requirements with only marginal manual touch-up.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic abrasive blast cleaning of steel in a fenced blast room. Abrasive blasting is the standard method for removing lead-based paint from steel and other rigid components; the robot's action, precision and accepted output (a specified surface-preparation standard) are identical whether or not the coating removed contains lead, so performance carries over once the workpiece is fixtured and presented.

sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University Robotics Institute / US Department of Energy
sources.title: A Robotic Pipe-Asbestos Insulation Removal System (Industrial Robot, 25(3))
sources.claim: The BOA pipe-external crawler automatically strips and bags asbestos-containing lagging from process piping; in an August 1997 field test on a 100-ft run of 4-inch pipe at the DOE Oak Ridge K-25 site it removed lagging at 29 linear feet per hour with no measurable fiber emission, passing hangers unaided, while humans placed it on the pipe and bagged material.

sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University Robotics Institute / US Department of Energy

tasks.label: Build containment areas prior to beginning abatement or decontamination work.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential asbestos or lead abatement in an occupied/vacated single-family home or apartment: move or wrap furnishings, seal doorways, windows, and HVAC registers with 6-mil poly and duct tape, lay two layers of floor poly, build a zip-pole or wood-framed three-stage decon chamber in a hallway, hang critical barriers, and set and duct a negative-air HEPA machine; irregular room shapes, clutter, trim, fixtures, ladders.

Full-scale containment in a commercial or institutional building (school, hospital wing, office floor) under renovation: erect large poly enclosures over hundreds of square feet, seal ceilings/ductwork/lights, build wood- or pole-framed airlocks and a three-chamber decon unit, run negative-air machines and smoke-test the barrier for leaks, often working from scaffolds or lifts.

Industrial plant, refinery, or power-house pipe-insulation job: build mini-containments and glovebag setups around pipe runs, elbows, valves, and vessels in congested, hot, poorly lit spaces, wrapping and taping poly to irregular cylindrical surfaces at height on scaffolding, plus a small decon unit at the access point.

Exterior containment for lead paint removal or exterior asbestos siding: hang tarps/shrouds and poly on scaffolding or a bridge platform, seal seams and ground sheeting with weighted edges and berms, secure against wind and weather, and set up a ground-level decon and waste-drop area.

Contaminated-soil or spill remediation site: lay out and stake the exclusion zone, place poly/geomembrane liner and staging pads for excavated soil, build bermed decontamination pads for equipment and personnel, install fencing/signage, using a mix of hand work and small earthmoving equipment.

Small mini-containment or glovebag setup for a short-duration repair in an occupied facility (corridor, mechanical room, classroom during off-hours): tape a small poly enclosure around a defined work spot, seal a nearby vent, and set a small HEPA unit, with strict clean-up before the space is reoccupied.

sources.developer: RWTH Aachen / EU Horizon 2020 consortium (incl. Robotnik, Eurecat)
sources.title: Bots2ReC: introducing mobile robotic units on construction sites for asbestos rehabilitation

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic asbestos removal. Transfer does NOT carry to building containment — the system grinds/abrades contaminated surfaces inside an already-enclosed room and has no capability to cut, hang, tape and seal poly sheeting, frame airlocks, or set negative-air machines.

sources.title: How a Drywall Robot Is Reshaping Interior Construction | Built

sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior wall finishing on commercial construction sites. Transfer does NOT carry: the robot needs human placement per wall and only applies compound to a flat, already-built surface; it cannot fabricate a sealed enclosure, work at height, or handle flexible film and tape.

sources.title: KEWAZO LIFTBOT - Edison Awards

sources.transferJustification: Related task: erecting temporary site structures (scaffolding), the closest analogue to building containment. Transfer does NOT carry: the robot only hoists materials; assembly, sealing and shrouding remain fully manual.

tasks.label: Prepare hazardous material for removal or storage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Asbestos abatement inside a building containment (school, hospital wing, commercial or residential renovation): worker amends/wets stripped ACM debris and poly sheeting, gathers it by hand/shovel, loads double 6-mil bags or lined drums, gooseneck-seals, wet-wipes and labels the bag, and stages it through the decon/load-out for removal.

Lead-paint chips/dust, contaminated PPE and filters, and universal waste (fluorescent lamps, mercury devices, batteries) on a renovation or demolition site: segregating hazardous from non-hazardous debris, placing it in approved drums/lined boxes, sealing, labeling and staging pending pickup.

Environmental remediation dig: excavating contaminated soil/media to survey-defined limits, loading it into lined roll-offs, dump trailers or drums, tarping/covering, collecting confirmation samples and staging containers with placards and manifests for transport.

Industrial plant or TSDF/consolidation yard: decanting waste oil, fuel, coolant or solvent from tanks/totes into drums or bulk containers, bunging/closing, weighing, labeling, palletizing and shrink-wrapping, and staging drums in a controlled storage area.

Licensed nuclear/radiological facility: sorting and segregating mixed radioactive waste by dose rate, size-reducing bulky items, loading drums/boxes or skips, grouting/lidding, surveying and swabbing the package, and staging it for storage or shipment.

Emergency spill response at a roadside, plant yard or transfer point: applying absorbents/booms, scooping saturated absorbent and product residue into overpack drums, sealing and labeling them, and staging for removal.

tasks.label: Comply with prescribed safety procedures or federal laws regulating waste disposal methods.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Asbestos abatement in a building undergoing renovation/demolition (school, office, apartment): erect poly containment and negative-air machines, don respirator/PPE, wet-remove ACM pipe lagging or tile, double-bag and label waste per OSHA 1926.1101 and EPA NESHAP, use the decon unit, and load out sealed waste for a licensed landfill with proper documentation.

Lead-based paint abatement or RRP-compliant renovation in housing, or lead paint removal from steel structures: set up containment sheeting, HEPA vacuum and wet-scrape/blast, capture and containerize the lead debris and spent abrasive, avoid prohibited practices, clean and pass cleaning verification, and package waste for TCLP-based disposal.

Hazardous liquid waste management at an industrial or commercial facility (refinery, plant, fleet shop): pump used oil, fuel, solvent or transmission fluid into drums/totes, keep containers closed, mark them 'Hazardous Waste' with accumulation start dates and DOT markings, stage in secondary containment, and release to a licensed transporter.

Outdoor spill response / contaminated soil remediation: excavate and segregate contaminated soil, control dust and runoff, load lined and covered trucks, decontaminate equipment at a decon pad, and ship the waste under manifest to a permitted disposal facility.

Radioactive or mixed waste handling at a licensed nuclear or DOE site: retrieve legacy waste, survey and characterize items, segregate LLW from ILW/TRU, place items into approved containers meeting waste acceptance criteria, monitor dose, and consign each item to the correct disposal route.

Work at a permitted hazardous-waste transfer/treatment facility: receive and sort incoming mixed waste streams to the correct disposal routes, consolidate and repack containers, and keep waste segregated by compatibility as the permit and RCRA require.

Transfer to containerizing used oil and similar hazardous liquid waste is close — identical 200 L steel/plastic drums, similar viscous petroleum liquids, ATEX-rated equipment, and the regulated output (a closed, sealed, correctly marked drum) is the same physical result RCRA container rules demand.

tasks.label: Clean contaminated equipment or areas for reuse, using detergents or solvents, sandblasters, filter pumps, or steam cleaners.

instances.label: Final cleaning inside an asbestos abatement containment in a commercial or institutional building: after gross removal, wet-wipe and HEPA-vacuum every surface (walls, ledges, pipes, floors, poly), encapsulate, and pass visual inspection plus air clearance before the enclosure comes down. Debris, negative-air machines, scaffolds and glovebags are present; layout differs on every job.

Cleaning contaminated surfaces inside a dwelling after lead-paint or small asbestos work: detergent wash and HEPA vacuum of floors, window troughs, sills, trim and furnishings to pass dust-wipe clearance levels; cluttered rooms, carpet, stairs, occupant belongings.

End-of-job decontamination of tools, containers and equipment at a site decon station or wash pad: steam/pressure washing hand tools, hoses, HEPA vacuum housings, sampling gear, drums and totes, and washing down excavator tracks or a vacuum truck, with rinsate captured and drummed for disposal so the equipment can be reused.

Cleaning process equipment at a refinery, terminal or chemical plant: de-sludging and washing a storage tank or vessel interior, hydroblasting a pulled heat-exchanger bundle, and running filter pumps to recover and separate the wash water/oil so the asset can return to service.

Radiological decontamination at a licensed nuclear or D&D facility: cleaning contaminated tools, components and small equipment (chemical decon, blasting, laser/CO2 ablation) until survey-clean for reuse or free release, working under RWP inside a controlled area.

Emergency response decontamination after a spill or clandestine lab: neutralizing and washing down a roadway, truck, or the interior surfaces of a contaminated structure, capturing wash water, and verifying by wipe sampling before the area is released.

tasks.label: Clean mold-contaminated sites by removing damaged porous materials or thoroughly cleaning all contaminated nonporous materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-family home after a plumbing leak or flood: worker sets containment and negative air, cuts and removes moldy drywall to 2 ft above the waterline, pulls baseboards, carpet, pad and batt insulation, bags debris and carries it out, then HEPA-vacuums and damp-wipes studs, subfloor and framing before clearance testing.

Confined crawlspace, attic or unfinished basement: worker crawls or kneels in tight, low-clearance space around ducts, joists and wiring to strip moldy fiberglass insulation, vapor barrier and sheathing, HEPA-vacuums joists and applies antimicrobial coating in poor light and awkward postures.

Occupied commercial or institutional building (school, office, apartment block, hospital wing) with localized mold from a roof or pipe leak: work under containment in a corridor or room, removing ceiling tiles and drywall sections, cleaning metal studs, concrete, ductwork and fixtures, protecting adjacent occupied space, hauling bagged waste out through the building.

Post-flood or post-hurricane whole-structure gut-out: multiple rooms demolished to studs — drywall, flooring, cabinetry, trim, insulation removed and hauled to a curb pile — followed by HEPA vacuuming and antimicrobial treatment of the entire remaining shell amid debris, standing muck and no utilities.

Industrial or warehouse space with mold on large nonporous surfaces only (concrete walls and floors, structural steel, tanks, racking, equipment housings): no porous demolition required; surfaces are HEPA-vacuumed, wire-brushed, wiped or media/dry-ice blasted to a visually clean standard, with residue collected.

It transfers to the 'thoroughly cleaning contaminated nonporous materials' half of mold remediation because both demand full-coverage, standoff-controlled surface treatment of hard non-absorbent substrates to a visual cleanliness standard, with the robot planning its own coverage from a 3D scan; it does not transfer to removal or bagging of porous building materials.

Liquid waste removal (waste oil, fuel, transmission fluid, sludge) at industrial plants, tank farms, sumps and gas stations: worker rigs and operates a vacuum truck, pumps and hoses, opens manways, transfers liquid to the tank or drums, and cleans up hoses and spills.

Over-the-road transport of a loaded waste vehicle: worker hooks/secures and drives a roll-off, dump, van or tanker load of hazardous waste on public roads to a transfer station, TSDF or landfill, weighs in, and dumps/drops the load at the receiving facility.

Radioactive/mixed waste handling in a licensed nuclear or DOE facility: worker operates remote-handling equipment, size-reduction gear, drum/box handling machinery and shielded transfer carts to retrieve, size-reduce, package, survey and store waste containers.

tasks.label: Sort specialized hazardous waste at landfills or disposal centers, following proper disposal procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Household hazardous waste (HHW) collection facility or one-day collection event: technician receives boxes and bins of consumer chemicals dropped off by residents (latex and oil-based paint, solvents, pesticides, pool chemicals, aerosols, motor oil, antifreeze, batteries), reads or infers labels, HazCat-tests unknowns, checks for leakers and swells, then segregates into compatible categories, bulks liquids into drums and lab-packs small containers with absorbent for shipment to incineration or landfill.

TSDF / hazardous waste consolidation facility receiving area: worker inspects incoming drums, totes, cubic yard boxes and lab packs against manifests and profiles, checks labels, dates, bulges and leaks, decides waste code and compatibility group, and moves containers with drum grabs, hand trucks and forklifts into segregated storage rows or staging lanes for treatment, incineration or landfill.

Landfill or transfer station load-check area: worker screens incoming mixed loads dumped on the tipping floor or at the working face, spots prohibited hazardous items (propane cylinders, paint and solvent cans, drums of liquid, lead-acid and lithium batteries, suspect asbestos bags, e-scrap), pulls them out of the pile, and containerizes them for proper disposal while documenting the load.

Landfill special-waste placement: worker directs and segregates bulk specialized wastes (contaminated soil, ash, treated debris, wrapped asbestos) arriving by truck into designated cells or stockpiles, verifying the profile and using loaders/dozers to place and cover material outdoors in variable weather and terrain.

Disposal/recycling center universal-waste room: worker sorts collected batteries by chemistry, fluorescent lamps by type, and e-scrap by category out of gaylords and bins into labeled, categorized containers and pallets for shipment to recyclers, removing battery-containing devices from the stream to prevent fires.

Specialized radiological / mixed-waste disposal facility: worker sorts and segregates retrieved legacy waste (metal, plastics, debris in skips and drums) by dose rate and material type into LLW vs ILW routes, size-reducing items to fit disposal containers, under shielding and strict procedure.

tasks.label: Identify asbestos, lead, or other hazardous materials to be removed, using monitoring devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-abatement/pre-renovation identification of asbestos-containing materials in a commercial, institutional or industrial building (school, office, hospital, plant): walk the spaces, judge which pipe lagging, floor tile, mastic, ceiling texture or roofing is suspect, cut/scrape small bulk samples with a knife or corer, wet them, bag, seal, label and log them for accredited lab (PLM) analysis, working around furniture, ladders, ceilings and crawl spaces.

Same suspect-material identification and bulk sampling in a private home or apartment (attic insulation, siding, popcorn ceiling, boiler lagging in a basement or crawlspace) — cramped, cluttered, occupant-owned space with no standard layout.

Lead-based paint identification in housing: room-by-room XRF scanning of painted components (walls, trim, window sashes, doors, stair risers, porch railings) per HUD protocol, positioning the analyzer flush against each surface, taking repeat readings on substrates, and recording results per component.

Lead / heavy-metal identification on commercial or industrial structures and in samples: XRF readings on painted steel, bridges, tanks or school walls, plus collection of paint-chip, dust-wipe and soil samples that are sent out for elemental analysis to define the material to be removed.

Atmospheric and vapor screening with portable monitoring devices (4-gas meter, LEL/H2S/O2, PID/FID, colorimetric tubes) across an industrial plant, tank farm, refinery or remediation site to find where hazardous substances are present before and during removal work.

Radiological contamination survey/characterization at a nuclear or DOE facility: using survey meters, frisker probes and dose-rate/gamma-mapping instruments to identify contaminated piping, components, surfaces and hot spots that must be removed or decontaminated, and logging measurements by location.

tasks.label: Remove or limit contamination following emergencies involving hazardous substances.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Transportation incident on a public road/highway: fuel or chemical released from a wrecked tanker or truck. Worker sizes up an uncontrolled scene, plugs/patches or offloads the leaking container, dams and booms the flow, applies absorbent, recovers product and spent absorbent into drums, cleans contaminated pavement/soil, decontaminates tools and personnel, manifests waste. Traffic, weather, unknown product, time pressure.

Release inside an industrial or commercial facility (chemical plant, refinery, warehouse, fuel depot): leaking drum/tote/valve/pipe. Worker enters in PPE, stops the leak, over-packs damaged containers, neutralizes or absorbs the spill among racking, machinery and floor drains, vacuums and drums residue, wipes surfaces, monitors the atmosphere and confirms the area is clean.

Emergency in a residence or small building: heating-oil release into a basement, mercury spill, illicit-lab or fentanyl contamination, contamination after fire or flood. Worker removes contaminated contents and building materials, HEPA-vacuums and wipes surfaces, applies neutralizers/encapsulants, bags waste, works to clearance sampling in cluttered, non-standard rooms.

Outdoor release reaching soil, a ditch, stream or harbor (derailment, tank overfill, pipeline seep): worker deploys containment boom and underflow dams, skims or vacuums product from water, places sorbent boom, recovers oiled debris and vegetation along an irregular bank or shoreline.

Contaminated-soil removal phase after the source is controlled at an outdoor spill site (roadside shoulder, yard, field): the impacted area has been delineated by field screening, and the worker strips the contaminated soil layer with an excavator, loads it into trucks or roll-offs, and stockpiles/backfills.

Radiological or biological incident inside an institution-controlled facility (nuclear plant, research lab, hospital): survey with instruments, remove and package contaminated items, debris and waste into approved containers, decontaminate or strip affected surfaces, then perform a confirmatory survey before release.

tasks.label: Organize or track the locations of hazardous items in landfills.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Household hazardous waste (HHW) drop-off building at a municipal landfill/transfer station: worker receives boxed loads from the public, identifies recognizable consumer products (latex/oil paint cans, aerosols, used-oil jugs, antifreeze, pesticides in original labeled packaging, lead-acid and lithium batteries, fluorescent tubes, propane cylinders), physically segregates them onto class-designated pallets, shelves and drums, and logs item counts and the staging location for each hazard class.

Same HHW facility, but the items are unknowns: unlabeled or degraded containers, mystery liquids, leaking bottles, reactives. Worker hazard-categorizes (field test kits, knowledge of markings), decides compatibility, lab-packs into drums with absorbent, labels and records what went into which drum and where the drum is staged pending shipment.

Permitted container storage area (indoor bay or paved covered pad) at a hazardous-waste landfill/TSDF or industrial site: worker organizes drums, totes and cubic-yard boxes on pallets by waste code and compatibility, moves them with a forklift, barcodes/inventories each container, and keeps the location record (row/bay/cell) current so containers can be found for inspection, consolidation or burial.

Active landfill cell/working face: special-waste loads arrive (asbestos-containing material, contaminated soil, containerized hazardous waste, treated debris). Worker meets the truck, directs it to the designated segregated area, oversees placement and immediate cover, stakes or flags the spot, and records the grid/GPS coordinates and load data in the waste-placement log and cell map required by the permit. Outdoors, mud, dust, heavy equipment traffic, terrain changes daily.

Closed/legacy landfill, old dump or illegal disposal area: worker supports locating buried hazardous items — geophysical/magnetometer survey over rough vegetated ground, test-pitting with an excavator, identifying and flagging drums or buried containers, and recording their coordinates on a site map for later removal.

Routine weekly inspection round of a hazardous-waste storage/accumulation area at the landfill or facility: worker walks the aisles, verifies each container is in its assigned location with correct labels and accumulation dates, looks for bulging, corrosion, leaks or spills, and records findings and any location changes in the inspection log.

Transfers to organizing hazardous items because the objects (cans, containers, batteries, cylinders) are comparable in size and weight, the required precision is bin-level placement, and the system records what it picks.

tasks.label: Identify or separate waste products or materials for recycling or reuse.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Asbestos or lead abatement / demolition-renovation job site: inside or just outside a containment enclosure in an older building, the worker identifies which debris is regulated hazardous waste (bagged ACM, painted components) and separates out scrap metal (ductwork, piping, radiators), clean wood, concrete and salvageable fixtures for recycling or resale. Layout differs building to building, footing and lighting are poor, PPE is worn, objects are novel and tangled.

Environmental remediation / spill cleanup site: outdoors on excavated ground, the worker sorts through soil, debris piles and recovered containers, pulling scrap metal, concrete, wood and empty drums out for recycling while keeping contaminated material segregated for disposal. Weather, mud, heavy equipment traffic, no fixed layout.

Waste transfer or industrial-waste processing facility: at a tipping floor or picking line the worker pulls recyclables (scrap metal, rigid plastics, wood, e-waste) out of incoming mixed loads and pulls hazardous items (lithium-ion batteries, propane cylinders, aerosol cans) out of the recycling stream. Fixed layout, standard conveyors, controlled premises.

Hazardous waste TSDF or consolidation warehouse: incoming drums, totes, carboys and lab packs are checked against manifests, unknowns are HazCat/compatibility tested, and containers are segregated by recovery route (fuel blending, solvent recovery, metals reclamation, universal-waste recycling) versus disposal. Requires reading labels and SDS, judging chemical compatibility, and safe handling of leakers.

Household hazardous waste collection facility or one-day collection event: residents hand over mixed consumer chemicals; the worker identifies each product (latex vs. oil-based paint, pesticides, pool chemicals, aerosols, motor oil, antifreeze, lamps, batteries), sets usable product aside for the reuse shelf, and bulks or segregates the rest into recycling streams. Many unlabeled, degraded or leaking containers.

On-site service call at a customer plant, garage, fleet yard or vessel: the worker walks the site, identifies waste oil, fuel, transmission fluid, coolant and solvents in assorted containers plus universal waste (lamps, batteries), decides what is recyclable, and labels and segregates it into the ... collection containers for pickup.

tasks.label: Process e-waste, such as computer components containing lead or mercury.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Receiving/triage line at a certified e-scrap or ITAD facility: worker takes whole incoming devices off pallets and a conveyor and sorts them by stream (CPU towers, laptops, flat screens, printers, loose boards, battery-bearing items), pulling out obvious hazards such as swollen lithium batteries and lamps into designated bins.

Bench teardown of computers: worker uses drivers, impact tools and pry bars to strip desktop towers, servers and laptops - removing covers, batteries and coin cells, hard drives, power supplies, heat sinks and lead-solder circuit boards - and drops each fraction into labeled gaylords, working through a mixed stream of models and conditions.

Shredder line work and post-shred picking: charging the shredding system, then sorting the shredded fractions coming off eddy-current/magnet separators (printed circuit boards, capacitors, aluminum, copper, brass, wire, plastics) into clean commodity streams while wearing respiratory protection for lead-bearing dust.

Flat-panel display (LCD/LED monitor and TV) processing: opening the case, removing the boards and frame, and extracting or containing the mercury-bearing CCFL backlight tubes intact under ventilation before the remainder goes to shredding.

CRT monitor and television breakdown: removing plastic housing, yoke and electron gun, venting the tube, separating leaded funnel glass from panel glass and containerizing phosphor dust and leaded glass under negative-pressure/dust-controlled conditions.

Off-site work: collecting e-waste at a customer office, school, warehouse or a municipal collection event - carting, stacking and loading unsegregated equipment into trucks, handling breakage and any spilled/leaking components on the client's premises.

tasks.label: Apply bioremediation techniques to hazardous wastes to allow naturally occurring bacteria to break down toxic substances.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-situ biostimulation/bioaugmentation at a contaminated property (former gas station, dry cleaner, industrial parcel): crew mixes amendment (emulsified vegetable oil, nutrients, oxygen-release compound, microbial culture) in totes/tanks, connects hoses to direct-push rods or injection wells, injects at controlled pressure/volume, watches for daylighting, breaks down and moves point to point across the site.

Land treatment/biopile of excavated petroleum-contaminated soil at a permitted soil treatment facility or fixed treatment cell: soil spread in lifts on a lined pad, nutrient/bulking amendment added, pile or windrow turned and tilled periodically and watered to hold moisture, with periodic sampling until cleanup criteria are met.

On-site treatment cell/biopile built at an active remediation site (UST excavation, tank farm, brownfield): liner and berms placed, excavated soil staged, amendment and bulking agent mixed in with excavator or tractor-drawn disc on uneven as-found ground amid trenches, spoil piles and site traffic; pile watered, covered and re-turned.

Spot treatment of a fuel, oil or hydraulic-fluid spill with a bioremediation product at a truck yard, substation, tank farm apron or road shoulder: worker judges the stained area and depth, sprays or spreads the microbial/nutrient product at label rate, rakes or rototills it into the top soil around curbs, drains and equipment, waters, and re-applies over following weeks.

Installing and operating an engineered bio-treatment system (bioventing/biosparge blowers and well field, biopile aeration piping, nutrient dosing loop, biofilter) at a site remediation compound: piping and headers assembled, blowers/pumps started, flows and nutrient dose adjusted over months, filters and tanks serviced.
