instances.label: Radiological/nuclear waste conditioning at a licensed waste-processing building (utility radwaste building, DOE site, or commercial processor): worker charges resins, sludges, filters, or debris into 55-gal drums or steel boxes, meters cement/slag/fly-ash grout, mixes in-drum or fills from a grout line, tops off and caps the drum, and records the recipe for the waste-acceptance record.

Stabilization/solidification of hazardous (RCRA) waste at a permitted TSDF or fixed on-site treatment building: worker blends Portland cement, kiln dust, or fly ash with sludge, waste oil residues, paint waste, or contaminated liquids in drums, cubic-yard boxes, or roll-offs using a drum mixer or pug mill and pours to fill the container for landfill disposal.

Field encasement at a remediation or demolition site: worker builds or sets formwork around contaminated debris, an asbestos-laden pipe section, or a waste container, then mixes ready-mix or site-batched concrete and pours it into the form (chute, buggy, or pump hose), vibrating and screeding to leave a void-free monolith; weather, uneven ground, and site clutter vary job to job.

Small-quantity manual work in a building basement, lab, or fenced yard: worker mixes bagged concrete in a portable mixer or wheelbarrow and pours it into drums, overpacks, or small wooden forms to encase asbestos debris, lab packs, a sealed radioactive source, or mercury-contaminated items; access is tight and the pour is done by hand.

Grouting a structure in place for closure: worker sets up a pump and hoses and fills an abandoned underground storage tank, sump, vault, or entombment cell that holds residual hazardous or radioactive material with flowable concrete/grout, monitoring fill level and venting until the void is full.

sources.system: Westinghouse Cementation Facility (in-drum mixer cementation line)
sources.title: Cementation | Westinghouse Nuclear
sources.claim: Westinghouse in-drum cementation systems dose waste, water and additives into a drum at a loading station, add and mix cement in the drum, and are offered as a fully automated line integrated with drum transport systems; ten such cementation facilities have been built at nuclear power plant sites since 2006.

sources.title: Grouting System | Westinghouse Nuclear
sources.claim: The Westinghouse grouting system (mobile silo, grouting mixer, PLC control unit, filling station with drum/container docking) continuously mixes cement grout and fills drums or containers of packed waste with continuous level monitoring; dosing and mixing run fully automated and the system has been supplied on more than 15 projects globally, in stationary and mobile versions.

sources.title: NUKEM Completes Tests for Advanced Waste Cementation System
sources.claim: NUKEM Technologies completed a full-size mock-up of its in-drum cementation plant, which seals liquid waste in 200-litre drums with cement; the company states the process is designed for automatic ... and that its cementation plants also treat NORM and hazardous waste from oil and gas, refinery, chemical and medical sources.

sources.title: First Sellafield fuel pond sludge encapsulated - World Nuclear News
sources.claim: Sellafield's encapsulation plant processed the first 500-litre drum of legacy pond sludge: cement was added to the drum and mixed with the sludge, a cement cap was added after curing, and the sealed drum was moved remotely to storage, showing that in-cell drum grouting of hazardous legacy waste is routine industrial practice.

sources.system: Box Encapsulation Plant waste treatment cell (KUKA robots)
sources.developer: Jacobs / Sellafield Ltd / Balfour Beatty joint venture
sources.title: Robotic Solutions for Sellafield's Waste Processing Challenge | Jacobs
sources.claim: Sellafield's Box Encapsulation Plant waste treatment cell, handed over for commissioning in March 2024, uses nuclearized KUKA robots to process legacy waste and grout it into 3 cubic metre boxes in a cell no human can enter; the robots are stated to work in automated mode with remote operator oversight.

sources.system: MCT/Marcantonini automated precast batching plant with automatic casting machines
sources.title: Automated precast plant for high quality concrete - MCT Group
sources.claim: A precast concrete plant in the United States runs fully automatic concrete distribution: planetary mixers, high-speed flying buckets and automatic ... batch, mix and discharge concrete into moulds throughout the factory without a worker placing the concrete.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: batching, mixing and casting concrete into forms in a precast plant. The physical act, proportioning a concrete mix and discharging a metered volume into a stationary form to a controlled level, is the same act as pouring concrete into a form that encases waste; objects (moulds/containers) and precision are comparable, and the plant is the purpose-built (E1) presentation of the work.

sources.title: Automated Mobile Batching Plant - Advanced Construction Techniques
sources.claim: Advanced Construction Techniques built and operates a self-contained mobile grout batch plant with PLC control in which grout batching is fully automated, ..., bentonite and admixtures and discharging automatically to agitation tanks that feed the grout pumps, used for remote-site drilling and grouting work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated batching and mixing of cementitious grout to recipe at a field site. It substantiates the mixing half of this task (machine-controlled proportioning and mixing) but not autonomous placement into forms, so it supports only the E1 counterfactual where the form is presented at a filling station.

sources.system: Saltstone Production Facility and Saltstone Disposal Units
sources.developer: U.S. DOE Office of Environmental Management / Savannah River Mission Completion
sources.title: SRS Completes Major Construction Milestone on Another Mega-Size Disposal Unit | Department of Energy
sources.claim: At the Savannah River Site, decontaminated salt waste is mixed with dry cementitious materials in the Saltstone Production Facility and the resulting grout is pumped into large concrete Saltstone Disposal Units, where it hardens into a monolith encasing the waste.

roles.title: Highway Maintenance Workers
roles.description: Maintain highways, municipal and rural roads, airport runways, and rights-of-way. Duties include patching broken or eroded pavement and repairing guard rails, highway markers, and snow fences. May also mow or clear brush from along road, or plow snow from roadway.

tasks.label: Set out signs and cones around work areas to divert traffic.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Freeway/expressway lane closure: crew sets advance warning signs (ROAD WORK AHEAD, RIGHT LANE CLOSED) on the shoulder plus an arrow board, then lays a taper and channelizing line of 50-150 cones from the back of a moving cone truck beside 55-70 mph live traffic, frequently at night, adjusting around ramps, gores, debris and rumble strips.

Two-lane rural road or city street short-duration closure for pothole patching, sign or guardrail repair: worker drops roll-up warning signs on gravel shoulders or grass, sets 10-30 cones around the work area and taper, works around driveways, parked cars, pedestrians, mailboxes and wind, and shifts cones as the work moves.

Mobile/moving operation (mowing, sweeping, crack sealing, striping, litter pickup): cones and portable signs are repeatedly set out, advanced and picked up along the route many times per shift behind a shadow truck with attenuator, in and out of the travel lane.

Emergency/incident and weather response: crash debris, downed tree or sign, flooding, sinkhole or ice at an unplanned location; crew rapidly places cones, barricades, flares and portable signs on uneven shoulders in rain, snow or darkness while coordinating with police and passing traffic.

Closure inside an institution-controlled facility: airport runway/taxiway or apron, toll plaza, tunnel or bridge facility, maintenance yard or park/campus road; cones, barricades and portable signs placed on standard paved surfaces to a fixed closure plan, with the operator controlling who and what is present.

sources.developer: Hong Kong Highways Department / Hong Kong Productivity Council
sources.title: HKPC Smart Inventions Win Two Prizes at Hong Kong ICT Awards 2019
sources.claim: RoadBot 1, built by the Hong Kong Highways Department with HKPC, is a truck-mounted system whose cameras, LiDAR and sensor-fusion algorithm recognise cones/lanterns and compute placement positions, which robotic arms then execute, for placing and collecting cones on high-speed roads.

sources.title: Highways Department - Robot System for Placement and Collection of Traffic Cones and Warning Lanterns at High Speed Roads
sources.claim: The Highways Department describes Roadbot 1 as a prototype robot system with cameras, LiDAR and robot arms that understands its surroundings to place and collect traffic cones and warning lanterns on high-speed roads; Roadbot 2 upgrades it onto a road maintenance vehicle.

sources.system: Machine-vision automatic traffic cone placement and retraction system (improved YOLOv5)
sources.title: Application of Traffic Cone Target Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv5
sources.claim: A vehicle-mounted automatic traffic cone placement and ... guided by an improved YOLOv5 machine-vision pipeline placed and retrieved cones at 30 cones/minute with the carrier vehicle moving at 20 km/h in reported tests.

sources.title: AutoCone: An OmniDirectional Robot for Lane-Level Cone Placement
sources.claim: AutoCone is a fleet of low-cost omnidirectional robots carrying traffic delineators that drive themselves into position at lane-level precision using RTK GPS (2 cm minimum position error); a university research prototype tested on controlled ground rather than in highway service.

sources.system: Robotic Highway Safety Markers (robotic safety barrels)
sources.developer: Shen et al., University of Nebraska-Lincoln
sources.title: Are Work Zones and Connected Automated Vehicles Ready for a Harmonious Coexistence? A Scoping Review and Research Agenda
sources.claim: Robotic safety barrels that self-deploy and self-retrieve under a central localization station were developed and tested for work zones, with maximum final positioning error of 11 cm; a research system, never commercialised.

sources.title: Falcon 100 Automated Cone Laying Machine (ACLM)
sources.claim: The Falcon 100 Automated Cone Laying ..., approved by National Highways and in production since 2022 for the UK strategic road network, mechanically lifts, places and retrieves cones from a human-driven truck, removing operatives from the truck bed.

sources.title: Falcon 75 Automated Cone Laying Machine (ACLM)
sources.claim: The Falcon ACLM family is operator-run: cone laying, spacing and taper mode are commanded from a touch-screen in the cab of a driver-operated vehicle and monitored on cameras, so the machine is an operator-controlled attachment rather than an autonomous robot.

sources.system: AHMCT Cone Machine / Traf-tech automated cone machine
sources.developer: AHMCT Research Center, UC Davis / Caltrans
sources.title: Cone Machine Overview | Advanced Highway Maintenance and Construction Technology
sources.claim: The Caltrans/AHMCT automated cone machine, commercialised by Traf-tech, places and retrieves lane-closure cones but every operation is commanded by a human inside the cab of the cone truck.

sources.title: Kratos Defense Self-Driving Trucks are on the Road Across the United States, Increasing Worker Safety and Addressing Workforce Shortfalls
sources.claim: Kratos' Autonomous Truck-Mounted Attenuator is a driverless follower truck deployed with several US state DOTs in live highway work zones; it demonstrates unmanned vehicle movement in work zones but performs no cone or sign handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (driverless shadow-vehicle operation in live highway work zones): shows autonomous driving in the same environment, but the system handles no cones or signs, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

tasks.label: Flag motorists to warn them of obstacles or repair work ahead.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: One-lane, two-way alternating traffic control on a rural or suburban two-lane public road while the crew does stationary work (pavement patching, culvert, guardrail, tree removal) for a few hours in daylight: the worker stands at the end of the closure with a STOP/SLOW paddle, coordinates by radio with a flagger at the other end, and releases platoons alternately.

Moving/mobile maintenance operation on a public highway (sweeping, mowing, crack sealing, an advancing patch crew, striping): the worker warns and slows approaching motorists of the slow-moving work ahead, repositioning continuously as the operation advances, often from or beside a shadow/attenuator vehicle.

Holding traffic briefly so equipment enters, exits, backs, or crosses the travel lane (dump trucks entering the closed lane, loader backing, mower crossing the road): the worker reads the equipment operator's hand signals and machine movement and stops or releases traffic on demand.

Flagging on an urban or suburban street at or near an intersection or along a stretch with many driveways and side streets: turning vehicles, pedestrians and cyclists, buses, interaction with adjacent signals, and drivers needing individual hand direction.

Emergency and adverse-condition flagging: crash scene, downed tree or wires, washout, rockfall, snow/ice or night operations; the layout is improvised, emergency vehicles and tow trucks arrive, and motorists are directed around an obstacle or into a detour.

sources.system: Portable/temporary traffic control signals (trailer- and pedestal-mounted, auto mode)
sources.developer: Multiple vendors (North America Traffic, Horizon Signal, Ver-Mac); guidance issued by NCDOT
sources.title: 2023 CAPA/NCDOT Workshop - Work Zone Traffic Control Update
sources.claim: State DOT work-zone traffic control guidance states that portable (temporary) traffic signals can replace flaggers on ... one-lane, two-way operations and may be left unattended running in automatic mode.

sources.title: TxDOT Portable Traffic Signals Help Improve Safety - Work Zone Safety Information Clearinghouse
sources.claim: TxDOT deploys portable traffic signals in maintenance work zones specifically to remove flaggers from one-lane operations, cutting the crew from two flaggers plus a pilot car driver to the pilot car driver alone.

sources.title: PTL2.4x - North America Traffic
sources.claim: Commercial portable traffic signal trailers run actuated, detection-driven control (radar/microwave vehicle detection to 2,000 ft) and can be networked in multi-trailer setups covering work zones with many intersecting driveways and side roads.

sources.system: Temporary traffic control signal (MUTCD Section 6E.05 method)
sources.developer: FHWA (national standard); equipment from PTS vendors
sources.title: Chapter 6E One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Control (MUTCD)
sources.claim: The MUTCD lists the temporary traffic control signal method as an accepted alternative to the flagger method for one-lane, two-way TTC zones, so unattended signal control is an output road agencies accept in place of a flagger.

sources.system: AFAD (Wanco AFAD, North America Traffic RCF2.4, Site 20/20 Guardian SmartFlagger)
sources.title: Automated Flagger Assistance Devices - General (MUTCD)
sources.claim: Automated Flagger Assistance Devices, the machines marketed most directly as flagger substitutes, are remote-controlled: the MUTCD requires a trained flagger to operate each AFAD and forbids leaving it unattended, so AFAD evidence counts as teleoperated.

sources.title: Kratos Defense Self-Driving Trucks are on the Road Across the United States
sources.claim: Driverless leader-follower attenuator trucks are in fleet service on US public highways, running with no occupant behind mobile maintenance operations and carrying the arrow board and warning lights that alert approaching motorists to the work ahead.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile work-zone warning and protection. The follower truck travels driverless in live traffic behind a moving maintenance crew and presents the connected arrow board and warning display that warns motorists of the operation ahead - the same warning function, the same public-highway environment, and no added precision requirement.

sources.title: FAQ - Frequently Asked Questions - Royal Truck & Equipment
sources.claim: The ATMA follower operates completely driverless when paired with a leader ... and carries a connected arrow board used to warn traffic around the mobile work zone.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task: this is the vehicle carrying the advance warning display for a moving highway maintenance operation, occupying the traffic-facing position from which the worker would otherwise warn approaching motorists.

sources.developer: Royal Truck & Equipment / Kratos, operated by Colorado DOT
sources.title: Colorado DOT Launches Autonomous Vehicles to Improve Worker Safety
sources.claim: Colorado DOT put a self-driving impact protection vehicle into live highway work zones, the first US agency to do so, and has continued deploying them; the vehicle runs in traffic without a driver.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warning and shielding traffic at a moving highway work operation on public roads; shows a state DOT accepting a driverless machine in the traffic-facing position a worker would otherwise hold.

sources.system: Residential Driveway Temporary Signal (RDTS) / Driveway Assistance Device
sources.developer: PTS vendors (Street Smart, Superior Traffic Services); standard adopted by WSDOT
sources.title: Traffic: Work zone traffic control (WZTC) - WSDOT
sources.claim: WSDOT's standard work-zone toolkit includes Residential Driveway Temporary Signals that automatically control driveway and side-road approaches inside a one-lane, two-way closure, a function otherwise assigned to a flagger.

tasks.label: Perform preventative maintenance on vehicles and heavy equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily pre-trip/post-trip service of an assigned dump/plow truck at the county or state maintenance yard: walk-around inspection, check and top off engine oil, coolant, hydraulic and DEF levels, check tires and lights, inspect plow hitch, hoses and spreader chain, fuel the truck and log defects.

Lubrication service on heavy equipment (front-end loader, motor grader, backhoe, boom mower, plow pivot points): locating and wiping dozens of grease fittings in varied positions, pumping grease with a hand gun, checking for blown seals and leaking hoses, in the shop bay or beside the machine in the yard.

Scheduled shop service on trucks and equipment: engine oil and filter change, air/fuel/hydraulic filter replacement, coolant and hydraulic fluid changes, battery and belt checks, performed by the crew in a maintenance garage bay with a lift or pit.

Servicing attachments and small equipment: changing plow cutting edges, swapping/sharpening mower blades, chainsaw chain and bar service, string trimmer and small-engine tune-up, cleaning spreader conveyors and spinners, done at the yard apron or shop floor with hand and power tools.

Post-storm washdown of plow trucks to remove road salt and debris for corrosion prevention, at the maintenance facility's wash bay: rinse cab, body, chassis and undercarriage, wash the plow and spreader before parking the unit.

sources.system: Fully automated DOT truck wash bays (Alaska, Delaware, New Jersey DOT installations; Westmatic / InterClean / Pseco automatic truck wash systems)
sources.developer: Clear Roads pooled fund / state DOTs; wash system vendors Westmatic, InterClean, Pseco
sources.title: Snowplow Truck Washing Practices: Synthesis Report (Clear Roads CR 16-S1)
sources.claim: Multiple state DOTs operate fully automated wash bays that wash snowplow trucks unattended in short cycles as part of corrosion-prevention maintenance; the report also documents commercial automatic truck wash vendors (Westmatic, InterClean, Pseco) used by agencies.
sources.transferJustification: Washing salt and debris off plow trucks is itself a preventative-maintenance step performed by highway maintenance crews; the automated bay performs the same washing on the same vehicles.

sources.system: InterClean drive-through and Ultra Gantry truck wash systems (municipal configuration)
sources.title: Gantry Wash Systems – Highly Customizable Wash Solutions / Municipal Vehicle Wash Systems
sources.claim: Commercially sold drive-through and rollover gantry automatic wash systems clean heavy municipal fleet vehicles, including chassis/undercarriage washing to remove salt and corrosive agents, with the vehicle driven through a fixed wash lane.

sources.title: SCOTT making ROBOFUEL refuelling system progress with AHS mining truck fleets – International Mining
sources.claim: A robotic arm with vision refuels mining haul trucks autonomously in a dedicated refuelling bay, in use at several mine sites including with an autonomous Komatsu 930E ....
sources.transferJustification: Refuelling is the closest deployed robotic analogue to fluid servicing of heavy equipment: it shows a robot can locate one standardized receiver on a truck in a fixed bay, but not open hoods, read dipsticks, change filters or grease fittings.

sources.system: Outrider System with TrailerConnect robotic arm
sources.title: The autonomous distribution yard just got safer – Commercial Carrier Journal
sources.claim: Autonomous yard trucks use a deep-learning-driven robotic arm to locate and connect/disconnect trailer air-brake and electric lines on unmodified trailers in commercial distribution yards.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the current state of autonomous manipulation on heavy trucks in a yard: a single, geometrically standardized coupling task, far narrower than a multi-point inspection, top-off and lubrication service.

sources.title: RoboTire Installs First Revolutionary Tire Changing System at Discount Tire – RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: A robotic cell installed in tire retail service bays removes and mounts wheels on passenger vehicles, deployed at Discount Tire and other retailers.
sources.transferJustification: Vehicle-service task in a purpose-built bay; it demonstrates robotic wheel service on passenger cars only, and does not cover fluid checks, filter changes, greasing, or heavy-truck components.

tasks.label: Drive trucks to transport crews and equipment to work sites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Crew truck run: worker drives a crew-cab pickup or 1-ton truck with 2-5 crew members, hand tools, cones and signs from the county/state maintenance yard out to a job location on public roads (patching, sign repair, litter/brush work), often a spot described by mile marker rather than an address; parks on the shoulder or in a lane closure, then shuttles the crew between several sites during the shift.

Materials haul: worker drives a tandem dump truck or flatbed loaded with hot mix, cold patch, aggregate, guardrail sections or a small roller from the yard/stockpile/asphalt plant to the work site on state highways and rural roads, then backs into position beside the crew or the paver and spots the load.

Towing equipment: worker tows a trailer carrying a mower, air compressor, arrow board, skid steer or attenuator to the site, including hitching at the yard, driving narrow two-lane roads with shoulders and low clearances, turning onto unpaved access/ramp areas, and backing the trailer into position to unload.

Repositioning within a mobile operation: worker drives the truck (shadow/TMA truck, material truck, or striping support truck) continuously forward along the live work zone at low speed as the crew advances, staying in the closed lane with public traffic passing in the adjacent lane.

Night, storm, and emergency callouts: worker drives crew and gear at night or in rain, snow, ice, fog or wind to crashes, downed trees, flooding or spot icing, on roads that may be snow-covered, unlit, partially blocked or without visible lane markings.

sources.developer: Kratos Defense (Unmanned Systems Division), with Royal Truck & Equipment
sources.title: Kratos Defense Autonomous Trucking Overview (Autonomous Trucking Conference presentation, UGPTI)
sources.claim: Kratos' Autonomous Truck-Mounted Attenuator is a driverless follower truck used in live highway maintenance work zones by state and federal DOT agencies; 18 systems are deployed nationwide and several operate with no person in the vehicle, following a human-driven lead truck as the mobile operation advances.

sources.title: Kratos Defense Self-Driving Trucks are on the Road Across the United States, Increasing Worker Safety and Addressing Workforce Shortfalls
sources.claim: Kratos self-driving trucks are deployed on US roads as shadow vehicles that replace human-operated TMA trucks in mobile highway maintenance operations, i.e. driving a maintenance truck along the work zone in place of a DOT driver.

sources.title: Cat® MineStar™ Command for hauling manages the autonomous ecosystem
sources.claim: Cat MineStar Command for hauling runs driverless heavy haul trucks commercially at mine sites across three continents, hauling material over unpaved site haul roads to loading and dump points; more than 8.6 billion tonnes moved autonomously with no reported injuries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hauling materials by truck between points inside an institution-controlled industrial site. It transfers to driving a dump/flatbed truck of material and equipment to a work location: same vehicle class, same load-haul-position-dump cycle, mixed light-vehicle traffic, unpaved roads.

sources.title: The Future of Canadian Mining is Autonomous — and Suncor is Leading the Way
sources.claim: Suncor operates roughly 120 driverless ultra-class haul trucks at its Base Plant mine near Fort McMurray, Alberta; all ore is now moved by autonomous trucks that run around the clock, with performance validated on varied pit and road configurations and ... (including Alberta winters).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: night and winter truck haulage inside a controlled site. Transfers to night/adverse-weather truck driving to a work location within a structured facility: same heavy trucks, snow and darkness, varying road surfaces, 24/7 operation.

sources.title: The autonomous distribution yard just got safer | Commercial Carrier Journal
sources.claim: Outrider's driverless yard trucks maneuver tractor-trailers with precision in mixed-traffic logistics yards, including coupling trailers and spotting them at docks; the company has executed hundreds of thousands ... and its safety approach was assessed against TÜV SÜD's AV conformity framework.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless towing, hitching and reverse-positioning of a trailer inside a facility. Transfers to towing equipment trailers and backing a truck into position at a job spot: same articulated-vehicle control, similar tight maneuvering around people.

sources.title: Aurora Triples Driverless Network to 10 Routes and Prepares to Expand Across U.S. Sun Belt
sources.claim: Aurora runs driverless Class 8 trucks commercially on public highways and surface streets across a Sun Belt network of ten pre-mapped routes between fixed terminals and customer endpoints, with about 250,000 driverless miles as of ...; new customer facilities are served first with a supervising person aboard, and weather constrained driverless operations about 40% of the time in 2025.

sources.title: Waymo crosses 450,000 weekly paid rides as Alphabet robotaxi unit widens lead on Tesla
sources.claim: Waymo operates a fully driverless commercial ride-hailing service carrying passengers on public roads at large scale (over 450,000 paid rides per week as of December 2025), showing that driverless vehicles can transport people, not just freight.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless transport of human passengers to a destination. Transfers to the crew-carrying element of this task (people riding in the vehicle to a work location), though in a mapped geofenced service area rather than to arbitrary roadside sites.

sources.title: Taking riders further, safely with freeways (Waymo blog)
sources.claim: Waymo began carrying passengers on freeways in the San Francisco Bay ... in November 2025, extending driverless passenger transport to higher-speed limited-access highways.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless highway driving with people aboard, relevant to the highway leg of crew transport; still confined to mapped metro geofences with designated stops.

sources.developer: Kodiak AI (Kodiak Robotics) / Atlas Energy Solutions
sources.title: Kodiak AI Delivers First Customer-Owned Driverless RoboTrucks to Atlas
sources.claim: Kodiak-equipped driverless trucks owned by Atlas Energy Solutions haul proppant commercially without a human aboard on private industrial roads across the Permian Basin, including unpaved desert lease roads to well sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless heavy-truck delivery of bulk material to industrial work sites on private, operator-controlled roads. Transfers to hauling materials/equipment to a job site inside a controlled facility (E2), not to arbitrary public-road destinations.

tasks.label: Erect, install, or repair guardrails, road shoulders, berms, highway markers, warning signals, and highway lighting, using hand tools and power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Crash-damage guardrail repair on a highway shoulder: set up traffic control, cut/unbolt bent W-beam panels, pull damaged and corroded posts and blockouts, drive replacement posts on a sloped, variable-soil roadside, splice and torque new rail to grade and line, backfill.

Install or replace roadside signs, delineator posts and mile markers on rural or urban roadsides: locate position, auger or drive the post (sometimes in rocky or root-filled soil, sometimes in a base plate), bolt on the panel, plumb and align it, next to live traffic.

Bulk shoulder or berm restoration with equipment on a closed or lightly trafficked section: aggregate dumped along the shoulder, then bladed/graded to profile and cross-slope, compacted; rebuilding an eroded earth berm or drainage windrow.

Spot shoulder/berm repair with hand tools and small power tools in tight quarters: filling an edge drop-off around guardrail posts, culvert headwalls, mailboxes and inlets, shoveling, raking, tamping with a plate compactor, immediately adjacent to live traffic.

Install or repair warning signals and warning devices: solar-powered flashing beacons, warning-sign assemblies, barricades and advance-warning devices; unbolt failed unit, mount bracket and device on post or mast, connect the supplied leads/panel, verify operation.

Highway lighting repair: from a bucket truck at an interchange, on a mast arm or in a tunnel, diagnose an outage (fuse in pole base, photocell, driver/lamp, damaged conductor), replace the luminaire or component, re-terminate wiring, restore and test the circuit.

sources.title: Built Robotics develops automated pile driver for large-scale solar construction
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 is a fully ... surveys, distributes, drives and inspects steel piles to tight tolerance at utility-scale solar construction sites, sold commercially with a two-person crew.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving foundation piles. Guardrail line posts and sign/delineator posts are the same class of operation — driving a steel post to a surveyed position, depth and plumb tolerance — so the post-setting portion of guardrail and marker work transfers, though the machine does no rail or panel attachment.

sources.title: Built Robotics releases 1st fully autonomous construction machinery in US
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem turns standard excavators into machines that autonomously dig trenches and grade building pads on ordinary construction sites, available commercially to contractors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous earthmoving/grading to a design surface. Shoulder and berm restoration is the same operation — moving and shaping granular material to a specified profile — on comparable open, unfixtured ground.

sources.system: XCMG unmanned road construction fleet (autonomous rollers and pavers)
sources.title: XCMG robots complete highway project - Construction Briefing
sources.claim: XCMG operated a fleet of ten unmanned tandem rollers and two unmanned wide pavers, guided by a BeiDou reference station, to complete a resurfacing/maintenance project on a section of the ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unmanned paving and compaction inside a highway maintenance work zone. It shows GNSS-guided machines finishing a surface to profile in a real highway corridor, the same class of machine work as bulk shoulder/berm rebuilding.

sources.system: Universal Robots screwdriving cells (UR cobots with screwdriving end-effectors)
sources.title: Screwdriving Automation: industrial cobots deliver precise and repeatable automotive fastening – Universal Robots
sources.claim: Robotic screwdriving stations are a standard commercial capability in automotive assembly, with the robot guiding a driver to each fastening point at controlled torque in a fixtured workstation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: torque-controlled bolted assembly of rigid parts held in fixtures. Bolting a W-beam panel to posts, or a sign panel to a u-channel post, is the same bolt-pattern fastening operation once the parts are presented and held.

sources.system: National Sustainable Robotic Centre disassembly cell (KUKA KR500/KR20 with nutrunner, ITRA + visual servoing)
sources.title: Electric Vehicle Battery Disassembly Using Interfacing Toolbox for Robotic Arms
sources.claim: A robotic disassembly facility uses heavy-duty KUKA KR500 arms to lift and manipulate EV battery packs and a rail-mounted KR20 with a nutrunner to automatically unbolt fasteners, using visual servoing to locate them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated unbolting and removal of heavy bolted components in a fixtured cell. Removing damaged guardrail panels and blockouts is the same operation — locating and backing out bolts, then lifting a heavy rigid part clear.

sources.developer: RoadPrintz Inc. / Case Western Reserve University
sources.title: Revolutionizing road safety: RoadPrintz puts groundbreaking robotic pavement-marking system to use across Cleveland
sources.claim: RoadPrintz fielded a truck-mounted robotic arm that paints detail pavement markings on public streets in Cleveland, but the road worker directs the robot from inside the truck rather than the system running unattended.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic marking work on public roads. Included to show the closest fielded roadside manipulator; it is operator-directed and paints markings rather than erecting hardware, so it does not substantiate any positive judgment here.

tasks.label: Clean and clear debris from culverts, catch basins, drop inlets, ditches, and other drain structures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled catch-basin/curb-inlet cleaning on urban and suburban streets: crew sets cones in a live travel or parking lane, lifts the cast-iron grate, works a vac-truck hose into the sump to pull out grit, gravel, leaves and litter (often with standing water), rakes out what the hose misses, reseats the grate, and hauls the spoil to a decant site.

Post-storm and seasonal clearing of matted leaves, litter, sticks and ice from grates, curb-inlet throats, drop-inlet openings and culvert headwalls along roadsides, done by hand with rake, shovel and pitchfork, frequently during or right after rain with water flowing and traffic passing.

Cross-road culvert clearing on rural highways: removing silt, gravel, brush, beaver dams and other blockages from the pipe barrel and its inlet/outlet ends, using a jet/vac truck nozzle, hand tools, chainsaw and sometimes a mini-excavator on the embankment, with water flowing through.

Roadside ditch cleaning and reshaping with an excavator, backhoe or ditching machine to remove accumulated sediment and vegetation and restore the flowline grade, spoil loaded to a truck or spread on the shoulder; live traffic beside the work, driveway pipes, guardrail, mailboxes and buried utilities in the way.

Drainage structures inside institution-controlled facilities: airfield inlets and trench drains airside at an airport, plus inlets in maintenance yards, rest areas, tunnels and pump-station wet wells, cleaned on a scheduled maintenance visit with controlled access and a fixed, mapped layout.

sources.system: Ovivo Brackett Bosker Automatic Raking Machine (automatic trash rake)
sources.date: 2025-11 (product page last modified); product line long in service
sources.title: Brackett Bosker® Automatic Trash Rake | Ovivo
sources.claim: Brackett Bosker automatic raking machines are commercial, fully automated debris-removal machines for water intakes: triggered by timer or level signal, the machine travels to the screen, lowers a gripper, collects accumulated debris and discharges it into a skip or trailer without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic removal of leaves, sticks and litter caught on an intake bar screen. It transfers to clearing debris from drain grates and inlets because the objects (matted leaves, branches, litter), the action (grab material off a grating, lift it clear, discharge into a container) and the precision required are the same; the difference is that the structure is purpose-built around the machine, which is exactly the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: AERODREDGE Grit and Grease Removal System
sources.title: Aerated Wastewater Grit and Grease Removal System | Veolia
sources.claim: The AERODREDGE grit and grease removal system is a commercially sold, automated machine that collects settled grit and sand out of a purpose-built grit tank and pumps it away, requiring little attention from plant personnel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated removal of settled grit, sand and sludge from a fixed settling/drainage basin. It transfers to emptying a catch-basin sump because the material (waterlogged grit, sand, sludge) and the operation (move the accumulated solids out of a basin sump and convey them away) match; it is demonstrated only where the basin is purpose-built around the machine.

sources.title: The World’s First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofit turns a standard excavator into a fully autonomous trenching robot that digs to a planned line and depth within 0.1 ft on outdoor jobsites, working unattended shifts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous excavation of a trench to a specified line and grade. It transfers to ditch cleaning/reshaping because the machine, the spoil material and the grade tolerance are comparable, but only where the dig plan is laid out and the work zone is cleared and geofenced for the machine — not on a live-traffic roadside with unmapped driveway pipes and utilities.

sources.title: Built Robotics raises $64 million for robotic excavator Exosystem | Equipment World
sources.claim: Trade press reports Built Robotics as among the first to commercially ... excavator systems, with the Exosystem converting excavators into autonomous trenching robots.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the Built Robotics product page: it establishes that autonomous excavation to plan is a fielded commercial capability, which is what ditch excavation would need in a machine-prepared work zone.

sources.title: Bandicoot Robot, Human Centered Robotic Innovation for Global Urban Sanitation
sources.claim: Bandicoot manhole-cleaning robots are widely fielded in Indian cities to clear sludge and debris out of manholes, but the machine is lowered in and its arms are worked from an operator's control station rather than running autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Closest fielded system for cleaning debris out of a street drainage structure; autonomy is unclear/operator-driven, so under the rules it cannot support a positive judgment, which is why the street and culvert instances get no credit above the purpose-built counterfactual.

sources.system: RedZone Solo autonomous pipeline inspection robot

tasks.label: Drive heavy equipment and vehicles with adjustable attachments to sweep debris from paved surfaces, mow grass and weeds, remove snow and ice, and spread salt and sand.

Growing-season roadside mowing: tractor with flex-wing, flail or boom mower cutting grass and weeds on shoulders, medians, foreslopes/backslopes, ditches and around guardrail, signs, culverts and delineators; uneven terrain, hidden rocks/litter/animals in tall grass, and live traffic feet away.

Street/curb sweeping of municipal and low-speed paved surfaces with a mechanical-broom or regenerative-air sweeper: spring sand cleanup, leaf and debris runs, curb lines, intersections, bike lanes and park-and-ride lots, working around parked cars, pedestrians and cyclists on a mapped route.

High-speed sweeping of freeway shoulders, ramps, gore areas and bridge decks in live traffic, typically behind a shadow/attenuator truck, clearing sand, gravel, tire debris and crash litter at highway speeds.

Winter clearing at agency-controlled facilities: plowing and salting DOT maintenance yards, salt shed aprons, rest areas, weigh stations, park-and-rides and their walkways with a pickup/loader plow and small spreader; fixed known layouts, controlled access, limited public traffic.

Airport airside work under the same job family: sweeping and plowing runways, taxiways and aprons, blowing/brushing residual snow and mowing airfield grass, on an operator-controlled field with mapped geometry, controlled access and movement coordinated with operations.

tasks.label: Haul and spread sand, gravel, and clay to fill washouts and repair road shoulders.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Linear shoulder repair on a paved rural two-lane highway: crew hauls a dump-truck load of crushed gravel from the maintenance yard stockpile, spreads it along a low or eroded shoulder edge (tailgate spreading while creeping forward), then shapes it flush with the pavement edge with a grader/box blade and compacts it; cones and a flagger, live traffic passing at speed, mailboxes, delineators and drop-offs along the run.

Post-storm washout repair off the pavement: an erosion gully at the road edge, ditch line, culvert outlet or embankment slope. Worker hauls several loads of gravel/rock/clay, dumps into the void, and rebuilds the irregular eroded geometry with a loader/backhoe/skid steer plus shovel work; soft, wet ground, uneven slope access, geometry judged on the spot.

Unpaved/gravel road maintenance on county or rural roads: haul and spread gravel to fill ruts, washboard and washouts and restore the crown, blading the surface with a motor grader and compacting; road open to occasional local traffic, no fixed layout, dust and soft spots.

Small hand spot repairs: shovelling sand, gravel or clay from the truck bed into shoulder drop-offs and washed-out pockets at guardrail posts, driveway aprons, mailbox turnouts, sign bases and bridge approaches; small volumes, tight obstacle-rich spaces, raked and hand-tamped, done close to live traffic.

Work on institution-controlled closed premises: filling washouts and repairing gravel shoulders/edges on a DOT maintenance yard, rest-area or park-and-ride lot, or an airport service road/runway shoulder — loading at a fixed stockpile, hauling within the site, dumping and spreading to grade with a loader or grader, no public traffic present.

tasks.label: Inspect, clean, and repair drainage systems, bridges, tunnels, and other structures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine cleaning of catch basins, drop inlets, grates and culvert inlets/outlets along a highway shoulder: lifting grates, raking and shoveling out leaves, trash and sediment, vac-truck hose work, restoring flow, under cones/traffic control in all weather.

Cleaning and reshaping roadside ditches and swales over long open runs with an excavator, gradall or grader: cutting out accumulated silt and vegetation to restore the flow-line grade, casting or loading spoil, within a coned-off work zone.

Internal condition inspection of cross culverts and storm-drain pipes (push camera, crawler, or entry) to find blockage, silting, joint separation, corrosion or collapse, with findings documented for follow-up repair.

Bridge cleaning during a lane closure: sweeping/washing the deck, flushing or rodding scuppers and deck drains, blowing and vacuuming dirt and debris out of expansion joints, bearing seats and behind abutments, clearing brush at abutments.

Minor repairs to structures: patching spalled concrete on decks, curbs, headwalls and parapets, sealing joints and cracks, replacing broken grates, frames and railing, repairing culvert ends and washed-out riprap/erosion at inlets.

Routine visual condition inspection and documentation of bridges and tunnels and their drainage: checking decks, girders, undersides, joints, bearings and liners for spalls, cracks, corrosion and leaks, and reporting to engineers.

sources.title: Trenchless Technology Game Changers: RedZone Robotics
sources.claim: RedZone Robotics' SOLO is a commercially available, untethered autonomous robot that drives itself through sewer lines collecting video/laser/sonar data without an operator present, replacing CCTV crawler trucks.

Highway culvert/storm-drain inspection uses the same objects (buried concrete/metal pipe with silt and debris), the same deliverable (geo-referenced video/defect coding) and the same found, uncontrolled underground setting.

tasks.label: Remove litter and debris from roadways, including debris from rock and mud slides.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine hand litter pickup along the right-of-way: crew walks shoulders, ditches, medians, interchange grass and fence lines with grabbers and bags, collecting bottles, cans, cups, fast-food packaging, plastic bags, cardboard, tire fragments and small blown debris on uneven, sloped, vegetated ground while traffic passes at speed.

Mechanical sweeping of lower-speed municipal, rural and local roads, curb lines, gutters and parking areas: operator drives a broom/vacuum sweeper to remove winter sand, gravel, leaves, glass and small litter, working at low speed among parked cars, pedestrians and driveways.

Mechanical sweeping of freeway travel lanes, shoulders, gore areas and bridge decks under live high-speed traffic, typically with a shadow/attenuator truck and lane closure, removing sand, gravel, glass and crash debris along miles of high-speed roadway.

Dispatched response to a reported hazard in a live travel lane: drive to the location, deploy cones/arrow board or truck-mounted attenuator, then drag or lift a shredded truck tire, mattress, ladder, lumber, appliance, crash debris or dead animal off the pavement into the truck and clear the scene quickly.

Post-storm clearing of rock or mud slide debris: heavy equipment (loader, excavator, dozer, dump trucks) removes boulders, soil, mud and downed trees from the roadway and ditch, working below an unstable cut slope, often at night or in rain, finishing by grading and sweeping the pavement clean before reopening lanes.

Clearing accumulated debris from drainage features and structures: pulling matted leaves, branches, sediment and trash from culvert inlets, catch basin grates, ditches, bridge scuppers and guardrail bases, by hand tools or vacuum truck, on roadside slopes.

sources.title: Product – Angsa Robotics
sources.claim: Angsa Robotics' autonomous outdoor trash-picking robot removes litter from grass, gravel and paved public spaces, but its vacuum-based pickup is limited to small items; collection of larger packaging is still only being tested.

sources.title: AMP's Horowitz on Bringing AI to the Recycling World

sources.claim: Sandvik's AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 gives underground mine loaders fully automated production cycles — autonomously filling the bucket from broken rock at a drawpoint, tramming and dumping — without operator intervention at the loading point.
