tasks.label: Dump, spread, and tamp asphalt, using pneumatic tampers, to repair joints and patch broken pavement.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Municipal/urban street pothole patching: two- or three-person crew works from a dump truck or hot-box on a city street with traffic passing behind cones; workers clean loose debris from an irregular, often damp pothole, shovel cold-mix or hot-mix in, rake/lute it level with the surrounding surface, and compact it with a hand tamper, vibratory plate, or by rolling truck tires over it; several dozen holes per shift at scattered locations.

State highway / rural route patching under a mobile or short-term lane closure with a truck-mounted attenuator: hot mix delivered from a patch truck onto a blown-out wheel-path pothole or raveled edge, spread by shovel and rake, compacted with a jumping-jack rammer or plate compactor, edges sealed; high-speed traffic in the adjacent lane, variable weather and pavement condition.

Square-cut / full-depth patch and utility-cut or trench restoration: saw-cut and remove broken pavement, clean and tack the cut, place asphalt in lifts, and tamp each lift with a pneumatic tamper tight against vertical edges, curbs, gutter lips, and manhole or valve castings in confined geometry; finish flush with existing surface.

Joint repair work: patching failed longitudinal lane joints, transverse joints, and bridge-approach/expansion joint headers; asphalt dumped into narrow linear voids, spread by hand, and tamped hard against joint edges, armoring, or bridge rails, frequently at night on a closed lane.

Larger deteriorated section repair (mill-and-fill patch, ramp or shoulder strip) during a full lane closure: hot mix dumped from trucks and spread with a mini-paver or skid steer, compacted with a small roller, with hand tamping at the perimeter, tie-ins, and against the existing pavement edge.

Patching on institution-controlled paved areas with no public traffic: airport apron/taxiway shoulders, DOT maintenance yards, port or campus service roads; access controlled, work in scheduled night windows, but pavement defects still taken as found.

sources.system: ARRES PREVENT (Robotiz3d / University of Liverpool / Hertfordshire County Council)
sources.title: UK Council deploys alien truck-like world's first pothole-fixing robot
sources.claim: Robotiz3d's ARRES PREVENT, an autonomous road-maintenance vehicle, completed its first out-of-lab trial on public roads in Potters Bar, Hertfordshire, where it detected defects and sealed cracks; it seals cracks with sealant and does not dump, spread or tamp asphalt patch material.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous crack sealing on public roads) is the closest fielded robotic road-repair capability; it is cited to show the state of the art stops short of dumping, spreading and tamping asphalt patch material.

sources.title: Robots Can Now Find And Repair Even The Biggest Potholes - BGR
sources.claim: As of February 2026 the ARRES Ultra machine — the member of the Robotiz3d line intended to actually repair fully formed potholes (site preparation, filling, compacting) — remained in development; no autonomous full pothole-repair robot was in service in the US.

sources.system: ARRES Eye / ARRES Prevent / ARRES Ultra
sources.title: Robotiz3d Technology Ltd | Top Road Maintenance Technology Services in UK 2026
sources.claim: A June 2026 trade profile of Robotiz3d again describes ARRES Eye as a survey platform and ARRES Prevent as a crack-sealing robot, with the pothole-repair platform ARRES Ultra still described as developing.
sources.transferJustification: Confirms currency as of mid-2026 that the fielded robotic capability is crack sealing, not asphalt patching.

sources.system: InfraROB pothole-repair robot (Sapienza University of Rome et al.)
sources.developer: InfraROB consortium / Sapienza University of Rome
sources.title: A Small Robot to Repair Asphalt Road Potholes (Infrastructures 9(11):210)
sources.claim: The Horizon 2020 InfraROB project built a small autonomous carrier with a 3D printer that navigates to mapped potholes and extrudes a cold-asphalt mixture; its tank holds about 5 kg, enough for 3-4 very small potholes (about 2 cm deep, 20 cm wide) per mission, and it was tested on Italy's A24 motorway as a research prototype.

sources.system: Automated pothole filling machine (modified 3D printer with digitally designed asphalt cartridges)
sources.developer: academic研究 group publishing in Construction Robotics (Springer)
sources.title: Automating the repair of potholes using machine techniques and digitally crafted asphalt cartridges
sources.claim: A laboratory study of an automated pothole-filling machine (a modified 3D printer extruding asphalt cartridges) found the machine-made fills performed below hand-made fills in rutting resistance, i.e. below the quality of manual patching even under controlled conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (machine placement of asphalt into potholes) under maximally controlled, purpose-built conditions; cited to show worker-quality output is not yet reached even at E1.

sources.system: XCMG unmanned paving fleet (autonomous pavers + tandem rollers, BeiDou-guided)
sources.title: XCMG deploys driverless rollers, pavers on highway project | Equipment World
sources.claim: XCMG deployed a fleet of autonomous tandem rollers and unmanned wide pavers on a resurfacing project on the Nanjing-Shanghai Expressway, spreading and compacting asphalt at full-lane scale under satellite positioning and remote monitoring.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous spreading and compaction of asphalt on a highway) shows machine-scale mat laying is fielded, but the geometry is a continuous prepared lane, not irregular potholes, saw-cut patches, or hand tamping against joints and castings, so it does not transfer to this task.

tasks.label: Perform roadside landscaping work, such as clearing weeds and brush, and planting and trimming trees.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cyclical route mowing of grass and weeds on shoulders, medians and interchange turf along a state highway, using a tractor-mounted batwing or a riding/stand-on mower, working within a shoulder taper or lane closure with live traffic passing at speed.

Rough vegetation control on ditch lines, back slopes, fence lines and behind guardrail: tall weeds, briars and light woody brush cut with a flail, boom or slope mower on uneven, sometimes steep terrain littered with debris, culverts and sign stubs.

Hand vegetation work: string trimmer or brush saw around guardrail posts, sign posts, bridge ends, headwalls and delineators; hand weeding, edging and mulching of landscape beds at interchanges and rest areas; hauling cuttings and litter away.

Tree work in the right-of-way: pruning or removing limbs overhanging the travel lane or blocking signs/sight distance, felling small hazard or volunteer trees with a chainsaw, dragging brush to a chipper, clearing storm-downed limbs.
Chemical weed and brush control: backpack or truck-mounted spraying of herbicide along guardrail, pavement edges, around signs, posts and drainage structures on assigned road segments.
Planting and establishment work: setting out trees and shrubs, seeding or sodding slopes, mulching and watering new plantings on interchange and roadside landscaping projects.

sources.title: Autonomous Airfield Maintenance Is Moving Beyond the Pilot Phase | Aviation Pros
sources.claim: RC Mowers' autonomous mowing robots are in service cutting airfield turf at Sugar Land Regional Airport, running unattended overnight while the human crew worked elsewhere, under supervised autonomy (one supervisor overseeing several units).
sources.transferJustification: Same task class (large-area grass/weed mowing with commercial mowers) as roadside route mowing; the article reports the units operating in uneven terrain, at night and in inclement weather at airfield turf standards.

sources.system: RC Mowers Autonomous Mowing Robot / R Series
sources.title: Robotic Mowing Solutions | Robotic Mowers | RC Mowers
sources.claim: RC Mowers sells Autonomous Mowing Robots to public agencies and contractors for large grounds (sports fields, parks, airports, campuses); its roadside and slope machines are separately marketed as remote-operated rather than autonomous.

sources.developer: Scythe Robotics (acquired by Autonomous Solutions Inc. in 2026)
sources.title: Scythe Robotics debuts video series for M.52 autonomous mower onboarding - Lawn & Landscape
sources.claim: Scythe's M.52 autonomous commercial mower has been fielded with landscape contractors across 14 states on varied turf types and terrain.
sources.transferJustification: Commercial grounds mowing with a full-size zero-turn class machine: same cutting operation and accepted output standard as roadside turf mowing, performed on maintained commercial properties.

sources.title: Renu Robotics - Solar Power World
sources.claim: The Renubot is an autonomous electric vegetation-management vehicle working on utility-scale solar plants, mowing day or night including under panel rows, supervised from a remote mission control.
sources.transferJustification: Solar-site vegetation management is rough-terrain cutting of tall grass and weeds around fixed obstacles (piles, panel rows, fencing), comparable to ditch-line and fence-line rough mowing on a right-of-way.

sources.title: Renu Robotics | siliXcon
sources.claim: Renubot Generation 3 is described as a fully electric mowing robot that maps terrain with RTK GPS and lidar and operates completely autonomously on large solar farms.
sources.transferJustification: Corroborates the autonomy and cutting duty of the Renubot cited above for rough vegetation cutting inside a fenced, institution-controlled outdoor facility.

sources.title: Brief: SwarmFarm lands $8.3m to move autonomous farming beyond driverless tractors | AgFunderNews
sources.claim: SwarmFarm's autonomous SwarmBots operated commercially at scale, logging 64,000 hours across 1.3 million acres in one year performing spraying and other field operations.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous boom-sprayer herbicide application over defined ground is the same operation as banded/broadcast roadside herbicide spraying from a truck-mounted sprayer; the same platform also carries mowers and slashers.

sources.title: SwarmBot 5 | GOFAR - Agricultural Robotics
sources.claim: Over 120 commercial SwarmFarm robots run with full autonomy (obstacle detection, path planning) and have weeded, sprayed or mowed more than five million acres ..., carrying third-party mowers, slashers and sprayers.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous carrier running slashers/mowers and sprayers over broad ground transfers to rough vegetation mowing and herbicide application inside a controlled facility.

sources.system: ROWMow Sim / INDOT Autonomous Mower Project
sources.developer: Purdue University Evans Lab with Indiana DOT
sources.title: ROWMow Sim: Purdue and INDOT collaborate for safer highway mowing
sources.claim: INDOT and Purdue treat highway right-of-way mowing as fundamentally harder than existing autonomous mowing; their project built a digital-twin simulator to test autonomy before any deployment on actual highways, and the pilot phase concluded without fielded roadside autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about this task instance (roadside mowing); shows autonomous roadside mowing was still in simulation-based research rather than fielded operation.

sources.system: Autonomous Maintenance Technologies pooled fund study
sources.developer: INDOT with 11 partner state DOTs and Purdue University
sources.title: Funding Opportunity Announcement for Year 2025-2026 — Autonomous Maintenance Technologies
sources.claim: A 12-state DOT pooled-fund program led by INDOT was, as of December 2025, soliciting research to advance autonomous mowing capability for roadside vegetation management, including obstacle detection for debris and sign stubs hidden in tall grass.
sources.transferJustification: Same task; state DOTs treat autonomous roadside mowing and drone herbicide application as unsolved capability gaps rather than available deployments.

sources.developer: Electric Sheep Robotics (acquired by Oso Electric Equipment in 2025)
sources.title: Electric Sheep Verdie robot uses large world models for autonomous landscaping - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Electric Sheep announced Verdie, a robot intended to edge and trim lawns ... blow leaves; the source is a product debut with no independent evidence of autonomous, worker-quality field service.
sources.transferJustification: Closest published system to hand trimming and edging around fixtures; treated as non-supporting because autonomy in service and output quality are unverified.

sources.title: Continental and Land Life Advance Reforestation with Tree Seeding Robot - Continental AG
sources.claim: Continental and Land Life demonstrated an autonomous tree seeding robot that sows seed pits in difficult terrain at roughly 60 pits per hour — a reforestation seeding prototype, not installation of nursery stock.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest system to roadside planting; it sows seeds rather than installing trees and shrubs with mulch and watering, and remains a demonstrator, so it does not substantiate completion of the planting instance.

tasks.label: Apply poisons along roadsides and in animal burrows to eliminate unwanted roadside vegetation and rodents.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Broadcast/boom herbicide spraying from a truck-mounted sprayer along rural highway and interstate shoulders, ditch lines and fence lines: operator mixes and loads the tank, drives at low speed on the shoulder under traffic control, and runs booms/nozzles over uneven ground, cutting off near driveways, mailboxes and water bodies.

Spot treatment with a hose-reel handgun or backpack sprayer around roadside furniture: guardrail posts and rails, sign posts, delineators, culvert headwalls, bridge abutments, pavement edges and joints, working on foot on slopes next to live traffic.

Targeted treatment of noxious/invasive weed patches and woody brush regrowth on steep embankments, interchange slopes, ditch banks and drainage areas, often off pavement in rough vegetated terrain, with scattered patches that must be found and treated selectively.

Urban/suburban municipal street work: treating weeds in medians, curb lines, sidewalk and pavement cracks, and around street furniture, with pedestrians, parked cars and adjacent private property requiring careful drift control.

Weed control on institution-controlled paved facilities: bare-ground/pre-emergent treatment of airport runway and taxiway shoulders and pavement edges, maintenance yards, salt sheds, storage lots and rest areas, behind gates with no public traffic.

Rodent control: locating active ground squirrel, gopher or rat burrows in roadside embankments, slopes and under guardrails, then placing rodenticide bait pellets or fumigant cartridges down the burrow and closing the opening.

sources.title: Herbicide GUSS: Autonomous Sprayer Redefining Precision Weed Control in Orchards
sources.claim: Herbicide GUSS is a self-driving orchard/vineyard herbicide sprayer that operates with minimal human intervention, one operator supervising up to eight machines remotely.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying herbicide to unwanted vegetation along planted tree/vine rows. Same physical act (self-propelled ground sprayer dispensing herbicide onto ground vegetation over uneven outdoor terrain with fixed obstacles), differing only in setting, so it substantiates roadside-type herbicide application inside an institution-controlled facility.

sources.title: Herbicide GUSS: Autonomous Sprayer Redefining Precision Weed Control in Orchards
sources.claim: The same GUSS platform uses GPS/LiDAR navigation and weed-detection sensors to spot-spray herbicide only where weeds are present, around trunks and obstacles in rows.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sensor-targeted herbicide spot spraying around tree trunks, irrigation lines and posts in orchard rows — comparable objects (small ground weeds beside fixed vertical structures) and comparable precision to spot spraying at guardrail and sign posts.

sources.title: John Deere acquires GUSS Automation to expand autonomous spraying in vineyards and orchards
sources.claim: GUSS autonomous sprayers are deployed at commercial scale, with hundreds of machines and hundreds of thousands of logged autonomous spraying hours.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (autonomous herbicide/pesticide application on outdoor farm ground); this item establishes the autonomy is real, remotely supervised only, and operating at commercial reliability rather than as a demo.

sources.title: Solinftec's self-refilling spray robots close the loop on 24:7 autonomy on the farm
sources.claim: Solinftec's Solix solar-powered robots autonomously patrol open outdoor cropland and spot-spray individual weeds; over 300 units operate on farms globally.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unsupervised outdoor navigation plus targeted herbicide application to individual weed plants on open ground — the same chemical act and comparable targeting precision required for roadside spot treatment, on an institution-controlled outdoor property.

sources.system: Contract spray drone service (Ward County Weed Board)
sources.title: Drones become weed control tool - Minot Daily News
sources.claim: Roadside noxious-weed herbicide application by drone is being purchased by county road/weed agencies, but as a piloted contractor service rather than an autonomous machine.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same task (herbicide application on county road right-of-way), cited to show the state of the art on real roadsides: the aircraft is flown by a licensed applicator-pilot and no source establishes unattended autonomous operation.

sources.system: Spray drones for noxious weed management (Montana counties)
sources.title: Emerging Drone Technology for Noxious Weeds Management - Montana Weed Control Association
sources.claim: Spray drones are used for noxious weed treatment on steep slopes and hard-to-access terrain, operated by licensed drone applicator pilots.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (herbicide application to weed infestations on steep, rough ground); cited because it is the closest real-world unstructured-terrain evidence, but the source frames it around licensed pilots, so autonomy is not established.

sources.system: Greenzie Powered Autonomy (Wright, Bobcat, Mean Green mowers)
sources.title: Greenzie releases Version 5.0 software to advance commercial-ready autonomy
sources.claim: Greenzie-powered autonomous mowers operate commercially on institution-controlled grounds such as athletic fields, ..., campuses and warehouse sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous outdoor vegetation maintenance (mowing) on grounds an institution controls. It supports the navigation/coverage half of facility weed treatment — same terrain and obstacle class — while the chemical application itself rests on the GUSS and Solix evidence.

tasks.label: Measure and mark locations for installation of markers, using tape, string, or chalk.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Layout/pre-marking on a resurfaced or newly paved highway section: crew measures offsets from centerline/joints and chalks or spot-paints the line and marker positions over a mile or more of pavement, inside a coned-off work zone with live traffic in adjacent lanes.

Marking positions for raised pavement markers and delineators at standard spacing (e.g., every 40-80 ft on tangents, closer on curves) along a rural two-lane highway, using a measuring wheel/tape from a reference point and chalk or paint spots on pavement and paved shoulder.

Marking post locations for guide posts, snow poles, mile markers or small sign posts on a clear, mowed or graveled roadside shoulder: measuring station-to-station distances and offsets from edge of pavement, marking with chalk, paint or flags.

Same post-location layout but on rough roadside: steep fill slopes, ditches, brush and tall grass, behind or between guardrail runs, where the worker must scramble over uneven, obstructed ground to place each mark.

Ad hoc small job: one or a few replacement markers/signs after a knockdown. Worker measures from existing field features (curb, driveway, old post stub, culvert) to decide and mark the spot with chalk or tape, under live traffic, no plan data or coordinates available, whole job under 20 minutes.

Intersection detail layout in an urban street: measuring and stringing/chalking positions for crosswalk bars, stop bars, arrows and symbol markers off curb lines and centerlines, under flagged traffic control.
Airfield layout: measuring and pre-marking positions for runway/taxiway markings and marker/sign locations on an airport airfield closed to traffic and controlled by the airport authority.

sources.title: Large-Scale Highways Project in the UK Using Robotic Pre-marking - TinyMobileRobots
sources.claim: TinySurveyor Terra, an autonomous GNSS-guided pre-marking robot, performed 8 km of setting-out (pre-marking) for surface works on the live M6 motorway upgrade for road-marking contractor WJ Group, with operators supervising from a distance.
sources.transferJustification: Setting out / pre-marking on a highway is the same act as measuring and marking locations for installation: the robot lays the chalk/paint reference marks a crew would otherwise place with tape and string.

sources.title: VHS: Tiny Mobile Robot Stakeout - TinySurveyor - Utility Scoop
sources.claim: A US highway contractor (Austin Bridge & Road, Texas) has integrated the TinySurveyor into routine pre-marking, replacing a 3-person, 3-hour-per-mile manual measuring and marking process with roughly 20 minutes of robot work per mile.
sources.transferJustification: Contractor pre-marking of roadway layout is the same measuring-and-marking work highway maintenance crews do with tape and chalk; it is performed on the same public roadway surfaces.

sources.title: NEW Road Marking Robot - TinySurveyor Plotter | Aptella
sources.claim: The TinySurveyor Plotter road-marking robot stakes out up to 600 points ... at 2-3 cm accuracy from CSV/DXF files using GNSS or a robotic total station, and carries a safety beacon and ultrasound sensors so it can work in spaces with live traffic.
sources.transferJustification: Staking out discrete points is precisely 'marking locations for installation of markers'; the robot sprays a mark at each specified position instead of a worker taping and chalking it.

sources.title: Solar Park Installation and Stake-Out – 230 Points Per Hour | TinyMobileRobots
sources.claim: On a Danish solar park, a TinySurveyor autonomously marked out 115,000 discrete pile-installation points on open unpaved ground, averaging 230 points per hour, replacing manual end-point marking and tape-measure layout.
sources.transferJustification: Marking pile positions for installation on graded outdoor ground is the same operation as marking post/delineator locations along a roadside: discrete points, centimetre tolerance, unpaved surface.

sources.title: TinySurveyor Terra – TinyMobileRobots
sources.claim: The all-terrain TinySurveyor Terra is built to mark out points and lines on grass, gravel, dirt, sand, asphalt and concrete, taking jobs from CSV/DXF files sent from the operator tablet.

sources.title: Land Surveyors Complete Pre-marking 5 Times Faster Brisbane Airport, Australia - TinyMobileRobots
sources.claim: Surveyors used the TinySurveyor to pre-mark 50 km of line and stake-out work for the new runway at Brisbane Airport in five days, ahead of the marking crews; the vendor also documents recurring airport sign and marking pre-marking from airports' existing CAD data.

sources.title: TinyMobileRobots launches robot TinySurveyor | Global Highways
sources.claim: The TinySurveyor accepts road-layout coordinates (LandXML/CSV) and, where no digital data exists, can collect a few key points on site and generate the full layout itself, cutting layout work to about a third of the manual time.
sources.transferJustification: Maintenance layout often lacks CAD data; this documents that the marking robot can derive a spacing layout from a few field-captured reference points, as a crew does with a tape from a known reference.

tasks.label: Paint traffic control lines and place pavement traffic messages, by hand or using machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Long-line striping on rural/state highways and municipal arterials: repainting miles of centerline, edge line and skip lane line with a truck-mounted or ride-on striping machine (waterborne paint plus glass beads), running a moving operation behind traffic control with live traffic in the adjacent lane, matching the existing line and skip cycle.

Transverse intersection markings on public streets: crosswalk bars, stop bars, yield triangles and gore/channelizing lines laid out with tape measure and chalk and applied with a walk-behind striper or hand gun during a short-term lane or intersection closure, often with pedestrians and turning vehicles nearby.

Pavement legends and symbols on public roadways: turn arrows, 'ONLY', bike and HOV symbols, school-zone words, railroad crossing symbols, placed with stencils and hand-sprayed paint or preformed/hot-applied thermoplastic, positioned relative to existing lane geometry.

Striping of agency-controlled paved areas: park-and-ride and rest-area lots, maintenance yard and garage lots, weigh stations — stall lines, ADA stalls and symbols, fire lanes, arrows, stop bars — laid out from a plan on a lot closed or coned off for the work.

Temporary and spot markings in active work zones and after repairs: touching up or re-striping short segments over new patches or seal-coated areas, temporary lane delineation during staging, curb and object painting, frequently done at night under a lane closure and against a deadline to reopen the road.

Airfield markings at a publicly owned airport: runway centerline, threshold and designation numbers, taxiway centerlines and hold-position markings, painted to FAA layout tolerances with beads/sand during a scheduled runway or taxiway closure controlled by airport operations.

sources.title: STRIPING ROBOTS | 10Lines
sources.claim: 10Lines builds autonomous striping robots that apply pavement markings (lines, symbols) on paved surfaces including parking lots, roadways and airports, without pre-marking, using a digital layout.

sources.title: Joining the dots between space technology, autonomous robots and road safety (ESA Business Applications)
sources.claim: Independent ESA business-applications article describes 10Lines' autonomous road-marking robot for all paved surfaces, notes completed pilot projects in Estonia and first robots operating in the United States, and states that parking lots and airports are the current focus areas while highways remain a future expansion goal.

sources.system: 10Lines robot operated by Strike Force Striping
sources.title: Parking Lot Striping in Greenville, SC | Robotic — Strike Force Striping
sources.claim: A US striping contractor performs commercial parking-lot work with an autonomous 10Lines robot, covering restriping, new layouts, ADA marking, fire lanes, directional arrows, ... at standard 15-mil wet film, including night operations, with a 100-space lot completed in 2-3 hours.

sources.title: TinyLineMarker Pro X | Origin Amenity Solutions
sources.claim: TinyMobileRobots' TinyLineMarker Pro X is a commercially sold, GPS-guided line-marking robot that paints line markings autonomously on both asphalt and turf, including custom logos/text, and is used by councils and contractors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous paint line-marking of sports/amenity surfaces including asphalt, with centimetre-level GPS layout and custom text/logo printing. Same physical act (spray paint to a digital layout on a paved surface) and comparable precision to painting traffic lines and legends.

sources.title: Airport Signs, Markings, and Maintenance for Runways and Taxiways - TinyMobileRobots
sources.claim: TinyMobileRobots' TinySurveyor robot is used at airports to place runway and taxiway marking layout (numerals, letters, positions) working in automatic mode on the airfield; crews then fill the shapes with paint.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated layout/pre-marking of airfield markings, the measuring-and-spotting half of this task, performed autonomously on live airport pavement to marking tolerances; shows marking robots operate on airfield surfaces, though a crew still applies the final paint.

sources.system: RoadPrintz Electra (robotic detail pavement marking truck)
sources.developer: RoadPrintz Inc. / Case Western Reserve University
sources.title: Cleveland, Ohio, using new road painting robot truck Electra (Fox 8)
sources.claim: RoadPrintz's truck-mounted robotic arm paints detail markings (turn arrows, stop bars, 'BUS ONLY', bike symbols, crosswalks) on public streets in Cleveland and elsewhere, but the developer states the system is not autonomous: a human drives the truck and an operator specifies each marking and its placement.

sources.title: LifeMark-400 Product Page | LimnTech
sources.claim: The most advanced commercial highway long-line automation, LimnTech's LifeMark-400, is a vehicle-mounted auto-layout plus operator-assist re-striping system — the striping truck is still driven and supervised by a human operator.

tasks.label: Apply oil to road surfaces, using sprayers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chip seal / seal coat on a rural two-lane highway or county road: a distributor truck shoots hot asphalt emulsion across the lane at a specified rate (roughly 0.3 gal/sy) immediately ahead of a chip spreader and rollers, under flagger traffic control, with joint papering and start/stop lines, in variable weather.

Machine tack-coat application ahead of an asphalt overlay or large mill-and-fill on a highway, ramp or city street: distributor truck sprays a thin uniform emulsion film over the swept/milled lane in a coned-off work zone, timed so the paver follows before the tack is tracked or broken.

Dust-control oiling: repeated spray passes of oil, emulsion or liquid dust suppressant on unpaved gravel roads, unpaved shoulders and detour surfaces, loose application-rate tolerance, on open public rural roads with occasional traffic and driveways.

Hand-wand / spot spraying: worker drags a hose from the truck and sprays tack or oil on irregular small areas - pothole patches, utility cuts, milled edges, joints, around manholes, curb lines and bridge deck edges - judging coverage by eye while traffic passes.

Application on institution-controlled paved areas: fog seal, prime, tack or dust oil on airport service roads and aprons, DOT/municipal maintenance yards, park and facility parking lots and closed campus roads, with outside traffic excluded and a fixed known layout.

sources.system: Cat 789D Autonomous Water Truck (Cat Command / Cat Water Delivery System)
sources.title: New Cat 789D Autonomous Water Truck defeats dust and controls costs through automated water delivery
sources.claim: Caterpillar sells a fully autonomous mining water truck that drives haul routes and meters liquid onto road surfaces for dust control, integrated with the Cat Command autonomous fleet on active mine sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: spraying liquid (water/dust suppressant) onto a road surface from a truck-mounted tank and spray system. Same vehicle class, same action and same road-surface target as oiling a road; the truck both drives the route and controls liquid delivery without an operator.

sources.system: Autonomous water trucks (Caterpillar chassis, Rio Tinto Autonomous Haulage System)
sources.title: Rio Tinto to deploy world's first fully autonomous water trucks at Gudai-Darri
sources.claim: Rio Tinto deployed fully autonomous water trucks at the Gudai-Darri iron ore mine that sense conditions and apply water to site roads without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous application of liquid to road surfaces for dust control across a haul-road network - the same operation as oiling unpaved roads, including judging where and how much liquid to lay down, in an institution-controlled outdoor road setting.

sources.title: Videos - ASI Robots
sources.claim: ASI sells an OEM-agnostic autonomy product for water trucks that runs repeatable spray routes with precision control of the spray application for dust suppression at industrial sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unmanned truck-mounted spraying of liquid onto site roads with controlled application rate - the same driving-plus-metering problem as oiling a road from a distributor-style truck, minus the heated binder.

sources.system: XCMG unmanned road construction fleet (autonomous pavers and tandem rollers, BeiDou-guided)
sources.title: XCMG deploys driverless rollers, pavers on highway project
sources.claim: XCMG ran unmanned asphalt pavers and rollers on a maintenance job on a live Chinese expressway, with the fleet reported to meet thickness, compaction and friction requirements.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous application of asphalt material to a highway surface to specification inside a maintenance work zone. Shows driverless heavy road machines in a closed lane, but the machines are pavers/rollers at paving speed, not spray distributors, so it does not carry the spray application to E3.

sources.title: TinySurveyor Terra | TinyMobileRobots | Monsen Engineering
sources.claim: A commercially used GNSS line-marking robot drives itself along a planned path and sprays paint on pavement to centimetre accuracy; the same model was used for 8 km of pre-marking inside an M6 motorway upgrade work zone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile spraying of a liquid coating onto paved surfaces outdoors (road pre-marking, lots). Same target surface and spray mechanism, but thin lines rather than full-width coverage at a specified gallons-per-square-yard rate.

sources.title: Paint Robots & Paint Machines - Duerr
sources.claim: Robotic spray stations automatically apply liquid coatings to workpieces presented to them in enclosed paint booths, a standard industrial capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: programmed spray application of a uniform liquid film to a surface brought to the machine in a purpose-built booth - the E1 form of applying a sprayed coating to a presented surface.

sources.developer: Robotiz3d / University of Liverpool / Hertfordshire County Council
sources.title: Researchers deploy world's first pothole-fixing robot | GlobalSpec
sources.claim: An autonomous road-repair robot detected pavement defects and filled cracks during on-road trials in Hertfordshire, UK - a narrow crack-filling trial rather than surface oiling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous placement of bituminous material on a public road surface. Cited to show that the state of the art on public roads is a narrow crack-filling trial, not full-width binder application, so it does not substantiate E3 completion of this task.

tasks.label: Inspect markers to verify accurate installation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: After a crew or contractor installs roadside delineator posts, mile/route markers and object markers along a rural or suburban highway, the worker travels the segment (drive-and-stop or walk) and verifies each marker against the plan: spacing, offset from pavement edge, mounting height, plumb, and reflector facing; deficiencies are logged for correction. Live traffic, weather, gravel shoulders and vegetation.

Verification of newly installed raised/snowplowable pavement markers and lane reflectors in the travel lanes of a multilane highway: correct spacing and alignment with the stripe, seating/adhesion of the casting or epoxy pad, correct color and orientation, plus a night-time reflectivity check from a vehicle. Done in a lane closure or between traffic gaps.

Check of markers mounted on hardware after installation - guardrail delineators, curve chevrons, object markers on posts and barriers, hydrant/culvert markers at intersections: bolt tightness, post embedment and firmness (pushed by hand), correct height and facing to oncoming traffic; small misalignments are corrected on the spot with hand tools.

Verification of markers set off the pavement - snow poles, culvert and drainage markers, right-of-way and survey markers - located from plan sheets or GPS coordinates in ditches, embankments, soft shoulders and tall grass; worker confirms each is at the staked location, at correct height, and visible from the road.

Verification of marker installation inside an institution-controlled facility: airport runway/taxiway edge markers, reflectors and airfield delineation, or markers on an agency-controlled campus/maintenance road or a fully closed, traffic-controlled work zone, checked against a layout plan with access controlled by the operating authority.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot + Trimble X7 / FieldLink
sources.title: Trimble Releases Turnkey Autonomous Robotic Scanning Solution for Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot
sources.claim: Commercial turnkey solution in which Boston Dynamics' Spot autonomously follows a predefined waypoint path on jobsites carrying a Trimble X7 laser scanner, with scheduled repeat missions used for design validation (as-built vs. design) and progress reporting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated as-built capture and design validation on a jobsite. sources.title: Robotic inspection in Power & Utilities - ANYbotics

sources.system: Skydio X10 + Skydio Dock / Remote Ops

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous scheduled aerial inspection of infrastructure assets at controlled sites. tasks.label: Place and remove snow fences used to prevent the accumulation of drifting snow on highways.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Autumn installation of rolled snow fence (orange plastic mesh or wood-slat) on steel T-posts in the right-of-way or an adjacent field, 200-1,000 ft runs set back 30-100 ft from the pavement: crew lays out the line, pounds 6-ft T-posts ~8 ft apart with a hand or hydraulic driver, unrolls the fence from the truck, tensions it, ties it to each post with wire clips/zip ties, and sets ~1 ft of bottom ground clearance over uneven, sloping, vegetated ground.

Spring removal of the same fencing: cutting or untwisting every tie, walking the roll back up by hand or with a reel/winder, pulling each T-post with a hand puller or loader-mounted puller, bundling posts, loading rolls and posts onto a flatbed, and hauling to the shop yard for storage - all in soft, muddy spring ground with vegetation grown into the mesh.

Mid-winter repair and re-set of downed or buried fence sections: driving the route to find sections flattened by wind, drifted over, or knocked down by plows/deer; re-driving leaning posts into partially frozen ground, re-tying torn mesh or splicing in new fence, in cold, wind, snowpack and near live traffic.

Placing or removing fence on difficult ground: rocky or frozen soil requiring an auger or heavy driver, steep ditch backslopes, around culverts, guardrail and utility conflicts, or on private land behind gates (livestock present), with access limited to a pickup and hand tools.

Structural/semi-portable snow fence work (e.g., Wyoming-type tall wood-slat panels or bracket-frame sections): hauling prefabricated panels or frames on a flatbed, setting and anchoring them with a loader or telehandler along a windward line, bracing and pinning them, and disassembling/relocating sections at season's end.

sources.date: 2023-04 (launched 2023-03; customer deployments from Q4 2023, still marketed 2025-2026)

It transfers only for that sub-step; the RPD 35 handles no flexible fence material, no tying, and no removal, so it cannot deliver a completed, tensioned snow fence.

Transfer fails for snow fence because TyBot works only from a rail-mounted gantry over a flat, pre-placed rebar mat; it cannot handle a tensioned mesh roll, vertical T-post clipping, or untying during removal.

tasks.label: Blend compounds to form adhesive mixtures used for marker installation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Spot replacement of a handful of raised pavement markers on an active highway shoulder under lane-closure traffic control: worker opens pails/kits of two-part epoxy marker adhesive, proportions Part A and Part B, and blends them by hand or with a drill paddle in a bucket or on a mixing board, within a few minutes of pot life in whatever ambient/pavement temperature exists that day.

Production marker-installation run with a truck- or cart-mounted machine-mix epoxy system: worker loads/connects the Part A and Part B supply, brings both components to application temperature, sets and verifies the mix ratio, purges the static/dynamic mixer, and monitors the blended output (color, cure, yield) along the roadway as markers are set.

Hot-applied bituminous marker adhesive: worker loads blocks/kegs of bituminous compound into a melter kettle on a truck or push applicator at the work site, heats to roughly 350-400 F, runs the agitator until the material is uniform and free of lumps or char, and holds it at application consistency through the shift.

Preparation at the district maintenance yard or shop before the job: pre-heating and charging the bituminous melter, batching epoxy adhesive kits into working containers, or mixing two-part epoxy/anchoring grout for marker posts and delineators on a bench, with materials drawn from shop shelves and drums.

Small two-part anchoring adhesive/grout jobs at the roadside for markers, delineator posts and snowplowable marker castings: dual cartridges run through a static-mixer nozzle with a caulk gun, or a small hand-mixed batch of epoxy grout, sometimes in cold, wet or dusty conditions.

sources.claim: Production lines run two-component structural epoxy through a static or dynamic mixer mounted on a robot arm that combines Part A and Part ... a programmed ratio, with continuous ratio monitoring, automatic stop on off-ratio conditions, and programmed purge cycles of the mixer - machine-controlled blending of adhesive in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is structural 2K epoxy bonding in manufacturing. roles.title: Rail-Track Laying and Maintenance Equipment Operators
roles.description: Lay, repair, and maintain track for standard or narrow-gauge railroad equipment used in regular railroad service or in plant yards, quarries, sand and gravel pits, and mines. Includes ballast cleaning machine operators and railroad bed tamping machine operators.

tasks.label: Repair or adjust track switches, using wrenches and replacement parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Classification or industrial rail yard, routine turnout maintenance: worker inspects the switch, tightens loose switch-rod, headblock, gauge-plate and rail-brace bolts with track/impact wrenches, replaces broken cotter keys and bolts, adjusts the connecting rod so the point fits the stock rail within tolerance, and adjusts/lubricates the switch stand. Ballast footing, variable weather, yard traffic under railroad protection.

Mainline turnout in the field during a track-time window: replace a worn or broken switch point, gauge plate, rail brace or joint bars. Bolts are rusted or seized and often torch-cut, heavy steel parts are moved with bars and hoists, ties re-spiked and gauge reset, then point fit adjusted. Remote right-of-way, weather, tight possession time.

Emergency call-out: a switch will not line or the points will not close (bent or loose rod, sheared bolt, packed snow/ice or mud, derailment damage). Worker diagnoses the fault in the field, often at night in bad weather, and repairs it with wrenches and replacement parts to restore traffic quickly.

Power switch at a yard or terminal interlocking: adjust the switch machine throw rod, point-detector rods and basket/lug bolts with wrenches so the points close to the required gap standard, verified with gauges, coordinated with the signal maintainer and dispatcher.

Plant yard, mine or quarry track: hand-throw switch worn or fouled with spillage; replace bolts, switch rods, clips and small parts and readjust the throw with wrenches. Dirty and uneven conditions but on company-controlled premises with standard light-duty turnouts.

Turnout renewal or installation with a track gang: bolting up new switch components — switch rods, plates, braces and joint bars torqued to spec on a new or pre-assembled turnout panel — followed by final adjustment of point fit after installation.

sources.system: IAS Corp automated railroad turnout processing line (Yaskawa Motoman robots)
sources.title: Automated Production Lines - IAS Corp.
sources.claim: IAS Corp built a fully automated railroad turnout processing line using four Yaskawa Motoman robots that drills ties, handles and plates turnout tie plates and spikes them while holding gauge, with automated vision gauging of each finished tie, in a factory production cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fabricating turnout (switch) ties by fastening switch plates and spikes to gauge. Same objects (turnout plates, spikes/bolts) and the same gauge-critical precision as replacing and re-fastening switch components; it shows a purpose-built cell can do fastener-level turnout work autonomously when the work is conveyed and fixtured.

sources.system: Fori Automation robotic toe-set / wheel alignment system
sources.title: End of Line Testing Systems – Wheel Aligners, Headlamp Aimers, Robotic Toe Set & Automated Tooling Changeover
sources.claim: Fori Automation robotic end-of-line alignment cells use robots with nutrunner-driven socket gear heads to turn a threaded tie rod and set vehicle toe to +/-0.03 degrees, i.e. measure-and-adjust of a bolted linkage to a geometric spec inside a fixtured cell.

Adjusting a switch connecting rod so the point closes within a few millimetres is the same closed-loop measure-turn-remeasure operation on comparable threaded hardware in a fixtured setting.

sources.title: A Bavarian startup is automating Europe's track maintenance

sources.transferJustification: Related task: repair of worn switch components in a fixtured robot cell. Same workpieces (switch points, frogs, manganese castings) at the same scale, showing that when a turnout component is brought to the machine and fixtured, a robot can carry a switch repair through to an accepted output.

sources.developer: ROBEL Rail Automation GmbH with ProRail, Strukton Rail, VolkerRail
sources.title: A Bavarian startup is automating Europe's track maintenance
sources.claim: ROBEL's Robot welding platform, a container-mounted FANUC robot system on a rail wagon, scans, mills, preheats, welds and grinds rail and switch-frog defects end to end with one supervising operator; it is in trials on the Dutch network with provisional homologation for manganese switch ... and no confirmed deployment timeline.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-track repair of switch and rail defects. It is the most advanced field robot for switch repair and it performs only welding/machining from a rail-borne platform — it does no wrench work, fastener removal or component replacement, so it bounds what field (E2/E3) systems can do.

sources.system: Union Pacific robotic welding trucks (Cold Metal Transfer)

sources.claim: Union Pacific is using truck-mounted robotic welding to repair frogs, the switch component that guides cars through turnouts, in the field; crews position the robotic arm and activate it before the automated weld runs.

sources.system: Intelligent Maintenance Robot Platform for Railway Catenary
sources.title: China's First Intelligent Maintenance Robot Platform for Railway Catenary Was Launched on Shuohuang Railway
sources.claim: An intelligent catenary maintenance robot platform on China's Shuohuang Railway entered trial operation with multi-arm cooperative control that autonomously performs bolt fastening and geometric adjustments on overhead line equipment, replacing about 40% of manual maintenance operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous bolt fastening and dimensional adjustment of railway infrastructure hardware from a rail vehicle. Nearest field (E2) analogue to switch adjustment, but it covers only standardized overhead fittings presented at arm height and replaces a fraction of manual work, so it does not carry a whole switch repair.

sources.title: RoboTire's tire-changer aims to evolve service bay
sources.claim: RoboTire's vision-guided twin robotic arms remove wheel lug nuts, take off the wheel assembly and reinstall it torqued to spec in a tire service bay after an operator initiates the cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided unbolting, component swap and torque-to-spec re-bolting of a heavy part on a vehicle positioned at a fixed station. Supports the fastener-removal/replacement element of switch repair when the workpiece is presented in a known position, though on clean, standard fasteners.

tasks.label: Patrol assigned track sections so that damaged or broken track can be located and reported.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine periodic patrol of Class I/regional mainline and controlled sidings: inspector drives a hi-rail truck at 5-25 mph over an assigned 40-100 mile territory (FRA-required twice-weekly inspection), watching for broken rails, cracked joint bars, missing fasteners, defective ties and gauge/alignment deviations, and reporting or protecting defects found.

Patrol of yard, terminal and industrial-lead tracks: on foot or in slow hi-rail among stored and moving cars, close inspection of switch points, frogs, guard rails, joint bars, crossings and low-speed track; defects logged and reported to the roadmaster.

Special/emergency patrol after storms, flooding, extreme heat, or a broken-rail signal indication: right-of-way taken as found with debris, washouts, mudslides and sun kinks; often at night and in bad weather, on foot and by hi-rail, checking slopes, culverts and ditches as well as rail.

Commuter/heavy-rail transit patrol: walking inspection of tunnel, subway and elevated-structure track in third-rail territory during short night work windows or between trains with lookout protection; checks rail, fasteners, slab track, third-rail hardware and drainage.

Short line, tourist railroad and industrial plant/quarry/mine trackage: light-density, deferred-maintenance track with vegetation, mud and rough ballast, patrolled on foot or in a hi-rail pickup by a small crew with no automated inspection fleet.

sources.claim: ENSCO's Autonomous Track Inspection Systems on a MARTA heavy-rail work car autonomously measure geometry, rail profile and track components and detect broken rail, broken frogs and battered joints via a vehicle/track interaction monitor, transmitting exceptions to field staff, explicitly to reduce manual walking inspection in tunnel and third-rail territory.

tasks.label: Engage mechanisms that lay tracks or rails to specified gauges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Production rail relay on a Class I mainline: the operator runs rail-laying/threading equipment (rail lifters, rail threaders, tie cranes, gauger-spiker) in a track window, placing new CWR strings into tie plates/fastenings and holding them to 56.5 in gauge on curves, grades and superelevation, on ballast, in whatever weather and light the day gives, under roadway-worker protection alongside live track.

New track construction or major renewal: operator engages the laying mechanisms of a track-laying train, sleeper-laying machine or gantry crane spread to place ties/sleepers and thread rails onto a freshly prepared ballast/subgrade on a new alignment, keeping design gauge and alignment as the machine advances continuously across a linear construction site.

Turnout/switch panel installation or renewal at a junction: operator works cranes and laying equipment to set switch ties, stock rails, points and frog, then works jacks, gauge rods and adjustment mechanisms to bring the through and diverging routes to specified gauge and geometry with bespoke, project-specific components.

Yard, industrial plant, quarry or mine track: operator lays or relays short sections of standard- or narrow-gauge track with lighter machines (rail lifters, small cranes, tie inserters, clipping/spiking tools) inside premises the employer controls, with level ground, fixed layout and controlled access.

Spot rail replacement (plug rail) on mainline or branch line: operator engages machine mechanisms to lift out a defective rail length and lay in the replacement, seating it in the fastenings and gauging it against the reference rail before it is spiked/clipped, on track taken as found with worn ties and fouled ballast.

sources.system: Plasser & Theurer / Eiffage Rail 09-4x4 continuous-action tamping machine with Plasser SmartTamping
sources.title: Plasser & Theurer demonstrates autonomous tamping machine operation | Railway Gazette International
sources.claim: Plasser & Theurer and Eiffage Rail ran a track tamping machine autonomously (no operator in the tamping ...) through a turnout on a demonstration siding at the IAF trade show, with automated positioning of work units and automatic setting of tine opening width.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: ballast tamping and track lining. It shows autonomous control of a heavy on-track machine in a real rail setting, but the machine neither handles nor places rails or sleepers and never sets gauge, so it does not substantiate autonomous laying of rail to a specified gauge in the field.
