Same objects and a tighter precision than gauge tolerance, in a fenced plant where rails are conveyed and fixtured — the E1 presentation assumed for laying rail to gauge.

sources.system: ONE Rail Group fixed flash-butt welding plant
sources.title: Flash Butt Rail Welding Services | Rail Welding Plant
sources.claim: Fixed flash-butt welding plants are purpose-built lines in which rail handling, welding, grinding and finishing line processes are automated with dedicated plant infrastructure and equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Supporting context for the E1 environment: rails are routinely brought to purpose-built plant lines where the rail-handling cycle is machine-controlled. Cited only as context; the positive E1 judgments rest on evidence items 4 and 5.

tasks.label: Cut rails to specified lengths, using rail saws.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field cut on in-service mainline or branch track during rail replacement / plug-rail insertion: worker measures and marks the rail in track, sets a clamp-on abrasive or cold rail saw on 115-141 lb rail, cuts square within tolerance for welding, working on ballast in a limited track window, in any weather, at a site whose layout differs every time.

Emergency or defect work: cutting out a broken rail or detected defect, trimming battered rail ends, cutting rail at turnouts, bridges, crossings or in tight clearances; rail may be under thermal stress and pinch the blade; cut must be made fast to restore traffic.

Cutting rail to length in a rail yard, CWR welding plant, material yard or panel-assembly shop: stick or ribbon rail staged on racks or roller lines, cut to ordered lengths, ends cropped square for flash-butt or thermite welding, with plant lighting, power and cranes available.

Transit work: cutting running rail in a subway tunnel, elevated structure or transit yard during a night possession — restricted clearances, third rail and signal cable nearby, cold-saw preferred over sparking abrasive discs.

Industrial trackage: cutting rail in a mine, quarry, sand/gravel pit, plant yard or port — often lighter or worn rail, crane rail or non-standard sections, uneven footing, work done by a small crew with portable saws.

sources.system: Cembre ROBOKATTA RDS-14PN-AA automatic rail disc saw
sources.title: Cembre - RDS-14PN-AA Automatic rail disc saw with automatic arm
sources.claim: Cembre's ROBOKATTA RDS-14PN-AA is a commercially sold rail disc saw whose automatic support arm feeds the abrasive disc through a rail and stops at the end of the cut; once clamped on the rail the cutting cycle runs under machine control rather than by hand feed.

sources.system: Rail production line hot saw (rail rolling mill finishing line)
sources.developer: Nippon Steel & Sumitomo Metal (patented rail production line)
sources.title: Rail cooling method (US 9,429,374)
sources.claim: Railroad rails are cut to length in-line inside rail rolling mills by a hot saw integrated into the production line between the finishing mill and the cooling bed, i.e. the workpiece is conveyed to the machine and cut under mill control.

sources.system: Universal finishing mill hot saws with length gauges
sources.developer: Bethlehem Steel (mill practice described in patent)
sources.date: 1981 (patent describing rail/beam mill practice, still standard)
sources.title: Method for cooling hot-rolled shapes (US 4,282,048)
sources.claim: In rail-and-beam mills the hot saws work with gauges and are commanded electrically to subdivide the rolled rail into desired lengths — cut-to-length rail sawing performed by fixtured machinery, not by a hand-held saw.

sources.system: Scunthorpe Rail & Section Mill cold saws
sources.title: Scunthorpe mill celebrates golden anniversary | British Steel
sources.claim: British Steel's Scunthorpe rail and section mill cuts rolled rail sections to ordered customer lengths with cold saws on the mill's finishing line after straightening — production cut-to-length rail sawing in a purpose-built machine line.

sources.system: KASTO automatic bandsawing centres (KASTOtec FC 4 / KASTOwin, with KASTOsort handling)
sources.title: Metal Cutting Saws from KASTO for Industry and Trade
sources.claim: KASTO supplies fully automatic sawing systems with ... handling that cut steel bar, tube and profile stock to programmed lengths with little or no operator attendance; one installation (KASTOtec FC 4 at Schmolz + Bickenbach Stahlcenter) runs unmanned sawing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic cut-to-length sawing of hot-rolled steel bar and profile stock. A rail is a hot-rolled steel profile of comparable section and hardness, and the accepted output (a square cut at a programmed length) is the same; the transfer holds only for the E1 case where the workpiece is fed and clamped by the machine, as in these sawing centres.

sources.system: ROBEL Rail Automation ROBOT (FANUC robot arms on a rail wagon)
sources.developer: ROBEL Rail Automation GmbH with FANUC
sources.date: 2023 (prototypes on European networks); still pre-commercial as reported through 2025
sources.title: Robots Repair Railway Tracks | FANUC Global
sources.claim: The closest on-track robotic system, ROBEL Rail Automation's rail-traversing wagon carrying two FANUC arms, autonomously detects rail and switch defects and repairs them by welding, milling and grinding; first prototypes ran on European networks. It performs surface machining, not through-cutting of rail to a specified length.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic machining of rail in track) cited to bound field capability, not to support a positive judgment: the demonstrated operations are welding, milling and grinding of defects on the railhead and switch components, which does not include severing the head, web and base of a rail at a measured mark, so it does not substantiate cutting rail to length at E2 or E3.

tasks.label: Operate single- or multiple-head spike driving machines to drive spikes into ties and secure rails.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mainline production tie gang: after ties are renewed and tie plates set, the operator runs a multi-head production spiker along miles of open main line under track-and-time authority, driving cut spikes through plates into new timber ties in ballast, in all weather, on tangents and curves.

Spot and section-gang maintenance: driving replacement spikes on individual bad ties, re-spiking loose/high spikes, gauging on curves, at turnouts, grade crossings and bridge approaches, using a small single- or dual-head spiker; fouled ballast, mud, old plates, varied spike patterns, adjacent live track.

Yard, industrial spur and plant-track work (plant yards, quarries, sand/gravel pits, mines, port and steel-mill trackage): spiking new or repaired track inside a facility the owner controls, with tight clearances, debris, grease and frequent switching moves.

New track construction / rail relay gang: spiking freshly laid rail and plated ties on a prepared roadbed at a linear construction site (new siding, industrial lead, rebuilt line), coordinating with tie-plate setters, anchor machines and cranes.

Transit, commuter and short-line work: spiking in transit yards, tunnels, station areas and light-density short-line track, often at night in short windows with restricted access, lighter machines and non-standard plate/spike patterns.

sources.title: NXV Spiker - Nordco
sources.claim: Nordco's NXV (Nexxus Vision) Spiker is a production spike-driving machine whose AI vision system and automatic spike feeder automate the spiking cycle so that a single operator, riding in the cab, drives spikes by pressing a button rather than manually aiming each gun.

sources.title: Technology - Nexxus CANBUS System - Nordco
sources.claim: The NXV's Nexxus Vision system uses cameras and machine-learning to locate tie-plate holes, recognize spiking patterns and align the spikes automatically, compensating for environmental conditions, rail alignment and wear — i.e., the perception and aiming portion of spike driving is machine-controlled, not hand-guided.

sources.title: Nordco Ships First 5 NXV Spiker Units - Nordco
sources.claim: The NXV Spiker has moved from development into field service on North American main-line track: the first five units were delivered to Class 1 railroads in May 2026, cutting the crew required to run the machine from three operators to one.

sources.title: NXV Spiker | Automated Rail Spiking Machine by Nordco
sources.claim: The NXV automates the whole spike path — bulk bin, singulation, orientation, delivery to the hammer — and identifies tie-plate holes in real time across changing plate styles, lighting, ..., with four guns driving simultaneously at production speed.

sources.system: Viking Turbo 505 / Voyager nailing machines with Joutech automated lumber feeding
sources.title: Joutech Explains More Details on Its Automation Partnership with Viking Engineering - Pallet Enterprise
sources.claim: Fully automatic nailing lines drive fasteners into fixtured timber in factories with no human in the fastening loop: Viking's Turbo 505 and Voyager nailing ... are being paired with Joutech automated lumber feeding for hands-off production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic driving of steel fasteners into dimensional timber held in a fixture on a conveyorized line. It transfers to the E1 counterfactual for spiking because the workpiece (softwood/hardwood member), the fastener-driving action, and the positional tolerance are comparable once the tie/plate/rail assembly is presented in a known, fixtured position; the rail-specific perception and hammer hardware are supplied by the cited Nordco NXV system.

tasks.label: Operate track wrenches to tighten or loosen bolts at joints that hold ends of rails together.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Section-gang work on jointed mainline or branch-line track in open country: walking the line and re-tightening loose joint (track) bolts and replacing broken or missing bolts at bonded and standard joints, using a gas or hydraulic impact track wrench in all weather, with rusted threads, ballast and mud around the joint bars.

Rail cut-in or rail replacement: loosening and removing the four or six bolts on each joint bar to take out a defective or worn rail, handling the heavy joint bars, then reinstalling bars and bolts and torquing the new joint (or a temporary joint in CWR) under a track-time window with a work train or hi-rail gang.

Yard, plant-yard, quarry or mine track: bolting and unbolting joints on yard leads, turnouts and industrial spurs, often in tight quarters between cars and structures, on poorly maintained low-speed track, using portable impact wrenches.

Insulated joints, compromise joints and joints at grade crossings and switch points: torquing bolts to specified values (and re-checking torque) on signal-critical or specialty joints, often with road traffic or crossing surfaces to work around.

Transit, subway tunnel, elevated structure or bridge track: joint bolt tightening and removal during short night maintenance windows, near third rail or on open deck bridges, with restricted access and lighting.

Shop or panel-yard assembly: bolting joint bars onto rails to build track panels or pre-assemble turnouts and crossing diamonds before they are shipped to the field, working at bench or jig height in a controlled yard/shop.

sources.system: 3D vision-guided robotic bolt-tightening station (van rear axle damper line)
sources.title: Robots Automate Bolt-Tightening on Automotive Assembly Lines | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Vision-guided six-axis robot autonomously tightens the rear axle-damper bolts on vans moving through a workstation on an automotive assembly line, using 3D perception to compensate for vehicle position variation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: torquing structural bolts on a vehicle undercarriage. Transfer: the same physical act as rail joint bolting - locate a steel fastener whose position varies, engage a socket, run it to a specified torque - performed autonomously in a purpose-built station, which is how an E1 setting would present a fixtured rail joint.

sources.system: Mech-Eye PRO M-GL 3D vision-guided bolt tightening cell
sources.developer: Mech-Mind Robotics (deployed at construction machinery manufacturer)
sources.title: 3D Vision-Guided Bolt Tightening | Mech-Mind Robotics
sources.claim: 3D-vision-guided robot locates and tightens the large chassis bolts on wheel-loader frames in a construction-machinery plant, running 24/7 in production with at least 99% recognition and plus/minus 1 mm bolt positioning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-torque bolting of heavy steel machine frames. Transfer: bolt size, joint stiffness and torque class are comparable to rail joint (fish) bolts, and the robot works from vision on parts presented at a fixed station - the E1 analogue of a fixtured rail joint.

sources.developer: RoboTire (with Discount Tire and Hunter Engineering)
sources.title: Discount Tire testing RoboTire system for use in stores | Tire Business
sources.claim: Camera-guided robots in a tire-service bay autonomously remove wheel lug nuts from customer vehicles and re-torque them to manufacturer specification; the first system was installed ... a Discount Tire store.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: loosening and re-torquing nuts on in-service, weather-exposed hardware. Transfer: lug nuts are commonly corroded and over-torqued like rail joint nuts; the robot finds them by camera, breaks them loose and torques to spec with the workpiece brought to a fixed machine position, matching the E1 presentation of a rail joint.

sources.title: New technologies for the disassembly of electric vehicle batteries and motors - Fraunhofer IPA
sources.claim: A robot-based demonstration platform with vision-based screw detection loosens screws and bolted connections to open used electric-vehicle battery packs in a purpose-built automated disassembly station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic unbolting of used, dirty field-returned assemblies. Transfer: it demonstrates the loosening half of the task - detect fastener, engage, break loose, extract - autonomously on hardware not designed for robots, in a fixtured cell, which is the E1 presentation for removing rail joint bolts.

sources.title: "DeMoBat": Battery disassembly for electric cars using KUKA robots | KUKA Global
sources.claim: KUKA KR QUANTEC industrial robots in the Fraunhofer IPA disassembly cell remove bolts from automotive battery packs, with image processing automatically detecting screws so the robot need not be manually taught each position.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-directed bolt removal by a high-payload industrial arm. Transfer: confirms unscripted (not taught-point) unbolting of steel fasteners on varying incoming units inside a fenced cell, the capability needed to loosen bolts at a rail joint presented in a fixture.

sources.title: Railchap robot showcased in Oslo, revolutionising railway safety and reducing maintenance risks | Global Railway Review
sources.claim: Rail-bound maintenance robot demonstrated on Norwegian railway infrastructure travels along the track to inspect and lubricate switch slide plates; the demonstrated physical work does not include tightening or loosening bolts.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the state of the art for robots working on live track: the demonstrated work is inspection and slide-plate lubrication, not fastener torquing, so it does not substantiate joint-bolt work in the track environment.

sources.system: Railway Bolt Tightening Robot (rail bolt torque control robot)
sources.developer: Shandong China Coal Industrial & Mining Supplies Group
sources.title: Rail Bolt Torque Control and Railway Track Maintenance Robot Fastening Robot
sources.claim: Trade listing for a self-propelled railway bolt tightening robot claiming automatic travel, recognition, positioning and bolt tightening/loosening under one-key control; no primary technical or deployment documentation of autonomous work on rail joints was found.
sources.transferJustification: Closest marketed product to this task, but a B2B sales listing with operator 'one-key' control and no independent documentation; autonomy cannot be established, so it is treated as teleoperated and supports no positive judgment.

tasks.label: Raise rails, using hydraulic jacks, to allow for tie removal and replacement.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Class I mainline production tie gang under a track possession: a consist of machines works tie-to-tie along open tangent/curve track, ties pre-marked for replacement; the rail is raised by hydraulic rail-lift jaws/jacks on the tie exchanger or a dedicated rail lifter so old ties can be pulled and new ones inserted, hundreds to a couple thousand ties per shift, in ballast, dust and weather.

Spot tie replacement by a section/maintenance gang on mainline or branch line: a handful of scattered bad ties, reached by hi-rail truck; hydraulic track jacks are set by hand under the rail (or a hi-rail tie exchanger is spotted) to raise the rail a couple of inches, with variable ballast, mud, drainage and traffic protection.

Special trackwork: switch ties, grade-crossing timbers, bridge timbers and joint locations, where the rail must be raised with hydraulic jacks in obstructed space (guard rails, switch rods, crossing panels, bridge decks, signal/third-rail apparatus) and each lift point must be chosen and cribbed by hand.

Industrial and extractive track: plant yards, quarries, sand and gravel pits and mines; poorly maintained spurs with fouled or buried ballast, mud, vegetation, non-standard fasteners and tight clearances; rail raised with hand hydraulic jacks or an excavator-mounted tie changer while a small crew swaps ties.

Transit/commuter track work in night windows: tunnels, elevated structures and station areas with restricted clearance, third rail or catenary, limited machine access; rail is raised with portable hydraulic jacks to change timbers/ties before the morning service restoration.

sources.system: Harsco Rail machine vision + Tie Finder / Jupiter control system
sources.title: Harsco Rail advances technology in track maintenance and repair
sources.claim: Harsco Rail developed, with a railroad partner, a machine-vision plus Tie Finder system for tie-gang machines that automatically moves the machine to the tie to be worked and performs the work; first four equipped machines were commissioned in late 2017 for work on mainline track.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated spike/fastener removal-application and spot tie removal by tie-gang machines. Transfer: these are the same machine class and workheads used to clamp and jack the rail for tie exchange, indexed to the same object (an individual tie/rail seat) to within a fraction of an inch, in the identical mainline-track environment.

sources.title: Harsco Rail advances technology in track maintenance and repair
sources.claim: Harsco's Tie Finder probes combined with the machines' existing automatic workhead cycle are described by the manufacturer as enabling fully automatic work on wood or concrete ties, including through poor visibility and inclement weather.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic indexing and cycling of hydraulic tie-gang workheads. Transfer: raising the rail is one such hydraulic workhead cycle on the same machines, requiring the same tie-location accuracy and acting on the same rail/tie objects on the same track.

sources.title: Multipurpose, Efficient Track Maintenance Equipment in Demand
sources.claim: Harsco introduced an unmanned 'Drone' chase tamper in 2009 that works ties skipped by a manned lead tamper; encoder wheels and tie finders of both machines are synchronized, after which the unmanned machine moves and works independently on live mainline track.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: ballast tamping at each tie by an unmanned machine. Transfer: it demonstrates that a heavy hydraulic maintenance-of-way machine can locate individual ties and cycle powerful workheads between rails, unmanned, in the same production-gang mainline environment in which rails are jacked for tie exchange.

sources.system: Harsco DRONE Chase Tamper; DRONE Anchor Adjuster
sources.title: Tie and switch tamping - Railway Age
sources.claim: Trade press confirms the DRONE chase tamper is an unmanned production machine following a lead machine, and that Harsco extended the unmanned 'Drone' concept to a Drone Anchor Adjuster, built on tie-finding technology approaching very high accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unmanned tamping and unmanned rail-anchor adjusting within a tie gang. Transfer: the anchor machines clamp the rail and cycle hydraulic workheads at each tie, the same rail-engaging, tie-indexed hydraulic action as raising the rail with jacks, in the same mainline gang.

sources.system: Harsco Drone Anchor Spreader / Drone Anchor Squeezer
sources.title: Tie Equipment - Harsco Rail | Railway Equipment Company
sources.claim: Harsco Rail's current tie-equipment product line includes unmanned 'Drone' rail-anchor machines alongside spike pullers, indicating unmanned tie-gang machines that clamp and work on the rail are productized, not just prototypes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unmanned rail-anchor spreading/squeezing in tie gangs. Transfer: the workhead clamps the rail at a specific tie and applies large hydraulic force, the same registration and force control needed to jack the rail off a tie, in the identical environment.

sources.title: TPX Tie Exchanger - Railroad Tie Replacement Machine - Nordco
sources.claim: Current production tie exchangers that raise the rail during tie exchange are single-operator, joystick-controlled cab machines with partial automation (automated plate handling, auto-centering workhead, optional rail-lift spotting feature), i.e. the rail-lift function is a machine-executed hydraulic cycle commanded by a human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: the TPX raises the rail (internal LVDT rail-lift cylinders, rail-lift spotting option) so ties can be removed and inserted; cited to establish that the rail-lift hardware and its cycle are standard, while autonomy is not established.

sources.title: Nordco | Auto Lift - Rail Lifter
sources.claim: Nordco's Auto Lift rail lifter is a machine whose hydraulic cylinders lift both rails off the ties so plates can be handled, used by rail and tie gangs, with operators activating the lift.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: machine-borne hydraulic raising of the rail off the ties. Cited to establish the hardware exists as a self-contained rail-lifting machine; operator activation means it cannot by itself support an autonomy judgment.

sources.title: Wabtec Debuts New Rail Technology at Railway Interchange 2025 - Railway Age
sources.claim: Wabtec displayed a next-generation Spiker Vision maintenance-of-way prototype described as its first closed-loop AI solution, aimed at rail-yard track work productivity.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: AI closed-loop spike driving on track. Transfer is partial: it shows vision-closed-loop control of track workheads on rail in yards, but as a prototype it is cited only as corroboration, not as the decisive evidence for any instance.

tasks.label: Lubricate machines, change oil, or fill hydraulic reservoirs to specified levels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-shift/daily service of an on-track production machine (tamper, ballast regulator, spike driver) at the work site on the right-of-way: pump grease into dozens of zerk fittings on workheads, pins and bushings, check the sight glass and top off the hydraulic reservoir, check engine oil and coolant. Machine sits on ballast on live track, dusty or wet, cramped access under workheads, fluids carried from a service truck.

The same lube-and-fluid service performed in the railroad's yard or maintenance-of-way equipment shop between shifts: machine parked on a level service track or shop floor, shop grease pumps, bulk oil reels and drip pans available, several different machine makes and models serviced by the same operator.

Scheduled engine oil-and-filter change on a MOW machine (shop or field with a service truck): pull the drain plug or open the drain valve, capture and dispose of waste oil, spin off and replace spin-on oil and hydraulic filters, refill the crankcase and re-check the dipstick to the specified mark.

Servicing portable hydraulic power units and tools at the job site (rail saw, impact wrench, tie drill, hydraulic pump packs, small gas engines): unscrew fill caps, top up hydraulic oil and engine oil from cans to the marked level, oil chains and fittings, wipe up spills. Done on the ballast shoulder or off the back of a truck.

Start/end-of-shift fluid service of hi-rail trucks and on-track machines at the yard fuel/service rack: refuel and top up engine oil, hydraulic oil, DEF, coolant and washer fluid to specified levels, then log the readings.

sources.title: SCOTT making ROBOFUEL™ refuelling system progress with AHS mining truck fleets - International Mining
sources.claim: ROBOFUEL uses a robotic arm with vision and sensing to refuel large mine haul trucks autonomously; a Pilbara installation achieved site acceptance in late ... was operating in production, with further systems built for autonomous haulage fleets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous refuelling of heavy diesel machines. It transfers to 'fill reservoirs to specified levels' because the robot locates the fill port on a large off-road machine, couples a nozzle and dispenses fluid to a set level with automatic shut-off — comparable object scale, coupling precision and fluid handling to topping a MOW machine's fuel or hydraulic reservoir. It does not cover greasing fittings or filter changes.

sources.title: Dürr Compact Filling Stations - Dürr
sources.claim: Dürr's Somac/BlueStart filling stations are fully automatic filling systems integrated into vehicle assembly lines that fill motor and gearbox oil, coolant, brake fluid and other fluids into vehicle reservoirs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line vehicle fluid filling. It is the same physical act as 'fill hydraulic reservoirs / add oil to specified levels' — machine-controlled docking to a reservoir opening and dispensing a metered charge — but on workpieces presented in a fixtured, purpose-built station rather than on a machine parked trackside.

sources.title: Dürr Filling Adapters - Dürr
sources.claim: Dürr's filling adapters clamp onto container openings of brake, coolant and power-steering systems and set the liquid level in the vehicle container with a height-adjustable nozzle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated adapter docking and level-controlled filling. Substantiates the 'to specified levels' requirement of this task in a fixtured setting; it does not address dipstick checks on varied machines parked in the field.

sources.system: DOPAG automated greasing production cell with FANUC LRM 200ID7L
sources.title: Automated Grease Dispensing System | DOPAG
sources.claim: DOPAG and FANUC built an automated greasing production cell in which a FANUC LRM 200ID7L six-axis robot carries out the entire greasing operation on parts held in a workpiece carrier, with flow measurement guaranteeing exact grease dosage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of a metered grease charge to specified points on a fixtured workpiece. It transfers to 'lubricate machines' only where the work is presented in a purpose-built cell with lube points at known positions; the parts are small and clean, unlike ballast-covered fittings on a tamper.

sources.system: Grease Jockey Series automatic lubrication systems
sources.title: Grease Jockey Series Automatic Lubrication Systems - Graco
sources.claim: Graco's Grease Jockey automatic lubrication systems are commercially sold and fitted on heavy on- and off-road equipment, delivering metered grease to the machine's lube points on a machine-controlled cycle in place of manual greasing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled metered grease delivery to the same pins, bushings and bearing points an operator hits with a grease gun. It is hard-plumbed onto the machine — every lube point presented at a fixed, purpose-built connection — and it does not check or fill oil and hydraulic reservoirs, so it cannot carry a whole service visit on its own.

sources.system: UFR AutoFuel (E20C robotic base with UFR Autonomy)
sources.title: Autonomous Truck Refuelling with Universal Field Robots - Universal Field Robots
sources.claim: Universal Field Robots' AutoFuel places a mobile robotic base with a refuelling attachment beside a mine haul road; the robot positions itself and connects the nozzle to the truck for unattended refuelling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous connection of a fluid nozzle to a heavy machine at a designated service point; supports fluid filling of large machines where the machine comes to the robot's station, not free-form field servicing.

tasks.label: Drill holes through rails, tie plates, or fishplates for insertion of bolts or spikes, using power drills.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Joint/plug-rail work on mainline or branch line in the field: crew brings a portable hydraulic or gas rail drill to a rail end (broken rail, plug rail, or new joint), clamps it to the web, drills 2-3 bolt holes to the joint-bar pattern, chamfers them, then bolts on joint bars. Done on ballast, often at night, under a limited track window, in any weather.

Rail relay / new-track construction: drilling bolt holes in the ends of newly laid rail strings, closure rails, insulated-joint locations and transition rails along a linear construction worksite with materials, machines and other crews present; multiple rail sections and weights, holes positioned by gauge/template.

Yard, plant-yard, quarry or mine track: drilling rail ends for joint bars on spur, siding and yard tracks inside a facility whose owner controls access; flat standardized track layout but outdoor ballast, grease and mixed rail sections.

Ancillary in-track drilling: holes in the rail web for signal bond wires, holes for guard-rail bolts, wheel stops, restraining-rail or switch component attachment, occasional field drilling of a tie plate or bracket; small numbers of holes at scattered locations along the line.

Bench/shop drilling: at a section house, welding plant or on a work train, drilling loose workpieces - cut rail sections, joint bars/fishplates, tie plates - laid on stands or a bench, using a rail drill or shop drill press before the parts go to track.

sources.system: Robel Rail Automation robotic rail repair system (with FANUC robots)
sources.title: Robots Repair Railway Tracks - FANUC
sources.claim: Robel Rail Automation's rail-traversing wagon carries two FANUC industrial arms that detect rail and switch defects and carry out fully automatic welding, milling and grinding repairs on rail in track; first prototype systems are running on European networks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ machining of rail in track (milling/grinding/welding) rather than drilling bolt holes. It shows robot arms can locate and machine rail steel trackside, but no drilling end-effector, rail-web access or bolt-hole quality is demonstrated, so it does not substantiate completion of this drilling task in the field.

sources.title: Technology: Robel's rail grinding robot - ROLLINGSTOCK
sources.claim: The Robel/FANUC unit is a prototype mounted in containers on a flat car; it has been in field trials on mainline tracks ... since 2024 and is claimed to work in all weather conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic restoration of rail geometry on mainline track. Establishes that a supervised robot can work on open-line track in weather, but the demonstrated processes are milling/welding/grinding of the rail head, not drilling through-holes in the web for bolts.

sources.system: FICEP VANGUARD three-spindle CNC beam drilling line
sources.title: VANGUARD | Ficep
sources.claim: Commercially sold CNC beam drill lines automatically drill, countersink and mill holes in rolled steel sections that are conveyed, probed, measured and clamped by the machine, with automatic tool changers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic drilling of bolt holes through the webs and flanges of rolled structural steel sections held in the machine's clamps. A railroad rail is a rolled steel section and a fishplate/tie plate is a steel flat; hole diameter, web thickness and millimetre-level position tolerance are comparable, so a fixtured rail or plate presented to such a line is drilled to the standard the track crew must meet.

sources.title: High-strength Fishplate | Rail Joint Bar - AGICO
sources.claim: Railway fishplates (joint bars) are produced with CNC precision drilling of their bolt holes so the holes align with the rail bolt pattern.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers one of the workpieces named in the task (fishplates/joint bars): the holes are produced by machine-controlled drilling in a purpose-built production setting, to the alignment tolerance required for bolting to rail.

sources.title: Self-Feed Rail Drill (03500) for Efficient Drilling of Track - Pandrol
sources.claim: No autonomous machine that drills bolt holes in rails in track was found in search; field rail drilling is still done with man-portable rail drills that an operator carries, positions and clamps on the rail.
sources.transferJustification: Baseline for the human method: the commercial state of the art for in-track drilling is an operator-carried, operator-clamped drill, indicating no fielded autonomous alternative for the in-track instances.

tasks.label: Drive vehicles that automatically move and lay tracks or rails over sections of track to be constructed, repaired, or maintained.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Class I mainline rail relay: operator drives a self-propelled rail train / rail-unloading machine along the running track under track-and-time authority, threading and laying continuous welded rail strings (400 m ribbons) onto ties and rollers alongside the old rail, coordinating with a ground crew, over curves, grade crossings, bridges and in all weather.

Production tie-and-rail gang on mainline: operator drives self-propelled machines (tie inserter/remover, rail-lifting/threading equipment, spike and anchor machines) that advance tie-by-tie down the track during a work window, laying new ties and rail among a dozen other machines and workers on foot, with periodic stops for trains.

New construction / major reconstruction: operator drives a track-laying machine, track renewal train or gantry that lays prefabricated track panels or continuous new track over a freshly graded roadbed or slab (new line, siding, industrial lead, transit extension), with panels staged by crane, mud and uneven ground, and surveyors setting line and grade.

Transit/commuter agency night work in a yard, at-grade line or tunnel: operator drives rail-laying/renewal machinery to replace rail or track panels in a controlled facility with third rail or catenary de-energized, tight clearances, standardized layout and a fixed work window before service resumes.

Short line, industrial plant yard, sand-and-gravel or quarry trackage: operator drives a hi-rail crane, small track-laying vehicle or tie/rail handling machine to replace a rail section or a few panels on light, often out-of-standard track with debris, weeds, buried crossings and small crews.

Underground mine or open-pit operation: operator drives a track-shifting/laying machine or rail-mounted panel handler to move and lay portable track panels as the working face or dump advances, on rough, wet, unfenced ground with varying gauge and light rail.

sources.system: Harsco Rail Drone Tamper (AutoMag Tie Finder)
sources.developer: Harsco Rail (Enviri / Wabtec-era track equipment maker)
sources.title: Drone Tamper - Harsco Rail | Railway Equipment Company
sources.claim: Harsco Rail's Drone Tamper is an unmanned self-propelled maintenance-of-way machine that runs behind a manned lead tamper on the running track, finds each tie with its own sensors, actuates its work heads automatically and stops itself for obstacles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: railroad bed tamping, explicitly part of this occupation and performed by the same class of self-propelled on-track machine. It substantiates unmanned self-propulsion, tie-level indexing and automatic actuation of heavy work heads on rail — the 'drive the vehicle that automatically works the track' element of this task — but not the rigging, threading and placement of rails/ties, which at E1 is supplied by fixtured presentation.

sources.title: History - Harsco Rail | Railway Equipment Company
sources.claim: Harsco Rail states it launched an automated Drone surfacing vehicle requiring no operator in 2010, i.e. a commercially fielded driverless on-track work machine.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the Drone Tamper item: surfacing/tamping rather than rail laying, cited only for driverless operation and automatic work cycles of a heavy on-track machine.

sources.title: Multipurpose, Efficient Track Maintenance Equipment in Demand | Metro Magazine
sources.claim: Trade press confirms the Drone tamper is an unmanned chase machine used in production surfacing gangs on North American railroads, tamping the ties skipped by the manned lead tamper.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (tamping) in the same occupation and the same environment (mainline running track); cited for deployed unmanned operation of a track machine, not for rail/tie placement.

sources.system: Unimat 09-4x4/4S E³ with Plasser TampingAssistant / SmartTamping
sources.title: Autonomous tamping machine demonstration | Railway Gazette International
sources.claim: Plasser & Theurer and Eiffage Rail publicly demonstrated a fully autonomous continuous-action tamping machine working through a turnout with an empty work cab, on a demonstration siding next to a DB InfraGo line, in May 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tamping/lining of track by a heavy on-track machine in the same occupation, using rail-referenced positioning and AI object classification; supports autonomous driving and precise positioning of track machinery, not autonomous handling and laying of rails or panels.

sources.developer: China Tiesiju Civil Engineering Group (CTCE) / China Railway No.4 Bureau, with Central South University and Zhuzhou Xuyang
sources.title: Smart tech boosts 'most beautiful rail' - China Daily
sources.claim: The most advanced dedicated track-laying system reported, China's WPZ-500 intelligent ballastless track-laying unit, laid a 500 m pair of rails on a high-speed line with three human drivers operating its vehicles — field rail laying remains human-driven.

sources.title: Rail engineer trials automatic track laying system in China - Global Construction Review
sources.claim: The same WPZ-500 smart track-laying method, described as using robots, laser scanners and autonomous vehicles, is claimed only to reduce on-site labour by about 63 percent, so substantial human crew and driving remain.

sources.title: Robel Rail Automation Uses FANUC Robots to Repair Railway Lines - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: ROBEL Rail Automation's ROBOT system mounts two FANUC industrial arms on a rail wagon that detects rail and switch defects and repairs them automatically by welding, milling and grinding, showing rail-referenced robotic manipulation on track (in testing, not production laying).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic rail and switch repair carried out from an on-track wagon. It shows industrial robot arms working autonomously to rail-level precision on track components, supporting a fixtured (E1-style) laying cell, but it does not handle or place rails, ties or panels.

tasks.label: Clean tracks or clear ice or snow from tracks or switch boxes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Winter storm at a classification yard or commuter terminal: worker moves switch to switch clearing packed snow and ice from turnout points, frogs, rod pockets and switch machine/heater boxes with broom, shovel, scraper, portable blower or torch, and checks/relights switch heaters so the yard's switches stay operable through the storm.

Mainline interlocking or remote junction during/after a storm or freeze-thaw: crew hi-rails out to a specific frozen switch, chips ice off point rails and stock rails, blows or brooms drifted snow out of the switch and its rod pockets and switch box, applies de-icer, and confirms the switch throws and locks.

Bulk snow removal after a storm: operating hi-rail plow, Speed Swing/Snow Fighter with wing plows, snow buckets and track-cleaning bucket, rotary or jet-engine snow blower to clear drifted snow from running tracks, yard leads, and grade crossings over long stretches of line.

Year-round track cleaning of debris and spilled material: sweeping, shoveling, vacuuming coal, grain, sand, mud, ballast and trash out of the track, flangeways at crossings and platforms, and out of switch and crossing hardware in railroad yards, plant yards, quarries and mines.

Cleaning fouled ballast and mud spots during a track window on mainline or yard track: operating an undercutter/ballast cleaning machine or rail-mounted vacuum excavator to remove fouled ballast and debris from cribs and around ties, turnouts and crossings, then restoring the section.

Transit night possession in a subway tunnel or station: clearing litter, dust, oil-soaked debris and ice accumulation from the track bed, flangeways, drains and contact-rail area between rails so the line reopens for service.

sources.system: Railway Equipment Co. (RECo) Magnum gas/electric hot air blower switch heaters with snow detectors and Sno-Net monitoring
sources.title: Rail Insider - Railroad snow plows, air blowers and switch heaters help combat winter weather (Progressive Railroading)

sources.system: Thermon Hellfire 400/900/905 and Fastrax Switchblade heating packages; Pettibone Speed Swing 445F2 with sweeper-broom, V-plow, track-cleaning bucket

sources.system: JR West / Nippon Signal / Human Machinery rail-mounted humanoid maintenance robot

sources.claim: The most advanced railway field maintenance robot in service, JR West's rail-mounted humanoid for overhead-line work and obstacle clearance, is human-controlled through a VR interface rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (clearing obstacles/debris from the railway right-of-way); cited to show that even the leading rail field robot is teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous track cleaning.

sources.system: Yeti Snow Technology / Yeti Move autonomous snowploughs and runway sweepers
sources.developer: Semcon and Øveraasen (Yeti Snow Technology) for Avinor
sources.date: 2018-03 first runway clearing; framework agreement 2021; fleet operation at Oslo Airport since 2018/19
sources.title: Autonomous snowploughs used to clear airport runway - ADAS & Autonomous Vehicle International
sources.claim: Autonomous snow clearing is deployed on paved airfield surfaces (runways and taxiways) by Yeti/Semcon-Overaasen self-driving ploughs and sweepers for Avinor, but these machines work on open pavement, not on ballasted track with rails, flangeways and switch points.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous bulk snow clearing at an institution-controlled outdoor facility); cited to bound the transfer — the demonstrated surface is flat pavement with no rails, flangeways or switch mechanisms, so it does not substantiate clearing snow from track.

tasks.label: Dress and reshape worn or damaged railroad switch points or frogs, using portable power grinders.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open mainline/branch or industrial lead track: after a welder builds up a spalled or battered railbound-manganese or solid-manganese frog (point, wings, flangeway edges), the operator dresses the weld back to running-surface profile with a portable/rail-clamped power grinder. Outdoors on ballast, inside a track possession, weather as found, hi-rail or on-track access, live track sometimes adjacent.

Open mainline turnout: dressing worn or chipped switch points - grinding the point tip and gauge face, removing metal flow, lipping and burrs from point and stock rail so the point closes flush against the stock rail. Worker kneels in the switch, working in the few-millimetre gap between point and stock rail, ballast underfoot, weather as found.

Classification yard, terminal, port rail complex, or plant/mine/quarry yard track: scheduled dressing of a worn frog on premises the facility controls, with road and rail access, level walking, planned work window and a maintenance program.

Yard, terminal or transit interlocking, including night windows in subway tunnels and station approaches with third rail and tight clearances: dressing switch points, stock rails and check rails and deburring the turnout during a scheduled maintenance window on institution-controlled premises.

Urgent field response: an inspection or detector run finds a battered frog point, broken point tip, or derailment-damaged switch; a welder/grinder responds within hours at an arbitrary line location and grinds the damage back to a safe profile to lift a slow order, often at night, in rain, snow or mud, with only truck-carried tools.

sources.title: ROBOT - ROBEL Rail Automation (product page)
sources.claim: ROBEL Rail Automation's ROBOT, a container-mounted twin-arm FANUC system carried on a rail wagon, performs local rail and switch defect repair end-to-end - scanning, milling, preheating, welding and grinding - as a fully automated process run by one operator.

sources.title: A Bavarian startup is automating Europe's track maintenance - The Rail Agenda
sources.claim: As of June 2026 the ROBOT scans, mills, preheats, welds and grinds rail end-to-end with one supervising operator, has provisional homologation for manganese switch ..., and has placed eight welds at the Maasvlakte port rail complex monitored for close to a ....

sources.title: Technology: Robel's rail grinding robot - ROLLINGSTOCK
sources.claim: The ROBOT prototype has been in field trials on mainline tracks ... since 2024, working from a flat car with a jib arm and dual manipulators that scan, mill, weld and grind the damaged section; switch geometry adjustment and a 7 m range remain future development.

sources.title: ROBOT Automated Switch and Infrastructure Maintenance - Railway-News
sources.claim: In November 2024 the ROBOT was tested in real railway conditions in the Netherlands with ProRail, Strukton Rail and VolkerRail, completing switch frog repairs with final profiling restoring rail geometry, overseen by one operator and one helper, working full shifts in any weather on closed track.

sources.title: Automation: Robel embraces robots - Railway Gazette International
sources.claim: The ROBOT's two heads assess and repair a switch without manual handling: a Lidar head measures damage and instructs the treatment unit on the weld and subsequent milling to ..., with a final quality scan; the milling head was refined for cast manganese crossings. Robel positions it for planned interventions rather than reactive repairs.

sources.title: ROCENTER - ROBEL Rail Automation (product page)
sources.claim: ROBEL's ROCENTER is a modular robot cell (robot on two linear axes, pull-out fixing frame giving an 8 m x 3.5 m processing area) that scans, mills, welds and grinds rail-steel and Mn13 components, offered as a reconditioning service for manganese and steel switch frogs.
sources.transferJustification: Same task with the work brought to the machine: the worn switch point or frog is fixtured in the cell and the robot restores its profile by milling/grinding - the same components, materials and profile tolerances as hand-grinder dressing.

sources.title: A Bavarian startup is automating Europe's track maintenance - The Rail Agenda
sources.claim: ROCENTER is described as a workshop system for the ....
sources.transferJustification: Reprofiling worn switch components in a fixtured cell produces the same reshaped output on the same parts as dressing points and frogs with portable grinders.

sources.title: HAMR Automated Frog & Diamond Restoration - Holland
sources.claim: Holland's HAMR, the in-track frog and diamond restoration service deployed in North America, automates only the welding; pre-weld material removal and finish grinding are performed by the human crew.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as context/negative evidence: the in-track robotic frog repair service actually deployed in the US does not automate the grinding step that constitutes this task.

sources.title: Robel Rail Automation Uses FANUC Robots to Repair Railway Lines - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Robel's rail-borne wagon with two FANUC robots detects internal and external defects and ... repairs them using welding, milling and ..., aimed particularly at repair work on points.

tasks.label: Clean or make minor repairs to machines or equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-shift/periodic exterior washdown of a large on-track machine (production tamper, ballast regulator, ballast cleaner, brush cutter): hosing or pressure-washing off caked ballast dust, mud, grease and oil from body, undercarriage, steps and glass, typically trackside or on a service/wash track in a yard.

Daily walk-around cleaning of machine subsystems in the field: blowing/brushing ballast dust out of radiators, coolers and air cleaners, clearing spilled ballast and vegetation from workheads, undercarriage and walkways, cleaning lights, mirrors and cab glass, sweeping and wiping out a cluttered cab; done trackside in weather as found.

Minor field repair on the machine during a track window: locate and replace a burst hydraulic hose or leaking fitting, a worn tamping tool tip or wear plate, broken lamp, belt, air line or clamp, re-torque loose fasteners and top off fluids, working on ballast alongside live track to get the machine producing again.

Minor repairs and servicing in the maintenance-of-way shop or yard facility with the machine spotted on a shop track: filter and fluid changes, hose, lamp and belt replacement, swapping worn wear parts, small bracket weld or fastener repair, using shop tools and a parts crib.
Bench-level cleaning of removed components and hardware in the shop: degreasing pumps, valves, brackets and tool bits, cleaning screens, strainers and filters before reinstallation.

Cleaning and minor repair of powered hand tools and portable equipment (rail saw, impact wrench, hydraulic spike puller, generator, welder, torch): clearing swarf and dirt, changing blades, bits and spark plugs, cleaning air filters, adjusting and lubricating, at the hi-rail truck or tool room.

sources.system: InterClean robotic industrial/mining vehicle wash system
sources.date: 2026-04 (product page last modified; systems in mining service for years)
sources.title: Industrial Vehicle Washing Systems - Manual & Robotic Solutions | InterClean
sources.claim: InterClean's robotic industrial wash systems automatically wash heavy mining and industrial vehicles up to 400-ton haul trucks inside a wash bay with no personnel present, using software that recognizes each vehicle and directs the water monitors to designated areas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated exterior washdown of very large diesel-hydraulic machines caked in mud and rock dust. A tamper or ballast regulator is comparable in scale and soiling to a haul truck, requires no fine precision, and the wash bay presents the machine the same way, so performance carries over to washing on-track maintenance machines.

sources.system: KKE automatic train wash equipment (modular arches, drive-through)
sources.title: Train Wash Equipment with Reclaim Systems & Modular Arches - KKE Wash Systems United States
sources.claim: Automatic train wash plants wash rail vehicles through a fixed arch under sensor-triggered PLC control, with brush and touchless modules cleaning fronts, sides, rear and chassis as the vehicle passes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing rail rolling stock. On-track maintenance machines are rail vehicles of similar size that can be run over the same wash track, so a plant that washes locomotives and cars unattended substantiates exterior washdown of MOW machines in a purpose-built bay.

sources.title: Fives’ Smart Automation Solutions Division | RoboWash™ Robotic Industrial Parts Washer
sources.claim: Fives' RoboWash is a commercially sold robotic parts washer that manipulates a part with a 6-axis robot through pre-wash, high-pressure wash and drying chambers to clean complex components such as engine blocks, cylinder ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: degreasing and washing removed machine components in a shop. The greasy cast and machined parts handled (engine blocks, cases) match the pumps, valves, brackets and fittings a track machine operator cleans at the bench, and loading the part into the machine matches an E1 presentation.

sources.system: Downer/Deakin IISRI autonomous rollingstock cleaning robots
sources.developer: Downer Group with Deakin University IISRI
sources.title: Downer develops the world’s first fully autonomous rollingstock cleaning robots
sources.claim: Downer and Deakin University developed two autonomous rollingstock cleaning robots (a floor robot and a 6-DOF surface-cleaning manipulator) for train interiors in rail depots, with initial operational deployments planned from 2025; they clean passenger saloon floors, seats and windows alongside cleaning staff.
sources.transferJustification: Closest rail-sector cleaning robot to cab and detail cleaning, but it cleans open passenger saloon interiors in a depot, not a cramped machine cab, radiators, air cleaners or ballast-fouled workheads; cited to bound, not to substantiate, instance 1.

tasks.label: Observe leveling indicator arms to verify levelness and alignment of tracks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Production surfacing gang on Class I mainline: operator of a continuous-action tamper watches the levelling/lining indicator arms and shadowboard/ALC readouts as the machine works, verifying that achieved longitudinal level, cross-level (superelevation) and alignment match design/target values, pass after pass, under track-and-time authority.

Switch and spot tamping in yards, sidings and plant/industrial yards: operator verifies level and alignment through turnouts, crossings and short spot locations where geometry is complex, lifting references shift, and readings must be checked sleeper by sleeper.

Post-work quality verification before releasing track: reading the machine's recorder chart/measuring trolley output, or walking the tamped section with a track level or string line, to confirm cross-level and alignment are within tolerance and the section can be returned to service at speed.

New track construction or renewal worksite: verifying levelness and alignment on newly laid, unconsolidated track against design/survey references, amid construction conditions (loose ballast, temporary benchmarks, other machines and crews, mud, no established as-built geometry).

Adverse or degraded conditions on short-line, transit, quarry, sand/gravel pit and mine track: night work, rain/snow, dust, poor sightlines, tight curves, narrow gauge or badly worn track where indicator readings are hard to trust and must be cross-checked.

sources.system: Plasser & Theurer ALC automatic guiding computer / tamping machine measuring system
sources.title: Plasser & Theurer Technology — How do tamping machines work?
sources.claim: Tamping machines in worldwide commercial service measure longitudinal level, cross-level and alignment on board (steel chords, pendula, measuring wheels) and an automatic guiding computer (ALC) takes over control and computes the corrections, replacing the operator's reading of levelling indicator arms.

sources.system: Plasser & Theurer 3-point measuring method with ALC
sources.title: Plasser & Theurer aktuell 131 — Tamping technology: Key parameters under control
sources.claim: The on-board measuring system checks track geometry before, during and after tamping, with pendula measuring crossfall and steel chords providing the reference for longitudinal level and alignment, and is built to give precise data in rain, snow, vegetation or dust.

sources.system: Unimat 09-4x4/4S E³ with automatic guiding computer / EM120VT measuring vehicle
sources.title: Future track technology – NOW: Plasser & Theurer at iaf (Railway Gazette International)
sources.claim: Machine-to-machine workflow shown in service: measurement data feeds the tamper's automatic guiding computer, which guides tamping of plain line or turnouts, and the standards-conformant tamping report documenting achieved geometry is produced without operator input.

sources.system: Plasser DRP data recording processor / DAR 8-channel recorder
sources.title: Plasser & Theurer Technology — Documentation of the work results
sources.claim: On-board recording systems fitted to track laying and maintenance machines document the achieved track geometry and evaluate it in real time after the work — i.e. they perform and record the levelness/alignment verification; over 200 units supplied to more than 35 countries.

sources.system: Harsco Rail TX16 tamper with Callisto ProTamp and Jupiter II Control
sources.title: Harsco Rail Unveils New TX16 Tamper at Railway Interchange 2019 (Railway-News)
sources.claim: North American production-and-switch tampers carry an inertial non-contact measuring system that records track geometry and automatically generates best-fit and correction values, covering plain line and turnout work in yards and on mainline.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated measurement of track geometry from the tamper itself. It substantiates this observation/verification task because the parameters the operator reads off levelling indicator arms (longitudinal level, cross level, alignment) are the ones the machine senses and evaluates, on the same track at working speed.

sources.system: ENSCO Autonomous Track Geometry Measurement System (ATGMS)
sources.title: Automating geometry measurement offers real-time benefits (International Railway Journal)
sources.claim: Autonomous track geometry measurement systems installed on unattended revenue-service vehicles continuously measure track geometry (level, cross level, alignment) and flag defects; deployed on freight and passenger networks including in the United States since 2008.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended machine verification of track levelness and alignment on mainline track. The accepted output of this task is a judgement that level/cross-level/alignment are within tolerance, which these systems produce autonomously to recognised standards on the same track.

sources.system: BNSF automated/autonomous track geometry inspection cars
sources.developer: BNSF Railway (with ENSCO-type geometry measurement systems)
sources.title: Federal court orders FRA to allow BNSF Railway to expand track inspection program (Trains)
sources.claim: Automated track geometry inspection is the dominant means of finding geometry defects on a US Class I railroad, with regulators and courts addressing its substitution for human inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated detection of track geometry (surface, cross level, alignment) defects in place of human observation, on the same mainline track this occupation surfaces and then verifies.

sources.system: Tamping machines working in 'geometry/design mode' (Plasser & Theurer and Matisa tampers, Balfour Beatty fleet)
sources.developer: Plasser & Theurer / Matisa (operated by Balfour Beatty Rail)
sources.title: Tamping essential for good track alignment (Rail Engineer)
sources.claim: On renewal and new-construction worksites the tamper is loaded with the design geometry, makes its own measurement run of the site ... computes the deviation from design, so the verification of level and alignment is machine-performed on the worksite.

sources.system: Nordco/Harsco Mark IV production and switch tamper (Delta Leveling system, System V Lining)
sources.title: Mark IV - Production/Switch Tamper Rebuild Program (Nordco product profile)
sources.claim: US switch/production tampers used in yard and turnout work are fitted with automatic levelling systems using an infrared projector/shadowboard with receivers on rapid-response actuators plus an inclinometer for cross level, and a lining system with optional lasers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the machine's automatic levelling/lining sensing is precisely what the levelling indicator arms report; the operator's observation is of these sensors' output, and the electronic system measures and closes the loop on the same quantities in yard and switch work.

tasks.label: Operate single- or multiple-head spike pullers to pull old spikes from ties.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Class I mainline out-of-face tie renewal: operator rides a self-propelled two-rail multi-head spike puller (e.g., Nordco SP2R) ahead of the tie extractor, spotting claws over field and gauge spikes and pulling them from wood ties at hundreds of ties per hour inside a track-authority window; spikes are rusted, over-driven, bent or headless, ballast and weather vary, and missed or broken spikes must be re-attacked before the tie machine arrives.

Yard, siding and secondary main spot tie renewal by a section gang: single-head puller or hand-held hydraulic claw used to pull spikes on scattered defective ties, working around switches, parked cars, road crossings and yard clutter, moving the machine on and off track repeatedly.

Special trackwork: pulling spikes at turnouts, frogs, guard rails, joint bars, bridge timbers and grade-crossing panels, where claw heads cannot reach standard positions, requiring frequent repositioning, partial pulls and hand finishing.

Transit/commuter or passenger-territory night work: short single-track work window with adjacent live tracks, third rail or catenary, floodlighting, wet or cold conditions; spikes pulled on a limited number of ties then track restored to service before traffic resumes.

Industrial, quarry, mine or short-line branch track: light-section rail, ties buried in mud, spillage or vegetation, non-standard track held to no maintained standard; portable or excavator-mounted spike puller/claw used to pull old spikes for tie or rail replacement.

sources.title: Spiker Puller Two-Rail (SP2R) - Nordco
sources.claim: Nordco's current spike-pulling machines (SP2R two-rail puller) are operator-controlled hydraulic claw machines with manually adjustable claw height, width and spike-pattern alignment; no vision or autonomy is described for pulling.

sources.system: Nordco Nexxus AI Vision system / NXV Spiker
sources.title: Technology - Nordco
sources.claim: Nordco's AI vision automation is applied only to spike driving, on the NXV Spiker; the vision system detects track conditions, recognizes spiking patterns and aligns spikes, but no equivalent exists on its spike pullers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is spike driving on the same objects (cut spikes, tie plates, wood ties) on live track; it shows vision-guided workhead alignment is deployed, but no spike-extraction counterpart exists and the machine is not autonomous.

sources.title: Nordco Ships First 5 NXV Spiker Units - Nordco
sources.claim: The NXV Spiker was delivered to Class I railroads in May 2026; it reduces operators from three to one but retains an operator in the cab who initiates each tie's spiking cycle with a button push.
sources.transferJustification: Spike driving is the inverse operation on identical objects; even here a human operator remains in the cab and triggers each tie, so the state of the art in spike-handling automation is operator-in-the-loop, not autonomous.

sources.title: NXV Spiker | Automated Rail Spiking Machine by Nordco
sources.claim: The nxvspiker product site confirms operator-initiated cycles: one button push drives all spikes on a single ..., with a single operator running the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Same objects and precision as spike pulling, but the per-tie operator button push is step-by-step control, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of an extraction task.

sources.title: Rail Clip Driver Machine CD400 for Pandrol Fastenings | Pandrol
sources.claim: Automated fastener handling on track elsewhere (Pandrol clip drivers) is limited to sensor-triggered tool actuation on human-guided, self-propelled or walk-behind machines for elastic clips, not machine-autonomous fastener extraction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is clipping/de-clipping rail fasteners on track; it shows only sensor-triggered actuation while a worker positions and advances the machine, so it does not substantiate autonomous spike extraction.

sources.system: STAR-TRACK (Trivedi et al.) multi-robot track maintenance concept
sources.title: Importance and Applications of Robotic and Autonomous Systems (RAS) in Railway Maintenance Sector: A Review
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic removal of track fasteners exists only as research proposals and feasibility studies (e.g., the STAR-TRACK multi-robot concept for Shinkansen sleeper bolts), not as fielded systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous fastener removal from sleepers; it is a proposal/feasibility study rather than a demonstrated or deployed system, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Robel Rail Automation shows inspection vehicle - International Railway Journal
sources.claim: The most advanced automated on-track repair machine shown by a European MOW supplier is a wagon-mounted rail defect repair robot exhibited at a trade fair, addressing rail defects rather than spike or fastener extraction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is automated on-track repair; the objects (rail head defects, welding/milling) and tooling differ entirely from claw extraction of cut spikes, so performance does not carry over.

tasks.label: Grind ends of new or worn rails to attain smooth joints, using portable grinders.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Finish-grinding a fresh aluminothermic (thermite) field weld on open main or branch line: shear/rough-grind the weld collar, then profile-grind railhead crown and gauge corners to straightedge tolerance with a portable hydraulic or petrol profile grinder, outdoors on ballast in a limited track window, weather and lighting as found.

Grinding battered, lipped or mismatched rail ends at bolted joints and welds inside a railroad yard, industrial/plant yard or transit yard: track owned and controlled by the institution, graded flat working surfaces, standard rail sections, easy machine and crew access.

Deburring and chamfering ends of new or freshly saw-cut rails during rail laying/relay work in the field: rail strings and plug rails on the ballast shoulder or just placed in track, burrs and saw lips removed with a portable grinder before joint bars or welding.

Weld finishing inside a rail welding plant or CWR/porta-plant line: flash-butt welds on rails moving along a roller line are sheared and then ground/polished to profile, plus rail-end preparation grinding before welding; workpieces are fixtured and presented by the line.

Grinding rail ends and welds at turnouts, frogs, crossing diamonds, guard/restraining rail, grade crossings, tunnels and third-rail transit territory, and on quarry/mine plant track: confined access, complex geometry, often night possessions.

sources.title: Robots Repair Railway Tracks (FANUC press release)
sources.claim: ROBEL Rail Automation's Robot is a rail-wagon-mounted pair of FANUC arms that detects rail and point defects and repairs them by automatic welding, milling and grinding; first prototypes are running on European networks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: localised rail defect repair. Its final step is robotic grinding of the railhead running surface and gauge corner back to profile on rail in track — same workpiece, same millimetre tolerance and same setting as grinding rail ends/welds smooth at a joint.

sources.developer: ROBEL Rail Automation with ProRail, Strukton Rail, VolkerRail
sources.title: Rail welding robot makes 'tangible progress' - Railway Gazette International
sources.claim: The ROBEL welding robot works in track at night and in bad weather on plain line rails and switch components; eight welds it made have been monitored in service for nearly a year on the Dutch network.

tasks.label: Clean, grade, or level ballast on railroad tracks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Production surfacing on a Class I / regional main or branch line: operator runs a ballast regulator (shoulder and centre plows, wings, broom) behind the tie gang and tamper, redistributing ballast from over-full shoulders to lean spots, dressing the ballast section to the railroad's design profile and brooming ballast off tie tops, working under track authority in a work window in all weather.

Production tamping/surfacing on main or branch line: operator runs a continuous-action or switch tamper that lifts, lines and packs (levels) ballast under ties over plain line and through turnouts, referencing design or relative track geometry, in a limited possession window.

Ballast cleaning: operator runs an undercutter/shoulder ballast cleaner over fouled track — excavating the fouled ballast, screening it, returning clean stone and disposing of spoil, coordinating with spoil and ballast cars, avoiding buried cables, signal foundations and drainage, on main line under possession.

Yard, siding and terminal trackage: leveling and grading ballast with an on-track regulator or small tamper around yard tracks, sidings and turnouts inside railroad-controlled premises, with tighter clearances, more switches and more frequent obstacles than plain line.

Spot/hand and hi-rail work: shoveling and leveling ballast at grade crossings, switch points, bridge approaches and platform edges; clearing ballast out of flangeways, switch rods and drainage; spot ballast grading on quarry, mine and plant-yard spurs where the track is rough, fouled and shared with road traffic or plant equipment.

tasks.label: Weld sections of track together, such as switch points and frogs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field aluminothermic (thermite) weld joining rail ends on mainline or branch line: rail cut and gapped, ends cleaned and aligned, moulds luted and clamped, preheat, crucible ignited and tapped, weld sheared hot, then ground to running profile — done outdoors on ballast in a track possession window, all weather.

In-track repair/build-up welding of special trackwork: worn or battered manganese frogs, crossing diamonds and switch points in turnouts on operating mainline or yard track — defect removal (plasma/grinding), multi-pass build-up welding with heat control, then grinding to gauge and profile.

Mobile electric flash-butt welding to join rail sections into continuous welded rail during in-track construction, rail relay or short-plug defect repair: road-rail welder positioned over the joint, rail ends prepared and clamped, weld cycle run, flash sheared and joint ground.

Welding track sections in industrial plant yards, quarries, sand and gravel pits or mines: lighter or non-standard rail, crane rail and narrow-gauge track, cramped or cluttered surroundings, joints welded or built up with thermite or arc welding and dressed by hand.

In-track weld repair of rail running surface defects adjacent to welded joints — engine burns, rail-end batter, spalls and joint-bar-hole plugs — built up by arc welding and then reprofiled by grinding on mainline or yard track.

tasks.label: Spray ties, fishplates, or joints with oil to protect them from weathering.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-line (mainline/branch) track: worker walks a stretch or works off a hi-rail truck under track authority, spraying joint bars/fishplates, bolts and rail ends with oil or rust preventative; footing on ballast, varying curves, grades, weather, vegetation and remote locations.

Railroad or transit yard / terminal trackage: oiling joints, switch components, tie plates and ties across many parallel yard tracks; layout fixed and railroad-controlled, but cars may be present and crews work between tracks.
In-plant, quarry, mine or port trackage: spraying ties and joints on industrial track often embedded in pavement, buried in spilled material, muddy, congested with trucks and loaders.
Bridges, trestles, tunnels and elevated structure: oiling bridge ties/timbers, joint bars and fastenings with restricted footing, working at height or in confined clearances, limited access windows.
Section house / material yard prep: oiling new or reclaimed fishplates (joint bars), track bolts, tie plates and tie stock stacked on pallets or in piles before they are installed in track.

sources.system: ROBEL Rail Automation ROBOT (FANUC arms on rail wagon)
sources.title: Robel Rail Automation Uses FANUC Robots to Repair Railway Lines - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: ROBEL Rail Automation's ROBOT: two FANUC arms on a rail wagon that detect rail and switch (points) defects and repair them autonomously by welding, milling and grinding on in-track components.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is in-track rail/switch repair rather than oiling. Transfer holds because the objects are the same (rails, joints and switch components lying in ballasted track), the machine must autonomously locate the component and place a tool head on it, and weld/mill precision far exceeds the coarse coverage precision needed to coat a joint bar or tie with oil.

sources.developer: ROBEL Rail Automation GmbH (with ProRail, VolkerRail, Strukton Rail)
sources.title: A Bavarian startup is automating Europe's track maintenance - The Rail Agenda
sources.claim: The ROBEL Robot scans, mills, welds and grinds the rail without manual intervention; demonstrations were run on track at the Railcenter facility in Amersfoort, Netherlands, and it works night possession windows in rain and cold with a single operator supervising.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: autonomous perception and tool placement on in-track steel components in real railway conditions; applying an oil spray to the same components requires the same locate-and-apply capability at far lower precision.

sources.title: ROBOT Automated Switch and Infrastructure Maintenance | Railway-News
sources.claim: The ROBEL robotic unit is a self-contained container unit on a flat wagon that can be taken anywhere on the network and works full shifts in closed track in any weather, staffed by two workers.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the autonomous in-track working unit operates in a real, weather-exposed rail possession with only supervisory staffing; the treated components (rails, joints, switch parts) are the same ones this task oils.

It supplies the travel-and-position capability an oiling run needs (moving along track from component to component) in a railway setting, complementing the fixed-position welding robot evidence.

sources.system: Fraunhofer IPM green-detection system on herbicide spraying trains
