sources.transferJustification: Related task is sensor-triggered spraying of liquid along track from a rail vehicle. It corroborates machine-controlled spraying in the rail corridor, but the vehicle is crewed so overall autonomy is not established and it is not used to support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: String and attach wire-guidelines machine to rails so that tracks or rails can be aligned or leveled.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Class I / regional mainline production surfacing: at the start of a work block (and after each obstruction) the operator sets the tamping machine's guideline reference on the rails — lowering the measuring trolleys that carry the tensioned chord wire / optical beam onto the rail head and engaging the roller lifting-lining clamps — so the machine can level and line ballasted track. Outdoors on open-line right-of-way, ballast underfoot, all weather.

Hand-set guideline references outside the machine along the open line ahead of the surfacing gang: clamping a stringline / shadow-board or laser target to the rail at fixed points (bridge approaches, platform edges, grade crossings, tie-in transitions), walking the ballast between points, and adjusting for obstructions and traffic protection.

Stringlining a curve by hand: clamping a 62-ft chord wire (or cord device) to the gauge side of the high rail, moving it station to station, reading mid-ordinates and marking throw amounts on ties so the curve can be realigned. Remote or spot locations, often without a production machine present.

Yard / plant-yard / quarry / transit maintenance-yard spot surfacing: stringing line and attaching the reference to rails for a small tamper or for jacking and lining a short section of yard track, in a confined, institution-controlled yard with fixed layout and standard track.

Turnouts, crossings and other complex trackwork: setting and re-setting the guideline reference on the rails through switch points, frogs, guard rails and closure rails, where the measuring system must clear obstacles and the design geometry is fixed.

sources.system: Unimat 09-4x4/4S E³ autonomous tamping machine (Plasser SmartTamping)
sources.title: Autonomous tamping machine demonstration — Railway Gazette International
sources.claim: Plasser & Theurer and contractor Eiffage Rail publicly demonstrated a Unimat 09-4x4/4S E³ continuous-action tamping machine working autonomously through a turnout on a demonstration siding adjacent to an operating DB InfraGo line, with no operator in the tamping (work) cab; demonstrated features included automated positioning of the work units and machine assessment of inner and outer absolute track geometry — i.e. the machine established and used its own alignment/level reference on the rails.
sources.transferJustification: The task's output is a guideline reference held against the rails so track can be aligned/levelled; on a tamper this reference is the machine-carried chord/optical guideline and the rail-gripping lining clamps, which this machine positioned and used without staff in the work ....

sources.system: Plasser SmartTamping / TampingAssistant on Unimat 09-4x4/4S E³

sources.claim: Plasser & Theurer's own account of the IAF 2025 demonstration confirms the tamping machine worked a turnout fully automatically with no staff in the work cab, and that its assistance suite automatically calculates and positions the working units (tamping ..., etc.) for each position.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: the rail-referenced guideline/measuring system and rail-gripping lining units are what the human task strings and attaches; here they are set and operated by the machine itself.

sources.system: Tamping machine three-trolley chord measurement / guidance system (generic modern tampers, e.g. Plasser)
sources.developer: Plasser & Theurer / Matisa / others (described by Rail Engineer)
sources.title: In case you missed it - Tamping essential for good track alignment — Rail Engineer
sources.claim: Modern high-performance tamping machines carry the wire guideline themselves: three trolleys running on the rails (front, measuring, rear) with a tensioned wire or light beam stretched between them, whose deviations feed the machine's control system to level and line the track; guidance computers compute the design line over a site up to a mile long, with operators inputting fixed points.
sources.transferJustification: Directly describes the machine form of this task: a wire guideline strung on trolleys attached to (running on) the rails so track can be aligned and levelled. Cited as description of the mechanism; the crewed machine itself is not treated as autonomous.

sources.title: Plasser & Theurer: Machine — Plasser SmartTamping: Plasser TampingAssistant
sources.claim: Plasser's TampingAssistant automatically positions the machine's working units (tamping unit, roller ... that grip the rail, lifting hook, third-rail lifting unit, dynamic stabiliser, sleeper-end consolidator), with the operator confirming or adjusting the recommended actions; the product is offered commercially and supports complex turnout tamping.
sources.transferJustification: Attaching the lining/levelling machine's units to the rails is the machine analogue of 'attach ... machine to rails'; operator confirmation each step means this item is treated as supervised, not decisive for positive judgments.

sources.title: Federal Register :: Track Geometry Measurement System (TGMS) Inspections
sources.claim: Autonomous track geometry measurement systems (ATGMS) are recognised by FRA as automated inspection equipment mounted on on-track equipment, in some cases ..., conducting geometry inspections with minimal direct human involvement — producing the alignment and surface data (62-ft chord equivalents) that hand stringlining yields, but without placing any physical guideline on the rails.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: measuring track alignment/level for realignment. It substitutes the measurement purpose but performs no stringing or attachment of a guideline to rails, so it is cited as context only and is not used to support any positive judgment.

tasks.label: Push controls to close grasping devices on track or rail sections so that they can be raised or moved.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mainline/branch tie-replacement gang: operator on a tie crane or boom-mounted grapple closes tie tongs on worn crossties skewed and half-buried in ballast after they are pulled from track, and on new ties in strung-out piles along the right-of-way; ballast surface, curves, weather, crew and other machines working close by inside a track-authority work window.

Open-line rail handling: closing rail tongs/clamps from a rail-bound crane, excavator or rail-lifter on 39-ft jointed rail, plug rails, or continuous welded rail strings lying in the ballast or on the shoulder, so they can be raised, swung into position beside the ties, or loaded onto rail racks; uneven ballast, ditches, brush, grade crossings.

Yard and materials-yard handling: in a railroad maintenance-of-way materials yard, plant yard, quarry or mine yard, closing grapples, tongs or magnet/clamp attachments on stacked and racked material - rail bundles, tie packs, tie plates, panels - to unload flatcars and trucks and re-stack in fixed racks; fixed layout, controlled access, standard equipment.

New construction / panel and turnout work: closing grapples or lifting clamps on prefabricated track panels, turnout segments, or rail strings on a new line, transit project or industrial spur, and setting them on prepared subgrade; site layout changes day to day, other trades and equipment present.

Emergency and spot repair: night or bad-weather response to a broken rail, derailment cleanup, or grade-crossing renewal; gripping and lifting rail pieces, ties and debris in confined, cluttered conditions near road traffic or damaged track, working quickly to restore the line.

sources.system: Künz Automated Stacking Cranes (ASC) with automated spreader
sources.title: Spreader - Kuenz
sources.claim: Künz fully Automated Stacking Cranes autonomously engage a spreader's twistlocks on containers and move them in seaport container yards without human involvement, i.e. a machine-controlled close-grip / raise / move cycle on heavy steel loads in an institution-controlled outdoor yard.

Closing a spreader's grasping devices on a 20-40 t rigid steel load so it can be raised and moved is the same grip-lift-move cycle as closing rail tongs on rail, panels or tie packs; loads sit in managed stack positions in a fixed-layout, access-controlled outdoor yard, matching the materials-yard instance in object weight, rigidity and required alignment tolerance.

sources.claim: Nabors' RZR rig-floor robotics module autonomously performs repetitive pipe-handling tasks (connections, tripping in and out of ..., offline stand building) and has been used on a retrofitted rig that drilled multiple horizontal wells for ....

sources.claim: Track-renewal trains such as the Matisa UM P95 operated by SPITZKE take up old sleepers and lay new ones through a mechanised on-board unit in continuous working action on open line, though grasping is a fixed-geometry mechanism and the machine's material gantries remain operator-controlled.

Autonomy of the grasping function is not established - the description is a vendor/operator claim about a fixed-cycle mechanism on a manned train - so it is treated as teleoperated and cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Harsco Rail Tie Finder / machine vision automated track maintenance (Drone Tamper lineage)
sources.title: Harsco Rail Advances Track Maintenance and Repair Technology
sources.claim: Harsco Rail's machine-vision system lets a track maintenance machine move itself to a work location, judge tie/fastener condition and perform the work with little or ... - field automation in the rail corridor, but for positioning and tamping/fastener work rather than grappling and lifting rail or ties.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated track maintenance on the right-of-way. It shows what rail-corridor autonomy currently covers - self-positioning and tool work on the track structure - and does not extend to closing grapples on rail or tie sections and lifting them.

tasks.label: Adjust controls of machines that spread, shape, raise, level, or align track, according to specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Production surfacing on Class I / mainline track: operator sits in the work cab of a continuous-action production tamper and adjusts lift, line, cross-level and squeeze controls to bring tangent and curved track to design geometry, running miles of track during a several-hour track window behind a ballast drop, with the railroad holding track authority.

Ballast regulator work on mainline and yard track: operator adjusts plow, wing and broom controls to spread and shape the ballast section, dress shoulders, fill cribs and sweep tie tops to the railroad's standard ballast profile, ahead of and behind the tamper.

Switch/turnout and spot surfacing in yards, interlockings, industrial spurs, transit track: operator repeatedly repositions and adjusts tamping/lifting units around switch rods, guard rails, signal cables, frogs and grade crossings on jointed or lower-class track, with frequent set-ups and short work segments.

Ballast distribution along a work zone: operator controls hopper/ballast-car gates, doors or conveyors to spread specified ballast quantities at specified locations (curves, tunnels, bridge approaches) ahead of tie gangs or surfacing programs on the railroad's mainline.

Capital renewal or new-construction site: operator raises, lines and surfaces freshly laid track and shapes ballast behind tie/rail gangs, undercutters or a renewal train, on a torn-up site with temporary conditions, disturbed subgrade, other machines and crews moving about, and no reliable existing geometry reference.

Emergency and degraded-condition work: restoring surface and alignment at washouts, mud spots, heaved or storm-damaged track and post-derailment locations, with debris, water, skewed or broken ties, no design data, adverse weather, often with small hi-rail or hand-guided equipment.

sources.system: Unimat 09-4x4/4S E³ with Plasser SmartTamping / TampingAssistant

tasks.label: Paint railroad signs, such as speed limits or gate-crossing warnings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-place repainting of a lineside sign on the mainline right-of-way (milepost, whistle post, permanent speed-restriction board). Worker reaches the location by hi-rail or on foot under track authority, clears brush, wire-brushes rust and flaking paint from the metal or wood post and board, brushes or spray-cans a background coat and refreshes stenciled numerals/letters. Uneven ballast and embankment, weather, live-track protection.

Batch painting and stenciling of new or refurbished sign boards, posts and blades at the section house / MOW paint shed before installation: degrease, prime, roll or spray the background color, mask and stencil numerals and warning text, dry and stack. Controlled indoor shop space with benches and a spray area.

Painting grade-crossing warning items in place at a public road crossing: crossbuck and advance-warning sign posts, red/white stripes on gate arms, signal mast bases and cabinets. Alongside roadway traffic with flagging, on shoulder or gravel, exposed to weather and public passers-by.

Painting signage and marked hardware in place inside a railroad yard or terminal: yard speed and clearance signs, derail and blue-flag signs, switch stand targets and number plates. Railroad-controlled premises, graded and drivable surfaces, standard sign types, restricted access.

Small touch-up work incidental to other track work: spot-priming rust bleed-through, re-blacking faded numerals, covering graffiti or overspray on a sign already in service, using a brush or aerosol can from the truck, at scattered locations along the line.

tasks.label: Drive graders, tamping machines, brooms, or ballast spreading machines to redistribute gravel or ballast between rails.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Production surfacing/tie gang on a Class I freight mainline: operator runs a production tamping machine (e.g., Plasser 09-3X, Harsco Mark IV/TX16) for a shift under track-and-time authority, raising, lining and tamping ballast under successive ties for miles of track, working ahead of/behind other gang machines, in heat, cold, dust and darkness.

Ballast regulator/broom operator on mainline behind ballast dumps and tampers: plowing ballast from the crib and shoulder, setting wings to shape the shoulder profile, brooming stone off ties, rail seats and fastenings, and lifting wings/plows clear of grade crossings, switch rods, cable troughs, signal apparatus, platforms and bridge decks.

Tamping and regulating in a classification yard, terminal or industrial/plant yard track: many turnouts and short tracks, tight curves, cars and equipment standing nearby, walkways and crossings, workers on the ground, frequent repositioning and coordination with yard switching moves.

Spot maintenance on branch, short-line or lower-class track: small switch tamper, hi-rail broom or small regulator sent to correct localized surface defects, dress ballast at a turnout, road crossing or bridge approach; ad-hoc set-on/set-off, no pre-measured geometry, varying ballast condition and fouling.

Transit/commuter track maintenance in a short night window: tamping and regulating ballasted track in tunnels, on elevated structure or through stations, with third rail or catenary, tight clearances, cable runs and a hard hand-back deadline.

Grader, dozer or spreader used to redistribute gravel/ballast at a public grade crossing rebuild, a storm washout, a new industrial spur or a quarry/pit track: surface taken as found, road traffic and flaggers, mud, no established profile reference.

tasks.label: Turn wheels of machines, using lever controls, to adjust guidelines for track alignments or grades, following specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Production out-of-face surfacing on a Class I mainline: riding a production tamper/liner in a surfacing gang, the operator sets and continuously adjusts the leveling (grade) and lining (alignment) reference - shadowboard/chord-wire/laser targets and lift-and-slew values - through tangents, curves, spirals and run-offs to fixed points, following the engineering surfacing spec, under traffic windows, weather and varying ballast.

Surfacing turnouts, crossings, insulated joints, bridge approaches and other restricted-lift locations on the main line: guides and reference points must be re-set repeatedly for third-rail lifting, limited lift/slew at fixed points and switch components, to a spec that tolerates little error.

Spot maintenance on branch, short-line or industrial-lead track: raising a mud spot, correcting a low joint or a misalignment with a small or older tamper, reference set from hand-driven grade stakes, string line and hand level, often with no design data and with grade crossings and rough terrain nearby.

Surfacing and lining yard, plant-yard, quarry or mine track and transit-system yard track: switch/yard tamper working tight, congested layouts with poor ballast and no survey data, references adjusted by eye against yard clearances and existing structures.

Ballast regulating/profiling and companion grade work on the main line after surfacing: setting and adjusting plow, wing and profile guides so the ballast section and shoulder are dressed to the specified profile and cross-level references.

sources.system: ALC automatic guiding computer on Plasser & Theurer tamping machines
sources.date: product page current 2026; ALC standard equipment on 09-series tampers for decades
sources.title: Plasser & Theurer Technology - How do tamping machines work?
sources.claim: Plasser & Theurer production tampers carry the ALC automatic guiding computer, which takes over control of the machine's level and alignment correction during work - the machine itself sets and holds the alignment/grade reference the operator would otherwise dial in - on plain line and in turnouts.
sources.transferJustification: Direct: the task is adjusting the machine's alignment/grade guidelines to specification; the ALC computes and applies those level and alignment corrections in place of the operator's manual reference setting.

sources.title: Plasser & Theurer - Digital equipment: SmartALC
sources.claim: SmartALC computes the lifting and lining target values automatically, either from a measuring run (compensation method) or from known absolute/design track geometry (precision method), and includes automatic localisation of isolated spot defects.
sources.transferJustification: Direct: 'following specifications' corresponds to the precision method, in which design geometry is the input and the machine derives and applies the alignment/grade correction values itself.

sources.title: Plasser American: 09-2X DYNACAT
sources.claim: A Plasser American 09-2X DYNACAT switch/production tamper completed an autonomous switch-tamping cycle on a US Class I freight main line, with the TampingAssistant/TampingReport suite logging unit positions and obstacle detections.

tasks.label: Operate tie-adzing machines to cut ties and permit insertion of fishplates that hold rails.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Production tie gang on mainline track: after new wood crossties are inserted, the operator runs a self-propelled ride-on kribber-adzer (e.g., Knox Kershaw KKA-1050, Nordco dual-crawler adzer) down the line under track time, cutting a level rail-seat on each new tie so tie plates bear flat; hundreds to thousands of ties per shift, in ballast, dust, heat/cold, with a crew working nearby.

Rail relay / regauging or plate-change job on main or branch line: rail lifted or one rail removed, plates pulled, and existing in-service ties adzed in place to remove plate-cut, weathering and crushed fiber before new plates are set; depth of cut judged tie by tie against decayed, split, hard or spike-riddled wood.

Spot tie renewal in a yard, siding, or industrial/plant/quarry/mine track: a few dozen ties at a time, tight clearances, switches, road crossings and paved-in track; adzing done with a small ride-on or portable powered adzer, sometimes finished with a hand adze, by a small crew.

Turnout and bridge-timber work: adzing switch ties and bridge timbers of varying width and length, with irregular plate/riser patterns, skewed plate positions, guard rail and frog hardware in the way; largely hand-guided adzer work at awkward angles.

Off-track preparation before installation: ties, switch timbers and bridge timbers adzed (and usually bored) on a shop/plant line — conveyor-fed through an adzer-borer at a tie plant or company shop, or staged at a material yard — so that plates seat flat when the timbers reach the job.

sources.date: 2023 (product listing; K2-Industry line in market since ~2019)
sources.title: 5-axis machining center - K2-Industry series - Hans Hundegger
sources.claim: Hundegger's K2-Industry is a commercially sold 5-axis CNC timber machining centre that mills, planes, saws and drills structural timber beams automatically from stored data, with no manual measuring, marking or setup between parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: CNC machining of structural timber. Adzing is milling a flat rail-seat recess of specified depth and position into a 7x9 in wooden beam; a CNC timber centre planes/mills/bores beams of that cross-section to millimetre tolerance, so the cutting operation, the workpiece material and the required precision all carry over when the tie is presented to the machine.

sources.title: New & Used Hundegger for sale (Machinio)
sources.claim: Hundegger machine lines include fully automatic timber infeed, loading cross conveyors and automatic four-sided planing lines, i.e. the workpiece is presented, clamped and fed to the cutting heads by the equipment rather than by a person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated presentation and planing of beams. It establishes the E1 counterfactual condition — the timber arrives fixtured and conveyor-fed — which is exactly how a purpose-built setting would present a crosstie for adzing.

sources.title: … and it can also do the joining (timber-online.net)
sources.claim: A production timber company installed and operates a Hundegger K2 Industry joinery machine for series production of machined timber components, showing the technology is in real production use, not only demonstrated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial CNC beam machining. Confirms deployment of the machine class cited for the E1 counterfactual (milling/boring wooden beams to spec on a fixtured, conveyor-fed line).

sources.claim: Purpose-built crosstie adzing-and-boring machines exist that move crossties automatically along a conveyor travel path through the frame, with motor-driven adzing heads forming the rail seats and boring heads drilling spike holes.

sources.system: crosstie plant adzing and boring process
sources.developer: US wood-preserving / crosstie industry (documented in Managing Treated Wood, ch. 2)

sources.title: Knox Kershaw KKA-1050 Kribber Adzer - Relam Inc.
sources.claim: The state-of-the-art field tie adzer is a self-propelled on-track machine run continuously by an on-board operator; it clears cribs and adzes ties but has no autonomous mode.

sources.title: Adzing Machines • AMECO - American Equipment Company
sources.claim: Ride-on tie adzers sold for US track maintenance seat an operator on the machine who steers and controls the cutter head along the right of way.

sources.title: NXV Spiker - Nordco
sources.claim: The most automated in-track workhead machine now shipping — an AI-vision spiker — still requires a single on-board operator who triggers each tie's work cycle by button; no in-track maintenance-of-way machine works the ties unattended.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided workhead positioning on in-track ties (spiking). It is the closest field analogue to autonomous adzing and shows that even the most automated on-track workhead is operator-riding and per-tie triggered, so no field system supports an E2 judgment.

tasks.label: Drive trucks to transport crews, materials, and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Drive a loaded/empty vacuum pumper truck from the company shop over suburban and rural public roads to a residential customer, then maneuver up a narrow gravel or paved driveway, past parked cars, low branches and soft lawn, and spot the truck within hose reach of the septic tank access.

Drive a heavy combination sewer cleaner / hydro-jet truck through city traffic to a street or alley work site (manhole, catch basin, commercial building lateral), park in the lane or at the curb, and reposition between adjacent manholes during the shift.

Drive the loaded tanker from the last job over local roads and highway to a wastewater treatment plant, transfer station or land-application site, enter the facility, queue, and position at the dump station; then return to the yard.

Drive a service pickup or box van carrying a two-person crew plus tools, camera/locator equipment, pipe, gravel or a trailered mini-excavator from the shop to several job sites in a day, including highway segments, gas stops and parking at customer premises.

Drive the truck within an institution-controlled site — municipal treatment plant, industrial facility, mobile-home park, school or hospital campus — moving between lift stations, manholes or grease interceptors on the premises along a fixed internal road layout.

tasks.label: Inspect manholes to locate sewer line stoppages.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Emergency/complaint response in a residential street: crew sets cones in live traffic, pries open cast-iron covers at the upstream and downstream manholes of the suspect run, and checks whether each manhole is surcharged with sewage or running clear to isolate the blocked segment; an answer is needed within the hour so the jetting crew can clear it.

Routine/preventive survey ahead of a scheduled cleaning route: crew pops covers at each manhole along 8-15 in. mains in streets, alleys and rear easements, looks down the line for grease, roots, sediment and slow flow, and records which segments are approaching stoppage.

Deploying an inspection camera/robot through an open manhole to pinpoint the obstruction's location and distance down a partially flowing municipal line (investigating repeat backups, or verifying after jetting); truck or portable kit at the manhole in a public street or easement.

Manholes on institutional or industrial premises - wastewater plant, university campus, airport, hospital, industrial park - where access is controlled, the layout is mapped, covers are maintained and no public traffic is present.

Private-property collection systems: manholes on the private mains of an apartment complex, mobile-home park, shopping centre or restaurant row; grounds cluttered with parked cars, landscaping and paved-over covers, line 6-10 in.

Confined-space entry: crew gas-tests, sets a tripod/harness, and a worker descends into a deep or junction manhole to inspect the benching, channel and incoming pipe openings for the obstruction that cannot be seen or reached from the surface.

sources.title: SOLO® Pipeline Inspection Robot CCTV | RedZone Robotics
sources.claim: RedZone Robotics' SOLO is a commercially deployed, unmanned autonomous crawler for 8-12 in. sewer mains: a crew opens a manhole and launches it, after which it traverses the segment on its own, records 360-degree video, detects and attempts to pass obstructions, and returns to the launch manhole. Its spec sheet limits it to water level 0-1/4 of the pipe.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous in-pipe condition inspection launched from a manhole; it transfers to locating stoppages because the same run through the same 8-12 in. main between the same two manholes records debris, roots and the point at which the pipe is obstructed.

sources.system: SOLO autonomous robots at DC Water
sources.title: Impacts of Autonomous Sewer Inspection at DC Water — Trenchless Technology
sources.claim: DC Water operationally uses SOLO autonomous robots across its small-diameter collection system; blockages, sediment build-up and flow ... among the operational conditions the robot data establishes, without human entry.
sources.transferJustification: Condition-assessment output explicitly includes locating blockages and sediment in the same municipal sewer mains a servicer checks from manholes.

sources.title: Unmanned Sewer Inspection Robot — Lane Rental Industry Publication
sources.claim: Thames Water/TfL field trial of SOLO in London streets: the robot autonomously surveys manhole-to-manhole and returns, but the human crew performs the site work - traffic management, opening the cover, deploying and retrieving the robot, replacing the cover - and deployments were aborted where debris, grease, roots or seized/buried covers were encountered.
sources.transferJustification: Same setting and purpose (street manholes on a live network, blockage hotspot surveys); documents that in-pipe travel is autonomous while manhole access remains manual crew work.

sources.title: Vertue™ | RedZone Robotics
sources.claim: RedZone's Vertue is a tripod-and-winch multi-sensor payload lowered into a manhole to capture 360-degree imagery, laser data and 3D models of the chamber; the crew transports, sets up and lowers it, and no autonomous field operation is documented.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the manhole-interior inspection step; cited to show the available manhole-structure tool is crew-deployed with autonomy not established.

sources.title: Transforming Wastewater Inspections: Drones vs. Traditional Methods - Coptrz
sources.claim: Flyability's Elios 3 is used for sewer and confined-space inspection through manholes, but it is flown by a human pilot from outside the manhole with live video, with autonomy limited to stabilisation and return-to-home behaviours.
sources.transferJustification: Same access route (manhole) and purpose (seeing inside the structure/line to find obstructions); cited as a negative because the method is piloted.

sources.title: Bandicoot – The Manhole Cleaning Robot | Grand Challenges
sources.claim: Genrobotics' Bandicoot is deployed in city streets to enter manholes and pull out the solid material causing blockages, but it is a remote-operated machine run from a control panel at the surface.
sources.transferJustification: Closest system that works inside street manholes on blockages; cited as a negative because a human operator controls it throughout.

tasks.label: Operate sewer cleaning equipment, including power rodders, high-velocity water jets, sewer flushers, bucket machines, wayne balls, and vac-alls.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine municipal sanitary sewer main cleaning: crew drives a combination jet/vac truck to a manhole in a city street, sets traffic control, opens the manhole, feeds jet hose upstream through an 8-15 in. line, jets grease/roots/sand back to the manhole, then vacuums the debris out with the boom hose and hauls it off. Live traffic, weather, unknown debris and pipe condition.

Building drain and lateral cleaning at a private home or small business: power rodder/sectional cable machine or small jetter run through a basement cleanout, roof vent, or yard cleanout to clear a 3-6 in. line of roots, grease, wipes or scale; cramped, cluttered, occupied space; camera used to confirm the line runs clear.

Storm drain, catch basin and culvert cleaning with a vac-all/vacuum truck: street-side basins full of grit, leaves, trash, bricks and standing water; hose worked by hand into the sump, debris vacuumed to the truck body, grate replaced, spoil hauled to a dump site.

Septic tank pumping/servicing at a residence: locate and dig out the lid in a yard, open the tank, insert the vacuum hose, break up and pump the scum and sludge with the vac truck, backflush/rinse, inspect baffles and effluent filter, replace lid and backfill.

Line cleaning inside an industrial or institutional facility: jetting process lines, floor drains, wet wells, grease interceptors and digester/tank lines at a wastewater plant, food plant, hospital or school; controlled premises, standard fixtures and access points, scheduled work.

sources.title: Kerala engineers create Bandicoot that cleans manholes and sewers with precision

sources.title: SOLO® Pipeline Inspection Robot CCTV | RedZone Robotics
sources.claim: RedZone Robotics' SOLO robot autonomously traverses live municipal sewer mains after launch through a manhole and is used in production programs (e.g., DC Water, Pittsburgh), but its function is CCTV inspection, not cleaning or debris removal.

Cited as the ceiling of demonstrated field autonomy in sewers - navigation and imaging only, with no jetting, rodding or vacuuming - so it does not substantiate completion of the cleaning task at E2/E3.

sources.title: Crude Oil Tank Cleaning | Oreco
sources.claim: Oreco's BLABO system performs non-man-entry cleaning and sludge removal from large storage tanks with jet nozzles and closed-loop pumping, described as automated and requiring few operators; the degree of machine autonomy versus operator control from the control unit is not established in the sources found.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: emptying and cleaning a sludge-filled tank without human entry, analogous to septic tank pumping; autonomy is unclear, so it is treated as teleoperated and does not support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Clean and repair septic tanks, sewer lines, or related structures such as manholes, culverts, and catch basins.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential septic tank service at a private home: locate and hand-dig/uncover the lid, break the crust, insert the vacuum hose from the pump truck, pump sludge and scum, backflush and rinse the tank, inspect/clean the effluent filter and baffles, reseal the lid and backfill, haul the load to disposal. Yard is uneven, tanks are of varied age and design, access is often tight.

Municipal sanitary or storm sewer main cleaning: set traffic control in a street, open a manhole, feed a hydro-jet hose with root/grease nozzles from manhole to manhole, flush debris to the downstream manhole, vacuum out sand, grit, grease and roots with a combination truck, verify with a push camera or CCTV. Buried lines of unknown condition, live flow, variable depth and offsets.

Clearing a blocked building sewer lateral or drain line at a home or small business: locate the cleanout (basement, crawlspace, or yard), run a cable machine or mini-jetter, cut roots or pull the obstruction, run a camera to confirm and locate the defect, clean up sewage spillage inside the occupied building.

Catch basin, culvert and storm structure cleaning: roadside work with a vacuum truck boom, breaking up compacted sediment, removing leaves, trash and rocks by boom, shovel and rake, clearing culvert inlets/outlets in ditches, replacing grates, disposing of the spoils.

Cleaning at a controlled facility: lift station wet well, grease interceptor at a restaurant chain commissary or food plant, or process/drain lines inside a wastewater treatment plant or industrial site, with plant staff controlling access, fixed known layout and standard fittings.

Repair work: rehabilitating a deteriorated manhole (patching walls with mortar, sealing infiltration, resetting frame/chimney), patching septic tank walls or replacing damaged drain tile, or excavating and replacing a broken section of underground pipe / installing a spot liner or CIPP patch.

sources.title: Genrobotics Innovations: Leading Robotic Sanitation Safety & Automation in India 2025
sources.claim: Bandicoot, the most widely fielded manhole-cleaning robot (hundreds of units across Indian municipalities), is lowered into the manhole and its arm, grabber and shovel actions are driven by a human operator at a joystick control panel outside the manhole; it is teleoperated, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task: cleaning manholes/sewer structures. Cited to show the state of the art in this exact work is operator-driven teleoperation, which cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Solinas Integrity News: Sanitation 2.0 with Robots
sources.claim: HomoSEP, the leading septic-tank desludging robot, is deployed in 15-30 Indian cities as truck-mounted equipment that homogenises and pumps septic tank sludge under operator control; no autonomous septic pump-out cycle is documented.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task (septic tank cleaning). Autonomy is not established — the machine is set up and driven by a crew — so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Collect 6x the inspection data with SOLO - RedZone Robotics
sources.claim: The one genuinely autonomous sewer robot in routine municipal service, RedZone's SOLO, is an untethered inspection crawler: it drives manhole-to-manhole collecting CCTV data but performs no cleaning, desludging or repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous sewer inspection. It shows autonomous navigation of live sewers is feasible, but it carries no cleaning, cutting, vacuum or repair payload, so it does not transfer to cleaning or repairing the pipe.

sources.system: Re-Gen Robotics no-man-entry tank cleaning robots
sources.title: Re-Gen Robotics launches ‘No Man Entry’ robotic tank cleaning company
sources.claim: Robotic 'no man entry' cleaning of large sludge-filled tanks — the closest industrial analogue to desludging a septic tank — is performed by remote-controlled machines driven by a three-man crew, over dozens of days per tank.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing sludge from a confined storage tank, comparable material and confined-space access to septic tank pump-out. It is fully teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment even in a purpose-built setting.

sources.system: Robotic cutting / milling robots for sewer rehabilitation

sources.title: Robotic Cutting - MJ Pipeline Solutions
sources.claim: In-pipe sewer repair robots (root/lateral cutters, milling and patching robots used for trenchless rehabilitation) are driven step by step by an operator watching a camera monitor at the surface.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the repair portion of the task (removing obstructions and reinstating laterals inside sewer pipes). Cited to establish that this work is continuous teleoperation, which cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: AI Driven 'Project Shudh' To Abolish Manual Scavenging
sources.claim: The most recent claim of autonomous sewer cleaning, Project SHUDH in Hyderabad, is a utility pilot demonstration launched in 2026; press accounts describe a demonstration with 'minimal human interference' rather than documented autonomous completion of cleaning jobs at production quality.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task (manhole and pipeline cleaning). Autonomy rests on launch-event press claims with no technical documentation of unattended operation, so it is treated as unclear and cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Measure excavation sites, using plumbers' snakes, tapelines, or lengths of cutting heads within sewers, and mark areas for digging.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential sewer lateral backup/collapse: worker opens a 4" cleanout in the yard or basement, runs a drain cable or push camera, notes footage on the cable/counter where the root mass, break or belly is, walks the yard with a sonde locator or tapes the offset from the house, and spray-paints or flags the dig spot on lawn, shrub bed or driveway.

Municipal main or lateral in a public street/right-of-way: crew lifts a manhole lid, runs a rodder/jetter or CCTV crawler with footage counter to the obstruction or defect, measures the distance along the pavement from the manhole with a tape or measuring wheel, and paints the dig box on asphalt amid traffic control and existing 811 utility marks.

Commercial/institutional property (restaurant grease line, school, apartment complex): cleanout in a paved service area or parking lot; worker runs a cutter head or cable, records the length paid out, sonde-locates the point, and paints the excavation area on asphalt or concrete. Premises controlled and maintained by the owner institution.

Septic system work: locating the tank lid, inlet/outlet baffles, distribution box or failed drainfield line by probing the soil with a rod, flushing a transmitter, and measuring offsets from the foundation and as-built sketch, then staking/painting the dig area in a rough, vegetated yard.

Laying out a planned excavation from known positions: white-lining the dig footprint or staking the trench line for a replacement lateral/main from as-built plans, GIS coordinates or a prior locate, on open ground or pavement before the excavator arrives.

sources.title: SOLO® Pipeline Inspection Robot CCTV | RedZone Robotics
sources.claim: RedZone Robotics' SOLO is a commercially deployed, unmanned sewer inspection crawler that is dropped into a manhole and then traverses 8-12 in. municipal sewer pipe on its own, logging distance-referenced video that is delivered as NASSCO PACP-coded defect records (defect position expressed as footage from the launch manhole) — i.e., the in-pipe measurement half of locating a dig point.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-pipe CCTV inspection. It carries over to 'measure ... lengths of cutting heads within sewers' because the robot's own odometry/PACP coding produces the distance-from-access-point measurement that the worker otherwise reads off a snake or cutter cable in the same pipes.

sources.title: Trenchless Technology Game Changers: RedZone Robotics
sources.claim: Independent trade press confirms SOLO has been in municipal service since 2009 as an unmanned autonomous sewer inspection robot deployed in squads from street manholes.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (autonomous in-pipe inspection with distance logging); cited for maturity and real municipal deployment rather than a lab demo.

sources.title: Automated Layout Startup Civ Robotics Secures $7.5M Series A Funding Round | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Civ Robotics' CivDot/CivDot+ is a commercially sold ground robot that drives itself around large outdoor sites and spray-paints surveyed coordinates to ~8 mm accuracy, up to 3,000 points/day, so crews can follow with flags or stakes — the surface marking half of 'mark areas for digging'.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: construction layout/stakeout marking. Transfers because the physical act is identical — driving to a computed ground position outdoors and spray-painting a mark for excavation crews — at precision far exceeding the few-inch tolerance of a dig mark.

sources.title: CivDot+ GPS Layout Tool | Construction Layout Robot | Civ Robotics
sources.claim: Civ Robotics' own product documentation describes the layout robot spray-painting at GNSS-derived positions from an uploaded coordinate file, with the operator supervising from up to 100 ft away.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: coordinate stakeout/pre-marking. Same objects (paint marks on soil and pavement) and same outdoor settings as marking a sewer dig area.

sources.title: Premarking Robot - Automated Road Marking | Monsen Engineering
sources.claim: TinyMobileRobots' TinySurveyor is a commercially available robotic surveyor that automatically pre-marks lines and points on roads and construction/infrastructure sites using GNSS or total-station positioning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated road pre-marking. It transfers to marking a dig area because the robot lays paint at surveyed positions on street pavement, the same surface and accuracy class used when a sewer crew paints an excavation box.

sources.title: Robotic Utility Mapper Reduces Costs, Improves Safety During Infrastructure Planning and Maintenance | Volpe National Transportation Systems Center
sources.claim: Surface-side robotic location of buried utilities remains at SBIR prototype stage: RUMI is a mobile ground robot combining GPR and other sensors to map buried lines, developed with US DOT SBIR support; no autonomous field deployment marking dig points is documented.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic subsurface utility mapping. Cited to show the surface-side locating step (converting a buried feature to a ground position) has no autonomous fielded system, supporting negative judgments above E1.

tasks.label: Service, adjust, and make minor repairs to equipment, machines, and attachments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled preventive service on the vacuum/pump truck at the company yard or shop: grease driveline and PTO zerks, check and change vacuum-pump oil, drain the moisture trap and primary shutoff, change air/oil filters, check hydraulic and coolant levels, check belt tension, inspect and replace worn camlock gaskets and hose clamps. Cramped, greasy access under and behind the tank.

Job-site troubleshooting and minor repair of jetting/rodding gear when it fails mid-call: a leaking or blown high-pressure hose fitting, a sheared or kinked drain-cleaning cable, a seized chuck or slipping clutch on the rooter, a jetter that will not build pressure (clogged strainer, bad seal). Done on a driveway, roadside, or wet basement floor with hand tools from the truck.

Routine exchange of worn consumable/wear parts and attachments on jetting and rodding equipment: unscrew and replace a worn or plugged jet nozzle, swap cutter heads/blades or a root saw, change a hose-end coupling or cable end, fit the right nozzle for the next line. Standardized threaded parts kept in the truck's parts bin.

Service and minor repair of CCTV pipe-inspection and line-locating equipment: clean and de-fog the camera lens, replace a camera head or centering skid, renew o-rings and seals, repair or re-terminate a pushrod/reel connection, replace batteries, check and calibrate the locator/sonde. Delicate electro-mechanical work done in the inspection van or shop.

Minor repairs to the truck's tank and pumping system in the shop: replace a leaking valve seal or manway gasket, replace a worn section of suction hose, repack or reseal the water pump, replace a jetter drive belt, reset or replace a pressure-relief valve, chase a hydraulic leak on the boom or tank hoist.

Servicing and adjusting customer-side septic/pump equipment during a call: clean and reset an effluent pump screen or filter, adjust or replace a float switch, replace an aerator diaphragm or air filter on an aerobic treatment unit, clear and adjust a high-water alarm. Wet, confined pump chamber in a residential yard.

sources.title: Epiroc introduces Automatic Bit Changer for hands-free bit changes on blasthole drills - International Mining
sources.claim: Epiroc's Automatic Bit Changer performs hands-free exchange of worn rotary tricone drill bits on Pit Viper blasthole rigs at the touch of a ..., with no person handling the drill string; sold as an option and ordered in fleet quantities (e.g., BHP, 2025).

sources.date: 2024-08-01 article; in-pit testing at Roy Hill since 2016
