It covers only a single-fluid fill at a purpose-built receptacle, so it substantiates that step but not the multi-point greasing, oil/filter changes and gasket work that make up a truck preventive-service instance.

tasks.label: Locate problems, using specially designed equipment, and mark where digging must occur to reach damaged tanks or pipes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential building sewer lateral: technician feeds a push camera with sonde from a cleanout in the yard/crawlspace, identifies a break, offset, belly or root intrusion at a given footage, then walks the lawn/driveway with a handheld receiver to pinpoint the sonde position and depth and sprays paint or sets flags where the excavator must dig.

Locating a buried septic tank, tank lid, distribution box or drainfield laterals on a residential property using property records, a steel probe rod, metal detector, flushable transmitter, or ground-penetrating radar; the tech flags/paints the location and outline for the dig to expose or repair the tank.

Municipal collector main: CCTV crawler launched from a manhole in a public street, defect (collapse, offset joint, protruding tap) found at a measured footage; crew locates the point above ground with a sonde/locator or by taping from the manhole and paints the dig location on pavement, working under traffic control.

Commercial/institutional premises (restaurant, apartment complex, school or hospital campus, industrial plant): camera and locator used on a building sewer or grease line running under a maintained parking lot or slab; the defect point is located and marked on pavement or floor for the excavation contractor.

Adverse or emergency conditions: surcharged, collapsed or debris-filled line that must first be jetted or flushed, work at night or in rain/mud, poor access; the tech re-runs the camera, locates the failure point and marks it in difficult terrain for immediate excavation.

sources.system: DEFECTOMAT in-line eddy current test system with FOERSTER Color marking system
sources.developer: Institut Dr. Foerster GmbH und Co. KG
sources.date: product page retrieved 2026-07; long-standing commercial product line
sources.title: Color marking system | Institut Dr. Foerster GmbH und Co. KG
sources.claim: FOERSTER's DEFECTOMAT in-line eddy-current inspection line for tubes and other long products can be fitted with a color marking system that automatically sprays a mark at the position of each detected defect on the workpiece as it passes through the machine — automated locate-and-mark on pipe presented to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-line non-destructive inspection of pipe/tube in a production line. Transfer holds at the E1 counterfactual, where the pipe is fixtured and presented to the machine: the system locates the flaw with purpose-built sensing equipment and physically marks its position with sprayed paint for the crew that will cut/repair it — the same locate-and-mark output on comparable pipe workpieces at comparable (centimetre-scale) positional precision.

sources.system: In-line ultrasonic flaw-detection systems with paint marking on tube/pipe mills
sources.developer: Industrial NDT system suppliers (as described by The Tube & Pipe Journal)
sources.title: Choosing an NDT process for tube, pipe production
sources.claim: In tube and pipe mills, automated ultrasonic inspection systems are routinely configured so that a detected flaw triggers a paint sprayer that marks the defect's location on the pipe for downstream handling, with no operator in the loop for the marking decision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated flaw detection in pipe on a production line. It corroborates that, when the pipe is brought to the machine (the E1 counterfactual), commercially deployed equipment both finds the defect with specially designed sensing gear and physically marks where the defect is.

sources.title: Impacts of Autonomous Sewer Inspection at DC Water — Trenchless Technology
sources.claim: RedZone Robotics' SOLO robots inspect small-diameter municipal sewers autonomously — deployed into manholes without human confined-space entry — and are used in production by DC Water to find operational and structural defects; the robots do not perform any above-ground locating or marking of dig sites.

sources.title: Civ Robotics spots Series A funding for automated surveying - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Civ Robotics' CivDot autonomously drives outdoor job sites and sprays paint marks at uploaded survey coordinates, with more than 100 robots deployed worldwide and over 10 million coordinates marked; it marks only positions supplied to it and performs no subsurface problem-finding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous ground marking at specified coordinates on outdoor construction sites. It shows the paint-marking half of this task is automatable outdoors, but it supplies no locating of buried defects, so it cannot by itself complete an instance.

sources.system: Robotic CCTV crawler with sonde plus handheld surface receiver
sources.developer: Underground Surveying (service provider using commercial crawler/locator equipment)
sources.title: Robotic Crawler Video Inspection Technology | Underground Surveying
sources.claim: Standard field practice for this task uses an operator-driven crawler or push camera carrying a sonde, with a technician at the surface holding a receiver to find the sonde and depth and then hand-marking the ground with paint or flags to show exactly where to excavate.

tasks.label: Dig out sewer lines manually, using shovels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential septic service call: in a customer's yard, locate and hand-dig through sod and 6-36 in of soil (roots, sprinkler lines, uncertain lid position) to uncover the septic tank lids/risers, baffle covers or distribution box so the tank can be pumped or inspected; accepted output is the covers cleanly exposed and undamaged.

Repair-ready bell hole over a broken or root-crushed residential lateral: hand-dig 3-6 ft down, expose the pipe all the way around and undercut it so a coupling or new section can be fitted, cut roots, work in wet or caving soil beside a foundation, driveway or shrubs, and keep the hole open and safe for the repair crew.

Expose the top of a known line at a residence: dig down onto a lateral or buried cleanout at a locate mark to verify a defect, cut in an access point or set a saddle; only the upper surface of the pipe must be uncovered, spoil piled aside.

Hand-finishing after machine excavation: in a backhoe-dug trench, shovel the last several inches of soil off the pipe, square the trench bottom, remove slough and muck, place and level bedding stone around the pipe, and keep the hole clear of spoil and groundwater while the repair is made.

Potholing/daylighting in a street shoulder, sidewalk strip, alley or parking lot: after utility locates are marked, hand-dig test holes inside the tolerance zone to find the sewer main/lateral depth and confirm no conflicting gas, electric or water lines before mechanical excavation; traffic and pedestrians nearby.

Commercial/institutional property (restaurant, school or hospital campus, apartment complex): hand-dig in a paved service area or maintained landscape strip to uncover a grease interceptor lid, cleanout or lateral, working around active business operations on premises the owner controls.

sources.title: Roadwork Robot Autonomously Digs Out, Repairs, Buried Utility Lines - Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: ULC Technologies' RRES prototype autonomously performs the sequence of locating a buried utility with GPR, cutting a keyhole in the surface and excavating the soil above the asset; demonstrated on test pavement for industry press with operators supervising rather than driving the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is exposing a buried gas main rather than a sewer line; transfer holds because the physical act is identical - removing soil from above a buried pipe of similar diameter and burial depth without damaging it - at the same scale of excavation the servicer digs by shovel.

sources.title: Roadwork Robot Autonomously Digs Out, Repairs, Buried Utility Lines - Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: RRES excavation envelope and productivity: about 6 ft working depth, keyholes up to a 36-in oval, roughly 20 minutes to excavate down to a utility, 2-3 excavations per day - the same envelope as a hand-dug septic-lid or lateral pothole.
sources.transferJustification: Same system and related task as above; the depth and hole-size envelope determines whether the robot could substitute for shovel work on laterals and tank lids.

sources.title: The Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System (RRES): From Innovation Funding to Field Trials - ULC Technologies
sources.claim: In a two-week UK field trial on SGN's Epsom gas holder site, RRES scanned ground with little existing utility data, identified crossing pipes, cut a keyhole above one and successfully exposed the buried pipe without damaging it.
sources.transferJustification: Exposing a buried utility pipe on a utility-controlled site is the same physical operation as potholing or daylighting a sewer lateral: locate, break the surface, remove soil down to the pipe crown without striking it.

sources.title: Robotic Roadworks - ULC Technologies
sources.claim: RRES removes soil with a vacuum excavation head using supersonic air nozzles (soft-touch digging) intended to avoid damaging buried assets; a force sensor makes the arm retract on contact with the asset, i.e. it stops at the pipe rather than digging around or beneath it.
sources.transferJustification: Soft-touch soil removal over a buried pipe is the mechanised equivalent of careful shovel work over a sewer line; it substantiates soil removal down to the pipe but not undercutting, root cutting or bedding placement.

sources.title: World-first robotic roadworks system being trialled in the UK - SGN
sources.claim: SGN describes RRES as an autonomous, all-electric robot able to run the end-to-end excavation process on its gas network, the basis for the Epsom trial on the utility's own controlled premises.
sources.transferJustification: Utility excavation to reach a buried pipe; transfers to sewer potholing because the object, burial depth and surface-cut-then-dig sequence match.

sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution - Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofit gives conventional excavators fully autonomous trenching and is in commercial use on US utility-scale solar and data-centre jobsites, i.e. bulk earth removal in unstructured outdoor sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is machine trenching of new, open ground to a programmed line and depth. It does not transfer to shovel work on sewer lines: it neither locates nor delicately exposes an existing fragile pipe, undercuts it, nor cleans and beds a trench bottom, which is precisely why that work is done by hand.

tasks.label: Clean and disinfect domestic basements and other areas flooded by sewer stoppages.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Unfinished residential basement flooded by a main-line stoppage: several inches of raw sewage over a concrete floor, soaked cardboard boxes, stored belongings, water heater/furnace bases. Worker pumps/vacuums out standing sewage, shovels and bags solids and ruined stored items, hoses and scrubs the slab and lower walls, applies disinfectant, deodorizes, hauls waste.

Finished residential basement (carpet and pad, drywall, baseboards, furniture) contaminated by a sewer backup: Category 3 remediation — set containment, extract water, tear out and dispose of carpet/pad and wet drywall, clean and disinfect framing and slab with EPA-registered antimicrobial, set air movers/dehumidifiers, verify dryness.

Small residential backup confined to a bathroom, laundry room, or utility closet: shallow contaminated water on tile/vinyl over a small area with fixtures (toilet, washer, floor drain). Worker wet-vacs the water, wipes and disinfects floor, baseboards, fixture bases and adjacent walls, deodorizes.

Sewage-saturated crawl space under a home: low clearance, dirt floor or torn vapor barrier, insulation contaminated. Worker crawls in, pumps/vacuums standing waste, removes contaminated vapor barrier/soil and insulation, sprays disinfectant/lime, re-lays barrier.

Commercial or institutional space flooded by a sewer stoppage — restaurant basement storeroom, apartment building laundry room, retail back-of-house — with shelving, stock and equipment on the floor. Worker pumps out, moves/discards contaminated stock, washes floor toward drains, disinfects surfaces, deodorizes.

Bare, essentially empty hard-surface structure flooded or fouled by a stoppage — municipal lift-station dry well, mechanical/pump room, garage bay or vault with existing floor drainage — walls and slab coated with sewage residue. Worker hoses/pressure-washes surfaces, squeegees to drain, applies disinfectant.

sources.developer: Washpower A/S (distributed by ACO Funki, PFP Sales)
sources.title: ProCleaner X100 | Washpower
sources.claim: Washpower's ProCleaner X100 is a commercially sold barn washing robot that runs pre-taught soaking and high-pressure wash cycles unattended in emptied pig houses, with an optional module that applies disinfectant automatically after washing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing and disinfecting manure-fouled pens. Transfer holds only for the bare, drained, hard-surface variant of this task: same contaminant class (fecal), same surfaces (concrete walls/floors), same tooling (high-pressure water plus disinfectant), and the pen must be emptied and the routine taught to that fixed geometry, which is an E1-style purpose-built setting.

sources.title: EVO Cleaner for pig barns - Envirologic
sources.claim: Envirologic's EVO Cleaner is a commercially sold pig-barn washing robot that is taught a wash routine by joystick and then performs automated washing of the barn unattended around the clock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-pressure washing of fouled livestock rooms. It substantiates unattended machine washdown of a room-scale, emptied, drained enclosure with fixed geometry, i.e. the E1 counterfactual of 'wash and disinfect a sewage-fouled bare structure'; it does not cover debris/contents removal or bulk water extraction.

sources.title: Manure Solutions | Barn Cleaning | Valorising | Lely
sources.claim: Lely's Discovery Collector/Scraper robots autonomously navigate barn floors on predefined routes and vacuum or scrape manure off them; they are widely sold commercial products.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous removal of fecal material from open floors in a fixed-layout facility. It shows autonomous fecal-waste pickup exists, but only on clear, purpose-designed barn alleys with no clutter, no bulk standing liquid extraction and no disinfection step.

sources.system: Neo 2 autonomous floor scrubber with Disinfection Add-On
sources.title: Disinfection Add-On for Autonomous Cleaning - Facility Executive Magazine
sources.claim: Avidbots' Neo 2 is a fully autonomous floor-scrubbing ... deployed in fleets in hospitals, airports and warehouses (over 1,000 robots deployed), and offers an add-on that autonomously applies disinfectant to surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine autonomous floor scrubbing and surface disinfection in structured facilities. It does not transfer to sewer-backup cleanup: the machine scrubs lightly soiled open floors, and cannot pump out standing sewage, pick up solids and soaked contents, or perform Category 3 material removal and drying.

sources.title: SOMATIC - bathroom cleaning robots for office buildings
sources.claim: Somatic's BCR autonomously navigates commercial buildings and cleans and disinfects restrooms with a touch-less spray, rinse and vacuum process, cleaning fixtures, floors and picking up trash.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cleaning and disinfection of restrooms in an institutional building. It covers routine sanitation of pre-mapped fixtures and floors, not remediation of an overflow event with standing contaminated water, paper solids, soaked porous materials and documented antimicrobial treatment.

sources.title: Robot for cleaning small, confined spaces in non-ATEX zones | KOKS
sources.claim: Industrial cleaning of sewers, tanks, water basins and other confined spaces fouled with sludge is done with remote-controlled (operator-driven) robots, not autonomous ones.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing sewage sludge from confined structures. It is the closest industrial analogue to washing out a sewage-fouled space, but it is continuously teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Water Damage Restoration Process | IICRC S500 Steps
sources.claim: Category 3 (sewage) losses require removal of all porous materials plus antimicrobial treatment of remaining structural ... — the acceptance standard the worker's output must meet.
sources.transferJustification: Not a robotic system; cited to establish what 'worker quality' completion of this task requires (bulk extraction, demolition and disposal of porous materials, antimicrobial application, drying), which the cited robots do not perform.

sources.title: Gatsby Makes History with First Humanoid Robot Cleaning for a U.S. Consumer
sources.claim: A humanoid robot was dispatched to clean a consumer's San Francisco apartment in May 2026; the release describes a general residential cleaning service and does not establish unsupervised autonomy or any remediation capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: light residential cleaning in a home. Even taken at face value it covers tidying and surface cleaning of an intact apartment, not pumping out sewage, hauling contaminated contents, or biohazard disinfection; autonomy is unverified, so it is treated as teleoperated.

tasks.label: Withdraw cables from pipes and examine them for evidence of mud, roots, grease, and other deposits indicating broken or clogged sewer lines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service call: after rodding a clogged kitchen/bath branch or 4-inch house lateral from a basement cleanout, crawlspace, or yard cleanout of a single-family home, the servicer power-feeds/hand-hauls 50-100 ft of steel cable back onto the drum machine in a cramped, cluttered space, then inspects the cutter head and cable for root hairs, grease, soap/hair, or mud and tells the homeowner what is wrong with the line.

Municipal sewer main work: crew rods a 6-15 in. main from a manhole in a public street using a continuous rodder, sectional machine, or bucket machine; rods/cable are retracted onto the reel while traffic passes, and the crew examines the cutter, rod, and hauled-back spoil for roots, grease balls, and grit/mud (mud indicating a broken pipe) and reports the segment's condition.

Commercial food-service line: rodding a grease-fouled kitchen floor drain, grease-trap line, or building branch in a restaurant or retail food facility; the cable is withdrawn onto the machine in a working kitchen with wet floors and staff nearby, and the head is examined for congealed grease, food solids, and rags to determine whether jetting or a repair is needed.

Institutional / multifamily building: sectional or large drum machine run from a basement cleanout, mechanical room, or stack cleanout in a hospital, school, or apartment complex; long cable is withdrawn section by section and inspected for roots, scale, rags/wipes, and grease to diagnose a shared building drain.

Rural septic / drain-field work: cable run through a septic tank inlet or outlet baffle, distribution box, or drain-tile lateral on a private property; cable is withdrawn and inspected for mud and root mass indicating crushed or broken drain tile, often in a muddy excavation or lawn.

sources.system: Canrig Red Zone Robotics (RZR) Rig Floor Module / iRacker
sources.title: Nabors retrofits robotics module onto existing land rig to achieve full automation - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: Canrig RZR rig-floor robotics module autonomously handles tubulars and trips the pipe string in and out of the hole on a working land rig, i.e. machine-controlled withdrawal of a long linear element from a bore in a purpose-built, human-excluded machine zone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pulling a drill string out of a borehole. It is the same physical operation as withdrawing a rodding cable from a sewer pipe - a heavy linear element extracted from a bore, then spooled/racked under machine control with people kept out of the work zone - at equal or greater load and precision, showing the withdrawal step is mechanizable where the work is fixtured and presented to the machine.

sources.system: AutoBox 3L flex-lance tractor with Sentinel Automation Technology
sources.title: StoneAge | Automated Equipment for High-pressure Industrial Cleaning
sources.claim: StoneAge AutoBox 3L with Sentinel automation drives flexible high-pressure lances into and out of heat-exchanger tubes hands-free, positioning nozzles with sensors and running the lances end to end through each tube of a fixtured bundle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: flexible-lance tube cleaning. The lance is the functional equivalent of a rodding cable - a limp line pushed through and then retracted from a pipe under machine control on a fixtured bundle - but the operator still supervises positioning by remote controller, so this item is treated as teleoperated and only corroborates the mechanical feasibility of machine-driven cable withdrawal.

sources.title: TOMRA 5A premier optical sorter for nuts, dried fruit and IQF | TOMRA
sources.claim: TOMRA optical sorters autonomously identify and eject roots, stones, soil clods, wood and other foreign material from a machine-fed product stream at high throughput inside processing plants, using near-infrared and colour sensing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated foreign-material identification. Discriminating roots, soil clods and organic debris from other material at >98% accuracy on a presented stream is the same perceptual judgement as reading root mass, mud and grease off a withdrawn cutter head, and it is demonstrated in a purpose-built machine setting.

sources.date: in service since 2009; product page updated 2025-10
sources.title: SOLO® Pipeline Inspection Robot CCTV | RedZone Robotics
sources.claim: RedZone's SOLO is an autonomous unmanned crawler launched into a municipal sewer manhole that traverses small-diameter pipe on its own and captures 360-degree video used to score pipe condition; the field crew still lowers and recovers it, and it handles no cleaning cable.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-pipe condition assessment in the field. It marks the limit of field autonomy in sewers today - a hand-launched, hand-recovered camera crawler - and performs no cable feeding, retraction or spooling, so it does not substantiate completing this task in E2 or E3 settings.

sources.title: How AI Pipeline Inspection Software Improves Defect Detection | Plumber
sources.claim: SewerAI's AutoCode automatically recognises NASSCO-coded conditions such as roots, deposits and broken pipe in sewer inspection video; it is analysis software with no physical embodiment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: classifying roots, deposits and breaks from imagery. Software only, so it cannot by itself support a positive judgement; it corroborates that the diagnostic half of this task is within demonstrated machine perception once imagery is presented.

tasks.label: Ensure that repaired sewer line joints are tightly sealed before backfilling begins.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential sewer lateral / building drain repair: after cutting out a broken clay or cast-iron section in a hand- or machine-dug yard trench, the servicer joins new PVC with shielded rubber couplings, torques the band clamps, wipes and eyeballs each joint in mud and groundwater, then runs water from the house (or fills the line with a test ball) and watches the joints for weeping before the homeowner's trench is backfilled.

Municipal sewer main or lateral point repair in a shored street excavation: after setting a new gasketed pipe section between manholes, the crew sets inflatable test plugs, runs a low-pressure air test (or exfiltration/water test) on the repaired segment, holds and times the pressure drop against the spec, re-seats or re-grouts any joint that fails, and retests before the inspector allows backfill.

Septic system piping: replacing/resealing the tank inlet and outlet connections, D-box, and drainfield lateral tile joints in an excavated yard; the servicer packs or grouts the pipe penetrations, checks that gaskets and cement seals are watertight (often by filling the tank/line with water and watching for drop or seepage), before the tank and lines are covered.

Post-repair internal camera verification with the trench still open: a push camera or crawler is run from a cleanout or manhole through the repaired run to confirm each joint is home, gasket not rolled, no offset, protruding sealant, or infiltration; footage is recorded for the municipal/owner inspector who signs off on backfill.

Repair on institution-controlled property (plant yard, campus, commercial parking lot, mobile-home park): excavated repair of a sewer or grease line, joints checked visually and by air/water test with a facility engineer or third-party inspector present, documented, and any leaking joint re-made before the contractor backfills and repaves.

sources.title: Hydrostatic testing: fast and accurate | Fives Group
sources.claim: Fives' Taylor-Wilson hydrostatic pipe testers are purpose-built production machines that seal the ends of pipe up to 26 in diameter and pressurize it under PLC control with automatic length, grade and pressure settings — i.e., machine-executed leak/seal verification of pipe in a fixtured, purpose-built test bay.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production pressure testing of pipe. It transfers to 'ensure joints are tightly sealed' because the physical act is the same — seal the pipe ends, pressurize, hold, and judge pass/fail on pressure decay — on pipe of the same diameter class as sewer pipe, at pressures far above the 4 psi field air test.

sources.system: TQC leak test cell with robotic handling (Fanuc 6-axis + MALT air decay testers)
sources.title: Case Study - Fully Automatic Leak Test Cell with Robotic Handling
sources.claim: TQC built and delivered a fully automatic leak test cell in which a Fanuc 6-axis robot loads and unloads assemblies, air-decay leak testers verify each assembly, vision inspects it, and the cell automatically segregates pass, fail and QC parts without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line leak verification of assembled parts. It transfers because the verification logic is identical to the field air test on a repaired joint — pressurize the sealed assembly, measure decay over a hold time, accept or reject — and the cell also handles the part and inspects it visually, covering the 'look at the joint' element.

sources.system: RedZone SOLO autonomous pipeline inspection robot
sources.date: 2025-10 (product page updated); in commercial service since 2009
sources.title: SOLO® Pipeline Inspection Robot CCTV | RedZone Robotics
sources.claim: RedZone's SOLO is a commercially deployed, battery-powered sewer inspection robot that, once lowered into a manhole by the crew, drives the pipe run and records 360-degree video without an operator driving it; it is used by utilities such as Rochester Hills, MI for collection-system assessment. It gathers condition imagery but performs no pressure/leak test and makes no accept-before-backfill decision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-service sewer CCTV inspection. Cited to show the limit of field autonomy: it covers only camera transit inside a live manhole-to-manhole main, not entering an open trench, setting test plugs, air-testing a fresh joint, or re-making a joint that fails.

tasks.label: Rotate cleaning rods manually, using turning pins.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service call: worker opens a cleanout in a crawlspace, basement, or yard of a private home, threads sectional cleaning rods into a 2-4 in. branch or main drain and rotates them by hand with turning pins to bore through a grease/hair/paper clog where a powered machine cannot fit or would damage old pipe; must feel resistance, avoid rod breakage, and verify flow.

Public right-of-way work: rodding a service lateral or small line from a curb cleanout or street manhole, hand-turning rods with pins to start or free a blockage before jetting; traffic, weather, debris, and unknown pipe condition (roots, offset joints, collapsed clay).

Septic system service at a rural or suburban property: hand-rodding the inlet/outlet baffle line, the line to the distribution box, or a drain-field lateral to clear sludge or roots after pumping; uneven ground, buried access, variable pipe layout.

Commercial/institutional building interior: rodding a restaurant grease line, school or hospital floor drain, or apartment stack cleanout in a mechanical room; fixed layout, standard fixtures, facility staff control access and shut down the area during the work.

Industrial plant or process facility: hand-rodding small process drain lines, sumps, or trench-drain runs during a maintenance window under a permit, with standard piping and access ports and site control of who is present.

sources.system: Terydon automated tube-bundle lancing system (Smart Indexer, Lunch Box control, M3)
sources.title: Company advances tube bundle cleaning through upgrade - BIC Magazine
sources.claim: Terydon's automated flex-lancing systems drive cleaning lances into fixtured tube bundles, index automatically from tube to tube and row to row, and run the cleaning cycle to completion with the worker acting only as a monitor outside the blast zone — commercial industrial pipe-interior cleaning with the work brought to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: internal cleaning of pipe runs by feeding a rod/lance in from an access port and driving it through deposits, then withdrawing it — the same mechanical act as rotating cleaning rods into a drain with turning pins. Comparable objects (fouled pipe interiors), comparable precision (align to the pipe mouth, push and rotate to length), and the workpiece is fixtured and presented to the machine, which is exactly the E1 counterfactual.

sources.title: StoneAge releases Sentinel Automation Technology - BIC Magazine
sources.claim: StoneAge's Sentinel Automation Technology on the AutoBox 3L lance tractor senses tube positions and automatically positions the cleaning nozzles and cleans exchanger tubes end to end, replacing manual lance handling in commercial industrial cleaning work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: clearing fouled pipe interiors by driving a flexible lance the full length of the pipe and back. Same action class as rodding a drain line; the machine finds the pipe opening by sensing rather than fixed teaching, and the bundle is presented to the machine on a cleaning pad, matching the E1 counterfactual of work brought to the machine.

sources.system: Sewer Cleaning Robot (SCR) with Detection-Localization-Cleaning mode
sources.developer: Xiong, Zhang et al. (Applied Sciences / MDPI)
sources.title: Sewer Cleaning Robot: A Visually Assisted Cleaning Robot for Sewers
sources.claim: A vision-guided Sewer Cleaning Robot detects, localizes and cuts hard obstructions inside 280-780 mm pipe, validated in a purpose-built simulated pipeline; a research prototype, not fielded service work.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: machine-controlled removal of obstructions from inside sewer pipe, the purpose of rotating cleaning rods. Demonstrated only in a controlled test pipeline, so it supports a purpose-built (E1) setting and not field service.

sources.title: TECH TALK/BANDICOOT – ScienceIndiamag
sources.claim: Bandicoot, the most widely fielded sewer-maintenance robot, desilts manholes with a lowered robotic arm under an operator at a surface control unit; it is remotely operated and does not rod out blocked laterals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized removal of sewer blockages in the field. Cited as the state of practice in unstructured/field settings; because control is remote and the work is bucket desilting of manholes rather than rod work in laterals, it cannot support a positive judgment at E2 or E3.

tasks.label: Install rotary knives on flexible cables mounted on machine reels, according to the diameters of pipes to be cleaned.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential drain job: tech works in a basement, crawlspace, under a kitchen sink, or at an outside cleanout of a private home; sizes up a 2-4 in. line, picks the matching cutter/blade holder from the machine's tool box, seats it on the hex coupling or leader at the end of the drum machine's flexible cable and secures it with a pin, bolt or set screw; often kneeling in a tight, wet, poorly lit space, sometimes swapping heads once or twice during the job.

Municipal/street sewer main: crew at a manhole or curbside cleanout with a rodder or continuous-rod truck installs a root saw / expanding blade of the size matching a 6-12 in. main onto the leader or coupling of the rod on the truck reel; outdoors at the roadside, in traffic, in any weather, cable greasy and wet.

Shop or truck-bay prep: at the company yard, technician loads or replaces cable on the machine reel and installs or swaps cutter heads and worn blades on leaders at a bench or vise, building out the head sets for the day's scheduled pipe sizes.

Commercial/institutional building interior: tech in a restaurant kitchen, apartment or hospital mechanical room, or school basement fits the correct-diameter cutter (grease cutter, spade, saw blade) to the sectional machine's cable at the cleanout, changing heads as the job moves from a 3 in. branch to a 6 in. building drain.

Adverse mid-job change: blade sheared off, cutter fouled with roots or hardened grease, or the retaining bolt/pin seized or deformed; the worker must free and remove the damaged hardware and install a fresh knife on a mud-caked cable, down in a pit, manhole, or crawlspace.

sources.system: Mirka AutoChanger (with AIROS 650CV/350CV robotic sanding heads)
sources.title: Mirka® AutoChanger: a new level of automation for robotic sanding
sources.claim: Commercial robotic sanding systems autonomously select and mount a fresh consumable working head of the specified size from a magazine onto the powered tool head, then discard it and repeat, inside an industrial robot cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: changing the consumable cutting/abrading head on a rotating tool. It matches the core of this task — choosing the head of the correct size (the system is offered for 77 mm and 150 ... discs, i.e. size-indexed magazines) and seating it on the tool's mount — at comparable object scale and coupling precision, in a fixtured cell.

sources.system: FerRobotics Media/Sandpaper Changing Station and Magazine
sources.title: Sandpaper changing station - FerRobotics
sources.claim: A patented commercial changing station plus magazine performs automated removal and replacement of the abrasive working media on robot grinding/sanding units, designed for unmanned operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended change of a rotating tool's consumable head from a magazine. Demonstrates that removing a spent head and fitting a new one of the selected media size is done without a human in a purpose-built robot cell, the E1 counterpart of fitting a knife to a cable end.

sources.system: WEBER SER screwdriving system on KUKA industrial robot
sources.developer: WEBER Schraubautomaten GmbH / KUKA (user: BSH Hausgeräte)
sources.title: Automated screwdriving technology for dishwashers - WEBER Schraubautomaten GmbH
sources.claim: In series production at BSH Dillingen, a KUKA industrial robot positions and a WEBER SER screwdriving system drives and torque-monitors the threaded fasteners of a sealed pump-base joint on the dishwasher assembly line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic driving of a threaded fastener to a monitored torque on a production line. Securing a rotary knife/blade holder on a cable coupling is the same act — locating the fastener and running it down tight — at comparable or coarser precision, with process monitoring giving worker-level reliability.

sources.system: Portaband Saw Blade Automation Robot Work Cell (3 Fanuc LR Mate robots, Fanuc iRVision)
sources.title: Portaband Saw Blade Automation Robot Work Cell - AAE North America 2025
sources.claim: A three-robot Fanuc production cell feeds flexible bandsaw blade stock from reels, uses vision to locate the blade ends and grip each end precisely, then welds, anneals and grinds the joint at four parts per minute.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling flexible reel-mounted linear stock and precisely locating and gripping its end for a joining operation. This is the part of the present task that involves the machine reel and the flexible cable end, at comparable stiffness and scale, in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Single-arm wire-harnessing framework (Koopman-MPC with twisting primitives)
sources.developer: University of Michigan / General Motors research team (Toner, Molazadeh, Saez, Barton et al.)
sources.title: Harnessing with Twisting: Single-Arm Deformable Linear Object Manipulation for Industrial Harnessing Task
sources.claim: A single robot arm with force/torque sensing autonomously tensions and inserts a flexible wire into clamps on the NIST assembly task board, an industrial-level wire harnessing benchmark, with high success rates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation of a deformable linear object's end into a rigid receptacle. It substantiates that the flexible-cable aspect of seating a blade holder on a cable/leader end is tractable for autonomous robots on a fixtured bench, though only at benchtop/demo maturity.

tasks.label: Start machines to feed revolving cables or rods into openings, stopping machines and changing knives to conform to pipe sizes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Private home, interior: technician sets a drum/sectional cable machine at a basement cleanout, floor drain, or pulled toilet, starts the motor, hand-feeds the revolving 3/8"–3/4" cable down a 1.5"–4" line, stops the machine when it hits the stoppage, and swaps cutter heads (spade, C-cutter, small root saw) to suit the line size before finishing and testing flow. Cluttered, occupied, unknown piping layout.

Exterior residential/small-commercial sewer lateral: machine set at an outside cleanout, cracked-open pit, or roof vent in a yard or alley; larger sectional rodder run 50–100 ft into 4"–6" clay/cast lateral; blades and root saws changed to match lateral diameter; mud, weather, roots, unknown grade.

Commercial/institutional building interior: restaurant grease line, apartment stack, school or hospital floor drain accessed from a back-of-house or mechanical-room cleanout; mid-size cable machine started and fed into 2"–6" lines; cutter heads changed between branch and main sizes; premises controlled by facility staff, layout documented.

Municipal sewer main: crew sets a truck-mounted continuous rodder or power rodder over a street manhole, feeds revolving rod/cable into the 6"–15" main, stops to change root saws, porcupine brushes, and expanding blades to the main's diameter; traffic control, confined-space rules, live flow, unknown debris.

Industrial plant maintenance: process drains, trench drains, and small process piping in a refinery, food plant, or wastewater facility cleaned with rod/cable machines during a scheduled outage; tool heads changed to line size; plant-controlled premises with permits and standard access points.

sources.title: StoneAge releases Sentinel Automation Technology - BIC Magazine
sources.claim: StoneAge's Sentinel Automation Technology, integrated with the AutoBox 3L flex-lance tractor, uses sensors to automatically position the cleaning lances/nozzles at tube openings and clean heat-exchanger tubes end to end without an operator at the workpiece — machine-controlled feeding of a long flexible lance with a rotating cleaning head into pipe openings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated heat-exchanger tube lancing. It is the industrial form of the rated task — a machine started to feed a long revolving cleaning head (rotary nozzle on a flex or rigid lance) into pipe openings to cut and flush hard deposits, stopping and indexing between openings. Objects (fouled pipe bores), tool geometry (rotating cutting/scouring head on a flexible shaft), and required precision (entering and traversing a bore without damaging the wall) are comparable to feeding a revolving cable into a drain opening.

sources.system: StoneAge AutoBox ABX-2L with Banshee rotary nozzles
sources.title: StoneAge releases cutting-edge AutoBox flex lancing system for heat exchanger cleaning
sources.claim: The AutoBox automated flex lancing system is a hands-free rig mounted on the exchanger via a positioner and run with Banshee rotary tube-cleaning nozzles, i.e. rotating cleaning heads fed into fixtured tube bores by the machine rather than by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (automated tube lancing); this item establishes that the revolving cleaning head is machine-fed into a fixtured workpiece with a positioner, which is the E1 presentation of the rated task.

sources.system: StoneAge automated tube cleaning systems (single/dual/triple-lance tractors)
sources.title: StoneAge | Industrial Automated Tube Cleaning Equipment Solutions
sources.claim: StoneAge's automated tube-cleaning systems are designed so the work is done inside a blast exclusion zone with personnel kept outside it — the setting is built around the machine, with the tube bundle fixtured in place or in a wash bay.
sources.transferJustification: Used to characterize the environment (fixtured workpiece, people excluded from the work zone) in which the automated lancing evidence was obtained, i.e. an E1 purpose-built robotic work setting.

sources.system: ATI Quick-Change Robotic Tool Changer (QC series)
sources.title: Product - Robotic Tool Changer (ATI Industrial Automation)
sources.claim: Automatic robotic tool changers are standard, long-deployed production hardware that let a machine exchange its working end effector (including rotary motors and cutting tooling) without human hands, which is the mechanism by which 'changing knives to conform to pipe sizes' would be executed in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic end-effector/tool exchange in fenced industrial cells. It carries over to the 'stop the machine and change knives to conform to pipe sizes' element: coupling a keyed cutting head of a chosen size to a driven shaft, at repeatable position and with reliable locking, is the same class of action performed millions of cycles in production cells.

sources.title: SOLO Pipeline Inspection Robot CCTV | RedZone Robotics
sources.claim: RedZone's SOLO is a genuinely autonomous sewer robot deployed by US utilities, but it only inspects: launched into a live main from a manhole it drives itself, and when it meets a blockage it makes three attempts to pass and then returns — it does not cut, rod, or clear the obstruction.

sources.system: Robotic lateral reinstatement / milling cutters (IMS Robotics, Sewer Robotics)
sources.title: Sewer Robotics - A1 Total Service Lining
sources.claim: In-pipe robotic cutters used in municipal sewers and building laterals (IMS Robotics, Sewer Robotics class machines) are remote-operated by skilled technicians watching a camera feed, not autonomous; cutter heads are selected and fitted by hand before deployment.

tasks.label: Update sewer maps and manhole charts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Cover repaired pipes with dirt, and pack backfilled excavations, using air and gasoline tampers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential yard: after repairing a broken sewer lateral or septic line, the crew shoves the spoil pile back into a 3–6 ft deep, 2 ft wide trench in a homeowner's lawn (first covering the repaired PVC/clay pipe with sand or screened soil by shovel so rocks don't crack it), then compacts in 6–12 in lifts with a gasoline jumping-jack rammer, crowns the trench for settlement and resets sod. Landscaping, fences, sprinkler lines and unmarked utilities crowd the work.

Public street or right-of-way: sewer main/lateral repair in a traffic-controlled trench cut through asphalt; imported sand/gravel backfill placed in lifts by mini-excavator and hand, compacted with rammer, plate or trench roller to the municipality's density spec (often density-tested), with live gas/water/electric crossing the trench, then base prepared for the pavement patch.

Tight-access or hand-dug spot excavation: a small hole beside a foundation, at a cleanout, saddle connection or under a deck/porch, dug and refilled by shovel, with the repaired fitting hand-covered and the fill packed with a hand tamper or small air tamper, working around the exposed pipe in a confined pit.

Septic tank or drainfield excavation on a rural/suburban lot: backfilling over a set or repaired tank, risers and leach lines — soil pushed in evenly around the tank so it isn't shifted or crushed, gentle cover over drain tile with no heavy compaction there, sides tamped, then the area graded and crowned. Large excavation, soft soil, machine plus hand work.

Commercial/institutional grounds (school, plant yard, hospital campus, parking lot): trench over a repaired sewer line backfilled and compacted to spec inside a facility the owner controls, with escorted access, marked utilities and a paved or turf surface to restore.

sources.system: Kawasaki Autonomous Excavation System for Excavators
sources.title: Kawasaki Develops "Autonomous Excavation System for Excavators", Achieved "Autonomous Operation" for Trench Excavation at Construction and Civil Engineering Sites
sources.claim: Kawasaki's Autonomous Excavation System for excavators performed autonomous trench excavation and, in company verification testing, also autonomously performed trench-floor leveling and compaction work using LiDAR terrain sensing and 3D design data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (trench excavation) with an explicitly verified compaction capability by the same machine: the same excavator-mounted autonomy moves soil into/out of a trench and compacts it, which is the machine-scale version of covering a pipe and packing backfill. Demonstrated only in controlled verification testing, not on live service excavations.

sources.title: The Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System (RRES): From Innovation Funding to Field Trials – ULC Technologies
sources.claim: The Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System (RRES) performs keyhole road excavation over buried utility mains and, after work on the asset, uses an air compactor on its robotic arm to reinstate the stored loose material and replace the road core; capabilities listed include backfill and reinstatement.
sources.transferJustification: Closest match to the task itself — machine-controlled refilling of an excavation over a repaired utility pipe and packing it with an air tamper — but only at keyhole scale, and the trials took place at SGN's Epsom gas holder site rather than on varied live customer excavations.

sources.title: Roadwork Robot Autonomously Digs Out, Repairs Buried Utility Lines
sources.claim: In the RRES press demonstration the robot compacted the returned soil layer by layer while human operators shovelled the material back into the hole, and the system was described as a working prototype needing operators to swap its tools.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, but shows the human role that remains in the covering step and that the demonstration was on test pavement under a tent with operators present, limiting the claim to structured, prepared settings.

sources.system: A4CSEL automated vibratory rollers and bulldozers
sources.title: A⁴CSEL for DAM | Technology & Services | KAJIMA CORPORATION
sources.claim: Kajima's A4CSEL system runs automated vibratory rollers, bulldozers and dump ... that place and compact embankment layers at dam construction sites; more than ten automated machines worked day and night on the Naruse Dam CSG embankment, and the technology was applied to land-development earthworks in FY2024.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (spreading and compacting fill in lifts) transfers partially: same physical operation of placing soil and packing it to a density standard under machine control, but performed on wide embankment lifts inside machine-organised exclusion zones ('site as a factory'), not in narrow trenches over fragile repaired pipe.

sources.title: Roller Autonomous System - GeoControl Roller | DeepX
sources.claim: A retrofit autonomy kit turns existing vibratory rollers into autonomous compactors: the operator specifies the compaction area and pass count and the roller executes compaction autonomously with obstacle detection and GNSS-RTK accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (soil compaction) supports the packing half of the task where the compaction area is a defined, open, machine-accessible surface; it does not address covering a repaired pipe or compacting inside a narrow trench with a rammer.

sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' commercially deployed Exosystem autonomy kit performs autonomous trenching only; the marketed benefit is that its evenly spaced spoil piles streamline the work of the human backfill and compaction crews that follow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous trenching on live utility/solar sites) shows what commercial field autonomy covers today — digging — while backfill and compaction on those same unstructured sites are still done by human crews.

sources.developer: Develon / HD XiteSolution with Gravis Robotics
sources.title: Develon puts autonomous excavator to work in Switzerland
sources.claim: A Develon DX225LC-7X fitted with the Real-X system developed with Gravis ... was put into practical use by contractor KIBAG, operating autonomously in a former quarry in ... to excavate a 300 m trench.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous bulk earthmoving/trenching) shows soil-handling autonomy has reached a real, institution-controlled industrial site; it does not cover careful covering of a repaired pipe or tamped backfill to a density spec.

tasks.label: Cut damaged sections of pipe with cutters, remove broken sections from ditches, and replace pipe sections, using pipe sleeves.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential sewer lateral spot repair: crew excavates a 3–6 ft trench in a homeowner's yard, exposes a broken clay/cast-iron/PVC 4-inch lateral, cuts out the damaged section with a snap cutter or recip saw, lifts the broken pieces and root mass out of the muddy ditch by hand, and splices in a new PVC section with shielded Fernco-type sleeve couplings, torquing the band clamps and checking flow.

Municipal sewer main or public right-of-way point repair: 6–12 ft shored street trench with traffic control and flow bypass; heavy VCP/ductile/cast-iron main (6–12 in.) cut out with a chain-type cutter or saw, broken barrel and shards hoisted out of the trench, replacement section set on bedding and joined with repair sleeves/couplings to line and grade.

Septic system piping repair: replacing crushed or root-damaged drain tile, leach-field laterals, or the inlet/outlet line at the tank or distribution box; shallow trench in a yard or field, corrugated HDPE or thin-wall pipe cut and rejoined with split couplings/sleeves, with grade and pitch verified.

Commercial/industrial site drain or building sewer repair: broken cast-iron or PVC line under a parking lot, slab, or in a cramped crawlspace/pit; short trench or hand-dug hole, pipe cut with a snap cutter in confined space and rejoined with no-hub shielded couplings, working around adjacent utilities and structures.

Emergency/adverse-condition repair: collapsed or offset pipe with active flow, groundwater and mud in the ditch, unstable soil or unmarked adjacent utilities; hand-digging around the pipe, cutting out the failed section in poor visibility and sealing in a replacement with sleeves under time pressure.

sources.system: KRANENDONK Robotic Pipe Shop (Apollo milling / Aurora welding stations)
sources.title: Robotic Pipe Shop — KRANENDONK
sources.claim: KRANENDONK's Robotic Pipe Shop is a commercially delivered automated pipe-spool line that performs cutting, beveling, fit-up and welding of pipe sections as one integrated robotic workflow inside a fabrication shop cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pipe-spool fabrication. It covers the same physical operations as this task under the E1 counterfactual — cutting steel pipe to a cut line, handling/removing cut sections, and joining a replacement section to the remaining ends — on comparable pipe diameters and with tighter precision than a sewer repair sleeve requires.

sources.system: KRANENDONK Robotic Pipe Shop at JGC Corporation
sources.title: KRANENDONK strengthens collaboration with JGC through advanced Robotic Pipe Shop installation
sources.claim: The Kranendonk automated Robotic Pipe Shop has been installed and is in production use at fabricator JGC, with an expanded fully integrated pipe shop adding cutting, beveling, welding and material-handling automation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pipe-spool fabrication in a purpose-built cell. Shows the cut-and-rejoin sequence is performed at production quality by machines when the pipe is fixtured and presented, which is exactly the E1 presentation of this repair task.

sources.system: Novarc Spool Welding Robot (SWR) with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2
sources.title: Novarc automates arc welding processes with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2 — The Robot Report
sources.claim: Novarc's Spool Welding Robot with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2 performs pipe joint welding autonomously with no operator intervention and is sold to pipe fabrication shops.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: joining pipe sections in a shop cell. The accepted output of this task is a restored, sealed pipe run; autonomous machine joining of fixtured pipe ends substantiates the 'replace the section and make the joint' step at E1.

sources.system: BLM GROUP Lasertube tube laser cutting machines (and TRUMPF TruLaser Tube part-removal automation)
sources.title: Tube laser cutting machines | BLM GROUP
sources.claim: Industrial tube/pipe laser cutting machines cut pipe up to 24 in. diameter with automatic loading, unloading and part-removal stations that clear cut sections without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting pipe to a cut line and removing the severed piece. Same objects (round pipe of comparable diameter) and the same two physical steps this task names — 'cut damaged sections of pipe with cutters' and 'remove broken sections' — performed unattended in a fixtured machine.

sources.system: Vision-guided robotic nutrunner cell (automotive lug-nut fastening); Universal Robots automotive nut running
sources.developer: Integrator cells reported by Manufacturing AUTOMATION / Universal Robots
sources.title: Vision-guided Robot Key To Automated Lug-nut Fastening — Manufacturing AUTOMATION
sources.claim: Vision-guided industrial robots position nutrunners and torque fasteners to specification on production assembly lines, including wheel/lug-nut fastening where part position varies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: torqued fastener assembly in a fixtured cell. Installing a shielded repair sleeve means seating the sleeve over the pipe ends and torquing band-clamp screws to a set torque — the same fastener-driving operation, at lower precision than wheel fastening.

sources.title: Roadwork Robot Autonomously Digs Out, Repairs Buried Utility Lines — ENR
sources.claim: ULC Technologies' RRES robot autonomously cores and excavates a keyhole in a roadway, exposes a buried gas pipe, and can clean, clamp, cut the pipe and install a thermoplastic fitting; at the time reported it was a prototype under trials on mock roadways, with operators changing tool carts, inspecting work and shovelling backfill.
sources.transferJustification: Closest E3 analogue: machine work on buried pipe in a street excavation. Cited to show the state of the art outdoors — a prototype on 30-ft mock roadbeds doing gas keyhole fittings, not sewer section removal and sleeve replacement at worker quality — so it does not substantiate completion at E3 or E2.

sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem converts standard excavators into fully autonomous trenching machines used on utility and solar job sites, digging trenches to 0.1 ft accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: trench excavation on open job sites. It establishes that outdoor autonomy today covers bulk earthmoving only; it provides no manipulation of pipe (cutting, lifting broken sections out of a ditch, seating sleeves), so it cannot substantiate this task at E3.

tasks.label: Requisition or order tools and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Break asphalt and other pavement so that pipes can be accessed, using airhammers, picks, and shovels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Private residence: break out a concrete or asphalt driveway, walkway or patio section (typically 2-6 ft across, often reinforced) over a sewer lateral or septic line, muck out the rubble and dig 2-5 ft down with pick and shovel to expose the pipe for a spot repair; tight side-yard access, unknown pipe alignment.

Public street, alley or curb line: saw-cut and jackhammer a large pavement section (often several feet by ten or more) over a sewer main or lateral in the right-of-way, remove slab pieces, then excavate 5-12 ft deep with traffic control and shoring; live traffic, mixed base materials, other utilities crossing.

Commercial or institutional paved lot / facility service yard (restaurant grease line, apartment complex, school, plant): break a 2-4 ft asphalt opening over a lateral, grease line or buried cleanout and dig 2-5 ft to expose the pipe; premises controlled by the owner, standard paved surface, work area coned off.

Small localized breakout: chip out a 1-2 ft patch of pavement, concrete collar or old patch around a buried cleanout, fitting or pipe crown, working shallow (under ~3 ft) and carefully by hand with pick, hand breaker and shovel so the pipe is not damaged; often in a driveway apron, parkway or street shoulder.

Interior slab: break a concrete floor in a house basement, crawlspace or commercial kitchen with an electric/air hammer to reach a buried drain line, control dust, haul out rubble by bucket and hand-dig to the pipe in a confined, obstructed space.

sources.title: The Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System (RRES): From Innovation Funding to Field Trials
sources.claim: ULC Technologies' RRES robot, during a two-week field trial at SGN's gas holder site in ..., UK, scanned for buried assets, cut a keyhole in the surface and vacuum-excavated down until it exposed the buried pipe.
sources.transferJustification: Direct analog of the task: opening a paved surface and removing material so a buried pipe can be accessed. Scale demonstrated is a keyhole over a shallow gas main, not a person-sized working pit.

sources.title: The Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System (RRES): From Innovation Funding to Field Trials
sources.claim: The trial environment was an institution-controlled utility compound (SGN's Epsom gas holder site) rather than a public street, and the system had been validated beforehand at US test locations.

sources.title: Power industry first sees robotic excavator
sources.claim: Trade coverage of the RRES programme states the machine was performing autonomous operations that include cutting the road surface and vacuum excavation.
sources.transferJustification: Road-surface cutting plus excavation to an asset is the same output as breaking pavement so a pipe can be accessed.

sources.title: Robotic Roadworks – ULC Technologies
sources.claim: RRES cuts the road surface with a robot-arm-mounted concrete cutting chainsaw, lifts out the core, and uses a soft-touch vacuum/air excavation head to remove soil down to buried assets without damaging them.
sources.transferJustification: Describes the tooling envelope: keyhole-scale cores in road surfaces and soft-touch soil removal, not slab demolition or person-sized pits.

sources.title: World-first robotic roadworks system being trialled in the UK
sources.claim: SGN describes RRES as an all-electric autonomous robot able to carry out the end-to-end excavation process, first trialled on its gas network in Epsom, Surrey.

sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Leads Major Autonomous Excavation Push
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics runs supervised-autonomy excavation on live US construction sites (mass earthmoving, truck loading), with fully autonomous customer deployments targeted for 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk earthmoving/excavation on unstructured jobsites. It transfers only to moving soil in open ground; it does not demonstrate breaking asphalt or concrete pavement, nor careful exposure of an existing buried pipe.

sources.title: Built Robotics raises $64 million for robotic excavator Exosystem
sources.claim: Built Robotics sells an autonomous trenching product: retrofitted excavators dig utility trenches to spec on jobsites after contractors set the robots up.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous trench excavation in greenfield soil. Transfers to digging in open dirt only; no pavement breaking, no work over existing live pipes, no confined residential access.

sources.title: Gravis Robotics brings physical AI to earthmoving
sources.claim: Gravis Robotics demonstrated a retrofit kit at CONEXPO 2026 letting a Hitachi excavator dig a trench autonomously after an operator trains it, in a show demonstration area.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous trenching in a prepared demonstration plot. Shows soil digging autonomy in a purpose-built setting only; pavement demolition and pipe exposure are not shown.

tasks.label: Tap mainline sewers to install sewer saddles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Standard residential/small-commercial service tap: contractor's open trench in a public street, 6-10 ft deep, exposes an 8-12 in. VCP or PVC gravity main with live flow. Worker marks the crown, cores a 4-6 in. hole with a hole saw/shell cutter on a drill motor, retrieves the coupon and cuttings from the flowing main, lubricates the gasket, seats an Inserta-Tee or gasketed saddle at the correct angle and torques/seats it, then checks alignment for the lateral.

Large-diameter or deep main: 15-36 in. RCP, ductile iron, or brick main in a 10-20 ft shored trench or confined-space excavation on an arterial street under traffic control, sometimes with plugging/bypass of flow. Heavier bolt-on or strap-clamp saddle set with mastic/mortar, cut with a core drill or shell cutter, torqued to spec.

Tap on private property or easement: backyard, parking lot, campus or mobile-home-park private main, or a septic-to-sewer conversion. Cramped access, hand digging near unknown utilities, wet/muddy trench, PVC or asbestos-cement pipe, saddle set and sealed with limited working room.

Repair/rework connection: an existing tap has failed (broken saddle, intruding hammer tap, root-infiltrated hole). Worker grinds or cuts out the old connection, dresses the irregular, cracked or offset opening in the main, and fits a new saddle or repair coupling in the trench, occasionally working from inside a large-diameter main or manhole.

Tap made on a new or replacement main section at the job site with no flow: pipe staged on the surface or freshly laid in the trench, dry standard PVC/DIP main, saddle or tee cut and fitted at a marked station before the line is put in service.

sources.system: HGG ProCutter 600-900 / SPC pipe profiling machines
sources.title: HGG Debuts All Profile Cutter at FABTECH
sources.claim: HGG ProCutter CNC pipe-profiling machines clamp a pipe in a self-centering chuck and cut saddle profiles and branch holes automatically from a program, on pipe 2-24 in. diameter (up to 36 in. OD) - i.e., the tapping/hole-cutting step on fixtured pipe of municipal-main size.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: CNC branch/saddle hole cutting in pipe fabrication. It is the same physical operation as tapping a main (cutting a branch opening of several inches in a pipe wall), on the same pipe diameters as municipal sewer mains, performed under machine control with the pipe fixtured - exactly the E1 counterfactual presentation.

sources.system: Robotic Pipe Shop (Apollo Spool Milling Station + Aurora Spool Welding Station)
sources.title: Pipe Spool Automation - KRANENDONK
sources.claim: Kranendonk's Robotic Pipe Shop is a ... line combining an automated milling station and a robotic spool welding station that digitally defines and produces spools including tees and fittings, covering cutting, beveling, fit-up and joining without manual intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic fabrication of branch/tee connections on pipe. Fitting a branch onto a machined opening in a fixtured pipe and joining it leak-tight is the 'install the saddle' half of this task; the objects (pipe of comparable diameter, branch fittings) and the required positional precision are comparable.

sources.system: The Quadbots (Accurate Robot with multi-function end effector)
sources.title: Neighboring Mobile Robot Cell with Drilling and Fastening (SAE 2017-01-2094)
sources.claim: Electroimpact's 'Quadbots' cell at Boeing performs, autonomously on fixtured aerostructure parts, the full sequence of drilling, inspecting hole quality, applying sealant and inserting fasteners.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated drill-seal-fasten assembly in a fixtured cell. The saddle tap is the same chain of operations - cut a hole at a located position, verify it, apply sealant/gasket, and set and torque the fitting - showing that hole-making plus sealed mechanical fitting installation is done autonomously when the workpiece is fixtured and presented.

sources.system: Robotic lateral reinstatement / milling cutters (IMS Robotics, Sewer Robotics, KASRO, Picote)
sources.title: Technological Advancements Help Lateral Cutters Keep Pace with Evolving Rehab Processes
sources.claim: The robots that actually work on live mainline sewer connections in the field (in-pipe milling/lateral cutters from IMS Robotics, Sewer Robotics, KASRO and others) are driven continuously by an operator with joystick controls from a truck; they cut openings at connections but are not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related field task (cutting an opening at a mainline-to-lateral connection). It is cited as negative evidence: the field capability exists only under continuous teleoperation, so it cannot support an autonomous E2/E3 judgment for tapping a main and installing a saddle.

sources.title: How robotics is transforming excavators and the construction hire industry
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofits standard excavators for autonomous trenching on utility and solar construction sites - field autonomy in trench work is limited to earthmoving, with no pipe tapping or fitting installation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous excavation on job sites (E3). Cited to bound field capability - the autonomous field systems in this work domain dig trenches but perform no pipe coring, fitting placement or sealing, so they cannot complete this task in the field.

sources.title: Roadwork Robot Autonomously Digs Out, Repairs, Buried Utility Lines | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: ULC Technologies' Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System performs keyhole coring and vacuum excavation over buried utilities in roadways and is intended to install a fitting on a ... reinstate the surface, but it was a working prototype in utility field trials rather than a deployed autonomous system.
sources.transferJustification: Closest field analog: excavating to a buried main and installing a fitting on it in a public road (E3). Cited as negative/limiting evidence - the fitting-installation step's autonomy is not established and the system remains a trial prototype, so it cannot support an E3 judgment.

tasks.label: Prepare base for installation by removing unstable or unsuitable materials, compacting and grading the soil, draining or stabilizing weak or saturated soils and taking measures to prevent water penetration and migration of bedding sand.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential backyard patio or walkway (200-600 sq ft): access through a 3-4 ft gate, excavate 8-10 in of topsoil by mini-excavator or by hand near the foundation, utilities and tree roots, place separation geotextile, spread and plate-compact aggregate base in 3-4 in lifts, cut a 1-2% pitch away from the house and check with string line/level.

Residential driveway or large front walk (600-1,500 sq ft): open street-side access, skid steer/mini-excavator excavation, spoil hauled to a truck, subgrade proof-rolled, fabric laid, 8-12 in of aggregate placed and compacted in lifts with a walk-behind roller/plate, graded to design slope and tied into existing garage slab and curb.

Commercial or municipal open-site bulk base prep (plaza, parking area, industrial yard, thousands of sq ft): machine excavation and cut/fill, spoil hauling, aggregate spread and compacted in lifts, graded to design surface with GPS/laser control; no fabric, drainage structures or confined edges involved in this portion.

Commercial or municipal paver base prep with detail work: geotextile/geogrid placement, edge drains and catch-basin tie-ins, hand compaction around structures, curbs and existing pavement, work sequenced under traffic control and inspected against spec.

Weak or saturated subgrade remediation: identify soft spots by proof-rolling, undercut and remove unsuitable clay/organic material, install geotextile or geogrid, backfill with open-graded stone, install perforated drain pipe and outlet, recompact and re-grade before base placement.

Repair/reset of a settled or failed paver area (a sunken patio section, a rutted driveway apron, a heaved walkway): lift existing pavers, excavate contaminated or washed-out base in a confined patch, correct the drainage cause, recompact and re-grade flush with surrounding undisturbed pavement.

sources.title: Built Robotics releases 1st fully autonomous construction machinery in US | Construction Dive
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofit turns standard excavators into fully autonomous machines that dig trenches, excavate foundations and grade building pads on outdoor greenfield construction sites, commercially available to contractors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous bulk excavation and pad grading. Transfers to segmental-paver base prep on open sites because the objects (soil, aggregate), the machine (excavator working to a CSV grade model) and the outdoor construction setting are the same as excavating a paver base to depth and rough grade.

sources.system: A4CSEL for Earthworks (automated vibrating roller, bulldozer, backhoe, articulated dump truck)
sources.title: A⁴CSEL for Earthworks | Technology & Services | KAJIMA CORPORATION
sources.claim: Kajima's A4CSEL automated construction system uses automated vibrating rollers, bulldozers, backhoes and dump trucks that spread, level and compact ground; it has been applied at dam sites and at the Achiwa District Industrial ... land-development project, automating the full loading-hauling-leveling-compaction earthwork cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated embankment/land-development earthwork (loading, hauling, leveling, compaction). Transfers to open-site paver base prep because the material (soil and granular fill placed in lifts), the required compaction and grading to a design surface, and the outdoor site conditions are the same; it does not cover geotextile, drains or confined hand work.

sources.system: XCMG unmanned tandem rollers and pavers
sources.title: XCMG deploys driverless rollers, pavers on highway project | Equipment World
sources.claim: XCMG deployed a fleet of unmanned tandem rollers and pavers, guided by BeiDou satellite positioning, on a maintenance project on the Nanjing-Shanghai Expressway, compacting pavement layers without operators in the cab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unmanned compaction of pavement layers on a live roadway. Transfers partially to compacting a paver base on large open sites (same rolling passes over granular/bituminous layers), but not to confined residential lots or hand-compacted edges.

sources.system: BOMAG ROBOMAG BW154 autonomous tandem roller
sources.title: BOMAG Exhibits ROBOMAG Fully Autonomous Tandem Roller at CONEXPO 2020 | For Construction Pros
sources.claim: BOMAG's ROBOMAG is a fully autonomous tandem vibratory roller shown at bauma 2019 and CONEXPO 2020; it operates independently only within a defined, pre-set work area and remains a concept machine rather than a sold product.

sources.system: Teleo Supervised Autonomy retrofit (compact track loaders, dump trucks)
sources.title: Teleo Announces Customer Launch of Autonomous Capabilities for Heavy Construction Equipment | PR Newswire
sources.claim: Teleo's product for compact equipment on residential earthwork sites is supervised autonomy: a remote operator sits at a desk and switches machines between remote operation and autonomy, rather than the machines working unattended.

sources.system: Wacker Neuson RTLx-SC3 remote-controlled trench roller
sources.title: RTLx-SC3 Trench Roller | Wacker Neuson
sources.claim: The commercially available compaction equipment for confined excavations and sub-bases (trench rollers) is remote-controlled by a nearby human operator, not autonomous.

tasks.label: Supply and place base materials, edge restraints, bedding sand and jointing sand.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small residential patio/walkway (~200-600 sq ft) in a fenced back yard with landscaping and tight access: wheelbarrow crushed aggregate onto excavated subgrade, spread and compact in 2-4 in lifts with a plate compactor, cut and spike flexible plastic edge restraint along straight and curved edges with 10-in spikes, set screed rails and strike off ~1 in of bedding sand to slope, later sweep and vibrate polymeric jointing sand into joints.

Residential driveway or large patio (600-2,000 sq ft): skid-steer places and spreads 6-12 in of aggregate base, grade checked to fall/crown, compacted with ride-on or heavy plate compactor; aluminum/concrete edge restraint installed at perimeter; bedding sand screeded over the base; joint sand swept in and vibrated. Uneven subgrade, utilities, weather, and homeowner obstacles.

Commercial/institutional hardscape (retail plaza, campus walkway, hotel entry) built in a phased work zone amid pedestrians and traffic control: aggregate or cement-treated base placed and graded to spec tolerance, cast-in-place concrete or steel edge restraints formed and set, bedding course screeded, joint sand swept and vibrated, work inspected against project specification.

Large mechanized project (municipal street reconstruction, port/industrial yard, airport apron): trucked aggregate spread by loader/dozer/grader and rolled to density and tolerance, concrete curbs or edge beams placed, bedding sand spread by a towed screed box ahead of a mechanical paver-laying machine, joint sand spread by broom/spreader and vibrated over thousands of square feet, with survey checks.

Repair, reinstatement and maintenance: lift a settled or utility-cut area of existing segmental pavement, top up and recompact base, re-screed bedding sand to match surrounding grade, reset units and re-sand joints; or re-sand an existing pavement after cleaning. Small irregular areas bounded by existing pavement, obstacles and structures.

sources.system: Trimble Earthworks Grade Control Platform for Autonomous Compactors (on Dynapac CA5000)
sources.date: 2024-01 (test reported); platform still in beta testing thereafter
sources.title: Trimble tests autonomous soil compactor in BC - Equipment Journal
sources.claim: Trimble equipped a Dynapac CA5000 soil compactor with an autonomous compaction platform and ran it unmanned on a live earthworks jobsite, completing 37 hours of compaction alongside manned machines; this covers only the compaction sub-step of base placement on very large open fills, not fine grading, edge restraints, bedding sand or joint sand.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk soil compaction on an earthfill dam. It bears on 'place base materials' only in its compaction step, over huge open lifts with no perimeter detail work; it does not address edge restraints, screeded bedding sand or jointing sand.

sources.title: Exosystem Kit Converts Excavator into a Robot | Construction Kenya
