sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofits excavators for unmanned digging to an uploaded depth/grade plan inside a geofenced area on greenfield construction sites, i.e. bulk earthmoving autonomy exists outdoors, but the product line is trenching/piling and excavation, not aggregate base finishing, edging or sand bedding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous trenching/excavation on outdoor sites. Shows the state of the art for autonomous earthmoving is bulk soil removal to a plan in a geofenced area; it does not demonstrate placing aggregate base to paving tolerance, spiking edge restraints, or screeding a 1-inch sand bed.

sources.system: Tiger Stone / GF-6 brick road laying (road printing) machine
sources.developer: Tiger Stone (Vanku B.V., NL) / Linyi Brick Mate Machinery (GF-6 clone)
sources.title: A paving machine makes laying brick roads as easy as it gets | TheCivilEngineer.org
sources.claim: The best-known machine for segmental paving, the Tiger Stone / GF-6 road-printing laying machine, still needs one to three workers riding the machine to hand-feed and arrange the paving units, and it does not place base, bedding sand or jointing sand; the prepared sand bed must already exist ahead of it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical laying of the paving units themselves, the step immediately downstream of this task. It shows that even the most mechanized segmental paving equipment is human-fed and human-steered and presupposes a hand-screeded bedding course, so it cannot substantiate autonomous placement of base, edging or sand.

sources.title: Big Tech Roundtable 2026 | Part 4: Forecasting Future Compaction Technologies | For Construction Pros
sources.claim: A 2026 OEM roundtable on compaction technology states that full autonomy in field compaction remains distant because of jobsite complexity (other equipment, people, traffic, changing conditions), with current products aimed at operator assistance rather than unmanned operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: field compaction of pavement layers, a sub-step of base and bedding placement. Manufacturer's own assessment confirms that even this single, machine-friendly sub-step is not autonomous in normal jobsite conditions as of 2026.

tasks.label: Discuss the design with the client.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Set pavers, aligning and spacing them correctly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Backyard patio, pool deck or front walkway at a private home: 15-80 m2 of concrete pavers or natural-stone flags bedded on screeded sand, curved edges and radius borders, level changes and steps, mixed unit sizes/thicknesses, tight access through a side gate or between house and fence; alignment to the house line and consistent joint spacing checked by string line and eye; many perimeter units cut to fit.

Residential driveway or apron at a private home: 50-150 m2 rectangular field of standard rectangular concrete pavers set in herringbone between an installed soldier-course border and edge restraint; street-accessible; bond lines and joint spacing checked periodically against string lines; closure pieces cut in at the garage apron, borders and drains.

Commercial/institutional hardscape on an active construction site: entrance plaza, campus walkway or retail courtyard, 100-500 m2 of modular pavers with accent banding, changing patterns, curves, tree wells and utility castings; work sequenced around other trades and stored materials on a site taken as found.

Large uniform paving on institution-controlled premises: airport landside lot, port/terminal yard, bus depot or industrial yard paved or repaved with heavy 80-100 mm concrete pavers over a screeded bed; open rectangular areas of 500 m2 and up, one repeating bond, unrestricted machine access, controlled premises.

Municipal streetscape detail in the public right of way: brick crosswalks, curb ramps, tree-pit surrounds and historic brick sidewalk repairs; narrow strips, cambers and cross-slopes, utility castings and poles to work around, many cut pieces, live traffic and pedestrians beside the work zone.

Roadway paver reinstatement in a closed street work zone: relaying clay or concrete klinker paving over a straight carriageway run at least 2.4 m wide in a standard herringbone bond after utility or resurfacing work, referenced off the existing gutter course or kerb.

sources.title: Strobo – Street Robotic – Lo Minck Engineering
sources.claim: Strobo is an autonomously driving paving vehicle that de-stacks pavers from a pallet, aligns them and places them precisely into the existing street paving with a gripper, guided by a triangulation sensor and lidar, at roughly 120-160 m2 per day.

sources.title: Machinaal straten - Street Robotics
sources.claim: The Strobo paving robot works autonomously with a single operator, lays small-format pavers in the two most common bonds (herringbone and elbow bond) at about 180 m2/day, needs a street width of at least 240 cm, and works from the existing paving, gutter course or edge restraint as its reference after a paver has made the initial set-out.

sources.title: Succesvolle inzet straatrobot op Schiphol | DeJongCeba
sources.claim: At Schiphol airport the Strobo street robot autonomously repaved a 1,000 m2 lot with 100 mm thick concrete pavers, with no hands involved other than the operator's.

sources.title: Vooruitstrevend infrawerk begint bij DeJongCeba – INTO business
sources.claim: Contractor DeJongCeba states it laid fully robotized paving at Schiphol for the first time in November, confirming the deployment date and that the work was done on an operating airport's premises.

sources.title: Machinaal Bestraten - De Kracht Van Efficiëntie | De Krom B.V.
sources.claim: Paving contractor De Krom B.V. offers autonomous machine paving with the Strobo robot as a commercial service, with one operator supervising the machine.

sources.title: Hadrian X bricklaying robot builds first homes in demo program - The Robot Report
sources.claim: FBR's Hadrian X is a mobile robotic blocklaying ... that places concrete masonry units to CAD-defined positions outdoors on uncontrolled home-building sites; it completed the first five homes of a US demonstration program with CRH ... 2024.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying concrete masonry units to designed positions. It corroborates that precise, autonomous placement of paver-sized concrete units is achievable on as-found outdoor sites (comparable objects and millimetre placement tolerances), though it builds walls rather than bedding units into a sand-set pavement.

sources.system: Optimas Pacer P22 / PaveJet paver laying machines
sources.title: Optimas Paver laying machine type Pacer P22
sources.claim: Mainstream mechanised paver-laying equipment used on commercial jobs (paver laying machines and vacuum/clamp heads that set pre-arranged paver layers) is directly controlled by a machine driver, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (setting paving units). Cited as context showing that the commercially dominant mechanised paving equipment is operator-driven and therefore cannot support a positive autonomy judgment.

tasks.label: Sweep sand into the joints and compact pavement until the joints are full.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential patio or walkway (200–800 sq ft) at a private home: worker pours dry or polymeric joint sand over the freshly laid pavers, sweeps it diagonally into joints with a stiff push broom, blows/sweeps excess off the surface, runs a walk-behind vibratory plate compactor (with protective pad) over the field in several directions, then re-sands and re-compacts until every joint is full to the chamfer; must work around planters, steps, house walls, curved edges and cut pieces.

Residential driveway or large patio with slopes, curves, permeable or wide joints: bulk joint sand or chip dumped and spread, swept in with broom or push-type joint filler, plate-compacted in multiple passes; joints checked and topped up repeatedly, edges and soldier courses hand-worked; occasional wetting/settling of polymeric sand and clean-up before it sets.

Commercial or municipal streetscape work: plaza, crosswalk, transit platform or sidewalk paver panel inside an active traffic/pedestrian work zone; sand swept into joints by hand broom or walk-behind filler, compacted with plate compactor, repeated passes until joints fully consolidated, then surface swept clean for immediate public use, working around utility covers, tree pits, bollards and lane closures.

Large mechanically installed pavement (port container yard, industrial hardstand, big parking lot or airport apron): joint sand spread from bulk bags or spreader, broomed in with tow-behind/loader-mounted brooms, compacted by several linked heavy vibratory plate compactors over thousands of square feet, with repeated sand-and-vibrate cycles until joints are completely filled and consolidated; the paving jobsite is open, dusty and shared with material trucks and laying machines.

Maintenance/repair re-sanding of existing segmental pavement: joints cleaned of weeds and washed-out sand, new joint sand swept in, surface plate-compacted and re-sanded until joints are full; done on an occupied driveway, courtyard or commercial entrance with furniture, parked cars and pedestrians present.

sources.title: Autonomous Equipment in the Asphalt Industry | For Construction Pros
sources.claim: BOMAG's ROBOMAG is a fully autonomous tandem roller that can compact a pre-planned area using geo-fencing and GPS, but it is an asphalt/soil compaction concept machine shown at trade shows, not a system that spreads or sweeps joint sand into segmental paver joints or plate-compacts pavers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous compaction of asphalt with a ride-on roller. It covers only the compaction half of this task, on a continuous asphalt mat rather than on segmental pavers, and provides no capability for spreading and brooming joint sand or judging when joints are full, so it cannot substantiate completion of the whole instance.

sources.title: XCMG deploys driverless rollers, pavers on highway project | Equipment World
sources.claim: XCMG operated driverless rollers and pavers on a highway project, completing scheduled driving, steering and rolling compaction under satellite positioning; again this is roadway asphalt compaction, not paver joint sanding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous highway asphalt paving and rolling. Transfer fails because the task here requires distributing granular joint sand over laid units, brushing it into 2-5 mm joints, and iterating sand/vibrate cycles until joints are full — none of which a driverless roller performs.

sources.system: Optimas paver joint filling device (wheel loader / Mini 3.0)
sources.title: Used Optimas H 88 for sale on Machineseeker.com
sources.claim: Purpose-built joint-filling machines for segmental pavers exist commercially, but they are wheel-loader attachments or push units that require a continuous human operator; no autonomous version is documented.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (sweeping joint material into paver joints), but the machine is an operator-driven attachment on a manned wheel loader, i.e. continuous human control, so under the limited-intervention rule it cannot support a positive judgment at any tier.

sources.title: EB Sweeping Broom | Probst
sources.claim: Probst's sweeping broom for brushing joint sand into paver joints is a manually handled tool, confirming that the joint-sanding step is currently done with human-guided implements.
sources.transferJustification: Exactly this task's sweeping step, but performed by a hand-guided broom under continuous human control; it shows the tooling is manual rather than robotic and cannot substantiate autonomous completion.

sources.title: Monumental raises $32 million to scale its construction robots to more building sites | I amsterdam
sources.claim: Monumental operates autonomous brick-and-mortar laying robots on active European construction sites, demonstrating autonomous masonry unit placement outdoors, but not horizontal joint sanding or vibratory plate compaction of paved surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous laying of masonry units with mortar joints on unstructured construction sites. It shows outdoor jobsite autonomy for unit placement, but the reported capability is placing bricks and beds of mortar with a crane-mounted arm; there is no evidence of spreading loose sand over a laid field, brooming it into joints, running a vibratory plate compactor, or verifying joints are full.

sources.system: Mobile robot for grouting floor tile joints
sources.title: Development and implementation of a mobile robot for grouting floor tile joints | IJRA
sources.claim: The nearest robotic analogue for filling joints in a laid floor is a research mobile robot that grouts floor tile joints, but it executes user-defined coordinates rather than perceiving and finishing joints autonomously, and includes no compaction step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: filling the joints of a laid tile floor with jointing material indoors. Transfer fails: it is a coordinate-scripted laboratory prototype with no vibratory compaction, no repeated sand/compact cycles, and no demonstrated outdoor paver-field operation.

tasks.label: Screed sand level to an even thickness, and recheck sand exposed to elements, raking and rescreeding if necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential driveway, patio or walkway: after the compacted aggregate base is graded, the paver installer sets screed rails (pipes/angle) on the base, spreads ~1 in. of bedding sand, pulls a screed board to a uniform loose thickness following the drainage slope, removes rails and fills the voids by hand, working in an irregular area bounded by house walls, steps, tree roots and utility boxes, never walking on the screeded bed.

Commercial/municipal hardscape: plaza, sidewalk, crosswalk or streetscape section paved in stages beside live traffic or pedestrians; bedding sand screeded in strips between rails or off curb/edge restraints, worked around manhole and valve covers, tree pits and expansion joints, matching adjacent finished grade.

Large open-area paving: parking lot, industrial pavement or port/yard slab of several thousand square meters, bedding course spread and screeded in long uniform lanes ahead of a mechanical paver-laying machine or crew, few obstructions, tight elevation tolerance over long runs.

Rechecking sand exposed to the elements: returning to a bed screeded the previous day or left through rain/wind, inspecting for saturation, washouts, wind drift and footprints, deciding what to discard, raking out or replacing damaged sand and re-screeding the affected areas before laying resumes.

Tight detail bedding: steps and risers, curved or radius edges, tree surrounds, narrow paths, small repair/relay patches where the bed is struck off by hand with a short board or trowel against fixed adjoining pavers, and voids under lifted units are refilled and levelled flush.

sources.title: VX7000 – The New Benchmark in Large-Format 3D Printing enters customer production
sources.claim: voxeljet's VX7000 large-format sand binder-jetting system uses an automated recoater that spreads and levels foundry sand layer by layer across a 7 x 7 m build area, handling over 60 tonnes of sand; it entered customer production in early 2026. This is a purpose-built enclosed machine (E1-type setting) that screeds sand to a uniform thickness without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: spreading and striking off a bed of silica sand to an even thickness over a large fixtured area. Same material class and same physical operation as screeding bedding sand, at far finer thickness tolerance than the ±3 mm/3 m required of a paver bedding course, over an area comparable to a residential patio — but only inside a purpose-built machine where the bed is bounded by the build box.

sources.system: ExOne S-Max / S-Max Pro sand 3D printer
sources.title: SANDHELDEN Turns to Binder Jetting and ExOne for its Sustainable, Sand Projects
sources.claim: ExOne's industrial sand printers (S-Max / S-Max Pro) run a fully automated recoater that lays a thin, even layer of foundry sand for each pass, in continuous 24/7 production use in foundries; the machine, not a human, produces the level sand surface.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated screeding of sand to an even thickness. Confirms that levelling loose sand to a specified uniform thickness is a solved, commercially reliable operation when the sand is presented inside a purpose-built, fixtured enclosure — the E1 counterfactual for this task.

sources.system: Four-Wheel Concrete Laser Screed Robot / ZP-415A
sources.title: Four Wheel Concrete Laser Screeding Robot for Sale
sources.claim: Fangshi's four-wheel concrete laser screed robot autonomously drives over freshly placed concrete and distributes, vibrates and levels it to a laser-referenced plane; the company's floor robots are sold commercially and used on building projects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laser-referenced screeding of a freshly placed loose material to a flat plane. The screeding action and tolerance class (±5 mm) are comparable to a bedding course, supporting the same operation in a flat, obstruction-free bay; it does not transfer to a real paver bed on site because the machine tracks over the material it levels, which would rut and differentially compact an uncompacted 25 mm sand bed.

sources.system: Fangshi concrete floor construction robot series (incl. ZP-415A laser screed robot)
sources.title: Chinese Construction Robotics Company Fangshi Technology Expands to Singapore
sources.claim: Fangshi's concrete floor construction robots were deployed on a project in Singapore and inspected floors held flatness deviation within 5 mm, evidencing real deployment of autonomous screeding-class machines on building floors (construction-site setting).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine screeding of placed material on jobsite floors. Shows the maturity level of autonomous screeding is ±5 mm flatness on large flat concrete pours; it does not cover screeding an uncompacted granular bedding course on a prepared aggregate base outdoors, nor rail setting, edge work or weather repair.

sources.title: POWERPLAN PP Screeding Machine
sources.claim: The state of mechanisation for bedding-material screeding in block paving is operator-driven attachments: Probst's POWERPLAN PP screeding machine is a machine-mounted screed designed for bedding material, steered by an equipment operator rather than run autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same task (screeding bedding sand for block paving), but the machine is operator-controlled, so it cannot support a positive autonomy judgment; it is cited to show that no autonomous jobsite bedding-screed system was found.

sources.title: Autonomous Dozer Sand Grading Under Localization Uncertainties (IEEE Xplore)
sources.claim: Autonomous grading of loose sand piles by a dozer remains a research problem addressed in academic experiments, not a fielded capability at paving-bedding tolerances.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous levelling of sand outdoors. Cited only as context for negative judgments: the work is a research demonstration on prepared sand piles, far from the ±3 mm bedding-course quality and site conditions of segmental paving.

tasks.label: Cut paving stones to size and for edges, using a splitter and a masonry saw.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential patio/walkway/driveway job: straight cut-offs and half-pavers for the border and field edges, marked off the as-laid gap and produced on a hydraulic or manual block splitter set up beside the work area; dozens to a few hundred quick splits, cut pieces handed to the layer within seconds.

Residential/light-commercial job: curved, angled and notched cuts on a wet masonry saw \wuts around drains, utility covers, downspouts, posts, step nosings, tree grates and radius borders; each piece scribed to the field as actually laid, dry-fit and re-trimmed as needed.

Commercial or municipal streetscape/plaza installation: high-volume repetitive cutting at a saw station on site (table wet saw, water/dust control), producing soldier-course and border pieces to a specified pattern, sometimes full days of cutting for a laying crew.

Natural stone work: irregular flagstone, bluestone treads, granite setts/cobbles 50-100 mm thick \wutrimmed and scribed to fit hand-laid joints, split on a guillotine or cut on a saw, with grain, thickness and color variation from piece to piece.
Segmental retaining wall, steps and caps: splitting SRW blocks for corners and curves and mitring/cutting cap units on the splitter and saw to close radii and returns on the wall as built.

sources.system: BACA Robo SawJet / Robolution Pro (KUKA KR 210 QUANTEC)
sources.title: Innovative solutions in the stone cutting industry: 100 robots for BACA Systems in North America | KUKA Global
sources.claim: BACA Systems builds robotic stone-cutting cells (Robo SawJet, Robolution Pro) in which KUKA industrial robots carrying a saw and a waterjet nozzle cut stone slabs to programmed sizes, shapes, angles and miters; hundreds of these cells are in commercial use in North American fabrication shops.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting stone slabs to programmed size and profile with a diamond saw blade and abrasive waterjet. It is the same physical operation as sizing paving stones and cutting edge pieces (hard mineral material, diamond blade, straight/angled/curved cuts) at equal or better precision, with the workpiece fixtured on a cell table.

sources.system: BACA Robo SawJet at Hard Rock Stone Works
sources.title: Case Study: Hard Rock Stone Works - BACA Systems
sources.claim: A US granite fabricator has run a BACA Robo SawJet since 2016; the robot cuts slabs continuously on a dual-table cell while operators only load and unload, i.e. the cutting itself runs unattended.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (programmed saw/waterjet cutting of stone), evidencing sustained worker-quality throughput and reliability in daily commercial production rather than a one-off demo.

sources.title: Fully Automated Cutting Line | Stone Fabrication | BACA Systems
sources.claim: BACA's Autocut Line adds robotic loading and unloading to the Robo SawJet cell so that a high-volume cutting line runs with minimal labor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated stone cutting including material presentation. Shows the cutting cell can run with limited human intervention once the work is brought to the machine, which is the E1 counterfactual for paver cutting.

sources.title: Creative And Artistic Paver Installations - Turf Magazine
sources.claim: Colored concrete pavers are cut into precise custom shapes by CNC waterjet at Paverart's facility; the finished cut pieces are shipped to hardscape contractors who install them instead of free-hand cutting the shapes on site.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same objects and cut geometry as the task (concrete paving units cut to size and to curved/irregular edge shapes), performed by a machine-controlled cutting head with the paver fixtured on a table in a plant rather than by a worker with a saw on site.

sources.title: Masa Splitting machines - Concrete block production
sources.claim: Masa supplies splitting machines for concrete block and paver plants in which blocks are pushed automatically onto the splitter table and hydraulically driven knives produce a defined break line; the splitter can run online inside a production plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: guillotine splitting of concrete paving/wall units to a defined line \w the machine equivalent of the hand block splitter named in the task, on the same material and unit sizes (40-250 mm high), with automatic feed of each unit to the knife.

sources.title: Stone splitting - MEC
sources.claim: MEC supplies automatic stone splitting lines built from H-frame splitters that incorporate automatic movement of the material and automatic actuation of ..., used on quarry-layer and sawn natural stone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: splitting natural stone (granite, limestone, sandstone, porphyry) into setts, cubes and slabs \w the same splitter operation and the same natural-stone paving materials a segmental paver splits by hand, with automated handling and splitting.

sources.title: Hadrian X bricklaying robot builds first homes in demo program - The Robot Report
sources.claim: FBR's Hadrian X is a truck-mounted blocklaying robot that works outdoors from a 3D CAD model, unpacks blocks from pallets and cuts them to size with an on-board saw module before laying them; five houses were built with it in a US demonstration program with CRH ... 2024.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous on-site cutting of concrete masonry units to size (height, mitre and gable cuts) for a course. Transfer is partial: the cut is made inside the machine's own fixtured saw module on blocks it unpacks itself, driven by a CAD model, not on found pavers scribed to an as-laid field, so it substantiates machine-fixtured cutting (E1) rather than on-site paver fitting.

tasks.label: Compact bedding sand and pavers to finish the paved area, using a plate compactor.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential backyard patio or pool deck: irregular/curved field with steps, seat walls, fire pit, planters and coping; plate compactor with protective pad run over laid pavers in several directions, right up to the house wall and curved borders; narrow side-yard access, sloped grade, homeowner property.

Residential driveway or large rectangular patio: a big, essentially flat and regular open paver field; the plate compactor is walked over the whole surface in overlapping passes to seat pavers into the bedding sand, then again after joint sand, with edges at the garage apron and edge restraint.
Residential walkway/garden path: narrow, curved strip a few feet wide bordered by lawn, beds and soft edges; short runs, frequent turns, plate must not drop off unrestrained edges.

Commercial/institutional open field: retail or campus plaza, courtyard, entry apron, parking bay or heavy-duty industrial/port yard paving; large flat regular areas, often mechanically installed pavers, compacted with a large reversible plate under a contractor-controlled work area.

Municipal streetscape: sidewalk paver bands, curb extensions and crosswalks in the public right-of-way; utility castings, tree pits, poles and curb faces inside or bordering the field, live traffic and pedestrians adjacent, staged in short segments.

Repair/reset work: lifting and resetting a settled or heaved section, utility-cut restoration or small patch; small confined areas, matching surrounding grade, compaction feathered into existing pavement.

sources.title: Ammann develops innovative autonomous plate compactor | Global Highways
sources.claim: Ammann built a prototype autonomous vibratory plate compactor: after the operator teaches the perimeter, the machine plans its own pattern and compacts the bounded area strip by strip using GPS, an electronic compass and collision detection.
sources.transferJustification: Same tool class as the task (vibratory plate compactor) and the same operation (covering a bounded paved/granular area with overlapping compaction passes); the difference is the surface compacted (soil/gravel vs. bedding sand with pavers over it, which normally requires a paver pad).

sources.title: AMMANN UNVEILS FIRST-EVER AUTONOMOUS VIBRATORY PLATE | Ammann Group
sources.claim: The Ammann prototype's work area is defined by an operator remotely driving the plate around the borders of the area ... ('Teach In'), after which it works on its own inside that polygon.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the autonomy is boundary-defined area coverage, i.e. the same 'compact this defined paved area' problem, but only for a taught, obstacle-free polygon.

sources.system: Trimble Earthworks Grade Control Platform for Autonomous Compactors on Dynapac CA 5000
sources.title: Trimble Completes First Test of Fully Autonomous Soil Compactor on a Live Jobsite | Trimble Resource Center
sources.claim: A fully autonomous Dynapac CA 5000 soil compactor running Trimble Earthworks autonomy completed 37 hours of real production compaction on the Site C dam construction project alongside a human-operated fleet.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: compaction of a granular layer to a specified standard by planned pass coverage. It shows autonomous compaction can reach accepted production quality, but with a 12-tonne roller on open earthworks, not a plate on laid pavers.

sources.title: Trimble tests fully autonomous soil compactor on B.C. dam project | Heavy Equipment Guide
sources.claim: Trimble/press coverage notes the Site C proving ground was chosen because the work areas are simple and the compaction task repetitive, indicating autonomous compaction is proven only in uncomplicated open areas.
sources.transferJustification: Scopes where autonomous compaction works today: simple, open, obstacle-free work areas rather than the curved, stepped, obstacle-filled fields typical of segmental paving.

sources.title: A⁴CSEL for Earthworks | Technology & Services | KAJIMA CORPORATION
sources.claim: Kajima has deployed its A4CSEL automated construction system in production, running autonomous vibratory rollers, bulldozers and dump ... to place and compact CSG embankment layers at Naruse Dam.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeated-pass compaction of granular fill to a quality-controlled standard, performed autonomously in a large, cleared, machine-only work area; demonstrates area-coverage compaction autonomy at production quality, but not on segmental paver surfaces.

sources.title: Bomag previews autonomous compaction robot - Construction Briefing
sources.claim: Bomag's ROBOMAG autonomous tandem roller concept operates fully autonomously only inside a pre-defined work area, using GPS geofencing plus obstacle detection, with joystick remote control needed outside that area.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous compaction confined to a purpose-defined, people-free work area — supports capability at a purpose-built (E1) presentation only, not in open human worksites.

sources.title: Big Tech Roundtable 2026 | Part 4: Forecasting Future Compaction Technologies | For Construction Pros
sources.claim: Compaction equipment makers state that full autonomy on real jobsites remains distant because of jobsite complexity (people, traffic, other equipment, changing conditions), with soil applications expected to be automated before complex paving sites.
sources.transferJustification: Negative/context evidence on the state of compaction autonomy in unstructured and human-occupied paving worksites as of mid-2026.

tasks.label: Design paver installation layout pattern and create markings for directional references of joints and stringlines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Standard residential job (patio, walkway or driveway) at an occupied home: installer walks the yard, picks pattern type and orientation off the house wall or existing hardscape, squares the field with tape and 3-4-5, drives stakes, pulls stringlines, and paints/chalks border and joint-direction reference lines on the compacted aggregate base. No georeferenced CAD model or survey control; fenced yard, trees, plantings, grade changes, loose granular surfaces.

Custom residential feature work: curved walkways, radius borders, circle kits, pool decks, banding and inlays. Pattern and starting course are designed on the spot to fit existing steps, coping and walls and to minimize cuts; curves are marked with paint, flexible forms or trammel arcs on the base.

Commercial/institutional hardscape built to engineered drawings with survey control on an active construction site (plaza, courtyard, entry drive, permeable parking bay): installer establishes baselines and control lines from the plan, marks border/soldier-course and joint-direction references over a large area on a concrete or bituminous base or graded aggregate, and sets stringlines from those marks.

Municipal streetscape work in the public right-of-way under traffic control (crosswalk pavers, sidewalk bands, transit plaza): layout referenced to curb lines and survey stakes from roadway plans, markings created for pattern direction, band edges and saw-cut lines, often on night or staged closures.

Podium deck / rooftop pedestal paver or interior slab paving inside a building under construction: flat concrete slab, coordinated drawings available, installer snaps grid and joint-direction lines on the slab and marks control points for the pedestal or bedding layout.

sources.title: HP SitePrint prints 2D plans on construction site floors - AEC Magazine
sources.claim: HP SitePrint is an autonomous construction layout robot that prints layout lines, arcs and text directly onto site surfaces including concrete, tarmac and pavement, guided by a robotic total station; used by Skanska and on 80+ pilot projects (residential, parking, airport, hospital).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: construction layout marking. The paver task's physical output is the same artifact - reference lines and text marked on a prepared paving surface from a design - on the same media (concrete, pavement, tarmac) and at tighter precision than paver joint references need.

sources.title: HP SitePrint - Robotic Layout Solution | HP Official Site
sources.claim: HP states a layout accuracy tolerance of about +/-2 mm for SitePrint printing with total-station guidance, tighter than the tolerance paver installers hold on layout baselines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: construction layout marking; establishes that printed reference lines meet the precision a paver layout baseline demands.

sources.title: HP SitePrint: Autonomous Construction Layout Robot | HP Tech Takes
sources.claim: Contractors have used HP SitePrint in production for complex geometry, including curved line layout, with reported cost reductions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: construction layout marking of curved geometry, matching curved borders and radius bands in hardscape work when the curve is supplied as a design file.

sources.title: Civ Robotics FAQ | Answering Your Questions on Construction Layout Robots
sources.claim: CivDot Mini is a GNSS-guided autonomous marking robot that sprays continuous solid or dashed layout lines outdoors for roadway, parking-lot and airport layout at sub-inch (2 cm) accuracy, explicitly replacing pulling tape and string lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor construction layout line marking from DXF design files on pavement and graded base - the same act as marking joint-direction and stringline reference lines for a large paved area, at comparable precision.

sources.title: From 8 Hours to 2: Fast-Tracking Highway Layout with CivDot Mini
sources.claim: CivDot Mini has been in production use ... months on an active outdoor highway construction project (I-485 Express Lanes, Charlotte NC) doing night-shift road layout that previously used tape measures, string lines and spray paint.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: field layout marking on an unstructured outdoor civil site, showing worker-quality output in traffic-staged night-shift conditions comparable to municipal paver streetscape layout.

sources.title: Robot Surveyors Bring Autonomous Precision to Construction Layouts
sources.claim: CivDot autonomously drives an outdoor site and spray-paints surveyed coordinate marks on the ground to about 0.3 inch precision from an uploaded coordinate file; a worker follows only to add flags or stakes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: construction stakeout marking on unpaved graded ground - the surface condition of a compacted aggregate paver base - showing paint reference marks placed autonomously to sub-inch precision.

sources.title: Line Marking Robot - TinySurveyor Terra | Aptella
sources.claim: TinySurveyor is a commercially sold autonomous pre-marking robot that marks out road lines and sports-field lines outdoors from uploaded design files using GNSS or total station positioning, with repeatable 2-3 cm accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor pre-marking of design lines on pavement and open ground, the same output as directional reference marking for paving joints, performed autonomously in live-traffic roadway settings.

sources.title: BIM-Driven Layout for Construction | Dusty Robotics
sources.claim: Dusty Robotics' FieldPrinter is an autonomous layout ... that prints full-size model geometry directly on jobsite floors (concrete slab, plywood, asphalt) at up to 1/16 inch accuracy, operated by a single person, and is used by general contractors such as Turner.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: printing full-scale layout geometry on flat slabs, matching the marking of grid, border and joint-direction lines on a slab for pedestal or bedded paver installation.

tasks.label: Sweep sand from the surface prior to opening to traffic.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small residential patio or walkway (150-600 sq ft) behind a house: after plate-compacting joint sand, the installer sweeps/blows residual sand off the pavers, working around steps, coping, curved edges, planting beds, house walls and a narrow side-yard gate, without pulling sand out of the joints.

Residential driveway or large open patio (800-2,000 sq ft): a broad, essentially flat paved field bounded by a garage apron, curb and lawn edge; the crew sweeps excess joint/bedding sand off the whole surface with a push broom or walk-behind power broom before the homeowner drives on it.

Commercial hardscape jobsite (retail/office plaza, campus walkway, entry drive, parking area, 5,000-50,000 sq ft): after final compaction and sanding, residual sand is swept from large open paved areas with a power broom or ride-on sweeper, amid staged pallets, cones and phased work areas, before the area is opened.

Municipal segmental pavement in a traffic-controlled work zone (street section, alley, crosswalk, bus pad): excess sand is swept from the finished surface and gutter line before the lane is reopened to vehicles, under lane closures with public traffic adjacent.

Industrial/institutional paved area on institution-controlled premises (port container yard, transit plaza, airport landside apron, distribution-yard paver section): very large open surfaces of segmental units swept clear of residual sand before heavy traffic returns.

Repair, reset or utility-cut restoration patch (a few dozen square feet) in a driveway, sidewalk or street: after re-sanding the reset area the worker sweeps sand off the patch and the surrounding pavement, working around parked cars, curbs, meters and street furniture, often finishing by hand.

sources.title: Robotic Trombia Free sweeper system in operation in Jätekukko, Kuopio, Finland
sources.claim: An autonomous Trombia Free electric sweeper works as a yard-duty sweeper at a waste-sorting facility, clearing grit, fines and debris from an outdoor paved yard; routes are taught once, then missions are scheduled and monitored remotely and the machine docks for autonomous emptying.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing accumulated grit/fine granular material from a paved outdoor working surface. Same physical action (mechanical broom sweeping of sand-grade material off hard pavement) and comparable surface, so performance transfers to sweeping residual joint sand off finished paver surfaces.

sources.developer: Trombia Technologies / Port Authority of NY & NJ
sources.title: Busy cargo port tests robot street sweepers
sources.claim: A driverless Trombia Free was tested at Port Newark cleaning parking lots, container warehouses and garages, navigating with 3D lidar and stopping or manoeuvring around obstacles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sweeping loose debris and grit from large paved lots and yards. The material (dust, sand, grit) and surface (hard paving on institution-controlled premises) match the sand-removal step on large paver installations.

sources.title: ViaBot officially launches new parking lot sweeping solution
sources.claim: ViaBot's RUNO autonomous mobile robot sweeps parking lots and walking paths at corporate campuses and has been deployed to Bay Area properties by facility manager Cushman & Wakefield, autonomously dumping collected debris.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor sweeping of paved lots and walkways at managed properties. Comparable open paved areas of driveway-to-plaza size and comparable fine granular debris, so it substantiates sweeping sand off a finished paved field.

sources.title: Tennant Company Unveils X16 SWEEP for Autonomous, Around-the-Clock Industrial Sweeping
sources.claim: Tennant's X16 SWEEP, launched with Brain Corp's BrainOS, is an autonomous robotic sweeper for warehousing, logistics and light manufacturing that generates and optimizes its own cleaning paths rather than following pre-programmed fixed routes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous sweeping of dry debris and dust from hard industrial floors. Same physical action on a flat hard surface; supports sweeping sand from a paved area presented as a plain flat field.

sources.title: Gausium Launches WeatherSense Guard: Bringing Intelligent Weather Awareness to the Beetle Outdoor Sweeper
sources.claim: The Gausium Beetle is a ... autonomous sweeping robot sold for industrial sites and outdoor spaces such as sidewalks, parks and ..., with weather-aware auto-docking; Gausium reports real-world deployments in high-traffic areas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor robotic sweeping of paved plazas and walkways. Comparable surface and debris; supports clearing loose sand from mid-sized paved areas inside managed premises.

sources.system: Trombia Free; Bucher CityCat 2020ev with Enway autonomy
sources.title: Driverless sweepers - Transport Engineer
sources.claim: Trade-press assessment of driverless sweepers: Trombia and Bucher/Enway machines operate only within predefined, previously mapped routes or zones, and Trombia is judged ready for deployment only inside private industrial sites or ...; the Singapore road trial ran with a safety driver aboard.

sources.title: Scythe Robotics debuts video series for M.52 autonomous mower onboarding
sources.claim: Scythe Robotics' M.52 is a fully autonomous commercial mower deployed with landscape contractors across 14 states, showing that contractor-owned autonomous ground machines can be set up per property and then cover outdoor grounds without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous area coverage of outdoor grounds by a contractor crew that brings the machine to a new managed property and defines the work area once. Shows the per-site deployment workflow a paving crew would need, though the working tool is a mower deck rather than a broom.

tasks.label: Resurface an outside area with cobblestones, terracotta tiles, concrete or other materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential hardscape at a private home: resurfacing a driveway, patio or walkway with concrete pavers, clay pavers or stone. Irregular outline, curves, soldier-course borders, steps, utility covers and planting beds; many units must be cut to fit; access is through gates and side yards; the finished surface must look right to the homeowner.

Repair / re-lay of an existing paved area (home or commercial): lifting settled, rutted or broken pavers over a patch, salvaging reusable units, re-screeding bedding sand, resetting units so they match the surrounding surface in bond, color and level, then re-sanding joints.

Commercial or institutional hardscape on an active construction site: plaza, campus walkway, courtyard or entry apron with banding, multiple unit sizes/colors, radii, tree pits, drains and steps; laid to architectural layout drawings alongside other trades.

Large uniform outdoor runs for municipal or commercial clients: resurfacing a straight street section, parking bays, alley or permeable-paver parking lot with one standard rectangular concrete paver in a standard bond, laid curb-to-curb over a screeded bed inside a traffic-controlled work zone.

Heavy-duty segmental paving on controlled premises: airport airside service areas, port/terminal or distribution-yard pavement, large rectangular lots of thick heavy-duty concrete pavers, machine-laid, with site access controlled by the operator of the facility.

sources.system: Straatrobot (StreetRobotics / De Krom / DeJongCeba paving robot)
sources.developer: StreetRobotics (De Krom Groep, DeJongCeba, MBI, LoMinck Engineering)
sources.title: Succesvolle inzet straatrobot op Schiphol | DeJongCeba
sources.claim: The StreetRobotics/De Krom 'straatrobot' repaved a 1,000 m2 airside lot at Schiphol Airport with 10 cm thick concrete pavers; the company states the machine operates autonomously and no hands touch the paving except the operator's.

sources.title: Ruggenbreekwerk automatiseren | BouwBelang
sources.claim: De Krom used its electric paving robot on the municipal reconstruction of the Sint Martinusstraat in Rucphen; the machine lays stones fully automatically on tracks, guided by a vision scanner that continuously reads the street from curb to curb including height differences, with one operator on the machine.

sources.title: Launch event - Street Robotics
sources.claim: Technical description of the paving robot: a laser scanner makes a 3D scan of the street and finds the last laid row and the depth of the sand bed, and a robot arm takes up to five concrete pavers from a pallet, sets them against the previous row and presses them into the sand bed; a human paver is still needed to lay the starting point and to finish corners at manhole covers and curbs.

sources.title: Specificaties - Street Robotics
sources.claim: Vendor specifications for the Strobo paving robot: fully autonomous, several laying bonds in 'keiformaat' concrete pavers, one operator, production capacity about 180 m2 per day.

sources.developer: Street Robotics (Johan de Krom, Joost Groefsema)
sources.title: Dit is de stratenmaker van de toekomst: 'Geen rugklachten meer' (Omroep Gelderland, via Headliner)
sources.claim: In July 2025 the Street Robotics paving robot was presented in Ulft as a machine that can pave straight roads by itself, alongside a packaging machine that stacks reclaimed paving materials into new packs.

sources.developer: not stated in article (Dutch paving-robot supplier)
sources.title: Primeur in Julianadorp: bestratingsrobot aan het werk aan de Vijverweg
sources.claim: A paving robot was put to work resurfacing the Vijverweg, a public street, in May 2026 — the first use of such a robot by that municipality — indicating continued field deployment of autonomous paver-laying machines on public streets.

sources.system: PavePal P900 Floor Tile Paving Robot
sources.title: Partner Robotics picks up funding to deploy more construction robots - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Partner Robotics sells the PavePal P900 floor tile ..., which automates indoor tile laying on building floors and is being deployed on construction sites; it handles tile formats from 450x450 mm to 800x800 mm and larger.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying large-format floor tiles onto a mortar bed to a level, aligned surface. It shares the objects (rigid modular units), the millimetre-level alignment and levelling tolerance, and the row-by-row placement logic of laying terracotta tiles or pavers on a bedding layer; the demonstrated environment is an indoor building floor rather than an outdoor area.

sources.title: Autonomous Equipment Makes Its Way to Paving Job Sites | AsphaltPro Magazine
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Autonomous Track Loader performs excavation, grading, pad preparation and compaction on job sites without an operator, showing that the earthwork/base-preparation stage of outdoor surfacing is automatable on site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: site earthwork and pad preparation, the step that precedes laying segmental units. It substantiates autonomous grading/compaction of the sub-base outdoors, but not placement of paving units, so it is used only as supporting context.

tasks.label: Cement the edges of the paved area.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential driveway, walkway or patio: after the paver field is laid and compacted, the installer clears/cuts a shelf along the perimeter, mixes bagged or barrow-delivered concrete, places a haunch against the outer course, shapes it to a ~45° toe below finished grade, and backfills with soil/sod. Irregular curves, plantings, fences, slopes, weather-dependent cure.

Commercial/municipal hardscape (plaza, streetscape, sidewalk or crosswalk paver panel): long runs of cast-in-place concrete edge restraint or mortared soldier course against curbs, buildings and utility structures, using ready-mix or a site mixer, inside an active traffic-controlled work zone with pedestrians nearby.

Mortar-set perimeter units on a concrete base: buttering and setting a bond/soldier course, pool coping, step treads or clay-paver borders in a mortar bed, then pointing/striking the perimeter joints to a finished appearance.

Tight-radius and obstruction work: hand-working small pockets of concrete haunch around tree wells, catch basins, bollards, posts, stoops and curved bed lines, in confined kneeling space with a hand trowel and small batches.

Repair/retrofit of an existing paver area: chipping out failed or heaved edge concrete, cleaning the exposed paver faces and subbase, re-cementing the edge to match existing as-built grade and line, often with restricted access alongside an in-service surface.

sources.system: Unitechnik UniControl / UniCAM automated precast plant (shuttering robots, concrete spreaders)
sources.title: Software and automation for precast concrete plants — Unitechnik
sources.claim: Pallet-circulation precast concrete plants run concreting, compacting and smoothing work stations fully automatically, with concrete spreaders and shuttering robots placing formwork and distributing wet concrete according to CAD/CAM element data inside a purpose-built plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated placement, compaction and smoothing of wet concrete around fixtured moulds/units per digital contour. It carries over to cementing paver edges at E1 because the material (wet concrete), the tolerance (centimetre-level haunch profile) and the action (deposit a controlled volume along a defined perimeter contour and smooth it) are the same once the paved unit is fixtured and presented to the machine.

sources.system: FANUC dispensing and sealing robot cells (LR Mate 200iD, M-10iD)
sources.title: Dispensing and Sealing Robots and Cobots | FANUC America
sources.claim: Six-axis industrial robots and cobots autonomously dispense continuous beads of adhesive, urethane, epoxy and seam sealer along the contoured perimeters of fixtured parts in fenced production cells, with vision/laser checks for bead placement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic bead dispensing along a fixtured part's perimeter. Perimeter edge-bonding of pavers with polymeric adhesive/mortar is the same operation — a continuous viscous bead laid along a known contour at standoff — so performance transfers when the paved unit is presented fixtured in a cell.

sources.title: Retooled robotic mason brings added might to sites — BuiltWorlds
sources.claim: A track-mounted masonry robot autonomously applies mortar to each brick and places it in its specified location at about 150 bricks per hour on real building sites, working alongside a mason who strikes the joints and tends the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine application of mortar to masonry units and placement to line. It supports the mortar-set perimeter-course instance at E1 (units and mortar presented to a rig on a fixed track), but not at E2/E3 because SAM needs a purpose-built track, continuous human tending and a mason to strike the joints.

sources.system: Vertico 3D concrete printing facility (three ABB robot arms, one on a 7 m track)
sources.title: Dutch company Vertico opens its 3D concrete printing facility — 3D ADEPT MEDIA
sources.claim: Robotic arms deposit cementitious mortar along programmed 3D contours to build concrete elements inside a dedicated printing facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: programmed extrusion of stiff cementitious mortar along a defined path in a purpose-built facility. An extruded mortar haunch along a fixtured paver perimeter is the same deposition problem (same material class, same centimetre tolerances), supporting E1 only — the printers work in prepared, machine-built envelopes.

sources.system: Wirtgen SP-series slipform paver with AutoPilot 2.0
sources.title: Wirtgen AutoPilot 2.0 | PR | Wirtgen
sources.claim: On-site concrete edge/curb extrusion is machine-guided rather than autonomous: GNSS controls steering and cross-slope of the slipform paver automatically, but a trained operator must run the machine and crews feed it concrete.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: extruding a concrete curb/edge profile outdoors. It is cited only as a negative marker: the closest field system for on-site concrete edging still requires an on-board operator and a supporting crew, so it cannot support an E2/E3 positive judgment.

sources.system: Okibo EG7 / EG7+ autonomous plastering and finishing robot
sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market — The Robot Report
sources.claim: Fully autonomous mobile finishing robots that scan a space and apply plaster/drywall compound and paint are working at real construction sites, but the work is interior wall and ceiling surfaces, not at-grade concrete placement or trowelled edge haunching.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous application of a paste finishing material in an as-found construction setting. Cited to bound the field state of the art — these robots handle vertical interior surfaces with light paste, not barrowed concrete placed and shaped in an excavated perimeter trench, so they do not substantiate E3/E2 for this task.

roles.title: Construction and Related Workers, All Other
aliases: Pipe Cleaning and Priming Machine Operator
roles.description: All construction and related workers not listed separately.

roles.title: Weatherization Installers and Technicians
roles.description: Perform a variety of activities to weatherize homes and make them more energy efficient. Duties include repairing windows, insulating ducts, and performing heating, ventilating, and air-conditioning (HVAC) work. May perform energy audits and advise clients on energy conservation measures.

tasks.label: Test combustible appliances, such as gas appliances.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Combustion safety test of an atmospherically vented gas furnace in a single-family home basement or utility closet: set thermostat to fire the unit, establish worst-case depressurization (close interior doors, run dryer, bath and kitchen exhaust fans, air handler), check vent connector draft and spillage at the draft hood with mirror or smoke, insert the analyzer probe into the flue upstream of the diverter, record undiluted CO and ambient CO, and judge against BPI/WAP action levels.

Draft, spillage and CO test of an atmospheric gas storage water heater in a home basement, closet or garage: open a hot tap to fire the burner, cold-vent and warm-vent spillage checks at the draft hood, probe the flue for undiluted CO, verify vent connector rise/condition, often in a shared combustion appliance zone with the furnace.

CO test of a gas range/cooktop and oven in the home kitchen: light each surface burner and the oven, hold the analyzer probe in the burner plume or oven vent, watch ambient CO in the room, note flame quality and unvented operation, and advise on cleaning/adjustment or replacement.

Combustion appliance test in an occupied multifamily or public-housing apartment unit: closet-mounted furnace/water heater with limited clearance, tenant belongings blocking access, common venting shared with other units, testing done around residents during a scheduled unit visit.

Combustion appliance test in a manufactured/mobile home: sealed-combustion or vented furnace in a narrow interior closet, water heater in an exterior compartment, cramped access, non-standard vent terminations, sometimes crawling under or reaching into tight cavities to reach the vent connector.

Gas leak / gas-tightness check on the appliance connections and supply piping in the dwelling: walk the piping with a combustible gas detector, confirm suspect joints with bubble solution, sometimes perform a pressure-drop test at the meter or shutoff, then tag, repair or refer the leak.

sources.system: Spot with FLIR MUVE C360 gas detection payload and Enhanced Autonomy Payload
sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / MFE Inspection Solutions / Teledyne FLIR
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped, carrying a FLIR MUVE C360 gas sensor, autonomously detected a plume of combustible ... from a pinhole leak while walking scheduled inspection rounds at a 40-acre midstream gas plant; plant staff then located and mitigated the leak. This is ambient gas sensing on a taught route, not operation or flue-gas testing of an appliance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: combustible-gas leak surveillance in an industrial plant. It is the nearest robotic analogue to a technician's gas sniff check, but the robot only flags an ambient plume along a fixed route; humans identified the leaking fitting, and the robot never fires an appliance, samples flue gas, or evaluates draft/spillage, so it does not carry over to a combustion appliance safety test.

sources.title: Robotic inspection in Power & Utilities - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal performs scheduled autonomous inspection rounds in power and utility facilities, taking thermal readings, reading gauges and detecting gas presence without physical interaction with the equipment; it does not operate appliances or insert sampling probes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous sensor-based inspection of fired and gas-handling equipment in industrial plants. Shows the ceiling of deployed mobile-robot diagnostics — non-contact sensing on fixed routes — and confirms no deployed inspection robot manipulates appliance controls or flue probes.

sources.system: ATEQ differential pressure-decay / mass-flow leak testers on appliance production lines
sources.title: Appliance Leak Testing | Industrial Leak Detection | ATEQ
sources.claim: ATEQ supplies automated in-line leak testers that are integrated into appliance production lines and verify the gas-tightness of appliance gas lines and seals by differential pressure decay and mass-flow methods, producing logged pass/fail results at production cycle times.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production gas-tightness testing of appliance gas circuits. It substantiates only the leak-check portion of this task, and only when the gas circuit is sealed into a fixture and presented to the machine, i.e. an E1 presentation; it does not fire the appliance or evaluate combustion products.

tasks.label: Determine amount of air leakage in buildings, using a blower door machine.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied single-family detached home in a weatherization/energy-audit program: technician hauls the blower door kit in, walks the house to prepare it (close windows and exterior doors, open interior doors, shut down combustion appliances, cover ashes), fits the adjustable aluminum frame and nylon panel into a non-standard exterior doorway around a storm door, mounts the fan, runs tubing outside, takes a baseline and a single- or multi-point depressurization test, records CFM50/ACH50, then tears down.

Apartment or condo unit compartmentalization test in a multifamily building: gear carried up stairs or in an elevator, unit interior occupied with tenant belongings, blower door fitted in the unit entry door or a bedroom/patio door, sometimes a guarded test with a second fan in the corridor or neighboring unit, coordination with residents, leakage per unit recorded.

New-construction single-family home or townhome tested for energy-code/HERS compliance: house is unoccupied but a live jobsite (dust, materials, unfinished mechanicals, other trades present), rough or newly hung doors, technician seals intentional openings, verifies dampers, runs the test and issues the compliance report.

Small commercial or institutional building (school wing, office suite, church, clinic) tested by a whole-building airtightness crew: multiple fans set in one or more entry doors, extra pressure taps run through the building, HVAC shut down and lobbies/vestibules controlled by facility staff, multi-fan multi-point test and report.

Difficult-conditions residential test: heavily cluttered or hoarded older home, pets and occupants present, odd or undersized door openings, high wind or extreme temperature requiring repeated baseline readings and retests, sometimes a manufactured/mobile home with a small door and skirting issues.

sources.system: TEC Minneapolis Blower Door (Model 3 / DG-1000 gauge) with TECTITE Express 5.0
sources.date: 2026-02 (product page last modified); product line commercial for years
sources.title: TECTITE Express 5.0 - The Energy Conservatory
sources.claim: TECTITE Express 5.0, the commercial test-analysis program for The Energy Conservatory's Minneapolis Blower Door, runs fully automated blower door tests: computerized control of the fan through the required pressure stations, automated flow and pressure measurement, calculation of CFM50/ACH50/leakage area, and report generation. It automates the measurement once the fan is installed and sealed into an opening.

sources.system: Retrotec blower door fans + DM32 manometer + FanTestic Pro/Lite software
sources.title: FanTestic Pro & FanTestic Lite | Retrotec Blower Door Software
sources.claim: Retrotec's FanTestic software with DM32 digital manometers automatically controls up to 24 blower door fans, captures pressure and flow data in accordance with standard enclosure air-leakage testing procedures, and generates the standards-compliant report — i.e., the determination of building air leakage is machine-run once the fans are mounted.

sources.system: AeroBarrier (blower-door-based pressurization and real-time leakage measurement)
sources.developer: Aeroseal / AeroBarrier dealers (e.g., Green South Energy)
sources.title: Aerobarrier - Never Fail A Blower Door | Wilmington, NC
sources.claim: AeroBarrier is a commercially deployed system in which, after a crew installs a blower door and pressurizes the space, a computer controls pressure and conditions and software measures envelope leakage in real time during the process in actual houses — evidence that automated, machine-controlled blower-door leakage measurement performs to accepted standards in real buildings once the apparatus is in place.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (automated air sealing) shares the identical measurement step: computer-controlled blower door pressurization with continuous leakage quantification in the same buildings, so the measurement performance transfers directly.

sources.system: Generic blower door test procedure (adjustable enclosure and fan mount)
sources.title: Quantitative testing - airtight
sources.claim: Field practice requires a human to temporarily install the blower door: an adjustable enclosure and fan ... are fitted into a door or other opening, and only then is the fan run by a software-based control system. No robotic system performs this transport, fitting and sealing step.

sources.title: 1X's $20K Robot Targets US Homes in 2026, Aims to Reduce the 'Creepy' Factor
sources.claim: State-of-the-art home humanoid robots entering houses in 2026 are not autonomous for unfamiliar multi-step tasks; the first units rely on teleoperation and remote 'expert mode' piloting, so no cited mobile manipulator can autonomously carry in, assemble, fit and seal a blower door in an arbitrary dwelling.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only as negative context for whether any mobile manipulator could perform the field setup in homes; not used to support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Test and diagnose air flow systems, using furnace efficiency analysis equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-family home, gas furnace in basement/closet: tech drills or uses existing flue port, inserts combustion analyzer probe, fires the unit to steady state, records O2/CO/CO2, stack temperature, draft, and steady-state efficiency, compares to manufacturer spec, and reports whether combustion/venting is acceptable.

Occupied home combustion safety test under worst-case depressurization: set up house (close doors, run exhaust fans, dryer), measure CAZ depressurization with manometer, test furnace/water heater draft and spillage with analyzer and smoke, measure ambient CO, then diagnose whether the appliance/venting is safe with the weatherized envelope.

Installed duct/air distribution diagnostics in a home: drill test ports upstream/downstream of the air handler and coil, read total external static pressure with a digital manometer, measure temperature rise across the heat exchanger, and diagnose restricted returns, dirty coil/filter, or wrong blower speed in an attic, crawlspace, or basement.

Room-by-room airflow and duct leakage testing in a home: balometer/flow hood readings at supply registers, pressure-pan readings at each register with the blower door running, duct blaster setup (seal registers, attach fan to return), CFM25 leakage measurement and interpretation.

Multifamily building or small commercial mechanical room owned by a housing authority/property manager: combustion analysis and airflow/draft check on a common-area boiler or rooftop unit in a fixed-layout, institution-controlled mechanical room, with documentation for the weatherization file.

sources.system: ECR International automated end-of-line boiler test stand (Viewpoint Systems / NI LabVIEW test executive)
sources.date: 2022-02 (case study page last modified; system in production use)
sources.title: Automated End-Of-Line Tester Upgrade - Boiler - Viewpoint Systems
sources.claim: ECR International, a heating equipment manufacturer, uses an automated end-of-line test stand (software by Viewpoint Systems) on which each boiler is fixtured and test fired, combustion optimized, and results automatically recorded against the serial number, with automated temperature-based test parameter control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory functional/combustion test of a fired heating appliance. It transfers to the appliance-level part of this task because the same object (a gas-fired heating unit) is fired and its combustion evaluated against limits by machine-controlled instrumentation, with the unit presented fixtured as an E1 setting would present it; it does not transfer to in-situ house-coupled duct or depressurization diagnostics.

sources.system: HORIBA ADS-7000 automated driving system with MEXA-7000 emissions bench / VETS test cell
sources.date: product line in commercial use; page retrieved 2026-07
sources.title: ADS-7000 - HORIBA
sources.claim: HORIBA's ADS-7000 automated driving system, integrated with dynamometer and emissions bench, allows unmanned operation of a purpose-built test cell in which a fixtured combustion machine is run and its exhaust gases measured automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated exhaust-gas analysis of a fixtured combustion machine in a purpose-built cell. Measurement class (O2/CO/CO2 sampling, flow and temperature) and machine-controlled test sequencing match furnace combustion-efficiency testing when the appliance is brought to the machine; it says nothing about diagnosing an installed building duct system.

sources.system: Fluiomet AMCA 210 automated airflow & pressure test rig
sources.title: AMCA 210 Wind Tunnel | Custom Fluid Dynamics Test Bench
sources.claim: Commercial automated airflow/pressure test rigs built to AMCA 210 measure fan and blower airflow versus static pressure automatically once the unit is mounted in the chamber.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated airflow/static-pressure characterization of a blower or air handler on a fixtured test chamber. It covers the measurement quantities of this task (CFM, static pressure) for a fixtured appliance, but cannot substitute for diagnosing a specific house's installed duct system, which cannot be brought to a chamber.

sources.system: HVAC robotics research corpus (review of 101 studies, 2005-2025)
sources.developer: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory et al.
sources.title: Robotics for HVAC applications: A critical review and future perspectives
sources.claim: A 2025 LBNL-led review of 101 studies of robotics in HVAC finds robot use concentrated in inspection, maintenance and indoor monitoring, with real-world performance limited and many systems still at prototype stage; no field system performing combustion-analyzer diagnostics on installed residential heating systems is reported.

sources.system: Telerobotic air-conditioning duct inspection and cleaning robot (AcTEA-bot related work)
sources.title: Air Conditioning Ducts Inspection and Cleaning Using Telerobotics - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: In-duct HVAC robots that exist for inspection and cleaning are telerobotic prototypes, not autonomous diagnostic systems, and they perform cleaning/inspection rather than combustion or airflow performance diagnosis.

tasks.label: Install and seal air ducts, combustion air openings, or ventilation openings to improve heating and cooling efficiency.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied single-family home: technician crawls the attic over joists in heat and blown insulation, pulls back duct wrap, brushes mastic and applies mesh/foil tape to leaking joints, boots, and plenum seams, then restores insulation; verified by blower-door/duct-blaster test.

Existing home crawlspace or basement: sealing and re-supporting leaking flex and metal ducts in 24-36 in. clearance, damp soil, spider webs, obstructions; strap repairs, mastic on collars and boots, tape on flex inner liner.

Installing or replacing duct sections in an existing home: cutting in a takeoff/boot at the plenum, fitting and joining rigid or flex duct, screwing and strapping, insulating and sealing the new run to code.

Installing combustion air openings/ducts for a furnace or water-heater closet: cutting through rim joist or closet wall, installing a sleeve/louver or high-low combustion air ducts, air-sealing around the penetration.
Installing ventilation openings/terminations: bath fan or dryer duct run to a wall cap or roof jack, cutting the exterior penetration, flashing, mounting the cap, sealing and insulating the duct.
Manufactured-home belly duct repair and crossover sealing, or multifamily unit duct sealing: patching belly board, sealing floor register boots and crossover connections in tight, dirty spaces.

sources.system: FANUC dispensing/sealing robots and cobots (seam sealer dispensing)
sources.title: Dispensing and Sealing Robots and Cobots | FANUC America
sources.claim: Commercially deployed industrial robots apply beads of sealant/adhesive along seams of fixtured sheet-metal parts autonomously inside dispensing cells, the factory analogue of brushing mastic on a duct seam.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive seam-sealer dispensing. It applies high-viscosity sealant along sheet-metal joints held in a fixture at bead-level precision — the same material class, substrate and geometry as mastic-sealing a duct joint — so performance carries over when the duct is brought to the cell.

sources.system: Automated sealant application system for assembled HVAC duct components (robot applicator + fixture)
sources.title: Automated sealant application to assembled HVAC duct components and blanks for forming assembled HVAC duct components
sources.claim: A patented production system holds an assembled HVAC metal duct component in a fixture and has a robot applicator lay sealant along the seam to a specified coverage and thickness, i.e. robotic duct-seam sealing in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Automated coil line / auto duct line
sources.developer: Sheet-metal fabrication equipment makers (industry guide, ACHR News)
sources.title: Bringing Duct Fabrication In-House: A 2026 Equipment Guide for Sheet Metal Shops | ACHR News
sources.claim: Automated duct coil lines in sheet-metal shops fabricate rectangular duct — cutting, notching, forming the seam and flanging — under machine control with only one or two operators tending the line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: duct fabrication. Making up and closing seams on duct sections in a purpose-built line is the E1 form of joining duct; the same machine-controlled forming and seaming produces the joints a weatherization tech would otherwise assemble by hand.

sources.claim: In the most automated US modular-housing plant, robots cut ventilation, window and door openings in fixtured wall panels and pick, place and fasten panel components; MEP work at the next station is still installed manually by people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting openings and fastening components into fixtured wall panels. Creating a ventilation/combustion-air opening in a wall and mounting hardware in it uses comparable objects and millimetre-level precision, in a purpose-built line.
