tasks.label: Inspect buildings to identify required weatherization measures, including repair work, modification, or replacement.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-work walk-through of an occupied older single-family home: technician moves through cluttered living areas, checks windows, doors, weatherstripping, caulking, plumbing/electrical penetrations, wall outlets, appliances and visible moisture/health-and-safety hazards, and records which items need repair, modification or replacement on the work order.

Attic assessment: set/climb a ladder, open a hatch or scuttle, crawl over joists in a hot, low-clearance attic with loose fill, measure existing insulation depth and type, look for bypasses, ductwork, knob-and-tube wiring, roof leaks, bath-fan terminations and venting, and specify air sealing/insulation measures.

Crawlspace or basement/foundation assessment: enter a dirt or low-clearance crawlspace (or unfinished basement), inspect floor insulation, vapor barrier, band joist, ducts, water heater and pipe insulation, moisture and pest damage, and specify duct sealing, insulation and repair items.

Diagnostic testing during the inspection: set up and run a blower door (frame, fabric panel, fan, manometer), duct blaster or pressure pan readings, combustion-safety/CO and draft testing on the furnace and water heater, and IR camera scan of walls and ceilings, then interpret the numbers to determine required measures.

Inspection of a multifamily apartment unit or a manufactured/mobile home: tight rooms with tenant belongings, belly/skirting and duct access under a mobile home, older windows and doors, mechanical closet and shared systems; identify unit-specific weatherization repairs and replacements.

sources.title: Actively-exploring thermography-enabled autonomous robotic system for detecting and registering HVAC thermal leaks - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: AcTEA-bot is an autonomous ground robot that self-navigates and detects/localizes HVAC thermal leaks in ceilings; it was evaluated only in a purpose-built, true-to-scale ceiling mockup with five known leaks, i.e. a narrow sub-step of a building inspection in a lab setting.
sources.transferJustification: Thermal-anomaly detection is one sensing sub-step of a weatherization inspection; it transfers only partially because the demonstration covers a single defect class on a built mockup and produces no list of required repairs, modifications or replacements.

sources.title: TEA-bot: a thermography enabled autonomous robot for detecting thermal leaks of HVAC systems in ceilings
sources.claim: TEA-bot, the predecessor system, is an autonomous thermography robot aimed at replacing manual inspection of HVAC thermal leaks in ceilings; it remains a low-cost research prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Same partial transfer as AcTEA-bot: autonomous thermal leak sensing in ceilings, not an end-to-end assessment of a building's weatherization needs.

sources.title: Using Robots for Home Inspections | AHIT
sources.claim: Commercially available crawlspace/attic inspection crawlers used in residential inspection are remote-controlled by the human inspector, who drives them and interprets the video; the robot supplies imagery, not a diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same setting (residential crawlspaces and attics), but continuous teleoperation and human interpretation mean it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Thermal Sensing & Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot with a thermal payload performs autonomous inspection rounds inside industrial plants, capturing thermal data on fixed routes and flagging equipment anomalies for maintenance work orders.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile thermal inspection inside a structured facility (E2). It shows walking a taught route and flagging hot spots on equipment, but not ladder/hatch access to attics, crawlspace entry, diagnostic test setup, or specification of envelope repair/replacement measures.

sources.system: PARIS (Precise Air-sealing Robot for Inaccessible Spaces)
sources.title: Robotics for HVAC applications: A critical review and future perspectives - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A 2025 review of robotics for HVAC applications reports that the PARIS attic air-sealing robot is only semi-autonomous and still requires a human operator to navigate it to the work area in attic spaces.
sources.transferJustification: Attic-traversing retrofit robot in the same physical setting as the attic inspection instance; the review documents that autonomous navigation of real attics is not yet achieved.

sources.title: DOE Announces its E-ROBOT Prize Phase 1 Winners | Department of Energy
sources.claim: DOE's E-ROBOT prize concepts include wall-EIFS, described as an autonomous robot that scans ... before applying sprayable insulation; these are prize-stage prototypes rather than deployed inspection services.
sources.transferJustification: Envelope scanning/analysis is the closest analogue to identifying weatherization measures, but the source describes a prize entry with no demonstrated autonomous end-to-end assessment, so it is treated as non-supporting.

sources.system: Building energy audit robotics (research roadmap survey)
sources.title: A Roadmap for Climate-Relevant Robotics Research
sources.claim: A 2025 climate-robotics research roadmap identifies robotic assessment of existing buildings' performance and retrofit needs as an unsolved bottleneck, because existing buildings are all different.
sources.transferJustification: Survey-level statement on the state of the art for exactly this task (building energy/retrofit assessment); it corroborates the absence of a system that completes the inspection autonomously.

tasks.label: Apply insulation materials, such as loose, blanket, board, and foam insulation to attics, crawl spaces, basements, or walls.

instances.label: Blowing loose-fill cellulose or fiberglass over ceiling joists in the attic of an existing single-family home: hose run from a truck-mounted blower through a scuttle hatch, installer crawls on joists in 3-4 ft headroom, installs baffles and dams around recessed cans, flues and the hatch, blows to uniform marked depth.

Installing fiberglass or mineral-wool batts/blankets in an occupied existing home: knee walls, floors over vented crawl spaces, basement band joists and open stud bays, cutting and split-fitting each batt around wiring, plumbing, ducts and irregular framing, then friction-fitting or wire-supporting it.

Spray polyurethane foam applied in a crawl space or unfinished basement of an existing house: rim/band joists, foundation walls, or underside of a suspended floor, in an 18-36 in. dirt-floor void with debris, moisture and obstructions, with masking, ventilation and PPE.

Dense-packing cellulose into closed exterior sidewall cavities of an older home: locating studs and fire blocking, drilling holes through siding or interior plaster, feeding the fill tube down each cavity to refusal density, then plugging and patching the holes.

Cutting and fastening rigid foam board to basement/foundation walls, to a mobile-home belly or skirting, or to attic hatches and knee-wall backs in an existing dwelling, then taping/foaming the seams and edges.

tasks.label: Make minor repairs using basic hand or power tools and materials, such as glass, lumber, and drywall.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-situ wood repair in an occupied single-family home or mobile home: measure, cut and fit lumber to replace a rotted door jamb, threshold, window trim, sill or floor board, or add blocking/framing so insulation and weatherstripping can be installed. Cluttered, furnished rooms, attics and crawlspaces; cordless drill, circular saw, pry bar, hand tools.

Drywall or plaster patching in an occupied dwelling after air-sealing or dense-pack insulation access holes, or where board was damaged: cut out damage, add backing, cut and fit a patch, screw it off, tape, apply and feather compound coats, sand flush and blend to the existing painted surface, with dust control around the occupant's furnishings.

Exterior minor repair on the dwelling: patch or replace a section of siding, soffit, fascia or mobile-home skirting/belly board, re-flash and seal a vent or duct penetration, or screw plywood over a broken opening. Ladder work, varied cladding types, weather and uneven ground.

Window repair in the home: replace a broken pane or reglaze a wood sash (chip out old putty and glazing points, clean the rabbet, bed and secure new glass), replace a sash cord, parting bead or hardware, and refit the sash so it operates and seals.

Minor repair in an institution-controlled multifamily building's common or service space (housing-authority basement, corridor, mechanical room): patch drywall around a new duct or pipe penetration, build and fit a plywood cover over an opening, or repair a door frame. Fixed layout, cleared space, building staff control access.

Shop/van prefabrication of a simple wooden component delivered ready to install: measure from field notes, cut lumber and plywood to size and fasten them into an attic access hatch cover, insulation dam box, storm-window frame or cover panel, at the contractor's shop bench.

sources.title: How a Drywall Robot Is Reshaping Interior Construction | Bluebeam Blog
sources.claim: Canvas's drywall finishing robot is commercially deployed on US commercial construction interiors; a worker positions it and enters dimensions, then it maps the wall, finds seams and applies and sands compound on its own, but it only finishes already-hung board — it does not cut, fit or fasten drywall patches.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drywall finishing. Cited to bound capability — it covers only the mudding/sanding step of a drywall repair on open new-construction walls, not the cut-out, patch-fitting and fastening a weatherization patch requires.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7 is a fully autonomous plastering/painting and drywall finishing robot working on construction sites in Europe and the US with no site preparation; it coats and finishes wall surfaces but performs no carpentry, glazing or patch fabrication.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous wall plastering/finishing on jobsites. Shows surface coating is automated even in unstructured sites, but not the cut-fit-fasten steps of a minor repair with lumber, glass or board.

sources.title: Development of a humanoid robot prototype, HRP-5P, capable of heavy labor
sources.claim: AIST's HRP-5P humanoid autonomously handled and screwed a gypsum board to a wall in a simulated residential construction mock-up — a research demonstration of one fastening step, not a full repair, and never deployed commercially.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: board handling and screwing in a purpose-built mock-up. Bounds capability: a single fastening step at demo reliability, with no cutting-to-fit, taping, finishing or damage assessment.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cutting and fastening of dimensional lumber and sheet goods into small assemblies. Same materials, tolerances and operations as bench-prefabricating a hatch cover or dam box when stock is presented fixtured to the machine.

tasks.label: Wrap air ducts and water lines with insulating materials, such as duct wrap and pipe insulation.

instances.label: Single-family home attic: wrap existing sheet-metal supply/return trunks and branch ducts (plus a few boots, elbows and takeoffs) with R-6/R-8 foil-faced duct wrap, stapling and mastic-taping seams, while kneeling on joists in loose-fill insulation, 100-130 F, low clearance, poor light.

Crawlspace or unconditioned basement of an occupied home: sleeve or wrap hot- and cold-water supply lines (copper/PEX) with foam sleeves or fiberglass pipe wrap, including elbows, tees, valves and hanger points; damp, dirty, 24-36 inch clearance, obstructions and spiders/debris as found.

Home utility room, garage or basement mechanical area: insulate the accessible duct trunk and plenum near the furnace/air handler and the first several feet of water-heater supply lines; standing or crouching headroom, moderate clutter, homeowner's stored items around the equipment.

Multifamily building common basement or mechanical room controlled by a housing authority or property manager: insulate exposed heating/domestic-hot-water distribution piping and duct risers with pipe insulation, fitting covers and PVC/canvas jacketing to program specification.

Open, accessible straight runs during a gut-rehab, new-construction or open garage-ceiling/crawl job: apply continuous duct wrap to long straight round or rectangular duct runs and slide sleeve insulation onto straight pipe mains before other trades close the space up.

tasks.label: Prepare and apply weather-stripping, glazing, caulking, or door sweeps to reduce energy losses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Exterior caulking on an occupied single-family house: scraping/removing failed sealant, then gunning and tooling continuous beads around window and door perimeters, siding penetrations, sill plates and trim joints, often from a ladder, in variable weather and on irregular, weathered substrates.

Replacing or installing weatherstripping on exterior door jambs and window sashes in an occupied home: pulling out old kerf bulb seal or foam tape, cleaning the surface, measuring and cutting new stripping to length, and fitting/fastening it to an out-of-square existing jamb so the door closes and seals.

Installing a door sweep or threshold on an entry door in a home: measuring the door bottom, cutting the sweep to length with a hacksaw, drilling pilot holes, screwing it on and adjusting height for an uneven floor or worn threshold so it seals without binding.

Window glazing repair on older wood-sash windows in a home: removing loose or cracked glazing putty, re-setting the pane with glazing points, applying and tooling new glazing compound, and sealing sash-to-frame joints.

Interior/attic air sealing under a weatherization program: caulking and foaming bypasses and penetrations at top plates, chimney chases, plumbing and wiring holes, rim joists and duct boots, working in a cramped attic or crawlspace over insulation with a headlamp.

Multifamily weatherization: repetitive weatherstripping of unit entry doors and caulking of window perimeters across many apartment units in one program-managed building, each unit occupied and furnished with slightly different door/window conditions.

tasks.label: Clean and maintain tools and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-day cleanup of the crew kit at the customer's house/driveway or in the work van: knock and blow cellulose/fiberglass dust off cordless drills, saws, staplers and tool bags, wipe them down, coil extension cords and vacuum hoses, check for damaged cords/bits, and stow everything in cases and truck bins. Mixed, non-standard items; cramped, uncontrolled surroundings; dust and weather.

Shop or truck-bay servicing of the insulation blowing machine and its hose train after a job: dump leftover material, brush/vacuum out the hopper and rotary airlock, clear packed cellulose from clogged hose sections, check hoses, gaskets and belts for wear, grease bearings, blow dust off the motor and controls.

Cleaning applicator tools at the shop bench or tailgate: purge and flush the two-part spray-foam gun with solvent and swap its mixing tip/nozzle, scrape cured caulk and mastic off caulk-gun barrels and plungers, clean mastic brushes and pump, wipe sealant off gun bodies so they are ready for the next job.

Care of diagnostic and test equipment: wipe insulation dust off the blower-door fan, frame and shroud, clear and check the manometer tubing and filters, clean the combustion-analyzer probe and water trap, replace batteries and desiccant, wipe the IR camera lens, verify readings against a reference and repack the instruments in their cases.

Keeping cutting consumables in service: resharpen or replace dulled drill bits, hole saws, auger bits and utility/insulation knife blades, and change worn saw blades so the crew's tools keep cutting cleanly. Done in batches at the shop bench.

Servicing powered and safety equipment in the shop: oil and air-filter change and tank drain on the generator/compressor, HEPA vacuum bag and filter change, cleaning and disinfecting respirators and replacing cartridges, inspecting ladders, harnesses and cords and tagging out damaged gear.

tasks.label: Apply spackling, compounding, or other materials to repair holes in walls.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Occupied single-family home: after dense-pack wall insulation, patch the dozen-plus 2" to 2.5" holes drilled through interior drywall — set a foam/drywall plug or backer in each hole, apply setting-type compound in two or three coats, sand flush and feather into the existing painted wall; furniture moved and covered, ladders, dust control in a lived-in room.

Occupied home, flat painted drywall: fill small holes, dings, hairline cracks and gaps left by weatherization work — old thermostat/fixture screw holes, nail holes, gaps around new wiring, pipe or bath-fan penetrations — with spackling compound applied by knife, smoothed, lightly sanded, sometimes touched up with paint.

Older home with plaster-and-lath, textured (knockdown/orange-peel) or paneled walls: holes from drilling or removed fixtures patched with patching plaster or compound, bonded over lath or a backer, then the surrounding texture matched by hand so the repair disappears.

Larger access openings cut into a wall or ceiling to reach a blocked cavity, chase, old duct or exhaust fan: cut and fit a drywall patch, install backing strips, tape the joints, apply multiple coats of compound over several visits, sand and feather.

Unfinished or utility areas — basement rim/kneewall, attic, crawlspace, mechanical closet, garage, and exterior siding/stucco: fill holes around ducts, pipes and wire penetrations, or plug and patch drilled exterior holes, using patching compound, mortar-type patch or filler; cramped, poorly lit, uneven masonry or board surfaces.

Vacant multifamily unit or manufactured home during a retrofit: plain flat painted gypsum walls in empty rooms; small drilled holes, dings and screw holes are filled and the surface skim-finished and sanded before the unit is repainted, so a whole-wall finish is acceptable.

instances.label: Exterior triple-track aluminum storm windows on an older occupied single-family home: measure each opening, size/trim the unit, hold it against out-of-square wood casing or blind stop, drill pilot holes, drive screws, caulk head and sides leaving weep holes open, then check that sashes and screens slide, seat and lock. Upper-story units done from a ladder.

Storm/screen door on a home entry: measure the opening, cut hinge and latch rails to height, fasten the hinge rail to jamb/brickmold, hang the door, fit latch hardware, closer(s), sweep and bottom expander, then adjust until the door closes square, latches and seals against a frequently out-of-plumb frame.

Interior storm window inserts or low-e interior panels in a home or apartment unit: measure irregular, out-of-square existing openings, install compression-fit, magnetic or track-mounted panels inside the stops, and verify the panel seals all around, sits flush and can be removed.

Bulk installs across a housing-authority apartment building or mobile-home park: many identical-size storm windows/doors, materials staged on site, access and schedule controlled by the property manager; repetitive fastening, caulking and fit checks unit after unit.

Re-fitting or repairing existing storms: re-hang a sagging storm door and adjust its closer and strike, replace a broken glass/screen panel, adjust expanders and shims to stop drafts on a poorly fitting storm window, then verify fit and operation on weathered, painted-over, damaged woodwork.

tasks.label: Wrap water heaters with water heater blankets.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-family home, unfinished basement: gas storage water heater standing free with 2-3 ft of working room. Tech measures tank height/circumference, cuts a vinyl-faced R-8/R-10 fiberglass blanket to length with a utility knife, wraps it, cuts openings for the thermostat/gas control, burner access panel, T&P valve and pipes, tapes the vertical seam and around the cutouts, and keeps the top, draft hood and combustion air intake clear.

Apartment, condo or manufactured home: electric water heater jammed in a hall/utility closet or alcove with only a few inches of clearance on two or three sides. Tech works kneeling and overhead, feeds the blanket behind the tank by feel, trims around the element/thermostat access covers and the T&P discharge pipe, tapes seams in a confined, poorly lit space.

Attached garage, crawlspace or unconditioned utility area of a house: tank surrounded by stored clutter, dusty or damp, uneven footing or low headroom, sometimes on a stand or in a drain pan and secured by seismic straps. Tech clears access, wraps and tapes the blanket around straps/piping without covering controls.

Multifamily or small commercial mechanical/boiler room controlled by a property manager: one or more standard 50-100 gallon tanks on open floor with good clearance and lighting. Tech wraps each tank with a sized blanket, tapes or straps seams, labels, and leaves controls and relief valves accessible.

Non-standard job: an old sagging or torn blanket must be cut off, removed and disposed of before a new one is fitted, or the tank is a lowboy/short model, tucked under stairs or against ductwork, requiring the blanket to be cut into pieces and pieced around obstructions; may also require deciding the tank is factory-insulated R-16+ or blanket-prohibited and abandoning the wrap.

It is the same operation class as applying a water heater blanket — enclose a cylinder with a flexible sheet under tension and secure the seam with adhesive tape — with perception-driven, autonomous execution, though at much smaller scale (a 9 cm-radius container versus a ~45 cm-diameter tank) and with paper rather than vinyl-faced fiberglass.

roles.description: Rig derrick equipment and operate pumps to circulate mud or fluid through drill hole.

tasks.label: Start pumps that circulate mud through drill pipes and boreholes to cool drill bits and flush out drill cuttings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Modern land drilling rig (AC/VFD triplex mud pumps, PLC rig control, driller's cabin): derrickhand/driller starts a mud pump from the console, brings it up to the planned stroke rate/flow, watches standpipe pressure build, and holds circulation while drilling ahead. Suction already lined up from the active pit.

Conventional/older land rig: derrickhand walks to the pump house and mud pits, lines up the suction valve from the correct pit, primes/starts the centrifugal charge pump, opens the discharge valve to the standpipe manifold, engages the mud pump and brings up strokes, then checks the pump, relief valve and lines for leaks or knocking.

Offshore or high-spec rig with an automated drilling control system: pumps are started and ramped as part of a programmed circulating/connection sequence (come off bottom, stop flow, connection, ramp flow back up, tag bottom) at set ramp rates coordinated with top drive and hoisting.

Breaking circulation after a trip in, at kick-off, or before a cement/casing job: start the pump slowly against a full string, watch standpipe pressure and pit/trip-tank levels for losses or gains, ramp in stages to full circulating rate for hole cleaning, and back off if the hole takes or gives fluid.

Abnormal start-up: pump will not take suction or loses prime, washed valve/liner or leaking packing, screen or bit nozzle plugged causing a pressure spike, pop-off valve lifts. Derrickhand must diagnose on the spot, physically bleed/vent, clear or change out the failed part, and restart.

tasks.label: Control the viscosity and weight of the drilling fluid.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine mud property surveillance on a working rig: the derrickhand pulls samples from the suction pit/flowline each tour, runs a mud balance for weight and a Marsh funnel/viscometer for viscosity, watches pit levels and density gauges, logs values and reports deviations to the driller and mud engineer. Rig mud shack / mud pit area, 24-hour operation.

Routine sacked-additive treatment on a land rig: per the mud program, the derrickhand carries, cuts and dumps 50-100 lb sacks of bentonite, polymer, lime or soda ash into the mud hopper at the mixing pit, lines up the mixing pump and agitators, and checks the result. Pallets of sacks stored on location, outdoors, weather, muddy walkways, dust.

Weighting up with bulk barite: transferring barite from bulk silos/surge tanks through the hopper into the active system at a controlled rate, operating valves, mixing pump and agitators from the mixing panel, repeatedly checking mud weight until the target ppg is reached. Offshore rig mud module or modern land rig with bulk system.

Thinning and solids control: adding water or base oil to the active system to cut weight/viscosity, running and adjusting centrifuges, desilters and shakers, transferring and dumping mud between pits to hold solids, weight and rheology inside the program window.

Upset and special mixing: building an LCM pill, a kill-weight slug or a contamination treatment fast during losses, gas-cut mud or cement/salt contamination - coarse fibrous or nut-plug material out of sacks/big bags into a pill tank, hoppers prone to plugging, time pressure, coordination with the driller.

tasks.label: Listen to mud pumps and check regularly for vibration and other problems to ensure that rig pumps and drilling mud systems are working properly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Land drilling rig, routine round of the mud pump area during a tour: derrickhand walks the pump skid while the triplex pumps run, listens to each pump for knocking or off-note valves, looks and feels for abnormal vibration in pump and discharge lines, checks for mud/oil leaks and washouts, reads discharge-pressure and lube-oil gauges, verifies pop-off valve and pulsation dampener condition, and reports anything abnormal to the driller. Daylight, ordinary weather, maintained walkways.

Land rig, drilling ahead: the derrickhand works around the mud pits and mixing hopper while both pumps run, and must notice within moments a change in pump note or beat - a knocking valve, a washed liner or piston, a lost prime, a change in pulsation - and immediately alert the driller or shut a pump down. Detection latency of seconds to a minute matters; monitoring is continuous and concurrent with other duties.

Round of the wider drilling-fluid system on a land rig: mud tanks and pits, agitators, centrifugal charging/mixing/supercharger pumps, shale shakers and desanders. Listen for cavitation, squealing bearings or plugged suction, check pit levels and returns, look for leaks and packing failures on the small pumps, confirm valve line-ups. Mud-splattered walkways, hoses and lines underfoot.

Same mud-pump checks under adverse conditions: night tour or bad weather (rain, snow, ice, wind, extreme heat), drilling mud coating the pump skid and stairs, very high ambient noise from engines and drawworks masking the pumps, and cramped access around the fluid end and crossheads.

Offshore rig or platform mud pump room: enclosed, hazardous-area-classified pump room on a mechanized rig with steel gratings and stairs; scheduled operator/derrickman round listening to the mud pumps and charging pumps, checking vibration, leaks, lube systems and local instrumentation, logging readings for the control room.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine operator rounds at an oil-and-gas processing facility. It transfers because the objects (pumps, compressors, pressure gauges, piping), the judgment (is this asset running normally, is anything leaking or overheating) and the terrain (outdoor industrial steel walkways at a hydrocarbon facility) match a rig mud-pump round.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated acoustic/vibration condition monitoring of plant pumps. It is the same sensing act the derrickhand performs by ear and hand on a mud pump, on comparable machinery (large rotating/reciprocating pumps), and the output (flagging an abnormal sound/vibration signature) is the same.

tasks.label: Inspect derricks, or order their inspection, prior to being raised or lowered.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Land drilling rig, rigging up on a new well pad: before the mast is raised, the derrickhand walks the lowered mast end to end checking for loose bolts, tools, bars or drift pins without safety bolts, gravel/rocks on cross beams, verifies the monkeyboard/derrick board is pinned and clear, the derrick escape device is rigged, sheaves are greased and free, tong counterbalances tied down, winch and tong hanger lines secured, deadline clamped, and then signals the mast is safe to raise. Outdoor caliche/mud pad, wind, dust, night work, layout differs pad to pad.

Well servicing / workover rig at a lease location (several locations per week): pre-raise walkaround of the telescoping mast before it is raised and telescoped over the wellhead - hydraulic raising cylinders and hoses for leaks, pins and keepers, guy-line wires and anchors, crown and sheaves, wire rope condition, blocks and lines free of tangles, loose items removed - then giving the go-ahead to the operator at the controls.

Rig-down / pre-lowering inspection: before telescoping down and laying the mast over, verifying the derrick is clear of tools and loose equipment, that lines, hoses and cables in the mast are secured or disconnected, pins pulled or installed as required, raising line and cylinder condition checked, and that no personnel or obstruction is in the fall path. Often at the end of a job, under time and weather pressure.

Platform, jackup or inland-barge rig where the mast/derrick section is raised, skidded or lowered inside a controlled facility: the inspection is done on steel decks with a fixed layout, permit-to-work system, controlled access and standard equipment, checking structural members, pins, wire rope and clearance before the raise or lower.

Ordering an inspection: after a hard set-down, a wind or overload event, visible damage (bent members, cracked welds, damaged wire rope) or a due API 4G interval, the derrick operator makes an initial hands-on look, documents the condition, stops the raise, and arranges/escorts a qualified third-party or in-house structural inspector before the derrick may be raised or lowered again.

sources.title: ANYbotics Partners With SLB to Advance Autonomous Robotics Operations in Oil & Gas
sources.claim: Autonomous legged robot ANYmal is commercially deployed for routine inspection rounds at oil & gas facilities including offshore platforms, reading gauges and detecting corrosion/gas leaks, but the work is routine asset inspection on fixed process equipment, not a pre-raise structural/configuration safety verification of a mast.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous routine inspection rounds in an oil & gas facility. It shows mobility and sensing in an E2 industrial setting, but the objects (gauges, pumps, flanges) and the judgment required (reading instruments, detecting leaks) differ from verifying pins, keepers, secured lines and absence of loose objects on a lattice mast before it is raised.

sources.claim: An autonomous-navigation drone system has been permanently installed on an offshore platform for remote inspection rounds flown from an onshore control center; the flight is still piloted/supervised remotely and the mission is general asset imagery, not a derrick pre-raise safety determination.

Closest available analogue to flying a derrick, but the reported flights are BVLOS operations piloted from shore collecting imagery, so they cannot substantiate an autonomous go/no-go structural check.

sources.title: Drones and drone technology: Rethinking inspections
sources.claim: Fully automated (pilotless) drone inspection of a large structure with AI defect detection is commercially deployed for aircraft exteriors inside maintenance hangars, showing autonomous visual survey of a big asset in a structured facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous visual inspection of a large structure. Transfer to derrick pre-raise inspection is limited: Donecle scans a smooth fuselage in a clean hangar for surface defects, whereas the derrick check requires detecting small loose items and missing safety pins on an open steel lattice outdoors and verifying that lines, clamps, escape device and counterbalances are physically secured.

sources.title: World's First Inside-the-Derrick Inspection With a Drone
sources.claim: Inside-the-derrick drone inspection of an offshore drilling ... has been performed with an unmanned aircraft system, but as a piloted service inspection of derrick structure/piping, not an autonomous pre-raise check.
sources.transferJustification: Same asset (a drilling derrick) but a piloted survey flight producing imagery for human inspectors; autonomy is not established, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.claim: Autonomous drone scanning of tall lattice/mast structures such as crane masts is available as a software capability, but flights are conducted with a pilot on site and the output is imagery/3D models for human inspectors.

tasks.label: Position and align derrick elements, using harnesses and platform climbing devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rig-up/rig-down of a land drilling rig: derrickhand in fall-arrest harness climbs the mast and works from ladders/platforms to guide crane- or winch-lifted mast sections, racking board (monkeyboard) assembly, girts and braces into position, align pin/bolt holes, drive pins and torque bolts, and set safety-line anchors before the mast is raised or after it is telescoped. Outdoors on a lease pad, in wind, mud, cold or heat; pad and rig layout differ site to site.

Operating land drilling rig, tripping and stand-building: derrickhand at the monkeyboard sets and aligns the racking-board elements for the tubular program in use — finger spacing, latches/gates and guides — and works them open and closed at height as stands are racked and pulled, keeping stands aligned in the fingers. Contractor-controlled rig site, standard rig equipment, fixed layout for the well.

Operating rig, ancillary derrick elements: climbing in harness to hang and align tugger lines and sheaves, install and align the casing stabbing board, position/secure the standpipe and rotary hose clamps, align top-drive guide rails/dolly and bracketry in the derrick before a casing or BOP job. Work at height on a live, contractor-controlled site.

Offshore rig (jackup, semisub or drillship) derrick: derrickhand or roustabout positions and aligns the vertical racking system's derrick elements — fingerboard sections, latches, guide rails and setback guides — for the tubular program, working at height in harness inside a permanently installed, access-controlled derrick.

Well-servicing/workover rig at a producing wellsite: derrick hand climbs the telescoping mast in a harness to position and align the tubing board fingers and rod hangers, align mast guy-line anchors and centre the mast elements over the wellhead after the mast is raised. Site taken as found, varied terrain and surface equipment.

Corrective work found on inspection: a derrick element is bent, loose or out of alignment (sprung fingerboard finger, seized or damaged latch cylinder, misaligned guide rail); derrickhand climbs in harness to diagnose, free/replace and realign the element in place at height.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: positioning and aligning heavy structural steel elements onto a mating member and fixing them. Derrick legs, girts, racking-board and bracket elements are the same class of steel members at comparable fit-up tolerances; in a purpose-built cell the workpiece is fixtured and presented exactly as this machine requires.

tasks.label: Inspect derricks for flaws, and clean and oil derricks to maintain proper working conditions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Land drilling rig, active operations: tour/daily visual inspection of the derrick or mast for flaws - cracked or corroded welds and members, bent or missing girts, loose or missing bolts, damaged ladder/safety climb, worn crown sheaves and frayed drilling line - observed from ground and rig floor and while climbing to the monkeyboard, in wind, mud, cold or heat.

Cleaning: washing and wiping down the derrick, monkeyboard, fingerboard and derrick-mounted equipment to remove caked drilling mud, spilled oil and grease, ice and loose debris (dropped-object housekeeping), using water hose, rags and solvents while working at height on the rig.

Oiling/greasing: lubricating derrick-mounted moving parts on schedule - crown block sheaves, traveling block, racking-board fingers and rails, elevator links, guide rails - normally by climbing with a grease gun or working from the board, plus dressing/greasing the drilling line.

Periodic thorough derrick inspection during rig-up/rig-down or a maintenance day: hands-on checks of bolted connections and torque, welds, leg pins and guy-wire tension, drilling line slip-and-cut condition, plus a dropped-object survey, with findings written up for repair.

Offshore platform or drillship: inspection round on the derrick and derrick equipment for corrosion, cracks, loose items and dropped-object hazards, in an Ex-classified, permit-controlled facility with fixed layout, standard equipment and marine weather.

sources.title: Skydio drones for energy transmission asset inspection | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio 3D Scan performs fully autonomous flight patterns that capture every surface of tall steel energy structures at inspection-grade detail, the imagery basis for finding structural flaws.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous close-range photo scanning of steel lattice transmission towers for defect detection. A drilling derrick/mast is the same class of bolted/welded steel lattice at similar heights, inspected for the same defect types (cracks, corrosion, loose or missing members), so the flight, obstacle-avoidance and coverage capability transfers.

sources.title: Oil & Gas | Autonomous Inspections & Monitoring | Percepto
sources.claim: Percepto Air drone-in-a-box systems fly autonomous inspection missions at oil and gas sites, including across major US upstream basins, without an on-site pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: resident autonomous drone inspection of oil and gas site assets. It establishes that autonomous, unattended drone inspection sorties are routinely run inside operator-controlled oil and gas premises in field weather, which is the environment a rig derrick inspection would occur in.

sources.system: DJM Aerial Solutions drilling derrick drone inspection service
sources.title: Drilling Derrick Inspection | DJM Aerial Solutions | North East | Offshore
sources.claim: Drone inspection of drilling derricks is an established commercial service that replaces climbing and rope access for finding derrick defects, accepted by drilling contractors.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (derrick flaw inspection), but piloted, so it cannot by itself support a positive judgment; it establishes that aerial imagery of a derrick is accepted by employers as the inspection deliverable, which the autonomous scanning systems above supply.

sources.title: World's First Inside-the-Derrick Inspection With a Drone
sources.claim: A drone flew an inside-the-derrick inspection of an offshore ... for a major drilling contractor, previously done only by rope access.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, piloted flight; cited to show a drone platform can physically operate within the confined lattice of an operating rig's derrick and produce the inspection record, the manoeuvring problem the autonomous scanners must solve.

sources.claim: An Ex-certified legged robot ran autonomous inspection missions covering 70 inspection points on two decks of a North Sea offshore platform, with onshore remote takeover available.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous routine inspection rounds of equipment in an offshore oil facility. It substantiates that autonomous robots complete scheduled visual/sensor inspection rounds to operator-accepted quality inside a hazardous, institution-controlled rig environment, though at deck level rather than derrick height.

sources.claim: Automatic lubrication systems are supplied for oilfield drilling rigs and equipment, delivering metered grease or oil to bearings and other components on schedule under controller command.

tasks.label: Supervise crew members, and provide assistance in training them.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-tour safety and job briefing on the rig floor: the derrickhand reviews the day's drilling program, hazards, and task assignments with floorhands, answers questions, and confirms understanding before work begins.

Directing floorhands verbally and by hand/radio signal during a trip out of the hole — calling pipe stand handling sequence, pacing, and corrections from the monkeyboard or mud pit area while operations run.

On-the-job instruction of a new roughneck in mud system duties: explaining and demonstrating mud mixing ratios, pump lineup, pit level checks, and shaker screen changes, then watching the trainee do it and correcting technique.

Coaching and correcting unsafe or sloppy practice in the moment — PPE use, hand placement near elevators/tongs, housekeeping — including showing the correct method and confirming the crew member repeats it correctly.
Administrative supervision: assigning tasks for the tour, tracking trainee competency sign-offs and training records, and reporting crew performance and issues to the driller or toolpusher.

tasks.label: Repair pumps, mud tanks, and related equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Land drilling rig, mud pump fluid-end/expendables repair: derrickhand shuts in one triplex pump and changes liners, pistons/swabs, valves and seats, seals and packing, or clears a washed-out module — 40-100 lb parts, hammer wrenches, hydraulic liner puller, cramped mud-caked pump skid, often at night and in weather, while the second pump keeps circulating.

Land rig mud tank/pit system repairs: agitator gearbox, shaft or impeller repair, mixing hopper/jet and butterfly-valve replacement, unplugging or re-plumbing suction lines and hoses, patching or welding a leaking tank wall, replacing gauges and unions; sometimes tank washout and confined-space entry.

Land rig centrifugal charging/mixing pump and small-equipment repair: mechanical seal or packing replacement, impeller and wear-plate change, coupling and motor swap, plus repair of hoses, camlocks, relief valves and pressure gauges on the mud system skid.

Land rig solids-control equipment repair: shale shaker screen replacement and deck/seal repair, vibrator motor and spring replacement, desander/desilter cone and manifold repair, centrifuge scroll/bearing service — done on a slick, mud-sprayed shaker deck under time pressure.

Offshore platform or drillship enclosed mud-pump room and mud-module repairs: same pump, tank, agitator and solids-control repairs performed inside a fixed, standardized, access-controlled machinery space with lifting beams, tool cribs and permit-to-work procedures.

sources.system: NOV ATOM RTX robotic drill floor package
sources.title: Advanced robotics enable revolution on the rig floor - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: The most advanced rig-floor robotics deployed in drilling (NOV ATOM RTX robotic arms) automate pipe-handling and connection tasks; equipment maintenance remains a human task that crews perform while the robots make connections.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest robotic capability on a drilling rig: it handles tubulars and mud buckets at the same worksite, but the article states crews still perform equipment maintenance, so it does not substantiate pump, tank or solids-control repair.

tasks.label: Steady pipes during connection to or disconnection from drill or casing strings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Land drilling rig (AC triple, pad drilling): at each drilling connection, the derrickhand steadies/guides the incoming stand or single from the monkey board (and helps latch elevators) while the driller stabs it into the string and the iron roughneck makes up the connection; repeated every 30-90 ft of hole; day/night, outdoor weather.

Land drilling rig, tripping in/out of hole: derrickhand on the monkey board latches, steadies and swings the top of 90-ft drill pipe stands between well center and the fingerboard, setting stands back or pulling them out during break-out/make-up, hundreds of stands per trip.

Land drilling rig, running casing or liner: steadying and aligning casing joints as they are stabbed into the string (from the stabbing board/racking board or by tailing the joint), with the derrickhand supporting the crew and casing-running crew.

Offshore rig (GoM jackup, platform rig, semi or drillship): derrick worker steadies drill pipe/tubular stands in the derrick during connections and trips, on a rig floor with existing mechanized pipe-handling equipment; motion and marine conditions.

Well servicing/workover rig at a producing lease: derrickhand in the mast racks and steadies 30-ft tubing joints (and sucker rods) during pulling and running of the tubing string, with backing-out done by the floor crew's tongs.

Non-routine tubulars and conditions: steadying drill collars, heavyweight, mud motors/MWD subs and crossovers during BHA make-up/break-out, or handling wet, bent or damaged joints, on older mechanical rigs or in severe weather (high wind, ice) where standard sequences do not apply.

tasks.label: Weigh clay, and mix with water and chemicals to make drilling mud, using portable mixers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: US land rig, initial mud-up / building volume: derrickhand works the mud house, breaks pallets of 50-100 lb paper sacks (bentonite gel, soda ash, polymer), cuts and dumps them into the jet hopper while metering water into the pits, then checks mud weight and funnel viscosity. Dusty, weather-exposed, sacks stacked and leaning variably on pallets.

US land rig, routine treatment during drilling: repeated additions of sacked products (polymers, thinners, lime, lost-circulation material) per the mud engineer's written recipe, counted/weighed by sack and jetted into the active system through the hopper over the tour, with periodic property checks.

Weight-up and density maintenance on a rig with a piped bulk system: barite drawn from bulk P-tanks/surge tanks into the hopper or mixing line, plus liquid additives from totes/dosing stations, to hold mud weight at the programmed value while circulating; pits instrumented, transfers by valve line-up and pumps.

Offshore/deepwater rig mud module: batch-building mud and pills from bulk barite/bentonite/calcium-carbonate silos with metered liquid additives, sequenced from the mud control room; fixed layout, standard equipment, institution-controlled premises.

Small workover or remote-lease job: portable mixer and jet hopper trucked in, a few tanks of gel/polymer mud mixed from sacks on an ad hoc setup with no permanent mud plant; ground, weather and layout vary site to site.

tasks.label: Guide lengths of pipe into and out of elevators.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Tripping drill pipe on a modern high-spec AC land drilling rig (super-spec triple, pad drilling): from the monkeyboard the derrickhand guides the top of each 90-ft stand out of the elevators into the fingerboard when tripping out, and pulls stands back into the elevators when tripping in — hundreds of stands per trip, in mud, wind, heat or cold, working at height in a harness.
Same tripping/racking work on an older or lower-spec land rig (mechanical or lower-automation double/triple, manual link tilt and elevators, older mast and fingerboard, smaller crew).

Tripping/racking stands on an offshore unit (jackup, semisubmersible or drillship): stands moved between setback/fingerboard and well center with the rig heaving, on a drill floor with an existing mechanized pipe-handling suite.

Running casing or completion tubing on a drilling rig: single joints picked up from the catwalk are stabbed and guided into the elevators/casing tool at or above the floor (stabbing-board work), larger diameters, heavier joints, thread protection critical.

Handling drill collars, heavyweight drill pipe and BHA subs into and out of the elevators — thicker-walled, heavier, sometimes irregular components run with lift subs and safety clamps, racked back or laid down at the start/end of a bit run.

Well-servicing/workover rig on a producing lease: derrickhand at the tubing board guides 2-3/8 to 3-1/2 in. tubing doubles (and sucker rods) into and out of the elevators and racks them in the fingerboard, over a live wellhead, on a mobile mast rig.

tasks.label: Clamp holding fixtures on ends of hoisting cables.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Land drilling rig floor during tripping/pipe-handling: derrickhand or floor crew clamps a holding fixture (single-joint elevator, hook, safety clamp, or becket) onto the end of the catline / air-hoist (tugger) winch line to hoist tools, subs or a joint; done repeatedly per tour on an outdoor, muddy floor with moving loads.

Slip-and-cut of the drilling line: after new 1-1/8 in to 1-1/2 in line is pulled off the reel and strung, the crew installs and torques the wire-rope clamps at the drawworks drum end and re-sets the deadline anchor clamp to spec; heavy stiff steel rope, bolted clamps, safety-critical termination.

Well-servicing / workover rig at a remote lease well: clamping a rope socket, hook, clamp or hoisting plug on the end of the sand line or tubing hoist line, on uneven ground at a site taken as found, in all weather.

Rig-up / rig-down and mast raising at a fresh pad: attaching clamps and end fixtures to raising lines, guy-line ends and mast-hoist cables while the rig is partly assembled; work on the ground and at height.

Offshore rig or platform with an enclosed, standardized drill floor and mast: attaching hoisting-cable end fixtures (tugger hook, cable clamps, riser/handling slings) with dedicated equipment and controlled access.

sources.system: NOV ATOM RTX robotic arms (Precision AlphaARMS / H&P FlexRobotics)
sources.developer: NOV, with Precision Drilling and H&P
sources.title: Advanced robotics enable revolution on the rig floor - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: NOV's ATOM RTX robotic arms are deployed on land rig floors (Precision Drilling Montney rig, H&P Rig 618) but perform tubular handling - tailing, stabbing, doping - using the rig's existing elevators and drawworks to carry load; no cable-end fixture clamping is part of the scope.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic rig-floor work by a derrickhand. It shows what deployed rig robotics actually do (guide and handle tubulars); it does not substantiate clamping holding fixtures onto hoisting-cable ends, which requires threading/seating a load-rated fitting on a limp steel rope and fastening it.

sources.title: FlexRobotics® Hands-Free Rig Floor | H&P, Inc.
sources.claim: H&P's FlexRobotics package, the first full-scale robotic rig-floor system on its rigs, is limited to tubular handling from tailing to ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated derrickhand duties on a land rig floor. Scope is tubulars only; nothing in the product description covers rigging or attaching fixtures to winch/hoist line ends.

sources.title: Canrig® Robotics - Nabors
sources.claim: Nabors' Canrig robotics (RZR module, PACE-R801) provide autonomous hands-free tubular and tool handling on the drill floor, again without any cable-end fixture attachment function.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing crew from red-zone drill-floor work. Demonstrates the frontier of deployed rig automation is pipe/stand handling, not manipulation of hoisting cables or their end fittings.

sources.title: Mechanization, automation guide innovations in advanced robotic technologies for the drill floor - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: The RDS/NOV drill floor robot, run at Ullrigg and installed on Odfjell's Deepsea Atlantic, handles pipe and tools such as subs on the drill floor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general tool handling on an offshore drill floor by a manipulator. It is the closest general-purpose rig manipulator, but the cited capability is picking up and spinning rigid threaded tools, not seating and fastening a fixture on a wire-rope end; autonomy from the driller's cabin is not established.

sources.title: PLP AND FULCRUMAIR UNVEIL GROUNDBREAKING ROBOTIC SOLUTION FOR INSTALLING BIRD DIVERTERS ON OVERHEAD POWER LINES
sources.claim: Robotic clamping of clip-type fixtures onto suspended cables has been done commercially only for lightweight snap-on bird diverters installed mid-span on overhead conductors by an unmanned aerial system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: attaching a clamp-type fixture to a steel/aluminum cable. Transfer fails: the object is a light snap-on clip placed mid-span with no load-bearing or torque requirement, whereas a hoisting-cable end fixture is a multi-kilogram load-rated termination that must be seated on a rope end and fastened to spec; the system is also an operator-supervised aerial platform of unclear autonomy.

sources.system: Aerial manipulation robot for clip-type bird flight diverter installation
sources.developer: University of Seville / GRVC (published in Applied Sciences)
sources.title: Installation of Clip-Type Bird Flight Diverters on High-Voltage Power Lines with Aerial Manipulation Robot: Prototype and Testbed Experimentation
sources.claim: Even research prototypes for clamping fixtures onto cables from a robot are only semi-automated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic attachment of a clamp to a cable. Cited to show the state of the art is semi-automated testbed work on light clips, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of load-bearing hoisting-cable end terminations.

sources.title: 600t Swaging Press | SAHM SPLICE
sources.claim: Attaching end fittings to heavy wire rope in shops is done on hydraulic swaging presses that a human loads and actuates; the machine only closes the die once the operator has placed rope and ferrule.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fixing a fitting to a wire-rope end in a purpose-built (E1-like) setting. It shows that even in the most machine-structured version of this work the placement of the rope end and the fitting remains a human operation, so no cited machine completes the instance autonomously.

tasks.label: String cables through pulleys and blocks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Land drilling rig, rig-up: crew strings a new drilling line (1-1/8" to 1-3/8" steel wire rope, ~2-3 lb/ft) from the supply reel over the crown block fast-line sheave, down and through the traveling block sheaves for 8-10 lines, dead-ends it at the deadline anchor, and spools it on the drawworks drum. Work is outdoors on a wellsite pad, partly at height in the mast or on the laid-down mast, in wind/mud/cold.

Working land rig, periodic slip-and-cut of the drilling line: derrickhand and crew unclamp the drum, pull new line from the reel through the deadline anchor and over the crown sheaves, slip the reeved system a measured length, cut off and discard worn line, re-clamp and re-tension. Done between wells or during rig maintenance, at height in the derrick and at the drawworks.

Rig-down for a rig move: drilling line unstrung/respooled through the traveling block back onto the drawworks drum with a powered spooler, blocks secured, deadline released; then re-strung at the next location. Outdoor wellsite, heavy line under tension, crew guiding the line onto sheaves and drum.

Rigging auxiliary lines on a working rig: stringing tugger/air-hoist wire (3/8"-5/8"), sand line, or catline through snatch blocks, crown sheaves, and padeyes in the derrick and on the rig floor to hoist equipment; attachment points vary by lift, much of it done from the monkeyboard or derrick ladder at height.

Well-servicing / workover rig at a lease or urban well site: on rig-up of the telescoping mast, stringing the sand line and blocks through mast sheaves and reeving the hoisting line; site is taken as found — uneven ground, varied wellhead layout, nearby tanks and pumping units, no fixed pad standard.

Offshore rig (platform or floater) derrick: reeving 12-14 lines of 2"+ drilling line through crown and traveling blocks during major overhaul or line change-out, inside a derrick with fixed layout, controlled access, and permanent lifting aids.

sources.system: NOV RZR robotic drill floor module / ATOM RTX
sources.title: Automation, robotics and sustainability shaping visions for rig of the future - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous drill-floor robotics (NOV's RZR module) perform tubular handling, connections and tripping on the rig floor; the automated scope described is pipe handling, not stringing or reeving of wire rope through crown/traveling block sheaves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated pipe handling on the same drilling rig. It establishes what rig robotics actually cover (tubulars at well center and in the fingerboard); no capability for reeving wire rope over sheaves is claimed, so it does not transfer to this task.

sources.title: H&P deploys FlexRobotics on Permian rig - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: H&P's first full-scale rig-floor robotic package was deployed on a Permian land rig in 2025; it automates drilling and tripping activities (tubular handling and connections), with no reported drilling-line stringing or reeving function.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic tubular handling/connections on a land rig floor. Shows commercial rig robots operate only on standardized pipe at fixed positions; wire-rope reeving at height in the mast remains outside the demonstrated envelope.

sources.title: Multistage Cable Routing Through Hierarchical Imitation Learning | IEEE Transactions on Robotics
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic routing of a flexible line through a sequence of guides has been demonstrated only at benchtop scale: a single Franka Panda arm routing a thin electrical cable through small clips in an instrumented work cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = threading a deformable linear object through fixed guides. Closest robotic analogue to stringing cable through sheaves, but the objects (millimetre-scale flexible cable, gram-scale forces, benchtop clips) differ by orders of magnitude from 1-1/8"+ steel drilling line over multi-tonne block sheaves, so performance does not carry over.

sources.title: Powered Drill Line Spoolers Manufacturer in USA
sources.claim: Drill-line handling on rigs is mechanized with powered spoolers that wind line through the traveling block onto the drum, but these are crew-operated powered tools; the reeving of the line over the crown and traveling block sheaves is still performed by the rig crew.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (drilling-line handling). It is a powered winding aid operated by crew, with no autonomous perception or manipulation, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Set and bolt crown blocks to posts at tops of derricks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Land drilling rig rig-up on a well pad: the crown section/crown block is hoisted by the rig crane onto the mast top posts while the mast (or crown section) is horizontal or on the derrick stand; crew aligns holes with drift pins and spud wrenches, inserts and torques large structural bolts, then the mast is raised. Outdoor pad, wind/mud/cold, layout differs site to site.

Land rig-up with the mast already raised: derrickhand climbs the derrick in harness to the crown platform to set, secure and bolt crown-mounted items (crown block hold-down bolts, sheave guards, crown safety-line and SRL anchors), re-torquing to spec at 100+ ft with hand and impact tools.

Well servicing / workover rig: crown assembly of a telescoping mast bolted or re-torqued at the well location with the mast lowered onto the carrier; smaller crown block and sheave cluster, bolts checked or replaced after inspection findings, field conditions on a lease road or pad.

Rig yard or fabrication/repair shop: mast sections laid on stands under an overhead crane; crown block removed for sheave/bearing service, then set back onto the posts, aligned, bolted and torqued to spec. Controlled premises, standard rigging equipment, fixed shop layout.

Offshore rig or platform derrick (shipyard construction or major overhaul): crown block set and bolted to the derrick top posts high above the drill floor, using platform crane and rigging; institution-controlled premises with standard layout, work at height with weather exposure.

sources.title: NEXT.assembly: New body marriage trends with flex decking - Dürr
sources.claim: Dürr's flex decking marriage station joins a heavy chassis/powertrain assembly to the car body, using vision to bring all parts into position ready for bolting, in a fenced automotive assembly line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated 'marriage' of a heavy sub-assembly onto a mating structure. It transfers to setting a crown block on mast posts at E1 because both require presenting a heavy rigid assembly to mating holes on a fixtured structure with vision-guided alignment before fasteners are run.

sources.system: Dürr flex bolt automatic bolting stations

instances.label: Pre-tower/pre-shift safety meeting at the rig site: the driller gathers the crew (derrickhand, floorhands, motorhand) at the doghouse, walks through the job safety analysis for the coming tour, names hazards of the planned operations (tripping, casing running, cementing), assigns roles, and answers questions.

On-the-job coaching of a new or green floorhand during live operations: the driller explains and shows correct handling of slips, tongs, and spinning chain, watches the hand perform it, corrects technique verbally, and signs off that the hand is competent for the job step.

Introducing a new or revised procedure (updated well-control practice, revised lockout/tagout, new pipe-handling or red-zone policy sent down from the company or client): briefing the crew on what changed and why, posting it, collecting acknowledgment sign-offs, and enforcing it over subsequent tours.

Running required drills — BOP/kick drill, pit drill, H2S or fire and evacuation drill — calling the drill, timing crew response to stations and valve positions, then critiquing performance and recording results on the IADC report.

Structured training and record-keeping in the doghouse or field office: reviewing incident/near-miss learnings and safety alerts, going through toolbox-talk or e-learning material, completing competency assessments and training documentation for each crew member.

tasks.label: Observe pressure gauge and move throttles and levers to control the speed of rotary tables, and to regulate pressure of tools at bottoms of boreholes.

instances.label: Land development rig on a multi-well pad (shale/unconventional): driller sits at the console, watches standpipe/differential pressure, hookload, torque and RPM readouts, and works the brake/drawworks control and top-drive throttle to hold weight-on-bit, rotary speed and pump pressure at the programmed setpoints while drilling ahead in a known formation.

Directional work with a mud motor/RSS: driller orients and holds toolface by feathering the drawworks and top drive, controlling differential pressure across the motor and rocking the string, alternating slide and rotary intervals through the curve and lateral.

Off-bottom and pipe-movement operations on the same rigs: drilling off, making connections, breaking circulation, reaming/back-reaming and controlled tripping, throttling pumps and hoisting speed to keep surge/swab and circulating pressures inside the pore-pressure/frac-gradient window.

Offshore or narrow-margin/managed-pressure well: driller and MPD operator regulate annular back-pressure, pump rate and choke to hold bottomhole pressure within a tight window during drilling, connections and pump ramps on a deepwater floater or jack-up.

Drilling-dysfunction response during normal drilling: pressure/torque signatures show stick-slip, bit balling, a mud-motor stall, a pack-off or excessive vibration, and the driller backs off weight, changes RPM or pump rate to clear it and resume.

Abnormal well event: pressure and pit readings indicate a kick, lost circulation, washout or impending stuck pipe; the driller must diagnose the anomaly, stop rotation and pumps, space out and shut in, then work with the crew on the kill/remedial plan.

instances.label: Routine drilling connection on a modern AC land rig (super-spec pad rig, Permian/Appalachia): from the driller's cabin the operator works the drawworks joystick/brake to pick up off slips, raise the string one joint/stand, hold position while the joint is added and torqued, then lower back into the slips and tag bottom. Dozens of times per day, day and night, in all weather.

Tripping drill pipe out of and back into the hole for a bit or BHA change on a modern land or offshore rig with top drive and mechanized pipe handling: hoisting stand after stand at controlled speed to avoid swabbing, watching hookload/overpull, filling the hole, and slowing at the shoe and casing seat. Normal hole conditions.

Running casing or a liner into the well: lowering long, heavy, thin-walled tubulars at controlled speed to manage surge, easing through tight spots and the shoe track, holding weight while the joint is made up and the fill-up tool is used. Higher consequence, slower, one-shot operation with a casing crew on the floor.

Drilling ahead: feeding off the drawworks (brake handle or joystick/auto-driller setpoint) to maintain target weight on bit, differential pressure and ROP through changing formations, picking up off bottom for surveys, sliding and connections.

Non-routine hoisting under hole trouble: pulling through tight hole and ledges, washing and back-reaming out, working and jarring on stuck pipe, controlled pipe movement during a kick or lost circulation, fishing and running logging/completion tools. Requires reading hookload/torque 'feel' and improvising against a plan.

Older or less-automated rigs (mechanical/SCR drawworks with a manual brake handle, small shallow-hole or coring rigs, kelly rigs) where the driller manually brakes and hoists while a floor crew sets slips, uses tongs and works the derrick by hand signals; pipe is handled from the V-door and monkeyboard by people.

instances.label: Routine drilling connection on a modern AC-powered land rig (shale pad, e.g. Permian): with the top drive drilling ahead, set slips, break out the saver sub, add a joint/stand of 5-in. drill pipe from the mousehole or catwalk, stab, spin and torque with the iron roughneck to spec, dope the threads, and continue drilling. Repeated every 30-90 minutes; contractor-controlled pad, standard tubulars, weather exposed.

Tripping in or out of the hole on a modern land rig: rapid, repeated make-up/break-out of stands at the rotary, slips and elevators, mud bucket on break-out, derrickhand racking stands in the fingerboard, iron roughneck spinning and torquing, with the driller coordinating drawworks and top drive. Speed and consistency (stands per hour) matter.

Connections on an older / lower-spec land rig (mechanical or SCR rig, small operator or remote location) with no rig-floor automation: manual tongs, spinning wrench or spinning chain, hand-doping, kelly or basic top drive; crew makes up connections by hand under the driller's control.

Making up (or breaking out) bottomhole assembly and tool connections at the rotary: drill collars, stabilizers, jars, subs, crossovers and third-party MWD/LWD tools, using lift subs, special thread compound, torque-turn monitoring, mud bucket and sometimes manual tongs; non-standard geometries and one-off items, done a few times per well.

Connections on an offshore rig drill floor (Gulf of Mexico platform, jackup or floater): highly mechanized floor with pipe-handling machines, vertical/horizontal racker, iron roughneck and integrated drilling control system; institution-controlled facility, fixed layout, tightly enforced red-zone rules.

Hands-on preventive service of rig machinery: greasing and lubricating the drawworks, rotary and pump ends, oil and filter changes on engines and pumps, topping fluids, replacing shaker screens, tong/roughneck dies, packing and swab rubbers, cleaning and tightening fittings — done in tight, dirty spaces on the rig.

Corrective repair and mechanical readjustment when machinery falls out of spec during operations: changing mud pump liners, valves and pistons, chasing hydraulic or air leaks, replacing hoses and worn wear parts, adjusting brake bands and chain tension, and function-testing/recalibrating safety devices and sensors.

instances.label: Land drilling rig, routine treatment of the active system: worker moves 50-100 lb paper/poly sacks of bentonite gel, lignosulfonate, soda ash or polymer from pallets in the sack house to the mud hopper, cuts each sack and dumps it into the hopper while the mixing pump circulates, adds liquid chemicals from drums, and checks mud weight with a mud balance. Outdoors on a contractor-controlled pad, dusty, weather exposed.

Weighting up / holding mud density on a modern rig equipped with bulk barite and bentonite storage: barite is pneumatically transferred from P-tanks or silos to a surge tank and metered into the mixing hopper to raise density to a target (e.g., 9.5 to 12.5 ppg) while circulating, with density verified repeatedly and the rate adjusted to avoid overshoot.

Batch mixing of spud mud / premix before or at spud: large volumes of bentonite clay and water plus soda ash and polymer are made up in reserve or premix tanks on the rig site to a specified yield and viscosity, then transferred to the active system.

Offshore rig or platform mud module: bulk barite/bentonite from silos plus sacked specialty additives fed through a sack cutting/dosing unit and liquid additives from a dosing skid into enclosed mud pits, mixed and treated to a recipe, monitored from a control room in an enclosed, standardized mixing area.

Small remote operation - shallow exploration/coring rig or small workover rig with portable tanks or an earthen pit: bentonite and polymer sacks mixed with water using a small hopper, paddle or hand tools at a site taken as found (uneven ground, no bulk equipment, variable layout, weather).

Walk-around examination of the pump house/pump skids while circulating: look for washouts and leaks at the fluid ends, discharge lines and pop-off, listen for knocking valves, read discharge/charge pressure gauges and pulsation dampener charge, check liner-wash flow, flag abnormalities to the driller.

Mud consistency check at the pits/shaker house: mud weight in and out, funnel viscosity, sand content; compare against the mud program; call for water, barite or premix additions and verify density and pit levels respond as intended.

Offshore or highly instrumented rig: pumps run through the drilling control system; monitor circulation for anomalies (standpipe pressure drop from a washout or plugged jet, lost returns, pack-off, ECD exceeding limits), throttle or shut down pumps and take corrective action inside safe pressure limits.

Corrective intervention on a pump mid-job: change a knocked-out valve or washed-out liner, re-pack a piston, clear a plugged suction strainer or dumped charge pump, or bring the standby pump online and re-establish circulation with minimal downtime.

tasks.label: Clean and oil pulleys, blocks, and cables.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled greasing of crown block / mast-head sheave bearings on a land drilling rig: climb the derrick or mast with grease gun and rags, wipe dirt off each zerk or pressure-lube passage, pump grease into each sheave shaft until purge, check sheave grooves and guards; at height, outdoors, in wind, heat or cold.

Lubricating the traveling block, hook, and top-drive/swivel bearings and sheaves: block landed on the floor or accessed from the monkeyboard, old grease and mud wiped away, each fitting hit with a grease gun, wear surfaces oiled and inspected.

Cleaning and dressing the drilling line: wiping accumulated dirt and dried dope off the wire rope, applying wire-rope lubricant to the running line (often during or after slip-and-cut), inspecting for broken wires, corrosion and birdcaging.

Greasing sheaves and lubricating cables of auxiliary hoisting gear at floor/ground level: tugger and catline winches, sandline, deadline anchor sheave, drawworks and catworks shafts and guides; many grease points, some in cramped guarded spaces.

Washing and degreasing built-up mud, drilling fluid and old grease from blocks, sheaves, guards and lines on the rig, and wiping cables with rags and solvent so fittings and wear surfaces are visible; done in place on the rig structure.

Well-service / workover or truck-mounted rig at a remote wellsite: greasing and oiling sandline and wireline sheaves, blocks and cables in the open on uneven, muddy ground with equipment and clutter as found and no fixed facility layout.

tasks.label: Monitor progress of drilling operations, and select and change drill bits according to the nature of strata, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Land rig drilling a horizontal shale well: over a 12-hour tour the driller monitors progress from the driller's cabin — ROP, weight on bit, torque, pump pressure, MSE, cuttings/returns — adjusts parameters as strata change, logs footage, and judges the bit is still fit to keep drilling (no bit change this tour).

Planned bit change at section TD/casing point on a land rig: trip out 8,000-12,000 ft of drillpipe, set the bit breaker in the rotary table, break out the worn PDC bit from the mud motor with roughneck/tongs, dope and make up the bit selected for the next formation, torque to spec, and trip back in.

Unplanned bit change mid-run on a land rig: ROP collapses and torque spikes in a hard stringer; the driller diagnoses a dulled or wrong-type bit, calls the trip, picks a different bit type from the bits on location, changes it out on the rig floor with hand tools and the iron roughneck, and resumes drilling.

Land rig equipped with an automation/robotics package (autodriller, automated pipe handling, robotic arms): the driller supervises automated drilling and tripping from the cabin, while the bit/BHA change itself is done with mechanized floor equipment plus crew hands-on for the bit breaker and bit make-up.

Offshore platform, jackup or drillship: driller monitors drilling from an enclosed chair with rig-control automation; bit change performed on a mechanized drill floor with iron roughneck and pipe-handling machine, handling heavy large-diameter BHA components in a confined marine environment.

Small exploration/coring or shallow rig at a remote lease: monitor coring penetration and core recovery, and change the core bit or tricone with chain tongs and hand tools at ground level on unimproved terrain in whatever weather is present.
