tasks.label: Repair or replace defective parts of machinery, such as rotary drill rigs, water trucks, air compressors, and pumps, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mud pump maintenance on the drilling location: crew diagnoses a knocking/leaking pump, isolates it, opens the fluid end and replaces worn valves, seats, liners, pistons or packing with hammer wrenches, pullers and hand tools; heavy greasy parts, mud, weather, awkward access, seized/corroded fasteners; pump retorqued and pressure-checked before returning to circulation.

Small-component repairs on rig equipment during operations: replacing burst hydraulic/air hoses and fittings, leaking seals and gauges, tong dies and jaws, drawworks brake blocks, chains and sprockets, cathead lines; work at height on the derrick/rig floor or in tight spaces around the substructure, often under time pressure to resume drilling.

Auxiliary power/air equipment repair on location: air compressor, generator or rig engine faults - replacing belts, filters, unloader valves, starters, injectors, fuel lines, sensors - requiring fault diagnosis, disassembly with hand tools, part replacement and test run, in an outdoor skid or engine house.

Water truck or other support vehicle repair at the location: replacing blown hydraulic lines, PTO/water pump components, valves, belts, batteries or lights; vehicle parked on uneven ground at the pad, mechanic works from the ground or under the truck with hand tools.

Wheel/tire replacement on a light service vehicle (crew pickup or light-duty truck) taken to a shop bay or tire service in town: lug nuts removed, damaged tire/wheel swapped, wheel remounted and torqued.

Yard/shop rebuild during rig move or downtime: a removed component (pump module, swivel, air winch, gearbox, valve assembly) is set on a bench or stand in the drilling contractor's maintenance yard, torn down with shop and hand tools, worn parts replaced, reassembled to spec and bench-tested.

tasks.label: Locate and recover lost or broken bits, casings, and drill pipes from wells, using special tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Onshore land drilling rig: drill string twists off or parts downhole. Driller/crew determine depth and condition of the fish top (pull tests, impression block, logs), select and dress an overshot with the right grapple, make up a fishing BHA with jars/bumper sub/safety joint, run in, tag and engage the fish by controlled slack-off and rotation, jar it free, and trip out with the recovered pipe. Mud, weather, and repeated unsuccessful attempts are normal.

Junk retrieval from bottomhole on a drilling rig: lost bit cones, broken bit shank, dropped hand tools, bit breaker or tong parts. Requires diagnosing what is in the hole, running junk baskets/boot subs, junk magnets or a junk mill on the drill string, circulating to catch debris, and repeated runs until the hole is clean enough to resume drilling.

Slickline/e-line retrieval in a completed or producing well: lost toolstring, parted cable, stuck plug, gauge or radioactive source. Rig up lubricator on the wellhead, run gauge/impression tools to locate and characterize the fish, run the correct spear/overshot/cutter, latch and jar or pull it out under pressure control.

Workover rig on an older producing wellsite: stuck or parted tubing and casing recovery — free-point survey, back-off or chemical/mechanical cut, spear or overshot engagement, cut-and-pull of casing joints, sometimes washover pipe or section milling before recovery.

Offshore/deepwater rig: junk dropped into the BOP, wellhead or riser, or heavy fishing string work at depth. Includes ROV-assisted retrieval of items on the subsea stack and fishing runs with high-capacity tools under tight well-control constraints and rig-time pressure.

The sequences follow preplanned paths for standard tubulars.

It transfers only to that component — the tubulars are standard, the paths preplanned — and does not cover locating the fish, dressing/making up a fishing tool, engaging the fish, or jarring.

tasks.label: Line drilled holes with pipes, and install all necessary hardware, to prepare new wells.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Land shale rig (e.g., Permian/Appalachia pad): running surface or intermediate casing after the hole section is drilled — joints picked up from the pipe rack/catwalk, drifted and doped, stabbed and made up to torque spec with a casing running tool or power tongs, mud fill-up, shoe track and centralizers installed on the bottom joints, string run to setting depth and landed.

Land rig, long-lateral horizontal well: running the production casing string or a liner — several hundred joints, careful running speeds, circulating/reciprocating/rotating past tight spots, float equipment and liner-running hardware, string landed and prepared for cementing.

Between casing strings on a land rig: installing wellhead hardware — landing the casing hanger/slips in the cellar, cutting/dressing casing, setting the casing head or spool with gaskets, bolting flanges, nippling down/up the BOP stack and pressure-testing.

Offshore platform, jackup or drillship: running a casing string with the rig's mechanized tubular handling and hands-free casing running tools from the driller's cabin, including conductor/surface strings and deeper strings in a crowded, motion-affected drill floor.

Small exploration/coring or shallow-well rig at a remote, unimproved site: setting and cementing conductor or shallow surface casing and fitting the associated wellhead/diverter hardware, with the rig, tubular racks and site laid out ad hoc on rough terrain.

tasks.label: Cap wells with packers, or turn valves, to regulate outflow of oil from wells.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Land drilling rig, active drilling/tripping/connections: the driller regulates returns and bottomhole pressure by operating the choke manifold (and MPD chokes) and, on a kick, shuts in the well by closing BOP rams/annular and lining up the choke and kill valves from the console and remote panels. Gravel pad, standard API stack, operator-controlled site.

Offshore jackup/floater or platform rig: same well-control valve work through a subsea/surface BOP stack, rotating control device and MPD choke manifold, plus diverter and kill/choke line valve line-ups, executed from the driller's chair and the MPD/choke panel on a manned, tightly controlled installation.

Bringing the well on / regulating outflow after drilling or during a well test or flowback: opening wing and gate valves at the wellhead or christmas tree and stepping the surface choke through cleanup and rate steps to control oil/gas outflow to the separator or tanks, then shutting the well in.

Manual valve work around the wellhead and rig: turning handwheel gate valves in the cellar, kill/choke line and standpipe/mud manifold valves, hammer-union and needle valves, often with a valve wrench, in mud, wind, cold or at night, with visual leak checks between moves.

Running and setting a packer, bridge plug or cement retainer on drill pipe/tubing (or a DST string) to cap or isolate the well: picking up and making up the tool, running to depth, setting by weight/rotation/applied pressure, then pressure-testing the seal and confirming the well is shut off.

sources.system: Opla Energy Pressure Management Device (automated MPD choke)
sources.title: Machine learning-based pressure management technology brings full automation to MPD operations - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: Opla Energy's Pressure Management Device autonomously moves the choke to hold a target downhole pressure on working land rigs; commercially launched in 2022 and installed on 12 land rigs in the Permian, Eagle Ford, Anadarko, Haynesville and Montney, replacing MPD personnel on location.

sources.developer: Safe Influx / Finesse Control Systems (with Weatherford)

sources.title: Automated Well Control: From Automated Detection to Automated Shut-In (SPE/IADC MEDT)
sources.claim: SPE paper documents the automated shut-in sequence: on influx detection the system controls rig and BOP equipment with no driller input.

sources.system: Dynamic Annular Pressure Control (DAPC) automated choke manifold

sources.claim: Shell's Dynamic Annular Pressure Control automated choke manifold maintains constant bottomhole pressure by machine control of the chokes and was deployed offshore in the UK North Sea and Gulf of Mexico.

sources.title: Control Requirements for Automatic Managed Pressure Drilling System - SPE Drilling & Completion
sources.claim: Automatic managed-pressure-drilling choke control was applied successfully offshore on a producing North Sea field, with defined accuracy requirements for rate changes, connections and gas kicks.

tasks.label: Remove core samples during drilling to determine the nature of the strata being drilled.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Conventional whole-core run on a land rig (Permian, Bakken, Appalachia), end to end: pull the drilling BHA, make up a 60–90 ft core barrel assembly (outer barrel, inner barrel/aluminum liner, core catcher, core bit) on the rig floor, trip in, cut core while watching pump pressure for jams, trip out slowly, break the coring assembly down joint by joint, lay the inner barrels/liners over to the catwalk, break the catcher, cut liners into ~3 ft sections with a saw, mark top/bottom and depth, cap, tape, label and box the core, and log recovery. Outdoors, muddy floor, weather, contractor-controlled wellsite; core hand and wellsite geologist direct the crew.

Wireline rotary sidewall coring run at TD on a shale well: the rig crew rigs up the wireline unit and sheaves, monitors the well while the coring tool is run, then helps recover the tool and transfer 20–50 1.5-in. rock plugs out of the tool's storage magazine into numbered bottles/trays with depth labels for shipment. Rig floor plus wireline unit at the wellsite.

Problem or non-routine coring: jammed or blocked core barrel with partial recovery, unconsolidated/fractured/rubbly core that must be coaxed out, core stuck in the barrel requiring pumping or hammering, gassy core that must be handled quickly, or special preservation (freezing on dry ice, sponge or pressure core, wax/foil wrap) at the laydown area. Judgment-heavy, non-standard sequence, heavy manual handling.

Conventional coring run offshore on a drillship or platform with an automated pipe-handling drill floor: core barrel made up and tripped using rig automation and derrick equipment, core barrel laid down to a shipboard core-handling area, inner barrels cut, capped, labeled and racked/boxed by the crew, sometimes with a shipboard core lab. Institution-controlled vessel, standard layout, motion and weather.

sources.system: Canrig/Nabors Red Zone Robotics (RZR) rig floor module
sources.title: Nabors Marks Major Industry Milestone: Fully Automates Existing Land Rig with First-of-its-Kind Robotics Module
sources.claim: Nabors' Red Zone Robotics (RZR) module autonomously handles tubulars on a working land rig — making connections and tripping in and ... the hole — and has drilled horizontal wells in the Permian .... It automates standard drill-pipe handling only; nothing in the description covers core barrels, core recovery or core preservation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous tripping/handling of drill pipe on a rig floor, a step shared with running a core barrel. It is cited to show the limit of demonstrated rig-floor robotics: standard tubulars in the derrick/well-center envelope, not coring assemblies, inner barrels or the core itself.

sources.title: Manufacturers pave path to hands-free drilling with automated tubular handling - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: NOV's ATOM RTX deploys up to three robotic arms on the drill floor for tubular-handling tasks (tailing stands, stand transfer, doping, mud containment) with no human operator managing the individual robots; it is a tubular-handling system, not a coring or core-processing system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of tubulars in the rig-floor red zone. Cited to bound what drill-floor robots do today — pipe and equipment handling with dedicated end effectors — with no demonstrated handling of core barrels, liners or recovered core.

sources.system: Boart Longyear LF160i coring rig with automated inner-tube handling
sources.title: Automated exploration drill rigs: the next frontier - Mine | Issue 151 | April 2025
sources.claim: In the most automated core-drilling rigs available (mineral exploration), machine automation now extracts and delivers the core-filled inner tube onto the core tray, but disassembly of the tube and removal of the core sample itself remain manual work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving a core-filled inner tube on a rotary core rig, the same physical step as laying down an inner barrel at an oil-well catwalk. It substantiates only inner-tube delivery; the source states sample removal from the tube is still done by people, so it does not substantiate completion of core removal/processing.

sources.title: Sea-floor drill rig MARUM-MeBo200
sources.claim: The MARUM-MeBo200 seafloor core drill is a purpose-built robotic coring rig with an automatic core-barrel magazine and loading arm, but it is remotely controlled from the vessel, and recovered core barrels are opened and the core processed by hand on deck.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unmanned rotary core drilling with automated core-barrel exchange, the closest analogue to running and retrieving a core barrel at an oil well. It is remotely operated rather than autonomous, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Large-Volume Sidewall Cores | SLB
sources.claim: Wireline rotary sidewall coring tools are downhole machines that cut and store many small rock plugs in one run, but the service is commanded from the surface by a wireline crew and the recovered plugs are unloaded, bottled and labeled by people at surface.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (removing rock samples from the formation to characterize strata) performed by a downhole machine. Autonomy of the coring cycle is not established in the source, and the source describes only downhole sample capture — not rig-up or the surface recovery, packaging and labeling that complete the instance.

sources.system: CoreVault with Hostile Rotary Sidewall Coring Tool (HRSCT-B)
sources.title: Halliburton introduces CoreVault system for hydrocarbon measurement | Hydrocarbon Engineering
sources.claim: Halliburton's CoreVault, run with the HRSCT-B rotary sidewall coring tool, captures and seals up to ten cores at reservoir conditions in a ...; the sealed vessel is then recovered and opened by service personnel at surface or in a lab.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: mechanized capture and sealed preservation of rock samples from the borehole wall. Cited for scope: it substantiates downhole sample capture and sealing, not the surface handling, and its autonomy is not established in the source.

sources.system: Perseverance Sampling and Caching System (SHERLOC/corer, sample handling arm, sealing station)
sources.title: The Extraordinary Robotic Sample-Gathering System of NASA's Perseverance Mars Rover
sources.claim: NASA's Perseverance Sampling and Caching System autonomously drills rock cores, extracts them into tubes, hermetically seals and caches them on the Martian surface — autonomous coring plus sample sealing, but at centimeter scale from surface outcrops, with no drill string, mud system or heavy tubular handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous rock coring with sealed sample capture and labeling/caching. Transfer fails for this task: the cores are ~13 mm x 60 mm from surface outcrop taken over hours, whereas the oil-and-gas instance requires cutting and recovering 60–90 ft of 4-in. core from thousands of feet of hole through a drill string and processing hundreds of pounds of liner and rock at the catwalk.

tasks.label: Bolt together pump and engine parts, and connect tanks and flow lines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rig-up on a fresh land wellsite pad: bolting mud pump modules to skids and coupling pump/engine/drive components — heavy sub-assemblies landed by crane or picker, aligned by hand, large bolts started and torqued outdoors in dirt, wind and variable terrain.

Rig-up on a land wellsite: making up suction and discharge flow lines between mud tanks and the pumps — heavy hard iron, hammer unions and bolted flanges with gaskets, hoses dragged into place, joints aligned and torqued/hammered in mud and weather.

Rig-up on a land wellsite: setting mud tanks/pits and connecting them to each other and to the flow line, shakers and manifolds — jumper lines, valves, clamps, walkway and stair bolts, all at a pad whose layout differs from the last one.

During drilling operations on an erected land rig: re-bolting pump and engine parts after service — fluid-end covers, liner/valve retainers, packing, guards, engine accessories — on dirty in-place equipment with fasteners in variable condition.
Offshore rig or platform: bolting pump parts and hooking up flow lines inside the mud pump room — indoor, fixed layout, standard equipment, controlled access, work planned under permit.
Contractor rig yard/shop before mobilization: bolting up pump-engine skid packages and making up pipe spools, manifolds and tank jumper lines on stands with overhead crane and power tools available.

sources.system: MIRAI AI-vision system on assembly robots with automatic torque wrench
sources.developer: Micropsi Industries (deployed at a leading US automotive OEM, California)
sources.title: Leading US automotive OEM — Automated bolt torquing
sources.claim: An AI-vision-guided robot fleet performs bolt torquing autonomously on an automotive OEM assembly line, coping with position variance, inconsistent parts and changing lighting — i.e., robots reliably start and torque bolts on engine-scale assemblies presented in a fixtured/conveyed cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production bolt torquing of engine assemblies. Transfers to 'bolt together pump and engine parts' when the parts are presented fixtured: same objects (engine/pump components), same operation (locate hole, engage socket, torque to spec), same precision class.

sources.system: Collaborative robot engine bolt fastening line (six-axis cobot with servo torque gun)
sources.title: Collaborative Robot Engine Bolt Fastening — Oil-Pan & Vacuum-Pump Final Torque, Fully Automated
sources.claim: A commercial robot cell performs final bolt torquing on engine oil-pan and vacuum-pump joints, including automatic socket changing, positioning and tightening, all running automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bolting a pump (vacuum pump) and engine covers to an engine in a fixtured cell. Same fastening operation, comparable components and torque control as bolting pump and engine parts together.

sources.system: Vision- and force-guided robotic bolt-tightening stations
sources.developer: Multiple integrators/OEMs (reported by ASSEMBLY magazine; INESC TEC evaluation)
sources.title: Robots Automate Bolt-Tightening on Automotive Assembly Lines | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Robots equipped with 3D vision and force sensing now perform bolt-tightening on automotive assembly lines under real factory conditions, a job previously considered infeasible for robots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial bolt tightening with vision/force guidance. Supports the fastening element of bolting pump and engine parts and bolted flange joints when parts are presented in a structured cell.

sources.title: TMT Boltron — Autonomous Flange Bolting Robot (product datasheet)
sources.claim: An autonomous flange-bolting robot tightens and loosens nuts on large industrial bolted flanges (500–4000 mm, single- and double-sided) in harsh plant conditions; it is supplied to refineries and processing plants, including a contract with the Queensland Alumina refinery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making up and breaking large bolted pipe/heat-exchanger flange joints in process plants. Comparable to bolting flanged flow-line and pump-discharge connections — same joint type, bolt sizes and torques — though the machine must be set on a joint already positioned by people.

sources.system: ROBOFUEL autonomous refuelling system (ABB/KUKA robot arm plus bunded tanks)
sources.title: SCOTT making ROBOFUEL refuelling system progress with AHS mining truck fleets — International Mining
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic refuelling system uses vision and sensing to locate a haul truck's fill point and connect the fuel line to the tank without an operator; it is in use at multiple mine sites, including with an autonomous Komatsu 930E ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously mating a fluid line to a tank connection point at a purpose-built station. This is the core act of 'connect tanks and flow lines', at smaller scale and with a standardized coupling rather than heavy oilfield iron.

sources.system: Canrig Red Zone Robotics (RZR) Rig Floor Module; PACE-R801 automated land rig
sources.title: Retrofit Kit Makes Robotic Drilling a Reality for Existing Rigs — JPT
sources.claim: Wellsite robotics that are actually deployed on drilling rigs are fixed, purpose-built drill-floor modules that handle standardized tubulars (making drilling connections, tripping, stand building); no cited system performs rig-up bolting of pump/engine packages or hooks up mud tanks and flow lines at a wellsite.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound, not support, higher tiers: the related task (torquing tubular connections) is done only for uniform pipe delivered by the rig's own handling machinery in a fixed red zone, and does not transfer to bolting pump/engine packages or rigging up mud tanks and flow lines.

tasks.label: Plug observation wells, and restore sites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plugging a cased observation/monitoring or exploration well with the drilling or workover rig on an operator-controlled lease pad: rig up over the wellhead, pull tubing/rods, run the work string, mix and pump cement to set plugs across the required intervals, tag and pressure-test the plugs, pull out of hole.

Plugging a shallow observation hole, core hole or seismic shot hole at a remote exploration location: run the tremie/drill string, pump cement or bentonite grout to fill the hole to the depths required by state rule while pulling rods, top off the hole.

Surface wellhead work to complete the abandonment: excavate around the conductor, cut and pull casing three to six feet below grade, remove the wellhead and cellar, weld a steel plate/marker cap on the stub, backfill the hole.

Site restoration earthworks: close and backfill the reserve pit and cellar, remove or rip the gravel pad, and recontour/regrade the location back to the approved design surface with dozer and excavator work on soft, uneven, weather-affected ground.

Final reclamation of the location: pick up and haul off flowlines, tanks, matting and scattered debris, respread stockpiled topsoil, seed and mulch, install erosion-control measures, and touch up until vegetation is accepted by the landowner/regulator.

sources.title: Autonomous drilling at scale: How close are we? - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: Nabors' PACE-R801 fully automated land rig ran a nine-well pilot for ExxonMobil in the Permian ..., drilling, tripping and running casing with a robotic pipe handler that replaced the catwalk, with a crewless rig floor supervised by a driller.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated drilling, tripping and casing running. Plugging a well with a rig is the same rig-floor work on the same objects - making up and running tubulars into the same wellcenter, circulating and placing cement - at the same precision, so tripping/casing autonomy carries over to running a plugging string.

sources.title: Autonomous drilling at scale: How close are we? - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: The PACE-R801's robotic working area is a purpose-built machine environment: the rig floor was crewless and the red zone fenced with motion detection that stops equipment if a person enters.

sources.title: Montney's automated drilling rig | spiritnow stories (ConocoPhillips)
sources.claim: Precision Drilling rig PD 868, working for ConocoPhillips in the Montney, uses three robotic arms to handle tubulars hands-free; 400,000 m of tubulars were handled and 105,000 m drilled without manual connections, eliminating about 8,400 personnel hours from the rig floor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic tubular handling for drilling. The same robotic arms handle the same tubulars that must be run and pulled to set cement plugs in an observation well; motions, loads and tolerances are identical.

sources.title: Halliburton and Aker BP achieve offshore automation milestone
sources.claim: Halliburton's LOGIX automated cementing unit, used with Aker BP offshore, executes a programmed cement job and adjusts delivery itself without human intervention, with the operator in an onshore realtime centre.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated placement of cement slurry through a cementing unit. Setting a cement plug in an observation well is the same physical act - mixing to density and pumping a designed slurry volume into the well - with the same equipment.

sources.title: First autonomous managed pressure cementing operation
sources.claim: Halliburton executed a managed-pressure cementing operation in which the control software ran the job completely autonomously, with no user input or interaction during cementing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous control of a cement job's pumping and pressure schedule, which is the control problem in placing a balanced cement plug for abandonment.

sources.system: SLB remote and automated cementing service
sources.title: First-ever fully automated cementing job successfully executed, offshore Norway | SLB
sources.claim: SLB executed a fully automated cement job on a Norwegian Continental Shelf ..., run from an onshore Performance Live centre.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cement placement, the same plug-setting step; job is remotely managed so autonomy is treated as unestablished and it only corroborates.

sources.title: Built Robotics raises $64 million for robotic excavator Exosystem | Equipment World
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofit turns standard excavators into machines that dig autonomously and has been commercially deployed on outdoor construction sites, including a 1.1-GW solar farm.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous excavation, trenching and backfill on as-found outdoor construction sites. Well-pad restoration earthwork moves the same soil with the same machine class to a surveyed design grade, in the same terrain and weather.

sources.title: Built Robotics Unveils Autonomous Pile Driving Robot, Expediting Solar Rollout | Forbes
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 robotic pile driver surveys the site, distributes, drives and inspects piles autonomously at utility-scale solar construction sites with a two-person crew.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous self-navigating ground work on unprepared outdoor sites, showing the localization and terrain handling needed to work a well location without fixtures.

sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Announces Supervised Autonomy Testing on Active Construction Sites
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics ran supervised-autonomy mass excavation on active US construction sites in 2025, with fully operator-less deployments still a stated target for 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous earthmoving on construction sites; supervised only, so it corroborates rather than establishes capability.

tasks.label: Position and prepare truck-mounted derricks at drilling areas specified on field maps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Seismic/shot-hole work: a self-contained truck- or buggy-mounted drill is driven cross-country from a field map/GPS list of flagged shot points across ranchland, farmland or brush; at each point the operator spots on the stake, sets leveling jacks, raises the mast and readies onboard air/water for a shallow hole, doing dozens of setups a day through gates, fences, soft ground and weather.

Truck-mounted core/exploration drill positioned at survey-marked sample locations in remote or rough terrain (slopes, mud, timber, snow); the operator picks the approach, sometimes mats or winches in, levels on jacks/outriggers, erects the mast plumb and sets rod racks and onboard pump before coring.

Truck- or trailer-mounted rotary rig moved to a newly constructed well location shown on the field map: navigate lease roads, gates and cattle guards, spot the rig on the surveyed stake/conductor, level with jacks and pads, raise the derrick and then rig up ancillary gear - mud pump, tanks, water and suction/discharge lines, catwalk, pipe racks - before drilling.

Well-service/workover-style truck-mounted mast spotted over an existing wellhead on a producing, operator-controlled lease pad: back in within inches of the wellhead, set outriggers on uneven gravel, telescope and raise the mast, set guy-line anchors and tension guys, and connect to the wellhead/BOP equipment.

Repeat positioning inside one already-cleared, surveyed drilling area with controlled access (multiple shot points or slots on a single pad or cleared lease): lower mast, make a short move to the next mapped position, re-level and re-erect, repeated several times per shift with a known layout and site personnel present.

sources.title: Epiroc and Luck Stone launch first fully autonomous SmartROC D65 drill rig in U.S. aggregate market
sources.claim: Fully autonomous surface drill rig executes entire drill patterns - moving itself to each mapped hole, setting up and drilling - under remote supervision at a US quarry.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: surface blasthole drilling. The machine performs the same position-and-prepare cycle as this task - self-propelling to each hole location specified in a survey/drill plan, deploying jacks and mast, then drilling - with comparable mast-scale hardware and collar-placement precision, in a graded, access-controlled outdoor drilling area.

sources.system: Cat MineStar Command for drilling (MD6310-class rotary drills)
sources.title: Caterpillar, Thiess, and WesTrac achieve autonomous drilling milestone
sources.claim: Three fully autonomous rotary blasthole drills at a working coal mine are supervised by one remote operator; the system automates the drill cycle including tramming between holes of the pattern.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous pattern blasthole drilling. Positioning at each map-specified hole, levelling and preparing the mast is the same work as positioning and preparing a truck-mounted derrick at mapped drilling points; scale, precision and outdoor industrial conditions are comparable.

sources.system: Cat MD6310 rotary drill with Drill Assist / Command for drilling
sources.title: MD6310 Rotary Drills | Cat | Caterpillar
sources.claim: Commercial rotary drills ship with onboard automation that levels the machine, retracts jacks and raises/lowers the mast without operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: setting up a mast-mounted drill on site. Auto-level, auto-jack and auto-mast-raise are precisely the 'prepare the derrick' steps of this task, performed on self-propelled drill machinery of comparable mass and mast height.

sources.title: Command for drilling | Cat | Caterpillar
sources.claim: Autonomous pattern drilling automates drill ... across an entire blast pattern with one operator managing multiple machines; semi-autonomous mode already includes autonomous tramming between holes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving a drill between mapped hole positions on a bench, i.e. the 'position at drilling areas specified on maps' element of this task, in the same outdoor industrial setting.

sources.system: Epiroc Pit Viper autonomous drill rigs
sources.title: Epiroc's drill rig Pit Viper celebrates 25 years including a decade with autonomous operations
sources.claim: A decade of autonomous operation of these surface drill rigs, with tens of millions of metres drilled autonomously and improved spatial accuracy of hole collars.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous surface drilling at mapped hole locations; establishes that positioning, levelling and mast handling by these machines is mature production practice, not a one-off demonstration.

sources.system: Built Robotics RPD 35 robotic pile driver
sources.title: Built Robotics develops autonomous solar piling robot
sources.claim: A fully autonomous piling robot surveys, moves itself to surveyed positions and drives H-pile foundations to inch-level accuracy on utility-scale solar construction sites with a two-person support crew.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving a mast-mounted machine to survey-staked points on an outdoor site and setting it plumb before driving/drilling. It is the closest unstructured-site analogue, but works inside one cleared, staked project block with a support crew, not cross-country rig moves with ancillary rig-up.

tasks.label: Maintain and perform safety inspections on equipment and tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-job / pre-shift walkaround safety inspection and minor servicing of the service unit (workover rig, pump/acid truck, coiled-tubing or wireline unit) on a lease pad: check engine oil, coolant and hydraulic levels, look for leaks and damaged hoses/belts, check tires, brakes, guards, lights, kill switches, gas detectors and fire extinguishers, top up fluids and grease points, complete and sign the inspection checklist, tag out defects. Outdoor, weather-exposed, layout differs at every well.

Wellsite inspection and testing of pressure-containing equipment before and during the job: visual/wear inspection of treating iron, hammer unions, swivels, chiksans, high-pressure hoses and whip checks, valves and BOP; hammer-check and torque connections, replace worn seals/gaskets, function- and pressure-test the stack and lines to certification pressure, watch for leaks, record results.

Wellsite inspection and servicing of hoisting and rigging gear on the unit: sand line and drill line wire rope (broken wires, birdcaging, corrosion), blocks, sheaves, elevators, links, slings, hooks, guy lines and mast/derrick structure; lubricate rope and sheaves, adjust or cut-and-slip line, remove damaged rigging from service.

Scheduled preventive maintenance in the company yard or shop between jobs: grease all fittings on rig and pump, change engine oil and filters, service transmission/hydraulic fluid and air filters, service pump fluid ends and packing, replace worn belts, hoses and small parts, wash down the unit and complete PM records.

Shop or pipe-yard inspection and certification of downhole tubulars and tools for wear and cracks: tubing/drill pipe and fishing tool bodies checked for wall loss, pitting, cracks and thread damage using visual, EMI/ultrasonic and magnetic-particle methods, defects marked and the item accepted, downgraded or rejected with a written report.

tasks.label: Operate controls that raise derricks or level rigs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Standard rig-up of a mobile well-servicing/workover rig on a modern, operator-maintained multi-well pad: with the carrier spotted at the wellhead, the operator sets the hydraulic outriggers/jacks on the graded gravel surface, levels the carrier to the rig's level indicators, then works the mast-raising and telescoping controls to bring the double/triple mast upright and lock/pin it. Dry weather, cleared overhead envelope, access controlled by the producing company.

Rig-up at an older or remote single-well lease taken as found: soft, rutted, muddy, snowy or sloped ground; the operator must judge bearing capacity, have mats/cribbing placed under the jacks, level iteratively as jacks settle, re-check level after loading, and decide whether wind and footing permit raising the mast at all.

Rig-down at job completion: unpin/unlock the mast, telescope it down and lower it to the carrier under hydraulic control, retract outriggers and leveling jacks, and secure the unit for road travel - frequently at the end of a ..., in the dark or in bad weather.

Raising the mast/derrick and leveling an ancillary service unit (swabbing unit, small pulling unit, pump-down/slickline mast) on a congested multi-well pad, where the raising envelope must clear adjacent live wellheads, tank batteries, flowlines and other units, with the pad and its traffic controlled by the operating company.

Rig-up at a hazard-constrained location - urban, roadside or farm well site with overhead distribution lines, fences, trees and tight setback - where clearance to the energized lines governs where the unit can sit and whether/how far the mast can be raised, and the operator may have to reposition or raise at reduced height.

tasks.label: Listen to engines, rotary chains, or other equipment to detect faulty operations or unusual well conditions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-job and periodic equipment checks on the service unit and auxiliaries (diesel engine, transmission, hydraulic and triplex pumps, air compressor, generator) parked on a gravel lease pad or in the service company yard: the operator walks around the running equipment listening for knocking, misfire, bearing whine, gear noise, belt squeal, air/exhaust leaks, and reports faults for repair.

Live pumping job (cement, acid, frac, hot oil, nitrogen): operator monitors the running pump trucks by ear alongside gauges - listening for fluid-end/valve knock, cavitation, engine and transmission strain, changes in pitch - to catch a failing unit or abnormal pumping behavior while the job is underway on a temporary multi-truck pad, in high ambient noise.

Well-servicing (workover) rig at the controls while tripping rods or tubing: operator listens to the rig engine load, drawworks, chain drives and rotary equipment for lugging, chatter or unusual sounds that signal tight spots, stuck pipe, pump-off, or a parted rod string, and reacts in real time while operating the brake and throttle at a temporary lease site.

Fishing / stuck-pipe operations: fishing-tool technician listens to jars firing, engine and pump strain, and tool-string sounds to judge whether the fish is engaged or freed, with a one-off tool string and improvised rig-up at a site that differs job to job.

Service work at an institution-controlled facility - offshore platform, unmanned wellhead platform, gas processing plant or a developed pad with permanent production equipment: operator listens to installed engines, compressors, pumps and the service unit during routine rounds and during the job to detect faulty operation of the equipment.

tasks.label: Install pressure-control devices onto wellheads.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Land well-servicing/workover rig on a producing oil well: after killing the well and removing the tree, the crew nipples up a BOP stack (double ram and/or annular) on the tubing head — rig hoist lifts the stack, hands guide it, ring gasket set, studs/nuts installed and torqued, hydraulic/accumulator lines connected, function and pressure test to API standard. Outdoor lease, varied vintage wellheads, mud, wind, heat/cold.

Slickline/e-line job at a land well: rig up wireline pressure-control equipment onto the Christmas tree — tree adapter/quick test sub, wireline BOP, lubricator sections, grease injection head or stuffing box — lifted with a mast/crane truck, unions or flanges made up, then pressure tested before running tools. Site layout, tree height and configuration vary well to well.

Coiled tubing job: crane lifts and lands the CT pressure-control stack (quad BOP, shear/seal, stripper, injector head) onto the wellhead flange, alignment and stud-up on a heavy flanged connection, hydraulic control lines run to the CT control cab, function and pressure test. Multi-ton components, outdoor pad, live-well conditions.

Active multi-well frac pad, plug-and-perf: install/exchange frac tree components, wellhead isolation tool, greaseless/hydraulic frac valves and pump-down wireline pressure-control equipment (with remote hydraulic connectors) on the well being treated, tied into the zipper manifold; operator-controlled pad with red-zone protocols and standardized equipment.

Snubbing/hydraulic workover or high-pressure/H2S live well: install stripper rubbers, annular and ram-type pressure-control stack on a live wellhead with the well under pressure; extra torque, sealing and testing scrutiny, PPE and gas monitoring, often in remote or sour-service locations.

Offshore platform well bay (Gulf of Mexico): install wireline/coiled-tubing pressure-control equipment or a BOP on a tree in the well bay using the platform crane and fixed handling equipment; permanent deck layout, controlled access, standardized trees, but confined space and motion/weather exposure.

sources.title: Boltron Flange Bolting Robot | Total Marine Technology Products
sources.claim: Boltron is a commercially supplied autonomous flange bolting robot that tightens and loosens nuts on large industrial bolted flanges at refineries, power stations and processing plants; it performs the bolting step only, not the lifting, gasket setting, alignment or pressure testing of the joint.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making up bolted flange joints on pressure equipment, which is one sub-step of nipple-up. It does not transfer to the whole instance because it does not hoist, align or land the pressure-control device, set the ring gasket, connect control lines, or pressure test.

sources.title: Robo-Spider Automated Riser-Flange-Bolt Torque System | SLB
sources.claim: The Robo-Spider is a commercially deployed automated hydraulic torquing system that torques a marine drilling riser flange's bolts simultaneously on the rig floor; crews still position it and handle the riser joint.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: torquing the flange bolts of pressure-containing well equipment. Only the torquing step is automated; the joint is still assembled, aligned and gasketed by crew, so it does not substantiate completing a wellhead pressure-control installation.

sources.title: FlexRobotics® Hands-Free Rig Floor | H&P, Inc.
sources.claim: The most advanced deployed oilfield rig-floor robotics automate tubular handling (and doping/mud containment end effectors), not the installation of wellhead pressure-control equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous heavy-object handling and threaded make-up on a drill floor. It shows the state of the art in field oilfield robotics is limited to tubulars in a purpose-built handling envelope; no capability to nipple up BOPs or wireline pressure-control stacks is claimed.

sources.title: Automated Robotics Solutions for Oil & Gas - ANYbotics
sources.claim: Autonomous legged/tracked robots deployed at oil and gas production facilities perform inspection and monitoring rounds, not manipulation or installation of wellhead pressure-control hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous operation at oil and gas facilities. Capability is confined to inspection sensing; there is no heavy manipulation, bolting or equipment installation, so it cannot substantiate this task.

tasks.label: Operate pumps that circulate water, oil, or other fluids through wells to remove sand or other materials obstructing the free flow of oil.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Sand/fill cleanout on a mature conventional land oil well: a workover rig runs washpipe while the service unit operator lines up and runs a truck-mounted triplex pump, circulating produced water down the string at controlled rate/pressure, watching gauges and returns to the frac tank/pit, adjusting rate as fill is washed up, then shutting down and bleeding off. Rural lease, uneven ground, dust/mud/weather; treating lines are rigged up under a separate task.

Post-frac fill/plug-debris cleanout on a modern multi-well shale pad: coiled tubing unit run in hole while pump units circulate water/gel/nitrogen at programmed rates, returns routed through a separator/flowback tank; operator manages pump rate and pressure against CT depth and downhole conditions from digitally instrumented controls on a prepared, access-controlled pad.

Hot oil / hot water circulation on a producing land well to melt and flush paraffin or soft blockage from tubing and flowline: operator fires the truck's heater, circulates heated fluid down the annulus or tubing at controlled rate and temperature, monitors pressure and return temperature, then flushes and shuts down. Rural lease, cold-weather work.

Acid, solvent, or high-pressure flush treatment pumped by a pump/acid truck to break up scale, sand bridges, or near-wellbore plugging on a land well: blend chemical, pump at prescribed rate/pressure staying under fracture pressure, monitor for pressure spikes, displace and flush.

Circulating cleanout on an offshore platform or larger rig-based workover: fill washed out using rig or cement-unit pumps (or CT), fluid handled through fixed platform piping, pumping controlled and monitored from an instrumented unit/control room on a crewed, standard-layout installation.

sources.system: OCTIV Auto Frac (ZEUS electric fracturing platform)

sources.claim: Halliburton's Octiv Auto Frac service autonomously executes the pumping program on land frac fleets, making pumping decisions in real time in response to changing downhole conditions; commercially deployed with Coterra across Permian Basin completion programs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hydraulic fracturing pumping. Transfer: it is the same surface act rated here — machine-controlled positive-displacement pumps forcing fluid through the wellhead into the well at commanded rate and pressure, with closed-loop response to pressure/downhole feedback. Circulating water to wash out sand is a less demanding pumping program on the same class of equipment.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: pump-down of plug-and-perf toolstrings. Transfer: the machine circulates fluid down the wellbore at controlled rate/pressure while a conveyance string moves in the hole — the same coupled pump-rate/string-movement control problem as circulating fluid to lift sand while running or pulling washpipe or coiled tubing.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: offshore primary cementing. Transfer: the identical surface act — machine-actuated valve line-up, fluid mixing and pumping through the wellhead at controlled rate, density and pressure, plus automated wash-up — on a pumping unit of the same class used for well flushing and cleanout circulation.

sources.claim: SLB reports autonomous well intervention solutions deployed offshore Norway with Aker BP and StimWell, covering wireline, slickline and coiled tubing ..., including the first autonomous offshore wireline/slickline plug-setting workflows.

instances.label: Long move from the service company yard: operator drives a truck-mounted unit (workover/swab rig carrier, coiled tubing, cement/acid/pump truck) out of a yard in town, through city streets and 30-100 miles of public state and county highways, then onto a lease access road to a producing well; destination differs most days, dispatched same-day.

In-field move on private lease/caliche roads within an active development area: from a staging yard or the previous well to the next pad, through operator gates and mixed oilfield traffic, dust, unpaved gravel access roads, ending with the unit parked in position on the graded pad.

Ranch, farmland or backcountry well reached by narrow county roads and two-track lease trails: cattle guards, unmarked turns, soft/muddy spots after rain, no cell coverage; operator judges passability, opens gates, and picks a spot on a small unimproved location.

Night call-outs and adverse conditions: winter ice/snow in the Bakken, Rockies or Appalachia, rain-slick caliche and mud, high wind and blowing dust, long remote distances; the unit must still arrive in time to serve the well.

Oversize/heavy specialty move: relocating a masted workover rig carrier, large nitrogen or frac pump unit or heavy fishing-tool truck, sometimes with permits and pilot escorts, tight turns onto the location, and precise spotting of the unit relative to the wellhead, on rough or hilly access.

tasks.label: Thread cables through derrick pulleys, using hand tools.

instances.label: Stringing up the sandline/swab line on a mobile well-servicing (workover) rig at a producing well: after the mast is raised over the wellhead, the operator pulls line off the sand reel, climbs or is hoisted to the crown, threads the line over the crown sheave and down through the traveling block/sand line hanger, and secures the end with a clamp or socket using wrenches and hammer. Outdoor lease site, uneven gravel pad, wind/mud/heat, live wellhead nearby.

Re-reeving or replacing the worn hoisting (drilling) line on a service rig: a stringing/lead line is used to pull 1-inch class wire rope through 4-8 sheaves of the crown block and traveling block in the correct pattern, dead-end anchored and clamped with wire-rope clips torqued by hand tools, often in a slip-and-cut or full re-string at the wellsite or on location before the mast is raised.

Rigging up wireline/slickline at the wellhead: threading the small-diameter line off the unit drum through the ground-level hay pulley and the upper sheave hung in the derrick or on the lubricator, then through the stuffing box, closing loading gates and securing pins/shackles with hand tools, at a well pad with the unit spotted nearby.

Threading auxiliary lines through mast sheaves and pulleys during rig-up: tong counterweight lines, catline/winch lines, elevator or tubing-board lines, pull-down or guy lines routed over blocks and snatch blocks in the derrick and tied off with hand tools, on a well pad among trucks, tanks and pumping equipment.

Reeving/threading cables through blocks and sheaves in the company yard or maintenance shop during rig refurbishment or scheduled line change: mast laid down or blocks set on stands, tools and overhead crane available, controlled premises with a fixed layout.

It transfers only partially: the arms handle rigid tubulars presented at fixed positions on an engineered drill floor, and the cited coverage describes tripping, tailing, doping and stabbing — not threading flexible wire rope over crown sheaves at height or fastening clips with hand tools, so it does not substantiate completion of this task.

tasks.label: Close and seal wells no longer in use.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Permanent plug-and-abandonment of an old conventional/stripper oil or gas well on a rural lease: crew moves a pulling unit onto an unimproved dirt location, rigs up over a corroded wellhead, nipples down the tree and installs BOP, pulls sucker rods and tubing (frequently parted, stuck, or paraffin/scale-bound, requiring fishing), runs tubing to depth, sets bridge/cement plugs with a cementing contractor, tags plugs, cuts casing below grade with a backhoe and torch, welds a steel cap, and restores the site.

P&A of a modern horizontal shale well on an operator-controlled multi-well pad: graded gravel pad with standardized wellheads, workover rig plus wireline and cement units; pull production tubing/packer, set cast-iron bridge and cement plugs across perforations and casing shoes per state rule, pressure-test/tag barriers, then remove wellhead, cut casing below grade and weld cap.

Plugging an orphaned/legacy well under a state or federally funded (e.g., IIJA) program: well must be located and the wellhead excavated in a pasture, wooded lot, or residential yard; no reliable records, unknown casing condition, junk or debris in hole requiring clean-out or re-entry, then cement plugs, cut and cap, and surface reclamation.

Temporary abandonment / shutting in and securing a well no longer producing: close and lock the master valve, bleed down and disconnect flowlines and surface equipment, install a blind flange or bull plug on the wellhead, set a retrievable bridge plug or pump a shallow cement plug with a pulling unit, and tag/identify the well per regulation at a lease site of variable layout.

Offshore abandonment work on a Gulf of Mexico platform or subsea well: through-tubing or rigless P&A from a platform deck or intervention vessel, setting downhole barriers, cementing, then severing casing/conductor below mudline and removing the wellhead with ROV or mechanical cutting support.

tasks.label: Direct drilling crews performing activities such as assembling and connecting pipe, applying weights to drill pipes, or drilling around lodged obstacles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fishing job on a workover/drilling rig: the fishing-tool technician stands on the rig floor and tells the driller and floorhands how to make up and connect the fishing bottom-hole assembly (overshot, bumper sub, jars, drill pipe) — which tool goes on next, make-up torque, orientation — using voice, radio and hand signals over the rig-floor noise. The crew does the handling; the technician issues the instructions and confirms each step.

Directing the application of weight and pull during a fishing/jarring sequence: the technician watches the weight indicator and instructs the driller how much weight to slack off, how much overpull to take, how to stroke the jars, and when to stop — a running series of verbal calls to the driller in the doghouse or at the brake.

Directing milling or drilling around a lodged obstacle (junk mill, washover pipe, whipstock sidetrack): the technician calls out weight-on-bit, RPM, pump rate and circulating pressure targets to the driller and pump operator and tells them when to back off, ream or circulate, based on torque and pressure readings.

Pre-job briefing and procedure walkthrough with the rig crew, company man and toolpusher before the fishing/coiled-tubing run: explaining the sequence of operations, tool limits, pull and torque limits, and hazards, and assigning who does what.

Remote or degraded-conditions direction: coordinating with the crew by radio at night, in bad weather, or from the service unit/doghouse when the job deviates — the tool does not latch, pipe parts, or pressure spikes — and the technician must redirect the crew's next actions on the fly.

tasks.label: Apply green technologies or techniques, such as the use of coiled tubing, slim-hole drilling, horizontal drilling, hydraulic fracturing, or gas lift systems.

instances.label: Treatment execution on a multi-well shale completion pad: from the data van/treating controls, run a stage sequence — ramp rate and pressure, step proppant concentrations, watch for screenout, sequence the zipper manifold between wells, log the stage as pumped to design.

Frac spread hands-on work on the same pad: spot and hook up pumps/blender/hydration, make and torque high-pressure iron connections, pressure test the treating line, grease valves, walk the iron for leaks during pumping, isolate and swap a failed pump/fluid end mid-job, rig down and move.

Coiled tubing plug drill-out/mill-out on a horizontal shale well: crane-set injector head and stripper over the wellhead, stack pressure-control equipment, make up the BHA and motor/mill, run to the toe milling 40-60 composite plugs while managing weight-on-bit, motor stalls, returns and sand transport, then clean out and rig down.

Light conveyance intervention runs at a producing well: slickline/wireline or CT trips to install or retrieve gas lift valves in side-pocket mandrels, tag fill, correlate depth, set/pull plugs, nitrogen kickoff of the well — pressure control equipment rigged up on the wellhead, tools run in and out under depth and tension control.

Applying the gas lift system on producing wells across a field: adjusting injection gas rate and wellhead choke to unload and stabilize wells, tuning setpoints to maintain flowing bottomhole pressure, repeated visits/adjustments as well conditions change.

Well servicing on mature, scattered leases: workover rig or CT applied to convert a well to gas lift, re-enter or clean a slim-hole/older wellbore, or fish stuck tools/tubing — uneven ground, non-standard old wellheads, weather, one-off downhole problems requiring judgment.

tasks.label: Operate specialized equipment to remove obstructions by backing off or severing pipes by chemical or explosive action.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Land drilling rig, stuck drill pipe: operator rigs up an e-line unit at the rig floor, runs a free-point tool to find the stuck point, then makes up and arms a string shot (primacord) back-off assembly, runs it to the selected tool joint, coordinates left-hand torque and neutral weight with the driller, fires the shot, and the joint backs off so free pipe can be tripped out.

Land producing or injection well (workover rig or rigless): tubing or rods stuck by scale, sand or a parted string; operator rigs up wireline pressure control, loads a chemical cutter (corrosive charge) or jet/split-shot cutter, runs to the correlated depth, severs the tubing above the stuck point, and the cut is confirmed by pulling the free pipe.

Offshore platform or offshore drilling rig: pipe recovery in a deep, deviated or high-pressure well; tool string rigged up through lubricator/BOP with crane support, chemical cutter, jet cutter or radial cutting torch conveyed on e-line (sometimes with tractor), depth correlated on CCL, severance fired, tool recovered under pressure control.

Casing severance for plug-and-abandonment or casing recovery at a land well: explosive or chemical cutters run on wireline to cut casing strings (sometimes multiple concentric strings, sometimes below surface/mudline), followed by pull test and recovery of the severed section.

Remote legacy/stripper well, non-standard wellhead and no prepared pad, poor access road, work at night or in bad weather: sever stuck tubing or sucker rods with a chemical cutter or string shot from a truck-mounted wireline unit with minimal supporting equipment.

tasks.label: Perforate well casings or sidewalls of boreholes with explosive charges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Plug-and-perf stage on a horizontal shale well during zipper-frac operations on a multi-well pad: crew builds the gun string with a setting tool and frac plug, inserts the detonator/arms it, lifts and makes it up into the lubricator on the pressurized frac stack, pumps down on wireline to the toe-ward interval, correlates depth on CCL/GR, selectively fires 3-8 guns, pulls out, and safes out the string between stages, dozens of times per well.

Initial completion perforating of a new vertical or conventional cased well: wireline unit and mast/crane rigged over the wellhead, guns assembled and armed on location, run on e-line (gravity conveyed), gamma-ray/CCL depth correlation to the pay interval, fired, retrieved and inspected; performed on a prepared company location with a workover rig or crane assist.

Re-perforating/recompletion of an older producing well on a legacy lease: through-tubing or casing guns run with a workover rig at a small, muddy, variably laid-out wellsite in remote country; well conditions (scale, deviation, live pressure, unknown completion) are uncertain and often require re-runs or misfire handling.

Remedial casing perforation on a service job: shooting circulation holes or a casing/tubing punch for a squeeze cement job, casing repair, or pre-abandonment perforation, coordinated with pumping equipment on a workover location; small gun string, tight depth tolerance, live or killed well.

Fishing/stuck-pipe work with explosives: running a string shot, chemical or jet cutter on wireline inside the drill string or tubing at a rig site to back off or sever stuck pipe; torque applied at surface, depth of the free point determined on the fly, single shot placed under time pressure.

Offshore platform or workover-rig perforating: tubing-conveyed or wireline-conveyed guns handled on the rig deck through pressure-control equipment, run and fired in a live or overbalanced well, with long gun strings and strict RF/ballistic safety procedures.

sources.title: OCTIV® Auto Pumpdown™ service
sources.claim: Halliburton's commercially deployed OCTIV Auto Pumpdown service provides closed-loop automated control of the wireline winch and pumpdown pumps to convey perforating gun/plug toolstrings to depth; it automates conveyance only, not gun assembly, arming, rig-up, firing or retrieval handling.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (pumpdown plug-and-perf conveyance); cited to show the only field-proven automation covers tool conveyance, not the explosive handling and rig-up that make up the task.

sources.claim: A research 'self-locating perforating' system (DTPPMP) integrated into a perforating gun autonomously processed casing-collar signals downhole and fired at designated intervals in a field test in an actual oil well ...; surface handling, arming and deployment remain human work.

tasks.label: Examine unserviceable wells to determine actions to be taken to improve well conditions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Call-out to a rural land lease where a rod-pumped oil well has quit producing: operator drives to the location, walks the pad, checks the pumping unit, polished rod, stuffing box and wellhead, bleeds/reads casing and tubing pressure, shoots a fluid level and/or takes a dynamometer card, and decides whether the job is a rod job, pump change, tubing leak repair or paraffin/scale cleanout. Outdoor, weather- and terrain-exposed, gravel/caliche or grass lease, layout varies well to well.

On a workover with the service rig rigged up and the well killed: examine the well by pulling rods and tubing, inspecting the recovered string and downhole pump (parted or worn rods, rod-wear holes, corrosion, split couplings, scale, worn pump barrel/plunger), plus tag fill on bottom, to determine which joints/rods to replace and what remedial work the well needs. Muddy, congested rig site with equipment laid out ad hoc.

Fishing/obstruction diagnosis on a drilling or workover well: with the rig floor and tool string available, determine what is stuck and how it is oriented by running a gauge ring, lead impression block or camera, correlating tally, weights and torque history, examining recovered pieces, and selecting the fishing tool and approach. Occurs on a controlled rig site with standard rig equipment.

Diagnostic wireline/slickline/logging run on a producing land well with no rig on location: rig pressure control equipment onto the wellhead, run caliper, corrosion, cement-bond, production log or downhole camera, evaluate casing/tubing integrity, scale, leaks and fill, and determine the remediation (patch, squeeze, cleanout, recompletion). Wellsite pad, unit truck, outdoor conditions.

Examination of a shut-in or underperforming well on an offshore platform or a large institution-controlled gas facility: check wellhead and tree condition, annulus and tubing-head pressures, valve and gauge readings on the deck, correlate with diagnostic logging data, and determine the intervention required. Fixed layout, standard equipment, controlled access, housekeeping maintained.

Hard-case diagnosis on a remote marginal/stripper well with poor or missing records: overgrown lease road, aging surface equipment, unknown completion history, possible casing collapse or junk in the hole; operator must piece together the cause from surface symptoms, limited tag/swab tests and well history, and decide whether the well is worth repairing and how.

sources.transferJustification: Diagnostic logging/intervention runs are how a service crew physically examines a downhole problem; autonomous conveyance plus automated depth correlation and data acquisition covers the examination step of this task on the same wells and hardware.

sources.transferJustification: Establishes worker-equivalent quality and genuine autonomy for the machine that physically conveys diagnostic tools into a well during an examination.

sources.claim: SLB delivers end-to-end autonomous well integrity logging in which winch and data acquisition run autonomously and ML/AI are applied to the downhole data to evaluate well condition.
sources.transferJustification: Well integrity logging is the examination that determines whether casing/tubing corrosion, leaks or cement failure are the cause of an unserviceable well and what remediation is required.

sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs autonomous inspection rounds across a 40-acre midstream gas plant, including anomaly detection, thermal inspection, gauge reading and combustible gas detection.
sources.transferJustification: Reading pressure gauges and detecting leaks on production equipment is a component of examining a well's surface condition, but only in a controlled, standard-layout facility.

sources.title: Autonomous Methane Detection for Regulatory Compliance | Percepto
sources.claim: Percepto's drone-in-a-box systems fly autonomous inspection and optical-gas-imaging missions over US oil and gas well pads with no field presence required during day-to-day operations.
sources.transferJustification: Shows autonomous robotic surface surveying of unstructured land well pads, but limited to visual/thermal/gas imaging — it cannot make the hands-on measurements (fluid level, dynamometer, pressures) that a well examination requires.

sources.system: ARKK Goodwater automated tubing inspection facility; ARTIS 4 computerized inspection tool
sources.title: Arkk Tubing – Inspection Services
sources.claim: ARKK operates a fully automated tubing inspection ... with hydraulic conveyors and air rams handling the tubulars, plus computerized rig-floor tubing inspection while pipe is tripped out of the well, to identify defective joints.
sources.transferJustification: Grading production tubing and rods recovered from a workover to decide which joints are unserviceable is the determination this task produces for the tubing string; same objects (recovered OCTG) and same accept/reject output, with the pipe machine-fed rather than hand-inspected.

tasks.label: Monitor sound wave-generating or detecting mechanisms to determine well fluid levels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine acoustic fluid-level survey on scattered rural/marginal leases: operator drives lease roads to a rod-pumped stripper well, screws a portable gas gun onto the casing valve, charges it with nitrogen/CO2, fires the shot, records the echo on a laptop/chart, counts collars and reports fluid level and pump submergence. Wellheads, terrain, weather and access vary well to well.

Same routine fluid-level shot but on a modern operator-controlled multi-well pad (gravel pad, gated access, standardized wellheads and valve ports, several wells surveyed in one visit) as part of a scheduled optimization program.

Fluid-level shots in support of an active well-service job (service rig, swab unit or coiled tubing on location): shooting before/during/after swabbing, unloading or a treatment to track fluid recovery or kill-fluid level, with rig equipment and crews around the wellhead and a changing wellbore configuration.

Extended pressure buildup/drawdown surveillance: the acoustic instrument is left mounted on the wellhead and shots are repeated over hours or days while the operator monitors the recorded shots and the liquid-level/casing-pressure trend, then reports the buildup curve.

Wells equipped with remote-fire or permanently installed acoustic guns tied to a controller/SCADA: worker monitors incoming shot traces and fluid-level trends from a truck or control room, triggers extra shots remotely, uses results to set pump-off/pumping speed, and services the gun (gas charge, solenoid cleaning).

Problem wells: foamy or gassy annulus, high casing pressure requiring implosion shots, deep/deviated or noisy (compressor) wells where the echo is ambiguous; operator adjusts gun pressure and gains, repeats shots, may run a foam-depression test by venting casing gas, and interprets the chart by judgment.

sources.title: Automated Acoustic Well Sounder - Surface Solutions Inc
sources.claim: Commercial oilfield service in western Canada deploys an automated acoustic well sounder that is left on the well and takes liquid-level and casing-pressure measurements on a preset schedule with no operator present, delivering depth-to-liquid results to the cloud.

sources.system: Wellhead-mounted automated acoustic fluid level gun (SPE 93832)
sources.developer: S. Lieberman, American Energy Advisors, Inc.
sources.title: Automated Continuous Fluid Level Monitoring (SPE-93832-MS)
sources.claim: A wellhead-mounted, remote-operated acoustic fluid-level gun fires pressure waves into the casing up to ... and transmits liquid-level and casing-pressure data offsite, with the data automatically or manually analyzed and used to regulate pumping.

sources.title: Well Monitoring Systems | Summit ITC
sources.claim: A hazardous-area-certified acoustic fluid level instrument sold for well monitoring fires repeated shots automatically and determines fluid depth automatically, without an operator triggering or reading each shot.

sources.system: JAWS II Acoustic Fluid Level Instrument
sources.title: Acoustic Well Fluid Level Machine - JAWS 2
sources.claim: A current commercial acoustic fluid level machine offers an auto-fire mode with automatic fluid depth determination once connected to the wellhead.

sources.title: Echometer Model-M Digital Dual Channel Fluid Level Instrument Operating Manual
sources.claim: The Echometer Model M instrument, when set to AUTO gain, itself commands the solenoid Remote Fire Gas Gun to fire and records the echo without the operator pressing the fire button.

sources.title: Advanced Techniques for Acoustic Liquid-Level Determination
sources.claim: Interpretation of the acoustic record - locating the liquid-level echo and counting tubing collars to obtain acoustic velocity and depth - is normally performed automatically by the instrument software.

sources.system: Echometer wireless fluid level survey practice
sources.title: Echometer Fluid Level Surveys: How They Work | Downhole Diagnostic
sources.claim: Service providers running Echometer surveys state that a human must check the software's automatic identification of tubing-collar reflections because the computed depth depends on it; some wellbore conditions yield no interpretable acoustic data.

tasks.label: Insert detection instruments into wells with obstructions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Producing land well on a developed pad: crew spots the slickline/e-line truck, rigs up lubricator and pressure-control equipment on the wellhead, makes up a gauge cutter, multifinger caliper or downhole camera, and runs it in a live well to tag and characterize an obstruction (scale, wax, junk, collapsed tubing), then pulls out.

Land drilling rig with stuck pipe: e-line free-point indicator / string-shot tool is rigged up through the rig floor and run inside the drill string to locate the stuck point before back-off or fishing; done under rig-crew supervision, often at night and under time pressure.

Workover/fishing job at an older or remote lease: pulling unit on an uneven, muddy pad; run an impression block, junk-detection tool or camera on pipe or line into a well with unknown junk/debris, frequently repeating runs after hang-ups, with non-standard wellhead and improvised rig-up.

Highly deviated or horizontal well: detection instrument (caliper, camera, imaging tool) must be conveyed past restrictions on a wireline tractor or coiled tubing to reach the obstruction in the lateral, with tension/hold-up management throughout.

Offshore platform well: instrument run through the platform's lubricator/BOP stack from a permanently or temporarily installed wireline winch to locate an obstruction, under a controlled permit-to-work regime on a fixed-layout deck.

sources.system: SLB Neuro autonomous wireline/slickline conveyance and spooling
sources.developer: SLB (with Aker BP and StimWell Services, Intervention and Stimulation Alliance)
sources.title: Autonomous Well Intervention | SLB
sources.claim: SLB's autonomous well intervention solutions performed the first autonomous offshore wireline ... offshore Norway, with automated conveyance and spooling executing run-in-hole and pull-out-of-hole activities.
sources.transferJustification: Running a tool string into and out of a live well on wireline/slickline is the same physical act as inserting a detection instrument; the same winch, cable and pressure-control interface and the same tension/depth control are used.

sources.system: Autonomous wireline/slickline conveyance system (automation server in the wireline unit)
sources.title: Autonomous Slickline and Wireline Conveyance Improves Performance of Offshore Interventions | SPE Offshore Europe (OnePetro)
sources.claim: Autonomous wireline and slickline conveyance ... was implemented in the North Sea with more than 50 runs completed, enabling comparison against manual job execution.
sources.transferJustification: Peer-reviewed SPE documentation of the same conveyance operation used to place instruments and tools downhole; the run itself is the task's core physical act.

sources.system: SLB Neuro autonomous conveyance and spooling
sources.title: Investor Highlights Archive | SLB
sources.claim: SLB states the automatic conveyance and spooling ... runs without user intervention, matching experienced operators, and has been integrated into routine operations.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes worker-quality performance and limited intervention for the run-in/run-out act that constitutes inserting an instrument into a well.

sources.system: Autonomous well integrity logging (Neuro autonomous solutions)
sources.title: Autonomous Well Integrity Logging | SLB
sources.claim: In SLB's autonomous well integrity logging service the wireline winch and data acquisition run autonomously, with an ML autospooling system and a real-time tension model adjusting conveyance parameters.
sources.transferJustification: Well integrity logging runs slim inspection instruments (e.g., caliper/corrosion tools) on wireline into cased wells with restrictions - the same instrument sizes, conveyance and tension management as detection runs in obstructed wells.

sources.system: Coiled tubing autonomous conveyance (edge automation system)
sources.title: Coiled Tubing Autonomous Conveyance Improves Consistency of Offshore Intervention Operations (SPE-216196-MS) | SLB
sources.claim: SLB implemented autonomous coiled tubing conveyance in the North Sea, described as the first documented case of ..., with automatic reaction to anomalies while running.
sources.transferJustification: Coiled tubing is the standard conveyance for instruments in highly deviated/horizontal wells where gravity conveyance fails; autonomous CT conveyance covers the running of the detection instrument to depth.

sources.title: SLB Launches OnWave Autonomous Logging Platform | SLB
sources.claim: SLB's OnWave platform autonomously acquires downhole measurements without a wireline unit or cable, and was deployed in US and Middle East basins, including an Eagle Ford well where deployment and logging were described as fully autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Untethered conveyance and autonomous acquisition of downhole measurements in difficult wells is the same functional act as placing a detection instrument at depth, though for formation evaluation rather than obstruction identification.

sources.title: FlexRobotics Hands-Free Rig Floor | H&P, Inc.
sources.claim: H&P's FlexRobotics rig floor uses three NOV ATOM RTX six-axis robotic arms to automate drilling and tripping activities on US land rigs, removing personnel from the red zone.
sources.transferJustification: Where a detection instrument (impression block, camera sub) is conveyed on pipe, the conveyance is a pipe trip; robotic drill-floor arms already perform the make-up and tripping of standard tubulars in a machine-built well-center layout.
