roles.title: Excavating and Loading Machine and Dragline Operators, Surface Mining
roles.description: Operate or tend machinery at surface mining site, equipped with scoops, shovels, or buckets to excavate and load loose materials.

tasks.label: Move levers, depress foot pedals, and turn dials to operate power machinery, such as power shovels, stripping shovels, scraper loaders, or backhoes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Active pit bench at a surface mine (coal, iron, copper, phosphate): operator runs a large hydraulic shovel/excavator or production front-end loader, cycling continuously for a 10-12 hour shift filling haul trucks with blasted rock or overburden - spotting trucks, judging bucket fill and pass counts, working the muck pile face, cleaning the floor, handling oversize and wet/sticky material.

Aggregate quarry or sand-and-gravel pit: operator uses a wheel loader or excavator to dig from the working bank and stockpiles and load haul trucks, plant feed hoppers and customer highway trucks in a company-controlled load-out area; also blends and rebuilds stockpiles and loads to order.

Ancillary earthmoving with a backhoe/excavator around the mine or pit: cutting drainage ditches and sumps, trenching for pipe and utilities, building and repairing access roads and benches, cleanup, and reclamation grading - variable ground, buried services, no fixed layout.

Surface coal mine dragline stripping overburden: operator works the dig-hoist-swing-dump-return cycle for hours, positions spoil piles, keeps pit geometry, and periodically walks the machine to a new position.

Degraded and congested conditions at the pit: night shift under lights, rain, mud, dust or cold; loading within meters of ground crews, pickups, drills and the highwall; frequent repositioning, unstable footing, oversize rock and blocked buckets.

Fixed plant area of the pit/quarry: loader reclaims from a stockpile on a short fixed cycle to feed a crusher or screen hopper, and cleans up spillage under conveyors, in a surfaced, institution-controlled plant yard.

sources.developer: Baidu Research Robotics and Auto-Driving Lab / University of Maryland
sources.title: Baidu Research Robotics and Auto-Driving Lab present autonomous excavator concept - International Mining
sources.claim: Baidu Research/UMD's Autonomous Excavator System performed material loading (digging and loading trucks/hoppers) autonomously for 24 hours in a real outdoor waste-disposal site, at productivity close to an experienced operator.

sources.title: Sandvik AutoMine Autoload 2.0 eliminates operator intervention in LHD drawpoint loading - International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 is a commercial product that lets LHD loaders run fully automated production loading cycles - filling the bucket from a blasted muckpile at a drawpoint and dumping at a dump point - without operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bucket loading of loose blasted rock by a mining loader. It is the same physical act as this surface excavating/loading task - fill a bucket from a fragmented pile, tram/swing, discharge into a truck or dump point - with comparable machine class, material and precision; it differs only in that the mine workings are institution-controlled and geometrically fixed.

sources.system: Sandvik AutoMine / AutoLoad 2.0 at George Fisher Mine
sources.title: George Fisher Mine leads the way in underground automation - Glencore Australia
sources.claim: Glencore's George Fisher mine runs a fleet of Sandvik automated loaders and trucks; with AutoLoad 2.0 loaders and trucks complete loading and tramming cycles without human intervention, and traffic control lets multiple loaders work close together.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production loading of blasted rock into haul trucks in a mine at commercial production rates around the clock; the bucket-filling, spotting and discharge motions transfer directly to surface shovel/loader truck-loading.

sources.claim: Develon's Real-X autonomous crawler excavator (DX225LC-7X, with Gravis Robotics AI control) is in first commercial use at a former KIBAG quarry ... Switzerland, digging a 300 m trench with no operator in the ....

sources.title: Real-X excavator marks major step towards autonomous construction - Materials Handling World News
sources.claim: At the Swiss quarry handover the Develon Real-X excavator dug with no operator in the ... without remote control, confirming autonomous rather than teleoperated excavation.

sources.claim: Gravis Robotics' autonomy platform is deployed on infrastructure and materials projects in seven countries, including a 60-mile pipeline job where multiple 36-tonne excavators autonomously dig trenches in compacted, heterogeneous soil and shallow bedrock.

sources.title: Video: Gravis Robotics unveils earthmoving autonomy platform - Equipment World
sources.claim: Gravis Robotics demonstrated autonomous truck loading with a ... and autonomous trenching with a Hitachi electric excavator in live demonstrations at Bauma 2025.

sources.title: Autonomous Operation of Excavators - DeepX
sources.claim: DeepX, Fujita and Japan's Public Works Research Institute demonstrated a hydraulic excavator autonomously running the complete excavate-and-load-a-dump-truck cycle continuously at a dedicated test field.

sources.system: Shitoumei No.1 open-pit mine automation (autonomous trucks plus remote-operated excavators)
sources.developer: Chinese autonomous mining vendors / mine operator
sources.title: Xinjiang mine deploys autonomous trucks for safer coal transport and workforce reduction - Global Times
sources.claim: At one of China's most automated open-pit coal mines (91 autonomous haul trucks), the excavators and dozer are retrofitted for remote operation rather than autonomy - loading units at surface mines remain human- or teleoperator-driven.

sources.system: CSIRO/QCAT dragline automation (swing cruise control, DTM)
sources.title: Dragline Automation - Robotics, CSIRO Research
sources.claim: CSIRO's long-running dragline automation work has produced operator-assist technologies (swing cruise control, digital terrain mapping) demonstrated on a scale-model dragline; no full autonomous dig-swing-dump production dragline is cited.

tasks.label: Set up or inspect equipment prior to operation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily pre-shift inspection of a hydraulic excavator or wheel loader parked on the mine's graded service/parking pad: walkaround for hydraulic leaks, damaged hoses, cracked welds, tire or track condition and bucket/teeth wear; check engine oil, coolant and hydraulic levels via dipstick and sight glasses; check lights, mirrors, fire extinguisher, seat belt, guards; then in-cab tests of horn, back-up alarm, brakes, steering and controls; record defects on the pre-op checklist and report or tag out.

The same required pre-shift inspection performed where the machine shut down at the pit face or bench: standing on loose muck, rock and mud, in wind, dust, rain or pre-dawn darkness, climbing the machine's steps and catwalks to reach the upper deck, fuel and fluid fills, and cab.

Pre-operational inspection of a large electric rope shovel or dragline: climbing multiple decks and stairways, checking hoist/drag ropes and rigging, dipper and tooth/adapter wear, automatic lube reservoirs and grease lines, trailing power cable and connections, walking/propel mechanism, air and electrical systems, and the machinery house.

Physical set-up/fit-out before operating: swapping the bucket or attachment on a quick coupler, replacing worn teeth, adapters and pins with hammer or hydraulic tool, fitting a cutting edge, adjusting track tension, and adjusting mirrors, cameras and seat for the shift.

Setting the machine up for the dig: tramming the excavator/loader into position at the face or stockpile, levelling and stabilising it on a prepared pad, establishing the loading/truck-spotting geometry, configuring and taring the onboard payload-weighing and machine-guidance system, and cycling the hydraulics to warm up before production.

Small sand-and-gravel pit or quarry: operator inspects an older wheel loader, backhoe or small excavator in an open unpaved yard before the shift, checking fluids, greasing pins, checking tires, hydraulic lines and brakes, often doubling as the person who fixes minor items found.

sources.title: Spot at Mariana Minerals | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped is deployed at a US copper mine to run routine inspection rounds autonomously, but the work is sensor-based data capture on fixed plant assets along walked routes, not pre-operational checks of mobile earthmoving machines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous industrial inspection rounds at a mine. It shows a legged robot can traverse a mine plant and collect visual/thermal/acoustic data, but it does not open service doors, read dipsticks, grease, or perform in-cab functional tests, so it covers only part of an equipment pre-operational inspection.

sources.developer: Tessellate Robotics (with Minerai de fer Québec, MISA Vortex program)
sources.title: Automated Haul Truck Inspection by Tessellate Robotics | Groupe MISA
sources.claim: A mobile robot is being developed and field-tested to inspect mining haul trucks autonomously during refuelling, running a predefined route and producing a maintenance report from visual, thermal and 3D data; it covers external surfaces (notably tires and underbody) only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated pre-operational inspection of mining mobile equipment. Same object class (large mining machines) and same purpose, but the routine is limited to external imaging; fluid-level checks, service-door opening and cab function tests remain manual, and the system is still in prototype/field-validation phases.

sources.title: SCOTT making ROBOFUEL™ refuelling system progress with AHS mining truck fleets - International Mining
sources.claim: A robotic arm autonomously refuels mining haul trucks at a purpose-built station on a mine site; an installation in the Pilbara has been in production since late 2019, showing robots can manipulate a single standardized fitting on a heavy mining machine that presents itself at a fixed station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic pre-shift servicing of mining equipment. It demonstrates vision-guided manipulation on a haul truck at a fixed bay (opening a fuel door, connecting a hose), but it is a single scripted fitting interaction, far short of the multi-point inspection and setup a machine operator performs.

sources.title: Donecle Raises €10 Million to Expand Drone-Based Aircraft Inspection Platform
sources.claim: Autonomous drones perform exterior visual inspection of large machines (aircraft) inside maintenance hangars for airlines and MROs, replacing part of manual visual inspection with AI-analysed imagery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated exterior condition inspection of a large machine before it is returned to service, in an institution-controlled hangar (E2). It substantiates only the visual-surface portion of a walkaround; it cannot check fluid levels, actuate controls, or judge and correct defects.

sources.title: Built Robotics Launches Piling Robot to Accelerate Solar Energy Transition
sources.claim: A fully autonomous heavy construction machine surveys, positions itself at each work location, and performs the work on an as-found outdoor construction site, with first customer deployments from late 2023.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heavy machine self-positioning and self-setup at the work location outdoors. This maps to the machine-positioning/configuration element of setting up an excavator before digging (comparable machine class, comparable siting accuracy, unstructured outdoor site); it does not cover walkaround inspection or attachment changes.

sources.system: Pit Viper (Rig Control System / autonomous drilling)
sources.title: Epiroc's drill rig Pit Viper celebrates 25 years including a decade with autonomous operations - Canadian Mining Journal
sources.claim: Large surface blasthole drill rigs have operated autonomously at open-pit mines for a decade, including auto-levelling, tramming hole-to-hole and rod handling, i.e. the machine sets itself up on the bench before and between drilling cycles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous setup of a mining machine on the pit bench prior to operation (levelling, positioning over the hole, deploying jacks, handling drill string). Same environment (surface mine bench) and same machine class as an excavator setup, supporting the positioning/configuration instance only.

tasks.label: Become familiar with digging plans, machine capabilities and limitations, and efficient and safe digging procedures in a given application.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Observe hand signals, grade stakes, or other markings when operating machines so that work can be performed to specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Production loading at the digging face of an active pit or quarry: a hydraulic excavator/shovel or front-end loader digs blasted rock, coal, sand or gravel and loads haul trucks, keeping to the dig plan and marked ore/waste or blast limits, watching truck-driver spotting and stop/go hand signals, in dust, rough footing and changing muckpile geometry.

Cutting and trimming to a specified grade: bench floors, ramps, sumps, drainage ditches, pads and trenches worked to grade stakes, laser or a GPS/3D design model, with depth and slope checked against survey marks so the finished surface meets spec.

Plant-yard work: wheel loader feeding the crusher hopper and loading customer/highway trucks from stockpiles on maintained pads in the fixed plant area, following painted markings, stockpile signage and hand signals from truck drivers and plant staff.

Close-quarters work directed by a person on the ground: a spotter or flagger hand-signals the bucket in near buried utilities, pipe/culvert setting, structures, the highwall toe or crews working beside the machine; dig limits shown by paint, flags or ribbon; stop signals must be obeyed instantly.

Reclamation and off-pit support earthwork in unstructured ground: regrading spoil and overburden, backfilling and shaping to survey stakes and flagging, berm building and haul-road repair, sometimes adjacent to public roads or property lines.

sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem converts standard hydraulic excavators into fully autonomous machines that dig trenches to a specified depth using RTK GPS, holding depth tolerances of about 1/10 of a foot — i.e., producing work to a surveyed specification without an operator reading stakes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous trenching/grading on outdoor earthmoving sites. It substantiates the specification-conformance core of this task (digging to a designed elevation and line, checked by RTK GPS rather than stakes) with the same class of machine (mid-size hydraulic excavator) and the same soils/terrain.

sources.system: Built Robotics Exosystem / autonomous pile driver
sources.title: Blattner Picks Autonomous Pile Drivers from Built Robotics for Solar Projects
sources.claim: Built Robotics' autonomous excavator packages are in commercial field use with a national contractor (Blattner) on utility-scale solar construction sites, with the developer describing an ongoing fourth project under a nationwide deal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous excavator trenching and pile installation to surveyed plan positions on greenfield sites. Transfers because the machine, the outdoor unstructured ground, and the requirement to hit surveyed positions/depths match the grade-and-marking conformance required here.

sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Leads Major Autonomous Excavation Push
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics' autonomy kit ran 20-80 ton excavators that autonomously dug and loaded human-driven articulated dump trucks on a live 130-acre site-preparation job in Phoenix, moving more than 65,000 cubic ... using the same workflow as manual ..., under remote/human supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mass excavation and truck loading on an unstructured earthmoving site. Same machine class, same loose material, and the same requirement to dig to the design surface and coordinate with human truck drivers as at a surface-mine face.

sources.developer: Develon (HD Hyundai XiteSolution) with Gravis Robotics; operated by KIBAG
sources.title: Develon puts autonomous excavator to work in Switzerland
sources.claim: A Develon DX225LC-7X fitted with the Real-X system (developed with Gravis ...) works autonomously with no operator in the ..., excavating a specified 300 m x 6 m x 3 m trench as part of restoring the site, supervised by a technician rather than teleoperated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous excavation of a dimensioned trench and quarry-restoration earthwork. It is the same machine and the same requirement to hold specified dimensions/elevations, performed in a quarry rather than a laboratory or fenced cell.

sources.title: Sandvik introduces AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 for improved autonomous bucket loading
sources.claim: Sandvik's AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 lets underground loaders complete full production loading cycles — approaching the muckpile, filling the bucket and dumping at a defined dump point — without operator intervention once loading profiles are set, in access-restricted automation areas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous bucket loading of loose blasted rock and discharge at a designated point, with material presented at fixed drawpoints and people excluded from the automation area — the purpose-built-setting analogue of loading to a designated target without a ground signaller.

sources.developer: Baidu Research Robotics and Auto-Driving Lab / University of Maryland
sources.title: Autonomous excavators ready for around the clock real-world deployment (EurekAlert)
sources.claim: Baidu Research and the University ... Maryland's Autonomous Excavator System performed material loading with no human intervention for more than 24 hours continuously in real-world outdoor scenarios, with performance reported as close to an experienced operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: uncrewed excavator material loading in unstructured terrain, i.e., the dig-and-load cycle of this occupation performed autonomously with irregular loose material.

sources.title: Built Robotics raises another $64M to make construction equipment autonomous (TechCrunch)
sources.claim: Built Robotics' autonomous excavators operate unmanned on live jobsites behind a layered safety system — geofence shutdown, wireless and hardwired e-stops, and computer vision that scans continuously for people and obstacles — rather than by taking direction from a ground signaller.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (autonomous excavation on live sites); cited to show how deployed systems handle people on site — exclusion and stopping — which is not equivalent to taking productive direction from a spotter's hand signals.

tasks.label: Operate machinery to perform activities such as backfilling excavations, vibrating or breaking rock or concrete, or making winter roads.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bulk backfilling/regrading of mined-out ground at an active surface mine: pushing and placing overburden/spoil back into the cut, building the reclamation surface to plan with a large dozer, loader or excavator on an open bench; mine-controlled premises, engineered benches and dumps, changing but surveyed terrain, production shifts around the clock.

Backfilling a narrow or confined excavation on the property: pipe/cable trench, culvert, sump or equipment-foundation hole. Operator pushes/places spoil back around buried services and pipe, works in lifts with a compaction wheel or vibratory plate, with ground crew, spotters and surveyed stakes close to the bucket.

Breaking oversize rock in the pit with a hydraulic hammer on an excavator: hammering boulders on the muck pile or bench, breaking a hard ledge or a toe left after the blast, tracking over broken uneven ground and repositioning between rocks.

Breaking oversize at a fixed breaking station: hammering rocks bridging the grizzly over the ROM hopper or the primary crusher dump pocket to keep the feed running; material is delivered to the station by haul trucks or a feeder.

Breaking out concrete with a hammer attachment: old machine foundations, conveyor footings, slabs, walls or a frozen/concreted pad at the plant or a small demolition job; rebar, rubble and debris to break down and clear.

Making and maintaining winter roads: plowing, packing and grading snow on access and haul routes, building a snow/ice road over unimproved ground to reach a remote pit or drill site in northern operations.

sources.system: Cat MineStar Command for dozing (semi-autonomous tractor system, SATS)
sources.title: Command for Dozing | Cat | Caterpillar
sources.claim: Cat MineStar Command for dozing is a commercial mining product whose semi-autonomous mode lets one operator manage several large dozers doing production dozing/spoil work.
sources.transferJustification: Dozing spoil into a cut and regrading it is the machine action of backfilling a mined-out excavation: same material, same machines, same grade tolerances as the task's backfill instances.

sources.system: Cat MineStar Command for dozing SATS at Lake Vermont mine
sources.title: Big names in mining team up to demonstrate remote semi-autonomous dozer technology
sources.claim: Six Cat D11 dozers run under SATS semi-autonomy at Thiess's Lake Vermont open-cut mine, moving 8.2 million bank cubic metres with operators controlling multiple dozers off-site; Thiess describes autonomous mining and rehabilitation (reclamation) as its service offering.
sources.transferJustification: Open-cut spoil dozing and mine rehabilitation is backfilling/regrading of excavated ground - the same work, machines and site type as the bulk backfill instance.

sources.system: A4CSEL (automated bulldozers, vibratory rollers, dump trucks)
sources.date: 2020-2024 (Naruse Dam placement from May 2020; earthworks application FY2024)
sources.title: A⁴CSEL for DAM | Technology & Services | KAJIMA CORPORATION
sources.claim: Kajima's A4CSEL system ran more than ten automated dump trucks, bulldozers and vibratory rollers around the clock placing and compacting the CSG embankment of Naruse Dam, supervised by three 'IT pilots' in a control room 400 km away; from FY2024 it is applied to land-development earthworks.
sources.transferJustification: Placing fill in lifts with an automated dozer and compacting it with an automated vibrating roller is the same physical operation as backfilling an excavation and vibrating/compacting it: bulk earth/aggregate, same machines, similar grade and density acceptance.

sources.title: Normet Xrock Launches the World's First Autonomous Rock-Breaking System, Xrock Autobreaker
sources.claim: Normet Xrock's Autobreaker autonomously identifies, targets and breaks oversized ... at a grizzly/crusher station using camera vision and sensor fusion, planning strike positions and executing breaking sequences with only remote supervision; commercially available starting with grizzly ....
sources.transferJustification: Launched for underground crusher/grizzly stations, but a surface mine's ROM-hopper grizzly and breaker boom are the same installation and the same job - hammering oversize rock so the feed keeps running.

sources.title: Freeport rolls out world-first autonomous rockbreaker fleet at Grasberg - MINING.COM
sources.claim: PT Freeport Indonesia deployed a fleet of mobile rockbreakers billed as fully autonomous at Grasberg using RCT ControlMaster Guidance, with operators managing the ancillary fleet from remote automation centres; the autonomy of the breaking cycle itself (versus autonomous tramming with remote breaking) is not established in the sources.
sources.transferJustification: Breaking oversize at drawpoints with a mobile rockbreaker is close to hammering oversize on a muck pile, but autonomy of the breaking action is unclear so it is used only as context.

sources.developer: Yeti Move (Semcon, Øveraasen, Husqvarna) for Avinor
sources.title: Yeti – world's first autonomous snowploughs at airports | Semcon
sources.claim: Autonomous snowploughs operating in formation cleared snow at Norwegian airports for operator Avinor, navigating by RTK GPS on digitally planned clearing patterns with several vehicles monitored by one control system.
sources.transferJustification: Clearing and packing snow on defined routes at an institution-controlled facility is the maintenance half of making winter roads; the plough hardware and the snow are the same, the routes are pre-planned in both cases.

sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem performs autonomous trenching commercially on greenfield construction sites, but the product hands spoil to human backfill and compaction crews rather than backfilling itself.
sources.transferJustification: Closest commercial autonomous excavator on unstructured sites; cited to show that autonomous trench backfill around pipe and crews is not offered, supporting the negative judgment at E2/E3 for confined backfill.

sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Announces Supervised Autonomy Testing on Active Construction Sites in Move Towards Commercialization
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics is running supervised-autonomy mass excavation on live construction sites, moving 65,000+ cubic yards loading human-operated trucks, but is only targeting its first operator-less deployments in 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Mass excavation and truck loading on an as-found site is adjacent earthmoving work; cited as context on the state of unstructured-site autonomy, not relied on for a positive judgment because supervision level is not established.

tasks.label: Receive written or oral instructions regarding material movement or excavation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Move materials over short distances, such as around a construction site, factory, or warehouse.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wheel loader load-and-carry at a quarry or sand-and-gravel pit: scoop from a muck pile or product stockpile, tram 20-100 m over rutted, dusty ground, and dump into a crusher hopper, feed bin, or waiting truck; repeated cycles all shift alongside other machines.

Hydraulic excavator or shovel at the pit face: load haul trucks and shift overburden, spoil, or blasted rock short distances to an adjacent dump, ramp, or rehandle pile; variable bench conditions, spotters and trucks moving nearby.

Loader, excavator, or skid steer moving loose material (aggregate, backfill, spoil, rubble, trench arisings) around an active construction site: layout changes daily, other trades and pedestrians present, mud, buried utilities, temporary stockpiles.

Material moving around the fixed processing plant and maintenance yard: rehandling product stockpiles, cleaning up conveyor spillage in tight areas near structures, and shifting supplies (pallets, parts, blocks, pipe) with bucket or forks near ground personnel.

Moving materials inside a factory or warehouse and its yard: transporting pallets, bulk bags, bins, or finished product short distances between docks, staging lanes, and storage on a flat paved floor or yard.

sources.system: Aramac L140B loader with sensmore automation
sources.title: Cemex and sensmore showcase digital and automated quarry at Rüdersdorf - International Mining
sources.claim: An Aramine L140B loader automated by sensmore runs autonomous load-haul-dump cycles in production at Cemex's Rüdersdorf limestone quarry, loading loose muck, tramming, and dumping onto a conveyor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is mine mucking: the same bucket-machine load-carry-dump cycle over tens of metres with loose fragmented rock, the core of moving materials short distances at a mining or plant site.

sources.title: Sandvik introduces AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 for improved autonomous bucket loading - Mining Weekly
sources.claim: Sandvik's AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 enables fully automated loader production cycles, including automated bucket filling, in commercial mines; AutoMine loading systems have been supplied since 2004 with roughly 800 automated units.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is drawpoint mucking with an LHD: identical bucket fill, short tram, and dump sequence with loose rock, transferring to loader material moving at a pit or plant.

sources.developer: Baidu Research Robotics and Auto-Driving Lab / University of Maryland
sources.title: Autonomous excavators ready for around the clock real-world application
sources.claim: The Autonomous Excavator System performed material loading tasks (digging and loading loose material into trucks) at a real waste-disposal site for over 24 hours continuously without human intervention, at productivity near an experienced operator.

sources.system: Built Robotics Exosystem / Autonomous Track Loader
sources.title: Built Robotics releases 1st fully autonomous construction machinery in US - Construction Dive
sources.claim: Built Robotics' software lets excavators and track loaders perform earthmoving tasks fully autonomously with remote supervision rather than an operator in the cab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous trenching/grading with an excavator or track loader: the same machine class digging and relocating loose spoil over short distances on an as-found jobsite.

sources.title: Built Robotics raises $64 million for robotic excavator Exosystem - Equipment World
sources.claim: Excavators fitted with Built Robotics' autonomy kit have been working on large solar-farm construction sites, including a 1.1-gigawatt project.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous excavation/trenching on live construction sites; it establishes that this machine class operates unattended in the unstructured jobsite setting where short-distance material moving occurs.

sources.system: Bedrock Operator autonomy kit on excavators
sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Moves Earth with Autonomous Excavators - Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics ran supervised-autonomy excavators (20-80 t) doing repetitive truck loading and mass excavation on a live 130-acre heavy-civil site with Sundt Construction, moving over 65,000 cubic yards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous mass excavation and truck loading; it uses the same bucket machines handling loose material on an as-found construction site, with a supervising operator rather than continuous control.

sources.title: Walmart to deploy Fox Robotics autonomous forklifts across four distribution centers - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Walmart deployed 19 FoxBot autonomous forklifts across ... a 16-month proof of concept; about 110 FoxBots were installed at roughly 55 US warehouses and distribution centers, including cold storage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous trailer unloading and pallet transport inside distribution centers: the same short-distance movement of palletized material between dock, staging, and storage that a warehouse material-moving instance requires.

sources.title: How Fox Robotics went from scrappy startup to making self-driving forklifts for Walmart - Modern Retail
sources.claim: About 110 FoxBot autonomous forklifts were installed across roughly 55 US warehouses and distribution centers spanning retail, CPG, logistics, and food and beverage customers.

sources.system: Pronto AHS on Komatsu HD605 / Cat haul trucks
sources.title: Caterpillar, Komatsu Autonomous Dump Trucks Successfully Complete Trial at Texas Quarry
sources.claim: Pronto's autonomous haulage system operates retrofitted Caterpillar and Komatsu haul trucks driverlessly at Heidelberg Materials' Lake Bridgeport limestone quarry, completing loading and dumping cycles; the mixed fleet moved over 2 million tons.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is driverless quarry haulage: it establishes that machines move bulk material between loading and dumping points on live quarry premises with people and other equipment present.

sources.system: Huaneng Ruichi autonomous electric mining trucks
sources.title: China launches world's first fleet of driverless mining trucks - People's Daily Online
sources.claim: China Huaneng commissioned a fleet of 100 driverless electric mining trucks hauling stripped soil and rock to the dumping site at the Yimin open-pit coal mine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is surface-mine haulage of excavated material; it shows unmanned machines moving bulk material across an active open-pit mine kept to the operator's working standard.

sources.system: Volvo FH autonomous trucks (V.A.S. virtual driver)
sources.title: Volvo Autonomous Solutions removes safety driver at Brönnöy Kalk - Volvo Group
sources.claim: Volvo Autonomous Solutions removed the safety driver from its autonomous FH trucks hauling limestone from pit to crusher at the Brønnøy Kalk mine, an active commercial operation that has since hauled over one million tonnes autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous mine-site material transport, establishing driverless bulk material movement on institution-controlled mining premises in harsh conditions.

tasks.label: Create or maintain inclines or ramps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large open-pit coal/metal mine: excavator or front shovel (with a support dozer) cuts a new haul-road ramp or bench access ramp into blasted rock/overburden, working to a surveyed design grade, width and switchback alignment, leaving safety berms, while haul trucks and light vehicles move nearby and highwall stability must be respected.

Routine maintenance of an existing pit ramp/incline at a mine or large quarry: pushing spilled and sloughed material back, filling ruts, potholes and washouts after rain, re-shaping the running surface, crown and berms with a loader, excavator or dozer, in short repeated interventions between haul cycles with traffic present.

Aggregate/sand-and-gravel quarry: loader or excavator builds and keeps open a working ramp down to a lower bench or a ramp up to a stockpile/crusher feed, judged largely by operator eye rather than a survey design, single machine, plant and customer truck traffic on site.

Overburden dump, spoil pile or reclamation area: dozer/excavator builds access ramps up onto the dump and shapes dump-platform slopes, counter-slopes and perimeter safety berms in loose spoil, dusty repetitive work in a designated dumping zone.

Site development / remote work by the same operators: cutting an access ramp or incline at a new pit development, borrow pit, reclamation cut or after storm damage, on ground taken as found, no fences or fixed layout, mixed soils, boulders, weather and other trades or landowners around.

sources.title: World's First AI-Powered Electric Unmanned Bulldozer Commences Operations
sources.claim: Shantui's DE26-X3 AI-powered electric unmanned bulldozer was deployed at a large open-pit ... entered routine operations, accumulating over 160 hours of operation with commands issued from a remote control room.
sources.transferJustification: Mine spoil-yard dozing is the same machine class and the same terrain-shaping-to-a-specified-geometry work as building and maintaining ramps, performed on the same kind of premises (an active surface mine).

sources.title: World's First AI-Powered Electric Unmanned Bulldozer Commences Operations
sources.claim: The DE26-X3 autonomously performs slope construction, safety-berm/retaining wall building and spoil disposal inside designated mine work zones, perceiving trucks, personnel and berms with LiDAR and cameras.
sources.transferJustification: Building counter-slopes and berms on a mine dump is the closest deployed analogue to creating and maintaining inclines/ramps: loose material shaped to a preset grade by a tracked dozer on mine premises.

sources.system: A4CSEL automated construction system (automated bulldozers, rollers, dump trucks)
sources.title: A⁴CSEL for DAM | Technology & Services | KAJIMA CORPORATION
sources.claim: Kajima's A4CSEL system runs automated bulldozers, vibratory rollers and dump trucks on real dam construction sites, with more than ten automated machines placing and leveling the Naruse Dam CSG embankment around the clock.
sources.transferJustification: Constructing an embankment — automated trucks delivering fill, automated dozers leveling it to a designed layer geometry, rollers compacting — is the same operation as building a fill ramp/incline to a designed grade, at comparable scale and precision.

sources.title: A⁴CSEL for Earthworks | Technology & Services | KAJIMA CORPORATION
sources.claim: Kajima states the automated leveling (bulldozer) and compaction (roller) technologies proven on dams are applied to land-development earthworks, with A4CSEL applied to land-development construction sites in fiscal 2024.
sources.transferJustification: Land-development earthworks (cut, fill, level to design) covers the grading operations by which ramps and inclines are formed and maintained, using the same machines.

sources.system: Built Robotics Exosystem / autonomous equipment platform
sources.title: Built Robotics releases 1st fully autonomous construction machinery in US | Construction Dive
sources.claim: Built Robotics commercially released autonomy software letting excavators, dozers and track loaders perform earthmoving tasks fully autonomously, including trenching, foundation excavation and grading building pads, with remote operators supervising.
sources.transferJustification: Grading a pad or digging to a GPS design line is cut/fill earthmoving to a designed surface with the same excavator/loader class used to cut and dress a ramp.

sources.title: Exosystem | Robots in Construction
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem excavators execute the dig-and-grade cycle autonomously against pre-loaded GPS design lines on solar construction projects, monitored by a single remote equipment operator, with reported 93% machine uptime.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous excavation to a digital design with in-ground grade checking on outdoor greenfield sites is the nearest commercial capability to cutting a ramp to design grade, though demonstrated for trenching rather than bulk ramp cut/fill.

sources.system: HEAP (Hydraulic Excavator for an Autonomous Purpose), Menzi Muck M545
sources.developer: ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab / Gramazio Kohler Research
sources.title: Autonomous Excavator Builds Retaining Wall | Vision Systems Design
sources.claim: ETH Zurich's HEAP autonomous walking excavator excavated and shaped a digitally planned landscape — digging soil and redepositing it to form terraces — and built a 6 m dry-stone wall, on a real outdoor site with contractor Eberhard AG.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomously excavating and redepositing material to realize designed terraces and slopes in outdoor terrain is the same geometry-to-design earthmoving as forming an incline, with the same machine class.

sources.system: Cat MineStar Command for dozing (semi-autonomous tractor system, SATS)
sources.title: Command | Cat | Caterpillar
sources.claim: Cat MineStar Command for dozing provides remote-control and semi-autonomous dozing at surface mines, with one operator managing up to four dozers remotely; large deployments include Thiess at Lake Vermont and Arch's Black Thunder mine.
sources.transferJustification: Mine dozing (reclamation, stockpile, highwall work) overlaps ramp shaping, but the published description mixes remote control with semi-autonomy, so the degree of independent operation cannot be established.

sources.system: Bedrock Operator autonomy retrofit for excavators
sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Raises $270 Million in Series B Funding to Accelerate the Future of Autonomous Construction
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics is running supervised-autonomy excavation on active construction sites and, as of February 2026, was still targeting its first fully operator-less ... later that year.
sources.transferJustification: Mass excavation on construction sites is the closest work to ramp cutting, but operation is still supervised, so it does not substantiate unattended completion.

tasks.label: Lubricate, adjust, or repair machinery and replace parts, such as gears, bearings, or bucket teeth.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shift lubrication round on a hydraulic excavator, front-end loader or shovel at a surface mine or quarry: greasing boom, stick, bucket linkage pins, bushings and swing bearing (dozens to 150+ points) with a grease gun, or managing/monitoring the machine's onboard centralized grease system; done on the pit floor or a parking pad in dust, mud, heat or cold.

Prestart/shift-end fluid servicing at a fuel and service bay or from a service truck: refuelling the machine, topping up engine oil, hydraulic oil and coolant through fill points, and refilling the auto-lube grease reservoir; institution-controlled service area with standard fittings.

Replacing worn ground-engaging tools on the bucket - tooth points and adapters, corner shrouds, cutting edges and wear plates on excavator, loader or dragline buckets - using pin/lock tools, sledges or a torch and welder, on the pit floor or a service pad with the bucket grounded.

Field adjustments and small repairs where the machine sits: tensioning tracks, replacing a burst hydraulic hose or fitting, changing filters, tightening loose fasteners, replacing lights/wipers/mirrors, freeing packed material - requires finding the fault first, then fixing it with hand tools in the pit.

Larger component work in the mine maintenance shop, usually assisting or under a mechanic: pulling and replacing bearings, gears, final drives, idlers or pumps on a fixtured component using hoists, pullers and torque tools; indoor bay with standard equipment.

sources.system: SKF Lincoln P203 progressive automatic lubrication system
sources.title: SKF Lincoln automatic lubrication systems drive mobile mine machine reliability and uptime - Kenya Engineer
sources.claim: SKF Lincoln P203 centralized automatic lubrication systems are fitted to mining excavators, wheel loaders and dump trucks and machine-dispense metered grease to up to 150+ friction points, pins and bushings while the machine works, removing the need for manual daily greasing. Grease points are pre-plumbed at fixed positions on the machine.

sources.system: SKF Lincoln SL-6 automatic lubrication injector
sources.title: New SKF Lincoln Lubrication System Injector Provides New Design and Performance
sources.claim: SKF Lincoln single-line automatic lubrication injectors are marketed and sold for construction and mining equipment, continuously delivering grease to bearings, pins and bushings while the machine is in motion - i.e. performing the operator's greasing round by machine.

sources.title: Robotic refuelling for mines - Robofuel | Scott
sources.claim: Robofuel is a robotic arm station with vision sensing that locates a mine truck's fuel tank and couples the nozzle to refuel it autonomously, in purpose-built relocatable modules placed on the haul circuit or in-pit; Scott states it can also be used ... replenish drills and excavators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic replenishment of service fluids on mining machines. Coupling a nozzle to a machine's fill point and dispensing a measured charge is the same class of act as topping up oil/coolant or charging an auto-lube reservoir through fixed fill points on the same machines.

sources.title: SCOTT making ROBOFUEL refuelling system progress with AHS mining truck fleets - International Mining
sources.claim: A Robofuel autonomous refuelling installation for an autonomous haul truck fleet in the Pilbara iron ore region achieved site acceptance in late ... was operating in production, with further installations following - evidence of unmanned fluid servicing in real mine service bays.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: demonstrates that the fluid-replenishment part of routine machine servicing is completed by a robot at worker quality in a producing surface mine.

sources.system: Automatic Bit Changer (ABC) on Pit Viper 271/290/351
sources.title: Epiroc wins large order for autonomous surface mining equipment in Australia
sources.claim: Epiroc's Automatic Bit Changer performs hands-free replacement of heavy rotary tricone drill bits on Pit Viper blasthole rigs - making and breaking the joint and selecting/adding/removing bits from an onboard carousel at the touch of a ..., with no human contact with the drill string; ordered by BHP for autonomous surface fleets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: replacing a heavy consumable wear part on surface mining excavation equipment. An ~80 kg tricone bit is comparable in mass and handling to a bucket tooth point/adapter; both require breaking a worn, dirt-packed joint under force, retrieving a replacement from a fixed magazine, and seating and locking it. The ABC does this with the part presented in a fixed onboard cradle - the E1 counterfactual for a fixtured bucket lip.

sources.title: Path Robotics | Intelligent Welding Cells
sources.claim: Path Robotics sells autonomous 'intelligent welding cells' that scan parts as presented and generate weld paths without programming, aimed at mining equipment, excavator and loader arms and industrial buckets, reporting 97%+ first-pass yield.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: welded attachment/replacement of bucket wear parts. Cutting-edge, shroud and wear-plate renewal on a fixtured bucket is weld work on the same heavy mining components these cells already weld autonomously in a purpose-built cell.

tasks.label: Handle slides, mud, or pit cleanings or maintenance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine pit cleanings on an active bench: the shovel/loader/excavator operator cleans up spillage and loose muck around the loading face, under the truck spotting area, along ramps and at dump points, loading it into haul trucks or casting it aside. Ground is blasted rock and loose fill, geometry changes every shift, haul trucks and support equipment move nearby.

Cleanup at fixed plant areas: loader operator clears spillage and carryback around the ROM pad, crusher/hopper, conveyor transfer points and stockpile yard, feeding it back or trucking it out. Fixed layout, standard equipment, mine/quarry controls access to the pad.

Pit and working-area maintenance in normal conditions: cutting and cleaning drainage ditches and sumps, trimming and re-shaping ramps and benches, building and repairing safety berms/windrows, maintaining the dump crest and tipping area with bucket or blade.

Mud and wet-ground work: after rain or in a wet seam, mucking out sloppy saturated material with poor bucket release, clearing mud and slop off the pit floor and ramps, keeping water pumped/drained away, judging where the machine can safely track without bogging, and recovering the working area.

Slides and slope failures: removing sloughed material from a failed highwall, bench or spoil pile, working near unstable ground under geotechnical direction, standing off from the crest, watching for further movement and re-establishing the bench or ramp after a failure.

Operator-level servicing of the machine at the face or service pad: pre-shift walkaround inspection, greasing/fluid checks, checking and replacing bucket teeth and cutting edges, cleaning mud off tracks/undercarriage, clearing the cab and windows, minor repairs and assisting maintenance crews.

sources.title: Sandvik introduces AutoMine® AutoLoad 2.0 for improved autonomous bucket loading
sources.claim: Sandvik's AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 enables fully automated loader production cycles — bucket filling from a muck pile at fixed drawpoints and dumping at fixed dump points — as a commercial product for underground mines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mucking/loading of loose blasted rock. Pit cleanings are the same physical act — approach a pile of loose muck, fill a bucket, tram and dump — with the same machines, material and bucket-level precision.

sources.system: Sandvik AutoMine / Toro LH517i loaders at George Fisher mine
sources.title: Sandvik Boosts Safety at George Fisher Mine Through Automation
sources.claim: Ten fully automated Toro loaders run AutoMine at Glencore's George Fisher mine, approaching muck piles, filling buckets and hauling to dump points without human ... in a live production operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production mucking in an institution-controlled mine. It substantiates unattended bucket clean-up of loose rock in a defined-layout, access-controlled mining facility, the same work as clearing spillage at a fixed loading/dump area.

sources.title: Built Robotics raises $64 million for robotic excavator Exosystem
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofit turns a standard excavator into a fully autonomous trenching machine that digs to an uploaded depth/grade spec inside a geofence with nobody in the cab; offered commercially in the US.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous trenching to a specified line and grade. Cutting and cleaning drainage ditches and sumps in a pit is the same bucket operation on comparable soil at comparable precision; the demonstrated environment is an open earthmoving site.

sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Announces Supervised Autonomy Testing on Active Construction Sites in Move Towards Commercialization
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics ran supervised-autonomy mass excavation on live construction sites, its retrofitted 20-80 ton excavators loading human-driven dump trucks; over 65,000 cubic yards moved on one 130-acre site. Operator-less deployments were still a stated 2026 goal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repetitive excavate-and-load-truck cycles on an as-found earthmoving site. Same machine class and material as pit cleanup, but the work is still run under continuous human supervision, so it does not establish unattended surface-pit capability.

sources.developer: Baidu Research Robotics / University of Maryland
sources.title: Baidu Research Robotics & University of Maryland develop autonomous excavator system
sources.claim: Baidu Research and University of Maryland's Autonomous Excavator System performed material loading at a real waste disposal site, running more than 24 hours continuously without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended excavation and loading of heterogeneous loose material in an industrial yard, comparable to scooping up loose spillage and muck with an excavator bucket.

sources.title: Cat Command for Dozing in Mining
sources.claim: Caterpillar's MineStar Command for dozing is sold for mining as remote operation with a semi-autonomous mode in which one remote operator manages up to four dozers; the emphasis remains on operator control from a station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dozer clean-up and dump/bench maintenance at surface mines. Autonomy level is only 'semi-autonomous' with operators in continuous control from a station, so it is treated as teleoperated and does not support positive judgments.

sources.title: Unmanned Excavator System (UES) - Hitachi Construction Machinery
sources.claim: Hitachi states it is still developing technologies toward autonomous operation of ultra-large mining excavators, with current work focused on advanced remote control and operator checking to avoid collisions and maintain stability.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (mining excavator operation), but shows the state of the art for large surface-mine shovels remains remote control under development, supporting negative judgments for hazardous slide and mud work.

tasks.label: Measure and verify levels of rock or gravel, bases, or other excavated material.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-cycle depth/grade verification while digging: excavator or loader operator working a bench, pit floor, ramp or trench repeatedly checks the elevation of the material being cut against a target grade (onboard GNSS grade display, laser receiver on a mast, or reference marks) and corrects the cut in real time. Active pit, dusty, terrain reshaped hour by hour.

On-foot verification of a finished surface: operator dismounts with a grade rod, laser receiver or GNSS rover and shoots elevations at several points on a finished pit floor, trench bottom or excavated pad to confirm it is at design level before sign-off or before the next material is placed. Rough, muddy, uneven ground taken as found.

Stockpile level/quantity verification in the pit or product yard: loader operator checks heights and volumes of crushed rock, sand or gravel piles against inventory or a customer order, notes whether a pile is drawn down or over-built. Outdoor yard, piles reshaped daily by loading and stacking.

Base/subbase level and thickness verification for site-built haul roads, ramps and equipment pads: operator verifies the elevation and lift thickness of placed crushed rock against stakes or a design surface before further material is spread. Outdoor, on newly placed loose aggregate.

Material level checks at the fixed processing plant/load-out: verify the level of rock in a crusher feed hopper, surge pile, product bin or covered/domed storage as material is fed or loaded out, to keep feed steady and avoid overfill or run-out. Fixed plant with standard equipment and controlled access.

sources.developer: Percepto (deployed by RockBlast at a Chilean mining conglomerate)
sources.title: RockBlast Improves Mining Operations with Autonomous Drones
sources.claim: Percepto's autonomous drone-in-a-box system is deployed at a large Chilean mining operation where it scans stockpiles weekly or daily and generates volumetric measurements automatically, measuring the levels/quantities of piled material without a person on the pile.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: measuring and verifying the level/volume of piled rock and gravel; the drone produces the surface elevations and volumes the operator would otherwise estimate or shoot with a rover.

sources.system: Exyn Nexys / ExynAero autonomous LiDAR drone
sources.title: Drones map depths of Northern mines - North of 60 Mining News
sources.claim: Agnico Eagle uses Exyn autonomous LiDAR drones to measure ore stockpiles inside the enclosed Dome storage at its Meadowbank Complex, replacing manual stockpile measurement in a fixed mine facility.
sources.transferJustification: Same task in an enclosed plant/storage setting: measuring the level and volume of stored broken rock, which is what the operator verifies at a feed hopper, surge pile or covered storage.

sources.title: Drones for Mining: Data gathering using autonomous robots.
sources.claim: Exyn supplies autonomous drones that perform frequent stockpile volume measurement for mining inventory control, stating the autonomous platform replaces traditional manual measurement methods.

sources.title: Skycatch, DJI build custom drones for Komatsu | Pit & Quarry
sources.claim: Skycatch's Explore1 drones fly job sites autonomously to build high-accuracy 3D site maps and models, delivered at scale (1,000 units) for Komatsu Smart Construction earthmoving sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (site topographic survey): the 3D surface model gives the elevations of excavated surfaces and material piles that the operator verifies with a rod or rover, over the same terrain and materials.

sources.system: Skycatch mine-site spatial data platform (drone automation)
sources.title: Caterpillar Expands Mining Technology Capabilities with Skycatch Acquisition
sources.claim: Caterpillar acquired Skycatch in July 2026 to fold high-frequency drone spatial data capture and automated measurement of mine sites (stockpiles, haul roads, pit surfaces) into MineStar, indicating commercial maturity of automated drone measurement at surface mines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (mine-site spatial measurement): stockpile measurement, haul road monitoring and pit analysis are the measure-and-verify-levels function performed on the same materials and surfaces.

sources.system: UAV photogrammetry stockpile volumetrics (Njuli quarry case study)
sources.title: Comparative utilization of drone technology vs. traditional methods in open pit stockpile volumetric computation: A case of njuli quarry, Malawi
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed comparison at an open-pit quarry found drone-derived stockpile volumes met the plus/minus 3% accuracy tolerance required for mine volumetric reporting, i.e. worker-quality measurement output.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, quality benchmark: establishes that automated aerial measurement of quarry material meets the accuracy standard an employer accepts from a manual survey.

sources.title: Built Robotics releases 1st fully autonomous construction machinery in US | Construction Dive
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem converts standard excavators into fully autonomous machines that dig trenches, excavate foundations and grade pads to pre-programmed GPS depth and grade using GPS and LiDAR, on active US construction/energy sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous excavation to grade): the machine continuously measures the elevation of the surface it cuts against the design depth/grade and holds it within tolerance - the same measure-and-verify-level function, on the same materials and machines, in open outdoor earthwork.

sources.title: Building the Future of Construction - Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' autonomous trenching robots have accumulated large-scale field operation on US and Australian energy projects, showing sustained autonomous dig-to-depth work rather than a one-off demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the Exosystem item: autonomous excavation to a specified depth/grade requires the machine to measure and verify the level of the excavated material continuously.

sources.system: Propeller Aero PPK drone survey workflow
sources.title: Measuring Cut and Fill for Your Mining and Aggregates Sites
sources.claim: Drone photogrammetry platforms used at mines and quarries generate centimeter-accurate 3D models and cut/fill quantities over pit areas, the measurement used to verify how much material was moved and whether surfaces match design.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (cut/fill and layer-thickness measurement): differencing successive surveyed surfaces yields the lift thickness and finished elevation of placed rock or gravel that the operator checks with a rod.

sources.system: Trimble Earthworks Grade Control Platform for excavators
sources.title: Trimble Earthworks for Excavators - SITECH Construction Systems
sources.claim: 3D machine-control systems on excavators measure the exact position of ... against a design surface and automatically control boom and bucket to stay ..., performing grade measurement/verification by machine (operator remains in the cab).
sources.transferJustification: Corroborating only (operator in cab): shows the in-cycle level measurement and grade verification already executed by machine sensing and control on production earthmoving machines.
