tasks.label: Adjust dig face angles for varying overburden depths and set lengths.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Sand & gravel pit or soil-overburden strip: operator runs a hydraulic excavator (or loader) stripping loose topsoil/clay overburden whose thickness varies across the deposit; sets the working-face angle so the face stands and the bucket reaches the toe, decides how long a strip to work from each machine position before tramming, and loads trucks or casts to stockpile. Unblasted loose material; survey stakes or GPS grade control usually available.

Crushed-stone / hard-rock quarry: 40-90 t hydraulic excavator (or large front-end loader) digging a blasted muckpile against a 10-15 m bench face; operator changes attack and face angle as lift and overburden depth vary, keeps the toe clean and prevents overhang, works a set length of face before repositioning, and loads haul trucks amid dust, oversize boulders and loose rock.

Large open-pit coal or metal mine: ultra-class shovel or 250-800 t hydraulic excavator cutting overburden benches to the survey design as overburden depth changes along the strip; operator adjusts bench face angle and cut geometry, positions for double-side loading of 200-400 t haul trucks, and coordinates with dispatch/autonomous haulage.

Coal strip mine dragline: operator works each dragline set - setting dig-face and spoil-side angles for the overburden depth in that block, keying the cut, and choosing the set length before walking the machine to the next position; must manage pit water, uneven blast fragmentation and limited spoil room over a full shift.

Adverse ground mid-shift: overburden turns wet, sloughing, or mixed with boulders/old workings; operator flattens the face angle, shortens the length of cut worked from each position and repositions the machine onto stable ground to avoid a face failure; small crew, no up-to-date design model.

Opening a new cut or bench: establishing the first face on virgin ground at the start of a new strip or bench - cutting the box cut/ramp to the planned face angle and cut length per the pit plan, with no existing working face and only the survey plan to work to.

sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Deploys Industry's Largest Supervised Autonomous Excavator Test | Equipment World
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics' Operator autonomy kit on 20-80 t excavators performed mass excavation and truck loading over months on a live 130-acre site-prep project in Phoenix with Sundt Construction, moving 65,000+ cubic yards under human supervision (operator-less deployment still a stated 2026 goal).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mass excavation and truck loading in soil with the same 20-80 t excavator class and loose material as pit overburden stripping; sustained production cutting to a planned surface transfers to stripping a lift of overburden, though the cut geometry comes from the site plan and a human supervises.

sources.developer: Baidu Research / Baidu USA (with Univ. of Maryland)
sources.title: AES: Autonomous Excavator System for Real-World and Hazardous Environments (arXiv 2011.04848)
sources.claim: Baidu's Autonomous Excavator System excavated and loaded material at a waste-disposal facility yard, running 24 hours between human interventions with hourly production close to an experienced operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: continuous autonomous digging of a working pile and loading of trucks in a controlled outdoor facility; comparable machine and loose material to overburden stripping, and the uptime/productivity figures show shift-length output rather than a single scripted cycle.

sources.title: Watch: UK first trial of autonomous excavator helping to build car park at Manchester Airport | New Civil Engineer
sources.claim: Gravis Robotics' retrofit kit let a standard excavator dig to an uploaded 3D design model without human intervention during a UK trial on car-park works at Manchester Airport with Taylor Woodrow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous excavation to a surveyed 3D design; holding a designed depth/geometry with an excavator is the execution half of adjusting a cut as overburden depth varies, on comparable machines and soil.

sources.title: HEAP - The autonomous walking excavator (Automation in Construction) - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: ETH Zurich's autonomous walking excavator HEAP autonomously and accurately excavated free-form embankments (sloped, designed shapes) in natural granular material.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously shaping sloped faces to a specified geometry in loose granular material - the closest demonstrated analogue to cutting a dig face to a chosen angle, with comparable machine and material, but done in a controlled test area.

sources.title: AES: Autonomous Excavator System for Real-World and Hazardous Environments (arXiv 2011.04848)
sources.claim: The same AES system was evaluated across scenarios including rock manipulation (isolating and removing oversize rocks and loading smaller rock) with compact and standard excavators in controlled indoor/outdoor test settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous excavation of rock/mixed material presented as a pile; relevant to digging a blasted muckpile, but demonstrated only on prepared piles in controlled areas rather than against a working quarry bench.

sources.system: industry-wide review (Caterpillar, Komatsu, Gravis, Teleo, Pronto systems)
sources.title: The Intelligent Machine Has Arrived | Highways.Today
sources.claim: Industry review of heavy-equipment AI as of July 2026: autonomous haulage is proven at mine and quarry scale (Komatsu's 1,000th autonomous truck, Pronto's mixed-fleet quarry), but end-to-end autonomous excavation is still the frontier.
sources.transferJustification: Used only to support negative judgments: it establishes that, as of mid-2026, autonomy in mining/quarrying covers haulage and drilling while excavating and loading units remain operator-run or supervised.

sources.system: Dragline Automation (swing cruise control, Digital Terrain Mapping)
sources.title: Dragline Automation - Robotics - CSIRO Research
sources.claim: CSIRO/QCAT dragline work produced operator-assist technology - swing cruise control and digital terrain ... - to help dragline operators and planners; the dig cycle remains with the operator and the remote demonstration used a scale model dragline.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about draglines: the available automation is operator assistance for the swing cycle plus terrain mapping, not autonomous control of dig-face geometry or set advance.

tasks.label: Drive machines to work sites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shift start/end: tram a wheel loader or hydraulic excavator from the equipment parking/fuel-and-service yard to the assigned pit face over maintained mine or quarry haul roads, sharing roads with haul trucks and light vehicles, in dust and on grades, following radio/right-of-way protocol.

Short repositioning of the machine on the working bench between successive dig/work positions inside a planned, signed-off work area (bench top graded, positions known from the mine plan), moving a few machine lengths at a time as the work advances.

Driving up to and onto freshly blasted muck, soft or rutted pit floor after rain, or over spoil/overburden dumps at the tip head, in close proximity to haul trucks spotting at the face; ground taken as found and changing hourly.

Relocating the machine across the property between pits, benches or the plant area: long slow travel on steep temporary ramps cut by dozers, over pioneer roads, and sometimes across or briefly along a public road with flaggers/escort.
Small pit / portable-plant variant: driving a front-end loader from the yard to the stockpile and crusher-feed area over the hardstand within the plant, among trucks and plant staff.

Walking the machine onto or off a lowboy/float trailer with ramps in a laydown area for transport to another site: lining tracks up within inches, cresting the ramp break, centering on the deck and setting the machine down for tie-down.

sources.system: Cat MineStar Command for hauling (Cat 777G autonomous trucks)
sources.title: Caterpillar and Luck Stone celebrate one million tons hauled autonomously at Bull Run Quarry
sources.claim: Cat MineStar Command for hauling runs driverless haul trucks on active mine and quarry haul roads, navigating between loading and dumping locations around other equipment and personnel; deployed commercially at mines and, since Nov 2024, at Luck Stone's Bull Run aggregates quarry, which passed one million tons hauled autonomously by July 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous haulage. Transfer holds because the machine-driving portion is identical — a large off-highway machine self-navigating the same mine/quarry haul roads, ramps and pit floor to a designated work position among traffic — which is what 'drive machines to work sites' consists of.

sources.system: Cat MineStar Command for drilling (MD6250/MD6310 drills)
sources.title: Command for drilling | Cat | Caterpillar
sources.claim: Caterpillar's autonomous pattern drilling moves surface blasthole drills autonomously between holes across an entire blast pattern on a mine bench, with a single remote operator supervising drills across the site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous blasthole drilling. The tramming element is the same act as this task — a tracked heavy mining machine driving itself, unmanned, to each successive work position on an active bench, with the same terrain, obstacles and precision demands.

sources.title: Sandvik enables fully autonomous drill fleet operation with AutoMine AutoCycle
sources.claim: Sandvik's AutoMine Surface Drilling AutoCycle gives surface drill rigs autonomous hole-to-hole tramming with path planning, obstacle detection and ..., allowing a fleet of rigs on a bench to be run from a remote control room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous surface drilling. Its tramming step is exactly 'drive the machine to the next work position' on an active mine bench, with obstacle detection and path planning over as-found bench ground.

sources.system: Pit Viper autonomous surface drill rigs
sources.title: Epiroc's ground-breaking drill rig Pit Viper celebrates 25 years including a decade with autonomous operations
sources.claim: Epiroc Pit Viper surface blasthole rigs have been operating autonomously at mines for a decade, drilling over 90 million metres in autonomous mode, generally supervised from off-site control rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous surface drilling at production mines. Establishes that unmanned heavy mining machines routinely relocate themselves around an active bench under remote supervision at production reliability.

sources.title: Develon puts autonomous excavator to work in Switzerland
sources.claim: A Develon DX225LC-7X crawler excavator fitted ... working autonomously — no operator in the cab ... not remote-controlled — digging a 300 m long trench at a former KIBAG quarry ..., under a technical supervisor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous trenching/earthmoving. Digging a 300 m trench requires the excavator to track itself along the work line and reposition repeatedly over disturbed quarry ground without an operator, which is the driving/repositioning act in this task.

sources.system: Huaneng Ruichi / XCMG ZNK95 autonomous mining trucks with Huawei autonomous driving
sources.title: North China's Yimin Mine deploys world's first fleet of 100 5G-A connected, self-driving electric trucks
sources.claim: Huaneng's Yimin open-pit coal mine commissioned a fleet of 100 driverless battery-electric mining trucks (XCMG hardware, Huawei autonomy) that operate on the mine's haul roads in extreme conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous haulage in an open-pit mine. Shows unmanned heavy machines driving themselves at scale between the pit face, dumps and service areas on the same haul-road network the excavator operator would use.

sources.title: Sandvik to automate new LHD fleet at Codelco's El Teniente copper mine
sources.claim: Sandvik AutoMine Fleet runs fleets of underground loaders (LHDs) and trucks autonomously in a shared production area, with the machines tramming between loading and dumping points under remote supervision; deployed at operations such as Codelco's El Teniente.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous load-haul-dump operation. The machine class is a bucket loader identical in control to a surface front-end loader, and the tramming leg — driving the loader unmanned along mine roadways to its work position — is this task.

sources.title: The World's First Autonomous Piling System for Utility-Scale Solar — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 is a commercially offered fully autonomous robotic pile driver built on a Caterpillar excavator base that surveys, distributes and drives piles across utility-scale solar construction sites, positioning itself at each pile location; EPC contractor Blattner contracted in Sept 2025 to deploy dozens of Built's robots on US solar projects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous solar pile driving. To install hundreds of piles per day the tracked excavator-based robot must drive itself unmanned between successive work positions across an earthwork site, the same self-relocation act as this task.

tasks.label: Perform manual labor to prepare or finish sites, such as shoveling materials by hand.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: After the shovel/loader has worked an area, the operator gets down and finishes it by hand: shoveling loose spoil off a bench floor, trimming the toe of a bench or the bottom of a drainage ditch/sump, dressing a slope, cleaning up a spot the bucket cannot reach. Active surface pit, uneven muddy ground, wet rock, weather exposed, layout changes daily.

Hand-shoveling spilled rock, coal or fines at the fixed plant: under and alongside conveyors, at the crusher/ROM hopper, at the truck loadout and stacker. Heavy shovel and broom work in confined space beside running equipment; fixed layout, company-controlled premises, standard walkways.

Careful hand digging with a spade/bar to expose or protect buried services before or during machine excavation: water and dewatering lines, power and blast cables, culverts, pipe crossings on haul roads. Must expose the line without striking it; soil and backfill unknown, site taken as found.

Clearing the working area by hand before machine work: throwing loose rock and boulders aside, pulling roots/brush and scrap steel, picking rocks out of a pad or road, hand-spreading gravel or shot rock over soft spots. Open pit or haul road, mixed and novel debris, outdoors.

Placing and installing site items by hand to prepare or finish the site: silt fence, straw wattles and berms for erosion control, grade stakes and lath, barricades and berm markers, timbers/cribbing, sandbags, pipe sections; backfilling and tamping around a structure. Varied fasteners, ground conditions and layouts.

Cleaning the machine and its immediate work area by hand at the end of a ... or after wet digging: shoveling and barring packed mud/spoil off tracks, undercarriage, steps and decks, knocking sticky material out of the bucket, clearing material from around the machine. Pit floor or laydown yard, outdoors.

sources.developer: Baidu Research Robotics and Auto-Driving Lab / University of Maryland
sources.title: An autonomous excavator system for material loading tasks | Science Robotics
sources.claim: Baidu/UMD Autonomous Excavator System autonomously digs and loads loose material from piles into trucks at real outdoor sites, running 24 hours without human intervention, including at a waste disposal site and in extreme cold.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine excavation and loading of loose material. Hand shoveling moves the same loose rock/soil to clear or finish a spot; when the material is presented to the machine in a purpose-built setting the scooping, transport and dumping operation is the same, with the same material and no finer precision than a graded surface requires.

sources.system: HEAP (Hydraulic Excavator for an Autonomous Purpose)
sources.developer: ETH Zurich (Robotic Systems Lab / Gramazio Kohler Research)
sources.title: Autonomous excavator constructs a six-metre-high dry-stone wall | ETH Zurich
sources.claim: ETH Zurich's autonomous walking excavator HEAP scanned, grabbed and placed multi-tonne boulders and demolition debris to build a 6 m x 65 m dry stone wall and excavated the surrounding landscape to a digital design.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous on-site handling of rock and debris and shaping of terrain, which is what manual site preparation/finishing accomplishes with a shovel and by hand, on the same materials.

sources.system: Built Robotics Exosystem (autonomous trenching, RPD 35 pile driver)
sources.title: Blattner Picks Autonomous Pile Drivers from Built Robotics for Solar Projects | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Built Robotics sells aftermarket kits that put excavators under full robotic control for trenching and pile driving, used commercially by US contractors, hitting depth tolerances of about 0.1 ft.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous excavation to a specified line and grade. Hand finishing of a ditch bottom or bench floor targets the same graded output; the cited system meets tighter than hand tolerances on loose ground.

sources.title: C&D Waste | Sorting Bulky Waste | ZenRobotics
sources.claim: ZenRobotics Heavy Picker robots pick bulky, heavy construction and demolition debris (items up to 40 kg) off a conveyor in sorting facilities, unmanned and around the clock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: identifying and picking heavy, novel, irregular debris (rock, wood, metal, concrete) and depositing it elsewhere - the same act as hand-clearing rock and scrap from a work area, when the debris is presented to the machine as a purpose-built setting would present it.

sources.title: Sandvik AutoMine Autoload 2.0 eliminates operator intervention in LHD drawpoint loading - International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 runs fully automated loading cycles for underground LHD loaders, mucking loose blasted rock at fixed drawpoints and dumping it at fixed points without operator intervention, in mines where the autonomous area is barricaded off from people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous scooping and relocation of loose broken rock at fixed points in a mine, which is the same physical operation as shoveling spillage back into the flow when the spill is presented at a station built for the machine.

sources.title: ENR: Autonomous Equipment: Roadworks robot digs out, repairs buried utility lines
sources.claim: ULC Technologies' RRES is a self-contained robot that autonomously cores pavement and vacuum-excavates down to buried gas mains, exposing and reburying them; it was field trialled on live UK gas networks with SGN.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: careful excavation to expose a buried utility without striking it, which is exactly why the mine worker digs by hand around services; the cited system uses soft-touch/vacuum excavation for the same objects and the same damage-avoidance requirement.

sources.system: Bedrock Operator (retrofit autonomy kit for excavators)
sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Leads Major Autonomous Excavation Push | Equipment World
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics ran autonomous excavators moving mass earth on an active 130-acre construction site with Sundt, loading human-driven trucks under supervised autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous earthmoving on an unstructured active jobsite, showing bulk loose-material handling outdoors; it does not cover hand-tool-scale finishing, so it is used only to support the lower, purpose-built tier.

roles.title: Earth Drillers, Except Oil and Gas
roles.description: Operate a variety of drills such as rotary, churn, and pneumatic to tap subsurface water and salt deposits, to remove core samples during mineral exploration or soil testing, and to facilitate the use of explosives in mining or construction. Includes horizontal and earth boring machine operators.

tasks.label: Operate controls to stabilize machines and to position and align drills.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Surface mine or quarry blasthole drilling: operator trams a track-mounted rotary or DTH rig onto a graded bench, sets/levels the machine on hydraulic jacks, positions it over the surveyed collar of the next hole in the pattern, and sets mast angle/azimuth before collaring.

Water well drilling at a rural, farm or residential property: operator backs a truck- or track-mounted rig onto a customer-chosen spot (soft ground, trees, septic fields, overhead lines), deploys outriggers, levels the carrier, raises the mast and plumbs it over the marked well location.

Solar/ground-mount foundation work on open, graded construction sites: machine is moved to each surveyed pile or pre-drill location in a large repetitive grid, stabilized, and the mast/hammer aligned vertically to sub-inch tolerance before drilling/driving.

Other construction and geotechnical drilling at varied sites (urban drilled shafts and micropiles, rock anchors, highway rock cuts, SPT/soil borings at exploration or site-investigation locations): rig maneuvered onto a staked point among obstructions, cribbed/jacked level, mast plumbed or set to a design rake.

Underground mine or tunnel drilling: jumbo or longhole rig trammed to the face/drift position, stabilized on jacks, and each boom/feed positioned and aligned to the drill plan's hole coordinates and angles before collaring.

Horizontal directional drilling / utility boring in a street, right-of-way or yard: rig driven onto the entry location, anchored or staked down, frame angle set, and the drill string aligned to the planned entry angle and bore path amid traffic and buried utilities.

sources.system: Epiroc SmartROC D65 MKII (autonomous surface drill rig)
sources.title: Epiroc and Luck Stone launch first fully autonomous SmartROC D65 drill rig in U.S. aggregate market
sources.claim: A fully autonomous Epiroc SmartROC D65 MKII surface drill rig has been deployed in a US crushed-stone quarry, executing complete drill patterns (tramming, positioning, collaring, drilling) with no operator in the ..., at GMG Level 4 autonomy under remote supervision.

sources.title: Epiroc South Africa introduces new SmartROC MK II surface drill rig - Aggregates Business

sources.system: Sandvik AutoMine Surface Fleet / AutoCycle (surface boom and rotary drill rigs)
sources.title: Sandvik introduces 'future of autonomous drill rig operation' with AutoMine Surface Fleet - International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik's AutoMine Surface Fleet automates, with minimal human intervention, exactly the acts in this task — stabilising the rig, precise positioning over the hole, collaring, and tramming to the next ... — on surface mine and quarry benches in rock and weather conditions.

sources.system: Cat MD6250 / MD6310 with MineStar Command for drilling (OMA, S-ADS, ADS)
sources.title: Collaboration delivers world first autonomous drilling success for Thiess | WesTrac
sources.claim: Cat MineStar Command for drilling has been put into production at mine sites (Thiess/WesTrac), where MD-series drills navigate hole to hole and auto-drill each hole, with semi-autonomous drilling systems and on-site remote operating stations running multiple drills.

sources.system: Epiroc Pit Viper 291 with Rig Control System (AutoDrill, AutoLevel, BenchREMOTE)
sources.title: Epiroc Introduces Pit Viper 291 Single-Pass Blasthole Drilling Rig with Autonomous Drilling Options | OEM Off-Highway
sources.claim: Large blasthole rigs are sold with on-board automation that levels the machine automatically (AutoLevel) and with fully autonomous drilling options requiring almost no human interaction with the drill.

sources.system: Epiroc Boomer face drilling rigs with ABC Total / Underground Manager
sources.title: Advanced Boom Control | Epiroc US
sources.claim: Epiroc's Advanced Boom Control (ABC) Total automatically positions the boom and feed to the drill plan and drills a full round automatically underground, including automatic collaring, through breaks and shift changes.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: the machine positions and aligns the drill feed to planned hole coordinates and angles underground, then collars the hole.

sources.system: Built Robotics RPD 35 (Robotic Pile Driver, Exosystem autonomy on an excavator base)
sources.title: Built Robotics develops autonomous solar piling robot - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 autonomously carries out the whole foundation-pile cycle on utility-scale solar construction sites — surveying, positioning at each pile point, driving and inspecting — hitting tolerances of under an inch.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (foundation piling): the robot self-positions on unimproved graded ground at surveyed points and aligns a vertical mast/hammer to sub-inch accuracy before penetrating the ground — the same stabilize-position-align act this task requires of a drill mast, at comparable precision.

sources.system: Built Robotics autonomous piling/drilling excavators deployed with Blattner
sources.title: Blattner Picks Autonomous Pile Drivers from Built Robotics for Solar Projects | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Blattner, a major US renewable-energy EPC, contracted in 2025 to deploy dozens of Built ... machines on US solar projects for pile driving, surveying, drilling and trenching, with the autonomous machines installing piles unaided around the clock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (solar foundation installation, which the contract also covers drilling for): the machines self-position and align a vertical mast at surveyed ground points on an open construction site.

instances.label: Utility horizontal directional drilling / horizontal boring: operator runs a Vermeer or Ditch Witch HDD rig from a launch pit or setup in a street, driveway or right-of-way, starting and stopping rotation and thrust, varying penetration rate and mud flow as soil, cobbles and rock change, cycling drill rods out of the rod box, then pulling back conduit/casing for fiber, gas, water or sewer. Buried utilities, traffic and property boundaries are present. (Largest industry group for this occupation: utility system construction.)

Blasthole drilling on construction and heavy-civil jobs: crawler/track drill on a road cut, building excavation, pipeline trench or dam site; operator collars, starts drilling, adjusts feed pressure/rotation for seams, voids and overburden, adds and pulls rods, and stops at design depth on a marked pattern. Site layout changes daily, other trades work nearby.

Water well drilling on rural, residential, farm or small municipal property: air or mud rotary rig set up on the customer's ground, driller controls rotation speed, pulldown and air/mud as formation changes, adds drill pipe, then runs and joins steel or PVC casing into the hole, sets screen and grouts. Site conditions and formations differ at every address.

Production blasthole drilling at a surface mine or quarry bench (rotary or DTH, holes on a surveyed pattern), plus underground longhole/face drilling in a mine drift: rig is leveled on a prepared bench or drift, drilling parameters controlled to formation, drill pipe added and removed from the carousel, hole cleaned and left ready for loading. Company-controlled premises with access control.

Mineral exploration core drilling at a remote pad or an underground drill cuddy: driller starts the rig, controls bit speed/feed to keep core recovery, trips rods with a rod handler, and where ground is caving installs casing to stabilize the hole. Weather, remote access, and highly variable ground.

Geotechnical and environmental drilling for engineering firms: hollow-stem auger or sonic rig on a roadside, brownfield, urban lot or levee; operator starts/stops the head, controls advance rate for SPT sampling intervals, and installs monitoring-well casing and screen in the borehole. Access is tight and each site is taken as found.

Geotechnical soil-test borings and mineral-exploration core drilling at field sites (roadside, farm field, remote claim, or underground exploration drift): feed pressure, rotation speed and fluid/air pressure regulated to recover intact core or samples without burning bits or plugging the hole.

Horizontal directional drilling for utilities along a street or easement: operator regulates thrust/pullback force, rotation speed and mud pressure as the bore passes through soil, cobbles, or rock during pilot bore, reaming and pullback.

tasks.label: Select and attach drill bits and drill rods, adding more rods as hole depths increase, and changing drill bits as needed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Horizontal directional drilling / earth boring crew installing utilities (fiber, gas, water service) along a street, easement or yard: operator attaches the drill head/bit and starter rod, then adds a 10-15 ft drill rod from the onboard rod box every joint as the bore advances, swapping bit/reamer when ground changes; work occurs in a public right-of-way with traffic, pedestrians and unknown buried utilities.

Water well / geothermal well drilling on a rural, farm or residential property: driller selects and makes up a tricone or DTH hammer bit, adds 20 ft drill pipe from the rack as the hole deepens to 150-500 ft, and changes bits when formation changes (overburden to bedrock) or the bit dulls; uneven, untended ground, site taken as found.

Construction-site rock drilling: blastholes for a road cut or building excavation, or anchor/micropile holes, using a crawler top-hammer or DTH rig; operator selects the bit, couples rods/extension steels from the rig's rod handling carousel as the hole deepens, and changes worn button bits between holes, on sloped, cluttered, changing ground shared with other trades.

Surface mine or large quarry production blasthole drilling on a prepared, surveyed bench: rotary or DTH rig drills a pattern of holes, adding pipe from the onboard carousel for multi-pass holes and swapping tricone/hammer bits when penetration rate drops; controlled site with exclusion zones and standardized drill patterns.

Underground mine or tunnel drilling: longhole production rings or development face rounds with a jumbo/longhole rig; extension rods added from the rig carousel as the hole deepens and bits replaced when worn, in a ventilated, surveyed heading controlled by the mine.

Geotechnical, environmental or mineral-exploration sampling drilling at varied sites (bridge foundation borings, brownfield monitoring wells, greenfield core/RC holes): repeatedly making up and adding rods, tripping the string in and out, and swapping among augers, core bits, tricones and split-spoon samplers as the program requires.

tasks.label: Drive or guide truck-mounted equipment into position, level and stabilize rigs, and extend telescoping derricks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Water well / geothermal drilling at a rural or residential property: driver takes the truck-mounted rig down a gravel driveway or across a yard, spots the hole over the marked location while judging soft ground, septic fields and overhead power lines, deploys outriggers/leveling jacks with cribbing, levels the deck, and raises the telescoping derrick.

Geotechnical / environmental soil-test borings: truck-mounted auger or CPT rig moved between a dozen scattered boring locations across a construction site, road shoulder, parking lot or industrial property in one day; each stop requires spotting on the survey stake, setting hydraulic jacks on uneven or paved ground, and raising the mast, often inside a traffic-control zone.

Foundation, anchor or caisson drilling on a building or infrastructure construction site, frequently a congested urban lot or slope: crane-carrier or truck-mounted drill walked/driven through mud and around trades and materials, set over a layout point with limited swing room, outriggers matted and leveled, mast erected under overhead constraints.

Large greenfield energy-site foundation drilling/piling (utility-scale solar or similar): graded open field, thousands of surveyed foundation points on a regular grid, machine repeatedly repositioned to the next point, stabilized and plumbed, and mast/leader erected to install the foundation.

Blasthole drilling on a quarry floor or open-pit mine bench: drill trammed onto the surveyed blast pattern on a dozer-graded bench inside a controlled, fenced operation, leveled on hydraulic jacks, mast raised and angled for each hole, repeated hole to hole across the pattern.

Mineral-exploration rig setup on a remote pad reached by bush track, and horizontal/earth-boring machine setup in a road right-of-way: off-highway or roadside travel to a marked entry point, cribbing and leveling on uneven or sloping ground, machine anchored/stabilized, and mast or drill frame erected to the required angle.

tasks.label: Operate machines to flush earth cuttings or to blow dust from holes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-pit mine or large aggregate quarry production blasthole drilling: operator runs a rotary or DTH crawler rig on a prepared, surveyed bench, managing bailing/flushing air and the dust-collection or water-injection system so cuttings are lifted from the hole, then cleans the hole during rod retraction so it stands open for charging.

Construction rock drilling (highway cuts, building foundations, utility trench blasting, rock anchor/dowel holes): crawler top-hammer or DTH drill on an active, congested construction site with other trades, traffic and weather; operator manages flushing air, water mist for dust, and blows each hole clean of cuttings/dust before it is loaded with explosives or grout.

Air-rotary / DTH water-well or closed-loop geothermal borehole drilling in rock on a rural or suburban property: operator runs the compressor and injects foam/water to blow cuttings and dust out of a 200-600 ft hole through the annulus, and blows the hole clean at completion.

Fluid-circulation drilling in unconsolidated or mixed ground — mud-rotary water wells and diamond-core holes: operator runs the mud/water pump, mixes and conditions fluid, watches the returns and pits for cuttings load and lost circulation, and circulates the hole clean before casing or coring runs.

Geotechnical and environmental soil test borings and monitoring wells on construction sites, roadsides and urban lots: small track/truck rig with hollow-stem auger or wash boring; operator circulates water/mud or blows the hole out between split-spoon samples and at tool changes, on ground taken as found.

Reverse-circulation exploration and grade-control drilling on exploration pads and mine leases: operator manages compressor/booster air and water/foam injection to lift cuttings up the inner tube to the cyclone and to blow the hole clean between rods and at hole completion.

tasks.label: Verify depths and alignments of boring positions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Production blasthole drilling on a bench at an open-pit mine or large quarry: the driller confirms each hole is collared on the surveyed pattern position at the design angle (GPS/staked marks, mast/feed angle indicators) and drilled to design depth, and re-checks depths (tape or rod tally) for sloughed or short holes before the shot is charged.

Rock drilling for construction and small quarry work with a crawler/track drill (highway rock cuts, building excavations, trench rock, presplit lines): the operator verifies hole layout positions and angles against the shot plan on uneven, cluttered ground near traffic and structures, and verifies each hole's depth by rod count and tape.

Geotechnical, environmental, or mineral-exploration boring: the driller verifies the depth of the hole at each sample or core-run interval against the rod string, checks that the mast is plumb (or set at the design angle) at each staked location, and records verified depths on the boring/core log for the engineer or geologist.

Water well drilling on rural, residential, or small-municipal property: the driller verifies total depth and depths to water-bearing formations by pipe tally and sounding line, verifies casing and screen setting depths, and checks plumbness/alignment of the borehole and casing (plumb bob, dummy, or deviation probe) against specification.

Deep foundation drilling at a building or bridge site (drilled shafts/caissons, tiebacks, micropiles): before concrete or steel placement the operator verifies shaft tip depth with a weighted tape or Kelly-bar depth readout against the toe elevation, and verifies verticality/batter of the hole against tolerance, often in a congested site with slurry or casing.

Horizontal directional drilling / earth boring under a road, driveway, or railway for utilities: the crew verifies the drill head's depth of cover and lateral alignment against the bore plan at each rod, using a walkover locator or steering tool, and verifies entry/exit alignment and clearance from existing utilities.

instances.label: Routine greasing/lubrication service of the drill rig at the job site: 60+ zerks on the rig plus ~30 on the carrier chassis, including points up in the derrick and under the deck; some points every 12 hours, others weekly; done with grease gun or grease banks, roughly 1.5 hours to cover every point.

Scheduled maintenance in the company shop or yard: oil and filter changes, engine/compressor/pump servicing, removing and replacing major components, welding repairs on the mast or deck, on a rig backed into a bay with hand and shop tools.

tasks.label: Assemble and position machines, augers, casing pipes, and other equipment, using hand and power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Production blasthole drilling on an open-pit mine or aggregate quarry bench: the driller trams the rotary/DTH rig to the next surveyed hole on a dozed bench, sets and levels the jacks, positions and aligns the mast over the collar, and adds/removes drill pipe from the carousel as the hole advances; bits and hammers are changed with hand and power tools.

Rock drilling for construction blasting (highway cut, pipeline trench, building excavation): a crawler drill is walked over broken, sloping ground amid other trades and equipment, positioned on the marked pattern, drill steels/rod strings coupled up, and air/water hoses and the compressor connected by hand.

Water well drilling on a rural/residential or farm property: the truck rig is spotted and leveled over the site, mast raised, drill pipe made up joint by joint, then steel or PVC casing sections are hoisted, threaded or welded, run into the hole, and the pitless/grout equipment rigged, all with tongs, wrenches and power tools.

Geotechnical/environmental soil boring at staked locations on varied sites (roadway shoulders, building pads, brownfields): the track or truck rig is walked in and set up level over each stake, hollow-stem auger flights or sonic/rotary rod sections are lifted, pinned or threaded and added as the boring advances, and sampling tooling is swapped between runs.

Horizontal directional/utility boring in a street or right-of-way: the rig is positioned at the entry angle over the bore path, staked or anchored down, rod boxes loaded, drill rods made up and broken out through the bore and pullback, and reamers, swivels and product pipe assembled with hand and power tools.

Mineral exploration core/RC drilling at a remote pad: the rig and mast are set up and leveled on the prepared pad, rod racks and rod handler set, rod strings assembled and tripped, and surface casing run and cemented to stabilize the collar.

tasks.label: Retrieve lost equipment from bore holes, using retrieval tools and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Water-well/geothermal rig on a rural or residential property: a drill rod, bit, DTH hammer or dropped pump/pipe string is lost in the hole. Driller sizes up the fish from tally and feel, selects/dresses an overshot, spear, tap or magnet, makes it up on the string, runs in, engages by feel (torque/weight indications), jars and pulls out; may re-ream or wash over first.

Diamond core exploration drilling at a remote pad (surface or underground): inner tube/core barrel fails to latch or the overshot/wireline parts, or rods twist off. Recovery with wireline overshot re-runs, rod taps/spears, left-hand rods, plus judgment on when to abandon and wedge/redrill.

Blasthole drilling on a prepared quarry or open-pit bench: DTH hammer, bit or drill steel breaks off or is dropped in a 10-30 m hole. Retrieval with fishing taps/overshots on the rig's own string or a service rig, in blast dust, water and loose cuttings; sometimes the hole is written off.

Geotechnical/environmental drilling on a construction or urban site: split-spoon sampler, casing, augers or downhole instrumentation (inclinometer, sonde) stuck or dropped in a small-diameter hole. Retrieval with slim overshots, casing pullers, wireline fishing, working around traffic and adjacent trades.

Horizontal directional boring under a street or yard: broken-off drill rod, lost sonde housing, or stuck bore head along the bore path. Recovery by pull-back attempts, downhole fishing subs, or locating and potholing/excavating to the fish from the surface.

sources.title: Epiroc and Luck Stone launch first fully autonomous SmartROC D65 drill rig in U.S. aggregate market
sources.claim: Epiroc's SmartROC D65 MKII, deployed at Luck Stone's quarry in Virginia, drills complete blasthole patterns autonomously (GMG Level 4) under remote supervision, including automated rod handling; its autonomy covers planned pattern drilling, not recovery of equipment lost or broken off in a hole.

It shows how far drilling autonomy reaches today, but does not transfer to retrieving lost equipment: the autonomy executes a pre-planned pattern within defined parameters and has no demonstrated ability to diagnose a fish, select and dress a fishing tool, or engage it by feel downhole.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated rod and inner-tube handling on exploration core rigs, the same rigs on which fishing jobs arise. tasks.label: Fabricate well casings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Water-well site, steel casing: driller measures and torch/saw-cuts 20-ft steel casing joints to length, bevels ends, tacks and girth-welds joint to joint (and welds on a drive shoe) as the string is lowered into the borehole. Outdoor mud pad, wind/rain, uneven ground, rig and crew moving around.

Water/monitoring well site, PVC casing and screen: driller cuts PVC casing and slotted screen to length, cuts or slots screen sections, threads/solvent-welds couplings, fits bottom cap and centralizers to build the casing-screen string before running it.

Drilling company shop or yard, pre-job fabrication: casing racked on stands is cut to length, ends squared/beveled, couplings, reducers, drive shoes and centralizer guides welded on, and casing slotted or perforated to make screen. Fixed layout, saws, welders, overhead hoist, company controls the premises.

On-site custom modification or repair fabrication at the wellhead: cutting a window or perforations in casing already in place, welding a patch/plate over a split, fabricating a casing extension or pitless-adapter connection, often working in a pit or awkward position with one-off dimensions.

Large-diameter conductor/surface casing or environmental well casing fabricated at the site: heavy-wall pipe cut to length, multi-pass girth welds, weld-on centralizers/lifting subs and tremie tube attachments, inspected for leak tightness before running.

tasks.label: Pour water into wells, or pump water or slush into wells to cool drill bits and to remove drillings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/farm water well or geothermal borehole on a private rural property: driller sets mud pan or pits, hooks hoses from a water tender, mixes bentonite/polymer slush, starts and throttles the mud pump, tops up water and additives, and watches returns and cuttings all shift in mud- or air-rotary drilling.

Geotechnical or environmental soil boring at a construction site, roadside or brownfield: small track/truck rig, driller fills the onboard water tank from a tote or hydrant, pumps water or thin mud down hollow-stem/sonic/rotary rods to cool the bit and lift cuttings, manages returns into a tub, and hauls water to keep drilling.

Surface blasthole drilling on an open-pit mine or quarry bench: rotary or DTH rig drills a laid-out pattern with air flush plus metered water injection to cool the bit, suppress dust and clear cuttings; driller sets injection rate for ground conditions and has the rig water tank refilled from a water truck or fill station.

Underground mine or tunnel face/production drilling: jumbo or longhole rig drills a round or ring with water flushing supplied by the rig's water pumps off a mine service water line; driller connects water hoses at each setup and controls flushing pressure to clear cuttings from the holes.

Construction rock drilling: blastholes, anchor or foundation holes at a road cut, urban excavation or utility trench, drilled wet (water flush/mist) for cuttings removal and silica dust control; driller connects the rig to a water buffalo or hydrant hose, refills tanks and adjusts flow around uneven, congested ground.

Horizontal directional boring for utilities in a street or right-of-way: operator mixes bentonite drilling fluid in the mixing system (dumping sacks, setting water rate), pumps it down the drill string to cool the bit and carry cuttings, monitors returns and frac-out, and adjusts mix and flow as soils change.

tasks.label: Create and lay out designs for drill and blast patterns.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Aggregate quarry (limestone/granite/trap rock): after the previous shot is mucked out, the driller/blaster measures the face and bench, works out burden, spacing, subdrill and hole depths for a 20-100 hole production pattern, then lays it out on the bench top, marking each collar with paint, flags or a handheld GPS. Access-controlled MSHA site, graded bench, rough rock underfoot.

Large open-pit mine production bench (iron ore, copper, coal): a 100-300 hole pattern is designed against the surveyed bench and pit design in planning software, then realized in the field - collars staked, or more often loaded straight into GPS drill navigation; the driller verifies positions against ground conditions (soft ground, previous-shot damage, crest stand-off).

Construction blasting: highway rock cut, building/pier foundation excavation, or pipeline trench. The driller sizes a small pattern in the field to the irregular rock surface, utilities, property lines and vibration/scaled-distance limits, then marks holes by hand on unprepared, often sloping or littered ground with traffic, other trades and the public nearby.

Underground development round or tunnel face: design the round (cut, relievers, lifters, perimeter/contour holes) for the actual face profile and rock conditions, then lay it out - traditionally spray-painted on the face, now positioned from a drill plan on the jumbo. Controlled mine or tunnel with standard drift profile, wet and dark.

Judgment-heavy, odd-shaped work: secondary breakage of oversize boulders in a muckpile, toe/trim shots, ditch or ramp patterns squeezed around infrastructure, where each hole is placed by eye from the rock condition rather than from a geometric pattern.

tasks.label: Place and install screens, casings, pumps, and other well fixtures to develop wells.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/farm water well on a rural property: after drilling, the crew assembles the PVC (or steel) casing string with a slotted or continuous-slot screen and bottom cap, adds centralizers, lowers the string into the open borehole to a tallied depth, tremies the gravel/filter pack around the screen, sets the bentonite/neat cement annular seal, and surges/airlifts to develop. Rig is parked over the hole in an open yard or field; weather, mud, and uneven ground as found.

Submersible pump installation in a completed well at a private residence or farm: bolt pump to drop pipe (PVC or galvanized), splice and band the power cable and safety rope along the pipe, add torque arrestor and check valve, lower the assembly by hand/hoist into the cased well, install pitless adapter or sanitary well seal, set the well cap and vent, and wire to the pressure switch/control box.

Environmental/geotechnical monitoring well at an industrial, brownfield or roadside site: 2-inch flush-threaded PVC screen and riser assembled and set through hollow-stem augers or a direct-push casing, filter sand poured or tremied in measured lifts with continuous tagging, bentonite pellet seal hydrated, grout to surface, protective steel casing or flush-mount vault set in concrete, then well development.

Large-diameter municipal, irrigation or industrial water well on a controlled but open job site: heavy steel casing joints welded or threaded and run into the hole, stainless/louvered screen and blank sections landed at logged depths, centralizers attached, gravel pack placed through tremie pipe while tagging, annular cement seal pumped, and well developed with airlift/swabbing.

Other well fixtures: dewatering wellpoints or deep wells jetted/drilled and connected to header pipe on an active construction site, geothermal loop insertion and tremie grouting, sand points, and wellhead/vault fittings — congested, changing sites shared with other trades.

It transfers to placing well casing and screen strings because the objects are the same class (4-13 in. tubulars with threaded joints), the act is identical (make up joint, take weight, lower to a tallied depth), and depth/torque precision requirements are at least as strict as water-well casing. It does not cover accessories such as gravel pack, pumps or pitless adapters.

tasks.label: Operate water-well drilling rigs and other equipment to drill, bore, and dig for water wells or for environmental assessment purposes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rural domestic water well: truck-mounted air-rotary/DTH rig mobilizes to a homeowner's property, sets up on sloping ground amid trees, driveways, septic fields and unmarked utilities; drives surface casing through overburden, drills a 6-8 in hole 150-600 ft into bedrock, watches cuttings and water yield to decide total depth, grouts the annulus and leaves a plumb, code-compliant borehole.

Agricultural irrigation or municipal/commercial supply well: large mud-rotary rig on a farm field or municipal parcel; multi-day drilling of a 12-24 in borehole to 300-1,500 ft, managing the mud program, lost circulation and formation changes, reaming, and setting casing/screen with gravel pack before development.

Environmental monitoring well / soil boring at a contaminated site (gas station, brownfield, active plant): hollow-stem auger, sonic or direct-push rig; continuous soil sample recovery for logging by a geologist, hole advanced 20-60 ft, then 2 in PVC well with screen, sand pack, bentonite seal, grout and flush-mount cover; decontamination between borings, cuttings drummed.

Geotechnical borings for construction/foundation investigation: track- or truck-mounted auger rig on raw land or an active construction site, uneven terrain and weather as found; SPT split-spoon sampling at 5 ft intervals plus rock coring, borehole logging and grout abandonment, several borings per day at surveyed locations.

Direct-push (Geoprobe-type) Phase II ESA sampling in developed settings: limited-access rig working in a paved parking lot, loading dock or inside a building; utility clearance, 15-30 ft probes for soil cores and temporary groundwater samples, hole grouting and surface patching, working around traffic and occupants.

tasks.label: Drill or bore holes in rock for blasting, grouting, anchoring, or building foundations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-pit mine production blasthole drilling: rotary or DTH blasthole rig on a prepared, surveyed bench inside a large mine; drills a designed pattern of 6-16 in holes to depth, moving hole to hole, with mine access control and geofenced work areas.

Quarry / aggregate pit bench drilling: crawler top-hammer or DTH rig drilling a blast pattern (3-6 in holes, 20-60 ft) on a quarry bench; fixed site, company-controlled premises, standard rig and drill plan, repeated shift after shift.

Civil construction rock blasting: road cuts, building/basement excavation, pipeline and trench rock; crawler drill drilling blast, presplit or line-drill holes on irregular, sloping, congested ground near traffic, utilities and other trades, moving frequently between small shots.

Underground mine or tunnel drilling: jumbo drilling a full face round of blast holes, long-hole production rings, or bolt/anchor holes; planned drift geometry, controlled access, but as-found rock face, water and muck underfoot.

Construction-site foundation and anchor drilling: rock sockets for drilled shafts/caissons, cased micropiles, tiebacks and soil nails on active urban, bridge or highway sites; mixed overburden-to-rock, casing and tooling changes, tight verticality/alignment tolerances, obstructions and utilities.

Grout-hole and stabilization drilling: dam curtain/consolidation grout holes, tunnel pre-excavation grouting fans, slope and abutment stabilization holes; staged split-spacing patterns drilled to design angle and depth from benches, galleries or slope platforms at as-found sites.

tasks.label: Perform pumping tests to assess well performance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New residential/domestic water well on a rural or suburban private lot: after drilling and development, the driller sets a temporary test pump (or uses the rig's air-lift), pumps 1-4 hours, measures static and pumping water levels with an electric sounding tape or transducer, gauges discharge with a bucket/stopwatch or flow meter, disposes of discharge water on the ground, and reports yield (gpm), drawdown and recovery on the well log. Site taken as found: mud, uneven ground, trees, no utility power.

Irrigation/agricultural or stock well in an open field: a larger temporary test pump on column pipe is set with the rig or a crane, powered by a generator or PTO, pumped for several hours to a day, sometimes in steps, to size the permanent pump; drawdown measured by airline or transducer, discharge to a ditch or field, results used for pump selection and permit reporting.

Municipal or industrial production well at a utility wellfield: step-drawdown test followed by a 24-72 hour constant-rate aquifer test; the crew rigs a large submersible test pump on temporary column pipe, an orifice weir or flow meter and discharge piping, sets transducers/dataloggers in the pumping well and nearby observation wells, collects water-quality and sand-content samples during the test, and delivers drawdown, specific capacity and aquifer parameters to the consulting hydrogeologist.

Environmental or geotechnical monitoring-well hydraulic testing at a contaminated or investigation site: 2-inch wells, small portable submersible or bladder pump, low-flow or short constant-rate pumping test (or slug test) with pressure transducer and datalogger, purge water containerized in drums, results used to estimate yield/hydraulic conductivity.

Performance retest of an existing, permanently equipped well (municipal, industrial or mine dewatering) inside a well house or fenced wellfield compound: the production pump, discharge meter and water-level access (airline/transducer) are already installed; the operator runs the pump at set rates, records pumping level and flow, computes specific capacity, and compares it with the original test to decide whether the well needs rehabilitation.

sources.system: Optimized (feedback-controlled) aquifer-test pumping system (Young, Rasmussen, Lyons & Pennell), field-tested at the Savannah River Site
sources.developer: University of Georgia / Savannah River Site researchers, published in Ground Water
sources.title: Optimized system to improve pumping rate stability during aquifer tests - Document - Gale Academic OneFile
sources.claim: A closed-loop system of datalogger, flow controller and variable-speed pump motor executes aquifer (pumping) tests with machine-controlled discharge rate, holding a stable rate within 1-3 minutes across confined and leaky aquifer tests with 3.5-6.9 m of drawdown, while transducers log water levels.

sources.system: Wellfield SCADA control of production-well pumps and control valves (Florida water utilities)

sources.claim: At instrumented water-supply wellfields, the SCADA control system is programmed to run drawdown tests on production wells automatically to verify well performance, using the installed pump, control valve, level instrumentation and flow recording.

sources.system: FSDF solar-powered automated well pumping system
sources.developer: U.S. DOE Office of Environmental Management / CDM Smith

sources.claim: A solar-powered automated well pumping system installed at DOE's ETEC site (Santa Susana Field Laboratory) has operated since May 2024, replacing manual pumping of groundwater wells; operators review data on a human-machine interface at the solar skid.

It uses the same physical acts a pumping test needs after rig-up - starting/stopping and regulating a well pump and logging volumes and levels - at an institution-controlled site.

sources.system: Nabors PACE-R801 with Canrig robotics and SmartROS
sources.developer: Nabors Industries / Canrig (well drilled for ExxonMobil XTO)
sources.title: Nabors drills first well from fully automated land rig - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: Nabors' PACE-R801 land drilling rig, combining Canrig robotics with automated drilling software, reached total depth on its ... with an unmanned rig floor, i.e. machine handling of tubulars into and out of the wellbore in a purpose-built rig setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: running and retrieving a pipe string in a well. Setting a test pump on column pipe involves the same objects (threaded tubulars at a fixed wellhead), similar make-up torque precision, and shows machine handling of well tubulars is achievable only in a purpose-built rig environment.

sources.system: Pressure transducer / datalogger water-level recording (standard aquifer-test instrumentation)
sources.title: Pumping Tests :. Aquifer Testing 101
sources.claim: Pressure transducers with data loggers are the standard means of recording water levels in pumping tests, taking frequent readings unattended for long periods.
sources.transferJustification: Supports the measurement half of the task: the drawdown/recovery record that the pumping test must produce is already collected by machine, so the residual human work is rig-up and rate control.

tasks.label: Disinfect, reconstruct, and redevelop contaminated wells and water pumping systems, and clean and disinfect new wells in preparation for use.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New private domestic well just completed at a rural residence: driller measures water depth and casing volume, mixes and pours/injects chlorine solution into the casing, recirculates with a hose to wash the casing and pitless adapter, draws chlorinated water through the yard hydrant and household plumbing, lets it stand overnight, returns to purge to waste away from septic/vegetation, then collects a coliform sample for the lab. Muddy, uneven ground; hoses, chemicals, and drop-pipe handled by hand.

Rehabilitation/redevelopment of a fouled or bacteria-contaminated existing domestic, stock, or irrigation well: pull the submersible pump and drop pipe with a service rig, run a downhole camera, wire-brush and swab the casing/screen, work a surge block and airlift line, apply acid or chlorine chemical treatment, pump the well to waste until clear, reinstall pump and seal, disinfect and re-sample. Farm/rural site, variable well depth and construction, unknown obstructions downhole.

Rehabilitation, reconstruction, and disinfection of a municipal or industrial production well at a utility wellfield/pump house: rig up over the wellhead, pull column pipe and lineshaft/submersible pump, brush and chemically treat the screen, redevelop by swabbing/airlift/jetting, install liner or repair casing where needed, disinfect the well and discharge piping to AWWA C654, then sample and return to service under utility oversight.

Cleaning and disinfecting the pumping and storage system rather than the borehole itself: shock-chlorinating pressure tanks, pump-house piping, cisterns or storage tanks and distribution lines after a pump replacement, a flood-inundated wellhead, or a coliform hit; opening taps to draw chlorine through every fixture, holding contact time, flushing, and verifying residual. Home basement, crawlspace, or small pump house.

Development and decontamination of new monitoring/environmental or test wells before use: surge and purge the new well, airlift or bail sediment, steam-clean/decontaminate drilling tools and downhole equipment between holes, disinfect the well, and containerize purge water. Remediation or construction sites with mixed traffic and site-specific layouts.

sources.system: Welltec Well Cleaner / Well Miller robotic intervention tools
sources.title: Finding Petroleum - Welltec – precision robotics in the well
sources.claim: Welltec markets wireline-conveyed robotic downhole tools for oil and gas wells that remove scale and sand, perforate, and set barriers; the tools are conveyed and directed by a surface crew/operator, not autonomous, and operate in cased tubing of oil/gas wells rather than performing water-well disinfection, surging, or pump work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: downhole cleaning/scale milling in oil and gas wells. Transfer fails: the tools are surface-operator directed on wireline (autonomy unclear), work inside small-diameter production tubing, and do not perform chlorination, surge-block redevelopment, pump pulling, or bacteriological verification required by water-well disinfection and redevelopment.

sources.system: Geoquip well rehabilitation rig (hydraulic winch) and BoreSaver rehabilitation tools
sources.title: Well Rehabilitation Equipment - Geoquip Water Solutions
sources.claim: Dedicated water-well rehabilitation equipment sold to the trade is a skid- or trailer-mounted hydraulic winch operated by a human crew that raises and lowers brushes, swabs and surge tools; no autonomous control is offered.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (well rehabilitation/redevelopment). Shows the state of the art in ... trade is human-operated winches, brushes and chemical products, with no cited system that performs the cycle under machine control.

sources.system: ID-TEC Sewer Rehabilitation SERIES robots; ROV tank-cleaning/dredging machines
sources.title: Sewer rehabilitation robots | WaterWorld
sources.claim: In-pipe rehabilitation and cleaning robots used in water and sewer infrastructure are remotely controlled by an operator: cutting/milling robots for relined pipes and ROV tank-cleaning machines require an operator to place the machine and drive the cleaning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cleaning/reconstructing water-carrying conduits. Transfer fails on autonomy (continuous operator control) and on scope: these machines work in man-entry-scale horizontal pipes, not in 6-16 inch vertical well casings, and do not chlorinate, surge, or handle pumps.

sources.system: Epiroc SmartROC D65 autonomous surface drill rig
sources.title: Epiroc and Luck Stone launch first fully autonomous SmartROC D65 drill rig in US | Global Mining Review
sources.claim: The autonomous machinery actually deployed in this occupation is surface blasthole drilling: a fully autonomous Epiroc SmartROC D65 drills production holes at a Virginia quarry, an institution-controlled, surveyed bench area, but it performs drilling only, with no well servicing, chemical handling, or disinfection capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drilling holes in the earth, in the same occupation. Transfer fails: the rig autonomously positions and drills blastholes on a prepared bench; it cannot pull pumps, mix and inject chlorine, run brushes/surge blocks downhole, or sample and verify disinfection.

tasks.label: Withdraw drill rods from holes, and extract core samples.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Surface production/quarry blasthole drilling: on a prepared bench at an aggregates quarry or open-pit mine, the operator finishes a 20-60 ft hole (single- or multi-pass), retracts the string, breaks out each rod and racks it in the carousel, blows the hole clean, then trams to the next hole in ... pattern. Dozens of such rod withdrawals per shift, dusty, no core taken.

Construction and utility drilling/boring: track drill on a road cut, foundation or trench-shoring job drilling blast/anchor holes, and horizontal directional/auger boring under a street or easement. At completion the operator withdraws the drill steel or rods joint by joint and racks them in the carousel or rod box, working amid traffic control, utilities, mud and uneven ground.

Water well, geothermal loop and dewatering well drilling at a rural, residential or industrial site: after reaching depth or at a bit change the driller trips the full rod string out of the hole (15-30 joints of 20-30 ft pipe), breaking each joint with the spinner/breakout wrench and racking or laying down rods; hole may be caving, rods coated in mud; cuttings samples logged for the well record.

Mineral exploration diamond core drilling from a bush pad or underground drill cuddy: every 3-6 m run the driller drops the overshot, winches the inner tube up the rod string on the wireline, breaks the tube open, empties the core into trays in correct order and marks the run blocks; periodically trips the whole 100-500 m rod string out for a bit change. Core recovery, orientation and depth marking must be right.

Geotechnical and environmental soil boring at a building site, roadway or brownfield: driller withdraws augers/rods and retrieves split-spoon or Shelby-tube samplers at each interval, opens the sampler, extracts the soil core and containerizes/labels it for the boring log, then pulls the auger string at hole completion.

sources.title: Luck Stone, Epiroc launch 'first' autonomous drill
sources.claim: Epiroc's SmartROC D65 MKII autonomous surface drill was deployed at a Luck Stone quarry in Virginia (Sept 2025) and drills complete blasthole patterns, including hole cycles with rod handling, with no operator in the ....

sources.title: Epiroc and Luck Stone launch first fully autonomous SmartROC D65 drill rig in U.S. aggregate market

sources.claim: Nabors' Canrig RZR robotics module, retrofitted to land rig X29 and used to drill multiple horizontal wells for ExxonMobil ..., autonomously makes and breaks connections and trips pipe in and out of the hole with no crew on the floor or in the derrick.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tripping drill pipe out of an oil/gas well. Withdrawing drill rods from a hole is the same physical operation - hoisting the string, breaking threaded steel joints with a wrench/spinner and racking the joints - on comparable steel tubulars at comparable precision, performed on a prepared well pad like a water-well or utility drill pad.
