sources.title: Tribe Tech's RC Drilling System Update
sources.claim: Tribe Technology's TTDS GC 700 autonomous reverse-circulation exploration rig, delivered to Australia in 2024, was still in commissioning with autonomous drilling yet to be demonstrated as of December 2024.

tasks.label: Inspect core samples to determine nature of strata, or take samples to laboratories for analysis.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Geotechnical soil test boring for a building or roadway project: driller advances hollow-stem auger, drives split-spoon samples at set depth intervals, opens the spoon, examines and describes the soil (color, texture, moisture, density/consistency), seals samples in labeled jars/bags, and hauls the sample box to the firm's soils lab. Open construction site or roadside, mud, weather, traffic.

Environmental site investigation drilling (direct-push/hollow-stem) on an industrial or brownfield property: soil recovered in acetate liners, inspected for staining, texture change and odor, field-screened, sub-sampled into preserved jars/VOC vials with labels and chain-of-custody paperwork, packed on ice and delivered to an analytical lab within holding times.

Mineral exploration diamond core drilling at a remote pad: crew pumps core from the split inner tube into core trays in order, marks depth blocks and recovery, gives the core a quick look to call rock type/alteration for the shift report, straps and trucks the trays over rough tracks to the core shack or logging facility.

Water well drilling (mud/air rotary) on rural or residential property: driller catches cuttings from the return at intervals, washes and inspects them to call the formation (sand, clay, gravel, shale, limestone) for the driller's log, and bags selected samples for the state survey or a lab.

Blasthole or RC grade-control drilling on an open-pit mine bench or quarry: driller collects cuttings from the cyclone/cone splitter into numbered bags at each hole, inspects the chips for ore/waste indications, and stages the bags for pickup by the mine's on-site assay lab.

Core shed / logging facility work at the end of the hole: driller delivers core boxes, lays trays out in run order under cover, photographs and checks recovery, then racks the boxes or hands sample intervals to lab intake with paperwork.

sources.title: LKAB starts core logging automation, digitalisation process with Minalyzer CS - International Mining
sources.claim: Minalyze's Minalyzer CS continuous XRF core scanner was implemented by iron ore miner LKAB (Kiruna, Malmberget) to automate and digitalise drill core logging, generating geochemistry, high-resolution images, RQD and specific gravity from core scanned directly in trays fed through the machine.

sources.title: This is Minalyzer CS | Minalyze: Swedish Mining Innovation
sources.claim: The Minalyzer scans core directly in trays of any material with minimal preparation, and can also scan chip trays, pellets and ... — i.e. the drill cuttings/chip samples a water-well or RC driller would inspect.
sources.transferJustification: Water-well and RC drillers inspect cuttings/chips rather than core; the same scanner handles chip trays, so the strata-determination output transfers to that sample type.

sources.title: Hyperspectral Core Imager | Epiroc US
sources.claim: Corescan's hyperspectral core imaging system (now Epiroc) automatically handles core trays, rock chips and ... on a 3-axis translation table and produces mineralogical logs of the scanned material.

sources.title: Multi-Sensor Core Logger (MSCL-S) – Geotek Ltd.
sources.claim: Geotek's Multi-Sensor Core Logger automatically moves whole or split sediment cores in liners and rock cores past a sensor array (imaging, density, colour, magnetic susceptibility, hyperspectral), giving depth-registered data used for stratigraphic analysis in geotechnical as well as mineral workflows.

sources.title: GeoTek Multi-Sensor Core Logger Facility | U.S. Geological Survey
sources.claim: The USGS operates a Geotek core-logger facility that automatically collects line-scan imagery and geophysical/geochemical measurements on soft sediment and rock cores and on discrete subsamples and hand samples — the soil and rock material a geotechnical or environmental driller submits.
sources.transferJustification: Substantiates automated inspection of soft-sediment (soil) cores and discrete subsamples, the material handled in geotechnical and environmental boring, not just hard rock core.

sources.title: Scott | Rocklabs AMS Prep Line
sources.claim: Rocklabs' AMS Prep Line, using collaborative robotics with RFID-tracked trays, cups and vials, runs the sample receipt-to-preparation workflow in Mineral Resources' Ken's Bore minesite laboratory, doubling sample capacity while removing manual handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laboratory intake, registration, splitting and preparation of drill samples. It covers the 'samples to the laboratory for analysis' leg once samples are presented to the cell — same granular rock/soil samples, same labelling and tracking requirement.

sources.title: Smarter Blast Hole Sampling: Methods, Equipment & Results — IMA Engineering
sources.claim: IMA Engineering's drill-mounted Blast Hole Sampler-Analyzer samples cuttings automatically every 20–30 cm of drilling depth and analyses them on-line at the rig, delivering ore/waste (strata) determinations in real time; the system is field-proven across gold, nickel-copper, iron and limestone operations and is designed for autonomous drill rigs.

sources.title: Sampling and Analysis Solutions for Mine Grade Control by Ima Engineering | Africa Mining Insight
sources.claim: IMA's Autosampler, mounted on production drills, automates the collection, splitting and bagging of blasthole cuttings samples on the bench, preserving the geological structure in the bag for ore/waste boundary recognition.

sources.system: TruScan (Veracio, formerly Boart Longyear geological data services)
sources.title: Veracio’s TruScan chosen by Idaho Copper to scan cores - Canadian Mining Journal
sources.claim: Veracio's TruScan core scanning platform is sold commercially as a service; Idaho Copper contracted it to scan and measure roughly 18,300 m of drill core, showing automated core scanning is used in place of manual logging at production scale.

tasks.label: Retract augers to force discharge dirt from holes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Geotechnical/environmental soil-test borings with hollow-stem or solid-stem augers from a truck- or track-mounted rig at sites taken as found (road shoulders, parking lots, fields, back yards). Every few feet and at hole completion the driller raises the auger column, spins/scrapes cuttings off the flights beside the hole, and breaks out 5-ft flights; sticky clay, cobbles, caving sand, and nearby traffic or property owners are routine.

Drilled shaft / caisson foundation work on a building or bridge construction site: a large-diameter Kelly auger is run down a few feet, hoisted clear of the hole, and shaken/spun off onto a spoil pile beside the shaft, cycle after cycle, with casing, slurry, obstructions, rebar cages, and other trades working nearby.

Utility pole, sign, light-standard, or fence-post holes augered with a truck-mounted auger/digger derrick along road rights-of-way, easements, and yards; the auger is repeatedly retracted and spun to sling spoil beside the hole, close to traffic, overhead conductors, and buried utilities.

Water-well or monitoring-well drilling on rural or residential property, augering overburden with hollow-stem augers; augers pulled and cleared of cuttings, spoil piled or drummed, before setting casing/screen. Access is by farm lane or back yard, ground is unimproved and varies hole to hole.

Horizontal auger boring under a road or railroad from a jacking pit: the auger string inside the casing conveys spoil back to the machine, and the augers are retracted section by section to clear packed spoil and muck out the pit. Confined pit, groundwater, mixed soils, spoil handled by hand and by excavator.

Production/blasthole pattern drilling on a prepared quarry or open-pit mine bench (surveyed pattern, graded bench, controlled access): the driller completes each hole, retracts and racks the drill string, and clears the hole of cuttings so it stands open for charging.

sources.title: Epiroc and Luck Stone launch first fully autonomous SmartROC D65 drill rig in U.S. aggregate market
sources.claim: Epiroc's SmartROC D65 MKII surface drill has been deployed at Luck Stone's US quarry operating at GMG Level 4 full autonomy, executing complete drill patterns (hole cycle including drill-string handling and hole completion) with no operator in the ..., under remote supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended completion of the full hole cycle by a hydraulic earth-drill rig, which includes withdrawing the drill string from the hole and leaving the hole clear of cuttings. Same machine class, same heavy steel down-hole tooling, same loose tolerance on where spoil ends up as when an auger is retracted to discharge dirt; the environment (a prepared, access-controlled working bench) is at least as demanding as a structured facility.

sources.system: Epiroc SmartROC D65 MKII Autonomous at Iron Bridge
sources.title: Autonomous approach to drill rig development
sources.claim: An autonomous SmartROC D65 MKII working a drill pattern at the Iron Bridge mine completes a hole, retrieves its drill pipes and moves itself to the next hole in ... sequence, continuing through blasting and operator breaks.
sources.transferJustification: Confirms that the retraction and stowing of the down-hole string at the end of each hole is executed autonomously, which is the machine action closest to retracting augers to force spoil out of a hole.

sources.system: Cat MD6250/MD6310 with MineStar Command for drilling
sources.title: Caterpillar Drill Rigs Hit Autonomous Milestone
sources.claim: Three fully autonomous Cat surface drill rigs (MD6250 and MD6310) running MineStar Command for drilling and supervised by a single remote operator passed one million metres drilled at the Mt Arthur South mine; Command for drilling automates the whole drill cycle and tramming across a blast pattern.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous execution of complete drilling cycles (collar, drill, retract string, clear hole, tram) at production volumes on prepared benches. Demonstrates that string retraction and hole clearing by a large earth-drill rig is reliably autonomous at worker quality in a controlled outdoor industrial setting.

sources.title: Machine Automation | Epiroc US
sources.claim: Epiroc's surface rig control system provides AutoDrill and automatic rod-handling (Auto-RHS, auto pick-up of drill rods) so the rig drills a hole to target depth autonomously after a few button presses.
sources.transferJustification: Automated rod handling is the machine equivalent of tripping an auger string out of the hole and racking flights; it substantiates that string retraction can be performed without hands-on operator control when the tooling is presented to the machine as designed.

sources.title: Automatic Shake-Off for Kelly drilling tools | Liebherr
sources.claim: Liebherr sells an Automatic Shake-Off function for Kelly drilling rigs that performs the auger/bucket emptying motion beside the borehole automatically once commanded, with operator-set rotation angle and speed; the operator still runs the surrounding cycle from the cab.
sources.transferJustification: This is the task itself (emptying an extracted auger beside the hole) rendered as a machine-executed motion on production foundation rigs, but it is initiated by an operator in the cab, so it is treated as non-autonomous and only corroborates that the motion is within machine control.

sources.title: Assistance Systems | BAUER AG
sources.claim: Bauer's B-Tronic assistance package for Kelly drilling rigs includes one-directional and bi-directional spoil discharge assistants that empty the drilling tool automatically by rotational movement of the rotary ..., on operator-manned rigs.
sources.transferJustification: Directly matches the discharge half of the task on the actual machine class used for drilled shafts, but it is an operator-triggered assistant inside a manned drilling cycle, so it cannot by itself support a positive autonomy judgment.

sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem converts standard excavators into fully autonomous trenching machines that have been used on utility-scale solar construction sites; the same company's RPD 35 autonomously surveys and drives solar piles on those sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soil excavation and spoil placement on construction sites taken as found. It shows heavy foundation/earthmoving autonomy at E3, but the tool is a bucket and the RPD drives piles rather than augering, so neither substantiates retracting an auger and shedding adhering spoil in an unstructured setting; it is cited to bound the E3 judgments.

tasks.label: Monitor drilling operations, by checking gauges and listening to equipment to assess drilling conditions and to determine the need to adjust drilling or alter equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Water-well drilling: operator at a rotary/air-hammer rig on a rural or residential property watches penetration-rate, air/mud pump pressure, rotary torque and pulldown gauges and listens to the compressor, hammer and drill string to judge formation changes, bit wear or lost circulation, and to decide whether feed, rotation or fluid should be changed.

Blasthole drilling at a surface mine or quarry: operator in the cab of a rotary/DTH blasthole rig monitors pulldown pressure, rotation torque, bit air pressure, rate-of-penetration readouts and vibration/chatter sounds across a pattern of holes, deciding when to back off, change rods, or flag a worn bit.

Geotechnical/environmental soil boring and core sampling with a track or truck-mounted rig at construction and site-investigation locations: operator tracks hydraulic pressures, head torque, advance rate and rod chatter/sound to detect boulders, refusal, voids or core blockage and decide on adjustments.

Horizontal directional boring for utility installation along streets and easements: operator monitors thrust/pullback force, rotary torque, drilling-fluid pressure and locator/steering readouts and listens to the power unit and mud pump to judge bore conditions and decide whether to slow feed, increase fluid, or ream.

Underground mine development drilling (jumbo/longhole): operator watches percussion, feed and flushing pressure gauges on the rig control screen and listens for rod jamming or hollow rock, deciding whether to reduce feed, re-collar, or change steel.

Foundation drilling (large-diameter auger, caisson, or micropile) on building sites: operator monitors crowd/torque and hydraulic gauges and listens to the rotary gearbox and engine load to judge hard strata, tool binding, or hole instability and decide on adjustments.

roles.title: Explosives Workers, Ordnance Handling Experts, and Blasters
aliases: Explosive Detection Canine Handler (Explosive Detection K9 Handler)
roles.description: Place and detonate explosives to demolish structures or to loosen, remove, or displace earth, rock, or other materials. May perform specialized handling, storage, and accounting procedures.

tasks.label: Examine blast areas to determine amounts and kinds of explosive charges needed and to ensure that safety laws are observed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Aggregate/limestone quarry production shot: before loading, the blaster walks the drilled bench, dips each hole for depth and water, checks for collapsed holes, voids and mud seams, profiles front-row burden against the irregular face, notes distance to crest and nearest structures, then fixes powder factor, product (ANFO vs. emulsion/water-resistant), decking and stemming, and confirms burden/stemming satisfy state and MSHA rules.

Large open-pit coal or metal mine production blast: pattern drilled by rigs logging depth and rock hardness; blaster/drill-and-blast engineer inspects the bench for hole condition, water, blocked or short holes, checks highwall and previous-shot backbreak, then sets per-hole explosive type and load, and verifies exclusion distances and blast-area security requirements.

Construction/civil rock excavation near occupied structures (road cut, building foundation, utility trench): examine the site and surroundings, pre-blast survey of nearby houses/wells/utilities, judge rock condition and hole burden, compute maximum charge weight per delay to meet scaled-distance vibration and airblast law, decide matting and exclusion zone.

Underground mine or tunnel development round: examine the drilled face and heading — check for butts/misfires from the previous round, loose ground and support, water in holes, hole depths and lookout — then determine charge per hole and initiation for the round and verify ventilation/ground-support safety rules.

Structural demolition survey: walk a building, chimney, silo or bridge, verify member sizes, materials and reinforcement against drawings, check hazards (asbestos, stored materials, weak floors), calculate charge per column/member, and confirm exclusion zone, permits and public-safety measures.

Pre- and post-blast safety examination of the blast area: before firing, confirm the area is clear and secured; after firing, examine the muckpile, face and remaining collars for undetonated product, misfires, cutoffs and unstable ground before crews and equipment re-enter.

sources.system: DIPPeR (Downhole Inspection, Probing and Perception Robot)
sources.developer: Australian Centre for Robotics, University of Sydney / Rio Tinto Sydney Innovation Hub
sources.title: Blast Hole Seeking and Dipping – The Navigation and Perception Framework in a Mine Site Inspection Robot
sources.claim: DIPPeR is an autonomous ground robot developed at the Rio Tinto Sydney Innovation Hub that drives an open-pit blast pattern, finds each blast hole from LiDAR, and lowers a sensor sonde down the hole to log depth and subsurface material — the core physical examination of a drilled pattern. Field trials at a WA mine (2023) and a Utah mine (2024).
sources.transferJustification: Hole dipping/downhole logging is the physical measurement step of examining a blast area: hole depth, water and downhole material determine how much and what kind of explosive each hole takes. Same objects (blast holes), same bench environment, same precision as the blaster's dipping.

sources.title: Study Introduces Robotic Inspection of Mine Blast Holes
sources.claim: Independent trade coverage confirms DIPPeR is an autonomous ground ... with LiDAR, GNSS/INS and a dipping actuator for inserting sensors into blast holes; performance in as-found conditions was site dependent (bowl-shaped cuttings at the Utah mine cut detection/alignment success to just over half of 70 holes).
sources.transferJustification: Corroborates the autonomy and hardware of the blast-hole inspection robot cited above; same transfer argument (hole inspection is the measurement core of blast-area examination).

sources.system: DIFFERENTIAL ENERGY / ΔE² with DYNOBULK MPU
sources.title: The difference is Differential.
sources.claim: Machine-collected drill data is converted algorithmically into a per-hole explosive loading plan (amount and energy distribution) that the delivery unit executes with automated gassing; commercially supplied to multiple Pilbara customers.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the determination half of the task (amount and kind/energy of charge per hole) is already computed from machine-collected bench data, but the delivery unit is operator-crewed, so this item cannot by itself support a positive robotic judgment.

sources.system: DJI Mavic 3 Enterprise UAV + Strayos photogrammetry/blast-design software
sources.developer: DJI / Strayos (case study by Wrocław researchers)
sources.title: Application of UAVs to Support Blast Design for Flyrock Mitigation: A Case Study from a Basalt Quarry
sources.claim: In an operating basalt quarry, a DJI Mavic 3 Enterprise UAV flying software-planned survey paths produced centimetre-accurate 3D models of the bench face used to find improper burden zones and correct blasthole charges, cutting flyrock range 42% near sensitive areas — the burden/flyrock element of blast-area examination.
sources.transferJustification: Face profiling and burden measurement is exactly the part of examining a blast area that sets front-row charges and satisfies flyrock safety requirements; the robot (UAV) performs the sensing, though engineers finalise the design.

sources.title: Top 10 Practical Uses For Autonomous Drones on Mine Sites
sources.claim: Docked autonomous drones deployed at production mine sites (BMA's Bowen Basin coal mines, Rio Tinto Gudai-Darri, Gold Fields Gruyere) fly scheduled and event-triggered missions, including post-blast capture of fragmentation, misfire-check and clearance imagery, without a surveyor entering the pit.
sources.transferJustification: Post-blast area examination for misfires and clearance is part of the safety-law half of this task; the docked drone autonomously captures the imagery, but human blasters still interpret it and must physically confirm the muckpile before re-entry.

sources.system: Autonomous Drilling System (Epiroc Pit Viper rigs)
sources.title: Mining robots: Rio Tinto doubles down on autonomous drilling
sources.claim: Rio Tinto operates autonomous blast-hole drilling systems across its Pilbara iron ore mines, with one remote operator supervising several rigs; the rigs drill the pattern and log drilling data on the bench without an on-board operator.
sources.transferJustification: Blast-hole drilling is a related task on the same bench; the rigs' measure-while-drilling records of depth and rock hardness are the geological inputs a blaster gathers when examining a pattern, and they show unmanned machines working a production bench.

sources.title: Mining: Autonomous Mapping & Safety - Emesent
sources.claim: Hovermap-equipped drones autonomously map underground stopes, shafts and drives in GPS-denied conditions at major mines, and the resulting scans are used for evaluating blast designs; the system captures geometry only, not hole condition or charge determination.
sources.transferJustification: Underground void/face scanning is the data-capture part of examining an underground blast area; it does not cover face inspection for butts/misfires, hole condition, or the round's charge determination.

sources.system: Spot with Enhanced Autonomy Package / Autowalk
sources.title: Automated Construction Site Documentation
sources.claim: Spot legged robots live on construction sites with a charging dock and run programmed Autowalk missions autonomously, capturing 360 imagery and laser scans and navigating obstacles and changing layouts without operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous reality capture on an as-found jobsite is the closest analogue to walking a demolition structure or construction blast site, but it produces documentation only — no member-by-member charge determination or regulatory safety verification.

tasks.label: Tie specified lengths of delaying fuses into patterns in order to time sequences of explosions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-pit mine or quarry production bench: after loading, the blaster walks a multi-row pattern of dozens to hundreds of drilled holes and ties the initiation network - snapping shock-tube downlines into surface delay connectors (or clipping detonating-cord trunklines and MS connectors, or wiring electronic detonator leads) per a designed timing sequence - over drill cuttings, loose rock and mud, in wind, rain or heat, then re-walks the pattern to verify every connection before hooking the lead-in line.

Construction blasting (road cut, building foundation, utility trench, pipeline ditch): a small pattern of roughly 5-50 holes on irregular, sloping or confined ground close to structures; the blaster ties downlines into the specified surface delay pattern, routes trunklines out from under blasting mats, and connects the lead line.

Underground mine or tunnel development round: at a freshly charged face in a confined, wet, muck-strewn heading, the crew connects burn-cut, relief, perimeter and lifter hole detonator leads / shock tubes into the specified delay sequence (or hooks them to a bus wire) and runs the initiation line back from the face.

Structural demolition of a building, stack or bridge: dozens to hundreds of charges on columns, beams and webs across several floors are linked with detonating-cord trunklines and branch lines (knotted or clipped), with delay connectors set between floors and sections to produce the collapse sequence; work occurs in a partially stripped structure with debris, stairs, ladders and variable geometry.

Specialized field work: seismic shot-hole strings, avalanche-control charges, ditching shots, and military/EOD demolition where safety (time) fuse is cut to specified lengths, crimped to caps, and cord ring-mains or fuse trains are tied to sequence multiple charges, in remote or improvised outdoor locations.

sources.title: ABB, Boliden and LKAB complete successful testing of industry-first automated robot charger for increased safety in underground mines
sources.claim: ABB's Robot Charger uses machine vision and robot arms to automatically detect blastholes and charge them at an underground mine face, including a second robot arm that assembles the primer and detonator; tested with Boliden and LKAB at Garpenberg.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic charging of blastholes. It shows robot arms autonomously locating holes and assembling/handling live primer-detonator hardware, i.e. the initiation components involved in tie-in; it does not itself tie a delay network into a timing pattern.

sources.system: Komax Omega 750 S / Omega 740-750 block loader
sources.title: Komax Introduces the Omega 750 S: Revolutionizing Fully Automated Wire Harness Assembly - Wiring Harness News
sources.claim: Komax's Omega 750 S is a commercially sold, fully automatic machine that produces wire harnesses, cutting flexible conductors and inserting their ends into connector blocks on both sides without operator involvement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated wire-harness assembly. Modern tie-in is cutting/handling flexible linear lines (shock tube, det cord, detonator legwires) to specified lengths and seating their ends in specified connector positions per a plan - the same class of deformable-linear-object handling at similar precision, done here in a purpose-built fixtured machine cell.

sources.title: Omega 745/755: fully automated wire harness production | Komax
sources.claim: Komax fully automatic harness machines monitor each insertion and verify that every terminal is correctly locked in its housing, with connector housings fed automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated connector insertion with in-process verification. Blast tie-in requires each downline to be fully seated in its delay connector and then checked; this machine performs and self-verifies that connection at production reliability in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Avatel (Epiroc Boomer M2C carrier + Orica LOADPlus / WebGen 200)
sources.title: Epiroc, Orica secure Newcrest Cadia trial for commercial Avatel charging system - International Mining
sources.claim: The leading mechanized underground charging rig, Epiroc/Orica Avatel, does not perform tie-in robotically: it is run by an operator from the cab and uses WebGen wireless initiation specifically to remove the tie-in step from the charging cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized underground charging. The industry's most advanced charging rig avoids tie-in with wireless detonators rather than automating the tying of delay networks, evidencing that no fielded robot performs this task at a face.

sources.title: TieBot: Learning to Knot a Tie from Visual Demonstration through a Real-to-Sim-to-Real Approach
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous robot knot-tying with flexible cord remains at laboratory success rates well below production reliability (50% for a dual-arm knot-tying system).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous knot tying in flexible cord, the manipulation used when detonating-cord trunklines and branch lines are knotted. Demonstrated success rates are far below the near-zero-defect reliability a blast initiation network requires.

sources.title: Blast Hole Seeking and Dipping -- The Navigation and Perception Framework in a Mine Site Inspection Robot
sources.claim: Autonomous field robots working on open-pit blast patterns (DIPPeR) navigate the bench and position a sensor down each blasthole for inspection; the demonstrated field capability is hole seeking and dipping, not connecting initiation networks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous operation on an open-pit blast pattern. It bounds what field robots do on benches today - navigation and probe insertion - and provides no manipulation of shock tube, det cord or delay connectors.

tasks.label: Place safety cones around blast areas to alert other workers of danger zones, and signal workers as necessary to ensure that they clear blast sites prior to explosions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-pit mine or aggregate quarry production shot: before firing, the blaster drives the perimeter of a several-hundred-foot exclusion zone over rough benches and haul roads, sets cones, portable barricades and 'blast area - do not enter' signs at ramp and haul-road entries, posts guards, then sounds the siren and radios each equipment operator, drill crew and plant operator until all are confirmed clear. Dust, uneven muck, pit layout changing with every shot.

Construction blasting for a highway rock cut, pipeline trench or building foundation next to an active public road: cones and warning signs set on the shoulder, sidewalk and stopped-traffic approaches, flaggers positioned, the site swept for laborers and inspectors, air-horn signals given before the shot. Mixed public traffic, mud, site layout changing day to day.

Underground mine or tunnel round: barricades, warning lights, tape and signs hung across drift entries, cross-cuts and travelways leading to the face; the blaster checks working places, tags off access and signals crews out over the mine phone before firing. Dark, wet, uneven ground, headings that move every cycle.

Urban structural demolition/implosion: cones, barrier tape and barricades placed around the building perimeter, adjacent sidewalks and street closures; the structure and surrounding blocks swept for stragglers with police and spotters, then horn and radio countdown signals confirming everyone is clear.

Military demolition range or ammunition-plant disposal operation: cones, range flags and markers placed at gated access roads, paved pads and control-point approaches; personnel accounted for by radio roll-call, siren sounded and all-clear confirmed before initiation. Fixed range layout, controlled access, standard equipment.

Small rural job - seismic shot-hole, boulder or stump blasting, or a utility trench on private property: a few cones set on a gravel drive or two-track approach, verbal and hand signals to a two- or three-person crew plus any landowner or bystander before firing.

sources.system: FANUC R-2000iC/125L and M-410iB material-handling/palletizing robots
sources.title: Material Handling Robots | FANUC America
sources.claim: Industrial six-axis robots in fenced cells autonomously pick presented items and place them at programmed positions at production rates - the motion class needed to set standard cones or barricades from a magazine onto marked positions in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: palletizing / material handling. Traffic cones and barricades are rigid 5-10 kg objects; setting them at known coordinates from a presented stack is the same grasp-transport-place cycle at looser tolerance, inside a fenced cell that keeps people out.

sources.developer: Hong Kong Highways Department with Hong Kong Productivity Council
sources.title: Robot System for Placement and Collection of Traffic Cones and Warning Lanterns at High Speed Roads - Highways Department
sources.claim: A truck-mounted robot system with cameras, LiDAR and robot arms picks traffic cones and warning lanterns from an on-board bay and places or collects them on high-speed roads; prototype built 2019, upgraded 'Roadbot 2' still in detailed design, with the carrier vehicle driven by a person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: highway lane-closure cone placement. Same objects and placement tolerance as marking a blast danger zone; establishes machine-controlled grasp and placement of cones from a presented magazine.

sources.system: Autonomous traffic-cone deployment/retrieval mobile robot platform (Applied Sciences 15(19):10845)
sources.title: YOLO-Based Object and Keypoint Detection for Autonomous Traffic Cone Placement and Retrieval for Industrial Robots
sources.claim: A purpose-built skid-steer UGV carrying 30 cones with a collaborative arm, gripper and GNSS-RTK executes cone deployment and retrieval missions autonomously from operator-defined map positions; a research prototype, evaluated mainly on perception, with no demonstrated personnel-clearance or signalling function.

sources.title: AutoCone: An OmniDirectional Robot for Lane-Level Cone Placement
sources.claim: Omnidirectional self-driving cone units position themselves to lane-level accuracy (2 cm RTK) on highway surfaces, but a human operator must first set each unit down on the road, and the work stops at delineation - no clearance sweep or worker signalling.

sources.developer: Highway Care Ltd (to National Highways specification)
sources.title: Falcon 100 Automated Cone Laying Machine (ACLM) - Highway Care
sources.claim: The cone-laying machine actually approved and sold for live road use drops and collects cones from a truck, but every operation is run by a person in the cab and the truck is human-driven - no autonomous set-up of a closure.

sources.title: AI-powered Autonomous Drones Are Changing Critical Business Operations
sources.claim: Autonomous drone-in-a-box systems deployed at working mines fly patrols and confirm that the safety zone is clear before planned blasts - the surveillance and clearance half of the task at a real blast site, with no ability to place cones or barricades.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pre-blast exclusion-zone verification at open-pit mines. It covers the 'ensure workers are clear' element in the task's own E3 setting but not the physical placement of cones or barricades, so it cannot by itself complete an instance.

tasks.label: Place explosive charges in holes or other spots; then detonate explosives to demolish structures or to loosen, remove, or displace earth, rock, or other materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Surface mine / quarry production bench blast: crew works a drilled bench pattern of 30-200 large-diameter vertical holes 15-30 m deep, dips holes, lowers primers/detonators, loads bulk ANFO or emulsion from a mobile manufacturing truck, stems each hole with crushed rock, ties in surface delays, clears the area and fires. Outdoor, dusty, uneven muck-covered bench, weather variable, mine controls access.

Construction / civil rock excavation blast: road cut, pipeline trench, building foundation or site pad, often close to houses, roads or utilities. Shallow small-diameter holes hand-loaded with cartridges or bagged/bulk product, stemmed, tied in with shock tube, heavy blasting mats placed by excavator, seismographs set, area guarded, then fired.

Underground mine or tunnel round: charging a development face or production long-holes with primer/detonator assemblies and pumped bulk emulsion from a charging rig or hose, in a drift with variable ground, water and muck; crew then retreats and fires the round remotely (wired or wireless initiation).

Explosive demolition of a structure (building, chimney, bridge, industrial plant): partially pre-weakened structure, charges (shaped/cutting charges, dynamite in drilled holes) placed on columns, girders and piers at many levels, wrapped and covered, tied into a delay sequence, exclusion zone established, then detonated.

Miscellaneous field shots: seismograph shot holes in remote terrain, secondary breaking of oversize boulders, ditch/stump blasting, and blow-in-place disposal of unexploded ordnance with donor charges at ranges or field sites; small charges hand-placed, hooked up and fired.

Avalanche-control shot: explosive charge delivered to a start zone on a steep, snow-covered slope above a highway, railway or ski area, by hand-throw, tram, helicopter or fixed dispenser, then detonated to release the slab; cold, wind, poor visibility, no controlled premises.

sources.title: ABB, Boliden and LKAB complete successful testing of industry-first automated robot charger for increased safety in underground mines
sources.claim: ABB's Robot Charger, tested at Boliden's Garpenberg underground mine, automatically detects drilled boreholes in a rock face and fills them with explosives ... without people present at the face.

sources.title: Automated robot charger pilot solution for remote blasting of rock face - Mining Automation | ABB
sources.claim: ABB documents the full autonomous charging cycle: vision-based hole detection over the face, reach/charging plan, detonator cassette taken from a magazine and fixed to a primer, hose pushed to hole bottom, explosive pumped while retracting, then on to the next hole; demonstrated 1 km underground at Garpenberg.

sources.system: ABB robotic explosive charging system (IRB4600 + IRB1300 on hydraulic boom)
sources.developer: ABB Mining R&D / ABB Corporate Research / KTH
sources.title: Behavior Trees in Industrial Applications: A Case Study in Underground Explosive Charging (arXiv:2403.19602)
sources.claim: The ABB engineering team's own paper on the underground charging robot (two ABB manipulators on a hydraulic boom that assemble charges and place them in holes on the ...) states the system still requires human supervision and feedback rather than fully unattended running.

sources.title: Normet introduces underground explosives charging system | Global Mining Review
sources.claim: Normet's commercially offered Charmec Revo underground charging unit uses a servo-robotic arm with machine vision and uploaded borehole maps to guide the charging hose to holes, but the machine is remote-controlled by an operator.

sources.system: Avatel (Epiroc Boomer M2 carrier + Orica explosives/WebGen)
sources.title: Orica, Epiroc and Agnico Eagle carry out world-first development charging milestone at Kittila - International Mining
sources.claim: Orica/Epiroc's Avatel semi-automated development charging machine loaded and fired a complete live development round at Agnico Eagle's Kittila underground mine, but the whole cycle is executed by an operator sitting in the machine's cab.

sources.system: Enaex Open Pit Robotics (Mine-iTruck, Stemming-iTruck, RoboPrimer, iControl)
sources.title: Open Pit Robotics - Enaex Australia & New Zealand
sources.claim: Enaex's open-pit blasting robotics fleet performs priming, bulk loading, stemming and firing, but the loading and stemming trucks are remote-controlled from a control station rather than autonomous.

sources.title: Enaex continues to innovate for mining's bright future - International Mining
sources.claim: Enaex's surface mobile manufacturing unit working at a Chilean operation is trammed manually and then switched to remote-control mode for hole loading; the fully autonomous surface truck is still in design and software development.

sources.title: Surface Automation solutions | Orica
sources.claim: Orica, the largest commercial explosives supplier, states that automation of the surface blasting cycle is not yet achieved and remains some years away.

sources.system: Alford Technologies demolition robots (with EOD-type remote vehicles)
sources.title: Ten robots and Finnish explosives used in Didcot demolition - Construction News
sources.claim: Remote-controlled robots scanned a damaged power-station structure and carried and planted cutting charges on its columns for an explosive demolition at Didcot, showing charge placement on structures is done by teleoperated machines, not autonomous ones.

sources.system: AVSS Precision Avalanche Management System (PAMS) with SnowDart charges
sources.title: AVSS Completes First Live Avalanche Drone Testing In Jasper National Park - DroneXL
sources.claim: AVSS's Precision Avalanche Management System flies drones under autonomous flight planning to predetermined avalanche start zones and drops SnowDart explosive charges to trigger controlled slides; live explosive tests were completed in Jasper National Park under a Transport Canada certificate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: avalanche-control shooting. The robot delivers a live explosive charge to a designated spot on natural terrain and it is detonated there, which is the same place-and-detonate act the blaster performs on the slope.

sources.system: MONTIS avalanche control drone (Freefly Alta X airframe)
sources.title: MONTIS Avalanche Control Drone Deploys New Electronic Ignition - Drone Amplified
sources.claim: Drone Amplified's MONTIS avalanche-control drone, operated with Alaska DOT&PF, flies to target slopes and deploys and ignites explosive charges; it received FAA approval for US operations in July 2026, but is flown by a remote pilot in command under visual line of sight.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: avalanche-control shooting; the drone performs the same delivery-and-detonation of a live charge on an uncontrolled slope, but flight is under a remote pilot, so it is treated as teleoperated.

tasks.label: Insert, pack, and pour explosives, such as dynamite, ammonium nitrate, black powder, or slurries into blast holes; then shovel drill cuttings, admit water into boreholes, and tamp material to compact charges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large surface mine bench (coal, metal, industrial minerals): blaster works a drilled pattern of large-diameter (150-310 mm) vertical holes, dips holes, pumps bulk ANFO/emulsion from a mobile manufacturing unit hose, dewaters or uses water-resistant product in wet holes, then stems each hole with drill cuttings or aggregate delivered by stemming truck/loader. Rough but graded bench, mine-controlled access, exclusion zones.

Quarry/aggregate or small mine bench: 75-140 mm holes, mixed loading - bulk product from a truck hose for some holes, hand-poured bagged ANFO or cartridge decks for others, hole dipping, water in some holes, stemming shoveled or poured back into each collar and tamped.

Construction rock excavation: road cuts, utility/trench blasting, foundation and site work, often near structures. Small-diameter (50-90 mm) holes on irregular, ungraded terrain; packaged cartridges or bagged product inserted and tamped with a wooden pole, water bailed out or admitted, cuttings shoveled in as stemming.

Underground mine or tunnel charging: development-face rounds and production rings; primer/detonator assembly pushed to hole bottom with a charging hose and pumpable emulsion, or cartridges inserted and tamped, in a drift at an unsupported face with confined space, dust and water.

Structural demolition: charges packed into holes drilled in concrete columns, walls or steel members inside a building or bridge being taken down; each charge sized, inserted, packed/stemmed and the member wrapped; access via scaffolds, stairs and partially deteriorated structure.

sources.system: Jevons Robotics ARTEV6000 (Automated Rugged Terrain Electric Vehicle)
sources.title: Jevons ARTEV to take part in 'world first' explosives delivery at Fortescue's Eliwana - International Mining
sources.claim: Jevons Robotics' ARTEV6000, a 6 t battery-electric rugged-terrain robot, uses vision and hole-finding technology to position over blast holes and deploy bulk explosives and stemming material; it ran stemming operations at Fortescue's Eliwana open-pit iron ore mine with ANFO deployment as the next phase.

sources.title: Jevons Robotics launches ARTEV1000 with Orica among the first to adopt - International Mining
sources.claim: Trade press reporting of the ARTEV1000 launch states the larger ARTEV6000 achieved autonomous stemming and explosives loading milestones through 2024/2025; the smaller ARTEV1000 automates hole dipping, stemming and hose handling in small-diameter patterns on constrained benches, Orica took delivery of the first unit, and both models are commercially available.

sources.system: Jevons Robotics ARTEV1000 pre-split loading robot
sources.title: Jevons Robotics deal with Newmont to deploy auto pre-split loading robot - International Mining
sources.claim: Newmont Australia is deploying an ARTEV1000 fitted with an automated packaged pre-split loading payload to load explosives into highwall pre-split holes without personnel at the hole.
sources.transferJustification: Pre-split loading is loading packaged (cartridge-type) explosives into small-diameter drilled holes on a bench - the same insert-and-pack operation, objects and precision as hand-loading small holes in the rated task.

sources.title: ABB, Boliden and LKAB complete successful testing of industry-first automated robot charger for increased safety in underground mines
sources.claim: The ABB Robot Charger detects drilled ... an underground rock face with a vision system and charges them with explosives with the cycle fully automated; testing was completed at Boliden's Garpenberg zinc mine with LKAB.

sources.system: Underground explosive charging robot (ABB IRB4600 + IRB1300 on hydraulic boom)
sources.title: Behavior Trees in Industrial Applications: A Case Study in Underground Explosive Charging (IEEE Xplore)
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed case study describes the underground charging robot (two ABB industrial manipulators on a hydraulic boom) that assembles detonator/primer/emulsion charges and places them in ... tunnel rock face under autonomous behaviour-tree control with human supervision.

sources.system: Jevons Robotics ARTEV6000 with RCT remote control
sources.title: Mitigating the risk of loading blast holes with Jevons Robotics & RCT technology | Epiroc US
sources.claim: The ARTEV platform is also operated in line-of-sight or teleremote mode using RCT remote-control hardware, replacing manual blast QA, loading and stemming with one battery-electric machine able to work on any bench condition including severely contoured or cavity-filled ground.

sources.system: CSIRO automated blast hole charging arm (Mobile Charging Unit)
sources.title: Blast Hole Charging Automation - Robotics, CSIRO Research
sources.claim: CSIRO developed and demonstrated an automated Mobile Charging Unit arm that finds pre-drilled blast holes with a scanning laser and inserts the emulsion charging hose using visual servoing, for underground development charging.

tasks.label: Mark patterns, locations, and depths of charge holes for drilling, and issue drilling instructions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-pit mine or large quarry production bench: after the bench is mucked and cleaned, the blaster walks the bench with a GNSS rover/tape, lays out the burden-and-spacing pattern relative to the crest and free face, spray-paints or flags each collar, assigns a depth (incl. subdrill) for each hole from bench-floor elevation, and hands the drill operators the pattern sheet or digital plan with angles and depths.

Open construction rock excavation (highway/rail cut, large building pad, dam or pipeline right-of-way): stripped rock surface in a large graded working area; blaster/driller lays out the pattern with GNSS or tape from stakes, paints collar points, sets each hole's depth to design subgrade from the irregular top-of-rock, and briefs the drill crew.

Confined construction blasting near structures: utility/pipeline trench in a street, footing or basement excavation next to occupied buildings, benched slope work. Small tight patterns marked by hand with tape, paint and flagging on broken sloping rock; holes shortened or shifted for utilities, seams and vibration limits; hole-by-hole verbal instructions to a track-drill operator.

Underground mine drift or tunnel heading: the round pattern (cut, relievers, lifters, contour holes) is transferred to the newly exposed face - traditionally chalked or painted on the face from a survey line - with lookout angles and hole depth for the round given to the jumbo operator.

Structural demolition prep: blaster marks drill-hole locations, angles and depths on concrete columns, shear walls and piers (and burn/charge points on steel) throughout a multi-story structure being prepared for implosion, per the loading plan, amid pre-weakening debris, dust and no permanent lighting; instructs the drilling crew floor by floor.

Small-scale field work on unimproved ground: secondary/boulder blasting (choosing where to drill each irregular boulder by eye), ditch and stump blasting, avalanche and agricultural work, and staking seismic shot-point locations across fields, woods and wetland, marking with paint, lath or flagging and telling the driller the depth.

sources.system: Epiroc Hole Navigation System (HNS) with Surface Manager drill plans
sources.title: Hole Navigation System (HNS) | Epiroc
sources.claim: Epiroc's Hole Navigation System takes hole positions, angles and depths from a drill plan transferred to the rig as GPS coordinates, and the vendor states it removes the need for a person ... mark the bench - the machine performs the collar-location function this task describes.
sources.transferJustification: Same output as the task: hole pattern, location and depth realised on the bench. Autonomy is recorded as unclear (operator-driven rig with GPS guidance), so this item is used only as supporting context, not as a decisive item.

sources.system: Epiroc SmartROC D65 MKII (GMG Level 4 autonomy) at Luck Stone quarry, Virginia
sources.title: Epiroc and Luck Stone launch first fully autonomous SmartROC D65 drill rig in U.S. aggregate market
sources.claim: A fully autonomous surface blasthole drill executes an entire designed drill pattern on a working quarry bench with no operator in the ..., positioning itself at each designed collar and drilling to plan depth.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = drilling the pattern. The machine consumes the digital pattern and physically realises each hole location and depth on the bench, which is the accepted output that the blaster's marks and drilling instructions exist to produce.

sources.system: Sandvik AutoMine Surface Drilling AutoCycle with Leopard DI650i
sources.title: Sandvik launches AutoMine Surface Drilling AutoCycle for fully autonomous surface drilling fleet operation
sources.claim: Multiple surface drill rigs run a whole pattern autonomously from a control room, including tramming hole-to-hole, path planning, obstacle detection and ... of the working area.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = executing the blast pattern. Autonomous hole-to-hole positioning on a mine or quarry bench substitutes for physically marking each collar and instructing the driller.

sources.system: Epiroc Pit Viper autonomous drilling (incl. Rio Tinto Pilbara fleet)
sources.title: Epiroc's Pit Viper - the past, present and future | International Mining
sources.claim: Autonomous blasthole drilling from designed patterns is a mature, fleet-scale deployment in open-pit mines, with large improvements in hole spatial and depth accuracy over manual work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = pattern drilling. Demonstrates worker-quality (in fact better) realisation of designed hole locations and depths on open-pit benches with no person marking the bench or directing holes.

sources.date: 2025-06 (Series A coverage); in the field since 2021
sources.title: Civ Robotics Secures $7.5M Series A to Advance the Future of Construction Automation
sources.claim: An autonomous four-wheel-drive rover navigates outdoor construction sites and spray-paint marks thousands of designed coordinates per day to about 8 mm accuracy on rough, uneven terrain; used commercially by EPCs on solar farms, roads, earthworks and foundations since 2021.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = construction stakeout/layout marking: taking a coordinate file and paint-marking each point on open ground. That is physically the same act as marking charge-hole collars from a blast pattern, on the same kind of surface, at far tighter precision than blast layout requires.

sources.title: Video: Civ Robotics' robots can perform autonomous surveying | Equipment World
sources.claim: The layout rover marks coordinates in paint on the ground, announces the point description for the crew, and records ground elevation at each marked point.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = stakeout. Recording ground elevation at each marked point is what lets a per-hole depth be computed from the design subgrade, which is the depth half of this task, and the spoken point description is the issued instruction.

sources.system: Epiroc Advanced Boom Control (ABC) Total on Boomer face rigs; Sandvik DTi jumbos with iSURE and iNav total-station navigation
sources.title: Advanced Boom Control | Epiroc
sources.claim: Underground face drilling rigs navigate themselves in the heading from survey/total-station references and drill a full round automatically from a digital drill plan, so the round need not be chalked on the face.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = drilling the round. Automatic boom positioning to each planned hole on a navigated rig replaces the blaster's marking of the pattern on the face and the verbal depth/angle instructions to the jumbo operator.

sources.title: Hilti Unveils New Drilling Capabilities to BIM-Enabled Construction Jobsite Robot | Walls & Ceilings
sources.claim: A commercial construction robot locates itself inside a building from a digital model, then marks and drills holes at planned positions on ceilings and on vertical concrete walls between 0.9 m and 4.8 m height.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = model-driven hole layout and marking on concrete structural surfaces inside a building - the same physical act (locate the planned point on a column or wall and mark it) that demolition charge-hole layout requires, at tighter tolerance.

sources.title: Normet Xrock Launches the World's First Autonomous Rock-Breaking System, Xrock Autobreaker
sources.claim: An autonomous rock-breaking system at a grizzly/crusher station identifies oversized boulders, plans the strike point on each irregular rock and executes the sequence with nobody in the area.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = secondary breaking. Selecting a target point on an individual irregular boulder from perception is the same judgment a blaster makes when marking where to drill a boulder; it is demonstrated only at a fixed purpose-built breaker station, so it supports E1 only.

tasks.label: Compile and keep gun and explosives records in compliance with local and federal laws.
