tasks.label: Measure depths of drilled blast holes, using weighted tape measures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Large open-pit mine bench (surface coal, metal ore, taconite/industrial mineral): blaster walks a drilled production pattern of 100-300 vertical holes of 6.75-12 in diameter, drops a weighted tape in each hole to confirm depth against design, records water depth and finds collapsed/plugged holes before the loading trucks arrive; broken rock floor, drill-cuttings cones, dust, heat, snow or rain.

Aggregate quarry or mid-size surface mine bench (limestone, granite, trap rock) with 5-6.5 in holes: 30-100 holes per shot, blaster dips each hole with a weighted tape to verify depth and water, marks holes that have caved or been backfilled by drill cuttings, computes stemming and charge weights; uneven bench floor, edge of a highwall, weather exposed.

Small quarry, sand-and-gravel or small surface job with 3-4.5 in holes drilled by a track rig: shallow benches (15-40 ft), tight working room near the crest, holes frequently sloughing or wet; blaster hand-dips each hole with a weighted tape immediately before loading.

Civil construction blasting (highway rock cut, building foundation, trench/utility line, pipeline): 2.5-4 in holes, small irregular patterns on steep, muddy or congested ground close to structures and traffic; blaster dips holes for depth, checks for water and mud, adjusts loads hole by hole.

Underground mine or tunnel: charge crew checks depth of drilled holes in a development face round or of longhole/stope downholes before charging, using a weighted tape or charging rod to find blocked or short holes; confined, wet, poorly lit heading with rough rock walls.

Structure demolition and specialty work: holes drilled in concrete columns, walls and piers at varied heights and orientations, or secondary blasting of boulders and presplit lines on steep slopes; each hole gauged for depth before loading small charges.

sources.system: DIPPeR (Downhole Inspection, Probing and Perception Robot)
sources.developer: Rio Tinto Sydney Innovation Hub / Rio Tinto Centre for Mine Automation, University of Sydney
sources.title: Blast Hole Seeking and Dipping -- The Navigation and Perception Framework in a Mine Site Inspection Robot (arXiv 2508.13785)
sources.claim: DIPPeR, an autonomous tracked mine-site inspection robot, drives a drilled blast pattern, detects each hole through its drill-waste cone with LiDAR and lowers a sensor sonde into the hole ("dipping"); it was run at two production mines, in Western Australia (2023) and Utah (2024).
sources.transferJustification: Dipping a sonde to the bottom of a blast hole is the same physical act as dropping a weighted tape: same object (10 m deep, 200-400 mm blast hole in a bench), same centimetre precision, same setting.

sources.developer: University of Sydney / Rio Tinto Sydney Innovation Hub
sources.title: Blast Hole Seeking and Dipping: Navigation and Perception Framework in a Mine Site Inspection Robot, Robotics 14(12):173
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed version of the DIPPeR work: an autonomous navigation and perception framework for repetitive blast-hole inspection with precise down-hole sensor insertion, validated in real open-pit mine-site field experiments with noisy GPS and variable bench terrain.

sources.developer: IMDEX Limited with Universal Field Robots
sources.title: IMDEX | BLASTDOG™ Orebody Knowledge System
sources.claim: IMDEX BLASTDOG is a commercial robotic bench-logging service: a tracked robot deploys a 105 mm multi-sensor sonde down blast holes of 125-300 mm diameter between drilling and loading, supplying hole physicals (water level, void detection, verticality, volume specification for blasting) for each hole; the robot is semi-autonomous and supervised by an operator in a nearby vehicle.
sources.transferJustification: Wireline logging of a blast hole yields the hole's depth and water column as its base output; the physical action (running a probe to the hole bottom on every hole of the pattern before loading) is the tape-dipping task.

sources.title: BLASTDOG transforms bench scale data into real time decisions for open pit mining
sources.claim: IMDEX product manager, presenting at APCOM 2025, states BLASTDOG logs every blast hole in the window between drilling and loading at 1,500-1,700 m per day, in wet or dry holes and varied bench conditions, and that the unit is capable of full autonomy although currently run semi-autonomously with an operator at the side of the bench.
sources.transferJustification: Logging every hole of the pattern for depth-referenced physicals (including water level and voids) before loading replaces the blaster's dip-and-record pass over the same pattern.

sources.title: Better orebody understanding with Blast Dog from Imdex - Canadian Mining Journal
sources.claim: Blast Dog reached its first commercial contract in August 2022 at the Iron Bridge iron ore operation in the Pilbara (up to three units, staged), with the sensor carried on a tracked robotic platform that positions and aligns itself over holes across variable bench terrain.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: robotic probe insertion into every blast hole of a production pattern on an open-pit bench is the mechanised form of dipping holes with a weighted tape.

sources.title: Universal Field Robots – Australia's Robotics and Automation R&D Powerhouse (Australian Mining Review)
sources.claim: Trade coverage of the robot builder describes BLAST DOG as an autonomous system for multi-parameter ..., built on a two-tonne tracked excavator base using ROS/ROS2.

sources.title: ABB, Boliden and LKAB complete successful testing of industry-first automated robot charger for increased safety in underground mines
sources.claim: ABB's Robot Charger locates drilled holes in an underground rock face with a vision system and inserts charging hose/primer into them in a fully automated cycle; testing was completed with Boliden at Garpenberg and LKAB in 2023, with the system not yet reported in routine commercial service.
sources.transferJustification: Charging is a related task that includes finding each small-diameter face hole and running a hose to its bottom; however it is demonstrated only at development faces and as a pilot, so it does not establish worker-quality depth gauging of stope downholes or bench holes.

sources.system: Electroimpact accurate robot drilling cell (multi-function drilling/countersinking head with inspection probe)
sources.title: Advances in Automated Drilling for Aerostructures (SAE 2010-01-1836), Electroimpact white paper
sources.claim: Production robotic drilling cells for aerostructures perform automated in-process probing of each drilled hole, measuring hole diameter and countersink depth on fixtured workpieces presented to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated depth gauging of a drilled hole with a probe. It transfers to the E1 counterfactual only, where the drilled workpiece is fixtured and presented at a known position; precision far exceeds a weighted tape, but no traverse of an as-found blast pattern is involved.

tasks.label: Connect electrical wire to primers, and cover charges or fill blast holes with clay, drill chips, sand, or other material.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-pit metal or coal mine production bench: crew makes up primers (cast booster + electronic/shock-tube detonator), lowers them into 150-310 mm holes, bulk truck loads emulsion/ANFO, crew connects detonator leads into the surface harness and tests the circuit, then a stemming truck or loader backfills each hole with drill cuttings or crushed rock. Hundreds of holes, weather-exposed broken ground, hole conditions (water, collapse, depth) vary.

Quarry / aggregate bench shot: two- to four-person crew hand-loads 75-130 mm holes with cartridged product and ANFO, assembles primers with detonators, ties the shock-tube or det-cord surface network hole to hole, and stems each hole with drill cuttings or aggregate by hand, bucket or small stemming machine.

Underground hard-rock mine: charging a jumbo-drilled development face or production longholes - inserting a primer with detonator into each hole, charging emulsion or ANFO, hooking up the initiation circuit (or programming wireless detonators), occasionally plugging/stemming collars. Confined, wet, freshly blasted rock face, often unsupported ground.

Civil / construction blasting: road cut, trench, foundation or utility excavation; small-diameter holes drilled in irregular terrain, often near structures. Blaster primes cartridges with electric or shock-tube caps, lowers and connects them, stems each hole with drill cuttings or sand, and blasting mats are placed over the shot.

Structural demolition: shaped/kicker charges taped to steel or loaded into holes pre-drilled in concrete columns inside a standing building, wired or det-corded together floor by floor, drilled holes stemmed with clay, and columns wrapped with chain-link and geotextile. Cluttered multi-floor interior, no two structures alike.

Specialty shots: seismic exploration shot holes in remote terrain, avalanche-control charges, or land-clearing/boulder shots - charge or charge string primed and its wire connected, hole backfilled with cuttings, sand or clay. Access on foot, ATV or helicopter.

sources.title: Enaex claims world first completely robotic & autonomous underground explosives loading operation using its UG-iTruck - International Mining
sources.claim: Enaex's UG-iTruck carried out a claimed world-first 100% remote, robotic and autonomous ... underground development, with a robotic arm that positions and loads explosives at ..., assembles boosters and detonators robotically, and eliminates tie-in by using wireless detonators.

sources.title: Enaex autonomous UG-iTruck arrives at Codelco El Teniente - International Mining
sources.claim: The UG-iTruck was moved into Codelco's El Teniente, the world's largest underground copper mine, for use on tunnel development charging.

sources.title: Enaex continues to innovate for mining's bright future - International Mining
sources.claim: As of mid-2024 Enaex's robotic surface priming unit had only been tested at the company's own test grounds and was not in commercial use at client sites, while the UG-iTruck was already running at an underground operation; the surface Milodon MMU is remote-controlled from a control station rather than autonomous.

sources.title: Open Pit Robotics - Enaex
sources.claim: Enaex markets RoboPrimer as a robotic and autonomous priming solution for open-pit blasting, described as assembling, placing and connecting high explosives with robotic dexterity.

sources.title: Enaex y Codelco realizan la primera tronadura subterranea 100% teleoperada del mundo - Portal Minero
sources.claim: In July 2025 Enaex and Codelco completed a full tunnel face blast remotely at El Teniente with the UG-iTruck, which automates face inspection, hole scanning and cleaning, robotic assembly of boosters and detonators, emulsion manufacture, loading and wireless initiation; eight successful tests had been run at the mine.

sources.title: Epiroc Partners with Orica on Semi-Automated Explosives Delivery System - OEM Off-Highway
sources.claim: The commercially deployed Avatel underground charging rig (Epiroc/Orica, live blasting at Agnico Eagle's Kittila mine since 2022) mechanises face charging but keeps a human operator continuously controlling the booms from the machine cabin.

sources.system: ABB underground explosive charging robot (research prototype)
sources.developer: ABB Mining R&D / ABB Corporate Research with KTH
sources.title: Behavior Trees in Industrial Applications: A Case Study in Underground Explosive Charging (arXiv:2403.19602)
sources.claim: An ABB Mining R&D robotic system that assembles explosive charges and places ... an underground rock face still requires human supervision and feedback and cannot run fully autonomously.

sources.title: Open Pit Robotics - Enaex
sources.claim: Enaex's open-pit stemming machine, which fills loaded blastholes with gravel, is operated by remote control rather than autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stemming (covering charges/filling blast holes) on open-pit benches. It shows the mechanism exists but under continuous remote control, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion.

sources.system: Blast hole seeking and dipping mine site inspection robot (research platform, arXiv:2508.13785)
sources.title: Blast Hole Seeking and Dipping - The Navigation and Perception Framework in a Mine Site Inspection Robot
sources.claim: A mine-site inspection robot with a navigation and perception framework for seeking blast holes and inserting a dipping probe was field-trialled on active open-pit benches in Western Australia and Utah, in heat, snow and ice, between drilling and charging.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: locating blastholes on a live bench and inserting a probe into them - the same object and approach precision as inserting a primer or stemming a hole. Autonomy level of the full cycle could not be confirmed, so it is treated as supporting context only.

tasks.label: Lay primacord between rows of charged blast holes, and tie cord into main lines to form blast patterns.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Quarry or open-pit mine bench shot: 30-100 loaded holes in rows on a freshly drilled bench. Blaster walks the pattern with a reel of detonating cord, lays trunklines down and between rows over broken rock and drill cuttings, ties each hole's downline into the trunkline with knots or connector clips, adds surface delays, and runs the lead line off the bench. Dust, wind, rain, mud, uneven footing; loaded holes must not be disturbed.

Civil/construction rock blasting (highway cut, foundation, trench or pipeline ditching): small pattern of 10-40 holes on sloped, congested ground near structures, utilities and traffic control. Cord laid around obstacles, tied into main lines, then blasting mats placed. Tight schedule between other trades.

Underground development round or production ring (mine drift, tunnel face): downlines from each charged hole at the face are gathered and tied into a main detonating-cord line running back down the drift. Confined, dark, wet, muck-covered floor, loose rock overhead.

Structural demolition: charges placed on columns, beams and walls across multiple floors of a partly stripped building. Cord is run vertically and horizontally through the structure between charges, laced around loaded members and tied into trunk lines converging on the initiation point; debris, stairs, poor light.

Specialty/field shots: seismic exploration shot lines, land clearing, stump/boulder shots, avalanche control routes. A few holes spread over long distances in fields, marsh, forest or snow; cord laid along a line and tied into a main line at each shot point.

sources.title: Test Completed on Automated Blasthole Charger for Underground Mining - E&MJ
sources.claim: ABB's Robot Charger autonomously locates drilled blastholes at an underground rock face with a vision system and completes the charging cycle, using a second robot arm ... primer and detonator; it does not perform tie-in of detonating cord.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: charging blastholes and handling primer/detonator assemblies at a blast face. It shows vision-guided arms can find hole collars and handle initiation components in that setting, but the demonstrated cycle stops at hole charging; no cord is unspooled, routed between rows, or tied into a trunkline, so it does not substantiate this task in the field.

sources.title: Epiroc Partners with Orica on Semi-Automated Explosives Delivery System | OEM Off-Highway
sources.claim: The most advanced field explosives-charging machines still keep a human operator in the cab running the cycle, and the automated variant uses wireless initiation that removes the cord tie-in step rather than automating it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized charging and initiation of a development round. Cited to document the state of field explosives automation: an operator drives the cycle, and where tie-in is eliminated it is by wireless detonators, not by a robot laying and tying cord.

sources.system: Single-arm wire-harnessing pipeline (Koopman-operator MPC plus insertion primitives)
sources.title: Harnessing with Twisting: Single-Arm Deformable Linear Object Manipulation for Industrial Harnessing Task (arXiv:2410.10729)
sources.claim: A single robot arm with force/torque sensing autonomously routes deformable wire under tension and inserts it into clamps on an industrial-level wire-harnessing fixture, reported with high success rates for single and multiple wires.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routing a flexible cord along a fixtured path and securing it at defined points. Detonating cord is a comparable deformable linear object (about 5 mm, flexible, tension-tolerant) and trunkline layout demands no tighter precision; in a fixtured cell, routing cord and securing downlines to a main line is the same manipulation problem.

sources.title: In-air Knotting of Rope using Dual-Arm Robot based on Deep Learning (arXiv:2103.09402)
sources.claim: A dual-arm two-finger robot autonomously ties overhand knots and bowknots in rope on a bench setup, with motions generated online by neural networks from its own visual and proximity sensing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tying knots in flexible cord. 'Tying cord into main lines' is exactly a knot (or clip) joining a downline to a trunkline; the rope handled is of similar diameter and stiffness with no tighter precision requirement, in a purpose-built bench setting.

sources.title: New generation of rebar-tying robot TyBot 3.0 hits the market | Equipment World
sources.claim: TyBot autonomously navigates bridge decks and ties rebar intersections at about 1,000 ties per hour and has been used commercially on dozens of US bridge projects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously making repeated tie connections at grid intersections on an outdoor jobsite. It shows the per-intersection tying element can be autonomous outdoors, but TyBot rides a gantry over a flat, pre-laid, fixed-spacing mat with a dedicated wire-twist tool; it does not unspool or route cord, cannot form a blast circuit, and cannot traverse loaded holes, so it does not substantiate this task at E3.

tasks.label: Assemble and position equipment, explosives, and blasting caps in holes at specified depths, or load perforating guns or torpedoes with explosives.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-pit mine or aggregate quarry bench shot: worker walks a freshly drilled pattern of 100+ vertical blastholes (75–311 mm dia., 5–20 m deep) on a rough, sometimes wet/muddy bench; dips holes for depth and water, assembles a cast booster with a detonator on a downline, lowers it to the specified depth, positions the bulk-emulsion/ANFO hose from the MMU truck, loads decks to design, stems with cuttings, and ties in surface delays.

Construction / heavy-civil blasting: road cut, pipeline trench, foundation or urban rock excavation. Small-diameter holes (50–100 mm) on irregular, sloping, congested ground near structures; worker loads cartridge or bulk product, places a non-electric or electronic cap at a specified depth, stems each hole, and hooks up the initiation system before mats are placed.

Oil & gas well perforating: at a wireline service company's gun-loading building/magazine or at the wellsite, the explosives handler inserts shaped charges into the loading tube, threads and seats detonating cord, phases and inserts the tube into the gun carrier, installs the detonator/switch, and makes up the loaded gun string (or a well torpedo/setting tool charge).

Underground metal mine or tunnel development round: charging a drilled face or production rings — blowing out and measuring holes, assembling primer plus detonator, pushing the charging hose to the toe, filling each hole with pumped emulsion or ANFO to the specified column length, and connecting the initiation system, all at an unsupported rock face.

Ordnance facility work: at an ammunition load-assemble-pack plant or depot, filling/assembling explosive components into munition bodies (explosive fill, booster/fuze well components) with fixtured tooling and remote/automated equipment inside a hardened bay, under strict accounting procedures.

sources.developer: ABB (with Boliden, LKAB, Forcit, LKAB Kimit)
sources.title: Automated robot charger pilot solution for remote blasting of rock face – ABB Mining
sources.claim: ABB's Robot Charger, mounted on a charging carrier vehicle, uses vision to detect drilled boreholes at an underground mine face, assembles detonator and primer with a second arm, pushes the charging hose to the hole bottom and pumps explosive — the full charging cycle at the unsupported rock face.

sources.title: ABB, Boliden and LKAB complete successful testing of industry-first automated robot charger for increased safety in underground mines
sources.claim: ABB, Boliden and LKAB completed testing of the automated robot charger at the Boliden Garpenberg underground mine in October 2023, with control handed to the customer; the machine detects boreholes and charges them without people at the face.

sources.system: Avatel (Orica/Epiroc) and surface drill-and-blast automation generally
sources.title: What's new in automated drilling and blasting? – Mining Technology
sources.claim: Trade review of drill-and-blast automation: blasting automation lags drilling because of high variability and difficult bench access; the leading fielded charging product (Orica/Epiroc Avatel, underground development) still requires a human operator to run the charging cycle from an enclosed cabin, and no comparable system is cited for surface benches.

sources.title: Enaex y Codelco realizan la primera tronadura subterránea 100% teleoperada del mundo – Portal Minero
sources.claim: Enaex and Codelco charged and fired a full tunnel face at El Teniente with the UG-iTruck robotic charging vehicle, publicised as the world's first 100% remotely operated (teleoperated) underground blast.

sources.developer: General Dynamics Ordnance and Tactical Systems / U.S. Army
sources.title: New production facility opens to streamline Army artillery production – U.S. Army
sources.claim: The Army/General Dynamics Camden facility runs two purpose-built load-assemble-pack lines in which 155mm projectile bodies are filled with explosive, assembled and packed at 50,000 rounds per month using advanced automation rather than hand loading.
sources.transferJustification: Same task branch as the ordnance instance: filling munition bodies with explosives and assembling explosive components, done on fixtured purpose-built lines.

sources.title: New Perforating Gun System Increases Safety and Efficiency – JPT (SPE)
sources.claim: In the most industrialised perforating-gun operation (DynaEnergetics' factory-assembled DynaStage), automation covers inspection and electrical verification; the gun assembly/loading itself is a manual high-volume line staffed by gun loaders, and patents likewise describe guns being manually loaded with shaped charges.

tasks.label: Verify detonation of charges by observing control panels, or by listening for the sounds of blasts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Move and store inventories of explosives, loaded perforating guns, and other materials, according to established safety procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Surface mine/quarry blaster at shift start: draws packaged product (cast boosters, cases of packaged emulsion/dynamite, boxes of electronic detonators, bags of ANFO) from on-site Type 1/Type 2 magazines in a fenced gravel magazine yard, hand-carries and forklifts cases into a powder truck/pickup day box, logs quantities on the explosives inventory record, hauls across the pit to the shot, and returns unused product to the magazine and reconciles counts at shift end. Outdoor, weather, uneven ground.

Oilfield wireline/perforating crew: at the district shop and licensed magazine, moves factory-assembled loaded perforating guns, shaped-charge kits and detonators out of the magazine, stages and secures the 3-20 ft loaded gun assemblies in the wireline truck's gun rack and explosives box, transports to the pad, offloads, and returns unfired guns and detonators to the magazine with entries in the explosives log.

Military ordnance handler at an ammunition supply point/depot: forklifts palletized ammunition, missile canisters and boxed ordnance between earth-covered igloo magazines, flatbed trucks and ISO containers on concrete pads and aprons; restows by compatibility group, blocks and braces loads, performs cycle counts and posts transactions in the ammunition accounting system.

Explosives distributor/manufacturer plant magazine keeper: receives trailer loads of cased high explosives, boosters and detonators, offloads pallets and floor-loaded cases at the dock, stores them by compatibility group in Type 1 magazines and racks, picks customer orders, loads delivery trucks, and maintains the daily receipt/disposition inventory records.

Construction/demolition blaster on a highway cut or building demolition site: moves the day's explosives and detonators from a vehicle magazine to the work area (over rubble, scaffolds or stairs), stores them separately in day boxes, guards and secures them, and hauls excess back to a licensed off-site magazine with records at day's end.

Underground mine powder crew: draws explosives and detonators from the surface magazine, transports them down the decline or shaft in an approved explosives vehicle to an underground storage niche/magazine, distributes cases to headings, and reconciles quantities issued and returned.

sources.title: DHL to Deploy 1000 Boston Dynamic Stretch Robots
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously unloads floor-loaded boxes/cases from trailers and containers in logistics warehouses, and DHL has committed to deploying 1,000 additional units across its global network, showing commercial-scale case handling in human-staffed facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unloading and moving cased goods in a warehouse. Explosives inventories move as ~50 lb cardboard cases and standard pallets, the same objects, weights and placement precision as the boxes Stretch handles.

sources.title: Seegrid Sets the Standard with Industry-Leading Forklift AMR Payload Versatility
sources.claim: Seegrid forklift AMRs autonomously transport standard 48x40 pallets, bins and oversized custom loads in customer manufacturing and warehouse facilities that are also occupied by people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility pallet transport. Depot and magazine inventory movement is palletized transport between storage locations, trucks and staging areas, with comparable loads and tolerances.

sources.title: Holman Logistics to implement Third Wave Automation forklifts in multi-client warehouse
sources.claim: Third Wave Automation's autonomous high-reach forklifts are being deployed at Holman Logistics to run full-pallet inbound moves, racking put-away, pallet picking to outbound dock positions and location replenishment, with one person supervising several trucks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse put-away and retrieval. Storing inventories in magazines/igloos and pulling them for issue is the same receive–store–retrieve–ship cycle on racked or floor-stacked pallets.

sources.title: Dexterity partners with FedEx to debut trailer loading robots
sources.claim: Dexterity's DexR mobile dual-arm robot autonomously drives to a trailer and builds walls of boxes inside it from a conveyor at FedEx facilities, covering the truck-loading step of moving inventories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading cased goods into a trailer. Loading a magazine truck with cases of explosives requires the same box handling and stacking inside a trailer.

sources.system: PCAPP Projectile/Mortar Disassembly system and plant AGVs
sources.title: Chemical Demilitarization in the Classroom - PEO Assembled Chemical Weapons Alternatives
sources.claim: At the Pueblo Chemical Agent-Destruction Pilot Plant, automated guided vehicles moved munitions between processing buildings and robotic disassembly systems handled the explosive components of projectiles and mortars inside explosion containment rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant: machine transport and handling of fuzed, explosive-configured munitions within a facility, i.e., the movement and staging of ordnance inventories this task covers, in a purpose-built setting.

sources.title: Pueblo Chemical Agent-Destruction Pilot Plant - Bechtel
sources.claim: PCAPP's robotic munitions process ran at production scale, dismantling more than 780,000 explosive-configured projectiles and mortars, evidencing sustained reliability of robotic handling of energetic ordnance in a purpose-built plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-volume machine handling of live munitions. Demonstrates worker-quality reliability and damage rates when robots move and position explosive items in fixtured, purpose-built cells.

sources.system: BGCAPP rocket destruction line robots / Rocket Warhead Containerization System
sources.developer: U.S. Army PEO ACWA / Bechtel Parsons Blue Grass
sources.title: Facts: Blue Grass Rocket Destruction Process

instances.label: Surface mine or aggregate quarry production shot: after holes are loaded and the surface harness is hooked up, the blaster clears the bench, moves to a designated firing point, arms the electronic blasting machine or remote firing device (key, code, dial), presses fire, and confirms the round detonated. Underground mine or tunnel round: the blaster inserts primers/detonators into face holes and connects the round, then initiates either from a safe location with a shot exploder or wirelessly/from surface via a centralized blasting controller once the workings are cleared. Construction rock blasting (road cut, foundation or trench shot) near roads, houses and utilities: mats placed, traffic and personnel held, blaster arms the blasting machine at a shelter or truck and fires a small, closely controlled shot, then inspects for misfires. Structural demolition / building implosion: after final hookup and a last walk-through, the blaster fires the shot from a remote control point with a firing device once the exclusion zone is confirmed clear. Congested urban site, one-off geometry, spectators and traffic nearby.

Avalanche control: patroller or DOT blaster pulls the fuse igniter on a hand charge and throws or lowers it into a start zone (on foot, from a lift, or from a helicopter), or triggers fixed remote avalanche control installations. Steep alpine terrain, storm conditions, no fixed layout.

Seismic exploration and oilfield shooting: dropping or lowering a detonating device (seismic cap/charge, perforating gun) into a shot hole or well, arming the encoder/blaster box and firing the shot on signal. Operator-controlled wellsite pad or shot-hole line with standard rig-up.

Service-company perforating shop / magazine building: used port-plug and hollow-carrier guns are returned from the field and redressed on benches or in vises — ports degreased and cleaned of debris, gauged with go/no-go plug and ring gauges for erosion and thread damage, plugs and ports lubricated with thread compound and seal grease, and the carrier accepted or scrapped. Fixed layout, standard fixtures, company controls access (explosives-licensed premises).

Perforating gun manufacturing / factory gun-loading plant: new or refurbished carriers move through a production sequence where scallop/port surfaces are cleaned of machining swarf and oil, port and thread dimensions are gauged to spec, and seals, plugs and threads are lubricated before charges and detonators are installed. High volume, repeat part numbers, fixtured handling.

Military ordnance-handling variant: at an armory, ordnance depot or aboard ship, the ordnance handler cleans a gun mount's bore/ports and breech of combustion residue and copper fouling, gauges the surfaces for wear, erosion and pitting with bore gauges or inspection instruments, and applies preservative lubricant before the weapon is returned to ready status. Institution-controlled premises, standard equipment.

tasks.label: Lower perforating guns into wells, using hoists; then use measuring devices and instrument panels to position guns in correct positions for taking samples.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Land unconventional (shale) multi-well frac pad, plug-and-perf: the perforating gun string plus frac plug is picked up on the wireline unit's mast/hoist, run through the pressure-control stack and pumped down a horizontal cased well; the operator drives the winch and watches line speed/tension and CCL-gamma traces on the unit's instrument panel to land the guns on the planned stage depth. Repeated 8-15 times per day, dusty/hot/cold outdoor pad, red-zone exclusion during arming and firing.

Land conventional cased-hole perforating in a vertical or moderately deviated well, run from a wireline truck (sometimes with a workover rig/mast over the wellhead): gravity-conveyed gun string lowered on cable, depth set by correlating casing collar locator and gamma ray against the reference open-hole log on the instrument panel, guns positioned across a short interval and fired.

Offshore platform or rig: wireline-conveyed perforating and explosive setting-tool runs through a long lubricator/riser, gun string hoisted vertically with the platform crane/wireline winch, run in hole and positioned on depth using CCL/gamma correlation from the wireline cabin instrument panel; live-well pressure control, weather and deck constraints.

Long horizontal or highly deviated well where gravity conveyance will not reach: perforating guns conveyed by wireline tractor or on coiled tubing, with winch/injector speed coordinated to the tractor or CT and depth confirmed by CCL/gamma correlation before firing each cluster.

Sampling runs: sidewall coring gun or formation-tester/sampler lowered on wireline into an open or cased hole at a drilling rig site, positioned at depths picked off the correlation log using CCL/gamma and depth-measurement wheels on the instrument panel, then fired/set to recover rock or fluid samples.

tasks.label: Create and lay out designs for drill and blast patterns.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Aggregate quarry / dimension-stone operation: the blaster designs the next production shot on a bench face — number of rows and holes, burden and spacing, hole diameter, depth and subdrill, stemming, explosive product and powder factor, and the delay/initiation timing sequence — working from the face survey or laser/drone profile, prior shot performance, and the geology, and issuing the pattern as a shot plan/drawing or software file for the driller.

Large open-pit metal or coal mine: the blaster/blast engineer builds the pattern in mine-planning or blast-design software from drone or laser survey, block model and hole-deviation data, tunes burden/spacing and timing for fragmentation and wall control, and exports the digital pattern to GPS-guided drills and the blast-management system.

Construction or excavation blasting close to occupied structures (road cut, building foundation, utility trench, pipeline): designs a pattern with reduced hole diameters and charge weight per delay to stay under vibration and airblast limits, adds controlled perimeter work (presplit, line drilling, cushion blasting), and documents the design in the blast plan submitted to the regulator or owner.

Underground mine or tunnel development: designs the round — cut holes, relievers, lifters and perimeter holes, look-out angle, hole length, charge and timing plan — for the drift profile and rock class, produced as a drill plan drawing or a file transferred to the drill jumbo's control system.

Structural demolition (implosion or partial takedown): lays out the charge-placement pattern for columns, beams and shear walls from structural drawings and a site walkthrough, deciding which members are cut, charge sizes per member, and the delay sequence, and issuing the loading diagram to the loading crew.

tasks.label: Operate machines to flush earth cuttings or to blow dust from holes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-pit mine or large quarry bench: production blasthole drilling where the rig's compressor supplies flushing air that lifts earth/rock cuttings out of the hole continuously, with dust collector running and the hole blown clean at completion before the pattern is loaded. Graded bench, surveyed drill pattern, mine-controlled access.

Aggregate/stone quarry, smaller crew: crawler drill on a bench with uneven footing and some wet or muddy holes; operator manages air flush and dust suppression while drilling and blows each hole out at the end of the hole so depth can be checked and the hole loaded.

Heavy civil / construction blasting (road cut, building foundation, trench, utility line): track drill and a portable compressor with a blow pipe; holes cleared of cuttings and dust individually amid site clutter, traffic control, nearby structures and variable ground; site layout differs job to job.

Underground mine or tunnel: face jumbo or longhole rig drilling to a digital drill plan with water/air flushing carrying cuttings out of the holes, plus blowing holes out before the round is charged; confined drift, mine-controlled access, ventilation and standard equipment.

Re-cleaning previously drilled holes before loading: blaster walks the pattern with an air lance/blow pipe off a compressor to blow out dust, sloughed material or rain fill from holes drilled on an earlier shift, then re-checks depth.

Seismic shot-hole or small remote charge-hole drilling (fields, woodlots, ditching/agricultural work): portable rig with mud or air flush circulating cuttings out of small-diameter holes in soil and weathered rock at a site taken as found.

Construction site rock excavation: track drill/air-track and jackhammer work for road cuts, building foundations, utility trench blasting, or boulder/secondary breakage. Cramped, uneven, congested setting near roads, buildings and utilities; setups change hole to hole; hoses, compressors and hoists rigged on the spot; hole depths adjusted to found rock.

Underground mine or tunnel: jumbo/longhole rig drills the face round or production ring per a digital drill plan in a development drift or stope; rig tramming, boom set-up, collar location on an irregular rock face, plus hoisting/handling of drill steel and equipment in confined, wet, ventilated headings.

Structural demolition: boring charge holes in concrete columns, shear walls, piers and slabs of a building or bridge slated for implosion, using handheld rotary hammers/jackhammers, magnetic drills and hoists on multiple floors amid debris, rebar, partial pre-weakening, and no reliable as-built model; holes angled to specified depth (typically ~2/3 member thickness) at 1-1.5 in. diameter.

tasks.label: Hang ventilation tubing and ventilation curtains to ensure that the mining face area is kept properly ventilated.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground coal room-and-pillar section: hang and advance line brattice (curtain) in the entry/crosscut to within the required distance of the face — cutting cloth to the 36–72 in seam height, nailing/wedging it to the roof and ribs, weighting the bottom edge, and moving it up with each cut, on a muck-covered uneven floor in dust, water and low light.

Coal heading: extend flexible ventilation tubing from the auxiliary fan/scrubber toward the face — carrying duct sections in, coupling them, and hanging them on hooks/wire or roof-bolt hangers as the miner advances, working around cables, water lines and the mining machine.

Mid-shift repair: a shuttle car, scoop or the miner knocks down or tears a curtain or vent tube; the operator re-hangs or patches it (new nails, hangers, tape or a replacement panel) quickly so airflow and methane/dust control are restored before mining resumes.

Underground stone, salt or trona mine: hang rigid or flexible vent ducting along an established, standard-dimension drift from roof-bolt hangers or a messenger wire, usually from a boom basket or scissor lift, extending the line as the heading advances.

Outby the face in already-bolted entries: hang check curtains or temporary brattice across crosscuts to direct intake/return air, nailing or clipping cloth to roof and ribs across a standard-width, previously mined opening.

sources.claim: The nearest in-mine manipulation robot is a Chinese underground pipe-installation robot that uses vision to locate pipes and a manipulator to carry, lift and install rigid pipes of 120–250 mm diameter in coal-mine roadways, lifting up to 0.5 t to 4.5 m; its travel is remote-controlled and it handles rigid pipe, not fabric ventilation tubing or brattice.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic installation of long service lines in a coal-mine roadway. Transfer is not established: it positions rigid steel pipe against the rib with a heavy manipulator and its tramming is remote-controlled, whereas hanging vent tubing/brattice requires unfurling limp fabric, threading it onto overhead hooks, sealing couplings and nailing cloth to irregular roof and ribs.

tasks.label: Conduct methane gas checks to ensure breathing quality of air.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Gassy underground coal mine, active continuous-miner section: during production the operator makes methane tests at least every 20 minutes with a permissible handheld multigas detector at the working face — low seam (36-72 in), water sprays, heavy dust, dark, muddy uneven floor, trailing cables, machine cutting under remote control.

Underground coal mine working place before energizing/starting the miner or on returning to an idle place: operator tests methane within 12 inches of the roof, face and ribs across the entry or crosscut, records the reading, and reports/withdraws if 1.0-1.5% is found; freshly bolted roof, loose rock, supplies and cables underfoot.

Checks prompted by an unusual condition at the face: after a roof fall or roof cavity, after ventilation curtain/brattice disruption, before repairs or before energizing idle equipment — detector must be reached up into cavities and along the roof line, in a place whose geometry has just changed.

Checks in established outby parts of the section along fixed routes — last open crosscut, section return, intake and belt entries with permanent stoppings, standard clearances and a stable layout — done as part of on-shift examination duties before or between production cycles.

Non-coal underground mines worked with continuous miners (limestone, salt, some potash/trona headings): periodic atmospheric checks of a heading or newly opened area to confirm air is safe to breathe (methane pockets, blast fumes, oxygen deficiency); large openings, no explosive-atmosphere equipment restriction in the non-gassy cases.

sources.title: ExRobotics develops 'new and improved' version of its inspection robot
sources.claim: ExRobotics' ATEX/IECEx Zone 1 certified ExR-2 tracked robot performs daily autonomous gas-detection rounds on pre-planned routes in petrochemical plants, notifying the control room with the leak location; the robots are in use at Shell, Equinor, BP, Chevron and other operators' sites.
sources.transferJustification: Same act as the human gas check: carry a calibrated combustible-gas sensor to prescribed points on a route, obtain readings, log them and raise an alarm above threshold — here for methane in an explosive-atmosphere (Zone 1) plant.

sources.system: Spot with FLIR MUVE C360 gas sensor
sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / MFE Inspection Solutions / Teledyne FLIR
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas Leaks | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: A Boston Dynamics Spot fitted with a FLIR MUVE C360 gas sensor and Enhanced Autonomy Payload ran autonomous inspection rounds across a 40-acre midstream gas plant, detected a combustible-gas plume from a pinhole leak during a standard round and autonomously shut down at the set LEL threshold.
sources.transferJustification: Equivalent to the miner's gas check: a mobile machine travels a work area on its own, samples the atmosphere for combustible gas, quantifies concentration against a threshold and triggers the safety response (deenergization).

sources.title: ANYmal X — The World's First Ex-Proof Legged Robot
sources.claim: ANYmal X, an IECEx/ATEX Ex-proof legged inspection robot, carries gas detection sensors for methane, carbon monoxide and hydrogen sulfide and performs autonomous inspection missions in oil, gas and chemical facilities with operators including PETRONAS, Equinor, Petrobras, Woodside and Shell.
sources.transferJustification: Directly comparable: a legged robot walks a human-built facility on autonomous missions and measures methane concentration, the same measurement the miner makes with a handheld detector.

sources.system: Autonomous UAV with onboard gas sensing (Routine Inspection Autonomy framework)
sources.developer: Luleå University of Technology, Robotics & AI Group
sources.title: Safety Inspections and Gas Monitoring in Hazardous Mining Areas Shortly After Blasting Using Autonomous UAVs
sources.claim: Researchers at Luleå University of Technology flew a fully autonomous UAV carrying a Dräger gas sensor into an underground mine roughly 40 minutes after a real production blast to measure lingering gases, using their Routine Inspection Autonomy stack under heavy dust and map deformation.
sources.transferJustification: Same purpose and environment class as the miner's check: an autonomous machine enters an underground heading taken as found and measures the atmosphere to establish whether it is safe for workers to be there.

sources.system: Spot with edge-hardware autonomous navigation stack
sources.developer: Missouri University of Science and Technology
sources.title: Efficient Autonomous Navigation of a Quadruped Robot in Underground Mines on Edge Hardware
sources.claim: A Boston Dynamics Spot with an onboard edge-computer autonomy stack completed 20 fully autonomous traverses to four goal locations in the Missouri S&T Experimental Mine, but the system performs navigation only, after a prior mapping pass, in an inactive research mine.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the state of mobile-robot autonomy inside mine workings (navigation in a pre-mapped, inactive experimental mine, no gas payload, no MSHA-permissible rating), bounding what is available for gas checks at an active coal face.

tasks.label: Check the stability of roof and rib support systems before mining face areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground coal room-and-pillar section, low-to-mid seam (roughly 40–72 in): before backing the continuous miner into a heading and starting a cut, the operator visually examines the freshly exposed roof, face and ribs under lamp light in dust and water spray, looking for cracks, slips, draw rock and drummy top, and where height permits makes sound-and-vibration tests with a bar from under supported roof.

Coal section: verifying the installed support system in the place before mining — bolt spacing/pattern against the roof control plan, plates and bearing washers seated, straps/mesh/mats intact, posts, cribs and temporary supports (ATRS, pumpable cribs) set and tight — plus checking ribs for loose coal and barring down or calling for supplemental support.

Coal section re-check after conditions change: water infiltration, cutter roof or kettlebottoms appearing, rib sloughage after the previous cut, or a place idle over a weekend; the operator re-examines roof and rib support, judges whether extra bolts/posts are needed, and coordinates with the section foreman before mining resumes.

Walk/ride-through check of established section entries and intersections outby the face (engineered 18–20 ft entries, rock-dusted, standard bolt pattern, standing supports at intersections) along the route the miner and haulage will travel, confirming supports are intact and travelways safe before work begins.

Underground metal/nonmetal room-and-pillar mine (trona, salt, potash, industrial minerals) with high openings: checking the back and ribs and the installed bolts/screen/resin support in a large heading before running the continuous miner or borer, sometimes scaling loose material from a platform or with a mechanized scaler.

Instrument-assisted examination in an established, instrumented area: reading roof-sag telltales, convergence stations or extensometers, observing bolt/plate deformation trends over shifts, and recording the examination results (date, initials, conditions) as required before mining continues.

sources.title: Mining: Autonomous Mapping & Safety - Emesent
sources.claim: Emesent markets Hovermap-equipped Boston Dynamics Spot for underground mine data collection including change detection, convergence monitoring and remote ground support inspection, but the vendor states that remote, autonomous routine mapping with Hovermap-Spot is still under development.
sources.transferJustification: Closest commercial offering to a robotic ground-support inspection in an underground mine; cited to show the state of the art. It collects LiDAR geometry for human geotechnical review, does not perform contact sound-and-vibration roof testing or clear a face for mining, and the vendor calls autonomous routine operation 'currently under development'.

sources.system: Hovermap STX autonomous drone (operated by Unmanned Aerial Services)
sources.title: Case Study | When Minutes Matter Underground: UAS's Autonomous Drone Response to a Mine Collapse with Hovermap STX
sources.claim: An autonomous LiDAR drone was deployed after a 22-acre fall of ground at an Iowa limestone mine, mapping over 5 km of unstable underground workings within 48 hours so engineers could assess the damage without sending people in.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: remote assessment of unstable ground in an underground mine. It transfers only partially — the drone autonomously captures 3D geometry of voids for later human geotechnical interpretation; it does not examine installed bolts/plates/mesh for integrity, does not perform sound-and-vibration testing, and does not issue the pre-mining safety determination.

sources.title: Exyn mapping tech put to the test at Pogo - Metal Tech News
sources.claim: Exyn's Level 4 autonomous LiDAR drones are used commercially for underground mine mapping and survey, flying preprogrammed missions in GPS-denied workings without a pilot, as tested at the Pogo gold mine in Alaska.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous navigation and survey data capture inside an underground mine. Establishes that autonomous mobility/sensing underground is mature, but the deliverable is a survey point cloud, not an inspection judgment about roof and rib support stability, and no contact testing is performed.

sources.system: CSIR mine safety robot / automated 3D-thermal mine scanning tool
sources.title: The design of an automated 3D-thermal mine scanning tool
sources.claim: A robotic platform combining thermal imaging with a modified sounding probe to detect loose rock in mine hanging walls has been described only as a research design by CSIR, not as a fielded system.
sources.transferJustification: This is the closest robotic analogue to the roof-testing element of the task (detecting loose/drummy rock). It is cited as a negative indicator: the platform is stated in the future tense as a design goal and no deployed or commercial version was found in search.

sources.developer: University of Nottingham / Headlight AI et al. (per Science Robotics)
sources.title: Reconfigurable aerial robot for subterranean mine inspection | Science Robotics
sources.claim: A 2025 Science Robotics study of a reconfigurable aerial robot for subterranean mine inspection reports that fully autonomous operation across all deployment phases was not achieved.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inspection of confined underground mine spaces. Cited as evidence of the maturity ceiling — even research-grade mine inspection robots in 2025 do not run fully autonomously end to end, let alone render ground-stability determinations.

sources.system: Manual roof/rib examination and testing procedure (regulatory standard, not a robotic system)
sources.developer: MSHA / US Code of Federal Regulations
sources.title: eCFR :: 30 CFR 75.211 -- Roof testing and scaling
sources.claim: US regulation defines what the worker's roof and rib check must include: a visual examination of roof, face and ribs immediately before work, plus sound-and-vibration or equivalent tests where mining height permits, with hazardous conditions corrected before further work.
sources.transferJustification: Not robotic evidence; cited only to fix the worker-quality bar (contact testing plus a documented safety determination) used in the negative judgments.

tasks.label: Operate mining machines to gather coal and convey it to floors or shuttle cars.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground bituminous room-and-pillar section, normal conditions: operator stands off the machine with a radio remote, trams the continuous miner into the place, sumps and shears a 20-40 ft cut to the mine plan's roof/floor horizon, swings the discharge boom to load a string of shuttle cars in turn, cleans up the floor and moves to the next place, handling the trailing cable and ventilation curtain between cuts.

Room-and-pillar cutting in adverse or variable ground: thin seam (<42 in.), rock partings, seam rolls or faults, water and mud on the floor, draw rock or bad top, or retreat pillar extraction, where the operator continually adjusts cut depth, height and heading, watches roof and rib behavior, and abandons or shortens cuts on judgment.

Continuous-haulage section: continuous miner cutting into a flexible conveyor train or mobile bridge conveyor chain that must follow the miner in and out of the cut, so coal is conveyed continuously to the section belt rather than into batch cars.

Longwall face: shearer operator runs bidirectional cutting passes along the face, sets roof/floor horizon and web depth, loads the cut coal onto the armored face conveyor, coordinates powered roof support advance and face alignment; run from the face, the gate end, or a surface remote operations centre.

Surface highwall/auger mining: operator positions the highwall miner on a prepared bench, drives the cutter module into the exposed seam on push beams, steers to stay in seam, and conveys the coal back out to the stacker/loadout.

sources.system: Komatsu Joy Continuous Miner Automation (CMA) level 2 + Flexible Conveyor Train follow-me mode
sources.title: Komatsu on gaining control in room and pillar mining through automation - International Mining
sources.claim: Komatsu's level-two Continuous Miner Automation runs the machine's sump-and-shear cut cycles from a sequence table, repeating cycles until the operator stops it, and the Flexible Conveyor Train can be automated to follow the miner in and out of the cut; it is running in more than five ... coal, potash and salt.

sources.system: Komatsu Joy CMA levels 2 and 3 (Sequenced Table-based Automation, lidar heading control)
sources.title: Automation Advances With Room-and-Pillar Mining - Coal Age
sources.claim: With Komatsu's sequenced table-based CM automation the operator positions the machine and the miner then cuts 50-100 ft of coal to programmed heights and floor patterns with no operator input; level 3 adds lidar heading control, and the feature is in use in coal, potash and salt in more than five countries.

sources.system: Komatsu room-and-pillar automation roadmap (Joy continuous miners)
sources.title: Inside the Future of Room-and-Pillar Mining - Coal Age
sources.claim: As of late 2025 room-and-pillar automation is still limited to operator-assist functions such as automatic sump and ...; longer autonomous cuts, surface remote operation and full-section automation are described as later steps, not current practice.

sources.system: Joy Advanced Shearer Automation / Faceboss longwall control
sources.title: Longwall automation | Komatsu
sources.claim: Komatsu's Joy longwall shearer automation executes fully automated cutting sequences, including gate-end turnarounds, replicating a programmed cutting profile and extraction height, ... the operator able to override the roof drum horizon; sold across the Joy longwall product line for remote management from underground or the surface.

sources.system: Cat Command for Longwall (advanced state-based shearer automation, Longwall Navigator)
sources.title: Cat Longwall Shearer Automation - Mining
sources.claim: Cat Command for Longwall advanced automation runs complete cutting cycles from customizable state tables with automated direction, speed, cutting method and ranging-arm heights, plus horizon control and automatic face-straightness corrections; the system has been in ... at Yancoal's Moolarben underground coal mine since 2017.

sources.title: LASC longwall automation: case study (ACIL Allen, CSIRO impact case study)
sources.claim: CSIRO's LASC inertial-navigation longwall automation (shearer positioning, horizon control, automated face alignment) has been installed in 24 ..., about 72% of Australian underground coal mines, and is licensed through longwall OEMs internationally.

sources.system: Anglo American Remote Operation Centres (Komatsu longwall systems)
sources.title: Mining's digital evolution: Delivering technology for safety and sustainability – Anglo American Australia
sources.claim: Anglo American's Bowen Basin underground coal mines all operate their longwalls from surface Remote Operation Centres, having cut 10,000 longwall shears from those ROCs; the first shear fully controlled from surface was in 2018 at Grosvenor on Komatsu longwall equipment.

sources.system: Eickhoff / HBT / FAMUR longwall automation systems (shearer automation, remote mining)
sources.developer: Eickhoff Mining Technology, HBT GmbH, FAMUR
sources.title: Unfolding longwall automation - North American Mining Magazine
sources.claim: Industry engineers (Eickhoff, HBT, FAMUR) report that automated longwalls now run cutting sequences with automatic roof-support advance and inertial face alignment from surface control rooms, but seam detection and seam models remain unresolved, so human corrective intervention and manual exception handling at the face are still required.

sources.title: HW300 - Highwall Mining System (Caterpillar brochure)
sources.claim: Caterpillar's HW300 highwall mining system, whose cutter module is a continuous miner head pushed into the seam on push beams with a conveyor string behind it, offers an optional gyro-based navigation and steering system for precise cutterhead guidance; autonomy of the cut itself is not established.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: highwall mining drives the same continuous-miner cutter head in straight sump-and-shear cuts with a conveyor train behind it, the same objects and precision as underground CM cutting.

tasks.label: Drive machines into position at working faces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Appalachian low-seam underground coal, room-and-pillar section: the operator, standing under supported roof with a radio remote-control box, trams the continuous miner out of a completed place and into the next cut place within the section — turning through a crosscut, crossing wet/muddy uneven bottom and loose gob, dragging and clearing the trailing 995 V cable, with the bolter crew, shuttle cars and ventilation curtain nearby, in 1.1–1.8 m seam height.

Underground coal working place: fine positioning of the miner at the face for a cut sequence — squaring the machine to the projected cut line/survey spads and the rib, setting cutter-head height to the seam, sumping in and backing off, slabbing over for the next lift, and backing out of a deep cut, all done with the machine kept inby of the last row of bolts and off the ribs.

Underground coal panel/section move: tramming the miner several hundred metres out through developed, rock-dusted mains and entries to a new section — negotiating belt crossings, power centers, low clearance and turns, with the machine unplugged, cable reeled or the machine towed, and crew spotting.

Underground non-coal (salt, trona, potash, industrial minerals): positioning a continuous/borer miner at the face in large, dry, dimensionally regular rooms — advancing into the face for the cut and then place-changing to the next room in the grid past haulage and services; higher back, better floor, often cab or tele-remote control.

Longwall face: tramming the shearer along the armored face conveyor into cutting position for the next pass/snake cut, holding horizon and face alignment, with the crew on the face and supports advancing behind.

Surface/highwall mining: positioning the continuous highwall miner launch vehicle on the graded bench at the next planned hole, squaring it to the highwall, and driving the cutter module into the highwall on the planned hole line beside the previous web pillar.

sources.developer: Sandvik Mining and Rock Solutions / Agnico Eagle
sources.title: Sandvik technology enables dynamic automation at La Ronde Zone 5 - International Mining
sources.claim: At Agnico Eagle's LaRonde Zone 5 gold mine, Sandvik AutoMine loaders and trucks tram autonomously through underground drifts and haulage ramps between drawpoints, loading bays and surface, with tele-remote engagement only for bucket filling and dumping; routes are re-programmed daily and vehicles run during shift changes and weekends.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving a heavy self-propelled mining machine underground into position at a production face (drawpoint) and back. Same GPS-denied underground setting, comparable machine mass and confined-drift clearances, and the same core act of navigating to and stopping at a designated face position.

sources.title: Sandvik AutoMine Autoload 2.0 eliminates operator intervention in LHD drawpoint loading - International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik's AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 automates the full loader production cycle at fixed drawpoints — the machine positions itself and fills the bucket using taught per-drawpoint profiles without operator intervention; field-tested with customers in Europe and ... and released as a commercial AutoMine feature.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeatedly driving a large mining machine into a known, fixed face position underground. Demonstrates that when the face location is fixed and taught (an E1-style presentation), the machine positions itself autonomously at production quality.

sources.title: Automation Advances With Room-and-Pillar Mining - Coal Age
sources.claim: Komatsu's room-and-pillar continuous miner automation (sequence table, trialled with an FCT and shuttle cars at a Canadian salt mine) automates the sump/shear cutting cycle, but the operator still manually trams and places the machine at the face before initiating automation and may override the traction motors to steer.

sources.title: From longwall to room and pillar – how OEM Komatsu is transforming the mining sector - Informa Australia
sources.claim: Komatsu reports a Canadian salt room-and-pillar section running with one person in the section where the continuous miner cuts autonomously with occasional operator straightening and the Flexible Conveyor Train follows autonomously; its Autocut automated cut sequence on a Joy 12CM30 completed trials at a central Queensland coal mine and was entering the normal development cycle. Machine placement at the face remains an operator function.

sources.system: Sandvik MB670-1 / MB672 bolter miner with Cutronic automated cutting cycle
sources.title: New Sandvik MB672 bolter miner set to accelerate longwall mining - International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik bolter miners for underground coal longwall development carry a fully automated cutting cycle (Cutronic) in which the machine advances itself into the face and cuts the profile, reducing panel development time in ...; MB670-1 is a long-standing commercial product and the upgraded MB672 was launched in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the automated cycle advances (drives) the cutting machine into the coal face and holds its line for each cut, the in-place portion of positioning a mining machine at a working face, in an operating underground coal mine.

sources.developer: CSIRO with Australian coal industry and OEMs
sources.title: LASC Longwall Automation - CSIRO
sources.claim: CSIRO's LASC longwall automation, licensed to all major OEMs and widely installed in Australian and international longwalls, continuously steers longwall equipment and plots its three-dimensional position in real time, removing personnel from face positioning duties that previously required stopping production for manual correction.

sources.title: FrontRunner Autonomous Haulage System | Komatsu
sources.claim: Komatsu's FrontRunner autonomous haulage system has operated at commercial scale in surface mines for 17+ years, with more than 900 autonomous trucks commissioned as of October 2025, navigating active benches and spotting at loading units without drivers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously driving a very large mining machine across an active mine bench and positioning it at the working (loading) face. Same institution-controlled surface-mine setting as highwall mining, though spotting precision is coarser than aligning a highwall miner to a hole line.

sources.title: Potash mining goes tele-remote at Nutrien's Lanigan - International Mining
sources.claim: Nutrien's Saskatchewan potash mines, including Lanigan, run borer miners tele-remotely from surface control rooms using radar, LiDAR and AI-assisted sensing — the operator remains in the control loop rather than the machine navigating and placing itself autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task for non-coal borer positioning: establishes that the state of the art for moving and placing borer miners in potash is tele-remote human control, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment.

tasks.label: Move controls to start and regulate movement of conveyors and to start and position drill cutters or torches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground room-and-pillar coal mine, working section: operator stands back from the face with a handheld remote control box, starts the cutter drum, gathering head and machine boom conveyor, positions the drum to sump into the coal face and shears top-to-bottom through a 20-40 ft cut, swinging the discharge boom to load shuttle cars. Dust suppression sprays running, variable roof/floor and rock bands, methane monitoring.

Longwall face in an underground coal mine: crew start the armored face conveyor and stage loader and position the shearer's ranging drums to the cutting horizon, running bi-directional passes and gate-end turnarounds and lifting/lowering drums for seam rolls and floor corrections; increasingly supervised from the maingate or a surface room.

Underground nonmetal mine (salt, potash, trona, limestone/aggregate): borer miner, continuous miner or roadheader operator starts cutting head and machine conveyors and positions cutters to advance a room or heading through hard salt/rock; large engineered openings, repetitive mine plan, but variable ground and cutting conditions.

Section conveying/haulage control during production: starting and regulating a flexible conveyor train or mobile bridge conveyor, feeder-breaker and section belt conveyor as the miner cuts, keeping the tailpiece positioned under the miner boom, sequencing belt starts and stopping for spillage or jams.

Surface highwall/auger mining from a bench: operator at the launch-vehicle console starts the conveyor car string and thrusts, positions and steers the cutter module hundreds of feet into an exposed seam, monitoring web and pillar width; outdoor bench, weather and bench-grade variation.

Occasional cutting-torch work: positioning and lighting an oxy-fuel or plasma torch to cut steel at or near the working place (jammed bit blocks, mesh, rails, damaged machine structure) or in the section shop.

sources.system: Komatsu (Joy) Continuous Miner Automation (CMA) Level 2 - Sequenced Table-based Automation, Faceboss control system
sources.title: Automation Advances With Room-and-Pillar Mining - Coal Age
sources.claim: Komatsu's Level 2 Continuous Miner Automation (sequenced table-based automation) lets the machine execute complete sump/shear cutting cycles, controlling every continuous-miner function except the pump motors, after the operator positions the machine and initiates the sequence.

sources.title: Automation Advances With Room-and-Pillar Mining - Coal Age
sources.claim: Komatsu's Level 2 continuous miner automation is in production use in coal, potash and salt mines in more than five countries, with reported gains in cycle time, machine life and rib/floor quality.

sources.title: Automation Advances With Room-and-Pillar Mining - Coal Age
sources.claim: Level 3 CMA adds lidar-based heading control: the machine scans the previously cut ribs and corrects its own heading while executing the programmed sump-and-shear sequence, with operators present in the area but not driving the cut.

sources.system: Joy Advanced Shearer Automation / Faceboss longwall automation
sources.title: Longwall automation | Komatsu
sources.claim: Komatsu sells Advanced Shearer Automation for longwalls: fully automated cutting sequences including gate-end turnarounds, in which the shearer repeats a programmed cutting profile and drum positions automatically, with operator override available.

sources.system: Komatsu Longwall Command and Control with Height-Based Pitch Steering (HBPS)
sources.title: Komatsu pioneers underground shearer automation - Australian Mining
sources.claim: Komatsu's height-based pitch steering automatically positions the longwall shearer's floor drum to hold a planned pan pitch, converting an operator's height target into passes the machine executes itself, on Australian production longwalls.

sources.system: Joy 4FCT Flexible Conveyor Train, follow-me mode (UWB sensing)
sources.title: Komatsu | 4FCT
sources.claim: Komatsu's 4FCT flexible conveyor train tracks and positions itself under the continuous miner's discharge boom during production using onboard sensing, without an operator driving it.

sources.system: Sandvik MB672 / MB670-1 bolter miner with Cutronic automated cutting cycle
sources.title: New Sandvik MB672 bolter miner set to accelerate longwall mining - International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik's bolter miners for underground coal offer an automated cutting cycle (Cutronic on MB672; an adaptable auto-cutting cycle on the in-service MB670-1) that advances the heading consistently in stable ground.

sources.title: Sandvik MB670-1 FLP Bolter Miner For Longwall Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik's currently deployed MB670-1 bolter miner includes an adaptable auto-cutting cycle that speeds advance cycles in longwall gate-road development.

sources.system: Epiroc Simba long-hole production drill rig with Rig Control System automation
sources.title: Epiroc accelerates transformation as its autonomous drills reach a milestone
sources.claim: Epiroc Simba production drill rigs run autonomously in underground mines, with one customer drilling over a million metres autonomously on a single rig.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous underground production drilling. The rig positions its boom and feed on a planned hole pattern and drills unattended in an underground mine heading - the same 'start and position drill cutters' control actions, on comparable rock, in the same class of underground mine environment.

sources.system: Nutrien Lanigan tele-remote borer miner operation
sources.title: Potash mining goes tele-remote at Nutrien's Lanigan - International Mining
sources.claim: Nutrien mined a full potash production wing with borer miners operated tele-remotely, with no personnel in the mining area - remote control by human operators, not autonomous cutting.

sources.system: Cat HW300 / ADDCAR-type highwall mining systems
sources.title: Highwall Miners Selection Guide: Types, Features, Applications | GlobalSpec
sources.claim: Highwall mining systems keep cutterhead control with a human operator in the launch-vehicle cab; the PLC controls machine functions but the operator oversees and steers the cutter module.

tasks.label: Reposition machines to make additional holes or cuts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground room-and-pillar coal section: after completing a sump-and-shear pass, the operator (on remote control, standing under supported roof) repositions the continuous miner — trams it forward/back, angles it, re-aims the cutter head — to take the next slice of the same cut place until the planned cut depth and entry width are achieved. Dust, water spray, uneven floor, trailing cable, roof-bolter and haulage working nearby.

Underground coal/industrial-mineral section, place change: the operator trams the miner out of the finished place, moves it through the section past shuttle cars, ventilation curtains and the bolter, and repositions it squarely at the face of the next entry or crosscut on the survey line so cutting can begin. Cable must be pulled and dressed, sight lines are short.

Underground industrial-mineral mine (salt, trona, potash, limestone): continuous/borer miner repositioned between successive cuts in a large opening with good roof and dry conditions; wide entries, repetitive geometry, no methane restrictions on sensors.

Longwall face: shearer repositioned for each successive pass along the face — reversing direction, executing gate-end turnarounds and re-setting drum heights so the next cut can be taken as supports and AFC advance.

Surface quarry bench (aggregate or dimension stone): operator repositions the drilling/cutting machine along the bench to the next planned hole or channel in a line-drilling or blast pattern, levels and aligns it, then makes the hole/cut. Graded bench, surveyed pattern, weather exposure.

Surface highwall/auger mining: after finishing an entry into the seam, the operator repositions the highwall miner/auger machine along the bench to the next hole location and aligns it to the highwall to keep the web pillar to plan before launching the next hole.

sources.system: Komatsu (Joy) Continuous Miner Automation — Level 2 Sequenced Table-based Automation
sources.title: Automation Advances With Room-and-Pillar Mining — Coal Age
sources.claim: Komatsu's Continuous Miner Automation (Sequenced Table-based Automation) lets the operator place the machine and start an automated sequence in which the miner repeatedly sumps, shears and repositions itself for further cuts until the operator ends automation; trialled with FCT and shuttle cars at a Canadian salt mine.

sources.system: Komatsu Autocut / room-and-pillar automation on Joy 12CM30 continuous miner and Flexible Conveyor Train
sources.title: From longwall to room and pillar – how OEM Komatsu is transforming the mining sector (Informa)
sources.claim: In a Canadian underground salt mine a Komatsu-equipped room-and-pillar section runs with one person in the section, the continuous miner cutting autonomously with only occasional operator steering corrections; Autocut trials on a Joy 12CM30 at a central Queensland coal mine were completed and moved into the normal development cycle.

sources.system: Continuous miner automatic sump and shear (Komatsu Joy continuous miners)
sources.title: Inside the Future of Room-and-Pillar Mining — Coal Age
sources.claim: Komatsu's global continuous-miner product manager describes automatic sump and shear as an operator-assisted function already widespread in room-and-pillar mining today, with longer autonomous cuts the next step; full-section automation and surface control are still future stages.

sources.system: Komatsu Advanced Shearer Automation / Faceboss RS20 longwall automation
sources.title: Longwall automation | Komatsu
