tasks.label: Observe and listen to equipment operation to detect binding or stoppage of tools or other equipment malfunctions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground room-and-pillar coal mine: operator stands 30-60 ft from the continuous miner running it by remote control, watching the cutter drum and gathering head while listening through ambient noise, dust and water spray for bits binding in rock, motor bog-down, or a stalled conveyor chain, and calls/stops the machine when an abnormality is heard.

Underground metal/nonmetal mine (limestone, salt, trona, potash) with a continuous miner or borer: operator monitors cutting-head sound and vibration against harder rock, watching for stalled cutter motors, jammed muck in the loading boom, or hydraulic squeal, in a noisier, higher-headroom heading.

Operator seated in or on a cabbed/deck-mounted machine (older track-mounted miner, highwall or borer control station): detects malfunction through felt vibration, motor sound changes and gauge/ammeter readings while cutting, with limited direct sight of the tools.

Monitoring the attached haulage and conveyance while cutting: listening for belt slip, chain binding in the machine conveyor or continuous haulage bridge units, cable reel and tram motor noise, and spotting a blocked water spray or plugged discharge before it stops production.

Pre-shift/startup and post-jam checks: briefly running the machine unloaded to listen for abnormal cutter-motor, gearbox, pump or gathering-arm noises, checking spray nozzles and bit condition, and reporting suspected faults to maintenance before resuming the cut.

tasks.label: Repair, oil, and adjust machines, and change cutting teeth, using wrenches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground room-and-pillar coal section: operator and helper change worn conical picks/bits on the continuous miner's cutting drum at or near the face — dozens of bits knocked out with a bit punch, hammer or hydraulic extractor and new ones driven in, in a low, dusty, wet heading with uneven floor and limited headroom.

Routine lubrication and fluid service: greasing the miner's fittings on pins, bearings, boom and conveyor with a grease gun or filling the auto-lube reservoir, checking and topping up hydraulic and gear oil, wiping and inspecting for leaks — done at the section or in a crosscut between production cycles.

Adjustments and minor running repairs at the face: clearing or replacing plugged water spray nozzles, tightening or replacing bolts and retainer clips, adjusting cutter/conveyor chain tension and gathering head, replacing a blown hydraulic hose or damaged cable, freeing the tail conveyor — varied, diagnosed on the spot with wrenches and hand tools.

Larger scheduled maintenance or component change during a maintenance shift, in an underground shop area or a surface/shop bay: replacing a cutter motor, gearbox, conveyor chain or drum section, rebuilding bit blocks, working with mechanics using wrenches, torque tools and lifting gear.

tasks.label: Install casings to prevent cave-ins.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground coal room-and-pillar section: after the continuous miner takes a cut, permanent roof support (resin-grouted roof bolts with plates, sometimes straps or mesh) is installed across the freshly exposed entry/crosscut roof, in 4-8 ft seam height, on a rubbly uneven floor, in water and dust, with roof and rib conditions that change cut to cut.

Underground coal: hand-erected standing supports where roof or ribs are bad - timber posts and wedges, crib blocks, pumpable cans, jacks/props, or steel sets - at intersections, around a roof fall or draw-rock zone, along the tailgate, or to secure a damaged area before re-entry; one-off cramped geometry, materials carried in by hand.

Underground metal/nonmetal or hard-rock heading (limestone, salt, trona, potash, ore drift): after a cut or blast, ground support installed with a mobile bolting rig - resin/cement rock bolts plus welded-wire screen or shotcrete lining - in a large opening with irregular, freshly exposed back and walls.

Longwall face: the line of powered roof supports (shields) is lowered, advanced and re-set against the roof behind the shearer, cut by cut, to hold the immediate roof over the face and conveyor as the panel retreats; engineered face line maintained by the mine, natural roof and floor.

Installing casing/liner pipe in an opening: running steel casing or a standpipe into a ventilation, degasification, water or grout borehole at a fixed collar, or setting a liner/lagging in weak ground behind a small opening, with the rig set up over the hole and pipe handled at the collar.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Room-and-pillar underground coal section, development bolting: at the face the operator works the levers to run the machine-mounted automated temporary roof support (ATRS) canopy/safety bar up against the freshly exposed roof, keeps it pressurized while the bolting crew installs the permanent support, then lowers it so the machine can advance. 4-8 ft seam, dust, irregular but competent roof.

Longwall face: operator works the electrohydraulic controls of the hydraulic powered roof supports (shields/chocks) that hold the roof over the shearer, AFC and walkway - lowering, advancing and re-setting them to set pressure as the face advances, and setting/lowering them during face setup, recovery and while crews work under them.

Underground metal/nonmetal or stone mine (trona, salt, potash, limestone): temporary support jack/safety bar raised against the back over the machine while the crew installs bolts, screen or steel sets; larger openings, variable back height, harder rock.

Retreat/second mining at the pillar line: mobile roof supports or breaker-line supports set against the roof over the continuous miner and lowered/walked as the pillar is extracted, holding the roof while posts and timbers are set; rubble floor, active convergence and caving nearby.

Adverse ground: the roof is too high, soft or broken for the bar to pressurize, so crib blocks, wedges or header boards must be placed between the support and the roof, or hand-set hydraulic props/jacks must be positioned in irregular, restricted spots near the face before and while framing proceeds.

tasks.label: Apply new technologies developed to minimize the environmental impact of coal mining.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground coal face, room-and-pillar or gate-road development: cut the face with the continuous miner/bolter miner while the machine's environmental control technology is applied — water sprays on the cutting drum, machine-mounted flooded-bed scrubber running, cutting sequence and depth kept to the approved dust-control plan and in-seam to limit out-of-seam dilution. Dark, wet, dusty, gassy; geology and roof vary cut to cut.

Underground face area: set up and maintain the face ventilation and dust-control hardware that the newer controls depend on — hang and move line brattice/curtain, extend or reposition ventilation tubing and scrubber discharge ducting, replace clogged spray nozzles, clean the scrubber screen and check water pressure. Confined, low-seam, irregular ribs and roof; flexible cloth and hose handling.

Underground belt and return entries: keep inert rock dust and chemical suppressant applied along roadways and belt lines using newer continuous/automated dusting technology (trickle dusters fed from surface silos, mine-wide dusting systems, wetting-agent sprays at transfer points) to meet incombustible-content compliance.

Underground working section: spot and bulk rock dusting of the newly advanced section with a mobile duster or slinger machine, dusting ribs, roof and floor around the miner and crosscuts as places are cut.

Section-level environmental monitoring and response: take methane/CO/air-velocity and dust readings with handheld and machine-mounted monitors, place or wear continuous personal dust monitors, log the readings, and act on them — de-energize, adjust sprays or airflow, move the curtain — before resuming cutting.

Surface side of a coal operation (surface miner/highwall pits, haul roads, stockpiles, loadout): apply dust-suppression technology — spraying haul roads and stockpiles with water or chemical suppressant from a water truck or fixed sprinkler/spray system to control fugitive dust and meet permit conditions. Outdoor, graded haul roads, access-controlled site.

tasks.label: Guide and assist crews laying track and resetting supports and blocking.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Room-and-pillar coal section, after a cut: the continuous miner operator helps the crew set temporary supports — carrying and standing wooden posts and safety jacks, driving wedges and placing wooden headboards/blocking against an irregular draw-rock roof in a 4–6 ft seam, on a muddy rutted floor in dust and cap-lamp light, giving hand signals for placement.

Bad-top or roof-fall area: crew resets supports where the roof has sagged or fallen — debris is cleared, wooden cribs are built and blocked tight to fit an irregular cavity of unknown shape, with unstable ground overhead; conditions differ every shift.

Laying, extending or repairing rail track for supply/haulage in section entries: placing ties on an uneven wet floor, positioning and joining rail sections, gauging and aligning, spiking or bolting joint bars, blocking track and cars; operator guides and helps the track crew.

Staging and securing materials around the section: handling timbers, blocks, cribbing and rail delivered by scoop or supply car, chocking and blocking equipment and cars standing on grade, wedging blocking behind set supports, spotting the equipment for the crew.

Underground metal/nonmetal or thick-seam operation: assisting the ground-support crew in a heading — handling timber sets and posts, mesh and blocking placed behind sets against variable rock, guiding placement in a drift taken as found.

sources.system: Joy Faceboss RS20n / Joy-engineered Powered Roof Support (PRS) solution
sources.title: Komatsu | Joy-engineered powered roof support (PRS) solutions

A shield lowers, advances and sets against the roof with controlled force — the machine analogue of 'resetting supports' — but only within a purpose-built, machine-built support line, not with hand-set posts and wooden blocking.

sources.title: LASC Longwall Automation - CSIRO

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic advance/alignment of the powered support line underground. Shows support setting is automated only where the supports are part of an engineered machine system; it does not cover hand-set timbering, cribbing or track work in entries.

sources.title: Robot FEEDBOT F-500 | HOMAG
sources.claim: The Weinmann FEEDBOT F-500 six-axis robot picks heavy dimensional lumber from feed racks and inserts studs and plates into a framing jig fully automatically and with high ... timber-frame production lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic handling and precise placement of heavy timber members into a fixtured jig, with automatic computation of pick and place positions. Transfers to setting posts, cribbing and wooden blocking when the timbers are presented in fixtures at known positions (E1), not to hand-fitting timbers to irregular rock.

sources.title: TyBot Deployed On The I-95 / Betsy Ross Bridge In Philadelphia, PA | Advanced Construction Robotics
sources.claim: TyBOT autonomously locates and ties rebar intersections on bridge ... from screed rails, with no operator or pre-programming during operation, and has been deployed commercially on numerous US bridge projects.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing ground support in an as-found underground heading. Used only as negative context: even the mechanized, machine-friendly form of ground support is not yet autonomous underground, so hand-set supports and blocking are not achievable at E2/E3.

roles.title: Roof Bolters, Mining
roles.description: Operate machinery to install roof support bolts in underground mine.

tasks.label: Drill bolt holes into roofs at specified distances from ribs or adjacent bolts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: US underground coal mine, room-and-pillar section: dual-boom roof bolter at the face, operator under the ATRS drilling 4-8 ft holes on a ~4 ft grid into a coal/shale roof per the MSHA roof control plan, holes kept within specified distance of the rib and of adjacent bolts; dust, water, uneven floor, seam height 5-8 ft.

Coal mine, low/thin seam or awkward locations: bolter operator working from a low deck in 36-48 in seam, or drilling extra holes at intersections, turnouts and close to ribs where the pattern must be adjusted to the actual cut and to bad top.

Longwall gate-road development: dedicated bolter or bolter-miner following the continuous miner, drilling standardized primary-support patterns at a high production rate in a straight, repetitive entry.

Hard-rock metal mine development or production heading: mechanized bolting rig (Boltec/DS412i class) in an arched drift, drilling bolt holes in the back on the engineered ground-support pattern, often through mesh, with resin/cement or self-drilling anchors.

Underground stone (limestone) mine: wide 40 ft entries with 20-30 ft high roof, mobile roof bolter drilling long holes on a wide pattern across the entry from a boom or platform, dry regular pillar layout.

Rehabilitation / secondary support: adding holes for supplemental bolts, cables or straps in older or deteriorated entries, positioning each hole relative to existing bolts, cables, mesh and utilities in irregular, damaged roof.

sources.system: Epiroc Boomer face drilling rigs with Rig Control System / Advanced Boom Control (ABC Regular, ABC Total)
sources.title: Advanced Boom Control | Epiroc
sources.claim: Epiroc Boomer underground boom drill rigs offer Advanced Boom Control, where ABC Total drills a full sequence of holes automatically according to a digital drill plan, including over shift changes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drilling blast/face holes at plan-specified positions in an underground rock heading with the same class of hydraulic boom drill and same rock as bolt-hole drilling. It shows a machine can index a boom to plan coordinates and drill a sequence of holes to position tolerance, which is the core of drilling bolt holes at specified spacing once hole locations are presented.

sources.claim: Chinese coal-mine drilling/anchoring robot research reports that hole-positioning pose of drilling robots is still set by manual remote control plus manual re-checking, and full automatic adjustment has not ....

sources.transferJustification: Related task: the robot performs the bolt-hole/bolt handling motions of a coal roof bolter in a controlled test setup, showing the drilling motions are within reach of a fixed industrial arm when the work is presented at a known position, which is the E1 counterfactual for this task.

sources.system: Komatsu / Joy room-and-pillar bolting systems, Fletcher bolters with ATRS
sources.title: A Different Approach to Improving Room-and-Pillar Productivity - Coal Age
sources.claim: In current US room-and-pillar coal practice, cutting and bolting sequences run under remote control with bolter operators working under automated temporary roof supports; hole placement is directed by the operators.

tasks.label: Pull down loose rock that cannot be supported.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground coal mine, active face: while bolting a newly cut place, the operator sounds and visually examines the roof, then reaches from under supported roof with a scaling bar of suitable length to pry down loose draw rock/slate (fist-size pieces to slabs) that cannot be held by bolts, then resumes bolting.

Underground coal mine, entries and crosscuts near the face: pulling down loose, drummy rib coal and rock (rib rolls, sloughing ribs) with a bar from a safe position, deciding which rib material is loose and how far to stand back as material sheds.

Underground coal mine: loose roof brow or slab too large or too high to bar down by hand, taken down using the roof bolting machine itself (boom, drill head, ATRS beam) or by having the continuous miner/scoop knock it down, with the operator working from under the machine canopy.

Underground stone, salt or hard-rock metal mine, heading after blasting: back and ribs 15-30 ft high are scaled before crews and bolting rigs go under, using a mechanized scaling boom/hammer or bolter-mounted scaling tool; operator judges loose rock by sound, sight and hammer feel over an irregular blasted profile.

Developed, maintained outby areas (intersections, travelways, shop and belt entries) of an underground mine: loose roof or rib rock found on examination or before re-support/rehab work is scaled down from a bolting machine or with bars before new bolts, straps or mesh are installed.

sources.system: Normet Scamec LC 065 A / LC 095 A scaling machines
sources.title: Safer scaling — CIM Magazine
sources.claim: State-of-the-art dedicated underground scaling machines (Normet Scamec LC 065 A / LC 095 A) are operator-in-cab machines; automation and remote operation are described by the manufacturer as future additions, not current capability, as of July 2026.

sources.title: Safer scaling — CIM Magazine
sources.claim: MacLean's WC5 water cannon, used to bring down hang-ups and loose ground underground without people in the hazard zone, is run by human operators over line-of-sight or surface tele-operation links, i.e. continuous teleoperation rather than autonomy.

sources.system: Scaletec MC / LC mechanized scaling rig
sources.title: The Scaletec MC Rock Drill Scaling Rig from Atlas Copco (AZoMining)
sources.claim: Mechanized scaling rigs of the Atlas Copco/Epiroc Scaletec family provide the operator with control of boom positioning and hammer percussion; the rig control system assists a human operator rather than scaling autonomously.

sources.system: Infrared thermography + acoustic emission loose-rock detection prototype
sources.developer: Institute for Advanced Mining Technologies, RWTH Aachen University
sources.title: Application of Infrared Thermography and the Acoustic Emission Technology for Loose Rock Detection
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed mining research as of January 2026 states that identifying which rock is loose — the perceptual core of this task — still depends on subjective human operator experience, with sensor-based detection still at feasibility-trial stage in a single German mine.

sources.system: Loose rock detection methods for automating scaling (research review)
sources.developer: Radl, Mitra, Clausen (Mining Technology, Taylor & Francis)
sources.title: Loose rock detection methods for automating the scaling process — Mining Technology
sources.claim: Research on automating the scaling process reports that loose-rock detection remains a task carried out by experienced personnel, i.e. automated scaling of mine backs and ribs has not been achieved.

sources.title: Normet Xrock launches fully autonomous underground rock breaker — International Mining
sources.claim: An autonomous boom-hammer rock-breaking system exists, but it works on already-fallen muck at a fixed grizzly/crusher station, planning strikes on a point cloud of the ore ...; it does not scale in-situ roof or rib rock in a mine heading.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: secondary breaking of oversize boulders at a fixed grizzly. It does not transfer to pulling down loose rock: the boulders are already down and lying on a fixed grate in a permanently instrumented station, whereas scaling requires a mobile machine to distinguish drummy, loose rock from sound rock overhead in an as-found heading — a perception problem the 2022 and 2026 literature says is still done by experienced people.

tasks.label: Position bolting machines, and insert drill bits into chucks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground bituminous coal mine, room-and-pillar low seam (roughly 40-70 in): operator trams the dual-boom roof bolter under freshly exposed roof at the face, sets the automated temporary roof support, positions each drill head at the planned hole location under an irregular coal/shale roof, and hand-loads a 4-6 ft drill steel with a carbide bit into the chuck for every hole. Dust, water, muddy uneven floor, sloughing ribs, cramped seam height, cable and ventilation curtain in the way.

Underground coal mine, mid to high seam, newer electrohydraulic bolter with automated drill/bolt cycle controls: operator trams the machine forward a row at a time as the place advances, spots and levels it, swings/positions the booms to each hole in the pattern, and inserts drill steels and replacement bits into the chucks, including changing dull or bound steels several times a shift.

Coal mine outby work in established, ventilated entries, intersections and belt roadways: supplemental support and rehabilitation bolting where the roadway layout is already surveyed and maintained; machine is trammed along the known entry, spotted under specified locations, and drill steels/bits are loaded into the chucks.

Bolting from an integrated machine - bolter-miner or continuous-miner-mounted bolting rigs, and mobile roof support/walk-through bolter configurations: operator positions the onboard bolting rigs relative to the cut, aligns the drill heads with the roof, and loads drill steels/bits into the chucks of the onboard drill units in a confined, moving machine envelope.

Hard-rock metal/non-metal underground mine: operator trams a mechanized bolting rig (Boltec/DS-class or similar) to a 4-5 m development heading over a mucked but uneven floor, spots and jacks the rig, positions the boom/feed to each bolt location on an as-blasted rock profile from the cabin, and changes the drill rod/bit when worn.

sources.system: Sandvik DS412iE / DS412i rock bolter ('one bolt' automation)
sources.title: Sandvik to add rock bolter to battery-powered mining line up - International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik's most automated underground rock bolters run one complete bolting cycle unassisted, but the operator must still manually relocate the boom from bolt location to bolt location and tram/spot the carrier - i.e. the positioning act itself is not automated on commercial bolters.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (mechanized rock bolting underground); cited to establish which parts of positioning are and are not automated on fielded bolters.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: face drilling with a boom-mounted hydraulic rock drill in an underground heading. Positioning a boom-mounted drill feed against the rock to a planned hole location is the same act as positioning a bolter's drill head, with the same machines, rock and precision class.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading and coupling drill rods into the rotation unit of an underground rock drill from an onboard magazine is mechanically the same act as inserting a drill steel/bit into a bolter chuck, with comparable objects and precision.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: mounting a drill bit onto a rotary drill string from a fixed onboard carousel is the same manipulation as inserting a bit/steel into a bolter chuck - same object class, same thread/collar precision - performed by machine from a presented, known position.

sources.system: Epiroc Simba underground production drill rig (autonomous drilling)

sources.claim: Epiroc reports that a mining customer drilled more than a million ... with a single Simba production drill rig, which drills planned holes with automatic rod handling from an onboard carousel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: underground production drilling. It shows a drill rig positioning its feed to planned holes and feeding rods into the drill unattended inside a mine drift, the same positioning-and-rod-loading acts this task covers.

sources.developer: University of Kentucky (with USC; Alpha Foundation funding)

sources.developer: University of Kentucky / University of Southern California

sources.title: DL432i: precision in underground longhole drilling | Sandvik
sources.claim: Sandvik's underground drill automation package moves the operator to a remote station but is a tele-remote system: an operator remotely controls and supervises the drills during drilling and ring-to-ring tramming.

sources.title: Boltec Auto Bolt Reload | Epiroc US
sources.claim: Epiroc's Boltec Auto Bolt Reload automatically transfers bolts from a 44-bolt carrier magazine to the eight-bolt feed carousel with a dedicated transfer boom, so the operator never leaves the cabin to reload consumables on an underground bolting rig.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling of bolting consumables from an onboard magazine into the working position of an underground bolting rig - the same class of machine-fed insertion as loading a drill steel/bit into the chuck.

tasks.label: Perform safety checks on equipment before operating.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shift-start pre-operational exam of a twin-boom roof bolting machine parked near the working face of an underground coal mine (low seam, 40-70 in., dark, dusty, wet, uneven floor). Operator walks/crawls around the machine with a cap lamp: checks hydraulic hoses, fittings and cylinders for leaks, cuts and chafing; drill chucks, steels, bits and wrenches; ATRS/temporary roof support pads; canopies and guards; dust collector box, filter and suction; water sprays and hose; trailing cable for cuts; then energizes and function-tests boom, feed, tram, deadman/panic bars and emergency stops before drilling, reporting and tagging any defect found.

In-shift re-checks before resuming operation after tramming to a new place or after changing consumables: re-inspect trailing cable and hoses after the move, confirm water spray and dust collection function, verify bit/steel condition and chuck retention, check that guards and canopy are secure and that the machine is stable on the new floor before the next bolt row.

Gas and electrical safety checks on the bolter before energizing it at the face: test for methane at the machine and near the roof with a handheld/machine-mounted methane monitor, confirm the machine methane monitor is operating and within calibration, inspect the trailing cable, plug and ground connections, and check permissibility (covers bolted, no gaps or damaged flame paths) before switching on.

Metal/non-metal (hard rock) mine variant: pre-op inspection of a mobile bolter (e.g., Boltec/MacLean-type carrier) in a drift before the shift - walk-around for hydraulic and water leaks, rock drill and feed condition, boom pins and hoses, FOPS canopy, tires/tracks and brakes, fire suppression and extinguisher, lights and horn, fluid levels, followed by a function test of boom, feed and brakes.

Check of the bolter in a controlled setting: on the surface pad or in the mine shop after maintenance or before the machine is taken underground - verify repairs, fluid levels, hose routing, guards, e-stop and interlock function on a level, lit floor with the machine positioned for access, then release it to service.

Pre-shift verification of the personal gas detection instrument the bolter carries underground (multi-gas/methane monitor): confirm it is bump-tested/calibrated, sensors respond, battery charged, and the record shows it is fit for use, done in the lamp house/supply area before entering the mine.

sources.system: DSX Docking Station (DSXi / DSX-L / DSX Standalone)
sources.date: 2024 (product line in commercial use; manual dated 2020)

sources.claim: Automated gas-detector docking stations physically bump-test and calibrate portable gas monitors on a schedule and log the results, so instruments are verified fit for use before a shift; the docked instrument is tested without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the pre-use safety check of gas-detection equipment. Same object (the portable methane/multi-gas monitor a miner carries), same accepted output (pass/fail plus a record of the check), performed by the machine once the instrument is docked.

sources.title: Galaxy GX2 Automated Test System for Gas Detector Calibration | MSA Safety
sources.claim: A second commercial automated test system performs testing and calibration of portable gas detectors without the user having to operate the device manually.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pre-use verification of gas detection instruments. Same instruments and same pass/fail output as the miner's pre-shift detector check; the station performs the gas application and sensor verification itself.

sources.date: 2023-10 (launch), scaled across hundreds of delivery stations by 2025
sources.title: Amazon unveils new AI-powered technology that will inspect delivery vans and help keep drivers safe
sources.claim: Automated drive-through inspection tunnels replace manual daily vehicle inspection reports at fleet depots, scanning tires, undercarriage and exterior for defects in seconds; coverage is limited to external imaging and does not include functional tests of controls, brakes, hydraulics or fluid levels.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the pre-operating safety inspection of a machine (DVIR walk-around). Cited to show the reach and the limit of deployed automation: purpose-built imaging tunnels cover exterior/tire/undercarriage defects only, not the hydraulic, functional and permissibility checks a roof bolter exam requires.

sources.system: ANYmal (with gas leak and presence detection payload)
sources.title: ANYbotics launches new gas leak, presence detection solution for inspection robots - International Mining
sources.claim: Legged inspection robots autonomously patrol industrial facilities collecting visual, thermal, acoustic and gas readings, including locating and quantifying gas leaks, but they sense only - they do not actuate machine controls or perform function tests.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine autonomous equipment inspection in industrial plants. Cited to bound capability - deployments are sensor sweeps of fixed plant in structured facilities, with no manipulation, no functional testing and no underground mobile-machine pre-op exams.

sources.title: Smarter tyre systems for haul road management - Australian Mining
sources.claim: Fixed autonomous thermal-imaging stations at mine sites inspect haul truck tyres as trucks pass, flagging hot spots and tread separations - an automated equipment check limited to a single component.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated condition checking of mining equipment in service. Cited to bound capability - deployed mining automation checks one component class (tyres) from a fixed station, not a multi-item pre-operational exam of a face machine.

tasks.label: Perform tests to determine if methane gas is present.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine methane test at the active working place during roof bolting in a room-and-pillar coal section: the bolter operator uses a permissible handheld methanometer to test before energizing the machine and at roughly 20-minute intervals while bolting, holding the detector within about 12 inches of the roof, face and ribs. Conditions: 4-7 ft seam, dust, water on an uneven mine floor, freshly cut ribs, moving equipment, ventilation curtain nearby; the place changes every cut.

Checking for layered or pocketed methane in hard-to-reach spots at the face: a high roof or roof-fall cavity, a drilled bolt hole, or the space above a brow, using an extendable probe or by raising the detector to the top of the cavity. Conditions: irregular void geometry, loose rock overhead, poor ventilation in the void.

Methane checks outby along the section's maintained entries and crosscuts: at the return, near the belt entry, at the power center and before energizing or trailing-cabling electrical equipment, and along travel routes to the working section. Conditions: rock-dusted, ventilated, standard-layout entries with fixed infrastructure, controlled access, generally clear travelways.

Pre-entry gas check of an idle, dead-end or seldom-travelled place before work begins there: an area idled for a shift, an area behind or beside a roof fall, the edge of a worked-out panel, or a low-seam crawl place with weak airflow. Conditions: taken as found, obstructed, poorly ventilated, no recent human presence.

Functional check and calibration of the gas-testing instruments themselves: bump-testing/calibrating the handheld permissible methane detector with calibration gas at the start of the ..., and functionally checking the machine-mounted methane monitor's alarm and power-shutoff on the bolter or nearby miner. Conditions: shop, lamp house or on the section, instrument in hand.

sources.title: ExRobotics develops 'new and improved' version of its inspection robot
sources.claim: ExRobotics' ATEX Zone 1 certified ExR-2 ground robot runs daily autonomous gas-detection rounds on pre-planned routes in petrochemical/oil-and-gas plants, checking each round for methane and automatically notifying the control room with the leak location; robots are in use at Shell, Equinor, BP, Chevron, Repsol, BASF and Woodside sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scheduled fugitive-methane detection rounds in a hazardous-area process plant. It transfers to mine methane testing because the measured quantity is identical (methane concentration in air at designated points on a fixed route), the robot is certified for potentially explosive atmospheres as mine gas testing requires, and the accepted output is the same - a pass/alarm determination reported to a control room.

sources.title: ExRobotics launches UL-certified inspection robot for hazardous environments - The Robot Report
sources.claim: ExRobotics' explosion-protected inspection robots have completed thousands of autonomous missions for major oil and gas operators, indicating routine commercial operation rather than one-off trials.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the ExR-2 item (routine gas-detection rounds in a hazardous-area facility); cited here to establish deployment maturity of that capability.

sources.system: ANYmal (Gas Leak and Presence Detection); ANYmal X
sources.title: ANYbotics Launches New Gas Leak & Presence Detection Solution for its ANYmal Inspection Robot
sources.claim: ANYbotics launched a Gas Leak and Presence Detection ... the ANYmal legged inspection robot that automates the whole gas concentration measurement and leak ... using the robot's autonomous mobility; ANYmal X is ATEX/IECEx Zone 1 certified for explosive atmospheres.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated gas-presence measurement rounds inside industrial plants. Transfers to methane testing because the payload is a swappable gas detector (hydrocarbons among them), the robot walks a route and takes concentration readings at designated points, and the deliverable is a presence/alarm determination, as in a mine gas exam.

sources.title: ANYbotics Launches Gas Leak and Presence Detection Solution for ANYmal Inspection Robot - Inside Unmanned Systems
sources.claim: ANYmal's modular gas detectors can be swapped for different gases and calibrated on site, and the robot continuously monitors gas concentrations around its body ... autonomous missions in industrial facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the preceding ANYbotics item; cited for the detail that concentration monitoring runs during autonomous (not only teleoperated) missions.

sources.system: ExynAero / ExynPak with Maestro IIoT gas sensor
sources.developer: Exyn Technologies and Maestro Digital Mine
sources.title: Exyn Technologies partners with Maestro Digital Mine | Global Mining Review
sources.claim: Exyn's fully autonomous underground drone was integrated with Maestro's IIoT gas sensor so it can be flown down mine drifts and into stopes to detect and ... hazardous gases; readings are captured in flight and geo-referenced. This is a product integration presented in 2022 rather than a documented production gas-exam deployment, and it is a hard-rock (blast-gas) application, not a permissible coal-mine methane instrument.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous gas measurement in underground mine headings before re-entry. Closest available analogue to the mine-face methane exam, but it measures blast gases in hard-rock drifts with non-permissible hardware, so it is recorded as context rather than as substantiation of an E3 coal-face methane exam.

sources.developer: Exyn Technologies with Maestro Digital Mine
sources.title: Exyn's drone-based mining autonomy ambitions taking flight - International Mining
sources.claim: Exyn's gas-monitoring drone captures gas sensor readings while flying under ExynAI autonomy and displays them in real time, with readings saved to coordinates in the point cloud.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile gas measurement in an underground mine. Supports that autonomous flight and gas sensing are combined in one platform, but the source describes a presented capability, not an accepted routine gas exam.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Maestro air quality station
sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / Maestro Digital Mine / Dwyka Mining Services
sources.title: Boston Dynamics - Dwyka Mining Services
sources.claim: A mining technology reseller describes sending Boston Dynamics' Spot carrying a Maestro air quality station with gas sensors to the working face after blasting to check for hazardous gases before re-entry; the page advertises programmable autonomous missions but does not establish that the underground gas runs are performed autonomously rather than under operator control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: post-blast atmospheric testing at an underground working face. Would be the closest analogue to a face gas exam, but autonomy is not established and the gases cited are blast gases, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: MSA GALAXY GX2 Automated Test System
sources.title: Galaxy GX2 Automated Test System for MSA Altair Gas Detectors | MSA
sources.claim: Automated test systems perform the whole bump test and calibration of portable gas detectors once the instrument is docked, applying calibration gas and recording pass/fail without a technician performing the gas application.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instrument bump test/calibration, which is the content of the instrument functional-check instance. It transfers directly: the machine applies the span gas, evaluates sensor response and records the result, i.e. the same accepted output the worker produces, with the work (the detector) brought to the machine.

sources.system: MSHA-approved machine-mounted methane monitors (30 CFR Part 27 / 75.342)
sources.developer: MSHA-approved methane monitor manufacturers (e.g. Conspec, Strata, Matrix)
sources.title: eCFR :: 30 CFR 75.342 -- Methane monitors
sources.claim: US underground coal mines run machine-mounted methane monitors that continuously test the atmosphere at the working place and act automatically: warning at 1.0 percent methane and automatic de-energization of the machine at 2.0 percent or on monitor failure.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, machine-performed: a fixed sensor positioned where the atmosphere to be tested is presented to it performs the methane determination continuously and acts physically on the equipment (power shutoff) without a person taking the reading.

tasks.label: Force bolts into holes, using hydraulic mechanisms of self-propelled bolting machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground bituminous coal mine, room-and-pillar development: dual-boom roof bolter working behind a continuous miner under an ATRS. Operator at deck controls indexes the head to each hole in the row, inserts resin cartridges and a 4-6 ft fully grouted bolt, and uses the hydraulic feed to force the bolt through the resin, spin-mix, hold and torque. Seam 42-84 in, dust, water, mud, uneven floor, freshly exposed roof that changes cut to cut.

Coal mine supplemental and adverse-ground support: cable bolts, extra-long bolts and trusses at intersections, rehab/re-bolting under deteriorated or drummy top, low-seam (<42 in) machines. Bolt placement and count adjusted on the fly from drill feel and roof feedback; irregular roof line, sloughing ribs, restricted working height.

Coal longwall gateroad or place-change development with bolting integrated on the mining machine (bolter miner / miner-bolter): bolts forced into holes from operator platforms alongside the cutting head while the machine advances; confined, dusty, noisy, with limited sightlines and continuous machine movement.

Underground hard-rock metal mine: mechanized bolting rig (jumbo-style bolter with carousel/magazine) installing resin, SDA or cement-grouted bolts, plus mesh, in 4-5 m drift backs after scaling, in development headings and in rehabilitation of squeezing/seismically damaged ground.

Underground stone/limestone or other nonmetal mine: mobile high-roof bolter installing 4-8 ft resin bolts on a standard pattern in wide, high (up to ~7-9 m) room-and-pillar openings; generally dry and competent ground, bolts installed from a cab or man-up basket.

sources.title: Boltec Auto Bolt Reload | Epiroc
sources.claim: Epiroc's Boltec Auto Bolt Reload rock bolting rig, a commercial product using self-drilling anchors and pumpable resin, offers autonomous functions including single-bolt auto, multi-bolt auto and teleremote operation for bolt installation in underground mine headings.

sources.title: Epiroc makes the 'impossible possible' with launch of Boltec ABR - International Mining
sources.claim: The Boltec ABR prototype was proven in production rehabilitation bolting at LKAB's Kiruna and Malmberget iron ore mines; in multi-bolt auto mode the machine continues installing bolts (magazine holds 8 in the feed, 44 on the carrier, 52 per heading) while the operator reloads, and the mode is offered for bolting during shift changes when no operator is on the machine.

sources.system: Sandvik DS412iE / DS512i rock support drill rigs
sources.title: Sandvik to add rock bolter to battery-powered mining line up - International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik's i-series rock bolters (DS412iE/DS512i) execute a complete bolting cycle - collaring, drilling, grouting, bolt handling from the magazine and tensioning - unassisted, with the operator only relocating the boom between bolt positions, in underground mine drifts and tunnels.

sources.title: Sandvik adds battery-electric cable bolter to underground mining equipment offering - International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik's battery-electric cable bolter launched in late 2025 carries one-hole automation, repeatable bolting accuracy, ... operation and full fan automation for cable bolt installation in underground mines.

sources.system: Joy Smart Bolter on 12CM miner bolter
sources.title: Smarter Bolters May Help Level the Field - Coal Age
sources.claim: Komatsu's Joy Smart Bolter, offered integrated on 12CM miner-bolter models used in underground coal, runs automatic drilling and bolting cycles from preset bolting parameters, but each cycle is initiated by an operator at the push-button control station who also positions the head.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: the automatic bolting cycle is exactly the hydraulic forcing of the bolt through resin into the drilled hole, plus spin and torque, on a coal roof bolter.

sources.system: J.H. Fletcher roof bolters (HDDR / automated bolting circuits)
sources.title: Smarter Bolters May Help Level the Field - Coal Age
sources.claim: J.H. Fletcher coal roof bolters provide an automated resin-spin and torque circuit after the bolt is fed through the resin, so the bolt-setting step itself runs to preset time and torque values without operator modulation.

sources.title: 3035-AD Remote Roof Bolter | J.H. Fletcher & Co.
sources.claim: Fletcher AD-series mobile bolters carry a bolt carousel so that, once loaded, drilling, resin insertion and bolt installation are all carried out by machine functions commanded from the enclosed cab, with no hand placement of bolts under unsupported roof.

sources.title: New Sandvik MB672 bolter miner set to accelerate longwall mining - International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik's newest coal bolter miner for longwall development (MB672, introduced August 2025) advances bolting automation but the manufacturer positions autonomous machine operation as a future step, indicating full-pattern autonomous bolting is not yet available in coal development machines.

sources.title: MacLean Engineering testing new robotic rock bolting in Sudbury - Sudbury News
sources.claim: MacLean Engineering is prototyping a robotic rock bolter (drills, withdraws steel, takes a bolt and inserts it) at its Sudbury test mine, but as of 2023 it was at prototype stage and the industry view is that ground support is the hardest mining step to make fully autonomous.

tasks.label: Perform ventilation tasks, such as hanging ventilation curtains and tubes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Room-and-pillar coal section, working face: hang and advance line brattice/check curtain to direct air to the face after each cut — unrolling brattice cloth, nailing/wedging it to the roof and ribs, weighting the bottom, sealing gaps, in a 4–7 ft seam with muddy uneven floor, dust, and freshly cut roof.

Coal section heading: hang, extend and connect flexible ventilation tubing from an auxiliary/scrubber fan to within a few feet of the face — lifting duct sections, attaching hangers/wire to roof bolts or the rib, joining sections and checking for leaks as the face advances.

Section crosscuts and travelways: hang, move, patch or replace check curtains and temporary curtain stoppings damaged by shuttle cars, scoops or roof falls; re-nail torn cloth, re-hang after ventilation plan changes.

Established intake/return or belt entry away from the face: hang curtains and route/secure vent tubing along a maintained, bolted, fixed-layout entry where equipment traffic and conditions are routine and the operator keeps the roadway to standard.

Underground metal/nonmetal mine or tunnel heading: install and extend larger-diameter rigid or flexible vent duct (bag) sections hung from roof-anchored hangers in a high, irregular blasted heading, typically working from a scissor lift or basket.

sources.system: Sandvik Roll Mesh Handler for bolters
sources.title: Roll mesh handler for bolters | Sandvik Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik's Roll Mesh Handler is a mechanized attachment on bolting rigs that grasps and unwinds a steel mesh roll along the tunnel profile so crews avoid working under unsupported ground; it is an operator-controlled aid on the rig, not an autonomous installer of flexible ventilation cloth or duct.
sources.transferJustification: Closest mechanized analogue to hanging sheet material against a mine roof (steel mesh rather than brattice cloth). It does not transfer: the handler positions a rigid steel roll that the rig then bolts, it is directed by the rig operator rather than run autonomously, and no source shows it nailing/sealing deformable brattice or connecting ventilation tubing.

sources.system: Epiroc Boltec with Auto Bolt Reload (ABR)
sources.title: Epiroc makes the ‘impossible possible’ with launch of Boltec ABR | International Mining
sources.claim: Epiroc's Boltec ABR automates the bolt reload and bolting sequence for underground rock reinforcement, showing that automation in this occupation has reached the bolting cycle itself but not auxiliary ventilation work such as curtain or duct hanging.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is roof/rock bolting by the same occupation in the same underground environment. It does not transfer to hanging ventilation curtains or tubes: bolting handles rigid steel consumables fed from a magazine, whereas brattice cloth and flexible duct are deformable materials that must be lifted, aligned to an irregular roof line, fastened and sealed.

sources.title: NORMET – For Tough Jobs (Normet International Ltd. catalog)
sources.claim: Normet Utilift machines are the standard equipment used underground for installing pipes and ventilation equipment, but they are human-operated scissor-lift platforms that carry workers who do the hanging, not autonomous robots.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers underground ventilation-equipment installation, the same task family. It cannot support a positive judgment because the machine only lifts and positions a crew and materials; the installation itself is performed manually by the miners on the platform.

tasks.label: Dust rocks after bolting.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dry rock dusting of the place just bolted, at or near the working face of a room-and-pillar section: the bolter crew runs a hose from a machine-mounted or portable pneumatic (bantam) duster and coats roof, ribs and floor of the freshly bolted heading to within 40 ft of the face. Geometry changes with every 20-40 ft cut; floor is rutted with cable, bolt trash and water; visibility poor in the dust cloud.

Hand/spot dusting after bolting: the operator opens 50-lb bags of rock dust and casts or brushes it onto areas the duster hose missed - corners, behind standing support, around the bolter and power center, ribs sloughed since the last pass - checking coverage by eye against the 80% incombustible standard.

Wet/foam slurry dusting of the newly bolted entry once the bolter is pulled, using a scoop- or trailer-mounted applicator and a hand-held wand to spray roof and ribs while other crew members work in the adjacent entry.

Low-seam mine (36-48 in): after bolting, the operator dusts kneeling or lying under a low, irregular roof, dragging the duster hose or bags through restricted clearance, often in wet or muddy bottom, with limited room to swing the nozzle to cover roof, ribs and floor.

Mechanized bulk dusting of the entries and crosscuts already developed behind the bolter on the section - a mobile pod/slinger duster or a trickle duster set in an established, fixed-layout roadway with ventilation controls in place, run to bring the entry back to required incombustible content.

sources.system: Strata Automatic Stone Dust Storage and Dispersal System (20-tonne POD + trickle dusters)
sources.date: 2018-2022 (installation from late 2018; case study page current)
sources.title: Automatic Stone Dusting in Australia | Strata Worldwide
sources.claim: Deployed installed system at Moolarben Coal Mine that pneumatically moves bulk stone dust from a surface silo to underground PODs and feeds trickle dusters that continuously apply stone dust at the longwall tailgate; transfer is PLC-controlled and dispersal is set and monitored from surface or underground control rooms rather than applied by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Same task material and output standard (stone/rock dust applied to underground coal mine surfaces to hold the TIC ratio), performed by a fixed purpose-built installation instead of a worker; it substantiates machine application of rock dust where dust and surfaces are presented to the machine (E1-style), not mobile face dusting.

sources.system: Trickle dusters / high-pressure mechanical rock dust distribution systems
sources.title: P13-V-11 | Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA)
sources.claim: MSHA guidance describes mechanical rock dust distribution systems - trickle dusters and high-pressure rock dusting machines - running continuously in critical mine areas to maintain the required incombustible ..., i.e. machine-applied rock dusting that meets the regulatory acceptance standard.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (applying rock dust to mine surfaces to a measured incombustible-content standard) done by an installed machine that runs unattended at a fixed point; it does not travel to freshly bolted headings, so it supports machine dusting only where the work is brought to the machine.

sources.system: ABB Compact Interior Paint Station (12-robot paint cell) / ABB automotive paint robots
sources.date: 2020-11-24 (product launch; technology in series production use since)
sources.title: Compact Interior Paint Station designed by ABB to minimize space, costs | The Robot Report
sources.claim: Commercial fenced robotic coating cells apply sprayed coatings to complex surfaces presented to the robots by conveyor at production quality, including multi-robot stations that coat vehicle interiors inside paint booths.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of a sprayed coating to surfaces brought to the machine on a fixture/conveyor. Rock dusting is a coarser version of the same action (uniform particulate coverage of a surface) with far looser precision tolerances, so a purpose-built coating cell fed bulk dust could cover presented surfaces.

sources.title: Innovative Rock-Dusting System to Assist with Respirable Dust Compliance - Coal Age
sources.claim: In current US practice the dusting done right after the bolter is pulled is manual: a scoop operator plus a miner holding the applicator wand spray the roof and ribs of the freshly bolted place.
sources.transferJustification: Same task; cited to characterise the instances (hand-guided application after the bolter is pulled) and to show the best available mechanised face-dusting equipment is human-operated, not autonomous.

sources.system: Underground coal mine auxiliary-operation robots (shotcreting, dredging, etc.)
sources.developer: Chinese coal-robotics research community (review by Wang Lei, CCTEG)
sources.title: 王雷：煤矿井下辅助作业机器人研究与应用进展_智能矿山网
sources.claim: Review of underground coal-mine auxiliary-operation robotics in China states that roadway auxiliary work such as wet shotcreting is still done with manually operated semi-mechanised equipment and that existing products cannot yet meet reduced-crew or unmanned requirements for roadway auxiliary operations.
sources.transferJustification: Closest analogue inside an underground coal roadway (spraying material onto roadway surfaces). It reports such machines remain manually operated, so it does not support autonomous surface-coating work inside a mine.

sources.title: GRIT BLASTER | J.H. Fletcher & Co.
sources.claim: Mining-equipment maker Fletcher offers a long-reach robotic water/grit blasting machine with a semi-autonomous cycle that automatically maintains nozzle direction, speed, angle and distance ... the surface being treated; machine positioning remains operator-directed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated stand-off surface treatment of large irregular surfaces by the same manufacturer that builds roof bolters. Only the nozzle cycle is automated and the operator positions the boom, so it is treated as teleoperated and supports no positive judgment.

tasks.label: Install various types of bolts, including truss, glue, and resin bolts, traversing entire ceiling spans.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground coal room-and-pillar/development section, medium seam (roughly 5–8 ft): following the continuous miner, the bolter operator installs a full row pattern of resin-grouted (glue) roof bolts across the entire entry span (4–6 bolts per row, ~4 ft centers), setting bearing plates and occasional straps, drilling with dual booms under ATRS, in dust, water and variable roof.

Underground coal low-seam section (36–54 in mining height): same primary resin/mechanical bolting across the entry span, but with the operator working from a kneeling/prone platform on a low-profile bolter, hand-feeding short drill steels, resin cartridges, bolts and plates in severely confined space with muddy, uneven floor.

Supplemental/secondary support in coal: installing roof trusses (paired angled holes near the ribs, resin-anchored tendons, cross tie-rod threaded and tensioned with turnbuckles) and long cable/tendon bolts at intersections and adverse-roof areas, with placement chosen from observed roof conditions.

Rehabilitation / re-support work: re-bolting deteriorated main and belt entries, ground around roof falls, longwall setup and recovery rooms — installing bolts through mesh/straps into irregular, broken or previously supported roof, working around debris, cribs and existing hardware.

Underground hard-rock metal/nonmetal mine heading: mechanized bolting rig (cabin-operated) installs a designed pattern of resin- or cement-grouted and friction bolts, plus welded mesh, across the back and shoulders of a 4.5–5 m drift after each round, in freshly blasted ground.

sources.system: Automated bolting and meshing system for continuous miners (University of Wollongong / ACARP roadway development automation project)
sources.developer: University of Wollongong (with CSIRO Mining Technology / ACARP)
sources.title: Automated bolting and meshing on a continuous miner for roadway development - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: University of Wollongong / CSIRO-linked ACARP research built reprogrammable electromechanical manipulators retrofitted to a continuous miner that automate the complete primary support cycle (roof and rib bolts plus mesh); above-ground trials ran the full automated bolting cycle without human intervention at production-consistent rates.

sources.system: Automated bolting and meshing system for continuous miners
sources.title: Automated bolting and meshing on a continuous miner for roadway development - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: The same automated bolting/meshing system was dimensioned for large roadways (minimum 2.8 m roof height, 5 m width) and a support density of six roof bolts and four rib bolts per metre of advance — i.e. it was not built for low-seam coal openings.

sources.system: Autonomous roof bolt installation robotic assembly (industrial robotic arm)
sources.developer: University of Kentucky, Department of Mining Engineering
sources.title: A METHODOLOGY FOR AUTONOMOUS ROOF BOLT INSTALLATION USING INDUSTRIAL ROBOTICS
sources.claim: A robotic assembly using an anthropomorphic industrial arm was developed to carry out the entire roof-bolting sequence (drill steel positioning, drilling, resin placement, bolt placement and securing) autonomously, and was tested in a purpose-built mock mine.

sources.system: Epiroc Boltec ABR (Auto Bolt Reload), Boltec M10/E10 carriers
sources.title: Boltec Auto Bolt Reload | Epiroc
sources.claim: Epiroc's commercial Boltec Auto Bolt Reload rock bolting rig offers machine-executed bolting modes — single bolt auto and multi bolt auto — plus bolt plan navigation, automatic resin injection and automatic reloading of the feed magazine from a 44-bolt carrier magazine, using self-drilling anchors and pumpable resin.

sources.title: Epiroc makes the ‘impossible possible’ with launch of Boltec ABR - International Mining
sources.claim: In multi-bolt auto mode the Boltec ABR installs bolts while the operator carries out other work such as magazine reloading; the prototype rig has been used underground for bolt-and-mesh rehabilitation at LKAB's Kiruna mine and trialled at Malmberget.

sources.system: Sandvik DS412iE / DS412i / DS512i rock bolting rigs
sources.title: Sandvik to add rock bolter to battery-powered mining line up - International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik's i-Class bolters (DS412iE/DS412i/DS512i) execute a complete single bolting cycle — drill, resin/cement, bolt insertion — under machine control, but the operator must still manually relocate the boom from ... position to the next, so full-pattern bolting underground is not autonomous.

sources.system: MacLean robotic/autonomous bolting development (975 Omnia bolter platform)
sources.title: MacLean Engineering testing new robotic rock bolting in Sudbury - Northern Ontario Business
sources.claim: As of 2023 the leading North American bolter OEM described autonomous rock bolting as being in very early testing, with its robotic bolter only at prototype stage and under test in a company test mine near Sudbury.

tasks.label: Drill test holes and test bolts for specified tension, using torque wrenches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground coal section, active face: after installing a row of tension-type (mechanical/combination) roof bolts, the bolter operator torque-tests a required sample of the installed bolts overhead with a calibrated torque wrench under the ATRS/supported roof, judges whether each meets the specified torque/tension, re-tensions or reports failures, and records results for the roof control plan. Low seam height, dust, water, uneven floor, bolts at varying heights and angles.

Underground coal section, active face: drilling roof test holes at plan-specified locations (each intersection, at fixed intervals along the entry) to a specified depth, watching drill penetration, feel, water/cuttings and hole depth to identify voids, soft strata, bed separation and remaining competent roof thickness, then reporting the finding and calling for supplemental support if needed.

Underground metal/nonmetal (hard-rock) mine drift: quality-assurance testing of installed resin/mechanical/friction rock bolts — torque check or pull test on a sampled bolt from a bolter deck or basket, attaching the tool to the bolt head in an irregular rock back, applying load to the specified value and logging the result.

Areas of adverse roof or rehabilitation work: drilling test holes and re-checking bolt tension where the roof is broken, sagging, cut by slips or already carrying straps, mats, cribs and supplemental supports; bolt heads are obstructed or corroded, positions are irregular, and the ground is only partly supported.

Established, maintained coal mine entries/mains and travelways: periodic spot re-torque checks of previously installed bolts during examinations along a graded, rock-dusted roadway with fixed layout and controlled access, recording torque readings for the record book.

sources.system: Epiroc Boltec ABR (Auto Bolt Reload) rock bolting rig
sources.title: Epiroc makes the 'impossible possible' with launch of Boltec ABR
sources.claim: Epiroc's Boltec ABR rock bolting rig, sold commercially for underground mines, offers a multi-bolt auto mode (and tele-remote) in which the rig drills the hole and installs bolts in a heading without an operator physically on the ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drilling bolt holes in the rock back/roof of an underground heading and installing bolts. Transfer to drilling test holes: same environment (underground mine roof), same tool (hydraulic rock drill on a boom), same output (a hole of specified depth at a plan-specified roof location); only the purpose of the hole differs.

sources.system: Epiroc Boomer face drill rigs with ABC Total / Auto RHS
sources.title: Advanced Boom Control | Epiroc
sources.claim: Epiroc's Advanced Boom Control (ABC Total), a commercial automation option on Boomer face drill rigs used in underground mines and tunnels, positions the boom and drills a complete sequence of holes automatically to a digital drill plan.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic drilling of planned hole patterns in rock in an underground drift. Transfer to drilling test holes: identical environment and rock-drilling hardware, holes are located from a digital plan and drilled to specified depth, which is what a roof test hole requires mechanically.

sources.system: Epiroc Measure While Drilling (MWD) with Underground Manager
sources.title: Measure While Drilling | Epiroc US
sources.claim: Epiroc's Measure While Drilling, a commercial system on its underground drill rigs, automatically registers drilling parameters for each hole and analyses them with geological information to characterise the rock being drilled.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: rock-mass characterisation from drilling response. Transfer to test holes: the information a miner obtains by feel and cuttings while drilling a test hole (voids, soft bands, competent thickness) is the same information MWD extracts automatically from thrust/rotation/penetration logs on the same class of underground rock drilling.

sources.system: Instrumented Fletcher twin-head roof bolter with drill-parameter monitoring (NIOSH research)
sources.title: An Approach to Identifying Geological Properties from Roof Bolter Drilling Parameters
sources.claim: An instrumented J.H. Fletcher twin-head roof bolter with an automated drill-control and data-collection system recorded thrust, rotation speed, torque and penetration velocity during roof bolt drilling in underground coal mines to infer roof strata properties, including void and bed-separation locations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sensing roof strata while drilling with a coal roof bolter. Directly relevant to the interpretive half of drilling a test hole, but boom placement and the drilling cycle remain operator-controlled, so autonomy is unclear.

sources.system: Robot guided bolt tensioning tool (self-adaptive assembly system)
sources.developer: ZeMA / Saarland University with industry partners (published in Production Engineering)
sources.title: Robot guided bolt tensioning tool with adaptive process control for the automated assembly of wind turbine rotor blade bearings
sources.claim: A robot-guided bolt tensioning tool with adaptive process control locates each bolted joint, mounts the tensioning tool and applies the specified preload to each bolt in sequence in an automated wind turbine hub assembly system, using integrated measurement to compensate tolerances.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying and verifying a specified preload/tension on large structural bolts. Transfer to torque-testing roof bolts: comparable fastener sizes and torque levels, same operation of locating a bolt head, engaging a socket/tensioner and driving to a specified tension with sensed feedback — but demonstrated only with the workpiece fixtured in an assembly cell.

sources.system: Automated bolt tensioning system with Reis RV60-60 industrial robot
sources.title: An adaptive and automated bolt tensioning system for the pitch bearing assembly of wind turbines
sources.claim: An adaptive, automated bolt tensioning system built around a Reis RV60-60 industrial robot was developed to tension the bolted joints of wind turbine pitch bearings, replacing manual hydraulic tensioning in the assembly process.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic tensioning of large bolted joints to a specified clamping force in a fixtured assembly station; same manipulation and precision class as torque-testing a roof bolt, but only in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: AUTOBOLT R&D Project | quality NDT services
sources.claim: AUTOBOLT, a 10 kg robot placed into a wind turbine tower by a technician, is under development to drive autonomously along a flange bolt circle and measure the tension of each bolt with an EMAT ultrasonic sensor instead of a manual torque tool.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated verification of installed bolt tension in the field. It runs on a regular flange bolt circle inside a tower and is still an R&D device placed by a technician, so it does not substantiate completion on an irregular rock roof.

sources.system: Sandvik Pull Test Module (digital ground support platform)
sources.title: Rock Bolt Pull Test Module Technology for Mining Safety
sources.claim: Sandvik's Pull Test Module, the current digital tool for verifying installed rock bolts underground, is a hand-attached instrument: operators attach the module to the bolt head and the hydraulics apply the load while data uploads automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (verifying installed bolt tension underground); cited to show the state of the art in mines is an operator-attached instrument, not a robot, so no positive judgment above E1 rests on it.

tasks.label: Position safety jacks to support underground mine roofs until bolts can be installed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground coal room-and-pillar development section: after a cut, the bolter operator trams the roof bolting machine (or bolter-miner) from under supported roof toward the face and positions the machine-mounted temporary support — ATRS canopy and boom mast jacks — pressurizing it against freshly exposed, variable roof before each drilling/bolting cycle; repeated many times per shift in a dusty, wet, uneven-floored entry.

Coal mine: setting free-standing safety jacks, jack posts, props or timber by hand where the machine-mounted ATRS cannot be used or is insufficient — wide places, intersections, brows, low-seam areas, spots with drummy or draw-rock top — carrying the jack in, choosing the set point from the roof condition, and pressurizing it until permanent bolts go in.

Underground stone/metal-nonmetal mine (limestone room-and-pillar, hard-rock drift): mechanized bolter with machine-mounted temporary support/safety jack positioned against a high, irregular rock back in a large opening before bolts are installed; standard mine equipment, larger and more variable geometry than coal.

Bad-ground, roof-fall or rehabilitation work: setting jacks, props and cribs amid fallen rock, irregular cavities and debris to secure an area before re-bolting; set points chosen ad hoc from the shape of the fall, footing uneven, work done under a compromised roof.

Longwall-related support work: positioning supports in gate roads, at longwall setup/recovery, or advancing mobile roof supports along a pillar line during retreat mining, holding the roof over the work area until bolts or permanent support are installed.

sources.system: Automated longwall powered roof supports with electrohydraulic/programmable face automation
sources.developer: Eickhoff Mining Technology / HBT GmbH (longwall automation control systems)
sources.title: Unfolding longwall automation - North American Mining Magazine
sources.claim: Automatic advance and setting of powered roof supports (hydraulic legs with canopies pressed against the natural mine roof) as the shearer passes is the defining, deployed feature of modern longwall automation in operating underground coal mines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: advancing and setting powered roof supports. Powered roof supports are hydraulic props (jacks) with canopies set against as-found mine roof to hold it over a work area, then lowered, advanced and re-set — the same physical act, forces and precision as positioning temporary support ahead of permanent support, in the same underground coal environment.

sources.system: Joy Faceboss RS20n / RS20s powered roof support (PRS) electro-hydraulic control
sources.title: Komatsu | Joy-engineered powered roof support (PRS) solutions
sources.claim: Komatsu's Joy powered-roof-support control system provides automated roof-support sequences and automatic gate turn-arounds for a largely operator-free longwall face, with proximity interlocks that block shield advance when a person is detected.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic control of hydraulic roof supports underground. It substantiates that setting, releasing and repositioning temporary hydraulic roof support against natural rock is executed by machine control at production reliability in a working mine.

sources.system: ATRS (Automated Temporary Roof Support) on roof bolting machines
sources.developer: MSHA-mandated; built by J.H. Fletcher & Co., Komatsu (Joy) and others
sources.title: eCFR :: 30 CFR 75.209 -- Automated Temporary Roof Support (ATRS) systems.
sources.claim: US underground coal mines are required to use machine-mounted Automated Temporary Roof Support (ATRS) with roof bolting machines; the ATRS canopy and boom mast jacks are hydraulically pressurized against the roof, but actuated by the operator from the machine's protected compartment.

sources.system: ATRS systems on roof bolting machines and integral bolters
sources.developer: US Bureau of Mines / MSHA / equipment OEMs
sources.title: Automated Temporary Roof Support Systems: An Update (OneMine)
sources.claim: Machine-mounted ATRS has largely replaced manual setting of temporary roof supports in US coal mines, but it is an operator-commanded hydraulic canopy rather than an autonomous system.

sources.title: MOBILE ROOF SUPPORTS | J.H. Fletcher & Co.
sources.claim: Mobile roof supports used for pillar recovery and gate-road protection are self-propelled hydraulic roof supports, but they are moved and set by radio remote control by an operator, not autonomously.

sources.system: Epiroc Boltec ABR (Auto Bolt Reload), with multi-bolt auto and tele-remote options
sources.title: Boltec Auto Bolt Reload | Epiroc US
sources.claim: Epiroc's Boltec ABR rock bolting rig performs mechanized, automated reloading and multi-bolt automatic installation of rock support elements from an on-board magazine in underground mine headings, keeping the operator in the cabin.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine handling and installation of discrete rock-support elements. It shows a machine can take a support element presented in a known position (magazine/carousel) and place it against the mine roof under machine control — the handling step needed to set a presented jack in a purpose-built presentation.

sources.system: Temporary support robot for section-coal-pillar excavation (virtual prototype)
sources.developer: Xi'an University of Science and Technology group (Applied Sciences 2025)
sources.title: Research on Temporary Support Robot for the Integrated Excavation and Mining System of Section Coal Pillar
sources.claim: Purpose-built 'temporary support robots' for coal mine roadway excavation remain at the research/virtual-prototype stage, though self-moving temporary support equipment able to advance itself is reported in coal mine roadway excavation.

sources.system: Gantry shield-type intelligent tunneling robot system (includes temporary support robots)
sources.developer: Xi'an University of Science and Technology / Xi'an Coal Mining Machinery Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Research and practice of intelligent coal mine technology systems in China
sources.claim: Chinese intelligent tunneling robot systems that include temporary support robots alongside tunneling and anchor drilling robots are reported as developmental system concepts rather than production deployments with established autonomy.

tasks.label: Rotate chucks to turn bolts and open expansion heads against rock formations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground coal room-and-pillar section, standard entry (~5–7 ft seam): operator on a dual-boom roof bolter under the ATRS seats a resin/combination or mechanical-anchor bolt in the drill chuck, spins it to mix resin or expand the shell anchor against the borehole wall, and torques the head against the bearing plate; dust, water, uneven floor, roof lithology varying hole to hole.

Low-seam coal (under ~48 in): operator kneeling/lying on the bolter deck in a confined seam performs the same chuck rotation to set expansion heads/anchors and torque bolts, with very limited clearance between machine, roof and floor.

Coal intersections, rib bolting, and rehabilitation/secondary support in older entries: longer bolts and cable bolts, re-torquing loosened bolts, bolting at odd angles behind obstructions, sometimes with hand-held tools or wrenches.

Underground hard-rock metal/non-metal mine development drift (4–5 m heading): operator runs a mechanized bolting rig from a cabin; the bolting head takes a bolt from the carousel, inserts it into the drilled hole, rotates it to set the anchor/mix resin and tightens against the plate, with screen/mesh often installed.

Hard-rock narrow-vein, stope or rehab work in confined places a rig cannot reach: hand-held jackleg/stoper bolting, bolts spun up with a hand-held rotation unit or wrench to open the expansion shell against the rock.

Civil tunneling / shaft or portal ground support: bolts installed into a blasted or bored tunnel profile from a mechanized bolting rig standing on a prepared invert, expansion-shell or resin anchors spun and torqued to a specified pattern.

sources.system: Sandvik DS412iE / DS412i rock bolter (BHi bolting head, SICA control)
sources.title: DS412iE FULLY ELECTRIC ROCK BOLTER — brochure and specification sheet
sources.claim: Sandvik DS412iE is a commercially sold underground rock bolter whose bolting head performs the bolt installation step automatically ('one bolt automation'), with the maker claiming up to 90% of bolt installation done automatically.
sources.transferJustification: The automated cycle includes rotating the bolt in the bolting head to mix resin/cement and tighten the bolt against the plate — the same chuck-rotation act used to open an expansion head against the rock, on the same class of 1.5–3 m steel bolts in overhead rock.

sources.title: Sandvik to add rock bolter to battery-powered mining line up — International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik states the rig executes a complete bolting cycle without operator assistance, the operator only relocating the boom between bolt positions.
sources.transferJustification: The unassisted cycle covers inserting the bolt and spinning/tensioning it in the hole, which is the chuck-turning and anchor-setting act described by this task.

sources.title: Sandvik follows up new battery DS412iE bolter with the diesel DS412i model — International Mining
sources.claim: The diesel Sandvik DS412i, sold for underground mining and tunneling, offers up to 90% automatic bolting via one-bolt automation and handles a wide range of bolt types with automatic cement mixing and resin injection.
