sources.transferJustification: Bolt installation automation covers the insertion and rotation/tensioning of the bolt, transferring directly to turning bolts and setting anchors against the rock.

sources.title: Epiroc makes the ‘impossible possible’ with launch of Boltec ABR — International Mining
sources.claim: Epiroc's Boltec ABR bolting rig offers a multi-bolt automatic mode and tele-remote operation so bolts can be installed without an operator on the machine; it is a boom-mounted bolting rig for underground mine headings.
sources.transferJustification: Multi-bolt auto mode performs successive bolt installations, including driving/rotating the self-drilling anchor and setting it with resin — the machine-side equivalent of spinning bolts to anchor them against the rock.

sources.title: Epiroc’s new Boltec with Auto Bolt Reload redefines safety and productivity within rock reinforcement — Epiroc newsroom
sources.claim: The Boltec ABR was trialled underground in a production hard-rock mine (LKAB Malmberget) and roughly doubled bolting productivity versus the mine's conventional bolting fleet.

sources.system: Epiroc Boltec S / M / E rock bolting rigs (RCS)
sources.title: Rock bolting rigs | Epiroc US
sources.claim: Epiroc's mechanized bolting rig range covers roof heights from 1.8 m upward and uses a computerized Rig Control System for positioning, drilling and bolting, with automatic resin injection and automatic cement systems.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the automated bolting head can work in low headings comparable to a mid-height coal entry, and that bolt installation (including rotation and grouting) is machine-controlled.

sources.title: New Sandvik MB672 bolter miner set to accelerate longwall mining
sources.claim: Sandvik's newest coal longwall-development bolter miner (MB672, 2025) presents bolting automation as a direction of development rather than an existing capability, indicating that automated bolt installation is not yet fielded in coal.

sources.system: J.H. Fletcher CHDDR-4 coal roof bolter
sources.title: CHDDR-4 Coal Roof Bolter | J.H. Fletcher & Co.
sources.claim: Current US coal roof bolters remain manually operated machines requiring operators at each drill mast.

sources.title: MacLean Engineering testing new robotic rock bolting in Sudbury — Sudbury News
sources.claim: As of 2023 a leading hard-rock ground-support OEM described autonomous rock bolting as at a very early testing stage, with its human-collaborative bolting machine only a prototype.

sources.system: Robotic roof bolting module (six-axis arm on a roof bolter)
sources.title: Integrating robotic systems in underground roof support machine — ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Academic work has integrated a six-axis robotic arm into an existing coal roof bolter to automate the bolting module, but this remains a research prototype rather than a fielded system.

tasks.label: Remove drill bits from chucks after drilling holes, and insert bolts into chucks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: US underground coal mine, low seam (roughly 30–60 in.), room-and-pillar section: operator on a dual-boom bolter (e.g., Fletcher LOW RRII/LTDO class) kneeling or lying under the ATRS, pulls the hot, wet drill steel with bit out of the chuck by hand, sets it aside, then hand-loads a 4–6 ft resin-anchored bolt with plate into the same chuck; dust, water spray, mud, restricted headroom, repeated 40–100 times per shift.

US underground coal mine, medium-to-high seam (5–10+ ft) development or longwall gate-road section: operator standing at the bolter deck removes the drill steel/bit from the chuck after each hole and inserts resin bolts, occasionally longer steels or cable bolts requiring coupling, under a temporary roof support canopy; uneven floor, changing roof conditions.

Underground hard-rock metal mine development heading (drift-and-fill, ramp, stope access): bolter operator works from a mechanized rock-support rig cab; between holes the drill rod/bit must be withdrawn and swapped for a friction, resin or self-drilling anchor bolt (5–20 ft), often with mesh, in a muck-strewn heading with variable back profile.

Underground nonmetal room-and-pillar mine (limestone, salt, trona, industrial minerals): mobile roof bolter with high back (12–30 ft), long drill steels and long resin or mechanical bolts; steel/bit is removed from the chuck after each hole and a bolt inserted, sometimes at angles for rib support, in a dry, dusty, high-clearance heading.

sources.system: Sandvik DS512i rock support drill rig (i-Class)
sources.title: Sandvik improves rock bolting safety and efficiency with DS512i - International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik's i-Class rock bolter DS512i is sold with a 'one bolt' automation package in which the rig itself performs collaring, drilling, grouting, bolt handling and tensioning, i.e. the drill-rod-to-bolt changeover is machine-executed rather than done by hand; the rig also carries an eight-bolt carousel.

sources.system: Sandvik DS412i rock support drill rig
sources.title: DS412i | Sandvik Mining
sources.claim: The Sandvik DS412i rock support drill rig, a commercial bolter for 4.5 m x 4.5 m underground headings, carries an eight-rock-bolt carousel feeding its bolting head, so bolts are indexed to the head mechanically instead of being hand-loaded, with 'various levels of automation' offered on the i-Class platform.

sources.title: Boltec Auto Bolt Reload | Epiroc
sources.claim: Epiroc's Boltec Auto Bolt Reload rig mechanizes the entire bolt supply chain on the machine: bolts are transferred automatically from a 44-bolt carrier magazine to the feed carousel that presents them to the bolting head, with no operator handling; product video shows the rig working underground at LKAB's Kiruna mine.

sources.system: Epiroc Boltec M10 S / E10 S rock bolting rig
sources.title: Boltec M10 S and E10 S | Epiroc US
sources.claim: Epiroc's commercial Boltec M10 S / E10 S underground rock bolting rigs offer a 'Single Bolt Auto' function in which the rig runs the drilling and bolt-installation sequence for a bolt automatically, improving repeatability of bolt installation over manual handling.

sources.system: Automated roof bolting machine with six-axis robotic arm (prototype)
sources.developer: University research team (published in Mining, Metallurgy & Exploration)
sources.title: Development of an automated roof bolting machine for underground coal mines
sources.claim: A research prototype integrated a six-axis robotic arm into an existing coal roof bolter so that the machine executes drilling, removal of the drill steels, resin placement and bolt installation in sequence, with the human reduced to supervising via a touchpad; the work is a development prototype rather than a mine deployment.

sources.system: Automated bolting and meshing manipulators for continuous miner roadway development
sources.title: Automated bolting and meshing on a continuous miner for roadway development - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: An Australian program built manipulators to take over the manual consumable-handling tasks (bolt and mesh handling) of roadway-development bolting on a continuous miner; their performance was evaluated in laboratory surface trials, not in an operating mine.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: transferring drill steels and bolts into the bolting head on a coal roadway-development machine; establishes only laboratory (purpose-built) performance.

sources.developer: J.H. Fletcher & Co. / SME conference paper authors (Willaman, Saeler)
sources.title: Automation of Roof Bolting in Underground Coal Mines Through Electrohydraulic Control | OneMine
sources.claim: State of the art in underground coal roof bolting: electrohydraulic rigs installed in mines provide only partial automation of the drilling and bolting cycles, and an automated bolt storage and loading system is still described as the next development stage, i.e. bolt loading into the chuck remains a manual field task.

sources.system: J.H. Fletcher AR-D coal bolter / 3035-AD remote bolter
sources.title: AR-D Coal Bolter | J.H. Fletcher & Co.
sources.claim: Commercial US coal roof bolters remain manual-insertion machines: Fletcher's coal models are described as booms designed for manual drilling and ..., while carousel-fed, cab-operated bolters are offered for hard-rock/high headings.

tasks.label: Tighten ends of anchored truss bolts, using turnbuckles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Low/medium-seam room-and-pillar coal mine intersection (42–60 in. roof height): after angled truss bolts are anchored in the roof, the bolter operator assembles the tie-rod/turnbuckle across the diagonal span and tightens the turnbuckle with an impact or ratchet wrench to the specified tension, then verifies with a torque wrench. Work is overhead, from under the bolter canopy/ATRS, in dust, water and poor light.

Higher-seam coal entry or haulage/belt roadway (6–8 ft): truss installed as supplemental support along the roadway or at a fault/slip; worker snugs the nuts at both anchored bolt ends and then tensions the turnbuckle to spec, working overhead from the bolter deck or a scoop/mantrip deck.

Rehabilitation of deteriorating roof in older workings or return entries: broken/uneven roof, sloughed ribs, mud and water underfoot, restricted access; trusses installed to stabilize an area and the turnbuckles tightened with hydraulic/impact wrench, sometimes with blocking, plates or wedges added and re-seated during tensioning.

Re-tensioning previously installed trusses: during examination or scheduled maintenance, turnbuckles found loose or trusses that have relaxed are re-tightened to specified tension and the result recorded/reported.

Underground stone/metal–nonmetal mine or civil tunnel: cable truss or rod truss installed in a limestone/trona entry or tunnel back, tensioned via turnbuckle from a scissor lift, basket or bolting rig platform at greater back heights.

sources.system: Atlas Copco Fixtured Nutrunner QST / fixtured assembly solutions
sources.title: Fixtured Nutrunner QST | Atlas Copco
sources.claim: Commercially supplied fixtured nutrunners are built for fully automated robotic tightening of high-torque threaded joints in purpose-built assembly stations — the core physical act of this task (running a threaded member down and torquing it to spec) when the work is fixtured and presented.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated torque-controlled fastening of steel threaded joints. Transfers because a truss turnbuckle/anchor nut is an ordinary high-torque threaded joint tightened to a specified torque/tension; in a fixtured cell the socket engagement geometry is known, which is the condition these nutrunners are designed for.

sources.title: Tightening Cell Robotics - Atlas Copco USA
sources.claim: Turnkey robotic tightening cells combining industrial robots, vision, torque tools and part presentation are sold and installed as standard automated assembly stations with per-joint torque/angle traceability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic fastening cells in manufacturing. Transfers to the E1 counterfactual because the cell supplies exactly what E1 assumes — the workpiece presented in a known position, a robot-carried torque tool, and closed-loop torque verification equivalent to the worker's torque-wrench check.

sources.system: Burke E. Porter suspension assembly & alignment / toe-set systems
sources.date: 2019-12 (page); technology in plant use for decades
sources.title: Suspension Assembly & Alignment | Burke Porter Group
sources.claim: Production machines that adjust a threaded tie-rod (a turnbuckle-type length adjuster) to a target and re-torque its lock nuts are sold as fully automatic fixtured stations in vehicle assembly plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated toe setting, in which a machine grips and rotates an adjustable threaded tie rod to a measured target and then tightens the clamp/lock nuts. Objects (coarse steel threaded adjuster), torque levels and the measure-adjust-lock sequence match tightening a truss turnbuckle to a specified tension; environment is the fixtured station assumed at E1.

sources.system: Epiroc Boltec with Auto Bolt Reload (ABR)
sources.title: Epiroc's Boltec with ABR redefines underground safety - Safe To Work
sources.claim: State-of-the-art underground rock-bolting rigs automate bolt reloading and single-hole drill/bolt cycles but keep a human operator in the cab positioning the boom; no automated handling or tensioning of truss tie-rods/turnbuckles is offered.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the closest in-mine (E3) automation to this task: it installs bolts under operator control, does not autonomously locate and torque a separately assembled truss turnbuckle, so it cannot support a positive judgment at E2 or E3.

sources.system: MacLean robotic rock bolter (robotic arm on bolting truck)
sources.title: MacLean Engineering testing new robotic rock bolting in Sudbury - Northern Ontario Business
sources.claim: Robotic rock bolting that drills and installs bolts under machine control in an underground drift remains at prototype/testing stage in a company test mine, not in production use.
sources.transferJustification: Cited for the negative: the most advanced underground bolting robot found is a prototype for bolt installation, with no demonstrated autonomous engagement or tensioning of truss turnbuckles in a mine, so E3 (and in-facility E2 equivalents) are unsupported.

emergingTasks.label: Check roof or ribs for hazardous conditions.
emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

emergingTasks.label: Clean equipment, such as dust collectors.
emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

roles.title: Loading and Moving Machine Operators, Underground Mining
roles.description: Operate underground loading or moving machine to load or move coal, ore, or rock using shuttle or mine car or conveyors. Equipment may include power shovels, hoisting engines equipped with cable-drawn scraper or scoop, or machines equipped with gathering arms and conveyor.

tasks.label: Handle high voltage sources and hang electrical cables.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shuttle-car/loader operator manages the trailing (reel) cable through each haul cycle at the working section: watching pay-out and take-up, steering to keep the cable out from under wheels and away from the continuous miner and roof-bolter, and getting off the machine to free, flip, or drag the energized cable clear when it fouls on rubble, roof falls, or standing water. Seam height 4-6 ft, muddy uneven floor, coal dust, other machines moving nearby.

Hanging the continuous miner's and section's trailing cables on insulated cable hangers/J-hooks along the rib or roof as the face advances: lifting 60-100 lb spans of 1-2 in. diameter mining cable overhead in a low seam, picking hanger points on roof bolts, posts or timbers, keeping the cable off the floor, out of water, and out of the travelway.

When the section power center is advanced, extending and re-hanging its incoming medium/high-voltage feeder cable (2,400-7,200 V) down the entry: pulling long lengths off a reel or coil by hand, dragging them past crosscuts, hanging them on hangers, and coiling and securing the slack, working with the mine electrician.

Making and breaking cable couplers at the section power center or load center: confirming the breaker/disconnect is open, locked and tagged, dragging heavy muddy cable ends up to the box, mating or separating three-phase couplers with ground and ground-check pins, tightening the locking collar, then re-energizing the circuit.

Examining trailing cables and couplers during the shift for cuts, burns, pinches and loose connections; moving cable out of standing water and off haul roads; tagging out and taking damaged cable out of service and reporting it to the mine electrician.

sources.title: Hyster® trucks to use Rocsys robotic charging
sources.claim: Rocsys ROC-1 autonomous charging robot plugs and unplugs high-power charging connectors into parked electric terminal tractors without a human, supplied commercially to Hyster port equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making and breaking a heavy high-power electrical connection. Like plugging equipment couplers into a mine power center, the robot must locate a mating interface on a machine, align a multi-pin high-current connector and seat it reliably, with energization interlocked to a verified mate; it does so from a fixed dock with the cable held in a known holster, i.e. a purpose-built presentation.

sources.title: Rocsys to build autonomous charging system at the Port of Oakland
sources.claim: Rocsys robotic charging systems were contracted to automatically charge part of SSA's electric yard tractor fleet at the Port of Oakland container terminal.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (autonomous mating of a high-power connector); this item establishes real-site deployment rather than laboratory demonstration.

sources.system: ABB eMine FastCharge Robot Automated Connection Device (Robot ACD)
sources.title: ABB's eMine™ portfolio helping electrification drive in South America - International Mining
sources.claim: ABB's eMine FastCharge with a Robot Automated Connection Device performs fully automated high-power electrical connection to mining haul trucks; it is a technology demonstrator being tested at Boliden's Aitik open-pit mine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot makes and breaks a high-power electrical connection to mining equipment. Comparable to connecting equipment cables at a mine power center in current and voltage class and in requiring interlocked energization, but the truck parks at a marked charging pad and the connector is machine-side and fixtured.

sources.system: Dual-arm wire harness assembly robot (Tampere University)
sources.developer: Tampere University / Malvido Fresnillo et al.
sources.title: A dual-arm robotic system for automated multi-branch wire harness assembly in automotive industry - Tampere University Research Portal
sources.claim: A dual-arm robotic system with tactile, force and vision sensing autonomously routes and secures multi-branch automotive wire harnesses on a fixtured assembly board, evaluated in two real assembly scenarios.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routing a flexible cable along a defined path and securing it at retainer points. This is the same manipulation problem as laying a cable into hangers, in a fixtured cell where the cable is presented from a known start point; the cables are far lighter than mine trailing cable, so the transfer holds only under a purpose-built (fixtured, heavy-payload) presentation.

sources.title: AI 3D Vision for Cable Handling and Wire Harness Assembly | Cambrian Robotics
sources.claim: Cambrian Vision is a commercial AI 3D vision product that guides industrial robots to detect, pick, route and clip cables and connectors in factory cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided robotic routing and clipping of cables. Establishes that cable pick/route/clip is done commercially by robots inside structured factory cells, i.e. with the cable presented in a controlled workspace, which is the E1 form of hanging a cable on hangers.

sources.system: Liebherr cable reeler system for electric mining excavators
sources.title: Liebherr cable reeler system: Enhancing electric excavator mobility and safety
sources.claim: Liebherr's cable reeler system on electric mining excavators automatically retracts the trailing cable as the machine moves, removing the need for an operator ... handle the cable manually.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: keeping a machine's heavy trailing power cable managed while the machine travels. The automatic reel performs the pay-out/retract part of trailing-cable handling for mining-class cable, but only along the machine's own travel path; it does not free, lift or re-route cable that has fouled.

sources.title: Motor-Driven Reels | Conductix-Wampfler
sources.claim: Motor-driven cable reels are standard commercial equipment that automatically handle the heavy trailing power cables feeding large mining and port machines, including medium-voltage cables.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled handling of heavy trailing power cable. Shows that where the cable route is engineered (fixed travel path, guides), heavy cable tensioning and take-up is fully machine-handled, which is the E1 counterfactual for a haulage machine's cable.

sources.system: Autonomous mobile inspection robots in deep underground mining (survey of fielded systems)
sources.title: Autonomous Mobile Inspection Robots in Deep Underground Mining—The Current State of the Art and Future Perspectives
sources.claim: A 2025 review of underground mining robotics reports that fielded underground robots are inspection platforms; physical interaction with the environment is limited to research manipulators collecting samples, deploying sensors or clearing small obstacles.
sources.transferJustification: Context for negative judgments: underground mine manipulation is at research-prototype level, with no system that hangs cable or makes up couplers underground. Autonomy unclear, so this item supports no positive judgment.

tasks.label: Drive loaded shuttle cars to ramps and move controls to discharge loads into mine cars or onto conveyors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Low-to-mid seam (1.2-2.1 m) underground coal room-and-pillar section: operator drives a cable-reel electric shuttle car loaded by a continuous miner out of the working place, threading crosscuts and entries while paying out/reeling a trailing cable, past miners on foot, roof bolters and power centers on a wet, rutted floor, then docks at the section feeder-breaker and runs the car's chain conveyor to discharge onto the panel belt. The load point moves with every cut and the route changes several times per shift.

Higher-seam or battery-powered coal haulage in a room-and-pillar section: battery hauler/ram car or scoop carries coal from the miner or a stockpile to the feeder-breaker or loading point and discharges it; same section conditions (dust, water, sloughing ribs, changing routes) but no trailing cable.

Underground hard-rock metal mine (gold, zinc-lead, copper): operator trams a loaded LHD from a stope drawpoint or muck pile along development drifts and ramps to an ore pass, grizzly or truck-loading bay and dumps the bucket; surveyed level layouts, wet uneven floor, one-way traffic rules, radio dispatch.

Underground hard-rock metal mine: operator drives a loaded underground haul truck (40-65 t) up decline ramps from a loading bay to a tip, crusher hopper or shaft loading pocket and raises the box/ejects to discharge; long fixed haul routes shared with other traffic.

Underground limestone or salt room-and-pillar mine with large openings: operator moves blasted stone with a large front-end loader or haul truck from the muck pile to the underground crusher/feeder hopper and discharges onto the conveyor; wide, graded, well-maintained roadways and high back.

Underground potash or trona room-and-pillar mine: operator runs a shuttle car or rubber-tired hauler taking ore from a continuous borer to the panel conveyor feeder/breaker and discharges it; flat dry floor, heavy dust, haulage cycle tied to the advancing borer.

sources.system: Sandvik AutoMine (Multi-Lite) with Toro LH517i loaders
sources.developer: Sandvik Mining and Rock Solutions / Glencore Mount Isa Mines
sources.title: Glencore adds automated Sandvik trucks to the operating mix at George Fisher - International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik AutoMine-equipped Toro LH517 LHDs at Glencore's George Fisher underground zinc-lead-silver mine haul loaded buckets along mine drifts and dump them autonomously, with remote operators taking control only for bucket filling; ten automated loaders were in operation as of 2025.

sources.system: Sandvik AutoMine with Toro TH663i trucks and Toro LH517 loaders (AutoLoad 2.0)
sources.title: George Fisher Mine leads the way in underground automation - Glencore Australia
sources.claim: Glencore reports automated Sandvik Toro TH663i trucks added at George Fisher in 2024 and AutoLoad 2.0 loaders and trucks running complete load-tram-dump cycles underground without human intervention.

sources.title: Sandvik launches AutoMine Aura 'first-of-its-kind' automation platform - International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik states its AutoMine underground automation platform is proven across more than 140 mines ..., indicating broad commercial deployment of autonomous loading and hauling in operating mines.

sources.system: Sandvik AutoMine Core / Access Control System (ACS)
sources.title: AutoMine Core for loading and hauling - Sandvik Mining
sources.claim: AutoMine machines run inside mine areas isolated by an access control system with barriers and gates, with flexible safety zones that can create shared areas for manual and automated equipment, and traffic management coordinating loaders and trucks.

sources.system: Cat MineStar Command for underground (R1700 / R1700 XE LHD)
sources.title: Command | Cat | Caterpillar
sources.claim: Caterpillar's MineStar Command for underground automates load-haul-dump machines with capability levels extending to full autonomy, and is factory-fitted on R1700 series underground loaders.

sources.system: Cat MineStar Command for hauling with autonomous Cat 777 trucks
sources.title: Scaling a Proven Autonomy System to Support New Industries - Caterpillar
sources.claim: Autonomous Cat 777 haul trucks under MineStar Command went live at Luck Stone's Bull Run aggregate operation in November 2024 and hauled over 2 million tons of blasted stone in the first year.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hauling blasted limestone from a loading point to a fixed crusher/dump and discharging it. Same material, vehicle class and discharge target as the underground stone-mine haul cycle; the only difference is surface versus underground, which the underground AutoMine truck evidence covers.

sources.system: Autonomous coal shuttle car research prototype
sources.developer: University of Kentucky (Androulakis, Sottile, Schafrik et al.)
sources.title: Elements of Autonomous Shuttle Car Operation in Underground Coal Mines - University of Kentucky
sources.claim: Autonomous operation of coal-mine shuttle cars remains at the research stage: University of Kentucky work reports preliminary autonomous navigation results from a lab-scale prototype rather than a production machine working in a mine.

sources.system: Komatsu 10SC32 shuttle car with optional remote control
sources.title: Komatsu 10SC32 Shuttle Car - The Machine Market
sources.claim: Commercially available 'unmanned' coal shuttle car operation is human remote control, not autonomy: Komatsu's 10SC32 shuttle car offers an optional remote-control system so the car can follow the continuous miner under unsupported roof.

tasks.label: Pry off loose material from roofs and move it into the paths of machines, using crowbars.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Coal room-and-pillar face: after the continuous miner takes a cut, the operator sounds the newly exposed roof and ribs with a slate/pry bar, pries down loose draw rock, coal and slate, and pushes or rakes the fallen material into the path of the continuous miner or scoop so it is loaded out. Dusty, low light, roof condition varies cut to cut, done under supported roof at the edge of unsupported ground.

Hard-rock/metal mine development heading right after a blast: barring loose rock off the back and shoulders (by hand bar from under supported ground, or after machine scaling) and dragging/kicking the barred material onto the muck pile so the LHD or loader can pick it up. Irregular blasted profile, water, changing ground.

Developed entries, haulage roads and belt entries of an established mine: during travel or a pre-shift check the operator finds loose rib or a drummy roof slab near the travelway, bars it down with a crowbar and moves the debris into the path of the scoop/loader for cleanup. Bolted roof, standard entry dimensions, controlled access.

Low-seam confined work (36-48 in. coal) around and behind the loading machine or shuttle car: kneeling or crouched, prying loose top and rib material that has sloughed around the equipment and pushing it into the loader's gathering-arm path, in tight clearance with cables, hoses and ventilation curtain nearby.

Underground stone/limestone room-and-pillar or shaft/slope area with a high back (15-30 ft): loose slabs pried down from the back and ribs, often from a mechanized scaler basket or with a long bar, and the fallen rock moved into the path of the front-end loader for mucking.

sources.system: Normet Scamec LC 065 A mechanized scaler
sources.developer: Normet (Finland), developed/tested with Agnico Eagle at Kittilä mine
sources.title: Safer scaling — CIM Magazine
sources.claim: Purpose-built mechanized scaling machines (Normet Scamec family) remove loose rock from underground faces, but they are carrier machines with an operator cab and a boom the operator aims at the rock; the 2026 trade review describes tele-remote operation and lists autonomy features such as autonomous tramming as still 'emerging', i.e. the scaling action itself is human-directed.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same task (removing loose rock from the back/ribs after excavation), but performed by an operator in a cab or tele-remotely, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Scaling – Safe Rock Removal for Underground Excavation (Normet)
sources.claim: Normet's Scamec LC 065 A is ... purpose-built underground scaling machine with a 6.5 m vertical reach used for scaling loose rock after drilling and blasting; it is an operator-driven carrier, not an autonomous system.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (mechanized scaling of loose rock underground); vendor material establishes the machine class exists but does not establish autonomous operation, so it is treated as teleoperated.

sources.title: Scaling - Brokk Global
sources.claim: Brokk remote-controlled demolition robots have been used for scaling in mines and tunnels for decades, but every scaling cycle is directed by a human operator who must keep line of sight to the work.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (prying/knocking loose rock off backs and ribs underground) with a machine-mounted tool instead of a hand crowbar; it is continuous teleoperation, so under the rules it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Sensor-based loose rock detection methods (review; no fielded system)
sources.developer: Radl, Mitra, Clausen — RWTH Aachen / academic review, Mining Technology
sources.title: Loose rock detection methods for automating the scaling process, Mining Technology 131(4)
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed review of loose-rock detection for automating scaling finds that the perception step at the heart of ... task — deciding which rock on the back or rib is loose — is still done by experienced people, and surveys only candidate sensor approaches for future automation.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about this task; establishes that no fielded system autonomously identifies the loose material that must be pried off.

sources.system: Retrofitted autonomous scaling machine (ReNAM-style research platform)
sources.developer: University/OEM research collaboration (Luleå University of Technology robotics group and Epiroc are the partners in this line of work)
sources.title: Towards the Deployment of an Autonomous Scaling Machine in Underground Mines — IEEE Xplore
sources.claim: The most advanced published work on autonomous scaling is a research retrofit of a scaling machine at an active mine, framed as 'towards' deployment and concerned with sensor integration, localization and navigation in GNSS-denied mine workings rather than a validated autonomous scale-down-the-back work cycle at production quality.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same task; it is a research-stage retrofit ('towards deployment') with autonomy focused on navigation/localization, so it does not substantiate whole-task completion at worker quality.

tasks.label: Move trailing electrical cables clear of obstructions, using rubber safety gloves.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shuttle car or scoop operator in an active coal section repeatedly moves the machine's energized trailing cable out of the wheel path while tramming between the continuous miner and the feeder: grabbing the cable with rubber gloves, flipping/dragging it to the rib side over an uneven, muddy, rock-strewn floor in a 4-7 ft seam, with the cut location changing every few hours.

Operator hangs or re-hangs the trailing cable on insulated hooks along the rib or lifts it over timbers, crosscut junctions, water pools and other equipment so it stays out of the travelway and out of water, working in low headroom with a headlamp.

During a move to a new place or when the section advances, the operator relocates long runs of cable: coiling, dragging and re-routing 100+ ft of heavy energized trailing cable from the power center to the machine, clearing it of debris and obstructions along the way.

Clearing and repositioning cable along established, maintained haulage/track entries and around the section power center, where the roadway is graded, the layout is standard and access is controlled by the mine.

Freeing a cable that has become pinched, snagged or run over: wedged under a fallen rock, trapped under a machine wheel or track, or tangled with another cable or a water hose - requiring high force, inspection for jacket damage, and sometimes de-energizing before handling.

sources.title: Rocsys and ICT Group roll out hands-free EV charging for ports
sources.claim: Rocsys sells and deploys an autonomous robotic charging system that grasps, moves, plugs and unplugs heavy charging cables at port terminals and vehicle depots without human intervention, in a purpose-built charging bay.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous handling of a heavy, energized flexible power cable - grasping it, moving it along a planned path to a target position, and returning/stowing it. That is the manipulation core of moving a trailing cable clear, when the cable is presented in a known, fixtured location as a purpose-built (E1) station presents it.

sources.title: Rocsys launches integrated platform to enable hands-free charging for autonomous mobility
sources.claim: Rocsys' connection device uses computer vision and machine learning ... autonomously detect the vehicle, open the port, plug in the cable and unplug it; customers include port and logistics operators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided autonomous pick, transport and placement of a heavy power cable end into a defined receptacle - comparable to lifting a presented cable and placing it clear of a defined obstruction or onto a hanger in a structured cell.

sources.system: Robotic heavy-cable manipulation system (CNN cable-effect model with ADRC/sliding-mode control)
sources.title: Learning-based cable coupling effect modeling for robotic manipulation of heavy industrial cables (Scientific Reports)
sources.claim: A Tsinghua group demonstrated closed-loop robotic manipulation of heavy industrial cables on a real robot, compensating the cable's dynamic payload effect and achieving accurate positioning of the manipulated cable.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the manipulation physics of this task: a robot arm holding and repositioning a heavy, stiff, flexible cable whose weight and coupling forces disturb the arm. Demonstrated only on a fixed lab robot cell, i.e., a purpose-built (E1) setting.

sources.system: ABB eMine FastCharge Robot Automated Connection Device (Robot ACD)
sources.developer: ABB, with Boliden, BHP and Komatsu
sources.title: ABB's eMine portfolio helping electrification drive in South America - International Mining
sources.claim: ABB's eMine Robot Automated Connection Device, an automated robotic device that makes high-power charging connections to haul trucks, is being tested at Boliden's Aitik ... on a fixed charging pad.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a robot at a mine site autonomously handling a heavy high-power cable/connector and mating it to a vehicle. Shows heavy energized-cable handling works where cable and target are presented at a purpose-built station, not on an as-found mine floor.

sources.title: Robotic refuelling for mines - Robofuel | Scott
sources.claim: Scott's Robofuel robotic refuelling system autonomously locates a mining truck's fuel receiver with vision and couples the nozzle, removing manual nozzle and hose ... at mine refuelling bays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous grasping and routing of a heavy flexible line (fuel hose and nozzle) to a target on a mining vehicle, but only at a fixed, purpose-built refuelling station rather than in as-found mine workings.

sources.system: Underground coal mine auxiliary operation robots (pipe installation robot, roadway repair robot)
sources.developer: Chinese coal-mine robotics groups, reviewed by Wang Lei
sources.title: 王雷：煤矿井下辅助作业机器人研究与应用进展_智能矿山网
sources.claim: A Chinese review of underground coal-mine auxiliary-work robots reports that underground auxiliary work is still done mainly by hand and that such robots (including cable laying and recovery) are at an early research stage; the prototype pipe-installation robot's platform is moved by remote control.
sources.transferJustification: Context and negative evidence for the mine setting: the closest underground heavy-handling prototypes (pipe installation, roadway repair) are early-stage and partly remote-controlled, and none handles trailing cables in working sections.

tasks.label: Control conveyors that run the entire length of shuttle cars to distribute loads as loading progresses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Coal room-and-pillar section, typical conditions: shuttle car operator positions the car under the continuous miner's discharge boom and jogs/runs the car's full-length chain conveyor rearward in bursts as coal is discharged, spreading the load from the front bumper to the tail so the car fills to capacity without spilling over the sides or burying the conveyor; dark, dusty, 40-80 in. seam, layout changes with every cut.

Same face loading but under adverse conditions: wet sticky fines or oversize rock that jams or bridges on the chain conveyor, muddy uneven floor, heavy dust and water spray from the miner, awkward car angle in a crosscut or deep cut, requiring the operator to reverse/jog the conveyor, watch for spillage behind the car and avoid overloading before tramming out.

Discharge end of the cycle at the section feeder-breaker (fixed dump point in a maintained entry): operator runs the full-length conveyor forward at a controlled, metered rate to unload coal into the feeder hopper without choking or overflowing it, easing the car forward/back as the load discharges.

Continuous-haulage variant: operator runs the conveyors of a mobile bridge conveyor train or flexible conveyor train that is being loaded continuously by the continuous miner at the face, keeping the receiving tailpiece under the miner discharge and the belts loaded without spillage or overload as the miner advances into the cut.

Non-coal underground room-and-pillar operations (salt, trona, limestone, gypsum, potash): shuttle car or conveyor-bed hauler loaded at the face by a continuous miner or loader; larger openings and coarser, more abrasive rock; conveyor run to distribute the load along the deck as loading progresses.

sources.system: Autonomous shuttle car (research prototypes, e.g., Univ. of Kentucky lab-scale car; ACARP assistive shuttle car)
sources.developer: University of Kentucky / CSIRO (reviewed in NIOSH-funded report by Haight & Burgess-Limerick)
sources.title: Automation Experience with a Global Perspective – An Assessment of the Automation Impact on Worker Safety and Health (Final report)
sources.claim: NIOSH-funded global review of mining automation states that, despite research, automation of shuttle cars in underground coal mines has not been achieved in practice; work to date is lab-scale prototypes.

sources.title: Self-Propelled Forage Harvesters | John Deere
sources.claim: Commercial forage harvesters automatically distribute bulk material into a haulage vehicle as loading progresses: a 3D camera detects the trailer and its fill level and the machine controls the discharge to fill it evenly without spillage, in open fields.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: closed-loop distribution of a flowing bulk load into a haulage vehicle during loading. Same objective as the shuttle-car conveyor task (uniform fill front-to-back, no spillage, stop at capacity), same class of material (loose bulk), sensing of fill profile in real time; it actuates the discharge spout rather than the receiving vehicle's deck conveyor.

sources.title: iLoadout - indurad - 3D Radar Machine Vision
sources.claim: Radar-based loadout control system automates the filling of open-top railcars with coal and iron ore, measuring car and material profile in real time and controlling material flow so each car is filled evenly to capacity; 20+ installations worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: metering and profiling a bulk coal load into a moving haulage vessel so it is evenly distributed and not overloaded — the same accepted output as the shuttle-car conveyor task, with the same dusty coal material, but at a fixed purpose-built loadout where the chute (not a deck conveyor) is the actuator.

sources.system: Moving Floor Conveyor System (automated truck loading system)
sources.title: Moving Floor Loading System | Safe Trailer Loading in 2 Minutes! | Joloda
sources.claim: Slat conveyors running the full length of a trailer automatically load and unload the vehicle from a dock, moving the load progressively along the trailer deck under machine control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine control of a vehicle-length deck conveyor to distribute a load along a haulage vehicle during loading and to discharge it during unloading — mechanically the same function as the shuttle car's chain conveyor, but with palletised goods at a purpose-built dock.

sources.system: Joy 4FCT Flexible Conveyor Train with 'Follow me' and Faceboss control
sources.title: Komatsu | 4FCT Flexible Conveyor Train
sources.claim: Komatsu's flexible conveyor train, used underground at the coal face, has a sensor-based 'follow me' mode in which the machine positions its receiving tailpiece under the continuous miner discharge and matches the miner's tram speed automatically while it is being loaded, freeing its operator.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the continuous-haulage form of this task: keeping a full-length conveyor unit correctly presented to the loading machine and running its belts as loading progresses, at the working face of an underground coal mine.

sources.system: Sandvik AutoMine with AutoLoad 2.0 (Toro LH517i loaders)
sources.developer: Sandvik Mining and Rock Solutions / Glencore
sources.title: Glencore adds automated Sandvik trucks to the operating mix at George Fisher - International Mining
sources.claim: Autonomous underground loaders run complete load-haul-dump production cycles, including automatic bucket filling at drawpoints and dumping, without human intervention in access-controlled underground zones; ten automated loaders in production at Glencore's George Fisher mine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous loading and discharge of broken rock inside an underground mine, showing that machine-controlled bulk-material handling to production quality is achieved underground where the institution keeps the area cleared and routes defined — but with a bucket, not a deck conveyor, and not coordinated with a continuous miner's discharge.

tasks.label: Observe hand signals, grade stakes, or other markings when operating machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground coal room-and-pillar section: shuttle car / ram car operator trams into the face under unsupported roof, spots under the continuous miner's discharge boom on hand signals and cap-lamp signals from the miner operator, watches the trailing cable, ventilation curtains and spads, then hauls to the feeder. Low seam (1-2 m), muddy uneven floor, dust, face position changes every cut.

Underground coal section scoop / battery hauler: moving supplies (rock dust, cribs, cable, roof bolts), cleaning up spillage and hauling to the feeder along established, rock-dusted entries; takes hand and light signals from the section crew and foreman, follows survey spads and belt-line markings, works around bolters and cable handlers.

Hard-rock or industrial-mineral metal mine production level: LHD operator mucks established drawpoints/stopes, trams the maintained level drift, and dumps into an orepass or loads a truck; coordinates with the level crew, traffic lights/tags and level survey marks; drift layout is fixed for months.

Underground haul truck / ore hauling loop: operator spots under the loader on the loader operator's signals, hauls loaded on a maintained ramp or main haulage drift to an underground crusher, orepass or shaft, following grade/curve markings and passing-bay signals in mixed traffic with other machines and people.

Development heading mucking after a blast: loader operator mucks a fresh, irregular muck pile in a newly driven heading, guided by the jumbo/bolter crew's hand signals, spray-painted grade and centerline marks and the survey laser; heading location and ground conditions differ each round, poor visibility from dust and blast fumes.

sources.title: Sandvik introduces AutoMine® AutoLoad 2.0 for improved autonomous bucket loading
sources.claim: Sandvik's AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 enables fully autonomous loader production cycles (including bucket filling) at fixed drawpoints and dump points, validated in field tests with customers in ....
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: the loading/hauling machine cycle this occupation performs; loading, tramming and dumping muck are executed under machine control instead of an operator watching signals and markings.

sources.title: Sandvik launches AutoMine® Aura, a first-of-its-kind automation platform for the future of mining
sources.claim: AutoMine is in production use at more than 140 mines worldwide; the 2026 Aura release adds a 3D-perception navigation system validated at customer sites, first on underground loaders.

sources.system: Epiroc Scooptram Automation Total (Traffic Management System)
sources.title: Epiroc sets the standard of loader automation
sources.claim: Epiroc's Scooptram Automation Total runs a fleet of autonomous loaders in shared mine drifts under a Traffic Management System, with the automation area isolated by safety barriers that stop the machines if personnel enter.

sources.system: Sandvik AutoMine battery LHD fleet at George Fisher Mine
sources.title: Sandvik Automated Loaders Are Gamechanger for Glencore
sources.claim: At Glencore's George Fisher underground mine, AutoMine-equipped production loaders navigate the mine on their own between operator-selected start and end points, sensing and mapping the drift in darkness.

sources.system: Sandvik AutoMine for Trucks (Toro TH545i) at Zimplats Mupani
sources.title: Sandvik & customer achieve fully autonomous low profile truck loop in Zimbabwe
sources.claim: Five Sandvik TH545i low-profile trucks run a fully automated haulage loop to an underground crusher in a low-profile room-and-pillar mine (Zimplats Mupani), sharing haulages with manual trackless equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: hauling broken ore underground from load point to dump in a low-seam room-and-pillar layout, the geometry a coal shuttle-car/hauler operator works in; machine control replaces the operator's watching of signals and traffic markings.

sources.system: Sandvik AutoMine for Trucks / Autodig at Syama
sources.title: Syama's automation surge
sources.claim: At Resolute's Syama gold mine, Sandvik AutoMine haul trucks run autonomously underground using LiDAR navigation and switch to GPS on surface; autonomous bucket loading (Autodig) was reported only about 70% effective at that stage.

sources.system: Laboratory-scale autonomous shuttle car prototype (room-and-pillar navigation research)
sources.developer: University research (AusIMM Future Mining Conference paper)
sources.title: Automation considerations for underground shuttle car haulage
sources.claim: Autonomous shuttle car haulage for underground coal room-and-pillar sections remains at research stage: a laboratory-scale prototype navigating a scaled room-and-pillar section, not a mine deployment.

tasks.label: Examine roadway and clear obstructions from the path of travel.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Developed main haulage entry/drift on the operator's regular route (coal entry or hard-rock drift, supported, rock-dusted/graded, access-controlled): while tramming the loader or shuttle car the operator scans the road for spilled coal or ore, rib sloughage, potholes and water, low-hanging cables and vent tubing; minor spillage and a few loose lumps are bladed or scooped aside from the cab and the machine continues.

Accumulated muck on a developed haulage road (rib sloughage, spillage at a loading point, ore-pass or feeder overflow) must be mucked out with the machine's bucket, carried to a dump point, and the floor smoothed so haulage units can pass at speed.

Active production/face area or newly advanced entries: trailing cables, water and air hoses, ventilation tubing, timbers and crib blocks, bolt plates, tools and spilled coal lie in the travel path; the operator dismounts, moves items by hand or shovel, repositions the miner cable, then trams through. Layout changes with every cut; wet, muddy, dark, confined.

Substantial blockage: a fall of ground or an oversize boulder blocks the roadway. The operator examines roof and ribs, decides whether to bar down, break the rock (sledge or breaker) or call the support crew, mucks out the debris and restores safe travel, sometimes only after temporary ground support is set.

Conveyor or track haulage entry: clearing belt spillage along the travelway and at transfer/feeder points, removing material from between rails, clearing derailment debris and stray supplies in tight clearances, largely shovel and hand work alongside fixed installations.

sources.title: Sandvik AutoMine Autoload 2.0 eliminates operator intervention in LHD drawpoint loading - International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik's AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 gives underground loaders fully automated load-haul-dump production cycles including autonomous bucket filling, but only where material is presented at fixed drawpoints with pre-taught loading profiles and fixed dump points.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mucking of broken rock. Filling a bucket from a pile of loose rock and hauling it to a dump point is the same physical act, machine, material and precision as clearing fallen or spilled material from a mine roadway - but only when the pile sits at a fixed, pre-taught point.

sources.title: Sandvik launches AutoMine Aura, a first-of-its-kind automation platform for the future of mining
sources.claim: AutoMine autonomous loaders run in production drifts at over 140 mines; the 2026 Aura release adds 3D-perception navigation validated at customer sites and still relies on the mine's access-control (barricade) systems to keep people out of the automated area.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous tramming of underground haulage routes. It substantiates that a machine can travel and perceive a mine roadway autonomously, but the documented response to a perceived hazard is to stop for a remote supervisor, not to clear the path.

sources.title: Normet Xrock launches fully autonomous underground rock breaker - International Mining
sources.claim: Normet's Xrock Autobreaker autonomously identifies, targets and breaks oversize boulders blocking a grizzly or crusher - a fixed boom installation from which people are excluded - and is commercially available.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: clearing an oversize-rock blockage. Same objects (mine-run boulders) and same act (examine the blockage, break it, restore passage), but the rock must arrive within reach of the fixed boom.

sources.system: AMP Cortex / AI-Benkei and AI-Musashi (AMP Neuron)
sources.title: AMP Robotics' Dual-robot Recycling System Increases Productivity - Waste360
sources.claim: AMP Robotics' AI-guided C&D robots autonomously recognise and pick mixed construction and demolition debris - wood, concrete, metal, electronics - including heavy pieces up to 40 kg, from a conveyor in a recycling plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing assorted debris items from a defined path. The objects (timber, rock/concrete lumps, metal, flexible items) and required precision match hand-clearing of roadway debris, but only when the debris is presented to the arm on a conveyor.

sources.system: Underground inspection robots at Jinneng Tashan coal mine
sources.developer: Jinneng Holding Shanxi Coal Industry (robot supplier unnamed)
sources.title: Robots revolutionizing risky mining operations - China Daily
sources.claim: Rail-guided explosion-proof inspection robots patrol the underground roadways of the Tashan coal mine, moving along their track independently, imaging and listening for faults and self-recharging.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: examining an underground roadway. It covers the inspection half of this task in the actual setting, but the robot runs on installed rail and has no means of clearing anything from the path.

sources.title: Underground mine drone survey takes another step as Exyn achieves Level 4A Autonomy - International Mining
sources.claim: Exyn's autonomous LiDAR drones fly and map GPS-denied underground mine workings without a pilot, exploring and documenting drifts and stopes on their own.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous survey and inspection of underground roadways. Supports the examine half of the task in the same environment; the aerial platform cannot move any obstruction.

tasks.label: Drive machines into piles of material blasted from working faces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mechanized hard-rock metal mine, production level: operator drives an LHD/scoop repeatedly into ore blasted into a fixed drawpoint or stope brow, fills the bucket, and trams to an ore pass or truck; access-controlled production area with engineered drawpoints, maintained drifts and underground network coverage.

Hard-rock metal mine development heading: mucking a freshly blasted round at an advancing face — pile heaped against the face, ventilation duct, water and power services close by, ground not yet fully supported, floor to be cleaned to grade; the heading location changes with every round.

Underground stone/limestone room-and-pillar mine: large wheel loader or LHD drives into a shot pile at a bench face and loads haul trucks; heavy dust, mixed fragmentation with oversize boulders, rooms constantly advancing into new ground.

Small or contract mine / narrow-vein operation: older diesel scoop tram operated in-cab or line-of-sight, wet muddy uneven floors, tight headings, hangups and oversize requiring judgment, no automation network or access-control infrastructure.

Underground coal (conventional/room-and-pillar section): battery scoop or loading machine with gathering arms driven into shot coal and rock at the face and loaded into a shuttle car; permissible explosion-proof equipment required, methane and respirable dust, low seam height.

sources.system: Epiroc Scooptram battery LHD with Deep Automation / NEXGEN SIMS autonomous loading stack
sources.developer: Epiroc (NEXGEN SIMS consortium, with Agnico Eagle)
sources.title: Epiroc & Nexgen SIMS partners demo fully autonomous solution for material handling at the face
sources.claim: Epiroc and Nexgen SIMS partners demonstrated a fully autonomous material-handling cycle at the face — including evaluating the muck pile, driving in and filling the bucket — with battery-electric Epiroc loaders 750 m underground at Agnico Eagle's Kittilä gold mine.

sources.system: Sandvik AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 (on Toro/LH-series underground loaders)
sources.title: Sandvik introduces AutoMine® AutoLoad 2.0 for improved autonomous bucket loading
sources.claim: Sandvik's commercially released AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 automates the bucket-loading (driving into the muck) step for loaders mucking from fixed drawpoints, removing the need for operator assistance during mucking.

sources.title: Sandvik introduces AutoMine® AutoLoad 2.0 for improved autonomous bucket loading
sources.claim: Field testing of Sandvik's autonomous bucket loading with customers in Europe and ... produced faster cycle times and consistent bucket ..., indicating output at or above manual-operator quality in drawpoint mucking.

sources.system: Cat R1700 XE / R2900 XE underground loaders with Autodig
sources.title: R1700 XE battery electric underground loader (MINExpo 2021 product page)
sources.claim: Caterpillar sells Auto Dig on its R1700 XE / R2900 XE underground loaders, which performs the digging and bucket-filling into the pile without operator input as part of fully autonomous machine operation.

sources.system: Cat Autodig + Cat MineStar Command for Underground
sources.title: Dig, Load, Haul — Repeat (Engineering & Mining Journal)
sources.claim: Trade press describes Cat AutoDig combined with MineStar Command for Underground as allowing loaders to tram, dig and dump ... nobody at the controls, with the dig cycle controlled by hydraulic sensing to fill the bucket properly.

sources.system: Stereo-vision muck pile detection integrated with Epiroc LHD autonomous loading (NEXGEN SIMS)
sources.title: Stereo Vision-Based Underground Muck Pile Detection for Autonomous LHD Bucket Loading (Sensors)
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed 2025 paper reports a stereo-vision muck-pile detection system integrated into a complete autonomous LHD loading system, tested in two operating underground mines (Epiroc test mine and Agnico Eagle), loading reliably without human intervention as the pile shape changed each cycle.

sources.system: Epiroc Deep Automation with Scooptram ST18 loaders
sources.title: Golden hour for automation (Epiroc customer story, Newmont Cadia)
sources.claim: Newmont Cadia runs an entire block-cave production level from a surface control room with six to eight Epiroc Scooptram ST18 loaders working simultaneously from draw points, showing that automated loader fleets are deployed in access-controlled underground production areas (though the autonomy level of each bucket fill is not stated).

tasks.label: Operate levers to move conveyor booms or shovels so that mine contents such as coal, rock, and ore can be placed into cars or onto conveyors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground hard-rock metal mine (block/panel cave or sublevel cave), established production level: LHD operator works bucket and boom controls to muck fragmented ore from fixed drawpoints on a mapped, barricaded extraction level and dumps it into an ore pass, crusher or truck. Repeating engineered layout, standard machines, occasional hang-ups and oversize rock.

Underground hard-rock metal mine, open stope or development heading: scoop/LHD operator muck-loads a freshly blasted, as-found pile at the face and loads a haul truck box or trams to an ore pass. Pile geometry, ground conditions, water and oversize differ every round; heading advances daily.

Underground coal room-and-pillar section: continuous-miner operator, standing 30-60 ft back with a remote control box, works the gathering head and swings the machine's discharge conveyor boom back and forth to fill the shuttle/ram car spotted behind it without spilling. 4-8 ft seam, heavy dust, water sprays, trailing cable, loose roof and ribs.

Underground coal section: shuttle car / ram car operator hauls coal from the miner to the section feeder-breaker and operates the car's onboard chain conveyor and discharge boom to place the load onto the feeder/section belt without overloading it. Routes change with every cut; cable reel, mud, water, other equipment and crew present.

Underground coal mine: battery scoop operator cleans up loose coal and rock spillage along entries, at the feeder and around the face, scooping scattered material and dumping it into cars or onto the section conveyor. Low seam, cables, roof supports, timbers, crews working close by.

Underground stone, salt or trona room-and-pillar mine: loader/LHD operator loads blasted limestone or salt from an as-found muck pile into haul trucks or dumps it onto a feeder/conveyor in large rooms. Oversize boulders, dust, uneven muck-covered floor, ramps, trucks arriving on varying schedules.

sources.system: Sandvik AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 (LHDs such as Toro LH514/LH621i)
sources.title: Sandvik AutoMine Autoload 2.0 eliminates operator intervention in LHD drawpoint loading - International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik's AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 automates the bucket-filling step itself for underground loaders working fixed drawpoints and dump points, giving fully automated production loading cycles; field tested with customers in Europe and ... with reported gains in tons loaded per hour.
sources.transferJustification: For the coal instances this is a related task: autonomous filling of a bucket at a taught, fixed loading point and discharging at a fixed dump point handles the same material (broken rock/coal) with the same kind of boom/bucket placement precision required to put material into a car or onto a conveyor.

sources.system: Epiroc Scooptram ST14 SG battery loader with Deep Automation (Nexgen SIMS)
sources.title: Autonomous material handling – a crucial step toward the mine of the future | Epiroc US
sources.claim: The Nexgen SIMS project demonstrated a complete autonomous face material-handling cycle at 750 m depth in Agnico Eagle's Kittila gold mine: the loader evaluated the stope muck pile, chose where to dig, filled the bucket and dumped it into a mine truck box, with no human intervention.

sources.system: Sandvik AutoMine Fleet (Toro/Sandvik LHDs and trucks)
sources.developer: Sandvik Mining and Rock Solutions / Codelco
sources.title: High yield and safety in the Andes | Sandvik Solid Ground
sources.claim: Codelco's El Teniente underground copper mine runs a large deployed fleet of autonomous Sandvik loaders and trucks across multiple production areas, with roughly a third of production handled by automated solutions.
sources.transferJustification: Supports the shuttle-car instance as a related task: autonomous underground haulers tram mapped routes and discharge their loads at fixed dump points in an operating mine, the same placement-of-material action a shuttle car performs at the feeder-breaker.

sources.title: Inside the Future of Room-and-Pillar Mining - Coal Age

tasks.label: Clean, fuel, service, and perform safety checks on all equipment, and repair and replace parts as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-operational / on-shift safety examination of the assigned shuttle car, scoop-tram/LHD or haulage unit underground before it is put in service: walkaround of the machine at the section or parking spot, checking lights, horn, back-up alarms, brakes and panic bar/deadman, tram controls, methane monitor, fire-suppression cylinders and guarding, trailing-cable insulation and couplers, tires/tracks, hydraulic and oil leaks, fluid levels; correcting or tagging minor defects and recording the exam on the machine's checklist.

End-of-shift or periodic cleaning of the machine: washing/hosing down accumulated mud, muck, rock fines or coal dust from the body, deck, wheels/tracks, radiators and screens, either in an underground wash bay or in place near the section.
Refueling the diesel scoop/LHD or haulage unit at the underground fuel bay at the end of a ... (or, on battery machines, plugging in / swapping the battery pack at the charging bay).
Routine lubrication service: greasing the machine's fittings (articulation pins, bucket pins, driveline, bearings) on the daily/weekly schedule.

Repair and parts replacement with hand and power tools, mostly underground at the machine or in the underground shop: changing bucket teeth/cutting bits, conveyor chain flights or belt lacing on the loading machine, replacing burst hydraulic hoses, lights, guards, worn tires, and repairing or splicing the trailing cable.

Routine examination of the conveyor haulage system the machine feeds: traveling the belt line looking for hot or seized idlers, belt misalignment and rubbing, spillage accumulation, and reporting/recording the defects found.

sources.title: Robotic refuelling for mines - Robofuel | Scott
sources.claim: Scott Automation's ROBOFUEL is a robotic arm refuelling station for mine haul trucks that uses vision sensing to locate the truck's fuel tank and couple the nozzle without a person present.

tasks.label: Clean hoppers, and clean spillage from tracks, walks, driveways, and conveyor decking.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Main-line conveyor spillage cleanup in a maintained belt entry: shoveling and loading spilled coal/ore from under the belt structure, at tailpieces, drive units and transfer points; low headroom, wet muddy bottom, fines mixed with lumps and rock dust, belt de-energized/locked out, hand shovel with occasional scoop assistance.

Clean-up in the active working section: spillage around the feeder-breaker/loading point, the section belt tailpiece, and along shuttle-car roadways, done between production cycles; the location moves every shift as the section advances, with trailing cables, hoses, ventilation curtains, ragged rib and uneven floor.

Scoop/LHD clean-up of loose muck and spillage on haulage roadways, ramps and driveways and around dump points and loading pockets, then tramming the material to a dump; maintained, mapped haulage drifts shared with other equipment.

Clearing hang-ups, plugs and oversize at fixed material-transfer points: grizzlies over ore-pass mouths, crusher and loading hoppers, restoring flow so the hopper runs clean; fixed installation, boulders and blocky rock.

Cleaning caked, sticky or frozen buildup out of hoppers, bins, chutes and skip pockets (feeder hoppers, coal bunkers), scraping walls and clearing the discharge; confined-space work with bars, hammers, air or water lances.

Hand cleaning of track and switches, walkways, stairways, and conveyor decking/side platforms: shoveling and brooming spilled material off travelways and out from between rails so the track and walks stay clear, in tight clearances alongside energized equipment.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: secondary breaking / blockage clearing at grizzlies and crusher hoppers. It is the same work as keeping a hopper clear of hung-up and oversize material at a fixed transfer point, on the same objects (rock/ore) in the same fixed underground station.

sources.title: Normet Xrock launches fully autonomous underground rock breaker - International Mining
sources.claim: The autonomous rock-breaking module is commercially available for grizzly applications and retrofits into existing Xrock breaker boom installations at crusher/grizzly stations.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: clearing blocked hoppers/grizzlies is the hopper-cleaning portion of this task, performed on ore and rock at a fixed underground transfer point.

sources.claim: Sandvik's AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 enables fully automated LHD load-haul-dump cycles, including autonomous bucket filling, at fixed drawpoints and dump points underground.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mucking (scooping broken rock and hauling it to a dump). Scoop clean-up of spilled muck on a roadway uses the same machine, same material and same load-tram-dump cycle, provided the pile is presented at a configured load point.

tasks.label: Oil, lubricate, and adjust conveyors, crushers, and other equipment, using hand tools and lubricating equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-of-shift/daily lubrication of the mobile loading or hauling machine (scoop/LHD, shuttle car, loading machine) in the active underground workings: grease pivot pins, articulation and boom pins, wheel ends and cable reel with a grease gun, plus check and top hydraulic and gear oil. Muddy, uneven floor, low seam height, dust, layout advances daily.

Lubricating conveyor components along underground belt entries: head and tail pulley bearings, drive-unit and gearbox oil, take-up bearings, snub/bend pulleys and roller bearings, walking the belt line with grease gun and oil can through low headroom, water, coal dust and rock-dusted travelways.

Lubricating and servicing the underground crusher or feeder-breaker at a fixed crusher chamber/section: circulating oil system checks, greasing bearings and eccentric points, oiling drive chains, and adjusting crusher clearance/setting and breaker components; permanent installation with fixed layout, mine-controlled access.

Adjusting conveyor running parameters during the shift: setting belt tension at the take-up/winch, adjusting belt-cleaner (scraper) blade pressure at the head pulley, and tweaking belt tracking so the belt runs centered — done on the installed conveyor while it runs or during a short stoppage.

Hand-tool mechanical adjustments and minor repairs found during lubrication rounds: realigning or swapping a seized idler roller, tightening loose bolts on stands and guards, adjusting gathering-arm/flight-conveyor chain tension on the loading machine, adjusting couplings, brakes, or worn picks/breaker bars.

Lubricating and adjusting auxiliary underground equipment on the round: dewatering pump and fan bearings, hoist/hoisting engine and scraper winch, roof bolter and section power center components — grease fittings and oil cups on scattered, varied machines.

sources.title: Mining Lubrication Solutions — Graco
sources.claim: Graco supplies on-vehicle centralized automatic lubrication systems for mining equipment in which a central pump feeds metered grease through divider valves to every lube point (pins, bearings, bushings) automatically while the machine works — i.e., machine-controlled greasing once each point is hard-plumbed to the dispenser.

sources.title: Automatic lubricators and Arcanol grease ensure conveyor motor bearings run reliably at opencast mine
sources.claim: At the Visonta lignite opencast mine, 65 Schaeffler CONCEPT2 automatic lubricators were installed on conveyor drive motors and 130 CONCEPT8 units on rope pulley bearings, continuously relubricating the bearings during operation and freeing personnel from manual relubrication rounds.

sources.title: Automated conveyor belt tensioner reduces maintenance — Canadian Mining Journal
sources.claim: Martin Engineering's N2 Twist Tensioner is a commercially sold, sensor-equipped powered tensioner that continuously monitors and automatically applies the correct torque to keep belt-cleaner blade pressure correct on bulk-handling conveyors, replacing the manual daily wrench adjustment of the tensioner.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fluid servicing (fuel filling) of heavy mining machines. It shows a robot arm can couple to and fill a fluid port on mining equipment when the machine is brought to a purpose-built service station, which is the same class of action as connecting and filling lubricant at a designated fill point; it does not show grease-gun work on scattered fittings as found.

tasks.label: Monitor loading processes to ensure that materials are loaded according to specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground coal room-and-pillar section: shuttle car / battery hauler operator spots under the continuous miner's discharge boom and monitors coal filling the car — easing forward and back to trim the load evenly, keeping it below rib/roof clearance, watching for rock or gob contamination and spillage, and pulling out when the car is full. Low seam, heavy dust, water and uneven floor, face position moving every cut.

Underground coal: scoop/loading-machine operator dumping into the section feeder-breaker or loading a hauler, monitoring the feed so the belt is not overloaded or starved, spillage is avoided, and out-of-spec material (large rock, roof bolts, wet fines) is caught before it reaches the panel belt.

Hard-rock metal mine: LHD (load-haul-dump) operator mucking a drawpoint or blasted muck pile, monitoring each bucket for fill factor and tonnage against the shift target, watching for oversize boulders and hang-ups, and keeping ore and waste to the right destinations per the grade-control plan.

Underground metal or limestone mine: loader/LHD operator loading haul trucks, monitoring load placement in the truck box, target payload (no over- or under-load), even distribution, and avoiding boulders dropped from height that damage the box or spill in the drift.

Fixed underground loading point: operator works a chute/gate from an ore pass, loading pocket or bin to fill mine cars, skips or trucks, monitoring flow rate, tonnage per conveyance, sticky/wet muck and hang-ups, and stopping the flow when the specified load is reached.

sources.title: Sandvik AutoMine Autoload 2.0 eliminates operator intervention in LHD drawpoint loading — International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik's AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 gives commercially available, fully automated production loading cycles for LHDs at fixed drawpoints and dump points, removing the operator from the bucket-filling step and holding bucket fill factors consistent; field tested with customers in Europe and ....
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task: the system judges when a bucket is properly filled (fill factor / tonnage per bucket) and repeats the loading cycle to that specification without operator assistance.

sources.system: NEXGEN SIMS autonomous material handling (Epiroc battery-electric LHD and mine truck)

sources.system: Kanawha Scales & Systems batch-weigh train/truck loadout

sources.claim: Kanawha Scales & Systems designs and supplies high-precision batch-weigh train and truck loadout systems for mines and terminals that can run completely unattended, loading bulk material to target weights at high throughput.

sources.claim: Sandvik automated (AutoMine) loaders have operated in production underground mines for over two decades, accumulating more than two million operating hours, indicating deployed rather than experimental autonomy for underground loading machines.
