tasks.label: Replace hydraulic hoses, headlight bulbs, and gathering-arm teeth.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Burst or weeping hydraulic hose on a shuttle car, scoop or loading machine at the working section underground: operator locates the failed hose among a bundle, isolates and depressurizes the circuit, removes guards/clamps, breaks possibly seized JIC/ORFS fittings, routes and torques a replacement hose, tops up oil, tests for leaks and cleans up spilled oil — done in low seam height, mud, water and dust, machine parked wherever it failed.

Worn or broken gathering-arm teeth (or bucket-lip teeth/cutting bits) on the loading machine's gathering head, changed out at the section: mud-packed noses cleaned, retaining pins driven out with hammer/pin pusher or bolts broken loose, new teeth seated and pinned/torqued, all in a cramped, unlit entry with the machine de-energized and blocked against motion.

Burnt-out headlight/lamp on a shuttle car, scoop or loader underground: unbolt the permissible light housing or lens ring, remove the sealed-beam lamp or bulb, inspect and reseat the gasket and wiring to maintain explosion-proof integrity, reassemble and test — vibration-loosened, corroded fasteners common.

The same hose, bulb and tooth change-outs performed with the machine trammed to an established underground maintenance bay or surface shop during a maintenance shift: level floor, better lighting, hoists, air tools, parts on hand, mine-controlled premises and fixed layout.

Complicated field cases: hose failure behind covers or inside a boom/hose bank, seized or rounded fittings, a tooth with a bent/rusted pin needing cutting or heating, requiring improvisation and partial disassembly wherever the machine sits underground.

sources.system: Sandvik DL422i / DL422iE longhole drill rig with automatic bit changer
sources.title: DL422iE: Sandvik electric efficiency in underground drilling
sources.claim: Sandvik's underground longhole drill rigs offer an on-board automatic bit changer with a revolver carousel that lets the rig change worn drill bits and keep drilling autonomously — the closest commercial case of automated wear-tool replacement on a mining machine, but it works only through the rig's own threaded drill-string interface.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: replacing a worn wear tool (drill bit) on a mining machine. Transfer to gathering-arm teeth is limited: the bit is a purpose-designed threaded component made up and broken by the rig's own rotation head at a fixed pose, whereas teeth are pin- or bolt-retained parts that must be cleaned, driven out and seated with impact tooling in arbitrary poses.

sources.system: Epiroc Automatic Bit Changer (ABC) on Pit Viper rotary blasthole drills
sources.title: Epiroc's ground-breaking drill rig Pit Viper celebrates 25 years including a decade with autonomous operations
sources.claim: Epiroc's Automatic Bit Changer on Pit Viper blasthole rigs performs hands-free tricone bit change-outs in fleet service, with thousands of bits changed automatically since 2022 — automated wear-tool exchange using purpose-built bit adapters on the machine's own deck.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated replacement of a consumable wear tool on mining equipment. It substantiates only threaded bit exchange on a fixtured drill string with special adapters; it does not substantiate removing/installing pin-retained teeth, hydraulic hoses or lamp assemblies.

sources.title: Sandvik goes underground with autonomous Amelia
sources.claim: Sandvik's AutoMine Concept Underground Drill demonstrated an AI-guided automatic bit changer that detects worn bits and replaces them automatically on a cabinless autonomous underground rig.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous wear-tool change on an underground mining machine. Shows automation confined to the machine's own tool interface and carousel; no evidence of general repair work (hoses, lamps, pinned teeth) on other machines.

sources.developer: Chinese tunnelling equipment consortium (reported by CGTN)

tasks.label: Stop gathering arms when cars are full.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Room-and-pillar coal section: the continuous miner's gathering head/chain conveyor discharges into a shuttle car spotted behind the machine; the operator watches the car heap up and stops the gathering arms and conveyor as the car reaches capacity, then signals the car change. Face position advances with every cut; dust, uneven floor, roof support cycle.

Same coal-face loading but under adverse conditions: low seam, water and mud on the floor, visibility badly cut by dust, cars loaded in tight crosscuts; the operator must stop the arms early enough to avoid spilling coal into the place or overloading the car.

Underground stone/metal-nonmetal mine: a loading machine, scoop or LHD fills a haul truck or mine car from a blasted muck pile at a heading or drawpoint; the operator stops loading when the body is full to avoid overloading and spillage, then the truck trams away.

Fixed loading point on a maintained haulage level or at a feeder-breaker/loading station: material is fed by gathering arms or conveyor into rail mine cars or a surge hopper spotted at a known position; the operator stops the feed when the car/hopper is full and calls the next one.

Continuous-haulage face: gathering arms discharge into a mobile bridge conveyor or surge car train; the operator stops the arms when the receiving conveyor backs up or the surge unit fills, and restarts when the system clears.

sources.title: Sandvik AutoMine Autoload 2.0 eliminates operator intervention in LHD drawpoint loading - International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik's AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 gives underground loaders fully automated production cycles at fixed drawpoints and dump points, removing operator intervention from the bucket-filling (loading-termination) step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mucking. The machine senses the fill state of its receptacle (bucket) in broken ore/coal and terminates the loading action itself, the same sensing-and-stop decision as stopping gathering arms when a car is full, with the same material and the same underground-mine setting.

sources.title: Sandvik introduces AutoMine® AutoLoad 2.0 for improved autonomous bucket loading
sources.claim: AutoLoad 2.0 was field-tested with customers in Europe and ..., producing consistent bucket fill factors and higher tons per hour, i.e. the automatic fill-and-stop judgment reached production quality.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: automatic termination of loading when the receptacle is full, benchmarked against operator-loaded cycles in producing underground mines.

sources.system: Sandvik AutoMine Loading Lite (Automatic Bucket Loading Assistant)

sources.claim: Sandvik AutoMine automated loading, including bucket filling without remote-operator help, is in service at named producing underground mines.

sources.system: Sandvik AutoMine Lite (Access Control System 2, Integrated Weighing System)
sources.title: AUTOMINE® LITE 2 product sheet
sources.claim: AutoMine automation zones in mines are guarded production areas, and the system records loader bucket and truck box weights through an integrated weighing system, i.e. payload/fill state is machine-measured.

sources.claim: Commercial bulk-loading installations use automation controls that start and stop material flow into railcars/trucks to hit an accurate loaded weight and ..., i.e. the 'stop when the car is full' decision is executed unattended.

tasks.label: Move mine cars into position for loading and unloading, using pinchbars inserted under car wheels to position cars under loading spouts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Spotting empty mine cars under a permanent loading chute/spout at an ore-pass or loading pocket on an established underground haulage level: fixed maintained track, standard car fleet; the locomotive drops a string of cars and the operator levers each car the last few feet with a pinchbar so the car body sits under the spout, easing it forward as it fills.

Spotting loaded cars at the fixed unloading point (shaft-bottom dump, tipple, rotary dumper or grizzly): nudging each car with a pinchbar onto the dump platform or over the opening, holding spacing between cars, then releasing the emptied car to the empty track. Permanent, lit, well-maintained station.

Spotting cars at a working/development section loading point where track is temporary and advancing, floor uneven and wet, spillage and rock under the wheels; the loading machine or feeder discharges into the car and the operator repeatedly levers the car forward with a pinchbar to fill it evenly, under low roof, dust and poor light.

Small non-mechanized underground mine (small coal, stone, industrial-mineral or legacy operation) with hand tramming: worker pushes and pinchbars light narrow-gauge mine cars along uneven, muddy, variably graded track to line them up under a chute or loader, then trams them out.

Off-nominal recovery: a car stalls short of the spout, wheels bound by spilled rock, or a flange has climbed off the rail; the worker inserts the pinchbar under the wheel to lift/lever it back onto the rail and re-spot the car under the chute before loading resumes.

sources.date: 2024 (product line in commercial use for years)

sources.claim: Automated hydraulic railcar indexers/positioners spot strings of rail cars to +/- 25 mm at fixed loading and unloading stations, automatically acquiring successive axles and indexing cars one car length at a time through the receiving/loading position - the machine equivalent of pinchbar spotting, on purpose-built indexed track.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is spotting rail cars at a loading/unloading station rather than pinchbarring mine cars; the objects (rail cars on track), the act (moving a car a few feet to a spot under a chute or dumper) and the accuracy demanded (+/-25 mm, finer than hand spotting) are the same, in a purpose-built installation.

tasks.label: Advance machines to gather material and convey it into cars.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground coal room-and-pillar section (BLS: coal mining is ~45% of this occupation's employment): the operator advances a continuous miner / gathering-arm loading machine into the coal face, gathers the cut coal with the gathering head and discharges it over the boom conveyor into a shuttle car or ram car. Low seam (40-70 in), dust, water, trailing cable management, methane-permissible equipment, roof supported by temporary supports, face position changing every cut.

Underground coal mine, battery scoop / rubber-tired loader work away from the cutting cycle: mucking loose coal and rock, cleaning spillage at the feeder, belt and along entries, loading it into the scoop bucket or a car and dumping at the feeder/conveyor. Locations vary shift to shift, muddy or heaved floor, rib sloughage, cables and vent tubing in the way.

Underground metal mine (zinc/gold/lead/silver) production mucking: an LHD (scoop tram) repeatedly advances into a blasted ore pile at a stope drawpoint or brow on a production level, fills the bucket, trams the drift and dumps into a haul truck at a loading bay or into an ore pass. Fixed loading and dump points for the life of the stope, standard drift profile, ground-supported, mine-controlled access.

Development heading mucking (mine development crews and contract miners): after a blast round, an LHD advances into a fresh, irregular muck pile at the end of an advancing heading, loads and hauls it to a truck or muck bay. The pile geometry, floor profile and heading location change every round; oversize boulders, unsupported brow, ventilation bag and services close by.

Underground nonmetallic mineral mine (salt, trona, potash, limestone; ~13% of employment): a large LHD or front-end loader advances into blasted or cut stone/salt in a wide room-and-pillar opening and loads it into haul trucks or into a feeder-breaker/conveyor hopper. Big standard openings, dry dusty conditions, but the loading location advances with the face and is not a fixed drawpoint.

Small or legacy operations and tunnelling contracts: narrow-vein workings, slusher/scraper-hoist scraping of broken rock into a chute or car, or mucking a drill-and-blast tunnel heading for a highway/utility project. Irregular openings taken as found, timbered or shotcreted ground, no standard layout, frequent hand-work alongside the machine.

sources.claim: Sandvik's AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0, launched June 2023, makes the bucket-filling step of LHD mucking autonomous at fixed drawpoints and dump points, so a loader runs full production loading cycles without an operator assisting during loading; field-tested with customers in Europe and ....
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: a machine is advanced into a pile of broken rock/ore, gathers a bucket load and conveys it to a haul unit. For the coal and fixed-point (E1) counterfactuals the transfer is that the material is broken bulk mineral presented at a fixed, taught location and discharged into a car/truck - the same objects, precision and machine class.

tasks.label: Signal workers to move loaded cars.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Guide and stop cars by switching, applying brakes, or placing scotches, or wooden wedges, between wheels and rails.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: At an active loading point in the working section: the operator loads coal/ore into mine cars and must spot each empty car under the loader or chute, ease it forward, pull the loaded car clear, set its brake and scotch it on grade. Track is temporary track advanced with the face; wet, uneven floor, spillage, low headroom, changing layout.

On the main haulage road / at a parting: guiding a trip of cars between the loading point and the shaft bottom, throwing track switches to route cars into and out of sidings, controlling speed and stopping the trip with brakes on maintained permanent track with fixed layout and controlled traffic.

At the shaft bottom, tipple or rotary dump: guiding cars one at a time into the dump or onto the cage, stopping each car at an exact spot with brakes, retarders or car stops, and releasing the empty on the other side. Fixed, permanently installed handling point.

Securing standing cars: placing wooden scotches/wedges between wheels and rails and setting handbrakes to hold parked or uncoupled cars on grade at partings, storage tracks, loading points and during repair or coupling work; wedges placed by hand at whatever spot the car happens to stand.

Abnormal events: a car running away on a grade, a car derailed or off-track at a curve or switch, cars fouling the track after spillage or a roof-fall; the worker blocks, scotches, rerails and hand-guides cars back under control in cramped, cluttered conditions.

tasks.label: Push or ride cars down slopes, or hook cars to cables and control cable drum brakes, to ease cars down inclines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Slope hoist operator at a small underground coal or stone mine: on signal from the trip rider, releases and modulates the cable drum brake (and clutch) to ease a trip of loaded cars down a permanent inclined haulageway at controlled speed, holding the trip and spotting it at the bottom landing. Fixed rail, fixed landings, established bell/phone signals.

Trip/rope rider at the head of the slope: couples loose cars into a trip, hooks the hoist rope clevis and safety chain onto the lead car's drawbar, gives the signal, rides or walks the trip down the incline, then unhooks and shoves the cars clear at the landing. Confined, dark, wet, variable car positions.

Car changing at the loading point in an advancing working section: pushing loaded cars by hand or with a scoop down a short grade, uncoupling and spotting empties under the loading machine, using sprags/blocks to control roll-away on muddy, uneven temporary track.

Small or irregular operation: steep, wet, poorly maintained incline; ad hoc rigging with chains and clevises, low clearance, cars occasionally derailing and needing re-railing before the descent can continue.

Trip haulage on graded track between the loading point and the slope bottom or dump: moving loaded cars along established track, controlling speed on the grade, and spotting the cars accurately at the dumping station or parting.

sources.system: ABB mine hoist system (ControlIT/OperateIT hoist control, hydraulic disc brake system)
sources.date: circa 2003 brochure; systems in service since

sources.claim: ABB supplies mine hoist systems whose control system runs the hoisting cycle fully automatically, with hydraulically controlled multi-caliper disc brakes and controlled retardation of rope-drawn conveyances in mine shafts and inclines (ten hoists modernized at LKAB Kiruna).

roles.description: All underground mining machine operators not listed separately.

roles.title: Rock Splitters, Quarry
roles.description: Separate blocks of rough dimension stone from quarry mass using jackhammers, wedges, or chop saws.

tasks.label: Locate grain line patterns to determine how rocks will split when cut.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Granite or other hard dimension-stone quarry bench: before drilling the next line of holes, the splitter examines the exposed ledge/face - sheeting joints, seams, colour and 'sap' changes, and the rift and grain lines in the crystal fabric - to decide the orientation and position of the split. Outdoors, wet and dusty rock, uneven bench that changes shape daily.

Freed rough block (5-30 t) lying on the quarry floor: the splitter walks around it, brushes or wets the faces, taps with a hammer, and reads rift/grain plus hidden seams, knots and drys to fix the plane along which plug-and-feather or wedge splitting will run when the block is sized.

Bedded/sedimentary stone (limestone, sandstone, bluestone, flagstone): the worker inspects lifted slabs and blocks in the pit or stockyard for bedding planes, clay partings, shakes and seams to determine where the stone will part and where chop-saw cuts or wedges should be placed.

Splitting shed or mill bench: smaller blocks and slabs handled at a hydraulic splitter, guillotine or chop saw; the worker examines each piece's grain or bedding under roof lighting and orients it before splitting to size for curbing, setts or veneer.

Diagnostic re-reading during the split: after the first holes are drilled or when a split runs off line, the worker inspects drill cuttings, the fresh break surface and spalling at the face to re-read the grain and revise the split plan.

sources.system: Automatic stone-block internal-structure tomography prototype (3D Cartesian robot with ultrasonic and electrical-resistivity electrodes, SCADA/PLC control)
sources.developer: University of Evora (Mechatronics Dept.), with Metal Vicosa and Marmetal, Portugal
sources.title: A New Prototype for Automatic Identification of Stone Block Internal Structure (Applied Sciences 11:6630)
sources.claim: Laboratory proof-of-concept machine: a PLC-controlled 3D Cartesian robot presses ultrasonic transducers and resistivity electrodes against a stone block and automatically performs tomographies to identify the block's internal structure, replacing the expert's empirical prediction from external observation; limited to sample blocks of known, small dimensions scanned in 5 mm sections.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: predicting a dimension-stone block's internal structure (cracks, discontinuities) before sawing - the same determination the splitter makes on the same class of objects. Transfer fails on timeliness and scale: the rig is a lab proof of concept that 'is able to accept sample blocks with limited and known dimensions' and scans in 5 mm sections, so it cannot deliver a split-plane call on a multi-tonne quarry block in the time the work requires, and its accuracy was compared only with manual tomography, not with an expert's prediction.

sources.system: Strayos Rock Mass AI (drone photogrammetry + computer vision)
sources.title: Understanding drill and blast AI in quarrying - Quarry Magazine
sources.claim: Commercial mining/quarry analytics platform that ingests drone aerial imagery and automatically detects geological structures - bedding planes, joints, spacing, fractures, dip and strike - on quarry highwalls to inform drill-and-blast design.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mapping rock-mass discontinuities on a quarry face to predict how the rock will break. It does not transfer to dimension-stone splitting: output is metre-scale joint-set statistics for blast fragmentation, not the centimetre-scale rift/grain and seam reading that fixes a plug-and-feather split line, and the imagery-collection flight autonomy is not established in the source, so it is treated as teleoperated.

sources.system: Linear/nonlinear ultrasonic measurement setup for granite cleavage-plane anisotropy
sources.developer: Academic study published in Scientific Reports
sources.title: Linear and nonlinear ultrasound parameters attributed to anisotropy in granite - Scientific Reports
sources.claim: Laboratory ultrasonic measurements on granite specimens quantify the anisotropy of the three cleavage planes, correctly ranking rift as the weakest and hardway as the strongest split direction; performed on prepared specimens with coupled transducers, not by any robotic system on quarry stone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instrumented identification of the rift/grain/hardway planes that the splitter reads by eye. It cannot substantiate robotic completion: it is a benchtop measurement on cut specimens with hand-coupled transducers, with no embodied system demonstrated doing this on rough quarry blocks or a quarry face.

sources.title: D2 Iris Scanner for Stone Fabricators | Northwood Machine
sources.claim: Commercial slab-imaging station for stone fabricators: an automatic 12K scanner images stone slabs and applies AI defect detection so veining and imperfections can be seen and worked around when planning cuts; it inspects already-sawn slabs, not rough stone to be split.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine reading of natural structure (veins, fissures) in stone to plan cutting. It does not transfer: the objects are finished slabs on a scanning table in a fabrication shop, the output is a layout/aesthetic and defect map, and nothing in the source shows prediction of how a rough block will fracture when wedged or sawn.

tasks.label: Remove pieces of stone from larger masses, using jackhammers, wedges, and other tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Primary separation at the working face: worker reads the rift/grain, marks the split line on the ledge, drills a row of holes into the in-situ bedrock with a hand-held or wagon drill, sets feathers-and-wedges (or hydraulic splitting cylinders) and drives them in sequence until a sheet or bench block breaks free of the mass. Outdoor quarry bench, irregular natural rock, weather, loose muck underfoot.

Secondary splitting of an already freed block lying on the quarry floor or block yard: line-drilling with a hand drill or drill rig and plug-and-feather/sledge, or a hydraulic splitter, to break the multi-tonne block down into smaller rough blocks or slabs of the ordered size, following the grain so faces come out clean.

Jackhammer / pneumatic-hydraulic breaker work: breaking up waste stone and oversize pieces, knocking off unwanted knobs and ledges, barring and scaling loose rock, and cutting a channel or relief so a piece will come away. Rough, coarse breaking on the pit floor and bench.

Trimming and squaring freed blocks in the quarry block yard to rough dimension: chop saw / squaring saw cuts plus wedge-and-hammer or breaker work to knock the block to a rectangular, saleable shape, on a prepared staging pad with loaders and standard rigging.

Splitting thin, layered stock by hand: slate or flagstone lifted from the ledge is split along its cleavage with chisel, mallet and wedges into flat pieces of usable thickness, and trimmed to size, judging each piece by feel and sound.

sources.title: Normet Xrock launches fully autonomous underground rock breaker - International Mining
sources.claim: Normet Xrock's Autobreaker autonomously identifies oversized boulders on a grizzly, plans strike positions and executes hydraulic-hammer breaking sequences with no personnel in the breaking zone; commercially available from December 2025 for grizzly installations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: secondary rock breaking. Same physical act as the quarry jackhammer/breaker step - driving a hydraulic impact hammer into hard rock to knock pieces off a larger mass - on comparable material at comparable (coarse) precision, executed autonomously at a fixed boom station.

sources.title: Xrock Automation: Scalable Solutions for Breaker Boom Control
sources.claim: Normet's own product page for Xrock automation states the Autobreaker locates, analyses and breaks oversized material autonomously using vision and sensor fusion, with no personnel in the hazardous zone.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: autonomous hydraulic-hammer breaking of rock at a purpose-built breaker-boom station is the machine analogue of the quarry worker's jackhammer/breaker work on waste and oversize stone.

sources.system: Steinex automatic splitting lines (Menhir / Sherpa / CUB AUT)
sources.title: Steinex Automatic Lines | Steinex | Stone & Glass Group
sources.claim: Steinex supplies fully automatic stone splitting lines (Menhir/Sherpa machines, CUB AUT plants) that take sawn monolithic stone blocks and split them by hydraulic blade/wedge into cubes, slabs and boulders with automatic handling under PLC control; splitting forces 220-320 t, slabs to 1600 x 600 mm.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production splitting of natural stone. The machine performs the same physical act as plug-and-feather work - forcing a wedge/blade into stone to break pieces off a larger mass - on the same material, with the workpiece conveyed and positioned automatically.

sources.title: Steinex automatic plants: innovation in stone splitting
sources.claim: Steinex's own site describes four types of automatic systems for producing cubes, slabs and ... and a range of semi-automatic to fully automatic splitting machines and plants.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the previous item: hydraulic splitting of natural stone into smaller pieces inside an automated, purpose-built plant.

sources.title: HYDRASPLIT Stone Splitter | Hydraulic Stone Splitting Machines
sources.claim: Park Industries' HYDRASPLIT hydraulic stone splitter (90-600 ton models, openings up to 12 ft) splits large stone with an automatic split cycle and motorised in-feed/out-feed conveyors, but the operator positions each stone using joystick controls.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hydraulic wedge splitting of large stone in US plants. Cited only as context on machine force and scale; the operator loads and triggers each split, so it is treated as non-autonomous and supports no positive judgment on its own.

sources.title: Meet ROBOTOR, the Robotic Sculptor of Marble Statues - 3Dnatives
sources.claim: Robotor's multi-axis stone-milling robots in Carrara remove material from multi-tonne marble blocks to a specified 3D geometry; the OR-OS control software generates toolpaths automatically and the robots run the machining without operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic stone carving. It is autonomous removal of stone from a larger stone mass to a target shape, on the same material (Carrara marble blocks) at far tighter precision than rough squaring/trimming of quarry blocks; the environment is a purpose-built robot cell in a stone yard.

sources.system: Epiroc SmartROC D65 MKII (autonomous surface drill)
sources.title: Epiroc and Luck Stone launch first fully autonomous SmartROC D65 drill rig in U.S. aggregate market
sources.claim: Epiroc and Luck Stone deployed the first fully autonomous SmartROC ... MKII surface drill rig in a US quarry, executing complete drill plans autonomously on the quarry bench.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous blasthole drilling on a quarry bench. It covers only the hole-drilling step of drill-and-wedge work in an aggregate pit; no cited system sets or drives wedges or otherwise frees dimension stone from the in-situ mass, so it does not complete the face-splitting instance.

sources.title: Fantini 70RATA Bank Chain Saw Machine
sources.claim: Fantini's 70RATA bank chain saw machine can perform vertical and horizontal cuts ... the quarry in unattended mode once the operator sets cut depth and length, using PLC and encoders; positioning, rail setup and block separation remain manual.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: chain-sawing dimension stone free of the quarry bench. The preset cut cycle automates one step only; the machine must be positioned and rigged by workers for each cut and the block is still separated by hand, so it does not show whole-instance autonomy.

tasks.label: Insert wedges and feathers into holes, and drive wedges with sledgehammers to split stone sections from masses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Freeing a dimension-stone block from the quarry bench/face in situ: a line of holes has been drilled along the intended split plane in granite or limestone; the worker seats plug-and-feather sets in every hole with the feather ears aligned to the split line, then walks the line driving each plug with a sledgehammer in repeated light passes, listening for the tone change and watching the crack run, until the section breaks free. Outdoor bench, uneven rubble footing, weather, variable rock.

Squaring or dividing a loose multi-ton rough block on the quarry floor: block lying on rubble or dunnage, grain/rift read and a hole line drilled to the ordered dimension; wedge sets inserted and driven in sequence, wedges re-tightened over several passes until the block halves cleanly with a saleable split face.

Repetitive sizing of slab/ledge stock into wall stone, building stone or paver-sized pieces on a level pad in the quarry yard or plant area: short hole lines or shallow plug holes in relatively regular slab stock, quick wedge-and-hammer sequences, high piece counts, institution-controlled yard with fixed layout and standard handling equipment.

Detaching a block that has already been partly cut free (wire-saw, channel or chain-saw cuts) by driving wedges into the back cut or a drilled hole line to tip or separate the block from the mass; awkward body positions at the face, sometimes in a confined underground marble quarry or against a high bench.

Recovering usable stone from irregular masses, boulders or ledge in a small operation: grain and defects uncertain, splits wander, so the worker repositions and re-drives wedge sets, adds holes, and works stone lying at odd angles on uneven, muddy or snowy ground.

sources.title: Rock Splitters Product Overview | Darda GmbH
sources.claim: Commercial hydraulic rock splitters split rock by a wedge driven into a pre-drilled hole, but a person drills the hole and inserts/orients the splitting insert; the tool is hand- or carrier-operated, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical operation as the task (wedge in a drilled hole to split stone), but hole preparation, insert placement and orientation are done by a human and the carrier is operator-controlled, so it does not substantiate autonomous completion.

sources.system: Brokk C20 Rock Splitter on Brokk demolition machines
sources.title: Brokk brings more power and safety, less noise with Darda Rock Splitters
sources.claim: The most machine-like implementation of wedge splitting in the field is a rock-splitter attachment on a remote-controlled demolition machine, i.e. a human drives every motion.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related task (mechanical rock splitting from a drilled hole); cited to show that field-proven systems are remote-controlled, which under the rules cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: SmartROC D65 MKII autonomous surface drill rig
sources.title: Epiroc and Luck Stone deploying fully autonomous SmartROC D65 drill rig | International Mining
sources.claim: Quarry automation that is genuinely autonomous today covers drilling of hole patterns on a quarry bench, not the insertion of wedges or the splitting operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related upstream task (drilling the hole line in a quarry). It shows autonomous machines can work an outdoor quarry bench, but it performs no wedge insertion, hammer driving or split-quality judgement, so it cannot complete this task.

sources.title: Normet Xrock Launches the World's First Autonomous Rock-Breaking System, Xrock Autobreaker
sources.claim: Autonomous hammer-based rock breaking exists only as a fixed breaker-boom installation that fragments oversize rock at a grizzly; the goal is shattering rock, not producing a clean planar split of a dimension-stone block.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous impact breaking of rock). It does not transfer: no wedge/feather handling, no drilled-hole insertion, and its accepted output is fragmented rock rather than an undamaged block split along a chosen plane.

sources.system: Steinex automatic splitting plants / automatic splitting line for stone cubes
sources.title: Steinex automatic plants: innovation in stone splitting
sources.claim: Automatic stone splitting plants split stone under machine control in a purpose-built line, taking slab stock on automatic feeds and producing sized split-face cubes and products at commercial quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical splitting of stone stock into sized pieces with split faces, the same accepted output as hand wedge-splitting of slab/ledge stock, achieved by a fixed automated line with conveyor/ramp feeding rather than by hand-driven plug-and-feather.

sources.title: Epiroc makes the 'impossible possible' with launch of Boltec ABR | International Mining
sources.claim: Mechanised insertion of hardware into drilled holes in rock is automated only for rock bolting rigs underground, which install bolts and resin but perform no splitting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (placing steel hardware into drilled holes in a rock ...). Cited only as the closest mechanised analogue; the rig is operator-run, installs bolts rather than wedge sets, and never drives wedges or judges a split.

tasks.label: Mark dimensions or outlines on stone prior to cutting, using rules and chalk lines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: At the working ledge/bench of a dimension-stone quarry (granite, limestone, marble): the splitter measures off the previously cut wall with tape and rule and snaps chalk lines across the bench top and down the vertical face to define the outline of the next block and the drill/wire-saw line. Outdoors on wet, dusty, rubble-strewn rock; no georeferenced digital plan exists and marks are referenced to the rock's own edges, seams and rift.

On the quarry floor after a ledge or large block has been dropped: the splitter measures the multi-ton irregular block and chalks the split lines on its top and sides plus the spacing marks for plug-and-feather or line-drill holes, so it can be broken down into smaller blocks. Uneven ground, block lying as it fell.

In the quarry block yard: squaring/trimming layout on a rough block staged on timbers or gravel - marking the outline of the finished dimensions on an irregular blank with rule, square and chalk line, shifting the outline to clear seams, iron spots or fractures.

In the quarry's mill or processing shed: marking cut lines on sawn slabs or sheets resting on a saw table, cart or A-frame - rule, straightedge and chalk line to lay out the ordered sizes before the bridge saw or splitter cuts. Indoor, fixed layout, standard equipment, company-controlled premises.

Marking non-rectangular or custom outlines on stone - curbing, monument blanks, veneer, landscape or flagstone pieces - transferring a pattern/template or curved outline onto the stone with chalk and rule, often on pieces staged outdoors in the yard.

sources.title: HP SitePrint Autonomous Robotic Layout Solution Leverages HP's Multi Jet Fusion 3D Printing to Reduce Cost and Inefficiencies in Construction | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: HP SitePrint is a commercially sold autonomous mobile robot that prints layout lines, arcs, points and text directly on construction site surfaces (concrete, plywood, tarmac) from CAD, referenced by a robotic total station, at about +/-2 mm layout accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: construction layout marking. Same output type as chalk-line marking (physical lines on a hard surface guiding a later cut), but it replays a pre-existing georeferenced CAD plan on relatively even floor surfaces rather than measuring a workpiece or marking vertical faces.

sources.title: Automated Layout Startup Civ Robotics Secures $7.5M Series A Funding Round | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: CivDot is a commercially deployed autonomous 4WD outdoor layout robot that spray-paints layout points from an uploaded coordinate file on solar, grading and road sites at 8-30 mm accuracy, on uneven ground and in bad weather.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor construction layout marking. It marks positions on the ground outdoors, but only discrete points from pre-computed GNSS coordinates; it does not measure a stone workpiece or mark on block faces.

sources.title: Automatic Layout Marking | PeddiWriter | Peddinghaus
sources.claim: Peddinghaus PeddiWriter and SignoScript are commercial CNC layout-marking machines in steel fabrication lines: workpieces are conveyed to the machine and layout lines and text are marked automatically from the digital model, replacing manual layout technicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pre-cut layout marking on a workpiece. Identical function to chalking dimensions on stone before cutting - transferring plan dimensions into physical marks on a rigid workpiece at mm precision - with the workpiece brought to the machine (E1 presentation).

sources.title: Sculptor Robotic Fabrication Software Powered by OR-OS - LITIX SPA
sources.claim: Robotor is a commercial multi-axis robotic stone-milling system used in Carrara marble workshops; its OR-OS software self-programs from a 3D model and the system then executes the milling of the stone block autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic machining of natural stone blocks in a fixtured cell. Shows machine-controlled tools tracking precise paths on rough natural stone surfaces; inscribing an outline is a lower-precision subset of the same motion on the same objects.

sources.title: 7-Axis Robotic Arm for 3D Stone Carving & Cutting | DINOSAW
sources.claim: DINOSAW sells 7-axis KUKA-based stone robots for granite, marble and limestone that carve, cut and engrave lettering on fixtured stone workpieces from CAM programs, with consistent engraving depth compared with manual work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: engraving/inscribing lines and lettering on stone in a purpose-built cell. Producing a visible outline on stone is the same physical act as marking a cut line, at precision far exceeding chalk-line tolerance.

sources.system: Computational design + robotic fabrication pipeline for limestone
sources.title: Computational design and robotic fabrication of dry-stacked non-standard spanning limestone assemblies | Construction Robotics
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed work demonstrates 3D scanning of a library of 50 irregular limestone fragments, algorithmic computation of the cut/machining plan for each stone, and robotic milling to realize it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: deciding and executing a cut layout on irregular natural stone. It supplies the judgment part of marking - computing where the lines fall on a scanned irregular blank - with robotic execution in a fixtured cell.

sources.system: Robo SawJet M Series / Robo SawJet 2.0
sources.title: Robo SawJet M Series | Mitering Robotic SawJet | BACA Systems
sources.claim: BACA Robo SawJet is a commercially deployed KUKA-robot sawjet cell in stone fabrication shops that nests DXF part outlines across scanned slabs and cuts them to that digital layout.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying out part outlines on stone slabs before cutting. Same objects (natural stone slabs) and the same layout decision the marker makes, executed by machine with the slab presented on the machine's table.

sources.title: Hole Navigation System (HNS) | Epiroc
sources.claim: Epiroc's Hole Navigation System guides surface drill rigs to GNSS drill-plan positions on quarry benches, explicitly removing the need for a person ... mark hole positions on the bench; the operator trams the rig to each collar point.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: quarry bench layout. Shows bench layout being eliminated by machine guidance rather than physically marked by a robot; the rig is operator-steered, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Cut slabs of stone into sheets that will be used for floors or counters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In a stone fabrication shop attached to a quarry operation, cutting a granite/quartzite slab into countertop pieces: slab set on the saw table with a vacuum lifter/overhead crane, layout marked or nested around veins and fissures, straight and mitered cuts made on a bridge saw or sawjet, pieces unloaded to carts.

At the quarry's processing plant, running slabs through a cut-to-size line to make floor tiles/pavers: slab fed onto the conveyor, longitudinal multi-blade cutter makes strips, cross-cutter makes tiles to a fixed size, pieces sorted and stacked on pallets.

At the mill, resawing or splitting oversized/thick sawn slabs into thinner sheets or narrower panels for flooring: slab loaded onto a belt bridge saw or horizontal wire/slab saw, thickness and cut lines set, machine cuts, sheets removed with lifter.

Out in the quarry yard, trimming and sizing rough or natural-cleft slabs into usable sheets with a portable slab saw or handheld chop saw: work done on dunnage or uneven ground beside the stone pile, cut lines judged from bedding planes, seams and edge damage, in dust, wet and variable weather.

In the splitting shed, reducing sandstone/slate/bluestone slabs to flooring or paving sheets on a hydraulic guillotine splitter or shear: slab positioned against stops, split repeatedly to size, off-size or broken pieces culled.

sources.system: BACA Systems Robo SawJet (KUKA KR 210 QUANTEC)
sources.title: Innovative solutions in the stone cutting industry: 100 robots for BACA Systems in North America | KUKA Global
sources.claim: BACA Systems' Robo SawJet is a commercially deployed robotic stone-cutting cell (KUKA industrial robot carrying a saw blade and abrasive waterjet) used across North American stone fabrication shops to cut slabs into countertop pieces.

sources.title: Case Study: Hard Rock Stone Works - BACA Systems
sources.claim: A US fabricator (Hard Rock Stone Works) has run a Robo SawJet since 2016 as its primary cutting machine, producing fully cut slabs on one table while the ... is loaded/unloaded — i.e., accepted production-quality cut countertop pieces.

sources.system: BACA Systems Robo Lift (KUKA robot with vacuum tool)
sources.title: Robo Lift | Robotic Stone Slab Lifting Equipment | BACA Systems
sources.claim: BACA's Robo Lift adds robotic loading of uncut slabs and unloading of cut material to sawjet/CNC stations, so the load-cut-unload cycle in the cell runs without a human handling the stone.

sources.title: Autocut Line | Automated Systems | BACA Systems
sources.claim: BACA sells a fully automated cutting line combining robotic loading/unloading with the Robo SawJet, targeted at ~2,000 sq ft of cut stone per shift with minimal labor.

sources.system: Park Industries JAVELIN CNC Sawjet / SABERjet XL
sources.title: Countertop Cutting Machines for Stone Fabricators - Park Industries
sources.claim: Park Industries (US) sells CNC sawjets that cut slabs into countertop pieces to high accuracy under numerical control, the standard machine class in US stone shops.

sources.system: Simec TT2200 / TTS 2200 cut-to-size machines and Simec FINGER-C automatic slab loader
sources.title: Simec FINGER -C Automatic Loader for Slabs Stone Handling Machine from Italy - StoneContact.com
sources.claim: Simec builds transversal and longitudinal multi-disc cutting machines for slabs that operate as cut-to-size lines producing tiles, plus automatic slab loaders that feed the processing line without manual handling.
sources.transferJustification: Cut-to-size lines perform exactly this task (slab reduced to floor tiles) with the same objects and tolerances; the loader shows the feeding step is also machine-handled.

sources.title: Slabs Loading Robot - Prussiani Engineering
sources.claim: Prussiani supplies a robotized system that automatically loads slabs onto a belt bridge saw, removing the manual slab-handling step ahead of sawing.

sources.title: Breton Jot | Handling robot marble granite Lapitec ceramic quartz
sources.claim: Breton's Jot is a CNC handling robot used in highly automated stone plants for loading, unloading, moving and flipping slab/sheet-form products including natural stone.
sources.transferJustification: Shows that presenting and removing slabs at cutting stations in stone plants is machine-handled, completing the non-cutting portion of the sawing instances.

sources.system: Steinex Wind Star / Menhir splitting machines and automatic splitting lines
sources.title: Wind Star splitting machine - Steinex S.R.L.
sources.claim: Steinex Wind Star hydraulic splitting machines are configured in automatic splitting lines fed by conveyors and pushers that split sawn slabs and blocks into setts, slabs and tiles; Menhir splitters are installed in quarries and stone plants worldwide.

sources.system: D2 Iris Scanner (12K slab imaging, AI defect detection)
sources.title: D2 Iris Scanner for Stone Fabricators | Northwood Machine
sources.claim: Slab imaging/scanning systems with AI defect detection integrate with sawing operations so that cut layouts on natural stone avoid fissures and match veins.
sources.transferJustification: Addresses the judgment step of the cutting task — placing cuts around natural flaws and veining — showing the machine-side layout decision is handled without a human eyeing the slab.

tasks.label: Set charges of explosives to split rock.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Granite quarry bench: after a ledge has been channeled/wire-sawn on the ends and back, the splitter loads the line of horizontal lift holes drilled along the base of the open face with detonating cord strands or light black-powder charges, stems them (often with water or sand), and ties the downlines into a trunk line to lift and free a large sheet from the quarry mass. Outdoor, wet and dusty holes, uneven footing, charge weight judged so the stone loosens without fracturing.

Quarry floor: a freed ledge or large block is split into mill-size blocks along a line of closely spaced (4-6 in) small-diameter drilled holes; the splitter threads detonating cord or places light cartridge charges to the correct depth in each hole, water- or sand-stems them, connects the line, and shoots. Blocks lie where the derrick or loader set them; access from all sides varies.

Softer-stone quarry (limestone, sandstone, slate, some marble): low-energy black powder or light charges placed in pre-drilled holes along a bench to loosen large volumes of stone without fragmenting it, then stemmed and tied in. Fewer, deeper holes; charge sized by seam and bed conditions.

Secondary and trim shots: small charges set in isolated boulders, oversize or badly shaped pieces, overhangs and waste stone on the muck pile or against the highwall, to break them for removal or to square a block. Hole positions and piece geometry differ every time; the splitter often drills and charges one or two holes by hand from an awkward stance.

Adverse-condition charging: deep vertical relief/back holes at the rear of a bench, holes partly filled with water or caved material that must be cleared or re-drilled, work on narrow ledges above a drop, in cold, rain or mud; the splitter adjusts charge placement and quantity to seams and hole condition before stemming and tying in.

sources.title: ABB, Boliden and LKAB complete successful testing of industry-first automated robot charger for increased safety in underground mines
sources.claim: ABB's Robot Charger locates drilled holes in an underground mine rock face with a vision system and charges them with explosives, including robotic assembly of primer and detonator, with the charging cycle fully automated; piloted at Boliden's Garpenberg mine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: charging blast holes at an underground mine face. It shares the core action of this task - locate a drilled hole in rock, assemble a primer/detonator, insert the charge to depth - with comparable object handling. It differs in explosive product (pumped bulk emulsion vs. detonating cord/black powder) and in tolerance for rock damage, since dimension stone must split without fracturing, so it substantiates the action only where the charge and hole are presented to the machine in a purpose-built way (E1), not the as-found stone-quarry job.

sources.title: Orica and Epiroc fire world's first semi-automated, wireless development blast with Avatel at Kittila mine
sources.claim: Orica and Epiroc's Avatel, the commercially deployed underground development charging system, is semi-automated: a single operator in an enclosed cab performs the whole charging cycle, i.e. the machine is operator-controlled rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanised explosive charging of a rock face. Cited to show that the state of the art in fielded charging equipment keeps a human operator in the control loop, so it cannot support a positive autonomous judgment for this task.

sources.system: Enaex Robotics open-pit fleet (RoboPrimer, Mine-iTruck, Stemming-iTruck, iControl)
sources.title: Open Pit Robotics - Enaex US & Canada
sources.claim: Enaex's open-pit blasting robotics (RoboPrimer, Mine-iTruck, Stemming-iTruck) perform priming, loading and stemming of surface blastholes, but the fleet is described by the vendor as remote-controlled and semi-autonomous, operated from a control station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: charging blastholes in a surface pit, the closest environment match to a quarry bench. Cited as a negative-side check: the surface systems that exist are remotely operated from a control station, so they cannot support an autonomous judgment at E2 or E3.

sources.system: CSIRO robotic blast hole charging system
sources.title: Robotic Explosive Charging in Mining and Construction Applications (IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering)
sources.claim: Research robotic charging systems for blast holes rely on teleoperated arm control and human-in-the-loop visual servoing rather than fully autonomous charge placement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inserting primer-detonator assemblies and pumping explosive into blast holes. Cited to characterise autonomy limits of research systems; because control is human-in-the-loop it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Safe Robotic Handling of Energetic Materials robotic system
sources.developer: ARM Institute / Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute with Ensign-Bickford Aerospace & Defense and DEVCOM Armaments Center
sources.title: Project: Safe Robotic Handling of Energetic Materials
sources.claim: A robotic cell developed for Ensign-Bickford handles canisters of energetic (explosive) material, uncaps them and pours the powder into a hopper, running the replenishment cycle automatically through the day inside a purpose-built, camera-monitored workstation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic handling and metered dispensing of explosive material in a fixtured industrial cell. It supports the E1 realization of this task - charges presented in a magazine and placed into holes at known positions - by showing that live energetic material can be gripped, uncapped and dispensed by a robot under machine control in a purpose-built setting.

tasks.label: Drill holes along outlines, using jackhammers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Granite/limestone quarry bench: worker drills a line of vertical holes (roughly 32-45 mm dia, 1-3 m deep, spaced 10-25 cm) along a chalk-marked outline in the in-situ quarry mass, using a hand-held pneumatic sinker/jackhammer or a quarry-bar mounted drill, standing on uneven rock, outdoors in dust, water and weather.

Quarry face: worker drills horizontal, undercut or angled line holes into a vertical face or under a ledge to complete the outline of a bench, working from an awkward stance close to the wall, with limited clearance and variable, jointed rock.

Quarry floor/block area: worker line-drills along outlines chalked on a large detached ledge or block lying on the working floor, standing on or beside the block with a hand-held jackhammer, to break it down and square it into shippable blocks.

Small or irregular operations (sandstone, slate, thin-bedded limestone, boulder/fieldstone work): hand-held pneumatic drill only, on sloping ledges, on top of boulders or in cramped spots where no rig fits; rock quality and terrain vary hole to hole.

Underground dimension stone quarry (marble/limestone chamber): drilling hole lines along marked outlines on sawn walls and pillars, confined space, artificial light, wet floor, rig- or hand-drill work.

sources.title: Legacy — OSM
sources.claim: OSM's Legacy is a commercial tracked drilling machine sold for dimension stone quarries that, once set on a large flat rock surface, executes a full line of drilled holes automatically; the machine itself is maneuvered by radio remote.

sources.system: DINOSAW LMZK-600 / ZDZK-300 automatic stone drilling machines
sources.title: Automatic Stone Drilling Machines | Gantry & Vertical Driller - DINOSAW
sources.claim: PLC-controlled gantry and vertical stone drilling machines drill programmed holes up to 600 mm diameter and 900 mm deep in granite, marble and limestone workpieces fixtured in a factory, with one-button automatic processing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: programmed hole drilling in dimension stone. Same material (granite/marble/limestone) and hole scale as split-line holes; when the block is fixtured and the hole line is programmed, drilling the outline is the same operation.

sources.system: Monumental Labs robotic stone-carving cells (KUKA 7-axis arms)
sources.title: Stone is being carved by robots and AI. Buildings could be next — Fast Company
sources.claim: Monumental Labs runs KUKA seven-axis robotic arms that machine multi-ton marble, granite and limestone blocks fixtured in a workshop, producing commercial architectural stone that is then hand-finished.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic machining of fixtured stone blocks. Removing stone along a programmed geometry in the same materials at finer tolerance than a split line demonstrates that drilling a hole line into a presented block is within reach of a fixtured cell.

sources.system: Epiroc Boomer rigs with ABC Total (Advanced Boom Control)
sources.date: 2026-07 (product page accessed; feature commercial since the 2010s)
sources.title: Advanced Boom Control | Epiroc US
sources.claim: Epiroc's Advanced Boom Control (ABC Total) on Boomer face drill rigs positions the booms and drills a full round of percussive holes in a rock face automatically from an imported digital drill plan, letting one operator supervise several booms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drilling a planned pattern of percussive holes in rock, including perimeter/contour holes along a designed outline. Same tool principle (hydraulic rock drill) and material; shows the drilling sequence itself is machine-executable once geometry is given.

sources.system: Epiroc (Atlas Copco) SpeedROC 2F / 2FA dimension stone drill rig
sources.title: New rig for stone drillers | Epiroc US
sources.claim: Epiroc/Atlas Copco's SpeedROC 2F/2FA is the standard mechanized dimension stone rig for line drilling 28-45 mm vertical and horizontal holes in marble, granite, sandstone and limestone quarries, but positioning and drilling are commanded by an operator over radio remote control.

sources.system: Epiroc Pit Viper autonomous blasthole rigs (IAMGOLD Côté; Rio Tinto Autonomous Drill System)
sources.title: IAMGOLD's Autonomous Pit Viper Fleet: A First for Epiroc Canada | Global Mining Review
sources.claim: Fully autonomous blasthole drill fleets (Epiroc Pit Viper, supervised from remote control rooms) drill planned hole patterns on open-pit benches in as-found rock, but the holes are large-diameter blastholes on metre-scale spacing, not closely spaced dimension-stone split lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous drilling of planned holes in rock outdoors. It shows outdoor autonomy exists for blasthole geometry (GNSS hole navigation, ~decimetre collar accuracy), which does not meet the 10-25 cm spacing and alignment a wedge-split outline requires, so it does not carry over to this task at E2/E3.

tasks.label: Drill holes into sides of stones broken from masses, insert dogs or attach slings, and direct removal of stones.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Granite dimension-stone quarry bench: after a block is split and turned down from the mass, the splitter drills lifting-dog holes with a hand-held pneumatic/hydraulic drill into two opposite sides of a 10-30 ton rough block lying on broken rock, drives in steel lifting dogs, hooks the dog chains to the derrick, and hand-signals the hoist operator to lift the block clear of the pit. Outdoors, dust and water, uneven footing, block pose different every time.

Limestone/marble quarry floor: no holes drilled; the worker wraps wire-rope or nylon slings or chains around an irregular split block or ledge stone lying on the quarry floor, sets chokers and dunnage, checks the hitch, and directs the crane or wheel-loader operator to remove the stone.

Quarry loading/block yard next to the pit: squared blocks staged in rows on compacted ground; the worker drills fresh dog holes or re-rigs blocks with dogs, clamps or slings, then directs the gantry/derrick or block-handler operator to load them onto trucks or the mill car.

Underground dimension-stone mine (limestone/marble rooms with pillars): the worker drills holes into the sides of a block just cut free at the face, sets dogs or slings, and directs the overhead bridge crane or loader to remove the block along the haul route; confined, wet, artificial light.

Small/irregular product: ledge rock, flagstone, riprap or trimmed offcuts hand-rigged with chains, hooks or clamps on an uneven working face or waste pile, then directed out by loader or small crane; frequent hand handling of odd-shaped pieces.

sources.system: SmartROC D65 MKII autonomous surface drill rig
sources.title: Epiroc and Luck Stone launch first fully autonomous SmartROC D65 drill rig in U.S. aggregate market
sources.claim: Epiroc's SmartROC D65 MKII, deployed at a Luck Stone quarry in the US in September 2025, drills complete blasthole patterns in rock in an open quarry with no operator in the ... (GMG Level 4 autonomy, remote supervision).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous drilling of holes in rock at a quarry. It shows machine drilling in the same outdoor quarry environment, but the holes are pre-planned vertical blastholes collared on a prepared bench, not holes located and drilled into the side of an irregular loose block, and the rig performs no rigging or hoisting, so it does not substantiate the whole task at E2/E3.

sources.system: Sandvik DS412i / DS412iE rock bolting rig (one-bolt automation)
sources.title: Sandvik to add rock bolter to battery-powered mining line up - International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik's DS412i/DS412iE rock bolters carry out a complete bolting cycle - drilling a hole into rock and installing a steel bolt in it - unassisted, with the operator only relocating the boom between bolt positions; commercial underground bolting rigs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drill a hole in rock and insert a steel element into it. That is the mechanical core of drilling a dog hole and driving a lifting dog - same material, similar hole size class and insertion tolerance - and it runs machine-controlled once the boom is positioned, which is exactly what fixturing supplies at E1.

sources.system: Dual-arm construction robot for automatic fixation of structural parts
sources.title: Dual-Arm Construction Robot for Automatic Fixation of Structural Parts to Concrete Surfaces in Narrow Environments (arXiv)
sources.claim: A dual-arm construction robot autonomously drills holes in concrete and inserts and hammers anchors into the drilled hole using force/torque-controlled insertion, completing fixation of structural parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic drilling of a hole in a hard mineral workpiece and force-controlled insertion of a steel anchor into that hole - the same drill-then-insert sequence as drilling a dog hole and setting a lifting dog, at comparable clearance and force levels.

sources.title: Monumental Labs Turns to Automation and Robots to Revive the Art of Stone Carving - Architectural Record
sources.claim: Monumental Labs runs KUKA robotic arms that machine (rough-cut, carve, mill) marble blocks in a fixed workshop, with infrastructure for moving blocks as heavy as 20 tons; a commercial stone-shaping operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-controlled cutting and milling of large fixtured stone blocks. It shows that when a block is presented in a known pose in a purpose-built cell, a robot removes stone at commercial quality on multi-ton blocks, which covers the hole-drilling step of this task at E1.

sources.system: Stone CNC machining centre (Blue Elephant 3015 automatic stone machining center)
sources.title: 3015 Automatic Stone CNC Machining Center | Blue Elephant CNC
sources.claim: Commercial stone CNC machining centres hold granite, marble and quartz workpieces on a fixed table and cut, drill holes, mill and engrave them under numerical control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drilling holes at specified positions in natural stone held in a fixture. Same material and hole-making operation as drilling dog holes; only workpiece presentation differs, which is what the E1 counterfactual supplies.

sources.title: Breton Jot | Handling robot marble granite Lapitec ceramic quartz
sources.claim: Breton Jot is a commercial CNC handling robot that loads, unloads, relocates and flips marble, granite and engineered-stone slabs inside a stone factory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled lifting and removal of heavy stone inside a purpose-built plant. It substantiates the 'direct removal of the stone' step at E1, where the lift is executed by the automated handling system rather than signalled to a human hoist operator.

sources.developer: ETH Zurich (Robotic Systems Lab / Gramazio Kohler Research)
sources.title: Autonomous excavator constructs a six-metre-high dry-stone wall | ETH Zurich
sources.claim: ETH Zurich's HEAP autonomous excavator located, grasped and placed irregular boulders weighing several tons to build a 65 m long, 6 m high dry-stone wall on an outdoor site, using onboard lidar/cameras and autonomous planning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous perception and handling of multi-ton irregular natural stones in unstructured outdoor terrain. It bears on the 'removal of stones' step only; the machine grapples boulders and neither drills lifting holes nor sets dogs or slings, and it is a research demonstration, so it does not substantiate the whole task at E3.

tasks.label: Cut grooves along outlines, using chisels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open quarry bench/ledge, in situ: after the outline is chalked or scribed on the rock mass, the splitter cuts a starter groove/kerf along that line with a hand or pneumatic chisel (or drives a plug drill along it) so wedges can free the block from the mass. Irregular natural rock surface, dust, weather, grain and seams read by eye.

Quarry block yard / dressing pad: a rough block (granite, limestone, marble, sandstone) sits on the ground or on dunnage after primary separation; the splitter chisels a groove along a chalked outline to square or size it, following grain, before wedging or wedge-and-feather splitting.

Quarry mill or fabrication shed: blocks and slabs handled with hoists on a fixed shop floor; the worker chisels grooves along outlines to rough out edges, notches, curves and custom shapes on dimension stone before sawing or splitting.

Slate/flagstone splitting shed or bench: slabs are scored/grooved with a chisel along marked lines to trim them to size and rectangular shape before splitting or trimming; repetitive, indoor, standard bench and tooling.

Pit floor and awkward locations: grooving oversized, overturned or partly split blocks and attached ledge remnants where a machine cannot be set up; wet, cold or confined conditions; hand hammer and chisel used to correct or extend a split line.

sources.system: Monumental Labs robotic stone-carving cells (KUKA arms)
sources.title: Monumental Labs Turns to Automation and Robots to Revive the Art of Stone Carving | Architectural Record
sources.claim: Monumental Labs runs KUKA robotic arms that carve marble architectural elements (e.g., column capitals) from blocks in its Mount Vernon, NY workshop, executing programmed toolpaths unattended for long stretches, with humans doing only finish work; commercial commissions include Carnegie Hall and the Frick Collection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic carving/roughing of fixtured stone blocks to a programmed geometry. Cutting a groove along an outline is a subset of this geometry work on the same materials (marble/limestone blocks up to ~20 t), at tighter precision than a hand-chiselled kerf, in a fixtured cell.

sources.title: Robotor, the sculptor robot shaping Carrara marble — TorArt
sources.claim: Robotor's BOT-ONE robot arms with OR-OS software analyse the raw marble block, plan the machining sequence and select tools from roughing to finishing without an experienced operator; the machines are sold commercially and used in Carrara.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated machining of an as-quarried rough block held on a 7th-axis turntable. Scanning an irregular raw block and cutting programmed geometry into it is the same operation as cutting a groove along a marked outline on a rough quarry block, on identical material.

sources.title: Case Study: Hard Rock Stone Works - BACA Systems
sources.claim: BACA Systems' Robo SawJet — a KUKA industrial robot integrated with an abrasive waterjet and a direct-drive saw — is installed and in daily production in US stone fabrication shops cutting granite and other hard stone slabs to programmed outlines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting programmed outlines, notches and kerfs in hard stone slabs on a fixtured table. This matches grooving/scoring along marked outlines on slabs and slate in a shed, on harder material (granite) than most quarry chisel work, at finer precision.

sources.system: MEC automatic H-frame stone splitting line
sources.title: Stone splitting - MEC
sources.claim: MEC supplies automatic stone-splitting lines built from H-frame splitters with automatic material movement and automatic actuation of the ..., whose stated best application is quarry layer material or sawn stone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled splitting of quarry layer stone along a defined line inside a purpose-built line. It delivers the accepted output the chisel groove exists to produce (a controlled split to outline) on the same quarry material, with the work conveyed to the machine.

sources.system: Epiroc SmartROC D65 MKII autonomous surface drill
sources.title: Epiroc and Luck Stone deploying fully autonomous SmartROC D65 drill rig - International Mining
sources.claim: Epiroc and Luck Stone deployed the first fully autonomous surface ... rig in the quarry market: the SmartROC D65 MKII drills complete GNSS-planned patterns on a quarry bench with no operator in the ..., under remote supervision (GMG Level 4).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous percussive rock working on an unprepared quarry bench. Cited to bound the in-situ instances: it shows autonomy at the face, but its 89–127 mm blastholes on GNSS-planned patterns in an aggregate quarry are not the chalk-line-accurate groove needed to split dimension stone, so it does not substantiate this task in situ.

roles.title: Roustabouts, Oil and Gas
aliases: Field Service Installation Technician (Field Service Installation Tech)
Generator Field Service Technician (Generator Field Service Tech)
roles.description: Assemble or repair oil field equipment using hand and power tools. Perform other tasks as needed.

tasks.label: Unscrew or tighten pipes, casing, tubing, and pump rods, using hand and power wrenches and tongs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Lease/production surface piping: at a well site or tank battery, break out and make up threaded pipe, nipples, valves, unions and flowline connections with pipe wrenches and chain tongs; joints are often rusted, scaled or paraffin-filled, worked at grade, overhead or in a cellar, outdoors in all weather, with a layout that differs at every location.

Well-servicing rig tubing: with a workover/pulling unit rigged up over the wellhead, break out and make up 2-3/8 to 3-1/2 in. tubing joints using hydraulic power tongs and backup while pulling and running the tubing string; joints are wet with oil and must be torqued to spec while the joint is stabbed at floor level.

Sucker rod (pump rod) work: on the same pulling unit, break out and make up sucker rod pin-and-coupling connections with rod tongs or a rod wrench to circumferential-displacement spec, plus polished rod, sinker bar and downhole pump connections, working at the wellhead beside the rod rack.

Drilling rig floor: on a land drilling rig, make up and break out drill pipe and collar connections while drilling and tripping, and run casing, using the iron roughneck, spinning wrench and power tongs at specified torque, working alongside the rig crew.

Yard or shop: at the company pipe yard or maintenance shop, make up and break out tubing/casing joints, subs, crossovers, pump barrels and downhole tool assemblies using power tongs or a bucking unit before equipment is hauled to location.

sources.system: Canrig Red Zone Robotics (RZR) Rig Floor Module on Nabors rig X29
sources.title: Nabors retrofits robotics module onto existing land rig to achieve full automation - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: Nabors' Canrig Red Zone Robotics (RZR) Rig ..., retrofitted to land rig X29, autonomously makes drilling connections and trips pipe hands-free, and handles casing in upper, ...; it drilled multiple horizontal wells for ....

sources.system: Vero Automated Connection Integrity / VERO OneTouch Automated Tubular System
sources.title: Vero Automated Connection Integrity Made Up 3,000 Connections, Saved Over 42 Hours of Rig Time for Major Operator in Deepwater Gulf of Mexico | Weatherford
sources.claim: Weatherford's Vero Automated Connection Integrity ... made up about 3,000 casing and tubular connections on a deepwater Gulf of Mexico rig, with the makeup and evaluation cycle run under computer control from a one-touch start and no personnel in the rig-floor red zone.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class as running tubing on a well-servicing rig: identical threaded oilfield tubulars stabbed at a rig floor over a wellhead and made up/broken out to OEM torque spec, so performance carries to workover tubing strings.

sources.title: Case study: Automated tubular running system demonstrates operational gains in the GoM | Offshore Magazine
sources.claim: Expro's automated tubular running system, built around an intelligent tong (iTONG), executed and verified connection makeup autonomously in Gulf of Mexico rig operations, supervised from the driller's chair or a tablet.
sources.transferJustification: Tubular running (casing/tubing makeup and breakout to torque spec on a rig floor) is the same physical operation as the roustabout's tubing and casing wrenching, on the same objects and tolerances.

sources.system: FlexRobotics hands-free rig floor (developed with NOV)
sources.title: H&P deploys FlexRobotics on Permian rig - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: H&P installed its FlexRobotics three-arm robotic package on Rig 618 and deployed it to the Permian Basin in ... 2025; the arms perform rig-floor tasks including connections and tripping in place of a floor hand, with a gate system stopping motion if anyone enters.

sources.title: Bucking Systems | Weatherford International
sources.claim: Weatherford's ComCAM bucking unit automates makeup and breakout of tubing, casing, completion and premium connections with the joint clamped in the machine, and is sold for repair shops, offline stand building and pipe-threading facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Bucking units perform exactly the task verb — screwing and unscrewing pipe, casing and tubing connections to torque spec — but with the workpiece brought to and fixtured in the machine, which is the E1 counterfactual.

sources.developer: Nabors / Canrig Robotics (formerly Robotic Drilling Systems)
sources.title: Robotic Roughneck - Nabors
sources.claim: Canrig markets a fully electric Robotic Roughneck that makes connections during drilling operations and replaces casing crews and manual tongs, handling up to 270 kNm of torque with full parameter control.

sources.system: Hydraulic bucking unit for sucker rod, drill pipe, joints and casing
sources.developer: Dongying Jinxiu Petroleum Machinery (and comparable vendors, e.g. Lake Petro)
sources.title: Hydraulic Bucking Unit for Sucker Rod, Drill Pipe, Joints and Casing
sources.claim: Hydraulic bucking units are commercially sold for sucker rod, drill pipe, joint and casing make-up and break-out, clamping the workpiece and applying controlled high torque with automatic speed control during the makeup cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the sucker-rod and pump-rod connections named in the task, made up and broken out by a fixtured machine rather than by hand tongs.

sources.system: McCoy Torque Turn System for Bucking and Make/Break Units
sources.title: McCoy Torque Turn System for Bucking and Make/Break Units — McCoy Global Inc.
sources.claim: McCoy Global supplies torque-turn systems designed specifically for bucking and make/break units that monitor, control and analyse tubular connection makeup so that tubing and casing connections conform ....
sources.transferJustification: Shows the makeup quality decision (torque/turn acceptance) in a fixtured bucking cell is made by the machine, supporting worker-quality output at E1.

tasks.label: Dismantle and repair oil field machinery, boilers, and steam engine parts, using hand tools and power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field repair of a beam pumping unit (pumpjack) on a remote lease pad: change worn V-belts and sheaves, adjust/replace brake bands, repack the stuffing box, replace bearings or seals, drain and refill the gearbox, re-torque or cut off seized structure bolts. Outdoors on gravel/caliche, in heat, wind, mud or ice; heavy greasy components; hand tools, impact wrench, cutting torch, and a truck-mounted crane for lifting.

Dismantling and repairing production equipment inside a fenced tank battery, saltwater disposal site, or gas processing/compressor facility: transfer and injection pumps, control and relief valves, separator internals, piping unions and flanges. Fixed layout, operator-controlled premises, standard equipment, work done with wrenches, impact guns, grinders and torches, often after depressurizing and locking out.

Shop or yard rebuild of components pulled from the field: tear down a pump fluid end, valve, gearbox, or engine subassembly on a bench or stand; clean and inspect parts, measure wear, decide what to replace, machine or lap sealing surfaces, reassemble to torque spec and pressure/run test before return to service. Indoor shop with vise, press, torch and power tools.

Engine and prime-mover repair on wellsite or compressor skids: gas engine tune-up, plugs and coils, injectors, filters, belts, hoses, cooler and radiator work, top-end teardown, plus starter/alternator and driveline components. Performed at the unit in the open, often in confined space between skid frames, with hand and power tools.

Boiler, steam generator, heater-treater and line-heater work at steam-flood or treating facilities: pull and replace burner assemblies and nozzles, open manways and clean/plug tubes, replace gaskets, sight glasses, valves and packing, patch refractory, reassemble and re-fire the unit. Institution-controlled facility with fixed layout, hot and dirty conditions.
