Emergency breakdown repair under adverse conditions: called out at night or in a storm to a remote location, diagnose why a unit failed (sheared shaft, blown seal, broken rod, damaged coupling), improvise a fix or swap the failed part using whatever is on the truck, rig heavy parts with slings and a crane truck, and return the unit to production.

sources.system: Spot (Boston Dynamics) with gas-detection and thermal payloads
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: The most mature robot deployed at US oil and gas production facilities, Boston Dynamics' Spot, performs autonomous inspection rounds (gauge reading, thermal imaging, gas leak detection) at a 40-acre midstream plant; it does not dismantle or repair machinery.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the frontier of deployed autonomous field robotics in oil and gas: the same environment as this task, but limited to sensing rounds, with no tool use, fastener removal, or component replacement.

sources.developer: TotalEnergies / Taurob with Equinor, ADNOC, Petronas
sources.title: Autonomous robots on oil & gas sites | ETABLISSEMENT PAU LACQ - TotalEnergies
sources.claim: TotalEnergies' ARGOS-derived 'operator-robot', the most capable autonomous manipulation robot fielded for oil and gas sites, can perform only simple arm actions such as turning, pushing and pulling manual valves; it was delivered end-2024 and is still on test sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (valve operation) at the same oil and gas sites; it establishes that autonomous field manipulation is limited to single gross actions, far short of dismantling machinery with hand and power tools and reassembling it.

sources.title: Sarcos demonstrates robots for shipyard operations to the US Navy - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Field maintenance/repair robots demonstrated in industrial settings, such as Sarcos' Guardian XT/DX, are teleoperated dexterous systems controlled continuously by a human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (shipyard maintenance, inspection and repair) with comparable tools and components; it is teleoperated, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous repair work.

sources.system: Robotic fastener extraction system (UR-class arm with force/torque sensing and custom tooling)
sources.developer: University of Rhode Island (M. K. Jouaneh)
sources.title: A System for Robotic Extraction of Fasteners (Applied Sciences)
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic removal of threaded fasteners — the first step of any teardown — remains a research capability, achieving 78–89% first-pass success on clean end-of-life electronics in a fixtured laboratory cell, with long cycle times.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic disassembly by unscrewing) in a purpose-built cell; it bounds what an E1 setting could do with oilfield fasteners, which are larger, corroded and often galled, and it covers only teardown, not diagnosis, parts replacement or reassembly.

sources.system: Optomec LENS + Acme robotic finishing automated blade repair work cell
sources.title: Optomec and Acme Manufacturing Showcase the Industry's First Fully Automated Work Cell for the Additive Repair of Turbine Parts
sources.claim: The most advanced automated repair cells operate on a single fixtured component type: an Optomec/Acme work cell automatically preps, additively repairs and finishes titanium aviation compressor blades at up to 85,000 blades per year.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (MRO component repair) in a purpose-built cell; it shows automated repair is achieved only for a single geometry-controlled part undergoing material addition and grinding, not for tearing down and rebuilding multi-part oilfield assemblies.

sources.system: Canrig RZR Rig Floor module with iRacker
sources.title: RZR™ Rig Floor Automation Module - Nabors
sources.claim: The most automated purpose-built oilfield work zone, the robotic rig floor, autonomously handles tubulars only; the Canrig RZR/iRacker system performs hands-free pipe racking in the red zone but does no machinery teardown or repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous handling of heavy oilfield tubulars in a machine-centric zone); it demonstrates that even a fully purpose-built oilfield robotic environment is limited to repetitive handling of one standardized item, not tool-based repair of varied machinery.

tasks.label: Guide cranes to move loads about decks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Offshore platform/rig deck during a supply-boat call: the roustabout rigs slings/shackles to mixed cargo (offshore containers, baskets, cutting boxes, chemical totes, tanks), hooks and unhooks the crane whip, gives hand/radio signals as banksman, steadies loads with taglines, and lands them in the laydown area while the vessel deck heaves in wind and swell.

Moving tubulars and drilling equipment about the pipe deck of a rig or platform: guiding the crane to lift bundles of casing/drill pipe, pipe racks, pumps and skids from deck storage to the catwalk/V-door or between racks, hooking up, signalling, and landing loads squarely on stops and bearers.

Land well site or lease: guiding a truck-mounted picker/knuckleboom or rig crane to set tanks, pumps, wellhead components, matting and skids on a muddy, uneven, site-specific pad, with soft ground, overhead lines, wind and varying load geometry; the roustabout rigs the load, signals, and controls swing with taglines.

Shore base, dock or fabrication yard: guiding overhead, mobile or pedestal cranes to load and unload skids, baskets, pipe bundles and equipment between trucks, laydown areas and vessels in a paved, operator-controlled yard.

Congested lift on a live deck: guiding the crane to route pumps, valve skids, scaffold bundles or drums through tight spaces around live process equipment, into module openings and cellar decks, often a blind lift requiring relayed signals and inch-level spotting onto foundations or cribbing.

sources.system: Optilift Autonomous Crane Control System + Aker BP AutoHook (Palfinger offshore crane)
sources.title: Milestone reached for autonomous lifting - Optilift
sources.claim: Optilift's Autonomous Crane Control System, developed with Aker BP and Palfinger, performed automated hook-on and hook-off of containers on a supply-vessel deck using an offshore rig crane, reaching only TRL4 in offshore testing (a demonstration, not routine service).

sources.system: Optilift offshore crane autonomy features with Aker BP AutoHook
sources.title: Offshore - Optilift
sources.claim: Automatic hooking/unhooking without deck crew is offered only where the cargo carriers themselves are fitted with a purpose-built AutoHook interface, i.e. the load must be standardized for the machine.

sources.system: Palfinger remote-operated offshore cranes for Aker BP
sources.title: Remote-controlled cranes developed for offshore platforms - Riviera
sources.claim: The Aker BP/Palfinger offshore cranes intended to remove deck crew are remote-operated from an onshore control room, with offshore commissioning of the remote capability scheduled for 2026-2028; no autonomous platform-deck cargo handling is in service.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (moving loads about platform decks); cited only to show the offshore state of the art is remote human operation, supporting the negative judgment at E2.

sources.title: Advanced robotics enable revolution on the rig floor - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: NOV's ATOM RTX is a fully automated robotic ... with up to three arms that executes drill-floor load-handling tasks such as tailing pipe and racking tubulars at height.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hoisting, guiding and landing heavy tubulars on a rig deck. Same objects (drill pipe/collars), comparable mass and inch-level landing precision as crane-guided pipe-deck moves, but only inside a barriered robotic work zone.

sources.title: H&P deploys FlexRobotics on Permian rig - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: H&P installed the FlexRobotics package (three-arm RTX robotic platform built with NOV) on Rig 618 and deployed it to the Permian Basin, delivering automated pipe handling in field service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized lifting, guiding and precise landing of heavy tubulars on a working rig, substituting for the crew members who otherwise guide and steady the load.

sources.title: FlexRobotics Hands-Free Rig Floor | H&P, Inc.
sources.claim: FlexRobotics works by removing personnel from the red zone, with sliding gate barriers that e-stop the robots if a person opens a gate - the setting is rebuilt around the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Same robotic load-handling system as the preceding item; cited to establish that its working environment carries E1 marks (fenced exclusion of people).

sources.title: Electric and Hydraulic iRacker System - Nabors
sources.claim: Nabors/Canrig's iRacker is an autonomous tubular handling system enabling completely hands-free pipe handling with no workers required on the rig floor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hoisting and precisely landing heavy tubular loads on a rig - the physical work a roustabout guides a crane through - achieved only in a purpose-built, personnel-free machine zone.

sources.title: Automated container handling in port terminals - Control Engineering
sources.claim: Automated stacking cranes in container terminals lift, carry and land standardized containers continuously without any operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: crane movement of containerized loads about a yard. Offshore deck cargo is largely carried in standard offshore containers/baskets of comparable mass and footprint with similar landing tolerance, but the crane engages the load through standardized fittings inside a fenced automated block.

sources.system: LBCT automated container terminal (ASCs and autonomous vehicles)
sources.title: Long Beach Container Terminal: Sustainable, autonomous and electric - Trellis
sources.claim: Long Beach Container Terminal runs roughly 72 automatic stacking cranes and about 100 automated rail-mounted cranes plus autonomous vehicles in commercial service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine, high-volume autonomous crane movement of unitized loads about a yard, evidencing that fixtured/standardized load handling by crane is reliable at scale when people are excluded from the machine's block.

tasks.label: Walk flow lines to locate leaks, using electronic detectors and by making visual inspections, and repair the leaks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine walkaround of an onshore well pad / tank battery: roustabout walks the wellhead, flow line risers, valves, unions and flanges on a gravel pad in open country, using a handheld combustible-gas/LEL detector plus sight, smell and sound; finds a weeping valve packing or dripping threaded fitting and repairs it on the spot — bleeds down, tightens the packing gland or breaks out and re-makes the fitting with pipe wrenches and dope, then re-pressurizes and re-checks. Mud, wind, heat, livestock, site-to-site layout variation.

Walking a flow line right-of-way across pasture/rangeland or desert between a wellhead and a battery (often 1/4 to several miles of buried or surface line), scanning for oil-stained soil, dead vegetation, gas bubbles in standing water, seeps and pressure loss; on locating a leak, exposing the line by hand digging/backhoe assist and installing a repair clamp or full-encirclement sleeve, then testing the repair.

Fugitive-emissions style survey at a fenced compressor station or central tank battery: walking the piping, separators, thief hatches and connectors with a gas detector or optical gas imaging camera to pinpoint the leak source, then repairing it — re-torquing bolted connections, replacing a thief-hatch or flange gasket, swapping a leaking gauge or valve — and re-surveying to confirm the repair.

Deck/process-area walk on an offshore platform or gas processing facility: following piping runs on grated decks and stairs with fixed and portable gas detectors, locating a small leak at a fitting, instrument tubing line or gland, and making the minor repair (tighten, replace tubing ferrule/gasket, install a temporary clamp) under permit-to-work.

Heavy repair after leak location: a corroded section of flow line must be cut out and replaced — excavate, isolate and drain the line, cut with saw or torch, thread or weld in a new joint/spool, backfill and pressure-test, all in the open field with hand and power tools and often in poor weather.

sources.system: ANYmal (ANYbotics) with Gas Leak & Presence Detection payload
sources.title: ANYbotics Launches New Gas Leak & Presence Detection Solution for its ANYmal Inspection Robot
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal legged inspection robot has a commercially launched gas leak and presence detection ... that autonomously navigates industrial facilities, localizes and quantifies leaks and alerts personnel; it performs detection only and does not carry out the mechanical repair.
sources.transferJustification: Substantiates only the 'locate leaks using electronic detectors and visual inspection' half of the task, in oil & gas facilities; no evidence the robot performs the repair, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion.

sources.system: Spot with combustible gas detection payload
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot, running autonomous inspection rounds with a gas detection payload at a midstream gas plant, detected a plume of combustible ... from a pinhole leak; the robot reports the leak for human repair crews.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous gas-leak detection walkdowns in a hydrocarbon processing facility; transfers to the detection element of this task but provides no capability for the hand/power-tool repair that completes it.

sources.title: Percepto launches AI emission detector for remote, drone-based methane surveying
sources.claim: Percepto's autonomous drone-in-a-box OGI system performs methane/emission surveys at upstream oil and gas sites and is in daily use across major U.S. basins; findings are handed to field teams for repair.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the leak-location element over unstructured well-pad and flow-line terrain (E3 setting), but an aerial platform performs no physical repair, so the whole instance is not completed.

sources.title: 21st-Century Repairman: The Robot in the Gas Main
sources.claim: ULC Technologies' CISBOT, the closest fielded example of robotic leak repair on live gas piping, seals leaking cast-iron main joints from inside the pipe, but it is positioned and operated by a technician using onboard cameras and controls from a surface trailer, with a crew performing the excavation and launch.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic sealing of leaking gas-pipe joints. It is teleoperated and confined to the inside of large-diameter distribution mains, so it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous in-situ flow-line leak repair.

sources.system: ATEQ robotic sniffing leak test system
sources.title: Robotic Leak Testing l Sniffing & Tracer Gas Turnkey Systems
sources.claim: In purpose-built production cells, robot-guided sniffing leak-test systems (ATEQ with a robot arm; VIC/ABB sniffer cobot) automatically locate and quantify leaks on fixtured components, but such cells sort failed parts rather than repairing them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated leak location on work brought to the machine; establishes the E1 counterfactual for detection only. No cited cell disassembles a leaking, corroded connection and re-makes the seal, so the repair half is unsupported even at E1.

sources.title: Automated Robotics Solutions for Oil & Gas - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' explosion-proof ANYmal X is used for autonomous inspection of offshore fixed platforms and FPSOs, including corrosion and gas detection and localization, under a commercial agreement with PETRONAS; the robot inspects and reports rather than repairs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous walkdown inspection and gas localization in an E2 offshore production facility; transfers to leak location on deck piping but not to the tool-based repair that completes the instance.

tasks.label: Lay gas and oil pipelines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New steel flowline/gathering line on a lease: backhoe a shallow ditch from wellhead to tank battery, unload and string 20-40 ft joints of 2-8 in. line pipe, align and weld or thread joints, set risers, tie in at wellhead and separator/tank, pressure test, backfill. Uneven ground, mud, wind and heat, layout differs at every location.

Working with a pipeline construction spread on a cross-country right-of-way (gathering or transmission line, 8-36 in.): stringing joints along the ditch, fit-up with line-up clamps, mechanized/manual welding, field-joint coating, lowering-in with sidebooms, backfilling and cleanup over rough terrain, road and creek crossings.

Cut-out and replacement of a damaged or corroded section of buried line: dig a bell hole, expose and cut out the bad joint, fit a new pipe spool, weld or flange it in, coat, hydrotest, backfill and restore. Confined muddy excavation, live-line hazards, unpredictable soil.

Laying temporary surface transfer lines across leases and pastures: rolling out lay-flat hose or HDPE poly pipe from reels, dragging line over fences, ditches and road crossings, connecting cam-lock or fused joints, then recovering the line after the job.

Installing and tying in piping inside a company facility yard (central tank battery, compressor station, central delivery point): cutting and fitting small-bore pipe, welding or bolting flanged spools on racks and supports, connecting to vessels, pumps and headers. Fixed layout, graded pad, controlled site access, permit-to-work.

sources.system: Novarc Spool Welding Robot (SWR) with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2
sources.title: Novarc Technologies Inc. Launches A Computer Vision Product In Arc Welding - Canadian Manufacturing
sources.claim: Novarc's Spool Welding Robot with NovEye Autonomy Gen 2 performs multi-pass pipe welding autonomously in fabrication shops on pipe presented on powered positioners, adapting to real fit-up variation (HiLo, varying root gaps) with no operator intervention after setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: joining steel pipe joints/fittings into leak-tight, code-quality pressure piping — the same joining operation, pipe material and weld-quality standard that laying a gas or oil line requires, performed on a fixtured workpiece.

sources.title: NOVARC TECHNOLOGIES LAUNCHES AN INDUSTRY FIRST WITH AI, MACHINE LEARNING COMPUTER VISION IN ARC WELDING TO FULLY AUTOMATE THE PIPE WELDING PROCESS
sources.claim: Novarc states NovEye Autonomy delivers x-ray quality ... after setup, and the SWR handles pipe from 2 in. to 60 in. diameter in carbon and stainless steel.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: covers the pipe-joining core of pipeline laying, on the diameter range (2"-60") used for oilfield flowlines, gathering lines and mainline pipe.

sources.title: Ganotec-Muga Fab Boosts Welding Efficiency w/ Novarc's SWR
sources.claim: Deployed SWR cells in commercial pipe fabrication shops produce welds at repair rates below 1% (0-0.5% for some customers) versus a 3-5% North American shop average, i.e. at or above skilled-worker quality.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes worker-quality output for the pipe-joining step that pipeline laying depends on.

sources.system: Canrig Red Zone Robotics (RZR) Rig Floor Module with iRacker
sources.title: Nabors retrofits robotics module onto existing land rig to achieve full automation - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: Nabors' Canrig RZR rig-floor module autonomously handles tubulars and makes pipe connections hands-free on retrofitted land drilling rigs, removing crew from the pipe-handling area.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking up individual steel pipe joints from a rack, aligning them and making up connections into a continuous string — the handling and joint-making motions of laying pipe, done autonomously in a purpose-built machine environment.

sources.title: RZR Rig Floor Automation Module - Nabors
sources.claim: Nabors describes the RZR module's iRacker as a fully autonomous tubular handling system giving completely hands-free pipe handling on the rig floor.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: autonomous heavy steel pipe handling and connection make-up in a purpose-built (fenced red-zone) setting.

sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofit turns standard excavators into autonomous trenching machines used in production on outdoor construction and energy jobsites, i.e. the ditching sub-step of pipe laying is automated at E3 — but the system only digs; it does not string, join, lower in or tie in pipe.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: trench excavation on unstructured jobsites, one sub-step of laying a buried pipeline; cited to show what is and is not automated outdoors.

sources.system: CRC Evans automatic pipeline welding systems (IWM, external welders)
sources.title: ADIPEC 2025: CRC Evans CEO talks offshore welding for a digital future | Offshore Magazine
sources.claim: Pipeline field welding as practiced today (onshore right-of-way and offshore) is mechanised but not autonomous: CRC Evans' CEO states machines do much of the ... while human operators still perform setup and supervision, with fully robotic welding described as a future goal.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about joining pipe on pipeline spreads and lay vessels; cited as negative evidence that field pipe laying is not completed autonomously in E2/E3 settings.

tasks.label: Bolt together pump and engine parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: At a producing wellsite/lease: bolting the prime mover assembly of a pumping unit together — mounting and bolting an engine or electric motor to the skid base, bolting up gearbox/sheave and belt-guard hardware. Outdoors on an uneven pad, dirty and often rusted hardware, wind and heat, impact and torque wrenches, no fixturing.

At a tank battery or well pad: setting and bolting a transfer/charge or plunger pump to its skid and bolting up flanged suction and discharge connections to piping (gaskets, studs, cross-torque pattern). Outdoors, as-found piping alignment, drifting bolt holes, live facility.

Field repair on installed equipment: replacing and re-bolting pump or engine components in place — fluid end/stuffing box, packing gland, pump head, water pump or manifold — with corroded fasteners, cramped access, parts carried in on a truck.

In the company yard/shop: building up a new pump-and-engine skid package — bolting engine, gearbox and pump to a common base, fitting coupling and coupling guard, shimming and checking alignment before torqueing down.
Bench work in the shop: reassembling a pump after rebuild — bolting casing halves, bearing caps, end covers and cover plates to torque spec with parts cleaned and laid out on a bench.

At an institution-controlled facility (gas plant, compressor station, saltwater disposal site) during a scheduled turnaround: bolting engine or pump components on a compressor/pump package under a permit system, fixed layout, standard equipment.

sources.system: SymbioDCS robotic bolt-running cell (UR10 + Acradyne nutrunner + ATI force/torque sensor)
sources.title: Intelligent Bolt Running Using AI Feedback-Based Search – Metrology and Quality News
sources.claim: A deployed production workcell at a large automotive assembly plant uses a UR10 robot with an Acradyne nutrunner and force/torque sensing (SymbioDCS) to locate and tighten bolts on parts that shift in their fixtures, raising reliability to 99% in production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic bolt running on mechanical subassemblies. It is the same physical operation as bolting pump and engine parts — engaging a threaded fastener with a socket and driving it to controlled torque — with vision/force search compensating for part-to-part misfit inside a fixtured cell.

sources.developer: INESC TEC with Europneumaq Industrial Solutions
sources.title: Robots Automate Bolt-Tightening on Automotive Assembly Lines | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Robotic bolt tightening on an automotive assembly line (fastening rear axle dampers to a van undercarriage) has been demonstrated with 3D vision and force sensing to compensate for vehicle position variation, at a 160-second cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic tightening of chassis bolts on a conveyor-borne vehicle. Fastener sizes, torque levels and the need to find attachment points on an imperfectly located part are comparable to bolting pump/engine components presented in a cell.

sources.system: KUKA KR 1000 titan cylinder-block assembly work island at FAW
sources.developer: KUKA (integrated at FAW Group engine plant)
sources.title: KUKA KR 1000 titan assembles cylinder blocks at the FAW Group | KUKA Global
sources.claim: A heavy-payload industrial robot handles and positions 500 kg engine cylinder blocks through an automated engine assembly work island where connecting rods, cylinders and oil pans are installed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling and assembly of engine components. It shows engine/pump-scale masses (500-700 kg) can be manipulated and mated by robots in a fenced cell, which is the handling half of bolting pump and engine parts together.

sources.title: TMT Boltron – Autonomous Flange Bolting Robot (datasheet TMT-NSS-642)
sources.claim: A commercial autonomous flange-bolting robot tightens and loosens nuts on large industrial flanges at 950-3400 Nm on refinery and process-plant equipment (heat exchangers, pressure vessels); it is base-mounted to the flange by workers and only services nuts on already-mated flanges.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous high-torque nut running on installed process equipment at an industrial facility. It shows oilfield-magnitude torques are within robotic reach, but the machine is set on the flange by workers and does not lift, align or mate the parts.

sources.system: Robotiq Screwdriving Workcell (cobot + screw feeder + fixture)
sources.title: Screwdriving Automation and Cobot Components for Electrical Equipment Manufacturers | Robotiq
sources.claim: Robotiq screwdriving workcells were deployed at Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories, scaling from one pilot cell to 27 production ... that autonomously drive 1.4 million fasteners per year in fixtured cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production-volume robotic fastener driving at accepted quality. It establishes that fastening cells with fed fasteners and fixtured workpieces run unattended at worker-replacing quality, which is the E1 form of these bolting instances.

tasks.label: Move pipes to and from trucks, using truck winches and motorized lifts, or by hand.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Unloading new joints of tubing, casing or line pipe (20–40 ft, 500–2,000 lb each, some banded bundles) from a flatbed/gooseneck pipe truck at a lease or well pad, using the truck's winch and gin pole or a forklift/skid steer with forks, and laying them out on ground rails or pipe racks; dirt/gravel surface, wind, mud, spotters on the ground.

Loading pulled tubing, sucker rods, surplus or scrap pipe from a wellsite, tank battery or flowline right-of-way back onto a truck for return to the yard: mixed sizes, muddy/oily joints, hand-rigging slings and chains, tight working space among wellhead and vessel equipment.

Hand-carrying small-diameter pipe, short joints, fittings and flowline sections off the bed of a pickup or service truck (often a two-person carry) and stacking or staging them at scattered field locations over uneven ground.

Loading and unloading pipe at the company pipe/supply yard: level compacted surface, marked racks, forklift or gantry/overhead crane, controlled access, staged bundles and racked joints being moved between racks and flatbed trucks.

Unloading drill pipe, casing and joints from pipe trucks at an active drilling rig location onto the pipe racks beside the catwalk, and loading pipe back out on rig release; graded pad, standard rig layout, rig contractor controls access, weather-exposed, crane/forklift plus hand rigging.

sources.title: Semi-automated loading for containers and regular, nonmodified trucks — Actiw LoadPlate brochure
sources.claim: Actiw LoadPlate is a commercially deployed automated loading machine (100+ customers) that transfers a complete staged load — including steel pipes and plates and other long cargo — into ordinary unmodified trucks, trailers and containers in a purpose-built loading station, with a ~5 minute cycle and up to 30,000 kg per load.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (moving pipe onto trucks), same objects (steel pipe), performed by machine once the load is staged on the plate; only the truck-loading transfer itself is judged here.

sources.system: Ancra ATLS chain conveyor truck loading/unloading system
sources.title: Ancra Systems: Automatic Truck Loading and Unloading Solution Chain Conveyor System
sources.claim: Ancra Systems supplies commercially installed Automatic Truck Loading Systems (ATLS) that load and unload trailers with chain-conveyor or skate systems at a dock without a person handling the goods, covering the reverse (unloading) direction of truck transfer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic unloading of unitized loads from trailers. It transfers to pipe unloading only in a purpose-built dock where the load is presented on conveyors/plates, as Actiw shows is done for steel pipe.

sources.system: Automated tube/pipe packing line with pick-and-place robot
sources.developer: Tube and pipe packaging line suppliers (reported in Tube & Pipe Journal)
sources.title: The next generation of automated tube and pipe packing
sources.claim: Automated tube and pipe packing lines use robots and chain conveyors to pick individual tubes and place them into bundles without an operator handling the pipe, showing machine handling of individual pipe pieces in a purpose-built line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving individual pipe joints by machine instead of by hand. Same objects (steel tube), comparable weights and placement precision, but only inside a fixtured line.

sources.system: KASTO UNICOMPACT 5.0 automated long-goods storage with magnet bridge crane
sources.title: Automated Steel Storage System for SPS
sources.claim: KASTO's UNICOMPACT automatic storage and retrieval system, installed at steel distributor Steel and Pipe Supply in Kansas City, uses automated gantry/bridge cranes with magnetic lifting devices to store and retrieve bundled long steel goods (bars and tubes) with automated loading and unloading processes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine handling of bundled long steel stock (bars/tubes) equivalent in size and weight to oilfield joints, but inside an enclosed purpose-built automated aisle, not an open yard or truck bed.

sources.system: Canrig Red Zone Robotics (RZR) rig floor module / iRacker; Nabors PACE-R801
sources.title: RZR™ Rig Floor Automation Module - Nabors
sources.claim: Nabors' Canrig RZR rig-floor module with the iRacker performs fully autonomous, hands-free handling of oilfield tubulars on land rigs; it was retrofitted to rig X29 and drilled multiple horizontal wells for .... Its autonomous scope is the drill floor, derrick and catwalk area, not transfer of pipe to or from trucks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous handling of oilfield tubulars at a wellsite. It shows deployed wellsite pipe automation is confined to a fixed machine workspace (racks/catwalk/floor) and does not cover truck loading or unloading, supporting the negative E2/E3 judgments.

tasks.label: Clean trucks used in the fields.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pressure-washing the exterior of a crew pickup or flatbed work truck at the company yard wash rack: caliche dust, dried lease-road mud, oil spatter on body, bed and toolboxes; hot water, soap, hand wand; truck must come out presentable for road and customer sites.

Washing a heavy oilfield unit (vacuum truck, water/frac tank truck, winch or gin truck) at the yard wash pad: thick caked drilling mud, produced-water salt and crude residue on frame, tanks, wheels and undercarriage; high-volume hot water and degreaser, 30-60 minutes of work.
Steam cleaning / degreasing a truck's chassis, frame rails and undercarriage in the shop bay before maintenance, DOT inspection or welding repair, so grease and mud do not hide cracks or leaks.

Cleaning out the truck cab and interior at the yard: pulling trash, rags, empty bottles and paperwork, knocking mud off floor mats, vacuuming floorboards, wiping the dash and cleaning glass, and clearing loose debris and tools from the bed.

Washing a truck down on location at the well pad or lease road with a portable pressure washer or water-truck hose, before leaving location, to knock off drilling mud, spilled fluids or brine; uneven caliche pad, wind, no wash infrastructure.

sources.title: Industrial Vehicle Washing Systems - Manual & Robotic Solutions
sources.claim: InterClean sells robotic industrial vehicle wash systems for mining and oilfield vehicles that run completely automatic wash cycles with no personnel in the wash bay, programmable for multiple vehicle types up to 400-ton haul trucks, removing mud, oil and debris.

sources.title: Heavy Vehicle Washing Systems - Reduce Vehicle Equipment Downtime
sources.claim: InterClean's robotic heavy-vehicle wash system senses and recognizes the vehicle presented in the bay and directs its water cannons to designated areas while avoiding sensitive sections, i.e. it adapts its automatic cycle to the vehicle rather than running blind.

sources.system: Hydro-Chem Systems automated drive-thru truck wash
sources.title: Automated Truck Wash Systems - Hydro-Chem Systems, Inc.
sources.claim: Hydro-Chem Systems touchless automated drive-thru truck wash systems are installed at fleet facilities and wash a heavy truck in 2-5 minutes with the driver simply pulling through; a Michigan Department of Public Works fleet installed one and then added a second at another facility.

sources.title: Chassis Wash Systems - Heavy-Duty Undercarriage Cleaning
sources.claim: InterClean automated chassis wash systems clean truck, bus and mining-vehicle undercarriages of dirt, grime and corrosive material with the operator only driving through, no manual scrubbing, making the underbody easier to inspect and maintain.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: undercarriage/chassis degreasing of heavy trucks. Same objects (oilfield/mining truck frames and underbodies), same heavy soil (mud, grease, corrosives) and same purpose (cleaning before inspection/maintenance) as the roustabout's steam-clean-before-repair job.

sources.system: InterClean mining vehicle wash (robotic / automatic drive-through)
sources.title: Mining Vehicle Wash - Haul Trucks, Equipment & Heavy Vehicle Solutions
sources.claim: InterClean's mining wash line includes robotic systems that run cleaning cycles on haul trucks and heavy equipment caked with mud in high-risk environments without any operator in the wash bay, and fully automatic drive-through packages for haul-truck washing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing mud-caked mining haul trucks. Comparable vehicles and soil loads (heavy clay mud, grease, dust) to oilfield vacuum/winch/water trucks, and the same accepted output (a clean unit ready for maintenance and service).

sources.title: Confinity Robotics unveils first interior cleaning robot at The Car Wash Show
sources.claim: Robotic cleaning of vehicle interiors is still at the trade-show and beta-testing stage, and is aimed at passenger-car seats and footwells in car-wash tunnels, not at cluttered work-truck cabs.

tasks.label: Dig holes, set forms, and mix and pour concrete into forms to make foundations for wood or steel derricks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New rig/derrick substructure or mast foundation at a well pad: stake layout, excavate footing/pier holes with a backhoe plus hand trimming, set and brace lumber forms, tie rebar, place ready-mix from a truck chute, set anchor bolts to template, screed/float and strip forms. Outdoor lease site, uneven graded caliche/dirt pad, live traffic of trucks and crews.

Small equipment foundations around the lease: pump-jack base, tank battery pad, separator/compressor skid pad, pumphouse slab. Dig with skid steer or shovel, level and compact, set plywood/lumber forms and mesh, pour ready-mix or site-mixed concrete, level and finish.

Post and anchor foundations: hand-dig or auger holes for guy-wire anchors, pipe supports, gate/sign posts and small stands; set the post plumb, mix bagged concrete in a wheelbarrow or portable mixer, pour around the post and crown the top.

Buried anchor blocks (deadmen) and deep pier footings: excavate a pit with a backhoe, cut and place rebar cage, build heavier braced forms in the pit, mass-pour concrete, embed anchor rod/plate, backfill after cure.

Repair or extension of an existing in-ground foundation: break out spalled/cracked concrete with jackhammer, excavate alongside, dowel and form a patch or extension, pour and finish, non-shrink grout under equipment baseplates.

sources.system: Progress Maschinen & Automation shuttering & deshuttering robot (ebos-controlled)
sources.date: 2026-07 (product page retrieved); product line commercial since the 2010s
sources.title: Shuttering Robot | Progress Maschinen & Automation
sources.claim: Commercial shuttering/deshuttering robots in precast concrete plants build the mould (set the forms) fully automatically from CAD data: a storage robot picks the required magnetic shutter profiles and the robot positions and locks them on the casting bed, then removes them after casting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: erecting formwork for a precast concrete element. It is the same act as 'set forms' — assembling the mould that wet concrete is poured into and stripping it after cure — performed to tighter tolerance than field lumber forms, but only in a machine-fixtured casting line.

sources.system: Form Master shuttering/deshuttering robot at Schwörer Bausysteme GmbH
sources.title: Schwörer Bausysteme relies on modernization in the precast plant - Concrete Plant Precast Technology
sources.claim: A combined shuttering/deshuttering/storage robot that also positions embedded mounting parts automatically has been installed and running in a production precast plant since 2021.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: form setting plus placement of cast-in inserts/anchors in a precast plant. Transfers to 'set forms' and to embedding anchor bolts/posts, since the objects (steel shutters, embedded steel parts) and the placement precision required equal or exceed field formwork and anchor setting.

sources.system: SMART CAST automatic concrete spreader with SMART COMPACT2 compaction (Baoye Group precast plant)
sources.title: Chinese Baoye Group continues to invest in precast concrete production
sources.claim: Automatic concrete spreaders deployed in precast plants dose and place fresh concrete into the shuttered moulds to a preset batch quantity, with automatic compaction following, without a worker placing the concrete.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing structural concrete into a mould in a precast plant. This is the 'pour concrete into forms' step; concrete volume, consistency and placement tolerance are comparable to a field pad pour, but the mould is machine-presented.

sources.system: EBAWE concrete spreader / concrete distributor (ebos control)
sources.date: 2026-07 (product page retrieved); machine line long commercial
sources.title: Concrete Spreader | Ebawe
sources.claim: Concrete spreaders take concrete directly from the mixer ... fill shuttered pallets and battery/element moulds, under manual or automatic control, in carrousel precast plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated filling of moulds, including heavy element and battery moulds used for footings, plinths and columns. Same act as pouring concrete into forms for a foundation block, with reinforcement already in the mould.

sources.system: MCT automated precast batching and casting plant (United States)
sources.title: Automated precast plant for high quality concrete - MCT Group
sources.claim: A US precast plant runs fully automatic concrete batching, mixing and distribution with flying buckets feeding automatic casting machines — the 'mix and pour' portion of foundation casting done by machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial batching, mixing and casting of structural concrete. It substantiates the 'mix and pour concrete' element of the task, in a plant where the mould is brought to the casting machine.

sources.title: Built Robotics releases 1st fully autonomous construction machinery in US | Construction Dive
sources.claim: Aftermarket autonomy kits let standard excavators dig trenches, excavate foundations and grade pads fully autonomously on open construction sites, supervised remotely; deployed on utility-scale solar jobsites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous excavation for foundations on unstructured outdoor sites. It substantiates only the 'dig holes' component of this task; no form setting, concrete mixing or pouring is performed by this system.

sources.title: Robotic pile driver faster than manual versions, says US startup – pv magazine International
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic pile driver surveys, distributes, drives and inspects steel foundation piles at utility-scale solar construction sites, i.e. installs foundations outdoors without a manual crew placing each one.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous installation of structural foundations on unstructured outdoor sites. It shows hole-making and foundation placement can be autonomous outdoors, but it uses driven steel piles — no forms, no concrete mixing or pouring — so it cannot substitute for a formed cast-in-place foundation.

tasks.label: Supply equipment to rig floors as requested and provide assistance to roughnecks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Tubular supply during drilling/tripping on a land or offshore rig: at the driller's request, moving joints and stands of drill pipe, drill collars, casing or tubing from the pipe racks onto the catwalk and up through the V-door to the rig floor, cleaning/doping threads and tallying, then handing off to the floor crew. Standard rig layout, contractor-controlled site, day and night, all weather.

Extra hands on the rig floor during connections, trips and casing runs: tailing pipe to well center or the mousehole, helping stab, applying pipe dope, holding the stabbing guide, positioning the mud bucket, dragging hoses and lines, and keeping the floor clean and clear while roughnecks work tongs and slips.

Fetch-and-carry of non-tubular equipment and consumables on request: hand and power tools, bits, subs, slips and dies, wear bushings, valves, chemical/mud sacks, hoses and spare parts retrieved from the tool house, laydown area or yard and hauled across the pad and up the stairs to the rig floor, then handed to the crew. The item requested varies job to job; footing may be muddy, icy or greasy.

Heavy equipment moves and rigging: slinging, hooking and tag-lining loads (pumps, BOP components, tool baskets, skids, tanks, containers) with a rig crane, boom truck or forklift and spotting them where the drill crew needs them; offshore, working the deck with the crane operator to land and break out supply-boat lifts destined for the drill floor.

Rig-up/rig-down, rig moves and workover-site assistance on unimproved ground: laying out and connecting hoses, lines and small equipment at a location whose layout differs every time, on mud, gravel or uneven terrain, in weather, doing whatever the drill or service crew calls for.

sources.system: Nabors PACE-R800/R801 robotic rig (Canrig pipe handler, ground handling system)
sources.title: PACE®-R - Nabors
sources.claim: Nabors' PACE-R robotic land rig uses a robotic electric pipe handler plus a ground handling system that moves tubular handling activity off the rig floor, with a two-level floor keeping personnel away from operating equipment; R801 drilled a well campaign for ExxonMobil.

sources.system: Canrig Red Zone Robotics (RZR) Rig Floor Module on Nabors rig X29
sources.title: Nabors retrofits robotics module onto existing land rig to achieve full automation - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: Nabors retrofitted the Canrig Red Zone Robotics (RZR) rig ... onto an existing land rig (X29), which drilled multiple horizontal wells for ExxonMobil/XTO in the Permian Basin; the module performs rig floor pipe tasks autonomously and removes the floor and derrick hands.

sources.title: RZR™ Rig Floor Automation Module - Nabors
sources.claim: The RZR rig floor module's iRacker is a fully autonomous triple racking ... giving hands-free delivery and racking of pipe, controlled from the driller's cabin; an upgraded RZR version was deployed in 2025.

sources.system: NOV ATOM RTX robotic arms (H&P FlexRobotics)
sources.title: Advanced robotics enable revolution on the rig floor - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: On H&P Rig 618, NOV ATOM RTX six-axis arms on rig-floor tracks perform the helper work around the roughneck: one arm does all tailing and stabbing, the other handles doping, mud containment and the stabbing guide, integrated into the rig control system.

sources.system: H&P FlexRobotics rig floor (Rig 618) gate safety system
sources.title: Advanced robotics enable revolution on the rig floor - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: The robotic rig floor is run as a machine-exclusive hazard area: a gate safety system on H&P Rig 618 halts all robot motion if a person enters, so people are kept out rather than working alongside the arms.

sources.system: Precision Drilling AlphaARMS (NOV ATOM RTX arms)
sources.title: PRECISION DRILLING Corp - Form 40-F - FY2025
sources.claim: Precision Drilling deployed AlphaARMS rig floor robotics (three modular robots plus automated iron floor hand) on a Super Triple land rig in 2024 and reports it reached human-crew efficiency in 2025.

sources.title: Advanced robotics enable revolution on the rig floor - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: AlphaARMS automated about 95% of rig floor activities on its wells, eliminating tens of thousands of manual touchpoints by rig floor personnel.

sources.title: FlexRobotics® Hands-Free Rig Floor | H&P, Inc.
sources.claim: H&P's FlexRobotics package, three Yaskawa six-axis manipulators developed with NOV, was commercially deployed on Permian Rig 618 in September 2025 and automates tubular handling from tailing ... while keeping crews out of the red ....

sources.title: Manufacturers pave path to hands-free drilling with automated tubular handling - Drilling Contractor
sources.claim: ATOM RTX arms retrieve equipment for themselves from a fixtured storage rack beside the drill floor - tailing claws, doping head, stabbing assist head, modular mud bucket - and bring it to well center as the job requires.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving a requested piece of equipment from a fixtured store and delivering it to the work point on the drill floor - the same fetch-and-present function a roustabout performs for the floor crew, with rig-floor-scale objects and precision.

sources.system: Seegrid Palion autonomous lift truck / tow tractor AMRs
sources.title: Seegrid Lift Truck AMR is the Market's Most Advanced Automated Forklift
sources.claim: Seegrid autonomous fork trucks and tow tractors move palletized material between defined pick and drop points in manufacturing and warehouse facilities, with over 18 million autonomous ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hauling requested materials and heavy palletized loads from a storage area to a delivery point on a fixed route - the transport core of supplying equipment once the load is presented on a standard pallet or skid.

sources.system: Agility Robotics Digit at GXO/SPANX facility
sources.title: GXO Signs Industry-First Multi-Year Agreement with Agility Robotics
sources.claim: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid is under a multi-year commercial RaaS agreement with GXO, autonomously moving totes from AMRs onto conveyors in a live logistics facility, passing 100,000 totes by late 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking up a container of supplies presented at a known position and delivering it to a fixed handoff point - the same carry-and-hand-off action with comparable payloads, once items are kitted into totes as a purpose-built setting would present them.

sources.system: LBCT automated stacking cranes and AGVs
sources.title: What Makes Our Terminals Technologically Advanced? | Long Beach Container Terminal
sources.claim: Long Beach Container Terminal runs dozens of electric automatic stacking cranes with AGVs in fenced automated blocks, lifting and precisely spotting multi-tonne standardized loads without personnel in the working area.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: crane handling of heavy standardized units - lifting from a known position and spotting to a designated location without human riggers - matching the lift-and-spot core of roustabout crane work once loads carry standard lifting interfaces.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Cognite Data Fusion on Aker BP Skarv
sources.title: Offshore oil and gas industry embraces robotic technology | Offshore
sources.claim: Mobile robots working on live oil and gas installations are inspection platforms: Boston Dynamics' Spot ran missions on Aker BP's Skarv installation collecting images, scans and readings, not delivering equipment or assisting crews.

tasks.label: Clean up spilled oil by bailing it into barrels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small crude/produced-fluid spill at a wellhead or pumping unit on a lease pad: a leaking stuffing box or valve has pooled oil on gravel and soil. Roustabout scoops/bails free oil with buckets and a hand bailer into a 55-gal drum, spreads and collects absorbent pads, shovels stained gravel, seals and labels the drum. Outdoors, remote lease, weather, uneven natural terrain, layout differs site to site.

Spill contained inside a tank battery's lined secondary containment berm: oil from an overflowing or leaking tank/pump pooled on the graded, bermed pad of an operator-controlled facility. Worker bails pooled oil with buckets/hand pump into barrels, works around tank legs, piping and valves, wipes down equipment and stages drums for pickup.

Off-location release from a flowline or tank truck onto pasture, a bar ditch, or a creek crossing: pooled oil sits on soil, vegetation or standing water. Worker walks/kneels on rough ground, bails pooled oil and oily water into barrels, deploys sorbent booms and pads, hauls full drums out over soft ground.

Oil released during equipment work at a workover/servicing site: fluid caught in drip pans and puddled on mats and muddy ground when connections are broken or a pump/vessel is drained. Worker bails pan and puddle contents into barrels between other rig-site jobs, amid congested moving equipment and crew.

Spill on the concrete floor of a facility building (pump house, compressor building, gas-plant skid area, or maintenance shop): oil pooled around a leaking seal or a tipped container. Worker squeegees and bails the oil into a drum, applies absorbent, cleans the floor, stages the drum in the waste area. Indoors, fixed layout, institution-controlled.

sources.system: Re-Gen Robotics no-man-entry tank cleaning robot
sources.title: Tank Cleaning Service : Re-Gen Robotics
sources.claim: Commercial 'no-man entry' hydrocarbon tank/sump cleaning robots that recover crude sludge into vacuum tankers are remotely operated by an operator in a control room, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Closest industrial analog to bailing spilled crude into containers (recovering liquid/sludge hydrocarbons into a receiving vessel); cited to show the state of the art in this material class is teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Remote controlled tank/pit cleaning dozers and robots
sources.title: Rise of the Robots: Tank Cleaning Dozers and Robots - Oil and Gas Innovation
sources.claim: Sludge and oily-residue removal from pits and tanks in the oil industry is performed by remote-controlled dozers/robots craned into the pit or driven in through a manway.
sources.transferJustification: Pit/tank sludge recovery is the nearest task to bailing pooled oil into containers; the evidence shows human operators drive these machines continuously, so the capability does not transfer as autonomous work.

sources.title: Engineers create robot to clean up oil spills - Have a Go News
sources.claim: Robotic oil-spill recovery devices demonstrated to date are small marine skimmers operating on water surfaces, at prototype scale and remote-controlled.
sources.transferJustification: Same substance (spilled oil) but recovery from open water by a filter minibot; cited to show oil-recovery robotics is water-surface skimming at prototype scale, not scooping pooled oil from ground into barrels.

sources.title: An Autonomous Oil Skimming Robot for Crude Oil Spills | SPE Nigeria Annual International Conference and Exhibition
sources.claim: An autonomous crude-oil skimming robot exists only as a boat-mounted research prototype for spills on water, using oleophilic separation rather than bailing into containers.
sources.transferJustification: Same substance and purpose (recovering spilled crude), but the demonstrated environment is a water surface and the output is separated oil aboard a boat, not pooled oil bailed from ground or containment into labelled barrels.

sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Robots deployed autonomously at oil and gas facilities today perform sensing and inspection routes, not cleanup or liquid handling.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the ceiling of autonomous robot work in this industry's own facilities: navigation and inspection payloads, with no demonstrated recovery of spilled liquids into containers.

sources.title: Robots to the Rescue | Cleaning & Maintenance Management
sources.claim: Autonomous cleaning robots in commercial use are water-based floor scrubbers/sweepers for smooth indoor floors of structured facilities; they recover wash water into an onboard tank and do not containerize recovered hydrocarbons.
sources.transferJustification: Related task of autonomous liquid pickup from floors; cited to show the demonstrated capability is detergent/water on smooth indoor floors, not bailing viscous crude and transferring it into drums for disposal.

tasks.label: Dig drainage ditches around wells and storage tanks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cutting a new perimeter drainage ditch in open ground at a producing well pad or tank battery: rural lease, native soil/gravel, a rubber-tire backhoe or mini-excavator on the gang truck, ditch line staked or pointed out by the foreman, no buried lines in the dig corridor, weather and uneven terrain as found.

Ditching and re-grading drainage inside an established, fenced production facility (central tank battery / CTB) with a graded gravel pad, standard tank and berm layout, controlled access and posted work permits; open ground between the firewall berm and the fence line is worked with a small excavator or skid steer.

Hand-shovel work: digging shallow drainage cuts tight around the wellhead cellar, tank bottoms and skirts, valve sets and pump jack bases, and by hand over or beside buried flowlines and electrical conduit where a machine cannot be used without risking a strike; includes hand finishing and spoil cleanup.

Re-opening silted-in, overgrown or storm-damaged ditches around wells and tanks after heavy rain: standing water, soft mud, brush and grass, washed-in debris, culverts and driveway crossings on a remote lease with rutted access.

Ditch work in a congested existing facility where lines must be located first: potholing, digging around and between buried flowlines, gas lines and power runs and existing piping supports, cutting the ditch in short careful passes with hand cleanup at each crossing.

sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofit turns a standard excavator into a fully autonomous trenching machine that digs to a specified line and depth with 0.1 ft accuracy; sold as a commercial product for buried infrastructure work on energy jobsites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is cable/utility trenching. Transfer to digging drainage ditches around wells and tanks: same machine (excavator bucket in native soil), same output (an excavated channel cut to a planned line, depth and grade, with spoil placed alongside), same outdoor unimproved worksite; drainage ditches are shallower and looser-toleranced than the 0.1 ft trench accuracy demonstrated.

sources.title: Built Robotics raises $64 million for robotic excavator Exosystem | Equipment World
sources.claim: The Exosystem excavator digs inside an operator-set geofence from an uploaded dig plan specifying depth and grade, and executes the excavation with nobody in the cab.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: a dig plan with depth/grade uploaded to the machine is exactly how a graded drainage ditch would be specified; the geofence handles keep-out zones such as tanks and located buried lines in open ground.

sources.title: Building the Future of Construction — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built's autonomous trenching robots have cut more than 100 miles of trench on ... construction projects in the US and Australia, with over 50,000 hours of operation across the robot fleet.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes sustained field production of autonomous excavation on as-found outdoor energy jobsites, the same class of open ground a lease-site drainage ditch is cut in.

sources.system: Built Robotics robot fleet (incl. trenching excavators)
sources.title: Blattner and Built Robotics Announce Contract to Improve Safety in Solar Construction
sources.claim: Blattner (Quanta Services) contracted to deploy dozens of Built ... robots on US solar projects for pile driving, surveying, material handling, ...; Built states its robots have already worked five Blattner projects delivering an accepted work product.
sources.transferJustification: Confirms commercial acceptance of autonomous excavation output by a contractor on real jobsites, supporting the 'worker quality' element for trench/ditch excavation.

sources.system: Bedrock Operator autonomy platform on excavators
sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Deploys Industry's Largest Supervised Autonomous Excavator Test | Equipment World
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics and Sundt Construction ran supervised-autonomy excavators on a 130-acre facility site in Phoenix, moving over 65,000 cubic yards of material with retrofit LiDAR/GPS/camera autonomy racks on 20-80 ton excavators.
sources.transferJustification: Bulk earthmoving on an outdoor construction site; supervision level is not established (described as 'supervised autonomy'), so it is treated as corroborating context only, not as a basis for a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Cut down and remove trees and brush to clear drill sites, to reduce fire hazards, and to make way for roads to sites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Seasonal brush-hog/rotary-cutter pass (tractor or skid steer) over an established well location, tank battery or compressor yard and its graveled perimeter, knocking down grass, weeds and light woody regrowth to keep fire load away from wellheads, tanks and flowlines. Gated, operator-controlled lease with a fixed equipment layout on mostly drivable ground.

Brush-cutting pass along lease access roads, turnarounds and flowline/pipeline rights-of-way to keep them open and reduce fire hazard: grass, weeds and woody regrowth on native ground with ruts, culverts, cattle guards, rock and livestock, outside any maintained pad.

Hand vegetation work with weed-eater, machete and small chainsaw tight around wellheads, pumping units, separators, tank stairs, meter runs, guy wires and fence lines where a mower or tractor cannot reach.

Chainsaw felling of trees and cutting of heavy brush to open or widen a drill site: dropping stems, limbing, bucking, dragging and piling slash, and burning or hauling debris off the location. Wooded, sloped, sometimes wet ground taken as found.
Clearing timber and brush along the route of a new access road to a site, working ahead of or alongside a dozer: felling trees in the corridor, cutting brush, and stacking or burning the debris.

Removing hazard or storm-downed trees leaning over lease roads, fences, flowlines, tank batteries or power lines: precision felling/limbing near infrastructure, then cutting up and hauling off the wood.

sources.system: Swap Robotics solar vegetation cutting robot
sources.title: Solar Vegetation | Swap Robotics
sources.claim: Swap Robotics' electric vegetation-cutting robots run pre-mapped cutting routes autonomously at utility-scale solar sites, supervised only by a remote guardian — the same rough-cut vegetation control done on outdoor energy-facility ground.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is vegetation/brush cutting for fire-load and access control at a large outdoor industrial energy facility; the objects (grass, weeds, woody regrowth), the machine (self-propelled rotary/flail deck) and the ground (gravel/graded industrial site with fixed equipment obstacles) match a well pad or tank battery mow.

sources.title: Swap Robotics secures $7m to ramp up solar cutting operations
sources.claim: The Swap robots are built for variable terrain and their cutting decks handle thick grass and woody stems up to two inches in ... — the brush class a roustabout knocks down with a brush hog.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the vegetation size the deployed robot actually cuts (woody brush up to 2 in.), which is the vegetation class in routine pad and lease-road brush control.

sources.title: About Us - Renu Robotics
sources.claim: Renu Robotics sells and operates electric autonomous mowers doing vegetation management at utility-scale energy facilities for customers in 20 states, with a recharge pod and remote mission-control oversight.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above: recurring mechanical vegetation control across large fenced outdoor energy-industry sites with fixed equipment obstacles, at commercial scale and reliability.

sources.title: SOLV Energy partners with Swap Robotics to tackle thick vegetation on solar sites
sources.claim: A major utility-scale solar builder (SOLV Energy) adopted Swap's autonomous vegetation management for thick vegetation on its sites, with pre-mapping then autonomous cutting under remote oversight.
sources.transferJustification: Confirms real customer deployment (not a demo) of autonomous brush/grass cutting on institution-controlled industrial energy sites, the E2 analogue of a well pad or lease-road mow.

sources.title: The Future of Mowing | RC Mowers
sources.claim: RC Mowers' Autonomous Mowing Robots drive recorded paths and avoid obstacles on their own and are in commercial use by landscape contractors, showing autonomous rough-cut mowing on human-managed grounds.
sources.transferJustification: Second, independent line of evidence that taught-path autonomous cutting of grass/light brush on maintained but non-fenced grounds is a fielded commercial capability, supporting the pad and lease-road mowing instances.

sources.system: Green Climber / MDB TF forestry mulcher
sources.title: Radio-controlled forestry mulcher - Green Climber - MDB Srl
sources.claim: Heavy brush, sapling and small-tree clearing machinery in the field (forestry mulchers on tracked carriers) is remote-controlled by an on-site operator, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the tree/heavy-brush clearing task; documents that the fielded state of the art for this work is continuous teleoperation, which cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Kodama Systems teleoperation/automation platform for forestry machines
sources.title: Kodama Systems uses robotics to prevent wildfires - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Forest thinning automation in the woods is teleoperation-based: Kodama ran a teleoperated platform on a national-forest thinning project, with only skidding of bundles along skid trails done autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Closest fielded analogue to felling and removing trees/brush for fuel and site clearing; felling and machine control remain human-in-the-loop, so the instance is not completed autonomously anywhere.

sources.title: The World's First Drone Tree Harvest in a Real Forest - AirForestry
sources.claim: Autonomous tree felling is at single-tree demonstration stage: AirForestry harvested trees in a real stand and separately ran a fully autonomous fell-delimb-carry sequence on a test field.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant (mechanized felling and removal of standing trees), but the autonomous sequence was a single-tree test-field demonstration, far short of clearing a site of trees, brush and slash at worker throughput and quality.

roles.title: Helpers--Extraction Workers
aliases: Bottom Hole Pressure Recording Operator Helper
Horizontal Earth Boring Machine Operator Helper
roles.description: Help extraction craft workers, such as earth drillers, blasters and explosives workers, derrick operators, and mining machine operators, by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include supplying equipment or cleaning work area.

tasks.label: Observe and monitor equipment operation during the extraction process to detect any problems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Oil and gas land drilling or well-servicing rig: floorhand/lease-hand helper watches mud pumps, shale shakers, mud tanks, engines, hydraulic hoses, drawworks and hoisting gear while the well is being drilled or worked over; listens for abnormal noise, watches pressure gauges, spots leaks, overheating and vibration, and alerts the driller. Operator-controlled pad with standard rig equipment, 24/7, outdoor, noisy and muddy.

Surface mine or quarry: helper monitors a blasthole drill rig on the bench and/or the crushing-screening plant, conveyors, dust systems and pumps during production; watches for belt misalignment, overheating bearings, blocked chutes, hydraulic leaks and abnormal machine sounds. Institution-controlled premises with fixed plant and haul roads.

Underground coal or hard-rock mine: helper monitors continuous miner, roof bolter, shuttle car, conveyor drives, pumps and ventilation equipment during production in dust, low light and confined entries; watches for cable damage, hydraulic leaks, hot bearings, belt slippage and machine stalls.

Water-well, geothermal or construction foundation/earth drilling at an as-found site (residential yard, farm, roadside, building site): helper watches the mast, cathead, mud pump, air compressor, hoses and cuttings returns while holes are drilled; site layout differs every job, no fixed infrastructure, small crew.

Blasting/explosives crew: helper monitors the bulk explosives pump truck, hoses, augers, pumps and loading equipment while boreholes are loaded on a quarry or mine bench; watches flow, pressure and hose condition and signals the blaster when something goes wrong.

sources.title: ANYmal Helps Vale to Prioritize People in Mining - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYmal legged robot performs fully autonomous inspection rounds at Vale's Cauê iron ore mining/processing facility, checking belts, levers, electrical panels, gauges and thermal condition of milling machinery to verify proper functioning of operating equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Same task content as the helper's: observing operating extraction/processing machinery (belts, mills, pumps, gauges) during production to detect developing problems; objects, precision (gauge/thermal/acoustic reading) and industrial mining environment match.

sources.title: New tricks: the evolution of quadruped robots in mining - Mine, Issue 154
sources.claim: ANYmal is used to inspect active conveyor belts in mining, identifying faulty belt sections, pulleys and rollers before failure; quadrupeds are also reported in use for inspections at Glencore's Kidd Creek underground mine.
sources.transferJustification: Monitoring running mine equipment for incipient faults is the same detection task the helper performs; the robot works alongside live machinery in an operating mine.

sources.system: Spot with CAM+IR and MUVE C360 gas sensor, Enhanced Autonomy Payload
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas Leaks | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: A midstream gas plant deployed Spot for autonomous inspection rounds over a 40-acre facility — anomaly detection, thermal inspection and gauge reading around compressor stations — during which the robot detected a combustible gas plume from a pinhole leak and shut itself down.
sources.transferJustification: Oil-and-gas equipment watching: same objects (pumps/compressors, gauges, piping, hoses), same purpose (detect leaks, overheating, abnormal readings during operation) as the well-site helper's monitoring duty.

sources.title: Mariana Minerals and Boston Dynamics Announce Deployment of Spot® at U.S. Copper Mine
sources.claim: Spot is being deployed at Mariana Minerals' operating Copper One mine and refinery in Utah as an autonomous mobile sensing node that continuously captures thermal, acoustic and visual data to detect overheating equipment, gas or fluid leaks, and to read analog gauges.
sources.transferJustification: Continuous monitoring of operating mine equipment for overheating and leaks at a US mine site is the same detection task, on the same class of extraction machinery.

sources.title: ANYmal Robots Inspecting PETRONAS' Offshore Platform - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYmal X, an Ex-proof legged inspection robot, was run on PETRONAS' offshore platform Dulang B for multi-week autonomous inspection deployments in adverse oilfield conditions, following a commercial agreement to scale deployments across upstream and downstream facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous routine inspection of oil and gas production equipment (rotating machinery, valves, gauges) in wet, windy, slippery hydrocarbon facilities matches the well-site helper's equipment-watching duty and conditions.

sources.system: Pit Viper autonomous blasthole drill rigs (AutoDrill / Rig Control System)
sources.title: Epiroc's Pit Viper is at 25 years including a decade of autonomous ops - International Mining
sources.claim: Epiroc Pit Viper surface blasthole drill rigs have run autonomously for a decade, drilling patterns unmanned with fleets supervised remotely from control centres rather than from on-bench cabins; BHP ordered autonomous rigs supervised from a remote operations centre 1,100 km away.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the drilling machine executes and self-monitors the extraction process, with automated fault handling and remote supervision replacing the on-bench helper who watches the rig for problems; same equipment and same mine-bench environment.

sources.title: FlexRobotics hits the Permian: H&P's robotic rig makes its field debut
sources.claim: H&P's FlexRobotics package placed robotic arms performing pipe-handling on the floor of an active land drilling rig in the Permian Basin in its first commercial use, showing robotic hardware working inside an operating land-rig environment.
sources.transferJustification: Context only (autonomy not established): shows the land rig floor is a machine-workable, standardized industrial setting, supporting the E2 classification of the well-site instance.

sources.title: Automated Construction Site Documentation | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot can be stationed on a construction site with a dock and run programmed Autowalk missions autonomously to document site progress, traversing obstacles, standing water and changing conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the E3 judgment: the demonstrated unstructured-site work is scheduled reality-capture scanning from a fixed dock, not fault monitoring of a running drill rig at an ad hoc site, so it does not substantiate the task at E3.

tasks.label: Drive moving equipment to transport materials and parts to excavation sites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Oil & gas drilling/well-servicing helper (roustabout/floorhand helper): drives a pickup, flatbed or winch truck from the yard or staging area over gated, unpaved lease roads to the rig on the well pad, hauling drill pipe, tools, sacked mud, water, fuel and spare parts; unloading is by truck crane, forklift or the rig crew; day and night, dust, rough graded surfaces, other lease traffic.

Surface mine or quarry helper: drives a haul truck, loader, or flatbed/service truck along maintained pit haul roads and benches to bring drill steel, casing, bits, blasting supplies, fill or aggregate to the drill/blast bench or active dig face; mixed traffic with manned dozers, water trucks and light vehicles; site controlled by the mine operator with traffic rules and access control.

Underground mine helper (coal or hardrock): drives a supply/utility vehicle, shuttle car or LHD from the shaft bottom or portal through ramps and drifts to the working section, carrying roof bolts, timbers, ventilation tubing, pipe, rock dust and machine parts; confined tunnels, uneven floor, low light, crews working at the face.

Construction, water-well, geotechnical or foundation-drilling jobsite helper: drives a flatbed truck, skid steer or rough-terrain forklift on a residential lot, roadside, farm field or urban site to move casing, drill rods, gravel, grout, tanks and tools from the road or a staging spot to the rig; layout differs at every site, soft or sloped ground, public traffic and bystanders nearby.

Run between the shop/supply house and the site: drives a pickup with trailer or a flatbed on public rural roads and highways to pick up parts, pipe or consumables and deliver them onto the excavation site, including securing the load and the last leg off the public road onto the pad or pit.

sources.system: Kodiak Driver (Kodiak AI) driverless trucks operated by Atlas Energy Solutions
sources.developer: Kodiak AI (Kodiak Robotics) / Atlas Energy Solutions
sources.title: Inside Kodiak's Autonomous Trucking Operation in the Permian Basin Field Report
sources.claim: Kodiak Driver-powered Class 8 trucks owned by Atlas Energy Solutions run with no human in the ... Dune Express terminal over Permian Basin lease roads to changing well sites; 28 driverless trucks and 15,600 cumulative loads as of Q1 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hauling proppant to oilfield well sites. It is the same act as the helper's — driving a loaded heavy truck over unpaved lease roads from a staging point to an active drilling/completion site — with comparable vehicle class, route conditions and destination.

sources.title: Kodiak, Atlas scale autonomous truck deployment on private road network
sources.claim: Atlas/Kodiak driverless trucks hauled over 100 loads of ... by January 2025; fleet later expanded to 24/7 driverless service.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: commercial driverless transport of bulk material to oilfield sites over private industrial road networks.

sources.system: Cat MineStar Command for hauling on Cat 777 trucks
sources.title: Caterpillar | Scaling a Proven Autonomy System to Support New Industries
sources.claim: Autonomous Cat 777 trucks running Cat MineStar Command for hauling operate in a producing aggregates quarry (Luck Stone Bull Run, Virginia), hauling over 2 million tons in the first year with no reported safety injuries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous haulage of material between loading points and the plant inside a working quarry. It shares the driving, pit-road navigation, spotting and mixed-traffic interaction that transporting supplies to a dig or drill bench requires.

sources.title: Heidelberg Materials North America Achieves Milestone with Autonomous Haul Trucks at Lake Bridgeport Quarry
sources.claim: A mixed OEM fleet running Pronto's Autonomous Haulage System moved more than two million tons ... from pit to crusher at Heidelberg Materials' Lake Bridgeport Quarry in Texas over eight months.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous truck haulage on quarry pit roads. The driving, route-following and spotting skills are those needed to move materials to a bench or drill site in the same facility.

sources.system: Sandvik AutoMine (Toro LH517i loaders, Toro TH663i trucks)
sources.developer: Sandvik Mining and Rock Solutions / Glencore
sources.title: Glencore adds automated Sandvik trucks to the operating mix at George Fisher
sources.claim: At Glencore's George Fisher underground zinc mine, ten AutoMine-equipped Toro loaders and three automated Toro TH663i trucks tram and dump autonomously around the clock on separate ... (operators intervene remotely for loading).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous tramming of loaded haulage machines through mine ramps and drifts. Transporting supplies underground uses the same vehicles, tunnels and navigation; only the payload differs.

sources.system: Sandvik AutoMine Core / Access Control System (ACS)
