sources.title: AutoMine® Core
sources.claim: Sandvik's AutoMine underground automation isolates the autonomous working area with an access control system and safety barriers, splitting the mine into flexible safety zones so manual and automated equipment work in separate areas.

sources.system: Seegrid Palion / Lift RS1 autonomous mobile robots
sources.title: Seegrid Lift RS1 AMR Wins Material Handling's Products of the Year Readers' Choice Award 2025
sources.claim: Seegrid autonomous lift trucks and tow ... move palletized materials to designated drop zones in customer manufacturing, warehousing and logistics facilities, with over 18 million autonomous ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving powered industrial trucks to move discrete palletized materials and parts to a specified delivery point in a facility, which is the delivery half of the helper's transport task when it occurs inside a structured facility.

sources.title: Aurora Begins Commercial Driverless Trucking in Texas, Ushering in a New Era of Freight
sources.claim: Aurora runs commercial driverless Class 8 trucks with no human on board on Texas public highways (Dallas–Houston from May 2025, Fort Worth–El Paso from October 2025), but operations are terminal-to-terminal on fixed freight lanes.

tasks.label: Unload materials, devices, and machine parts, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Drilling site (oil/gas, water well, foundation): helper unloads drill pipe, casing, collars, bits and tool baskets from flatbed trucks onto pipe racks — releases binders/straps with bars and wrenches, hooks slings, hand-signals the picker truck or forklift, spots and chocks the load. Outdoor lease pad, rough/muddy ground, weather, layout differs at every well.

Rig-site consumables: helper unloads sacks of drilling mud, cement and lost-circulation material, cases of chemicals, small parts and hand tools from a delivery truck, cuts banding, carries/stacks them in the mud house or conex on site.

Surface mine or quarry: helper unloads machine parts and supplies (drill steel and bits, hoses, idlers, crated pump/gearbox components) from a service truck at the pit or laydown yard — rigs chains and slings, guides loader or crane, pries open crates and unbolts shipping brackets with hand tools on uneven ground.

Underground mine: helper unloads supplies (rock bolts, resin, rock-dust bags, ventilation tubing, pipe, replacement machine parts) from supply cars, scoops or flatbeds at underground stations and section faces, using bars, cutters and wrenches in a low, wet, confined heading.

Blasting crew: helper unloads cased explosives, boosters, detonators and bagged ANFO/emulsion from a magazine or powder truck at a surface bench or underground face, hand-carries and counts cases, stages them near loaded holes under non-sparking handling rules.

Company yard, maintenance shop or mine warehouse: helper receives palletized/boxed deliveries at a dock or shop bay — unloads pallets and cartons with forklift or pallet jack, cuts bands with a knife, breaks down loads and stages parts on racks. Fixed layout, controlled premises, standard pallets.

sources.system: Canrig PDH-3500 / Canrig Robotics automated tubular handling
sources.title: Custom Automation Solutions - Canrig
sources.claim: Canrig's PDH-3500 is an electric autonomous tubular handling ... delivers them hands-free — heavy long-goods handling from a fixtured presentation on a drilling rig.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving tubulars and subs between racked/magazine storage and the well center. It transfers because the objects (drill pipe, casing, BHAs), the weights, and the pick-and-place precision are those of the helper's pipe-unloading work, but only when the tubulars are presented in fixtured magazines.

sources.system: Canrig Red Zone Robotics (RZR) Rig Floor Module, rig X29
sources.title: Nabors Marks Major Industry Milestone: Fully Automates Existing Land Rig with First-of-its-Kind Robotics Module

tasks.label: Set up and adjust equipment used to excavate geological materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open-pit metal mine or aggregate quarry, blasthole drilling crew: helper helps set the rotary/DTH drill over surveyed collar marks on the bench, sets and levels the jacks, raises and aligns the mast, adds and pulls drill pipe or rods, changes tricone/hammer bits, hooks up dust collection and water, and adjusts feed, rotation and air as ground changes. Dust, weather, mobile equipment traffic; MSHA-controlled site.

Underground hard-rock mine: helper sets up a development jumbo, longhole production rig or bolter at the face - trams it into position, sets stabilizing jacks, aligns booms to the drill plan, loads rods into the carousel, swaps bits and shanks, connects air and water, adjusts percussion/feed for the rock. Confined wet drift, uneven floor, mine-controlled access.

Land oil, gas or geothermal drilling rig: floorhand-helper sets up and adjusts drill-floor equipment - handling and making up drill pipe, collars and casing, setting slips, positioning tongs/iron roughneck, hooking up and adjusting pipe-handling and mud-circulation gear during drilling and tripping. Contractor-controlled pad with standard rig layout.

Drilling-and-blasting or foundation-drilling contractor at a road cut or building excavation: helper walks the crawler drill onto a sloped, rubble-strewn bench taken as found, levels it, sets mast angle for the designed hole, fits steels and bits, connects hoses, and checks hole positions against paint marks. Other trades and public traffic nearby.

Excavation/utility crew at an as-found street or lot: helper sets up and adjusts the ancillary gear used to dig - swapping excavator buckets, augers and breakers with hydraulic lines, setting trench shields and shoring, positioning compressors, air hoses and pneumatic tools, dewatering pumps, and grade lasers/stakes for the excavator operator.

Water-well, geothermal-loop or geotechnical/exploration coring rig at a scattered site (farm yard, roadside, remote claim): helper cribs and levels the rig on soft or sloping ground, lays out and makes up drill rods and casing, rigs the mud pump, tanks and water lines, changes bits, and adjusts mud and feed as the hole advances.

tasks.label: Organize materials to prepare for use.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Oil & gas land drilling rig: helper organizes tubulars for use — pipe, collars and casing pulled from the pipe racks, doped, run up the catwalk and racked in the derrick/fingerboard ready for the string; 12-hour tours, day and night, all weather, contractor-controlled location.

Same well location, non-tubular materials: staging pallets and loose sacks of barite/bentonite/cement in the mud house, coiling and laying out hoses, sorting subs, bits, hand tools, spare parts, rig mats and drums scattered around the pad so the crew can grab them for the next operation.

Surface mine/quarry blasthole drill: keeping the drill in consumables during the shift — loading drill pipe into the rig's pipe rack/carousel, changing worn tricone or DTH bits, having the next bit, sub and hammer ready at the bench.

Blasting crew at a quarry, surface mine or construction shot: unloading explosives, boosters and detonators from the magazine truck, distributing cartridges and primers along the drilled pattern, making up primers, staging stemming material — on rough as-blasted ground, under regulatory handling rules.

Construction, geotechnical or water-well drilling helper at job sites that differ every time (road cut, building foundation, farm well, utility bore): unloading the truck and laying out drill rods and casing, bits, hoses, sacks of bentonite/grout, tremie pipe and hand tools around the rig on uneven ground, often with traffic or the public nearby.

Underground mine: moving and staging section supplies — roof bolts, resin cartridges, plates, ventilation tubing, pipe, timber, rock dust — from the shaft/portal store along ramps and entries to the working section supply point, and keeping that supply point in order.

tasks.label: Repair and maintain automotive and drilling equipment, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine preventive service on rig equipment at the well pad, quarry or mine bench: greasing fittings on the mast/rotary head/pumps, checking and topping fluids, draining oil and swapping filters on rig engines, air compressors and generators, changing hydraulic filters and cleaning components — outdoors on uneven ground in mud, dust, heat or cold with wrenches, grease guns and filter wrenches.

Replacing wear consumables on the drilling string/tooling at the rig: breaking out and making up a worn tricone or button bit, drill rods/steel, subs and stabilizers, changing hammer parts, using bit breakers, sledges, chain tongs and pipe wrenches on the rig deck in the field.

Fixing a breakdown in the field under time pressure: burst hydraulic hose or leaking fitting, mud-pump valve/seat, liner or packing change, broken belt, seized bearing, damaged air line, cracked bracket — diagnosing the fault on an as-found machine, freeing rusted or seized fasteners and installing the replacement with hand tools.

Servicing and repairing the crew's support vehicles and light trucks at the site or company yard: engine oil and filter changes, battery, lights, air filters, brake and suspension checks and minor mechanical repairs with hand tools, often parked outdoors on gravel with a jack and stands.

Changing or repairing a wheel/tire on a pickup, water truck or trailer used at the site: breaking loose lug nuts, jacking the vehicle, removing the wheel, mounting the replacement tire and torquing the nuts.

Bench work in the company maintenance shop or yard: tearing down, cleaning, inspecting and reassembling components brought in from the field (mud pump fluid ends, swivels, hydraulic cylinders, drill heads, gearboxes), replacing seals, bearings and packing with hand tools under a mechanic's direction.

sources.claim: Scott Automation's ROBOFUEL uses a vision-guided robotic arm to autonomously couple a nozzle and refuel mining haul trucks at unmanned fuel bays, in use at several mine sites including with an autonomous Komatsu 930E ...; it performs fuelling only, not lubrication, filter or repair work.

sources.claim: Trade coverage of remanufacturing automation reports that robotic disassembly of used machinery is only beginning to emerge and that seized bolts, deformed parts and ... remain major obstacles outside controlled, uniform-input environments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: teardown and rebuild of used mechanical assemblies, the core of shop-bench overhaul work; the source documents that this is not completed autonomously even in fixtured industrial cells.

tasks.label: Clean up work areas and remove debris after extraction activities are complete.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Underground metal/nonmetal mine: after a production blast, clear the blasted rock and debris out of the heading/drawpoint area with a loader (LHD) and tram it to the ore pass or dump point so the working place is clear for the next cycle; wet, dusty, uneven rock floor, ventilated drift, access-controlled level.

Underground mine detail cleanup: shovel spilled muck at loading points, chutes and conveyor transfer stations; clear ditches and sumps; pick up scrap timber, used shot wire, empty powder boxes, drill steels, hose and cable ends; hose down dust and wash equipment; carry debris to a skip. Uneven rock floor, restricted headroom, mixed heterogeneous objects.

Surface mine, quarry or sand-and-gravel pit: after blasting and loading, clean up the bench, loading area and plant surrounds - shovel loose rock and spillage from around the crusher, conveyors and stockpile feeders, clear rock off haul roads and equipment pads, pick up trash, banding, drill cuttings and scrap steel and load it into a truck or bin; outdoor, weather-exposed, mine-controlled site.

Oil and gas well pad / drilling or workover rig: after drilling, completion or rig-down, wash down the rig floor and equipment, shovel spilled drilling mud, cuttings and sand, clean mud tanks and catwalk, coil hoses and lines, gather pipe dope buckets, rags, banding and scrap, pick up trash across the pad and load debris into bins; muddy, oily, congested pad controlled by the operator.

Remote or roadside work: construction/road blasting shots, seismic and exploration drill sites, small pits - collect drill cuttings and core boxes, retrieve blasting mats, shot wire and stemming bags, clear rock debris and mud off the roadway or access track, pick up trash and restore the site; layout differs at every site, public traffic and natural terrain, no institution keeping the site to a standard.

sources.title: Sandvik introduces AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 for improved autonomous bucket loading
sources.claim: Sandvik's AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 gives underground LHD loaders fully automated production cycles, including autonomous bucket filling at fixed drawpoints, removing the need for operator intervention during mucking.
sources.transferJustification: Mucking is the removal of blasted rock (debris) from the working place after extraction: same material, same objective and same underground setting as the helper's post-blast clean-up of a heading.

sources.title: ZenRobotics 4.0 brings new smarts to automated garbage-picking - New Atlas
sources.claim: ZenRobotics Heavy Picker robots autonomously identify and pick heavy, heterogeneous construction and demolition debris (rock, wood, metal) off a conveyor into separate fractions in fenced sorting cells.

This is the E1 rendering of 'remove debris' - the same object classes and weights as extraction-site debris, with the work brought to the machine.

sources.title: Avidbots releases floor-scrubbing robot for industrial spaces - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Avidbots Neo autonomous floor-scrubbing robots clean industrial work-area floors that have floor debris and changing layouts, with over a thousand robots deployed commercially.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cleaning the floor of an industrial work area. Substantiates the surface-cleaning half of 'clean up work areas' on hard flat floors inside structured facilities and machine cells, but not on broken rock, mud or congested rig decks.

sources.title: Industrial Vehicle Washing Systems - Manual & Robotic Solutions
sources.claim: InterClean robotic vehicle wash systems clean mining haul trucks and heavy equipment in a purpose-built wash bay with no personnel present in the bay.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing down mud- and dust-covered extraction equipment. It is the E1 rendering of the wash-down component - equipment is driven into a fixtured bay and cleaned under machine control.

sources.title: WeRide Inc. - Form 6-K - FY2025 (SEC filing)
sources.claim: WeRide operates commercially deployed autonomous street sweepers ('robosweepers') on public streets in several cities, including a commercial sanitation deployment in Singapore.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous removal of loose litter and dust from paved surfaces in unstructured public settings. It bounds what is achievable at E3 - fine litter on pavement only, not rock rubble, blasting mats, hoses or mud.

tasks.label: Clean and prepare sites for excavation or boring.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Oil & gas well site: helper clears and levels the drilling location and keeps it clean — raking/shoveling spilled drilling mud and cuttings around the wellhead and cellar, moving hoses, cables and pallets, picking up trash and scrap, spreading gravel/mats, pressure-washing equipment. Rural pad, mud, weather, uneven ground, crew and trucks moving around.

Civil boring sites (water-well, geothermal, foundation/caisson, horizontal directional drilling in streets): helper clears brush, rocks and obstructions from the rig setup spot, lays timber mats/plywood, stakes and marks hole locations and utility lines, sweeps pavement and cleans up drilling fluid and spoil afterwards. Layout differs at every site; public traffic nearby.

Surface mine/quarry bench prep for blast-hole drilling: helper clears loose rock, broken drill steel and debris off the bench and access, cleans out hole collars and stemming spill, helps stake/flag the pattern, and hoses or waters down dust before the drill moves in. As-found muckpile and bench surface, dust, heavy equipment traffic.

Underground mine working area: helper clears broken rock and spillage from the heading and around loaders, conveyors and drill jumbos, bars down small loose, moves hoses, vent tubing and cables out of the way, and cleans up the face area before the next drilling round. Confined, wet, dark, irregular ground.

Drilling rig work platform: helper cleans the rig floor, cellar, mud tanks/shakers and pipe racks — shoveling cuttings, washing down mud, wiping and stowing tools and hoses — so the next boring operations can proceed. Standard rig layout controlled by the drilling contractor, but cluttered, greasy, grated surfaces.

sources.title: A⁴CSEL for DAM | Technology & Services | KAJIMA CORPORATION
sources.claim: Kajima's A4CSEL system runs automated bulldozers, vibratory rollers and dump trucks that spread and compact embankment material around the clock inside a construction area that people are barred from entering — an automated, person-excluded earthwork zone carved out of a real dam site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated bulk earthwork (spreading, dozing, compacting) is the same class of ground-clearing and leveling action used to prepare a drilling or excavation location, on comparable bulk material, and it is performed inside a purpose-built exclusion zone, i.e. an E1 presentation of a work site.

sources.claim: Built Robotics' autonomous excavator kits have been used by major contractors to trench and to drive foundation piles on utility-scale solar construction sites.

sources.title: $7.5M Series A Fuels Civ Robotics' Global Expansion of Construction Automation
sources.claim: CivDot robots autonomously mark surveyed coordinate points (pile, fence and boring locations) on utility-scale construction sites, used by contractors including Bechtel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: staking/marking hole and pile locations is one component of preparing a site for boring; it is performed autonomously outdoors, but covers only layout marking, not clearing or cleaning.

sources.title: Sandvik AutoMine Autoload 2.0 eliminates operator intervention in LHD drawpoint loading - International Mining
sources.claim: Sandvik's AutoMine AutoLoad 2.0 lets underground loaders complete fully automated production cycles — approaching the muckpile, filling the bucket and hauling — at fixed drawpoints and dump points.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing broken rock from a working area is the bulk-material half of cleaning a mine site for the next drilling round; it is autonomous only where the muck is presented at a fixed, surveyed drawpoint inside an access-controlled automation area.

sources.title: How Sandvik's AutoMine Aura Boosts Productivity 15% | Mining Digital

sources.title: Advanced robotics enable revolution on the rig floor - Drilling Contractor

sources.title: C&D Waste | Sorting Bulky Waste | ZenRobotics
sources.claim: ZenRobotics Heavy Picker robots autonomously identify and pick bulky construction and demolition debris — rock, wood, metal — from a sorting conveyor in recycling facilities.

tasks.label: Load materials into well holes or into equipment, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Surface metal mine or quarry bench: helper works a drilled blast pattern — dips holes with a tape, lowers primed boosters/detonators, guides the bulk emulsion/ANFO delivery hose into each 4–10 in hole, then fills the collar with stemming gravel by hand or chute; dozens to hundreds of holes per shift, outdoors in dust and heat near highwalls.

Oil & gas or large-diameter drilling rig, mud-mixing area: helper moves 50–100 lb sacks of barite, bentonite, polymer or lost-circulation material off pallets, slits them with a knife and dumps them into the mud hopper/mixing tank per the mud engineer's recipe; cramped, muddy pit area, all weather, standard rig equipment.

Water-well, geotechnical or foundation drilling site: after casing is set the helper shovels/pours gravel pack, bentonite chips and bagged grout or cement into the annulus and into the grout-pump mixer hopper, handling the tremie hose, on an uncontrolled site (residential yard, roadside, farm field).

Construction or small-scale blasting job (road cut, trench, building lot): helper hand-loads cartridge explosives or bagged ANFO into 2–3.5 in holes, tamps with a wooden pole, seats primers and stems the collar, on irregular broken terrain adjacent to public roads and property.

Underground mine or tunnel development/production face: helper charges face holes with cartridge or pumped emulsion using loading poles and charging hose, inserting a primer with detonator into each hole, in a freshly blasted heading with water, muck and unsupported ground.

sources.claim: ABB Robot Charger, mounted on a carrier vehicle with a second arm that assembles primer and detonator, locates drilled holes in an underground rock face with vision and charges them with the cycle fully automated; tested at Boliden's Garpenberg production mine with LKAB.

sources.claim: Enaex UG-iTruck performed a 100% remote, robotic and autonomous ... operation in a production underground mine: a robotic arm measures and cleans each drillhole, assembles boosters and detonators, positions itself and loads emulsion at the development face.

tasks.label: Provide assistance to extraction craft workers, such as earth drillers and derrick operators.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Floorhand/helper on a land oil-and-gas drilling or workover rig assists the driller and derrickhand through connections and trips: pulling and setting slips, latching tongs and spinner, handling the mud bucket, doping and stabbing pipe, guiding tubulars from the catwalk to the rotary, racking stands. Steel drill pipe and casing, mud and dope, noise, weather, 12-hour tours on a standard rig floor whose layout and equipment repeat well to well.

Lease/well-pad helper working around the rig and location: rigging up and down, spotting and chaining equipment, hooking up suction and discharge hoses, cutting and mixing mud sacks and chemicals, cleaning mud tanks and shale shakers, washing down the rig, shoveling and hauling debris, running tools out to the crew. Uneven graded pad, mud, weather, layout differing site to site.

Driller's helper on a water-well, geotechnical, foundation/anchor or mineral-exploration rig at scattered sites (rural lots, farms, roadsides, construction sites, remote exploration pads): breaking out and handing up rods/casing, wrenching tool joints, tending the mud pump and mixing pit, dragging water and air hoses, catching and bagging cuttings/core, cribbing and leveling, cleaning the site afterward. Two- or three-person crew, no fixed layout, site taken as found.

Helper to blasthole drillers and blasters at a surface mine or quarry: moving air/water lines and cables for the drill, fetching and changing bits and drill steel, staking and cleaning hole collars, carrying and lowering primers/boosters and det cord, holding the loading hose while the charge truck pumps, stemming holes, clearing the bench. Uneven blasted rock, dust, weather, bench layout changing with each shot.

Helper underground to continuous-miner, jumbo, bolter and charge crews: hauling and staging bolts, resin, mesh, timbers, powder and rock dust to the working place, extending ventilation tubing/curtain and water and air lines, dragging trailing cable, shoveling spillage along belts and at the face, assisting operators with bit and steel changes and with charging a round. Confined, wet, low-light headings that change shape and location every shift.

Shop, warehouse and staging work at the company yard between field jobs: pulling and kitting tools, bits, fittings and consumables for the crews, moving totes and boxes and staging them for loading, sweeping and scrubbing the shop floor and keeping the work area clean. Indoor, level floor, fixed racking and layout, employer controls who and what is on the premises.

tasks.label: Collect and examine geological matter, using hand tools and testing devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Land oil/gas drilling rig: helper/sample catcher takes drill-cuttings samples at the shale shaker at set depth intervals, washes and sieves them, bags and labels sample sets, and examines cuttings with hand lens/microscope and UV for shows; also draws mud samples for property checks. Noisy, greasy, 24-hour operation on a leased, access-controlled wellpad.

Water-well, geotechnical or environmental drilling: helper works beside the driller at varied sites (roadsides, building lots, farm fields, remote tracks), catching auger cuttings and split-spoon/core samples as they come out of the hole, jarring and labelling them, and field-screening (visual/manual soil classification, moisture, PID headspace) before delivery to a lab.

Reverse-circulation grade-control or exploration drilling: helper mans the cyclone and rig splitter, catches and bags a sample every 1-2 m of advance, tags and stacks bags in rows, sieves a fraction into chip trays for the geologist, and keeps the sampling train clean, on an open-pit bench or a bush exploration pad in dust, heat and rain.

Mine or quarry production sampling: helper collects grab/channel samples from the working face, muck piles, blasthole cuttings cones, stockpiles, truck loads or a conveyor belt using shovel, pick, hammer and sample bags; splits and labels them and may run quick checks (moisture, handheld XRF, dust/gas monitor) at the point of collection.

On-site sample preparation shed or mine/quarry QC lab: helper receives bagged field samples, dries and weighs them, runs the jaw crusher, riffle/rotary splitter and pulveriser, cleans between samples, and runs routine tests (sieve/gradation, moisture, specific gravity, benchtop XRF) and logs results.

Diamond drill core handling and logging support: helper pulls core from the split tube at the rig, lays it in trays in order, marks depth blocks, washes core, photographs trays, and assists with marking and cutting sample intervals in a core shed at the camp or mine site.

sources.title: Scott | Rocklabs AMS Prep Line
sources.claim: Rocklabs (Scott Technology) AMS Prep Line is running as a fully automated on-site sample preparation laboratory at Mineral Resources' Ken's Bore facility (Onslow Iron), crushing, splitting, pulverising and dispensing drill samples for analysis.
sources.transferJustification: Same task material and tests as the helper's sample-prep and testing work (bagged rock/ore samples, crushing, splitting, dispensing for XRF/TGA); used here for the E1 counterfactual where samples are presented to the machine.

sources.title: How Automation is Revolutionising Mining Operations at Onslow Iron
sources.claim: The Ken's Bore automated laboratory uses collaborative robotic arms through the crushing, pulverising and dispensing workflow and loads pulps into vials/crucibles for TGA and XRF analysis, running ~16 samples/hour and doubling daily capacity to ~500 samples.
sources.transferJustification: Covers both halves of the task - subsampling geological matter and examining it with testing devices (XRF, TGA) - on the same materials the helper handles; cited for instances where the work is presented to a purpose-built cell.

tasks.label: Dismantle extracting and boring equipment used for excavation, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Oil/gas or deep water-well drilling rig: helper/floorhand trips out and lays down the drill string at end of hole or for a bit change — breaking tool joints with tongs/iron roughneck, racking or laying down pipe and collars, breaking off the bit. Muddy but standard rig floor, contractor-controlled lease.

Surface mine or quarry blasthole drill on the bench: helper breaks the worn tricone bit or DTH hammer off the drill string, unthreads and removes drill pipe/rods from the string into the carousel or pipe rack, using hand tools, wrenches and the rig's breakout wrench.

Water-well, geotechnical, foundation or mineral-exploration rig at a field jobsite: helper breaks down the rod/auger string as it comes out of the hole — pipe wrenches and breakout table on each joint, pulling core barrel or bit, racking rods on the rod truck. Dirt, mud, weather, site taken as found.

End-of-job rig-down and teardown for transport: disconnecting hydraulic/air lines and hoses, unbolting outriggers, mast/tower sections, drive head, dust collector or cyclone; dismantling an auger boring machine in a bore pit or an HDD rig on a street; breaking down the mud system and loading components on a trailer. Varied outdoor sites.

Underground mine: helper dismantles jumbo drills, longhole rigs or roof bolters for repair or a section move — removing drill steels, chucks and booms, breaking down conveyor sections and loader components with hand tools in a confined, wet, low-clearance heading.

Company shop/yard: teardown of recovered boring tooling — DTH hammers, tricone and drag bits, auger heads, subs, mud pump fluid ends — with hand tools, sledges, impact wrenches and a breakout bench, for cleaning, inspection and rebuild.

tasks.label: Dig trenches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hand-digging with shovel, pick and mattock immediately around an active rig, pump, tank or mud system: drainage cuts, sumps, small ditches to divert water, short trenches to seat a hose or line. Irregular shapes, tight quarters among hoses, guy lines, skids and a working crew; wet, rutted, sometimes frozen or rocky ground.

Careful digging by hand around existing buried pipes, flowlines, cables and conduit (potholing, tie-in pits), plus hand-trimming and squaring the bottom, ends and sidewalls of a machine-cut trench to grade before pipe or cable is laid. Damage to a live line is unacceptable.

Shallow trenching/burial of geophone cable, shot wire, ground rods or small conduit along survey or shot lines crossing brush, rock, timber or pasture; hand tools or a walk-behind trencher packed in on foot; ground taken as found, no design data.

Cutting a linear trench in open ground on a lease, well pad, right-of-way or exploration site with a mini-excavator, backhoe or trencher: flowline, water line, power/comm conduit or a perimeter drainage ditch, dug to a set depth and width with spoil windrowed alongside, over tens to hundreds of feet.

Digging a drainage or pipe trench inside a quarry/mine plant yard or industrial pad operated by the employer: access-controlled, graded and maintained working surface, known utility layout, machine and hand work combined.

sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofit converts a mid-size excavator into a fully autonomous trenching machine that digs to 0.1 ft accuracy at up to 180 ft/hour on rugged greenfield sites and self-surveys the finished trench.

sources.title: Building the Future of Construction — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' autonomous trenching machines have cut more than 100 miles of trench on ... in the US and Australia, i.e. real field production, not a demo.

sources.claim: Kawasaki's Autonomous Excavation System planned and executed trench excavation autonomously from 3D design data and LiDAR terrain sensing, including levelling the trench floor, in company verification testing.

tasks.label: Inspect, test, and measure completed work, using devices such as hand tools or gauges to verify conformance to standards or repair requirements.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dealership or independent automotive/light-truck service shop: the shop foreman or service manager checks a completed repair order before delivery — verifies lug-nut torque with a torque wrench, checks fluid levels and for leaks under hood and underbody, measures brake pad/rotor thickness and tire tread, reviews alignment readings and scan-tool results, and road-tests the vehicle. Vehicles and repair types vary widely across the day.

Manufacturing plant, utility, or large building complex: a maintenance supervisor verifies a completed repair on installed machinery in place — checks shaft/belt alignment with dial indicator or laser tool, verifies fastener torque and guard reinstallation, takes vibration/temperature readings, pressure- or leak-tests piping, and runs a functional check before releasing the equipment to production.

Customer premises (residential HVAC/plumbing/appliance, telecom or cable installs, small-business security or elevator work): the field supervisor inspects a crew's completed installation or repair on site — manifold gauge readings and static pressure, signal-level meter readings, torque and mounting checks, code/standard conformance — in homes and small buildings of varying layout, clutter, and access.

Airline or MRO hangar: a lead/inspector-supervisor verifies completed maintenance on an aircraft — torque and safety-wire checks on reinstalled components, borescope of an engine after repair, dimensional and NDT check of a composite or sheet-metal patch, operational check of the system, then records sign-off to the maintenance manual.

Bench/component rebuild shop (engine or transmission remanufacturing, hydraulic component shop, motor rewind shop, electronics repair bench): the supervisor measures rebuilt components with micrometers, bore gauges, and comparators against tolerance, and runs the assembled unit on a test stand to confirm it meets specification before shipment.

Outdoor field or yard on heavy equipment (construction site, mine, rail yard, marine dock, farm dealer's lot): the supervisor inspects a completed field repair on a machine in place — hydraulic pressure readings, track/undercarriage wear measurements, weld and fastener inspection — under weather, dirt, and uncontrolled layout.

sources.transferJustification: Related task is production/near-line dimensional quality inspection rather than post-repair inspection, but the act is identical — gauging a finished workpiece against a dimensional standard and issuing an accept/reject decision — on the same class of metal and composite parts a rebuild-shop supervisor gauges with micrometers.

sources.title: 3D Infotech Unveils AI-Driven Inspection System Pioneering Adaptive Manufacturing
sources.claim: Robotic metrology inspection cells of this type are widely fielded, with over 350 systems installed, primarily in aerospace and automotive.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: fielded dimensional conformance verification of finished aerospace/automotive parts, which is the measurement step a supervisor performs on rebuilt components.

sources.transferJustification: Related task is end-of-line verification of a newly assembled vehicle rather than a repaired one; the measured quantity (toe/camber versus OEM spec) and the object (a complete vehicle presented on a stand) are the same ones a shop foreman checks after suspension or alignment work.

tasks.label: Inspect and monitor work areas, examine tools and equipment, and provide employee safety training to prevent, detect, and correct unsafe conditions or violations of procedures and safety rules.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shift/daily walkthrough of an active repair shop or maintenance bay (auto dealership, fleet garage, plant maintenance shop): supervisor watches technicians working on lifts, benches and machines, spots unsafe practices (missing eye protection, improper jack-stand or lift use, misused power tools, bypassed guarding), stops the work, coaches and corrects the technician on the spot, and follows up.

Scheduled documented safety inspection round of the shop/plant work areas: checklist walk covering housekeeping, oil/coolant spills, blocked aisles and exits, machine guarding, signage, fire extinguishers and eyewash stations in place, leaking or overheating equipment; findings logged and corrective work orders issued.

Hands-on examination of tools and equipment: picking up and testing hand and power tools, cords and grinders, ladders, jack stands, floor jacks, hoists, slings, chains and fall-arrest harnesses, torque tools; judging wear and damage, tagging out and pulling defective items from service, recording the inspection.

Delivering employee safety training: toolbox talks and new-hire orientation, hands-on demonstration of lockout/tagout, respirator fit, lift/hoist operation and safe lifting technique, answering questions and verifying each technician's competency before signing them off.

Unattended hazard-documentation walk of a large outdoor/field job site where installer or repair crews work (construction, utility or industrial project): covering the site to record conditions and surface hazards such as openings, drop-offs, debris and slippery surfaces for the daily safety report.

Field safety visit to a customer premises or job site with the crew present (HVAC, telecom, elevator, line work): verifying fall protection, ladder setup, traffic control, lockout/tagout and permits with the crew, questioning workers, correcting violations and stopping unsafe work.

sources.title: Spot at Cargill | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped, with the Orbit AI visual-inspection feature, runs programmed autonomous routes multiple times a day through Cargill's Amsterdam Multiseed oilseed crush and refinery plant performing visual safety checks — seed/oil spills that create slip hazards, emergency doors propped open, safety signage, 5S boards and fire extinguishers in place — and flags findings to plant staff.
sources.transferJustification: Direct: this is a routine documented walk of a human work area to detect unsafe conditions (spills, blocked/propped exits, missing safety equipment), the same detection output a supervisor's area safety round produces; it does not cover handling tools or interacting with workers.

sources.title: Quadruped robot boosts safety and maintenance at aging cement plant
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal quadruped has been in service at Vigier Ciment's Péry cement plant since early 2025, autonomously running nightly routes over 450 checkpoints across six levels and ..., detecting structural defects, overheating bearings, gas leaks and ammonia exposure without human supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous plant inspection rounds) transfers to the condition half of this task: same industrial work areas, same walk-the-route-and-flag-anomalies output, including safety-relevant findings such as leaks, overheating and gas exposure.

sources.system: Spot with FieldAI Field Foundation Models
sources.title: Case Study: Practical Autonomy on Construction Sites | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: FieldAI's Field Foundation Models running on Boston Dynamics Spot are deployed daily on active construction sites in Asia, Europe and North America, navigating with no prior maps or pre-planned routes and completing missions without frequent resets, and surface safety-related site observations including holes, drop-offs, PPE compliance, active ... and slippery surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous job-walk site documentation) transfers to the supervisor's site hazard-observation walk: same unstructured, changing job site, same output of recorded hazard observations delivered to the project team; it does not cover instructing or correcting crews.

tasks.label: Interpret specifications, blueprints, or job orders to construct templates and lay out reference points for workers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial/institutional building install job (new build or major fit-out): the mechanical/electrical install supervisor takes coordinated drawings and lays out reference lines and points on the slab or deck for the rough-in crew — equipment pads, hanger and attachment points, sleeve and penetration locations, rack centerlines — on an active site with other trades, debris and changing conditions.

Operating industrial plant or facility: supervisor of industrial machinery mechanics interprets equipment drawings and lays out reference points on the plant floor and foundation for installing or relocating a machine — baseplate outline, anchor-bolt centers, conveyor/line centerlines — in a cleared area of a facility the employer controls.

Fabrication or repair shop: supervisor reads a blueprint or spec and constructs a physical template (cardboard, sheet metal, plywood pattern) for a duct fitting, bracket, guard or obsolete replacement part, then marks layout lines and punch/center marks on stock so the fabricator can cut and drill.

Vehicle, aircraft or machine component work: supervisor interprets a job order or OEM spec sheet and marks reference points on the unit or a part — drill locations for an upfit bracket, hole pattern, alignment/index marks — sometimes producing a reusable drill template for repeated jobs, in a fleet or repair shop bay.

Customer premises field service (occupied home, small commercial, rooftop): supervisor walks the site with a job order and lays out mounting and reference points on walls, roof, ground or existing equipment for an install — mini-split brackets, condenser or generator pad, antenna/service mount, appliance clearances — with no model of the building, furniture and obstructions in place.

sources.title: Mechanical Contractor Solutions | Dusty Robotics

tasks.label: Perform skilled repair or maintenance operations, using equipment such as hand or power tools, hydraulic presses or shears, or welding equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Vehicle/mobile-equipment service shop: the shop foreman takes a job off the board that his technicians are struggling with — diagnoses a driveability, brake, suspension, hydraulic or electrical fault on a used car, truck, bus or piece of heavy equipment in a lift bay, disassembles the affected assembly with hand and power tools, replaces components, reassembles and road-tests. Corroded fasteners, varied model layouts, and a same-day turnaround commitment.

Field service call at a customer location (private home, small business, roadside, pole/tower, customer's plant): the supervisor rides out on a difficult HVAC, appliance, elevator, telecom or utility-equipment call, troubleshoots the installed equipment in place with hand tools, meters and cordless power tools, and repairs or replaces the failed part in a space taken as found.

Repair of installed machinery or building systems inside the employer's own facility (factory floor, hospital, transit garage, school district plant): supervisor works alongside the crew to replace a worn conveyor bearing and drive, rebuild a pump or valve in place, or swap a motor/gearbox during a scheduled outage, using hand and power tools, rigging and portable equipment.

Shop metal fabrication and weld repair: supervisor cuts stock on a shear or saw, forms it on a press brake, and MIG/TIG or stick welds a cracked bracket, wear plate, guard, frame member or exhaust/duct component, then grinds and finishes the repaired part in the maintenance/fab shop.

Bench overhaul work using the shop hydraulic press: supervisor presses worn bearings, bushings, pins, gears or U-joints out of a hub, axle, wheelset or linkage and presses new ones in to spec, with cleaning, measurement and press-fit control in the shop.

Aviation/precision MRO structural work in a hangar or depot: supervising mechanic performs hands-on structural repair — drilling out rivets and defastening a cracked skin panel, match-drilling and fastening the replacement, using pneumatic drills and precision measurement to airworthiness standards.

sources.system: Path Robotics AW-3 / AF-1 autonomous welding cells

sources.claim: Path Robotics' AW-3 and AF-1 robotic welding cells autonomously scan, fit up and weld steel parts and are in commercial use in fabrication shops in the US and Canada; the AF-1 picks, fits and welds without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production/low-volume fabrication welding rather than repair welding. Transfer holds for the weld-repair instance because the workpieces (steel weldments, brackets, frames), the joint-finding-by-vision requirement, and the fixtured shop cell are the same as for weld-repairing a cracked steel part.

sources.title: Path Robotics Launches Rove, Bringing Mobility to Welding Automation Powered by Physical AI
sources.claim: Path Robotics launched Rove, a mobile (quadruped-mounted) version of its autonomous welding AI intended to weld large immovable assemblies in shipyards and heavy industry; a shipbuilder is an early adopter evaluating it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: field welding of large structures. Cited only to show that autonomous welding outside a fixed cell is still at early-adopter evaluation stage, so deployed autonomy remains cell-based.

sources.title: Revolutionising industrial repair - CSIRO
sources.claim: CSIRO's Continuous3D gives an industrial robot arm carrying a welding torch, metal-spray or laser-cladding head the ability to scan a damaged metal component, decide where repair is needed and generate the repair tool path itself, without per-job programming; demonstrated on engine blocks and complex castings.

instances.label: Automotive / truck / fleet repair shop: supervisor walks the service bays on a daily or weekly round, checking lifts, hoists, jacks, air compressors, tire and alignment machines for leaks, damage or overdue PM, and checking housekeeping and safety conditions (oil spills, clutter in walkways, blocked exits, extinguishers, lighting), logging what needs repair or cleanup. Vehicles, techs and tool carts move through the space during the round.

Parts room / stockroom monitoring: supervisor reviews shelved and binned stock (filters, fluids, belts, fasteners, common replacement parts) against the shop management or CMMS system, spot-counts levels, identifies short, missing or damaged stock, and flags reorders so techs are not held up mid-job.

Tool room / tool crib control: supervisor checks that issued tools are accounted for and returned, counts consumable tooling (bits, blades, abrasives, PPE), notes broken tools and calibration due dates, and orders replacements. Common in industrial maintenance and aviation MRO tool-control programs.

Industrial maintenance shop inside a plant: supervisor makes rounds of the maintenance shop and adjoining equipment areas, checking shop machines (welders, lathes, presses, hoists and cranes), utility conditions (compressed air, lighting, ventilation) and safety equipment (eyewash, guards, extinguishers), then raises work orders for anything deficient.

Field / mobile operation (HVAC, telecom, elevator, appliance, mobile fleet service): supervisor checks stock and condition of service vans and trucks, job-site tool trailers and customer-site staging areas, verifying each vehicle carries adequate parts and serviceable tools; settings vary site to site and are not controlled by the employer.

Vehicle is in the service lane or on a lift; standard shop conditions.

Automotive/truck/fleet: supervisor verifies or performs diagnosis of a specific complaint (intermittent electrical fault, noise/vibration, no-start, warranty comeback) using road test, scan tool, partial teardown, plus review of the technician's findings and service history, to determine the repair and authorize it.

Manufacturing plant or institutional facility: maintenance supervisor makes routine rounds of production and building equipment (motors, pumps, gearboxes, compressors, gauges, air/steam leaks, thermal hot spots), reviews readings and CMMS/condition-monitoring data, and determines what preventive maintenance or repair is needed.

Plant/facility breakdown call: supervisor goes to a stopped machine or failed building system, opens guards and panels, checks hydraulics, drives, electrical and mechanical components by hand and with meters, and determines root cause, repair scope, parts, and labor.

Field service at customer premises (private homes, tenant spaces, small commercial buildings): HVAC/refrigeration, plumbing, electrical, appliance, elevator, or telecom install supervisor inspects the existing equipment and site conditions — attics, crawl spaces, closets, mechanical rooms — to diagnose the fault or scope and quote a new installation.

Outdoor infrastructure and equipment yards: utility/telecom/heavy-equipment supervisor inspects lines, poles, towers, tanks, wellsite equipment, substations, rooftop units, or parked machines in a yard to determine what repairs or installations are required.

instances.label: Scheduled/on-call service visit to a corporate office: drive a stocked van to the building, check in at reception, walk to the copy room, diagnose a multifunction copier fault (jams, streaking, error codes), open panels, clear jams, replace fuser/rollers/toner/drum, clean paper path, run test prints, reset counters, get customer sign-off.

ATM service call at a bank branch or a retail-sited ATM: diagnose card reader, dispenser, receipt printer or note-jam fault; open the fascia/chest, clear jammed notes, swap a dispenser or reader module, reload receipt paper, run test transactions, restore the machine to service and complete logs.

Retail store call for POS/computer equipment: work behind a counter or in a back room on a register PC, receipt printer, barcode scanner or cash drawer; unplug/replug cables, swap a terminal or internal component, reload drivers, verify a sale, all while the store is open and customers are present.

Call at a small independent business, professional practice, or home office taken as found: no fixed layout, machine crammed on a desk or in a closet with cluttered cabling, non-standard older equipment, pets/people around; diagnose and repair a PC, printer or fax on the spot.

Emergency/unplanned dispatch to a customer site with a hard-down machine and an unknown fault: triage across possibly several machines, improvise with parts on the van, decide repair-vs-swap-vs-depot, sometimes after hours, and communicate status to the customer.

Visit to a customer's server room or small data center: locate the flagged failed hot-swap disk in a standard 19-inch rack, pull the carrier, insert the replacement drive, confirm rebuild/inspection status, and document the swap.

tasks.label: Reassemble machines after making repairs or replacing parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench reassembly of a desktop PC or laptop at a repair shop/depot after a component swap (RAM, SSD, board, fan/heatsink, keyboard, battery): reseat modules, reconnect ribbon/flex and power cables, refit shields and covers, drive many small screws, then power-on test.

On-site reassembly of a multifunction copier/laser printer in a customer's office after replacing a fuser, drum, roller, or controller board: refit modules and drive gears, reroute and reconnect wiring harnesses, close and screw side/rear panels and doors, then run test prints and calibration.

Reassembly of an ATM or cash-handling kiosk in a bank branch, vestibule, or convenience store after replacing a card reader, dispenser, receipt printer, or display: reseat heavy modules on rails, reconnect harnesses in tight cabinets, secure fasteners, close and lock the top box/safe, then run diagnostics and a test transaction.

Reassembly of a small office machine or terminal at a retail or office site — POS terminal, receipt printer, check/document scanner, fax, label printer — after board, roller, or power-supply replacement: refit internal assembly, reconnect ribbon cables, snap/screw the housing back together, and verify operation.

Reassembly of rack-mounted server or network hardware in a server room/data center after a part swap: reseat DIMMs, drives, cards and fan modules, reconnect internal cables, refit the chassis lid, reinsert into rails and reconnect external cabling, then verify POST.

On-site reassembly of a home or home-office desktop/laptop at a residential customer's location after a part replacement, working on a kitchen table or desk with the customer's own space and lighting.

sources.system: HIL-SERL (human-in-the-loop sample-efficient RL) on Franka arm
sources.title: Precise and Dexterous Robotic Manipulation via Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Learning
sources.claim: A learned RL system on a Franka arm autonomously performs a computer motherboard assembly sequence — SSD installation, RAM insertion, grasping a free-floating USB cable and inserting it into a slot and a retaining clip — reaching 100% success with human intervention rate falling to zero, in a fixtured bench workcell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling components into a computer motherboard. It transfers to 'reassemble after repair' for PCs/servers because the objects (RAM, PCIe SSD, USB cable, connector clips), insertion forces and sub-millimetre alignment tolerances are exactly those a repairer handles when putting a serviced machine back together; the demo also ends with a functional power-on check.

sources.claim: An RL policy with force/vision conditioning autonomously performs precision PC-component assembly tasks: inserting a RAM card into its slot, mounting a heatsink on a motherboard, and fitting a fan onto the heatsink to form a ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precision assembly of PC internals. Heatsink/fan refitting and RAM seating are literally steps of reassembling a computer after a repair, performed on the same parts with the same tolerances, in a fixtured cell.

sources.claim: A commercially deployed collaborative-robot screwdriving cell (UR5e cobot with Robotiq Screwdriving Solution, integrated by Raruk/Vikaso) autonomously installs screws into the cover panel of an electronics enclosure at an electronics manufacturer.

sources.claim: Apple's Daisy line autonomously disassembles 23 iPhone models at 200 units per hour on a purpose-built disassembly line, separating components for recovery.

It shows industrial-reliability robotic handling of small device internals, but only in a purpose-built line, and only for disassembly — so it supports E1 for small-device work and nothing above it.

instances.label: Field service tech's van trunk stock: at the end of a route the tech opens the van's bin/tote system in a customer parking lot or home driveway, eyeballs and hand-counts what was consumed (fusers, rollers, toner, boards, card readers, cables), scans or keys used part numbers, and submits replenishment orders through the field-service portal so parts ship overnight.

Receiving inbound parts at the branch/depot stockroom: unboxing cartons and polybags, verifying items and quantities against the packing slip, labeling/bagging small parts, putting them away into labeled bins and shelves, and boxing defective cores/RMA returns with paperwork for pickup.

Periodic cycle count or annual physical inventory of the depot stockroom: walking the racks and bins, counting/scanning parts, and reconciling counts against the ERP/inventory system, investigating and adjusting discrepancies.

Picking and kitting parts from stockroom shelves for scheduled jobs (preventive-maintenance kits, an ATM dispenser swap, a copier fuser rebuild), staging them in totes with the work order, and relieving the stock in the system.

Desk procurement: identifying the correct part number from the machine model/serial and service documentation, checking min/max levels and vendor availability, placing purchase orders through supplier portals, and following up on backorders and warranty replacements.

Stocking consumables at customer premises: topping up the client copy-room supply closet or ATM consumables (toner, drums, staples, receipt/journal paper), checking on-hand levels on the customer's shelves, removing empties, and noting what to reorder.

sources.system: Corvus One Autonomous Inventory Management System
sources.title: LAPP USA Case Study: Corvus One Inventory Drones
sources.claim: Corvus One autonomous inventory drones fly unaided through a customer distribution center, producing pallet-level validation and discrepancy reporting that replaces manual cycle counting by warehouse associates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical inventory counting and reconciliation of stored goods. It transfers to a repairer's stockroom cycle count because the robot autonomously traverses racking built for people, reads location/part labels, counts stock, and reports discrepancies against the inventory record.

sources.title: Independent US grocer Harmons deploys Simbe Tally inventory robot across 17 of its locations
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally shelf-scanning robot autonomously audits item-level stock levels on shelves in grocery stores and reports availability gaps that drive replenishment, deployed across 17 stores.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf stock auditing in a human-built facility. It transfers to checking bin stock levels and flagging shortfalls for reorder, since Tally counts small packaged items on human shelving and outputs an out-of-stock/replenishment signal to the inventory system.

sources.title: Stow: Robotic Packing of Items into Fabric Pods (arXiv 2505.04572)
sources.claim: Amazon's Stow robot autonomously places a wide variety of individual items into fabric storage pod bins in production fulfillment-center workcells, at a rate and packing density comparable to human stowers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putaway/stocking of received goods into storage bins. Objects (small mixed retail items) and precision are comparable to binning small spare parts, and the output — items stored in the correct bin with the record updated — is the same.

sources.title: Amazon uses robots that sort, lift, and carry packages—see them in action
sources.claim: Amazon's Sequoia robotic containerized storage system identifies and stores inventory received at fulfillment centers, using mobile robots, gantries and robotic arms in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: receiving and putting away inbound stock. It transfers to depot receiving because the system identifies incoming items, allocates them to containers, and maintains the perpetual inventory record — the accepted output of stockroom putaway.

sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously unloads cartons from trailers and containers at warehouse loading docks and is in multi-site commercial deployment with DHL.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unloading inbound shipments at a receiving dock. It covers the carton-handling front end of stockroom receiving in a human-built facility, though not the unboxing, packing-slip verification and bin-level putaway.

sources.title: Staples deploys RightHand Robotics tech in its fulfillment centers
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick autonomous piece-picking arms are deployed across Staples' North American fulfillment centers, picking a wide range of office-product items in fixed robotic workcells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order picking of small heterogeneous items into totes. It transfers to picking/kitting spare parts for a work order: comparable object mix and precision, with the parts presented to the cell rather than fetched from human shelving.

sources.title: Autostore project — A Sustainable Year 2024-2025 (CNH Industrial)
sources.claim: CNH Industrial runs an AutoStore robotic grid in its spare-parts operation, where robots retrieve the bin holding the ordered part and deliver it to a station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: storing and retrieving small spare parts under a perpetual inventory record. It is the same class of work as maintaining a parts stockroom — stock kept in bins, located and retrieved on demand, with counts held by the system.

sources.title: AutoCrib Industrial Vending Solutions

tasks.label: Disassemble machines to examine parts, such as wires, gears, or bearings for wear or defects, using hand or power tools and measuring devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field teardown of a copier/MFP or production printer at a customer office, school, or print shop: pull covers and panels, extract the fuser, feed and transport assemblies, inspect rollers, drive gears, belts, bushings/bearings and wiring harnesses for wear, glazing, cracking or contamination with hand tools, feeler gauges and a meter; unknown machine condition, tight access, machine sitting where the customer installed it.

Bench teardown at a retail service counter or independent shop of consumer laptops, all-in-ones, tablets and small home printers: hundreds of model variants, adhesive and clip construction, hidden fasteners, ribbon/ZIF connectors, damage of unknown origin (liquid, drops, swollen batteries); open nondestructively, inspect fans, cables, connectors, hinges, boards for wear/defects, then reassemble.

Depot/refurbishment-line teardown of standardized business IT hardware (fleet desktops, standard-model laptops, rack servers, drives) at a repair depot, ITAD or refurb facility: strip known models to the module level, inspect and grade harvested parts as good/worn/defective, log results.

ATM field service teardown at a bank branch, retail location, or drive-up unit: pull and disassemble the cash dispenser, card reader, or receipt printer module, inspect drive belts, pick rollers, gears, clutches, sensors and wiring for wear, using hand tools and gauges, in the machine's installed position with cash-handling security constraints.

On-site teardown of business desktop PCs, workstations and thin clients at customer offices, schools and warehouses: open the chassis, remove PSU, drives, fans, cards, inspect for dust, failed fan bearings, bulging capacitors, chafed cables and burnt connectors, meter power rails, reassemble.

In-home/home-office teardown of a consumer PC or small office machine: work performed in a residence on a kitchen table or under a desk, machine of arbitrary model and condition, tools carried in, no controlled layout.

sources.system: Molg robotic Microfactory (with ABB robot arms)
sources.title: ABB Robotics and US start-up Molg tackle data center e-waste with robotic microfactories
sources.claim: Molg's robotic microfactory is stated by ABB to autonomously assemble and disassemble complex ..., in a purpose-built robotic cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-life disassembly for component recovery rather than diagnostic repair teardown. It transfers to depot teardown of standardized IT hardware because the objects (servers, laptops, drives), fasteners, connectors and required nondestructive care (parts must survive for reuse) are the same, and the parts must be judged good enough to harvest.

sources.system: MOLG robotic harvesting microfactory at Sims Lifecycle Services
sources.title: Looking Back and Looking Forward - Sims Lifecycle Services (2024 Year in Review)
sources.claim: A Molg robotic harvesting microfactory installed at an ITAD facility pulls servers from racks, disassembles them, harvests and sorts parts, performs an inventory audit, and reinstalls the chassis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: parts harvesting for reuse. Sorting harvested parts into reusable versus scrap is the same output as examining disassembled parts for wear or defects on a standardized-hardware depot line.

sources.title: Microsoft uses automated robots to disassemble and recycle HDDs
sources.claim: Microsoft's robotic hard-drive disassembly system uses computer vision to ... drive models, locate screws, take the drive apart and salvage reusable components; deployed as part of Microsoft Circular Centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: recycling teardown of drives. Transfers to depot teardown of computer hardware: same class of screwed precision assemblies, model recognition across dozens of variants, and selection of parts fit for reuse, all inside a fixed robotic cell.

sources.title: Apple Expanding Its Recycling Programs with Daisy, a New Disassembly Robot
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy line disassembles multiple iPhone models at high rate in a dedicated, purpose-built disassembly cell, identifying model, removing screws and separating modules.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-life device teardown. Shows that fully automated nondestructive teardown of consumer electronics works only for a closed, known set of models on a fixture-based line, which bounds what is credible for varied bench repair work.

sources.title: Appliance Manufacturer Uses Robots and AI to Disassemble Products
sources.claim: Panasonic has developed AI/machine-vision robotic workcells that dismantle used home appliances, detecting screws despite dirt or rust and removing fasteners with a robot-mounted screwdriver, at an R&D facility in Osaka.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: recycling dismantling of large electromechanical appliances. It is the nearest analogue to copier/ATM teardown, but it is an R&D separation line for materials recovery, not selective removal of a subassembly followed by wear judgment on gears and bearings.

sources.title: Graph-Based Adaptive Planning for Coordinated Dual-Arm Robotic Disassembly of Electronic Devices (eGRAP)
sources.claim: A dual-arm robotic system (eGRAP) autonomously disassembles 3.5-inch hard drives from several manufacturers using vision, adaptive graph planning and a screwdriver end-effector, in a laboratory cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: recycling teardown of drives. Supports adaptive, non-preprogrammed unscrewing and part removal on computer hardware in a fixtured cell, the disassembly half of depot teardown-and-inspect work.

sources.system: Machine vision system for gear defect detection (rotary-table inspection cell)
sources.developer: Ercetin et al., published in Processes (MDPI)
sources.title: A Machine Vision System for Gear Defect Detection
sources.claim: An automated machine-vision inspection station identifies gear defects including missing teeth, surface ... with over 98% accuracy and rejects faulty parts automatically on a production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production quality inspection of gears rather than wear assessment of used parts. It substantiates the 'examine parts for defects with measuring devices' half of the task inside a purpose-built cell, once parts are already removed and presented.

sources.system: OpenVLA / OpenVLA-OFT on UR5e for selective desktop disassembly
sources.title: Vision-Language-Action Models for Selective Robotic Disassembly: A Case Study on Critical Component Extraction from Desktops
sources.claim: Automating selective disassembly of components from end-of-life desktop PCs remains challenging; fine-tuned vision-language-action policies completed early steps but failed critical subtasks, needing a rule-based hybrid controller in a lab cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: selective teardown of desktop PCs. It bounds general-purpose capability on varied, unknown-condition machines and shows that where model variability is high, current systems fail without model-specific scripting.

Bench/depot repair in a service shop: desktop, laptop, printer or peripheral on a workbench; disassemble the case, unscrew and swap a mainboard, drive, screen, power supply or fan, reconnect ribbon/board connectors, reassemble and test.

Component-level board repair at a bench: desolder and replace capacitors, connectors, DC jacks or a BGA/SMD chip on a PCB with soldering/desoldering and hot-air equipment, then clean and inspect the joints.

ATM field service at a bank branch or retail site: replace a card reader, receipt printer, dispenser or note-transport module, swap worn rollers/belts, adjust and align the note path, working in a lobby or through-the-wall enclosure with the public nearby.

Data center / server room hardware replacement: pull and replace failed hard drives, SSDs, memory, power supplies, fans or network cards in standard racks, with tool-less carriers or a few screws, on a live aisle.
On-site residential or small-office repair: replace a power supply, drive, memory, keyboard or a printer part in a home office, under a desk, amid cables, furniture, pets and varied clutter.

tasks.label: Operate machines to test functioning of parts or mechanisms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Field call at a customer's office: after replacing a fuser, feed rollers or a finisher module in a copier/MFP, the tech puts the machine in service/diagnostic mode, loads paper, runs test-print and copy cycles, feeds originals through the document feeder, and inspects output for streaks, misregistration, skew or jams before releasing the machine.

Bench work in a shop or depot: a repaired desktop, laptop, tablet or handheld terminal is set up on the bench and run through diagnostic/burn-in software and physical exercise of touchscreen, keyboard, buttons, ports, camera and scan engine to confirm the repaired parts function.

ATM service at a bank branch, credit union or retail vestibule: after swapping a card reader, dispenser, deposit module or receipt printer, the tech puts the terminal in supervisor/test mode and runs test transactions - card in/out, PIN entry, note dispense and deposit cycles, receipt printing - checking each mechanism.

Component- or board-level testing on a shop bench: a suspect power supply, controller board or module is connected to a tester, fixture or test set (power-supply tester, board tester, meter/scope on a jig) and the test equipment is operated through its sequence to confirm which part or mechanism is faulty or repaired.

Residential or home-office service call: test a repaired home printer, all-in-one or PC in the customer's house - run self-test/print-test pages, cycle the paper feed, run hardware diagnostics amid household clutter and non-standard furniture.

Other office machines at customer sites (POS/receipt printers, mail folder-inserters, time clocks, shredders, check scanners): run the machine through its test cycle with media loaded and verify the mechanism feeds, prints or cuts correctly.

instances.label: Bench build of a desktop PC, workstation, or single server from kitted components in a repair shop, depot, or IT staging room: seat CPU and heatsink, press in DIMMs, mount drives and expansion cards and PSU, plug internal harnesses and front-panel leads, drive standoff/case screws to spec, close and label the chassis per the build sheet.

ATM or self-service kiosk assembly and installation at a bank branch or retail site: join safe and top-half enclosure, fit dispenser, card reader, receipt printer, screen and topper modules, anchor the unit to the floor, level it, and torque fasteners to specification.

Reassembly of a machine after repair or refurbishment on a shop bench: rebuild a laptop, printer, or ATM module around the replaced part, reseating flex cables and connectors, reinstalling shields and fasteners at specified torque, and checking clearances/alignment with gauges.

tasks.label: Install and configure new equipment, including operating software or peripheral equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Deploying new desktop PCs / laptop-dock workstations at user desks in a corporate, school or government office: unbox unit, monitors, dock, keyboard/mouse; place under or on a cluttered occupied desk; route and plug power, DisplayPort/HDMI, USB and Ethernet; power on, image or join the OS to the domain, map printers and verify with the user.

Installing and configuring a multifunction copier/printer/fax in an office print room: wheel in and level the machine, attach paper trays and finisher/stapler modules, load toner and staples, connect power and network, set IP and scan-to-folder settings, install drivers on the print server/clients, run calibration and test prints.

Installing new servers, switches, storage or network gear in an enterprise server room or data center: rack-mount the units on rails, run power cords and copper/fiber cabling, seat transceivers, label and dress cables, then apply firmware/BIOS and OS/network configuration.

Installing a new ATM or self-service kiosk at a bank branch or retail site: position the heavy machine, anchor it, connect power and communications, fit card reader/receipt/cash-dispenser modules and cassettes, load software and keys, run test transactions and commission the unit.

Installing peripheral equipment at retail, clinic or reception counters: POS terminals, barcode scanners, receipt printers, signature pads, scanners and monitors — mount or place the device, cable it to the host and power, load drivers and configure settings, test.

On-site install at a small business or residential customer premises (home office, unmanaged shopfront): set up a PC, printer or peripheral in a space taken as found, route cabling around furniture and existing wiring, configure Wi-Fi, drivers and accounts.

sources.title: Learning-augmented robotic automation for real-world manufacturing (arXiv:2604.22235)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: production-line cable insertion. Transfers to installing computing equipment because the decisive physical skill is the same — locating a port and mating a deformable cable/connector with sub-millimetre precision, at production reliability, on a workpiece presented in a fixture.

instances.label: Bench upgrade of a desktop PC or workstation in a repair shop, IT depot, or back-office staging area: open the case, add or swap DIMMs, install an SSD/NVMe drive or a PCIe expansion/graphics card, reassemble, power up and verify the upgrade is recognized. Varied chassis brands and layouts on a shared bench.

Upgrade of racked servers or network gear in a data center or server room: pull the unit, remove the lid and air shroud, add DIMMs, install NICs/HBAs/GPU or updated controller boards, reseat cabling, rerack and validate in a maintenance window. Hot aisle/cold aisle layout, live neighboring equipment.

Upgrade of a laptop, all-in-one, or thin client requiring disassembly: remove many small fasteners and a snap-fit cover, install SO-DIMM/M.2 memory or storage or an updated board, reassemble without damaging clips and ribbon cables, and boot-test. Done at a bench or deskside in an office.

Plug-in upgrade of an office machine at a customer site: adding a memory DIMM, hard drive, wireless/fax/interface option card, or finisher controller card into an accessible slot or bay on a copier/MFP or large printer, then confirming the option is recognized in the machine's configuration page.

Deep board replacement in an office machine in the field: removing outer panels of a copier/MFP, disconnecting multiple harness and FFC connectors, swapping a formatter/engine controller or scanner board, re-routing cables, reassembling and running test prints/scans. Cramped interiors, model-specific layouts.

Field upgrade of an ATM, kiosk, or POS terminal at a bank branch, retail store, or convenience store: opening the secured enclosure, swapping a card-reader module, dispenser or controller board, or adding memory, reconnecting harnesses, closing up, then calibrating and running a live transaction test.

tasks.label: Test new systems to ensure that they are in working order.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Newly installed multifunction copier/printer at a customer office, school or law firm: load paper in each tray, run test copies/prints (duplex, from each tray), test the document feeder, scan-to-email and fax, exercise the stapler/finisher, inspect printed output for streaks/registration, calibrate color, and confirm network printing from a workstation before customer sign-off.

Newly installed ATM or bank self-service terminal at a branch or retail site: load test cash, run test transactions (card insert, PIN entry, withdrawal, deposit/recycling), verify receipt printer, dispenser accuracy, screen flow, encryption key load and host/network connectivity before putting it in service.

Batch of new desktop PCs/workstations deployed at user desks in an office: connect monitor, dock, keyboard, mouse and network, power up, verify boot and POST, display, ports, peripherals, network/printer access, run vendor diagnostics and confirm the user can log in and work.

Bench/staging testing of new equipment at a service depot or configuration center before deployment: unbox, connect to a test bench, run diagnostic and burn-in suites, verify ports, drives, display and inputs, note failures, and repack the accepted units.

New POS terminals, self-checkout lanes or payment kiosks at a retail store: run test transactions with test cards, check barcode scanner, PIN pad, receipt printer, cash drawer and touchscreen, verify connection to the store server before go-live.

Field call to a home office or very small business: new PC/laptop and small printer set up in a cluttered, non-standard space; verify boot, peripherals, Wi-Fi/router connectivity and printing, then confirm with the customer that everything works.
