sources.system: Aerones robotic wind turbine maintenance platform
sources.title: How it works - Robotic Wind Turbine Care Systems | Aerones
sources.claim: Aerones' rope/winch robots are the most mature at-height robotic maintenance systems on tall structures (wind turbine towers and blades: inspection, cleaning, leading-edge repair), but each job is run by a crew of technicians who control and monitor the robots from the ground.
sources.transferJustification: Closest commercial analog to ascending a tall structure to service components at height; it shows such work is currently performed under continuous human control rather than autonomously.

sources.title: Skyline Robotics deploys Ozmo window cleaning robot in New York City - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Skyline Robotics' Ozmo performs autonomous robotic work at height on a 45-story building, but only on a planar glass facade served by the building's purpose-built maintenance unit - not ascent of tower steel or manipulation of mounted hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (facade work at height) cited to bound capability: it needs a building-maintenance-unit suspension and a flat surface, so it does not transfer to climbing tower steel and handling antennas, connectors and rigging.

sources.title: Multi-contact vertical ladder climbing with an HRP-2 humanoid | Autonomous Robots
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic climbing of vertical ladders exists only as laboratory humanoid research; no field system climbs communication tower structures carrying tools.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (vertical ladder ascent) is the core motion of a tower climb, but performance is limited to a controlled lab ladder without tools, wind or fall-protection transitions, so it does not carry over to tower work.

sources.system: Drone-based cell tower services (industry assessment, NATE/ETAK)
sources.title: Could drones replace tower climbers? - RCR Wireless News
sources.claim: Industry assessment of aerial systems at tower sites: drones collect imagery and can ferry small loads, but cannot perform the rigging, lamp-changing and hardware work that requires a worker physically at the component.
sources.transferJustification: Same task and setting: assesses whether aerial systems can substitute for the climb-and-work portion of tower technician jobs.

tasks.label: Climb communication towers to install, replace, or repair antennas or auxiliary equipment used to transmit and receive radio waves.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Carrier upgrade on a macro cell tower (lattice, monopole or guyed, 150-250 ft): climb with gear, rig a capstan hoist, remove old panel antennas/RRUs and mount new ones on sector frames, set azimuth and downtilt, torque U-bolts and mount hardware, land and weatherproof RF jumpers, secure jumpers to the mount. Outdoors, wind and temperature as found, legacy multi-tenant hardware on the steel.

Trouble-call climb on a macro tower after an alarm or storm: locate the fault at height (failed RRU, water-intruded or damaged jumper, cracked connector, loose or rotated mount), cut off weatherproofing, break corroded fasteners, swap the failed unit, re-plumb/re-azimuth the antenna and verify with a sweep. Condition of the hardware is unknown until the climber reaches it.

Rooftop, water-tank, steeple or 'stealth' site: climb a ladder/tank leg or work inside a fiberglass shroud or penthouse, install or replace an antenna and radio on a non-penetrating or pipe mount in confined space among other tenants' equipment and building obstructions.

Auxiliary equipment on the tower: run and clamp coax/hybrid cable with hangers up the leg, install waveguide bridges, tower-mounted amplifiers, grounding kits and lugs, replace obstruction lighting fixtures and wiring at height.

Tall broadcast/microwave structure (500-1,500 ft guyed or self-support): rig and install heavy antennas, transmission line sections or microwave dishes with a gin pole, bolt heavy steel mounts, align a dish to peak RF under RF-exposure lockout procedures.

Small cell / DAS node: short climb or bucket-truck ascent on a utility pole, streetlight or stub pole in the public right-of-way to mount a small-cell antenna and radio, bolt the bracket, and land fiber and power connections.

sources.system: GITAI Inchworm robots + Lunar Rover (with KDDI-specified antenna)
sources.developer: GITAI USA Inc. with KDDI Corporation
sources.title: GITAI Successfully Demonstrates Robotics Construction Capabilities for Lunar Communications Towers
sources.claim: GITAI's Lunar Rover and three Inchworm robots autonomously assembled a 5-meter communication tower in a desert analog site and attached a 3GPP mobile-network antenna to its apex, then connected power cables and later detached the antenna, using an antenna purpose-designed for robotic construction.
sources.transferJustification: Directly analogous to the task's core act: mounting a mobile-network antenna at the top of a tower structure and landing its cabling. Transfer is limited because the tower modules and antenna were engineered for robotic handling and staged for the robots, i.e. the work was built around the machine.

sources.title: Test and Measurement: Robots build a five-meter comms tower
sources.claim: Independent trade press confirms the same demonstration: the robots built the modular tower, connected the antenna at the tower top and connected power cables that energized the antenna; KDDI supplied base-station specifications so GITAI could develop an antenna suited to robotic construction.
sources.transferJustification: Same antenna-mounting-and-connection act as the rated task; corroborates autonomy and scope of the GITAI demonstration. Objects were robot-optimized, so it substantiates completion only where work is presented for the machine.

sources.system: ESTIC ERS series robotic fastening workcells
sources.title: New Tech for Robotic Fastening | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Preconfigured commercial robotic workcells install threaded fasteners automatically with monitored torque when parts are fixtured and presented, which is the fastening content of mounting an antenna bracket in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic threaded-fastener installation on fixtured workpieces in a fenced cell. Antenna mounting is bolted assembly (U-bolts/bracket hardware to specified torque) with comparable fastener sizes and positional tolerance, so performance carries over when the mount and antenna are fixtured as an E1 setting would present them.

sources.title: Smart Communications pilots robotic tech at cell tower sites in the Philippines
sources.claim: On real, in-service cell towers the current state of robotic intervention is a remote-controlled (teleoperated) arm that re-steers an already-installed antenna; it does not install, replace or repair antennas.

sources.title: Up the Tower: 2026 Trends to Watch - TowerClimber.com
sources.claim: In current tower-industry practice, unmanned systems on real towers are used for inspection and verification (pre-climb assessment, alignment checks, mount condition), not for performing the installation or repair work itself, which is still done by climbing crews.

tasks.label: Lift equipment into position, using cranes and rigging tools or equipment, such as gin poles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cell-site antenna / remote radio unit swap on a lattice tower or monopole: crew rigs the unit (30-200 lb) to a load line, a ground hand runs a capstan hoist, the load is raised 100-250 ft past existing appurtenances via a gin pole or tower-mounted block, and the climber catches, swings and positions it onto the mount pipe while tag lines control it in wind.

Mobile-crane lift at a tower site: crane sets a complete sector frame/top hat, a tower extension section, or a heavy microwave dish; riggers sling and shackle the load on the ground, signal the operator, and the tower crew guides it with tag lines into the mating position at height.

Rooftop/urban site: hoisting antennas, radios, coax/hybrid cable reels and small cabinets to a building roof using a davit, roof-mounted gin pole or crane, then moving and positioning them past parapets, penthouses, ducts and other carriers' legacy equipment onto sleds or mounts.

Ground-level heavy lift in the site compound: crane or boom truck sets equipment cabinets, a generator, battery cabinets, or a prefabricated equipment shelter onto the concrete pad; crew rigs the load, controls it with tag lines, and lands it on anchor bolts within tolerance.

Lift inside a controlled indoor facility: moving a heavy transmitter, amplifier, rack, or battery string into position in an equipment shelter, broadcast plant room, or in-building DAS/head-end room using a chain hoist, come-along, gantry or lift table.

Broadcast/tall guyed tower heavy hoist: gin pole (jumped up the tower) raising tower sections, large parabolic antennas, or rigid transmission line several hundred feet with a ground-mounted hoist, load line, blocks and tag lines.

sources.title: FANUC M-2000iA/2300 Robot - Ultra Heavy Payload Robot | FANUC America
sources.claim: Commercial ultra-heavy-payload industrial robot lifts and positions loads up to 2,300 kg, e.g. positioning an entire car body or loading bulky castings onto machine fixtures inside a fenced cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heavy material handling in a fenced cell. It is the same physical act as the instances' core - taking a heavy discrete unit and placing it in a defined position - at masses (0.9-2.3 t) exceeding tower antennas, cabinets and dishes, when the workpiece is fixtured and presented as at E1.

sources.system: KUKA KR 1000 titan (Mannstaedt steel profile handling)
sources.title: Handling robots automate the material handling tasks | KUKA Global
sources.claim: Six heavy-payload robots handle steel profiles weighing up to ... in a steel production plant, an installed production system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic pick-and-place of long, heavy steel members. Comparable mass and awkward geometry to tower sections, dishes and cabinets, and it demonstrates repeatable placement of heavy items when parts arrive in known positions (the E1 counterfactual).

sources.system: Morgan Automation unmanned overhead crane coil-yard system (Siemens controls), Arkansas steel mill
sources.date: July 2024 article; system in commercial operation
sources.title: US steel mill installs fully automated cranes system - Overhead Crane and Hoist
sources.claim: A fully automated, unmanned three-crane system in a US steel mill autonomously lifts ~28-ton hot coils and places them on transfer cars or floor saddles using grabs, laser positioning and thermal cameras.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unmanned crane hoisting and placing multi-ton loads. This is the crane-lifting element of the task performed under machine control, at far greater load than tower equipment, in a bay built around the crane with dedicated grabs and saddles (E1 presentation).

sources.system: Union Pacific autonomous wide-span cranes, Global IV terminal, Joliet IL
sources.title: Union Pacific Testing Autonomous Cranes That Operate Like High-Tech Robots | Union Pacific
sources.claim: Autonomous wide-span cranes at an intermodal rail terminal locate and lift containers and direct truck drivers, operating in a facility built for human work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous crane lifting in an E2 facility. It covers machine lifting only of standardized containers engaged by a dedicated spreader; it does not cover slinging, shackling and tag-lining non-standard telecom loads, so it does not carry over to these instances at E2.

sources.system: Obayashi Autonomous Crane with Skyjuster load control, Kawakami Dam project
sources.title: Report "Obayashi Automated Crane" | CIFE | Center for Integrated Facility Engineering
sources.claim: An AI/LiDAR-equipped autonomous crane was used on a real dam construction site, but a remote human operator retains the operator role and ground crews still rig and land the loads.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: crane lifting on an unstructured construction site. Autonomy is supervisory and rigging/landing stays manual, so it cannot support a positive E3 judgment for lifting equipment into position.

sources.system: Tower-industry drone inspection practice (no robotic installer)
sources.title: Up the Tower: 2026 Trends to Watch - TowerClimber.com
sources.claim: As of early 2026 the tower industry uses drones for inspection and documentation, while installation work at height still relies on climbing technicians with rigging competencies.

sources.system: Telecom tower maintenance climbing robots (research survey)
sources.developer: Shah & Dave, Nirma University (Journal of Field Robotics)
sources.title: A comprehensive review on deploying robotics application in telecom network tower's field maintenance
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed review of robotics for telecom tower field maintenance analyses feasibility and design requirements; climbing and grasping robots for tower work remain at research stage.

tasks.label: Perform maintenance or repair work on existing tower equipment, using hand or power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Tower-top antenna/RRU maintenance: climb a 60–300 ft lattice or monopole cell tower, unbolt and lower a failed panel antenna or remote radio unit, hoist and remount the replacement on the pipe/sector mount, torque mounting hardware to spec with hand and impact tools, reconnect RF/fiber/DC jumpers and verify. Outdoors, wind/temperature vary, mount configuration differs site to site.

Line and connector repairs at height: replace damaged coax/fiber jumpers and hybrid cable, reterminate or replace connectors, replace hoisting grips, hangers and grounding kits, cut away and reapply weatherproofing tape/boots on connectors, correct water-ingress and PIM faults found in sweep tests.

Structural and preventive maintenance at height: torque-check and replace corroded bolts on mounts, standoffs and step bolts, replace obstruction lighting fixtures/LED beacons and lamp cabling, tighten clamps and waveguide hangers, apply corrosion coating, adjust guy tension and safety-climb cable hardware on guyed and self-support towers.

Ground-level compound work inside the fenced cell site: repair or swap rectifier/BBU modules in outdoor cabinets or shelters, replace batteries and breakers, repair grounding/bonding, ice bridge and cable entry ports, service generators and HVAC, using hand and power tools. Gravel pad, standard cabinets, premises controlled by the tower owner.

Rooftop, façade and small-cell site maintenance: replace or repair small-cell radios and antennas on rooftop sleds, non-penetrating mounts or façade brackets, repair mounts, conduit and cabling, working around other tenants' equipment on varied urban rooftops with restricted access.

sources.system: ESTIC ERS series robotic screwdriving/fastening workcells (and comparable six-axis/SCARA fastening cells)
sources.title: New Tech for Robotic Fastening | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Preconfigured robotic workcells are sold commercially for automatic installation of threaded ..., including large screws and bolts, with programmed torque control in a fixtured cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production fastening rather than tower repair. Transfer holds for the E1 counterfactual only: the bolted mount hardware, torque-to-spec requirement and tool (powered nutrunner/driver) are the same class of work once the workpiece is fixtured and presented to the machine.

sources.system: KR QUANTEC robot cell in the Fraunhofer IPA 'DeMoBat' project
sources.claim: A KUKA KR QUANTEC industrial robot performed the disassembly steps of unscrewing screws, opening sealing joints ... on large, heavy end-of-life assemblies in a purpose-built robotic cell, with real-time sensor-based control of disassembly steps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: EV battery pack disassembly. Transfer holds because it is heavy-assembly maintenance work — removing fasteners, breaking sealed joints and demating cable connectors — the same manipulation primitives as removing an antenna/RRU from a mount, demonstrated on fixtured workpieces in a fenced industrial cell (E1).

sources.system: UR10e-based robotic unscrewing system with Intel RealSense D405 vision and custom mechatronic screwdriver
sources.developer: academic/industrial research group (published in Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing)
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A vision-guided robot arm with a custom powered screwdriver autonomously removes fasteners from a wide range of electronic ..., handling varied screw types and locations rather than a single scripted pattern.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: e-waste disassembly. Transfer holds for E1 because the electronic enclosures, fastener sizes and vision-guided tool placement resemble opening and servicing radio/rectifier modules on a bench; the demonstration is on fixtured parts presented to the machine.

sources.title: Meet Daisy and Taz: Apple's iPhone-Disassembling Robots | Supply Chain Digital
sources.claim: Apple operates a deployed automated disassembly line that takes in used iPhones and removes batteries, screws and components to yield separated parts, running as a production installation in Austin, Texas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated device teardown. Transfer holds for E1 only: it shows a purpose-built line can take in used electronic units, identify them and strip fasteners/modules at production reliability — the fixtured analogue of bench-repairing tower radios and modules.

sources.system: Telescent G5 Robotic Patch Panel / automated fiber cross-connect
sources.title: Telescent Introduces New G5 Robotic Patch Panel System - Silicon UK
sources.claim: Commercial robotic patch panel systems physically mate, demate and rearrange optical fiber connectors under software control in network and data center installations, i.e. machine-executed connector work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fiber cross-connect reconfiguration. Transfer is limited to the connector-handling element of jumper replacement, and only at E1: the machine is itself a purpose-built enclosure in which every connector is presented at a known position.

sources.system: review of robotics for telecom tower field maintenance
sources.developer: Shah et al., Journal of Field Robotics
sources.title: A comprehensive review on deploying robotics application in telecom network tower's field maintenance
sources.claim: In telecom tower field maintenance, robotics is at the survey/feasibility-analysis stage; the literature analyses the difficulties of tower field maintenance and the prospects for deploying robots rather than reporting fielded repair robots.
sources.transferJustification: Same task. Cited to support the negative judgment that no fielded robotic system performs tower equipment repair at E2/E3.

sources.title: Up the Tower: 2026 Trends to Watch - TowerClimber.com
sources.claim: At real tower sites, unmanned systems are used for inspection — pre-climb assessment, antenna alignment verification and mount condition checks — while the physical repair work continues to be done by climbing technicians.
sources.transferJustification: Same task setting. Cited to establish that fielded robotics at towers is confined to sensing, supporting the negative judgment for E3 tool-based maintenance and repair.

tasks.label: Locate tower sites where work is to be performed, using mapping software.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Install or repair tower lighting components, including strobes, beacons, or lighting controllers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Climb a 200-500 ft guyed or self-support communications tower to replace a failed top beacon/strobe head or LED obstruction fixture: hoist the new unit, open the weatherproof junction, disconnect and re-terminate conductors, unbolt the seized/corroded old fixture, mount and align the new one, verify flash operation. Outdoors, at height, weather as found.

Replace mid-level side-marker lights, flashheads or lenses and repair damaged conduit, wiring runs and junction boxes at intermediate levels on a lattice tower or inside/outside a monopole; includes pulling and terminating conductors at height.

Ground-level work at the tower base cabinet or equipment shelter: troubleshoot a lighting outage (photocell, flasher, controller board, alarm/monitoring unit, breaker, wiring), replace the failed component on its DIN rail/backplate, re-terminate wiring, then test the system and confirm alarm reporting / NOTAM close-out.

Full lighting system installation or incandescent-to-LED retrofit on a new or existing tower: mount beacons and side lights at several levels, run and support conductor/conduit up the structure, install the lighting controller and monitoring unit, commission to FAA advisory-circular requirements.
Install or repair obstruction lighting on a rooftop, building parapet, water tank or short structure reached by ladder, hatch or aerial lift, in an owner-controlled commercial or municipal facility.

Emergency outage response at a remote site under NOTAM time pressure - night, cold, wind, mud or ice - diagnosing the fault at the base and at height and effecting a repair or temporary fix the same visit.

sources.title: GITAI Successfully Demonstrates Robotics Construction Capabilities for Lunar Communications Towers
sources.claim: GITAI's Lunar Rover and three Inchworm robots autonomously assembled a 5 m communications tower in a desert test field, attached a communications antenna to the tower apex, connected its power cables and confirmed energization, then detached it again to simulate maintenance. Hardware was purpose-designed for robotic construction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mounting a powered device at the apex of a communications tower, connecting its power cables and confirming energization - the same physical operations as fitting a beacon/strobe head and lighting it. Objects and fasteners are comparable in scale, but parts were staged and optimized for robotic handling, i.e. a purpose-built (E1) presentation, so it substantiates E1 only.

sources.system: BJB ADS internal/through wiring systems and luminaire assembly automation
sources.title: Automatic assembly of LED modules, components and much more | BJB
sources.claim: BJB Automation supplies commercially deployed purpose-built machines that automatically grip, position, wire and test luminaire components - drivers, terminal blocks and LED ... - in lighting production lines; over 200 wiring systems delivered since 1995.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling and wiring lighting fixtures (mounting components, terminating conductors into terminal blocks, functional test) in a fixtured production cell. This is the purpose-built-setting form of installing a light fixture and terminating its supply wiring, with comparable conductor sizes and terminal hardware.

sources.title: Apple expands global recycling programs
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy line autonomously disassembles returned iPhones in a purpose-built facility, removing fasteners and extracting modules from 15+ presented models at 200 units per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous removal of fastened/retained components from units presented to the machine. It supports the take-off half of a fixture swap (unfastening and extracting the failed unit) when the workpiece is fixtured in a purpose-built cell, though only for known part geometries.

sources.title: Aerial Robot Modernizes Bird Flight Diverter Installation | T&D World
sources.claim: FulcrumAir's LineFly aerial robot autonomously installs bird flight diverters on energized transmission conductors in the field in commercial utility programs, but handles only purpose-designed clamp-on hardware, with no unfastening, wiring or component diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic attachment of hardware at height on outdoor utility infrastructure. It marks the ceiling of field aerial manipulation today - clamp-on devices engineered for the robot on a single conductor geometry - and does not extend to unbolting a weathered beacon, re-terminating conductors or commissioning a lighting circuit.

sources.title: Aerones introduces 'first' wind turbine maintenance and repair robot | GlobalSpec
sources.claim: Aerones' rope-suspended robots perform at-height wind turbine maintenance commercially in 30+ countries - cleaning, inspection, lightning-protection checks and leading-edge erosion repair - i.e. surface treatment and inspection, not replacement of bolted electrical fixtures or wiring.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic maintenance of tall outdoor structures. Cited to bound field capability: even the most mature at-height maintenance robots do coatings, cleaning and inspection on a standard blade surface, not fixture removal, electrical termination or fault diagnosis, so they do not substantiate E2/E3 completion of tower lighting work.

tasks.label: Calibrate and align components, using scales, gauges, and other measuring instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Tower-top cellular antenna alignment: technician climbs a monopole, lattice tower, or rooftop mount, loosens the mount clamps, sets panel-antenna azimuth with a GPS-based alignment tool, sets mechanical downtilt and plumb with an inclinometer/level, torques mounting hardware to spec, and records the readings for close-out. Wind, weather, varying mount geometry and site layout.

Microwave/mmWave backhaul dish path alignment at height: coarse-point the dish to the computed azimuth/elevation with compass/GPS alignment kit, then fine-peak on the receive-signal-level voltage while coordinating with the far-end technician, verify main lobe (not a side lobe), and lock down the fine-adjust bolts.

Ground-level in-situ calibration and verification at a cell site, DAS head-end, or repeater shelter: run the open/short/load calibration on a line-sweep test set, sweep the feedline and antenna for VSWR/return loss and DTF, torque RF connectors to spec, set radio unit / booster output power and gain, balance uplink-downlink levels against measured values.

Shop bench alignment/tuning of removable RF components: tune a repeater duplexer, cavity filter, or transmitter combiner to frequency by turning tuning screws while watching a VNA/service monitor; align mobile and portable two-way radios (transmit power, frequency error, FM deviation, receiver sensitivity/squelch) with a service monitor and adjustment pots or software alignment.

Mobile radio system alignment in a fleet garage bay: with a police/fire/service vehicle in the bay, align the installed mobile radio (power, deviation, channel setup) with a service monitor and tune/verify the vehicle antenna with a wattmeter or antenna analyzer for minimum VSWR, then verify operation on the live system.

Verifying/calibrating the shop's own measuring instruments and gauges against reference standards: checking a wattmeter, service monitor, power sensor, multimeter, or torque wrench against a traceable standard and adjusting or tagging it before field use.

sources.system: Fully automated robotic RF cavity filter tuning system (Yigit et al.)
sources.developer: Academic/industrial team, published in Journal of Field Robotics
sources.title: A Fully Automated Robotic System for Tuning Optimization of RF Cavity Filter - Journal of Field Robotics
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robotic cell tunes RF cavity filters by driving tuning screws with cobots and multi-axis arms while monitoring the response on a vector network analyzer, using vision and force-torque feedback — the same operation as bench alignment of duplexers/filters with measuring instruments.
sources.transferJustification: This is the bench form of the rated task: aligning/tuning an RF component (cavity filter, as used in repeater duplexers and combiners) to specification by mechanical adjustment while reading a measuring instrument. Same objects, same sub-millimetre-screw precision, same instrument-in-the-loop procedure.

sources.system: Trescal DMM and gage block calibration robots
sources.title: Innovation | Trescal Worldwide
sources.claim: Commercial calibration-laboratory robots automatically calibrate handheld digital multimeters and gage blocks against reference standards in a purpose-built robot cell, replacing the technician's manual instrument-calibration bench work.
sources.transferJustification: Directly matches the 'calibrate ... using scales, gauges, and other measuring instruments' instance in which the worker verifies/calibrates measuring instruments against traceable standards; the robot handles the instrument, applies reference stimuli and reads results.

sources.system: NOFFZ Universal Wireless Tester with collaborative robot loading
sources.title: NOFFZ Universal Wireless Tester: Efficient tests for wireless devices
sources.claim: A production wireless test system uses a collaborative robot arm ... load radio/telematics units into a shielded RF chamber and run automated RF test and calibration sequences in a fixtured cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated RF test/calibration of radio transceiver units in manufacturing. It transfers to bench alignment of radios because the objects (vehicle radio/telematics transceivers) and the instrument-driven power/frequency calibration steps are comparable, but only inside a fixtured, purpose-built cell.

sources.developer: Shah et al., Journal of Field Robotics review
sources.title: A comprehensive review on deploying robotics application in telecom network tower's field maintenance
sources.claim: Robotics for telecom tower field maintenance (climbing the tower and performing work at height on antennas) remains at the requirements-analysis and design-feasibility stage in the literature; no deployed system performs at-height antenna alignment.

sources.title: Top 10 CommScope Innovations: Base Station Antenna Beam Tilting
sources.claim: Remote electrical tilt actuators built into base station antennas let operators change the beam's electrical downtilt from a remote command by driving an electro-mechanical phase shifter, automating one sub-step of antenna alignment but not the mechanical azimuth/tilt/plumb setting or mount torqueing.

tasks.label: Examine malfunctioning radio equipment to locate defects such as loose connections, broken wires, or burned-out components, using schematic diagrams and test equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-service cell site ground equipment: technician responds to a sector/site alarm, opens the outdoor cabinet or shelter, inspects BBU/power modules, checks DC feeds and breakers with a meter, checks fiber/CPRI and coax connections, and traces the fault against site drawings. Live site, energized gear, mixed vendor hardware.

Tower-top or rooftop diagnosis: climb (or lift/rope access) to inspect antennas, RRUs, jumpers, weatherproofing and coax on a malfunctioning sector; look for water ingress, corroded or loose connectors, chafed/broken conductors, and confirm with line sweep/PIM or return-loss measurements at height, outdoors, in whatever weather and tower geometry the site presents.

Mobile two-way radio in a vehicle (police cruiser, ambulance, fleet truck): radio dead or poor range; technician works in a shop bay or roadside, pulls trim/console, checks fused power leads, control-head cabling, antenna and coax, and measures voltage/VSWR to isolate a loose connection, chafed wire or blown component in a cramped, vehicle-specific layout.

Bench diagnosis in a radio shop: a removed portable/mobile transceiver, repeater card, power supply or RF module is placed on the bench and examined with schematics, DMM, oscilloscope and service monitor to locate a burned component, cold/open solder joint or shorted device on the printed circuit assembly.

Fixed transmitter/station facility (broadcast transmitter building, marine coast station, airport ground radio, dispatch center): in-situ examination of a malfunctioning transmitter, exciter, combiner or power supply rack, reading front-panel meters and alarms, checking interlocks, wiring and connectors, and probing voltages against the equipment schematic.

sources.system: SPEA 4060 / 4080 Automatic Flying Probe Tester (Repair Test solution)
sources.title: Electronic Board Testing: ICT, Flying Probe & Functional | SPEA
sources.claim: SPEA's automatic flying probe testers (4060/4080) are sold as dedicated repair-center solutions that automatically move probes over an electronic board and identify the faulty part(s), producing a component-level diagnostic report - locating opens, shorts and failed components inside a purpose-built fixtured tester.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: board-level fault localization in electronics repair. Transfer: the printed circuit assemblies inside radios/transceivers are the same class of object, the defect classes named in the task (open/loose connections, broken conductors, burned-out components) are exactly what flying probe testers diagnose, and the test program is generated from the board's CAD/netlist, i.e. the schematic the technician would read.

sources.title: In-Circuit Test For Manufacturing | Keysight
sources.claim: Keysight in-circuit test systems (i3070 family) automatically detect and diagnose structural defects - solder opens, shorts, stuck-at faults, wrong or missing components - on fixtured boards in manufacturing and rework environments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated structural fault diagnosis of electronic assemblies. Transfer: same defect classes (opens/shorts/failed parts) and same object class (radio circuit boards) as this examination task, driven by netlist/CAD data derived from the schematic - but only with the board presented in a fixture.

sources.title: Scaling Cell Tower Inspections with 3D Tower Scan | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio's AI-enabled autonomous drones perform cell tower scans and inspections at scale (American Tower's UAS program ran roughly 20,000 automated inspections per year), producing high-resolution imagery and 3D models of tower-top assets; the output is visual data capture and asset documentation, not electrical fault isolation with test equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous visual/thermal inspection of tower-mounted equipment. It bounds rather than substantiates the tower instance: the drone images antennas and cabling but cannot open weatherproofing, disconnect a jumper, or attach a line sweep/PIM analyzer to confirm a defect.

sources.title: ANYmal Monitors High-Voltage Transmission at RTE - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal legged robot performs scheduled autonomous inspection rounds inside utility substations and industrial plants, reading gauges and taking thermal/acoustic readings on electrical shelves to flag irregularities; it does not open cabinets, use hand test instruments, or probe circuits against a schematic.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous condition inspection of electrical equipment in a structured facility. It bounds the in-facility instances: the frontier deployed capability is sensor rounds and anomaly flagging, well short of opening equipment and locating a loose connection or burned component with meters and schematics.

sources.system: Robotic Arm-Assisted PCB Diagnostic and Measurement System
sources.title: Implementation of a Robotic Arm-Assisted PCB Diagnostic and Measurement System
sources.claim: A robotic arm that positions meter probes on PCB test points to take voltage and resistance readings has been demonstrated only in research, using teach-and-playback programming for fixed, predefined test points.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic probing of a board with meter instruments. Cited only to bound the bench instance beyond fixtured ATE: probe-wielding manipulators outside a purpose-built tester remain scripted lab demonstrations.

tasks.label: Insert plugs into receptacles and bolt or screw leads to terminals to connect equipment to power sources, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ground-level cell site compound (fenced monopole/self-support site): tech connects a new radio/BBU or rectifier to power — pulls DC feeders into the power cabinet, strips and lands lugs on breakers/busbars, torques to spec, plugs DC power connectors into the radio, checks polarity and labels. Cramped cabinet interiors, live plant, outdoor weather, layouts differ by vendor and site.

Elevated work on a tower/monopole (60-300 ft): tech connects DC power leads and screw-locking circular connectors to remote radio units, TMAs, or obstruction lighting on congested mounts while harnessed, weatherproofs the connections, and verifies. Mount geometry, cable routing and clearances differ site to site.

Vehicle installation in a fleet shop bay: mounting a two-way radio / mobile data terminal in a police cruiser, ambulance, or utility truck — routing fused power leads through the firewall, bolting ring terminals to battery posts/studs or a distribution block, plugging harness connectors into the radio head and control head under the dash.

Indoor equipment room, broadcast plant, or dispatch center: plugging equipment power cords into rack PDU/UPS receptacles, landing DC leads on a fuse/breaker panel, bolting ground/bonding lugs to a busbar, dressing and labeling cables in an occupied rack aisle with live adjacent gear.

Rooftop small cell, DAS node, or pole-mounted radio in the public right-of-way: connecting the unit to a meter socket/disconnect or building panel, landing conductors on terminals, plugging the radio's power connector, working around varied building structures, ladders, and pedestrians.

sources.title: Automated Control Cabinet Wiring Solution for Scalable Renewable Energy Systems (GCSM, Springer)
sources.claim: Kiesling/Rittal's Averex portal-robot wiring centre automates the full wiring chain for control-cabinet mounting plates — cutting, crimping, connecting wires to terminals and routing them — and can wire both spring-loaded and screw-type connections, i.e. autonomous 'screwing leads to terminals' inside a purpose-built machine cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wiring electrical devices in a control cabinet. Same physical acts as the rated task — landing prepared leads on screw and spring terminals of power distribution and relay hardware with tool-equipped end effectors — at the same conductor sizes and terminal types techs land in telecom power cabinets.

sources.title: Automated Control Cabinet Wiring Solution for Scalable Renewable Energy Systems (GCSM, Springer)
sources.claim: Polygon Technologies' Wirebot combines a gantry and an articulated robot with vision and tactile sensing that plugs prepared wires into cabinet terminals and connects them to both spring-loaded and screw-type terminals, about one minute per wire.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic wiring of electrical cabinets. It performs exactly the rated task's two actions — inserting conductor ends into terminals and fastening screw terminals — on comparable wire gauges, in a fixtured cell where the cabinet is presented to the machine.

sources.system: Komax Omega 840/850 and Omega 745/755 automatic insertion machines
sources.title: Omega 840 / 850: Fully automatic assembly of unshielded twisted-pair wires now possible too! | Komax
sources.claim: Komax builds fully automatic insertion machines that take terminated (crimped) leads and insert them into connector housings without an operator, the standard automated route for 'connecting leads to terminals' in wire-harness plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated harness assembly. Machines seat terminated leads into connector housings/terminals to worker quality at production rates, the same mating action as inserting a radio's power leads into a connector, in a purpose-built machine environment.

sources.system: 6-axis robot with 3D vision (Sick TriSpector1030 / Photoneo PhoXi S) and force sensing for bolt tightening
sources.developer: INESC TEC (Institute for Systems and Computer Engineering, Technology and Science) with automaker
sources.title: Robots Automate Bolt-Tightening on Automotive Assembly Lines | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Industrial robots using 3D vision and force sensors now tighten bolts on car assemblies on the line, including fastening axle dampers to a van undercarriage at a conveyor-fed workstation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic bolt tightening on vehicles. Establishes that vision-guided robots can locate and torque threaded fasteners on a vehicle presented by a conveyor — the same act as bolting a ring-terminal lead to a stud when the vehicle is brought to the machine.

sources.system: Robotic battery-pack insertion plus automatic screwdriving system (Desoutter fastening tools)
sources.title: Fastening Tools for EV Assembly | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Robotic insertion of vehicle-mounted battery packs is followed by an automatic screwdriving system that drives the retaining screws, a deployed automotive fastening line using Desoutter tools.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fastening of electrical power components into a vehicle. Comparable objects (battery/power modules), comparable torque-controlled threaded fastening, in a fixtured, conveyor-fed cell — the E1 counterpart of bolting leads to terminals in a vehicle.

sources.system: Behavioral-cloning connector insertion policy on an industrial arm
sources.title: Behavioral Cloning for Robotic Connector Assembly: An Empirical Study
sources.claim: Learned visuo-tactile policies insert five different electrical connector geometries with 92.8% average success using only a grayscale camera and force-torque sensing, without pose information.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic electrical connector insertion. Directly matches 'insert plugs into receptacles' for multi-pin power/signal connectors at millimetre tolerances, in a bench/cell setting where the mating half is fixtured.

sources.date: March 2022 (Port of Oakland order); April 2025 (APM Terminals Maasvlakte II demonstration)
sources.title: ROCSYS TO SUPPLY AUTONOMOUS CHARGING SOLUTIONS TO SSA MARINE FOR ITS ELECTRIC YARD TRACTORS AT THE PORT OF OAKLAND
sources.claim: Rocsys' ROC-1 hands-free charging robot autonomously mates CCS connectors to electric yard tractors and autonomous trucks at container terminals, so drivers only park near the station instead of manually plugging in.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous plug insertion into a receptacle at an E2 facility (container terminal). It shows only single-connector mating at a fixed, purpose-built charging pedestal with the vehicle parked to it; it does not cover locating varied receptacles, routing cable, or screwing leads to terminals.

sources.title: SoftBank Corp. Develops "Robot-friendly" Server Rack to Enable Automation at Data Centers
sources.claim: SoftBank re-engineered the data-center rack with busbars, blind-mate and optical connectors so that robots need only push a server in — explicitly removing the cable-plugging step rather than automating it in the as-built facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: powering equipment in an equipment room. Cited as context that connecting equipment power in a human-built facility is handled by rebuilding the environment for the machine (E1-style blind-mate infrastructure), not by robots plugging cables as installed today.

tasks.label: Install, adjust, and repair stationary and mobile radio transmitting and receiving equipment and two-way radio communication systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mobile two-way radio install/de-install in a fleet vehicle (police cruiser, fire apparatus, utility truck, ambulance) at a fleet garage or upfitter bay: mount the radio head/control head and bracket, drill roof or trunk lid for the antenna, route coax through headliner/trim, run fused power leads to the battery, ground the chassis, then program and test the radio.

Cell site / land-mobile site work at height: climb a monopole, lattice tower, rooftop or water-tank mount and install or swap remote radio units, panel antennas, mounting pipes, RF jumpers and fiber, torque and weatherproof connectors, sweep-test lines. Outdoors, weather-exposed, structure geometry differs site to site.

Install a stationary base station, repeater, or dispatch console in an equipment room, telecom shelter, or public-safety comm center: rack or wall-mount the units, land DC power, ground, connect coax/fiber jumpers and duplexer/combiner, then power up, commission and verify.

Shop bench work on mobile/portable/base radios: diagnose a reported fault across a mixed fleet of models, disassemble, replace a failed board, connector or component, reassemble, then align/tune deviation, power and frequency on a service monitor and reprogram the codeplug.

Field adjustment/optimization of an already-installed antenna at a cellular or land-mobile site: re-aim azimuth or downtilt of a sector antenna to correct a coverage problem, verify the resulting signal, at an operator-controlled mast site.

sources.system: GITAI Lunar Rover + Inchworm Robots (with KDDI)
sources.title: GITAI demonstrates robotically-constructed lunar communications tower | Military Aerospace
sources.claim: GITAI's Lunar Rover and three Inchworm robots autonomously built a 5-meter communications tower and attached a mobile-network (3GPP) antenna to its apex in a desert lunar-analog testbed, using an antenna developed specifically for robotic construction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic erection of a mobile-network tower and mounting of its antenna. It transfers to 'install stationary radio transmitting/receiving equipment' because the workpiece is a real 3GPP base-station antenna to KDDI's specification, mounted at height on a tower, with the same mount-and-connect precision required at a terrestrial site.

sources.title: GITAI and KDDI Successfully Demonstrates Robotics Construction Capabilities for Lunar Communications Towers | KDDI News Room
sources.claim: In the same demonstration the robots connected the antenna's power cables and confirmed energization, then reversed the operation; the antenna was purpose-designed for robotic handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mounting a radio antenna and mating its power connections, verified by energization. This is the mount-and-cable core of installing stationary radio transmitting equipment; the hardware interfaces were redesigned for the robot, which is what a purpose-built (E1) presentation of the work would provide.

sources.title: GITAI tests robotic construction of lunar comms tower in desert simulation exercise
sources.claim: Reporting on the same demonstration states the robots performed the tower assembly, antenna attachment and power-cable connection autonomously in a desert environment simulating the lunar surface.

sources.title: TMGcore Unveils Robot-Managed Immersion Data Centers | Data Center Frontier
sources.claim: TMGcore's OTTO platform is a commercially launched modular data-center product in which fixed robotic arms remove and replace rack-mount server units (including faulty units) inside a purpose-built immersion enclosure with blind-mate connections, aimed at lights-out operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous insertion/removal/replacement of rack-mount electronic units with mated power and data connections in a purpose-built enclosure. Transfers to installing a rack-mounted base station/repeater unit in an E1 presentation: comparable object size and mass, comparable insertion precision and connector mating, machine-designed racking.

sources.title: SoftBank develops 'cableless' server rack for data center robots - DCD
sources.claim: SoftBank has developed a cable-less 'robot-friendly' server rack, with bus-bar power and blind-mate connectors, so that robots can install, remove and replace rack units by simple insertion; robot testing was still to come at the time of reporting.
sources.transferJustification: Context only for what an E1 presentation of rack equipment install looks like (fixtured, cableless, blind-mate). No autonomous robot completion is demonstrated in this source, so it is not relied on for any positive judgment.

sources.title: Vodafone trials robotic antenna pivot at 4G/5G mobile mast - Telecompaper
sources.claim: Vodafone equipped an operational 4G/5G mast in Albania with an AI-driven robotic arm (RoboRAN, with Humax Networks) that autonomously analyses where coverage is needed and physically re-aims the radio antenna, replacing engineer site visits.

sources.title: Vodafone Test 5G Mobile Mast Controlled by Robotic Arm and AI Brain - ISPreview UK
sources.claim: Independent reporting on the same trial confirms the mast-mounted system autonomously analyses coverage needs and automatically adjusts the radio ... signal toward the target area.

tasks.label: Monitor radio range stations to detect transmission flaws and adjust controls to eliminate flaws.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Live macro cell site (tower, monopole or rooftop): technician monitors sector performance and alarms (coverage holes, interference, RTWP/VSWR, throughput complaints) and corrects them by changing antenna downtilt/azimuth and radio power or parameters, often climbing to the antenna mount; outdoor, weather-dependent, layout differs site to site.

Fixed transmitter station (FM/AM/TV broadcast, public-safety repeater, aviation navaid): monitoring shows the RF chain out of spec (low forward power, high reflected power, off-frequency, wrong deviation/modulation level); technician tunes the transmitter output network, combiner, duplexer or cavity filters and resets power controls until readings are back within spec, inside the equipment shelter.

Fixed transmitter station: monitoring shows a flaw with no simple control setting behind it - distorted audio or exciter fault, spurious emissions, intermittent PA module, bad jumper/connector or grounding problem; technician diagnoses across the chain and corrects it at the rack.

Shop bench: a repeater, duplexer/combiner, mobile or portable radio is on the bench with a service monitor/VNA; technician measures transmit power, frequency, deviation and passband/notch response and adjusts tuning screws, trimmers and settings until the unit meets specification.

Fleet garage or motor pool: two-way radio installed in a service or emergency vehicle; technician keys the radio with a wattmeter/service monitor, finds low output or high SWR or wrong deviation, and adjusts radio settings, cabling or antenna match/trim on the vehicle until transmission is clean.

Field coverage/interference work away from the station: driving or walking a coverage area with test receivers and a spectrum analyzer to find dropouts, distortion or an interfering emitter, then changing station controls (power, tilt, frequency, filtering) to eliminate the flaw; public roads and varied uncontrolled terrain.

sources.system: Automated robotic RF cavity filter tuning system (Yigit & Afacan)
sources.developer: Yarkin Yigit and Engin Afacan (Journal of Field Robotics)
sources.title: A Fully Automated Robotic System for Tuning Optimization of RF Cavity Filter - Journal of Field Robotics
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robotic station tunes RF cavity filters: cobots and multi-axis arms turn the tuning screws while a vector network analyzer monitors the filter's transmission response, driving it into specification without a human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: post-production tuning of cavity filters used in radio transmitters and receivers. It is the same monitor-detect-adjust loop as this task - an instrument watches the passed/transmitted signal and the machine turns mechanical RF controls until the out-of-spec response is gone - on the same class of RF hardware, at screw-level precision, in a purpose-built bench cell.

sources.system: SpaceForest Automated Filter Tuning System (FTS / FTM / IAFTT)
sources.title: Automated Filter Tuning - AI Software & Hardware | SpaceForest
sources.claim: A commercially offered robotic filter-tuning station with a Cartesian manipulator and multiple tuning heads sets filter and diplexer characteristics ... while integrated with standard vector network analyzers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production and rework tuning of microwave filters and diplexers - the same duplexer/combiner alignment a radio technician performs on a bench with a VNA or service monitor; identical objects and precision, performed in a purpose-built robotic station.

sources.system: RoboRAN (Vodafone AI algorithm + HUMAX Networks robotic arm)
sources.title: Vodafone trials mobile mast powered with an AI brain and a robotic arm
sources.claim: A mast antenna mounted on a robotic arm autonomously analyses where coverage is needed and physically rotates or tilts the antenna to fix the shortfall, without human intervention; trialled at one operator site in Tirana, Albania.

sources.system: AirHop Auptim RET Optimization rApp driving in-antenna remote electrical tilt actuators
sources.title: AirHop Auptim AI/ML Remote Electrical antenna Tilt Optimization rApp - Ericsson
sources.claim: A commercially available AI/ML optimization application monitors live network KPIs and commands the antennas' remote electrical tilt actuators to change tilt dynamically, correcting coverage and interference problems without a site visit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated coverage/capacity optimization. The physical act is performed by the electromechanical tilt actuator built into the antenna, which the closed loop drives after detecting degraded signal quality - the same detect-flaw-then-adjust-the-antenna loop, but only where the actuation hardware is designed into the workpiece.

tasks.label: Mount equipment on transmission towers and in vehicles such as ships or ambulances.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Climb a 100–300 ft lattice tower or monopole at a carrier/tower-company site and mount RF gear at height: hang mounting pipes and sector frames, hoist and bolt 20–40 kg panel antennas and remote radio units, set azimuth/downtilt, torque hardware, connect and weatherproof jumpers and grounding. Outdoor, wind/temperature exposure, each tower carrying different legacy hardware and cable routing.

Mount small-cell/DAS antennas, radios and brackets on rooftops, building facades, streetlight or utility poles in an urban right-of-way: bolt or band mounts to varied structures, secure radios and cabling, coordinate around pedestrians, traffic and building tenants.

Upfit an emergency or service vehicle (ambulance, police cruiser, fire apparatus) in a fleet garage or upfitter shop: mount the two-way radio/control head and bracket in the console, drill and seal the roof for an antenna, route and terminate power and coax through headliner and firewall, then verify transmit/receive.

Ground-level mounting inside a fenced cell-site compound: bolt RRUs, surge suppressors, DC power gear and equipment cabinets to frames or the H-frame/ice bridge, clamp hybrid cable to the lower tower legs, and land connectors and grounds.

Install marine radio equipment on a vessel at a dock or shipyard: mount VHF/SSB radio and GMDSS gear in the wheelhouse console, fit antenna mounts and a satcom dome on the mast or deckhouse, route coax through cramped, ship-specific spaces and test.

sources.system: IBG / Göke Technology Group automated wheel assembly robot cell
sources.title: Wheel assembly: Fully automatic bolting and assembly
sources.claim: Two vision-equipped industrial robots pick wheels, determine hub pose in 3D and bolt complete wheels onto car bodies fully automatically while the vehicle moves on the line — mounting a heavy component onto a mating structure and torquing its fasteners inside a purpose-built robot cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bolting a ~20 kg wheel onto a hub. It transfers to mounting antennas, RRUs and radio brackets at E1 because the objects are comparable in mass, the alignment tolerance to bolt patterns is comparable, and torqued fastening is the same operation — provided the workpiece is fixtured and presented, as in this cell.

sources.system: MIRAI AI-vision software on Universal Robots cobots (bolt torquing)
sources.developer: Micropsi Industries with a leading US automotive OEM
sources.title: Leading US automotive OEM — Automated bolt torquing | Micropsi Industries
sources.claim: A North American automotive OEM runs seven AI-vision-guided robots with automatic torque wrenches that autonomously locate and tighten bolts on parts moving down a human-designed conveyor, coping with position, part and lighting variance at near-100% success.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: torquing structural bolts on seat assemblies. Mounting radios and antennas is fundamentally locating and torquing fasteners on brackets; this shows worker-quality reliability for that operation in a fixtured industrial cell, including tolerance to modest part-position variance.

sources.system: 3D-vision-guided robotic bolt-tightening station (INESC TEC / automotive assembly line)
sources.developer: INESC TEC with an automotive manufacturer
sources.title: Robots Automate Bolt-Tightening on Automotive Assembly Lines | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: In a car factory, a 3D-vision-guided robot autonomously tightens the bolts fixing rear axle dampers to the undercarriage of vans carried on an overhead conveyor, estimating the vehicle's 6-DOF pose to compensate for conveyor tolerances.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastening hardware onto a vehicle on a production line. It transfers to mounting radio hardware in a vehicle at E1: same class of vehicle-mounted bracket fastening, same torque-critical acceptance criterion, with the vehicle presented on a conveyor rather than parked in a shop.

sources.system: Ericsson USA 5G Smart Factory automation (robotic dispensing arm, robotic storage and retrieval system)
sources.title: Ericsson cranks out massive MIMO radios at its Texas factory
sources.claim: Ericsson's Lewisville 5G factory assembles massive MIMO radios on a 24/7 automated line where robotic arms dispense adhesive on radio boards and a robotic storage-and-retrieval system places finished radios; humans are still required for delicate handling steps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling and assembly of the very radios installers mount. It supports E1 handling and placement of radio units in a purpose-built line, while also showing the limits of robot dexterity for delicate, non-fixtured handling.

sources.system: Mini LineFly robot with heavy-lift drone
sources.developer: FulcrumAir (with PLP; used by American Transmission Co.)
sources.title: ATC uses drone to install bird diverters for the first time – ATC
sources.claim: A robot carried to overhead high-voltage transmission conductors by a heavy-lift drone installs bird flight diverters on live lines in the field; a US transmission utility used it commercially to install over 450 diverters across three Wisconsin counties.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: field installation of hardware on aerial infrastructure. It does NOT transfer to this task: the payload is a small clamp-on plastic diverter repeatedly attached to a uniform conductor, not a 20–40 kg antenna or RRU that must be aligned, bolted to torque, cabled and weatherproofed on varied tower steel.

sources.system: Review of robotics for telecom tower field maintenance
sources.developer: Shah et al., Journal of Field Robotics
sources.title: A comprehensive review on deploying robotics application in telecom network tower's field maintenance
sources.claim: Field robotics at telecom towers remains at the feasibility-analysis stage: a Journal of Field Robotics review surveys climbing robots and tower access arrangements and analyses whether robots could perform tower field maintenance, rather than reporting deployed installation systems.
sources.transferJustification: Same task domain (tower field work); cited only to show the absence of any fielded robot that climbs towers and mounts equipment, supporting negative judgments at E2/E3.

sources.developer: Humax Networks, piloted by PLDT/Smart Communications
sources.title: Smart Communications pilots robotic tech at cell tower sites in the Philippines
sources.claim: A carrier's cell-site robotics pilot uses a permanently mounted robot arm that lets operators remotely reposition antennas for network optimization — remote adjustment of already-installed antennas, not installation of equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Same domain (cell-site antenna work); cited to show that fielded cell-site robotics is limited to teleoperated adjustment of pre-installed antennas and cannot support a positive judgment on mounting equipment.

tasks.label: Remove and replace defective components and parts such as conductors, resistors, semiconductors, and integrated circuits, using soldering irons, wire cutters, and hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop bench, board level: a PCB pulled from a portable/mobile radio, base-station module or repeater is set on the bench under magnification; the tech desolders a defective chip resistor, transistor/diode or IC (SMD or through-hole) with iron/hot air, cleans the pads, solders the replacement, and re-tests.

Shop bench, assembly level: repair inside a still-assembled chassis or module - unsolder and replace a burnt coax/power connector, cracked wire leads, a heatsinked RF power transistor, relay or fuse holder; involves unscrewing brackets, cutting/stripping wires, resoldering leads and reassembly.

Cell site / equipment shelter, in place: replace defective conductors and hardware in a base-station cabinet or on the ice bridge - re-terminate a coax jumper connector, replace a surge suppressor, ground bond or terminal lug, solder/crimp leads, weatherproof, working outdoors in whatever weather and site layout exists.

Vehicle mobile radio: in a fleet garage bay or roadside, replace defective conductors and parts in a police/fire/utility installation - splice or replace power leads, fuse holders, control-head cabling and connectors under the dash, in the console or trunk, in cramped as-found vehicle interiors.

Broadcast transmitter or repeater site: at the transmitter building, replace failed high-power parts in an amplifier/PA cabinet - power semiconductors bolted to heatsinks, capacitors, contactors, RF connectors and interconnect wiring, using hand tools and a soldering iron, then bring the transmitter back on air.

sources.system: Ersa HR 600 XL automatic rework station
sources.title: HR 600XL - Automatic rework station by Ersa GmbH | DirectIndustry
sources.claim: Commercial automatic rework station that desolders a defective SMD component from a PCB clamped in its board holder, aligns and places the replacement with machine vision, and resolders it.

sources.system: Ersa HR 600 XL with AUTO SCAVENGER SC 600
sources.title: Ersa Rework System HR 600 XL
sources.claim: The same station automatically removes residual solder from the pads after the defective component is desoldered, closing the remove-clean-replace cycle without an operator touching the board.

sources.title: Automatic Rework - highly automated assembly repair
sources.claim: Vendor states such rework platforms are aimed at repairing boards in communication electronics and IT ..., i.e. the class of boards radio/cellular technicians repair.

sources.title: SMD Rework System for Complete PCB Repair Processes | Finetech
sources.claim: Bench rework system that performs the whole rework cycle - desoldering the defective part, residual solder removal, and soldering the replacement - on one machine, for packages from 01005 to large BGA.

sources.title: Proven a thousand times over: successful recovery of valuable materials from electronic devices - Fraunhofer ILT
sources.claim: Purpose-built cell that automatically locates and laser-desolders identified components from populated PCBs, trialed in an industrial setting - the removal half of component-level board repair, done autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated component removal from PCBs for recycling. Same objects (populated boards, chip and IC packages) and the same removal step required here; it shows machine identification and desoldering of a designated component, though not installation of a replacement.

sources.developer: University of Salford / IEEE Trans. CPMT
sources.title: Automated removal and replacement of through-hole components in robotic rework | IEEE Xplore
sources.claim: Fully automated robotic rework cell demonstrated removal and replacement of both through-hole and surface-mount components on PCB assemblies, using CAD/ATE data to locate the defective part.

sources.title: Hand soldering robot from Ersa - system supplier for electronics production
sources.claim: Commercial iron-soldering robot performing automatic soldering-iron joints on fixtured work in production cells - the soldering half of installing a replacement part in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production iron soldering of components/wires on fixtured boards. Same tool and joint types as replacing a part, but only in a taught, fixtured cell - no defective-part removal or in-situ work.

sources.system: Telecom tower field-maintenance robotics (survey of proposals)
sources.developer: Shah et al., Journal of Field Robotics
sources.title: A comprehensive review on deploying robotics application in telecom network tower's field maintenance
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed survey of robotics for telecom tower field maintenance analyses feasibility rather than reporting deployed field-repair robots.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the field instances: it establishes that tower/cell-site maintenance robotics remains at feasibility-study stage, so no cited system supports in-situ component replacement.

tasks.label: Repair circuits, wiring, and soldering, using soldering irons and hand tools to install parts and adjust connections.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop/depot bench repair of a two-way radio, repeater, or RF module: technician clamps the board in a holder, desolders and removes a failed component or cracked connector, cleans pads, installs and solders the replacement, reflows suspect joints, then reassembles and verifies. Service shop bench with ESD mat, iron, hot-air, magnifier.

Shop bench fabrication/repair of cable assemblies and terminations for radio gear: soldering/crimping coax connectors on jumpers, soldering multipin (D-sub, Molex, mic) connectors, tinning leads, crimping lugs and ferrules, building control/audio harnesses, using vise, stripper, crimper and iron.

Installing or repairing a mobile two-way radio in a patrol car, ambulance, or service truck: pulling trim, routing power and coax through the firewall, splicing/soldering and fusing power leads to the battery, crimping grounds, terminating control-head and antenna cables in a cramped under-dash space, in a fleet garage bay.

Ground-level work at a cell site or transmitter site: repairing or replacing wiring inside a BTS/DC power cabinet or shelter rack — landing lugs on breakers/busbars, re-terminating DC power and alarm/control conductors, repairing grounding leads, replacing a damaged cable run and dressing it, outdoors at a fenced compound whose layout varies site to site.

At-height work on a tower or rooftop: replacing a damaged coax jumper or connector at an antenna/RRU port, re-terminating a line, repairing a broken ground kit or AISG/DC feed, torquing and weatherproofing connections with tape and mastic, while tied off in wind and weather.

sources.title: RW1500 BGA Rework Station for SMT, BGA, and LEDs | Manncorp Rework
sources.claim: Commercial automated rework systems perform PCB component repair — optical alignment, automatic placement and soldering of SMD/BGA parts on a fixtured board loaded into the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class as bench-level circuit repair: removing/installing a part on a populated board and making the solder joints, at the same or finer precision than radio-shop rework.

sources.system: Japan Unix soldering robots (desktop, gantry, articulated cells)
sources.title: Robotic Soldering | Advanced Automated Soldering System — Japan Unix
sources.claim: Robotic soldering cells are a mature commercial product line that replace manual iron soldering with programmed motion, feeder-fed solder and thermal control, in desktop or in-line fixtured stations, with vision sensors and joint testers as options.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the soldering-iron work of the task (making and remaking joints on boards, terminals and wire leads), performed in a purpose-built fixtured cell rather than by hand.

sources.title: Automated Processing of Small RF and Coax Cables | ASSEMBLY Magazine
sources.claim: Automatic cable-processing machines cut, strip, tin and crimp RF/coax and fine cables to connectors, producing finished cable assemblies without an operator handling each step.
sources.transferJustification: Bench cable/connector work in the task is stripping, tinning and terminating coax and conductors to connectors; this machine performs those operations on the same class of cable to assembly-industry quality when the work is presented to it.

sources.date: 2014-06 launch; still marketed in Rittal Automation Systems portfolio
sources.title: Averex wiring centre from Kiesling | Rittal - The System.
sources.claim: A commercial gantry robot wiring centre automatically prepares wires and makes the connections between devices on a control/switchgear mounting plate, replacing manual cabinet wiring.
sources.transferJustification: Cabinet/rack wiring in radio equipment shelters uses the same objects (insulated conductors, ferrules/lugs, screw and spring terminals) and tolerances as control-cabinet wiring; the robot cuts, crimps, routes and lands the conductors when the plate is fixtured in the cell.

sources.system: Averex portal robot (cited in automated control cabinet wiring study)
sources.title: Automated Control Cabinet Wiring Solution for Scalable Renewable Energy Systems (SpringerLink)
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed engineering literature describes the Kiesling/Rittal Averex portal robot as a fully automated cabinet wiring solution covering wire cutting, crimping, connection and routing inside the cabinet.
sources.transferJustification: Independent confirmation that in-cabinet conductor termination and routing — the same physical operations as repairing wiring in a base-station or transmitter cabinet — is done by a fixtured robot cell.

sources.system: WAGO Cabinet Wiring Robot / Wiring Bot
sources.title: More Efficient Control Cabinet Wiring | WAGO
sources.claim: A current vendor robot cell prepares conductors (cut, strip, crimp, print) and wires mounting plates/rails for control cabinets, reducing manual wiring workload substantially.

tasks.label: Test batteries, using hydrometers and ammeters, and charge batteries as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine preventive-maintenance check of a -48V VRLA battery string in a ground-level equipment cabinet or shelter at a fenced carrier cell site: measure per-jar float voltage, clamp-ammeter float/charge current, check terminal torque and corrosion, take conductance/internal-resistance readings, verify rectifier float settings, log readings and equalize/recharge as needed.

Capacity/load or timed discharge test on a battery string at a cell site hut, repeater, or broadcast transmitter room: connect load bank and test leads to cells, monitor cell voltages and current through the discharge, then reconnect the rectifier and recharge the string to float.

Battery check at a rooftop cell site or remote rural/mountaintop site taken as found: ladder or hatch access, cramped or crowded cabinets of varying layout, weather and uneven ground; measure voltages/currents, test cells, top-off charge or swap a failed jar.

Older telecom or broadcast site with flooded lead-acid cells: draw electrolyte from each cell with a hydrometer to read specific gravity, check levels and water the cells, measure charging current, and apply an equalizing charge as necessary.

Two-way radio work on service/emergency vehicles at a fleet garage: test the vehicle battery and charging system with a battery tester/ammeter before or after a radio install, and charge or jump the battery as necessary.

Bench work in the radio shop: test portable radio battery packs, spare jars, and small UPS/backup batteries on an analyzer or with a multimeter/ammeter, and place them on chargers to bring them up to full charge.

sources.system: Chroma 17000 Battery Cell Formation / Turnkey Formation Solution
sources.title: Battery Cell Formation Turnkey Solution < Chroma
sources.claim: Commercial turnkey lithium cell formation/grading lines automatically load cells onto trays, convey them to stations that make electrical contact, run charge/discharge (formation) and OCV/ACIR/DCIR tests, and sort cells by result inside a purpose-built machine line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production battery testing and charging. Same objects (battery cells/jars with terminals) and the same measurements the technician makes (terminal voltage, current, internal resistance, charge/discharge capacity), performed with the battery presented fixtured to the machine, which is exactly the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: BBS Automation end-of-line battery pack testing systems
sources.title: End-of-line battery pack testing | BBS Automation
sources.claim: End-of-line battery pack test stations in automotive plants perform automatic contacting of pack terminals plus charging and discharging as part of the electrical validation of each pack.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line electrical test of assembled battery packs. It covers the same work content as the technician's bench/field test - contact the terminals, measure electrical parameters, charge/discharge - on comparably sized batteries, with the pack brought to the fixed test station.

sources.system: DITEC High Rate Discharge (HRD) test machine

sources.claim: A finishing-line machine for lead-acid batteries receives batteries on a conveyor, lowers a contact head onto the terminals and runs a high-rate discharge test to characterize battery performance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated capacity/load testing of lead-acid batteries in production. Same chemistry and battery format the technician tests, same electrical test (high-current discharge via terminal contact), with the battery conveyed and fixtured to the machine.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic probe placement on battery terminals for internal-resistance/impedance testing. This is the manipulation core of 'test batteries with an ammeter/conductance tester' - locating terminals and making reliable contact - on a used, non-fixtured module in a structured lab cell.

sources.title: NIO Power | NIO
sources.claim: Deployed NIO Power Swap Stations autonomously handle vehicle battery packs, run a health check on the ... during every swap, and recharge the removed packs inside the station without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated battery diagnostics plus recharging in a purpose-built station. It couples the two halves of this task - assess battery condition and charge as necessary - on large traction batteries handled entirely by machine.

sources.title: Innovative PowerHive Technology Drives Change | DC Velocity
