sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine handling of industrial lead-acid batteries with charge-state monitoring and connection to chargers. Same battery class (heavy lead-acid), same 'charge as necessary' decision and connection step, performed at a purpose-built station.

tasks.label: Test emergency transmitters to ensure their readiness for immediate use.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Agency radio shop: scheduled test/alignment of public-safety portable and mobile two-way radios (P25/DMR handhelds, cruiser radios) used for emergency response. Technician connects the radio to a communications service monitor, keys it, checks transmit power, frequency error, deviation, emergency-alert button and unit ID transmission, receiver sensitivity, realigns if needed, and files a pass/fail record.

Fleet garage bay: readiness test of emergency communications equipment installed in a service or emergency vehicle (police cruiser mobile radio, ambulance radio, in-vehicle eCall/telematics unit). Worker keys the set into a wattmeter/service monitor at the antenna feed, checks VSWR and audio, presses the emergency/SOS button and confirms the alert and ID reach dispatch, then documents.

Transmitter shelter at a base station, repeater, NOAA weather-radio or broadcast site: exercising the standby/emergency transmitter. Worker forces a changeover to the backup transmitter, measures forward and reflected power and frequency at the site, checks antenna/combiner, verifies alarms and remote-control telemetry reach the NOC or dispatch, restores normal configuration and logs the test.

Hangar or marine electronics shop: periodic test of a 406 MHz distress beacon (aircraft ELT, vessel EPIRB, PLB). Worker runs the beacon self-test, captures the 406 MHz burst and 121.5 MHz homing signal on a beacon tester, verifies the coded identity/registration, battery expiry and G-switch/mount condition, and records the result.

Off-premises field units: highway emergency callboxes, outdoor warning-siren radio controls, remote alerting/telemetry transmitters. Worker drives to the unit at a roadside or public site, activates it, confirms reception and acknowledgement at the dispatch center, checks battery/solar supply and antenna, in whatever weather and layout the site presents.

In-situ readiness check where the emergency set is installed: GMDSS radio and EPIRB on a vessel's bridge and mast, ELT and wiring in an aircraft tail cone or avionics bay, radios in a mobile command vehicle. Cramped, non-standard access; the worker tests the set where it sits and coordinates the live test with the receiving authority.

sources.claim: NOFFZ UTP 9010 RF end-of-line test system performs parallel RF functional tests on eCall modules (the in-vehicle emergency-call transmitter), telematics control units and antenna modules in a shielded RF chamber that can be loaded and operated fully automatically by a robot.

Same measurement content as a readiness test of an emergency transmitter - keying the unit, verifying transmit power/modulation and a successful emergency call - on comparable small RF transceiver hardware, with pass/fail and logging.

sources.system: NOFFZ Universal Wireless Tester with collaborative robot arm
sources.title: RF Tests - NOFFZ Technologies
sources.claim: A collaborative robot arm handles the RF test chamber and the device under test - opening and closing the chamber drawer and inserting and removing the telematics control unit - in NOFFZ's wireless-device test systems.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the physical handling half of a machine-run radio test cell: a robot presents and removes the radio module to the shielded test chamber, the part a technician performs when bench-testing a transmitter.

sources.claim: Rohde & Schwarz's eCall test solution (CMW500 wideband radio communication tester with CMW-KA094 software and a GNSS simulator) verifies that an in-vehicle emergency-call system can initiate an emergency call, transmit the correct minimum set of data and hold voice with a simulated PSAP, run as a fully automated sequence.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: conformance/functional testing of vehicle emergency-call transmitters. It exercises exactly what a readiness test checks - the emergency transmission is triggered, the distress message is received correctly, and voice works - and issues a machine verdict without an operator in the loop.

sources.system: VIAVI 3550R / 8800SX radio test sets with Auto-Test and alignment applications
sources.title: Land Mobile Radio Test | VIAVI Solutions Inc.
sources.claim: VIAVI communications service monitors run OEM-approved Auto-Test applications that execute model-specific test and alignment of land mobile radios - the radios used by police, fire and EMS - and generate the test report, cutting a 60-minute manual procedure to seven to ten minutes ....

sources.claim: ecoATM kiosks autonomously accept a handheld radio device from a member of the public, physically connect to it and run robotic electrical diagnostics plus machine-vision inspection to grade the device, unattended, across a large retail kiosk network (about 7.5 million devices collected in 2025).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended functional/electrical testing of a handheld radio transceiver (a cell phone), including the physical mating of the device to the test interface and an automatic verdict - the same handling-plus-electrical-test loop a bench test of a portable emergency radio requires.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Orbit / AIVI-Learning
sources.title: Boston Dynamics' Spot robot gets AI upgrade for fully automated industrial inspections
sources.claim: Deployed autonomous inspection robots in industrial facilities (Spot with Orbit/AIVI) perform routine rounds reading analogue gauges, indicator lights, thermal and acoustic signatures; the demonstrated capability is sensing and reporting, not connecting test instruments to radio gear or exercising transmitters.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to characterise the ceiling of autonomous robotic work inside structured human facilities (E2): routine sensing rounds, not instrument hookup, keying of transmitters or alignment; it therefore does not substantiate E2 completion of this task.

tasks.label: Test equipment functions such as signal strength and quality, transmission capacity, interference, and signal delay, using equipment such as oscilloscopes, circuit analyzers, frequency meters, and wattmeters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cell site commissioning or trouble call: at the tower base or inside the equipment cabinet in a fenced carrier compound, the tech connects a cable-and-antenna analyzer, PIM tester and wattmeter to jumpers, feedlines and RRU ports, runs swept return-loss/DTF and forward-power measurements, torques connectors and documents results. Outdoor, weather-exposed; cable runs and cabinets vary site to site within a carrier standard.

Tower-top or rooftop testing at 60-300 ft: climb or hoist gear, disconnect the antenna jumper at the antenna port, sweep the antenna and line, isolate PIM/VSWR faults, verify azimuth/tilt and sector-to-port mapping, then reconnect and weatherproof. Wind, height, limited free hands, work positioned on steel.

Shop bench test of two-way portable and mobile radios (public safety, utility, business band): place the radio on the bench, connect a service monitor/communications analyzer, wattmeter and oscilloscope, key the transmitter, measure output power, frequency error, deviation, spurious emissions and receiver sensitivity/SINAD, and align. Many different models and adapters.

Field/vehicle radio system test: emergency, service or fleet vehicle at a station apron, roadside or customer yard, or a remote repeater/mountaintop site. In-line wattmeter and analyzer connected at the antenna feed, VSWR and forward/reflected power checked, receive performance and interference checked; cramped and highly variable access.

Outdoor network coverage and performance verification over the area served by a site or route: measure signal strength and quality, throughput (transmission capacity) and latency (signal delay) with scanners and instrumented handsets along a driven route or flight path after a new site or upgrade, and report against coverage targets.

In-building walk testing and interference hunting: carry test handsets/scanner through a venue, or track down an interferer around a site with a spectrum analyzer and directional antenna, moving among people, floors, stairwells and public ground until the weak-coverage zone or interference source is located.

sources.system: ETS-Lindgren AMS-8050 Antenna Measurement System (multi-axis positioner + EMQuest software)
sources.date: 2026-01 (product page current; product line long commercial)
sources.title: AMS-8050 Antenna Measurement System - ETS-Lindgren
sources.claim: ETS-Lindgren's AMS-8050 is a commercial antenna/OTA measurement system in which a multi-axis positioner moves the wireless device under test inside a shielded chamber while measurement software runs the RF measurements automatically (radiated power, pattern, sensitivity) for design and production testing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated over-the-air/antenna performance measurement of a fixtured radio. It transfers to the technician's bench and antenna tests because the same quantities (transmit/radiated power, pattern, signal quality, receiver sensitivity) are measured on the same class of RF hardware, with the machine positioning the device and the instruments sequenced without an operator.

sources.system: NIST CROMMA / robotic-arm antenna measurement range (MOTOMAN six-axis arm + commercial VNA)
sources.title: Robots Execute Near-Field MM-Wave Measurements | Microwaves & RF
sources.claim: NIST operates antenna measurement ranges in which six-axis industrial robot arms position probes/antennas and a commercial VNA captures amplitude and phase, producing near-field and far-field pattern and gain data automatically inside a purpose-built range.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic antenna metrology. It transfers to the technician's antenna/feedline verification because the robot performs the physical positioning and connection geometry while a vector network analyzer performs exactly the reflection/transmission measurements (return loss, gain, pattern) the technician takes with a cable-and-antenna analyzer.

sources.system: Telescent G4 Network Topology Manager (robotic cross-connect with integrated OTDR/optical power monitoring)
sources.title: Bringing Automation to Physical Fiber Cross Connects | Data Center Frontier
sources.claim: Telescent's G4 Network Topology Manager is a deployed robotic machine that physically mates and re-mates fiber connections with a robotic arm and runs automated end-to-end loss and OTDR/power-monitor testing of those links with no labor time, in data centers and carrier facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic connect-and-test of transmission lines. It transfers to conducted RF line testing because the machine performs the connector mating the technician performs by hand and then runs loss and fault-location measurements (OTDR is the optical analogue of a swept distance-to-fault/return-loss test) to an accepted record, when the plant is built around the machine.

sources.title: Using Drones to Verify Antenna Performance | Microwave Journal
sources.claim: QuadSAT's drone flies pre-planned measurement paths autonomously with an RF payload to verify installed antenna performance in situ - radiation pattern, pointing, cross-polarization and regulatory/interference masks - as a commercial, fully automated field measurement system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-site over-the-air verification of an installed antenna's signal level, pattern and interference compliance. It transfers to the cellular technician's site RF verification for the over-the-air portion only; it does not perform the conducted connector-level sweeps (PIM, DTF, wattmeter) that dominate the tower and compound instances.

sources.title: QuadSAT commercialises its drone-based antenna testing | Electronics Weekly
sources.claim: QuadSAT's system has been used operationally to verify antennas at working satellite ground stations, including in-situ verification of ten antennas at KSAT's Svalbard station.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the autonomous drone RF measurement service is actually run at operating antenna sites (institution-controlled outdoor facilities), not only in a laboratory.

sources.system: R&S TSME/TSMA scanner + QualiPoc handsets on drone (Ericsson coverage verification)
sources.developer: Rohde & Schwarz / Ericsson (with Centria University of Applied Sciences)
sources.title: Ericsson verifies 5G coverage with Rohde & Schwarz drone - GPS World
sources.claim: Ericsson, using Rohde & Schwarz test gear, verified 5G/LTE network coverage and performance with scanners and instrumented handsets mounted on a drone programmed to execute the measurement runs automatically along selected routes, over more than twenty repeatable measurement flights.

sources.system: R&S TSMA6 RF scanner and QualiPoc Android handsets flown on drones
sources.title: Network measurements with drones: The next step to a connected sky | Rohde & Schwarz
sources.claim: Rohde & Schwarz reports field campaigns in which drone-borne RF scanners and instrumented handsets measure LTE coverage, data throughput and latency over real service areas at flight altitude, giving operators and authorities coverage, quality and latency results.

sources.system: Cohu pick-and-place test handlers (Eclipse, Diamondx platforms)
sources.title: Pick and Place Test Handlers | Cohu
sources.claim: Cohu supplies commercial pick-and-place test handlers that physically load wireless/mobility devices into test contactors so that automated RF/electrical test programs run at production throughput.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of a device into a test fixture followed by automated RF/electrical measurement. It transfers to bench radio testing at E1 because the physical act the technician performs - presenting the unit and mating it to the test instrument - is done by the machine, with the measurement sequence run under software.

sources.title: A comprehensive review on deploying robotics application in telecom network tower's field maintenance
sources.claim: A 2023 Journal of Field Robotics review of robotics for telecom tower field maintenance analyses climbing robots only at the level of literature designs and feasibility for the required at-height operations, indicating no fielded tower-climbing robot performing technician work.
sources.transferJustification: Context for a negative judgment only: tower-access robots remain design studies, so no cited system performs conducted testing at height in a carrier compound (E2).

tasks.label: Turn setscrews to adjust receivers for maximum sensitivity and transmitters for maximum output.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop bench alignment/peak-up of a two-way mobile or portable radio: unit clamped on the bench with cover off, service monitor, wattmeter and dummy load connected; technician turns trimmer screws, coil slugs and output-adjust pots with a tuning tool to peak receiver sensitivity (12 dB SINAD) and transmitter power/deviation, then re-checks against factory spec.

Shop-bench tuning of a duplexer, cavity filter bank or transmitter combiner for a repeater/base station: turn the tuning rods/screws with a wrench while watching a service monitor or vector network analyzer to place pass and reject notches, peak insertion loss and isolation, then tighten the locking setscrews/nuts.

On-site peaking inside a tower-site equipment shelter or outdoor cabinet: rack-mounted repeater, base station, preselector or duplexer adjusted in place against the installed antenna line and real interference environment, in cramped rack space at a carrier- or agency-controlled site.

Mobile radio installed in a service or emergency vehicle: radio deck under a seat, in the trunk or in a console; technician adjusts output/deviation and receiver alignment and trims the antenna setscrew for lowest SWR, working in a fleet garage or on the lot with the vehicle interior as found.

High-power transmitter plant work: adjusting tune/load controls, coil tap setscrews, coupling and matching-network adjustments in a broadcast transmitter or antenna tuning unit so the transmitter delivers maximum output into the antenna system, at a transmitter building or ATU enclosure.

sources.system: Autonomous RF cavity filter tuning system (COBOT + multi-axis arms + Cartesian platform, VNA in loop)
sources.developer: Yarkin Yigit and Engin Afacan (published in Journal of Field Robotics)
sources.title: A Fully Automated Robotic System for Tuning Optimization of RF Cavity Filter - Journal of Field Robotics
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robotic cell tunes RF cavity filters (the filters used in transmitters and receivers) by turning their tuning screws while a vector network analyzer measures S-parameters in the loop, with vision for screw location and force-torque sensing, including handling the screw-locking step.
sources.transferJustification: Same act as the task: turning tuning/setscrews on receiver and transmitter RF hardware to peak measured performance, closed-loop on instrument readings, in a fixtured cell.

sources.developer: INOVEOS with CISTEME, XLIM and INRIA
sources.title: Revolutionizing Microwave Filter Tuning with an Automated Robotic Solution - Inoveos
sources.claim: An industrial microwave filter tuning robot acts directly on each tuning screw, comparing live S-parameter measurements against the target specification and converting the computed electromagnetic correction into mechanical screw motion; it supports various tuning screw sizes and locking mechanisms across filter types and bands.
sources.transferJustification: Directly comparable: screw-by-screw adjustment of RF filter hardware to maximize measured passband performance for transmit/receive chains on a production line.

sources.system: Robot cavity filter tuning system with DDPG-based continuous RL controller
sources.title: Learning Human Strategies for Tuning Cavity Filters with Continuous Reinforcement Learning
sources.claim: A robotic cavity-filter tuning system with a three-axis arm and screw-rotation servo learns tuning policies by reinforcement learning, replicating what a technician does when he watches the S-parameter curve on a network analyzer and adjusts the filter's screws with a screwdriver.
sources.transferJustification: Corroborates that screw-turning to peak RF performance against instrument feedback is done autonomously by robots, not merely simulated.

sources.system: Vision-based mobile robotic manipulation system for assembly screwdriving
sources.title: From perception to precision: Vision-based mobile robotic manipulation for assembly screwdriving - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A vision-guided mobile manipulator performs high-precision screwdriving on assemblies using monocular RGB perception, aimed at low-volume, high-mix production where rigid fixtured cells are impractical; work still occurs on a manufacturing shop floor with known assemblies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (locating and driving small screws under vision without hard fixturing); supports the manipulation element but not the RF instrument-in-the-loop tuning of arbitrary radios in a shop or vehicle.

roles.description: Install, set up, rearrange, or remove switching, distribution, routing, and dialing equipment used in central offices or headends. Service or repair telephone, cable television, Internet, and other communications equipment on customers' property. May install communications equipment or communications wiring in buildings.

tasks.label: Note differences in wire and cable colors so that work can be performed correctly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/small-business service call: at a jack, NID, or patch panel the technician looks at the color-coded conductors of a twisted-pair drop (blue/white, orange/white, etc.) and notes which color pair goes to which pin/terminal before terminating, so the pinout follows T568A/B or the local convention.

Building telecom closet / MDU riser work: technician reads binder-group and jacket colors on multi-pair copper or the color-coded buffer tubes and fiber strands in a distribution cable, comparing what is seen against labels and as-built documentation to determine which count belongs to which unit or circuit.

Central office or cable headend: technician traces cross-connect jumpers and cable pair colors on a main distribution frame or in a routing bay, noting color differences between existing and new runs so the correct pair/port is worked on during a rearrangement or equipment turn-up.

Outside plant terminal, pedestal, aerial splice case, or crawlspace: technician notes conductor and cable colors under poor lighting, in weather, or on dirty/aged cable where colors are faded, oxidized, or obscured by grease or tracer stripes.

Troubleshooting a previously installed system where prior work used nonstandard, mismatched, or undocumented color conventions; the technician notes the discrepancy between the observed colors and the expected scheme and records/communicates it so the repair or re-termination is done correctly.

tasks.label: Test circuits and components of malfunctioning telecommunications equipment to isolate sources of malfunctions, using test meters, circuit diagrams, polarity probes, and other hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential trouble call: technician at a private home tests the coax/fiber drop, ground block, splitters, NID/ONT, in-home wiring and the modem/STB with a signal level meter, DMM and toner to isolate whether the fault is in the drop, the premises wiring or the customer device; clutter, pets, crawlspaces, no two homes alike.

Business or MDU premises: technician works a telecom/equipment room or riser closet, testing copper pairs, punch-down blocks, patch panels, Ethernet runs, PBX/VoIP ports and station equipment with butt set, tone-and-probe, cable certifier and DMM, referencing circuit diagrams and cable records to isolate the failing pair/port.

Central office or cable headend: technician isolates a fault in rack-mounted switching/transport equipment — suspect line/interface cards, backplanes, fuses and -48V power feeds, cross-connects at the frame — using test sets, DMM, polarity probes and schematics, then narrows to the failing card or component.

Central office, hut or headend optical plant: isolating loss, dirty connectors or a break on a fiber circuit by connecting OTDR/optical power meter test gear onto the circuit at the fiber cross-connect and interpreting the trace to locate the fault.

Outside access points on operator plant: pedestal, cross-box, tap, vault or building entrance terminal — technician opens the enclosure and tests signal levels, continuity, polarity and pair integrity in weather, roadside or backyard conditions to isolate the fault segment.

Bench/depot repair: failed telecom units and circuit boards (line cards, modems, amplifiers, STBs) are tested at a shop workbench with DMM, probes, scope and schematics to identify the faulty component or trace before repair or scrap.

sources.title: Flying Probe Tester for electronic boards PCB | SPEA
sources.claim: SPEA flying probe testers automatically move probes onto board nets and components to detect shorts, opens and faulty components, and are used in a repair workflow to give a precise diagnosis of the ...; heavy boards are loaded automatically by an input conveyor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated electrical test of printed circuit assemblies. It is the same operation as the human task — contacting nets/components with probes, taking electrical measurements against a known circuit description, and naming the failing part — on the same class of objects (telecom line cards, modems and amplifiers are PCBs), at finer precision, in a purpose-built enclosure.

sources.title: In-Circuit testing: detecting electronic board defects | SPEA
sources.claim: SPEA in-circuit testers run with minimal operator intervention using automatic board loaders/unloaders and robot integration, performing electrical measurement of components on boards to detect defects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-circuit electrical test of assembled boards. Same measurement operations (continuity, isolation, component value, polarity) that the technician performs with meters and polarity probes, and it establishes that the work arrives at the machine and is tested without step-by-step human control.

sources.system: Telescent G4/G5 Network Topology Manager (robotic patch panel)
sources.title: Smart Patch Panels: Revolutionizing Fiber Optic Network Management — Telescent
sources.claim: Telescent's robotic fiber patch panel physically reconfigures fiber connections on software command and includes power monitoring and an optional OTDR so that link diagnostics and fault location can be run on demand without a technician connecting test gear on site.

sources.system: Telescent G4 NTM with EXFO remote fiber testing
sources.title: Latest News — Telescent

sources.title: Microsoft Research details early-stage modular robotics for data centers - DCD
sources.claim: The most advanced in-rack robot work in live network facilities is Microsoft Research's transceiver manipulation robot, a research prototype that navigates cluttered cabling to reseat or swap optical transceivers; it performs no meter-based circuit or component testing.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only as the state of the art for in-situ robot work at equipment racks (an E2 human facility); it substantiates connector handling, not testing circuits or components with meters to isolate a malfunction, so it does not support a positive judgment for this task.

sources.system: Robotic arm-assisted PCB diagnostic and measurement system (Dobot Magician + Arduino)
sources.title: Implementation of a Robotic Arm-Assisted PCB Diagnostic and Measurement System | IJARIS
sources.claim: A research prototype couples a Dobot Magician arm to a measurement board to place probes on PCB test points and take voltage and resistance readings, but positions are taught by playback and accuracy is well below a calibrated multimeter.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same operation (robotic probing with a meter at circuit test points), but taught-playback control and 2–12% measurement error mean it is treated as scripted and does not support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Drive crew trucks to and from work areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine daytime drive in a metro/suburban service territory: leave the company garage or previous job, drive a service van or light bucket truck over residential streets and arterials to a subscriber home or small business, and park at the curb or in the driveway; fair weather, ordinary traffic; several such hops per day plus the return to the yard.

Drive into a dense urban core to a commercial building, central office, headend or MDU: heavy traffic, one-way streets, transit and pedestrians, ending at a loading zone, dock, alley or parking structure near the equipment room.
Evening, night or rainy-weather drive over the same metro/suburban territory: after-hours trouble call, overtime return trip, wet pavement, glare and darkness.

Rural/exurban run: two-lane county highways, then unpaved gravel or dirt access tracks, farm lanes and easements to a remote subscriber, pedestal, cabinet or tower site; no lane markings or curbs, gates, ruts, livestock and slow farm equipment; destinations vary trip to trip.

Storm or outage-restoration driving: snow, ice, high wind or post-storm conditions with downed lines, tree debris, flooded sections, closed roads and improvised detours; convoy travel to a staging area at odd hours.

Yard, depot and on-site vehicle handling: entering the fenced company yard, driving to the materials cage or loading bay, backing the truck into a bay or between parked vehicles, staging and repositioning the truck inside a controlled lot or work area.

sources.title: Waymo goes driverless in Las Vegas, with Denver, San Diego, Tampa next

sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving a road vehicle from an origin to a requested address on public roads and pulling over at the destination. This is the same act the telecom technician performs with a crew truck; the destination set (homes, businesses, downtown addresses) and the road environment are the same, and the vehicle is operated with a human occupant aboard.

sources.title: Waymo Safety Impact
sources.claim: Waymo's driverless fleet has accumulated over 220 million rider-only miles on public roads without a human driver in the vehicle, giving a large, audited record of at-scale road driving reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (point-to-point road driving); the mileage figure establishes that the driving is sustained and at worker-comparable crash rates rather than a one-off demonstration.

sources.title: Creating an all-weather Driver

sources.transferJustification: Related task: night and wet-weather road driving. Technician trips at night or in rain occur on the same streets with the same vehicle dynamics, so weather/darkness competence transfers directly.

sources.title: Gatik Becomes First U.S. Company to Operate Fully Driverless Trucks at Scale for Commercial Deliveries

sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving a work truck of similar class and size (26-30 ft box truck vs. service van/bucket truck) over public surface streets and highways to a commercial destination and up to a dock/lot. Vehicle mass, turning behavior and destination handling match a telecom crew truck more closely than a passenger car does.

sources.title: Aurora Begins Commercial Driverless Trucking in Texas, Ushering in a New Era of Freight
sources.claim: Aurora runs commercial driverless Class 8 trucks with no human in the ... on public Texas highways between Dallas and Houston, showing sustained highway-speed autonomous operation of a heavy work vehicle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: long-distance highway driving of a heavy truck on public roads, the freeway leg of a crew truck's trip to a distant work area.

sources.developer: Kodiak Robotics with Atlas Energy Solutions

sources.title: ISEE And TICO Partner To Deliver Autonomous Yard Trucks To Customers
sources.claim: ISEE has multiple fully driverless yard trucks operating in mixed-traffic logistics yards at active customer sites (Maersk, Lazer Spot and Fortune 100 retailers), performing hundreds of thousands of autonomous moves including docking and backing among people and human-driven vehicles.

tasks.label: Assemble and install communication equipment such as data and telephone communication lines, wiring, switching equipment, wiring frames, power apparatus, computer systems, and networks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential premises install/turn-up: tech arrives at a single-family home or apartment, mounts an ONT/NID or cable NID, drills a wall penetration, runs and staples a drop/coax/fiber inside, installs and grounds the modem/gateway/router and set-top, terminates or re-uses in-home jacks, tests signal levels and activates service. Clutter, pets, crawlspaces, attics, varying wiring vintages.

Small business/commercial premises install: tech installs a customer-side router/switch, VoIP phones, media converter or NIU in a telecom closet; punches down or patches at 66/110 blocks or a patch panel, runs short cable runs above ceiling tiles or in raceway, labels and tests circuits during business hours in an occupied office, clinic, or retail store.

Structured cabling build in a commercial building under construction or renovation: pull hundreds of Cat6/fiber runs through ceiling voids, J-hooks, sleeves and conduits, install and anchor racks/cabinets and cable tray, terminate patch panels and jacks, dress and label, then certify links. Site is an active jobsite with other trades, debris, and ladders/lifts.

Central office, headend, or data hall equipment installation: bolt and align relay racks/frames, mount switching or transmission shelves and line cards, install DC power feeds, fuse/breaker panels and battery leads, install cable racking and run/dress/tie power and signal cable to frames, ground and test the installation to carrier (NEBS/COP) standards inside a live, secured facility.

Circuit turn-up and rearrangement wiring at fiber/copper distribution frames in a central office or colocation facility: run, route and terminate jumpers/cross-connects between designated ports on the ODF/MDF or patch panels, verify continuity/loss, update records — a repeat, high-volume 'install the wiring' activity in an institution-controlled equipment room.

Outside-plant node, street cabinet, rooftop or small-cell electronics install: mount and wire node/cabinet electronics, power supplies and battery backup, land fiber and coax/copper, in a curbside cabinet, pedestal, pole-mounted enclosure or rooftop, in weather and traffic.

sources.system: Telescent G5 robotic cross-connect / optical circuit switch platform
sources.title: Telescent Introduces Highest Density Optical Circuit Switches for 1.6T DR4 and DR8 Interconnects in GPU Clusters
sources.claim: Telescent continues to ship higher-density robotic cross-connect systems for carrier and AI data center fiber plant, automating circuit turn-up and reconfiguration of large fiber counts.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the G4 item: automated physical-layer patching is the wiring-frame cross-connect element of this task, performed inside a purpose-built robotic panel.

sources.system: DeWalt autonomous drilling robot (with August Robotics)

sources.title: Microsoft Research details early-stage modular robotics for data centers
sources.claim: Microsoft Research has built early-stage prototype data center robots, including a transceiver manipulation robot that uses vision to navigate cluttered cabling and reseat, plug or unplug an optical transceiver.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: plugging optics into live network gear. It is an unproven prototype covering one sub-step (a transceiver insertion), not assembly and installation of equipment, wiring, frames or power apparatus.

sources.title: Video shows robotic installation Cat 6 cabling above drop ceiling
sources.claim: The demonstrated robots for running communication cable above suspended ceilings are small remote-controlled platforms driven by a human operator watching a video feed, not autonomous installers.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (pulling Cat 6 above a drop ceiling), but the platform is operator-driven by remote control and only tows a cable; it does not terminate, dress, or certify, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Hilti unveils new robot-powered drilling capabilities
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot semi-autonomous mobile drilling robot is used commercially on construction projects to drill overhead holes for mechanical, electrical and ... installation contractors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: overhead anchor-hole drilling that precedes hanging cable tray and conduit. It is a marking/drilling aid under operator supervision and performs none of the cable pulling, termination, or equipment mounting in this task.

tasks.label: Run wires between components and to outside cable systems, connecting them to wires from telephone poles or underground cable accesses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-family residential service drop: tech runs an aerial coax/fiber drop from the tap on a telephone pole (or a buried drop from a curbside pedestal/handhole) across the yard to the house, attaches hardware to the fascia, connects to the NID/ground block/ONT, drills the wall entry and connects the drop to the inside wire; weather, dogs, landscaping, varied house construction.

Inside-premises wiring in an occupied home: running coax/Cat6/fiber between components (ONT to router, splitters, amplifiers, set-tops, wall jacks), fishing walls, crawl spaces and attics, stapling and dressing wire, terminating both ends and verifying the path back to the demarc.

Multi-dwelling unit: running wire from the building demarc/lockbox or riser telecom closet through corridors, conduits and risers to a specific apartment, then to the subscriber's equipment; managed building, but tight, non-standard risers and tenant units.

Business/enterprise premises: running backbone and horizontal cable through ceilings, cable trays, conduits and risers between the equipment room and workstation outlets/components, and out to the building entrance facility where the carrier's underground or aerial cable terminates.

Central office, headend, or carrier/colo equipment room: running and re-running cross-connect jumpers and patch cords on distribution frames and patch panels between equipment ports and the terminations of outside plant cable arriving from the cable vault/underground access; connections tested and documented.

sources.system: Telescent G4/G5 Network Topology Manager (robotic patch panel)
sources.title: Why Automate Your Fiber Optic Infrastructure? — Telescent
sources.claim: Telescent's robotic patch panel physically grabs fiber jumper ends and re-routes them to a requested port under software control, performing add/move/drop cross-connects without a technician; NEBS Level 3 certified with over a billion port hours in operation.
sources.transferJustification: Same task at the frame: physically running and connecting a jumper between equipment ports and outside-plant terminations, the central-office/headend form of this task.

sources.title: Telescent's Automated Fiber Patch-Panel Solution Will be Highlighted at the 2023 Open Compute Project (OCP) Regional Summit
sources.claim: The Telescent robotic cross-connect platform is in commercial field deployment with network operators, not a laboratory demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployment maturity of the robotic patch panel that performs frame jumper/cross-connect work.

sources.title: Rittal Kiesling Product portfolio
sources.claim: Kiesling/Rittal's Averex robotic wiring centre automatically wires fixtured mounting plates: it cuts, strips and crimps each wire, routes it through cable ducts and connects it ...' terminals, in a purpose-built machine cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: running and terminating wires between components mounted on a fixtured panel. Comparable objects (insulated conductors, screw/spring terminals) and finer precision than telecom cross-connect termination, but only in a fixtured factory cell.

sources.title: Bombyx is being licensed for product development - Engineering at Meta
sources.claim: Meta's Bombyx robot crawls along medium-voltage power lines helically wrapping fiber cable and passing poles; it remained an R&D project licensed out for product development, and it deploys line-route fiber rather than making drop connections at a pole or premises.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: installing aerial cable along utility lines. Cited to show the closest outdoor field system does not make drop or component connections, so it cannot substantiate completing field instances.

sources.system: Cable-laying robot based on reconfigurable single-actuator-wave units
sources.title: Development of Cable-Laying Robot Based on Reconfigurable Single-Actuator-Wave Units
sources.claim: Automating the pulling of cables over cable racks and through ceiling spaces inside buildings is still a research problem, addressed by newly developed prototype robots rather than deployed products.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pulling cable through building pathways. Cited as evidence that in-building cable running remains a prototype capability, supporting negative judgments.

tasks.label: Inspect equipment on a regular basis to ensure proper functioning.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine inspection round in a telephone central office or cable headend: walking rack rows and the DC power plant, checking status/alarm LEDs and alarm panels, reading rectifier and battery-plant meters, feeling/listening for failed fans, checking rack temperatures, HVAC and cable trays, and logging anomalies for follow-up. Carrier-controlled, badge-access building with fixed aisle layout.

Periodic inspection of telecom rooms in an institutional or commercial building (office tower, hospital, campus, hotel): visiting multiple MDF/IDF closets on several floors, checking PBX/VoIP gateways, switches, patch panels, UPS status lights, closet temperature, dressing of jumpers, and confirming no alarms. Requires moving through corridors, elevators and locked closet doors.

Scheduled inspection of routing/switching and transport equipment in a data center, colocation hall or carrier network hub: aisle walk-throughs verifying line-card and optic status LEDs, thermal checks of racks and cabling, fan/PDU condition, environment readings, alerting on anomalies.

Inspection at a residential subscriber's premises during a routine/repeat service visit: verifying the modem/gateway/ONT/set-top box powers up and functions, reading status lights and diagnostics, checking connector seating, ground block, splitters and inside wiring, and measuring signal/power levels with a hand meter. Cluttered, variable homes with pets, furniture, crawl spaces.

Field inspection of outside-plant active equipment: HFC nodes, roadside cabinets, standby power supplies and batteries, pedestals and vaults along streets and easements — opening cabinet doors, checking status LEDs and meters, looking for corrosion, water intrusion, heat and loose connections, in all weather and traffic conditions.

Periodic visual inspection of cell-site and rooftop equipment: antennas, remote radio units, mounts, jumpers, waveguide/coax runs, grounding and weatherproofing on towers, monopoles and rooftops, checking for rust, misalignment, damaged connectors or loose hardware at sites taken as found.

sources.title: Digital Realty deploying Anybotics robot dogs in Swiss data center - DCD
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal quadruped has run daily autonomous inspection missions in Digital Realty's Zurich data center since 2022, monitoring up to 70 elements with visual, thermal and acoustic measurements and alerting operators to overheating cables or abnormal vibration — the same kind of rack/power/HVAC round a central-office technician performs.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (recurring equipment-condition inspection rounds) on comparable assets: racked electronic equipment, DC power and cooling plant in a badge-controlled machine hall, which is the same equipment class and precision demand as a telecom central office or headend round.

sources.system: Spot with Spot Arm / Autowalk / Orbit
sources.title: The Next Step in Safe, Autonomous Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs autonomous Autowalk inspection missions covering thermal monitoring, acoustic leak detection ..., and can now use its arm to open doors autonomously ... those missions, letting it move room-to-room on inspection routes.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class — scheduled inspection rounds reading indicator/gauge state and thermal condition of industrial equipment — with door opening enabling closet- and cabinet-level access comparable to telecom rooms and outside-plant enclosures brought into a facility.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor security robot autonomously patrols corporate office buildings on scheduled routes doing facility checks, calling elevators via the Otis dispatch API for multi-floor patrols and opening doors via access-control integration or its arm; remote specialists only handle escalated events.

sources.developer: Boston Dynamics; Ghost Robotics (data center operators)
sources.title: Meet the $300K Robot Dogs Guarding Massive Data Centers | eWeek
sources.claim: Robot dogs including Spot are being deployed by data center operators to navigate halls, inspect equipment, and flag leaks and temperature anomalies in real time while humans ... remotely.

sources.title: Scaling Cell Tower Inspections with 3D Tower Scan | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio's 3D Tower Capture is an autonomous capture mode of 3D Scan optimized for vertical ..., used commercially to scan cell towers and produce inspection-grade digital twins of tower-mounted telecom equipment without expert waypoint programming.
sources.transferJustification: Same task on the same assets: recurring visual condition inspection of antennas, radios, mounts and jumpers at cell sites, performed at outdoor sites taken as found rather than in a prepared setting.

sources.title: Testing & Grading - Reconext
sources.claim: Reconext's Titan is a deployed automated test platform for customer-premises equipment (modems, gateways, set-top boxes) with up to 24 test ..., delivering objective functional, cosmetic and diagnostic evaluations of the devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (automated functional and cosmetic evaluation of modems, gateways and set-top boxes in a fixtured test cell) covers exactly the 'ensure proper functioning' judgment a technician makes on the same CPE devices, when the device is presented to the machine.

sources.title: Turn Your Old Phone Into Cash: Everything About ecoATM Recycling
sources.claim: ecoATM's kiosks autonomously inspect a consumer electronic device placed in an evaluation chamber — scanning it, testing power-on, checking screen and buttons and assessing physical condition — in roughly a minute, at more than 7,000 retail locations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous physical + functional inspection of a small consumer electronics unit in a purpose-built chamber) transfers to verifying proper functioning of subscriber equipment of comparable size, ports and inspection criteria when the unit is brought to the machine.

sources.title: Automated Visual Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics markets Spot for autonomous facility-wide visual inspection with a 25x PTZ camera and integrated gauge-reading models that convert analog displays into digital readings.

tasks.label: Collaborate with other workers to locate and correct malfunctions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service call: premises technician on the phone/app with dispatch, a NOC engineer, or a partner tech at the node/tap to isolate a broadband/TV/voice fault - checks signal levels and error counts, then corrects it by re-terminating or replacing the drop connector/splitter, repairing inside wiring, or swapping the modem/ONT/set-top, and confirms restoral with the remote worker.

Business or MDU premises: tech works with the customer's IT staff or a second tech, one at the telecom room and one at the workstation/jack, to trace a dead port or noisy line - tone and test pairs, reseat/replace patch cords, re-terminate jacks or 110 blocks, swap a switch module or phone set, then verify end to end.

Central office / headend equipment fault: CO tech and remote NOC engineer work an alarmed circuit - run loopbacks and section tests, isolate to a failed line card, pluggable optic, amplifier, or power feed in a shelf, physically replace the module, restore service and confirm with the far-end worker.

Central office / headend / colo physical fiber-path fault: tech and remote engineer isolate a circuit problem to the cross-connect fiber path (high loss, dirty or damaged jumper, mis-patch shown by OTDR/power readings) and correct it by re-patching the cross-connect or rerouting to a spare fiber, re-testing the link with the remote worker.

Outside plant coordination: two techs, one at a pedestal, aerial terminal, or manhole and one at the CO/node, tone and test copper pairs or fiber to localize the fault, then repair it - re-splice, replace a terminal or corroded connector, swap an amplifier or power supply - in weather, at height, or in traffic.

Cell site, remote terminal, or node cabinet: technician at the site coordinates with the NOC to isolate a failed radio, optic, rectifier, or battery string in the cabinet, replaces the unit, re-cables it, and confirms the alarm clears with the remote worker.

sources.system: Telescent G5 Network Topology Manager (robotic fiber cross-connect)
sources.title: G5 Network Topology Manager (NTM) Product Data Sheet
sources.claim: Telescent's G5 Network Topology Manager is a commercial robotic fiber patch panel/cross-connect: an embedded pick-and-place robot reconfigures physical fiber connections on software command, with automated optical power and OTDR monitoring of all connections used to diagnose link faults remotely; the platform is stated to be deployed in critical production networks.
sources.transferJustification: Same task element: locating a physical-layer fault (OTDR/OPM diagnostics) and correcting it by changing the fiber cross-connect - the fiber-jumper work a CO technician performs jointly with a remote engineer.

sources.title: MOX Signs Agreement to Deploy Telescent's Fiber Automation Platform on its Next-Generation Long-Haul Route
sources.claim: A carrier (MOX Networks) deployed Telescent's G4 NTM robotic patch panel on a live long-haul route, giving remote engineers physical-layer diagnostics and remote re-patching of customer circuits - production use of robotic fiber fault handling in carrier facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Deployment evidence for the same diagnose-and-re-patch fiber work; the pick-and-place robot executes commanded connection changes itself rather than under continuous teleoperation.

sources.title: Overview ROME - Robotic Optical Management Engine (datasheet)
sources.claim: Wave2Wave's ROME is a commercial layer-0 robotic optical switch that makes and breaks physical fiber connections automatically and remotely without on-site manual intervention, corroborating robotic fiber re-patching as an available product class.
sources.transferJustification: Same corrective action as a CO technician re-jumpering a cross-connect to clear or bypass a faulty fiber path.

sources.system: MSR transceiver-manipulation and fiber/transceiver cleaning robots ('self-maintaining systems')
sources.title: Microsoft Research details early-stage modular robotics for data centers
sources.claim: Microsoft Research has built datacenter maintenance robots that autonomously navigate cluttered cabling to reseat, plug or unplug optical transceivers and to inspect and clean fiber end faces - corrective maintenance on network hardware, but explicitly still prototypes.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic analogue to a technician replacing a failed pluggable optic or cleaning a dirty connector in a CO/headend shelf; cited to show the capability exists only at prototype maturity, not worker quality.

sources.title: Future AI Infrastructure - Microsoft Research: Robotics
sources.claim: Microsoft Research describes its datacenter robots as autonomously manipulating optical transceivers and cables and performing fiber cleaning and installation in densely packed racks - research-stage capability aimed at self-maintaining networks.
sources.transferJustification: Corrective maintenance on communications hardware (transceivers, fiber) with comparable objects and precision to CO equipment repair, but demonstrated only as research prototypes.

sources.title: 5 Things You Can't Automate In Your Data Center
sources.claim: Industry reporting on datacenter automation states that hands-on corrective hardware work - swapping failed components, replacing worn cables and power ..., changing network cards - is still done by human technicians, with robots rare inside these facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Negative evidence bearing on whether a robot can perform corrective equipment repair inside a structured technical facility (E2).

sources.title: Automated Visual Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot is a commercially deployed quadruped that autonomously runs inspection missions in industrial facilities, detecting and reporting visual/thermal/acoustic anomalies - it locates problems but performs no corrective repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous anomaly-detection rounds in institution-controlled facilities) covers only the 'locate' half of this task; no corrective manipulation is performed.

tasks.label: Climb poles and ladders, use truck-mounted booms, and enter areas such as manholes and cable vaults to install, maintain, or inspect equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential/small-business service call: set and foot an extension ladder against a house, climb to the drop-attachment point, eave, or roof; attach or replace the aerial drop hook/clamp, route and fasten coax or fiber down the fascia, terminate connectors at the NID/ground block, bond it, and test the line. Ladder footing, siding type, foliage, weather and pets all vary site to site.

Climb a wood utility pole (hooks/gaffs, or a ladder set to the pole) at the roadside to reach the aerial terminal, tap, splitter or pedestal riser: connect or disconnect a customer drop, replace a corroded tap/terminal housing, re-seal, take signal-level readings, and clear trouble. Traffic, energized power in the supply space, other carriers' attachments, and midspan clearance all in play.

Truck-mounted boom/bucket work on aerial plant: position the aerial device at a roadside pole or midspan, replace or install a line amplifier, node, power supply, or aerial splice closure on the strand, lash or re-lash cable, open the closure, splice/re-terminate, weatherproof and test.

Underground plant: open a street manhole or handhole, gas-test, ventilate and enter the confined space; rack cable, open a splice case, pull or place cable through duct, repair a damaged sheath or fiber, re-seal and pump/clean the vault. Standing water, mud, debris and traffic control are routine.

Inspection/survey-only visit to aerial plant: ascend by climb or bucket (or otherwise reach) pole-, strand- or tower-mounted equipment to visually assess condition after storms, for attachment/post-construction audits, or for damage assessment, and document defects with photos and a report. No hardware is changed.

Central office / building entrance facility: descend into the cable vault, riser or equipment room to inspect cable and equipment condition (water intrusion, corrosion, hot spots, labeling, rack integrity), walk the route and report findings to engineering.

sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot runs unattended autonomous inspection missions (Autowalk) across a large industrial facility, doing anomaly detection, thermal inspection and gauge reading inside a controlled work facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine equipment-condition inspection rounds inside an industrial facility. Transfers to walking a central-office equipment room/cable vault route: same indoor structured premises, same visual/thermal condition assessment output, no manipulation required.

sources.system: Spot / Spark / Bolt quadrupeds at BC Hydro
sources.title: Four legs, high-tech: How BC Hydro is using robotics to improve safety
sources.claim: A utility used a Spot quadruped, lowered into an underground vault, ... scan the confined space and build a 3D model so engineers could plan repairs without a human entry; the same fleet performs automated substation patrols.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: underground utility vault condition scanning. Shows a legged robot can substitute for a human confined-space entry for inspection purposes, but the release does not establish the vault run was autonomous rather than driven, and no manipulation (splicing, cable racking) was performed.

sources.title: 3D Tower Capture: 3D Scan Gets Smarter With Telecommunication Towers | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio's 3D Scan / 3D Tower Capture autonomously plans and flies a complete photo capture of vertical structures including telecommunications towers, producing digital twins used for post-construction audits and annual inspections in place of climbs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial-structure visual inspection. Transfers to inspection-only ascents on poles/strand-mounted plant: same outdoor roadside structures, same deliverable (imagery/defect documentation), no physical contact needed.

sources.system: Skydio X10 distribution-network inspection program (American Electric Power)
sources.title: Autonomous drones for faster, safer utility inspection | Skydio
sources.claim: Utilities run production drone programs for distribution-network (pole and line) inspection with Skydio autonomous aircraft, tracking mileage flown and reliability savings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inspecting pole-mounted distribution assets outdoors at height. Same roadside pole environment and same visual condition-assessment output as a telecom inspection climb.

sources.title: Meta Bombyx & SLAM | Slamcore
sources.claim: Meta's Bombyx robot crawls along medium-voltage distribution lines wrapping fiber-optic cable, passing obstacles autonomously; it completed R&D and was licensed for product development in 2023. It places cable only and is set on and taken off the line by crews.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial cable placement from the line itself. Closest system to bucket-truck aerial work, but it only wraps cable — it does not mount, open, splice, seal or test aerial equipment — and crews must deploy and retrieve it, so it cannot complete the boom instance.

sources.title: ATC uses drone to install bird diverters for the first time – ATC
sources.claim: FulcrumAir's LineFly/Mini LineFly is a drone-carried robot that autonomously installs bird-flight diverters in sequence on energized overhead transmission conductors, used in utility projects in the US and Canada.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous installation of hardware onto overhead lines. It installs one purpose-designed clip-on device with a dedicated machine; it cannot prepare cable, terminate connectors, mount and seal a tap/amplifier or test, so it does not carry over to pole-top or boom equipment work.

sources.title: SOLO® Pipeline Inspection Robot CCTV | RedZone Robotics
sources.claim: RedZone Robotics' SOLO is a commercially deployed crawler launched into a manhole that then traverses and inspects sewer pipeline autonomously, without a human entering the confined space.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inspection launched from a street manhole. It shows entry and travel can be automated, but it only images pipe interiors; it performs no cable racking, splicing, sealing or repair, so it cannot complete telecom manhole work.

sources.system: 10 kV live-working robot with four-dimensional safety framework
sources.title: Research on Live Working Robots for 10 KV Distribution Networks Adopting Four-Dimensional Safety Guarantee Framework
sources.claim: State-of-the-art 10 kV distribution live-line work robots mounted on aerial platforms are operated by humans via remote/MR control during field verification, not autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pole-top manipulation from a boom. The most advanced fielded pole-top manipulators remain teleoperated, confirming that boom-based and pole-top equipment work is not autonomously completed.

tasks.label: Test connections to ensure that power supplies are adequate and that communications links function.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential install/repair (cable/fiber/DSL): after hooking up a drop, tech checks the AC outlet/grounding and the ONT/modem power supply or battery backup, connects a signal level meter or optical power meter at the ground block, ONT or splitter, plugs a tester/laptop into the modem, and confirms levels and that the link comes up. Cramped, varied, homeowner-controlled spaces.

Business/enterprise or MDU premises: certify newly installed copper and fiber links in a telecom room with a cable certifier/OTDR, verify PoE injectors and UPS/power feeds to equipment, patch to switch ports and confirm each link and VoIP set registers. Central office, headend or carrier data center: verify -48 VDC plant, rectifier/fuse and breaker positions and battery voltage at the power board with a DMM, then verify the transport circuit (optical power/OTDR trace, BER or loopback test on the new cross-connect) before turning the circuit up.

Outside plant field work: at a pedestal, tap, aerial node or cabinet, check standby power supply output and battery string voltage, test the coax/copper pair or fiber for continuity, loss and signal level, and confirm the link back to the node/CO. Roadside, weather, traffic, corroded and non-standard hardware.

Cell site / rooftop or tower-mounted equipment: check DC power plant and rectifier output and breaker feeds to radios, sweep or OTDR the coax/fiber runs to the antennas, and confirm the backhaul link and radios come online. Fenced operator-controlled compound with standard cabinets, but work outdoors and at height.

Cleaning tools after dirty jobs at the shop bench (parts washer available): crimpers, coring and cable-prep tools, dies, strippers, drill bits, fish tape, sockets and hardware caked with mud, grease and cable flooding compound are degreased/washed, dried, and returned to the tool kit.

Care of test equipment at the bench or in the central office: after fiber jobs the tech cleans and inspects the optical ports of the OTDR/OLTS/power meter and the end faces of launch cords and reference jumpers with a connector cleaner and video inspection scope, repeating until they pass cleanliness/loss checks, then re-caps and cases them.

sources.claim: Dusty Robotics' FieldPrinter 2 is an autonomous mobile robot ... localizes itself (laser tracker plus onboard sensors) and prints full-scale building-model geometry, points and text on the floor at 1/16 inch accuracy; the product is commercially deployed across building interiors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated building layout. It substitutes for exactly the manual step in this task - measuring off reference points and marking where equipment gets installed - with better precision, unattended over whole floors.

sources.title: Dusty Robotics Scales Project Layout Automation | For Construction Pros
sources.claim: Dusty's FieldPrinter replaces string-line-and-chalk manual layout, is about ten times faster than the human method, achieves 1/16 inch accuracy, and had been used by contractors on 25 million square feet ... in a single quarter.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: manual measure-and-mark layout. The cited comparison is to the identical human method (tape/string measurement from reference lines to mark installation positions), establishing worker-quality substitution at scale.

sources.title: HP SitePrint Autonomous Robotic Layout Solution Leverages HP's Multi Jet Fusion 3D Printing to Reduce Cost and Inefficiencies in Construction | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: HP SitePrint is a commercially sold autonomous layout robot with collision avoidance that prints lines, arcs, points and text from CAD files directly on building slabs, used on construction and exhibition sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated site layout marking. Printing dimensioned points from a plan onto the floor produces the output of this task (an identified exact installation site), autonomously, in a second independent commercial system.

sources.title: Robots Powered with Reach Speed up Stakeout for Construction Projects - Emlid Blog
sources.claim: Civ Robotics' CivDot is an autonomous GNSS/RTK ground robot that drives to design coordinates outdoors on open construction terrain and paint-marks each point to 1-2 cm accuracy, replacing crew stakeout.

sources.title: Civ Robotics provides CivNav AI navigation for solar construction systems - The Robot Report
sources.claim: CivDots are in production use on outdoor utility-scale sites - marking up to 3,000 pile locations per day on solar farms and, per a contractor, laying out over 300,000 point locations across three projects; also used on pipelines and roadworks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor construction stakeout at scale on unstructured graded sites - the same act of fixing and marking exact equipment installation points in the field that this task requires.

sources.title: Hilti Unveils BIM-Enabled Construction Jobsite Robot
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot locates itself indoors from BIM data and automatically drills and marks anchor holes at design positions in ceilings and concrete walls, but an operator drives it by remote control from one drilling position to the next.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: BIM-driven marking/drilling of installation points on walls and ceilings. It is the nearest system to marking non-floor installation points, but repositioning is operator-driven, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Trimble Releases Turnkey Autonomous Robotic Scanning Solution
sources.claim: Trimble's X7 laser scanner integrated with Boston Dynamics' Spot performs autonomous 3D measurement capture along preset waypoint routes on jobsites, tying measurements to the project coordinate system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous dimensional field measurement in buildings. Supports the measuring half of this task (distances from existing building features to candidate equipment locations) inside institution-controlled facilities.

tasks.label: Examine telephone transmission facilities to determine requirements for new or additional telephone services.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential or small-business premises service survey: technician drives to the customer address, opens the network interface device, traces existing inside wire and jacks, checks the drop/aerial or buried service wire, puts a test set or meter on the pair (or an optical power meter on the ONT drop), and determines what is required to add a line or new service (spare pair available, new drop needed, rewiring, ONT/battery, jack additions). Layout, wiring vintage, clutter, pets and weather vary site to site.

Outside-plant field examination: technician works at a pedestal, cross-connect cabinet, aerial terminal on a pole, or manhole/vault along a street or easement; opens the enclosure, identifies and counts working/spare copper pairs or fiber strands, tests for shorts, grounds, opens and loss, checks splitter/port availability and cable condition, and reports whether facilities exist for the requested service or what must be built.

Central office / headend copper frame and equipment survey: technician walks the MDF/IDF and equipment lineups, checks jumper and vertical/horizontal block capacity, counts spare line-card or DSLAM ports, verifies shelf slots, power feeds, fuses and rack space, uses frame test access to check a loop, and writes up what is needed to turn up an additional circuit.

Central office / headend / colocation fiber facility check: technician determines whether an optical path and free ports exist for a new or additional circuit - identifying available fiber terminations on the ODF/patch panel, verifying continuity and insertion loss with a power meter or OTDR, and confirming the cross-connect required to deliver the service.

Commercial building or multi-dwelling-unit survey: technician meets building management, inspects the telecom entrance room and riser closets, examines 66/110 blocks, house cable and existing PBX/key system terminations, counts spare pairs to the floor, and determines the requirements (backboard space, riser cable, new terminations) for adding telephone service to a tenant suite.

sources.system: Telescent G5 Network Topology Manager (robotic fiber cross-connect)

sources.claim: Telescent's G5 Network Topology Manager is a commercially available robotic fiber patch panel installed in data-center/central-office racks that keeps machine-accurate inventory of fiber terminations and performs remote optical power monitoring and OTDR-based diagnostics/testing of optical links, then physically makes the cross-connect under software control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated physical-layer inventory and optical testing of fiber terminations. This is the same determination a technician makes when examining fiber transmission facilities for a new circuit - which terminations are free and whether the path passes loss/continuity - on the same objects (fiber terminations in a frame), inside a purpose-built robotic enclosure.

sources.title: MOX Signs Agreement to Deploy Telescent's Fiber Automation Platform on its Next-Generation Long-Haul Route
sources.claim: The Telescent robotic cross-connect platform is deployed by a carrier (MOX Networks) on a live long-haul fiber route, where fiber connections are inventoried, tested and provisioned by the machine without dispatching a technician, including automatic cable-fault location.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: remote physical-layer diagnostics and circuit delivery. Establishing that a fiber facility is available and sound is exactly the 'examine facilities to determine requirements for new service' step, here performed by the robot on carrier fiber terminations in a rack.

sources.title: Telescent to Showcase Largest Capacity Optical Circuit Switch at OFC 2025
sources.claim: Telescent continues to ship larger-capacity robotic optical patch panels, demonstrating a G5 rack switching over 16,000 fibers in 2025, confirming the technology is current rather than historical.
sources.transferJustification: Currency evidence for the same robotic fiber-facility inventory/testing platform cited above.

sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed capability for walking a human-built facility and inspecting equipment; cited to bound what facility-inspection robots do - condition monitoring, not examination of frames, pairs and ports to determine service requirements.

tasks.label: Dig holes or trenches as necessary for equipment installation and access.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential service drop burial: at a customer's home, dig a shallow narrow trench (roughly 4-12 in deep, 20-150 ft long) with a trenching shovel, spade or small walk-behind trencher/vibratory plow from the pedestal/tap at the property line to the network interface on the house; must work around sod, flower beds, sprinkler heads and lines, invisible pet fence, tree roots, fences and a walkway, and leave the yard restorable.

Small hole in a yard or roadside easement for a piece of equipment: hand shovel or post-hole digger to set a new pedestal, small handhole/vault, ground rod, or cabinet pad, typically 1-3 ft deep, tight against a sidewalk, curb or driveway, in soil that may contain rock, roots or old concrete, with other buried utilities marked nearby.

Potholing / daylighting to gain access to existing buried plant: after locating a faulted or cut drop or feeder cable or a blocked conduit, carefully dig by hand (or with a small vacuum/hydro excavator) to expose the cable or conduit for splicing or replacement without damaging it or adjacent gas/water/power lines; in a lawn, road shoulder or planting strip.

Conduit trench at a business, MDU or campus premises: 50-300 ft trench, 18-36 in deep, cut with a walk-behind trencher or mini-excavator from a street vault or handhole to a building entrance or an outdoor equipment cabinet, crossing lawn, landscaping and sometimes asphalt/concrete, close to the structure and to existing marked utilities, with spoil managed and surface restored.

Digging in open, cleared ground inside a controlled telecom facility site: a fenced cell-site compound, headend/central-office yard or greenfield equipment-shelter pad where a trench for conduit or a ground ring, or holes for ground rods, are dug along a surveyed/staked line; machine access is available, no landscaping or public present.

sources.title: The World's First Fully Autonomous Trenching Solution — Built Robotics
sources.claim: Built Robotics' Exosystem retrofit converts standard mid-size excavators into machines that dig trenches fully autonomously at stated 0.1 ft digging accuracy and up to 180 ft/hour, with geofencing and remote monitoring as the safety layer.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical act as the task: excavating trenches in soil to lay buried cable/conduit along a surveyed line, though at larger machine scale than a telecom drop trench.

sources.system: Built Robotics autonomous excavators / RPD pile drivers

sources.transferJustification: Trenching and hole/pile placement in open ground for buried electrical infrastructure; transfers to digging trenches and holes for telecom conduit and pedestals where the ground is open and the line is staked.

sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Moves Earth with Autonomous Excavators | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: Bechtel has used Built Robotics' autonomous excavators for trenching on solar construction projects in Texas, and autonomous pile drivers on other projects.

sources.title: Bedrock Robotics Deploys Industry's Largest Supervised Autonomous Excavator Test | Equipment World
sources.claim: Bedrock Robotics and Sundt Construction ran supervised autonomous excavators (20-80 ton machines with a retrofit sensor rack) moving more than 65,000 cubic ... facility site in Phoenix, following the same workflow as ... crews.
sources.transferJustification: Mass excavation rather than utility trenching, but establishes that autonomous excavators can dig productively for sustained periods on an active earthwork site with only supervisory human involvement.

sources.title: Gravis Robotics brings physical AI to earthmoving | Equipment Journal
sources.claim: At CONEXPO 2026 Hitachi and Gravis Robotics demonstrated a retrofit kit on a 13-ton ZX135US-7 excavator in which an operator's inputs 'train' the machine, which then digs a trench autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Directly a trench-digging demonstration by a compact excavator in a prepared demonstration dig area, matching the digging act of this task in a setting arranged around the machine.

sources.title: The Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System (RRES): From Innovation Funding to Field Trials – ULC Technologies
sources.claim: ULC Technologies' Robotic Roadworks and Excavation System scanned for and identified a buried pipe, then performed a keyhole excavation over it and exposed the asset, during UK field trials with gas network SGN.
sources.transferJustification: Keyhole excavation to expose a mapped buried gas main is the same operation as potholing/daylighting to expose a buried telecom cable or conduit: soft-touch digging over a known utility without damaging it.

sources.title: ROBOTIC INNOVATION IN THE ENERGY AND UTILITY INDUSTRY BRINGS GLOBAL RECOGNITION FOR ULC – ULC Technologies
sources.claim: ULC describes RRES as performing end-to-end autonomous excavation, including cutting the road surface and vacuum excavation, using ground-penetrating radar and electromagnetic sensing to find buried assets in its path.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the autonomy level of the excavation system used for the potholing transfer above (locating, cutting, vacuum excavating and reinstating a small access hole over a buried utility).
