sources.claim: Built Robotics' RPD 35 is a fully ... survey data, pile distribution, driving and inspection, installing an estimated 300 piles per ... at surveyed locations on solar sites with a two-person crew.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously placing a vertical member into the ground at a surveyed point. Transfers to digging/driving small holes for pedestals, posts and ground rods when the location is staked and the ground is open.

tasks.label: Perform routine maintenance on equipment, including adjusting and lubricating components and painting worn or exposed areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled preventive-maintenance round inside a carrier central office, cable headend or edge equipment room: pull and replace/clean cabinet and HVAC air filters, vacuum dust from shelves and fan trays, clean and re-coat battery terminals in the DC power plant, torque/adjust rack and busbar hardware, lubricate fan and blower bearings, and touch up paint on scratched or rust-spotted relay-rack ironwork. Access-controlled carrier building, fixed rack layout, lighting and climate controlled.

Outside-plant preventive maintenance on street cabinets, pedestals and remote terminals at roadside/right-of-way: open the enclosure, clear debris and water intrusion, lubricate locks, hinges and door gaskets, wire-brush and touch-up paint corroded or worn cabinet exterior, re-seal and re-secure the door. Weather, traffic, vegetation and site-to-site variation.

Cell site, tower or rooftop PM visit: grease/torque antenna and coax mount hardware, re-tape and weatherproof connectors, wire-brush and paint rusted steel mounts, ice bridges and ground bars, and service outdoor cabinets/generator. Work performed in place, often at height on an erected structure, with layout differing at every site.

Customer-premises maintenance during a service or PM visit at a home or small business: clean and adjust installed equipment, re-aim and lubricate a dish or antenna mount, clean and lubricate NID/amplifier enclosure latches and hinges, and touch up paint or sealant on weathered exterior enclosures and entry conduit. Cluttered, unstandardized private property.

Bench/shop maintenance and refurbishment in a garage, warehouse or equipment shop: units and mechanical assemblies pulled from service (fan trays, cooling assemblies, dish actuators, cable reels, spare cabinets and aerial hardware) are set on a bench, cleaned, lubricated, fasteners adjusted and torqued, and worn housings sanded and repainted before redeployment.

Outside-plant remote terminal, pedestal or street cabinet: vacuuming out dirt, insects and moisture debris, cleaning corroded terminals, ground and battery contacts, applying contact cleaner/grease, replacing corroded terminal blocks or connectors, roadside with weather and traffic.

Customer premises (home or small business): cleaning contacts and connectors in NIDs, 66-blocks/MDFs, modem/set-top and PBX connections, vacuuming dust from a customer equipment closet, replacing corroded or burnt contacts, in cluttered, uncontrolled spaces.

tasks.label: Address special issues or situations, such as illegal or unauthorized use of equipment, or cases of electrical or acoustic shock.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential theft of service: while on a trouble or audit call, the tech finds an unauthorized splice, illegal tap connection, bypassed trap/filter or self-installed drop at an aerial tap, ground-block pedestal or NID. Tech verifies the account, disconnects and removes the illegal connection, re-terminates legitimate drops, installs a lock/trap, checks signal levels, and files a theft-of-service report. Outdoors, ladders/bucket, weather, possibly a hostile customer.

MDU or small-commercial building: audit of a shared lockbox, riser closet or basement demarc taken as found — legacy and unlabeled cabling from several providers, unauthorized taps feeding other units. Tech traces lines with a toner/meter, disconnects unauthorized drops, re-terminates and labels the legitimate ones, secures the enclosure, and documents.

Customer reports a shock (tingle) from a phone, coax or jack at a home. Tech tests for stray/foreign voltage on the pair or shield, isolates whether it originates in premises wiring, a faulty NID, an ungrounded/corroded bond, or the power service; corrects or replaces the bonding/grounding and defective equipment, verifies with a meter, advises the customer and reports the incident (may require escalation to the power utility).

Acoustic shock / loud-tone incident at a business call center or office: an agent reports a sudden loud burst and ear pain. Tech responds to the workstation, inspects and swaps the headset/amplifier, tests handset and line for noise, checks PBX/ATA levels and limiter settings, measures output, confirms the fix with the affected worker, and documents the incident for safety records.

Central office or cable headend: rogue/unauthorized equipment or an undocumented cross-connect found on the MDF, DSX or rack; or an energized frame / shock incident on the DC power plant or grounding system. Tech investigates records, traces and removes the unauthorized gear or jumper, verifies bonding and fuse/breaker integrity, restores affected circuits, and writes it up.

sources.system: Telescent G4 Network Topology Manager (robotic fiber cross-connect)
sources.title: MOX Networks to Deploy Telescent's Fiber Automation Platform

It does NOT transfer to this task: it only reconnects fiber jumpers already routed into its purpose-built enclosure, and cannot investigate unauthorized equipment, remove rogue jumpers or foreign gear from an open MDF/rack, or respond to an electrical shock incident. Cited to show the state of the art ... why it falls short.

tasks.label: Install telephone station equipment, such as intercommunication systems, transmitters, receivers, relays, and ringers, and related apparatus, such as coin collectors, telephone booths, and switching-key equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Business/hospitality station-set deployment: technician installs multiline key-system/VoIP desk sets and wall phones at existing jacks throughout an office suite or hotel floor — unpack set, mount bracket or place on desk, connect handset/line/power cords, label, program extension, test dial tone.

Intercom, paging or door-entry system installation in a managed commercial or institutional building (office, school, hospital, apartment lobby): mount head-end/amplifier panel and room or door stations on finished walls, run and dress station cable through ceilings and risers, terminate at blocks/terminals, test every station.

Residential or small-office premises work: install or replace station apparatus in a customer's home — wall phone, jacks and ringers, door intercom station, small intercom set — drilling and fishing cable through finished walls, working around furniture, pets and unknown existing wiring.

New-construction or renovation rough-in: mount backboxes, terminal blocks, station apparatus and backboards at framed-out station locations on an active construction site, pull and terminate station wiring, dusty/cluttered conditions, other trades present.

Shop/equipment-room prefabrication: assemble and wire station-apparatus panels and backboards on the bench (relays, ringers, terminal blocks, key/switching apparatus), cut, strip, crimp and land conductors, then bench-test before deployment.

Public/outdoor apparatus: install telephone booths, emergency call boxes, coin collectors and courtesy phones on sidewalks, campuses, parking garages — set/anchor enclosure, mount instrument, land outside-plant pair, weatherproof and test.

roles.title: Avionics Technicians
roles.description: Install, inspect, test, adjust, or repair avionics equipment, such as radar, radio, navigation, and missile control systems in aircraft or space vehicles.

tasks.label: Adjust, repair, or replace malfunctioning components or assemblies, using hand tools or soldering irons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Line/base maintenance on an aircraft: replacing a malfunctioning line-replaceable unit (radio, transponder, GPS/nav receiver, radar processor, control display unit) in an avionics rack, cockpit panel, nose bay or under-floor bay. Tech opens access panels, releases hold-down knobs/hooks or screws, demates rack/round connectors, slides the unit out, installs and secures the serviceable unit, reinstalls panels. Hangar or flight-line ramp, cramped overhead or kneeling access, time pressure.

Wiring and connector repair on the aircraft: cutting out a chafed or corroded wire section, stripping and splicing with environmental splices/heat-shrink, extracting and replacing a damaged connector contact with insertion/extraction tools, crimping new pins, re-pinning a connector, replacing a bonding jumper or terminal lug inside a bundle behind a panel. Hangar, confined access, adjacent systems live.

Shop/bench repair of a removed avionics unit or circuit card assembly at an ESD workstation: opening the box, removing the faulty card, using a soldering iron/hot-air tool to desolder and replace an identified failed component (capacitor, resistor, IC/BGA, relay, connector), cleaning the site, resoldering, reassembling and functionally checking the unit. Avionics repair shop with standard benches and test sets.

Adjustment, alignment and calibration of avionics components after or in lieu of replacement: tuning trim screws and potentiometers to meet spec against a test set, aligning an antenna or sensor mount, adjusting switch/detent travel on a control panel, shimming or torquing a unit into its tray, adjusting an autopilot servo linkage. Shop bench or on-aircraft.

Replacing airframe-mounted avionics hardware: external blade/GPS antennas, radome hardware, brackets, trays and racks, static wicks, probe heaters - drilling out or removing screws/rivets, cleaning bonding surfaces, applying sealant, installing and torquing fasteners, checking bond resistance. Hangar or ramp, work overhead or from stands.

sources.title: The slow rise of robots in the data center - DCD

sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above; it establishes deployed, timed, whole-cycle autonomous replacement of a failed electronic module, the closest fielded analogue to LRU removal and installation.

sources.title: Meet Daisy and Taz: Apple's iPhone-Disassembling Robots | Supply Chain Digital

sources.transferJustification: Related task: threaded-fastener removal and extraction of electronic modules from a fixtured housing - the hand-tool portion of pulling an avionics box from its tray, on comparable fastener sizes, in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Alpha 530 | Komax
sources.claim: Komax Alpha 530 is a fully automatic wire-processing machine that cuts, strips, crimps terminals and inserts seals on both wire ends to monitored crimp-quality standards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: terminating a presented wire - strip, crimp a new contact, set the seal - which is the core physical act of repairing a damaged aircraft wire or replacing a connector contact, at the same wire gauges and crimp-quality acceptance criteria.

sources.title: Connector Insertion Robot Cell for the Electronics and Electrical Industry [Nachi-Fujikoshi]
sources.claim: Nachi-Fujikoshi supplies a production connector-insertion robot cell for the electronics/electrical industry that mates connectors under visual feedback control at high precision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mating multi-pin electrical connectors, the step that dominates LRU installation and harness repair; comparable connector types and insertion tolerances, performed on fixtured work in a cell.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: adjusting screw/trim elements of an RF unit against instrument feedback until in-spec - the same physical act, precision and acceptance criterion as an avionics technician adjusting a malfunctioning radio or nav unit to specification.

tasks.label: Lay out installation of aircraft assemblies and systems, following documentation such as blueprints, manuals, and wiring diagrams.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: MRO hangar / completion center retrofit: technician lays out installation of an avionics box, tray or rack in a cockpit, E&E bay or under-floor area of an in-service aircraft per STC drawings and maintenance manuals — measuring from structural datums, checking clearance against existing wiring and structure, and marking bracket and hole positions in confined space.

New-build production line: technician lays out and marks mounting positions for avionics shelves, brackets and equipment racks on airframe structure or panels at a fixed production station, per engineering drawings and installation plans, with standard repeated configuration.

Wire harness / routing layout: from wiring diagrams, the technician determines and marks harness routing runs, clamp and standoff locations and bulkhead penetration points, or lays a harness out on a formboard, marking breakouts and cutting lengths in the shop.

Avionics shop bench: layout of an instrument panel, faceplate or equipment rack — transferring the drawing to the blank, marking and cutting instrument cutouts, hole patterns and fastener locations to drawing tolerance.

Cabin systems layout in a production or completion cabin: marking positions on the cabin floor and seat tracks for equipment locations (seat rows, in-seat power boxes, IFE units) per the specific aircraft's configuration drawing.

sources.title: CabinMarker: robotics in aircraft manufacturing | Airbus
sources.claim: Airbus's CabinMarker is a 4 kg mobile robot that moves through an aircraft cabin on the final assembly line and marks/positions seat-track locations from each aircraft's configuration data, replacing 150 minutes of manual measuring and marking with ~30 minutes of robot work; it received industrial certification in Dec 2025 and has been tested on the A330 FAL.
sources.transferJustification: Direct analogue of 'laying out an installation from documentation': the robot transfers a documented equipment layout (seat/monument positions from the cabin configuration) onto the actual aircraft floor tracks at millimetric precision inside the fuselage.

sources.title: Airbus deploys tiny cabin robot to speed up A321XLR seat installation
sources.claim: CabinMarker marks the correct points on the cabin floor tracks according to the configuration planned for each individual aircraft, with operators supervising rather than performing the marking; first units go to the A321 final assembly line in ....
sources.transferJustification: Same task family — transferring a documented installation layout onto the aircraft — performed inside a fuselage on a production line rather than on a fixtured part.

sources.title: Piper puts new robot to work on M600 - AOPA
sources.claim: Piper Aircraft runs a Wilder Systems Agile Manufacturing Robot in serial production that autonomously drills the hole patterns required to build PA-46-600TP wings, working inside a safety-scanner-protected cell on the assembly line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (programmed drilling of aircraft structure): the machine locates and places every hole of a documented pattern on aircraft structure, which subsumes the physical layout step of marking those positions, at equal or better precision than a technician.

sources.system: Dual-robot aerostructure drilling/fastening cell (kinematically redundant robots on linear axes with jig)
sources.developer: academic-industrial consortium (paper: Planning of efficient trajectories in robotized assembly of aerostructures)
sources.title: Planning of efficient trajectories in robotized assembly of aerostructures exploiting kinematic redundancy (arXiv)
sources.claim: An industrial robotic aerostructure assembly cell holds a panel in a jig and has an internal robot reference the area and compute drilling coordinates that are executed by an external drilling/fastening robot, i.e. the layout of the hole pattern is derived and realized by the machines on a fixtured workpiece.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic drilling of fixtured aerostructure panels): referencing the part and computing/placing the documented hole pattern is the machine equivalent of laying out an installation on the workpiece.

sources.system: Dual-arm harness form-board configuration and cable-routing system
sources.developer: Tecnalia / Basque Research and Technology Alliance

sources.transferJustification: Laying out a harness from the wiring diagram onto a form board is the E1 presentation of the wire-routing layout instance; the robot performs exactly this pin placement and routing from the drawing data.

sources.system: Datron M8Cube CNC panel fabrication (avionics shop)

sources.title: CNC Panel Cutting - Bend Aircraft

sources.transferJustification: Same as above: machine execution of the documented panel layout on a fixtured blank replaces hand layout and cutting.

sources.title: FieldPrint Platform | Dusty Robotics
sources.claim: Dusty Robotics' FieldPrinter is an autonomous mobile robot ... prints full-size BIM/CAD layouts directly onto jobsite floors at 1/16 inch accuracy, i.e. autonomous transfer of documented layouts onto a work surface.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (construction layout): autonomous printing of a documented layout onto a flat floor demonstrates the marking-from-drawings capability, but only on open, flat surfaces — it does not cover curved skins or confined aircraft bays.

tasks.label: Test and troubleshoot instruments, components, and assemblies, using circuit testers, oscilloscopes, or voltmeters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Line/hangar fault isolation of an installed avionics system after a pilot squawk (e.g., intermittent VHF comm, nav flag, radar altimeter fault): technician opens access panels, interrogates BITE, then probes connector pins and LRU racks in the avionics bay, cockpit and belly with a multimeter/circuit tester to decide whether the fault is the box, the wiring, or a ground/antenna, on a parked aircraft under turn-time pressure.

Post-installation or post-repair operational/certification checks on the aircraft: hook a ramp test set (transponder/altimeter/pitot-static, ELT, nav/comm signal generator) to the aircraft, run the required test sequences, read voltages/signals with meters, verify system responses against the maintenance manual, and sign off.

Continuity, insulation and voltage-drop checks on installed aircraft wiring during an avionics installation, STC modification or chafing/short investigation: ring out pin-to-pin through long harness runs behind panels and in confined bays with a multimeter/megohmmeter, checking against wiring diagrams.

Bench functional test of a removed LRU or instrument (radio, transponder, air-data computer, gyro/indicator) in a repair-station or depot shop: fit the unit to the bench/ATE station, connect the interface adapter and power, run the certified test procedure, compare readings to spec limits, and determine serviceability.

Board/component-level fault isolation on the shop bench: with the circuit card assembly out of its chassis and powered on a bench supply, probe nets and component pins with an oscilloscope and voltmeter, inject signals, and isolate the failed component or open/short before repair.

sources.system: Acculogic SCORPION FLS980Dxi flying probe tester with external oscilloscope

sources.system: SPEA 4060 S2 Automatic Flying Probe Tester

sources.claim: Automatic flying probe testers handle rugged/large assemblies typical of avionics, including backplanes with connectors and boards carrying transformers, heat sinks and front panels, inside a fixtureless automatic test machine.

sources.system: FormFactor Autonomous High-Power Measurement Assistant / CM300xi automated probe station
sources.title: Autonomous High-Power Wafer Probing for Power Devices | FormFactor
sources.claim: Fully automated probe stations position probes onto device pads and run instrumented electrical measurements hands-free around the clock, with automated handling of the units under test.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated electrical probing and parametric measurement of electronic devices. It transfers to bench-level electrical test and fault isolation because the machine contacts small conductors with probes and runs instrument measurements autonomously; it does so only inside a purpose-built prober enclosure, supporting E1 and no higher.

tasks.label: Connect components to assemblies such as radio systems, instruments, magnetos, inverters, and in-flight refueling systems, using hand tools and soldering irons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Avionics back-shop bench work: at an ESD workbench in a repair station, soldering wire leads into connector solder cups and to circuit boards, and connecting internal modules/pigtails of a radio, instrument, or static inverter LRU per the maintenance manual, then continuity/functional check.

Hangar installation on a general-aviation or transport aircraft: mounting a comm/nav radio, transponder or instrument in the panel/rack and connecting it — crimping contacts, inserting them into the connector housing per the wiring diagram, mating the rear/circular connector, coax and power leads, torquing hold-downs.

Connections made in confined airframe locations: reaching behind an instrument panel, into a tail cone, belly bay, wing root or overhead, to mate coax/circular connectors to antennas and sensors, attach bonding straps and clamp bundles, working blind and one-handed among installed structure and existing wiring.

Engine-compartment work with cowlings removed: connecting magneto ignition harness leads and shielded elbows to plugs and the magneto cap, and hooking up engine-mounted sensor/ignition connectors on a piston or turboprop aircraft.

Military/large-aircraft depot work: connecting inverters, in-flight refueling system components and large multi-pin harnesses — soldering shielded cables, crimping and inserting MIL-spec contacts, mating D38999-type connectors — largely on benches and jigs in the back shop with removed panels and assemblies.

sources.system: Komax Omega 750 S fully automatic harness assembly machine
sources.title: Komax Introduces the Omega 750 S: Revolutionizing Fully Automated Wire Harness Assembly
sources.claim: Komax's Omega 750 S is a commercially sold, fully automatic machine that cuts, crimps and loads terminals and inserts them into connector housings, with a force sensor verifying correct latching of each terminal in the housing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wire-harness manufacture. The avionics task's core physical act — terminating wires and seating contacts into connector housings to hook a component into an assembly — is the same operation on the same class of objects (small-gauge wire, crimp contacts, multi-pin housings) at equal or tighter precision, performed in a purpose-built machine cell.

sources.system: Apollo Seiko automated (iron-tip and laser) soldering robots
sources.title: New Benefits with Automated Soldering Innovations - Wiring Harness News
sources.claim: Apollo Seiko's iron-tip and laser soldering robots are commercial production machines used for filling connector solder cups and soldering wire leads to PCBs and connectors, replacing hand soldering with a repeatable automated process.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production soldering of wire leads and components. It is the same tool (soldering iron/laser) and the same joints avionics technicians make at the bench — leads into connector solder cups and to boards — with the workpiece fixtured in a machine cell.

sources.system: Flexiv Rizon adaptive robot (force-guided connector assembly)
sources.title: Assembly Automation | Flexiv
sources.claim: Flexiv Rizon adaptive robots perform vision- and force-guided connector insertion and screw fastening in industrial assembly, with 3D vision locating connectors and force-guided insertion seating them; the company reports work on production lines with Tier 1 automotive suppliers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: electronics/automotive connector mating in a production cell. Mating a connector to a component under force control is the decisive motion of 'connecting components to assemblies'; objects (multi-contact connectors, flexible cable) and insertion tolerances are comparable, and the demonstrated setting is a fixtured cell (E1).

sources.system: Dual-arm CAD-driven harness assembly system (two Kuka cobots)
sources.title: Robot-Assisted Assembly of Wiring Harnesses for Airplanes | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: A dual-arm Kuka cobot system configures the nail board and routes wires for aircraft wire harnesses directly from CAD data, executing trajectories in real time; it was validated in an aerospace harness production environment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerospace wire-harness board setup and cable routing. It shows robots handling aviation harness wires and routing them on a fixtured board in a workbench cell, the preparatory half of connecting avionics components; it does not cover connector termination, which the other cited systems supply.

sources.developer: academic/industrial research (Springer, Advances in Automotive Production Technology)
sources.title: Automotive Wire Harness Connector Installation Using Skill-Based Robotic Programming
sources.claim: State-of-the-art research on installing wire-harness connectors on an as-built product (a car door) using force-controlled search and insertion reports only 76.7% success, well below the reliability a technician's employer would accept.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: connector mating on a real product rather than in a fixtured feed. It bounds capability for in-situ (E2-style) avionics connections, where the connector pose and cable state are as-found.

sources.title: CoaxCenter 6000 - Cable shield processing machine by Schleuniger
sources.claim: Schleuniger's CoaxCenter 6000 processes micro-coaxial, coaxial and single-conductor cable fully automatically and with high ...; the 6000 Plus adds twisting and tinning for fully automatic all-in-one coax preparation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated coaxial cable termination preparation. Avionics connection work includes coax runs to radios and antennas; this shows the shield/center-conductor preparation done to production quality by a purpose-built machine when the work is fed to it.

tasks.label: Install electrical and electronic components, assemblies, and systems in aircraft, using hand tools, power tools, or soldering irons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: OEM production/final-assembly installation: at an aircraft or helicopter manufacturer, install electrical system hardware into airframe sections — route and clamp wire bundles through fuselage/wing/cockpit structure, mount equipment racks, brackets and ground studs, mate connectors, work in confined structural bays and overhead positions on a moving line.

Retrofit/upgrade install in an MRO or FBO hangar: mount an avionics stack, tray or rack in the instrument panel or equipment bay of a GA aircraft, bizjet or airliner; fabricate and route a custom harness behind the panel, crimp and solder pins, install circuit breakers, shields and grounds per an STC data package, working lying under the panel or in the nose bay.

Line-replaceable-unit installation: slide a radio, transponder, FMS, ADS-B or mission computer into its existing ARINC tray in the cockpit or avionics bay, mate the rear/cannon connector, torque hold-down clamps and safety-wire, then confirm the unit powers up — done on the flight line or in a hangar within a turnaround window.

Exterior and cabin equipment install: antenna, sensor, camera or external light on the fuselage skin (drill/cut per STC, apply sealant, torque fasteners, terminate coax, bonding check), or cabin IFE/connectivity boxes and cabling under seats and in overhead areas of an in-service airliner.

Shop/bench build-up feeding the install: lay out and fabricate the wire harness on a form board, cut/strip/crimp, pin connectors, solder terminations, apply backshells, lacing and labels, and build up the panel or tray subassembly at an avionics-shop workbench before it goes into the aircraft.

sources.system: Dual-arm Kuka LBR iiwa 7 harness assembly system (Basque Research and Technology Alliance / Tekniker)
sources.title: Robot-Assisted Assembly of Wiring Harnesses for Airplanes | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: A dual-arm Kuka LBR iiwa system developed by the Basque Research and Technology Alliance configures a nail/form board and routes wires for aerospace wire harnesses from CAD data; after a human joystick calibration step the robots execute autonomously, but the work is bench/board-level harness fabrication, not installation into an aircraft, and it is slower than manual work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerospace wire-harness fabrication on a form board, which is the shop-bench portion of an avionics installation job (same wires, connectors and routing precision), performed in a fixtured, purpose-built two-robot cell.

sources.system: Komax Omega 750 S (and Omega 740/750, Zeta series)
sources.title: Komax Introduces the Omega 750 S: Revolutionizing Fully Automated Wire Harness Assembly - Wiring Harness News
sources.claim: Komax's Omega 750 S is a commercially sold, fully automatic wire-harness production machine that cuts, crimps and inserts terminated wires into connector housings without operator intervention inside a purpose-built machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fabrication of terminated wire sets with connector housings — the bench-level wire preparation and connector termination that avionics technicians perform with hand tools before an installation; done entirely inside a purpose-built machine.

sources.system: AI-based visuotactile connector mating framework (MuTT + Shadow Program Inversion, ArtiMinds/KIT)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: mating multi-pin electrical connectors on a fixtured assembly — the connector step of an avionics unit installation; comparable sub-millimetre insertion tolerances and connector geometries, but demonstrated only on a fixtured automotive console in a robot cell.

sources.system: Finray-effect compliant gripper for electrical component assembly (literature review of state of the art)

sources.transferJustification: Cited only as negative/context evidence on the state of the art for in-product cable and harness installation, the core of this task.

sources.title: Meet the versatile Airbus robot automating aircraft seat installation | Airbus
sources.claim: Airbus's newest in-cabin production robot, CabinMarker, marks and positions seat-track locations on the cabin floor with operators kept in the loop; it received industrial certification in December 2025 with the first two units due at the A321 final assembly line in late 2026 — i.e. the frontier of robotics inside aircraft cabins is floor marking, not electrical installation.
sources.transferJustification: Context evidence on what robots currently do inside aircraft on a final assembly line; it marks positions rather than installing components, so it cannot support a positive judgment for installing electrical assemblies in aircraft.

sources.system: Custom rotary-dial electronic control module assembly system (six-axis robot, fixtured screwdrivers, presses)
sources.title: Automated System Assembles Electronic Control Modules | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: A custom automated assembly cell built by The Christopher Stephen Corp. assembles and tests an electronic control module in a 29-step process, including automatic feeding and driving of threaded fasteners, with the housing and internal parts loaded by an operator at the pre-assembly station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mounting and fastening an electronic unit into a housing with monitored force and torque in a fixtured cell — the mechanical securing step of installing an avionics box into its tray, at comparable part sizes and fastener precision.

tasks.label: Set up and operate ground support and test equipment to perform functional flight tests of electrical and electronic systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ramp or hangar functional check of installed comm/nav/surveillance gear on a GA, business or transport aircraft: tech positions a ground power unit and portable ramp test set (e.g. IFR6000, NAV-750), connects power and antenna couplers, sits in the cockpit tuning radios/transponder, verifies replies and signals, records results on the work order.

tasks.label: Inspect and test equipment to locate damage or worn parts and diagnose malfunctions, or read work orders or schematic drawings to determine required repairs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Intake diagnosis at an electric motor repair shop: a used industrial AC motor (5-200 hp, oily, unknown history) arrives on a pallet with a work order describing the customer's complaint. The tech reads the order and nameplate, visually inspects for burnt smell, water ingress, broken feet, damaged shaft/fan, turns the shaft by hand, then bench-tests with megohmmeter (insulation to ground), winding resistance/balance, surge comparison and sometimes a no-load run, and writes the fault diagnosis and repair recommendation (rewind, bearings, machine work).

Post-teardown inspection in the shop: after disassembly, the tech inspects and measures the internals - stator windings for burning, shorted turns, contamination and varnish breakdown (including core loss test), rotor bars/laminations, bearings and journals for wear and scoring, shaft runout, endbell and housing fits with micrometers/bore gauges - and decides which parts are reusable versus replaced or machined.

Scheduled predictive-maintenance/condition survey at a customer's plant: walking a route of installed motors, pumps and drives, taking infrared images, listening for and recording bearing noise/vibration, checking for overheating, leaks, loose mounts, and reporting which machines show developing damage or worn parts.

Field troubleshooting service call on a specific failed or misbehaving installed motor at an industrial plant or commercial building: check supply voltage and running current at the starter, insulation resistance at the terminal box, inspect couplings/belts and mounting, feel for heat and vibration, review the control schematic, and determine whether the fault is in the motor, the starter/drive, the wiring, or the driven load.

Bench diagnosis of a handheld power tool or small motorized appliance at a service center: customer drops off a drill, grinder, saw or nailer; the tech reads the work order, plugs it in or fits a battery, runs it, checks cord/switch/brushes/armature/commutator, gears and bearings, often partially disassembling it, and determines which parts must be replaced.

Diagnosis at an uncontrolled site: a submersible well or irrigation pump motor at a farm, a motor on a construction site, or equipment in a customer's garage/small shop - variable layout, weather, no institutional housekeeping - where the tech inspects the unit, tests leads with a megger/multimeter and judges whether the motor can be repaired in place or must be pulled.

instances.label: Motor service center bench: reassemble a repaired integral-horsepower AC induction motor (roughly 1–100 hp) after a rewind or bearing change — press/heat new bearings onto the shaft, insert the rotor into the stator without damaging windings, fit and torque end brackets, install fan, cover and seals, land leads in the conduit box per nameplate connection, then megger, winding-resistance and no-load run test against nameplate ratings. Mixed makes and frames, one unit at a time.

Bench reassembly of fractional-horsepower and small motors (pump, blower, HVAC, appliance and hand-tool motors), including batches of identical remanufactured units: press bearings, insert rotor, fit end bells and through-bolts, reconnect leads, then insulation-resistance and no-load current checks to rated values.

Power tool repair bench: reassemble a handheld tool (drill, grinder, circular saw) after armature/field, brush or switch replacement — seat armature and field in the clamshell housing, regrease gearbox, fit brush holders, route flexible leads to the switch, drive many small screws, then run and current/continuity test the finished tool. Many different tool models pass the bench.

Service center floor with overhead crane: reassemble a large machine (roughly 150–3,000 hp induction, synchronous or DC mill motor) after rewind or bearing work — induction-heat and mount bearings, rig the rotor into the stator, set air gap and end play, install sleeve bearings, oil seals, RTD wiring and brush rigging, verify runout with dial indicators, then megger/polarization index and test-floor run.

Field reassembly at the customer's site — plant floor, pump house, rooftop air handler, mine or wind-turbine nacelle: put the repaired motor back together in place or on a skid in cramped, dirty, variable surroundings, reconnect leads, and verify insulation resistance and rotation with hand meters before returning it to service.

Tech connects a multimeter/megohmmeter/surge tester to the leads, measures winding resistance balance, insulation resistance to ground, and turn-to-turn integrity, and judges whether the winding is grounded, shorted, or open. Motors vary in frame size, condition (dirty, oil-soaked, burned) and lead configuration.

Shop test panel / dynamometer run test: repaired or rebuilt motor is coupled or run uncoupled on the shop test stand; tech measures applied voltage, no-load and loaded amperage per phase, rpm with a tachometer/strobe, and estimated horsepower, plus vibration/temperature, comparing to nameplate to verify or diagnose a fault before shipment.

Field service call at an industrial or commercial plant (factory, water plant, hospital mechanical room): motor installed on a pump/fan/conveyor. Tech takes clamp-on amp readings on each phase at the motor control center, measures supply voltage and imbalance, checks rpm and control-circuit continuity, and megs the motor from the disconnect to isolate the problem.

Power tool / small appliance service center bench: cordless drill, grinder, or vacuum. Tech measures battery pack voltage and cell balance, tests trigger switch and field/armature continuity and resistance, growler-tests the armature, checks the electronic control board circuitry, and measures no-load current and speed to pinpoint the faulty part.

On-site call at a residence or small business (attic HVAC blower, well pump, garage door opener, customer-owned bench tool): cramped, uncontrolled space; tech uses a multimeter and clamp meter to measure voltage at the unit, running amperage, capacitor value, and winding resistance to decide whether the motor or an associated component has failed.

sources.system: KLOTZ fully automated end-of-line (EOL) test benches for high-performance electric motors
sources.title: End-of-line testing for high-performance electric motors

sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line motor test rather than repair-shop diagnosis. Transfer holds because the measured quantities (current, voltage, speed/performance, vibration) and the object (an assembled electric motor presented at a fixtured station) are the same, and the machine itself makes the electrical contact and flags faults.

sources.system: Baker WinAST Automated Stator Test System
sources.title: Automated Stator Testing System | Baker winAST
sources.claim: An automated stator/motor test system used on production lines runs AC/DC hipot, surge, winding resistance and inductance tests in automated sequences and classifies winding faults, configuring itself to different motor models without operator adjustment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production quality testing of windings versus diagnostic testing of a motor in a repair shop. The instruments and measurements (insulation resistance, hipot, surge, winding resistance imbalance) are exactly those a motor repairer uses to diagnose grounded, shorted or open windings.

sources.system: Flying probe testers (e.g., Hioki FA1283, Takaya/Seica class ICT systems)
sources.title: Flying Probe Testing: Modern PCB Quality Assurance

sources.transferJustification: Related task: PCB electrical test rather than power-tool part diagnosis. sources.system: Marposs E.D.C. electrical and functional testing systems for electric motors
sources.title: End-Of-Line Testing Of Electric Motors | Marposs
sources.claim: Commercial motor end-of-line testing systems combine insulation resistance, hi-pot, surge and partial-discharge measurement with functional tests (no-load, load, back-EMF, NVH) to reveal latent motor faults, delivered as in-line and off-line automated systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production motor testing. Same instruments and same diagnostic inferences (insulation failure, winding faults, speed/torque/current deviations) as a repairer's diagnostic test sequence on a motor presented at the test station.

sources.system: Valiant TMS Automatic End-of-Line Test Bench
sources.title: Automatic End-of-Line Test Bench - Valiant TMS
sources.claim: Automatic end-of-line test benches validate the function of complete electric drive units, supplying power through a battery simulator and measuring performance of the motor/electronics before assembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: powered run test of a drive unit in a fixtured cell versus a shop test-panel run test. The action (energize the unit, measure electrical and speed/performance parameters, pass/fail against spec) matches the shop run test.

sources.title: ANYmal X — The World's First Ex-Proof Legged Robot
sources.claim: Autonomous legged inspection robots deployed in industrial plants collect readings by camera, thermal and acoustic sensors and automated readout of analog gauges; their measurement repertoire is non-contact and does not include connecting ammeter/voltmeter leads to motor terminals.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to characterize what autonomous robots actually do inside structured human work facilities (E2): remote sensing and gauge reading, not probe-based electrical measurement on motors. It supports no positive E2 judgment for this task.

tasks.label: Repair and rebuild defective mechanical parts in electric motors, generators, and related equipment, using hand tools and power tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench overhaul of a small-to-medium industrial AC motor (fractional to ~100 hp) at an EASA-type electric motor repair shop: strip the motor with impact wrenches and pullers, remove seized/rusted through-bolts and end brackets, pull and replace worn ball bearings, inspect and clean shaft and bracket fits, replace fan, slinger and seals, reassemble to spec and run-test.

Power-tool and small-appliance motor repair at a service bench: cordless drill, angle grinder, circular saw, blower or vacuum motor of many different makes and models; diagnose the mechanical fault, disassemble the housing, replace gears, armature bearings, brushes, chuck or gearcase parts, regrease, reassemble and function-test.

Large motor / generator rebuild in a service center: crane the unit onto stands, withdraw the rotor, rebuild or replace sleeve or roller bearings and bearing housings, fit new seals and couplings, check runout and air gap, dynamically balance the rotor, reassemble and run-test at load.

Field repair of a motor or generator at the customer's site — pump house, rooftop fan, wastewater plant, quarry, mill or farm: work in place or partly stripped, replace bearings, fan, shaft key or coupling, re-align to the driven machine, in cramped, dirty, variable positions with portable hand and power tools.

Machine-shop restoration of a worn mechanical part from a motor: build up a worn rotor shaft journal or bearing seat, or an oversize end-bracket bearing bore, by welding / metal spray / laser cladding and re-machine it to tolerance on a lathe or mill; also re-cut keyways and sleeve housings.

sources.system: Robotic PM-motor rotor-extraction setup (Liang & Pham, Univ. of Birmingham Autonomous Remanufacturing Lab)
sources.title: Robotic disassembly of permanent magnet electric motors
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed 2025 study of robotic disassembly of permanent-magnet motors states that disassembly — only the first step of remanufacturing — remains labour-intensive and difficult to automate; the work itself addresses one sub-step (extracting the rotor from the stator) on a lab robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic disassembly of electric motors for remanufacturing. It bounds this task because teardown is the easiest part of repair-and-rebuild; the source shows even that is not solved, and component repair/reassembly/testing are not addressed.

sources.system: AgiProbot demonstrator factory (disassembly and inspection stations)
sources.developer: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (wbk Institute of Production Science)
sources.title: AgiProbot: Automating Components Disassembly Process For Remanufacturing Purposes

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated remanufacturing disassembly of starter motors in a purpose-built cell. Shows the state of the art for machine teardown of a single known motor model; it does not cover replacing defective mechanical parts, reassembly or run-testing.

sources.title: Turn old into new: second-hand electric motor (KIT NEULAND)
sources.claim: KIT's AgiProbot demonstrator factory is explicitly a feasibility demonstrator for automated remanufacturing, currently showing automated disassembly of a starter ... across four research stations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated motor remanufacturing. Confirms the scope of the most advanced motor-teardown cell is disassembly research, not a completed repair-and-rebuild of a defective motor.

sources.system: LASERTEC 3000 DED hybrid (also LASERTEC 65 DED hybrid)
sources.title: LASERTEC 3000 DED hybrid - DMG MORI
sources.claim: DMG MORI's commercially sold LASERTEC 3000 DED hybrid machine performs repair of worn parts — machining away the damaged surface, laser deposition of new material, and finish 5-axis machining — in a single chucking inside the machine enclosure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: additive/subtractive restoration of worn metal components (turbine blades, shafts, tooling). sources.system: SENFENG SFR6063 robotic laser cladding system

sources.claim: Commercially available six-axis robotic laser-cladding systems are sold specifically for heavy-duty repair and surface remanufacturing of large workpieces including shafts, with the robot executing the deposition program inside the cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic build-up of worn shaft surfaces for remanufacture. Motor shops restore worn rotor journals the same way (spray/weld build-up then machine); the objects, materials and tolerances match, and the work is brought fixtured to the robot cell.

sources.system: Adaptive unscrewing automation cell for electric motors

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic fastener removal on electric motors. Removing corroded through-bolts is a prerequisite of every motor rebuild; its research status bounds what automation can do on the whole task.

tasks.label: Lift units or parts such as motors or generators, using cranes or chain hoists, or signal crane operators to lift heavy parts or subassemblies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Motor repair shop receiving/teardown bay: worker rigs an incoming industrial motor (500–5,000 lb) that arrived on a truck or pallet — selects slings/eyebolts, hooks the bridge-crane hook, judges balance, lifts and walks it to a teardown stand while shop personnel work nearby.

Shop teardown/reassembly with jib crane or chain hoist: lifting rotors, stators, shafts and end brackets (100–1,000 lb) off/onto benches, presses, lathes and balancing machines, including lowering a rotor squarely into a stator bore without scraping laminations or windings.

Shop process routing: repeated crane picks moving motors and stators along a fixed route between standard stations — burnout oven, wash bay, VPI/dip-and-bake tank, paint booth, test panel — loads sitting in known positions on carts, pallets or oven racks.

Field service in a customer's industrial plant (paper mill, pump house, water treatment): rigging a disconnected motor off its base/skid and signaling the plant's overhead-crane or mobile-crane operator to lift it clear and set it on a truck or cart.

Awkward or confined sites: chain fall, come-along or portable gantry used in a mechanical room, rooftop, basement, ship or mine, with improvised anchor points, restricted headroom and no standard presentation of the load.

sources.system: Trutegra automated coil cranes (10 fully automated cranes across 3 buildings)
sources.title: Case Study - Trutegra Automation Technology for Automated Coil Cranes
sources.claim: Fully automated overhead cranes autonomously pick, transport and store metal coils weighing up to 50 tons in a dedicated storage warehouse, executing all maneuvers from Level-2 orders with sensor-based load verification and collision avoidance — heavy-load crane lifting without an operator, in a facility built for the machines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated crane handling of heavy coils rather than motors. Transfer holds for crane transport of heavy units within a purpose-built bay — comparable masses (tons), hook/lifting-device engagement, and set-down accuracy — provided the load is presented in a known position with a matching lifting device.

sources.system: Shenzhou Machinery smart unmanned crane (Rockwell Automation controls, PowerFlex 755TR anti-sway)
sources.title: Shenzhou Machinery Builds Smart Unmanned Cranes | Rockwell Automation
sources.claim: An unmanned overhead crane system completes loading, storage and discharge cycles without human intervention, with operators moved out from under the crane into a remote room, achieving +/- 3 mm positioning accuracy in metals/pulp industrial plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated crane cycles in metals/paper plants. It substantiates the lifting-and-placing element of this task (heavy loads, anti-sway control, millimetre set-down) in a crane bay from which people are excluded, i.e. a machine-built setting.

sources.title: FANUC M-2000iA/2300 Robot - Ultra Heavy Payload Robot | FANUC America
sources.claim: An ultra-heavy-payload industrial robot with 2,300 kg capacity handles cars and bulky castings onto machine fixtures inside guarded cells, explicitly substituting for cranes and lifters.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heavy part handling in automotive/foundry cells rather than motor-shop rigging. Payload class (2.3 t) covers most repair-shop motors and rotors, and the pick-move-place cycle onto machine fixtures matches lifting a motor onto a stand or machine when the part is presented in a fixed position.

sources.title: Machine Tending Robots | FANUC America
sources.claim: Heavy cast housings are located with 3D vision, re-oriented and loaded into a boring mill by a robot in an automated machine-tending cell — the same pick-and-load duty a shop hoist performs when placing a motor part on a machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine tending with heavy castings. Comparable objects (heavy metal housings), comparable precision (loading into a machine tool), and it shows the load need not be perfectly fixtured — vision locates it — supporting shop lifts of rotors/stators onto machines inside a guarded cell.

sources.developer: ATS Industrial Automation (also ABB e-motor assembly cells)
sources.title: Overcoming Challenges in the Rotor and Stator Marriage Process | ATS Industrial Automation
sources.claim: Automated e-motor assembly cells use robotic arms and presses to handle and position 80–150 kg motor components and mate rotor into stator with sub-millimetre guidance to avoid misalignment or damage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: motor manufacture rather than repair. The physical act is the same one the repairer performs with a hoist — lifting a heavy rotor and lowering it concentrically into a stator bore without contact — and it is done autonomously on fixtured parts in a fenced line.

sources.system: Robotized tower/mobile cranes (Obayashi automated crane; SAC-based autonomous crane framework)
sources.developer: Obayashi Corporation; academic (Comp.-Aided Civil & Infra. Eng.)
sources.title: Autonomous construction framework for crane control with enhanced soft actor–critic algorithm and real-time progress monitoring
sources.claim: Autonomous crane research and deployments for less structured settings still concern path planning and load transport with the load already rigged; no cited system autonomously selects and attaches slings to varied loads.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only as a negative bound: autonomous crane work outside purpose-built bays is at demonstration stage with pre-rigged, standardized loads, so it cannot substantiate E2/E3 rigging of arbitrary motors.

tasks.label: Disassemble defective equipment so that repairs can be made, using hand tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Repair-shop teardown of a standard-design small/medium industrial induction motor (1-50 hp) in ordinary condition: remove fan cover and fan, pull sheave/coupling, unbolt and break loose end brackets, separate rotor from stator, pull bearings, tag and free leads, lay out parts for rewind or bearing replacement.

Repair-shop teardown of an aged, corroded or specialty motor: paint-locked or rusted end-bell bolts, rounded or snapped fasteners, seized bearings and frozen shaft fits requiring penetrating oil, heat, drilling/cutting and improvised pullers, with parts to be preserved for repair.

Service-center teardown of a handheld power tool or small appliance motor unit (drill, grinder, saw, blower motor) of arbitrary brand and model: dozens of small screws, clamshell housing with hidden clips, routed wiring and switch, greased gearbox, press-fit armature bearings and brush gear; unit must be reassemblable.

Shop teardown of a large motor or generator (100+ hp, hundreds to thousands of pounds) using overhead crane, slings and stands: remove couplings, bearing housings and end shields with hydraulic pullers, presses and induction heat; rotor lifted out horizontally without damaging windings.

Field teardown at a customer site: motor installed on a pump, fan or conveyor in a plant, mechanical room or rooftop; lock out, disconnect conduit and leads in the terminal box, remove guards and coupling, and strip the unit in place or partially before removal, with cramped access and variable footing.

Bench teardown of high-volume remanufacturing units of a known family (automotive starters/alternators, small gearmotors, fractional-hp motors) presented one after another for cleaning, inspection and rebuild.

sources.system: AgiProbot disassembly cell (multifunctional robotic arm + Zivid 3D camera + clamping system)
sources.developer: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (wbk Institute of Production Science)
sources.title: 6D Pose Estimation on Point Cloud Data through Prior Knowledge Integration: A Case Study in Autonomous Disassembly
sources.claim: KIT's AgiProbot demonstrator factory clamps end-of-life automotive starter motors in a fixtured station and disassembles them with a multifunctional robotic arm, using vision-based 6D bolt pose estimation to drive the unscrewing motions.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class and same objects: non-destructive teardown of used electric motors so components can be inspected, repaired and reassembled; fasteners, end shields and rotors are the items a motor repairer removes with hand tools.

sources.title: 6D Pose Estimation on Point Cloud Data through Prior Knowledge Integration: A Case Study in Autonomous Disassembly
sources.claim: The same AgiProbot source states that remanufacturing's primary processes (of which disassembly is the first) are still performed manually today because returned products are complex, uncertain and inconsistent.
sources.transferJustification: Directly characterises the automation status of disassembly of used electromechanical products, the task being rated; used here to support negative judgments.

sources.system: AgiProbot demonstrator factory (four stations, driverless transport)
sources.title: TURN OLD INTO NEW: SECOND-HAND ELECTRIC MOTOR
sources.claim: AgiProbot's demonstrator factory is split into stations, and previously unknown products are torn down at a MANUAL station; as of the project write-up the team had not yet run a fully automated disassembly.
sources.transferJustification: Same system and task as evidence 0; establishes the limits of autonomous end-to-end motor teardown, supporting negative judgments for unfamiliar units.

sources.system: DeMoBat robot disassembly demonstrator (KUKA KR QUANTEC based cell, Fraunhofer IPA robot test field)

sources.transferJustification: Same object class (used electric motors) and same operation (loosening fasteners on dirty, worn units) as the rated task, performed in a fixtured industrial cell.

sources.system: Robotic PM-motor rotor extraction rig (Staubli TX90L)
sources.title: Robotic disassembly of permanent magnet electric motors (Royal Society Open Science)
sources.claim: University of Birmingham researchers experimentally studied and executed robotic extraction of a rotor from a stator in a permanent-magnet motor with a Staubli TX90L arm, generating an optimised pull-out path from a magnetic force model.
sources.transferJustification: Rotor/stator separation is a core sub-step of motor teardown; cited as supporting context only, since the path is model-planned rather than demonstrably self-directed.

sources.title: Microsoft uses automated robots to disassemble and recycle HDDs
sources.claim: Microsoft has deployed robotic cells (Dobot arms) in its datacenter recycling operation that use computer vision to identify different hard-drive models, locate their screws and take the drives apart component by component.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fixtured-cell teardown of small screwed electromechanical devices of several known models. It shows model variety can be handled in a purpose-built cell, but the output is material recovery (platters destroyed), not a repairable, reassemblable device.

sources.system: UR10e robotic unscrewing platform for e-waste
sources.developer: academic group (published in Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing)
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing
sources.claim: A 2025 robotic e-waste disassembly study integrates a UR10e arm, RealSense D405 vision and a custom mechatronic screwdriver to automate unscrewing of electronic devices; unscrewing is treated as the bottleneck sub-step rather than complete teardown.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-task (fastener removal from small electrical devices); shows automated unscrewing exists but only as one step of the teardown a power-tool repairer performs.

tasks.label: Adjust working parts, such as fan belts, contacts, and springs, using hand tools and gauges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench work in an electric motor repair shop: after reassembling a fractional-horsepower or industrial motor, the repairer adjusts brush spring pressure and brush-holder position, sets rotor end play with shims, and adjusts the centrifugal start-switch contacts, checking with feeler gauges, spring scales and dial indicators until values match the manufacturer's spec sheet. Motors vary widely in make, model, size and wear condition.

Field service on motor-driven equipment in an industrial plant or commercial mechanical room: adjusting V-belt or fan-belt tension and sheave alignment on a motor/blower or motor/pump drive by loosening motor-base bolts, sliding the motor on its rails or turning the tensioning screw, checking with a belt tension (deflection or sonic) gauge and a straightedge, then re-torquing the mounts. Work is done in place, in tight guarded spaces, sometimes hot or dirty.

Adjusting contacts, springs and gaps in motor controls: magnetic contactor/starter contact gap, wipe and pressure, relay armature travel, limit and pressure switch trip points and overload settings, using feeler gauges, screwdrivers and spring gauges, either on the bench or inside a motor control center cabinet with the circuit locked out.

Power tool repair bench in a shop or tool service center: adjusting parts in drills, saws, grinders and nailers — brush spring tension, gear-case shims, depth stops, blade bevel/miter detents and fence squareness, clutch and depth-of-drive settings — using hand tools, squares and gauges, then test-running the tool. Many different brands and models pass the same bench.

Small-site/residential service call: adjusting the limit and force springs/screws on a garage-door opener, the differential and cut-in springs and contacts of a well-pump pressure switch, or the belt on an attic or crawlspace blower — working overhead or in cramped, dusty, non-standard spaces at a customer's premises with only hand tools and a gauge.

sources.system: Vision-guided robotic bolt-tightening station (INESC TEC / automotive assembly line)
sources.developer: INESC TEC with automaker (reported in ASSEMBLY magazine)
sources.title: Robots Automate Bolt-Tightening on Automotive Assembly Lines | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Vision-guided six-axis robots with 3D vision and force sensing now perform bolt tightening to spec on a van assembly line, compensating for part position variation from conveyor tolerances.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: torqueing fasteners to spec on a fixtured workpiece. Adjusting belt tension or a motor mount requires the same loosen/position/re-torque fastener manipulation with force feedback on comparably sized hardware.

sources.system: SEETECH DRAGON X15 Robotic headlamp aiming machine
sources.title: Advanced Headlamp Aiming Machines with ±1 mm Proven Accuracy
sources.claim: A commercial end-of-line headlamp aiming machine measures beam position optically and, in its robotic configuration, has a collaborative robot arm find the adjustment screws and drive them until the lamp is within specification, fully automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: measure-with-a-gauge then turn an adjustment screw until the reading meets spec — the same closed measure/adjust/verify loop as setting contact gap, spring pressure or belt tension with hand tools and gauges, on a fixtured workpiece.

sources.title: End of Line Testing Systems – Wheel Aligners, Headlamp Aimers, Robotic Toe Set & Automated Tooling Changeover
sources.claim: Deployed end-of-line wheel alignment cells use robots carrying socket gear heads and nut runners to loosen, turn and re-lock tie rods and cam bolts until measured toe is within ±0.03 degrees, across several vehicle models with automatic tooling changeover.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: adjusting a threaded mechanical setting to a gauged specification. Same class of operation as sliding a motor on its base to a measured belt tension and re-torquing, with comparable hardware sizes and torque levels.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: gauge-referenced clearance setting with a screwdriver — mechanically the same operation as setting contact gap or armature travel with a feeler gauge, in a purpose-built fixtured station.

tasks.label: Lubricate moving parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Motor repair shop bench: during rebuild of a fractional-to-mid-size industrial electric motor, the repairer packs new ball bearings with the specified grease, charges the bearing cavity/end-bell housings to the correct fill percentage, and wipes excess before reassembly. Motor models vary from job to job; work sits on an open bench with hand tools, a grease gun and a bearing packer.

Power tool / small appliance repair bench: after opening a drill, grinder, saw or blower, the repairer cleans out spent grease and repacks the gear housing, oils sleeve bushings and armature bearing seats, and puts light oil on trigger-switch linkages and sliding parts before reassembly. Small parts, tight clearances, many different tool models.

Scheduled relubrication route in an industrial or institutional facility (plant, mill, water plant, HVAC mechanical rooms): technician visits installed motors, pumps and fans, wipes the zerk fittings, removes drain plugs, applies a metered number of grease-gun shots to each bearing on a PM schedule, checks for purge/leakage and logs the point. Recurring work at fixed, known grease points.

One-off field lubrication during a repair or installation call at an as-found site: greasing a rooftop fan motor, a farm irrigation pump motor, a hoist or conveyor drive on a construction/jobsite, or a customer's outdoor equipment. Ladder or awkward access, dirt, weather, unknown fitting locations and lubricant history, done as part of a single visit.

Batch/production-repeat lubrication in a rebuild or remanufacturing shop: identical units (e.g., small motors, starters/alternators, pump motors) come through in lots, and the same grease charge or oil dose is applied to the same bearing seats, gears or bushings on unit after unit, often at a dedicated station on the shop floor.

sources.system: DOPAG automated greasing production cell with FANUC LRM 200iD/7L robot (lubriLine pump, MR40 control)
sources.title: Automated Grease Dispensing System | DOPAG
sources.claim: A productized greasing cell built by DOPAG with FANUC uses a 6-axis industrial robot to carry out the complete greasing of plastic gearwheels: the robot picks parts from workpiece carriers, presents them to shot and spray valves, and grease is applied inside and out with metered dosing verified by a flow-measuring cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is production greasing of gearwheels rather than repair-shop lubrication; it transfers because the objects (small gears, housings), the lubricants (grease and oil), the metered dose and placement precision, and the required cleanliness are the same as repacking a power-tool gear housing or charging a motor bearing cavity, provided the part is presented fixtured.

sources.system: Nordson EFD EV Series 3-axis automated dispensing robot with Liquidyn P-Jet CT jet valve
sources.title: Automated Grease Dispensing for Automotive Switches | Nordson EFD blog
sources.claim: An automotive parts manufacturer runs Nordson EFD's 3-axis EV Series benchtop dispensing robot with a Liquidyn P-Jet jetting valve to place precise grease dots that lubricate radio and climate-control switch mechanisms in production, replacing a prior contact-dispense process that over-deposited grease.
sources.transferJustification: This is lubrication of small moving mechanisms (switch contacts/sliders) on a fixtured line rather than in a repair shop; it transfers to oiling power-tool trigger switches and small linkages because the parts, the dose sizes and the placement tolerances are comparable.

tasks.label: Inspect electrical connections, wiring, relays, charging resistance boxes, and storage batteries, following wiring diagrams.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Repair-shop bench: incoming/outgoing inspection of an industrial or fractional-hp electric motor. Worker inspects lead wires, terminal board and lug connections, brush/commutator or capacitor leads, verifies the wye/delta or dual-voltage connection against the nameplate wiring diagram, and checks continuity, winding resistance and insulation (megger). Motor is dirty, often decades old, unfixtured on a bench.

Customer plant floor or building mechanical room: inspection of motor control equipment in place — MCC bucket, magnetic starter, control panel. Worker opens the enclosure, checks contactor/relay contacts and coils, terminal tightness and corrosion, traces control wiring against a schematic, and measures control and line voltages with meters, often with equipment de-energized and locked out.

Shop bench, small equipment: inspection of a power tool or small appliance/small motor (cordless drill, grinder, blower motor) — cord and strain relief, trigger switch, brush leads, field and armature connections, control PCB, and its charger, checked against the exploded/wiring diagram with a multimeter.

Storage batteries and charging equipment: inspection of battery packs and banks (cordless tool packs, forklift/floor-scrubber lead-acid batteries, standby strings) and their chargers or charging resistance boxes — terminal and intercell connector corrosion and tightness, cell voltages, internal resistance, insulation, resistor/charger wiring per diagram. Occurs in a shop or a facility battery/charging room.

Unstructured customer site: inspection of a motor and its wiring in place at a residence, farm, construction site, or on mobile equipment (well pump, HVAC blower, boat/RV, mine locomotive). Cramped, as-found access; dirt, weather, unknown prior modifications; worker follows a diagram to check connections, relays and battery/charging circuits.

Shop wash bay: degreasing a large industrial motor frame/stator housing with pressure washer, steam or caustic detergent before rewind or reassembly; heavy part moved by hoist onto a rack, rinsed, then dried/baked.

Precision surface cleaning/polishing: buffing commutators, slip rings, shaft journals and bearing fits with buffing wheel, crocus cloth or fine abrasive to remove glaze, carbon film and light corrosion without removing base metal.

Power tool / small appliance repair bench: cleaning small armatures, field coils, gear housings, chucks and switch housings with solvent, brushes and compressed air; buffing corroded small metal parts. Delicate, small, varied parts.
Cleaning stator windings and rotor cores of accumulated carbon dust, oil mist and dirt without damaging insulation — solvent spray or dry-ice/abrasive-free blasting followed by drying/baking.

On-site field service at a customer plant: scraping and cleaning an installed motor's exterior, cooling fins, air vents and junction box in place — motor mounted on a pump skid or conveyor drive, cramped access, dirt and grease removed with scrapers, rags, solvent and compressed air.

tasks.label: Weld, braze, or solder electrical connections.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Electric motor / power tool repair shop bench: soldering small-gauge lead, brush and field-coil wires to terminals, tabs, switches and plugs on power tools and fractional-horsepower motors. One or a few units at a time, varied part geometry, hand iron and rosin-core solder, joint inspected and sleeved before reassembly.

Shop rewind of a DC/universal-motor armature: after winding, the coil ends must be fused, brazed or soldered to the commutator tangs or risers. Armature held in a chuck or V-block fixture; repetitive ring of identical joints around one part; joint must be electrically sound and mechanically strong at speed.

Shop rewind of a large form-wound / medium-voltage stator: silver-brazing (torch, resistance or TIG) of coil-to-coil, jumper and lead connections deep in the end turns, with sleeving and adjacent insulation that must not be scorched; joint geometry differs coil to coil and job to job.

Shop repair of a squirrel-cage rotor or heavy conductor assembly: brazing copper rotor bars to end rings, or brazing heavy cable lugs and bus connections, with high heat input, flux and filler, part mounted on a bench or turntable.

Field service at a customer site: motor, generator or drive installed in place in a plant, mill or pump house; technician brazes or solders connections in situ in the terminal box or on the machine, working in confined, awkward positions with portable equipment and hot-work permits.

tasks.label: Verify and adjust alignments and dimensions of parts, using gauges and tracing lathes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Motor repair shop bench/inspection area: after teardown of an industrial AC motor, the repairer measures shaft journals, bearing seats, commutator or slip-ring diameters and runout with micrometers, bore gauges and dial indicators (rotor in V-blocks or between centers), compares readings to spec, and records which surfaces are out of tolerance and must be restored.

Shop machine area: rotor/armature chucked in a lathe (or commutator/slip-ring turning attachment); repairer trues the commutator or slip rings, undercuts mica, takes light cuts to restore a concentric surface, then verifies diameter and runout with micrometer and dial indicator until within tolerance.

Shop machine area: restoring a worn shaft journal, bearing housing bore, or end-bracket fit to dimension (turning/grinding, sleeving or metal-spray then machining back), checking the worn as-found geometry first and gauging fit and concentricity to final tolerance.

Customer plant/mechanical room or outdoor pump skid: verifying and adjusting alignment of an installed motor to its driven load (pump, fan, compressor) with dial indicators or a laser alignment tool — checking soft foot, loosening hold-down bolts, inserting/removing shims, jacking horizontally, re-measuring until offset and angularity are within tolerance.

Bench repair of small power tools and fractional-horsepower motors: checking small armature commutator diameter and runout, gear mesh and bearing/housing fits with calipers and feeler gauges, and skimming the commutator on a small bench lathe before reassembly.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: production turning with gauge-driven correction rather than motor repair. Transfer holds because the objects (turned metal shafts/round parts), the instruments (dimensional gauging to ±0.001 in), and the corrective action (adjusting the lathe until the measured dimension is in tolerance) are the same operations the repairer performs on rotor journals and commutators.

tasks.label: Steam-clean polishing and buffing wheels to remove abrasives and bonding materials, and spray, brush, or recoat surfaces as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench/wash-bay reconditioning in a motor & power-tool repair shop: technician pulls a caked cotton or sisal buffing/polishing wheel off a bench polisher spindle, steam-cleans (steam jenny / hot pressure washer) to strip burned-on compound, loose abrasive grit and bond residue, dries it, inspects for glazing, tears and out-of-round, rakes/fluffs the face, recoats with fresh compound, remounts and test-spins.

Steam-cleaning the polishing/buffing machine assembly along with its wheels in the shop cleaning bay — guards, housings, spindle, table and hood coated in compound sludge and metal fines — then blowing dry and spraying or brushing a touch-up/rust-preventive coating on the cleaned metal surfaces before reassembly.

On-site field service at a customer's plant: cleaning buffing/polishing wheels and the installed equipment in place on the customer's production floor with a portable steam unit, masking and containing runoff around live production equipment, then brushing or spraying coating on cleaned surfaces.

Small power-tool accessories in a tool rebuild shop: felt bobs, wool/foam bonnets, small cloth buffs and mops from angle grinders, die grinders and bench grinders degreased/steamed at a bench sink, raked clean of caked compound, recoated with compound or discarded and replaced.

Recoating/rebuilding a cleaned wheel or lap: applying fresh bonding adhesive and abrasive grit (or spraying a coating/sealer onto a felt or leather wheel), curing/drying, then truing, balancing and a test run before return to service.
